text.enUS: Elwynn Forest. In Elwynn Forest, Stormwind draws timber, gold, fish, and crops from the land. Northshire Abbey sends human recruits into the woods, where vermin, displaced wildlife, and brigands threaten the peace. Elwynn Forest stretches south from Stormwind’s gates to the Nazferiti River. Rain feeds its fertile fields, while dense hardwood forests supply the capital. Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp send grain, livestock, lumber, and raw copper to Stormwind. Elwynn also breeds sturdy Evendale horses, prized by travelers and knights across the kingdom.

Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey trains new defenders in Northshire Valley, among Elwynn Forest's northern foothills. Rebuilt after the First War, it is the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a leading school for those answering Stormwind's call. Clerics from Lordaeron came south centuries ago to spread the Holy Light and founded the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery soon became part of kingdom life, caring for the sick and tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. In the First War, brigands and the Orcish Horde attacked it repeatedly, and the abbey was destroyed. After the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary and refounded its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire.

Dun Morogh. In Dun Morogh, dwarves and displaced gnomes face threats from troggs, Frostmane trolls, and leper gnomes. Its guarded peaks hold Ironforge and offer shelter to both peoples. Dun Morogh’s high peaks rise between Searing Gorge to the south and the Wetlands to the north. Snowmelt feeds rivers across Khaz Modan, while copper and iron veins run through the mountains. Dwarven Mountaineers watch the narrow routes through North Gate Pass and South Gate Pass. At the region’s heart, Ironforge lies beneath the mountain as the capital of King Magni Bronzebeard’s realm. The Deeprun Tram links the city directly to Stormwind.

Coldridge Valley. In Coldridge Valley, young dwarves and gnome refugees train for service to Ironforge. Snow blankets the sheltered vale in Dun Morogh's southwestern heights, and Coldridge Pass is its lone route to the wider mountain realm. Anvilmar is where new recruits learn to fight, move unseen, and wield sorcery. Veteran dwarven instructors train them alongside displaced gnome scholars. Beyond the hall, snow covers the valley floor, where boars and hungry winter wolves test the novices' skill at surviving the frontier. Sheer cliffs keep the vale apart from much of Dun Morogh's trade.

Teldrassil. Teldrassil rises from the sea off Kalimdor's northwest coast, its crown sheltering Darnassus. Druids raised the World Tree after the Third War, but its growth is troubled. You stand beneath Teldrassil's vast limbs above the Veiled Sea. Hills, rivers fed by morning dew, misty lakes, and ancient glades spread across its boughs. Darnassus, the kaldorei capital, lies at the western edge. At the base of the trunk, Rut'theran Village is the island's harbor, linked to the crown by a mystical gateway.

Shadowglen. Young night elves begin their training in Shadowglen, beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. The vale gathers around Aldrassil, where elders, priestesses, and mentors guide them before they travel farther into the world. Shadowglen lies beneath the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil, ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Eternal dusk falls over the vale, where Aldrassil rises as a massive barrow-tree. Its hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors who guide young night elves beginning their training. A narrow mountain pass leads south toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar. This single route out leaves the sanctuary sheltered and peaceful.

Durotar. In Durotar's red canyons, young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove themselves to the New Horde. Warchief Thrall founded this arid homeland after the Third War and named it for his father, Durotan. The Southfury River and the Great Sea hem it in. Razor Hill and the warrior city of Orgrimmar rise from its rock, while quilboar tribes and stranded Alliance troops still hold out. When Thrall led his people across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he chose an untamed frontier on purpose. Here the orcs would earn an honest living through labor and grit, not conquest. The cracked red soil, baked gullies and towering spires remind them of Draenor before its destruction. Water is scarce and little of the land can be farmed, but the Horde embraced its natural defenses and stark grandeur. Across the Southfury to the west lie the open Barrens, and to the north the ruined wilds of Azshara. Durotar is proof that the orcs have forged their own destiny.

Valley of Trials. In the Valley of Trials, young Horde recruits test their strength in southern Durotar. Orcs and Darkspear trolls face the valley’s wildlife and dangers before they leave ready to defend their people. Young fighters face the Valley of Trials before they venture into Durotar. Chieftains and trainers watch over them from The Den, a shelter carved into the cliffs. In the sunlit gulch, recruits hunt scorpids, cull aggressive boars, and keep lazy peons in line as they harvest scarce timber. The trial is hard, and only those who prove their mettle earn the right to leave as soldiers of the Horde. Those who fail are left beneath the desert sun.

Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear on Durotar's southern shore. Vol'jin founded it after Zalazane drove his people from the Echo Isles, naming it for his fallen father. The villagers endure exile and prepare to reclaim their home. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear survivors on Durotar's shore. After the witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin led them across the strait to the mainland. They raised crude huts beneath coastal cliffs, facing the water and the home they had lost. The village bears the name of Sen'jin, Vol'jin's father, who was captured and sacrificed by murlocs during the Third War. Though the Darkspear are closely allied with Thrall's Horde, exile remains their burden. Each day, the lost isles lie just across the shallows.

Mulgore. Mulgore shelters the tauren in a valley beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. High natural walls surround its emerald grasslands, plateaus, and plains. After Cairne Bloodhoof joined Thrall's Horde and drove out the centaur, the united tribes made Mulgore their homeland, with Thunder Bluff as their spiritual and territorial heart. The tauren have reclaimed a home after generations on the move. Centaur warbands hunted and displaced them across the central plains until High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof met Thrall and his displaced orcs. The tauren and orcs shared ideals of honor, shamanism, and strength, and the tauren joined the new Horde. With orcish help, Cairne broke the centaur hold on the region and led his people into Mulgore. They built permanent settlements here for the first time in centuries, and raised their capital, Thunder Bluff, on the highest northern mesas.

Camp Narache. Young tauren begin their training at Camp Narache, high on Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. The camp is the Hawkwind tribe’s ancestral home, where elders preserve old ways as quilboar press close and centaur scouts linger. Camp Narache sits at the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa, the main settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. Hide lodges and pavilions house the wounded, store weapons, bake bread, and offer a place for meditation and communion with ancestors. At the camp’s heart, elders and path trainers gather in a circle. Greatmother Hawkwind guides the newly initiated as they take up their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother.

Tirisfal Glades. In northern Lordaeron, Tirisfal Glades is home to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her Forsaken. Under blighted skies, fallen manors and dormant crypts surround their vast underground capital, the Undercity. Mindless Scourge and zealous Scarlet crusaders hem them in, and the free-willed dead fight for their survival. Tirisfal was once the fertile cradle of humanity, before the Lich King's plague withered them. The sun rarely breaks through the murky gloom over dying woods, neglected pumpkin patches and cold coastal hills. Old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills and Balnir Farmstead still stand, but most of their masters lie in mass graves or walk as restless dead. Yet a dark resilience holds on in towns like Brill and in the cloistered sanctuary of Deathknell, where freshly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life.

Deathknell. Newly awakened Forsaken gather in Deathknell, a fortified village in a secluded valley of southwestern Tirisfal Glades. Mindless Scourge, Scarlet zealots, and dangerous beasts press the settlement as the undead claim a place in Sylvanas Windrunner’s kingdom. You enter Deathknell through a narrow gorge, sealed by elite Deathguards against intruders. Newly awakened undead first open their eyes here, north of the Silverpine border and behind jagged hills. Most Tirisfal settlements kept the human names they bore under the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, but the undead who claimed this town gave it a new name. The old church anchors the southern grounds, where the Forsaken hold on. North of it, the village forge and surrounding streets remain overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Local caretakers bring new arrivals into the Banshee Queen’s service.

Zephras Isle. Zephras Isle is a flying island suspended within Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air. It serves as the ancestral starting home of the Skyborne, whose society now faces an existential crisis as the island's sustaining magic steadily erodes. With contact severed from neighboring sky-realms, its inhabitants struggle against elemental collapse and arriving refugees. Zephras Isle is an isolated landmass adrift in the endless winds of Skywall. For generations, the Skyborne lived here alongside native air elementals who helped preserve the magical currents holding the isle aloft. However, several centuries ago, those elemental stewards vanished entirely. Deprived of their presence and guardianship, the latent enchantments upholding the land have slowly begun to fail, causing Zephras to slowly fracture and destabilize.

Skyborne. The Skyborne, or shen'dorei, are an offshoot of high elves descended from rebels who fled Eldre'Thalas after opposing Prince Tortheldrin's demonic pacts. Striking a desperate bargain with wind spirits, their ancestors escaped Azeroth to dwell atop the floating Zephras Isle within Skywall. Today, with their elemental benefactors abruptly gone, their floating sanctuary faces internal fractures and physical collapse. Following the Sundering, the Shen'dralar of Eldre'Thalas languished without the Well of Eternity. Prince Tortheldrin devised a dark salvation: summon the demon Immol'thar and siphon its power. Horrified nobles and citizens resisted, fearing another Legion invasion. In response, Tortheldrin executed a bloody purge of dozens of houses. From the surviving shadows rose a resistance spearheaded by a masked figure known only as the Shal'nan ('the Veiled One'). When a desperate rebel raid on Tortheldrin's ritual sanctum descended into catastrophic chaotic magic, the Shal'nan rallied the survivors and fled west to the port of Eldre'narr, taking to the seas pursued by the Prince's fleet.

Darnassus. Darnassus shelters the night elves high among Teldrassil’s branches. Tyrande Whisperwind and the druids guide the city, where an ancient people face life without immortality and seek ties with the Alliance. Darnassus spreads across Teldrassil’s upper canopy, off northern Kalimdor’s coast. Wooden buildings and winding paths circle a quiet central lake. Bridges join terraces for tradesmen, craftsmen, Sentinels, and druids, leaving the wilderness close to the city’s daily life.

Ironforge. Carved into the heart of Ironforge Mountain in snowy Dun Morogh, Ironforge is the ancestral capital of the Bronzebeard dwarves and an unassailable bastion of the Alliance. Centered on the molten heat of the Great Forge, this sprawling underground city serves as a bustling hub of commerce, industry, and ancient dwarven lore. Under the steadfast rule of King Magni Bronzebeard, it now also shelters the displaced gnomes of nearby Gnomeregan. Ironforge was founded twenty-five hundred years ago when the first generation of dwarves awakened in Uldaman and journeyed west into Dun Morogh's jagged peaks. Delving into the tallest mountain, they built a massive shrine to their titan progenitor Khaz'goroth alongside the colossal Great Forge. Ever since, the city has expanded in concentric rings around that fiery hearth. Unlike surface capitals, Ironforge is entirely enclosed beneath stone ceilings, warmed by roaring hearths and subterranean rivers of molten magma. Its fortified gates and cavernous depths have proven near-impregnable throughout centuries of war.

Orgrimmar. Orgrimmar rises from the red canyons of northern Durotar as the orcs’ fortified capital and the New Horde’s heart. Trolls, tauren, and Forsaken allies also find shelter within its walls. Orgrimmar grew from the orcs’ search for a homeland after the Third War. Warchief Thrall led them to Kalimdor’s arid coasts, seeking freedom from demonic corruption and human bondage. He named the harsh land Durotar for his father and the city for his fallen mentor, Orgrim Doomhammer. Building the stronghold cost blood and sweat. With help from the tauren, Darkspear trolls, goblin engineers, and the Champion Rexxar, the Horde drove back centaur, harpies, and ferocious thunder lizards that threatened the canyons.

Stormwind City. In Stormwind City, the crown rests on a young prince while King Varian is missing. Rebuilt after the First War, the city is now the heart of the Grand Alliance, though debt and political turmoil trouble its white stone districts. Stormwind was founded over a thousand years ago by descendants of the Arathi. For generations, it was a flourishing, self-sufficient realm. The Orcish Horde crossed the Dark Portal and laid waste to the southern continent, razing the capital during the First War. Survivors followed Sir Anduin Lothar north across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. After the Horde fell in the Second War, King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance paid to rebuild the city. The Stonemasons Guild raised New Stormwind from polished white stone, with canals running through its boroughs.

Thunder Bluff. Across the plains of Mulgore, Thunder Bluff shelters the tauren above the grasslands. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof founded the city after uniting the nomadic tribes with the New Horde. Rope bridges and wooden lifts link its mesas, while its heights offer safety from centaur marauders and shelter travelers crossing Kalimdor. For generations, the tauren wandered across Kalimdor, struggling to survive centaur attacks. During the Third War, Cairne Bloodhoof joined Warchief Thrall, and together the orcs and tauren drove back the centaur and secured Mulgore’s pastures. Cairne led the allied tribes to these natural stone heights to guard their future. Thunder Bluff became their first unified, permanent home in centuries.

Undercity. Beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's Capital City, the Undercity is the Forsaken's dark stronghold. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner took it from the Scourge and remade it into an impenetrable sanctuary. Today it is the seat of Forsaken power and the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms. Long before the plague, the catacombs, dungeons and sewers beneath the palace were already called the Undercity. They held the tombs of nobles, the poorest people of the realm and the kingdom's deepest prisons, where the former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was held before his escape. In the Third War, Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas and laid waste to the capital. The prince then set his undead servants to dig out and expand the passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule.

Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a cold, ruined highland in central Lordaeron, once home to the treacherous human kingdom of Alterac and the scholarly magocracy of Dalaran. Today, the snow-dusted crags are overrun by the Crushridge ogres, the aristocratic bandits of the Syndicate, and remnant arcane forces. Travelers venture from nearby foothill settlements and the rebuilding city of Dalaran. During the Second War, Alterac was one of the Seven Kingdoms of humanity, but King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Alliance of Lordaeron to side with the Old Horde, hoping to preserve his realm. His treachery was discovered and stamped out, fracturing the nation into disputed borderlands. Following the kingdom's dissolution and the horrors of the Third War, Alterac's grand stone capital was reduced to rubble. Today, the Ruins of Alterac are occupied by the brutal Crushridge ogres, led by Mug'thol, while the surviving human nobility organized into the Syndicate, a vicious criminal syndicate fighting to reclaim their lost estates by force.

Arathi Highlands. The Arathi Highlands are a rugged plateau in southeastern Lordaeron, renowned as the ancient birthplace of the Empire of Arathor. Today, the kingdom of Stromgarde lies in ruins, leaving the craggy realm engulfed in multi-front warfare between the remnants of Stromgarde, the Horde, criminal Syndicate nobles, and invading ogres. Millennia ago, King Thoradin united the fractured human tribes under the banner of the Arathi, constructing the majestic capital of Strom across these dry, defensible plains. It was here that humanity forged its legendary compact with the high elves during the Troll Wars, mastering the arcane arts to push back the Amani. Over time, noble bloodlines migrated north into Lordaeron and south toward Stormwind, but the imperial guard stayed behind to form the martial realm of Stromgarde. For ages, Stromgarde stood as a bastion of stalwart warriors dedicated to keeping the forest trolls at bay.

Ashenvale. Ashenvale's sacred woods are now a battleground as the Horde cuts timber for Orgrimmar. The ancient forest lies between the Barrens to the south and Darkshore to the north, under the care of the Sentinels and Cenarius. Its canopy shelters moonwells and old ruins, alongside demonic blights, hostile tribes, and a contested frontier. Beneath Mount Hyjal, Ashenvale has belonged to the kaldorei and the children of Cenarius for millennia. Immense trees form a close canopy, turning the daily rain to mist and leaving the forest floor in twilight. Moss covers the ruins of elven settlements, where walking ancients and dryads keep watch. For thousands of years, the night elves built no true cities here. They hunted lightly and kept the wild domain in balance.

Azshara. Azshara is a rugged, windswept coastline in northeastern Kalimdor cloaked in vibrant, perpetual autumn foliage. Once part of the glorious night elven capital before the Great Sundering shattered it into the sea, it remains a dangerous wilderness littered with ancient ruins, brooding naga, and isolated practitioners of magic. Both the Horde and the Alliance maintain precarious outposts along its borders, wary of the restless ghosts and ocean horrors lurking within. Ten thousand years ago, this coast was the beating heart of the kaldorei civilization, surrounding the royal capital of Zin-Azshari. When Queen Azshara and her Highborne court drew the Burning Legion into Azeroth, the resulting War of the Ancients culminated in the catastrophic collapse of the Well of Eternity. The sea thundered inward, swallowing most of the magnificent city and leaving behind fractured cliffs, treacherous coral reefs, and waterlogged spires. The survivors renamed the ruined landscape after their fallen monarch, branding it as a cursed monument to pride and catastrophic betrayal.

Badlands. The Badlands is an arid, sun-baked expanse of cracked earth, dust storms, and rocky canyons nestled between Loch Modan and Searing Gorge. Despite being deep within dwarven Khaz Modan, it serves as a volatile frontier dominated by Dark Iron dwarves, troggs, Dustbelcher ogres, and nesting black dragonkin. It also houses the titan ruins of Uldaman and the Horde stronghold of Kargath, making it a critical strategic waypoint. Wedged south of Loch Modan's verdant hills, the Badlands quickly turns into a sweltering basin of barren flats and rugged ravines. Surviving here requires contending with merciless coyotes, cougars, vultures, and fierce sandstorms that obscure the horizon. Scattered across the plateaus are the crude encampments of the Dustbelcher ogres, while the brooding Dark Iron clan fortifies Angor Fortress and clashes with anyone trespassing on their territory.

Blasted Lands. The Blasted Lands are a desolate expanse of red clay and barren rock at the southeastern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, ruined by the chaotic energies of the Dark Portal. Once part of the verdant Black Morass, the shattered earth now harbors demonic remnants of the Burning Legion, brutal Dreadmaul ogres, and hardy desert beasts. Nethergarde Keep stands vigil over the desolate wasteland, guarding Azeroth from whatever horrors may spill out of the dormant gateway. Before the First War, this region was a continuation of the dense fenlands known as the Black Morass. That lush swamp was utterly eradicated when the warlock Gul'dan and the possessed Medivh tore open the Dark Portal to unleash the orcish Horde. Chaotic fel energies bled through the dimensional breach, stripping all moisture and baking the earth into cracked red clay. When the Dark Portal was later destroyed at the end of the Second War, catastrophic shockwaves scorched the terrain further, transmuting the native stone into its unearthly crimson hue.

Burning Steppes. The Burning Steppes are a scorched, volcanic wasteland flanking the southern base of Blackrock Mountain. Formed by the catastrophic summoning of Ragnaros centuries ago, this treacherous territory holds the primary overland passage between Stormwind and Khaz Modan. Today, it crawls with rogue Blackrock orcs, Firegut ogres, Dark Iron dwarves, and broodlings of the black dragonflight. Long ago, these foothills were simply the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains. During the War of the Three Hammers, the exiled Dark Iron clan established their kingdom here, raising their capital city of Thaurissan. Facing total defeat at the hands of the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, the desperate Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attempted to conjure elemental forces. Instead, he shattered the earth and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The violent explosion pulverized the surrounding mountains, tore open rivers of lava, and birthed the colossal volcano known as Blackrock Mountain, leaving the steppes forever charred and barren.

Darkshore. In Darkshore, Auberdine links night elf lands to the wider Alliance. This cold, misty coast in northwestern Kalimdor is the main gateway for travelers from Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. Ancient ruins and troubled wildlife mark the land, while cultists, naga, and a creeping rot threaten it. Darkshore stretches beneath the western shadows of Mount Hyjal and Felwood, where pine groves meet fog and cold, rocky shores. Millennia ago, the Kaldorei cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran flourished along this coast. The Great Sundering shattered them, leaving pillars and arches half-drowned or tangled in roots. Highborne spirits haunt the ruins, while scavenging murlocs and invading naga range among them.

Deadwind Pass. Deadwind Pass is a blighted, jagged canyon in central Azeroth connecting Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows. At its center looms the Ivory Spire of Karazhan, former seat of the Guardian Medivh, whose death unleashed corrupting magical runoff across the land. It is a lifeless corridor stalked by ogres, ghosts, and demonic winds, offering neither refuge nor civilized shelter. Once considered an extension of the Redridge Mountains, Deadwind Pass has devolved into a hollowed-out scar of bleached stone and petrified wood. A foul, relentless wind cuts through the ravines, giving the gorge its name. The sky above is locked in a perpetual sepulchral gray, threatening erratic lightning storms that make traveling with metal arms hazardous. Totemic effigies hang from lifeless branches alongside the main road, warning wayfarers to keep moving. There are no fertile soils here, no mineable mineral veins, and no towns or flight masters to offer aid.

Desolace. Desolace is a bleak, windswept desert on Kalimdor's western coast, defined by cracked gray earth, constant stormy skies, and the bones of fallen beasts. It is the ancestral cradle of the vicious centaur race and a contested wasteland scarred by ancient Highborne ruins, encroaching demonic cults, and bitter tribal warfare. Both the Horde and Alliance maintain precarious footholds amidst the dust, each seeking to carve out influence while warding off spreading corruption. Desolace was not always a barren expanse of ash and yellowed pools. Legend holds that the land withered when the earth elemental Princess Theradras drained the surrounding life force to regenerate her form. Zaetar, son of Cenarius, came to her, but rather than subduing her, he took the princess as his mate. From their unnatural union sprang the first centaur. In shame and bloodthirsty wrath, the newborn race murdered their father and overran the plains, leaving behind the scarred wasteland known today.

Duskwood. Duskwood lies beneath a curse, its sunlit past hidden by unending gloom. Stormwind has abandoned its human inhabitants, who cling to survival in Darkshire under the Night Watch's protection. Ghouls, giant venomous spiders, raiding ogres, and savage, mysterious worgen roam its groves and haunted barrows. Duskwood was once a rich agricultural tract in the Kingdom of Stormwind, with prosperous settlements such as Grand Hamlet and Raven Hill. Its ruin began when Guardian Medivh fell at Karazhan during the First War, unleashing waves of corrupted fel magic that twisted the woodland into a gnarled, shadowy morass. Spiders became terrifying predators, and fleeing wolves spilled north into Elwynn Forest. Grand Hamlet became Darkshire, where terrified townsfolk were left largely to fend for themselves after the royal garrison withdrew to defend the capital.

Dustwallow Marsh. Dustwallow Marsh is a vast, sweltering swampland in central Kalimdor, trapped between the arid plains of the Barrens and the Great Sea. Fed by perpetual subterranean springs, its treacherous fens harbor dangerous predators, covert faction skirmishes, and the lurking presence of the black dragonflight. It serves as home to the Alliance fortress-island of Theramore in the east and the Horde-allied Stonemaul ogres of Brackenwall Village to the northwest. Before the Great Sundering, Dustwallow was a high, grassy plain teeming with herd animals. The cataclysm shattered the valley, causing the water table to rise and drown the earth in endless stagnant pools, mossy shallows, and choking mud. Underground springs ensure the marsh remains perpetually humid and submerged, blanketed in thick fog and infested with crocolisks, raptors, and spiders. Jagged shallows and wandering bogs make travel perilous for any adventurer stepping off the crumbling causeways.

text.enUS: Eastern Plaguelands. The Eastern Plaguelands represent the devastated heart of the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, suffocated under Scourge blight, toxic mists, and corrupted fungal growths. Stratholme looms in the north as the undead power base in the region, while the zealous Scarlet Crusade entrenches in the east. Amid the nightmare, Light's Hope Chapel stands as a resolute, neutral sanctuary for anyone brave enough to fight back. Once known as the fertile Eastweald, this region was the agricultural spine of northern Lordaeron, anchored by the great metropolis of Stratholme and prosperous towns like Darrowshire and Corin's Crossing. During the Third War, Prince Arthas purged Stratholme after discovering its grain supply had been laced with the Plague of Undeath. Following the kingdom's collapse, the Scourge's dark magic ran unchecked. The soil turned brown and rotten, ordinary flora warped into colossal mushrooms, and an eerie orange mist settled across the valleys.

Felwood. Felwood is a blighted forest nestled between Ashenvale and Mount Hyjal, deeply poisoned by demonic magic during the Third War. Once a lush paradise of meadows and groves tended by the night elves, it now crawls with demonic satyrs, slavering beasts, and twisted ancients. Cenarion Circle druids, alongside outposts of the Alliance and Horde, desperately work to cleanse the land and purge the Shadow Council from its depths. Before the Third War, this valley was a peaceful haven of singing birds, clear streams, and tranquil groves guarded by ancient protectors. That ended when the dreadlord Tichondrius and the Burning Legion deployed the Skull of Gul'dan to poison northern Kalimdor ahead of their assault on Mount Hyjal. The skull's vile sorceries twisted the forest floor into a blackened mire. Though Illidan Stormrage eventually slew Tichondrius and consumed the artifact's essence, the land remained steeped in fel corruption. Mighty treants and ancients rotted from within, rivers turned to boiling bile, and the forest's beasts were driven into cannibalistic madness.

Feralas. Feralas is a vast, mist-shrouded rainforest nestled between Desolace, Thousand Needles, and the Veiled Sea. Sheltered by soaring mountain walls, it preserves an ancient ecosystem dotted with overgrown Kaldorei ruins and primordial beasts. Today, the wilderness is contested territory, caught between ancient Highborne remnants, invasive Gordunni ogres, and rival outposts established by the Alliance and the Horde. While neighboring Desolace and Thousand Needles have dried into barren badlands and desiccated canyons, Feralas remains intensely verdant. Mountain ranges seal off the canopy, sustaining a warm microclimate of deep mists, ancient trees, and towering waterfalls. Before the Great Sundering, much of Kalimdor looked like this. Over millennia, the deep jungle swallowed the monuments of the Kaldorei civilization that once ruled here, hiding forgotten temples and pavilions beneath strangling moss and thick fern brush.

Hillsbrad Foothills. Hillsbrad Foothills remains green while war tears through the last pastoral reaches of Lordaeron. Southshore's humans and the Forsaken at Tarren Mill clash across the fields, making the region a violent crossroads for Alliance and Horde armies. Hillsbrad remains green while blight consumes much of northern Lordaeron. Rolling pastures, pine groves, and working farms still recall the kingdom before the Third War. Armed patrols, rogue mercenaries, and scavenger beasts cross its fields and roads. Lordaeron's breadbasket has become one of its most contested borderlands.

Loch Modan. The Stonewrought Dam holds Loch Modan's great lake above the Wetlands. Around Thelsamar, troggs threaten the southern valleys while kobolds work the mines and ogres hold the northeast highlands. Loch Modan's lake fills a green valley east of Dun Morogh. Pines and birches climb toward the rugged peaks, while the Stonewrought Dam spans the northern rim. The dwarven town of Thelsamar draws mountaineers, hunters, and miners. Copper and tin veins run through the surrounding hills.

Moonglade. Moonglade is an ancient, secluded forest valley nestled high in northern Kalimdor, revered as the sacred heartland of druidism and the home of the Cenarion Circle. Sheltered beneath perpetual twilight and untouched by mortal corruption, it is a neutral haven where night elf and tauren practitioners study nature side by side. For non-druids, reaching this highland sanctuary requires braving the hazardous mountain tunnel of Timbermaw Hold. Ringed by sheer mountains north of Felwood and Winterspring, Moonglade exists in a state of eternal, serene night under the soft glow of Elune's moon. At its center lies Lake Elune'ara, a deep, tranquil body of water held sacred since the dawn of kaldorei civilization. The glade remained unmarred by the Burning Legion during both ancient invasions and the recent Third War, shielded by the vigilant demigod Cenarius and his offspring. Today, under the stewardship of Keeper Remulos, the valley serves as a peaceful redoubt where nature's balance is preserved free from factional conflict.

Redridge Mountains. Redridge Mountains face attacks from Shadowhide gnolls and Blackrock orcs of the Dark Horde. Rushing rivers cut through wooded slopes around Lake Everstill, but Lakeshire must hold the line with help from wandering mercenaries while Stormwind’s forces are tied up by strife at home. Redridge was once among the kingdom’s most peaceful regions, supplying Stormwind with timber, freshwater fish, and crops. Now Lakeshire stays fortified against aggressive incursions. Stonewatch Keep, once a proud stronghold of the kingdom, has fallen to renegade Blackrock orcs. Their control cuts off roads and threatens to overrun the eastern valleys.

Riverglades. The Riverglades is a contested river valley east of the Burning Steppes and Badlands, historically claimed by the Kingdom of Stormwind. Overrun by the Old Horde during the First War and largely abandoned by the crown, the region remains a battleground as local human loyalists clash with modern Horde outposts and local wildlife. It borders Redridge Mountains to the southwest, Swamp of Sorrows to the south, and faces Tanaris across the sea. Historically part of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the Riverglades fell into ruin during the First War when the Old Horde swept through the region. Its central settlement, Sunnyglade, was sacked by the orcs, who spared its mage tower solely to study human sorcery before enslaving the surviving townsfolk. Though Stormwind soldiers mounted an effort to liberate the captives and rebuild, the kingdom eventually deemed the entire valley lost and diverted resources toward defending the core homelands. For years, the region remained largely cut off from formal crown support.

Searing Gorge. Searing Gorge is a scorched, desolate canyon in southern Khaz Modan, bordering Blackrock Mountain to the south. Once a verdant expanse of the Redridge Mountains, it was devastated over two centuries ago by the apocalyptic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord. Today, the gorge is heavily worked by the Dark Iron clan, whose extensive slave mines in the Cauldron are closely monitored by the breakaway Thorium Brotherhood. Before the War of the Three Hammers, the territory that is now Searing Gorge was a green, rolling mountain region connected to the Redridge chain. That lush landscape ceased to exist over two hundred and thirty years ago when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, desperate to turn the tide of defeat, summoned Ragnaros from the depths beneath the world. The cataclysmic emergence of the Firelord tore the earth asunder, raised Blackrock Mountain, reduced the grand Dark Iron city of Thaurissan to smoking ruins, and burned the northern valley into a cracked expanse of ash, sulfur, and volcanic glass.

Shen'dralas. Shen'dralas is a rugged, contested wilderness situated between Feralas, Mulgore, and south-eastern Desolace. Dominated by ancient night elven remnants and troubled borders, it serves as a volatile crossroads where encroaching centaur, displaced outcasts, and bristling quilboar collide. Tucked away in the heights south-east of Desolace and bordered by Mulgore and Feralas, Shen'dralas is a raw borderland far removed from major faction capitols. Its craggy passes and hidden enclaves harbor desperate groups carving out existence on the edge of wild Kalimdor. From secluded vantage points like Evenshade Overlook to lawless refuges like Outcast Hideaway, the zone is defined by those who wish to watch unseen or stay forgotten.

Silithus. Silithus is a desolate, wind-scoured desert located in the far southwestern corner of Kalimdor. Beneath its arid sands lie vast colonies of insectoid silithid and the ancient ruins of Ahn'Qiraj, sealed a millennium ago behind the formidable Scarab Wall. Today, the druids of the Cenarion Circle maintain an embattled vigil against creeping swarms, doomsday cultists. Reaching Silithus requires navigating through the primeval jungle of Un'Goro Crater and ascending a wide, rocky pass nestled in its northwestern corner. The transition is stark: lush primordial growth vanishes into a vast expanse of shifting dunes, jagged stone, and unnatural towering hives. Water is virtually nonexistent, and the winds carry the hum of insect wings and the whispering sands. The Cenarion Circle maintains Cenarion Hold near the center of the desert, serving as the sole bastion of civilization and shelter for travelers, researchers, and warriors braving the hostile wastes.

Silverpine Forest. Silverpine Forest lies under Forsaken rule and threat from rival forces along Lordaeron's western coast. The Scourge's plague scars the woods, where worgen, diseased gnolls, and hostile human enclaves endanger travelers. Silverpine Forest lies between Tirisfal Glades and the sealed Greymane Wall. Once a lush wonder of Lordaeron, it has withered since the Third War. Ghostly fog moves among dying, silver-barked pines, and ruined farmsteads lie abandoned to the wilderness. Tirisfal Glades borders the forest to the north, and Lordamere Lake lies along its eastern shore. To the south, the Greymane Wall shuts Gilneas away from the chaos beyond. The Forsaken hold their central outpost at the Sepulcher and struggle to secure the woods from enemies on every side.

Stonetalon Mountains. In Stonetalon Mountains, sacred heights now face smoke, deforestation, and elemental ruin. Night elves and tauren revere the range, while border hostilities simmer below. Stonetalon Mountains rise from central Kalimdor beneath the Ill Winds. Moisture from the western seas brings sudden downpours and slick sandstone trails, while fierce gusts scour the lower valleys, blinding travelers with grit and hurling the careless from cliffs. Higher ridges carry evergreen forests around Stonetalon Peak. Night elves tend ancestral barrows and glades there, and watch sacred wyvern and hippogryph roosts along Mirkfallon Lake.

Stranglethorn Vale. Stranglethorn Vale is an untamed, dense jungle dominating the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, south of Duskwood. Once the seat of the great Gurubashi Empire, the rainforest is now strewn with crumbling troll ruins, savage beasts, and competing encampments of goblins, pirates, and soldiers. Control of the region is hotly contested by local troll tribes, the Venture Company, and rival factions carving out footholds in the heat. For millennia, the vale was governed by the mighty Gurubashi Empire from their capital city, Zul'Gurub. That dominion shattered when radical priests summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer, plunging the region into a catastrophic civil war. Though the Zandalari stepped in to crush the blood god's uprising, the empire splintered beyond repair. Today, the jungle is overrun by warring successor factions—most prominently the Bloodscalp in the northwest and the Skullsplitter in the east—both zealously slaughtering outsiders to reclaim their ancestral home.

Swamp of Sorrows. The Swamp of Sorrows is a murky, brackish wetland tucked between Deadwind Pass and the arid Blasted Lands. Once the northern expanse of the ancient Black Morass, its salt-crusted bogs are home to dangerous wildlife, green dragonspawn, and the ruined Temple of Atal'Hakkar sunken beneath the Pool of Tears. While the Horde maintains the fortified garrison of Stonard, the Alliance has no safe haven within the mire, leaving the wilderness largely untamed. Long before the coming of the Orcish Horde, these marshes formed the northern half of an enormous wetlands known as the Black Morass. Following the shattering of the Gurubashi Empire, the fanatical Atal'ai trolls fled into the mire to erect the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, intending to summon their bloodthirsty loa, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Sensing the catastrophe, the Aspect Ysera unleashed her powers, drowning the cursed pyramid beneath the waters of the Pool of Tears. Green dragonflight guardians led by Eranikus were stationed to vigilantly watch over the drowned structure. When the Dark Portal's cataclysm later scorched the southern morass into the Blasted Lands, this northern fen earned its current sorrowful name.

Tanaris. Tanaris is a vast, sweltering desert spanning the southern reaches of Kalimdor, defined by rolling sand dunes and blistering heat. At its heart lies Gadgetzan, a neutral trading outpost operated by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Beyond the bustling settlements, the dunes conceal hostile sand trolls, dangerous silithid hives, and the hidden domain of the bronze dragonflight. Tanaris is a barren, sun-scorched wilderness. Within the walled city of Zul'Farrak, the hardened Sandfury trolls guard their isolated domain. Today, the desert floor is ruled by hyenas, basilisks, and scorpids, while subterranean tunnels snake beneath the baking earth.

The Barrens. Across The Barrens, Horde outposts hold the roads while rival forces press in from every side. Once a forest before the Great Sundering, the central Kalimdor plain is now dry country of red dust, scrub, and wandering wildlife. The Crossroads anchors Horde traffic, but quilboar, centaur, and creeping corruption threaten its hold. For generations, tauren nomads hunted kodo and zhevra across the plains and fought a repeating defensive war against Kolkar centaur. During the Third War, Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor and helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive back the centaur and cross the savanna into Mulgore. The Barrens now links Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale. The Crossroads and Camp Taurajo guard trade along the Gold Road, while orcish homesteads endure the harsh climate as they build a lasting home.

The Hinterlands. The Hinterlands are a rugged, densely forested wilderness in eastern Lordaeron, tucked between the Plaguelands and the sea. The region is defined by ancient Amani troll temple ruins, the towering aeries of the Wildhammer clan at Aerie Peak, and a colossal Great Tree anchoring a mysterious rift to the Emerald Dream. Long before humans or dwarves walked northern Lordaeron, the forest trolls of the Amani Empire held dominion over the Hinterlands. Following their defeat in the ancient Troll Wars, their empire shattered into disparate tribes. Centuries later, after the tragic War of the Three Hammers drove the Wildhammer dwarves from Grim Batol, the dwarves migrated north and made their home on the surface at Aerie Peak. Taming the native gryphons and embracing shamanic traditions, the Wildhammer constructed a massive skybound stronghold. The trolls viewed these surface-dwelling dwarves as unwelcome squatters upon ancestral lands, sparking a ceaseless feud of skirmishes and raids.

Thousand Needles. Thousand Needles is a sprawling canyon of sheer sandstone pillars and sunbaked salt pans in southern Kalimdor. Tauren tribes cling to settlements atop towering mesas to escape aggressive centaur packs, while gnomish and goblin tinkerers run high-speed rocket cars across the dried-up seabed of the Shimmering Flats. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this territory was a lush river canyon fed by inland waterways flowing out toward the sea. The cataclysm tore the continent apart, thrusting the riverbed above the water table and altering the river's path until only dry stone and sandstone spires remained. Today, dozens of slender cylindrical columns rise from the canyon floor like a petrified forest. Tauren settled on the summits, stringing precarious rope bridges between peaks to establish villages out of reach of the hostile centaur marauders patrolling the shadow-draped canyon floor below.

Un'Goro Crater. Un'Goro Crater is a sunken, primordial jungle tucked between the arid wastes of Tanaris and Silithus. Dominated by roaming dinosaurs, living elementals, and a central volcano, this lush caldera is filled with ancient Titan relics and power crystals whose origins remain a profound mystery. Sandwiched between desert expanses, Un'Goro Crater defies the geography of southern Kalimdor. Ancient night elf records detailing the War of the Shifting Sands note that the insectoid Qiraji were turned back at the crater's edges, unable to penetrate what their tongue named the 'God Lands.' Scholars theorize the caldera served as a testing ground or ancient dwelling for the Titans during the shaping of Kalimdor. Stone pylons rise along the ridges, humming with energy, while crystal formations of blue, red, green, and yellow sprout through the primeval earth.

name.esES: Tierras de la Peste del Oeste

text.enUS: Western Plaguelands. Once the fertile agricultural breadbasket of northern Lordaeron, the Western Plaguelands now choke beneath a toxic mist and legions of undead. While Kel'Thuzad's cauldrons ruined the region's farms and towns, the soil still clings tenaciously to life. The Argent Dawn, the Alliance, the Forsaken, and the Scarlet Crusade all wage desperate campaigns across its blighted fields. Before the Third War, this land was a verdant corridor of farms stretching east from Tirisfal Glades toward Darrowmere Lake. Hearthglen governed the northern administration from Mardenholde Keep, while the sprawling town of Andorhal orchestrated the storage and export of grain across the kingdom. That crucial agricultural role made the region Kel'Thuzad's primary target. By introducing the Plague of Undeath directly into the grain shipments at Andorhal, the Cult of the Damned turned Lordaeron's sustenance into its doom.

Westfall. Westfall's farms lie exposed, and the Defias Brotherhood holds much of the countryside. Once Stormwind's breadbasket, the territory now struggles without crown support or military garrisons. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind with its pastures and wheat fields. After the Second War, the kingdom's finances ran thin and its leaders neglected the territory. Stormwind sent resources elsewhere and let its garrisons go, leaving the land fallow. Now barren pastures, harsh coastal winds, rogue harvest golems, and Riverpaw gnolls make survival hard for the few homesteaders who remain.

Wetlands. Fog and fighting shape life in the Wetlands, between Khaz Modan and Baradin Bay. Dwarven wars and orc invasions scarred the marsh, a rugged buffer between Ironforge and Lordaeron. Menethil Harbor keeps the Alliance connected to distant shores, amid Dragonmaw orcs, murlocs, and gnolls. Below the Stonewrought Dam, cold marshland lies under gray skies and heavy fog. Once home to thriving dwarven settlements, the Wetlands now hold sunken stone ruins, sodden bogs, and treacherous mires. You can enter by the narrow pass at Dun Algaz, coming north from Loch Modan, or cross the arches of the Thandol Span from the Arathi Highlands.

Winterspring. Winterspring is a vast, snow-covered valley nestled high along the northeastern slopes of Mount Hyjal, directly above the enchanted forests of Moonglade and Felwood. Known for its bitter cold, ancient Highborne ruins, and wandering apex predators, the region is anchored by the neutral goblin outpost of Everlook. It remains a land of fierce natural perils, sheltering remnants of the blue dragonflight while confronting demonic corruption along its southern heights. Perched thousands of feet above the surrounding wilderness, Winterspring rests beneath crisp mountain air and relentless snowstorms. Enormous exposed roots of the World Tree, Nordrassil, cut through the snowdrifts like towering wooden arches, warped and twisted during the climactic struggles of the Third War. While much of northern Kalimdor is dominated by dense woodlands and warm climates, Winterspring is a quiet land of medium alpine forests, rocky bluffs, and frozen lakes, home to formidable frostsabers, chimaeras, yetis, and thick-furred winter bears.

Blackfathom Deeps. Twilight's Hammer cultists now gather in the flooded halls of Blackfathom Deeps, along the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. The temple once honored Elune, the night elven moon goddess. Naga and satyrs have joined the cult in veneration of Aku'mai, a primordial hydra and servant of an Old God. Blackfathom Deeps once honored Elune, the night elven moon goddess. Long before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Highborne masons raised gem-encrusted bridges through its splendid halls. Queen Azshara commanded the waters around the sacred moonwell, keeping salt seas and mountain streams apart. When the Sundering broke the world ten thousand years ago, the temple sank beneath the coastal waters of the Veiled Sea. It lay undisturbed for millennia, until foul whispers began to rise from the darkness below.

Gnomeregan. In Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan lies ruined and quarantined after a desperate defense against troggs. Once the greatest technological wonder of the gnomish race, it was their underground capital. Its surviving people live as refugees in nearby Ironforge, while irradiated halls hold mutated troggs, deranged leper gnomes, and rogue mechanical sentries. Gnomeregan once gathered gnomish invention, competitive craft, and politics beneath Dun Morogh. With help from the nearby dwarves of Ironforge, its people built a vast mechanical complex powered by grinding engines and whirring gears. An intricate ventilation network needed fifteen technicians working around the clock to keep fresh air moving. At Tinkers' Court, gnomes debated and competed as their capital grew into a marvel of industry. During the Second War, they sent the Alliance of Lordaeron siege engines, flying machines, and armaments.

Hall of Thanes. Deep beneath the bustling city of Ironforge lies the Hall of Thanes, an ancient subterranean complex steeped in dwarven history. Intended for early Alliance adventurers, this secluded dungeon holds relics of the mountain kingdom's past that have fallen into peril. Gaining entry requires unearthing forgotten routes through the mountain itself. While Ironforge hums with the ringing of hammers in the Great Forge, forgotten halls delve far deeper beneath the stone. The Hall of Thanes represents one of these venerable subterranean reaches. Long tied to ancestral dwarven bloodlines and relics of stonecraft, it now requires intrepid Alliance champions to venture into its shadowed vaults to secure the depths.

Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm's volcanic tunnels shelter troggs and a demonic cult. The Searing Blade plots against the young Horde from caverns below the Cleft of Shadow, threatening the capital above. Ragefire troggs erupt from deep beneath Orgrimmar into a maze of volcanic corridors and lava pits. As orcish builders raise their new home above, the troggs grow aggressive. Magatha Grimtotem sends Maur Grimtotem to open talks on Thunder Bluff's behalf, but the troggs slaughter the envoy. They yield only to force.

Razorfen Kraul. In the far south of the Barrens, quilboar tribes defend the sacred brambles of Razorfen Kraul. They revere the thickets as the resting place of their ancestor, Agamaggan, while Charlga Razorflank’s rule threatens the region. Ten thousand years ago, during the War of the Ancients, Agamaggan joined the fight against the Burning Legion. The colossal wild god was slain, but his sacrifice preserved life on Azeroth. Legends say massive thorn-covered vines sprang up wherever his blood seeped into the earth, forming thick, defensive labyrinths across the southern plains. The quilboar revere Agamaggan as their divine ancestor and claimed these thickets as holy lands. The greatest became the Razorfen.

Ruins of Lordaeron. Perched directly above the subterranean Undercity, the Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollow remains of humanity's once-mighty northern kingdom. Fallen to the Scourge and Prince Arthas during the Third War, the surface streets and cracked plazas now crawl with wandering monstrosities, vengeful specters, and vile experimenters. Both the Alliance and the Horde dispatch ventures into this blighted citadel to reclaim relics of the fallen past or purge the horrors lurking above the Forsaken capital. Capital City was once the crown jewel of the Eastern Kingdoms, the seat of King Terenas Menethil II and the beating heart of human civilization. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend, he slew his father in the throne room and unleashed the undead upon the citizenry. Today, while the Forsaken dwell in the catacombs of the Undercity below, the surface ruins remain a forsaken twilight zone. Broken archways and weed-choked cobbles shelter feral beasts like Witherfang and deranged remnants of the past.

Scarlet Monastery. Perched in the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades, the Scarlet Monastery was once a peaceful sanctuary and center of learning for the Church of the Holy Light. Following the fall of Lordaeron, it was seized and heavily fortified by the Scarlet Crusade as their primary forward base in the west. Now, it stands as a sprawling stronghold divided into four wings, where fanatical zealots train, torture captives, and wage an uncompromising war against all outsiders. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a proud seat of Lordaeron's priesthood and a center for learning and enlightenment. Following the Scourge's devastation, surviving crusaders purged the halls of lingering undead and spiders, transforming the tranquil archives and courtyards into a fortified garrison. Driven by paranoia and grief, the Scarlet Crusade came to view all outsiders—living or undead, human or otherwise—as carriers of the plague who must be cleansed with fire.

Shadowfang Keep. In southern Silverpine, Shadowfang Keep shelters the rogue Kirin Tor wizard Archmage Arugal and the worgen he summoned. The old Silverlaine estate now holds feral beasts and the phantoms of its slaughtered defenders, while nearby Pyrewood Village remains bound to a horrifying curse. Shadowfang Keep was once Silverlaine Keep, a noble seat defended by the pious Commander Springvale. During the Third War, the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the rising dead, Archmage Arugal defied the Kirin Tor leadership and turned to the research of the wizard Ur. He summoned extra-dimensional worgen to turn the tide. The beasts savaged the undead, then slipped beyond mortal control and stormed southern Silverpine. Baron Silverlaine and his entire court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls beside the feral monsters that overran their home.

The Deadmines. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hide the Defias Brotherhood's staging ground. Once a source of Stormwind's gold, the tunnels were abandoned in the First War and long feared as haunted. Edwin VanCleef and goblin engineers work there beyond the realm's eyes, building an engine of vengeance against the kingdom. Before the First War, the Deadmines were called the greatest gold-producing center in human lands. Their gold supplied a third of Stormwind's reserves. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to darkness. Sir Anduin Lothar spent twenty months imprisoned by subterranean ogres while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity. Warchief Blackhand's rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages with the ogre Turok, and both met their ends there. Believed cursed and home only to shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades.

The Stockade. The Stockade holds dangerous prisoners beneath Stormwind's canal district near the Mage Quarter. Built as a high-security prison for cutthroats, political insurgents, and captured enemies of state, it has fallen into violent anarchy. Warden Thelwater is forced back to the entrance, seeking help to crush the riot before it reaches the capital. Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade has become a war zone. When the regular army marched to distant fronts, the understaffed prison relied on inexperienced youths, including fourteen-year-old recruits, to keep order. They failed. The inmates launched a bloody, coordinated rebellion, tore their wool blankets into gang scarves, and cut down the remaining guards. Warden Thelwater barely holds the entrance, while convicts control the cells, hallways, and holding blocks.

Wailing Caverns. Beneath the Barrens' Lushwater Oasis, the Wailing Caverns are named for the eerie whistle of trapped steam. Their maze of underground springs and fissures was meant to revive Kalimdor's sun-bleached savanna, a noble druidic effort. Now it is a warped, poisonous underworld, teeming with twisted wildlife and fallen disciples in the grip of a deep, unnatural nightmare. The night elf druid Naralex found this vast water system and devised an ambitious plan. Through a conduit into the Emerald Dream, he would draw pure primal life through the springs and turn the parched Barrens back into a thriving paradise. Deep in the caverns, anchored by his loyal acolytes, Naralex slipped into communion with the Dream. But his sleeping mind touched the Emerald Nightmare instead. The corruption seized him at once, and his conduit became a valve pouring venom and madness into the underground waters.

text.enUS: "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. At the Stonefield homestead in south-central Elwynn Forest, “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield keeps watch over the neighborhood. Widowed when her husband fell in the kingdom’s military campaigns, she is known throughout the valley for her pork belly pies. She stays outside the farmhouse beside Ma Stonefield and remains deeply suspicious of the rival Maclure family. Bernice carries the cost of war, as many common folk in the Kingdom of Stormwind do. Her husband fell in military campaigns, and she now lives with her kin at the family homestead. She helps Ma Stonefield manage the farm’s daily affairs, keeping the household fed and running. Her pork belly pies have made her famous among the people of the valley.

"Pretty Boy" Duncan. After tracking down Catelyn the Blade on behalf of her father, an adventurer learns that her weapon is no longer in her hands. She demands that her lost dagger be retrieved from a pirate named Pretty Boy Duncan before she cooperates further. Following the trail from Ansirem's Key leads directly to Catelyn the Blade, who ran away from a quiet life of scholarship and dusty tomes alongside mages. She cannot hand over her dagger at her father's request, since she no longer has it. If anyone hopes to secure her blade, they will first have to deal with the Bloodsail Buccaneer who took it.

... and Bugs. Morgan Stern in Theramore is working on a recipe that could become the next food craze in Stormwind. With the Mudrock tongues already in hand, the next part of the dish calls for the shelled legs of a giant crab, and only pristine, unscarred ones will do. Morgan Stern wants the shell of the crab leg to be a key part of how the dish looks, so every leg has to be pristine and unscarred. An adult crab might carry only one or two such legs, and the research calls for a lot of them. The Muckshells of Dustwallow Marsh will not do. Only the crabs of the faraway Swamp of Sorrows will suit, so a journey lies ahead.

text.enUS: ... and that note you found. In Westfall, a scorched note survives beside a dying campfire. Its brief message points toward a place called the twin land. Across Westfall's abandoned fields and wind-scoured plains, travelers find camps left by vagrants, outlaws, and desperate wanderers. This small camp may have been left in haste or secrecy; its provisions lie abandoned, and embers still glow. A scorched slip of parchment rests among the scattered debris.

99-Year-Old Port. The 99-Year-Old Port is an exceptionally rare bottle of vintage liquor shipped from Booty Bay as a personal gift for Gazlowe. After a cargo accident on the Ratchet docks, it was snatched away by a lunatic named Mad Magglish, who fled into the twisting tunnels outside the Wailing Caverns. Transporting precious freight across the Great Sea always carries risks, but Crane Operator Bigglefuzz made things far worse during a routine morning unloading in Ratchet. Attempting to clear an overwhelming shipment from Booty Bay, the goblin overloaded his crane and brought a mountain of crates crashing down onto the docks. In the chaos, the town eccentric—a troublesome figure known as Mad Magglish—snatched an extraordinarily aged bottle of 99-Year-Old Port and bolted into the hills toward the Wailing Caverns.

A Bad Egg. Curgle Cranklehop speaks of the eggs that cannot be saved, which will never hatch. Some hippogryph eggs cannot be saved, and a bad egg is one that will never hatch. It is Curgle Cranklehop who deals with such eggs.

A Baying of Gnolls. Gnolls raid Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire from the Redridge foothills. Blackrock orcs already threaten the region, and Verner asks travelers to drive off the brutes and mystics endangering his horses. Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire has become dangerous to run. Blackrock orcs hold the heights, and gnoll packs roam the ridges around town. Gnoll raiders have reached the northern edge of Verner’s paddocks, preying on horses that wander too close to the bluffs.

text.enUS: A Bloodstained Journal Page. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has a torn, bloodstained journal page examined during the investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle. A few words remain legible, and she asks Clerk Daltry to compare the handwriting with the Town Registry. Commander Althea Ebonlocke watches over Darkshire and asks that the handwriting on a torn, bloodstained page be examined. Though thick blood covers it, a few words remain legible for Clerk Daltry to compare with the Town Registry.

A Bump in the Road. Trackmaster Zherin looks after the track at the Mirage Raceway, and the animals out on the Shimmering Flats have grown big enough that their numbers must be kept down before they wander onto it. You are asked to thin out Saltstone Basilisks, Crystalhides and Gazers. A basilisk once collided with a racer belonging to the goblins, the Red Thunder, and in the aftermath Kronkrider took Zherin on to look after the track. Zherin cannot say what the animals out on the Shimmering Flats are eating to get so big, only that their numbers have to be kept down, or one will stray onto the course mid-race. Clearing wreckage is bad enough, and Zherin would rather not pick it out of burnt animal parts as well.

A Bundle of Hides. Jahan Hawkwing sends cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. The delivery takes you across central Kalimdor and introduces the Crossroads wind rider roost. Hunters bring game hides and meat to the Crossroads, where Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from across the Barrens. The outposts cannot process every raw hide, so he asks travelers to carry them west to Thunder Bluff. Master leatherworkers there can turn the pelts into gear for the Horde.

A Bundle of Trouble. At Eastvale Logging Camp, A Bundle of Trouble begins with timber left in the woods and a deadline near. Supervisor Raelen needs the cut wood brought back before the shipment falls behind. Supervisor Raelen has a shipment of timber due soon. Eastvale Logging Camp cuts wood for Stormwind, and her crew has fallen behind schedule. With the deadline close, Raelen needs the timber sent on its way.

A Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, a weathered parchment carries the trail of notorious pirate Captain Sanders. It marks the second step in a treasure hunt across the bluffs and coastlines. After you follow Captain Sanders' first treasure map, you find a parchment that points farther inland into Westfall. The scrawled note sends you east from the coast, up the bluffs toward the main road. Near crumbling stone ruins and an abandoned chimney, an old barrel marks the next place Sanders hid a clue, drawing seekers deeper into the troubled farmlands.

A Curious Pair. In the Sepulcher, Trevan Rol spots an unusual pair passing through Silverpine Forest. The tauren and high elf travel under the Earthen Ring's banner, a rare sight in Horde territory that draws suspicion. Trevan Rol sees two travelers claiming to represent the Earthen Ring pass along the road by the Sepulcher. The outpost is a grim waystation where strangers, especially those on diplomatic business, draw close scrutiny. A tauren traveling under the shamanic order's banner raises little surprise. His cloaked companion is another matter: the scout recognizes an unmistakable high elf, a sight that strikes the Forsaken as exceedingly strange.

A Dark Threat Looms. At Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII suspects sabotage and sends volatile powder north for examination. A courier must carry it through the perilous Wetlands to demolition expert Ashlan Stonesmirk at Dun Modr. A strange-smelling powder came from a suspicious barrel near the Stonewrought Dam’s eastern ramp, where Hinderweir had spotted Dark Iron sappers. Disturbances around the dam have put the chief engineer on alert. He suspects the powder is a refined explosive meant to shatter dwarven masonry, but the dam has no specialized equipment to test it. Before he draws a firm conclusion, he wants a military demolitionist to examine the sample.

A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, sabotage threatens a vital barrier in Loch Modan. A barrel hidden near the water holds strange smelling powder, and you bring a sample to Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Whispers of sabotage have drawn attention to the shoreline around the Stonewrought Dam. Near the water's edge, an out-of-place barrel holds strange, pungent powder that has no place among the dam's maintenance supplies.

A Dark Threat Looms. Dark Iron attacks in the Wetlands have Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII fearing for the Stonewrought Dam. With much of its garrison sent to the Alliance Front, you investigate sappers near the eastern ramp. The Stonewrought Dam holds back Loch Modan's waters, a great feat of Ironforge engineering. As conflicts spread across Khaz Modan and beyond, much of its security detail has been reassigned to the Alliance Front. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII and his small remaining crew now face the threat of an attack with little protection.

A Dark Threat Looms. At the Stonewrought Dam, suspicious powder puts Loch Modan and Ironforge in danger. Ashlan Stonesmirk in Dun Modr identifies it as unstable Seaforium, which can explode catastrophically when it touches water. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognizes the silver crystals and distinct odor in samples from the Stonewrought Dam as Seaforium. It stays inert while dry, but moisture makes it react violently. An unchecked explosion could blow Ironforge out of the mountain, Ashlan warns.

A Dark Threat Looms. The Stonewrought Dam faces a suspected Dark Iron plot, and Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs rare reagents from Loch Modan. You gather them so he can make a mixture to defuse explosives beneath the dam. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs a strange mixture to stop Dark Iron explosives. It takes Forest Lurker venom, a tear from a crocolisk in the Loch, and a Mo'grosh crystal. Together, these reagents can render the dwarven charges inert.

A Dark Threat Looms. In Loch Modan, Dark Iron saboteurs threaten the Stonewrought Dam. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII needs the charge disarmed before the loch floods the lowlands. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII saw Dark Iron Insurgents swim toward the base of the Stonewrought Dam with a keg of explosive Seaforium. No Mountaineers were nearby to stop them, and the infiltrators fastened the keg against the dam’s underwater foundation. If the dam breaks, the loch will pour into the lowlands, flooding the region and crippling dwarven trade and travel.

A Difficult Path. In Deathknell, a newly awakened Forsaken paladin begins training with the Light. After facing the undead outside the crypt, you are sent to the village church to meet Aramis Hammerhand and learn what holy power demands of the Forsaken. After you clear feral undead from outside the crypt, Shadow Priest Sarvis gives you an unexpected delivery. The Consecrated Scroll shines with holy energy, and Sarvis recoils before asking you to step aside. For one devoted to shadow and decay, the Holy Light burns like an open flame.

A Donation of Wool. A Donation of Wool is a material requisition organized by the Gnomeregan Exiles to gather essential textile supplies. Displaced from their technological home city, the exiled gnomes rely on sixty pieces of wool cloth from generous adventurers across the realm to sustain their community. Contributing to the drive grants formal recognition among the gnome refugees. Following the fall of Gnomeregan to trogg invaders and radioactive contamination, the surviving gnomes found themselves displaced from their high-tech metropolis. Operating as refugees primarily hosted by their dwarven cousins in Ironforge, the Gnomeregan Exiles face severe logistical strain. Routine material drives for basic goods like cloth are essential to keep their people clothed, supplied, and organized while surviving outside their ancestral halls.

A Dusty Unsent Letter. In Westfall, a dusty letter sheds light on Stalvan Mistmantle’s past in Moonbrook. The unsent parchment was found in an old footlocker and confirms that he lived there before his disappearance. Investigators searching for Stalvan Mistmantle’s past find an unsent letter in an old footlocker in Moonbrook. Darkshire’s town registry still gives his last address as the Moonbrook Schoolhouse, and Clerk Daltry wants to know whether he truly lived there. The letter confirms that Stalvan resided in the Westfall township for a time. Finding it disturbs a vengeful Forlorn Spirit, which guards the remnants of Stalvan’s past with bitter malice.

A Dwarf and His Tools. Prospector Ryedol warns that Dark Iron dwarves, looking like the Shadowforge clan, are all around. They just attacked the dig site where Ryedol worked, and Ryedol wants the lucky pick back. Dark Iron dwarves of the Shadowforge clan, by Prospector Ryedol's account, have attacked the excavation site where Ryedol worked. They killed nearly everyone, Ryedol's boss Hammertoe among them, and Ryedol barely escaped with life intact. The site lies to the north of Ryedol's position.

A Dynamite Plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket is eager to put dynamite to work in Stormwind. The inventive tinkerer in the Dwarven District has heard talk of industrial sabotage and wants a supply of coarse dynamite to begin her plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket, a gnome engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District, welcomes talk of industrial sabotage. Rather than urge caution, she asks passing mercenaries to bring her a bundle of coarse dynamite.

A Faded Journal Page. In eastern Elwynn, an old page points toward Stalvan Mistmantle's grim history. The Faded Journal Page lay for years in an old trunk at Marshal Haggard's home near Elwynn Forest's eastern border. Haggard had retired there, but his failing eyesight kept him from reading the weathered parchment. The page stayed neglected until investigators seeking the truth about Stalvan Mistmantle retrieved it.
