text.enUS: Another Message to the Wildhammer. After the first message, Otho Moji'ko at Revantusk Village says the Wildhammer and their gryphons are as close as a troll and a mate. Disgusting, but it can be used against them. Otho wants gryphons in the Hinterlands killed for their feathers. After the Highvale high elves, Otho Moji'ko has another message to send. The Wildhammer and their gryphons are said to be as close as a troll and a mate, which Otho finds disgusting, but useful. Kill the gryphons you meet across the Hinterlands and collect their Long Elegant Feathers. Gryphons are known to live in every region there. From the feathers, Otho will make the final message.

Another Power Source?. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan has more power sources and will sell you another one, at a price of ten Wastewander Water Pouches. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle guesses the first power source from Slake That Thirst ran out of time, or perhaps got lost in the sand. Whatever the reason, Bilgewhizzle has additional power sources to sell. This time the price is ten Wastewander Water Pouches, because times are tough all around and power sources do not grow on trees.

Ansirem's Key. Following his magical examination, Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver points toward an ancient troll dagger capable of disrupting the focal altar empowering the Stone of the Tides. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay. Ansirem Runeweaver determines that an altar or focal point amplifies the power of the Stone of the Tides. Overpowering that magic calls for another troll relic: an ancient dagger he found while researching in Stranglethorn. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay.

Anvilmar. In Anvilmar, young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomes gather to train and prepare for the road ahead. The fortified outpost stands in snowy Coldridge Valley, in Dun Morogh, around a great stone forge. At Anvilmar, a central forge burns within sturdy stone walls in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley. Class mentors and supply vendors are here, alongside veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before they set out into the wider kingdom. Snowdrifts shelter the outpost, but Frostmane trolls and wild beasts prowl the frozen valley, keeping its defenders on guard.

Apothecarium. In the Undercity’s southwest quarter, the Apothecarium drives the Royal Apothecary Society’s work. Under Master Apothecary Faranell, Forsaken alchemists pursue plagues, toxins, and engineered horrors for Lady Sylvanas’s campaign against the living and the Scourge. The Apothecarium fills the Undercity’s southwestern terrace with vats, dissection tables, and chemical fumes. Master Apothecary Faranell leads the Royal Apothecary Society’s work there, studying mortality and rot. Alchemists and surgeons experiment with tissue grafts and vivisection, and assemble mighty abominations. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has charged them with creating a plague that can eradicate both the Scourge and the lingering human presence across Lordaeron.

Apothecary Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim studies the Barrens for the Royal Apothecary Society. Sent to Kalimdor, he gathers unfamiliar reagents for the Forsaken. Apothecary Helbrim works beneath the harsh sun at the Crossroads, far from the Royal Apothecary Society's quarters in the damp undercity of Undercity. Sent across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he searches the Barrens for useful plants, fungi, and other natural specimens. He depends on travelers to bring him samples, including local fungal spores, and works with Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. Through Helbrim, the Forsaken's alchemists reach beyond the ruined borders of Lordaeron.

Apothecary Johaan. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan works to develop a plague for the Forsaken. The Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas have charged him with lethal experiments on local plants and animals. Apothecary Johaan works openly from Brill in Tirisfal Glades for the newly formed Royal Apothecary Society. Like his colleagues across Lordaeron, he follows direct orders to create biological and alchemical weapons. The Forsaken hope these weapons will secure their fragile future against the living and the Scourge alike.

Apothecary Lydon. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon studies poisons for the Royal Apothecary Society. Bored and sunk in gloom, he takes pleasure in lethal brews and the suffering they cause. His research seeks to secure Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and advance Sylvanas's New Plague. Inside Tarren Mill's chapel, now a laboratory, Apothecary Lydon carries out the cold work of the Royal Apothecary Society. Flowers in bloom and Hillsbrad Foothills' crisp air only deepen his languid melancholy. Deathcraft is the one diversion that lifts his gloom. Left alone, he poisons, dissects, and reanimates his pet frog, Umpi, again and again while he waits for new reagents.

Apothecary Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel advances Forsaken alchemy in Silverpine Forest. He studies the region’s corrupted wildlife and undead threats, and travelers help gather volatile reagents and investigate Scourge remnants. At the Sepulcher, Renferrel leads field research for the Royal Apothecary Society in Silverpine Forest. The society’s grand laboratories and high leadership are in Undercity, while he handles the work in the field. He secures native biological specimens, refines potent concoctions, and studies the grim ecology along Lordaeron’s western border.

Apothecary Zamah. Apothecary Helbrim needs his volatile fungal emulsion carried from the Barrens to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The mixture must reach her laboratory beneath Spirit Rise before it loses its potency. Apothecary Helbrim has cooked fungal blooms from the Barrens oases into a delicate emulsion. The brew quickly loses strength once prepared. Helbrim cannot travel to Mulgore in time, so he entrusts the flask to a reliable runner bound for Thunder Bluff.

Apothecary Zinge. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Apothecary Zinge works for the Forsaken. She studies biological specimens and arranges research shipments across Horde lands. Apothecary Zinge works in the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity. Under Master Apothecary Faranell, she searches for chemical and biological compounds that can advance the Forsaken's aims. Her work connects her with field researchers and scouts far beyond Tirisfal Glades, including at distant outposts in Kalimdor.

Applejack Still. The Applejack Still is a distillation apparatus used to process fermented apples into high-proof liquor. Approaching the device reveals a stinging vapor of concentrated fruit, which the machine condenses and dispenses as a clear spirit. The Applejack Still is a functional distillation device constructed to refine fermented cider into high-proof spirits. Anyone stepping close to the apparatus is immediately greeted by a pungent aroma of concentrated apples sharp enough to sting the nostrils. Its piping and condensing coils efficiently extract and concentrate the essence of the orchard harvest into potent liquor.

Apprentice's Duties. James Halloran needs giant crocolisk hides after his apprentice is mauled in the marshes. The tanner in Menethil Harbor asks travelers to finish the dangerous harvest. James Halloran sent his young apprentice into the Wetlands marshes to skin giant crocolisks. When the boy did not return, Halloran searched for him and found him badly mauled by the beasts. Menethil Harbor's tradesmen depend on materials from the surrounding country, where the bogs make such work dangerous.

Aquatic Form. In Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to master the waters. After proving worthy in Moonglade and attuning to the sea lion aspect, the druid comes home for formal recognition and Aquatic Form. Dendrite Starblaze sends the aspiring tauren druid back to Mulgore after the trials in Moonglade. The Pendant of the Sea Lion bears proof of balance and dedication through Kalimdor's waters. Carrying it shows the initiate has honored the ancient traditions needed to take an aquatic aspect.

Aquatic Form. You return to Darnassus with the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion. The rite teaches Alliance druids to attune their spirits to deep waters. For Cenarion Circle initiates, shapeshifting joins the druid’s spirit to the wild aspects of Azeroth. After enduring trials in the dark coastal depths and in Moonglade, young night elf druids receive the assembled Pendant of the Sea Lion from Dendrite Starblaze. They carry the sacred token back to Teldrassil as proof of their respect for the laws of air, water, and breath.

Arachnophobia. A Horde bounty sends you west of Windshear Crag after Besseleth, the ancient spider haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Claim her fang for Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat, and the mountain roads may grow safer for travelers after dark. A weathered wanted poster warns travelers on the main road south of Windshear Crag of dangers to the west. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path are overrun by spiders. At the heart of the threat is Besseleth, an unusually large orange spider who commands her brood. After sunset, she ambushes anyone who strays from the path.

Aramis Hammerhand. In Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand trains the newly risen Forsaken in holy combat. The Holy Light can answer their call, but wielding it burns their decayed flesh and demands fierce discipline. In Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand guides Forsaken who hold fast to their former faith. Before the Scourge swept across the north, many people of Lordaeron answered the Silver Hand's call. Aramis survived the fall of Lordaeron, then rose into undeath. He kept the martial and spiritual teachings of his former life, and now guides others who refuse to surrender their devotion.

Arcane Feedback. In Stormwind, Arcane Feedback prepares priests to face hostile spellcasters. High Priestess Laurena teaches the rite in the Cathedral of Light, where faith is shaped into a defense against arcane power. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena warns acolytes that arcane magic remains a danger. The Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order, while raw magic can turn volatile and lead to corruption or catastrophe. Warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts threaten the faithful. Priests learn that faith can become an active ward against spells around them.

Arcane Feedback. In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan directs human acolytes visiting Khaz Modan to seek their own teachings in Stormwind. The journey brings them to the Cathedral of Light, where human priests learn the traditions of their people. High Priest Rohan welcomes a human priest seeking deeper spiritual teaching in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward. Dwarven and human priests both serve the Holy Light, yet each people has its own rites, disciplines, and prayers of defense. Rohan keeps Ironforge’s teachings for his own clergy and sends human priests back to Elwynn, where they can learn the traditions of humankind.

Arcane Feedback. In Darnassus, Arcane Feedback sends human priests back to Stormwind. Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon reluctantly honors the Alliance summons. There, High Priestess Laurena prepares the acolyte for deeper instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. She recognizes the formal alliance between the kaldorei and Stormwind, yet distrusts human magical and spiritual practices. Night elves see arcane power as volatile and dangerous, a view shaped by ten millennia of grief since the War of the Ancients. Even human divine rites trouble the night elf clergy when they blur radiant faith with arcane workings.

Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. He serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. While the fanatical ranks of the Scarlet Crusade lean heavily on martial fury and holy fervor, Doan remained convinced that raw arcane power was essential to purging the Scourge from Lordaeron. Stationed deep inside the Athenaeum of the Monastery's library, he was entrusted as both a lorekeeper and an operational gatekeeper, safeguarding the Scarlet Key that secures crusade sanctuaries across the northern kingdoms.

Archaeologist Flagongut. At Menethil Harbor, Archaeologist Flagongut keeps in touch with field researchers across the Great Sea. The dwarven scholar of the Explorers' League is staying at the Deepwater Tavern while bound for the Whelgar Excavation Site. Archaeologist Flagongut rests with a mug at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Like many members of Ironforge's Explorers' League, he traveled west across Khaz Modan to help with discoveries near the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. Though far from the high halls of the library, he keeps ties with field researchers, processing lost relics and reports carried across the Great Sea from distant expeditions.

Archaeologist Hollee. In Auberdine, Archaeologist Hollee tracks dwarven research across Darkshore. The ancient ruins draw Ironforge scholars to the coast, where she keeps in touch with prospectors searching for relics and unusual geological formations. Archaeologist Hollee works from Auberdine, among the night elves who guard and settle Darkshore. The dwarven scholar is a regional contact for surveyors and expedition teams crossing the wilderness. The Explorers' League sends its people across the sea to uncover traces of ancient history, and Darkshore's ruins give them ground to study.

Archaic Rune. The Archaic Rune is an introductory quest given to fledgling dwarf Shamans in Dun Morogh. Imbued with elemental power from ancient Wildhammer inscriptions, this sacred tablet introduces young initiates to their elemental heritage. Delivering the stone to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar marks the formal beginning of their training in the ways of earth, air, fire, and water. Fledgling adventurers in Coldridge Valley discover the Archaic Rune after assisting local allies near Anvilmar. Bearing distinctive script carved in the style of the Wildhammer clan, the stone is visibly and palpably charged with ancient elemental power. The rune serves not merely as a relic of stonecraft, but as an elemental test: only those who possess a nascent attunement to the primordial spirits can comprehend the markings etched upon its weathered surface. For those capable of reading the script, it provides clear guidance to seek out proper instruction within the nearby dwarven outpost.

Archbishop Benedictus. In Stormwind City, Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church of the Holy Light from the Cathedral of Light. He guides the faithful and the Alliance through uncertain times. Archbishop Benedictus took the Church’s leadership after his mentor, Archbishop Alonsus Faol, died. He had seen the First and Second Wars devastate the kingdoms and helped oversee the building of the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. He vowed to uphold the virtues of the faith. After Lordaeron fell and the Scourge rose during the Third War, the human kingdoms looked to him for spiritual guidance. From the Cathedral, he counsels the royal court, trains newly initiated priests, and directs holy crusades against the undead and demonic forces threatening Azeroth.

name.zhCN: 大法师安斯雷姆·鲁因维沃尔

text.enUS: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver. Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver is a senior human wizard and a ruling member of Dalaran's Council of Six. Having survived the Scourge's destruction of Dalaran in the Third War, he oversees Kirin Tor operations from the Violet Citadel as Dalaran is rebuilt. Though dedicated to the rebuilding of his city, he also maintains discreet interests abroad—including a willful daughter who ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate. A veteran mage who helped defend Dalaran across decades, Ansirem Runeweaver sits on the Council of Six, the ruling magocracy of the Kirin Tor. He survived the devastation when Arthas Menethil and the Scourge marched upon the city and Archimonde was summoned. In the wake of Dalaran's fall, Ansirem has aided the efforts to rebuild the arcane city, whose protective shield was lifted early, and now works from the Violet Citadel.

Archmage Malin. Outside the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City, Archmage Malin directs arcane affairs. A former pupil of Archmage Trelane, he coordinates field agents seeking magical artifacts and rare reagents across the Eastern Kingdoms. Archmage Malin is the central contact for Stormwind's arcane practitioners, stationed beneath the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter. He learned magic under Archmage Trelane, and now works to protect the scattered legacy of his former master. While acolytes study inside the tower, Malin watches over matters across the realm that need magical oversight.

Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal is an arcane volume documenting the investigations of the master mage of the Tower of Azora. Delivered to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, the journal adds valuable magical insights to the great dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is known throughout the Alliance as an esteemed spellcaster stationed at the Tower of Azora in the eastern reaches of Elwynn Forest. Over years of solitary study, Theocritus has investigated curious artifacts, ley line anomalies, and nearby magical threats, recording his findings within detailed journals. Recovering such a volume represents a rare opportunity to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage.

Archmage Xylem. Archmage Xylem is an eccentric and reclusive human wizard dwelling in an isolated tower atop the cliffs of northern Azshara. Known for his volatile temperament and dangerous experiments, he has withdrawn from worldly affairs to pursue esoteric arcane research. Reaching him requires magical teleportation, and he only entertains adventurers who can assist in his peculiar studies or aid his personal vendettas. Perched high upon the jagged cliffs of northern Azshara, Archmage Xylem makes his home in a secluded spire overlooking the ruined elven coastline. Rather than building a road or trail, the wizard isolated his sanctuary entirely, relying on his servant Sanath Lim-yo to magically transport approved visitors up the cliff face. Observers across Kalimdor consider him profoundly eccentric and perilous to deal with; even fellow scholars treat him with deep caution, noting that he behaves unlike almost any other human mage.

Arena Master. Is there more to mastering the arena than this? Short John Mithril, the Pirate behind the Gurubashi event, may have the answer, and you will find him in the Stranglethorn Arena. Whatever you have gained at Gurubashi, it seems that mastering the arena asks for more. Short John Mithril, the Pirate who organizes the contests there, may know what. Look for him inside the Stranglethorn Arena.

Argent Dawn. The Argent Dawn is a neutral, knightly order dedicated to stamping out malevolent threats across Azeroth, most notably the Scourge and the Burning Legion. Formed by survivors of the Knights of the Silver Hand who rejected the fanatical zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade, they welcome champions of any race or faction who honor the cause of the Light. From their fortified sanctuary at Light's Hope Chapel to far-flung outposts across Kalimdor, they stand on the front lines against darkness. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine fell and Lordaeron collapsed into ruin, the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand broke into bitter disagreement. Many survivors surrendered to grief and paranoia, morphing into the xenophobic Scarlet Crusade. Yet veterans like Lord Maxwell Tyrosus recognized that their former comrades had abandoned the true tenets of the Holy Light. Refusing to succumb to madness or abandon the dead kingdom, they split away to form the Argent Dawn—an order committed to defending Azeroth alongside anyone willing to fight, whether Alliance or Horde.

Argent Guard Manados. At the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, Argent Guard Manados watches for corruption across Kalimdor. He serves the Argent Dawn and sends adventurers toward Blackfathom Deeps. Argent Guard Manados keeps the Argent Dawn's watch in Darnassus. While most of the order guards Lordaeron against the Scourge, he stands among the artisans and tradefolk of the Craftsmen's Terrace. His post lets him watch for threats to northern Kalimdor's balance. When word reaches him that the Twilight's Hammer has gained a foothold beneath Ashenvale's waves, he calls on capable heroes to strike at Blackfathom Deeps and recover the cult's artifacts of dark devotion.

Argent Guard Thaelrid. Wounded near the Pool of Ask'ar, Argent Guard Thaelrid is cut off in Blackfathom Deeps. The night elf scout entered the submerged ruins for the Argent Dawn, and now he has seen what gathers below. Reports of foul rites beneath the sea reached the Argent Dawn from the Zoram Strand. The order watches for rising evils and unnatural corruption across Azeroth, so it sent Scout Thaelrid into Blackfathom Deeps. He was to judge the threat, watch the flooded temple, and report back. Then the Dawn could decide where aid was most needed.

Argos Nightwhisper. In Stormwind's Park, Argos Nightwhisper guides Alliance travelers toward Darkshore. His brother Gershala studies the corruption spreading there. Argos Nightwhisper lives among the night elves gathering in Stormwind's Park. The district's quiet groves recall the kaldorei's ancestral woodlands. Like others of his kin stationed in the human kingdom, Argos connects the new allies across the Great Sea. Reports from across the ocean trouble him. He urges capable Alliance champions to travel to Auberdine in Darkshore, where his brother Gershala needs help against the spreading corruption.

Ariden's Camp. Ariden's Camp is an abandoned encampment nestled just north of the path threading through Deadwind Pass. Left decaying in the shadow of Karazhan, it stands as an eerie, quiet anomaly amidst the desolate canyon winds. Travelers between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows often pass it with unease, wondering who once pitched a tent here. Tucked against the crags north of the gorge road connecting Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows, this dilapidated campsite looks like an ordinary transient stop long forsaken by living men. Yet in the oppressive gloom of Deadwind Pass, nothing remains unmarred by dark sorcery. Whoever named the camp Ariden's and whatever fortune its owner sought in Karazhan's orbit, the pass's lingering horrors swallowed it, leaving only weathered cloth, cold ashes, and an enduring mystery.

Arikara. Magatha Grimtotem sends a warning from Thunder Bluff: Arikara may be hunting High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. She sends Horde adventurers to summon and slay the ancient wind serpent on the burial spires of Thousand Needles. Magatha Grimtotem enchants the refined Incendia powder, a reagent, to call Arikara. She warns that ancient tauren traditions have changed too quickly under the new Horde alliance, stirring the vengeance of the ferocious wind serpent spirit. Magatha sends you south to the canyon of Thousand Needles. She tells you to cast the powder onto a ritual pyre among the elevated burial sites of Darkcloud Pinnacle.

Arikara Serpent Skin. At Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arikara is summoned and slain, leaving a scaled hide behind. Carried to Whitereach Post, the skin proves the wind serpent was defeated. Arikara is a formidable wind serpent tied to ancient tauren legend. Rumor says she seeks retribution against Cairne Bloodhoof as tauren ways change. Under Elder Magatha Grimtotem's direction, champions prepare enchanted Incendia Powder. They light the sacred fire atop Darkcloud Pinnacle's burial bluffs, drawing the spirit-beast into the physical realm. Stripping Arikara's hide leaves the Arikara Serpent Skin, proof of her death.

name.frFR: En armes et prêt au combat

text.enUS: Armed and Ready. You carry Morbent's Bane back to Sven Yorgen, the weapon forged to strip away Morbent Fel's unholy defenses. Morbent Fel's hold over Raven Hill cemetery resists ordinary steel. Blades shatter or glance off the dark wards around the necromancer. A weapon made to break those wards is now ready. Grimand Elmore shaped the metal in Stormwind's Dwarven District, and sacred power consecrated it. Morbent's Bane can now sever Fel's tie to unlife.

name.esES: El ejército de los dragones Negros

text.enUS: Army of the Black Dragon. In Brackenwall Village, the ogre Tharg wants vengeance on the army of the black dragon. Tharg resents Overlord Mok'Morokk for telling the ogres to run rather than fight, and asks you to strike at the Firemane. Black dragons killed many ogres, and Tharg's wife was among the dead. Mok'Morokk, whom Rexxar made Overlord, told the survivors to run, and that is how they came to Brackenwall Village. Tharg says ogres are poor at running and ought to fight, and he believes Mok'Morokk cares only for Mok'Morokk. Tharg also says that Mok'Morokk tells all ogres to stay put and keep this place safe.

Arnak's Hoof. Arnak's Hoof is the macabre proof of death taken from the criminal Arnak Grimtotem. Hunted down on the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arnak was marked for execution by the defenders of Freewind Post after murdering a fellow tauren and kidnapping his sister. Arnak Grimtotem earned notoriety throughout Thousand Needles as an outlaw whose brutality crossed even the contentious lines of tauren clan politics. After murdering another tauren and abducting the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong, a formal bounty was posted for his death. Arnak holed up on the heights of Darkcloud Pinnacle, surrounded by Grimtotem guards. Slaying him and claiming his severed hoof serves as undeniable confirmation for Cliffwatcher Longhorn at Freewind Post that the murderer has finally answered for his crimes.

Arthas Menethil. Once the golden prince of Lordaeron and a celebrated paladin of the Silver Hand, Arthas Menethil fell from grace during the Third War while pursuing the demonic orchestrators of the plague. After claiming the cursed runeblade Frostmourne in the frozen north, he surrendered his soul, murdered his father King Terenas, and spearheaded the destruction of his own homeland as the Scourge's dark champion. Born to King Terenas Menethil II, Arthas was raised to embody the ideals of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Trained in combat by Muradin Bronzebeard and inducted into the Order of the Silver Hand under the tutelage of Uther the Lightbringer, he was revered by high and low alike as the future of humanity. Bold, skilled, and fiercely protective of his people, he fought tenaciously against Blackrock clan orc incursions and forest troll warbands. Yet beneath his radiant exterior lay an uncompromising pride and an obsessive dread of failure.

Arugal. In Shadowfang Keep, Arugal commands the worgen he summoned against the Scourge. Madness and grief have made the former Dalaran wizard their self-proclaimed father, while his power threatens Silverpine Forest. Before Lordaeron fell, Arugal belonged to the Kirin Tor. Some peers, including Dalar Dawnweaver, called him a charlatan who leaned on enchanted trinkets to make up for weak spellcraft. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Arugal searched for a weapon that could halt the undead. He used research by the late Dalaran mage Ur to pierce the veil between realms and summon the worgen. The ravenous beasts tore through the Scourge, but no one could contain their ferocity. Soon their hunger turned against innocent mortals.

Arugal Must Die. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver sends champions against Arugal. The rogue archmage holds Shadowfang Keep, and his worgen menace threatens the Forsaken’s hold on Silverpine Forest. Shadowfang Keep rises above the woods, where Archmage Arugal commands the worgen. The Forsaken have made the Sepulcher their base, but Silverpine Forest remains dangerous and fiercely contested. Driven mad by guilt and dark sorcery, Arugal unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. His ravenous beasts roam the forest paths and hinder Lady Sylvanas Windrunner’s efforts to secure the region.

Arugal's Folly. Assigned by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, this quest tasks Forsaken agents with securing Arugal's earliest spellbooks from a nearby farmstead. Uncovering the magic behind the worgen curse is vital for the Forsaken to turn it against the mad mage and secure Silverpine Forest. Recovering the Remedy of Arugal marks the first step in unraveling the threat looming from Shadowfang Keep. Dalar Dawnweaver, an ambitious Forsaken mage residing in the crypts of the Sepulcher, holds no respect for Archmage Arugal. To Dawnweaver, Arugal was an unremarkable practitioner whose inclusion in the Kirin Tor was baffling and whose magical understanding seemed amateurish. However, the monstrous beasts now roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver intends to deconstruct the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

Arugal's Folly. In Silverpine, Forsaken agents seek shackles worn by Moonrage worgen. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's notes to learn how the renegade mage strengthened his unstable magic. The bindings may help the Forsaken break the worgen threat. Dalar Dawnweaver studies Arugal's recovered research with open contempt for his former peer. He says Arugal was never fit to serve Dalaran, much less wield high sorcery in the kingdom's darkest hour. Lacking talent, Arugal turned to enchanted relics and devices to strengthen and bind the worgen he summoned. Dalar needs samples of those objects to study the magic tethering the beasts.

Arugal's Folly. Arugal's Folly is a key quest in the Sepulcher's ongoing campaign against the mad archmage's influence across Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver tasks Horde adventurers with infiltrating Deep Elem Mine to execute the corrupted foreman, Grimson the Pale, securing vital mineral wealth for Varimathras's forces. While unraveling the dark enchantments Archmage Arugal unleashed upon the forest, Dalar Dawnweaver receives urgent intelligence from the Forsaken Darkstalkers. The feral sorcery spreading from Shadowfang Keep has reached the Deep Elem Mine in the southeastern hills, where worgen now make their lair. The mine holds crucial ore needed to fuel Undercity's militarization, but its current occupants render it completely unusable.

Arugal's Folly. In Pyrewood Village, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks the magic binding its people to a curse. He needs enchanted shackles from the villagers to study Archmage Arugal's work and understand the worgen transformation. South of the Sepulcher, Pyrewood Village lives two lives. In daylight, its fearful, insular residents appear to be ordinary human peasants. At twilight, their human forms tear apart and become savage Moonrage worgen, roaming the streets under Arugal's sway. Dalar Dawnweaver seeks to learn what arcane bindings cause this horror.

As Water Cascades. Sacred water is brought to bear on the red crystal in Darkshore. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea hopes moonwell water from Auberdine will reveal what lies beneath its opaque surface. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea seeks a safe way to study the red crystal high on Darkshore's eastern cliffs. Moonwell water holds divine, restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda believes water from Auberdine's moonwell may react with the strange stone and pierce its opaque shell without destroying it.

Ashenvale Outrunners. Night elf scouts have slipped out from Silverwing Outpost into Ashenvale. Kuray'bin calls for a strike against the Ashenvale Outrunners before they can report on Horde encampments and defenses. Night elf scouts from Silverwing Outpost are moving through the woods east of their base and south of nearby Horde holdings. In Ashenvale's contested forest, they watch the paths and ridges, mapping fortifications and tracking troop movements. Kuray'bin has learned that these scouts, known as Ashenvale Outrunners, have slipped into the wilderness to gather intelligence.

Ashlan Stonesmirk. At Dun Modr, Ashlan Stonesmirk watches the border with the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. The dwarven explosives expert keeps alert for dangers threatening Ironforge. At Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands, Ashlan Stonesmirk serves the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. His knowledge of explosives makes him a useful contact when suspicious materials threaten dwarven defenses.

Assassin's Contract. A Shadowy Assassin in Hillsbrad Foothills carries a contract that orders the killing of Magistrate Henry Maleb. Red wax seals it, pressed with a distinctive signet ring, and you are to bring it to Maleb in Southshore. The paper orders the killing of Magistrate Henry Maleb. A seal of red wax closes it, pressed with a distinctive signet ring. A Shadowy Assassin in Hillsbrad Foothills carries it, and Maleb in Southshore is the one to show it to.

Assassination Plot. Assassination Plot is a Horde quest initiated by recovering intercepted centaur orders in Thousand Needles. The orders reveal an impending strike targeting the tauren Kanati Greycloud at his hunting camp by Whitereach Post. Thousand Needles has long been contested terrain dominated by warring centaur clans and dangerous wildlife. When the tauren brave Kanati Greycloud set up a hunting camp at Whitereach Post, the small post southwest of the Great Lift, the local centaur viewed it as an audacious intrusion into their territory. Rather than merely driving game away, the centaur resolved to eliminate Greycloud entirely to discourage any further Horde expansion through the canyon.

name.esES: Asalto a la Isla de Fenris

text.enUS: Assault on Fenris Isle. Forsaken agents move against the Scourge on Fenris Isle. High Executor Hadrec sends them to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of Thule Ravenclaw, the necromancer commanding the island stronghold in Lake Lordamere. The Forsaken hold the western roads and have established their presence at the Sepulcher, but the Scourge remain entrenched in Fenris Keep. The island lies in Lake Lordamere, east of Silverpine Forest, and its forces threaten the forest and the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity. High Executor Hadrec sees Thule Ravenclaw’s vile experiments as a danger to Forsaken control of Silverpine. Thule commands the Scourge from the keep, keeping their power close to the Forsaken shore.

Assault on the Kolkar. After Brutal Politics, Warug in Magram Village wants proof that you can kill Kolkar the way the Magram do. Head north and slay Kolkar centaurs, scouts and maulers. Warug sneers that the Kolkar believe themselves strong while the Magram laugh at them as they kill them. Warug wants you to prove you can kill Kolkar as the Magram do, so you head north: twelve Kolkar centaurs, twelve scouts and six maulers are to fall.

Assessing the Threat. Deputy Feldon needs a measure of the gnoll threat near Lakeshire. With the garrison stretched thin and Stormwind withholding reinforcements, he hires travelers to thin the packs and learn their strength. Lakeshire faces Blackrock orc warbands from the heights and aggressive gnoll packs in the valleys. Its defenders are too few for ordinary scouting patrols. When reports confirmed gnolls pressing toward the border, Deputy Feldon sought help from travelers. He pays champions to test the enemy in the wild, rather than send guards the town cannot spare.

Asterion. Asterion is an ancient Highborne spirit bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Once the trusted second to governor Athrikus Narassin ten millennia ago, he was mysteriously imprisoned in a magical moonstone seal that held him through mortal life and into the afterlife. Today, his specter remains shackled to the ruined shrine, surrounded by demonic beasts and dreaming of liberation. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara herself. Azshara appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern the twin settlements, and Asterion served as his right hand. Respected for both his physical combat prowess and his command of arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran while frequently traveling between the sister cities to manage the needs of their citizens.

Astor's Letter of Introduction. Astor Hadren carries a letter between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. Deathstalkers use it to pose as the courier and investigate Andron Gant, a shopkeeper suspected of leaking Forsaken intelligence. Astor Hadren carries messages between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. His letter of introduction gives its bearer credentials with illicit contacts in the city. Mennet Carkad, a Deathstalker handler, needs to investigate suspicious leaks in the Undercity, and Astor's travels make him a target. An operative can eliminate Astor and take his papers, then assume his identity and intercept the covert messages meant for him.

Astral Knot Garment. Wynne Larson works fine spider silk into a garment in Stormwind City. An adventurer brings her rare silk gathered from the wilds, and she tailors it into a magical weave for dangerous journeys and high-society gatherings. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, tailors serve arcane elites and visiting nobles. Wynne Larson is known for weaving pristine spider silk into durable, enchanted garments. Her playful humor comes through when she jokes about saving a few precious scraps for her own wardrobe before handing over her finished work.

Astranaar. Astranaar holds the Night Elves’ ground in central Ashenvale, across an island in the forest lake. The ancient forest road runs beside it, and Alliance travelers find refuge there as furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde threaten the region. Wooden footbridges link Astranaar’s island to the mainland, crossing the forest lake. It is Ashenvale’s largest night elven settlement, where sentinels, priests, and artisans keep watch over the woodlands. Travelers find an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker. On the high perches, a flight master sends hippogryphs to distant outposts across Kalimdor.

At Home in the Shadows. "At Home in the Shadows" is an introductory rogue quest on Zephras Isle. After aiding Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove, budding rogues are directed to read a summons and meet their local class mentor, Akeri Duskblade. The quest marks the moment young rogues transition from general village chores to serious stealth and combat training. While handling basic threats around Thendal Grove, young rogues draw the attention of Akeri Duskblade, the grove's resident rogue trainer. Rather than mingling openly in the settlement, Akeri passes a simple note through Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian recognizes that despite Akeri's suspicious demeanor, the mentor understands the practical skills needed to survive outside the grove's sheltered boundaries.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, the Forsaken strike at Scarlet Crusade forces threatening their borders. Executor Zygand sends champions after Captain Perrine and his garrison at a ruined tower southwest of Brill, using intelligence taken in Deathknell. Executor Arren recovered documents from the Scarlet Crusade in Deathknell, revealing troop movements across Tirisfal Glades. Rather than wait for the fanatics to attack newly fortified Brill, Executor Zygand uses the captured intelligence to strike their field commanders first.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand sends Forsaken fighters against the Scarlet Crusade near Balnir Farmstead. Their strike targets Captain Vachon and his friars in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, where Crusader raids threaten the Dark Lady's lands. The Forsaken guard Brill and the Undercity while the Scarlet Crusade holds fortified sites across the countryside. Executor Arren reports active Crusader incursions from a crumbling guard tower in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. The tower stands close to the abandoned Balnir Farmstead.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal, Executor Zygand sends Forsaken agents from Brill against the Scarlet Crusade. Captain Melrache and his personal vanguard hold a ruined watchtower past Faol's Rest. The Forsaken are securing the ruins of Lordaeron while Scarlet Crusade forces keep probing Tirisfal's borders. From a watchtower in northern Tirisfal, past Faol's Rest, crusaders lead raids against Forsaken patrols and lands. Executor Zygand chooses to strike at the officers directing those raids instead of waiting for another attack.

text.enUS: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. In Tirisfal Glades, Executor Zygand directs the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade. With intelligence recovered by Executor Arren, you are sent to strike Scarlet Warriors at a guard tower west of the Solliden Farmstead. The attack opens the Forsaken military effort to drive the crusaders from their borders. The Forsaken state under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner faces threats on several fronts. The Deathguard watches the growing armies of the Lich King, while the Scarlet Crusade contests Forsaken dominance over their former homeland. The Crusade condemns all undead as abominations to be purged with fire and blade. Its zealots fail to see that the Forsaken have broken free of the Scourge’s control.

Ataeric's Staff. At the Sepulcher, Ataeric's Staff marks the archmage's defeat. Archmage Ataeric, a senior Dalaran wizard in Silverpine Forest, wielded it to command local ley lines. Shadow Priest Allister feared Dalaran's growing reach in magic and ordered Ataeric killed. He also demanded the staff. Once Ataeric was slain and the staff recovered, the concentrated ley energies sank back into dormancy. Carrying the staff to the Sepulcher marked a clear victory over Dalaran's ambitions. Yet power still lies latent in the earth, and the Forsaken remain watchful.

Athridas Bearmantle. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle works to protect the settlement and its wilds. The night elf druid sends young adventurers to investigate corruption among local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle helps defend night elves arriving from Shadowglen. Teldrassil, the newly grown world tree, shows unnatural signs of decay and unrest. Athridas organizes local scouting and guards the township against threats from the surrounding wilds.

name.zhCN: 埃瑟里克斯·纳拉辛的头颅

text.enUS: Athrikus Narassin's Head. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Athrikus Narassin's Head proves the ancient warlock's death. The coven's demonic activity in northern Darkshore has been disrupted.

Attack on Camp Narache. Attack on Camp Narache is a vital discovery made within the quilboar den of Brambleblade Ravine. A dirt-stained map reveals that the aggressive Bristleback tribe is actively plotting an organized siege against Camp Narache. Delivering these plans to Chief Hawkwind alerts Camp Narache in time to summon aid from Bloodhoof Village. While scouting deep inside the caverns of Brambleblade Ravine, young tauren adventurers uncover a crude, dirt-stained map laying on the rock floor. Upon closer inspection, the parchment reveals deliberate tactical markings made by the Bristleback quilboar. Rather than engaging in mere opportunistic skirmishes, the quilboar are coordinating a full-scale, prolonged siege against Camp Narache.

Attack on the Tower. With the tower's defenses awake, Skuerto at Refuge Pointe sends you into the ogre-held tower for Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. They should lie in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be more than pleased if you bring them back. After Kryten's enchantment, Skuerto tells you what to look for: Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three should be sitting in chests inside the tower, and you should have no trouble opening them yourself, though the ogres call for care. The tower's defenses will not deal with them on their own, and if the ogres find you stealing from them, they will put the hurt on you.

Auberdine. Ships crowd Auberdine's docks, linking Darkshore with Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. The night elven town is the Alliance's main port in northern Kalimdor, set between the Veiled Sea and pine-covered bluffs. Auberdine sits on the Veiled Sea, the only major settlement still thriving in Darkshore. Its ships sail to Stormwind Harbor and, by way of Southshore, to Menethil Harbor. Ferries cross to Rut'theran Village beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Unlike Teldrassil's secluded treetop cities, Auberdine welcomes travelers from across the sea. Lamps light its stone streets, and dwarves and gnomes mingle with merchants among low, arched timber houses.

Austil de Mon. In Brill, Austil de Mon trains Forsaken warriors at Gallows' End Tavern. He teaches the newly risen to fight in service of the Dark Lady. Austil de Mon trains Forsaken warriors inside Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Warriors leaving Deathknell come to him among their first instructors. The living once drank and rested in the inn. Now Austil teaches newly liberated undead to master martial discipline and combat against the foes surrounding the kingdom.

Avenge My Village. Makaba Flathoof asks Horde travelers to answer the Grimtotem assault on his village in southeastern Stonetalon. He barely survived, cut off from his kin and surrounded by the dead, and now seeks vengeance at the ruffians’ and hired sellswords’ encampment. Near the Barrens border, Makaba Flathoof is the lone survivor of a massacre in the red stone passes of Stonetalon. Grimtotem raiders descended without warning and slaughtered nearly everyone in his settlement. Makaba fought back and brought down several attackers, but they drove him into hiding with little more than his life and his wrath.

Avenging the Fallen. Huntsman Markhor of Revantusk Village says the Wildhammer train gryphons to slay trolls, and he wants the elder gryphons of the region, the Skylords, wiped out. You are to slay a Razorbeak Skylord and bring its plume back to him. Markhor, a huntsman of Revantusk Village in the Hinterlands, is bitter that the Wildhammer train gryphons to slay trolls. Justice will come for them, he promises, but first he wants you to turn on the elder gryphons of the region, the Skylords. Slay one and return with its plume. The Razorbeak Skylord is a rare breed that tends to keep to the wilds of the Hinterlands, and Markhor blames it for breeding murderous young.

Ayanna Everstride. In Shadowglen, Ayanna Everstride trains young kaldorei in the hunter’s way. Stationed in Aldrassil, she teaches marksmanship, tracking, and survival beneath the World Tree. Ayanna Everstride trains newly awakened kaldorei hunters inside Aldrassil, in the heart of Shadowglen. To the night elves, hunters are indispensable guardians of the sacred forests, not merely trappers or sharpshooters. Ayanna teaches novices early martial skills, ranged combat, and how to survive Teldrassil’s perilous woods.

Ayessa Dawnsinger. Ayessa Dawnsinger is a Skyborne leader found in Valanaar on Zephras Isle. She leads the Windshapers, guiding the Skyborne aligned with the Horde through their trials and politics. Standing within the settlement of Valanaar on Zephras Isle, Ayessa Dawnsinger serves as the paramount guide for the Windshapers—the faction of Skyborne aligned with the Horde. From this vantage, she directs critical efforts across the island, managing external threats, internal fractures, and the overarching survival of her people as they navigate alliances in Kalimdor and beyond.

Azar Stronghammer. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Azar Stronghammer guides new dwarven paladins. After completing his own training in the Holy Light, he sends promising recruits to Ironforge for further instruction. Azar Stronghammer guides new dwarven paladins at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Humans are often linked to the great cathedrals, yet the dwarves of Khaz Modan have embraced the virtues of the Holy Light. Azar has mastered his own martial and spiritual vows, and helps newly inducted paladins find their footing on Dun Morogh's freezing slopes. When a novice shows dedication and spiritual maturity, he sends them up the mountain path to Ironforge. There they can study under veteran champions such as Tiza Battleforge.

Azuregos. Azuregos is an eccentric blue dragon stationed along the coast of Azshara to protect ancient Highborne relics. Entrusted with safeguarding immense magical power by the Spell-Weaver Malygos, he prefers quiet study over violence, but he will readily swat aside any adventurer foolish enough to disturb his vigil. Drawn to the magic-soaked shores of Azshara, Azuregos chose the ancient ruins of Eldarath as his sanctuary. Countless relics survived the Great Sundering along these shattered coasts, and Azuregos considers it his sacred duty as a servant of Malygos to keep such powerful artifacts away from careless mortals. Rather than lurking in a dark cave, he freely roams the crags and beaches, proudly dubbing himself the lord of all magic in the region. Though blessed with a sardonic sense of humor, he fiercely defends Azshara's treasures against the endless stream of adventurers seeking fame or plunder.

Azurelode Mine. In southwestern Hillsbrad, Azurelode Mine sends iron to the Alliance war effort. Southshore's militia guards the human laborers who work its tunnels. Southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine cuts into the ridges along the coast. Human miners work deep underground under Foreman Bonds's watch, drawing iron for arms and armor. That iron helps Alliance defenders hold the region against the Undercity.

Back to Billy. You carry Bernice Stonefield's freshly baked pie across the road to Billy Maclure, who has information about her missing necklace. The delivery continues the feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families in central Elwynn Forest. The old feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without it. She hands you the pie with plain irritation and hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

name.esES: De vuelta a Bahía del Botín

text.enUS: Back to Booty Bay. Kravel Koalbeard trusts you to get a job done and to keep quiet about it. He has a new scheme, risky but with the promise of a bundle for you both. You carry his letter to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay. This follows Rumors for Kravel. Kravel Koalbeard, the dwarf at the Mirage Raceway, calls you someone he can trust, both to finish a job and to hold your tongue about it. His new scheme carries risk, yet if it pays off the two of you stand to make a bundle. He apologizes for sending you back to Booty Bay, where his last job took you, and asks you to find Crank Fizzlebub there and hand over a letter. If Crank needs help, Kravel wants you to do your best, and says it will be worth the effort.

Back to Darnassus. After meeting the Great Bear Spirit, a young night elf druid returns to Darnassus. The initiate has left Moonglade and now reports to Mathrengyl Bearwalker in the Cenarion Enclave for practical shapeshifting trials. Dendrite Starblaze sends the initiate from Nighthaven back to Darnassus after the meeting with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade. The journey joins two sanctuaries: Moonglade, where the young druid has communed with the spirit, and the unsettled world beyond. In Darnassus, local mentors watch over Teldrassil and guide the next stage of training.

name.ptBR: De volta ao Penhasco do Trovão

text.enUS: Back to Thunder Bluff. Your return from Moonglade brings you back to Elder Rise, where Turak Runetotem awaits. Dendrite Starblaze sends you home after your communion with the Great Bear Spirit, so your training can continue among your people. Moonglade brings night elf and tauren practitioners of nature magic together in the Cenarion Circle, apart from the mortal world’s factional divides. After your communion with the Great Bear Spirit, Dendrite Starblaze sends you back to your people. Night elves often see tauren as fledglings in Cenarius’s formal teachings, yet Starblaze recognizes the wisdom and balance of Turak Runetotem.

Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks to blunt Colonel Kurzen's military advantage by targeting his medical support. The renegades rely on powerful remedies and toxins concocted by their practitioners, leaving the resistance fighters desperate to turn those same concoctions to their own advantage. Colonel Kurzen has bolstered his jungle force with numerous medicine men who heal his forces and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extracts. To turn the tide of the conflict, Sergeant Yohwa directs adventurers into the Kurzen Compound to scavenge those vital supplies. Securing their jungle remedies will help treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp, while capturing a sample of their venom fern extract will enable the resistance to study the toxin and manufacture their own cures.

Badlands Reagent Run. In the outpost of Kargath, Jarkal Mossmeld, an alchemist of some note, needs reagents found out in the Badlands to replenish stocks. Coin is promised, but only to someone who brings the goods. Jarkal Mossmeld is short on ingredients: gizzards from five buzzards, fangs from ten crag coyotes, and shards from five rock elementals. All three can be taken from the creatures themselves. Anyone who is not the fighting type is told to find friends who are. Jarkal pays in coin, but only once the reagents are in hand.

Bael Modan. Dwarven crews blast into the red earth at Bael Modan, searching for Titan relics. Their fortified outpost has driven the Stonespire tauren from their sacred land and kindled a bitter fight. Bael Modan's walls guard Bael'dun Keep, siege cannons, gyrocopter landing pads, and a deep excavation pit. Dwarven prospectors came to Kalimdor convinced an ancient Titan facility lay beneath the red earth. Their blasting tore through sacred ground of the Stonespire tauren. The expedition answered no call to negotiate. Gunfire and explosives drove the tribe from its ancestral lands, leaving survivors scattered and vengeful.

Bael'dun Digsite. Dwarven prospectors cut into the western hills of Mulgore at Bael'dun Digsite. Their search for ancient Titan relics has brought them into conflict with the tauren, who see the digging as an insult to the Earth Mother. Dwarven prospectors dig into the mountain slopes of western Mulgore. Their camp marks the southernmost reach of the Explorers' League expedition based at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. The dwarves came with picks, shovels, and blasting powder, seeking ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains. They paid no heed to borders or to the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes.

Bael'dun Keep. Dwarven forces hold Bael'dun Keep above the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens. Under General Twinbraid, this imposing fortification anchors the Alliance's controversial presence in the region and brings it into violent conflict with the surrounding Horde territories. Bael'dun Keep rises over the Bael Modan excavation as the fortified military heart of Ironforge's presence in the southern Barrens. Dwarven architect Haggis Boatmurder designed the stronghold to protect the Prospectors and archaeologists searching the trenches for ancient titan artifacts. Ironworks and artillery arm its garrison, which keeps a vigilant watch, secures dwarven supply lines, and projects Alliance military power into Kalimdor's heartland.

text.enUS: Bag of Empty Ooze Containers. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle supplies empty containers for his ooze research. The jars are meant to hold pristine slime specimens gathered in the field. Laris Geardawdle studies the strange biology of Azeroth's oozes. He found that slime creatures quickly take on the corruption around them, including tainted residues from Felwood. To study oozes in their natural state, he commissioned sturdy jars that can hold acidic specimens without harming them. The bag contains enough jars to collect clean slime in wild regions, especially Un'Goro Crater, where ancient glutinous oozes live free from demonic taint.

Bailiff Conacher. In Lakeshire Town Hall, Bailiff Conacher keeps Stormwind law in force under Magistrate Solomon. He relies on travelers to uphold local decrees across the embattled Redridge Mountains. Bailiff Conacher works with Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire Town Hall to uphold law across the Redridge Mountains. Blackrock orcs and local gnolls besiege the town, leaving Conacher without ordinary civic procedures or royal garrisons to rely on. He issues legal decrees that authorize passing travelers to carry out capital justice in the realm's name.

Bailor Stonehand. In Thelsamar, Bailor Stonehand’s forge work has been set back by stolen ore. The skilled dwarven smith once taught the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell and makes a specialized alloy for masterwork arms. Bailor Stonehand works the forge in Thelsamar, where his knowledge of minerals and specialized alloys reaches beyond Khaz Modan. He once taught Jordan Stilwell, a human smith, the foundations of metallurgy and shared formulas used to forge blessed paladin weapons such as Verigan's Fist.

Bailor's Ore Shipment. Paladins seek Bailor's Ore Shipment in Loch Modan for Jordan Stilwell's sanctified weapon. Mo'grosh ogres plundered the alloy during an ambush on the road from the Wetlands. Jordan Stilwell needs ore refined by his old friend Bailor Stonehand, but the shipment never reaches Ironforge. As the caravan travels south from the Wetlands into Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres ambush and slaughter its guards. One wounded guard reaches a camp, then dies soon after. The shipment is left in ogre territory.

Baine Bloodhoof. In Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof guards his people and Mulgore. While Cairne leads from Thunder Bluff, Baine directs local defense against gnolls and outside threats. Baine Bloodhoof grew up traveling with his nomadic people, the son of Cairne. They settled in Mulgore’s grasslands, where centaur clans remained a threat. After the Third War, Khiragg’s warband captured Baine, and grief left Cairne nearly unable to lead the new settlements. Rexxar freed Baine from captivity. The rescue restored Cairne’s spirit, and the tauren stood with Thrall’s Horde against the invading Kul Tirans, securing their foothold on the continent.

Baited for Success. Baited for Success involves assisting local fisherman Jason Mathers in dealing with a disruptive murloc infestation. By coordinating with Remy to prepare a targeted poisoned bait, Mathers hopes to clear the waterways and safely resume selling his catch. Jason Mathers depends on open waters for his fishing trade, but an infestation of aggressive murlocs has disrupted his work. Unable to sell his fish safely, he seeks a solution to rid the area of the creatures. Remy steps in to craft a specialized poisoned bait designed to thin out the local murlocs so ordinary fishing can resume.

Bal'lal Ruins. Bal'lal Ruins are ancient Gurubashi troll ruins set along the northwestern shore of Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Overlooking the murky waters of the Vile Reef, the crumbling stone foundations are currently occupied by hostile Bloodscalp trolls. Perched on the coastline north of Grom'gol Base Camp, Bal'lal Ruins stand as another remnant of the shattered Gurubashi Empire. Once part of the grand troll civilization that dominated southern Azeroth, the site has decayed into moss-covered stone walls and cracked masonry. The ruins sit immediately adjacent to the Vile Reef, offering an elevated vantage over the treacherous coastal shallows. Today, aggressive Bloodscalp trolls hold the grounds, fiercely defending the weathered relics of their ancestors against intruders.

Balia'mah Ruins. The Balia'mah Ruins are the moss-covered remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Located east of Grom'gol Base Camp across the river, the crumbling stone tiers are currently claimed and guarded by warriors of the hostile Skullsplitter troll tribe. Like many of the stone edifices dotting the jungle, Balia'mah stands as a remnant of the sprawling Gurubashi Empire that once ruled much of the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Following the fall of their ancient capital, Gurubashi territory splintered into warring factions. Today, the ruins serve as a stronghold for the Skullsplitter tribe, who fiercely defend the stone terraces against wandering beasts, neighboring ogres from the Mosh'Ogg mound, and any outsiders foolish enough to cross the river.

Balir Frosthammer. In Coldridge Valley, Balir Frosthammer rallies recruits against the Rockjaw troggs. The dwarf guards Dun Morogh as the troggs press into dwarven lands. Balir Frosthammer calls new recruits to defend Coldridge Valley. Dwarven and gnomish novices have long found safety and training there, but trouble underground has driven violent Rockjaw troggs to the surface. Balir is among the first to raise the alarm. He urges recruits to thin their numbers before they push farther into Dun Morogh.

Balnir Farmstead. In eastern Tirisfal, Balnir Farmstead lies ruined beyond the Bulwark. Once worked by the Balnir family, the estate now draws Scourge that slip past the defenses. Snapdragons still bloom in the garden where the Balnir family worked their homestead for generations. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, the farm was overrun and its people were lost. The buildings now rot among the hills of eastern Tirisfal.

Balnir Snapdragons. At Balnir Farmstead, vibrant snapdragons grow where the Scourge's corruption presses toward Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken study their sensitivity to magic to watch for that corruption's spread. Balnir Snapdragons still bloom in the garden of Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. The homestead lies in ruin after the fall of Lordaeron and the rise of the Scourge. The Plaguelands border Tirisfal to the east, and the garden sits where the Lich King's blight presses against the region. Its flowers give the Forsaken a place to watch for the spread of that corruption.

Balthule Shadowstrike. Near the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike watches the northern Darkshore coast. He serves Delgren the Purifier as a forward scout, keeping watch on the dark practitioners in the ancient elven ruins. West of the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike keeps a lonely, dangerous watch. Restless spirits and shadowed ruins mark northern Darkshore, but the tower poses a particular threat. Under Delgren the Purifier’s direction, Balthule watches the dark casters who have entered the ancient Highborne ruins.

Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den beneath Teldrassil's roots. The sacred chambers were made for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, whose spirits commune with the Emerald Dream. Now the den is a dangerous warren, and the druids within are at risk. Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies beneath Teldrassil's roots, with upper and lower chambers. Barrow dens shelter night elf druids as they sleep and send their spirits into the Emerald Dream. This den was made for the Druids of the Talon to commune with nature. Its halls once held quiet meditation, but the corruption spreading through Teldrassil's wildlife reached the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They invaded the den and made its hollowed chambers a fortified warren.

Ban'ethil Hollow. South of the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, furbolgs threaten travelers in Ban'ethil Hollow. The ravine also hides the entrance to Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Furbolgs roam the rocky descent into Ban'ethil Hollow. Their strange affliction has driven them mad, and they stalk the nearby road, ambushing couriers and wandering sentinels. The hollow lies just south of the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, a reminder that Teldrassil's woodland is not wholly safe. At the ravine's back stands the entrance to Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Slumbering druids and ancient tunnels lie within, threatened by the maddened beasts outside.

Bandarion Keep. Bandarion Keep is a quest in Tirisfal Glades directing adventurers to meet Argent Dawn Commander Leonid Barthalomew at a secluded fortress. Once an Argent Dawn staging base against the Scourge, the stronghold is now maintained by Danitha and her order of paladins. Bandarion Keep is an Argent Dawn quest that directs adventurers across Tirisfal Glades to meet Commander Leonid Barthalomew. After aiding the Dawn against Cult of the Damned activity, travelers are pointed northwest toward the fortress to rendezvous with the commander and learn more about the order's ongoing crusade against darkness.

Bandarion Keep. At Bandarion Keep, defenders face threats from the coast and the woodland. The outpost near the Whispering Forest is named for Garek Bandarion and tied to Tyr's Watch. Bandarion Keep stands near the Whispering Forest in western Tirisfal Glades. Named for Garek Bandarion, the stronghold is closely tied to Tyr's Watch. Quartermaster Jorin Croge works to keep the garrison supplied, though the keep lies far from the courtyards of the Undercity.

Baradin Bay. In Baradin Bay, reefs and wrecks make each crossing perilous. Its waters lie between Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Kul Tiras once patrolled the bay with a powerful navy during the Second War. Baradin Bay links the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. Menethil Harbor lies on its Wetlands shore, and Southshore stands in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Shallow sandbanks and jagged shoals threaten ships, as do murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks.

Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks someone to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks an aspiring smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar under the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, and he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk of ending, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward.

name.esES: Alas de águila ratonera a la parrilla

text.enUS: Barbecued Buzzard Wings. Rigglefuzz swears by barbecued buzzard wings, a rich sauce on tangy meat. Everything for a batch is on hand except the wings themselves. Fetch enough of them and Rigglefuzz may part with the recipe. Rigglefuzz is proud of barbecued buzzard wings. The sauce is rich, the meat tangy, and the aroma carries to hungry folk a long way off. Every ingredient for a batch is already in hand, all but the wings. Bring four buzzard wings, and Rigglefuzz might share the recipe.

Barithras Moonshade. In Auberdine, Barithras Moonshade looks to the wilds of Darkshore for rare subterranean plants. The night elf seeks travelers willing to explore the shadowy land and gather them. Barithras Moonshade watches over Auberdine and helps the night elves study and manage Darkshore. He sends travelers into nearby caverns to gather fungi, including death cap mushrooms, for study and use.

Barkeep Daniels. At the Lakeshire Inn, Barkeep Daniels keeps drinks flowing as raiders disrupt the roads. The town guards, fishermen, and travelers who gather there depend on the inn for a welcome pause, but supplies are running low. Barkeep Daniels pours drinks and greets visitors at the Lakeshire Inn, near the bridge. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs have kept Lakeshire under pressure for months, and its defenders turn to the tavern after grim patrols. Raids and severed roads have disrupted trade across the region. With liquor running low when the town needs good cheer, Daniels welcomes travelers willing to fetch shipments from safer settlements.

Baron Aquanis. Blackfathom Deeps is where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair, and Baron Aquanis rises from its flooded Moonshrine Ruins. He appears when someone disturbs the Fathom Stone, while the Earthen Ring suspects the cult has corrupted him. The Fathom Stone lies beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who occupy them. Within the stone rests a fathom core, a device that reveals the history of nearby elemental activity when properly read. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover it. Disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

Baron Aquanis. Beneath Ashenvale, Baron Aquanis leaves a strange globe filled with tainted fluid. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring believes it may show what corrupted the elemental, and suspects the Twilight's Hammer cultists in the submerged ruins. Blackfathom Deeps holds Baron Aquanis, a water spirit twisted by foul sorcery. When the elemental is destroyed, a Strange Water Globe remains behind. The impervious orb holds putrid fluid that seems to have sustained and warped Aquanis's natural essence. Physical force cannot harm it, and its energies unsettle those attuned to the balance of the elements.

Baron Longshore's Head. Along the Merchant Coast, Baron Longshore's Head proves the pirate captain's death. Gazlowe posted a public bounty for Longshore's identifiable remains to protect Ratchet's commercial shipping. Baron Longshore led Southsea Freebooter raids from camps along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. His flagship, the Heedless, threatened goblin trade lanes between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Gazlowe, Ratchet's Chief Engineer, offered a bounty for identifiable proof of Longshore's death. The port authority pays a monetary reward when the pirate's head is delivered.

Baron Revilgaz. Baron Revilgaz is the cunning goblin leader of Booty Bay and the Blackwater Raiders, ruling the pirate haven on behalf of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Perched high on the balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern, he balances fragile trade neutrality with ruthlessly pragmatic opportunism. He hires passing mercenaries to secure his investments, undermine rivals like the Bloodsail Buccaneers, and retrieve ancient relics of the jungle. From his vantage atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Baron Revilgaz watches the bustling docks of Blackwater Cove through a custom enchanted spyglass. Flanked by his trusted advisor, the tauren Fleet Master Seahorn, Revilgaz exercises firm control over the town's cutpurses, merchants, and privateers. Originally a human settlement overwhelmed by trolls before the First War, the port was claimed and fortified by goblins, eventually evolving into the pirate-leaning commercial nexus of the Blackwater Raiders. Revilgaz ensures the port remains officially open to both Alliance and Horde travelers, strictly enforcing neutrality within harbor limits so that trade continues uninterrupted.

Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine's spirit lingers in the Great Hall above Pyrewood Village. He once ruled Silverlaine Keep, until Archmage Arugal unleashed worgen upon the region and they slaughtered him. Baron Silverlaine ruled a noble estate in the southern hills of Silverpine. His fortress guarded the surrounding lands and kept them safe. That peace ended when Archmage Arugal summoned worgen to fight the rampaging Scourge and unleashed them upon the region. The feral beasts could not be controlled. They stormed the stronghold, overwhelmed its guards, and butchered the baron.

Baron's Demise. The contract you recovered bears the name of Baron Vardus, a nobleman from the old kingdom of Alterac. Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore wants him found and brought to justice, and asks for the baron's head. After Assassin's Contract, Magistrate Henry Maleb tells you that Baron Vardus put his name to the contract. Vardus is a nobleman from the old kingdom of Alterac, a man of cold heart and brutal ways, so Maleb is not surprised to find him behind it. Southshore will not let the baron send his thugs against the town without answering for it. Maleb wants him found among the Syndicate's haunts, perhaps in Strahnbrad's ruins or in the valley north of them, and asks for the baron's head.

Baros Alexston. In Stormwind City Hall, Baros Alexston keeps watch over the capital he helped rebuild. Once a close friend of Edwin VanCleef in the Stonemasons Guild, he stayed loyal to the crown when the guild fractured. Baros grew up on the Alexston Farmstead in Westfall's rolling grasslands. Thieves overran and burned the family homestead while he was young. Before they fled, his father hurriedly hid their cherished heirlooms across the grounds. Baros later journeyed to the capital and joined the Stonemasons Guild. For years, he labored beside Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef as they raised Stormwind anew from the ashes of the First War.

Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder. Marleth Barleybrew sends a cask of Scalder toward the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. The ale is meant to prove his brewing against the Thunderbrews, his chief competitors. The Thunderbrews and Barleybrews compete fiercely over brewing in Dun Morogh. The Thunderbrews are renowned, with their busy distillery in Kharanos. Marleth Barleybrew refuses to live in their shadow. He brews the fiery Scalder to show his recipes can rival theirs, hoping those who taste it will see the Thunderbrews do not own the art of fine dwarven drink.

Barrel of Shimmer Stout. In Dun Morogh, Rejold Barleybrew sends a barrel of Shimmer Stout to the mountain watch. The experimental ale is meant for guards on the high passes, and drinkers say it brightens their vision. Rejold Barleybrew brewed Shimmer Stout after gathering ingredients across Dun Morogh. The recipe is the latest work of the Barleybrew family, whose dwarven brewers compete to make hearty ales against the mountain cold. Rejold made this stout to warm the gut and sharpen the senses of those posted in the wind.

Barrel of Thunder Ale. In Kharanos, a barrel of Thunder Ale has been taken from the Thunderbrew Distillery. Its place was meant to be taken by Marleth's Barleybrew Scalder, proof of a brewing feud turned to foul play. The Thunderbrews of Kharanos and the Barleybrews of Brewnall Village are bitter rivals. Marleth Barleybrew tried to slip a barrel of his Barleybrew Scalder into the Thunderbrews' cellar, hoping their patrons would choose his brew. The Thunder Ale barrel was seized in the exchange, evidence that the switch succeeded despite the local guards.

Barrow Key. Deep beneath Stonetalon Peak, the Barrow Key lies locked in the Talon Den. It is one of three druidic keys guarding the ancient treasures sealed within the den's hoard. Night elf druids placed wards throughout the Talon Den's underground barrows to protect their relics from intruders. The Barrow Key is hidden in a cache among the passages, one part of that layered defense. The cache opens only with the Gatekeeper's Key, so a seeker must know the druids' defenses to reach it.

Bartleby. Bartleby drinks and picks fights at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. His stubborn hold on his ale makes him a test for aspiring warriors who must face him in a tavern brawl. Bartleby spends his days at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. The tavern draws a rougher crowd than the taprooms of Cathedral Square. He clings to his favorite mug, drinks cheap ale, nurses grievances, and picks fights with anyone who disturbs him.

Bartleby the Drunk. In the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby the Drunk faces a test set by Harry Burlguard. An aspiring Alliance warrior must take Bartleby's prized mug before Harry will teach deeper combat skills. Harry Burlguard asks for proof of a novice's backbone before teaching deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man's mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge puts a warrior's resolve to the test.

Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, a stubborn brawler keeps Bartleby's Mug close. A warrior must win it in a tavern brawl, then watch Bartleby drain his drink before he surrenders it. Bartleby keeps his mug close, and a young warrior in Stormwind must wrest it from him. The stubborn brawler gives it up only after a fight leaves him beaten. Even then, Bartleby drains every last drop before handing over the mug as proof of victory.

Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Bartleby's Mug marks a young warrior's trial of grit. After besting Bartleby in the Pig and Whistle Tavern, you claim his drinking mug for your trainer, Harry Burlguard. Harry Burlguard tests young warriors with a brawl in Old Town. He asks you to take down Bartleby, a stubborn drunk at the bar of the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Once subdued, Bartleby reluctantly gives up his prized drinking mug, but first takes one final swig to drain the dregs.

Bashal'Aran. Demonic satyrs and grells shun one shrine in Bashal'Aran, where an unearthly blue aura burns. Thundris Windweaver, Auberdine's elder, sends you to find its source. Bashal'Aran once flourished under the ancient Kaldorei Empire. Now demonic taint fills its broken marble halls and overgrown arches. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed on the ruins' lingering magic, growing more malicious by the day. Yet Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine has noticed a mystery: atop a western bluff, a blue aura shines above a shrine that no demon will approach.

Bashal'Aran. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion seeks release from the magic binding his ghostly form. He suspects the grells have touched the seal that holds him, and asks travelers to gather their earrings so he can trace its lingering magic. Asterion waits among Bashal'Aran's shattered marble, bound there for centuries. The ancient night elf spirit is trapped between life and true death beneath Darkshore's canopy. Arcane craft ties him to the ruined settlement, and he cannot break free alone. Solitude and despair have worn down his mind through all those years.

Bashal'Aran. Asterion seeks release from his prison among the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran. He has traced the binding magic to the satyrs who command the grells and asks travelers to recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For more than a thousand years, Asterion has remained bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran. The marble pillars around him mark the limits of his prison, beyond the reach of his fading strength and ancient magic. A cursed relic holds him here. Through the centuries, he has watched Darkshore's canopy and wondered whether the wearing stone could ever set him free.

Bashal'Aran. Bashal'Aran lies in northern Darkshore, east of Auberdine, where satyrs and grells feed on lingering magic. A solitary elven ghost remains trapped by a centuries-old curse. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne in Bashal'Aran and its twin, Ameth'Aran. The powerful mage Athrikus Narassin governed both towns, whose splendid markets and temples honored Elune. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm destroyed the settlements. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his second-in-command, the mage Asterion, in a moonstone seal within Bashal'Aran. Asterion's body perished, but his ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine.
