Bashana Runetotem. On the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, Bashana Runetotem studies plants and corruption. She is the daughter of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem and aids the Cenarion Circle. Bashana Runetotem carries her father Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem’s druidic legacy on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise. While he guides tauren druids and advises Cairne Bloodhoof, Bashana studies unusual plants and regional threats. She gives travelers tools such as evergreen pouches to cultivate mysterious flora, including morrowgrain. She also coordinates Horde efforts against corruption spreading from places such as Blackfathom Deeps.

Bath'rah the Windwatcher. Bath'rah the Windwatcher is a solitary jungle troll shaman and weaponcrafter dwelling amidst the ruins near Chillwind Point. Far from his tropical homelands, he studies the tempestuous elements of the northern mountains, seeking champions powerful enough to help him craft formidable weapons of wind. While most jungle trolls keep to the warm forests and coasts of the south, Bath'rah has embraced the solitary life of a mountain hermit among the cold ruins of the Alterac Mountains. A seasoned shaman and craftsman, he devotes his days to listening to the howling winds and communing with nature spirits. His obsession is not merely philosophical; he seeks to bind the fury of violent elemental storms into tangible armaments for those who possess the strength to wield them.

Bathran's Hair. Among the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in northwestern Ashenvale, Bathran's Hair remains a rare herb. Night elf healers value its power against afflictions of the flesh and spirit. Bathran's Hair grows among the ancient ruins north of Maestra's Post, where night elf healers have long valued it. Common herbs soothe wounds of the body, but Bathran's Hair is said to restore the spirit as well. When a young night elf in Astranaar falls gravely ill, herbalist Orendil Broadleaf seeks the rare plant to prepare a remedy.

Bathran's Hair. At Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf seeks Bathran's Hair for a sick child in Astranaar. He believes the illness afflicts the child's spirit, and sends you north to the ancient ruins where the uncommon restorative herb was gathered in the past. Orendil Broadleaf, a night elf herbalist at Maestra's Post, faces a troubling illness. The post lies just south of the Darkshore border. A young child in Astranaar is grievously ill, and ordinary remedies have failed. Orendil believes the sickness afflicts the child's spirit as well as the flesh. He seeks Bathran's Hair, an uncommon restorative herb gathered in the ancient elven ruins to the north.

Bathran's Haunt. Forsaken herbalists now harvest rare plants at Bathran's Haunt, east of the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Their work is withering the woodland around the ancient kaldorei ruin. At Bathran's Haunt, crumbling night elf pillars stand north of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, tangled in Ashenvale's thick foliage. Once a tranquil kaldorei relic, the ruin now shelters Forsaken herbalists and their enforcers. They work among the broken marble in an open-air laboratory, harvesting rare woodland reagents for their experiments. The grass rots brown, blossoms wilt, and decay creeps through the grove as their work blights the ancient soil.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken strike at the farms that feed the human town. High Executor Darthalia orders the attack from Tarren Mill under Varimathras's command. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign from Tarren Mill. Varimathras in the Undercity has ordered her to break the human resistance in Hillsbrad Foothills. Before attacking the defended town, Darthalia targets its northern fields. The farms feed the town, and disrupting them cuts provisions to the human militia while bringing disorder to the homesteads.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, Forsaken forces press their assault south. After strikes on the northern farms, Horde operatives hunt the peasants fleeing to the orchards. The attack on Hillsbrad's human farms drives laborers south into the fields. After the northern farms are struck, many flee to the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad Fields, hoping to escape the advancing undead. High Executor Darthalia sees their flight as a chance to break the township's remaining labor force and morale.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. In the Hillsbrad Foothills, the Forsaken move against the humans resisting their advance. High Executor Darthalia orders the smithy in Hillsbrad Fields destroyed, hoping to cut off the weapons arming the local people. The Forsaken meet fiercer resistance in the Hillsbrad Foothills than High Executor Darthalia expected. Rural humans refuse to scatter or yield to the Deathstalkers and soldiers sent from Tarren Mill. The Forsaken learn that the peasantry are not fighting with pitchforks and scythes alone. In the fields, they are being armed for war.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. Forsaken forces strike Hillsbrad town, aiming to break its human rule. High Executor Darthalia directs the assault from Tarren Mill. Hillsbrad's human defenders cling to their remaining authority despite heavy losses in the fields and patrols. High Executor Darthalia knows that peasants and militia rally behind the town's leaders. She sends Forsaken operatives into the Town Hall to kill Magistrate Burnside and five councilmen, cutting off the town's command.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. Horde forces strike at Azurelode Mine in the Battle of Hillsbrad. High Executor Darthalia orders them to kill Foreman Bonds and his crew, cutting iron shipments to Alliance armories. High Executor Darthalia marked Azurelode Mine as vital to human strength after Horde forces seized the Hillsbrad Town Registry in earlier raids. The mine lies just south of Hillsbrad Fields, where workers keep extracting rich iron ore for Alliance weaponsmiths and armories. If the mine keeps operating, Southshore can rearm and strengthen its garrisons, undoing Tarren Mill's earlier victories.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken turn their campaign on Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia sends Horde champions to break the dwarven garrison aiding local humans and kill its commander, Captain Ironhill. High Executor Darthalia has already pressed the human farmers and town militia across the foothills. Now she turns Tarren Mill's fury on Ironforge's troops. Dwarven soldiers have taken up arms for Southshore, strengthening the human presence in Lordaeron. Darthalia sees that alliance as an obstacle to be broken. She means to show the Alliance that helping the human survivors will bring devastation.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Hillsbrad, the Forsaken campaign has broken the human township's defenses. High Executor Darthalia sends you to carry her commendation to Varimathras in the Undercity. The fighting in Hillsbrad Foothills has been a brutal struggle for southern Lordaeron. From Tarren Mill, Horde champions struck at the township's farmers, militia, blacksmiths, and civic leaders. With Alliance forces crippled and the territory secured for the Forsaken, High Executor Darthalia prepares an official commendation so the champion's deeds reach the highest ranks of command.

Battleboar Flank. In Mulgore, young hunters gather Battleboar Flanks from beasts threatening tauren hunting grounds. The meat feeds the tribe's youth. Bristleback quilboar train battleboars in Brambleblade Ravine to enter tauren hunting grounds. Their attacks threaten the young tauren at Camp Narache. Grull Hawkwind sends novice hunters to take the flanks and snouts from the beasts they kill. The flank meat is cooked into stew for the tribe's youth, feeding them with what the quilboar sent against their people.

Battleboar Snout. Young tauren hunters gather Battleboar Snouts near Red Cloud Mesa as the Bristleback press into their hunting grounds. The snouts also go into stews for the young in Camp Narache. Bristleback quilboar train battleboars in Brambleblade Ravine, in the shadow of Red Cloud Mesa, to probe tauren hunting grounds. Grull Hawkwind sends young braves to push back against the encroachment. A snout proves that a battleboar has been brought down. The tauren use the snouts with cuts of flank in rich stews for their young.

Battleworn Axe. In Redridge, Battleworn Axe blades mark the Blackrock orcs invading the mountains. Marshal Marris accepts the recovered weapons in Lakeshire as proof of the threat to its people. Blackrock reavers carry these heavy, nicked axes as they push south from the Burning Steppes into Redridge. Marshal Marris and Lakeshire's hard-pressed town watch collect the blades to confirm another marauding orc has fallen and to show how well armed the advancing warband is.

Bay of Storms. The Bay of Storms is an expansive, tempestuous gulf carving into the rugged eastern cliffs of Azshara. Its churning waters harbor ancient ruins, submerged caverns, and perilous marine beasts that make seafaring along this coast hazardous. Opening out toward the Great Sea, the Bay of Storms defines much of Azshara's dramatic coastal geography. Far from a tranquil harbor, its turbulent waters and rocky outcrops are home to dangerous wildlife and ancient aquatic threats. Within and along its waters lie landmarks like the sunken Temple of Arkkoran, the coral reefs of Hetaera's Clutch, and Scalebeard's Cave, leaving the bay largely avoided by casual sailors and claimed instead by coastal monsters.

Bazil Thredd. In the Stormwind Stockade, Bazil Thredd leads the Defias inmates in revolt from the eastern cell block. Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant has been imprisoned there since the Stonemasons' riots. Bazil Thredd stood beside Edwin VanCleef when the Stonemasons Guild rose against Stormwind's nobility. The guild had been refused payment for rebuilding the city, and VanCleef rejected the government's appeasements and sparked open revolt. Thredd served as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. The city guard captured Thredd during the violent clashes that followed. VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall and formed the Defias Brotherhood, while Thredd was sent into the Stormwind Stockade.

Bazil Thredd. In Stormwind, Bazil Thredd holds insight into the Defias Brotherhood's lingering plots. After an unsent letter is recovered from the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston directs you to the Defias leader's right-hand man, now locked beneath the streets in the high-security Stockade. Baros Alexston shares a bitter history with Edwin VanCleef. Both led the Stonemasons Guild, charged with rebuilding Stormwind from the ashes of the First and Second Wars. When the kingdom's magnificent white walls and towers were finished, the nobility refused to pay the masons their promised wages. Some senior members received bureaucratic posts to quiet them, but VanCleef refused to abandon the rank-and-file laborers. He led a violent riot out of the city and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

Bazzalan. Bazzalan commands the Searing Blade cult from the lava caverns beneath Orgrimmar. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he directs its work in Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Bazzalan has joined the Searing Blade cult in Ragefire Chasm. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, the satyr rogue commands the cult's field forces from winding lava caverns. He is swift and lethal with twin blades.

Beached Sea Creature. At Mist's Edge, a giant sea thresher lies stranded while murlocs feed on its carcass. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for night elf researchers in Darnassus, who seek to learn why deep-sea giants are washing ashore. Enormous thresher remains have appeared along Mist's Edge, where shipwrecks and tide-washed debris are familiar sights. This beast dwarfs the wildlife of Darkshore's shallows, suggesting it came from far beyond the calm waters of the Veiled Sea. Murlocs swarm over the corpse to feed, but they lack the strength and coordination to bring down a creature of this size. Something else killed the predator before the sea carried it ashore.

Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a giant sea mammal lies washed ashore beside an abandoned dig site. Its carcass and scattered tools draw murlocs and passing travelers. A giant sea mammal lies on Darkshore's sand, partly gutted and worn by the sea. A rusted wheelbarrow and discarded tools mark the place where an organized study began. The researchers left before they could finish.

Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a great sea mammal lies half-devoured on the sand. Murlocs gather around it, and Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples to learn why gentle sea beasts are dying on the shore. Far north along Darkshore's lonely beaches, a great sea mammal lies rotting and half-eaten. Murlocs pick over its bones, more vicious than usual. These beasts were gentle in life, and their deaths trouble the coast as much as the blighted forests inland.

Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore's rocky Twilight Shore, a colossal thresher lies stranded, far larger than any known local specimen. Its death and stranding add to the deep-sea troubles worrying the night elves. You find driftwood and sea debris along the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore, but one inlet holds the remains of an enormous thresher. Tides and scavengers have begun picking it apart, yet its skeleton dwarfs ordinary predators in these coastal shallows. The giant is an outsider to these waters. Sickness or disorientation may have driven it onto the rocks, or some deeper disturbance may lie out in the Veiled Sea.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s surf-battered shore, a massive sea turtle lies beached as murlocs pick over its carcass. Viable biological samples remain among the scavenged remains, and Auberdine naturalists send them to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for study. Darkshore’s long coast often catches the dead and confused from the Great Sea. Ancient sea turtles drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Their carcasses quickly draw scavengers, and hostile Greymist murlocs have made crude camps around this turtle’s skeletal frame. They carve away flesh and shell, yet viable bone, shell, or tissue samples may remain intact in the wreckage.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's shore, Beached Sea Turtle lies with a broken carriage on its shell. Greymist murlocs have gathered around the great carcass. You find a broken carriage strapped across a giant sea turtle's shell on Darkshore's misty shore. Many sea creatures have washed up along this coast, but this turtle was made to carry a load. Its handlers drove it onto the beach, and the carriage now lies abandoned in the tide.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s northern shore, Beached Sea Turtle remains untouched by nearby Greymist murlocs. A sample is carried to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to learn why great sea creatures wash ashore and scavengers leave them alone. Greymist murlocs crowd Darkshore’s northern coast and scavenge whatever food washes up from the Veiled Sea. Yet the great turtle’s skeleton lies mostly untouched. Those studying the shore wonder whether the murlocs missed it or avoided it for some unknown reason.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's coast, a Beached Sea Turtle lies dead beneath the carriage it once hauled. A box marked with strange runes rests in the wreckage. A dead sea turtle lies among the ancient bones scattered along Darkshore's coast. Splintered carriage boards still cling to its broad shell. The turtle was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo, rather than stranded by sickness or disorientation. A container carved with unfamiliar, serpent-like marks lies in the wreckage, amid scavengers feeding on the remains.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along the wind-battered coast of Darkshore, the bleached bones of giant sea turtles wash ashore with unsettling frequency. Investigating these tragic strandings provides Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine with specimens to study why Kalimdor's marine life is dying out. The mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore is strewn with the remains of great leviathans and majestic sea turtles. Many of these ancient reptiles have drifted onto the shoals or hauled themselves onto the sand to perish. Greymist murlocs frequently swarm the massive carcasses, picking the flesh down to the shell and bone while establishing crude camps around the carrion.

Bear's Head. Bear's Head is a secluded mountainous stretch along the southeastern cliffs of Azshara. Named for the resident Timbermaw furbolgs whose settlements dot the rugged high ground, it serves as an outpost linked to their larger homes farther north while lying directly beneath the cliffside sanctum of Archmage Xylem. Tucked away in southeastern Azshara, Bear's Head takes its name from the encampments of uncorrupted Timbermaw furbolgs established upon its heights. These rustic settlements act as outlying camps tied to the major furbolg dens of Ursolan and Timbermaw Hold to the north. Perched atop the looming cliffs directly above the area sits Xylem's Tower, an eccentric sanctuary where Archmage Xylem and his small retinue of apprentices conduct arcane studies in quiet isolation from the rest of the troubled coastline.

Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Bartleby guards the mug a young warrior must claim. The instructors send recruits to face him in a bare-knuckle fight and earn the vessel for their training. Stormwind's warrior instructors expect recruits to face combat without excuses or grand ceremony. As part of their formal training, young warriors must retrieve a particular mug from Bartleby, a notorious drunkard who lounges in the city. He scoffs at polite requests and swears no one will take his prized drinkware without prying it from his cold, dead fingers. For a fledgling warrior, words soon give way to a fistfight.

Becoming a Parent. Agnar Beastamer in the Hinterlands has found the egg much further along than expected, and wants a word with you about it. Agnar Beastamer was not prepared for how ready the egg turned out to be. Speak with Agnar in the Hinterlands, where you have been bringing food for the hatchling.

name.esES: Costillas de jabalí a la cerveza
name.frFR: Côtes de sanglier à la bière

text.enUS: Beer Basted Boar Ribs. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, hungry patrons wait for Ragnar Thunderbrew's famed ribs. His regular meat supplier is away with the King's Army, so Ragnar needs fresh crag boar ribs and Rhapsody Malt to keep them on the menu. The Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos is known for hearty dwarven ale and hearty tavern fare. Its famed Beer Basted Boar Ribs are among the favorites. But tavern keeper Ragnar Thunderbrew has a bare pantry: the local hunter who supplied fresh meat enlisted in the King's Army to reinforce the Alliance front. Eager customers still fill the tavern, and Ragnar needs passing travelers to help keep the ribs on the menu.

Beezil's Wreck. Beezil's Wreck marks the crash site of an unfortunate goblin zeppelin deep within the quagmires of Dustwallow Marsh. Resting east of Tabetha's Farm, the shattered vessel's cargo holds scattered supplies and volatile engineering components that attract scavengers. Hidden away in the humid muck east of Tabetha's Farm lies the splintered skeleton of a goblin zeppelin known as Beezil's Wreck. The craft was hauling cargo southward across Kalimdor before suffering a disastrous plunge into the swamp. While the wreckage still smolders amid tangled reeds, its eccentric captain, Beezil, has seemingly vanished from the marsh, leaving behind scattered crates and ticking machinery to slowly rot in the brine.

Beggar's Haunt. At Beggar's Haunt, Forsaken agents watch the eastern approaches from an old Stormwind tower. It rises on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. Beggar's Haunt overlooks the hills east of Manor Mistmantle. Stormwind once kept guards in this tower to watch the kingdom's eastern approaches. As Duskwood fell into gloom, patrols withdrew to Darkshire and left the tower to the elements. Forsaken agents now use the ruins to study the region and watch it from within Alliance territory. They include members of the Royal Apothecary Society and the Deathstalkers.

Beginnings. In Dun Morogh, Alliance warlock novices face their first trial under Alamar Grimm. They gather magical feather charms from Frostmane troll novices before learning to summon an imp. At Anvilmar, dark magic is tolerated out of necessity, though it is not openly celebrated. Alamar Grimm, an established warlock, pursues occult research in relative discretion. When a recruit shows raw promise, influential voices take an interest. Their pressure convinces Grimm to leave his studies and assess the novice himself.

Beldin Steelgrill. At Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh, Beldin Steelgrill keeps dwarven war machines running. He is its master technician, renowned in Khaz Modan for repairing siege engines and armored wagons. His work depends on a steady supply of specialized tools. Just down the road from Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot is where dwarven steam tanks and siege engines are tested and serviced. Beldin Steelgrill runs the work as its chief technician, known across Khaz Modan for repairing and tuning armored war wagons. The work is hard on heavy wrenches, cutters, and precision instruments. Beldin needs them constantly, keeping local ironworkers busy supplying his bench.

Berard's Journal. In Pyrewood Village, Berard's Journal holds research the Royal Apothecary Society needs. Berard studied an ancient plague that wiped out the aquatic life of Lake Lordamere. Before Arugal's shadow magic spread across Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard was one of the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising minds. From Pyrewood Village, he studied an ancient blight that had wiped out all aquatic life in Lake Lordamere centuries earlier. When Arugal's curse gripped the settlement, Berard lost his mind and became a thrall. His detailed field notes remained on a bookshelf in his quarters at the Pyrewood Village Inn.

Beren's Peril. Scourge gather in a hidden cave in southern Silverpine Forest, and Shadow Priest Allister moves to stop them. The Forsaken hope to strike before the undead can begin their offensive. Shadow Priest Allister hears that servants of the Lich King are gathering deep in southern Silverpine Forest. Their growing numbers threaten Forsaken operations across the region. Allister sends scouts to strike first and destroy the Scourge in their secluded lair before they can mobilize.

Beren's Peril. Scourge loyal to Thule Ravenclaw gather in the hills southwest of Ambermill, threatening the Forsaken. At Beren's Peril, a cave and mountain path lie high in the crags southwest of Ambermill, hidden from the main road. After the Third War, rogue Scourge undead fortified the refuge under the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. They refused to bow to the Dark Lady or flee north. Ravenclaw's regents, guardians, and drudgers gathered in secret to prepare an assault on the Forsaken base at the Sepulcher. Forsaken scouts uncovered them, and the quiet cliffs became a warzone. Horde fighters now move against the undead before they can attack.

Bernice's Necklace. At Stonefield Farm in Elwynn Forest, Bernice keeps her late husband's necklace close. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace once belonged to her late husband, a veteran of Stormwind's military campaigns. He carried it into battle as a charm for good fortune. Bernice says tragedy came only during his final campaign, the one expedition when he forgot to bring it. Since his death, the keepsake has remained among her most cherished possessions at Stonefield Farm.

Besseleth's Fang. In Sishir Canyon, Besseleth's Fang marks the end of a deadly spider's threat. Besseleth and her brood make Sishir Canyon dangerous for travelers. At night, the giant spider turns the Webwinder Path into a death trap for those crossing the gorge. Her fang measures nearly two feet and drips with potent venom. Local defenders have suffered her venomous strikes, and presenting the fang brings them relief.

Bethor Iceshard. In the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard commands the Magic Quarter's arcane and shadow practitioners. He holds authority in Sylvanas's realm, while old friendships still shape his past. Bethor Iceshard directs arcane and shadow practitioners from the Temple of the Damned in the Undercity. His intellect and icy resolve earn both respect and fear. He has the political and magical weight to instruct provincial magistrates across Lordaeron. Bethor sends Forsaken agents to secure valuable grimoires, investigate arcane anomalies, and suppress rival powers that threaten the Undercity's dominion.

Bethor's Scroll. Bethor Iceshard writes counter-incantations to help Apothecary Renferrel brew a protective draught against Thule Ravenclaw's dark sorcery. The scroll holds the key to facing the Scourge necromancy guarding Fenris Isle.

Betrayal from Within. At Camp Taurajo, Betrayal from Within begins with Mangletooth's offer of bloody vengeance. Imprisoned in a cage, the quilboar says his kin left him for dead. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the three Razormane warlords who emerged from Razorfen Kraul to organize assaults across the Barrens. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth has lost all loyalty to his Razormane kin. They left him behind in defeat, and he faces execution in his cage. Now he wants vengeance against the leaders who abandoned him. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the true architects behind the ruthless raids across the plains.

Betrayal from Within. In the central Barrens, the hunt for Lok Orcbane reaches its end. His fall will weaken the Razormane raids, and you carry his severed head to Thork at the Crossroads. Mangletooth, a captured Razormane quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, names Lok Orcbane as the chieftain directing attacks on Horde caravans. After you slay Lok deep in the southern thorn mazes, Mangletooth gives you the chieftain's skull. He finds it amusing that the orcs will benefit from betrayal within the tribe without knowing a captive quilboar helped them.

Big Game Hunter. Having proven skill across Stranglethorn Vale by hunting the region's deadliest predators, Hemet Nesingwary offers a final supreme challenge. The famed marksman asks for the head of King Bangalash, a great white tiger and the very reason Hemet is in the jungle at all. After completing the trials set by the expedition's huntsmen—slaying Sin'Dall, Bhag'thera, and Tethis—Hemet Nesingwary acknowledges your martial skill. According to the veteran marksman, who compares your prowess to the finest displays seen from Lordaeron's battlefields to the jungle depths, only one hunt remains to prove your abilities unmatched: felling King Bangalash, the grand white tiger that serves as the expedition leader's true target.

Billy Maclure. At Maclure Vineyards, Billy Maclure's pranks stir trouble between two neighboring farms. The young human boy dodges chores and plays at the feud between his family and the Stonefields, but fresh pastries can win his cooperation. Billy Maclure spends his days outside the barn at Maclure Vineyards, near farmer Gerard Tiller. He grows up among the grapevines in southern Elwynn Forest, often dodging chores and roaming the meadows. The Maclures and Stonefields have long been hostile toward each other. Billy treats their feud as a chance for pranks and petty theft.

Bingles Blastenheimer. On Loch Modan’s southeastern shore, Bingles Blastenheimer waits beside the wreck of his flying machine. Stranded among troggs and beasts, the gnomish aviator needs his tools and parts back. Bingles Blastenheimer took his customized flying craft into the skies, but bringing it down safely proved harder than lifting off. His gyrocopter malfunctioned and crashed on the Loch’s southeastern shore. Bingles survived, but the machine broke apart. Far from Ironforge, he stays near the wreck, wary of hungry crocolisks and hostile troggs. Troggs from a nearby island stole his tools and Blastencapper explosives, and he asks passing travelers to recover them.

Bingles' Blastencapper. Bingles Blastenheimer’s explosive lies in trogg hands after his gyrocopter fell into the Loch. Its loss threatens his plans to aid Gnomeregan’s liberation. Bingles Blastenheimer’s Blastencapper was aboard his gyrocopter when it crashed in Loch Modan. The pilot built the explosive for aerial strikes against the troggs and leper gnomes who overran Gnomeregan. Mechanical failure sent his craft into the Loch, though Bingles survived. Troggs from the lake’s northern islands raided the wreckage and carried the volatile weapon back to their camps.

Bingles' Hammer. Troggs have taken Bingles' Hammer from the crash site in Loch Modan. Bingles Blastenheimer, a stranded gnome aviator, needs his specialized gear to repair his flying machine and help free Gnomeregan. Bingles Blastenheimer survived his flying machine's plunge into the Loch, then lost his tools to troggs on the freshwater islands. They took his hammer and high-potency explosives from the crash site. He needs the hammer to repair the dented airframe and adjust the gyrocopter's mechanical parts. Without his equipment, Bingles cannot fly support runs for the gnome forces fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

Bingles' Missing Supplies. Bingles Blastenheimer is stranded on Loch Modan's southeastern shore after troggs steal his gear. He needs his tools and Blastencapper explosives to repair his gyrocopter and return to the fight for Gnomeregan. Bingles Blastenheimer crashes his gyrocopter into Loch Modan's cold waters. He survives and drags himself ashore, but troggs from the lake's central islands swarm the dazed pilot and steal his most valuable belongings.

Bingles' Screwdriver. Bingles' Screwdriver lies among the gear scattered across Loch Modan's northern islands. Gnome pilot Bingles Blastenheimer lost it when troggs plundered his crashed gyrocopter. Bingles Blastenheimer lost the tools he needs to repair his gyrocopter when he crashed into Loch Modan. Troggs on the nearby islands carried off his tool buckets, and the screwdriver was packed in one of them. Bingles needs the screwdriver to make fine adjustments as he repairs the craft and handles its armaments.

Bingles' Wrench. Bingles' Wrench is missing, along with the pilot's other tools. Troggs took it after Bingles Blastenheimer crash-landed his flying machine into the Loch. Bingles Blastenheimer survived his gyrocopter's crash into the Loch, but survival quickly became an ordeal. Troggs on the small northern islands raided the crash site, taking his specialized supplies and scattering his tools among buckets in their camps. Bingles' Wrench is one of three critical hand tools, alongside his high-yield Blastencapper explosives. Without the wrench, Bingles cannot repair his downed gyrocopter, delaying his planned aerial offensive to aid the exiled gnomes fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

Bink. Bink is a gnome mage trainer who resides within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Quick-witted and enthusiastic, she guides aspiring spellcasters through the intricacies of the arcane arts and connects them with prominent wizards across the Alliance. Located in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, Bink stands among the gathered scholars, priests, and arcanists in the Hall of Mysteries. Like many gnomes driven from Gnomeregan, she has adapted to life within the dwarven mountain stronghold, offering her keen intellect and knowledge of arcane craft to those learning the path of the mage. She is well connected to wizards across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, regularly pointing promising apprentices toward greater mentors such as High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind or Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh.

Bishop DeLavey. In Stormwind Keep, Bishop DeLavey hears the court's quiet concerns. He represents the Church of the Holy Light in the Petitioner's Chamber, where matters of faith and state meet. Bishop DeLavey advises Stormwind's court from within the keep. While Archbishop Benedictus tends to the Cathedral of Light, DeLavey lives among the nobility and petitioners. He brings spiritual counsel to the court while reckoning with the kingdom's politics. His place there lets him hear whispered rumors and delicate grievances before they reach Highlord Bolvar Fordragon or the young King Anduin.

Bitter Reaches. The Bitter Reaches is a rugged, windswept wilderness in northeastern Azshara. Largely untouched by civilization, the rugged cliffs are prowled by predatory beasts and massive mountain giants. Occupying the northeastern cliffs of Azshara, the Bitter Reaches remains a stark and untamed stretch of rocky terrain overlooking the Great Sea. Flocks of feral hippogryphs and two-headed chimaeras nest amidst the heights, while acidic oozes seep through the cold ground. Along the high northern ridges, colossal mountain giants have claimed the slopes as their own, driving away lesser creatures and turning the frozen approaches into a perilous hazard for any solitary traveler.

Bitter Rivals. In Dun Morogh, the Barleybrews and Thunderbrews compete for renown. Marleth Barleybrew sends you to the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos to replace a cask of Thunder Ale with her family's brew. Ale stirs fierce pride in Khaz Modan. The Barleybrews have long resented the fame of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Marleth Barleybrew admits that Thunderbrew makes a respectable ale, but she cannot accept that it alone is renowned in Dun Morogh. She plans to shake up the local palate by replacing a cask of Thunder Ale with her own fiery Barleybrew Scalder.

Black Channel Marsh. Raptors prowl Black Channel Marsh beside the road to Menethil Harbor. The mire lies in the Wetlands’ southwest, where travelers and couriers face danger along the coast. Black Channel Marsh spreads across the low ground southwest of the main road to Menethil Harbor. Caravan drivers and couriers know the danger there. The raised road may seem safe, but territorial raptors live among the stagnant channels and thick reeds. Hungry beasts often stray into the road, ambushing recruits and weary travelers who wander even a little from the path.

name.frFR: Bière brune de la Griffe noire

text.enUS: Black Claw Stout. Beneath Stormwind, Zardeth of the Black Claw prepares a drink for Lord Wishock. The stout is delivered as an ordinary tavern beverage.

Black Feather Quill. The Black Feather Quill lies in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, needed to wake the Druids of the Talon. The Black Feather Quill is one of four sacred focuses used to wake the Druids of the Talon from hibernation. The others are the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. The rite calls slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Without these items, a druid may remain trapped in the Dream and unable to return to their waking body.

Black dragonflight. Once the stalwart Earth-Warders charged by the titans to safeguard Azeroth's deep subterranean realms, the black dragonflight fell to madness and treachery. Corrupted by the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods, their leader Neltharion became Deathwing, turning his brood into one of the most destructive and hated forces on the planet. Today, their surviving scions weave plots from the shadows and wage covert wars against mortal kingdoms. Long ago, the Titan Khaz'goroth bestowed his blessing upon Neltharion, creating the black dragonflight to watch over the earth, raise mountains, and guard Azeroth's deep caverns. For ages, they stood alongside the other flights as patient, unyielding guardians. Yet their intimate bond with the world's subterranean foundations proved their undoing. Dwelling within the deepest hollows, they lay dangerously close to the sunken prisons of the Old Gods. Over centuries, dark whispers eroded the noble Earth-Warder's mind, driving him to madness and twisting his entire brood into vicious instruments of ruin.

Blackchar Cave. Blackchar Cave is a mysterious, sealed-off cavern tucked into the southwestern crags of Searing Gorge, close to the base of Blackrock Mountain. Its entrance is choked with impassable rubble and rock. Tucked away against the scorching crags near the approaches to Blackrock Mountain, Blackchar Cave presents a solid wall of stone where a deep cavern entrance might once have been. Heavy rubble and scorched slag choke the opening, preventing anyone from exploring whatever tunnels lie deeper within the mountain roots. The desolate terrain around it is scorched by ash and magma, offering little comfort to wanderers.

Blackened Skull. At Agamand Mills, Blackened Skull trophies mark the fight against the Scourge. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill wants them as proof that the Darkeye Bonecasters are being destroyed. Darkeye Bonecasters haunt the Agamand Mills. These skeletal spellcasters turn their necromantic malice against the living and the Forsaken, seeking to secure a forward base for the Lich King's armies in northern Tirisfal. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill asks for their ruined skulls as proof that the Scourge's mystical vanguard is being beaten back.

Blackfathom Deeps. Blackfathom Deeps lies flooded beneath the Zoram Strand on Ashenvale's northwestern coast. Its halls once honored Elune, but naga, satyr, and the Twilight's Hammer now hold the ruins. Beneath Ashenvale's northwestern cliffs, flooded halls mark the remains of an ancient temple. Before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the temple honored Elune and held its own moonwell. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the shrine sank beneath the waves and was presumed lost forever. Over millennia, shorelines receded and the ground shifted below, leaving the temple partly flooded beneath the cliffs.

Blackfathom Villainy. At Blackfathom Deeps, Argent Guard Thaelrid calls for the Alliance to stop Twilight Lord Kelris. The cult leader sacrifices captives to Aku'mai, and Thaelrid asks for Kelris's severed head as proof to bring to the Argent Dawn in Darnassus. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple devoted to Elune. Corruption from an ancient Old God rose through the rock, fouling the Moon Well and freeing Aku'mai, a voracious servant of that darkness. The Twilight's Hammer joined with local naga after the temple was defiled, making its holy halls a place of ritual murder.

Blackfathom Villainy. Inside Blackfathom Deeps, Blackfathom Villainy reaches a wounded scout who cannot finish his mission alone. Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid asks passing Horde champions to end Twilight Lord Kelris's blood sacrifices to Aku'mai in the sunken ruins. Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid lies wounded in the underground temple along the Ashenvale coast. His reconnaissance uncovered horrors beyond naga incursions, but his strength is spent and he cannot complete the mission alone. He calls on passing Horde champions to strike at the cult's leaders in the sunken halls.

Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir is free and carries news to Krusk in Tarren Mill. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, visited him and spoke of enslaving orcs who resist him. Perenolde also brought Elysa, a girl wearing the pendant the Warchief desires. Gol'dir has news for Krusk after a visit from Aliden Perenolde, head of the Syndicate. Perenolde called himself lord of the land and said he meant to enslave the orcs who resist him. His father and his mentor, the despised Blackmoore, had planned the same. Gol'dir sends you to carry this news to Krusk in Tarren Mill. He will follow after settling his own business where he is.

Blackrock Blockade. Marshal Marris is pressing the Blackrock Blockade east of Lake Everstill. Lakeshire's guard aims to starve out the Blackrock orcs and take their weapons. Blackrock raiders in Redridge are pushing Alliance forces to their limits. Cut off from regular supply trains, their forward parties live off the hills. Marshal Marris knows even fierce orcs cannot keep fighting without food and steel.

Blackrock Bounty. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon has Guard Howe offer a bounty as Blackrock forces gather in northern Redridge. Stormwind sends no royal soldiers, so the town pays independent fighters to strike at Blackrock Champions and disrupt the clan’s coordinated assault. Redridge belongs to the Kingdom of Stormwind, but the Blackrock clan ignores human borders. Orcs pour through the mountain passes from the Burning Steppes and fortify camps across northern Redridge. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and Stormwind’s regency withholds royal soldiers. With the town’s coffers dwindling, Magistrate Solomon and other local leaders offer bounties to protect Lakeshire.

name.esES: La amenaza de los Roca Negra

text.enUS: Blackrock Menace. Redridge's Blackrock orcs press in from the north and southeast, leaving Lakeshire under siege. Marshal Marris calls on adventurers to thin their ranks and bring back their battleworn axes. Lakeshire faces threats from several sides, but the Blackrock orcs are the gravest danger. These seasoned raiders have crossed south from the fiery Burning Steppes into Redridge. They have taken strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps townspeople penned inside Lakeshire, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads.

Blackrock Mountain. Blackrock Mountain is a massive, active volcano that towers between the Burning Steppes and the Searing Gorge. Borne from the cataclysmic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord, its hollowed depths house ancient dwarven masonry, warring armies, and smoldering horrors. Blackrock Mountain did not exist until the climax of the War of the Three Hammers two and a half centuries ago. Facing annihilation by the united armies of Ironforge and the Wildhammer clan, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan reached into the depths of the earth for a weapon. His reckless spell shattered the dimensional barriers and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The resulting apocalypse tore the Redridge range apart, gouging out the Searing Gorge and Burning Steppes while thrusting a colossal volcano into the sky. Thaurissan perished in the blast, and the surviving Dark Iron clan was bound into eternal servitude to the Firelord, carving their capital, Shadowforge City, deep within the mountain's roots.

Blackrock Pass. Blackrock Pass is a mountain corridor connecting the northern cliffs of Redridge Mountains to the arid wastes of the Burning Steppes. Passing beneath a heavy iron gate, it marks the sudden threshold between the tranquil human heartlands and the dangerous war grounds of the Dark Iron dwarves and the Blackrock orcs. For any weary traveler journeying north on foot, it represents a harsh and perilous frontier. Carved into the jagged spine of the mountains, Blackrock Pass serves as the overland route between Redridge Mountains and the Burning Steppes. A stout iron gate stands along the rocky boundary, demarcating the idyllic forests and lakes of the southern valleys from the volcanic ruin beyond. Crossing this line leaves behind the pastoral lands protected by Lakeshire's beleaguered militia, thrusting travelers into an open wasteland populated by fire elementals, dragonkin, and hostile orc warbands. Few make the crossing on foot unless bound for the shadow of Blackrock Mountain itself.

Blackrock Stronghold. Blackrock Stronghold is a heavily fortified encampment carved into the crags of the northern Burning Steppes, positioned right outside the entrance to Blackrock Mountain. It serves as a major field garrison for the Blackrock orcs and their allies under the Dark Horde banner. Sprawling across the scorched foothills below Blackrock Mountain, the stronghold functions as the primary ground base for the Blackrock clan in the Burning Steppes. Unlike Thrall's Horde, these orcs cling to their warlike legacy, serving Rend Blackhand and the dragonkin who lurk above in the spire.

Blackrock clan. The Blackrock clan is a martial orcish clan renowned for its strict military discipline, unmatched blacksmithing, and central role in the First and Second Wars. Today, the clan is deeply fractured: while some veterans follow Thrall in the New Horde, a vicious and renegade splinter group known as the Dark Horde occupies the upper peaks of Blackrock Mountain under Rend Blackhand. Hailing from Draenor, the Blackrock clan made its name through rigid hierarchy, heavy armor, and mastery over the forge. Under Chieftain Blackhand, they served as the brutal core of the Old Horde during the invasion of Azeroth, laying siege to Stormwind. When Orgrim Doomhammer slew Blackhand to cleanse the Horde of Gul'dan's direct puppet mastery, leadership of both the clan and the Horde remained firmly in Blackrock hands through the grueling campaigns of the Second War.

Blackthorn Ridge. At Blackthorn Ridge, Razormane quilboar guard the southern Barrens north of Razorfen Kraul. Brine, an orc shaman, keeps watch from a camp above a pool of unusually pure mountain water. Blackthorn Ridge rises beside Razorfen Kraul, its slopes crowded with dense thickets of sharp briars. The Razormane quilboar claim the ground as ancestral territory, using the thorny barriers to ambush outsiders and skirmish across the southern Barrens. Travelers seek out the ridge despite the danger, drawn to Brine, a hermit orc shaman. His camp sits above a spring famed across Kalimdor for its clear, spiritually pure water.

Blackwolf River. Blackwolf River runs from Cragpool Lake through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Venture Company's logging and industrial work has fouled its waters. Blackwolf River runs through Windshear Crag, fed by Cragpool Lake. Venture Company loggers cut the surrounding woods with heavy machinery and buzzsaws. Sludge, oil, and logging waste drain into the current. The river carries the cost of the company's work through the basin.

Blackwood Den. Blackwood Den lies under the Blackwood furbolgs’ corruption in southern Darkshore, near Ashenvale. The cave and camps that were once their peaceful home have fallen into madness. Volcor, a night elf scout, is trapped in the cavern and awaits aid from Auberdine. Blackwood furbolgs hold a rocky cave and crude camps near the southern border of Darkshore and Ashenvale. Corruption has taken hold of the tribe, and its members attack outsiders. Deep inside the cave, the night elf Volcor is pinned down and in danger. Scouts and travelers from Auberdine are needed to help him.

Blackwood Lake. Blackwood Lake is a blighted body of water situated in the southern Eastern Plaguelands, teeming with hostile, corrupted elementals. The area is haunted by memories of tragedy and war, watched over by a small frontline camp of the Argent Dawn. Like so much of the Eastweald, Blackwood Lake has been poisoned by the rampant plague of undeath. Diseased and foul water elementals churn beneath the murky surface, attacking anyone who ventures near the shoreline.

Bladefist Bay. Bladefist Bay opens onto the Great Sea along eastern Durotar, just beyond Orgrimmar's gates. Craggy bluffs rise above its shore, with Azshara's southern coast across the water. Bladefist Bay meets the Great Sea along Durotar's northeastern edge. Rocky cliffs rise above its treacherous surf, just east of Orgrimmar, the Horde capital. Across the water to the north, Azshara's ancient red cliffs and ruins mark the far shore. The bay forms a boundary between Durotar and the open sea.

Bladeswift the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Bladeswift the Elder's ancient spirit is honored in Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, travelers seek his wisdom beneath the stars and a blessing tied to night elven tradition. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth to share wisdom and bless travelers. In Darnassus, Bladeswift the Elder appears among the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave. This ancient spirit turns his gaze to the night sky and its mysteries, while the living face the trials of the present.

Blanchy. Old Blanchy is the loyal, hard-working mare belonging to Theodore and Verna Furlbrow, currently resting beside their wagon near the Jansen Stead in Westfall. Renowned for her gentle disposition and hefty appetite, she remains a steady companion to her owners amidst the turmoil gripping the countryside. Long before pulling the Furlbrows' wagon through the dust of Westfall, Blanchy worked the Furlbrows' farm in the breadbasket of Stormwind, where she earned a reputation as an exceptionally sweet-tempered, well-behaved mare. Years of heavy labor have worn her down to 'Old Blanchy,' and the arduous journey fleeing troubled homesteads has left her exhausted. Though visibly weary, her appetite remains hearty, and travelers who bring her nourishing handfuls of oats scattered across the surrounding fields are rewarded by Verna with Blanchy's own treasured blanket and feed pouch.

Blessed Arm. In Stormwind, Blessed Arm carries lightforge iron toward a weapon against Morbent Fel. After salvaging the ingots from the wreck of the Flying Osprey in the Wetlands, you bring the precious metal to master dwarven smith Grimand Elmore, who can shape it to face the necromancer. Glorin Steelbrow packs the recovered lightforge iron for Stormwind. The metal is rare, and its power against foul and unholy beings demands a smith who knows how to work it. After the shipment came from the wreck of the Flying Osprey off the Wetlands coast, Glorin knew of only one artisan in the southern kingdoms suited to the task: master weaponsmith Grimand Elmore.

Blind Cazul. In the Cleft of Shadow, an initiate seeks Blind Cazul’s help with a succubus ritual. The sightless warlock points toward an object charged with mortal emotion. A succubus answers to mortal longing, sorrow, and desire. To draw one across the veil, an aspiring summoner needs more than willpower; the demon is known to devour souls. Blind Cazul understands what the initiate seeks and knows where to find a fitting lure.

Blind Hunter. Deep within Razorfen Kraul, the Blind Hunter roosts in the sunless depths. This elusive albino bat prowls the quilboar redoubt, far from common bats near the cavern entrances. Razorfen Kraul winds through briars and dark caverns below ground. Common bats roost nearer the surface, where faint light reaches in from outside. The Blind Hunter keeps to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale hide and milky gaze may come from generations spent apart from natural sunlight.

Blind Mary. In a ruined farmhouse southeast of Darkshire, Blind Mary wanders as a tormented banshee. She was once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, but her violent death and transformation drove her to mutilate herself in grief over what she had become. Mary was known for her beauty before the shadows fell across Duskwood. She took great pride in it and rarely went without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept through the region, Mary and many of her neighbors were slain. Her spirit did not find rest in the earth. Instead, she became an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form.

Blisters on The Land. In the eastern Wetlands, Rethiel senses sickness spreading through the marsh. The bog beast warden asks travelers to destroy Fen Creepers, hoping to ease the land's rising fever. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches the Wetlands from a grove among the marshes. The mire has always been harsh, but now an unnatural sickness spreads through it. Rethiel senses a fever in the earth, warping wild nature into mindless, shambling horrors.

Blood Feeders. In Malaka'jin, the scent of butchered game draws Deepmoss spiders into the trolls' camps. Xen'Zilla asks the Horde to drive the predators back from the settlement. The trolls founded Malaka'jin as a frontier outpost in southeastern Stonetalon Mountains, where they could hunt. The craggy slopes yield plenty of game, but its meat draws nocturnal predators into camp. Deepmoss spiders are aggressive arachnids native to the crags and canyons to the north. Under cover of darkness, they slip in to scavenge the trolls' stores or hunt the hunters themselves.

Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Across the Barrens, blood shards carry the power of the fallen boar god Agamaggan. Quilboar say his blood sank into the earth and hardened into red stones. At Camp Taurajo, the captive Mangletooth trades their power to the Horde for his own reasons. Quilboar lore tells how Agamaggan fell ten thousand years ago in the War of the Ancients. His blood raised giant thorn mazes across the plains, then sank beneath the soil and seeped into minerals. In time, it hardened into blood-red stones. The quilboar honor the shards as sacred remnants of their creator. They gather them from mineral seams and holy grounds, then use them as totems for battle and sorcery.

Blood Tithe. Blood Tithe is a quest initiated by Alvarion Windfield, an ailing Skyborne farmer seeking aid in the settlement of Valanaar. Desperate to protect his livelihood, he recruits adventurers to travel west to his lowland orchard and assist his wife, Aamelia. In the settlement of Valanaar, an injured Skyborne man named Alvarion Windfield desperately searches for capable adventurers. Wracked with visible pain, Alvarion has traveled from his homestead into town to hire fighters who can help save his livelihood. Rather than tasking travelers on the spot, he implores those willing to help to journey westward into the lowlands, where his wife Aamelia maintains their family orchard.

Blood in the Streets. Dalaran's barrier has come down, and turmoil grips the city. With its patrols dealt with, Magus Wordeen Voidglare says there is no better time to slip inside and learn the mages' secrets. You are to carry the key from the internment camp to the city's sewers on its northern edge. After Dalaran Patrols, Magus Wordeen Voidglare says that whatever lowered Dalaran's barrier has thrown the city into turmoil, so now is the time for the Horde to get inside and learn the mages' secrets. You are to take the key from the internment camp and look for the sewers on the city's northern edge, by Lordamere Lake. With luck, the mages saw no need to ward so disagreeable an entrance.

Blood of Innocents. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks blood for a plan against the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains. The Royal Apothecary Society uses dark ingredients gathered from local bandits to pacify the encroaching company. The Horde faces a steady struggle in the Stonetalon Mountains, where the Venture Company ravages the wilderness and its people. Apothecary Lydon proposes an alchemical remedy instead of sending armies to blunt their axes. He plans to brew an agent that paralyzes and pacifies the mercenaries, leaving them weak and docile.

Bloodfeather Belt. In northern Teldrassil, Bloodfeather harpies wear crude leather belts as they crowd the Oracle Glade. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak collects them as proof that the nearby nests have been cleared. Bloodfeather harpies have built aggressive nests in the boughs around the Oracle Glade. Their presence threatens the ancient Oracle Tree and blocks travel through northern Teldrassil. After the flock ambushed and killed a runner carrying reports to Darnassus, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak called on travelers to strike at the nests. The belts taken from fallen harpies show that their numbers are being culled and the paths are being secured, so messages can reach the capital again.

Bloodfen Burrow. Bloodfen Burrow is a cavern in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with vicious raptors. The beasts have claimed the cave and the surrounding clearing, completely overrunning the ruins of a settlement that once tried to survive the wetlands. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Bloodfen Burrow serves as the primary den for the region's aggressive Bloodfen raptors. The cave mouth and surrounding hollow crawl with the pack, drawn to the sheltered crevice and the bountiful hunting ground the marsh provides. Just outside the entrance lie scattered debris and splintered remains of an unidentified settlement, serving as a grim reminder of who truly rules the swamp's interior. Travelers also whisper that Cortello, an adventurous buccaneer, left one of his hidden riddle clues somewhere within this deadly den.

Bloodfury Bloodline. In the Charred Vale, Maggran Earthbinder seeks to end the harpies’ hold. He sends you to kill their leader, Bloodfury Ripper, and bring back proof. Harpies at the edge of the Charred Vale keep threatening Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder believes their attacks will only end when their matriarch, Bloodfury Ripper, is dead. The flock treats her like a queen, and her leadership gives them the unity and boldness they show along the craggy western ridge.

Bloodfury Ripper's Remains. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder seeks Bloodfury Ripper's Remains as proof that the Bloodfury harpy leader is dead. Her death strikes at the threat to the tauren settlement. Bloodfury Ripper leads the harpies of the Charred Vale with fierce, territorial aggression. They nest among the scorched ruins and threaten travelers and shamans across the Stonetalon Mountains. Culling the flock eases the danger for a time, but Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat knows that lasting relief means removing its leader. Bloodfury Ripper rules almost like a queen, directing the harpies' attacks on their territory. Her remains prove she is dead, leaving the flock in disarray and giving the tauren who seek to heal and secure their rugged lands greater peace of mind.

Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren gather at Bloodhoof Village beside Stonebull Lake in central Mulgore. Led by Baine Bloodhoof, the village guides them from Camp Narache toward Thunder Bluff and tends the plains’ defense, trade, and rites. Bloodhoof Village gathers tauren around Stonebull Lake in central Mulgore. Young tauren arrive from their trials at Camp Narache to hone their skills before traveling onward to the great mesas of Thunder Bluff. Patient breeders here tame wild kodo beasts for travel, while the village is also a center of craft and ceremony.

Bloodhoof the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bloodhoof the Elder just north of Bloodhoof Village. The ancestral spirit appears near the bridge and offers a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village, near the bridge. Travelers honor the sacrifices of the past by approaching the elder, who offers words of encouragement and a Coin of Ancestry.

Bloodied Insignia. Bloodied Insignias are tragic remnants of the fallen defenders of Lordaeron, scattered among the kingdom's blighted ruins. Bearing the old crests of the Alliance, these battered badges represent soldiers whose families fled south to Stormwind during the Third War. When Prince Arthas returned to scour Lordaeron with the Scourge, its grand military was overwhelmed and butchered. Countless soldiers perished defending the Capital City and the surrounding lands, leaving behind few physical traces beyond rusted armor and bloodstained brass. These old Alliance insignias belonged to the men and women who stood their ground against the undead onslaught. Trampled into the soil and rubble of the ruins, each medal is an artifact of the kingdom's final, desperate stand.

Bloodmage Drazial. Bloodmage Drazial is a blood elf practitioner of arcane and blood magic camped in the northern reaches of the Blasted Lands. Alongside his sister Lynnore, he studies the native beasts of the red wastes to craft potent alchemical concoctions for traveling adventurers. Perched near the northern pass where the Swamp of Sorrows gives way to the Blasted Lands, Bloodmage Drazial pursues a peculiar brand of magic. While many high elves shun the forbidden arts or despair over Quel'Thalas, Drazial and his sister Lynnore harness blood magic to harvest power from the harsh environment. The blighted fauna of the wastes—scorpoks, snickerfangs, and blasted boars—show strange, unnatural vigor, which Drazial and Lynnore believe came from the energy released when the Dark Portal opened. By harvesting specific organs and tissues from these creatures, Drazial brews volatile concoctions that grant immense bursts of physical strength, agility, and endurance.

Bloodmage Lynnore. Bloodmage Lynnore is a blood elf practitioner of forbidden blood magic camped with her brother Drazial near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands. She assists adventurers by concocting potent alchemical draughts from the organs of local beasts. Camped near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands alongside her brother Drazial, Bloodmage Lynnore is one of the exceptionally rare elven practitioners of blood magic found in the Eastern Kingdoms. Unperturbed by the harsh and corrupting landscape of the Blasted Lands, she studies the latent arcane and vital energies coursing through native beasts. Travelers who bring her the brains and gizzards of local fauna find that she can distill these gruesome reagents into specialized elixirs granting profound enhancements to intellect and spirit.

Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Who he was in life is not recorded, but the plague of undeath claimed him, and he now lingers deep within the Crusade's holy grounds, hungering for vengeance. No record tells who Thalnos was in life. Whatever his past, the plague of undeath claimed him. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery, and crying out for vengeance and for more souls.

Bloodscalp Clan Heads. Following the sorting of trophies gathered in the jungle, Nimboya confirms that the missing young troll Yenniku was not among them. To discover the truth of Yenniku's fate, the Darkspear seek to compel answers from the leaders of the rival Bloodscalp tribe. After the earlier hunt proved Yenniku was not among the fallen Bloodscalp trophies, Nimboya looks to higher leadership for answers. The Bloodscalp chief, Gan'zulah, and his witch doctor, Nezzliok the Dire, are enemies of the Darkspear tribe and would never talk willingly. Nimboya means to force the truth from their dead lips, bringing their heads to the cauldron at Grom'gol Base Camp to make them talk.

Bloodscalp Ears. Kebok in Booty Bay is losing guards and agents to jungle clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe. Worried about climbing expenses and answering to Baron Revilgaz, he offers coin to any adventurer willing to hunt down the trolls and return with proof of the kill. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Kebok faces a serious operational dilemma. The local trolls in Stranglethorn Vale have been killing his agents in the jungle, and he has lost many of his best guards in skirmishes with them. With the casualties mounting, so too are the costs, leaving him frantic over how to explain them to Baron Revilgaz.

Bloodstone Choker. In Stormwind, the Bloodstone Choker binds a warlock’s ritual to the void. Gakin the Darkbinder once held the bloodstone talisman, until an apprentice stole it and fled to the Defias Brotherhood. Carved from bloodstone, the choker can bridge the mortal world and the twisting shadows of the Twisting Nether. Gakin puts it to use in the crypts beneath the tavern, channeling its magic at the summoning circle to draw a hostile Voidwalker from the void. A warlock must subdue the furious creature in direct combat while wielding the talisman to prove the will to command such a guardian.

Bloodtalon Matriarch. The Bloodtalon Matriarch is the formidable leader of a swift and cunning raptor pack near Sen'jin Village. After proving too dangerous and stubborn to tame as an adult, she must be confronted so her offspring can be raised from the egg as loyal companions for the Darkspear tribe. The Bloodtalon pack is renowned along the coast of Durotar for its remarkable speed and keen cunning. Handlers in Sen'jin Village prize these traits above all else when seeking dependable mounts and companions for the Darkspear tribe. However, full-grown raptors possess stubborn and violent instincts, making adults almost impossible to domesticate once they have adapted to life in the wild.

Bloodtooth Camp. In central Ashenvale, Bloodtooth Camp lies west of the Falfarren River. Ran Bloodtooth leads the corrupted furbolgs, who attack anyone who approaches. Alliance scouts target the camp as they work to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Bloodtooth Camp lies southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River. Its furbolgs were once bound to Kalimdor's sacred wilderness, but a lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Ran Bloodtooth commands the crude settlement. His followers attack travelers and night elven protectors alike.

Bloodvenom Falls. Bloodvenom Falls is a towering, foul waterfall plunging down the corrupted cliffs of northern Felwood. Its toxic flow feeds the Bloodvenom River, spreading demon-spawned rot down the mountains and into downstream lands. Pouring over the bluffs in Felwood, Bloodvenom Falls represents one of the most vivid wounds inflicted upon the ancient forests of Kalimdor. Once a pristine mountain cascade, the waters were warped into a virulent sludge during the Third War by demonic magics and the remnants of the Burning Legion. The falls feed directly into the Bloodvenom River, which weaves through the heart of Felwood. From there, the tainted torrent rushes down the mountain slopes to become the foul Wildbend River in Darkshore, carrying blight far beyond Felwood's blighted borders.

Bloodvenom Post. Bloodvenom Post is a remote Horde settlement perched on the rocky bluffs of western Felwood overlooking Darkshore. Its tauren-style structures and tauren guards provide a foothold in a region infested with demonic taint and corrupted wildlife. Tucked away along the high cliffs above Darkshore, Bloodvenom Post is reached by following the corrupted southern bank of the Bloodvenom River away from Felwood's main thoroughfare. Built with traditional tauren tents, totems, and watch posts, this encampment provides Horde wanderers with a vital base of operations amidst a dying forest. From here, scouts track the encroaching demonic forces, study the spreading corruption of the waters, and attempt to monitor the hostile wildlife mutated by the Burning Legion's lingering power.

Bloodvenom River. The Bloodvenom River is a foul waterway cutting through central Felwood, saturated with the demonic corruption that blighted the ancient forest. Its putrid waters seep downstream across the mountains into Darkshore, transforming into the tainted Wildbend River. Running through the corrupted heart of Felwood, the Bloodvenom River serves as an open conduit of the land's spiritual and physical decay. Its banks are thick with vile oozes, mutated beasts, and foul run-off left in the wake of the Burning Legion's invasion. The corruption within the channel is potent enough to taint lands far beyond Felwood itself, flowing westward down into the coastal forests of Darkshore as the Wildbend River.

Bloody Bone Necklaces. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp has his own agenda in Stranglethorn Vale beyond assisting Nimboya. He seeks to weaken the rival Bloodscalp tribe by gathering trophies from their warriors. Though Kin'weelay arrived in the jungle outpost of Grom'gol Base Camp to help Nimboya, he maintains private purposes of his own. The Bloodscalp trolls dwelling to the north are enemies of the Darkspears. Kin'weelay believes that claiming personal trophies from fallen foes bestows spiritual power over them, asking travelers to hunt Bloodscalp warriors and take the bloody bone necklaces they wear around their necks.

Bluefen. Bluefen is a soggy marshland nestled in northern Dustwallow Marsh just east of Brackenwall Village. Crawling with aggressive wetland predators, the mire has also become a staging ground for covert Theramore Infiltrators keeping watch on local Horde movements. Situated just east of the Stonemaul ogres of Brackenwall Village, Bluefen embodies the untamed hazards of Dustwallow Marsh. The humid swampland teems with predatory beasts, including raptors, giant spiders, carrion-feeding birds, and lurking crocolisks. Beyond natural predators, travelers must contend with Theramore Infiltrators who skulk through the murky terrain to spy on the Horde and project human influence deeper into the swamp.

Bluegill Marsh. In western Wetlands, Bluegill Marsh is claimed by the hostile Bluegill tribe. Their huts and waterways are guarded by Gobbler, and travelers risk being surrounded in the shallows. Bluegill murlocs crowd the muddy flats and reed beds of the western Wetlands. Their tribe has built crude camps in the stagnant water and claims the marsh as its own. They live and hunt in close-knit packs. Travelers and scouts from Menethil Harbor risk ambush from every direction when they wade into Bluegill territory, where the chieftain Gobbler prowls the shallows.

Blueleaf Tuber. Beneath Razorfen Kraul, Blueleaf Tubers grow hidden from the surface. Their rarity draws wealthy gourmands and traders from across the world. Blueleaf Tubers grow beneath Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. Dense roots and quilboar briars hide them from casual foragers. Though the ground is harsh, wealthy gourmands and traders across the world pay an exorbitant price for their distinct flavor.

Blueleaf Tubers. Mebok Mizzyrix seeks Blueleaf Tubers beneath the roots of Razorfen Kraul. The Ratchet goblin merchant sends trained snufflenose gophers to find and dig them up for trade. Blueleaf tubers are prized as a rare culinary delicacy across the world. They are hard to harvest because they do not grow in open fields or ordinary wild groves. Foragers find them deep underground in the southern Barrens, tangled among the roots of Razorfen Kraul.

Bluff Runner Windstrider. On Thunder Bluff's mesas, Bluff Runner Windstrider carries urgent messages across the city. He directs Horde travelers toward distant frontiers, including Ashenvale, Feralas, and the Plaguelands. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries messages across Thunder Bluff's high plateaus. His swift runs keep the city's leaders and visitors informed. He jogs along the rope bridges and pathways, calling out news and carrying dispatches. When outposts across Kalimdor or the Eastern Kingdoms need reinforcements, Windstrider calls on passing champions to carry word and answer the call to arms.

Boat Wreckage. Beside a wrecked row boat in the water you find a well-cared-for knife in the mud. Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold wants any clue you find brought back, and a feeling creeps over you that something else shares the water. Feeling along the mud near the wrecked boat, your fingertips brush the grip of a knife that looks well cared for. Whoever was on the boat may have lost it, and the large chunk missing from the boat might have a part in the loss. You take the knife, recalling that Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold asked you to bring any clue you found back to him, yet the feeling creeps over you that something else shares the water.

Body and Heart. In Darnassus, a young night elf druid nears the end of initiation into the path of the claw. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends the initiate into Darkshore to summon Lunaclaw and prove strength of body and heart before taking the form of the bear. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends night elf druid initiates east of Auberdine, the coastal settlement in Darkshore. A natural cavern there shelters wild moonkin and an ancient Moonkin Stone. Anointing the sacred stone with Cenarion Moondust awakens Lunaclaw, its ancient defender. The guardian challenges any initiate who seeks the sacred strength of the claw.

Body and Heart. At the Moonkin Stone, you face a trial of body and heart to master Bear Form. Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids from Thunder Bluff to summon and defeat Lunaclaw near the border of Mulgore and the Barrens. Turak Runetotem tests young tauren druids who seek the path of the Druid of the Claw. After you commune with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade, your training turns to a trial of strength. Turak, the elder druid trainer atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, gives worthy aspirants Cenarion Lunardust. He sends you to a sacred stone near the dry frontier where Mulgore meets the Barrens.

Bodyguard for Hire. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally lead their kodo past the Kolkar centaur village, yet they stop whenever the centaur war drums are heard. Cork asks you to protect the caravan past the Kolkar village, and payment is waiting with Smeed Scrabblescrew, a bit down the road. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally take their kodo straight past the Kolkar centaur. Now and then the centaur war drums are heard, and the caravan stops, because dead traders make no profit. Cork asks you to guard the caravan past the Kolkar village, a short distance, and keep it in one piece. The caravan waits north of the Kolkar Village and southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress.

Bolgan's Hole. Bolgan's Hole is a subterranean cavern nestled in the southern cliffs of Gelkis Village in Desolace. It serves as the inner sanctum of the Gelkis centaur clan, housing their highest chieftains and sacred earth relics. Carved deep into the craggy bluffs overlooking the Gelkis encampment, Bolgan's Hole functions as the command center for the tribe. It is here that the ruling khan holds court, surrounded by veteran guards and the tribe's most influential shamans. The cavern offers natural fortification against rival clans, most notably the bloodthirsty Magram centaur to the east.

Bolvar Fordragon. Stormwind’s crown and armies rest with Bolvar Fordragon while King Varian is missing. As Regent and Supreme Commander of Stormwind’s armed forces, he stands beside young King Anduin in Stormwind Keep and tries to hold the kingdom together. Domestic troubles grow, while Lady Katrana Prestor’s counsel often delays his military decisions. King Varian vanished on the way to a peace summit on Theramore Isle, leaving Stormwind in political disarray. Ten-year-old Prince Anduin was crowned to preserve continuity, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon took up the work of ruling as Regent. A venerated paladin devoted to the crown, Bolvar now faces a kingdom under strain. Stormwind’s soldiers are spread thin across Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood. Lady Katrana Prestor’s dismissive counsel adds to the burden, repeatedly blocking him from sending royal troops to towns on the frontier.

Bone Collector. At Kormek's Hut in Desolace, the goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle is certain that kodo bones are about to transform the world. Ten of them are wanted from the Kodo Graveyard, south of the hut, and something is promised in return. Bibbly insists the hut is sitting on a goldmine. Customers make furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder from kodo bones. Bibbly sends you south to the Kodo Graveyard to bring back ten of them, with something promised in return.

Bones of Grakkarond. The Bones of Grakkarond are the skeletal remains of a massive bronze dragon lying bleached under the sun of central Silithus. Slain during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands, this fallen wyrm serves as a grim monument held sacred by the qiraji's Anubisath sentinels. Sprawled across the windswept dunes of central Silithus lies the colossal ribcage and skull of Grakkarond, a bronze dragon who met his demise during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands. In that apocalyptic clash a millennium ago, the great dragon was struck down by Ossirian the Unscarred, an Anubisath warrior elevated by the dark powers of the city-kingdom. To the Anubisath, this battlefield trophy is a sacred testament to their might over the dragonflights, left untouched where he fell.

Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton is frustrated by misplaced and missing tomes. He asks young adventurers to find Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, and take stock of the library archives, but Daniel's thoughts keep wandering to local tradeskills, making a straight answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey preserves old scholarly works, spiritual writings, and historical records that survived the First War in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Brother Paxton, a meticulous monk, takes great pride in the collection. Lately, books have gone missing from the shelves, and Paxton needs a clear inventory to learn how widespread the loss is. He has little patience to chase after his daydreaming helper.

Book Return. Book Return is an Elwynn Forest quest directing adventurers to recover Brother Paxton's lost reading materials from the infested depths of Fargodeep Mine. Chief among the missing volumes is 'Fun with Elementals,' a beginner's guide that risks granting the mine's kobolds dangerous conjuration abilities if left in their clutches. While investigating the growing kobold menace within Fargodeep Mine, Marshal Dughan tasks adventurers with recovering missing volumes belonging to Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey. Among the scattered texts lost in the dim subterranean tunnels is a particularly volatile primer titled 'Fun with Elementals.' Paxton fears that the instructions within are so accessible that even the mine's crude kobold squatters could decipher them and conjure an elemental creature in the depths.
