text.enUS: Book from Sven's Farm. In Duskwood, Sven's ruined farm holds a dirt-stained journal with no title. Its fragments record an unknown onlooker's glimpse of the attack on Sven Yorgen's family. A loose mound of dirt among the charred remains of Sven's farm in southern Duskwood hides a weather-damaged journal. Its anonymous writer left frantic, incomplete notes about the tragedy at the homestead. The pages support Sven Yorgen's suspicion that someone watched from the shadows while his family was slain. The account breaks off without explaining who the writer was or what happened next. Sven's clue leads investigators to carry the book to Darkshire, hoping someone there will recognize the handwriting.

Book of the Ancients. Azore Aldamort of the Ethel Rethor tower trusts you with a gem. Set in the hand of a serpent statue on Ranazjar Isle, northwest of the tower, it calls up the protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. After Sceptre of Light, Azore Aldamort hands you the Gem of the Serpent. A Serpent Statue stands on Ranazjar Isle, a little island to the northwest of the Ethel Rethor tower, and the gem belongs on its hand. That will bring forth the guardian of the Book of the Ancients, a book that holds naga secrets kept for centuries. Azore hopes it will teach much about their scaled foes.

Book: Stresses of Iron. In Stormwind Keep, Margulf Blaggon’s book on metallurgy has been lent to Northshire Abbey for copying. Margulf Blaggon wrote about the practical and theoretical sides of metallurgy. Milton Sheaf cared for the volume in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep. The library lent it to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton copied it by hand for his own collection. Paxton’s work took far longer than expected, and Brother Kristoff waited anxiously in Cathedral Square for the book to return to the city.

Bookie Herod. Lieutenant Doren fears a spy among his own men after Kurzen discovered Thorsen's secret. To uncover how the secret slipped out, an investigator must infiltrate Kurzen's Compound and recover the records kept by Kurzen's logistics officer. Following the discovery of Thorsen's secret, Lieutenant Doren suspects that a traitor operates within their midst. The intelligence leak threatens their operations, and finding the traitor has become an urgent concern. Thorsen maintained a line of communication directly into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer. Because Herod knows how Kurzen's Compound is run from day to day, Doren believes the officer's written records hold the truth about how the operation was exposed.

Booty Bay. Booty Bay is a sprawling pirate haven built into the sheer sea cliffs of southern Stranglethorn Vale, operated by the Steamwheedle Cartel's Blackwater Raiders. Entered by land through the gaping jaws of a giant shark carcass, it serves as a fiercely enforced neutral port where Alliance and Horde mingle under the watchful eyes of heavily armed goblin bruisers. Originally known as Blackwater Cove when it was a human settlement later overrun by jungle trolls, the bay was eventually captured by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Today, it is an international crossroads and a haven for scoundrels, outcasts, and merchants alike. Overseen by Baron Revilgaz alongside Fleet Master Seahorn from the balconies of the Salty Sailor Tavern, the port is ostensibly lawless yet strictly managed: anyone may drink, trade, or hire mercenaries here, provided they obey the cartel's peace and pay their harbor fees.

Border Crossings. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends you to intercept Dalaran's supplies and learn why the Kirin Tor support Ambermill. The crates travel through Silverpine Forest toward a Dalaran camp near Pyrewood Village. Dalaran magi send wagons of supplies and arcane goods from the Hillsbrad Foothills through Silverpine Forest. Their shipments support outposts and staging grounds along the way. A camp just north of Pyrewood Village holds Dalaran personnel who watch the road. The human resistance at Ambermill is the main surviving stronghold in eastern Silverpine, and Dalaran has not left it to fend for itself.

Bottle of Disease. Forsaken alchemists brew disease near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in Ashenvale. The bottles hold virulent concoctions found at their encampment. Near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Forsaken alchemists brew contagions in an outpost beyond the Warsong Outriders' front lines. The bottles give night elves at Forest Song evidence of an offensive aimed at sickening the woodland soil and wildlife instead of meeting their sentinels in open combat.

Bottle of Moonshine. In Darkshire, a bottle of moonshine is sought for Lakeshire’s tavern. Barkeep Daniels needs one while Blackrock orc incursions keep regular supplies from reaching town. Blackrock orcs have cut off Lakeshire’s regular supply caravans. Barkeep Daniels seeks regional drinks to restock the tavern for the guards and townsfolk. One is brewed and sold at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire, where locals favor strong drinks.

Bottle of Zombie Juice. In Darkshire, a Bottle of Zombie Juice is bound for Abercrombie, a reclusive hermit in Duskwood. The potent liquor is brewed from rot blossom, and Abercrombie says he needs it to keep warm. Rot blossoms gathered in Duskwood go into this harsh brew. The bartender in Darkshire warns that it is potent enough to raise the dead. Most folk want nothing to do with such a vile drink, but Abercrombie, an eccentric hermit, says it is the only thing that keeps him warm on the damp, cold nights by his lonely shack.

Bottles and Baubles. Bottles and Baubles is a quest built around the quirky logic that because murlocs look like fish, they must think like them. Adventurers are sent to rummage through a nearby murloc camp for glittering junk and discarded trinkets that an eager angler can fashion into fishing bait. Bottles and Baubles begins with a rather unusual theory of aquatic biology: that because murlocs are fish-like beings, their minds must function just like the fish swimming in the deep. Driven by this logic, an eccentric angler posits that whatever curious oddities catch a murloc's wandering eye will surely entice a hungry fish on a hook. Scavengers are tasked with venturing into a nearby murloc camp to rummage through their hoard piles and gather shiny discarded junk to test the hypothesis.

text.enUS: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. Along Darkshore, the Bottom of Gelkak's Key is one of three fragments of a shattered winding key. It belonged to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast, and reef crawlers scavenged it from the shore. Threshadons sank Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore, casting the gnome and his belongings ashore. Among them was the winding key that activated his mechanical first mate. The key broke against the coastal rocks into three pieces, and local scavengers descended on the debris. Reef and tide crawlers seized the bottom fragment as they searched the tideline.

Bough Shadow. In northeastern Ashenvale, Bough Shadow lies east of Forest Song beneath a colossal Great Tree. Its roots surround an ancient portal into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow gathers beneath a Great Tree whose roots wind around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. The Green Dragonflight guards the quiet grove. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles patrol the swirling green portal at the tree’s base. Mortals who approach without permission are turned away.

Boulder Lode Mine. In the northeastern Barrens, the Venture Company tears into Boulder Lode Mine for its riches. Orcish banners and watchtowers mark a claim the Horde once held. Weathered orcish works frame the mine mouth, signs that the Horde once held or founded the claim. Now Venture Company overseers and enforcers answer to Boss Copperplug. The goblin syndicate strips the canyon for minerals, gems, and machinery, with little care for the land or its workers.

Boulder'gor. Boulder'gor is a rugged hill in the western Arathi Highlands, situated directly north of the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. It serves as an active encampment for the Boulderfist ogres and their unusual allies among the Witherbark forest trolls. Rising just north of the crumbling ramparts of Stromgarde Keep, Boulder'gor is a steep bluff claimed by the Boulderfist clan. Within its shadows sits the Boulderfist Outpost mound, making it a central bastion of ogre power across the highlands. Uniquely, the ogres here share their fires and fortifications with forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe, including shadowy spellcasters who lend their dark magic to the clan's brute force. This mutual cooperation poses an ongoing danger to any travelers passing along the central roads of Arathi.

Boulderfist Hall. Boulderfist Hall is a heavily fortified ogre mound nestled in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just north of Thandol Span. It serves as the local stronghold for the Boulderfist ogres, who exert their brute influence across the neighboring trade routes and valleys under the command of Kor'gresh Coldrage. Carved into the rugged southern bluffs of the Arathi Highlands, Boulderfist Hall is the principal redoubt of the Boulderfist clan in the region. Sheltered within its earthen ramparts and deep caverns, ogre brutes and magi maintain a fortified settlement mere steps from Witherbark Village and the strategic bridge at Thandol Span. Deep within the mound lurks their regional chieftain, Kor'gresh Coldrage, alongside enforcers like Phalanax. From this stronghold, the ogres project violent control over the surrounding roads, making any peaceful transit between Arathi and the Wetlands perilous for travelers and supply caravans alike.

Boulderfist Outpost. Boulderfist Outpost is a fortified mound nestled deep within the ogre settlement of Boulder'gor in the Arathi Highlands. Serving as an interior den and holding area, it houses aggressive Boulderfist ogres alongside a few Witherbark trolls. Carved into the earth and stone of western Arathi, Boulderfist Outpost functions as the heart of Boulder'gor. While brute enforcers dominate the settlement above, the outpost's interior concentrates the clan's core strength and provides a dark subterranean shelter. A handful of Witherbark troll witch doctors occasionally mingle among the ogres here, hinting at tenuous tribal cooperation.

Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide kobolds dig deep in Boulderslide Cavern, at the far end of Boulderslide Ravine. They search the stone for glowing mineral formations. Boulderslide kobolds have carved a stronghold into the Stonetalon crags. They dig frantically for resonite, a rare purple crystal embedded in the stone. Its glow carries traces of earthen magic, and the kobolds turn fiercely against anyone who approaches their excavation.

Boulderslide Ravine. Kobolds dig furiously for Resonite in Boulderslide Ravine, deep in the Stonetalon Mountains. From Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal sends Horde scouts into the caves for samples, troubled by a growing tension in the earth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal watches the Stonetalon peaks with concern. The earth feels disturbed, with an unnatural agitation rising from the southeast. In Boulderslide Ravine, kobolds have left their usual foraging to dig aggressively for Resonite, a rare mineral found beneath the surface. Mor'rogal sends Horde scouts past the kobolds and into the cave's deepest reaches to learn why they mine with such frenzy. He asks them to bring back raw samples.

Boulderslide Ravine. Along Webwinder Path, secluded Boulderslide Ravine cuts through the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. The ravine has seen little of the fighting between Horde and Alliance. Its rocky slopes lead toward Boulderslide Cavern, while wild mountain beasts still roam there. Boulderslide Ravine lies off Webwinder Path in the Stonetalon heights. Loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades elsewhere in the region, but military forces rarely disturb this narrow pass. Mountain rams and crag beasts such as Cliff Stormers roam its ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors watch the slopes, where rich mineral veins often surface along the way toward the deeper cavern network.

text.enUS: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. In Northshire, an Alliance bounty names Garrick Padfoot, a notorious local thief. Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey calls for recruits to hunt him near the vineyards. Northshire Valley once offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. As order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers.

Bounty on Murlocs. Murlocs are spreading through eastern Elwynn, and the Stormwind Army has put a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear the shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before the murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers now attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a minor nuisance has grown into a threat across eastern Elwynn, while the western roads remain comparatively secure.

Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg is an Alliance quest authorized by the Sentinels to curb the aggressive furbolg population corrupting Teldrassil. Shayla Nightbreeze recruits adventurers outside Darnassus to hunt the corrupted beasts and collect their fangs as proof of deed. On the road outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze acts on direct orders from the Sentinels to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. Once peaceful inhabitants of the ancient forests, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading corruption that stripped away their reason, turning them into vicious threats to the safety of travelers and the natural sanctity of Teldrassil.

Bracers of Binding. In Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil looks ahead to what the Magus may need next. The Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, and Bel'varil sends you to the ruins of Dalaran for four Bracers of Earth Binding. As the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Keeper Bel'varil expects another need to follow. Bracers of binding are worn on an elemental's wrists, where they bind the creature to a mage's service. Elementals wear them among the ruins of Dalaran. Bel'varil wants you to bring four Bracers of Earth Binding back to Tarren Mill.

Brackenwall Village. Brackenwall Village is the primary Horde outpost in Dustwallow Marsh, nestled among the bogs in the northwest corner of the zone. Founded by surviving Stonemaul ogres after dragons devastated their original settlement to the south, the village serves as a tenuous stronghold surrounded by Alliance spies, deserters, and the black dragonflight. When black dragonkin drove the Stonemaul ogres out of their ancient home at Stonemaul Village in the southern marsh, their leader, Overlord Mok'Morokk—successor to Rexxar—led the survivors north into the swamp to build Brackenwall. Formed around traditional earthen mounds, huts, and an old watchtower, the settlement gave the battered clan a defensible haven. Though aligned with the Horde, the village suffers from internal rot: Mok'Morokk sits idle, hoarding supplies and refusing to confront the draconic threat, leaving the clan's spiritual and tactical guidance to figures like the ogre mage Draz'Zilb and Horde emissaries.

Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Defias brigands have taken over Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in southeastern Elwynn Forest. The farm once belonged to the Brackwell family, but now its cottage and fields serve as a hideout where conspirators meet and stolen mine gold is received. You find the Brackwell farm southeast of the Stonefield homestead, its fields no longer tended. The Brackwell family has vanished, driven away or worse as crime spread through the area. The Defias Brotherhood now occupies the sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. Brigands regroup here beyond the reach of Goldshire's patrols. Morgan the Collector and other prominent conspirators use the isolated farm to receive illicit gold taken from the forest's mines.

Braelyn Firehand. At Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand lives among the Horde and draws travelers into a campaign against the night elves of Stonetalon Peak. At Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand is a blood elf living openly among tauren lodges and orcish tents. The retreat’s shamans and chieftains tolerate her, apparently unaware of her true loyalties. She calls herself an observer of the region’s magic and hires passing Horde mercenaries for dangerous work among the crags.

Braenna Flintcrag. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Braenna Flintcrag guides dwarves in the ways of the Holy Light. She trains priests in healing and spiritual discipline, and tells visiting night elf priests when they are called home to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Braenna Flintcrag trains priests in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. From the Mystic Ward, she teaches dwarven acolytes the Holy Light's healing arts and defensive wards, preparing them for a dangerous world. Her work tends the spiritual needs of Khaz Modan, amid a city renowned for its forges and warriors.

Brainwashed Noble. Deep in the caverns outside the Deadmines, Brainwashed Noble remains captive under Defias control. Magical manipulation has stripped him of his will, and he serves the Brotherhood alongside undead minions instead of walking Stormwind's grand halls.

Brambleblade Ravine. Bristleback quilboar raid Camp Narache from Brambleblade Ravine, cut into Red Cloud Mesa’s northeastern edge. Young tauren braves enter the ravine to defend their homeland and prove their strength. Brambleblade Ravine cuts into Red Cloud Mesa’s northeastern edge, its thorny briars and quilboar camps guarding the Bristleback tribe. From this den, the Bristlebacks raid Camp Narache and threaten young tauren coming of age. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the shamans and warriors who dwell deep in the ravine with trained battleboars. For the Shu'halo, striking into the canyon is both a rite of passage and a hard need if the plains are to be safe.

Bramblescar. Across the southern Barrens, Bramblescar's Razormane wage war with the Bristleback across the Gold Road. Thick brambles fortify their settlement. Bramblescar is carved into the jagged briars of the southern Barrens. The thick, sharp thorns make a vital redoubt for the Razormane quilboar and deter casual wanderers. The tribe is fiercely territorial and hostile to outsiders. They skirmish with anyone who approaches, treating all who are not quilboar as intruders on land blessed by their ancient boar gods.

Branch of Cenarius. In eastern Ashenvale, Geltharis holds the Branch of Cenarius, sacred to the dryads. Anilia died defending the relic, and her dying wish was to see it recovered. The Branch of Cenarius is sacred to the dryads who follow the Forest Lord. Anilia and her sister Illiyana treasured it until corrupt satyrs ambushed them. Their leader, Geltharis, seized the branch and mortally wounded Anilia near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. As she lay dying, Anilia pointed north toward the arch where Geltharis lurks. She pleaded for a champion to take back the bough and return it to the dryads at Forest Song.

Brandur Ironhammer. In Ironforge, Brandur Ironhammer guides young paladins in the Holy Light and sends them across the Alliance. In the Hall of Mysteries, Brandur Ironhammer trains novice paladins in the ways of the Holy Light. He and Tiza Battleforge watch over young dwarven champions as they face the trials of the Tome of Divinity. Tiza has spoken frankly about Brandur’s personal flaws. He works to master his envy and keep the inner purity expected of a warrior of the Light.

Brann Bronzebeard. Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni and Muradin, who is believed dead, renowned throughout Azeroth as a peerless explorer, archaeologist, and founding leader of the Explorers' League. Driven by an insatiable curiosity for titan ruins and ancient history, his wanderlust has led him deep into the deadly wastes of Silithus. His field companions in southern Silithus await news of his latest expedition. While his eldest brother Magni rules Ironforge from the throne and Muradin served on battlefield frontlines, Brann took to the open wilds. He was a veteran warrior of the Second War. Yet peacetime turned his formidable constitution toward uncovering the forgotten past. As a leader of the Explorers' League, Brann charted vast swathes of the Eastern Kingdoms—from Elwynn Forest to the untamed jungles of Zul'Gurub—before turning his gaze across the Great Sea to the mysteries of ancient Kalimdor.

Branstock Khalder. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder trains dwarven priests in the Holy Light and watches the trogg threat beyond the outpost. At Anvilmar, Branstock Khalder guides aspiring priests through their first prayers and sacred runes. This easy-going dwarf is devoted to the Light, yet keeps watch on the growing trogg threat to the local mountaineers. When a novice has learned enough of the Light, Branstock sends them through Coldridge Pass to Kharanos for further guidance from his superior, Father Maxan Anvol.

Brass Collar. At the Brackwell pumpkin patch, Princess wears a brass collar that Ma Stonefield wants as proof the sow is gone. Princess is a huge, prize-winning sow owned by the Brackwell family. She roams their pumpkin patch east of the Maclure homestead, and her appetite leads her into the Stonefield Farm’s crops. After losing valuable vegetables to the sow, Ma Stonefield seeks someone willing to slay her. Princess wears a brass band around her neck, and the collar proves she will not raid the Stonefield fields again.

Brave Moonhorn. Brave Moonhorn is a tauren scout stationed at the top of the Great Lift on the southern border of the Barrens. From this precipice, he keeps watch over the entry to Thousand Needles and alerts travelers to the local dangers ahead. Perched above the sheer drops of Thousand Needles, Brave Moonhorn stands guard where the northern plains meet the canyonlands. His primary role is keeping watchful eyes on regional threats moving through the canyon floor below, particularly the hostile centaur clans. Anyone looking to descend into the needles often crosses paths with him first, receiving crucial warnings before they step onto the massive platforms of the Great Lift.

Break Sharptusk!. Brave Windfeather sends you east from Red Cloud Mesa to face the raids on Mulgore. Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine, and his death could strike a hard blow against their attacks. Red Cloud Mesa is home to young tauren learning the hunt and the ways of the Earth Mother. East of the mesa, Brambleblade Ravine lies in the hands of the Bristleback quilboar. They see the tauren as invaders taking sacred ground, and their skirmishes threaten the tribes trying to make a stable home in Mulgore.

Break a Few Eggs. Break a Few Eggs is an errand assisting a harried cook who must keep up with endless meal preparations. Securing fresh, fragile ingredients without breaking them keeps the kitchen running and the cooking on schedule. Feeding a crowd is an exhausting, never-ending endeavor. Between breakfast, lunch, and dinner, there is scarcely any time to step away from the stove, let alone leave the kitchen to scrounge for raw provisions. In Break a Few Eggs, a hard-pressed cook turns to passing adventurers to secure fresh eggs before the next meal service falls behind.

Breaking the Keystone. Once the Stones of Binding were opened, much of the voice's confinement eased, yet a lock still holds it. That lock is the Keystone among a ring of stones, and the stone watcher Fozruk, one of the voice's captors, holds the key, known to the watchers as the Rod of Order. With the Stones of Binding opened, the voice's confinement has eased a great deal, but one lock remains: the Keystone, among the circle of stones around you. Its key is held by a captor, the stone watcher Fozruk, and the watchers call it the Rod of Order. Taking the rod from Fozruk and carrying it to the Keystone is how the lock will open. The voice promises that its gratitude, if you manage this, will shake the earth to its roots. The Keystone itself is charged with immense geomantic energy.

Brewer's Trade. In Hillsbrad, a case of Fallrook Varietal is bound for Dun Garok. The brew-kin there miss the Fallrook family's vineyards, and a sack of Homebrew Hops comes back in trade. The Fallrook cellars still hold cases of wine, though most of its best bottled years are long gone. The Dun Garok brew-kin miss the family's vineyards too, and a trade has been arranged with them.

Brewmaster Drohn. Above Ratchet's docks, Brewmaster Drohn tends his brewing craft. The orc lives just uphill from the port, making potent drinks with methods tied to the wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout. Travelers who find discarded kegs across Kalimdor are sent to Drohn's porch. Brewmaster Drohn brews from his home on the hill above Ratchet's goblin docks. Rather than devote himself to combat, the orc has given his craft to brewing. He lives peacefully in the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While many orcs favor coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn works with rare ingredients, carefully balanced flavors, and methods seldom practiced among his kin.

Brewmeister Bilger. Brewmeister Bilger waits in Southshore's inn cellar for deliveries from distant lands. The intoxicated dwarf passes his hours tasting potent spirits. Brewmeister Bilger paces the cellar beneath Southshore's inn, nursing hiccups as he seeks the strongest brews Azeroth can offer.

Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village sits in Chill Breeze Valley, near the entrance to Gnomeregan. The Barleybrew family keeps this dwarven camp for brewing experiments and defense against wild beasts. Brewnall Village shelters the Barleybrew clan in Chill Breeze Valley, among the gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The dwarven brewers work to perfect old recipes and make the finest stout. Tents and brewing gear fill the camp, with no permanent stone buildings. The Barleybrews test new ales while wolves and bears threaten the valley. Wandering mountaineers help gather rare ingredients and keep the area safe.

Bride of the Embalmer. In Darkshire, Lord Ello Ebonlocke sends you to find Eliza's grave. The town has learned that the Embalmer is real, and you are to take his living heart from her cursed remains to strip him of his power. Duskwood's children grew up hearing a tale of the Embalmer. He was said to be a kindly alchemist, driven mad when his beloved wife, Eliza, died. Desperate to cheat death, he turned to sorcery, cut out his own beating heart, and placed it in her chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke once dismissed the story as village folklore. Recent discoveries have shown that the Embalmer walks among the living, and his work festers beneath the graveyard dirt.

Brightwater Lake. Brightwater Lake is the largest body of water in Tirisfal Glades, stretching across the mist-shrouded lowlands northeast of Brill. Once a tranquil retreat for the kingdom of Lordaeron, its waters now lie cold and dark, surrounding a central isle where an outcast necromancer conducts his forbidden research. Spanning the northern plains between the town of Brill and the Scarlet Watch Post, Brightwater Lake is a quiet and eerie landmark in the heart of Tirisfal. In the peaceful centuries under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, the lake served as a scenic country haven. Today, like the rest of the glades, its pristine character is long gone. The Plaguelands lie not far to the east, and the murky, chilled waters reflect only grey skies, withered trees, and the constant threat of roving murlocs and hostile undead.

Brightwood Grove. West of Darkshire, Brightwood Grove's ruined farms shelter savage Nightbane worgen. Brightwood Grove lies within sight of Darkshire, where ruined farms and fences mark the town's edge. Nightbane worgen have made crude camps among the overgrown clearings and prowl close to town. Their presence threatens Darkshire, so the Night Watch and travelers passing through keep their numbers down to protect the settlement.

Brill. Brill is the primary Forsaken settlement in the heart of Tirisfal Glades, situated just north of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a prosperous human town, it now serves as the administrative and military hub for newly awakened undead stepping beyond the confines of Deathknell. Before the Third War, Brill was a lively village under the sway of regional nobles such as the Barov and Agamand families. That prosperity ended when Kel'Thuzad chose the area for the Cult of the Damned's earliest experiments with the Plague of Undeath. The devastating blight swept through the population so quickly that local militia were driven out, leaving a sprawling mass graveyard in its wake. Now rebuilt by the Forsaken under the leadership of Magistrate Sevren, the town retains its weathered Lordaeron architecture beneath an atmosphere of grim purpose. Brill functions as the regional command center, coordinating defenses against Scarlet Crusade incursions, roaming Scourge remnants, and native beasts warped by necromantic decay.

Brill Town Hall. Brill Town Hall anchors Forsaken rule in the shattered heart of Lordaeron. From its doors, the undead govern Brill and coordinate the defense of Tirisfal Glades. Brill Town Hall remains open under Forsaken rule while much of Lordaeron lies in ruins. Magistrate Sevren directs town affairs from his podium, issuing orders to Forsaken travelers. Beyond the Defiler's Den in the Arathi Highlands, few recognized town halls in the known world remain active under Forsaken control. Brill’s hall carries on Lordaeron’s old civic order beneath undead rule.

Brine. On Blackthorn Ridge, Brine guides shaman initiates toward the spirits of water. This orc shaman teaches them to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Brine lives on a hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, far from the Barrens' trading posts. Though dry savannas surround her, she has devoted her life to understanding water. Shaman across the Horde seek her wisdom after mastering earth and fire. She teaches that water calls for patience and perspective, qualities few understand as deeply as she does.

Bring Back the Mug. Durnan Furcutter sends you back across Coldridge Valley with Nori Pridedrift's empty mug. Returning it brings the Mornbrew delivery to a close. Durnan Furcutter has finished warming himself with the Mornbrew you delivered across Dun Morogh's snowdrifts. Now he sends you back with the empty tankard. In the biting cold, dwarven hospitality depends on mutual respect, and good dishware must not be left behind.

name.zhCN: 刺背野猪人的进攻计划

text.enUS: Bristleback Attack Plans. Bristleback Attack Plans warn of a planned siege on Camp Narache. Quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine drew crude maps and tactical notes for an assault meant to overrun the tauren settlement. The Bristleback quilboar plan a sustained assault on Camp Narache. Their leadership means to push beyond skirmishes along the borders of the Red Cloud Mesa and wipe out the young tauren training there. The plans lie deep within a dirt cave in Brambleblade Ravine. Chief Hawkwind can send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements, giving Camp Narache a chance to blunt the invasion before it begins.

Bristleback Belt. In Camp Narache, young tauren gather Bristleback Belts to prove their valor. The belts come from quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine and mark a step in the Rite of Strength. The Red Cloud tribe tests youths who seek respect in Thunder Bluff through the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. The first trial, the Rite of Strength, asks each initiate to protect the tribe from threats. Bristleback quilboar raid food supplies and ambush hunting parties outside Camp Narache. Chief Hawkwind demands their belts in return. Bringing him twelve proves an initiate can face danger and help defend the tribe.

Bristleback Quilboar Tusk. Across the northern and central Barrens, Bristleback Quilboar Tusks are taken from slain quilboar. Mankrik gathers them as proof of slaughter and tokens of vengeance. Bristleback quilboar defend their territory across the Barrens against Horde expansion. Their jagged ivory tusks serve as weapons in close combat. Mankrik, a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads, lost his wife in a vicious quilboar ambush. He gathers dozens of tusks as retribution, a bloody count of the suffering he means to return to the Bristlebacks.

Brock Stoneseeker. Brock Stoneseeker teaches mining in Thelsamar, in Loch Modan. At Brock's School of Mining and Surveying, he trains novice prospectors to extract ores and minerals. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker teaches miners at Brock's School of Mining and Surveying. Loch Modan's hills hold rich mineral veins, and miners need skill with a pickaxe and an eye for the rock. Brock teaches the basics of finding ore, extracting raw metals, and surveying underground deposits. His lessons help Alliance tradesfolk supply Ironforge's smithies.

Brock's List. Brock's List carries the names of mining pupils honored by the guild halls in Ironforge. Brock Stoneseeker, the mining instructor in Thelsamar, compiles the dispatch for students who earn honorary picks. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker records the mining pupils who prove their skill. Apprentices must show what they can do before taking on serious work in Khaz Modan's veins. The honored students earn picks from the guild halls in Ironforge, marks of their skill as miners.

Broken Alliances. In Kargath, Gorn wants the Horde's honor restored after its alliance with Deathwing. The ogre Boss Tho'grun, hired to help get the Sign of the Earth, turned on the Horde and kept it for himself, and you are to take it back at Camp Boff. During the Second War the Horde stood with the dragon Deathwing. Blacklash and Hematus, a pair of his lieutenants, ended up locked away in Lethlor Ravine, far off to the east. Gorn holds that these depraved allies of old must be silenced if the Horde's honor is to be restored. To open the drakes' prison the Horde needed the Sign of the Earth, and hired ogre mercenaries under Boss Tho'grun to help find it. Tho'grun turned on them, overwhelmed them and kept it for himself.

Broken Alliances. Gorn sends you to Lethlor Ravine in the far eastern Badlands, where the black drakes Blacklash and Hematus lie bound by the Seal of the Earth. This follows the first Broken Alliances. Three runestones keep the Seal of the Earth closed. Each rests in a pillar of Lethlor Ravine: Diamond, Opal and Amethyst. The Sign of the Earth, which Gorn gives you, draws the stones out and opens the seal. Countless drakes make their home in the ravine, and Blacklash and Hematus are formidable. Gorn wants both dead, and their bindings brought back.

Broken Hall. The Broken Hall serves as the flooded outer threshold of the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Shattered when the Great Dragon Aspect Ysera and her flight dragged the grand ziggurat beneath the waters, this ruin now stands deserted as the Atal'ai zealots retreat into deeper sanctums. When the green dragons brought down their wrath upon the Atal'ai priesthood and submerged their unholy ziggurat beneath the Pool of Tears, the outermost architecture bore the brunt of the cataclysm. The floor of the Broken Hall collapsed completely, allowing murky swamp waters to flood the chamber. Because of the damage and submersion, the troll cultists abandoned this entrance hall, withdrawing further into the complex. Adventurers entering the sunken temple must wade through these sodden ruins before mounting the stairs to reach the Hall of Masks.

Broken Pillar. The Broken Pillar is a weathered cluster of ancient troll ruins jutting from the dunes south of Gadgetzan. It serves as an isolated research post for the goblin prospector and scientist Marvon Rivetseeker, who studies the enigmatic artifacts buried beneath the surrounding sands. Rising out of the sands south of Gadgetzan and east of the treacherous Abyssal Sands, the Broken Pillar marks the remnants of ancient troll architecture long swallowed by Tanaris. Despite the desolate surroundings and encroaching desert beasts, the site offers rare clues to the continent's prehistoric civilisations. Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin researcher originally based out of Ratchet, has established a lonely camp beside the shattered stonework to examine curious relics known as Gahz'ridian scattered across the waste.
