text.enUS: Broken Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, a broken samophlange draws the notice of curious engineers. Its gears and shifting parts hint at a purpose no one has uncovered. The broken samophlange is a baffling contraption from the northern Barrens. Its moving assemblies and fine gears show careful workmanship, even in ruin. Sputtervalve, a goblin in Ratchet, damaged the delicate device by accident before anyone could document how it worked. The finder hoped to send working results to curious colleagues in Undermine, so they sought someone able to repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket, a clever tinkerer near the border outpost of Mor'shan Rampart, was the one they turned to.

Broken Tears. Warug says the Gelkis foolishly believe the centaur mother, Theradras, protects them. He sends you into the cave in their village to destroy the crystals they hoard there, the tears of Theradras, and bring him three of the broken pieces. Warug scorns the Gelkis for trusting Theradras, mother of the centaur, to protect them. To him no one protects the centaur, and the Magram, being the strongest, need no protection. He sends you to the cave in the Gelkis village, where they keep a hoard of crystals called the tears of Theradras. Smash them and bring Warug three broken pieces. He will only trust you with this if you are no enemy of the Magram.

Broken Tools. At the dig northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven picks lie broken on the forge. Baine Bloodhoof wants proof that the excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has been stopped. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators dig into Mulgore's hills in search of ancient history. The tauren see their work as a defilement of the Earth Mother. The digging's noise and destruction agitate the local wildlife, especially the roaming kodo herds. Young Baine Bloodhoof orders defenders to take the prospectors' iron picks and break them at a forge. With their picks ruined, the expedition cannot gouge further into the earth.

name.zhCN: 破碎的主动式负载平衡器

text.enUS: Broken and Battered Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, Venture Company machinery lies battered after a failed inspection. The damaged samophlange must reach goblin experts in Orgrimmar, where someone may understand how it works. The Venture Company made samophlanges for its resource work in the northern Barrens. Wenikee Boltbucket tried to inspect and modify one, adding gauges, levers, and dials to measure its stability. Her tinkering weakened the mechanism instead, leaving it battered and close to ruin. Knowing more additions might make it fail completely, she sent the fragile device to someone with factory experience.

Bromos Grummner. In Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner trains young dwarven paladins in the Holy Light. He teaches steadfast faith and the bond between dwarves and humans in the Knights of the Silver Hand. In Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner welcomes dwarven novices to the discipline of the Holy Light. He teaches young paladins their martial rites and sacred invocations. Beyond combat, Bromos urges unity. The Knights of the Silver Hand bring Ironforge and the human kingdoms of the Alliance together in a shared righteous purpose.

Bronzebeard Encampment. Bronzebeard Encampment is a rugged dwarven outpost perched in southern Silithus, just east of the massive Scarab Wall. Staffed by hardy explorers and researchers from the Explorer's League, the camp serves as an operational base for investigating ancient silithid glyphs and the lingering mysteries buried beneath the desert sands. Positioned against the desolate southern bluffs of Silithus, Bronzebeard Encampment offers a rare refuge of dwarven grit in an otherwise hostile wasteland. Founded under the auspices of Ironforge's archaeological pursuits, the camp sits within sight of the towering Scarab Wall. Here, researchers like Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge braved scorching heat, scorpids, and encroaching silithid swarms to study the peculiar inscriptions and monuments left behind by forgotten civilizations.

Bronzebeard clan. The Bronzebeard clan is the ruling dwarven royal line and dominant population of Ironforge. Following their victory in the ancient War of the Three Hammers, they forged strong ties with humanity and the gnomes, standing today under King Magni Bronzebeard as a cornerstone of the Alliance. Long ago, dwarven society in Ironforge flourished under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died of old age roughly 230 years ago, simmering rivalries erupted into civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded the traditional garrison and largest standing army within Ironforge, successfully driving both the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from under the mountain. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan mounted an assault to reconquer Khaz Modan, Madoran Bronzebeard led his clan in a decisive campaign that shattered the Dark Iron host, solidifying Bronzebeard supremacy over Ironforge.

Bronzebeard the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bronzebeard the Elder in Ironforge. His greeting offers wisdom and a token of esteem. The people of Khaz Modan revere their forebears and their long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with travelers who honor the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard embodies the Bronzebeard clan’s stalwart resilience. When travelers come to pay their respects, he is quietly pleased that the people still honor the lineage of the old races.

Brother Anton. Brother Crowley speaks of Brother Anton, a fellow warrior who learned of undead in distant Kalimdor and booked passage at once to destroy them. Anton is looking for people with bravery and resolve, and waits in Nijel's Point in Desolace. Brother Crowley says rumors of an undead infestation in Desolace, a land in far-off Kalimdor, reached Anton, who immediately booked passage to seek and destroy the menace. Anton wants help from those with bravery and resolve. If your heart is true, Crowley tells you to speak with Anton in Nijel's Point, the Alliance town in Desolace.

Brother Joshua. In Stormwind, Brother Joshua guides those who come to the Cathedral of Light to learn the ways of the Holy Light. He trains novice priests to heal wounds and strengthen their allies. Brother Joshua waits near the main altar in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, ready to teach new servants of the faith. A priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he instructs them in healing, protective wards, and the focus needed to commune with the Light. Young human priests beginning their service to the Alliance find one of their first guides in him.

Brother Kristoff. In Stormwind's Cathedral Square, Brother Kristoff preaches beneath Uther's statue. A human priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he stands outdoors near the great statue of Uther the Lightbringer and seeks practical books for sermons on spiritual strength. Brother Kristoff serves the Church of the Holy Light in Cathedral Square, beneath the statue of Uther the Lightbringer. He works among the citizens and pilgrims who pass through the plaza, rather than remaining within the Cathedral of Light. For sermons such as the Fortitude of the Spirit, he turns to worldly comparisons. In The Stresses of Iron, he finds a way to explain how the mortal soul endures pressure, comparing the Holy Light's gift of inner resolve to the tempered strength of worked metal.

Brother Neals. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Neals keeps watch over the food and drink stores. He oversees shipments and samples wine from the local vineyard. Brother Neals keeps Northshire Abbey supplied with food and drink from his rooms in the upper belfry. He follows the grape manifests from the Northshire vineyards and tastes the wine to check its quality. He also watches the shipments arriving from the fields around the valley.

Brother Paxton. At Stormwind's royal archives, Milton Sheaf sends you to Northshire Abbey for a missing dwarven treatise. The book was loaned months ago for copying, but has not returned to the city shelves. Stormwind's head librarian, Milton Sheaf, has a missing book on his hands. 'The Stresses of Iron,' a treatise on metallurgical techniques by dwarven prospector Margulf Blaggon, is gone from the capital's shelves. The book was loaned months ago to the clerics of Northshire Abbey so they could copy it. It was not misplaced in Stormwind.

Brother Sarno. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City, Brother Sarno welcomes visitors and worshipers. The human cleric also directs Alliance travelers to Ironforge, where Tinkmaster Overspark needs help reclaiming Gnomeregan. Inside the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, Brother Sarno greets pilgrims and travelers at the entrance. A brother of the Church of the Holy Light, he welcomes those who come seeking prayer, comfort, or guidance. His kind manner puts visitors at ease amid the cathedral’s daily life.

Brother Wilhelm. Behind Goldshire's blacksmith, Brother Wilhelm trains young paladins in the Holy Light. He guides them as they leave Northshire Abbey and take their first steps into Elwynn Forest. Brother Wilhelm trains new paladins behind Goldshire's smithy. Northshire Valley shelters those who begin their path in the Light, but many seek his guidance when they enter the wider forest. He teaches them their sacred duties as they leave the abbey and take up the work of protecting the realm.

Brotherhood of Northshire. The Brotherhood of Northshire is a holy human clerical order dedicated to the Church of the Holy Light, based out of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. Originally known as the Clerics of Northshire, the order suffered catastrophic losses during the First War before being reformed under Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Today, the Brotherhood serves as both a spiritual sanctuary and the primary training ground for fledgling Alliance defenders. Centuries ago, pious missionaries traveled south from Lordaeron into the kingdom of Stormwind, establishing Northshire Abbey to minister to the people and soothe the realm through the Holy Light. Originally known as the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, their compassion was legendary—they even tended to injured gnolls and jungle trolls during past border wars. When the Orcish Horde crossed through the Dark Portal, the clerics marched bravely to the front lines without armor or weapons to heal fallen soldiers. Because their healing sustained the Stormwind Army, the orcs ruthlessly targeted them. The order was decimated, the abbey was ransacked and burned, and the surviving clerics were forced to flee north across the sea to Southshore with Sir Anduin Lothar.

Brotherhood of Thieves. Deputy Willem sends recruits across Northshire's eastern river to face the Defias Brotherhood. Their red burlap bandanas give Stormwind its first tangible evidence of the brigands' organized presence in the valley. Northshire Valley has long been a safe haven in Elwynn Forest, guarded by Stormwind and used to train recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light. Recently, discipline along its perimeter has frayed. Vagrants and thieves have crossed the eastern river, lurking near the woods and making small camps close to the abbey. Deputy Willem maintains local order, but the guards cannot spare the manpower to watch every corner of the valley without volunteers.

Brotherhood's End. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Gregor Lescovar's killing leaves dangerous questions behind. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston and warns you to keep the killer's identity quiet. Baros Alexston, the City Architect who helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, is relieved to hear that Lescovar is dead. Edwin VanCleef had marked Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort for vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat to the kingdom's architects and nobility has passed.

Browman Mill. Browman Mill is a blighted lumber mill situated just north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron's timber trade, it now swarms with undead minions under the iron grip of the Scourge. Its former proprietor, Stephen Browman, remains trapped in death within his ruined workshop. Before the Third War, Browman Mill served the surrounding towns and homesteads of Lordaeron, processing lumber harvested from the rich forests of the Eastweald. When the Scourge plague rolled across the kingdom, the mill fell alongside the rest of the province. Today, rotting timbers and shattered wheels sit idle while abominations, banshees, and skeletal warriors patrol the perimeter. Its close proximity to Light's Hope Chapel makes it a constant and menacing reminder of the undead horde pressing against the Argent Dawn's doorstep.

Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle prowls the riot-torn halls of the Stormwind Stockade. The dangerous dwarf is a powerful brawler, and anyone trying to restore order may meet his fists. Bruegal Ironknuckle roams the Stormwind Stockade during its open revolt. The dangerous dwarf is known for his brutal brawling strength. Many of the city's most volatile cutthroats have seized the underground cellblocks, and Bruegal is among them. He does not stay in one cell, but prowls the riot-torn halls, ready to bash anyone trying to quell the uprising.

Brutal Armor. A warrior in the northern Barrens faces Thun'grim Firegaze's test. The near-blind smith sends seasoned Horde warriors across distant lands for rare ingredients and smelting agents. Fulfilling his scroll begins the forging of a full set of brutal battle gear. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze listens for news of war. The veteran orc smith's eyesight is failing, but his skill at the forge remains unmatched. Rumors reach him of a warrior whose strength and valor exceed those of ordinary soldiers. Thun'grim sets out to craft mail that can withstand the fiercest battles across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms.

Brutal Gauntlets. Ula'elek has finished a pair of Brutal Gauntlets for a seasoned Horde warrior. Rare materials gathered across distant lands have gone into the work, meant to honor both maker and bearer. Ula'elek brings his lineage and skill to the forging of armor for a seasoned frontline warrior. In Durotar, the Horde craftsman shapes brutal gauntlets from hardened trophies taken from dangerous foes. The finished armor is made to withstand fierce blows and strengthen the wearer's attacks.

Brutal Hauberk. Across the Barrens, Horde warriors face a trial before Thun'grim Firegaze will forge their mail. They gather rare materials and prove themselves against dangerous foes across the lands, then bring their bounty to the reclusive smith. He hammers it into armor built for battle. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze forges armor only for warriors who meet his demands. The reclusive orc sends them far and wide to gather tough beast parts, rare metal, and alchemical reagents before he lights his bellows. The finished hauberk offers protection and marks the endurance and grit its wearer has shown, earning recognition from veteran fighters throughout the Horde.

Brutal Helm. Brutal Helm marks the culmination of an arduous warrior trial overseen by Orm Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff. Having collected rare beast trophies across Kalimdor, an aspiring warrior is recognized with a formidable horned helm as a testament to their strength. Orm Stonehoof serves as a stern smith in Thunder Bluff, guiding Horde warriors through grueling rites of passage. These trials demand proof of martial capability, pushing initiates into treacherous territory to hunt ferocious creatures and claim rare trophies. Only those who have met Orm's exacting standards are granted audience for the completion of their armor.

Brutal Politics. Captain Pentigast believes whichever centaur clan wins the wars of Desolace will spill out and threaten the Alliance strongholds. To learn how to beat them, Pentigast wants an alliance with one clan: fight the Gelkis, win over the Magram, and speak with Warug. War rages across Desolace, centaur against centaur, and the Alliance believes the winner will spill out against its strongholds. That cannot be allowed. To learn how to beat the centaurs, Captain Pentigast says, the Alliance needs one of the clans as a friend.

Bugged. Bugged is a quest in Valanaar where an influx of seasonal lowland insects turns out to be an espionage plot. High Order mages discovered that local cultists are weaving listening charms onto skyhoppers to spy on the settlement, requiring an extermination effort to weed out the enchanted pests. During skyhopper season in the lowlands, swarms of native insects surge around the city of Valanaar. While usually regarded merely as a seasonal annoyance, an inspection by High Order mages revealed that several slain specimens carried sophisticated listening enchantments. A local cult has weaponized the insect swarm, transforming common lowland pests into inconspicuous surveillance tools to eavesdrop on the city.

Bulwark. The Bulwark is a fortified outpost straddling the border between Tirisfal Glades and the Western Plaguelands. Maintained jointly by the Forsaken and the neutral Argent Dawn, it serves as the Horde's front line against the Scourge and the primary launching point for expeditions into the tainted east. Positioned squarely on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades, the Bulwark is the final barrier protecting the Forsaken heartland from the blighted horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Today, rough wooden palisades and heavily armed guards defend the pass against roaming undead. It represents an uneasy but necessary collaboration, where Forsaken forces coordinate alongside the Argent Dawn to recruit seasoned champions of the Horde, turning back the minions of the Lich King before they spill into Tirisfal.

Bundle of Crocolisk Skins. In the Wetlands, hunters prepare crocolisk skins for Menethil Harbor. The hides are valuable trade goods for local leatherworkers. Crocolisk hides are an essential trade good for coastal Menethil Harbor. Hunters gather and cure the tough, water-resistant skins in the Wetlands before sending them west to artisans such as James Halloran. Einar has gathered this bundle, but asks a traveler to carry it into town. He wants to avoid returning home to face the temper of his frustrated wife, Sida.

Bundle of Hides. Across the Barrens, a Bundle of Hides travels toward Thunder Bluff with the Horde’s wind riders. The cured skins are a straightforward courier shipment for the leatherworkers, and their delivery introduces travelers to the wind rider network. Hunters skin the beasts of the Barrens for cured hides. The plains hold vast herds of kodo, prowling lions, and roving raptors. These skins supply the leatherworkers of Thunder Bluff, who turn them into gear, pouches, armor, and bindings for the Horde.

Bundle of Wood. Near Eastvale Logging Camp, Bundle of Wood waits in the trees for an urgent shipment west. Freshly chopped timber from Eastvale Logging Camp helps supply the Kingdom of Stormwind. The camp sends wood west for town buildings and other construction. Bears and wolves have pushed into the groves northwest of camp, and terrified loggers fled, leaving their freshly gathered Bundles of Wood among the trees. With delivery deadlines close, overseer Raelen needs travelers to pass the predators and recover the timber before the lumber contracts are breached.

Bungle in the Jungle. Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan has studied the silithid and likens them to bees, with the queen as the weak point. A lure must draw her out, and it calls for a scent gland and soil from Un'Goro Crater, to the west. Pestlezugg's research compares the silithid to bees. Destroy the hive's queen, and the rest should be thrown into disarray. A lure will be brewed to bring the queen out, and once she is summoned, you are the one to take her down.

Burning Blade Coven. In the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade Coven threatens the Horde’s newest recruits. Corrupted cultists and summoned demons haunt the old mineral caves, using them as a staging ground for dark magic on Durotar’s doorstep. Dark rituals now trouble the caves along the Valley of Trials’ northern edge. Imps and lesser fiends spill from the cavern mouth, stirring chaos and threatening the young orcs and Darkspear trolls who train here for service to the Horde. The Burning Blade cult has entrenched itself deep inside, led by the shadowy warlock Yarrog Baneshadow. What was a testing wilderness is now an active battleground against demonic corruption.

Burning Blade Medallion. Cultists in the Valley of Trials carry the Burning Blade Medallion. Yarrog Baneshadow holds it deep in the Burning Blade Coven, where its dark magic threatens Durotar's young warriors. Zureetha Fargaze's divinations point to the medallion in the Burning Blade Coven. Yarrog Baneshadow, an agent of the Burning Blade cult, carries it deep inside the winding caverns. The trinket channels dark power among the cult's impish familiars and felstalkers. Defeating Yarrog and taking the medallion ends the cult's attempt to undermine the Horde's training grounds from within Durotar.

Burning Blade Medallion. Zureetha Fargaze sends young Horde initiates into the Burning Blade Coven cave in the Valley of Trials. They face a hidden cultist and seek a dark relic, the Burning Blade Medallion. Its presence points to demonic corruption taking root near the Horde. Young orcs and trolls face trials of combat and survival in the Valley of Trials, while a menace gathers nearby. The warlock Zureetha Fargaze senses through divination that the vile familiars on the northern bluffs are only the vanguard of a darker presence. Deep in a nearby cavern, the Burning Blade cult has made a hidden coven, where its followers practice dark arts and keep dangerous relics of demonic power.

Burning Blade clan. Once an ancient orcish clan renowned for its deadly blademasters and consumed by chaotic frenzy during the early wars, the Burning Blade now largely persists as a sinister demon-worshiping cult. Its acolytes infiltrate Durotar and the Barrens, pursuing dark agendas whispered to be guided by hidden masters. Meanwhile, a handful of honorable blademasters have forsaken its demonic corruption to serve Warchief Thrall in the New Horde. Originating in the lands of Draenor alongside clans like the Warsong, the Burning Blade were long respected for the lethal tradition of their blademasters. When they drank the blood of Mannoroth and marched through the Dark Portal into Azeroth during the First War, however, the clan fractured mentally. By the Second War, they were scarcely an organized society, behaving instead like a berserk force of nature. Nomadic and demented, they threw themselves into battle with total disregard for survival, requiring ogres to hold them in check until unleashed. Ultimately, their numbers were battered and routed near the Dark Portal by the Alliance.

Burning Blood. In Stormwind, Grimand Elmore turns to Furen Longbeard’s smithing methods. He needs burning blood and a burning rock from Duskwood to test the armorcrafting technique himself. Grimand Elmore is one of the Alliance’s accomplished armorers, and he rarely accepts that another smith might surpass his methods. Hearing of Furen Longbeard’s unusual smithing discoveries stirs his professional curiosity. Grimand agrees to test Furen’s methods by making a piece of armor. He needs strange, volatile components from the dark reaches of the south to quench and temper the metal to his exact requirements; ordinary water and common coals will not do.

Burning Blood (quest item). In Duskwood, Burning Blood is gathered from the Nightbane worgen. Grimand Elmore needs twenty vials for experiments in smithing. Nightbane worgen prowl Duskwood with a strange fury, and their blood burns with real heat. The fluid can be drawn from worgen haunting the timberlands and Roland's Doom. Though foul to gather, its heat draws the interest of armorers seeking to temper resilient plate.

Burning Legion. The Burning Legion is an infinite, apocalyptic host of demons led by the fallen titan Sargeras, dedicated to scouring all life from creation. Having already shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the demons remain Azeroth's most relentless nemesis, orchestrating the corruption of the orcs and the horrors of the Third War. Long ago, Sargeras stood as the champion of the titans, tasked with hunting down and imprisoning the demons that plagued the cosmos. Over countless ages of battling their evil, he grew disillusioned and concluded that creation itself was fatally flawed and must be unmade in flame. To enact his crusade, he freed the demons he had imprisoned, bending them to his will through fel magic. He augmented their chaos with the intellect of the corrupted eredar—elevating Archimonde and Kil'jaeden as his chief lieutenants—and forged an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation.

Burning Rock. In Duskwood, Burning Rock smolders in the depths of Roland's Doom. Gutspill, leader of the Nightbane worgen, carries it, and Grimand Elmore in Stormwind needs it with fiery worgen blood to forge enchanted armor for promising warriors. Gutspill carries Burning Rock through the shafts of Roland's Doom. Grimand Elmore in Stormwind wants its heat for armor made with fiery worgen blood. He is testing smithing techniques developed by his peer Furen Longbeard, to make tough plates for veteran fighters.

Burning Shadows. Recovered from the Burning Blade cultist Gazz'uz in the depths of Skull Rock, this mysterious glowing pendant whispers urgent warnings into the bearer's mind. The voice specifically threatens Gazz'uz with the wrath of Neeru Fireblade, an orc warlock residing in Orgrimmar. Upon slaying Gazz'uz deep within Skull Rock, an ominous pendant known as the Eye of Burning Shadow is retrieved from his remains. Rather than being an inert magical trinket, the stone vibrates with psychic communication. A demanding voice speaks directly into the mind of anyone holding it, demanding reports from Gazz'uz and warning him that his clandestine operations east of Orgrimmar have been compromised.

Business in Auberdine. Borgus Steelhand seeks news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. The dwarven merchant asks travelers sailing west to check on Gorbold, who recently began trading in the night elven port. Their route links Stormwind Harbor with the shores of northern Kalimdor. Borgus Steelhand trusts his family's name among traders. His brother, Gorbold Steelhand, crossed the Great Sea recently to work a merchant stall in Auberdine. Gorbold hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without a word, and Borgus worries about how his brother fares so far from Ironforge and Stormwind.

Buzzbox 323. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s field research reaches Buzzbox 323, the third stop along Darkshore’s coast. You gather six Moonstalker fangs and place them in the machine north of Auberdine. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the speaker after you operate Buzzbox 411 farther south. Heavy drinking muddles his directions, but he points you north of Auberdine, to Buzzbox 323 near a road bridge. His research calls for six Moonstalker fangs from the fierce hunters roaming Darkshore’s forests.

Buzzbox 411. Along Darkshore’s coast, Buzzbox 411 needs thresher eyes to return to service. This Alliance errand comes through an eccentric, intoxicated gnome inventor, Wizbang Cranktoggle, who works through a mechanical relay network. After you help repair Buzzbox 827 farther south, gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the mechanical transmitter again. From somewhere safely out of sight, he directs adventurers north along Darkshore’s mist-laden beach to a damaged terminal called Buzzbox 411. His transmissions break with hiccups and muttered praise for crawler wine. He says local aquatic predators carry what his coastal apparatus needs to keep working.

Buzzbox 525. Along Darkshore’s coast, Buzzbox 525 waits for the last of Wizbang Cranktoggle’s strange requests. The gnome’s scattered machines call for animal remnants and ever stranger materials. After Buzzbox 323 is serviced, its rattling speakers carry Wizbang Cranktoggle’s garbled instructions. His words slur through drunken chuckles and rambling directions, sending his helpers far south along Darkshore’s main road. He asks them to hunt grizzled thistle bears and place four thick scalps in Buzzbox 525’s compartment. The machine is concealed behind a fence in the brush beside the road.

Buzzbox 827. Along Darkshore's coast, Buzzbox 827 waits silent for repairs. Wizbang Cranktoggle built it as the first of a chain of voice relays, each made to use parts from local wildlife. Restoring it lets Wizbang test his network from Auberdine. In Auberdine, gnomish engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle is trying to bridge Darkshore's wild coast with a chain of voice relays called Buzzboxes. Their levers and gears carry speech across great distances, a sharp contrast with the ancient ruins and somber forests around them. The machines break down often, and each needs constant care to keep working.

CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Ordinary chickens wander the farmsteads of Azeroth, and most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and clucking, and it may stop pecking to regard you with interest. In that brief moment, the bird scratches letters in the dirt. The message points to the farmer who can provide the food it wants.

name.esES: Carretilla de mezcla modificada de Zanzil
name.frFR: Cache de mixture altérée de Zanzil
name.ptBR: Esconderijo da Mistura Adulterada do Zanzil

text.enUS: Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. At the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen, a stockpile of potent poison lies locked away. The mixture bears the name of Zanzil, a jungle troll witch doctor, and draws the Shattered Hand's attention. North of the Sludge Fen in the Barrens, the Venture Company holds a tower outpost. At its summit, Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix keeps a cache of altered mixture bearing the name of the troll witch doctor Zanzil in his private strongbox. A poison has weakened everyone in the tower, leaving its goblin inhabitants vulnerable to a bold intruder.

Cactus Apple. In the Valley of Trials, Cactus Apples offer orcs a rare source of moisture in Durotar's dry heat. Cactus apples grow in clusters around the thick cactuses scattered across the Valley of Trials. Gathering them means working among the thorns, but the fruit gives welcome hydration in Durotar's heat. Galgar, an orc in the valley, gathers the apples to make Cactus Apple Surprise, a cooling treat for recruits enduring their early training.

Caer Darrow. Caer Darrow is a fortified island situated in Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. Formerly the aristocratic seat of the noble House Barov, the island's keep was secretly sold to Kel'Thuzad and transformed into the necromantic school of Scholomance, leaving the above-ground town plagued by wandering phantoms. Long before the Scourge, Caer Darrow was a strategic stronghold of Lordaeron that housed an ancient elven runestone. During the Second War, the Horde sacked the fortress and carved up the runestone to craft Gul'dan's Altars of Storms. When Lord Uther the Lightbringer sailed to offer relief to the survivors, his fleet was ambushed by Alterac privateers—an act of treachery that exposed Alterac's betrayal to the Alliance.

Cain Firesong. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Cain Firesong guides Forsaken mages in the arcane. He trains them in Tirisfal Glades before sending advanced students to the Undercity for deeper study. Cain Firesong teaches traditional arcane arts in Brill, where Forsaken mages begin their studies. Many Forsaken spellcasters turn to shadow or necromancy, but Cain keeps to the arcane. He mentors mages who set out from Deathknell. The Deathguards point visitors to the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern, where Cain can be found. They joke that he arrived too late to get a room.

Cairne Bloodhoof. In Thunder Bluff, Cairne Bloodhoof rules with hard-won wisdom. The venerable High Chieftain leads the united tauren tribes, and bound their fate to Thrall’s Horde after the orcs helped them escape extinction at centaur hands. Cairne Bloodhoof led the tauren from a life of flight to a home in Mulgore. For generations, centaur marauders hunted the wandering tribes across the Barrens and drove them toward extinction. When Thrall and his orcs reached Kalimdor, Cairne saw a rare nobility in them. Thrall offered military protection and an escort for Cairne’s desperate caravan across the plains, in return for guidance to the Oracle at Stonetalon Peak. The tauren settled on Thunder Bluff’s towering mesas, where Cairne united the tribes and gave them a permanent home.

Call of Air. At Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder sends seasoned shamans south to seek the Air Totem. Prate Cloudseer guides them toward the final elemental pillar of their craft. A shaman who has earned the favor of earth, fire, and water now stands ready to harness air, the last of the four elements. In Orgrimmar, troll trainer Searn Firewarder recognizes when a disciple has reached the height of early training and is prepared for this final foundational step. He sends the shaman south across the Barrens, then down into the canyon labyrinth of Thousand Needles.

Call of Air. Xanis Flameweaver sends seasoned Horde shamans from Thunder Bluff south to seek Prate Cloudseer in Thousand Needles. There they seek communion with the wind and the Air Totem, needed to channel its swift forces. A shaman who has attuned to earth, fire, and water now faces air, the final element. From Thunder Bluff, Xanis Flameweaver guides initiates through a trial of humility, focus, and respect for the sky. The winds are fickle and harder to control than the elements they have already learned.

Call of Earth. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller sets novice Horde shamans a test of endurance and patience. They hunt felstalkers to prepare a ritual sapta. A shaman begins by learning to bond with each element. For orcs and trolls, that path starts with earth, the bedrock of life, endurance, and patience. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller guides new shamans and teaches them that earth demands respect and steadfastness before it grants protection.

Call of Earth. At Spirit Rock, Canaga Earthcaller guides young shaman through their first communion with the elements. They drink an Earth Sapta on sacred ground to see the Minor Manifestation of Earth. A sapta is a mystical draught known to only a few shaman masters. Made with elemental magic, it bridges mortal perception and the spiritual plane, granting Sapta Sight to the strong-willed. Because it binds the drinker's spirit directly to an element, tradition forbids drinking it outside consecrated holy ground.

Call of Earth. In Durotar, a young shaman communes with a manifestation of the earth spirit. The initiate returns to Canaga Earthcaller with rough quartz and receives a first elemental totem. A novice shaman seeks communion with the earth through patience and humility, not brute strength. The Minor Manifestation of Earth grants the initiate a piece of rough quartz. The small stone proves the spirit has accepted the initiate’s pledge and remains a seed of power.

Call of Earth. At Kodo Rock, you seek communion with earth through a sacred tauren rite. Drinking an Earth Sapta lets you see a Minor Manifestation of Earth. Shamanic elders brew a sapta to bind an initiate’s mortal spirit to a primal element. Ancestral magic guards the brewing secrets, known to only a select few among the tauren. Drink the draught at a sacred site, and your mind opens beyond the physical world. The veil parts, and the elements can be witnessed in their raw form.

Call of Earth. After the first communion with the land spirits in Mulgore, a young tauren shaman returns to Camp Narache with a gift from the earth. Drinking the Earth Sapta lets the initiate speak directly with a spirit manifestation and receive raw stone, binding them to the first of the four elements. After drinking the Earth Sapta, you meet the Minor Manifestation of Earth atop the crags near Red Cloud Mesa. The spirit gives you a plain Rough Quartz. It represents your pact with the element and the endurance of stone. The spirit reminds you that patience and strength are the virtues the earth demands, and promises harmony with the land through mutual respect.

Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is an elemental trial undertaken by spiritual initiates to prove their steadfastness. By retrieving requested materials, the petitioner demonstrates their grit and determination to their instructor. Successfully enduring the task confirms their readiness to proceed to the next stage of their training. The Call of Earth is a foundational trial for aspiring practitioners of the elements. Initiates are tasked with fulfilling specific demands to test their patience, resilience, and connection to the stubborn, enduring nature of the earth. Fulfilling the request demonstrates that an adventurer possesses the inner fortitude required to commune with primeval forces.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial in which an elemental initiate drinks an Earth Sapta at the Rise of Spirits to pierce the veil between worlds. Guided by an elemental spirit, the seeker learns the endurance and steadfast resolve of the earth as the foundation for rekindling their lost bond with the winds. To perceive the unseen elemental world, shamans utilize saptas—potent magical brews specifically formulated to align a mortal spirit with a particular elemental realm. When consumed by those possessing sufficient resolve, a sapta opens one's spiritual vision to elemental manifestations that are otherwise hidden from mortal sight. Because of their profound nature, these potions are closely guarded secrets known only to select practitioners.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial of communion where an initiate obtains a piece of Rough Quartz from an earth spirit. Brought to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, this mineral shard becomes the core of the practitioner's first Earth Totem, grounding their bond with the elemental forces. The quest begins when an earth spirit grants an initiate a shard of Rough Quartz as living proof of their communion. The spirit instructs the bearer to take this token to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, explaining that even the smallest fragment carries enduring strength. The spirits demand patience, resilience, and wisdom before granting their favor and respect.

Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is a sacred trial overseen by Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar, testing initiates in the patience and resilience of stone. Aspirants must confront the Frostmane trolls to the south to claim their bear pendants before being granted an earthen sapta. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, the mentor Teo Hammerstorm watches over initiates ready to walk the rugged path of the earth. Viewing the land as a stout and unyielding foundation, Teo guides young wanderers to heed the wisdom of the mountains. He warns that while stone serves as an enduring shield, its favor is not given lightly, requiring true grit and deep respect before any secrets of the soil will be shared.

Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is a sacred shamanic rite that binds an initiate's mortal spirit to the enduring foundations of the world. By imbibing the visionary brew known as Earth Sapta at a secluded mountain Spirit Stone, the seeker learns humility, patience, and elemental awareness amid the snow and rock. The Call of Earth is a sacred trial of spiritual attunement, requiring an initiate to drink the enchanted brew known as Earth Sapta at an isolated mountain shrine. Forged through ancient elemental magic, sapta binds the drinker's spirit to the bedrock of the world, granting mortal eyes the rare power to witness elemental spirits and subtle currents invisible to ordinary sight. Because of its potency, the draught must only be consumed in a designated holy site where the bond between spirit and stone can safely take hold.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is an elemental rite of passage for young shaman in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. By communing with the local earth spirits, initiates receive a rough quartz to bring to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar. This simple stone proves their communion and serves as the core of their Earth Totem. The Call of Earth marks an initiate's first steps onto the spiritual path of the shaman in Dun Morogh. Deep within the frozen peaks, an aspirant must seek out the spirit of the earth and listen to its teachings. The trial demands humility: the spirit gifts only a rough quartz, a simple pebble intended to become the beating heart of an Earth Totem. It reminds the seeker that true endurance is not measured by sheer scale, but by patience, strength, and unwavering resolve.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is an introductory summons calling an initiate to attune with the spirits of the stone. Directed to Coldridge Valley, the traveler must seek out Teo Hammerstorm within the dwarven holdfast of Anvilmar. For an initiate walking the path of the elements, the call of earth is the vital first communion. While elemental energies may already stir across the skin, learning to speak directly with stone establishes a steadfast balance. It teaches the spirit how to find immovable strength, setting firm footing beneath one's boots and within the spirit itself.

Call of Fire. In the Barrens, an aspiring shaman begins the second trial in the search for communion with fire. Kranal Fiss sends the initiate across the Southfury River to a secluded mountaintop shrine in Durotar, carrying the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame. Kranal Fiss entrusts the shaman with the Torch of the Dormant Flame. Raw mystical strength alone cannot meet fire’s demands; the trial calls for temperance, focus, and respect. The torch is both ritual instrument and proof to the shrine’s keeper that the bearer has been judged ready to attempt the trial.

Call of Fire. Telf Joolam sends a shaman across Durotar and the eastern Barrens for a Fire Sapta's ingredients. The draught prepares an initiate to perceive and speak with fire spirits. A Fire Sapta opens a shaman’s senses to the Eternal Flame. Like the draught for earth, it lets a shaman see and speak with spirits hidden from mortal sight. Telf Joolam sends initiates across Durotar and into the eastern Barrens to gather ingredients bound to heat and flame.

Call of Fire. Atop Durotar's peaks, a shaman faces the trial that attunes them to fire. Telf Joolam guides the initiate to drink fire sapta, confront a Minor Manifestation of Fire, and claim its glowing ember to light the ceremonial torch. Fire spirits hide from untrained eyes on Durotar's summit. To see them, you drink fire sapta, a draught made from reagents gathered across the barrens and coast. It sharpens your senses to the unseen, revealing minor spirits and manifestations among the summit crags.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire sends an initiate through the winds of Skywall to seek out Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei Windshaper attuned to the element of fire. By bringing the Torch of Dormant Flame to the Shrine of Flames in the Gustberry Lowlands, the traveler begins learning to heed the call of the flame even within the domain of air. Even within Skywall, the domain ruled by the air elementals, the broader currents of the Elemental Plane remain connected. The spirits of earth, water, and fire still speak to those with the sensitivity to hear them. The Windshapers count among their fellowship individuals uniquely receptive to these other forces, including Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei who fosters a deep attunement with the element of fire.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a quest from the Windshapers commanding the execution of Skypriest Faladiel, a former brother who betrayed his order for power. Adventurers must track the rogue skypriest to the Gustberry Lowlands and retrieve his heart to fuel a powerful elemental ritual. Call of Fire tasks adventurers with hunting down Skypriest Faladiel, a former Windshaper who abandoned his loyalties to join the Al'Aketh. Once a dedicated caller of flame, Faladiel chose power over allegiance, turning on his fellow order members and leaving their blood upon his hands. The Windshapers dispatch an agent to deliver their uncompromising judgment upon him.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a quest in which adventurers are tasked by Olariaan Swiftburn to locate and confront the ancient forest sprite Kuramaa in the Shen'dar Highlands. By invoking the sprite from its stump and defeating it with flame, travelers obtain its powerful wooden mask. The relic is then brought to the Gustberry Lowlands to ignite an eternal flame and commune with the spirits of fire. In the Shen'dar Highlands, local residents whisper tales of Kuramaa, an ancient forest sprite that resides inside a twisted tree stump at the summit of a hill near the regional Anchor Pylon. To draw the reclusive entity into the open, a challenger must strike the bark of its wooden home with a bare fist, demanding its presence and testing their mettle in combat.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a shamanic rite of passage overseen by the Windshapers within Skywall. Initiates must aid in invoking spirits of flame, capture the Eternal Flame, and race against time to kindle the brazier at Valanaar. Successfully completing the trial proves one's respect for the elements and earns the initiate their Fire Totem. The Call of Fire is a sacred trial of elemental attunement conducted within Skywall. Led by Olariaan of the Windshapers, initiates gather at the Brazier of Offering to invoke the spirits of flame from the Firelands. If the offerings are deemed worthy, the spirits ignite the altar with the sacred Eternal Flame, ready to be harnessed by a worthy aspirant.

Call of Water. At Silverpine's coast, the shaman completes the Call of Water at the Brazier of Everfount. The rite clears nearby corruption, and a spirit of pure water appears. At the Brazier of Everfount, your final words call forth a burst of light. It scatters the minor spirits that threaten the spring, and the shore falls quiet.

Call of Water. Along Silverpine Forest's coast, shamans can renew their communion with water through Call of Water. Tiev Mordune offers another Water Sapta to those whose spirit-sight fades before they speak with the purified water spirit. Shamans drink a Water Sapta to see spirits near the elemental shrines. If its magic fades before they speak with the Minor Manifestation of Water, they can no longer enter the spirit realm to finish the trial. On Silverpine Forest's fog-shrouded shore, fellow shaman Tiev Mordune helps those whose visions end too soon.

Call of Water. Your path to the Call of Water begins in Thunder Bluff, where a shaman is ready to seek the element of water. To meet Islen Waterseer, you travel east across the Barrens to its eastern shore. The meeting begins a spiritual journey toward the Water Totem. You have mastered earth and fire, and now your trainers judge you ready to study water. In Thunder Bluff, Xanis Flameweaver recognizes when you have shown the discipline to approach this cleansing element. Your path leads away from Mulgore's mesas and east across the dry plains of the Barrens.

Call of Water. Islen Waterseer sends Horde shamans south through the Barrens to seek Brine. There, they learn what water can cleanse and heal. Islen Waterseer teaches that water brings rebirth. Its flow can carve rock, wash away impurities, and mend flesh, but its healing depends on purity. Polluted water brings blight instead of life. Every shaman must understand this balance before seeking communion with water.

Call of Water. A shaman travels from the Barrens to the Ruins of Stardust for the final gathering trial in the journey to earn Call of Water. Brine sends the initiate north into Ashenvale to draw pure water from its ancient fountain. After gathering water from the pool below Brine’s hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, the shaman needs one final essence. Brine sends the initiate north across the dry plains and into Ashenvale, an ancient woodland sacred to the night elves. The dry Barrens give way to Ashenvale’s deep canopy, where water takes another form. A shaman must understand this variety to live in harmony with the element.

Call of Water. Brine sends shamans into the Barrens to gather water for a sapta. The trial begins with a sample from the guarded pool below her hill, where water means survival. Brine asks shaman initiates to study water in all its forms before she grants the water sapta that lets them commune with the spirits. In the arid Barrens, water means the difference between survival and starvation. She asks them to notice what water makes possible: forests flourish where it flows, deserts starve where it is absent, and living beings will kill to protect even the humblest spring.

Call of Water. You set out from the Barrens for a pure spring in Forsaken-held Tarren Mill. The water will help Brine prepare the Water Sapta, and its survival offers a lesson in hope. Brine sends you across the sea to Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills for water to prepare the Water Sapta. Human resistance and the newly allied Forsaken surround the town, yet its small central well gives pure spring water. To Brine, the spring is a sacred remnant of cleanliness in an unhallowed land.

Call of Water. Brine's water reaches Islen Waterseer on the eastern Barrens coast, where the next part of the shamanic trial begins. The vial holds water Brine prepared and blessed, the base for a sapta that lets an initiate see water spirits in Silverpine Forest. After the trials in the southern Barrens, Brine gives the shaman initiate a Vial of Purest Water. The water comes from pure springs and has been consecrated by Brine's rites. The initiate carries it back to the eastern coast, where Islen Waterseer keeps watch. The water links Brine's teachings with the rites of the totem.

Call of Water. Swart sends a shaman from Razor Hill to seek Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. Earth and fire have tested the initiate; now water calls for a different kind of understanding. Swart, the shaman trainer in Razor Hill, guides initiates through the elements. Earth has taught them endurance, and fire has tested their command. Once a shaman proves they can wield flame without being consumed by it, Swart judges them ready to seek the teachings of water.

Call of Water. Across the sea, Call of Water carries Barrens shamans to Silverpine Forest. There, an initiate faces the blight on an ancient coastal shrine to earn communion with water spirits. After gathering drops of pure water with help from the hermit Brine, you return to Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. She sends you across the sea with the purified essence to Silverpine Forest's haunted shore, just west of the Forsaken refuge called the Sepulcher.

Call of Water. The Call of Water is a spiritual quest for shamans ready to commune with the purifying nature of the water element. Having established harmony with wind, earth, and flame, the initiate reaches Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, who urges them to take the first step toward learning water's purity. The Call of Water marks a vital stage in a shaman's journey into elemental balance. With earth grounding every step, the rush of the wind at one's back, and the inner fire burning bright, the traveler is called to grasp the deeper nature of water. It is not merely an external force, but a spiritual reflection of purity and resilience.

Call of Water. Call of Water sends spiritual seekers into the Wetlands to learn the cleansing power of water and seek the water sapta. In a secluded cave beneath the southern falls, the dwarf Hervdana Saegrund greets travelers braving the wilderness. The journey to understand water begins with a simple lesson on its dual nature: water embodies rebirth, carving stone and cleansing impurities when pure, but threatening ruin when tainted. Initiates seeking communion are sent into the wild to obtain a water sapta from those who dwell beside the element.

Call of Water. Call of Water is a spiritual quest in the Wetlands guiding an initiate on the path to earning the sapta. By gathering brackish estuary water where mountain falls meet sea tides, the seeker learns the vital energies of water while navigating the hazards of the marsh. To earn the sapta and commune with the spirits, an initiate must seek water in its various forms. Hervdana guides seekers to observe how water moves, changes lives, and sustains the land. The journey begins with understanding estuary waters where ocean tide meets fresh highland runoff.

Call of Water. Call of Water is a quest tasking travelers with journeying to Stonewatch Falls in Redridge to investigate suspected corruption in the runoff from Lake Everstill. By filling an Empty Red Waterskin and returning it to Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands, shamans uncover the true source behind mutated local murlocs while securing a key reagent for their spiritual trials. Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands dispatches aspiring shamans south to Redridge to investigate the waterways tumbling down Stonewatch Falls. While Lake Everstill nourishes the settlement of Lakeshire with pristine water, the murlocs lurking at the base of the cascade have grown into unusually massive, twisted beasts. Suspecting venom, foul sorcery, or seepage from the old fortress above, Hervdana tasks travelers with gathering a sample in an Empty Red Waterskin.

Call of Water. Call of Water tasks an adventurer with journeying into the emerald canopy of Ashenvale to collect pure, ancient water from the lake cradling Astranaar. It marks the final gathering step before the traveler is sent back to Norric. Call of Water charges an adventurer with filling a waterskin from the uncorrupted waters of Ashenvale. The seeker must venture to Astranaar, a haven nestled amidst clean, ancient waters that lap against sunken ruins from a bygone era. This pristine sample serves as the final liquid needed by the questgiver before the traveler is sent on to Norric.

Call of Water. The Call of Water is a spiritual trial for shamans seeking the sacred water totem rites. By delivering pure water blessed by Hervdana to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, seekers prepare the elemental sapta necessary to commune with spirits at Stendel's Pond. The Call of Water represents an essential trial of spiritual attunement for aspiring shamans seeking harmony with the element of water. Undertaking this path requires gathering water blessed by Hervdana herself, proving both patience and reverence for the spirits before bringing the vessel to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan.

Call of Water. Call of Water is an elemental quest requiring a journey from Loch Modan to Westfall to restore balance to a corrupted spring. By purging the tainted entity at Stendel's Pond and performing an ancient ritual at the forgotten shrine, petitioners earn the favor of the water spirits and their Water Totem. In the shadow of Moonbrook lies Stendel's Pond, once celebrated as a clear and pure spring. Dark influences sweeping across Westfall have fouled its tranquil waters, driving the local water spirits into profound silence. An aged shrine stands along the shore, neglected and draped in dust and cobwebs, waiting for someone to awaken the dormant powers within.

Call of Water. Call of Water is a quest centered in Westfall that tasks adventurers with purifying corrupted elemental forces. By unraveling restless spirits with radiant light, players commune with a Minor Manifestation of Water to safeguard the region's dwindling vitality. In the windswept lands of Westfall, the natural balance of the waters faces contamination by corrupt spirits. The rite known as the Call of Water requires confronting this malevolence, invoking sacred words that conjure radiant light to disperse the restless, tainted essences into harmless ash and quiet mist.

Call of Water. The Call of Water is an elemental rite of passage where shamans learn to commune with water spirits and wield their restorative powers. By retrieving a Shard of Water from Westfall for Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, initiates prove their dedication and receive their water totem. The Call of Water is a vital spiritual trial undertaken by shamans to forge a bond with the element of water. Initiates are tasked with journeying to Westfall and returning to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan with the Shard of Water. By demonstrating their understanding of water's life-giving essence and its role in purging corruption, shamans earn their water totem and take an essential step on their elemental journey.

Call of Water. You carry the Shard of Water back to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast. Your journey proves your harmony with restorative energies and earns you a Water Totem. You carry a gift from the Minor Manifestation of Water back across the sea. To earn it, you crossed continents to the tainted shores of Silverpine Forest and faced the corruption there. Water gives life, adapts, and heals, yet its pliant nature leaves it open to blight and dark magic. Before the Minor Manifestation, you witnessed pure elemental will and received the Shard of Water. Now, as you return to the sun-scorched Barrens, the shard reminds you that water connects distant corners of the world.

Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde military initiative directed by Drum Fel from the outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Threatened by an alliance between the local Witherbark forest trolls and Boulderfist ogres, the Horde launches a preemptive campaign against the Witherbark to secure their foothold in the region. From the fortified sanctuary of Hammerfall, Drum Fel organizes a preemptive military strike against the hostile native powers of the Arathi Highlands. Surrounded by old human ruins and aggressive local factions, the Horde settlement faces an imminent threat from a cooperative pact formed between the indigenous Witherbark forest trolls and the brute Boulderfist ogres. Rather than allowing their enemies to dictate the terms of survival, Drum Fel calls on champions to take the offensive.

Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde martial trial issued by Drum Fel at the Hammerfall outpost in the Arathi Highlands. Having proven their basic combat readiness, adventurers are ordered southwest toward the dwarven bridge to engage the dangerous Boulderfist ogres. Eliminating both front-line brutes and spellcasting magi tests the warrior's resolve while protecting the Horde's vulnerable foothold in Arathi. At the isolated Horde redoubt of Hammerfall, survival demands unwavering martial strength. Drum Fel, recognizing the growing capabilities of travelers aiding the outpost, refuses to let anyone rest on easy victories. Rather than facing minor skirmishers, warriors must prove their mettle against what Fel considers a genuine threat: the hulking Boulderfist ogres. These brutes have consistently harassed the Horde expedition and tested the resolve of Hammerfall’s defenders. Fel offers simple terms for the task—warriors are expected to return successful in flesh or honorably in spirit, with praise promised for sheer tenacity in battle.

Call to Arms. Following the previous Call to Arms, Drum Fel at Hammerfall declares that it is time to strike the head from the beast. He sends you after the Boulderfist lords and shaman who lair in the ruins of Stromgarde. Drum Fel says you have proven able enough to help deliver one last great blow. Those leading the attacks have made their lair in the ruins of Stromgarde, which he calls a symbol of human frailty. Hunt down the Boulderfist lords and the shaman who serve them, for they would try to drive the Horde out of these lands.

Calling in the Reserves. At Sun Rock Retreat, Calling in the Reserves sends you south to relieve a weary sentry at the Great Lift. Maggran Earthbinder gives you a letter for Grish Longrunner, who has stood watch far from home. Maggran Earthbinder keeps troop welfare and supplies in hand at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Across central Kalimdor, the Horde strains to keep its garrisons staffed, even in the years after the Third War. Maggran knows that endless watch duty wears seasoned soldiers down. He sends a reassignment letter south to the Great Lift, where Grish Longrunner has stood guard far from home.

text.enUS: Calm Before the Storm. After the queen's fall, Alchemist Pestlezugg wants the latest findings to reach people who can act on them. You carry the Un'Goro report to Gracina Spiritmight at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Pestlezugg says that the findings of the day must reach hands that might do something with them, since Gadgetzan cannot manage alone. The latest report is to go to Gracina Spiritmight in Darnassus, whom Pestlezugg hopes can be found at the Temple of the Moon. She has friends among the Alliance bigwigs, and if they can be drawn in, there may be a way through this alive.
