name.frFR: Caisses de ravitaillement de la Croisée

text.enUS: Crossroads Supply Crate. Stolen provisions for the Crossroads lie scattered among Razormane camps in the Barrens. A raided caravan left the settlement short of food, tools, and necessities. Razormane quilboar raided a caravan carrying supplies to the Crossroads. The crates were dragged into nearby camps among the underbrush and dirt dens. Thork, the settlement's commander, seeks their return before the outpost runs dangerously low on food, tools, and necessities.

name.frFR: Tour de garde de la couronne

text.enUS: Crown Guard Tower. Crown Guard Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower in the southern Eastern Plaguelands. The Scourge destroyed it during the invasion of Lordaeron in the Third War, and its broken stones have stood amid the blight ever since. Once part of the Kingdom of Lordaeron's defenses, Crown Guard Tower was a scout tower watching over the lands of eastern Lordaeron. When the Scourge overran the kingdom, the tower was destroyed and left in ruins, one of several fallen towers scattered across what are now the Eastern Plaguelands. Its charred stones stand in a land the undead still hold.

Crown of the Earth. At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to draw sacred water before they leave Shadowglen. The rite recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people gave up there. Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast cost them their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history as he gives novices a rite, preparing them with humility and purpose for a changing world.

Crown of the Earth. In Shadowglen, you set out with moonwell water for Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. The journey carries you from secluded training into the wider work of protecting Teldrassil. After tasting the enchanted water of Shadowglen's moonwell, you meet Tenaron Stormgrip at the crown of Aldrassil. He seals the gathered water in a larger vessel and sends you beyond the sheltered glade. The road runs south toward Dolanaar, through woods where danger has grown harder to predict.

Crown of the Earth. Near Starbreeze Village, you draw sacred water for Darnassus. Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar asks young night elves to replenish the city's moonwell, and the work teaches the history behind their care for Teldrassil's great boughs. You carry a jade phial made by druids to Starbreeze Village, where a lesser moonwell holds sanctified water. Its refined craft lets you draw and carry the luminous water without disturbing its purity. Darnassus's central moonwell depends on these scattered fonts, and the elders send initiates on foot so the city's fountains stay full of Elune's grace. The journey also teaches the young what it takes to nourish Teldrassil.

Crown of the Earth. Corithras Moonrage sends you to the Pools of Arlithrien for water as Gnarlpine furbolgs turn violent. His account of Teldrassil begins with Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance after the Third War. Corithras Moonrage sends you with a tourmaline phial to a moonwell southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the Pools of Arlithrien. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful, now lash out with sudden violence. They ambush travelers and harry Sentinel patrols across the region. What seemed like isolated skirmishes has become a threat to the night elves' new home.

Crown of the Earth. At the Oracle Glade, Corithras Moonrage sends you to gather water from Teldrassil’s sacred moonwell. The journey reveals the truth behind the World Tree’s creation. Corithras Moonrage sends you northwest across Teldrassil to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the Oracle Tree’s great boughs lies the first and most powerful moonwell raised on the island. You draw water into an Amethyst Phial from its sacred pool. The moonwell is the sanctuary where druids and the tree itself watch over the health of their new homeland.

Crown of the Earth. In Teldrassil, moonwell waters are gathered to tend the World Tree’s sickness. The rites lead to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus, where concern grows over a tree raised without blessings. Teldrassil rose after the Third War to give the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. The Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings and refused to sanction its creation. Without their divine protection, sickness spreads through the tree. Strange creatures emerge from its boughs, and once-peaceful furbolg tribes fall into madness.
Crude Flint. Across the Wetlands, Mosshide gnolls carry Crude Flint to kindle fires with freshly hewn marsh timber. Their fires anger Rethiel the Greenwarden, protector of the marsh.

Crusader Outpost. Scarlet Crusaders watch the eastern road from the heights of Crusader Outpost. Their tower guards the approaches to the Scarlet Monastery and waits for Forsaken incursions. Crusader Outpost watches the eastern road from bluffs above the valley. Scarlet sentries scan the route between Brill and Lordaeron’s eastern reaches, hoping to spot undead and scouting parties before they reach the Monastery gates. The tower also gives the garrison a way to flank forces marching up the valley toward their holy bastion.

Crusader's Armory. The Crusader's Armory is a fortified interior hall within the Scarlet Monastery Armory wing. Stockpiled with munitions, gunpowder, and cannonballs, it serves as a staging ground for the zealots guarding the path toward the inner sanctum. Beyond its locked iron door lies the Hall of Champions. Situated between the Footman's Armory and the grand Hall of Champions, the Crusader's Armory displays the full military readiness of the Scarlet Crusade. Unlike the training yards outside, these narrow stone corridors are packed to the ceiling with crates of volatile gunpowder, stacked cannonballs, and heavily armed crusaders ready to repel intruders. The Crusade has turned a former monastic compound into a bristling fortress, dedicating every available hall to the tools of total war. At the far end of the armory stands a heavy locked iron door, barring entry to the inner chambers unless one holds the Scarlet Key.

Crusader's Outpost. In western Tirisfal Glades, Scarlet Crusaders hold a fortified scout tower beside Solliden Farmstead. It marks the Crusade's westernmost position in all of Lordaeron, far from its main bastions and deep in hostile Forsaken territory. A stone tower rises in the western Tirisfal hills, just north of Deathknell. The Scarlet garrison here marks the farthest reach of the Crusade's power in Lordaeron. Its soldiers work with the surviving human laborers at Solliden Farmstead, trying to hold back the encroaching undead. Lookouts watch the nearby pumpkin fields and forest paths for Scourge fiends and patrols from the Undercity.

Crushridge Bounty. Marshal Redpath in Southshore warns that Crushridge ogres have settled by the ruins of Alterac and claimed them. A bounty is offered to anyone who will go north into the Alterac Mountains and hunt them. Redpath's scouts report that the Crushridge ogres have dug a mound in the Alterac Mountains, close to the ruined city, and have taken over its ruins as well. Redpath will not let them grow cozy: ogres who feel safe will move down into the foothills, right to Southshore's door. So Redpath sends you north to hunt the ogres and bring back the Dirty Knucklebones they carry, for a bounty.

Crushridge Warmongers. Marshal Redpath of Southshore wants the Crushridge ogres hit harder than before. You are sent into the Ruins of Alterac to find the Crushridge Warmongers, so the brutes will stay away from the Alliance. After Crushridge Bounty, Marshal Redpath wants the ogres to feel it in earnest. Redpath sends you into the Ruins of Alterac to seek out the Crushridge Warmongers and cut down plenty of them. Redpath holds that nothing else will teach the brutes to stay clear of Alliance territory.

Cry of the Thunderhawk. Cry of the Thunderhawk is the culmination of Jorn Skyseer's hunting trials in the southern Barrens. Entrusted by the elders at Camp Taurajo, a hunter must seek out a winged serpent soaring through the scrublands and bring back its wings to prove their mastery over the savanna's fiercest beasts. After proving their mettle against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, hunters in the Barrens are directed toward their ultimate challenge by Jorn Skyseer. The thunderhawk is considered one of the most fierce aerial predators inhabiting the scrublands surrounding Camp Taurajo. Slaying one requires patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess.

Crypt (Badlands). Tucked away high in the dusty hills of the Badlands lies a secluded underground tomb known simply as the Crypt. Inside rests the silent remnant of an ancient warrior: an armored skeleton seated upon a stone throne, flanked by urns, chests, and a massive relic sword. Perched southeast of Hammertoe's Digsite along an unmarked earthen path rising up the hillside, the Badlands Crypt is easily missed by passersby. Down in its dark stone chambers sits an armored skeleton poised atop a throne. Resting beside the remains is the Sword of the Barbarian King, surrounded by scattered bones, urns, and forgotten chests. While miners and adventurers frequent the surrounding gullies in search of dwarven ruins and riches, the true origin and history of this seated sovereign remain a mystery lost to the arid wastes.

Crypt (Stromgarde Keep). Deep within the ruins of Stromgarde Keep lies the royal crypt, situated past the sanctum chapel in the heart of the district held by the surviving Stromgarde defenders. It holds the tomb of the fallen King Thoras Trollbane and the ancestral treasures of his dynasty. Guarded closely by Prince Galen and faithful caretakers, the vault remains a sanctuary of royal honor amid a shattered kingdom. Hidden beneath the Sanctum of Stromgarde Keep, this subterranean burial vault serves as the final resting place of King Thoras Trollbane, the warrior monarch who led Stromgarde through the Second War. Despite the devastation engulfing the city—split among Syndicate rogues and Boulderfist ogres—the remaining Stromgarde militia fiercely maintains their grip on this quarter. Prince Galen Trollbane personally watches over the crypts alongside dedicated royal caretakers, ensuring his father's body and legacy remain undisturbed by the scavengers and enemies outside.

Crystal Kelp Frond. Murlocs carry Crystal Kelp Fronds from the ocean to Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. William Pestle in Goldshire seeks them for an invisibility liquor. Crystal Kelp Fronds come from saltwater oceans, so their presence in Elwynn Forest’s fresh water is unusual. Murloc tribes along Crystal Lake’s shores gather and keep the fronds for reasons of their own. Alchemists value their strange power to distort sight. William Pestle in Goldshire uses them as the chief ingredient in an invisibility liquor, meant to help sweethearts slip past watchful family eyes.

Crystal Lake. East of Goldshire, Crystal Lake draws travelers toward a shore claimed by murlocs. Their attacks make the water a danger to villagers and passersby. Crystal Lake lies east of Goldshire, within walking distance of the Lion's Pride Inn. Freshwater murlocs now claim its shore and shallow shoals, attacking anyone who comes too close. William Pestle, an alchemist at the inn, hires travelers to drive them back and gather the crystal kelp they carry for his experiments.

Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, Tenaron Stormgrip entrusts young night elves with a Crystal Phial. They carry it to a nearby moonwell to draw sacred water for rites honoring and nourishing Teldrassil. Young night elves receive a Crystal Phial atop Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip sends them to the moonwell just north of the bough to gather its glowing waters. The delicate vessel holds water touched by the sacred legacy of the Well of Eternity. Returning with a Filled Crystal Phial begins the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage, teaching the young kaldorei about the balance of magic, history, and nature in their new island home.

Crystal Shore. Crystal Shore is a stretch of sandy coastline along the southeastern edge of Stranglethorn Vale, washed by the waves of the South Seas. Tucked beneath steep coastal bluffs, the beach lies just south of the ancient Ruins of Aboraz and across the waters from Jaguero Isle. Running along the southeastern perimeter of Stranglethorn Vale, the Crystal Shore forms a natural boundary between the dense tropical interior and the open waters of the South Seas. The beach itself is walled off from the inland jungles by steep ridges, leaving only a couple of rugged passes for travelers attempting to move between the coast and the deeper wilderness of Mistvale Valley. To the north lie the crumbling troll structures of the Ruins of Aboraz, while the Wild Shore extends along the southern curves of the cape. Its location makes it a quiet, windswept margin far removed from the bustling docks of Booty Bay.

Crystal Vale. Tucked away in the far northwestern corner of Silithus, the Crystal Vale is a remote canyon dominated by jagged mineral spires and swirling elemental forces. Earth and air elementals roam its rocky flats, guarding rich veins of raw ore. It is also a site of potent summoning magic, deeply tied to the ancient elemental lords. The Crystal Vale stands distinct from the barren desert sands of southern Silithus. Framed by steep cliffs, the basin is filled with shimmering crystalloid formations, roaming earthen elementals, and roaring whirlwinds of living air. Rich deposits of thorium draw occasional daring prospectors, but the vale is far from quiet. The elemental beings here are inherently hostile to intruders, guarding a realm that feels steeped in the primal conflicts of primordial Azeroth.

Crystal in the Mountains. The Pendant of Myzrael pulses in your hand and a pleading reaches you, as if someone desperately needs help. A vision shows a gleaming crystal rising out of the ground in the northern mountains of Arathi, and you feel drawn to that place. The pendant pulses as you hold it. From it comes a sense of pleading, as if someone is trying to reach you and badly needs your help. Then a vision opens before you: the mountains in the north of Arathi, and a gleaming crystal thrusting up out of the ground. You feel drawn to that place.

Crystalized Scales. Basilisks in harsh Kalimdor lands yield Crystalized Scales for arcane work. The mineralized hides come from the Charred Vale and Thousand Needles, and Collin Mauren seeks them in Stormwind. Basilisks endure heat and ash in Stonetalon's Charred Vale and the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Their hides harden beneath a crystal crust, and the scales hold latent arcane resonance. Wizards across the Great Sea prize them for experiments in rare spellcraft.

Crystalvein Mine. Crystalvein Mine is a cavern in central Stranglethorn Vale, situated near the ancient ruins of Zul'Mamwe. The cavern is rich in valuable 'Singing Crystals', but aggressive native basilisks have completely overrun the site, turning prospective miners to solid stone. Tucked away in the jungle hills near Zul'Mamwe, Crystalvein Mine boasts rare deposits of Singing Crystals, a unique mineral that fetches a high price in southern trade ports. Enticed by the promise of immense profit, the Venture Company set its sights on extracting the veins. However, the mine's natural inhabitants have proved catastrophic for business. Local basilisks consume the strange crystals, hardening their scales and making them unnaturally lethal. Outside the cave mouth, petrified statues of trolls and humans stand as a silent testament to the Venture Company's failed expeditions.

Culling the Threat. In Astranaar, fear grows as the Thistlefur furbolgs multiply to the north. Raene Wolfrunner calls for Dal Bloodclaw's death before the tribe can assault the town. Astranaar stands in the heart of Ashenvale, with danger close on every side. The Thistlefur furbolgs dwell just north of town. Once peaceful forest dwellers, they have fallen to madness and aggression, as have many of their kin. Sentinel scouts have watched their numbers swell over recent months. Now they fear a coordinated attack on Astranaar is only a matter of time.

Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a secretive cabal of mortal zealots, necromancers, and aristocrats devoted to the Lich King. Formed in northern Lordaeron prior to the Third War, its members poisoned the grain supplies that spawned the Scourge and engineered the downfall of humanity's greatest kingdom. Today, the surviving cultists manage the plague cauldrons and necromantic academies across the Plaguelands while actively infiltrating the cities of the living. The Cult of the Damned was forged by the exiled Archmage Kel'Thuzad after he answered the telepathic whispers of the Lich King emanating from the Frozen Throne. Returning to Lordaeron with vast wealth and forbidden dark arts, Kel'Thuzad offered two false gospels: to the desperate, impoverished lower classes, he promised social equality and liberation from misery; to the wealthy landowners, such as the noble House of Barov, he promised eternal life and an unshakeable grip upon their domains. In truth, both the destitute and the affluent were cattle intended for slaughter, bound into a death cult designed to betray their homeland from the inside.

Curative Animal Salve. Across Darkshore and the Barrens, druids use Curative Animal Salve to treat sick wildlife. Herbalists prepare it in both lands, while the Cenarion Circle sees the animals’ afflictions as signs of a wider blight. Druids use Curative Animal Salve to ease sick wildlife in Darkshore and the Barrens. Alanndarian Nightsong directs young druids to treat sick deer between the Cliffspring River and the borders of Ashenvale. In the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem brews the same remedy for sick gazelles grazing north of the Crossroads. Each herbalist prepares the salve from locally gathered herbs in batches of ten doses. Field practitioners apply it directly to the animals, while both herbalists work with local authorities to produce larger supplies.

Curing the Sick. Darkshore’s deer are sick, and Curing the Sick asks you to bring them relief. Alanndarian Nightsong gives you salve to treat the poisoned animals before you report to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. In Darkshore, deer fall sick from the Cliffspring River south to the border of Ashenvale. They wander the misty woods, weakened by toxins in the soil and streams. After you gather the needed reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong gives you freshly brewed animal salve to treat the afflicted deer.

Curing the Sick. Curing the Sick is an essential trial for young Horde druids, tasking them with healing afflicted wildlife in the northern Barrens. By applying a freshly concocted herbal salve to ailing gazelles, initiates demonstrate both their practical field medicine and their commitment to preserving natural balance. Completing this duty proves their dedication directly to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Across the northern savanna of the Barrens, grazing gazelles have begun succumbing to an unnatural affliction. After gathering earthroot and kodo horns to assemble a curative remedy, Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads entrusts a young druid with administering the field treatment. The initiate must search north of the main crossroads to find and minister to ten suffering animals, providing immediate relief before the rot takes further root in the ecosystem.

Curse These Fat Fingers. Hansel Heavyhands, in the Searing Gorge, can no longer dish out beatings as before, thanks to swollen fingers. Hansel asks you to go pound the heavy war golems for them. Hansel Heavyhands says the climate in the Gorge, with its thin air, makes Hansel's fingers swell until they resemble huge Thelsamar blood sausages. As a result, Hansel cannot deliver beatings the way Hansel used to, and needs you to see to Hansel's business instead.

Cut-Throat Alley. Behind the canal shops, Cut-Throat Alley lies quiet and empty in Stormwind City. Reach it through the Shady Lady near the Dwarven District, where a paved courtyard ends at an unoccupied residence. Cut-Throat Alley lies in a quiet corner of Stormwind, charted with the Dwarven District but apart from its forge fires and soot. No main avenue leads here; the only footpath passes through the Shady Lady, a small canal-side shop just south of the bridge from Cathedral Square. Beyond its door, a paved dead end holds stacked crates, forgotten barrels, and one empty two-story residence. Passing guards and ordinary citizens cannot see the alley, which stays silent amid the capital.

Cutting Teeth. In the Valley of Trials, fresh recruits face a first test against mottled boars. Overseer Gornek sends aspiring warriors and spellcasters to thin the boars around the cactus dirt farms, where they can prove their fighting skill and readiness to serve the Horde. The Valley of Trials leaves little room for grand dreams. Young recruits may imagine hunting great beasts in the Barrens or winning glory on a battlefield, but overseer Gornek begins with the farms. Thinning the mottled boars is a grounded test of a recruit’s first skills with a weapon or spell. It shows whether they can face a wild attacker and have the sense to survive their first skirmish.

Cycle of Rebirth. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield seeks Gaea seeds to help heal Stonetalon. She asks the Horde to gather the rare seeds from Mirkfallon Lake, hoping to bless them and restore the mountain’s damaged soil. Stonetalon’s peaks bear wounds from commercial exploitation and regional conflict. Logging and clashes between rival factions have left forests scorched, cut down, or reduced to ash. For the tauren stationed at Sun Rock Retreat, the rapid destruction of the natural world is a grievous wound. Shamans like Tammra Windfield seek the Earthmother’s restorative cycle as they work to mend the land.

Cyclonian. Cyclonian is a mighty wind lord whose defeat has been sought for ages. To challenge him, a champion must gather the components required to summon the elemental and strike him down to claim his whirlwind heart. Defeating the wind lord allows the heart's power to be infused into a formidable weapon. Cyclonian is a raging elemental wind lord whose presence commands reverence and caution. For ages, an attentive watcher has kept vigil over the summoning site, waiting for a combatant possesses enough raw martial prowess to challenge and destroy this tempestuous entity.

Cyrus Therepentous. Cyrus Therepentous is a formidable black dragonspawn residing in the cavernous depths of Slither Rock in the Burning Steppes. Rather than immediately striking down intruders, he tests daring mortals to see if they possess the strength to serve the purposes of the Black dragonflight. Secluded inside a cavern at Slither Rock, Cyrus Therepentous oversees the volcanic crags of the Burning Steppes. Like many of his kind, he views mortal travelers with immense condescension, declaring that only fools would disturb his lair. Yet beneath his ferocious exterior lies a cold calculation: rather than consuming every trespasser on sight, he offers them a lethal challenge against his minions, willing to exploit those resilient enough to survive the trials of flame.

Dabyrie's Farmstead. Dabyrie's Farmstead is an Alliance-aligned rural settlement situated in northern Arathi Highlands. In a realm shattered by the Third War and overrun by Syndicate outlaws and Witherbark trolls, this estate remains a stubborn bastion of Stromgarde citizens led by Kenata Dabyrie. Perched in the northern fields of the Arathi Highlands, Dabyrie's Farmstead is one of the very few functioning human homesteads remaining in the fractured kingdom of Stromgarde. Owned by Kenata Dabyrie and worked alongside her sons, Fardel and Marcel, the grounds are fiercely defended by a local family militia. Surrounded by aggressive wildlife, opportunistic bandits, and the nearby Forsaken presence in the north, the farm stands as a symbol of human endurance in a ruined land.

Daelin's Men. Adjutant Tesoran has found Lieutenant Paval Reethe in the guard's records. They tell of an enlistment in the Kul Tiras marines at sixteen, distinguished service with promotions, and a place in the Theramore guard among the recruits who sailed over with Lady Proudmoore. The last entry lists Reethe as missing, and Captain Garran Vimes is to hear of it. Captain Garran Vimes sent you to Adjutant Tesoran, who has now searched the books and found Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Reethe signed up with the Kul Tiras marines at sixteen, and distinguished service brought promotions. Reethe went on to the Theramore guard, like most of the recruits who sailed over with Lady Proudmoore. The record ends with Reethe listed as missing. The news is for Vimes in Theramore.

Daffodil Bouquet. In Lakeshire, Guard Parker sends a bouquet to thank Darcy for packing his lunch. Martie Jainrose gathers the flowers, and their choice stirs gossip between the two women. Guard Parker wants to thank Darcy at the Lakeshire inn for packing his daily lunch. He asks the town herbalist, Martie Jainrose, to prepare a bouquet of daffodils. Martie says they are her favorite flowers. Darcy recognizes them as Martie’s signature bloom and suspects jealousy. Half-joking, she wonders whether Martie poisoned the stems out of spite.

Dagger Hills. Bandits hold the Dagger Hills, the rocky heights behind Moonbrook in southern Westfall. With royal patrols gone, the ridge threatens travelers and the plains below. The Dagger Hills rise above Moonbrook in southern Westfall, where Defias outlaws watch the rocky ridges. Stormwind's royal patrols are gone, leaving the dry highland as a natural stronghold for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen hide among the crests and scrub. They ambush travelers and watch the approaches to their strongholds below.

Daggerspine Scale. Along Hillsbrad Foothills' southern shores, Daggerspine Scale comes from tough reptilian scales harvested from prowling Daggerspine naga. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks them to activate virulent brews in the Forsaken's ongoing plague experiments. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks reagents for its toxins, plagues, and concoctions. While refining the experimental Elixir of Agony, its apothecaries found that scales from the local Daggerspine naga react in a useful way. Combined with troll regenerative elixirs and murloc organs, the scales chemically activate dormant contaminating agents suspended in raw mixtures. Gathering them means hunting along the rocky coastline east of Southshore, near both the vicious naga tribe and Alliance forces. The apothecaries need these scales for their research.

Daily Delivery. Einar Stonegrip keeps to the Wetlands while his hides make their way to Menethil Harbor. He asks travelers bound for town to carry cured crocolisk hides to a local tanner. Einar Stonegrip hunts the wildlife of the Wetlands, especially the aggressive crocolisks along its waterways. He gathers plenty of valuable skins, but taking them home means traveling to Menethil Harbor. With his marriage to Sida going through a rough patch, Einar would rather remain in the field than face her. He hands his parcels to travelers passing toward town.

Dal Bloodclaw's Skull. In northern Ashenvale, Dal Bloodclaw's Skull marks the end of a threat to Astranaar. Raene Wolfrunner receives it as proof that an attack on the night elf settlement has been averted. The Thistlefur furbolgs north of Astranaar have grown in number and aggression. Like much of Ashenvale's ancient forest, they have been corrupted. Raene Wolfrunner, a night elf sentinel, fears they will soon march on Astranaar. She orders their ranks culled and their leader, Dal Bloodclaw, slain. His skull gives grim proof that the tribe's leadership has been shattered, buying Astranaar's defenders precious time.

Dalar Dawnweaver. At the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver turns his arcane learning toward the Forsaken’s enemies. Once an archmage of Dalaran, he died when the Scourge destroyed the city and later broke free of the Lich King’s control. Now he studies Dalaran’s lingering presence and seeks to end the madness of Archmage Arugal. Dalar Dawnweaver once held high rank among the Kirin Tor, walking the Violet Citadel’s halls when Dalaran stood at the height of arcane mastery. His mortal life ended when the Scourge sacked the city to prepare for Archimonde’s summoning. Raised as a mindless thrall of the Lich King, Dalar broke free alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner when the Scourge’s grip faltered. Now at the Sepulcher, he keeps an archmage’s keen intellect and devotes it to protecting the Forsaken realm.

Dalar's Analysis. Dalar's Analysis is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest linking Shadow Priest Allister's espionage against Ambermill with the arcane research of Dalar Dawnweaver. After uncovering a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate, adventurers bring the relic to Dalar at the Sepulcher for scrutiny. The artifact reveals that the surviving mages of Dalaran are marshaling significant magical power for a hidden initiative. Following a raid on a Dalaran supply crate at a camp north of Pyrewood Village, Shadow Priest Allister receives a rune-inscribed pendant found beneath a bundle of old maps. Recognizing that its enchantment lies beyond his spiritual purview, Allister directs the relic to Dalar Dawnweaver, an arcane scholar stationed at the Sepulcher who is better suited to decipher Dalaran's magical warding.

Dalaran. Dalaran was once the shining magocratic capital of the Kirin Tor, nestled on the southern shore of Lordamere Lake. Shattered by the Scourge and the demon lord Archimonde during the Third War, its surviving magi are rebuilding the city, having removed its protective violet shield early in the reconstruction. Founded after the ancient Troll Wars by sorcerers of the Arathorian Empire, Dalaran stood for centuries as humanity's premier sanctuary for arcane study. Under the leadership of the Council of Six, the Kirin Tor amassed vast magical archives and guarded powerful artifacts within the Violet Citadel. That age of splendor ended abruptly during the Third War. The traitor prince Arthas led the Scourge through the city gates to seize the Book of Medivh, and soon after, the demon lord Archimonde crushed Dalaran's soaring spires into rubble.

Dalaran Mana Gem. Near Ambermill, Kirin Tor mages carry Dalaran Mana Gems to replenish their power. Forsaken tailors use the gems to weave enchanted robes. Kirin Tor mages, conjurors, and guards around Ambermill carry mana gems to focus and replenish their arcane power. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners prize the gems as a ready supply of concentrated magic. Some undead mages share an academic heritage with Dalaran, but survival comes first. To the Forsaken, the Kirin Tor are rivals whose magical stores can be taken.

Dalaran Patrols. In Tarren Mill, Magus Wordeen Voidglare turns his attention to Dalaran's outskirts. Beyond the city's great dome, ruined streets may hold treasures of magical worth, but wizards and their elemental slaves patrol them. Voidglare wants the patrols thinned. After Prison Break In, Voidglare turns his attention to the wizards of Dalaran. They raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. Some say it protects them from the violence of the age; others say they sought solitude to study and plot. Voidglare cares nothing for their reason. Beyond the dome, the ruined outskirts may hold treasures of real magical worth, but wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. You are sent to hunt six Dalaran Summoners and twelve Elemental Slaves, then return to Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

Dalaran Pendant. In Ambermill, Dalaran Pendants focus the Kirin Tor's magic. The Forsaken seek them to hinder the wizards' work and trace the source of their power. Kirin Tor sorcerers, conjurers, and protectors weave powerful spells in Ambermill, threatening Forsaken control of southern Silverpine Forest. Each carries an attuned Dalaran Pendant. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends Forsaken operatives to recover the pendants, slowing the mages' efforts and uncovering who guides their magical weave.

Dalaran Status Report. At Ambermill, the Kirin Tor watch Dalaran as the city is rebuilt in the open. Their report carries intelligence the Deathstalkers seek. The Scourge sacked Dalaran, and Archimonde brought down its towering spires during the Third War. Early in the rebuilding, the surviving magi removed the city's protective shield and began their work in the open. The Kirin Tor also keeps enclaves such as Ambermill in southeastern Silverpine Forest. Its wizards compile the Dalaran Status Report, which holds intelligence about the city's condition and draws the Deathstalkers' attention.

Dalaran's Intentions. Dalar Dawnweaver sends Shadow Priest Allister a warning from Silverpine Forest. A pendant bound for the Kirin Tor in Ambermill reveals their plan to awaken a dormant ley energy node beneath the town, and the Forsaken at the Sepulcher prepare to answer. Dalar Dawnweaver studies a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate and recalls an old Kirin Tor survey. Ambermill was chosen for a reason: the quiet village sits atop a dormant ley energy node. Dalar realizes the wizards intend to tap it. Awakening such a nexus takes immense magical reserves, and the enchanted pendants the wizards wear are key to channeling and catalyzing its power.

Dalin's Heart. Near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine Forest, Dalin Forgewright patrols with an honorable heart. Undercity warlocks seek hearts from truly virtuous mortals to call and bind a succubus to their service. Dalin Forgewright spends his days defending desperate Lordaeron refugees kept from safety by the sealed Greymane Wall. His selfless devotion marks him as a rare offering of unblemished purity, and his heart is carved for the rites held in the Temple of the Damned.

Dalson's Tears. Dalson's Tears is a blighted farmstead located in the heart of the Western Plaguelands. Once known as Dalson's Orchard, the land was overrun during the Third War and converted into a staging ground for one of the Scourge's noxious plague cauldrons. The undead remains of the former owners still haunt the fields and outbuildings. Before the Third War, this estate flourished as Dalson's Orchard, a productive farm in the breadbasket of Lordaeron. Today, the fields are choked with decay and rechristened Dalson's Tears. At the center of the ruined property stands a massive iron cauldron, constantly billowing virulent green plague vapors across the landscape. The device is overseen by Cauldron Lord Malvinious and defended by a pack of blighted zombies, rotting cadavers, and skeletal horrors serving the Lich King.

Dancing for Marzipan. During Hallow's End, travelers in Darnassus gather sweets for Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the trick-or-treat custom: a dance comes before her Darnassus Marzipan. Hallow's End brings a lighter spirit to Darnassus, the sacred forest city of the long-lived night elves. You come seeking sweets for Jesper, a sick child recovering in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the season's custom, even when the treat is meant for a child in need. First, she asks for a trick.

Dancing for Marzipan. Innkeeper Pala asks Dancing for Marzipan visitors to dance during Hallow's End in Thunder Bluff. The treat is meant for a sick orphan, and the custom brings holiday cheer to Mulgore's high mesas. During Hallow's End, Innkeeper Pala keeps the trick-or-treat custom in Thunder Bluff. Even when you come for an ailing child, she asks for a festive dance before giving up her Thunder Bluff Marzipan.

Dandred's Fold. Dandred's Fold is a secluded farmstead and manor tucked along the misty northwestern shores of Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains. Now overrun by the Syndicate, it serves as a secure hideout for Lord Aliden Perenolde and his co-conspirators. Both the Horde and the Alliance keep a watchful eye on this lakefront retreat for very different reasons. Perched on the western edge of the Uplands with private access to the waters of Lordamere Lake, Dandred's Fold was once a tranquil country estate, likely owned by an Alteraci noble named Dandred. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the estate transformed into a fortified enclave for the Syndicate. Syndicate assassins and enforcers now patrol its fences and docks, shielding the fallen nobility from the eyes of Southshore authorities and the Forsaken across the lake.

Dangerous!. At Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia has marked four Hillsbrad humans for execution. She calls them enemies of the Forsaken for killing their people and striking at supplies. Across the Hillsbrad Foothills, the fighting is brutal and personal. High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill see ordinary Hillsbrad citizens as deadly foes. A wanted notice names four people whose resistance has killed Forsaken and cost them valuable shipments from the Undercity.

text.enUS: Dangers of the Windfury. Ruul Eagletalon asks you to test your readiness against the Windfury harpies in Mulgore. The hunt takes you to the southeastern cliffs, where their speed and claws put your skill to the test before you leave the tauren homeland. In Bloodhoof Village, Ruul Eagletalon watches travelers pass through Mulgore. He asks those coming of age or preparing for wider travels to prove their combat instincts. Beyond Mulgore's sheltered valleys, survival demands poise against cunning foes, and Ruul measures your mettle against the land's fiercest native predators.

Daphne Stilwell. On Westfall's cliffs, Daphne Stilwell keeps an orchard above the Longshore. She and her husband Jordan fled the north and now aid the Church of the Holy Light while guarding their home from nearby outlaws. West of Moonbrook and the Deadmines exit, Daphne Stilwell tends a homestead and apple orchard on the bluffs. From the Longshore below or gryphon routes south to Stranglethorn Vale above, the farm looks quiet. But life there is not safe. Bandits and scavengers roam nearby, while Daphne works among the trees and watches over her isolated land.

Darcy. At the Lakeshire Inn, Darcy keeps the town's defenders fed and spirits up. She serves drinks and warm meals, with a special care for Guard Parker. Darcy keeps the Lakeshire Inn's counter working through long days and nights. The town's militia come there for food and drink while gnolls and Blackrock orcs keep Lakeshire under pressure. Darcy also looks out for guards posted around town. She asks travelers to carry hot meals and friendly errands to defenders stationed along the borders.

Dark Ceremony. After the Gordunni Scroll, Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache reads it as plans for a dark ceremony led by the Gordunni mage-lords. Rok Orhan wants you to take an orb from one of those mage-lords, to learn more about the ceremony and the Gordunni's magic. Rok Orhan has looked over the Gordunni Scroll you brought and reads it as the plans for a dark ceremony. As far as Rok can tell, the Gordunni mage-lords are the ones who conduct it. A mage-lord must be found, and an orb taken from him. A mage's orb holds great power, and it should reveal more about the ceremony and the magic the Gordunni wield.

Dark Cleric Beryl. In Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl guides newly awakened undead priests in the shadows. Stationed in the Gallows' End Tavern, he teaches them shadow magic and helps them adapt to their unholy existence under the Dark Lady. Dark Cleric Beryl mentors new Forsaken priests upstairs in Brill's Gallows' End Tavern. He teaches that a priest's power comes from darkness and shadow, yet mastering the dark also requires knowing the light. Newly risen priests turn their focus to shadow and the dark arts under his guidance. Their early trials include crafting their Garments of Darkness and proving their dedication to this new path.

Dark Council. Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore has learned that the letter you brought came from a being who goes by Nagaz and belongs to the Argus Wake. If the Argus Wake is allied with the Syndicate, Maleb says, they must be a threat. You are sent to hunt down Nagaz and the Argus Shadow Mages in the Uplands. After Further Mysteries, Maleb tells you the letter came from a being who goes by Nagaz and belongs to the Argus Wake. Maleb does not know what the Argus Wake is, but an alliance with the Syndicate would make them a threat. Maleb wants Nagaz and the Argus Shadow Mages named in the letter found and killed, and asks for the head of Nagaz. You are to search the Uplands, north of Strahnbrad, where the Syndicate is strongest. Maleb hopes the Argus Wake's envoys are there.

Dark Heart. Talo Thornhoof at Camp Mojache wants the dark heart of Edana Hatetalon, who is queen of the harpies of Northspring, living in ruins to the west. Talo calls her pure evil. Edana Hatetalon is the harpies' queen, ruling the Northspring brood in ruins lying west. Talo calls her pure evil, with no feeling in her except hatred for everyone, and has heard her heart is made of crystal. Talo wants you to face her and bring back her dark heart, because the hatred she spreads must be stopped.

Dark Iron Ambassador. Deep within Gnomeregan, the Dark Iron Ambassador draws notice as an envoy of his clan. His presence leaves the clan’s interest in the ruined gnome capital unexplained. Among Gnomeregan’s irradiated halls, the Dark Iron Ambassador represents his clan. No one explains the purpose of his mission.

Dark Iron clan. The Dark Iron clan is an ancient, ash-skinned dwarven faction ruling from the volcanic depths of Blackrock Mountain. Cast out of Ironforge during the War of the Three Hammers, they accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, who enslaved their empire. Today, under Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, they wage shadow wars against both the Alliance and the Horde while serving their fiery elemental master. Long ago, three dwarven factions lived together in Ironforge under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died, civil war erupted. The Bronzebeards defeated both rival factions, casting out the Wildhammers and Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan's Dark Irons. Vowing vengeance, Thaurissan established a settlement in the Redridge Mountains while his sorceress wife, Modgud, led an army against Grim Batol. When both assaults failed and the united Bronzebeard and Wildhammer armies marched on his stronghold, Thaurissan attempted to unleash an apocalyptic subterranean entity to save himself. His ritual breached the core of the world and freed Ragnaros the Firelord.

Dark Iron dwarf. Dark Iron dwarves are a distinct dwarven sub-race distinguished by their ashen skin, blazing red eyes, and innate affinity for fire. Banished from Ironforge following the civil War of the Three Hammers, they dwell deep within Blackrock Mountain where their society has fallen under the tyrannical rule of the Firelord, Ragnaros. Unlike their Bronzebeard and Wildhammer cousins, Dark Iron dwarves possess dark gray or soot-black skin and eyes that burn like glowing embers. Their history fractured during the War of the Three Hammers, when their Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan sought to conquer Ironforge. Defeated and driven south into the Redridge Mountains, Thaurissan attempted to summon dark powers to avenge his losses, inadvertently releasing Ragnaros the Firelord from the Elemental Plane. The catastrophic summoning shattered the surrounding peaks into the volcanic waste of Blackrock Mountain and bound the Dark Iron race into fiery servitude.

Dark Portal. The Dark Portal is a monumental stone gateway standing at the southern rim of the Blasted Lands. First torn open through the combined sorcery of Medivh and Gul'dan, it served as the fateful conduit that brought the Old Horde into Azeroth, initiating the First War. Before its opening, this region was part of the Black Morass, a sodden wetland that stretched across the south. That changed when Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, joined his Tirisfal magics with the fel sorcery of Gul'dan on Draenor. The ritual drained untold lives and tore the fabric of reality apart. The Old Horde raised massive stone architecture to anchor the rift, marching armies through its threshold to shatter the Kingdom of Stormwind in the First War. The portal's fel emanations fundamentally corrupted the surrounding terrain, reducing lush marshes to the red, petrified wastes seen today.

Dark Riders. The Dark Riders are a band of mysterious, hooded horsemen who terrorize Duskwood. Merciless hunters of magical relics, they strike from hiding and leave only slaughter in their wake. Little is known of the Dark Riders' origins. Witnesses describe hooded horsemen who speak in voices both harsh and shrill, and one was seen using a small gem to take orders from a master it called only its 'Lord'. They hunt objects of magical power across the kingdom, cutting down anyone who stands between them and their prize.

Dark Storms. In Durotar, Burning Blade cultists corrupt the land from Thunder Ridge. Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill has learned that the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm leads them, and asks you to end his threat. Orgnil Soulscar has learned that dark magic has taken hold in Thunder Ridge, northwest of Razor Hill. Burning Blade cultists prowl the ravine while young Horde defenders patrol Durotar’s borders. Their presence brings ruin to the wildlife and land.

Dark Vessels. Primal Torntusk in Revantusk Village says the Vilebranch fight with a supernatural ferocity, the work of Vile Priestess Hexx's foul weavings of magic. Throughout Jintha'alor lie dark vessels of tainted blood, radiating a foul magic that belongs to the faceless blood God. Torntusk asks you to steal them and bring them back, so the taint can be removed. Wherever you walk in Jintha'alor, you will find vessels of tainted blood. They radiate the dark power of the faceless blood God, which strengthens the Vilebranch and drives them to madness. Torntusk believes that taking the vessels away and removing their taint will loosen the blood God's grip on them.

Darkcloud Pinnacle. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified tauren settlement perched atop several interconnected mesas east of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. Held by the aggressive Grimtotem clan, the aerial stronghold serves as a base of operations for regional disruption and shady dealings. Spanning three main mesas joined by rope bridges, Darkcloud Pinnacle commands the canyon basin below. The heights are accessible only by a steep natural slope leading from the canyon floor across wooden bridges, or via a high crossing near Razorfen Downs. From these windswept rocks, the Grimtotem watch the valley, safe from casual assault and isolated from the broader tauren tribes.

Darkcore the Elder. Darkcore the Elder is a seasonal quest encountered during the Lunar Festival within the Undercity. By seeking out Elder Darkcore, travelers pay homage to the ancient spirits honored across Azeroth and receive a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear throughout the continents to share their wisdom and blessings. Elder Darkcore resides in the shadowed halls of the Undercity, bearing witness to the modern realm while offering remembrance to those who seek out the roots of the world.

Darkened Bank. At Duskwood’s northern edge, Darkened Bank follows the river beside Elwynn Forest. Its shore runs east toward the Redridge Mountains, between the safer north and the forest’s terrors. Darkened Bank follows the river that separates Duskwood from Elwynn Forest. The shore runs from western river bends east toward the stone span leading to the Redridge Mountains. Under Duskwood’s gloomy canopy, it is often the first ground travelers reach when coming south from Elwynn. Near its western tip, a makeshift camp shelters displaced refugees Sven Yorgen and Lars, just beyond the deep woods.

Darkhorn the Elder. At the Lunar Festival, Darkhorn the Elder receives travelers in Orgrimmar. Honored among the ancestors, she embodies age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestors appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within Orgrimmar’s fortified ramparts, watching the young warrior city. You can approach her to honor those who walked the earth generations ago, whether you fight for the Horde or brave the gates as an Alliance traveler.

Darkhound Blood. Darkhound Blood is a foul bodily fluid harvested from the tainted canine beasts roaming the fields and forests of Tirisfal Glades. Gathered at the behest of the Royal Apothecary Society, it serves as an early reagent in their dark experiments to engineer a lethal new plague. Under the command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Royal Apothecary Society strives to develop a virulent contagion capable of wiping out Arthas and his Scourge. Stationed in Brill, Apothecary Johaan theorizes that local beasts, corrupted by dark energies and resilient to the surrounding decay, possess unusual biological properties. By distilling the blood of wild darkhounds, Johaan aims to uncover biological compounds that can resist or propagate virulent necrotic strains.

Darkmaster Gandling. Darkmaster Gandling is the mortal headmaster of Scholomance, overseeing the instruction and training of necromancers for the Cult of the Damned. Operating from the depths of the ruined Keep of Caer Darrow, he serves the Scourge by orchestrating gruesome magical experiments upon the living and dead alike. Within the dark halls beneath Caer Darrow, Darkmaster Gandling governs Scholomance, the premier academy for the Scourge's aspiring necromancers. A living human serving the Cult of the Damned, Gandling worked alongside the lich Ras Frostwhisper to orchestrate atrocities against countless innocent captives taken from the surrounding lands. Students who enter his classrooms are instructed in plague brewing, reanimation, and flesh sculpting.

Darkmist Cavern. Darkmist Cavern is an abandoned mine tucked into northwestern Dustwallow Marsh, completely infested with predatory giant spiders. Crumbling ruins outside hint at an unfortunate former settlement swallowed up by the marsh's hazards. Locals remain divided on whether the cavern gave its name to the arachnids or the reverse. Situated in the northwest reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Darkmist Cavern appears to have once been an active mining venture. Today, any human presence has long vanished, leaving behind rotting, ruined shacks outside the entrance and a network of tunnels choked with thick webs. The cavern is overrun by Darkmist spiders, predatory horrors whose venom and size make the tunnels deadly to unwary wanderers. Marsh dwellers still dispute whether the cavern was named after the foul brood nesting inside or if the spiders took the title from the misty cave itself.

Darkshire. In Darkshire, the Night Watch holds the line as the town endures Duskwood's unnatural gloom. Stormwind offers little aid, leaving the people to guard their homes. Darkshire was once the peaceful woodland settlement of Grand Hamlet. The Old Horde razed it during the First War, and the village was rebuilt. After Medivh fell at Karazhan, the death throes left in the surrounding woods turned them into the shadowed wilderness of Duskwood. Though Darkshire belongs to the Kingdom of Stormwind, the crown sends virtually no aid to its town hall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled. Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council are left to govern on their own, enforcing harsh, insular justice in the shadows.

Darkshire Town Hall. Darkshire Town Hall anchors a town besieged by darkness and undead. Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke and his council govern from its dim halls. Darkshire Town Hall stands just west of the main square, where the town's leaders meet to govern an increasingly isolated territory. Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke struggles to keep order and protect the people while Stormwind sends little military aid. Clerk Daltry and other officials track town records and the travelers who brave Duskwood's dangerous roads. With danger all around, keeping those ledgers current is a grim task.

Darkshore Grouper. Along Darkshore, grouper are a familiar catch, though murloc attacks have driven fishermen from their boats. The fish is prized for food and sport, and a good haul is harder to find. Darkshore Grouper are a welcome catch in the cold waters off Darkshore. Anglers around Auberdine value them for the simple dishes they make, and travelers and residents alike enjoy those meals. A fishing line and basic gear are enough to bring one in. For many fishermen, the pleasure of catching a grouper matches the pleasure of eating it.

Darksoul Shackle. In Silverpine Forest, Moonrage Darksouls wear enchanted fetters forged under Archmage Arugal’s direction. Forsaken mages at the Sepulcher seek them to learn how the magic gripping the region can be undone. Archmage Arugal’s magic could not fully command or sustain the worgen he unleashed upon Silverpine Forest. He bound enchanted implements such as Darksoul Shackles to the beasts to make up for that failing. The fetters channel outside sorcery into the Moonrage Darksouls, strengthening them and anchoring the curse that keeps them thrall to Shadowfang Keep.

Darkspear Islands Clash. Darkspear Islands Clash is an Alliance military call to arms urging champions to defend vital ground against fierce Darkspear Raiders. Without immediate support on the front lines, the Alliance risks losing the contested archipelago entirely. The struggle for control of the Darkspear Islands has erupted into open war between the Alliance and aggressive warbands of Darkspear Raiders. Alliance commanders warning that without urgent reinforcements, their foothold in the archipelago will be overwhelmed, have sounded a call to arms for capable champions to stem the hostile tide.

Darkspear Islands Clash. Darkspear Islands Clash calls upon fighters to rally their companions and defeat the hostile Darkspear Raiders contesting the archipelago. The ongoing battle demands coordinated action to stem enemy incursions across the contested island chain. The Darkspear Islands Clash represents an active military push within the contested Darkspear Islands. Forces deployed to the theater are urged to stand fast against waves of Darkspear Raiders who continue to wage skirmishes across the beaches and interior grounds. Rather than an isolated incident, the clash forms part of a sustained campaign to secure foothold territory in the archipelago.

Darkspear Strand. At Darkspear Strand, the tribe’s refuge begins on Durotar’s southern coast. The trolls came ashore after exile from the Echo Isles and built Sen'jin Village nearby under Vol'jin’s leadership. The Darkspear trolls came ashore here after losing the Echo Isles. When witch doctor Zalazane seized their home, survivors crossed the narrow waters and landed on this coast. They gathered just yards inland rather than scatter into Durotar’s hostile red wastes, and built Sen'jin Village. The strand looks across the surf toward the islands they still hope to reclaim.

Darkspear tribe. The Darkspear are a tribe of jungle trolls who joined Thrall's Horde after being driven from their ancestral home in Stranglethorn Vale and rescued from a sea witch in the Great Sea. Led by Shadow Hunter Vol'jin from their temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village, they now serve as core members of the Horde across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite their alliance, they currently struggle to reclaim their new home, the Echo Isles, from the traitorous witch doctor Zalazane. Originally a smaller, less ruthless tribe within the broken Gurubashi Empire of Stranglethorn Vale, the Darkspear endured centuries of warfare and famine against brutal neighbors like the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes. Driven out to sea, they settled on remote islands, only to face aquatic murlocs, Kul Tiran sailors, and a naga sea witch. Their elder chieftain, Sen'jin, was captured and slain in dark sacrificial rites beneath the sea, but before dying he foretold that the orc Warchief Thrall would lead the Darkspear to a new destiny. Rescued by Thrall's passing fleet, the survivors pledged their undying loyalty to the new Horde and sailed westward to Kalimdor.

Darkwhisper Gorge. Darkwhisper Gorge is a treacherous, demon-infested ravine carved into the southern heights of Winterspring. When Archimonde was destroyed at the climax of the Third War, remnants of the shattered Burning Legion fled down the slopes of Mount Hyjal and entrenched themselves in these jagged chasms. Today, powerful fiends stalk its heights, guarding ancient minerals and dark planar relics. Following the defeat of Archimonde atop Mount Hyjal, surviving demons of the Burning Legion scattered into the surrounding mountain ranges. A disciplined vanguard took refuge in Darkwhisper Gorge, transforming the southern border of Winterspring into a lethal stronghold. Led by Hederine demons—including lethal manastalkers, slayers, and initiates under Lady Hederine—these fiends fiercely defend their subterranean tunnels and fiery camps. Beyond the immediate threat of its elite inhabitants, an ominous, sealed archway stands at the gorge's lowest point, hinting at sealed passages leading higher up the sacred mountain.

Darn Talongrip. Near Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip watches the Stonetalon frontier. The orc scout tracks threats in the crags and carries word between forward outposts and Horde commanders. Darn Talongrip watches the rugged climbs into Stonetalon from the southern Barrens. At Malaka'jin, he directs recruits toward the Horde's new fronts in Ashenvale. Travelers climbing into the contested peaks can reach the Horde through his post.

Darnassus. Darnassus rises among Teldrassil’s high boughs as the kaldorei capital and refuge. Its tranquil waters and groves make it the night elves’ spiritual heart and the Alliance’s primary bastion on northern Kalimdor. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Fandral Staghelm guide their people through the trials of newfound mortality. Darnassus took shape after the Third War, honoring the night elves’ survival after they lost the immortality granted by their sacred World Tree, Nordrassil. Unlike the stone cities of Ironforge and Stormwind, it is an open, tranquil settlement of wood-crafted lodges, glowing shrines, and arched bridges over crystalline lakes. Vigilant Sentinels, towering ancients of war, and druids who shape trees watch the paths and preserve nature’s quiet within the city.

Darnassus Marzipan. At Hallow's End, Darnassus innkeepers hand out festive marzipan to visitors who dance for it. Crafted in the night elven capital for the autumn celebration, this sweet is one of four treats Jesper needs. During Hallow's End, Alliance capitals share a tradition of lighthearted trick-or-treating. Dwarves offer sharp mints, Stormwind makes chewy nougat, and Darnassus innkeepers prepare delicate marzipan for visitors. To receive a piece, you must show some festive spirit and dance when the innkeeper asks. The sweet is one of four regional treats sought by Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind's Cathedral Square who cannot go out to collect sweets himself.

Darrow Hill. In northern Hillsbrad, Darrow Hill's rugged grassland rises beneath the Headland. Mountain lions and stags roam its open slopes, while feral yetis lurk in the Foothill Caverns. Alterac Granite draws travelers into this dangerous frontier. Darrow Hill stretches below the Headland, joining southern Hillsbrad's rolling pasture to Alterac's jagged, colder heights. Mountain lions and stags move through tall grasses on its rocky slopes, and towering yetis emerge from the Foothill Caverns. The cavern walls hold deposits of dense Alterac Granite, drawing quarry workers, miners, and adventurers into danger. Regional claims remain contentious, and travelers of either faction can be caught unaware on the trails.

Darrowmere Lake. Darrowmere Lake is an expansive freshwater lake situated in the southeastern reaches of the Western Plaguelands. At its heart lies the fortress island of Caer Darrow, whose ruined halls conceal the Cult of the Damned's dread necromantic academy, Scholomance. Darrowmere Lake is among the largest inland bodies of water in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by the blight-stricken forests of Lordaeron and fed by the Thondroril and Darrowmere rivers. During the Second War, these deep waters saw intense naval skirmishes between the Horde and Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde also struck the island fortress of Caer Darrow at the lake's heart, sacking it and carrying off its ancient runestone. Once a thriving waterway and trade artery for the House of Barov, the lake is now a grim, mist-veiled basin in the heart of the Plaguelands.

Darrowshire. Darrowshire is a ruined village in the southern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands, once a peaceful hamlet of Lordaeron. During the Third War, its residents mounted a desperate, tragic stand against an overwhelming Scourge force. Today, only shattered timbers, restless spirits, and bitter memories linger amid the silence. Before the plague consumed northern Lordaeron, Darrowshire was a humble rural settlement nestled beneath the southern cliffs. When the Scourge marched south during the Third War, a force led by the death knight Marduk Blackpool and the ghoul lord Horgus the Ravager besieged the town. The villagers and local defenders fought valiantly, momentarily holding the line against impossible odds. Ultimately, the defense collapsed, and the town was slaughtered down to the last soul. Rather than finding peace in death, many of Darrowshire's fallen defenders were reanimated as ghouls to bolster the Scourge's ranks, leaving the village an eerie, empty memorial of lost valor.

Darsok Swiftdagger. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern trails for threats. The orc scout directs Horde fighters against Witchwing harpies in the Dry Hills, whose raids endanger travelers and settlements. He is also an old friend of Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin. Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern scrubland from the Crossroads. The roads linking Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens’ northern reaches face raiders and centaur, as well as organized hunters from the sky. Darsok’s anger falls on the Witchwing harpies. Their roosts lie in the Dry Hills, northwest of the Forgotten Pools, where they threaten caravans traveling north.

name.frFR: Recommandation portant le sceau de Darthalia

text.enUS: Darthalia's Sealed Commendation. At Tarren Mill, Darthalia sends word of victories against Hillsbrad's humans to Undercity's high command. After the fighting across the Hillsbrad Foothills, High Executor Darthalia seals a dispatch recording victories against Hillsbrad's human defenders and the ruin of their positions. She addresses it to Varimathras, the dreadlord who advises Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. In the Royal Quarter, the report gives Forsaken leaders proof that Alliance enclaves south of Lordaeron can be broken, leaving northern garrisons free to face the Scourge.

Daryl the Youngling. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling tests his hunting skill among veteran dwarven trackers. He challenges travelers to prove their marksmanship against Loch Modan's beasts. Farstrider Lodge shelters dwarven mountaineers, trackers, and seasoned outdoorsmen who watch over Loch Modan's wilderness. Daryl is a young human trying to earn a place among them. He measures his hunting instincts against other travelers, challenging them to hunt the tough wild boars and beasts that roam the crags and lakeshore.

Dashel Stonefist. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist is known for his quick temper and heavy hands. The dwarf called Fist keeps to Stormwind City's rougher alleys, where dangerous connections draw the attention of covert investigators. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist is known as Fist for the street fights that have earned him the name. Locals and city guards see a drunken, combative dwarf ready to throw a punch outside a tavern. His place in the district puts him at the nexus of Stormwind's underworld, where smugglers, cutpurses, and political agitators trade coin and rumors beyond the eyes of Cathedral Square.

Data Hoarders. Jemma Quikswitch needs her lost punch cards found in the snow outside Gnomeregan. The exiled gnome in Ironforge copied her family's archives onto cards during the flight from the city. Now several are missing, along with records of submarine designs and family recipes. When troggs invaded Gnomeregan and radiation struck, thousands of gnomes fled with what they could carry. Jemma Quikswitch had copied generations of family knowledge onto punch cards. A damaged satchel spilled several cards into the snow around the fallen city. Without them, the surviving records read as gibberish, and her family's knowledge is at risk of being lost.

Data Rescue. In Gnomeregan, the fallen city's records lie beyond troggs and radiation. Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge sends you to recover a Prismatic Punch Card through the terminals' layers of clearance. Gnomeregan's fall to troggs and radiation drove its people from the city, leaving centuries of research, schematics, and civic records behind. Matrix Punchograph terminals still line its technological corridors, managing security clearance and storing files. Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge's Tinker Town wants those punch-encoded archives recovered from the city's depths.

David Trias. In Deathknell, David Trias trains the newly awakened Forsaken. He teaches stealth and bladecraft so they can serve Queen Sylvanas and the Forsaken. David Trias trains newly risen undead among Deathknell’s tombstones and ruins. He seeks those with a talent for killing unseen. For the fledgling Forsaken, survival calls for more than strength at arms; it calls for precise strikes from the dark. Trias deciphers orders and teaches initiates to wield daggers, hide their movements, and use their reanimated reflexes with lethal precision against the living and the Scourge.

Dawn in the Mountains. Dawn in the Mountains is a quest to deliver a shipment of holy candles to Father Gavin at Misty Pine Refuge. A gentle priest of the Argent Dawn, Gavin maintains this mountain shelter to heal and comfort weary travelers rather than wage war with weapons. While many within the Argent Dawn take up arms to purge unholy horrors from Azeroth, some choose the gentler calling of the Light. Father Gavin, a priest dwelling in the rugged mountain wilderness, has turned away from the blade to focus wholly on healing the afflicted and tending to the weary. Taking an abandoned structure, he restored it into Misty Pine Refuge, a safe stop for travelers facing the perils of the high passes.

Dawning Isles. The Dawning Isles lie blighted beneath the Vile Fin murlocs’ growing numbers. Along Silverpine Forest’s eastern edge, the islets rise from Lordamere Lake, where the Plague of Undeath has left their shores rotting. The Dawning Isles lie under the Vile Fin murlocs’ claim. Before the Third War, these keys rested amid Lordamere Lake’s calm, clear waters. When the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, corruption spread through the shallows. The vegetation turned pallid and rotting, and the islands lost their former peace. Now the Vile Fin murlocs hold the muddy shores and tangled brush. They defend their growing colonies against anyone who tries to cross the lake.

Dawning Wood Catacombs. Undead fill the Dawning Wood Catacombs beneath Raven Hill Cemetery in western Duskwood. Their stone tunnels hold skeletal guards and ravenous ghouls. The Dawning Wood Catacombs lie beneath the ruined Raven Hill Cemetery. Before the twilight curse came over the forest, the dead of the surrounding woods rested in these stone corridors. Now the catacombs hold some of the region’s deadliest undead, and their depths are dangerous for lone travelers. Two subterranean wings divide the catacombs. Ranks of animated skeletons guard ancestral tombs in the western passages. To the east, the tunnels descend into a foul warren overrun by ravenous, disease-bearing ghouls.

Dawnwatcher Selgorm. At the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Selgorm watches for threats across northern Kalimdor. The human serves the Argent Dawn as an observer and liaison in the night elven capital, tracking reports of shadowy cult activity and dark powers stirring nearby. Dawnwatcher Selgorm keeps watch in Darnassus for the Argent Dawn. The order's fight against the undead Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands does not end its vigilance elsewhere. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, Selgorm gathers reports of emerging threats in Kalimdor's wilds. He connects the night elves with the wider effort against ancient evil and seeks Alliance travelers able to strike at cultists and dark powers before their influence spreads.

Dawnwatcher Shaedlass. In Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass keeps watch for the Argent Dawn across Kalimdor. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, he seeks word of his fellow order members sent to scout hostile lands. The Argent Dawn fights the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands, yet its watch reaches beyond Lordaeron. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass keeps the order's interests in Kalimdor from the night elf capital of Darnassus. At his post on the Craftsmen's Terrace, he follows covert expeditions against dark cults and corrupting powers that threaten the wider world.

Dazalar. In Dolanaar, Dazalar trains young night elf hunters for the wilds of Teldrassil. He teaches them to aim true and form bonds with the beasts of the great boughs. Dazalar trains young hunters in Dolanaar after they leave Shadowglen. Night elf rangers and sentinels patrol the wilderness, and he teaches newcomers the patience and discipline needed to protect Teldrassil's fragile ecosystem.

Dead Acre. The Dead Acre lies burned and abandoned in southeastern Westfall, near the bridge to Duskwood. The Defias Brotherhood torched the farm during their uprising, and rogue harvest golems now stalk its blackened fields. You find the Dead Acre just north of the road from Sentinel Hill to Duskwood. Once a productive homestead among Westfall’s breadbasket farms, it met a violent end when the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt and drove out the local landowners. The farm and its crops went up in flames. Scorched timber and smoking earth remain, while mechanical Harvest Watchers still reap the barren soil.

Dead Field. Forsaken assaults falter at Dead Field, a ruined farmstead in northern Silverpine Forest. Rot Hide gnolls serve the Scourge there, while the banshee Nightlash turns back those who attack. The ruined farmstead lies in northern Silverpine Forest, its human occupants lost to the Third War. Rot Hide gnolls now use the plot as a base and willingly serve the Scourge. Deathstalker scouts passing through the region have noted signs of imminent military mobilization that threatens Forsaken supply lines and outposts. Small Forsaken assaults on the farm have repeatedly failed. Each time the gnolls are endangered, Nightlash, a wailing banshee, appears and drives the attackers back.

Dead-tooth Jack. A stolen badge puts Marshal Haggard's authority in Defias hands. The retired officer lives in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his official insignia. Jack wore a Stormwind tabard in the dark and posed as Marshal Dughan. Haggard needs the badge back before the Defias Brotherhood can use it to impersonate Stormwind officials. Marshal Haggard lives in an isolated cottage on Elwynn's eastern ridges. One night, a figure in a Stormwind tabard approached, claiming official business and asking for Haggard's old marshal's badge. Believing he was handing it to a fellow officer, Haggard complied. The stranger laughed in his face and vanished into the woods. The thief was a Defias rogue called Dead-tooth Jack.

Deadeye Shore. Deadeye Shore lies windswept along Durotar’s eastern edge, east of Drygulch Ravine. Named for Kilrogg Deadeye, the Bleeding Hollow chieftain, its barren sands are roamed by raptors, scorpids, and feral boars. Deadeye Shore runs beneath central Durotar’s red bluffs, with sand and rocky outcrops that faintly resemble a skull missing an eye socket. The coast takes its name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed Bleeding Hollow chieftain who fought in the First and Second Wars. No major settlement or military outpost holds the shore. It is far from peaceful: aggressive wildlife rules the sands, and Burning Blade cultists from nearby ravine hideouts have been seen prowling toward the water.

Deadman's Crossing. Deadman's Crossing is an ominous junction set within the bleak canyon of Deadwind Pass. Branching between Duskwood, the Swamp of Sorrows, and the haunted tower of Karazhan, it serves as a grim threshold marked by gallows and warning signs. Despite its gruesome appearance, the path remains a vital thoroughfare for travelers moving across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Situated at the eastern crossroads of Deadwind Pass, Deadman's Crossing links the shadows of Duskwood with the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows, while a foreboding southern track ascends toward the haunted tower of Karazhan. The crossing takes its name from the twisted hangman's tree planted at the road's fork, where a pair of rotting corpses dangle overhead as a stark warning to all who pass. Beside the tree, battered wooden signs offer blunt advice to travelers, urging them to turn back and abandon hope. The canyon itself is thick with hostile beasts and dark sorceries, yet travelers moving steadfastly along the packed dirt road will find the crossing itself oddly unmolested, so long as they do not wander into the blighted rocks.

Deadmines. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines lie silent under a ruined town in Westfall. Once the greatest gold producer in human lands, the mines were abandoned during the First War. Now rumors speak of sinister forces in the forgotten shafts, though their danger remains unknown. The Deadmines once led all human mines in gold, with Whitestone oak for timber and supports. When the orcish Horde pushed north, miners fled in haste. Sir Anduin Lothar entered the treacherous depths to recover the sacred Tome of Divinity. Subterranean ogres held him captive for twenty months before rescuers freed him. After the kingdom fell, the shafts went quiet, and people came to say they were cursed.

Deadmire. In Dustwallow Marsh, Deadmire suffers in the waterways north of the Stonemaul Ruins. Melor Stonehoof sends hunters from Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff to track the ancient crocolisk and bring back a tooth as proof. The hunt teaches tracking and mercy. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof teaches promising trackers the spiritual traditions of the hunt. Tauren hunters seek reverence and a bond with the natural world, not slaughter or trophies. Melor sends you east to Dustwallow Marsh to find Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk whose long life has become a burden.

Deadmire's Tooth. In Dustwallow Marsh, Deadmire stalks the murky waters, and his tooth marks an honorable hunt. Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff receives it as proof that the ancient crocolisk's suffering has ended. Tauren hunters on Hunter Rise see the hunt as a bond of balance, reverence, and mercy. Deadmire was once among the most magnificent crocolisks in Dustwallow Marsh. Great age turned his final years to torment, though he kept the fierce spirit of his prime. His massive bones and failing body had become a prison of pain. Deadmire's Tooth gives Melor Stonehoof proof that an honorable hunt has ended the beast's suffering.

Deadwood Village. Deadwood Village is a furbolg encampment nestled in southern Felwood. Once a peaceful clan attuned to nature, its residents fell victim to the demonic corruption that blighted the surrounding forest. Driven mad by fel taint, the Deadwood furbolgs now attack anyone who approaches their crude wooden settlement. Situated near the southern border of Felwood, Deadwood Village serves as the primary enclave of the Deadwood tribe. When the Burning Legion's demonic energies washed through the ancient woodlands, the furbolgs lacked the power to resist the creeping rot. Their minds warped by fel malice, they abandoned their ancient traditions and spiritual harmony. Today, the village is a squalid gathering of hostile brutes, shamans, and den watchers who violently defend their polluted grounds against intruders, earning the despair of their uncorrupted cousins, the Timbermaw.

Death Cap. In Darkshore, Death Cap grows in the cave behind Cliffspring Falls. Night elf herbalists seek the scarce fungus, but the Grove of the Ancients warns against approaching the falls. Death Cap grows in the damp cave behind Cliffspring Falls, along Darkshore's northeastern mountain ridges. Scaber stalks carpet the cavern floor, but Death Cap is scarce. Night elf herbalists such as Barithras Moonshade value it for experimental brewing. Finding even one means entering a cavern the Grove of the Ancients warns against, where corruption is taking root.
