text.enUS: Death From Below. In the Arathi Highlands, Shakes O'Breen expects the Daggerspine naga to attack from the sea, and the crew cannot sail home to Booty Bay without O'Breen's knowledge of the waters. You stay aboard beside O'Breen, man the cannon and drive the naga back. After Sunken Treasure, Shakes O'Breen sees the Daggerspines gathering to attack. Naga have a name for ruthlessness and will keep coming until O'Breen is dead. O'Breen does not value their own life above those of the crew, but asks you to defend them, since the crew cannot reach Booty Bay without that knowledge of the seas. You wait aboard with O'Breen for the naga to come from the water.

Deathguard Bartholomew. In Brill, Deathguard Bartholomew keeps watch over the town and helps travelers find their way. He helps keep order among the Forsaken defenders of Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Bartholomew keeps watch in Brill, part of the Forsaken guard defending Tirisfal Glades. Like other Deathguards, he protects reclaimed land from the lingering Scourge, fanatical Scarlet Crusaders, and other threats to Lady Sylvanas's domain. He also guides travelers around the town and helps keep order among the newly risen.

Deathguard Burgess. In Brill, Deathguard Burgess keeps watch over the town for the Forsaken. He guards the settlement and points travelers toward the services they need. North of the Undercity, Deathguard Burgess guards Brill against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade. Like other Deathguards in Tirisfal Glades, he guides arriving Forsaken to local tradesfolk, class trainers, and civic services, helping keep the vulnerable outpost running.

Deathguard Dillinger. At Brill's edge, Deathguard Dillinger watches the town and guides newly arrived Forsaken. He also sends recruits against the Scourge remnants threatening the nearby farms and mills. Deathguard Dillinger guards Brill and guides those arriving from Deathknell. At the town entrance, he points newly awakened undead toward the inn, town hall, and local trainers. They must learn their way through a changed life under the Dark Lady's rule.

Deathguard Humbert. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Humbert watches the Alliance presence in Hillsbrad. The Forsaken sentry has lost his military gear to dwarves from Dun Garok. Deathguard Humbert watches Dun Garok from a hidden camp for High Executor Darthalia. One morning, he left to gather firewood. Dwarven scouts from Dun Garok took his prized sword and other equipment while he was away. Now he must recover his arms and save his pride before high command learns what happened.

Deathguard Linnea. At a roadside post in southeastern Tirisfal, Deathguard Linnea watches the roads between Brill and the eastern borders. Her unit guards against the Scarlet Crusade and the lingering Scourge, with passing travelers sometimes helping on patrol. Deathguard Linnea guards a fortified post southeast of Brill. The Forsaken defend their young realm against Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and Scourge still prowling the wilderness. Linnea and her fellow guards patrol the road and coordinate reports with Magistrate Sevren in Brill. Their watch keeps the eastern road toward the Bulwark secure.

Deathguard Samsa. In Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa watches the tense frontier and sends travelers against threats near the settlement. Deathguard Samsa keeps watch in Tarren Mill, where the Forsaken hold their ground in the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Horde sentries face pressure from Alliance outposts such as Southshore and from savage local wildlife. Samsa guards the perimeter and directs capable adventurers against threats before they endanger the encampment.

Deathguard Simmer. At Deathknell’s edge, Deathguard Simmer sizes up newly risen Forsaken. He sends them west to raid a human pumpkin farm patrolled by the Scarlet Crusade, gathering reagents Brill’s apothecaries need. Deathguard Simmer guards the ground just outside Deathknell, where the Forsaken hold the line between their haven and Tirisfal Glades. Living humans roam the region, including the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, who see all undead as abominations to purge with fire and blade. Simmer tests newly risen Forsaken by sending them west to Solliden Farmstead. Scarlet Crusade soldiers patrol from a nearby tower. The recruits must steal ten pumpkins and carry them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

Deaths in the Family. Coleman Farthing, once a mill worker, seeks vengeance from Brill against the Agamand family. During the Third War, he stayed to defend their estate with his fellow workers, and they died beside their stubborn masters. The Agamands rose again as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential farming family. Their mills and fertile pastures yielded grain through the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crossed Lordaeron, the family refused to flee or abandon its ancestral lands. They believed their stone walls and loyal workers could hold back the horrors advancing from the east.

Deathstalker Faerleia. Deep inside Pyrewood Village, Deathstalker Faerleia works against its leaders. From the town hall, she directs covert strikes against the Pyrewood Council, the puppets Arugal uses to rule the village.

Deathstalker Lesh. At Southpoint Tower, Deathstalker Lesh watches the human farms in the Hillsbrad Foothills. She serves High Executor Darthalia and gauges when the Forsaken should strike. From Southpoint Tower, Deathstalker Lesh watches the human farmers and town militia in the nearby Hillsbrad Fields. The tower stands on the southern road through the Hillsbrad Foothills. Lesh belongs to the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken's covert network of scouts, spies, and assassins. She tracks enemy movements and numbers for High Executor Darthalia in Tarren Mill. When the moment is right, Lesh sends Darthalia a coded message: “The raven's cry from the west doth beckon.” The words signal that Hillsbrad is ripe for the Forsaken's attack.

Deathstalker Report. Deathstalker Rane Yorick sends word of Scourge resistance in Silverpine Forest to High Executor Hadrec. Deathstalkers Rane Yorick and Quinn Yorick faced a deadly ambush in northern Silverpine Forest. Pinned down by Scourge in the pine woods, they gathered their findings into a hurried dispatch. It describes stronger resistance than the Forsaken expected as they seek to claim the region. Quinn was grievously injured, so Rane entrusted the report to passing allies, who must carry it to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher without delay.

Deathstalker Vincent. Inside Shadowfang Keep, Deathstalker Vincent lies slain by Arugal. The Forsaken scout entered the stronghold with Deathstalker Adamant to learn its defenses, but the mission ended before the Forsaken could attack. The Deathstalkers needed to learn Shadowfang Keep’s layout before the Forsaken could assault it. Vincent and Adamant slipped past the barricades into the fortress. Their mission failed: Adamant was captured and locked in a dungeon cell, while Vincent was brought before the keep’s master. Vincent refused to serve Arugal or yield to him. The mage executed him, leaving his body on the stone floor.

text.enUS: Deathstalkers in Shadowfang. In Shadowfang Keep, Deathstalkers Adamant and Vincent have gone missing. High Executor Hadrec sends Horde adventurers inside to find the reconnaissance agents. Their intelligence is needed to prepare a Forsaken assault against Archmage Arugal and his worgen packs. Silverpine Forest remains contested, and Archmage Arugal's worgen hold Shadowfang Keep. The Forsaken at the Sepulcher seek to break his siege on their southern borders. High Executor Hadrec sent Deathstalkers Adamant and Vincent into the fortress to chart its defenses. Days pass without word, and Hadrec grows desperate for their reports. He sends Horde champions into the stronghold to recover the agents and salvage the operation.

Deathwing. Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth. Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation.

Decoy!. Narain Soothfancy has a plan for the ransom: a sack of rocks in place of money, and you in place of him. You carry his disguise to the handover spot the booknappers set down in Winterspring. This follows the ransom letter. The ransom note said Narain should make the delivery himself, and he means to, after a fashion. He fills a sack with rocks, looks you up and down, and decides you will do. His special kit holds a turban, a robe and the sack, and you carry it to the handover spot the booknappers set down in Winterspring. When the booknappers show up for the goods, Narain wants them snuffed out, as a lesson in what comes of crossing him.

Decrepit Ferry. At the Decrepit Ferry, broken docks leave Fenris Isle cut off across Lordamere Lake. The Scourge killed the ferryman and wrecked the boats, and undead and Rot Hide gnolls now overrun the shore. Before the Third War, daily traffic crossed Lordamere Lake from this dock. Local farmers brought fresh produce to the water and sold it to the wealthy lord of Fenris Isle and his household. For a modest fee, the ferryman carried trade goods, messengers, and visiting nobles between the mainland and the keep. That commerce ended when the Scourge swept through the kingdom. The ferryman was brutally killed, the boats were smashed, and the pier fell into decay.

text.enUS: Deep Cover. Shenthul sends a promising Horde rogue to Sludge Fen to contact an agent hidden among the Venture Company. The Shattered Hand has spent a year placing Taskmaster Fizzule inside the company’s drilling grounds, where he watches their plans. The Shattered Hand protects Orgrimmar’s interests through secret intelligence and assassination. For a year, its members worked to place an agent in the Venture Company’s ranks. Taskmaster Fizzule earned a place at their drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen, among the company’s mercenaries.

Deep Elem Mine. Deep Elem Mine lies in central Silverpine Forest, its tunnels claimed by worgen. Once an active mine, it fell when Archmage Arugal's magic swept through the region and transformed its miners. Deep Elem Mine once supplied the living people of Lordaeron with ore. When Archmage Arugal unleashed his lupine curse across Silverpine Forest, it spread through the tunnels. The laborers succumbed and became vicious worgen, abandoning their pickaxes to claim the cavern as a lair.

Deep Ocean, Vast Sea. North of Auberdine, the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil lie beneath the waves. Murlocs ambushed both night elf vessels as they sailed into port, and their surviving crews seek a way to mourn their lost captains. Murlocs overwhelmed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as the ships approached Auberdine. Both vessels sank in the shallows north of the settlement. Their surviving crews reached shore, but the loss of the ships and their captains weighs on the port.

Deep Sea Salvage. Following Land Ho!, First Mate Nilzlix asks you to bring back the charts and logs of two sunken ships before anyone leaves the cove. O'Breen led three ships into the cove, certain the treasure lay here. The Harbinger docked safely. Then, as the Maiden's Folly with the Spirit of Silverpine came in, the tides began to lower, and both ships ran aground on a temple-like structure in the reef and sank fast.

Deepfury's Orders. Beneath the Thandol Span, Deepfury's Orders lie with the fallen Ol' Rustlocke. The crumpled parchment carries grim instructions from the Dark Iron dwarves who ambushed the scouting defender. Ol' Rustlocke, a dwarven bridge defender, was scouting the foundations of the Thandol Span when Dark Iron dwarves cornered and slew him. Beside his clenched fist lay crumpled orders drafted by their leader, Deepfury. The parchment is direct proof of a coordinated plot against the bridge linking the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands.

Deepmoss Egg. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Deepmoss Eggs draw goblin merchants from Ratchet. Deepmoss spiders lay clustered clutches in the crags and canyons, and Booty Bay pirates prize them for omelettes. Deepmoss spiders nest across the Stonetalon Mountains, especially in Sishir Canyon and beneath the surviving trees of Windshear Crag. They leave clustered clutches of viable eggs in thick webbed sacks, sheltered by damp mountain moss. Most travelers have little use for them, but goblin traders see a chance to profit.

Deepmoss Spider Eggs. Mebok Mizzyrix sees a chance to sell Deepmoss Spider Eggs to Booty Bay. Spider egg omelettes have become a craze there, and he sends travelers into the Stonetalon Mountains to gather fresh clutches for the overseas trade. Booty Bay’s wealthy patrons and eccentric pirates have taken to spider egg omelettes, driving demand for rare ingredients across the Great Sea. Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix sees a chance to make a fortune by supplying the southern port. The Eastern Kingdoms have no supply of these spiders, so Mebok looks to Kalimdor’s wilderness for the eggs.

text.enUS: Deeprun Rat Roundup. Deeprun Rat Roundup is an Alliance task in the Deeprun Tram where players assist Monty with pest control. Using a charming musical flute, players round up living Deeprun rats to supply Monty's brother with fresh meat for rat kabobs. Down in the subterranean tube of the Deeprun Tram, a colorful character named Monty struggles to keep the underground transit line clear of pests. Speaking in salty sea slang and treating the tramway like a ship's deck, Monty enlists passing travelers to help round up the scurrying vermin infesting the station.

Deeprun Tram. The Deeprun Tram carries travelers beneath the earth between Ironforge and Stormwind City. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned it after the Second War, and its twin tracks now carry citizens, soldiers, and goods between the Alliance capitals. King Magni Bronzebeard wanted dwarven aid and supplies to reach Stormwind faster after the Second War. Mountain passes slowed the journey, so he asked High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design an underground railway. Gnomish engineers cut the route beneath a mountain and through a vast subterranean lake. Rats plagued the excavation, but the tram was completed. It carries thousands of travelers between Ironforge and Stormwind without charge.

Deepwater Tavern. At Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern gives travelers a place to rest and find work. The inn is a meeting spot and resupply stop, where harbor rumors mingle with the chance of a brawl. In Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern shelters travelers from the marsh's rain and difficult roads. Sailors, dockworkers, merchants, and weary adventurers gather beneath its timber beams to trade news, meet, warm themselves, and patch their wounds. Local merchants and a resident first aid trainer serve those bound for the marsh or setting out across the Great Sea. The tavern is lively, and disputes over spilled ale can turn into brawls. Tapoke 'Slim' Jahn is known to spark them.

Defeat Nek'rosh. In the Wetlands, the Alliance campaign against the Dragonmaw reaches its final strike. With their siege engines sabotaged, the defenders turn on Chieftain Nek'rosh to secure Menethil Harbor. His severed head must be brought to Captain Stoutfist to break the threat to the coastal port. The Dragonmaw have long plagued the marshlands of Khaz Modan, entrenched in fortified camps and threatening Menethil Harbor's sea lanes. After discovering and burning the clan's catapults, the marsh's defenders strike at the warband's leader. Chieftain Nek'rosh commands the local orcs and remains the last obstacle to breaking the siege. His death leaves the remaining raiders without their leader's direction.

Defias Brotherhood. The Defias Brotherhood is a widespread criminal network of bandits, brigands, and assassins waging an underground insurgency against the Kingdom of Stormwind. Their origins are a mystery to most, and they have grown into violent outlaws terrorizing the southern farmlands. From a hidden redoubt, they aim to overthrow the corrupt House of Nobles and lay waste to the kingdom.

Defias Docket. Defias operatives have hidden their orders at Addle's Stead in western Duskwood. The docket gives Stormwind's search for its missing emissary a lead into the Brotherhood's plans. Master Elling Trias points investigators toward Duskwood as they follow leads on the kingdom's missing diplomat. Watcher Backus has noted unusual Defias movements converging on Addle's Stead, the derelict farm south of the road from Westfall. A strongbox on the property holds the Defias Docket. Its records track the Brotherhood's movements, revealing work that reaches beyond highway robbery and local banditry.
Defias Hideout. Defias thugs and vagrants linger in a ruined house on Moonbrook’s southern edge. Its upper floor hides a route into the chambers beneath the town.

Defias Tower Key. At Klaven's Tower in Westfall, the Defias Tower Key proves an infiltrator reached the guarded perimeter. Stormwind operatives seek it from the malformed drones outside. Klaven's Tower stands on the Westfall coast as a Defias Brotherhood stronghold. Recent shipments from Duskwood brought new guards to its perimeter: malformed Defias drones, undead and covered in spikes. SI:7 operatives watch the grounds and direct field agents to pick the pockets of these sentries. Fighting them head-on is not the way to prove the perimeter has been breached. The key shows an infiltrator got through without raising an alarm.

Deino. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Deino trains Horde mages in the arcane arts. She teaches spellcasters to master arcane and elemental forces, and sends seasoned mages across Kalimdor to study ancient magic and seek remote tutors. Deino trains Horde mages in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Totems, huts, and quiet waters surround the raised platforms where she teaches. Troll spellcasters balance spiritual reverence with arcane mastery, a path Deino shares with fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo.

Delgren the Purifier. At Maestra's Post, Delgren the Purifier aids the night elves against demonic and shadow magic on Ashenvale's northern edge. He works with Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand to guard the frontier. Delgren the Purifier keeps watch over travelers heading south from Auberdine. Human paladins are rare in Kalimdor's ancient forests, but he came west with a band of holy warriors from the Argent Dawn. They set out to help the Alliance's new night elf allies face demons and undead remnants left by the Third War. Delgren is stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, where that danger reaches the road.

Deliah's Ring. A grim trail begins with Deliah's Ring, found among the Rot Hide gnolls’ corpse piles in Silverpine Forest. Its inscription, “For Deliah,” points back to a plague victim taken from Tirisfal’s mass graves. Among the gnoll mounds in Silverpine Forest, a ring rests on the pockmarked hand of a relatively fresh corpse. The band bears a simple inscription: “For Deliah.” The Rot Hide gnolls are doing more than scavenging battlefields. They raid the mass graves of Tirisfal Glades and carry human and Forsaken corpses south to Fenris Isle for their own purposes.

Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in Elwynn Forest given by Hamish Bergwort at the Tower of Azora. Hamish's sensitive arcane equipment is being disrupted by erratic magical surges radiating from the north. To restore stability, travelers must enter Jasperlode Mine and cull the kobold geomancers responsible for the disturbances. Inside the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort oversees delicate arcane apparatus that requires fine calibration. Unfortunately for the scholar, the surrounding countryside is far from quiet. Repeated surges of uncontrolled energy constantly throw off his measurements, rendering careful magical adjustments impossible until the source of the interference is addressed.

Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest focused on restoring magical stability to the Tower of Azora. Hamish Bergwort's sensitive equipment is being disrupted by erratic spellcasting practiced by nearby Defias rogue wizards. Resolving the disturbance requires putting an end to the amateur sorcery around Stone Cairn Lake. Within the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort attempts to conduct delicate magical experiments, only to be repeatedly interrupted by unexplained ambient disruptions. In an arcane sanctuary where precise measurements are everything, even slight ripples in the local magical weave can ruin hours of careful work. Bergwort suspects the disruptions are not natural, but rather the result of crude spells cast nearby.

Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where the garrison has few hands to spare. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Guards Malakai and Rolf have been killed by aggressive murloc tribes. With his remaining guards too few to contain them, Thomas sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report.

Deliver the News. Deliver the News is a quest concluding the plight of the Windfield family orchard in Skywall. After helping Aamelia secure the farm, the adventurer travels to Valanaar to deliver tidings of their safety to an anxious Alvarion Windfield. Deliver the News marks the resolution of an ordeal at the Windfield family orchard. Having stepped in to save the farm from an impending crisis, the adventurer receives heartfelt thanks from Aamelia, who is ready to put the danger behind them. With the orchard secured, the immediate priority shifts to reassuring Alvarion Windfield, who fled to the settlement of Valanaar to plead for assistance.

Deliver the Shipment. After Driftwood, Watcher Biggs has one last job for you while the wagon is being repaired. Biggs has packed up the key supplies rescued from the ogre attacks and wants you to carry them to Quartermaster Lungertz at Nethergarde Keep. While Biggs repairs the wagon, the key supplies rescued from the ogre attacks have been packed up for you to carry to Nethergarde Keep. The keep stands in the Blasted Lands' northern hills, watching over the Dark Portal. Biggs gives the route: follow the road east, head south into the Blasted Lands where it branches, and turn left at the next fork, with a warning to be wary.

Deliver the Signet. Deliver the Signet is a quest in which a traveler carries a recovered family ring to High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. The delivery brings tragic confirmation of his nephew's demise on Zephras Isle, while opening new opportunities to assist the local peacekeepers. When an adventurer journeys toward the settlement of Valanaar, they carry with them the Shadowsong Family Signet recovered from an isolated tower. Entrusted with this grim token, travelers seek out Talaanis Shadowsong, the High Elder of Zephras Isle. Beloved by his people despite widespread local hardships, Talaanis must face the painful confirmation that his nephew has perished, receiving condolences alongside the reclaimed heirloom.

Deliver the Thread. Madame Eva sends ghost hair thread from Darkshire across Duskwood to Abercrombie near Raven Hill Cemetery. The hermit says he needs it to guard his hut from restless spirits. Madame Eva gives you a spool of Ghost Hair Thread, spun from hair gathered from the ghost Blind Mary. You carry it west through Duskwood, where spiders and undead roam. Abercrombie waits in his ramshackle shack just north of Raven Hill Cemetery.

Deliver to MacKinley. Stoley hands you a bottle of Steamwheedle bilge rum for MacKinley, the "Sea Wolf" of Booty Bay, to put an end to MacKinley's beliefs about Booty Bay booze. After the help you gave with the shipment, Stoley gives you a bottle of Steamwheedle bilge rum. You are to take it to MacKinley, in Booty Bay, so that he can finally let go of his crazy beliefs about the booze there.

Deliveries to Sven. In Darkshire, Elaine Carevin sends aid to Sven Yorgen's camp in northwestern Duskwood. Sven and his few followers struggle against the dangers of the blighted woods. Sven Yorgen and a few companions keep a camp on Duskwood's northwestern frontier. Darkshire faces wolves, spiders, and restless dead, yet Sven's band holds its ground beyond the town's walls. Constant danger leaves them unable to spare anyone for the perilous journey back to town for provisions. Elaine Carevin arranges for travelers to carry supplies so the fighters can keep going.

Delivering Daffodils. In Lakeshire, you carry flowers from Martie Jainrose to Darcy, and an awkward rivalry comes to light. First, you bring lunch to Guard Parker, who asks you to collect a bouquet for Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn. Guard Parker thanks you for bringing his lunch and asks you to fetch flowers from Martie Jainrose for Darcy, the cook who prepared his meal. Martie arranges a bouquet of daffodils, her own favorite flowers, without knowing who will receive them.

Delivering the Relic. Latronicus Moonspear asks you to carry the Mysterious Relic to his wife, Vestia Moonspear, at Feathermoon Stronghold. He cannot make heads or tails of the device and hopes she can tell what it is. Latronicus Moonspear could not make sense of the device even with a wager riding on it. His wife Vestia, he says, is a fine priestess for their community and one of the most learned scholars to be found anywhere. If anyone can work out what the relic is, she can, and they need to know. She is only a short walk away and no doubt busy studying.

Delivery for Marin. Sprinkle in Gadgetzan hands you the Violet Powder to carry to Marin Noggenfogger, along with a reminder that Marin owes her a favor. With the Violet Tragan in hand, Sprinkle gives you the Violet Powder to take to Marin Noggenfogger, who is also in Gadgetzan. You are to tell Marin that a favor is owed to her.

Delivery to Mathias. Keryn Sylvius sends a sealed parcel from Goldshire to Master Mathias Shaw in Stormwind. The delivery gives a promising rogue entry into SI:7's inner workings. A parcel from the Lion's Pride Inn to the Stormwind Barracks may look like ordinary courier work. For a budding rogue, it is an audition for Stormwind Intelligence. Local trainer Keryn Sylvius entrusts the package to novice cutpurses, giving them a direct introduction to Master Mathias Shaw. The delivery tests whether they can cross the capital quietly, keep a low profile, and follow discreet orders without asking questions.

name.frFR: Livraison dans la forêt des Pins-Argentés

text.enUS: Delivery to Silverpine Forest. You carry Apothecary Johaan’s findings from Brill to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society needs them for its work on the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society answers directly to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and works to concoct a New Plague that can wipe out the living and the Scourge. Its laboratories are scattered across Forsaken territory, so researchers must share their findings to keep their work moving. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan has gathered experimental results for other field researchers. You carry them south to Renferrel at the Sepulcher.

Delivery to the Gnomes. Kravel Koalbeard now has what he needs, and wants the Delicate Car Parts carried to Fizzle Brassbolts in the Shimmering Flats, who has waited a long time for them. Kravel admits he removed a little piece from Fizzle's order, and suggests you leave it unmentioned. Kravel Koalbeard tells you the parts are for Fizzle Brassbolts, who has been waiting a long time. Kravel confesses he took one little piece out of Fizzle's order, but feels sure it will not be missed. He calls the piece small and worthless, advises you not to bring it up, and asks you to trust him.

Demisette Cloyce. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Demisette Cloyce teaches warlocks beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. She guides students in fel magic and sends those ready for more toward other summoners. Warlocks gather in the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, while the city's authorities uphold order and the Holy Light. Demisette Cloyce lives in the catacombs below, teaching those willing to study forbidden arts. She warns that dark energies corrupt only those without the discipline to master them.

Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon bears the scars of the battle that freed the orcs from the blood curse. Here, Thrall and Grommash Hellscream faced Mannoroth in southern Ashenvale. In southern Ashenvale, the canyon lies near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, its land scarred by the Third War. Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked the pit lord Mannoroth here to break his hold over the Horde. Mannoroth struck Thrall down, and Grom seized the chance to drive his axe, Gorehowl, into the demon’s chest. The infernal blast shattered Mannoroth and killed Grom. With the pit lord’s death, the orcs were free of their lingering demonic servitude.

Demon Fall Ridge. In southeastern Ashenvale, demons hold the high ground above the place where Mannoroth fell. Lingering fel magic stains the ridge, and the Burning Legion has claimed a night elf barrow den. Demon Fall Ridge rises west of Demon Fall Canyon, its cliffs stained by fel left from the Third War. Below, the canyon marks the clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth. Surviving demons use the ridge as a staging ground. Lesser demons patrol the rocky heights, defiling the woodland and threatening travelers along Ashenvale's southern border.

Demont's Place. Outlaws hold Demont's Place, a ruined farm west of Moonbrook in southwestern Westfall. The farm once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind, but economic collapse and the Defias Brotherhood drove its caretakers away. Its fields remain empty and its fences weathered. Demont's Place lies within sight of Moonbrook, among the family holdings that once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood and drove out its caretakers. Like the neighboring fields, it has fallen into a rough hideout, where outlaws use its grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook.

Den of Flame. The Den of Flame is a fortified cavern in western Dustwallow Marsh, situated just west of the Stonemaul Ruins. Originally constructed by the Stonemaul ogres as their mound, it has since been overrun by the dragonkin of the black dragonflight serving Onyxia. Built by the Stonemaul ogres to serve as their main mound and sanctuary, the Den of Flame bears the unmistakable, rough-hewn stone architecture of ogre masonry. However, when the black dragonflight laid waste to the Stonemaul clan's settlement, the brood did not merely scatter the ogres—they seized the stronghold for themselves. Today, black dragonspawn patrol the burning perimeter and cavern entrance under the shadow of Onyxia's nearby lair.

Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies Teldrassil's unusual plants and seeks remedies for its corruption. He tends a small lakeside plot and asks young adventurers to gather samples, examine timberlings, and test enchanted soil. Denalan studies plants on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore. He works beneath a cloth awning, with field tools and rows of planter boxes close at hand. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, he gives his days to herbalism. He chooses this plot over Darnassus's grand barrows, so he can examine the unusual flora that has grown since the new World Tree was planted.

Denalan's Earth. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf sends a late shipment of rare earth south to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth. The night elf researcher studies Teldrassil's young plants. Syral Bladeleaf stops travelers in Dolanaar with a special shipment of rare earth for Denalan. The soil came from Darnassus to support his botanical studies, but delays kept it from reaching Dolanaar until now. Syral seeks a courier to carry the parcel south along the forest trail to Denalan's campsite by Lake Al'Ameth.

Dendrite Starblaze. Dendrite Starblaze is a night elf druid residing in the sacred village of Nighthaven within Moonglade. Serving the Cenarion Circle, he acts as a vital mentor and guide for budding druids of both night elf and tauren descent. Through him, practitioners are summoned to the holy grove to master essential rites such as cleansing toxins and communing with nature's forms. Perched within Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze represents the nonpartisan, enduring spirit of the Cenarion Circle. When novice druids learn to attune their spirits to Teleport: Moonglade, Dendrite is among the first to welcome them upon arrival. He bridges the gap between ancient Kaldorei tradition and the emerging path of the tauren, treating all who heed the call of the wild as kin beneath the boughs of the sacred haven.

Deputy Feldon. South of the Great Lakeshire Bridge, Deputy Feldon watches the road into Lakeshire. Gnoll packs are creeping toward the town, and he keeps a nervous vigil. Deputy Feldon stands watch south of the Lakeshire bridge, guarding a road needed for trade and travel. Blackrock orcs press from the north while gnoll packs overrun the southern hills, stretching the town guard thin. Feldon cannot leave his post without weakening Lakeshire's perimeter. He depends on passing adventurers to drive back the gnolls before they cut the town off.

Deputy Rainer. Outside Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer holds Elwynn's western border. The Stormwind Army officer faces gnolls and bandits from Westfall, coordinating local defenses while reinforcements fail to arrive. At Westbrook Garrison, Elwynn Forest's westernmost post, the road crosses into Westfall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City leaves much of the army abroad or caught in bureaucracy, and border posts like this one lack troops. Deputy Rainer organizes the defense from outside the tower with the few forces at hand. Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves threaten the local roads, so he depends on passing travelers and mercenary adventurers to keep the forest trails secure.

Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, human priests seek a prayer for their own hour of need. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena teaches acolytes to call on the Holy Light when their lives are at risk. Priests in the Cathedral of Light learn to use their faith to shield companions, heal wounds, and strike at evil. Yet even the devout can be isolated, cornered, or brought close to death. In such moments, an acolyte may cry out to the Holy Light for help, with their own survival at stake.

Desperate Prayer. Promising priests from Elwynn Forest are summoned to Stormwind for further training in the Church of the Holy Light. After proving their devotion and discipline, they come before High Priestess Laurena at the Cathedral of Light. Priestess Josetta guides novice priests in Goldshire, while other local mentors serve the outlying settlements of Elwynn Forest. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word reaches the senior priesthood in Stormwind. A summons to the Cathedral of Light marks the move to deeper responsibilities in the faith and formal training at the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind.

Desperate Prayer. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight sends human priests home to Stormwind for further training. A fellow priest has crossed continents to summon them to the Cathedral of Light. In Dolanaar, Priestess Laurna Morninglight brings you word from home. A fellow priest has crossed continents to find you, and Laurna urges you to return without delay. She offers Elune’s blessing and good wishes for your faith as you leave Teldrassil.

Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, dwarven priests are called to deepen their service to the Light. High Priestess Laurena summons promising acolytes from Dun Morogh to the Cathedral of Light. There they take on wider duties among the Alliance. Dwarven priests trained in Dun Morogh can outgrow the lessons of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows promise, High Priestess Laurena sends a formal summons from the Cathedral of Light. Her attention means the young priest is ready for deeper study and greater duties in the faith.

Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, a summons carries a young priest from the Park to the Cathedral of Light. Nara Meideros sends you to High Priestess Laurena for further instruction. In Stormwind’s Park, Nara Meideros keeps faith with Elune. The city’s spiritual guides share ties across their different traditions. When the Cathedral seeks a promising student, Nara sends you across the canals with quiet encouragement. The message brings good tidings, not cause for alarm.

Desperate Prayer. In Ironforge, dwarven priests come of age through training in healing and survival. High Priest Rohan sends acolytes through the Deeprun Tram to Stormwind, where High Priestess Laurena guides their passage into deeper mysteries. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan guides dwarven initiates devoted to the Holy Light. When an acolyte shows discipline and faith, Rohan sends them southwest to Stormwind. Human and dwarven clerics share close spiritual ties, and advanced teaching is centered in Stormwind City's grand halls.

Desperate Prayer. In Darnassus, young human and dwarven priests find guidance in another faith. Priestess Alathea teaches the ways of Elune, while followers of the Holy Light are directed to Stormwind. There, High Priestess Laurena welcomes the returning acolyte to the Cathedral of Light. Alliance priests follow different sacred paths. In Darnassus, the priesthood tends to Elune, channeling the moon goddess's radiance and wrath. Priestess Alathea honors Elune and respects the Holy Light, but cannot teach another race the deeper prayers bound to a different devotion. Human and dwarven acolytes who seek those prayers must look elsewhere.

Destiny Calls. Syurna sends you to learn what Sethir the Ancient knows of Teldrassil's corruption. The satyr waits near the Oracle Glade, beyond the reach of those who tried force or diplomacy. Teldrassil's growing sickness troubles the night elf leaders in Darnassus. Syurna, the rogue trainer, needs someone subtle; armed patrols have died trying to reach Sethir the Ancient. The satyr roosts on a remote bough near the Oracle Glade and has turned away force and diplomacy alike. To learn what he knows, you need to enter his lair and take his personal possessions.

Destruction in Deadmines. Deep beneath Moonbrook, Defias industry is poisoning the land. Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source of the blight and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines shelter a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes this forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. Destroying it is her aim.

Destruction in Deadmines. In Westfall, Alba Fairmoon sends an operative to destroy the Defias forge in the Deadmines. The explosives are already planted, and Alba waits in the hills behind Moonbrook for the detonator. The Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength beneath Westfall. Alba Fairmoon directs you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are already planted beside it, and you return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook to set them off from a safe distance. She hopes destroying the forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal.

Detonation at a Distance. Sprite Jumpsprocket needs a safer way to set off explosives, and Stormwind holds the answer. She sends you to Stormwind Intelligence for a remote detonator. Sprite Jumpsprocket wants to set off explosives from a safe distance. Goblins and gnomes are known for handling volatile chemicals recklessly, but some blasts demand care. A standard fuse can put the person lighting it in danger. Sprite knows a controlled explosion needs a special trigger, the kind common tinkerers do not keep on hand.

Detonation at a Distance. In Moonbrook, explosions beneath Westfall draw SI:7's attention. Jasper Fel, a Stormwind operative, sends a remote detonator kit to help handle the work from a safe distance. Jasper Fel and SI:7 watch events across Stormwind's lands, including Westfall's troubled border. When word reaches him of explosive work in Moonbrook, Fel already knows what is happening in the abandoned mining tunnels beneath the countryside.

Deviate Eradication. Deviate Eradication is a task assigned by the night elf druid Ebru above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While other disciples focus on waking their slumbering leader, Ebru asks adventurers to purge the caverns of mutated deviate beasts spawned by his twisted vision. Ridding the subterranean oasis of these horrors is an essential step in stemming the corruption threatening the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex brought his followers to the subterranean springs of the Barrens with an ambitious vision: tap into the Emerald Dream to regrow the parched plains into a lush, thriving woodland. Instead, Naralex became ensnared within the Dream, his slumber twisting into an agonizing nightmare. Rather than healing the land, the power surging through the caverns warped the native wildlife and plant life into monstrous, aggressive mutants known as deviate beasts.

Deviate Hide. Deviate Hides are the mutated skins stripped from the beasts dwelling within the Wailing Caverns. Warped by the corrupting dream of the druid Naralex, these otherworldly pelts are sought by druids looking to repurpose the nightmare's taint into durable leather goods. When the night elf druid Naralex entered his deep slumber beneath the Barrens, his dream turned into an Emerald Nightmare that warped the local cavern ecology. The beasts lurking in the depths transformed into unnatural deviate predators with tough, mutated hides. While inherently touched by evil, these pelts possess unusual, supple resilience that makes them uniquely suited for leathercrafting. Nalpak, perched high above the cavern mouth in the skull-shaped rock formation, collects these hides to study their properties and fashion them into sturdy utility packs.

Deviate Hides. Deviate Hides is a task given by Nalpak, a disciple of Naralex stationed above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While Naralex lies trapped in a twisted nightmare, Nalpak seeks to salvage something useful from the mutated beasts spawned beneath the Barrens. By gathering skins from these deviate predators, he hopes to put their strange, otherworldly properties to practical use. When the night elf druid Naralex attempted to tap the subterranean springs beneath the Barrens to restore lush life to the arid plains, his mind slipped into a terrifying nightmare. That dark reverie bled into reality, mutating the native wildlife of the Wailing Caverns into vicious deviate beasts. Raptors, crocolisks, vipers, and shambling horrors emerged warped and aggressive, altered by the emerald corruption leaking from their dreaming master.
