text.enUS: Devils in Westfall. Dust devils roam Westfall, and Collin Mauren needs their remains for a spell. The Mage Quarter wizard is helping Gaxim Rustfizzle with an unusual experiment. Their work calls for a messaging scroll, and the dust holds what Mauren needs to enchant it. Collin Mauren is preparing a messaging scroll for Gaxim Rustfizzle. The wizard is helping the tinkerer with an unusual venture, but the spell needs more than ink and vellum. Dust devils roam Westfall with elemental magic swirling within them. Their remains provide the volatile medium Mauren needs to bind Gaxim's spell to parchment.

Devlin's Remains. Near Agamand Mills, Devlin Agamand’s bones carry a bitter legacy. The younger son of the wealthy family that owned the mills, he roamed the road by his ruined home as a mindless Scourge thrall. A traveler struck him down and brought his remains to a survivor in Brill, who sought vengeance. Devlin Agamand lived in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Thurman was gentle and tall, while Devlin was frail and sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect its lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall. The Scourge raised him as a ravenous ghoul, and his mad chattering haunted the roadside leading to Agamand Mills.

Devourer of Souls. In the Undercity's Temple of the Damned, Carendin Halgar guides Forsaken warlocks toward binding a succubus. Godrick Farsan knows how to lure one from the Twisting Nether with the hearts of pure, loving mortals. Carendin Halgar teaches that a succubus must be enticed across the threshold, not summoned by command. The demon hungers to ruin virtue and consume mortal essence. To draw it forth, you offer the hearts of genuinely virtuous, loving men as bait. Halgar sends you to Godrick Farsan, who knows where such rare quarry can be found.

Devourer of Souls. Gan'rul Bloodeye sends an aspiring Horde warlock to begin the path to summoning and commanding a succubus. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the warlock seeks Cazul's counsel on luring and binding the demon. Horde warlocks who master lesser demons such as imps and voidwalkers may seek a succubus next. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the dark arts beneath Orgrimmar and judges when a warlock is ready to call one from the Twisting Nether. A succubus can turn the frail against themselves, so binding one takes subtlety as well as strength.

Devourer of Souls. An Alliance warlock crosses the sea to seek Takar the Seer’s counsel on summoning a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder sends Stormwind initiates into the Barrens for the wisdom they need. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder guides promising warlocks toward summoning a succubus. The demon devours souls, destroys hearts, and dominates minds, so it cannot be called blindly into Azeroth. A warlock needs a potent lure: an object tied to pure love. That token draws the succubus from the Twisting Nether, where the warlock can defeat and bind it. Stormwind’s covens cannot teach them where to find such an object.

Devouring Plague. Across the sea, Devouring Plague awaits Forsaken priests who travel far from Lordaeron. Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff sends the adept to Aelthalyste in the Ruins of Lordaeron, where a signature form of Shadow magic awaits. In Thunder Bluff, Miles Welsh judges Forsaken priests who have honed their divine and shadowy disciplines. Posted among the tauren, he recognizes when an acolyte has grown strong enough for higher mysteries. Miles directs them back to the Ruins of Lordaeron rather than attempt to impart those teachings himself in Kalimdor.

Devouring Plague. In Orgrimmar, Devouring Plague training begins with Ur'kyo sending Forsaken priests home. They have come to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear, but Aelthalyste waits in Undercity to teach them the shadow arts of their own people. Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power in Orgrimmar. Among the Horde, Darkspear trolls and Forsaken share a curious bond in matters of faith, while orcs and tauren show little inclination toward priestly worship. Ur'kyo knows Forsaken initiates must master the shadow arts tied to their own condition. In respect between their peoples, he sends wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to complete their training.

Devouring Plague. Forsaken priests in the Undercity learn Devouring Plague from Priestess Aelthalyste. The rite is for those who have proven their dedication to shadow magic, and teaches a feared curse of the undead priesthood. In the Undercity’s War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste teaches Forsaken priests the grim arts of the Shadow. Priests of other races draw power from the Holy Light or ancestral spirits, but the Forsaken have shaped their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague gives form to that path: it torments foes and drains their stolen vitality to sustain the caster’s decaying body.

Devrak. At the Crossroads, Devrak keeps the Horde’s wind riders ready for the roads across Kalimdor. The orc flight master carries couriers and supplies between Durotar, Mulgore, frontier outposts, and the Horde’s capitals. At the Crossroads, Devrak tends the wind riders that link the Horde’s far-flung holdings. The outpost stands where Kalimdor’s major trade routes meet, exposed beneath the sun and vulnerable to quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Quick flights matter here. Devrak pairs seasoned travelers and new messengers with trained wind riders that cross the savannah and reach Mulgore’s mountains or Durotar’s stone canyons.

Dextren Ward. In the Stormwind Stockade, Dextren Ward remains a prisoner amid a bloody uprising. Before his capture, he dug up bodies at Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood and sold them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Darkshire's town council has marked him for death. Before chains bound him beneath Stormwind, Dextren Ward robbed graves in Duskwood for profit. At Raven Hill Cemetery, where sorrow and horror had grown, he dug up the newly buried dead. He sold the bodies to local practitioners of dark arts.

Dig Rat Stew. Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for a pot of dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens to bring back dig rats for his recipe. Across the dry Barrens, hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, craves something different: dig rats. He says he is hungry all day and offers to share his recipe with any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents.

Digging Through the Dirt. You search for the Embalmer’s missing heart in Duskwood at Raven Hill Cemetery. A mound marked Eliza hides a buried horror that will not stay dead. At Raven Hill Cemetery, a patch of loose, freshly turned soil bears the name Eliza. Other graves in Duskwood lie open to scavengers or feral ghouls, but someone placed this earth with care. Digging below the topsoil uncovers the splintered boards of a coffin. It seals away the remnant the Embalmer meant to hide from the light of day.

Digging Through the Ooze. In Menethil Harbor, Sida asks travelers to recover her bag from the ooze that swallowed it. She visits Ironbeard's Tomb regularly, but fled when foul oozes filled the barrows. Sida lives in Menethil Harbor and often travels northeast into the Wetlands to pay homage at Ironbeard's Tomb. On her latest visit, foul, dripping oozes had filled the ancient barrow. She panicked and hurled her satchel at one of them. The ooze swallowed the bag whole, giving Sida just enough time to flee back to the port town. Now she asks travelers to search for it.

Dirania Silvershine. Dirania Silvershine is a night elf resident of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. Deeply loyal and observant, she watches over the tranquil grove and looks out for her companion Iverron when his reckless ventures land him in peril. Dirania stands among the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, the secluded vale where young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance. While many in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries look to broad spiritual duties, Dirania stays mindful of those nearest to her, attentive to the quiet dangers that stir even in the heart of Teldrassil.

Dire Maul. Dire Maul is the ruined expanse of Eldre'Thalas, an ancient Highborne city hidden deep in the wilderness of Feralas. Once built to safeguard Queen Azshara's arcane secrets, its crumbling plazas and towering coliseums are now divided between occupying Gordok ogres, invading satyrs, and the withered remnants of its original elven caretakers. Twelve thousand years ago, Eldre'Thalas served as a wondrous bastion for Queen Azshara's favored sorcerers, the Shen'dralar. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, Prince Tortheldrin wove a magical barrier that shielded the city from ruin. Severed from their source of magic, the surviving Highborne trapped a colossal demon named Immol'thar beneath their sanctum, siphoning its fel essence to sustain their immortality and arcane powers for millennia.

Direforge Hill. Hostile Dark Iron dwarves hold Direforge Hill in the northeastern Wetlands, southeast of Dun Modr and northeast of the Green Belt. Dark Iron dwarves hold the northeastern Wetlands hill under Balgaras the Foul, a Dark Iron dwarf warlock. Their encampment lies southeast of Dun Modr.

Dirge Quikcleave. Inside Gadgetzan's inn, Dirge Quikcleave holds court as a goblin culinary master and vendor. His inventive dishes are renowned across Azeroth, and seasoned chefs come to him to master artisan cooking. In dusty Gadgetzan, Dirge Quikcleave serves drinks and meat to travelers parched by the Tanaris sands. Though his kitchen is in a frontier tavern, he claims to be Azeroth's greatest living culinary artist. Cooking trainers in cities send their most promising students to him when ordinary lessons are spent. Dirge's demanding recipes call for unusual ingredients, from giant clam meat and eggs for his Clamlette creations to exotic beasts from distant shores.

name.esES: Fabulosas chuletillas de quimerok de Dirge
name.frFR: Pyro-côtelettes de chimaerok à la Dirge
name.zhCN: 迪尔格的超美味奇美拉肉片

text.enUS: Dirge's Kickin' Chimaerok Chops. Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan has finished working out his recipe. He still needs twenty Goblin Rocket Fuel and twenty Deeprock Salt from you, and he wants them fast so the meat you brought him does not spoil. Dirge Quikcleave sees to the spices himself, and the meat you brought him makes up the remainder of the dish. All he lacks is rocket fuel and deeprock salt, twenty of each. With those in his hands, the chicken will be ready to go back to Narain Soothfancy. Dirge urges you not to dawdle, because he does not want the meat going bad.
Dirt-Caked Pendant. In the Barrens, a captive orc gives up the Dirt-Caked Pendant he carried. The keepsake reaches Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar, where it is used to draw a succubus.

Disarming Colloid. At the Stonewrought Dam, Disarming Colloid could keep Seaforium from exploding when wet. Ashlan Stonesmirk provides it in the Wetlands for a mixture that can neutralize the powder. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognized the powder left by Dark Iron sappers at the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan as Seaforium. Its scent and fine silver crystals gave it away. The powder is harmless while dry, but moisture makes it immensely destructive, a grave danger at the waterlogged dam. Stonesmirk provided Disarming Colloid to stop the reaction before detonation. Mixed with lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear, the colloid neutralizes Seaforium's explosive properties.

Disarming Mixture. At Stonewrought Dam, Disarming Mixture is prepared to stop a Seaforium charge from breaking the dam. Chief Engineer Hinderweir makes it to neutralize explosives planted by Dark Iron saboteurs. Dark Iron saboteurs planted a heavy Seaforium charge beneath Stonewrought Dam’s foundation. With no Mountaineer support close at hand, Chief Engineer Hinderweir used ingredients named by explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk to make the Disarming Mixture. Stirred into the planted powder keg underwater, the solution neutralizes its reactive compounds and leaves the charge fizzled and harmless.

Discipline. Executor Zygand turns to outsiders in Tirisfal Glades to keep his Deathguard sentries alert. He has little faith in the garrison and orders physical punishment for those who slacken. The Deathguard guard the Forsaken across Lordaeron. Freedom from the Lich King's control has brought its own troubles: apathy, fatigue, and neglect. Executor Zygand has little patience for sentries who let their discipline slip. The Scarlet Crusade and Scourge prowl Tirisfal's borders, and the garrison must stay ready. Its officers use force and close oversight to keep the troops alert.

Discover Rolf's Fate. In eastern Elwynn, two Stormwind guards are missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks lead toward a murloc village, where the search for Rolf continues. Guard Thomas sent patrols around eastern Elwynn Forest as threats grew, but Malakai and Rolf vanished near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints pressed into the mud lead east along the water's edge, straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

name.esES: Acabar con los ataques de los Crines de Acero
name.frFR: La défense du poste de Guet-Lointain

text.enUS: Disrupt the Attacks. Thork needs the Crossroads defended as Razormane quilboar cut its supply roads. Their ambushes have halted caravans from Durotar, and the outpost is running short on food and gear. You strike at the quilboar while scouts search for the one directing their warband. The Crossroads guards a key junction for Horde traffic through central Kalimdor. Freight wagons and caravans bring food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar, and the outpost depends on those supplies. Razormane ambushes along the northeast trails have stopped the deliveries. Stores are running low, and Thork cannot wait for peaceful talks.

Distracting Jarven. Jarven Thunderbrew watches the cellar stores at Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Forbidden to touch the barrels, he asks a passing traveler to bring him a mug of Thunder Ale from upstairs, hoping it will sharpen his wits on duty. In Kharanos, Jarven Thunderbrew keeps watch over the deep stores of Thunderbrew Distillery. His family forbids him to drink from the stock while on guard, though the finest stout in Dun Morogh surrounds him. The temptation wins out, and he asks passing travelers to fetch a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs.

Divine Retribution. Kalaran Windblade asks you to hear his tale in Searing Gorge. His father is dead at the hands of what lurks in the cauldron, and the Stormwind magistrate would not listen. Kalaran seeks vengeance and wants an adventurer to act for him. Kalaran says the filth in the cauldron killed his father. He pleaded with the Stormwind magistrate for help, but the pleas fell on deaf ears. Stormwind, he says, would rather not admit this part of the world exists, let alone send soldiers to see justice done here.

Divined Scroll. At Silverwind Refuge, the Divined Scroll can expose the mage behind Ashenvale's troubled waters. Night elves use magic from intact water elemental bracers to reveal the summoner's identity. Mystral Lake's tainted waters trouble the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. Sentinel Velene Starstrike gives travelers an uncharged divining scroll to trace whoever manipulates the water elementals infesting the lake. Gather intact bracers from slain elementals and use them as an arcane reagent; their latent bindings pass into the parchment. The Divined Scroll then reveals the magical signature of the rogue wizard behind the infestation.

Divining Scroll. At Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike gives investigators the Divining Scroll to trace the corrupted elementals to their creator. Corrupt water elementals rise from Ashenvale’s pools, and the Sentinels know the disturbance is unnatural. Sentinel Velene Starstrike obtains a scroll to find who is responsible. With intact elemental bracers as a focus, its magic draws out the summoner’s signature. The blank parchment becomes a Divined Scroll and names the guilty party.

Doan Karhan. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan studies the Burning Legion’s demonic artifacts. A human scholar and practitioner of the dark arts, he lives alone to pursue his research, especially into the enigmatic Orb of Soran'ruk. Doan Karhan keeps a solitary camp in the southern Barrens, far from the Alliance’s civilized bastions. He withdrew into the wilderness to study dangerous demonic relics without disturbance. He knows much about powerful fel vessels, possesses the Orb of Zargain, and is absorbed by the legendary Orb of Soran'ruk. Warlocks seeking knowledge of artifact crafting and dark rituals often come to him.

Doctor Gregory Victor. Doctor Gregory Victor is a Forsaken surgeon stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Renowned as the premier trauma physician within the Horde, he evaluates aspiring medics seeking to master advanced triage and battlefield first aid. His cold, clinical efficiency keeps frontline warriors stitched together amidst bitter regional conflicts. While many view Forsaken apothecaries with suspicion, Doctor Gregory Victor serves the Horde through practical battlefield surgery rather than blighted alchemy. Stationed deep within the contested Arathi Highlands at Hammerfall, he operates on soldiers battered by Syndicate brigands, Boulderfist ogres, and Alliance forces. His station doubles as the primary proving ground for Horde field medics, demanding ruthless efficiency and prioritizing critical patients under intense pressure.

Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. At Foothold Citadel, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen directs Theramore's medical care. He trains healers and tests seasoned medics in field triage and bandage work. On the ground floor of Foothold Citadel, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen oversees medical care for Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces and trains Theramore's frontline healers. Dustwallow Marsh makes their work harsh, and VanHowzen demands skill under pressure. He puts experienced medics through a demanding triage test, where they must judge which wounds need care first.

Dogran's Captivity. At Camp Taurajo, a warlock faces a vital trial in Horde training: rescue a captured orc warrior. With Ken'zigla's Draught, you must find battered Grunt Dogran in a quilboar camp and give him strength to escape. Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo will not risk Horde soldiers in a costly attack on the entrenched quilboar. Dogran's fate rests with you, an aspiring warlock armed only with Ken'zigla's Draught. Travel north through the brambles and hostile camps to find where the quilboar hold him captive.

Dogran's Pendant. Dogran's Pendant draws a succubus toward the warlocks of Orgrimmar. Dogran, a wounded orc, carries it while separated from his mate, Zankaja. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks turn the sorrow bound to it into a lure. Dogran's Pendant carries the sorrow of an orc separated from Zankaja. Captivity and crippling wounds have overshadowed their love. The warlocks of the Cleft of Shadow know that demons such as succubi prey on love, yearning, and vulnerability. They use the pendant's grief to draw a succubus across the Twisting Nether and into Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle.

Dolanaar. Dolanaar gathers travelers and guides beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. Southwest of Shadowglen, the town is the first place young night elves find after leaving their sheltered training grounds. Rangers, druids, and craftsmen help newcomers while strange afflictions spread through the World Tree. Dolanaar is a crossroads for travelers crossing Teldrassil. Beneath the canopy southwest of Shadowglen, its homes and platforms follow the traditional night elven way, woven into the woodland. Young night elves come here for their first broad training in trades, martial arts, and nature crafts. The road west leads toward Darnassus, the capital. From the surrounding boughs come reports of corrupted wildlife, aggressive furbolgs, and foul mosses, all brought before Dolanaar’s council.

Dolanaar Delivery. In Shadowglen, young travelers carry harvested herbs south to Dolanaar. Porthannius entrusts them with the bundle for Innkeeper Keldamyr. Fresh herbs from Aldrassil are bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius is occupied with matters among the druids of Shadowglen, so he entrusts the bundle to young travelers heading south along the road. They carry it to Innkeeper Keldamyr.

Dolanaar Delivery. Travelers leave Shadowglen with a parcel of herbs bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius, occupied with the druids, asks them to carry it south, marking their first venture beyond the sheltered glade. Porthannius asks travelers heading south from Shadowglen to carry a bundle of freshly harvested herbs along the forest path. He is occupied with pressing business alongside the druids tending the glade, and cannot leave to handle the errand himself. The bundle goes south as young adventurers prepare to leave the training grounds for the wider reaches of Teldrassil.

Doling Justice. With the sprite darters freed, Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal mean to take the fight to the Grimtotem clan. Jer'kai asks you to cut down Grimtotem Naturalists, Raiders and Shamans, then return to Jer'kai. This follows Freedom for All Creatures. After Freedom for All Creatures, Jer'kai Moonweaver tells you that Kindal and Jer'kai will now strike back at the Grimtotem. Together they can thin out some of the tauren without much risk to themselves, but they would welcome your help. You have seen the camp below, and there are more to the east. Use your own tactics against Grimtotem Naturalists, Raiders and Shamans, then meet back where Jer'kai waits.

Doling Justice. Out in the wilderness, Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal have little to give in thanks, so Jer'kai hands you a signet ring. It is yours to carry to High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where it will tell her that the two of them are well and lend weight to your story. This follows Doling Justice. Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal cannot offer much out in the wilds of Feralas, but they do not want you to feel unappreciated. Jer'kai hands over a signet ring and points you toward Darnassus, where High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind waits in the Temple of the Moon. The ring will show her that the pair are well, and it backs up the tale you will tell.

Donova Snowden. Donova Snowden is an intrepid dwarven researcher encamped alongside the thermal waters near Frostfire Hot Springs in Winterspring. Despite the bitter cold and hostile wildlife, she studies the strange thermal activity of the region and monitors the increasingly corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. While most travelers stick to the safety of Everlook, Donova Snowden has chosen to camp in the freezing wilderness near the Frostfire Hot Springs. She spends her days investigating the curious geothermic anomalies bubbling up through the permafrost, as well as the dark influences encroaching upon Winterspring's native wildlife. Practical and determined, she enlists passing adventurers of both the Alliance and the Horde to gather samples and help curb local threats.

Donyal Tovald. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s historical works. Under an initiative sponsored by young King Anduin Wrynn, he preserves and copies books for wider public use. Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s collection in Stormwind Keep. The library holds historical accounts, scrolls, and scholarly volumes, chiefly for the nobility and royal court. Young King Anduin Wrynn has sponsored an effort to make that knowledge more accessible to ordinary citizens. Tovald preserves and copies the texts, helping keep the Alliance’s lessons and triumphs recorded amid the kingdom’s political troubles.

Doom Weed. In Brill, Junior Apothecary Holland seeks doom weed for his research. The plant grows near Tirisfal's northern mass graves, where Rot Hide gnolls prowl. Junior Apothecary Holland researches for the Royal Apothecary Society from Brill. He wants doom weed to advance his experiments, but Gordo cannot tell the right plants from the wrong ones. Holland turns to more capable hands to gather what he needs.

name.frFR: Le Refuge des saisons de Dor'danil

text.enUS: Dor'Danil Barrow Den. In central Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post, Dor'Danil Barrow Den lies under Forsaken shadow. Druids once slept here while their spirits roamed the Emerald Dream, but now the sanctuary is filled with horror. Night elven druids have slept for centuries in barrow dens across Kalimdor, their bodies sheltered underground as their spirits traveled the Emerald Dream. When the Horde pushed into Ashenvale, Dor'Danil lay deep behind enemy lines. The orcs mostly left the sleeping elves alone, but the newly allied Forsaken saw an opportunity. Their agents entered the depths and began experiments to sever the druids from their spirits. The ordeal fractured the dreamers' minds and drove them mad. Now sinister Forsaken assassins prowl the dark hollows, alongside the tormented spirits of druids who cannot return to their bodies.

Doras. Above Orgrimmar, Doras directs the Horde's wind riders across Kalimdor. He oversees the capital's wyverns, sending couriers, scouts, and travelers on their way. Doras tends the wind riders on a wooden platform above the Valley of Strength. The Horde settled in Durotar, and these clever, leathery-winged beasts became its chief means of communication and travel across Kalimdor. Doras pairs resting mounts with riders and sees that important messages and reinforcements reach distant outposts. Their routes reach the Crossroads, Thunder Bluff, and settlements deep in Ashenvale or Dustwallow Marsh.

name.esES: Doras, maestro de jinetes del viento
name.frFR: Doras, le maître des coursiers du vent
name.zhCN: 双足飞龙管理员多拉斯

text.enUS: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka needs a courier to carry her thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads. She sends travelers to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar's skytower to arrange the flight back to the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka sends thanks to Zargh after a shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. With no time to travel through Durotar herself, she trusts the established aerial courier network linking major Horde settlements to carry her letter back across the frontier.

Doren. Lieutenant Doren commands the Rebel Camp nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Once an officer under Colonel Kurzen, Doren led a mutiny after his superior and fellow expeditionaries descended into madness. Now, he directs a guerrilla resistance determined to uncover the source of the affliction and eliminate Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren initially deployed to Stranglethorn Vale under the banner of Stormwind and the command of Colonel Kurzen. The expedition was meant to establish a foothold in the wild southern jungle, but it quickly soured as Kurzen and his inner circle succumbed to an erratic, violent insanity. Refusing to abandon their sanity or their honor, Doren and a cadre of loyalists broke rank. They fled north and carved out the Rebel Camp along the road, choosing defection over servitude to a madman.

Dormitory. In Gnomeregan, the Dormitory lies overrun by troggs and choked with radiation. Gnomes once lived here, but the fallen city's residential halls now belong to the creatures that drove them out. Past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory once housed Gnomeregan's inventors, laborers, and families. When High Tinker Mekkatorque opened the emergency radiation vents to fight the invading troggs, this crowded sector became a trap. No gnomish life remains in its communal halls or living quarters. Mutated troggs now thrive in the radioactive air. Travelers heading deeper through the city must fight through this reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears.

Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens.

name.esES: A lo largo de la costa

text.enUS: Down the Coast. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle leaves Southshore's defense to passing adventurers. Sent from Stormwind, he would rather drink ale than patrol, even as Torn Fin murlocs gather along the Western Strand. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle left Stormwind's city guard for a post in Southshore. The port feels dreary to him, and he cannot bear the fishy harbor odor. He spends his days drinking at the inn instead of patrolling the frontlines. Marshal Redpath has ordered him to protect Southshore from the dangers nearby, but Orinelle hires passing sellswords to do the work.

Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton says your deeds against the undead in Desolace are only a start, because the plague's real danger is in Lordaeron. He gives you a letter of commendation bearing his seal for Raleigh the Devout in Southshore. Anton speaks proudly of the Scarlet Crusade's bastions of cleansing in Lordaeron. The Crusade claims strongholds all the way between Hearthglen and Tirisfal Glades. Anton says your work against the undead in Desolace has proven you, yet the plague's real danger is in Lordaeron.

Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade, at Nijel's Point, says his order is at war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. He asks you to prove your allegiance by destroying thirty undead ravagers in the Valley of Bones. Brother Anton speaks bluntly. He says the Scourge must be halted before it swallows the land and pulls the world into darkness, and the Scarlet Crusade has pledged itself to that fight. If you are with them, he wants your courage and allegiance shown by destroying thirty undead ravagers. They are found south of Anton, in the Valley of Bones. Succeed, and the Crusade will welcome you.

Downstream. Downstream is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest tasked by Ormin Pelford at Eastvale Logging Camp. After Ormin's wagon accidentally overturns into the river, adventurers are asked to brave murlocs and wolves downstream to recover waterlogged timber supplies. While transporting a shipment of gear back from a local trading post, laborer Ormin Pelford suffered a mishap when his wagon tipped over along the waterway near Eastvale Logging Camp. The cargo tumbled into the current and was quickly swept downstream before he could secure it. Without these vital woodworking tools, the loggers face delays in their timber operations.

Draconic for Dummies. Narain Soothfancy remembers a book he stowed somewhere safe. To reach it you look for his crashed gyrocopter on Land's End Beach, then swim south from there to an island in the South Seas. This follows Translating the Ledger. Narain Soothfancy says the book is bound to come in handy, and that he hid it where nobody could hope to find it. He needed a gyrocopter to get there the first time and crashed it on the beach on the way back. That crash, he says, gave him his super-gnomish psychic powers. The wreck lies somewhere along Land's End Beach, and from there you swim south. Narain is sure you will recognise the place at a glance. The island where the book lies buried is out in the South Seas.

Draenethyst Crystals. Magtoor, at the Harborage, asks for six draenethyst crystals, sacred to Magtoor's people and stolen by the lost ones of the Fallow Sanctuary. Without them, Magtoor's people fear they too may lose their way. The lost ones of the Fallow Sanctuary look as Magtoor's people do, but the rigors of the journey to Azeroth drove them mad. Once brethren, they now dwell in the Sanctuary, to the east, and they seize or kill anyone who strays close. They have also stolen something sacred: draenethyst crystals.

Drag. In Orgrimmar, the Drag links the Valley of Strength, Valley of Honor and Valley of Wisdom. Crafters and traders line its shaded red-rock canyon, where the descent to the Cleft of Shadow also lies. The Drag runs between Orgrimmar’s red canyon walls, where crafters and traders fill the Horde capital’s streets. Unlike the Valley of Strength, with its military musters and commands, the Drag is where daily city life unfolds. High cliffs and hides shade the street, where tanning vats, alchemical cauldrons and tinkers’ gears fill the air with their sounds and smells. Craftsmen gather to practice their trades and teach aspiring adventurers. Their work ranges from leatherworking and tailoring to the goblin workshops of Nogg’s Machine Shop.

Dragonmaw Gates. At the Dragonmaw Gates, heavy fortifications bar the road climbing from the eastern Wetlands. They guard the ascent to Grim Batol, a mountain fortress in the cursed dwarven ruins. Carved into rugged peaks along the eastern Wetlands, the Dragonmaw Gates seal the winding road to Grim Batol. The barriers take their name from the Dragonmaw orcs, who held the dwarven mountain city during the Second War. The road remains a fortified checkpoint, and the ascent still brings danger. Powerful drakes haunt the pass, while grim reminders of the clan's dark history linger in the mountains.

Dragonmaw Shinbones. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely sends Horde warriors to gather Dragonmaw Shinbones for Brutal Legguards. The hunt leads to the southern Wetlands, where the hostile orcs carry bones thick enough to brace the armor. Velora Nitely, a Forsaken armorer in the Undercity, needs a strong brace for Brutal Legguards. She sends Horde warriors to the Wetlands for thick, resilient bone from the Dragonmaw orcs. Their dense frames can bear the heavy blows a seasoned warrior faces.

name.ptBR: Estandarte de Guerra Presa do Dragão

text.enUS: Dragonmaw War Banner. Dragonmaw War Banners rise over orc encampments in the Wetlands. Their clan markings give the dwarven defenders of Menethil Harbor proof of the growing threat. After the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan was shattered when they lost control of their enslaved red dragons. The enraged drakes turned on their captors and drove the survivors from Grim Batol into the eastern hills. Now the remaining orcs gather strength under Chieftain Nek'rosh and raise their banners over camps northeast of Menethil Harbor. Those rough standards mark their defiance and threaten the settlements in the marsh.

Dragonmaw clan. The Dragonmaw clan is an infamous orcish faction notorious for subduing and riding red dragons during the Second War. Guided by dark artifacts and foul magic, they imprisoned the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza beneath the cursed halls of Grim Batol until her liberation shattered their dominion. Today, their scattered remnants lurk in the wetlands and mountains of Khaz Modan, remaining hostile to both the Alliance and Thrall's New Horde. The Dragonmaw clan hailed from Draenor and crossed the Dark Portal with the Old Horde. On Azeroth, they turned their talents to subjugating its winged terrors.

Dragonmurk. Dragonmurk is a sprawling, hazardous tract of southern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with black dragonspawn and hatchlings. Flanked by ancient ogre ruins and scorched caverns, it serves as the hostile outer perimeter for the brood of Onyxia. Spanning the southern interior of Dustwallow Marsh, the Dragonmurk marks the threshold where damp wetlands give way to the dominion of the black dragonflight. The waterways and thick mud here crawl with black wyrmkins, dragonspawn, and ravenous whelps. The surrounding landscape has suffered deeply from their presence; adjacent territories such as the ruined village of Stonemaul and the scorched cavern known as the Den of Flame have both fallen completely under the flight's territorial grip.

Dreadmaul Post. Dreadmaul Post is an entrenched ogre settlement situated in the scorched wastes of the Blasted Lands. Established by the Dreadmaul clan, this mound serves as a fortified redoubt near the Dark Portal where ogres have lingered since their arrival from Draenor. Travelers passing through the region must contend with these fierce brutes and the treacherous terrain surrounding their encampment. When the Horde surged through the Dark Portal in decades past, clans of ogres marched alongside them into Azeroth. The Dreadmaul clan chose to dig in near the gateway itself, raising crude stone mounds and earthworks across the red wastes of the Blasted Lands. Dreadmaul Post stands as one of their primary outposts, maintaining a firm grip over the badlands and clashing with wandering beasts and any travelers foolish enough to draw near their territory.

Dreadmaul Rock. Thal'trak Proudtusk's wife Sha'ni was sent over three weeks ago to look into strange rituals among the Firegut ogres, and nobody has heard from her platoon. Thal'trak cannot leave his post, so he asks you to go and learn what became of her. Sha'ni's orders took her to the Burning Steppes, to look into strange rituals among the Firegut ogres. That was more than three weeks ago. Goretooth says nothing has been heard from anyone in her platoon, and advises Thal'trak to put it behind him and keep to his duty. Thal'trak will not accept that, for it is his wife who is missing. He cannot leave his post, so he asks you to go there and search for her.

Dreadmaul Rock. Dreadmaul Rock is a towering crag and cave complex rising out of the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. It serves as the primary base of operations for the Firegut ogres, who make their home within its winding, subterranean mounds. Towering above the scorched plains of the Burning Steppes, Dreadmaul Rock is a massive stone formation carved out by a labyrinthine cave system. Though its name hints at a possible connection to the Dreadmaul ogres of the Blasted Lands, the rock is held firmly by the Firegut clan. These brutish ogres use the elevated paths, crags, and interior earthen mounds as a defended encampment, dominating the surrounding wasteland and menacing anyone attempting to traverse the northern slopes toward Blackrock Spire.

Dreadmist Den. In the northern Barrens, Burning Blade cultists keep their rites beneath Dreadmist Peak. Red haze fills the cavern they use as a shrine to demons. Dreadmist Den cuts into the jagged slopes of Dreadmist Peak, where Burning Blade cultists gather in a dark sanctuary. Thick crimson vapor hangs through its stone tunnels, dimming the cavern in red twilight. Away from the Horde's watch in the plains below, the cult performs demonic rites, guards its blasphemous relics, and plots to spread corruption across Kalimdor.

Dreadmist Peak. Red haze cloaks Dreadmist Peak, northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens. The Burning Blade cult keeps a hidden refuge on its crags. Dreadmist Peak rises above the Barrens, its crags swallowed by a dense red haze that dims the sky. At the crest and in the hollows below, Burning Blade cultists shelter warlocks and toxicologists. They poison nearby water and scheme against the new powers claiming central Kalimdor.

Dreadmurk Shore. Dreadmurk Shore encompasses the foggy coastline and scattered islands of Dustwallow Marsh running north toward the Barrens. Dominated by aggressive Mirefin murlocs and sea beasts, these treacherous waters have recently become the hiding ground for shipwrecked Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Dustwallow Marsh between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold, Dreadmurk Shore is a dismal expanse of muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands. The coast is overrun by the Mirefin tribe, a territorial clan of murlocs that aggressively attacks any travelers nearing their coastal villages. Sea turtles and aquatic predators prowl the shallows, making the shoreline dangerous to navigate even without factoring in the surrounding swamplands.

Dream Bough. Dream Bough is a colossal Great Tree nestled on an island in the center of Jademir Lake in northern Feralas. The ancient tree shelters a mysterious gateway connecting Azeroth directly to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons loyally watch over the sanctuary, keeping unwanted intruders away from its verdant boughs. Rising high above the canopy of northern Feralas, the Dream Bough stands as the largest tree in the region. Situated in the tranquil waters of Jademir Lake, the towering sentinel houses a natural portal carved into its trunk, providing a direct threshold into the untamed Emerald Dream.

name.esES: Polvo de sueño en el pantano

text.enUS: Dream Dust in the Swamp. Krazek of Booty Bay says that learning about Nazz is quite a favor. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to bring 10 specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, for Krazek's snuff pouch. Bring it back and Krazek will give you the information you seek. Krazek tells you that learning about Nazz is a considerable favor, and that you have already come a long way from the Shimmering Flats for it. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to gather something. The choice falls on ten specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, which Krazek would love for a snuff pouch. Once you return with it, the information is yours.

Dreamer's Rock. Dreamer's Rock is a secluded natural sanctuary tucked deep within the Wailing Caverns past the Screaming Gully. Here lies the sleeping night elf druid Naralex, whose noble effort to revive the Barrens has instead birthed a living nightmare. It serves as both a sacred barrow chamber and the epicenter of the corruption mutating the surrounding subterranean ecosystem. Located in the heart of the Wailing Caverns, Dreamer's Rock functions much like an improvised barrow den. Here, the night elf druid Naralex entered a deep trance to tap the underground springs and channel the Emerald Dream into the arid soil of the Barrens. Instead of bringing life, his connection was seized by dark forces. The nightmare twisting his thoughts now spills physically into this chamber, twisting the local wildlife, turning his followers into the venomous Druids of the Fang, and manifesting terrifying aberrations into the waking world.
Dried Seeds. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem gives travelers Dried Seeds to test the life-giving power beneath the Barrens' waters.

Driftwood. After The Lost Caravan, Watcher Biggs still has a wagon to mend before reaching Nethergarde. Biggs needs strong, dry wood, and sends you east to the coast to search for driftwood dried by the sun. Watcher Biggs says you are owed great thanks, and asks for your help once more. If Biggs is ever to reach Nethergarde, the wagon must be fixed, and that takes strong, dry wood. Wood from the swamp's trees is spongy and tangled, and will not do.

Drowned Reef. The Drowned Reef is a treacherous stretch of coastal waters off the southern cliffs of the Arathi Highlands. Beneath the waves lie ancient sunken ruins, claimed by hostile Daggerspine naga who appear able to control the bay's tides, endangering passing vessels. Just outside the hidden entrance to Faldir's Cove, the Drowned Reef forms a watery graveyard for navigators. Shattered ships, including the Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine, lie submerged beneath the waves. Daggerspine naga led by Prince Nazjak inhabit the reef and appear able to control the bay's tides, dooming crews seeking refuge in the cove.

Drowned Sacellum. At Blackfathom Deeps' entrance, the Drowned Sacellum lies submerged beneath the coast. Brackish saltwater and cavern roots surround its broken stones, now occupied by murlocs and makrura. You enter the Drowned Sacellum just beyond Blackfathom Deeps' threshold. The chapel once offered quiet worship to Elune, but it has long since collapsed into the sea-swept abyss beneath Ashenvale's coast. Brackish pools swallow its ancient marble flagstones, where starfish cling beneath the cavern ceiling's massive roots. Dark wisps flicker dimly through the gloom, lighting a broken stone path. Careful steps along it lead deeper into the temple complex, toward the Pool of Ask'ar.

Drowned Sorrows. Captain Steelgut sits mourning at Faldir's Cove after losing the beloved Maiden's Folly. Steelgut asks you to go after the Daggerspine naga who slaughtered the survivors of the wreck. Captain Steelgut sits by the fire at Faldir's Cove, wishing for a watery grave instead. The crew fought hard to save the beautiful Maiden's Folly, but the sea sank it, with water rushing in all at once. O'Breen reached shore safely, yet naga killed the survivors. Steelgut wants Daggerspine raiders and sorceresses dead.

Druid. Druids are guardians of the natural world who draw power directly from the wild spirits, the celestial bodies, and the Emerald Dream. Master shapeshifters, they adopt the forms of primal beasts to protect the land or mend grievous wounds. Practiced primarily by the night elves, newly revived among the tauren and kept alive by the Skyborne, druids place the preservation of nature above all mortal allegiance. Druidism is far more than a martial art; it is an ancient way of life rooted in deep communion with nature and the demigod Cenarius. Druids wield raw natural energies, commanding roots to entangle their foes, directing the celestial brilliance of the moon and stars, and invoking restorative flora to knit bone and flesh. Their duty is to preserve the cosmic balance and protect the unfettered wild from exploitation and corruption.

Druid of the Claw. Oben Rageclaw’s spirit waits in the barrows beneath Teldrassil, unable to rest. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have bound his body with a dark enchantment, and you can break that bond by destroying his soulless shell. Oben Rageclaw was resting in the barrows beneath Teldrassil when the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs laid a voodoo enchantment over his sleeping body. The magic tore his spirit from his mortal flesh and trapped it in the Emerald Dream. Now his spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his body.

Druids of the Fang. The Druids of the Fang are a sinister sect entrenched deep within the labyrinthine Wailing Caverns. Severing all ties to the Cenarion Circle, these rogue night elves have adopted serpent-like forms under the command of the self-proclaimed Lord Serpentis. While the true origin of their dark communion remains a mystery to outside observers, they relentlessly pursue their grand design: to seize the subterranean waters and remake the Barrens into their own twisted paradise. The Barrens was not always an arid wasteland, and Naralex sought to return it to the lush, verdant sanctuary it once was. Naralex led a dedicated order of young druids into the subterranean depths of the Wailing Caverns, tapping into the natural underground fissures and subterranean springs. By entering an induced slumber, Naralex hoped to channel the living energies of the Emerald Dream into the waterways, nursing the scorched savannah above back to vibrant life.

Drum Fel. At Hammerfall, Drum Fel directs the Horde’s fight to hold Arathi against trolls, ogres, and human remnants. With his wife Korin, he works to secure a lasting foothold for the Horde in the region. Drum Fel commands Hammerfall’s defenses and the Horde’s push into Arathi. From the fortified refuge, he faces rival factions on every side. The Witherbark forest trolls and the Boulderfist ogres hold Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall. Drum knows Hammerfall cannot thrive by keeping to itself; its neighbors’ strength must be broken. He sends veteran champions into hostile territory to disrupt these threats before they can strike the Horde encampment.

Drusilla La Salle. Outside Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle teaches warlocks in the graveyard. The human trainer works beyond the Holy Order’s reach, guiding new spellcasters in shadow and summoning. When forbidden knowledge leaves the abbey, she moves to claim it. Drusilla La Salle teaches novice warlocks among the headstones outside Northshire Abbey. Paladins and priests practice beneath the abbey’s stained glass, while warlocks keep to society’s edges because demonology and fel magic are taboo in Stormwind. Recruits receive tainted correspondence before Drusilla shows them how to wield shadow power without drawing the abbey authorities’ immediate anger.

Dry Hills. Witchwing harpies menace the Dry Hills, where greener slopes rise above the Barrens. The Dry Hills grow greener than the dry plains below, on the Barrens' northwestern edge beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers find little safety among the bluffs. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing harpies from their roosts along the crags. Their raiding parties swoop down on supply caravans along the northern Gold Road. Abandoned orcish fortifications and derelict siege engines lie rotting in the brush.

Dry Times. Barkeep Daniels needs drink for Lakeshire's inn while Blackrock orcs keep the town under siege. The roads are unsafe, and the usual supplies have stopped coming. Blackrock orcs descend from Stonewatch Keep, pressing Lakeshire hard. With supply lines cut and roads unsafe, the inn is running low on drink. Barkeep Daniels turns to travelers who can cross the blocked roads and bring supplies back for frightened villagers and the town guards.

Drygulch Ravine. Dustwind harpies hold Drygulch Ravine, where they menace nearby supply caravans. The gorge lies among eastern Durotar's rocky bluffs, reached by a cave passage from Razorwind Canyon or a perilous drop from above. In the crags east of Orgrimmar, Drygulch Ravine forms a sheltered depression and a lawless pocket of Durotar. A cramped natural tunnel from Razorwind Canyon is its only ground-level route. Dustwind harpies roost along the steep cliffs, where they nest their broods and stockpile goods stolen from Horde supply trains on the regional trails.

Drywhisker Gorge. Drywhisker Gorge is a rugged cleft in the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands, situated northeast of the Horde outpost of Hammerfall. The gorge and its inner cavern are held by a hostile clan of kobolds, who fiercely guard rich mineral deposits and ancient elemental relics buried deep underground. Tucked away in the mountainous folds east of Hammerfall, Drywhisker Gorge serves as the primary redoubt of the Drywhisker clan of kobolds. While kobolds are often dismissed as simple mine pests, the Drywhiskers in Arathi are heavily entrenched. They guard their subterranean passages with fierce territorial tenacity, working veins of rare Lesser Bloodstone Ore and defending the deep recesses of the earth. Their proximity makes them a persistent nuisance to the nearby orcs of Hammerfall.

Duke Hydraxis. Duke Hydraxis is a noble water elemental commanding the Hydraxian Waterlords from a remote, wave-battered islet off the coast of Azshara. Pledged to Neptulon the Tidehunter, he rallies mortal adventurers to strike against his ancient elemental rivals, particularly Ragnaros the Firelord. Perched on a solitary rock northeast of the Ravencrest Monument in Azshara, Duke Hydraxis serves as the primary emissary of the Hydraxian Waterlords. While most elementals bound to Azeroth are hostile and chaotic, Hydraxis acts with measured purpose. As a devoted vassal of Neptulon the Tidehunter, he considers water the purest and most essential of the primal forces. He watches the rising turmoil across Azeroth with cold scrutiny, seeking champions capable of shifting the balance of elemental warfare.

Dun Algaz. Dragonmaw orcs have laid siege to Dun Algaz, cutting easy passage between Ironforge’s lands and Menethil Harbor. The fortified pass and its tunnels link Loch Modan with the Wetlands. Dun Algaz cuts through the jagged peaks between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. The pass predates the War of the Three Hammers. After the Wildhammer clan was driven from Ironforge, its people used this route to migrate north. Stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts guard the way. Whoever holds Dun Algaz controls the only overland road from the dwarven heartlands to Menethil Harbor on the western sea.

Dun Garok. Dun Garok guards the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Captain Ironhill commands its dwarven garrison, which defends Alliance interests and nearby operations such as the Azurelode Mine. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, the stronghold is a military threat on their border. Dun Garok holds the crags in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills. Captain Ironhill commands the Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen who defend the outpost. They guard human settlements in Hillsbrad and protect Alliance operations at the Azurelode Mine. Stone walls and deep entrenchments help the garrison hold against nearby threats.

Dun Mandarr. Dun Mandarr is an abandoned dwarven camp situated before an icy cavern in south-eastern Winterspring. Established by the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper, the site now sits in ruins after its occupants fled an onslaught of enraged local moonkin. Bearing the traditional dwarven prefix 'Dun', Dun Mandarr was established by the explorer Jaron Stoneshaper as a base of operations in the frozen reaches of southeastern Winterspring. Stoneshaper's curiosity proved his undoing when he uncovered a relic known as the Blue-Feathered Amulet. The artifact's disturbance provoked the fury of the native wildkin, who descended upon the encampment in an uncontrollable rage. Overwhelmed and driven out, the dwarves abandoned the camp entirely. Today, no friendly souls remain among the snowbanks; ferocious, territorial moonkin guard the cavern and prowl the broken shelters.

Dun Modr. Dun Modr has fallen to Dark Iron dwarves, leaving the Thandol Span's southern approach in hostile hands. The fortress once changed hands in a fierce struggle during the Second War. At Wetlands' northern edge, Dun Modr commands the main road between Khaz Modan and the northern human kingdoms. That route has drawn armies to the fortress across the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde seized the dwarven stronghold and used it to launch raids and resist Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors sailed from Tol Barad to reclaim it, and the Orcs struck back in a bloody struggle. Alliance forces under Lord Anduin Lothar eventually drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, returning the fortress to dwarven hands.

Dunemaul Compound. Dunemaul Compound serves as the central settlement and ogre mound for the Dunemaul clan in Tanaris. Tucked into the rocky ridges bordering the desert wastes, it houses the clan's brute enforcers and spellcasters. Carved into the rugged desert rock of western Tanaris, the Dunemaul Compound is the primary stronghold of the Dunemaul ogres. These hulking desert dwellers have adapted to the harsh arid climate, scratching out an existence through brute force and opportunism. The compound itself centers on an ogre mound and cave network. Though primitive, the clan fields a dangerous mix of warriors, enforcers, and twisted spellcasters practicing dark warlock and mage magics. For travelers journeying across the dunes, the settlement is a treacherous den of aggressive giants who violently reject uninvited guests.

Dungar Longdrink. At Stormwind's Trade District roost, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon transport for supplies bound to Westfall's embattled defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have pushed Westfall close to breaking point. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia are desperate for provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the requested equipment. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier.

Durnan Furcutter. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Durnan Furcutter outfits young dwarves and gnomes. He works inside the settlement as a clothier and leather merchant, selling light attire for the mountain cold. Inside Anvilmar, young dwarves and exiled gnomes prove themselves, and some need more freedom of movement than heavy iron allows. Durnan Furcutter sells light, pliable layers to scouts, rogues, and spellcasters who want to stay agile in Dun Morogh's bitter winds. He works near Anvilmar's hearth, offering everyday tailoring and stitched leather. He claims his stock is the finest in the valley.
