text.enUS: Excavation Progress Report. In Loch Modan, Ironband sends an excavation report to Thelsamar. Prospector Ironband asks you to carry his latest dispatches and renewed explosive supply orders to Jern Hornhelm. Prospector Ironband's dig in Loch Modan depends on supplies from nearby settlements. Excavation takes picks, workers, and plenty of blasting powder to break through bedrock. Ironband sends runners with regular reports and supply requests to Jern Hornhelm, his local contact in Thelsamar.

Excelsior. In Booty Bay, Drizzlik has finished the inner part of the Excelsior boots and now needs the skin of an elder saltwater crocolisk for the outside. With the inside done, only the outer layer remains, and for it Drizzlik uses nothing but the finest elder crocolisk skins, which are tougher and make a better surface for the designs and accents of the Excelsior line. The only skin that fits Drizzlik's plan is that of an elder saltwater crocolisk, and finding one is hard, for such elders come out only to guard other saltwater crocolisks. Drizzlik has also read somewhere that the numbers of saltwater crocolisks are dwindling, which would hurt business.

Executor Arren. At Deathknell, Executor Arren directs the settlement's defense as new undead rise from their graves. He leads efforts against Scourge zombies, wild beasts, and threats to the Forsaken. Executor Arren directs Deathknell's defense from outside its chapel. While caretakers in the crypts guide newly risen undead through their confusion, Arren turns their attention to survival beyond the graves. Under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's banner, he organizes efforts to clear mindless zombies from the village borders. The Forsaken secure ground here in the shadow of Lordaeron's fall.

Executor Zygand. At Brill's town hall, Executor Zygand directs Forsaken defenses across central Tirisfal Glades. He reports to the Undercity's high command and coordinates the fight against Scarlet Crusade forces pressing into Forsaken lands. Executor Zygand directs regional defenses from Brill after the Forsaken's awakening in Deathknell. Officers such as Executor Arren and field sentries such as Deathguard Linnea report to him. He gathers scouts' reports and sends able recruits to guard Lordaeron's borders against encroachment.

Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind. The letter asks City Architect Baros Alexston to recognize Auberdine's work and its home. Auberdine now links Darkshore to Stormwind by sea. Night elves once kept to Kalimdor's forests, apart from the Eastern Kingdoms, but after the Third War they joined the Grand Alliance. The new passage gives the northern port a direct tie to the human kingdom. Local leaders want the shipping route secured and Auberdine connected to the wider Alliance. Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, ruined cities nearby, have long drawn more notice than the living coastal settlement.

Explorers' League. The Explorers' League is a renowned dwarven archaeological guild headquartered in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Founded under King Magni Bronzebeard and led by his wandering brother Brann, the League seeks to uncover the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Their expansive digs span across Azeroth, uncovering ancient titan ruins while frequently igniting regional conflicts. For centuries, the dwarves of Khaz Modan focused their formidable energies on mining, stonework, and engineering. That focus changed drastically when ancient ruins were unearthed, hinting at a forgotten legacy connecting dwarves to mythical titan creators. Eager to solve the mystery of his people's beginnings, King Magni Bronzebeard decreed that dwarven industry pivot heavily toward archaeology. Magni, alongside his brother Brann, established the Explorers' Guild—now widely known as the Explorers' League—to scour the world for relics, forgotten cities, and traces of their ancient ancestry.

Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, toxic industry beneath the Deadmines is poisoning the farmland. You travel to Stormwind's Dwarven District to seek an engineer who can supply heavy explosives. Westfall faces displaced vagrants and banditry under the Defias Brotherhood. Evidence from across the region points to a coordinated, mechanised threat underground. Industrial refuse and caustic toxins foul the soil, and their trail leads into the Deadmines, where an organized operation works below the earth.

Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, Sprite Jumpsprocket sends a volatile charge to Alba Fairmoon. The primed explosives must reach her safely, with the detonator undisturbed. Sprite Jumpsprocket has finished a bundle of Extra-Destructive Explosives for Alba Fairmoon. Carrying a live charge through wartime Westfall adds danger to a road already threatened by Defias bandits and feral beasts.

Explosive Stick of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire turns stolen dwarven plans against Bael Modan. He built the charge to sabotage the dwarves’ flying machine. When Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor, the dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm’s blueprints to avenge his displaced and fallen kin. He studied the plans and assembled a charge with enough force to wreck heavy machinery.

Eyes of the Sentinels. Eyes of the Sentinels is a Darnassus quest where players assist Sentinel Dalia Sunblade in stationing magical scout owls at critical posts throughout the night elven capital. Facing growing unease across Teldrassil, this aerial surveillance bolsters the city's defenses while allowing the Sentinels time for prayer to Elune. In the sacred sanctuary of the Temple of the Moon, Sentinel Dalia Sunblade maintains the vigil over Darnassus. Guided by General Shandris Feathermoon's decree that every warrior must balance martial prowess with spiritual devotion, Dalia arranges the deployment of watchful sentinel owls across key city hubs. Taking over these daily duties affords the sentinel valuable moments of prayer and reflection before the Moon Goddess, while ensuring the kaldorei capital remains tightly guarded.

Facing Negolash. Following the trail of Captain Hecklebury Smotts' lost weapon, Sprogger reveals a plan to bait the giant Negolash using the creature's favorite delicacies. By staging a banquet in a wrecked lifeboat on the coast of Stranglethorn Vale, adventurers can confront the brute and reclaim the captain's stolen cutlass. When giants smashed Captain Smotts' vessel, one brute named Negolash headed straight for the galley. Unlike his brethren, he wasn't hungry for the crew. Sprogger saw that Negolash wanted wine and Barbecued Buzzard Wings, Sprogger's own specialty, whose recipe he had to travel to the Badlands to get.

Faded Shadowhide Pendant. A voice now comes from the Faded Shadowhide Pendant, found in the Redridge Mountains. The Shadowhide gnolls wore it to receive orders from Morganth, and the delayed message is a spell cast by Theocritus. The Shadowhide gnolls of the Redridge Mountains follow Morganth and coordinate their movements through enchanted pendants. From his sanctuary at Tower Azora, High Mage Theocritus studied the talismans and devised a spell to breach their magical link. His broadcast took weeks to appear. This faded pendant proves the gnolls’ communication can be intercepted, giving Theocritus a way to disrupt Morganth’s reach.

Faerie Dragon Muisek. After the hippogryph spirits, Witch Doctor Uzer'i wants the spirit of a faerie dragon next. You are sent west to hunt sprite darters and sprite dragons and capture what makes them strong. Uzer'i points out that faerie dragons seem delicate, yet their spirit is the real prize. They have been allies to the night elves, and Uzer'i wants the Horde to share in that strength. Uzer'i gives you a Muisek Vessel and sends you west to slay eight sprite darters or sprite dragons, then shrink and capture each fallen faerie dragon with it.

Falaath Village. Falaath Village is a gathering place for penitent shen'dorei seeking to win back the favor of the Windlord, Al'Akir. Marked recruits journey from Shen'dar Village to report to Missionary Jasaan and join their fellow faithful. In Shen'dar Village, Sania Silverstream laments that her people grew prideful, taking the bounty of the air for granted until the spirits of the wind abandoned them into stagnation. To remedy this fall from grace, penitent recruits are marked and sent to Falaath Village, seeking fellowship with fellow shen'dorei who believe that only acts of contrition can restore the wind's favor.

Faldir's Cove. Faldir's Cove is a secluded natural harbor nestled along the southern coastline of the Arathi Highlands. Steeped in human history, it is traditionally remembered as the departure point from which early settlers sailed south to found Stormwind. Today, it serves as an emergency shelter for stranded Blackwater Raiders whose fleet ran afoul of local hazards. Tucked away behind the rugged bluffs south of Stromgarde Keep, Faldir's Cove is linked to the mainland by a concealed cave tunnel. The cove honors the memory of Faldir, the ancient Arathor explorer whose expedition set sail from these very shores to cross the Great Sea and establish the southern kingdom of Stormwind. In the present day, however, its quiet waters house a very different crowd: an expedition of Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay, led by Captains Steelgut and O'Breen, who sailed north pursuing ancient elven treasures only to end up trapped in the bay.

Falfarren River. The Falfarren River cuts through central Ashenvale, from Mount Hyjal toward the northern mountains of the Barrens. Its banks mark the divide between night elven lands and Horde outposts, where travelers face wild dangers and open conflict. The Falfarren River descends from Mount Hyjal, spilling over waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. In ordinary weather, its waters are neither especially deep nor impassable. The river marks a rough boundary through central Ashenvale. Astranaar and the heart of the Kaldorei lands lie west; Horde camps and lumber operations lie east. The wooden bridges on the main road carry travelers into the contested forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

Falfindel Waywarder. Falfindel Waywarder is a night elf druid stationed at Thalanaar, the outpost guarding the border between Feralas and the Thousand Needles. From this frontier watchpost, he works to heal corrupted lands and safeguard the southern wilderness of Kalimdor. Travelers wandering down from Stonetalon or the Barrens often find him seeking aid to restore balance to the wild. Thalanaar marks the gateway where the lush forests of Feralas descend into the towering mesas and dry salt plains of Thousand Needles. Falfindel Waywarder stands watch at this remote outpost, greeting weary travelers who have ventured far across the continent. Surrounded by natural grandeur and lurking dangers, he serves as a point of contact for the night elves seeking to monitor both local threats and broader environmental calamities across Kalimdor.

Fall of Dun Modr. At Dun Modr, a northern fortress has fallen to a violent Dark Iron assault. In Menethil Harbor, a severely wounded survivor seeks an Alliance adventurer to go north and learn whether commander Longbraid the Grim or any of the garrison survived. For generations, Dun Modr has guarded northern Khaz Modan and the vital road and bridge across the Thandol Span, linking the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. After an ambush at the bridge, the garrison fell back to regroup inside the fortress. Before they could restore their defenses, overwhelming Dark Iron forces struck, slaughtering the defenders and driving them into a desperate flight.

Falla Sagewind. On a crag above the Barrens, Falla Sagewind watches the land for signs of trouble. Her camp lies between the Crossroads and the Lushwater Oasis, where she studies changes in nature and magic. Falla Sagewind keeps camp on a secluded summit southwest of the Crossroads, high above the Barrens trails. From there, she watches the savanna and the changes in its wildlife. She also studies corruption rising from fissures beneath the Wailing Caverns. Her vigil keeps her apart from the daily trade at the Crossroads, but her attention remains on the spirits and wounds of the land.

name.frFR: Héros de la Horde tombé au combat

text.enUS: Fallen Hero of the Horde. The Fallen Hero of the Horde is the lingering spirit of an orc warrior standing watch on the southern road out of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bound by regret and dishonor, he warns passing travelers of the horrors awaiting them in the Blasted Lands and seeks champions willing to deliver his tortured soldiers from demonic bondage. In life, this warrior was a celebrated champion dispatched with a handpicked regiment of soldiers to investigate the Blasted Lands and report back on the presence of the Burning Legion. His dispatch never made it; the courier sent north toward Stonard was ambushed and slain by the Swamp Talker and his murlocs. Stranded without orders or reinforcements, the commander eventually marched his soldiers south into the shattered wastes to confront the growing darkness. It was a fatal misjudgment. Overwhelmed by demonic forces, his army was scattered, captured, and subjected to horrific torment at the hands of the dreadlord Razelikh the Defiler.

Fallen Moonstone. At Fallen Sky Lake in Ashenvale, night elves gather luminous, magically charged Fallen Moonstones from its tranquil waters. Sacred lunar energy gives the stones restorative power that can renew vitality and cure severe frailty. Southeast of Astranaar, Fallen Sky Lake once yielded many stones along its shores and shallows. Night elves prized their restorative magic and lunar blessing when ordinary remedies failed. Gathering them grew dangerous after corrupt Shadethicket bog beasts overran the lake. Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, hoarded every stone it found on a small island at the lake’s center, cutting the local Kaldorei off from a vital source of healing.

Fallen Sky Lake. At Fallen Sky Lake, a moonstone may be the only hope for Relara, whose fever has broken but whose strength is nearly gone. Her father, Pelturas Whitemoon, sends you to the waters southeast of Astranaar, where a corrupted Shadethicket Oracle guards the fallen stones. Pelturas Whitemoon has watched his young daughter, Relara, slip closer to death through days of illness. Remedies made from Bathran's hair and stardust broke her raging fever, but left her body hollow and frail. Pelturas fears she has only breaths remaining before her spirit fades permanently into the night.

Fallen Sky Lake. In eastern Ashenvale, Fallen Sky Lake lies between Silverwing Outpost and the Warsong Labor Camp. Shadethickets defend its shores and central isle. Fallen Sky Lake lies south of Silverwing Outpost and west of the Warsong Labor Camp. Shadethickets, hulking bog beasts, roam its shores and the small isle at its center, treating intruders as threats. A powerful Shadethicket Oracle rules from the isle's heart. The Oracle hoards the fallen moonstones once gathered at the lake and keeps the shadethickets bound to the waters, ever watchful for travelers.

Fallen in the Fen. Fallen in the Fen is a somber journey begun by uncovering a fallen dwarf amidst an excavation site. Delivering the tragic news to his brother, Dorin Songblade in Lakeshire, brings closure to a heartbroken craftsman who had been forging gifts for his departed kin. A quiet tragedy unfolds at the excavation sites, where the lifeless body of an adventurous dwarf is discovered. After covering the remains with the dwarf's own cloak, an adventurer carries the grim news back to Lakeshire to find his kin.

Falling With Style. "Falling With Style" is an introductory rite of passage for young Skyborne in Thendal Village. Offered atop the local watchtower by the mischievous Myriaal Mistwake, it challenges novices to test their innate slow-fall ability by leaping from the platform toward Rorian the Dayseeker below. Perched high above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage through a game of daring. Rather than treating their innate magical gifts as sacred relics kept under strict restraint, Myriaal encourages newcomers to leap into the open air from the watchtower ledge. The purpose is practical as well as playful: mastering the instinctive art of walking upon air before life beyond the grove demands it in perilous situations.

Fallow Sanctuary. The Fallow Sanctuary is a secluded village hidden deep within the bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as home to an isolated tribe of mutated draenei known as the Lost Ones, whose severe grief and homesickness have driven them feral. Tucked away among the sunken trees of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Fallow Sanctuary was established by stranded Lost Ones seeking a place of their own. Severed from their ancestral world and deformed by dark energies, these wretched outcasts found no peace in the marshland. Over time, relentless sorrow and isolation shattered their sanity, reducing the tribe to a hostile, feral state where they fiercely attack any outsiders who trespass into their village.

Family Tree. Cliffwatcher Longhorn asks you to carry a report to Nataka Longhorn, Cliffwatcher's brother, who is stationed in Desolace. Word of unusual centaur activity is meant to reach Ghost Walker Post. Nataka, Cliffwatcher's brother, holds a posting at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. A year has passed since Cliffwatcher last wrote, and in that time the centaurs have been behaving unusually. Nataka should hear of it, and you are asked to carry the report.

Fandral Staghelm. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Stepping into power after Malfurion Stormrage vanished into the Emerald Dream, he championed the planting of the new World Tree, Teldrassil. Proud, abrasive, and relentlessly ambitious, Fandral advocates for an aggressive Kaldorei resurgence that frequently pits him against High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Following the Third War and the sacrifice of Nordrassil atop Mount Hyjal, the night elves lost their immortality and their sacred sanctuary. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished, Fandral took up leadership of the druids and convinced the Circle of Ancients that it was time for their people to rebuild and regain their immortality. With the Circle's approval, he led the druids in raising Teldrassil off the coast of Kalimdor. He envisioned the colossal bough as a monument to Kaldorei endurance and a vessel to restore their lost supremacy, even though the Dragon Aspects pointedly withheld their blessings from the unapproved endeavor.

Fandral's Message. In Darnassus, Fandral Staghelm sends a message across the sea to Onu in Darkshore. The sealed dispatch carries news about Oracle Glade in Teldrassil. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm writes from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. His sealed dispatch is addressed to Onu, the Ancient of Lore who dwells in the Grove of the Ancients. Reports have reached Fandral about the state of Oracle Glade in Teldrassil, and he sends a courier south of Auberdine with word for Onu. The journey crosses the waters to Darkshore, carrying a message from the heart of the new World Tree to Kalimdor’s older, shadowed mainland.

Fang of Githyiss. The Fang of Githyiss is a rare and formidable specimen taken from a giant arachnid stalking the wilds near Aldrassil. Delivering the fang to a naturalist in the sanctuary allows scholars to study the monstrous creature and monitor the predatory threats nesting within Shadowglen. The Fang of Githyiss is a trophy and biological sample harvested from the overgrown spider Githyiss, who lurks in the wilds of Shadowglen. A beast of such notable bulk poses a clear threat to young travelers venturing out from Aldrassil, making the recovery of its fang both a matter of safety and scientific interest. Rather than letting the creature's remains rot in the underbrush, resourceful scouts take the specimen back to the sanctuary of the great tree.

Fang of Vagash. In Dun Morogh, Vagash threatens the breeders’ prized rams from the snowy crags. The Fang of Vagash proves the notorious marauding predator has been slain. Vagash is a savage beast that stalks downhill from the ridges above Amberstill Ranch, often under cover of darkness, to slaughter prized rams. Dun Morogh’s high crags shelter bitter cold and fierce predators, but none have plagued the local ranches as Vagash has. Ironforge’s troops are stretched thin, leaving herdsmen without the city guard’s protection. A severed fang gives the breeders proof that Vagash is dead and the pasturelands are safe again.

Fangore's Paw. In the Redridge Mountains, Lieutenant Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnolls against Lakeshire. His severed paw proves his death to Magistrate Solomon, whose bounty seeks to end the threat Fangore poses to the besieged town. Lieutenant Fangore is a primary field commander among the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching across the Redridge Mountains. He serves the renegade mage Morganth and directs attacks on trade roads, outlying farms, and the defenses around Lake Everstill. Gnoll raiders leave no uniforms, official seals, or banners to confirm their dead, so the township authorities rely on physical proof. Magistrate Solomon demanded Fangore's paw to prove he had been executed, giving Lakeshire some relief amid the dangers closing around the town.

Faol's Rest. In eastern Tirisfal, Faol's Rest lies neglected southwest of the Scarlet Monastery. The gravesite holds the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, founder of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Beneath the blighted canopy, it is now a resting place for spirits who perish near the monastery. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, mourners traveled to Faol's Rest to honor Archbishop Alonsus Faol. He led the Church of the Holy Light through the dark days of the Second War and founded the paladins to protect humanity. Faol died peacefully before the Scourge arrived, spared the agony of seeing his kingdom fall. In those years, mourners journeyed up the road from Capital City to leave offerings and pay their respects to the beloved patriarch.

Far Watch Post. Horde defenders hold Far Watch Post west of the Southfury River bridge, guarding the homeland's frontier. The outpost protects vital trade caravans from quilboar packs and Alliance incursions. Far Watch Post guards the western foot of the bridge from Durotar into the Barrens. You enter a vast, arid savannah, where this is the first sign of Horde authority. The settlement is spare but built for readiness, with an orcish watchtower, a burrow, and siege catapults aimed across the plains. South of the main road, peons tend riding wolves for messengers or reinforcements. The post keeps the supply road to Crossroads secure, screening travelers and turning back raids by roaming quilboar tribes and Alliance scouts.

Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds now swarm through Fargodeep Mine, south of Goldshire in central Elwynn Forest. The mine once brought gold to Stormwind, but its tunnels are now a kobold warren. Gold once flowed from Fargodeep Mine into Stormwind's treasury. As the Kingdom's military presence in Elwynn dwindled, outlying resources became vulnerable. Kobolds soon filled the mine's dark tunnels and made a warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's authorities fear the lost ore and the danger to nearby farms, including the Stonefield and Maclure holdings.

Farmer Furlbrow. Near the Jansen Stead, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife are stranded beside their broken wagon. Driven from their northern Westfall farm by the Defias Brotherhood, they hope to reach Elwynn Forest. Theodore Furlbrow left his pumpkin patch in northern Westfall with his wife, Verna, as criminals drove them from their home. They salvaged what they could and set out for Elwynn Forest, urging neighbors such as Farmer Saldean to leave too. Near the Jansen Stead, their wagon broke down, leaving them exposed to bandits and wild beasts. Verna tends to their horse, Old Blanchy, while Theodore keeps watch over the road. He hopes to recover the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day and warn Sentinel Hill about the approaching bandits.

Farmer Saldean. At Saldean's Farm in central Westfall, Farmer Saldean keeps working the troubled fields beside his wife, Salma. While other farmers flee or give up, the veteran homesteader faces rogue harvest golems and growing banditry. Farmer Saldean remembers when Westfall prospered, before those years crumbled away. Overgrown fields, rampaging mechanical harvest watchers, and predatory bandits now surround his farm, but he refuses to yield his land. Other homesteaders have abandoned their acres or turned to thievery. Saldean and his wife, Salma, stay and work to harvest what little grain they can. He asks wandering adventurers to destroy the rogue Harvest Watchers that have taken over his fields and his neighbors' fields, so he can clear the soil for planting.

Farren's Proof. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle sends Alliance recruits along Southshore's coast to prove his patrol's success. Marshal Redpath wants evidence that the murlocs have been cleared from the Western Strand. After the first coastal sweeps in Down the Coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle faces scrutiny from Marshal Redpath and Southshore's leaders. Farren claims the local murlocs have been cleared, but his superiors want proof. He leaves the grim work to wandering Alliance adventurers and sends them back to the shore for evidence of the kills.

Farren's Proof. At Southshore, Farren's Proof brings Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's report to Marshal Redpath. The murloc heads prove the work is done, though Farren will not carry them himself. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle patrols and secures Hillsbrad Foothills' southern coast, but the brutal work of frontier warfare turns his stomach. After you cull the murlocs along the beaches, he cannot bring himself to touch the severed heads you bring back as proof. He sends you across Southshore to deliver them to the town's command.

Farren's Proof. At Southshore, Farren's Proof carries Marshal Redpath's orders to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. The Marshal wants him to turn his attention to the naga pressing along the Eastern Strand. Marshal Redpath sends word across Southshore to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Fresh reports speak of naga incursions on the Eastern Strand, and the Marshal wants Orinelle to focus on that threat. He orders the lieutenant to set aside other concerns, drive back the naga, and report his progress in person.

Farren's Report. In Southshore, Farren's Report carries Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's findings on the local naga. He hopes the dispatch will win him a return to Stormwind. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew tired of Southshore's embattled coast, its local leadership, and its remote frontier. He had adventurers hunt the Daggerspine naga to gather proof of their threat, then gathered the findings into a formal report. Farren plans to send it to Major Samuelson, captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep, rather than to his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath. Samuelson trained Farren, and Farren hopes the report will show his competence and earn him an immediate transfer back to Stormwind City's comforts.

Farsen's Watch. High above Gol'Bolar Quarry, Earthseer Farsen watches for Dark Iron movement in Dun Morogh. The visiting Wildhammer shaman uses farsight to reveal their growing infiltration near Ironforge, beginning a path toward the Hall of Thanes. Earthseer Farsen keeps a vigilant watch over the lower reaches of Dun Morogh from above Gol'Bolar Quarry. He journeyed south from the crags of Aerie Peak, bringing a Wildhammer's spiritual awareness to lands usually patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers. Farsen uses his clan's traditional arts to sense subterranean rumblings and watch for unexpected movement along the hillsides.

Farstrider Lodge. Hunters and travelers come to Farstrider Lodge in southeastern Loch Modan for training, supplies, and work in the wilds. Its high elven style sets it apart, though dwarves and humans live there too. Farstrider Lodge has an unusual look among the stone buildings of Khaz Modan. Its design suggests high elven craft. Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf who still lives there, among dwarves and humans. No one knows who founded the lodge or when it was built.

Farthing. Farthing serves the faithful from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. The kind and wise human clergyman guides parishioners and directs aid to settlements across the kingdom. Bishop Farthing tends to the spiritual needs of Stormwind City from the Cathedral of Light. Alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy, he counsels travelers, assists those pursuing the holy arts, and attends to the Church of the Holy Light's civic and pastoral duties.

Fathom Core. Beneath the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core records the elements at work in Blackfathom Deeps. The Earthen Ring seeks it to learn how the Twilight's Hammer is manipulating those forces. The Fathom Core rests inside an ancient fathom stone beneath the Moonshrine Ruins. It records shifts, disruptions, and surges in the elements over time. Je'neu Sancrea, an Earthen Ring shaman at Zoram'gar Outpost, seeks the core to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cultists are turning the region's elements to their own ends.

Favor for Krazek. While repairing a crock pot brought down to Booty Bay, the goblin Krazek demands a personal favor in return. He wants rare lesser bloodstone ore retrieved from a distant cave in the northern hills before he will hand back the repaired cookware. After accepting the broken cookware in Booty Bay, Krazek pauses his tinkering to ask for a trade. Rather than repairing the pot for free, he directs you far northward into the Arathi Highlands. Within a cave in Drywhisker Gorge lies lesser bloodstone ore, a low-grade yet prized mineral sought after by those who understand its properties.

Feast at the Blue Recluse. Your work for Morgan Stern in Dustwallow Marsh, ending with ... and Bugs, leads you back to Angus Stern at the Blue Recluse. Angus Stern is the uncle of Morgan Stern, whose recipe research you helped with in Dustwallow Marsh. Your road now leads back to Angus at the Blue Recluse.

Feather Charm. In Anvilmar, the Frostmane novices' Feather Charms draw a warlock instructor's interest. Their crude trinkets carry a faint magical power. Southwest of Anvilmar, Frostmane novices carry feather charms through the snowy caverns. Their tribe is known for territorial savagery, yet the young trolls dabble in primitive spellcraft. The charms hold a faint but unmistakable magical power. In Anvilmar, warlock instructor Alamar Grimm studies this crude trollcraft with interest. He uses the charms as a proving ground for fledgling warlocks seeking to master the binding of their first imp.

Feathermoon Stronghold. Feathermoon Stronghold is the premier night elf military base in southern Kalimdor, situated securely on Sardor Isle off the Forgotten Coast of Feralas. Commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, this fortified outpost projects Sentinel strength across the wild forest and keeps watch over regional threats. Perched on Sardor Isle across the channel from Feralas's mainland, Feathermoon Stronghold serves as the primary strategic base for the Sentinels in southern Kalimdor. Built among ancient elven groves and supplied with a sacred moonwell, the fortress houses archers, huntresses, and support staff under the direct supervision of General Shandris Feathermoon. From this insular sanctuary, the night elves project their influence over the verdant interior of Feralas, guarding against demonic corruption, hostile wildlife, and encroaching Horde expeditions.

Feathermoon Stronghold (Classic). Feathermoon Stronghold is a fortified night elf bastion situated on Sardor Isle off the western shores of Feralas. Established by General Shandris Feathermoon, it serves as the Alliance's primary staging ground and military anchor in southern Kalimdor. Perched on Sardor Isle just off the Forgotten Coast, Feathermoon Stronghold stands as a crucial bulwark for the Night Elves and the broader Alliance. Built under the direction of General Shandris Feathermoon—Tyrande Whisperwind's trusted lieutenant for ten millennia—the fortress projects Sentinel power deep into southern Kalimdor. Its isolated island geography shields it from the beasts, ogres, and Horde interlopers prowling the primeval jungles of mainland Feralas.

Feathers for Binding. Feathers for Binding is a quest in Shadowgale Forest centered on gathering insulating plumage from young shrieklings to craft a protective medicinal poultice. While these normally docile creatures have grown dangerously aggressive, their feathers remain essential for preserving antiseptic salves against the elements. Adventurers must brave the hostile fledglings to secure the materials needed for regional care. In the depths of Shadowgale Forest, preparing field medicine often demands resourcefulness from the land. When treating grave injuries, herbalists and healers turn to a specialized poultice built on moss and antiseptic tree sap. To ensure the sap does not rapidly dry out or lose its potency to harsh weather, durable insulative bindings are required. The juvenile feathers of Shadowgale shrieklings provide an ideal natural barrier, shielding the wound while sealing in the medicinal treatment.

Feegly the Exiled. Near the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens, Feegly the Exiled lurks alone. Once praised as one of the expedition’s finest diggers, he was driven off by General Twinbraid after claiming an uncovered relic’s power as his own.

Feero Ironhand. At Maestra's Post, Feero Ironhand guards the road between Darkshore and Ashenvale. He works with Delgren the Purifier against the Cult of the Dark Strand. Maestra's Post watches the road south from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Feero Ironhand serves at the outpost, keeping communication and trade with Auberdine moving while watching the surrounding woods. He and Delgren the Purifier oppose the Cult of the Dark Strand. Cultists and forest predators threaten the path between Darnassus's supply lines and Ashenvale's front lines.

Fel Cone. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones carry corruption into the forest. Night elf defenders put the pods to use against nearby tricksters. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones show that corruption has reached the young tree. Gnarled and fallen, the pine cones billow foul green smoke. They lie scattered just east of Dolanaar. Tainted magic has warped the surrounding flora, and the pods are dangerous to touch or eat without caution.

Fel Moss. Fel Moss spreads through Teldrassil’s forests, its insidious corruptive energies carried by hostile grell and grellkin. The taint threatens the World Tree’s wildlife and native furbolg tribes. Corruption has reached Teldrassil’s boughs, though the World Tree was planted to restore the night elves’ immortality and heal the natural world. Fel Moss is one clear sign of that decay. Impish grell and grellkin infest Shadowglen, with the unnatural, wicked magic of the moss clinging to them and radiating from their growth. The dryad Tarindrella gathers samples to measure how deeply the rot has entered the sacred woodland canopy.

Fel Rock. North of Dolanaar, Fel Rock has fallen under a spreading corruption. Lord Melenas and his grells have turned the once-tranquil cavern into a threat within Teldrassil’s woods. North of Dolanaar, Fel Rock lies among Teldrassil’s forested hills. Once a peaceful cavern in wood and stone, it is now overtaken by twisted roots, unnatural shadows, wild grells and grellkin. The taint reaches into the world tree’s boughs.

Fel'zerul. Fel'zerul is an orc warlock stationed at Stonard in the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows. Acting under direct orders from Warchief Thrall, he investigates the ominous presence lurking within the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar. While Thrall's Horde generally views dark arts with suspicion, the Warchief recognizes that understanding sinister powers requires those who study them. Fel'zerul was dispatched to Stonard specifically to unravel the corruption surrounding the Pool of Tears and the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. By directing adventurers to recover artifacts and investigate the exiled Atal'ai trolls, the warlock seeks to determine what evil stirs beneath the murky waters before it threatens the Horde's southern outpost.

Felfire Hill. In eastern Ashenvale, Felfire Hill remains a blighted rise crawling with demons. Infernals struck it during the Third War, and its soil still burns with fel power. Horde guards hold the bridges leading to the hill, near their settlements. During the Third War, the Burning Legion sent flaming meteors across Kalimdor, carrying its fearsome infernals. Several struck this ridge in Ashenvale, burning away the ancient woodland and corrupting the earth. The Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, but demons that survived its defeat still prowl the scorched slopes. Fel energy saturates the land they haunt.

Felgur Twocuts. Felgur Twocuts is a blunt orc scout stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. He coordinates Horde efforts against the regional centaur clans. Standing watch amid the bleak expanse of Ghost Walker Post in central Desolace, Felgur Twocuts has little patience for pleasantries. As a forward scout for the Horde, he assesses the threats facing travelers and settlers venturing west through the mountains, particularly the local Kolkar centaur.

Felix Whindlebolt. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Felix Whindlebolt seeks shelter after fleeing Gnomeregan. He lost his belongings in the rush, and Frostmane trolls carried them away. Felix Whindlebolt fled Gnomeregan when radiation flooded the city. In his haste, he lost his personal belongings and tools. Frostmane ice trolls carried his chest, box and bucket of bolts to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. Now stranded without his gear, Felix relies on travelers to retrieve it.

Felix's Box. Felix Whindlebolt's box lies in Frostmane camps southwest of Anvilmar, far from the gnome refugee who lost it. Radiation swept through Gnomeregan during the failed attempt to purge the trogg menace, and Felix Whindlebolt fled with the gnomes into Coldridge Valley. In his rush to escape the fumes, he left his personal possessions and crafting gear along the snowy road. Frostmane trolls plundered the roadside goods before Felix could return. They carried his box, his chest, and his bucket of bolts to their settlements southwest of Anvilmar.

Felix's Bucket of Bolts. In Dun Morogh, Felix Whindlebolt is missing the tools he carried from Gnomeregan. Frostmane trolls seized his bucket during his flight and took it to their camps. Felix Whindlebolt lost his tools while fleeing Gnomeregan. After the disaster against the troggs, radiation drove thousands of gnomes into Dun Morogh's freezing wilds with whatever they could carry. Felix escaped with his equipment and headed for Anvilmar, but Frostmane trolls from the crags southwest of town ambushed him. They plundered his belongings, including his bucket of bolts and parts, leaving the artisan without the materials he needed for his craft in exile.

Felix's Chest. Felix's Chest lies in a Frostmane camp southwest of Anvilmar. It holds belongings lost by the exiled gnome during the flight from Gnomeregan. Felix Whindlebolt fled Gnomeregan with the other gnomes when troggs and toxic radioactive fallout drove them from the city. The refugees crossed into snowy Dun Morogh with whatever they could carry. In the confusion, Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook scattered survivors. Felix lost his toolkits and belongings, and the trolls hauled his sturdy chest to their camps in the crags southwest of Anvilmar.

Felpaw Village. Felpaw Village is a corrupted furbolg settlement nestled in the far northern reaches of Felwood, guarding the mountain path leading directly to Timbermaw Hold. Inhabited by the fallen Deadwood tribe, its huts and gathering grounds are tainted by demonic influence and hostile to all outsiders. Situated at the northern edge of Felwood, Felpaw Village serves as the primary northern redoubt for the fallen Deadwood furbolgs. Once gentle forest wardens, the tribe fell victim to the demonic blight unleashed during the Third War, driving them into a state of feral madness. Now, the village stands as a blighted enclave filled with crude huts, ritual totems, and hostile warriors who attack anyone wandering near the tunnel entrance to Timbermaw Hold.

Felstalker Hoof. In Durotar's Valley of Trials, young shaman face demonic felstalkers as a test of readiness. Their hooves are brought to Canaga Earthcaller before they learn to commune with the earth spirits. Canaga Earthcaller sends young shaman against the demonic taint threatening Durotar. The Burning Blade Coven lies north in the Valley of Trials, where felstalkers roam among the coven's vile familiars. Taking a felstalker's hoof tests a shaman's endurance, resolve, and spirit. Those who subdue the beasts prove ready to receive the secrets of the earth and prepare the ceremonial sapta for communing with elemental spirits.

Felstone Field. Felstone Field is a blighted farmstead located in the northwestern Western Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron agricultural land, it has been claimed by the Scourge and anchored by a plague cauldron spewing toxic fumes across the ruined soil. Before the Third War, Felstone Field was a peaceful, productive family farm feeding the citizens of Lordaeron. When the plague swept through the north, the homestead fell swiftly to the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge. Today, the fields sprout dead weeds and creeping rot instead of grain. At the heart of the farmland sits an enormous plague cauldron, continuously churning foul vapors into the sky under the watch of Cauldron Lord Bilemaw and legions of skeletal flayers, sorcerers, and ravenous ghouls.

Fenris Isle. Rot Hide gnolls and a rogue Scourge necromancer hold Fenris Isle in Lordamere Lake, off Silverpine Forest. Fenris Keep once anchored Lordaeron’s military outpost on Fenris Isle. When the Scourge swept through northern Lordaeron, the garrison was slaughtered or fled into exile, leaving the island to the dead. Since then, Rot Hide gnolls have made it their stronghold, spreading a crude empire across the lake’s shores. The Forsaken of Silverpine Forest watch the island closely, fearing its entrenched inhabitants threaten their northern territories.

Fenris Keep. Fenris Keep is an isolated stone fortress situated atop Fenris Isle in the heart of Lordamere Lake. Once a strategic stronghold housing Lordaeron troops, it has fallen into the hands of the Scourge under the rogue mage Thule Ravenclaw.

Fenrus the Devourer. In Shadowfang Keep, Fenrus the Devourer prowls the upper sanctum. Archmage Arugal keeps the enormous worg as a pet and guardian, its body swollen by unnatural magic. Intruders seeking the archmage's study must face the beast and its master. Fenrus the Devourer lurks outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers deep within Shadowfang Keep. Unlike the worgen on the ramparts, Fenrus is a worg, swollen to enormous size. The beast prowls among the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatus in Arugal's private study. The archmage keeps Fenrus as both pet and guard against anyone who comes seeking his head.

Fenwick Thatros. In the Undercity, Mennet Carkad sends promising rogues after Fenwick Thatros on Lord Varimathras's orders. Thatros is suspected of organizing independent undead forces along Silverpine Forest's shores. Killing him proves an operative's mettle to the Deathstalkers and opens the way to advanced trade training. In the Undercity's Rogues' Quarter, Mennet Carkad handles Deathstalker contracts and training. The Deathstalkers are the Forsaken's secretive intelligence wing. Lord Varimathras has named Fenwick Thatros as a priority target, a charge too serious for novice recruits. Thatros has established a foothold among rogue undead in Silverpine Forest. If left alone, their independent leadership could threaten Forsaken control across Lordaeron's old holdings.

Fenwick's Head. Forsaken rogues seek Fenwick Thatros along the shores of Lordamere Lake. His head is proof of his execution, claimed on orders passed down from Lord Varimathras. Mennet Carkad acts from the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity on urgent intelligence from dreadlord Varimathras. Fenwick Thatros, a hostile undead leader, has established a foothold near the decaying docks along Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. To keep him from rallying hostile undead against the Forsaken, Carkad sends promising Deathstalkers to find and kill him, then bring back his head as proof.

Feral Scar Vale. Feral Scar Vale is a rocky gorge tucked within the High Wilderness of western Feralas. Overrun by territorial Feral Scar yetis, its cavernous tunnels are notoriously perilous to travelers who venture off the overgrown forest trails. Situated amid the thick foliage and sheer cliffs of the High Wilderness, Feral Scar Vale serves as the primary den for the savage Feral Scar yetis. While yetis are common in the snowy peaks of Alterac and Dun Morogh, these primal brutes have adapted completely to the wild, humid climate of Feralas. They fiercely defend the vale's cave network, hoarding bone trophies and aggressively driving off any intruders who wander into their hunting grounds.

Feralas: A History. You find a book that looks as if nobody has opened it in ages, and it may be exactly what Troyas needs. It belongs to Daryn Lightwind, so you need to ask whether you may borrow it. The book's covers are badly worn and its pages have yellowed. After looking it over, you suspect it may be what Troyas is searching for. You pick it up, then think better of borrowing it without asking. It is Daryn Lightwind's, so she should be asked first.

Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar sends you after a stolen emerald in northern Teldrassil. The jewel was pried from his damaged heirloom dreamcatcher by Gnarlpine furbolgs north of Starbreeze Village, and now hangs from their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot felt relief when the dreamcatcher recovered from the corrupted wilds came back to him, then dismay at its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame. Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the influence of a furbolg leader named Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. In Ferocitas's clutches, the sacred gem was useless and perverse, so Tallonkai sent defenders to take it back.

Fey Dragon Scale. Around Stonetalon Peak, faerie dragons yield scales coveted by Jin'Zil. The Darkspear witch doctor uses one as a reagent in a brew that mocks night elven nature magic. Around Stonetalon Peak, faerie dragons haunt the wild groves of Kalimdor. Their scales gleam with natural magic. Night elves revere them as harmless woodland spirits and allies, while outsiders prize the scales as rare magical ingredients.

Field Marshal Snowfall. In Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall directs the Alliance's preparations for war. The dwarven military officer tracks the supplies gathered to face the silithid threat in Silithus and rewards those who aid the realm's preparations. Field Marshal Snowfall directs the Alliance's war preparations from Ironforge's Military Ward. He sees the coming conflict as more than a border skirmish: it is a fight against an ancient enemy hostile to all creations of the Titans. Adventurers gather bandages, metal bars, leathers, herbs, and rations in great numbers. Snowfall oversees these stores so Alliance forces can be armed, armored, and fed when the march south to Silithus begins.

Field Marshal Stonebridge. At Stormwind's gates, Field Marshal Stonebridge helps oversee the city's defenses with General Marcus Jonathan. She also receives reports and trophies from major victories. Field Marshal Stonebridge watches the eastern archway at the entrance to the Valley of Heroes, beside Stormwind's main gates. A senior officer in the Grand Alliance, she works closely with General Marcus Jonathan. From the gate, she watches defenders, travelers, and returning champions enter the capital, ready to organize the garrison if danger breaches the outer defenses.

Field of Giants. The Field of Giants spreads across the southern Barrens, from Camp Taurajo to Dustwallow's marshes. Towering kodo, thunder lizards, and other great beasts graze its dry scrub, while silithids make the plain more dangerous. The Field of Giants follows the southern Gold Road, far from the Barrens' better-defended north. Wooden watchtowers along the road sit largely abandoned, while great herds roam the open flats. Hunters and naturalists come to see Kalimdor's enormous beasts, but the land is not safe. Dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, and a more sinister threat has begun burrowing underground.

Fields of Grief. Pumpkins are taken from a human farmstead north of Deathknell for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill. Deathguard Simmer sends newly risen Forsaken to gather them. Deathguard Simmer sends you from the crypts of Deathknell into a hostile land. He serves Sylvanas Windrunner's forces, where survival means taking what the living possess and putting it to use for the Undercity's darker aims.

Fields of Grief. Apothecary Johaan tests his pumpkin weapon in Brill. He has laced pumpkins from Solliden Farmstead with his latest alchemical concoction and sends you to feed one to a captive Scarlet Crusader. Apothecary Johaan believes the Forsaken must use every advantage against the Scourge to the north and human incursions to the south. The Royal Apothecary Society looks beyond blades and dark sorcery, seeking weapons in the ordinary produce of the land. Johaan has tainted pumpkins gathered from the mortal farmers at Solliden Farmstead. He means to prove common crops can be made deadly in service of the Dark Lady.

Fiery Blaze Enchantments. Sigrun Ironhew, waiting in the Badlands for word from Ironforge, knows a technique for imbuing weapons with fire. It needs blood from the still-beating heart of a rare black drake whelp, and the whelps of Lethlor Ravine are where to find one. Sigrun Ironhew learned a special way of imbuing weapons with fiery enchantments as an apprentice to Feranor Steeltoe, last heard of among a hunting party's smiths in Lordaeron. Sigrun is waiting for word from Ironforge and has little else to do.

Fiery Menace!. Hansel Heavyhands says that every time he wants a moment to relax and reflect on his life, the powers that be hand him another job. Greater lava spiders are causing a ruckus in the Searing Gorge, and he wants you to kill twenty of them. Hansel Heavyhands complains that the powers that be never leave him in peace. Greater lava spiders are causing a ruckus, and he would rather you did the killing than him.

Filled Amethyst Phial. In Teldrassil, water from the Oracle Tree's moonwell fills an amethyst phial. Corithras Moonrage receives it for the Cenarion druids to study the World Tree's troubled growth. The Oracle Glade lies in northwest Teldrassil, where the oldest and most potent moonwell rests beneath the Oracle Tree. Other moonwells across the boughs meet the night elves' daily needs, but the water here carries the raw essence of Elune's grace. Druids who watch over the World Tree's health collect it in amethyst phials, preserving it for testing and ritual cleansing.

Filled Blue Waterskin. Shamans gather water for their trials at the Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale. The Filled Blue Waterskin carries a pristine sample from the ancient fountain. Call of Water initiates cross north from the Barrens into Ashenvale's dense forests. Beyond Lake Mystral, the Ruins of Stardust lie against the mountains dividing Ashenvale from Stonetalon. Fierce forest beasts guard the secluded elven sanctuary. At the center of its lake, an untouched fountain holds water untainted by corruption or drought. A blue waterskin filled from its basin carries the sample sought by shaman masters for ritual attunement.

Filled Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, the Filled Brown Waterskin carries fresh water from the pond below Brine's hut. Aspiring shaman bring it to her to begin brewing sapta, used to commune with water spirits. The pond beneath Brine's hut is a rare source of fresh water in the Barrens. Nearby quilboar fight fiercely over it, and a novice shaman sees how scarce water can drive creatures to defend what sustains them.

text.enUS: Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler. Near Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, the Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler holds foul water drawn from the headwaters. The Cenarion Circle needs it to study the sickness striking local deer. Cliffspring Falls feeds much of Darkshore with water from the eastern highlands. Local deer have recently fallen ill with an unnatural sickness. At Dendrite Starblaze’s request in Moonglade, druidic initiates draw water from a cave mouth where hostile naga dwell. The liquid in the vial is visibly foul, showing that the fresh water supply is tainted.

Filled Containment Coffer. In the Undercity, Forsaken spellcasters use Filled Containment Coffers to capture erratic magical entities. A Cantation of Manifestation reveals and weakens rift spawn in the Apothecarium, so mages can seal them inside for examination. Magical disturbances have appeared in Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium. The Forsaken mage Anastasia Hartwell has called on arcane practitioners to capture the entities behind them. Rift creatures are living magical energy and cannot be seen, so ordinary cages cannot hold them. Spellcasters reveal them with a Cantation of Manifestation, defeat them in combat, and snap prepared coffers shut around them. The sealed boxes protect their carriers from volatile magical backlashes and keep the creatures intact for magical dissection.

Filled Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, the Filled Crystal Phial holds water drawn from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to gather it as a first lesson in Teldrassil’s sacred power. Tenaron Stormgrip sends young night elves to gather moonwell water before they venture into the wider world. The moonwell lies in Shadowglen, and its waters hold more than spring water: they carry energies traced to the ancient Well of Eternity. Sentinels honor moonwells as shrines of Elune, while druids use their restorative power to tend nature. The arcane sorcery of old remains forbidden. Gathering the water begins a lesson in the sacrifice at Mount Hyjal and the care needed to nurture Teldrassil.

Filled Cursed Ooze Jar. In Felwood, a Filled Cursed Ooze Jar holds a sample for Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. The gnome scholar seeks the ancient origins of slimes across Azeroth. Laris Geardawdle, a gnome researcher, sees mystery where most adventurers see vile puddles and caustic slimes. Slimes thrive in many places, and Forsaken apothecaries gather them with care. Those sights led Geardawdle to a bold theory: oozes may be primordial secretions bound to Azeroth's creation. To gather a sample, brave Felwood's blighted woods, defeat a cursed ooze, and scoop its acidic remains into an empty jar before they dissolve.

text.enUS: Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, a filled sampler holds water gathered by Horde druids from the summit pools. The Cenarion Circle studies the sample to learn what is poisoning wildlife in the northern Barrens. Dreadmist Peak’s high crags hold pools whose mists shape weather and rainfall across the northern Barrens. The Burning Blade, who worship demons, made their coven atop the summit, and the water soon soured. Cenarion druids suspect demonic rites poisoned the vapors that feed the surrounding savanna. They send initiates to collect a sample in a special sampler. The foul liquid confirms their fears: its corruption can sicken the herds below.

Filled Etched Phial. In Thunder Bluff, the tauren seek a dryad phial filled with moonwell water. Its rare spiritual power can quench the eternal flame shielding a sacred centaur relic. To fill the phial, you must enter night elf territory deep in Ashenvale. Dryads around Raynewood Retreat carry the empty vessels, crafted to hold pure restorative draughts. A sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River fills the phial with water rich in celestial and nature-bound power. Night elves regard taking it without leave as desecration. The tauren see the water as vital to meeting a threat farther south.

Filled Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, the Filled Jade Phial is carried back with sacred water from Starbreeze Village. The water helps replenish the central wells while young night elves learn their people's history. Druids in Darnassus draw sacred moonwell water from across Teldrassil to replenish their central wells. Corithras Moonrage entrusts young travelers in Dolanaar with a jade phial made to hold the pure water safely. The moonwell outside Starbreeze Village lies east of Dolanaar. Initiates collect its water as they tend the World Tree.

text.enUS: Filled Pure Sample Jar. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle studies how corruption changes living matter. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze gathered from the remote wilds, giving him an uncorrupted specimen for comparison. Laris Geardawdle studies oozes across Azeroth and how corruption changes living matter. He found that these shapeless creatures absorb and reflect the magic and conditions of their homes. After cataloging tainted slimes in Felwood, he sought a clean sample to compare with them. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze gathered from the wilds of Un'Goro Crater, where it can be studied apart from corrupted strains.

Filled Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, a well gives clear spring water for a shaman’s trial. The Filled Red Waterskin carries water drawn from the village well, amid ruins held by the Forsaken. Brine, a hermit in the Barrens, sends shaman initiates to Tarren Mill for water training. The journey leads to the Hillsbrad Foothills, where decay and the dead surround the town. Yet the central well still draws clear spring water. Brine sees this pure water as a sign of endurance in an unhallowed land. She compares the uncorrupted spring with Warchief Thrall’s resolve through hardship. Gathering the water tests an initiate’s respect for its purity, even in hostile surroundings.

Filled Tainted Ooze Jar. In Felwood, tainted ooze is gathered from the remains of corrupted oozes. The samples travel in containment jars to Ironforge, where they support bold theories about life’s origins on Azeroth. Across northern Kalimdor, tainted oozes carry Felwood’s lingering corruption. Gnomish researchers provide jars to contain them safely. Most travelers keep clear of the noxious creatures, but their remains yield samples for natural philosophy and biological study far from the blighted woods.

Filled Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, the Filled Tourmaline Phial carries moonwell water for Corithras Moonrage. Its waters help him watch the health and balance of the growing World Tree. The Filled Tourmaline Phial draws water from a moonwell southeast of the road to Darnassus, on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. Reaching the shrine has grown dangerous as the Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful neighbors, turn violently mad. Corithras Moonrage asks travelers to brave the hostile groves and bring back the water. He hopes it will help him find the deepening corruption unsettling the land.

Filled Vessel. At Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage gathers sacred waters for Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. The Filled Vessel carries samples from Teldrassil’s moonwells to aid his study of the World Tree’s ailments. Night elf acolytes gather water from moonwells across Teldrassil. The tree was planted without the blessings of the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu, leaving its boughs open to corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes. Corithras Moonrage gathers the phials in Dolanaar and pours them into the Filled Vessel for the journey to the capital. Together, the waters offer a vital sample of Teldrassil’s vitality. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm studies them in the Cenarion Enclave, seeking a remedy for the Great Tree’s flaws.

Filling the Soul Gem. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, an attempt is made to preserve the young troll Yenniku. With the youth caught in a trance, a prepared soul gem is brought forth to capture his spirit. Following the effort to save Yenniku, you stand face to face with the young troll in Stranglethorn Vale. His mind is lost, caught entirely in another place while he remains motionless before you. The only path forward involves the enchanted gem prepared specifically to hold his essence.

Filthy Paws. Mountaineer Stormpike needs the Filthy Paws supplies back from Silver Stream Mine. The Miners' League stored equipment there after the ore ran dry, but kobolds have overrun the tunnels. Stormpike wants the tools recovered before his warriors attack. Silver Stream Mine lies in the hills of northern Loch Modan, east of Algaz Station. Its last silver veins ran dry long ago. The dwarven Miners' League turned the empty shafts into a depot for spare excavation gear, picks, and staging materials. Across Khaz Modan, sturdy tunnels make good storehouses, as long as they stay guarded and locked against the wilderness.

name.esES: Pista final del tesoro de Sander

text.enUS: Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure. Along Westfall's coast, Captain Sanders' last directions point out to sea. A note in an old jug sends scavengers west toward his buried treasure. Captain Sanders left his final directions in an old whiskey jug on the Westfall coast. The pirate had scattered cryptic notes along the shoreline, and this one completes the trail. From the jug, the directions lead due west into the ocean. Follow them through the surf to a lonely offshore rock, where his ironbound sea chest lies.

Final Passage. Parqual Fintallas tells you that you have passed this test and the ones before it. You are sent back to Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles, who will sense the change in you and see whether you have grown strong in mind, body and spirit, enough to be honoured for your efforts. This is the last step of the Test of Faith, the chain of trials that Dorn Plainstalker began. Dorn waits in the Weathered Nook, in a cave reached by a ramp, north of Freewind Post. Parqual Fintallas urges you to stay true to the balance you have shown throughout these trials.

Find Agmond. Prospector Ironband has not heard from Prospector Agmond in weeks. Agmond was in charge of the excavation sites in the Badlands, and Ironband wants Agmond found so the report can be collected. Agmond ran the excavations in the Badlands, to the southwest. Ironband says "ran" on purpose, for there has been no word from Agmond in weeks. Ironband wants Agmond found, and the report with him. Agmond was last heard of at the farthest-south dig of the Badlands, a small outfit beyond Angor Fortress, and that is where the search should begin.

Find Bingles. In Ironforge, Gnoarn worries that Bingles Blastenheimer has been missing for more than a week. The gnome aviator vanished during a flight toward fallen Gnomeregan, and Gnoarn sends searchers to the shores of Loch Modan. There, Bingles is alive and needs mechanical salvage. Gnome aviator Bingles Blastenheimer was sent from Tinker Town in Ironforge on an aerial reconnaissance flight over the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. More than a week has passed without word, and Gnoarn fears Bingles may have blown himself out of the sky, a danger of gnome engineering. The last report placed the eccentric flyer somewhere above Loch Modan's waters.

Find OOX-09/HL!. An egg-shaped metal device in the Hinterlands springs open at the turn of a knob, and a gnome named Oglethorpe Obnoticus speaks from inside it. A homing robot of Oglethorpe's has crashed near Skulk Rock, and the beacon is to be carried to it. Fiddle with a knob on the strange metal egg and it opens into a gnomish contraption. A crackling voice gives the name Oglethorpe Obnoticus and says the homing robot has crashed. The coordinates have been worked out: the robot came down where the river begins, close to Skulk Rock. The beacon is to be taken to it.

Find OOX-17/TN!. A strange egg-shaped metal device you have uncovered springs to life when you fiddle with its knob, and a voice from inside introduces itself as Oglethorpe. Oglethorpe's homing robot has gone missing, and you are asked to carry the beacon to it. Fiddling with a knob on the strange egg opens it up into a gnomish robotic contraption, and a voice crackles to life from inside. The speaker gives the name Oglethorpe and says a homing robot has gone missing. Oglethorpe has now computed where it went down, near the Gaping Chasm in Tanaris, and asks you to take the beacon to the robot.

Find OOX-22/FE!. You come across a strange egg-shaped device of metal. A voice inside it introduces itself as Oglethorpe Obnoticus, whose homing robot has crashed. You are asked to bring the beacon to the machine, which lies in a cave close to Feral Scar Vale. Fiddling with a knob springs the metal egg open into a gnomish robotic contraption, and a crackling voice speaks from within. Oglethorpe Obnoticus says the homing robot has crashed, and promises payment if you recover it. The beacon is to be taken to the robot, and Oglethorpe has computed where it lies: a cave near Feral Scar Vale.

Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas is waiting at Elwynn's eastern bridge for word of two missing guards. Rolf and Malakai were sent north along the river to watch for murlocs, but neither has returned. Guard Thomas watches the eastern crossing of Elwynn Forest, where the King's road approaches Redridge. Murlocs have made the nearby waters more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent two Stormwind guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the riverbanks to scout the threat and clear out nests. Neither has returned, and Thomas fears violence stopped their patrol.

Find the Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, the Shattered Hand awaits a promising Forsaken rogue from Tirisfal Glades. The Deathstalkers send the initiate across the sea to Durotar to learn specialized arts from the clan. Mennet Carkad has seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken train their own covert order, the Deathstalkers, and their alliance with the Horde opens a path to learn darker arts. He directs promising rogues to seek the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, joining Lordaeron’s undead operatives with Kalimdor’s orcish assassins.

Finding Warmth. Finding Warmth is a humble errand centered on keeping a welcoming hearth fueled with firewood. With the host occupied by other responsibilities, travelers are asked to gather logs so that any soul seeking warmth can find comfort. Completing the task keeps the fire burning and opens the way to further chores. Finding Warmth is a simple chore undertaken to sustain a welcoming fire. The questgiver keeps an open hearth ready to warm any wandering soul, but mounting obligations have left them unable to gather fuel on their own. By stepping in to collect firewood, travelers ensure the hearth remains alight for anyone seeking shelter and comfort.

Finding the Antidote. Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar races to brew a cure for the poisoned hunter Rhinag. You gather venomtail poison sacs from scorpids outside the city walls before their venom proves fatal. Durotar's wildlife is unforgiving, and survival depends on wilderness preparation. Rhinag, a Darkspear troll, was hunting in Durotar when he faced venomtail scorpids without an antidote. Their potent venom struck quickly, leaving him in need of immediate aid. Kor'ghan, an experienced hunter in Orgrimmar, must mix a draught before the poison kills him.

name.esES: Trozos de cangrejo de gran calidad

text.enUS: Fine Crab Chunks. Fine Crab Chunks come from the Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers along Darkshore's coast. Gubber Blump seeks them for his cooking. Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers roam Darkshore's shores. Travelers may see them as pests or dangers by the water, while cooks prize their meat. The chunks can be boiled, broiled, fried, or added to stews.

Fine Moonstalker Pelt. In southern Darkshore, mature moonstalkers carry the hides Terenthis needs. Their Fine Moonstalker Pelt is thick and healthy enough for an enchanted cloak that helps searchers pass the region’s hostile beasts unnoticed. Moonstalker sires and matriarchs have coats dense and healthy enough to yield a fine pelt. They hold territories along the Wildbend River and farther south toward Ashenvale’s borders, where they hunt with patience. Common moonstalkers prowl across Darkshore’s forests, but their hides are not fine enough.

Fiora Longears. This errand introduces Alliance adventurers from the Eastern Kingdoms to the untamed continent of Kalimdor. Directed by the enthusiastic recruiter Red Jack Flint in Menethil Harbor, travelers take ship across the Great Sea to report to his high elf contact, Fiora Longears, in the inn of Theramore. For many humans, dwarves, and gnomes, the Eastern Kingdoms feel fraught with old conflicts and scarred earth. In the bustling port of Menethil Harbor, the sailor Red Jack Flint spends his days urging adventurous travelers to board a vessel bound across the Great Sea. Describing Kalimdor as an uncharted realm of fortune and opportunity, Flint directs bold wanderers to Theramore to meet his associate, an elf named Fiora Longears.

name.esES: Armadura de malla endurecida con fuego
name.frFR: Une cotte de mailles en acier trempé

text.enUS: Fire Hardened Mail. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard has a new armor design for an Alliance warrior. The dwarf armorer offers to forge Fire Hardened Mail if the warrior brings him rare materials from both continents. Furen Longbeard has forged an exceptional buckler for the aspiring warrior and now proposes a greater work: mail made to withstand fierce blows. His craft calls for more than iron or steel. He needs rare materials touched by elemental heat and natural resilience. Furen cannot leave his Stormwind forge, so the warrior seeking the armor must gather these dangerous ingredients.

name.esES: La forja del Penacho en Llamas

text.enUS: Fire Plume Forged. Krinkle Goodsteel points you to Fire Plume Ridge, a simmering volcano west in Un'Goro Crater, where the lava lake at the top is hot enough to forge the stem of a skeletal key. Afterward you carry it to Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Point in the Western Plaguelands. Forging the stem of the key takes two bars of thorium and fierce heat. The thorium is yours to find, but Krinkle Goodsteel can help with the heat. Your gold has bought a mold, and it only needs dipping in the lava lake on top of Fire Plume Ridge. The lava does the rest, fusing thorium and bone together.

name.esES: La forja del Penacho en Llamas

text.enUS: Fire Plume Forged. Krinkle Goodsteel points you to Fire Plume Ridge, a simmering volcano west in Un'Goro Crater, where the lava lake at the top is hot enough to forge the stem of a skeletal key. Afterward you carry it to Apothecary Dithers at the Bulwark in the Western Plaguelands. Forging the stem of the key takes two bars of thorium and fierce heat. The thorium is yours to find, but Krinkle Goodsteel can help with the heat. Your gold has bought a mold, and it only needs dipping in the lava lake on top of Fire Plume Ridge. The lava does the rest, fusing thorium and bone together.

Fire Plume Ridge. Fire Plume Ridge is the active volcano rising directly from the center of Un'Goro Crater. Its searing slopes and subterranean magma channels fuel the crater's geysers and steam pools while playing host to fierce fire elementals. Towering over the primeval basin of Un'Goro, Fire Plume Ridge stands in sharp contrast to the surrounding lush jungle. Lava steadily cascades down its scorched rock faces, carving a landscape of ash and basalt. Subterranean magma arteries spiderweb outward beneath the soil from the ridge, fueling the bubbling geysers and hot springs scattered across the basin. The oppressive heat here is legendary—far exceeding ordinary volcanic temperatures according to goblin measuring devices—making it perilous for ill-prepared explorers to wander without ample water and shade.

Fire Scar Shrine. At Fire Scar Shrine, fel corruption scars the forest southwest of Astranaar. Once a night elf place of worship, the shrine now draws demons to its altar stones. Fire Scar Shrine lies southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust. Demonic corruption has seized the shrine, fed by servants of the Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has scorched the earth around it, and demons gather openly among the trees, defying the forest's defenders.

Fire Taboo. Along the marsh roads of the Wetlands, Fire Taboo puts Rethiel's concern for the forest into action. The bog beast asks travelers to take the crude flints Mosshide gnolls use to burn living trees, hoping to spare the ancient boughs. Rethiel the Greenwarden feels the Wetlands' trees as kin. Rot and renewal belong to the swamp, but the Mosshide gnolls cut living timber and cast it into their hearthfires. The groans of those boughs weigh on Rethiel, who can no longer watch the trees suffer in silence.

Fire Tar. Across the eastern Barrens, Razormane spellcasters carry Fire Tar. Horde shamans use it to brew the Fire Sapta, which lets them commune with fire spirits. Razormane geomancers, mystics, and thornweavers carry Fire Tar. The quilboar use the flame-tuned substance in their harsh magic and rituals. Shamanic instructors prize it as a worldly reagent that helps mortal senses reach the raw fury of the elements.

Firewatch Ridge. Firewatch Ridge is a high volcanic bluff in the northern reaches of Searing Gorge, serving as a primary encampment for the Dark Iron dwarves. Looming directly above the vast excavation known as the Cauldron, the ridge is heavily fortified by dwarven sentries, mechanical golems, and nesting fire spiders. To the northwest, an ominous cave system reveals an entrenched presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Perched above the industrial devastation of the Cauldron, Firewatch Ridge functions as a critical staging ground for the Dark Iron clan's operations in Searing Gorge. Dwarven guards, engineers, and molten golem creations patrol the crags, fiercely defending their foothold alongside venomous flame spiders native to the smoldering rocks. Its elevation provides the Dark Irons an unobstructed view of the surrounding ash plains, ensuring early warning against rival incursions from Ironforge or the Thorium Brotherhood.

First Mate Fitzsimmons. Outside Menethil Harbor's Deepwater Tavern, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks through the days. Once first mate of the Wave Mistress in Kul Tiras's Third Fleet, he is its sole known living survivor after the fleet's destruction in the Second War. Now he seeks travelers willing to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks alone. His unwashed stench keeps many patrons away, and most see only a broken old sailor drowning his memories. Those who sit and listen hear how a proud fleet fell to fire and claw.

First War. The First War was the devastating five-year conflict in which the Orcish Horde emerged through the Dark Portal and completely destroyed the human Kingdom of Stormwind. Orchestrated behind the scenes by the demon-possessed Guardian Medivh and the warlock Gul'dan, it concluded with the assassination of King Llane Wrynn I and the flight of human survivors north to Lordaeron. Before the war, the Kingdom of Stormwind enjoyed long years of peace following the Gnoll War, guarded by its Knights and the Clerics of Northshire Abbey. That stability shattered when the Guardian Medivh, secretly possessed by the demon lord Sargeras, contacted the orc warlock Gul'dan on Draenor. Together, they forged the Dark Portal in the swampy Black Morass. Driven by demon blood and the slow death of their homeworld, the Orcish Horde crossed into Azeroth in force. Early rumors dismissed the invaders as vengeful spirits or strange offshoots of trolls, but Sir Anduin Lothar's scouting patrols quickly confirmed the arrival of a disciplined, bloodthirsty army.

Fish in a Bucket. Jinar'Zillen of Shadowprey Village in Desolace likes to do as little as possible. Many shellfish traps sit below the village docks, and anyone who gathers the shellfish from them will be repaid with something worth having. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village, and would far rather someone else did the collecting. Anyone willing to take on that work is promised something they want in return: one fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray's bait runs low as the fish begin to bite. He asks passersby to fetch supplies from a shop along the city's canals. Gilbert Gray spends quiet days fishing at the edge of Stormwind harbor. He watches his bobber on the water, but a good run of biting fish can empty his bait tin. With his supplies gone and the fish still biting, the elderly angler asks passersby to bring him more.

name.esES: Cinco sellos para los suministros bélicos
name.frFR: Cinq chevalières pour des fournitures militaires
name.ptBR: Cinco sinetes para abastecer a guerra
name.zhCN: 五枚荣誉徽章换取物资

text.enUS: Five Signets for War Supplies. In Ironforge, Field Marshal Snowfall gathers provisions and equipment for the Grand Alliance's war effort. Champions can trade commendation signets for field rations, bandages, and combat supplies. The stockpiles keep those working on the home front equipped for coming conflicts. Field Marshal Snowfall organizes the flow of materials as one of the Alliance's primary quartermasters in Ironforge. Armies need more than courage; they also need steady supplies for the fronts. Couriers and heroes bring commendation signets earned through civic service, and Snowfall trades them for survival rations and tactical gear.

name.esES: Cinco sellos para los suministros bélicos
name.frFR: Cinq chevalières pour des fournitures militaires
name.ptBR: Cinco sinetes para abastecer a guerra

text.enUS: Five Signets for War Supplies. Orgrimmar's stores gather supplies for the Horde's campaign across Kalimdor. Workers earn commendation signets for their contributions, and Warlord Gorchuk exchanges them for supplies to equip the fighters. Across Kalimdor, the Horde gathers raw goods, weapons, and provisions for a vast campaign. Gatherers and tradesfolk bring bandages, metals, and herbs into the cities, where military overseers award commendation signets for their work. The tokens mark each contribution to the stockpile growing along Orgrimmar's central avenues.

Fizzle Brassbolts. Fizzle Brassbolts is a prominent gnomish engineer stationed out on the baked salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles.
