Alongside his rival, the goblin Pozzik, Fizzle co-founded the raceway to pit gnomish precision engineering against reckless goblin ingenuity in high-speed rocket car races. He constantly seeks parts, fuel, and strange desert reagents to keep his racing team running. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, political alliances and ancient grudges yield to the roar of motorized engines. Fizzle Brassbolts arrived here with one goal in mind: proving once and for all that gnomish craftsmanship is vastly superior to crude goblin tinkering. Together with his goblin counterpart Pozzik, he helped lay out the Mirage Raceway, bringing race cars, pit crews, and spectators to an otherwise desolate basin.

Fizzle's Claw. In Thunder Ridge, Fizzle Darkstorm’s claw is carried to Razor Hill as proof of his death. The goblin warlock was a dangerous Burning Blade conspirator. Orgnil Soulscar sent forces to root out shadow cults threatening the orcish homeland. He identified Fizzle Darkstorm as an instigator spreading corruption in Thunder Ridge. The claw gives Horde commanders proof that the warlock, who operated under the Burning Blade’s banner, has been slain.

Flagongut's Fossil. At the Wetlands dig, Flagongut seeks answers in an ancient fossil. The Explorers' League keeps the specimen, and Flagongut believes the Stone of Relu can help him decipher its secrets. Prospector Whelgar keeps the fossil at his excavation site in the southern hills of the Wetlands. Dwarven expeditions across Khaz Modan unearthed it, and Archaeologist Flagongut believes its ancient stone holds forgotten powers. He sees a kinship with artifacts found across the sea in Darkshore.

Flame Crest. Flame Crest is a rugged neutral outpost perched atop a rocky ledge overlooking the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes. Accessed only across a crude span, this precarious encampment serves as a forward staging ground against the Dark Horde entrenched in Blackrock Mountain. It provides essential aerial connections and a haven for scouts, beast collectors, and strategists. Situated high on an isolated stone outcropping, Flame Crest commands a watchful view over the scorched ash and lava plains of the Burning Steppes. Reached only by crossing a narrow, rickety wooden bridge, the outpost is naturally defensible against the prowling beasts and roaming orc warbands of the wastes. Wind riders roost along the heights, connecting the camp back across the Redridge range to Kargath, Stonard, Thorium Point, and Rog'mar in the Riverglades.

name.esES: Fémur de puma de las estepas
name.frFR: Fémur de puma des basses plaines

text.enUS: Flatland Cougar Femur. Across Mulgore, cougars prowl the plains, and Maur Raincaller needs one of their bones. A Flatland Cougar Femur is part of the remedy he seeks for a venomous bite. Flatland cougars rank among Mulgore's most dangerous native stalkers. They blend into the dry brush, then spring upon unsuspecting prey. Hunters take their pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies, while their heavy, marrow-rich bones have use in local medicine. Maur Raincaller of Bloodhoof Village suffered a venomous wound from Mazzranache, a monstrous pink strider. He urgently asked for a cougar femur and parts from other local beasts. Crushed or boiled, the bone yields properties for an antitoxin poultice meant to draw fever and necrotic venom from a festering bite.

name.esES: Garra de merodeador de las estepas
name.frFR: Griffe de Rôdeur des basses plaines

text.enUS: Flatland Prowler Claw. Across Mulgore's plains, Flatland Prowler Claws mark a young hunter's trial. Hunters gather them to prove their resolve and fieldcraft to the elders of Thunder Bluff. Flatland prowlers stalk Mulgore's plains, quick to ambush prey in tall grass. Their cunning and territorial nature makes them dangerous to travelers and a hard test for young hunters. Gathering their claws is a recognized tradition. Skorn Whitecloud sends promising wanderers to bring the claws to Melor Stonehoof at Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, proof that they have the resolve and fieldcraft to follow the hunter's way.

name.esES: La piedra de energía con imperfecciones

text.enUS: Flawed Power Stone. Across the Barrens, Flawed Power Stone rests on arcane tables, charged with arcane energy. Its makers left it fatally flawed, so it consumes its own power soon after it is moved. In the Barrens, flawed power stones hold arcane essence within compromised structures. Their makers deliberately left them unstable, so they decay into inert matter moments after someone handles them.

name.ptBR: Mestre de Frota Chifre do Mar

text.enUS: Fleet Master Seahorn. Fleet Master Seahorn is a seasoned tauren mariner who serves as the naval commander of the Blackwater Raiders in Booty Bay. Stationed on the upper balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern alongside Baron Revilgaz, he oversees the goblin port's maritime defenses. His primary duty is protecting the harbor from the looming threat posed by their sworn enemies, the Bloodsail Buccaneers. While tauren are renowned across Kalimdor as plains-dwellers, Fleet Master Seahorn chose a vastly different life upon the ocean. Clad in pirate regalia, he commands the fleet of the Blackwater Raiders, the private naval arm of the Steamwheedle Cartel's operation in Stranglethorn Vale. Stationed atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Seahorn works shoulder-to-shoulder with Baron Revilgaz, coordinating shipping routes, crew deployments, and coastal defenses for the lawless yet strictly managed port of Booty Bay.

name.esES: Saca músculo a cambio de almendrados
name.frFR: Montrer ses muscles pour du nougat

text.enUS: Flexing for Nougat. During autumn's Hallow's End, you gather festive sweets for an orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Allison at the Gilded Rose asks you to flex before she gives you Stormwind Nougat. Hallow's End brings a lighter mood to Stormwind's streets. The holiday marks the turning of the seasons and wards off dark spirits. Common folk celebrate with disguises, revelry, and trick-or-treating. Alliance innkeepers join in, offering traditional sweets to those who perform a harmless trick.

name.esES: Saca músculo a cambio de almendrados
name.frFR: Montrer ses muscles pour du nougat

text.enUS: Flexing for Nougat. In Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka offers nougat to those who play along. During Hallow's End, she asks you to flex for a piece meant to cheer Spoops, a bedridden child. Hallow's End brings pranks and sweet-gathering to Azeroth's capitals. In Orgrimmar's inn, Innkeeper Gryshka keeps holiday sweets for those who take part in the season's custom. You face dragons and dark sorcery in your travels, but here the bargain is simple: perform a trick or leave without a treat.

Flight to Auberdine. You leave Teldrassil for Auberdine with a bundle of unusual fish specimens. Vesprystus sends you from Rut'theran Village by hippogryph to deliver them to Laird. Rut'theran Village is a sanctuary at the edge of the wider world for young adventurers leaving Teldrassil. A mundane ferry crosses the strait between the island and mainland Kalimdor, while night elves also travel by bonded hippogryph. Nessa Shadowsong entrusts you with a parcel of rare fish parts, and you take wing to reach the shores of Darkshore.

Flintfire's Shipment. Tognus Flintfire in Kharanos is facing a severe supply shortage after savage wendigos overran his primary source of ore at the Grizzled Den. With the miners forced to abandon their crates during the evacuation, adventurers are tasked with recovering the lost shipments to keep the local forges running. In the snowy settlement of Kharanos, Tognus Flintfire faces a critical supply crisis at his forge. The region's most productive and dependable source of ore has suddenly fallen silent after savage wendigos invaded the dig site. Caught off guard by the ferocious predators, the local miners were forced to abandon their posts on a moment's notice, fleeing for their lives and leaving behind freshly packed crates of valuable ore scattered across the cavern floor.

Flutterfly Dust. Flutterfly Dust is a local task in the Gustberry Lowlands involving the harvesting of powder from giant, winged flutterflies. While the insects are usually docile, isolated homesteaders rely on travelers to gather the messy substance due to the constant threat of roving bandits. The outer fields and orchards of the Gustberry Lowlands are home to giant flutterflies, picturesque winged insects that drift lazily through the rural landscape. While their gentle appearance lends a pastoral charm to the area, their fluttering wings shed a fine, pervasive dust that can be gathered in bulk. Though primarily wild insects, their presence draws the attention of nearby homesteaders who seek to harvest this airborne byproduct for practical domestic needs.

Foggy MacKreel. On the broken Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel worries about a moonshine delivery bound for Southshore. Stranded on ruined lower masonry above a dizzying drop, the dwarf keeps his mind on the task. Foggy MacKreel waits on broken pylons beneath the Thandol Span, calm despite his dangerous perch. Dark Iron sabotage and war damage shattered the bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. MacKreel gives little thought to rescue; he wants his potent moonshine delivered to the patrons of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He hires passing travelers nimble enough to reach his ledge and finish the delivery for him.

Follow That Kobold!. Follow That Kobold! is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley dealing with a bizarre theft from the local mines. A kobold has fled with a sack of Brother Paxton's books, prompting the abbey to recruit the dwarven hunter trainer Tordrin Sternblade to assist in tracking the thief. Just when the workers and clerics of Northshire Abbey believed the vermin problem in the mines was under control, an unusual report arrived from Kelsey: a lone kobold was spotted fleeing the tunnels hauling a heavy sack of books. The stolen volumes belong to Brother Paxton, who urgently requires their return to the abbey's collection.

Food for Baby. Agnar Beastamer will look after your egg for now, so that it is ready for the day it hatches. Sprite darters eat both meat and vegetation, and the young ones like flanks of meat, raw and juicy. Agnar wants Silvermane stalker flanks to feed the hatchling its first meal. Agnar Beastamer says sprite darters are omnivores, so a hatchling will need something good to eat once it is out of its shell. Raw, juicy flanks of meat are good eating for the little ones. Agnar will care for the egg meanwhile and wants Silvermane stalker flanks to feed it. Without a good first meal, the newborn might not make it past its first week.

Fool's Stout. Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay brews batches of Fool's Stout for travelers looking to return to the Shimmering Flats raceway. To concoct another serving, he requires twelve flasks of Zanzil's mixture. For travelers whose initial supply of Fool's Stout has expired before reaching the gnomes at the raceway, Crank Fizzlebub offers to brew a replacement. The goblin Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay requires twelve flasks of Zanzil's mixture to prepare the potent beverage once more, compensating anyone willing to fetch the ingredients while offering a little extra to keep the transaction discreet.

Foothold Citadel. Foothold Citadel serves as the central military barracks and command post within Theramore Isle. Overlooking the fortified settlement, it houses the officers and guards who protect the Alliance's primary bastion on southern Kalimdor. Rising within the fortified stone walls of Theramore Isle, Foothold Citadel is the nerve center of local Alliance defense. The citadel houses the high command of the Theramore Guard, including Captain Garran Vimes and Commander Samaul, along with field medics, logistics officers, and quartermasters. Its utilitarian stone halls bustle with regular patrols and drills, keeping Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces prepared against threats creeping out of the surrounding swamplands.

For Honor. For Honor is a quest dedicated to commemorating fallen warriors so their deeds are not forgotten. By completing the task, an adventurer ensures that the sacrifices of these combatants endure in memory. The quest For Honor is a solemn mission centered on memorializing fallen combatants. In a world continuously tested by conflict, ensuring that soldiers who gave everything are not forgotten stands as a vital duty for those who survive them.

For Love Eternal. In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to free Anaya Dawnrunner's spirit from torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has endured since the city's fall. Ten thousand years ago, the War of the Ancients tore ancient Kalimdor apart around the Well of Eternity. The catastrophe destroyed Ameth'Aran and took Anaya Dawnrunner from Cerellean Whiteclaw. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the druids' long hibernation. He hoped that walking the Emerald Dream through the ages would quiet his aching heart, but sorrow remained with him.

Forbidden Knowledge. Yagyin's Digest is handed over with a warning to guard it well from unfriendly hands. Theldurin the Lost is the one to carry it to. Gerrig Bonegrip in Ironforge, or Keeper Bel'dugur in the Undercity, gives you the digest. You are cautioned to guard it well and keep it away from unfriendly hands, for it carries many truths and truth has a way of burning. Carry it to Theldurin the Lost.

Forced Disarmament. Forced Disarmament is an Alliance quest in the Wetlands tasking adventurers with seizing weapon caches from the Dragonmaw clan at Dragonmaw Retreat. By collecting thirty bundles of armaments, players prevent the hostile orcs from equipping additional soldiers for future raids. The confiscated gear is delivered to Captain Stoutfist at Menethil Keep to safeguard the region's vital harbor. In the marshlands of the Wetlands, the hostile Dragonmaw clan has begun gathering an alarming stockpile of weapons within the Dragonmaw Retreat. Left unchecked, these supplies would allow the renegade orcs to equip fresh waves of warriors and launch devastating raids against neighboring settlements. Disarming their encampments strikes directly at their logistical capability, blunting any planned offensive before their warbands can fully mobilize and take the field.

Foreboding Plans. The Syndicate documents hold a list of supplies the Syndicate asked for, wanted in a hurry for what the papers call an important undertaking against Southshore. Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore awaits them. The documents include a list of requested supplies. Some are mundane: food, weapons and clothing. Others are more exotic: masks, oil and poison. What stands out most is the urgency, for the papers say the supplies were needed soon, for an important undertaking against Southshore. Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore is the one to receive them.

Foreman Oslow. At Lakeshire, Foreman Oslow struggles to rebuild the Everstill Bridge. Blackrock orcs shattered the crossing, while lost tools and stolen supplies have stalled the work. He needs help recovering his equipment and gathering materials so the town can restore its trade route. Foreman Oslow works beside the broken Everstill Bridge, trying to reconnect Lakeshire. The span crosses Lake Everstill, linking the western roads toward Elwynn with the eastern shore. Blackrock orcs came down from the crags of Stonewatch and struck the crossing to cripple Lakeshire's trade and military movement. With the bridge broken, the town is split and exposed.

Foreman Stonebrow. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Foreman Stonebrow faces a trogg attack that has driven miners from the pits. He speaks for the Miners' League and now needs help defending the excavation. Foreman Stonebrow directs the Miners' League's work at Gol'Bolar Quarry, east of Kharanos. Deep digging broke into trogg burrows beneath the quarry, and the creatures swarmed the pits, driving miners from their tools. Stonebrow remains at the quarry rim, seeking travelers willing to push the troggs back.

Foreman Thazz'ril. Peons work under Foreman Thazz'ril in the Valley of Trials. The orc labor supervisor keeps crews on schedule and supplies ready for young warriors, but slacking workers and nearby cultists frustrate him. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril directs peons who chop lumber and gather materials for the encampment and young warriors. Building a home in Durotar's harsh red rock takes steady labor, yet the peons often nap under the desert sun. Thazz'ril sends newly arrived recruits to rouse the sleepers with his blackjack, and keep construction moving.

Foreman Thistlenettle. In the Deadmines, Foreman Thistlenettle once led a dwarven mining crew. He worked for both the Miners' League and the Explorers' League until a cave-in trapped his crew below Moonbrook. He died with them and rose again as a ghoul, still carrying his guild badge through the dark, collapsed tunnels.

Foreman's Blackjack. Foreman's Blackjack keeps peons at work in Durotar's Valley of Trials. Foremen use the leather-wrapped cosh to wake laborers who fall asleep during the Horde's early construction. Durotar's rugged desert needs stockpiles of lumber for the Horde's new home. In the Valley of Trials, the work falls to the peons, and Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the crews moving with Foreman's Blackjack. The weighted bludgeon delivers a jarring wake-up call to laborers caught napping beneath the valley's shade trees, rather than a lethal blow. Peon life in the new Horde means grueling, unglamorous work under an iron fist.

Forest Song. Forest Song watches over northeastern Ashenvale, near Satyrnaar and Bough Shadow. The ancient kaldorei ruins are largely deserted, with the druid Kayneth Stillwind guarding the eastern border. Forest Song's white columns and broken arches rise among the trees of northeastern Ashenvale. Once an elegant kaldorei settlement, the ruin now lies overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Satyrnaar lies to the southwest, and the Warsong Lumber Camp presses in from the south. From here, eastern trails lead toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. Demonic corruption and Horde incursions trouble the surrounding woods, while the ruins remain quiet.

Forest's Edge. Riverpaw gnolls under Hogger threaten travelers at Forest's Edge, along Elwynn's southwestern frontier. At Forest's Edge, woodland runs southwest from Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers that border Westfall. Westbrook Garrison lies nearby, but Stormwind's thin ranks leave the woods open to wild beasts and raiding parties. Boars roam among the trees and along the banks. Riverpaw gnolls gather here in force, using the woods as a staging ground.

Forged Steel. Thun'grim Firegaze waits in the eastern Barrens for the steel stolen from his camp. He offers to forge a weapon for the warrior who brings it back. Thun'grim Firegaze keeps a smithy in the eastern Barrens, far from Orgrimmar. Years at the forge have dimmed his sight. The nearby Razormane quilboar used that weakness to steal an iron chest from his camp. Some snorted and made noise on one side to draw his gaze while others slipped in from the other and carried off his forged steel bars.

Forged Steel Bars. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze's steel bars are missing. Recovering them will prove a warrior's resolve to reclaim stolen property. Thun'grim Firegaze, a visually impaired orc smith, keeps a camp in the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar took his iron chest during a night raid, distracting him with grunts and snorts while thieves slipped away. Unable to work fine steel, the quilboar left the unopened chest near a ruined wagon in their encampment to the northwest. The bars remain intact for warriors willing to recover them.

Forging the Shaft. After The Flawless Flame, Kalaran Windblade says that holding the flawless flame takes both a shaft and a casing, and the shaft must come first. The Dark Iron slavers and taskmasters of the cauldron use enchanted thorium weapons, and eight thorium plated daggers can be reforged into a shaft. A shaft and a casing are both needed, Kalaran says, to hold the flawless flame. The slavers and taskmasters of the Dark Irons in the cauldron fight with enchanted thorium, a metal of great sturdiness. Kalaran can break eight of their thorium plated daggers down and reforge the alloy into a shaft.

Forgotten Coast. The Forgotten Coast forms the wild western shore of Feralas, where the ancient rainforest meets the Veiled Sea. Lumbering sea giants and water elementals roam this battered strand. Stretching along the western edge of Feralas, the Forgotten Coast is a windswept shoreline confronting the expanse of the Veiled Sea. Unlike the dense canopy inland, this frontier is exposed to the elements and dominated by towering sea giants and roving water elementals pacing the surf. Travelers emerging from the forest canopy must contend with these primeval coastal guardians while navigating access to the sea, where ferry connections link to the night elven bastion of Sardor Isle.

Forgotten Loa Idols. Forgotten Loa Idols centers on recovering sacred religious effigies for the Darkspear trolls. These lost relics are urgently needed to resume vital spiritual ceremonies and preserve the tribe's enduring bond of reverence with their patron wild spirits. For the Darkspear trolls, spiritual balance is inextricably bound to their connection with the loa—the primal animal spirits and wild gods of their ancestral heritage. Forgotten Loa Idols involves recovering displaced religious relics essential for conducting tribal ceremonies. Without these sacred objects, spiritual leaders cannot perform the rites required to maintain harmony with their divine guardians.

Forgotten Pool. Past the Moonshrine Ruins, Forgotten Pool lies beneath the flooded halls of Blackfathom Deeps. Its dark waters hide monstrous deep-sea predators. You reach Forgotten Pool by diving through the sunken waterways beyond the Moonshrine Ruins. Dark water fills this isolated cavern, cut off from dry ground. Twilight's Hammer cultists chant nearby, and naga patrol the flooded halls, but the pool lies apart from them. Old Serra'kis, an ancient aquatic terror, lairs in its depths, hidden by the water.

Forgotten Pools. The Forgotten Pools draw wildlife, Kolkar centaur, and the Horde into a contest for water in the northern Barrens. Northwest of the Crossroads, subterranean springs feed an oasis amid the dry savanna. Fresh water gathers in the Forgotten Pools, where thick reeds, palm trees, and Laden Mushrooms grow beside the parched Barrens. Plainstriders, snapjaw turtles, and zhevras come to drink. Kolkar centaur keep a camp along the banks and guard the water from travelers, bringing them into conflict with Horde travelers from the Crossroads. Wildlife, Kolkar, and the Horde all contend for the oasis.

Forlorn Cavern. Along Ironforge's northern underground lake, the Forlorn Cavern shelters those who keep to the shadows. Thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct business there, far from the Great Forge and prying dwarven guards. The Forlorn Cavern is cold, damp, and hushed beneath Ironforge's clang of anvils and the Great Forge's heat. Its winding paths follow the northern edge of the underground lake, out of sight between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Rogues and warlocks train there, and vendors serve them. Weapon merchants and fishermen work beside the lake as well.

Forlorn Cloister. The Forlorn Cloister is the haunted graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Here, members of the Scarlet Crusade desperately torch the bodies of fallen brothers to prevent them from rising into undeath, while restless spirits and shambling corpses roam among the tombs. Once a peaceful sanctuary where the priests and paladins of Lordaeron laid their honoured dead to rest, the Forlorn Cloister has become a grim charnel ground. Despite the Scarlet Crusade's fanatical vigilance, the taint of the plague has seeped deep into the earth. crusaders patrol the fog-shrouded cemetery with torches, frantically burning remains to stave off the rot. Even so, spectres glide between crypts and the dead pull free from their graves, ruled over by dark magic deep within the grounds.

Forlorn Ridge. Forlorn Ridge is a towering mountain ridge looming over southwestern Azshara. Its strategic elevation and commanding views over the coast have drawn the attention of both the Alliance and the Horde, who have each carved out fortifications along its slopes. Rising sharply above the autumnal forests of western Azshara, Forlorn Ridge dominates the surrounding terrain. Resembling an ancient, long-dormant volcano, its high vantage point offers a sweeping view over the coastal approaches and the ruined elven estates below. Because control over these heights dictates military dominance in the sector, both Alliance and Horde forces have established encampments and outposts along its mountain flanks, watching each other warily across the rugged bluffs.

Forlorn Rowe. At the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery, Forlorn Rowe lies under a shadow of dread. Morbent Fel makes his home on the hill, and his magic raises the restless dead across Duskwood. Forlorn Rowe rises along the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery, its slope lost in gloom. Morbent Fel makes his home atop the hill. The necromancer is responsible for much of the walking dead that haunt the surrounding wilderness. From this height, he directs his skeletal servants with foul enchantments, making Duskwood’s northwestern corner perilous for travelers.

Forsaken. The Forsaken are a free-willed faction of intelligent undead who broke away from the Scourge following the Third War. Led by the Banshee Queen Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, they dwell within the subterranean Undercity carved beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's capital. Though deeply distrusted across Azeroth, they maintain a tenuous alliance of convenience with the Horde. When the Lich King's grip over his northern armies slipped after the Third War, thousands of undead in the blighted ruins of Lordaeron suddenly regained their sapience and memories. Horrified by the butchery they had been forced to carry out while enslaved to his will, these former citizens found themselves reviled and hunted by the living. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the fallen ranger-general of Quel'Thalas who had been transformed into an unholy banshee, rallied these adrift spirits, claimed the catacombs beneath Capital City, and dubbed her new nation the Forsaken.

Forsaken Aid. In Thunder Bluff, Magatha Grimtotem sends you to seek help for Stonetalon's blighted spirits. She turns to Apothecary Zamah, the Forsaken emissary in the Pools of Vision, to bring tauren and undead knowledge together. Magatha Grimtotem sees practical value in the Forsaken alliance. When word reaches Thunder Bluff of corrupted elemental spirits and suffering land in the Stonetalon Mountains, she turns to the undead for help. She believes those who understand disease can help cure it, so she sends you to the Royal Apothecary Society instead of seeking traditional druidic remedies.

Forsaken Diseases. In eastern Ashenvale, Kayneth Stillwind watches the Forsaken draw nearer. He fears they are brewing blights to ravage sacred elven lands, and sends Alliance champions toward a camp near Dor'Danil Barrow Den to seize a sample. Ashenvale's night elves have long faced satyrs, raging elementals, and orcish logging crews. The Forsaken bring a darker threat. The undead arm of the Horde is taking root near ancient ruins and sacred barrow dens. Their presence brings war and the fear of alchemical plague spreading through Kaldorei groves.

Forsaken Duties. Forsaken Duties is a reconnaissance mission assigned by Magistrate Sevren in Brill to assess Scourge activity along the eastern perimeter of Tirisfal Glades. It establishes the constant threat posed by the Scourge slipping past The Bulwark and endangering local settlements. Magistrate Sevren oversees the security of Brill and the surrounding countryside, keeping a nervous eye on the eastern borders of Tirisfal Glades. With the Scourge swarming across the Western Plaguelands, Sevren requires constant reconnaissance from frontline sentries to ensure undead horrors do not slip past the perimeter unnoticed. Travelers willing to assist are dispatched south and east down the main thoroughfare to gather an urgent tactical assessment from Deathguard Linnea.

Foul Magics. Foul Magics is a Horde quest originating in Hammerfall within the Arathi Highlands. Tor'gan senses a disturbing demonic presence to the west and discovers traces of dark summoning rituals at Northfold Manor. He asks adventurers to venture into the manor and retrieve bloodstone amulets used in these summonings so he can study their dark magic. Tor'gan, an orc stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, began noticing an unsettling disturbance drifting through the Arathi Highlands. For an orc, demonic energies are not merely an abstract threat; they evoke a visceral, biological reaction rooted in the history of the blood curse. As Tor'gan tracked the source of his agitation westward toward Northfold Manor, the ambient corruption caused his blood to boil and stoked an involuntary rage within him. Recognizing the telltale aftermath of demonic summoning, he retreated before the dark influence overwhelmed his senses, seeking outside help instead of returning himself.

Foul Magics. Tor'gan in Hammerfall is sure that a powerful warlock lives within the walls of Stromgarde and uses an arcane relic to summon demons in large numbers. Following the first part of Foul Magics, he sends you to kill the warlock and bring back the relic. Tor'gan is certain that a warlock lives within Stromgarde's walls. Now and then the warlock uses an arcane relic to call up terrible demons in great numbers. The burning in Tor'gan's blood grows by the day. He wants the warlock found and killed, and whatever magical object is on the body brought to him, so that he can destroy it and keep its power from tainting the land. The warlock is Marez Cowl, and the object is a Befouled Bloodstone Orb.

Foul Matriarch. Foul Matriarch is a trial of survival assigned by Aetheen of the Gales to budding initiates in Thendal Village. The task demands delving into the southern caves to cull the scavenging ursera and slay their vicious den mother, Urs'anah. Completing the hunt proves that an adventurer possesses the resolve required to face greater perils across Zephras Isle. Aetheen of the Gales maintains a watchful eye on newcomers finding their footing around Thendal Village. Once an initiate demonstrates early competence, Aetheen issues a dangerous rite of passage: a direct assault against the predatory wildlife threatening the perimeter. Rather than simply fighting on the open paths, the initiate is sent directly into the dark caves to the south to thin the local ursera packs and confront their broodmother.

Fragments of Rok'Alim. Fragments of Rok'Alim are the shattered stone remains of a primeval earth elemental roaming the canyons of Thousand Needles. Brought to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, they serve as undeniable physical proof that a warrior has bested an ancient terror in single combat. While most elementals faded from Azeroth following the banishment of the Old Gods, a handful possessed enough raw power to endure on the surface without being summoned by mortal magic. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such survivor, wandering the canyon flats south of the main thoroughfare. Local centaur know him by the thunderous crashes of his stony fists pulverizing anything foolish enough to wander into his path. Striking down this living remnant of the primordial world yields jagged pieces of dense, animated rock—a trophy fit to prove unmatched physical prowess.

Frahun Shadewhisper. At Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Frahun Shadewhisper trains night elf rogues. He teaches new scouts and rogues stealth, agility, and covert strikes. Erion Shadewhisper, another rogue trainer in Darnassus, shares his family name. At Aldrassil in Teldrassil, Frahun Shadewhisper teaches new rogues concealment and bladecraft. Night elf society honors priests, sentinels, and druids, yet scouts and infiltrators also help safeguard the World Tree's boughs. Recruits bring Frahun an encrypted sigil. He weighs their potential and guides their first steps in the craft.

Fray Island. Warriors gather on Fray Island, just off the Merchant Coast of the Barrens. The rocky islet holds a rough training ring where fighters from across Azeroth test their skill. Fray Island lies off the eastern bluffs of the Barrens, beyond the watchful eyes of Orgrimmar and Theramore. Warriors of every race and creed train here. At the island's heart, Klannoc Macleod oversees a fighting arena where seasoned fighters and raw recruits meet in brutal brawls.

Frayfeather Highlands. The Frayfeather Highlands form an elevated wilderness in the dense forests of Feralas. This remote plateau is the ancestral roost and nesting ground of the wild Frayfeather hippogryphs. Intrepid scavengers and naturalists often brave its territorial flocks in search of intact hippogryph eggs. Rising above the surrounding forest floor of Feralas, the Frayfeather Highlands are dominated by steep slopes and crags where wild hippogryphs raise their broods. The local flocks are notoriously aggressive toward intruders, fiercely defending the scattered nests tucked among the rock shelves. Because these beasts are so well adapted to the rugged cliffs, their nesting grounds have drawn significant interest from outsiders—most notably goblin entrepreneurs in distant Gadgetzan who seek unhatched eggs for study and profit.

Free At Last. Free at Last is a rescue mission atop the windswept spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Lakota Windsong, a tauren woman held captive by Arnak Grimtotem, needs protection as she flees her captor's stronghold and returns to her friend Thalia Amberhide at Freewind Post. The Grimtotem clan's aggressive presence in Thousand Needles is not limited to skirmishes over land. Arnak Grimtotem sought to take Lakota Windsong as his bride, but when she refused his advances, he chose violence. Arnak returned in the night, struck down Lakota's brother when he tried to defend her, and dragged her away to Darkcloud Pinnacle.

Free From the Hold. Gilthares Firebough is held at Northwatch Hold after Alliance forces sink his ship off the Barrens coast. The elf deckhand wants to reach his captain in Ratchet. Gilthares Firebough is held in the dungeons at Northwatch Hold. Theramore uses the fortress as its military foothold on the Barrens coast, where its garrison watches for threats. Gilthares had been aboard a ship carrying moonshine along the trade route between Ratchet and Booty Bay when Alliance forces bombarded it and sent it beneath the sea. He alone survived the wreck. The soldiers took him to Northwatch and accused him of being an enemy agent conspiring against the Alliance.

Free the Hollows. Free the Hollows is a quest in Shadowgale Forest, where ghost-like spirits known as wind hollows linger among ancient ruins. Trapped by an ancient tragedy, their sorrowful singing haunts the surrounding woods until someone grants them release. Elves dwelling across the island have long regarded Shadowgale Forest as a haunted grove, and their superstitions are grounded in truth. Deep within the woods to the northeast lie old stone ruins where phantom apparitions known as wind hollows drift endlessly among the overgrowth. Rather than hostile malice, these spirits project an air of deep sorrow, trapped by the weight of whatever disaster befell the ruins in ages past.

Freed from the Hive. The pod you found in the Writhing Deep splits open at your touch, and inside is a night elf, alive though deeply stunned. He is Raschal, the missing courier. With him freed from the Zukk'ash hive, word must reach Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold that Raschal is alive and well. As you help the night elf down from the pod, he stirs. He gives his name as Raschal and says he woke paralyzed inside it after the bugs overwhelmed him. He looks healthy, but is deeply stunned. He asks whether you were sent by the Stronghold.

Freedom for All Creatures. The Grimtotem clan is capturing faerie dragons, and Kindal Moonweaver and Jer'kai do not know what for. Kindal asks you to bring strong friends, open the pen in the Grimtotem camp with a key and see the sprite darters out alive. Kindal comes with you; Jer'kai stays behind. Kindal Moonweaver calls the Grimtotem clan filthy for taking faerie dragons, and says that neither Kindal nor Jer'kai can guess their plans, only that they are up to no good. The two are not strong enough to fight their way into the camp, so Kindal turns to you. The Bamboo Cage Key opens the pen, and Kindal wants the sprite darters to escape with their lives. Strong friends at your side are welcome.

Freewind Post. Freewind Post is the primary Horde outpost in Thousand Needles, perched high atop one of the canyon's dramatic stone mesas. Accessible primarily by tauren lift and winding rope bridges, it serves as a defensive refuge against centaur warbands and a vital frontier staging ground. Built directly upon the canyon mesas, Freewind Post relies on ingenuity and height to safeguard its people. The Galak centaur dominate the arid canyon floor below, but they cannot effectively scale the towering cliffs or breach the heavy wooden elevators that haul Horde travelers up into the sky. A labyrinth of rope and plank bridges connects Freewind to neighboring spires, forming a secure aerie. Beyond keeping centaur raiding parties at bay, the outpost also helps manage the screeching harpies nesting along the bluffs and tends to the nearby wyvern grounds at Highperch, where wild eggs are culled and trained as loyal wind rider mounts for the Horde.

Fresh Meat. In the Swamp of Sorrows, Dar says customers in Orgrimmar have a high demand for crawler meat, especially that of the monstrous crawlers. Dar asks you to bring back some of their legs from the coast. Dar's customers have a taste for succulent crawler meat, particularly from the monstrous crawlers. Dar promises to make a trip to the coast worth your while if you bring back some of their legs, to be sent on to Orgrimmar. The coast lies east of here, where the creatures scurry over the beaches and into the surf. A cask of wine awaits your success, and Dar means to taste the goods before they ship.

Friend of the Kirin Tor. Archmage Modera's image admits that the council will dislike hearing of the subterfuge, yet cannot argue with results: Dalaran is calming, and the wards may come down. She gives you an arcane mote to take to Archmage Celindra, in the Violet Citadel. The Image of Archmage Modera admits that the council will dislike hearing of the subterfuge, yet cannot argue with results. The city is calming, and the wards may now be lowered. She thinks you should be the one to carry the good word, and gives you an arcane mote to take to Archmage Celindra, in Dalaran's Violet Citadel.

From The Wreckage..... Gar'Thok sends Horde scouts to the wrecks off the Scuttle Coast for Gnomish Tools. The Horde hopes to study Alliance engineering and turn its advantage to their own use. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore brought Kul Tiras's fleet to Kalimdor, where its ships crowded the shore near Tiragarde Keep. After his defeat, broken hulls sank along the Scuttle Coast. Kul Tiran soldiers who survived fortify the keep, while the fleet's wreckage lies scattered on the shoals beneath the tide.

Frostfire Hot Springs. Frostfire Hot Springs are a curious series of steaming pools nestled amidst the western snowdrifts of Winterspring. Despite the bitter sub-zero temperatures all around them, these waters bubble constantly, attracting curious scholars, hardy fishers, and hostile furbolgs alike. Situated near the tunnel leading to Timbermaw Hold, Frostfire Hot Springs represent one of the strangest natural anomalies in northern Kalimdor. The pools remain hot amid the surrounding snow, although the source of their heat is uncertain. The local Winterfall furbolgs maintain a presence near the water, though their aggressive territorial nature makes approaching the warm banks hazardous for unwary travelers. For those able to navigate the hostile wildlife and winter chill, the unfrozen waters provide a rare haven for fish.

Frosthowl. Frosthowl is a quest in Dun Morogh tasking adventurers with recovering a stolen sack of fish from a thieving wendigo. The beast ambushed a local dwarven fisher and fled into the depths of the Grizzled Den. Ice fishing across the freezing waters of Dun Morogh is grueling, bitter labor. A dwarven fisher and her husband, Paxton, spent days out on the frozen lake braving biting winds just to harvest a single sack of fish. Their hard work was abruptly undone when Frosthowl, a menacing and thunderous wendigo, ambushed the camp and made off with their entire haul into the snowy wilderness.

Frostmane Hold. In the peaks above Iceflow Lake, Frostmane trolls guard their cavern stronghold. Senir Whitebeard, stationed in Kharanos, sends scouts inside to kill headhunters and bring back intelligence for his reports. Senir Whitebeard tracks the Frostmane threat across Dun Morogh from Kharanos. The mountaineer and scout followed the aggressive tribes to their main cavern southwest of Brewnall Village, but armed trolls crowd its entrance. Senir is falling severely behind on his official reports, and he will not enter alone. He hires passing adventurers to scout the icy cavern in his place.

Frostmane Hold. Frostmane trolls hold the cliffs south of Gnomeregan in western Dun Morogh. The Ironforge Guard watches their camp and caverns as raiders press into dwarven lands. Frostmane Hold cuts into the cold cliffs of western Dun Morogh. Rough structures stand outside its winding caves, where hideskinners and headhunters guard the tribe's stronghold. Frostmane raiders leave from here to strike the valleys, threaten travelers on the mountain passes, and test the defenses around Kharanos.

Frostmane Hovel. Frostmane Hovel is a rugged cave den tucked into the southern crags of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. It serves as an entrenched shelter for aggressive Frostmane trolls pressing directly into dwarven training grounds. Carved into the southern mountains flanking Coldridge Valley, the Frostmane Hovel shelters indigenous Frostmane trolls who refuse to yield the high snows to Ironforge. Operating out of crude caverns like this, the trolls mount continuous raids against local dwarven camps and disrupt supply lines into the valley.

Frostmane tribe. Across Dun Morogh’s frigid peaks, the Frostmane tribe fights to reclaim its home. These ice trolls are native to the mountains, but dwarves drove them into caves and remote ridges centuries ago. From there, the Frostmane wage a guerrilla war against the dwarves. Long before the Bronzebeard clan united under Ironforge, the Frostmane trolls ruled across Dun Morogh’s snowbound reaches. The rise and spread of the dwarven kingdom crushed their realm, forcing survivors to retreat into caves and along frozen ridges and crags. That defeat bred a bitter hatred passed down through generations. To the Frostmane, every mountaineer, traveler, and homestead is an invader to drive out or slaughter.

Frostsaber Rock. Frostsaber Rock is a towering stone promontory rising above the snowy northern reaches of Winterspring. It serves as the primary sanctuary and training grounds for the noble frostsaber cats of the region. Rising high above the frozen wastes of northern Winterspring, Frostsaber Rock commands a sweeping view of the snowbound wild. The crag is named for the fierce, majestic frostsaber predators that prowl the slopes and valleys below. At its highest apex resides Rivern Frostwind, a solitary night elf dedicated to raising and tending these beasts. For champions loyal to the Alliance willing to brave the harsh conditions and prove their devotion, Rivern offers the rare privilege of learning to raise, tame, and ride one of these legendary snowy mounts.

Frostwhisper Gorge. Frostwhisper Gorge is a frigid canyon carved into the southern highlands of Winterspring, lying directly north of the sinister Darkwhisper Gorge. Ancient night elven ruins litter its icy floor and surrounding cliffs, while towering Frostmaul giants dominate the chasm. High above the eastern rim, a solitary dwarf camp looks out over the precipice toward the ocean below. Carved into the southern mountains of Winterspring, Frostwhisper Gorge serves as a threshold just before the demon-infested depths of Darkwhisper Gorge. Its snowy floor and cliffside ridges are strewn with the forgotten stonework of ancient night elven settlements. In the present day, the gorge is claimed by immense Frostmaul giants and their preservers. Travel down into the ravine is perilous, as the giants fiercely defend the frozen crags against any wandering intruders.

Frostwolf Banner. In Alterac Valley, Horde initiates seek the Frostwolf Banner in Wildpaw Cavern. Recovering it is an ancestral rite of passage that awakens their battle spirit and earns their first clan insignia. Horde warriors seeking a place among the Frostwolf clan face a trial of grit in Alterac Valley. Warmaster Laggrond sends new recruits south into Wildpaw Cavern, where territorial gnolls fill the damp, hostile corridors. Reaching the hidden banner and bringing it back unbroken proves their courage and shows their battle rage has awakened. The trial earns each warrior the Frostwolf initiate's insignia.

Fruit of the Sea. Fruit of the Sea is an Alliance quest offered by the fisherman Gubber Blump on the docks of Auberdine. Passionate about culinary crustacean dishes, Gubber asks travelers to scour the Darkshore coastline for fine crab chunks while he tends to his fishing lines. Gubber Blump, a fisherman casting his line off the long wooden piers of Auberdine, harbors an obsessive culinary devotion to crab meat. Viewing crabs as the true bounty of the ocean, Gubber envisions an endless repertoire of recipes ranging from baked, barbecued, and boiled preparations to elaborate local specialties like whipper root crab and Ironforge surprise crab.

Fuel for the Zapping. On the Forgotten Coast of Feralas, Zorbin Fandazzle has opened an engineering shop against better judgment, and the local elementals are a pest. They are also an ideal supply of raw power for refining the Ultra-Shrinker, and the water elemental cores are what Zorbin wants. Zorbin Fandazzle curses the unchecked powers of elementalism, and calls the elementals of the coast pests. Yet Zorbin also reckons them an ideal supply of raw power when refining the Ultra-Shrinker. Zorbin wants you to give the Sea Elementals and Sea Sprays of the coast what for, keep their water elemental cores, and bring them to Zorbin by the dock.

Full Leaden Collection Phial. Ozzie Togglevolt seeks a sample from Gnomeregan’s troggs in a heavy, lead-lined phial. He hopes to make a cure for irradiated leper gnomes, or perhaps a dangerously potent rum. The phial’s lead lining shields its carrier from the volatile green fallout that saturates Gnomeregan. High Tinker Mekkatorque’s advisors flooded the lower corridors with toxic radiation to stop the invading troggs. Instead, the disaster corrupted troggs and surviving gnomes into maddened, irradiated horrors. Fluid residue gathered from Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers gives refugee tinkerers in Kharanos, including Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket, raw material for their experiments on remedies.

Fungal Rock. Fungal Rock is a damp, cavernous hollow carved into the northeastern cliff walls of Un'Goro Crater. Dominated by aggressive primates and thick growths of Ghost Mushrooms, it is one of the crater's most dangerous ape dens. Tucked behind a small waterfall and pool along Un'Goro Crater's northeastern edge, Fungal Rock serves as the primary den for the region's massive gorillas. Inside the damp, subterranean corridors, towering Un'Goro Stompers and Thunderers patrol among clusters of rare Ghost Mushrooms. The deepest recesses house territorial behemoths, including the mighty silverback U'cha and the elusive albino gorilla Uhk'loc. Beyond its primal inhabitants, curious travelers may stumble upon artificial oddities near the cave mouth, such as A-Me 01, a damaged mechanical ape abandoned by gnome researchers.

Fungal Spores. Around the Barrens' oases, Fungal Spores gather in swollen mushrooms. The waters quicken the life around them, and the Royal Apothecary Society seeks the spores for its alchemy. The Barrens' oases bring unusual life to the dry plains. At the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis, the water does more than ease thirst. It quickens and changes the plants and wildlife nearby. Mushrooms along the damp shores swell with spores, carrying the waters' concentrated power to spur growth. Naturalists study this change, while the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the mushrooms for its alchemy.

Fungal Spores. At the Barrens oases, Horde adventurers gather Fungal Spores for Apothecary Helbrim of the Royal Apothecary Society. Strange, mutative energies flow through the springs and alter the local plants into potent reagents. Helbrim seeks the specimens to brew concoctions for his colleague in Thunder Bluff. The Barrens is a dry savanna, but the Forgotten Pools, Lushwater Oasis, and Stagnant Oasis brim with unnatural vitality. A curious surge of life energy flows from their waters, warping and invigorating plants and beasts that drink there. Laden mushrooms grow along the muddy banks, absorbing those currents. Their spores hold rare properties that draw the curiosity of passing alchemists.

Fungal Vale. The Fungal Vale is a deeply blighted depression located in the south-central Eastern Plaguelands, just north of the Crown Guard Tower and Marris Stead. Choked in a murky haze and blanketed with dark purple earth, the valley showcases the raw, mutating power of the Plague of Undeath. It swarms with roaming Scourge horrors and mortal acolytes serving the Cult of the Damned. Situated north of Marris Stead, the Fungal Vale represents one of the most thoroughly corrupted pockets in Lordaeron. The ground here has turned a sickly purple, swollen with alien fungal growths and drowning under a perpetual, murky haze produced by necrotic spores. Rather than simply killing the ecosystem, the Plague of Undeath has warped the soil to cultivate unholy flora, feeding monstrous carrion beasts and shambling undead. Cult of the Damned members frequent the area, tending to the blighted blooms and conducting foul rites amidst the unnatural decay.

Furbolg. Furbolgs are a hulking, reclusive race of bear-men native to northern Kalimdor who lived in harmony with nature and the night elves for millennia. In the wake of the Third War, demonic corruption and lingering fel magic have driven nearly every tribe into a frenzied madness. Today, former friends have become vicious territorial predators, with only a tiny handful of tribes clinging to their sanity. Furbolgs are an ancient people of Kalimdor who have long revered the wild god Ursoc. During the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago, tribal packs united under chieftain Unng Ak to fight alongside night elves and tauren against the first demonic invasion. Following the Great Sundering, they chose seclusion deep in the northern woodlands, maintaining peaceful ties with night elf druids and forest wardens while living in simple harmony with the wild.

Furen Longbeard. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, warriors seek Furen Longbeard's skill to forge specialized, battle-ready armor. Apprenticed to Grimand Elmore, the master armorer is known for his metallurgical expertise and heavy protective gear. Furen Longbeard works far from Ironforge's great forges, among the cobblestones and soot of Stormwind's Dwarven District. Like many dwarves, he brought traditional metallurgy south to help rebuild and defend the kingdom. His work keeps him connected with artisans throughout the city and beyond.

Furen's Armor. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard seeks help testing new armor. An aspiring warrior gathers spider fangs, chimaera horns, and phlogiston so the master smith can forge fire-hardened mail. Furen gives the finished armor to the warrior and promises to share what he learned with Alliance smiths. Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorer in Stormwind, works to improve how Alliance armor withstands heat and crushing blows. He asks an aspiring warrior to gather rare materials for his tests. The resulting mail proves a success and strengthens Furen's standing among Alliance armorers.

Furen's Instructions. In Stormwind, Furen's Instructions name the materials needed for fire-hardened mail. Furen Longbeard gives the parchment to Alliance warriors he has tested. Furen Longbeard offers to forge a resilient suit of mail for a warrior who has proved himself through simpler smithing work. The dwarven armorer asks the warrior to fetch the rare components himself. His parchment records what is needed and sends the warrior across continents to gather it.

Furen's Notes. Furen's Notes carry his discoveries in metallurgy and armorsmithing from Stormwind to Alliance craftsmen. After forging protective gear for veteran warriors, Furen Longbeard sends copies to help fellow smiths refine their work. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Furen Longbeard forges specialized armaments for warriors and records the methods and discoveries he makes along the way. Dwarven metalworking keeps changing, so he makes several copies for other smiths to use and build upon. His notes describe practical ways to temper, reinforce, and shape armor against deadly blows.

Furl Scornbrow. At a watchtower northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow keeps watch over Durotar. Too old for the front lines, he crafts sturdy packs for young travelers. Furl Scornbrow watches the central plains from a wooden tower northwest of Razor Hill. In the tense days after Orgrimmar was founded, sentries like Furl sounded signal horns against hostile quilboar, centaur, and Kul Tiras interlopers. Durotar has since grown more stable, and Razor Hill has secured its borders. Emergencies come less often, leaving Furl long quiet hours at his post.

Furlbrow's Deed. The Furlbrows are stranded near Westfall's border, and their land deed is in Defias hands. The paper bears Theodore and Verna Furlbrow's claim to their family farm, while the couple waits by their broken wagon. The deed bears Theodore Furlbrow's signature and Verna's as well, securing their family farm in Westfall. When the Defias Brotherhood overran the region, bandits drove the couple from their home and carried the paper into Elwynn Forest. Notes on its back show they meant to copy it when forging claims to other properties. The Furlbrows lost their home and livelihood, then took to the road. Their wagon broke near the border, leaving them stranded.

Furlbrow's Deed. The Furlbrows flee their farm as Defias bandits carry their land grant through Elwynn Forest. Returning the deed to Farmer Furlbrow near the Westfall border preserves the couple’s claim to their stolen homestead. Defias bandits in Elwynn carry a land deed signed by Theodore and Verna Furlbrow. A crude note on its back says they drove the elderly farmer from his property, then carried the document across the river into Elwynn to copy it and forge claims to other seized land. The note says the Furlbrows were stranded just over the border, beside the road, after their wagon broke.

Furlbrow's Pocket Watch. In Westfall, Farmer Furlbrow has lost a keepsake from his wedding day. His pocket watch came from Verna’s father, and it was left behind when Defias bandits seized the family’s pumpkin farm. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna fled their home in the night when Defias bandits swarmed the Furlbrow Pumpkin Patch. In the rush, he left a pocket watch from Verna’s father behind. The watch remains in a wardrobe in the overrun farmhouse, where Benny Blaanco and his cutthroats keep watch. The displaced couple now camps along the road, and the watch is one of the few pieces of their former life the outlaws have not ruined.

Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Bandits and harvest golems hold Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm in northern Westfall, off the road from Elwynn Forest. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna have lost their home to the Defias Brotherhood. Near Westfall's northern border, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm once grew crops to feed the kingdom. The Defias Brotherhood drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land. Mechanical harvest golems now roam the fields, attacking anyone who approaches. Bandits occupy the farm buildings, while the rightful owners camp beside the road near the Jansen Stead, mourning their lost home and livelihood.

Further Concerns. Marshal Dughan sends an Alliance courier east from Goldshire to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas, who watches the river crossing toward Redridge. Rumors tell of hostile aquatic creatures creeping along Elwynn's riverbanks. Marshal Dughan commands the Goldshire garrison, where banditry and vermin already trouble the center of the forest. He will not dismiss the reports, but he cannot spare guards from town. Instead, he sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge over the river toward Redridge.

Further Instructions. Ziz Fizziks sends stolen Venture Company plans from Windshear Crag to Ratchet. The documents may give his rival Sputtervalve an edge. After the Venture Company cast Ziz Fizziks out of its logging operations at Windshear Crag, he took sensitive documents, internal manuals, and technical schematics with him. Bitter over his dismissal, he sealed them in an envelope bound for Ratchet. Among the papers are blueprints for the experimental Super Reaper 6000. Fizziks hopes to find a buyer or ally willing to use what he stole.

Further Instructions. Sputtervalve carries an order from Undermine to Ziz Fizziks in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the gnome engineer hired by Mogul Razdunk, must be eliminated. The Venture Company’s hiring of Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle has stirred trouble among Undermine’s rulers. Mogul Razdunk brought the gnome engineer into the company, and word of it reached the Trade Princes. Director Riddlevox told Sputtervalve to intervene quietly. Sputtervalve believes the order comes from the highest trade authorities, so he passes the work to Ziz Fizziks, the operative nearest the scene.

Further Mysteries. Prospector Stormpike has decrypted the letter you found among thieves in the Alterac foothills, but cannot make sense of it. He tells you to take it to the magistrate of Southshore. After Letter to Stormpike, the prospector says he has decrypted the letter but cannot tell what it means. He finds it very strange that you came by it among thieves in the Alterac foothills. The letter is cryptic, yet Southshore lies nearest to Alterac, so if a threat is brewing, the magistrate there should hear of it. You are to carry the decrypted letter to Magistrate Henry Maleb.

Gadgetzan. Gadgetzan is the walled desert hub of the Steamwheedle Cartel, standing as an island of commerce in northern Tanaris. Open to both Horde and Alliance travelers, the town operates under strictly enforced goblin neutrality, welcoming anyone with coin to spend or odd jobs to undertake. Surrounded by scorching sands, Gadgetzan serves as the regional heart for the Steamwheedle Cartel's ventures in southern Kalimdor. Built with characteristic goblin ingenuity and haphazard architecture, the town boasts an independent auction house, bank, inn, and specialized crafting facilities for engineers, blacksmiths, and alchemists. It also houses flight masters catering to both major factions, ensuring steady traffic of adventurers heading toward Tanaris, Feralas, and the untamed basin of Un'Goro. Above all, commerce rules supreme: as long as visitors keep their weapons sheathed and their purses open, they are safe within its gates.

name.esES: Un estudio de agua de Gadgetzan

text.enUS: Gadgetzan Water Survey. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser in Gadgetzan is hiring a temporary junior-grade surveyor for the Gadgetzan Water Company. With the nomads seizing the company's wells, you are handed a dowsing widget to tap a sample from the pool near Sandsorrow Watch. The nomads have seized all the wells of the Gadgetzan Water Company, so the company must find more free sources of water. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser believes the desert holds some, though only for those clever enough to survey first, and wants a temporary junior-grade surveyor to help.

Gaea Seed. Along Mirkfallon Lake, Gaea Seeds offer a way to heal Stonetalon's wounded land. Tauren shamans value the hardy kernels for restoring places scarred by war and industry. Gaea Seeds wash ashore or grow along Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Small and fibrous, they look like coconuts, yet endure harsh conditions. As conflict and industry scar the land, shamans see the seeds as a means to heal it.

Gaerolas Talvethren. At Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren guards the Sleeping druids in troubled Teldrassil. He seeks aid against aggressive furbolgs and corruption spreading through the boughs. Gaerolas Talvethren guards the Sleeping druids at Starbreeze Village. They slumber in communion with the Emerald Dream, and his watch has grown uneasy as unnatural corruption spreads through the forest and unsettles Teldrassil.

Gaffer Jack. Off Auberdine, Gaffer Jack parts lie beneath Darkshore's waves. Wizbang Cranktoggle lost a crate of them during his voyage across the sea. Gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle booked passage to Auberdine, seeking quiet away from Ironforge's forge-works and taverns. During the voyage, he drank too much and fumbled an entire container of gaffer jacks over the railing. The small fasteners sank into Darkshore's coastal waters, leaving Wizbang without the parts he needed to tune his stintle pegs.

Gaffer Jacks. In Auberdine, Wizbang Cranktoggle needs his lost gaffer jacks back. The gnome inventor tossed a box of hardware into the sea during his voyage from Ironforge, and anglers can search for it along Darkshore's coast. Wizbang Cranktoggle crossed the Great Sea from Ironforge to find quiet in Darkshore. The gnome inventor drank too much on the voyage. Leaning over the rail in a drunken haze, he lost a crate of specialized metal parts called gaffer jacks in the water near Auberdine.

Gahrron's Withering. Gahrron's Withering is a corrupted farmstead nestled along the eastern border of the Western Plaguelands near the path to the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron farmland, it is now occupied by the Scourge and anchored by a massive cauldron pumping virulent plague vapors into the air. Before the Third War ruined the kingdom of Lordaeron, this estate was a working farm. Its fertile fields yielded grain for the realm until the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge swept across the land. Now called Gahrron's Withering, the homestead stands broken and derelict. Haunting visions, wailing wraiths, and restless spirits wander the ruined outbuildings, overseen by Scourge overseers sworn to the Lich King.

Gahz'ridian. Marvon Rivetseeker, a scientist and treasure hunter at heart, wants thirty ornaments left behind by the trolls who once lived in Tanaris. Marvon gives you a detector of their own invention to help find them. Long ago trolls occupied this land, and they made great numbers of ornaments in the likeness of Gahz'rilla, a hydra they revered as a god. Marvon Rivetseeker calls the element these were carved from Gahz'ridian, after the hydra god. Marvon has found a few and would like more to study.

Gakin the Darkbinder. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches the warlock arts in secret. He tests aspiring Alliance warlocks before they attempt to summon and bind demons. Below The Slaughtered Lamb's taproom, a cellar shelters those who study shadow and fel. The crypt-like room holds summoning circles and grim tomes, hidden from the eyes that watch Stormwind's open mage sanctuaries. Gakin guides young warlocks there, teaching discipline and restraint before they summon forces they cannot control.

Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks by Remen Marcot on behalf of Gakin the Darkbinder. It directs fledgling practitioners down into the crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter to begin their next stage of dark occult training. Demonology is strictly outlawed across the civilized districts of Stormwind, yet dark arts persist right under the noses of the city guard. When a warlock displays sufficient proficiency with their introductory imps, word quietly travels to senior practitioners. Remen Marcot delivers the message with deliberate discretion, urging initiates to keep the meeting place quiet and head into the shadowy recesses beneath the Mage Quarter.

Gakin's Summons. Lago Blackwrench sends Gakin's Summons from Ironforge to promising Alliance warlocks. It directs them south to Stormwind, where Gakin the Darkbinder awaits beneath the Mage Quarter to oversee their advancement in commanding greater fiends. Demonology remains hidden across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly watches wandering practitioners for the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock shows mastery over their first minions, word travels quickly. Lago passes along the directive: leave your business in the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay.

Galardell Valley. Gnolls prowl Galardell Valley beneath the Tower of Ilgalar in northeastern Redridge. The canyon is a danger to the settlements nearby. Redridge gnolls prowl Galardell Valley, beyond the reach of Lakeshire's defenders. They roam the lowlands and camp along the canyon floor under brutal pack leaders such as Lieutenant Fangore. Above the ravines rises the Tower of Ilgalar, stronghold of the renegade mage Morganth. The gnolls and the tower keep the valley a source of dread for nearby settlements.

Galen's Escape. Galen Goodward is in the Fallow Sanctuary, begging for rescue from the creatures there, and promises a great treasure to anyone who gets him out. It waits in a locked strongbox at his camp north of Stonard. Galen Goodward cries out that the creatures around him are going to eat him. Anyone who helps him out of danger is promised a great treasure. It sits at his camp, out in the swamp north of Stonard, locked in a strongbox that opens only through a trick known to Galen alone. If you help him escape, he will teach it to you.

Galgar. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar feeds young recruits serving the Horde. He asks newcomers to gather wild cactus apples for his Cactus Apple Surprise. Galgar cooks near the Den's fire in the Valley of Trials, feeding young orcs and trolls through their first rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, harsh red wasteland, where food must be found across the land. Galgar sends novice warriors to gather ripe cactus fruit, testing their attention and resilience while stocking his kitchen.

text.enUS: Galgar's Cactus Apple Surprise. In the Valley of Trials, Galgar sends fresh recruits to gather cactus apples for his cooling treat. The work teaches them to forage and survive in Durotar's arid land. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls take their first steps as defenders of the Horde in the Valley of Trials. Combat drills and fierce trials against native beasts quickly bring exhaustion and thirst. Learning to live off the land matters as much as learning to swing an axe. Cacti across the valley bear ripe, water-rich apples that offer relief from the desert sun.

Gallery of Treasures. The Gallery of Treasures is an ornate, heavily guarded corridor inside the Scarlet Monastery's halls, connecting the Huntsman's Cloister to the Athenaeum. Lined with recovered paintings, relics, and illuminated texts, it showcases the wealth and Lordaeron heritage preserved by the Scarlet Crusade amidst their zealous war against the undead. Situated deep within the Library wing of the Scarlet Monastery, the Gallery of Treasures serves as a grand hall connecting the kennels of the Huntsman's Cloister to the sacred archives of the Athenaeum. Unlike the hound pens of the cloister, this corridor is lined with fine paintings, historical artifacts, and small chambers filled with books salvaged from across the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. To the Scarlet Crusade, these relics represent the untainted legacy of humanity they have sworn to protect, fiercely guarded against all outsiders who dare intrude upon their sanctuary.

Gallows' End Tavern. Gallows' End Tavern is the principal inn of Brill and the heart of Forsaken hospitality in Tirisfal Glades. Beyond offering shelter and spirits to weary travelers, it serves as an essential hub for class mentors, trade instructors, and covert interrogations. Standing prominently along the road in Brill, Gallows' End Tavern serves as the primary gathering place for newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell and journeying south toward the Undercity. Despite their undead condition, Forsaken still frequent its halls for fellowship, trade, and refuge. The inn houses various class instructors—guiding young warriors, priests, mages, rogues, and warlocks—as well as vendors and medical practitioners.

Gallywix's Head. In Orgrimmar, Gallywix's Head proves that a Venture Company overseer was executed. The Shattered Hand demands the trophy as proof of the killing. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix directed the Venture Company's work from its tower north of the Sludge Fen. When word arrived that the Venture Co. planned something on a grand scale, the Shattered Hand sent operatives to dismantle the facility. Bringing Gallywix's head to Shenthul in Orgrimmar proves the overseer was executed and secures the rogue's standing within the guild.

Galvanized Horn. In the Charred Vale, chimaera matriarchs bear horns that Stormwind and Thunder Bluff armorers seek. These hardened growths go into specialized armor for warriors. Chimaera matriarchs prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains. Their horns grow unusually hard through ash, flame, and survival. Lesser fledgling chimaeras yield brittle, blackened horns, but a matriarch's horn has strength like treated metal. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff both seek one as a test of martial valor and a key ingredient for exceptional mail armor.

Gammerita, Mon!. Katoom the Angler, from Revantusk Village in the Hinterlands, has lost his best lure to Gammerita, the head of the saltwater snapjaws. You are asked to find her and get it back. Katoom describes Gammerita as no ordinary turtle: she heads the saltwater snapjaws, and Katoom brands her a thief. She snapped his best lure off his line, and since then the fish have not bitten the way they used to.

Gan'rul Bloodeye. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye trains warlocks beneath the city. In the Cleft of Shadow, Horde initiates learn darker demonic rites and how to bend voidwalkers and succubi to their will. Warlocks study out of sight in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. Warchief Thrall tolerates them in the new Horde, though Durotar's open sunlight is no place for their dark arts. The cavern gives shadow weavers, rogues, and fel casters room to study unmolested. From there, Gan'rul teaches rising practitioners of fel magic.

Gan'rul's Summons. Gan'rul's Summons is an urgent call delivered to young Horde warlocks by Ophek in Razor Hill. Senior warlock Gan'rul Bloodeye requires their immediate presence in the Cleft of Shadow to advance their training. It marks the first step toward mastering the dark art of summoning a voidwalker. Novice warlocks operating in Durotar do not remain unnoticed for long. Once a practitioner demonstrates sufficient mastery over their initial imp, word reaches the deeper subterranean recesses of Orgrimmar. Ophek, stationed out in Durotar, acts as a messenger for the senior dark casters, intercepting warlocks with an urgent demand to drop whatever they are doing and report to the Cleft of Shadow.

Gann Stonespire. Along the southern Barrens road near Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire seeks retaliation for his people’s displacement. The tauren nomad’s tribe hunted on land now occupied by a dwarven excavation. Gann Stonespire camps beside the southern Barrens road after the dwarven expedition arrived from Ironforge and built Bael Modan. The surrounding land had been his tribe’s ancestral territory and hunting grounds. Dwarven miners drove the tauren from their soil with pickaxes, firearms, and heavy machinery, and refused peaceful overtures. Gann will not surrender his heritage quietly. He calls on travelers to strike back at the excavators.

Gann's Reclamation. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire seeks travelers to strike back at Bael Modan. The wandering tauren exile was driven from his clan’s ancestral home and hunting grounds, and asks you to slay the dig’s workers and bring him its leader’s journal. Gann Stonespire walks alone along the southern road, seeking bloody restitution for his fallen kin. His clan’s ancestral birthplace and hunting grounds lay among the red bluffs south of the Barrens. Dwarves from Ironforge came to build Bael Modan, and drove the tauren out or killed them to make room for quarries and trenches. Gann says peaceful protests and diplomacy failed. Now he seeks vengeance for the clan that was displaced and slain.

Gaping Chasm. The Gaping Chasm is a sprawling silithid hive carved deep into the sands of southeastern Tanaris. Infested by aggressive insectoid horrors of the Hazzali brood, it serves as a grim warning of the growing silithid menace spreading beyond the western deserts. Breaking the rolling expanses of Tanaris, the Gaping Chasm plunges down into a teeming subterranean warren of tunnels, resinous mounds, and twitching carapaces. This hive belongs to the Hazzali, an aggressive brood of silithid that have burrowed beneath the desert wastes. Between subterranean stingers, swarmers, and hulking sandreavers, any travelers or treasure-hunters foolish enough to descend into the chasm quickly find themselves hunted as prey or preserved in sticky cocoons.

Gar'Thok. At Razor Hill, Gar'Thok directs recruits leaving the Valley of Trials to secure Durotar. The veteran orc warrior survived the Kul Tiras landings on Durotar's coast and now coordinates defense against human encroachers and native threats. After the Third War, Gar'Thok marched to Durotar under Warchief Thrall and served as a lieutenant under Nazgrel during the first days of building the new homeland. When Rexxar, the half-ogre wanderer, arrived in Durotar, Gar'Thok warned him that quilboar were raiding the settlement's perimeter. He enlisted the beastmaster to protect the fragile new settlement.

Gargantuan Tumor. In Teldrassil, a great growth was torn from Oakenscowl, the corrupted timberling by Lake Al'Ameth. The tumor bears witness to sickness spreading among the creatures there. Oakenscowl lurks in a cavern near Lake Al'Ameth's southern bank. Once a noble timberling elder, the creature has fallen to a vile affliction. A huge growth poisoned Oakenscowl, warped its behavior, and spread taint through the surrounding wildlife. The tumor was severed to end the beast's rampage and give local researchers a chance to examine the blight. They hope to learn how the malady took root in the boughs of the newly grown World Tree.

Garments of Darkness. In Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl tests fledgling Forsaken priests before they delve deeper into shadow. The trial shows whether they can heal and fortify an injured Deathguard, for the priesthood calls for more than afflicting enemies. Forsaken priests draw renown and a distinct identity from shadow and darkness. Dark Cleric Beryl also teaches that understanding darkness means learning light and restoration. Those who seek only ruin are urged to study arcane magic instead. A priest's calling includes strengthening and preserving comrades as well as afflicting enemies.

Garments of Spirituality. In Razor Hill, Tai'jin sends new priests to prove their healing in the field. They seek Grunt Kor'ja, wounded while standing against Kul Tiras survivors, and tend her injuries. Those who succeed earn ceremonial vestments and recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners. South of Razor Hill, the Horde still fights remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Tai'jin, the troll priest trainer, tests new priests in the work of real combat triage. She sends them to find Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior badly wounded while repelling human infiltrators. You tend her injuries and strengthen her before she succumbs.

Garments of the Light. At Goldshire, Garments of the Light mark a novice priest’s first trial under Priestess Josetta. She sends you east to Crystal Lake to tend the wounded Guard Roberts. The work tests your healing and earns you vestments recognized by the Church of the Holy Light. Priestess Josetta teaches acolytes who come to Goldshire from Northshire Abbey. Before the Church of the Holy Light formally recognizes a novice, she tests their skill with divine power. When Guard Roberts is reported wounded by the lake east of Goldshire, Josetta sends you to care for him. His need gives you a chance to prove your healing in practice.

Garments of the Light. In Kharanos, a wounded mountaineer needs the Light's aid before a young priest receives their garments. Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol sends the initiate just south of town to help him. Maxan Anvol puts a wounded defender's needs before ceremony. Acolytes traditionally face formal trials to prove they are worthy of church vestments, but the priest trainer in Kharanos favors practical results. Local patrols are hard-pressed against troggs and wild beasts, and defenders are bleeding in the snow.

Garments of the Moon. Laurna Morninglight sends a young priest to aid a wounded Sentinel south of Dolanaar. The duty tests an initiate's devotion and brings formal recognition in the Sisterhood of Elune. The Sisterhood of Elune guides kaldorei in worship and helps defend Teldrassil's borders. Sentinel Shaya is wounded while patrolling the wilderness south of Dolanaar, and priest trainer Laurna Morninglight cannot leave her post to help. She asks a newly trained initiate to tend Shaya's wounds and strengthen her with protective magic.

Garren's Haunt. Rot Hide gnolls prowl the ruined fields of Garren's Haunt in northern Tirisfal. The farm once belonged to the Garren family, until the Scourge slaughtered them and left the homestead to decay. Garren's Haunt once fed a human family under the Kingdom of Lordaeron. Before the Third War, its fields yielded bountiful harvests. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the countryside, the Scourge came to the farm and slaughtered Garren and his kin. Now gray, withered fields surround a farmhouse and barn that decay beneath Tirisfal's perpetual gloom.

Garrick's Head. At Northshire's vineyards, Garrick Padfoot's severed head proves the cutthroat is dead. The authorities at Northshire Abbey require it to pay the bounty. Garrick Padfoot and his gang harassed Northshire Valley's farmers and merchants for weeks. With Stormwind's defenses stretched thin, Garrick made his hideout in a shack near the vineyards and raided passing trade.
