Local guards were occupied by kobolds and Defias bandits, so Deputy Willem offered a bounty for the outlaw's death. He sought someone willing to kill Garrick and bring back proof.

Garrison Armory. The Garrison Armory is an Alliance mining operation carved into the hills southwest of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Miners and engineers work the underground veins to harvest valuable minerals, sustaining the lonely fortress and shipping raw wealth back to Stormwind. It forms a crucial industrial lifeline in an otherwise blasted, barren wilderness. Maintaining a permanent military garrison in the arid wastes of the Blasted Lands requires constant supply, and Nethergarde Keep cannot rely purely on long supply trains from Stormwind. The Garrison Armory serves as the keep's primary industrial excavation. Nethergarde miners, overseen by foremen and assisted by engineers, work these subterranean shafts to pull valuable minerals from the earth. The ore extracted here is utilized directly by Nethergarde's smiths and fortifications or hauled back to the capital in exchange for the foodstuffs, tools, and provisions the fortress needs to maintain its vigil over the Dark Portal.

Gart Mistrunner. At Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner guides novice tauren called by the Earth Mother. He teaches their first rites of nature magic on the Red Cloud Mesa. Gart Mistrunner watches over Camp Narache as the Shu'halo rekindle their ancient druidic path. New tauren druids are sent to him when they take their first steps on the Red Cloud Mesa, often with a note commending them to his care. Gart teaches them to commune with the natural world. They draw on nature's restorative power and Mu'sha's lunar radiance to heal allies and strike down threats to the land.

Gatehouse Goods. Gatehouse Goods is a local Stormwind task involving the transport of a shipment up the stairs within Trias' Cheese. Because the cheese shop shares a floor with the adjacent gatehouse, goods can be quietly dropped outside the stockroom door for guards to collect. The arrangement highlights the tight, interconnected urban design of Stormwind's commercial and defensive quarters. Gatehouse Goods entails a straightforward delivery task nestled within the bustling streets of Stormwind. The job requires carrying a gatehouse shipment up the interior stairs of Trias' Cheese. While the famed cheese shop is an entirely distinct business with its own separate inventory, its physical structure shares a floor with the neighboring gatehouse facilities. This architectural quirk makes the shop's upper landing a practical passage for moving supplies between neighboring quarters without disturbing the front avenues.

Gates of Ironforge. Travelers climb from Dun Morogh to the Gates of Ironforge, where a stone king guards the way into the dwarven capital. The gates open in the mountain face, with High King Modimus Anvilmar's statue just inside. The Gates of Ironforge rise above the snowy lowlands at the end of a winding, fortified ramp from central Dun Morogh. Beyond the massive portal, you enter the city proper beneath an enormous stone likeness of High King Modimus Anvilmar. He united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. The passage opens directly into the Commons, where Ironforge's trade and banking are centered.

Gates of Orgrimmar. At Orgrimmar's southern gate, timber and iron guard the entrance cut into northern Durotar's red rock. The passage leads from the arid wastes to the Valley of Strength, the capital's busy commons. The gate proclaims the Horde's endurance and strength in war. Orgrimmar's main gate guards the great chasm cut into the mountains around the city. Towering wooden palisades, iron spikes, and watchtowers fortify the entrance. Travelers coming from Razor Hill and Durotar's scrublands find a grand welcome and a warning to any who threaten the new Horde. Armed Orgrimmar Grunts patrol the approach and watch everyone entering the city.

Gath'Ilzogg. Stonewatch Keep remains under Gath'Ilzogg's command in the Redridge Mountains. The Blackrock warlord's force holds the fortress and raids Lakeshire, where Magistrate Solomon has placed a bounty on him. Gath'Ilzogg came north from the Burning Steppes to secure Redridge for the Blackrock clan. With help from the renegade human warlock Morganth's foul sorcery, his warband battered Stonewatch Keep's defenders and seized the heights above the region. From the fortress, Gath'Ilzogg directs raids through the valleys and toward Lakeshire's bridge, tightening pressure on the human settlement. Elite Blackrock guards and a vicious black dragon whelp named Singe stay close to him.

Gather Rot Blossoms. In Duskwood, Tavernkeep Smitts needs rot blossoms for his zombie juice. The plants grow inside the skulls of skeletal horrors and fiends in the graveyards. Tavernkeep Smitts sometimes brews a strange drink at the Scarlet Raven Tavern. His recipe for zombie juice calls for rot blossoms, which root inside the empty skulls of animated skeletons. Smitts avoids the undead, so passing mercenaries gather the blossoms for him.

Gathering Leather. Gathering Leather is a straightforward trade request offered by Veren Tallstrider on the rises of Thunder Bluff. To sustain the capital and test young hunters, Veren exchanges a bundle of cured light leather skins for crafted goods. It highlights the deeply ingrained tauren tradition of turning the fruits of the plains hunt into essential clothing and armor. In the newly settled capital atop the high mesas of Mulgore, craftsmanship and survival walk hand in hand. Veren Tallstrider works skins into clothing and protective armor needed by the growing population of Thunder Bluff. Rather than harvesting everything himself, he encourages young adventurers heading out into the plains to bring back their quarry, turning mundane hunting into honorable civic service.

Gathering Materials. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell sends aspiring Horde mages to Silverpine Forest for Dalaran mana gems. They also need linen to make their first true mage's robes. Undercity initiates gather the materials for their first true robes: a bolt of simple linen and potent Dalaran mana gems. The robes mark their station and personal worth, and Anastasia Hartwell directs the novices to harvest these raw components for an enchanted weave.

Gathering the Cure. Gathering the Cure is an essential trial for young night elf druids learning to master nature's healing powers in Darkshore. Guided by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine, the druid collects vital natural reagents to brew a restorative salve for the region's ailing wildlife. This task lays the practical foundation for understanding how herbal remedies combat venom and disease. Following the discovery of a contaminated water source plaguing the local wildlife, Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine sets out to concoct an effective curative salve. While the sampled Cliffspring water forms the base of the mixture, genuine healing requires potent natural catalysts. The afflicted forest deer cannot recover on their own, making the gathering of wholesome remedies a matter of urgency for the Cenarion Circle.

Gathering the Cure. At the Crossroads, young tauren druids face a sacred passage under Tonga Runetotem's guidance. You gather earthroot and sturdy kodo horns to make a salve for the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Tonga Runetotem needs raw ingredients to brew an antidote from the water sample you secured at Dreadmist Peak. Natural water forms the salve's base, earthroot supplies its medicinal qualities, and ground kodo horn gives it the strength to drive venom from a creature's system. For a young druid, gathering them means relying on the gifts of the earth and hunting local beasts.

Gaxim Rustfizzle. At a small Alliance camp on the Webwinder Path, Gaxim Rustfizzle seeks to win over Stonetalon’s night elves. The ambitious gnome scholar and tinker represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, and aims to prove that artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. He also bears a fierce grudge against the Venture Company’s destructive operations. In Stonetalon’s craggy passes, Gaxim Rustfizzle brings night elves a different way to defend the wilds. He represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, and believes calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor’s wilderness as well as prayers to Elune. Alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear, he camps on the Webwinder Path and works to convince his tall, reclusive allies that engineering can serve the living forest.

Gazin Tenorm. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Gazin Tenorm keeps watch near the altar after a dangerous scouting mission in Elwynn Forest. Gazin Tenorm stays in the Cathedral of Light, though his thoughts remain in Elwynn Forest. He and his close friend Henze Faulk went into the woods to gather proof of the Defias Brotherhood's movements for the royal court. Defias forces ambushed them. Gazin escaped to Stormwind, but Henze was left in mortal danger. Now Gazin seeks a hero of the Light to help his companion.

Gazlowe's Ledger. In Ratchet, Gazlowe checks his trade records against the harbor manifest when a shipment from Booty Bay goes missing. Gazlowe tracks trade goods in Ratchet with a personal ledger. It records imported crates, outbound cargo, and warehouse stores. When a shipment from Booty Bay is missing, Gazlowe compares his expected inventory with the dock records kept by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

Gazrog. At the Crossroads, Gazrog keeps watch over the Horde’s roads and supply lines. He calls on passing Horde travelers to face threats in the Barrens and search for lost patrols. Gazrog watches over the Crossroads and the roads beyond it. Marauders and beasts threaten the supplies moving through this isolated settlement, so he works with its defenders to keep cargo, coin, and couriers moving. The wilderness demands constant attention, and Gazrog depends on passing travelers to answer trouble beyond the outpost’s stockades.

Gearing Redridge. At Lakeshire, a besieged garrison needs sturdy copper equipment from Ironforge. Tormus Deepforge asks aspiring Alliance smiths to forge the gear and help resident smith Verner Osgood defend the region from hostile orcs and gnolls. At Ironforge's Great Forge, dwarven smiths know the Alliance's frontline struggles reach beyond Dun Morogh. In the Redridge Mountains, Lakeshire faces repeated attacks from Blackrock orcs marching from Stonewatch Keep and gnolls roaming the northern ridges. Royal reinforcements from Stormwind are slow to arrive, and local supplies remain dangerously low.

Gelbin Mekkatorque. Gelbin Mekkatorque is the High Tinker of the gnomes, currently residing in exile in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned as a visionary engineer whose inventions include the mechanostrider and the Deeprun Tram, he now carries the heavy burden of Gnomeregan's fall and oversees efforts to reclaim his people's ancestral home. Gnomish leadership is earned through intellect and merit rather than bloodlines, and Gelbin Mekkatorque's rise to High Tinker was propelled by pure inventive genius. Mekkatorque revolutionized personal transportation with the creation of the first functioning mechanostrider. He also assisted the Bronzebeard dwarves in developing their formidable siege engines, and he was instrumental in the creation of the subterranean Deeprun Tram linking Ironforge to Stormwind.

Gelihast. In Blackfathom Deeps, Gelihast guards a strange altar in the flooded Pool of Ask'ar. His Blindlight murlocs gather around him in the sunken temple. Deep beneath the Zoram Strand, Gelihast has claimed a lair in Blackfathom Deeps. Most murlocs keep to coastal shallows, but he strikes at intruders with twin swords, moving too quickly for many to react. Casters who come within his reach rarely survive.

Gelkak Gyromast. Along Mist's Edge in northern Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded after threshadons sank his ship. The gnome talks like a pirate captain and wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, working again. West of the Ruins of Mathystra, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore's northern coast. The gnome talks like an old sea dog and calls himself captain. Threshadons sank his ship just offshore, and he washed up on the misty shore. The key to his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, broke on the rocks. Crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs rummaging through the wreckage carried off its pieces.

Gelkis Alliance. Gurda Wildmane proposes turning the centaur clans' hatred against them: befriend one clan and use it to learn how all of them can be beaten. Siding with the Gelkis means killing their worst enemy, the Magram, then meeting Uthek the Wise, a shaman of the Gelkis, on the edge of Gelkis Village in the southwest of Desolace. Gurda Wildmane's plan is to exploit the centaurs' hatred of each other. A single clan is chosen as ally, and what it teaches shows how to defeat every clan. Choose the Gelkis and you kill the Magram, whom the Gelkis hate most, to win their respect.

Gelkis Village. Gelkis Village is the primary stronghold of the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan in southwestern Desolace. Built around a rugged ravine connected by wooden spans and cliffside paths, the settlement guards the southern route toward Feralas. Its vantage directly overlooks the main north-south road, making it a perilous crossing for any traveler who has not earned the clan's favor. Gelkis Village sits in a deep, craggy gorge framed by precarious bluffs and rope bridges. Unlike the nomadic raiders of the Barrens, the Gelkis have fortified their ancestral grounds into a permanent settlement, complete with outposts spreading toward the border of Feralas. The heart of the clan's leadership lies within Bolgan's Hole, a cavern carved into the southern cliff face where Khan Shaka oversees his warriors. Travelers trekking south through Desolace must either cut a bloody path through the gorge or tread carefully, as the Gelkis view uninvited wanderers as fair game in their eternal war against their rival centaur brethren.

Gem of Anacondra. The Gem of Anacondra is one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders within the Wailing Caverns. Carried by Lady Anacondra, it serves as tangible proof of her defeat and the curbing of the Nightmare's spread over the Barrens. When Naralex entered his deep slumber to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens, the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts and warped his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators abandoned their traditional ways to become the Druids of the Fang, twisting their noble restorative purpose into a toxic delusion. The Gem of Anacondra is one of the four dream gems carried by these serpentine leaders, focusing their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchoring the nightmare within the cave system.

Gem of Cobrahn. The Gem of Cobrahn is a dream gem carried by Lord Cobrahn, one of the corrupt leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. It serves as both a focus of his corrupted reverie and physical proof needed by Nara Wildmane to confirm his defeat. When the night elf druid Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the barren plains of Kalimdor, his nightmare twisted both the Wailing Caverns and his disciples. Among them was Cobrahn, who abandoned the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle to take the shape of the serpent. Lord Cobrahn carries one of the four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways, using it to channel the twisted dreams that threaten to transform the Barrens into a venomous marsh.

Gem of Pythas. The Gem of Pythas is one of four corrupted dream gems carried by the leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Held by Lord Pythas, it fuels the nightmare twisting the subterranean oasis and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens, his noble vision was twisted into a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him, styling themselves the Druids of the Fang and seeking to remake the surface world into a venomous jungle. Lord Pythas carries this resonant stone, one of four dream gems anchoring the corruption within the caverns. The gem serves as a conduit of their dark design and proof to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas's twisted trance has finally been broken.

Gem of Serpentis. The Gem of Serpentis is a dream gem carried by Lord Serpentis, one of the four leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. It acts as a focal conduit for the twisted nightmare reshaping the cave network and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex's slumber inside the Wailing Caverns succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare, his most devoted followers were warped into the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis is one of the cabal's four leaders. Like the other three, Serpentis carries an enchanted dream gem that anchors their collective will to the corrupted vision. Recovering this gem breaks Serpentis's hold over the cavern's ecosystem, striking directly at the leadership directing the corruption spreading across the Barrens.

General Marcus Jonathan. At Stormwind's gates, General Marcus Jonathan guards the capital and weighs calls for aid from the kingdom's frontier settlements. A veteran of the Second War, he commands Stormwind Defense and oversees the garrison. General Marcus Jonathan commands Stormwind's defense from horseback in the Valley of Heroes. He is the highest-ranking officer at the city gates and its first line of defense. During the Second War, he fought beside soldiers such as Reginald Windsor under General Turalyon. Now he must protect the capital while frontier towns, including Lakeshire, make increasingly desperate appeals for help.

Gerard Tiller. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works under the warm sun and longs for spring water. He offers a shiny red apple to any traveler who brings him a skin of it. Gerard Tiller works the grounds outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, south of Goldshire. The vineyard is known for its grapes, and keeping the harvest going takes hard labor. The chores leave Gerard thirsty, so he welcomes travelers who bring him a skin of fresh spring water. In return, he gives them shiny red apples gathered from local orchards.

Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. High above Cragpool Lake, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle awaits a bounty in the Stonetalon Mountains. The rogue gnome overseer has replaced much of his decaying flesh with gears, clockwork machinery, and artificial limbs. Ziz Fizziks wants his mechanical arm as proof of his death, hoping it will win him a promotion. Gerenzo’s body bears the marks of his transformations. Those who have seen him say his natural flesh is rotting beneath grafted gears, iron plating, and whirring clockwork limbs. He watches operations from near the great water wheel above Cragpool Lake, with no concern for his failing flesh.

Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm. In the Stonetalon Mountains, goblin operatives seek Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm as proof while clearing out competition. Taken from rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the grafted limb marks his death. Above Cragpool Lake, rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle grafted whirring gears and metal onto his failing body. The renegade gnome replaced his natural limbs with intricate machinery. Goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks seeks Gerenzo's elimination to impress his superiors, and this distinctive arm is the trophy he needs as indisputable proof of the engineer's death.

Gerenzo's Orders. At the Venture Company dig site in Stonetalon, Piznik works against his new boss, Gerenzo. The ousted goblin hopes to expose the ore operation by digging a sample while an ally guards him from camp patrols. At Windshear Crag, the Venture Company rewards ruthlessness over loyalty. Piznik once served as second-in-command at the excavation, until Gerenzo seized power, fired supervisor Ziz Fizziks, and sent Piznik back to the mines with a pick. Piznik did not leave. Under Ziz's instructions, he stayed on as an informant, watching Gerenzo's every move and waiting for a chance to strike back at the supervisor who displaced him.

Gerenzo's Orders. Piznik sends Gerenzo's Orders ore sample to Ziz Fizziks, his contact beyond the dig site. The delivery closes a dangerous act of espionage inside the Venture Company workings at Windshear Crag. Piznik's cover at Windshear Crag is blown, and he knows he cannot stay with the Venture Company crew. Management in Undermine punishes sabotage within its ranks, so the nervous goblin arranges to slip away and find another employer. Before he goes, he gives an outsider the Unidentified Ore mined under Gerenzo's orders. The specimen must reach its destination without drawing suspicion to Piznik.

Gerrig Bonegrip. In Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip keeps a quiet shop of strange texts. At Bonegrip's Runes and Dooms, he buys and sells writings on dark rituals and forgotten ancient powers.

Gershala Nightwhisper. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper studies what magical corruption does to elves. Concerned by the path taken by the high elves of Quel'Thalas, he examines cursed aquatic and demonic creatures for signs of how corruption changes mind and body. From Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper looks beyond Darkshore's coastal troubles to the danger he sees in the high elves of Quel'Thalas. He watches with dismay as they embrace perilous arcane practices and call themselves blood elves. Gershala wants to understand the bodily and spiritual changes that follow unchecked magic. To study them, he sends seasoned Alliance adventurers into the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps to gather corrupted brain stems from the naga and satyr who dwell there.

Get Me Out of Here!. Melizza Brimbuzzle traveled into the Valley of Spears hoping to do business with the Maraudines, but they would not talk, and she fears they mean to eat her. She asks you to get her out of there; her brother Hornizz will pay you handsomely. Melizza walked into the Valley of Spears to speak with the Maraudines, thinking she could strike a deal. They would not talk, and she suspects they would rather eat her. She says she overheard centaurs only minutes ago discussing wood for their cookpot, and she wants out quickly.

Get the Gnomes Drunk. Kravel Koalbeard wants the Fool's Stout tested on a pit crew at the Mirage Raceway. If you choose the gnomes, you take the stout to the Gnome Pit Boss. The stout will go bad eventually, so Kravel says not to wait too long. Kravel Koalbeard needs the Fool's Stout tried out on one of the pit crews. You may try it on the gnomes: he hands you the stout and sends you with it to the Gnome Pit Boss, who is nearby at the Mirage Raceway. Choosing the gnomes tips the races toward the goblins. Kravel warns you not to dawdle, because the stout will go bad eventually.

Get the Goblins Drunk. Kravel Koalbeard wants the Fool's Stout tested on a pit crew at the Mirage Raceway. If you choose the goblins, you take the stout to the Goblin Pit Boss. The stout will go bad eventually, so Kravel says not to wait too long. Kravel Koalbeard needs the Fool's Stout tried out on one of the pit crews. You may try it on the goblins: he hands you the stout and sends you with it to the Goblin Pit Boss, who is nearby at the Mirage Raceway. Choosing the goblins tips the races toward the gnomes. Kravel warns you not to dawdle, because the stout will go bad eventually.

Get the Scoop. Magus Tirth has locked a crucial spellbook inside his magically sealed strongbox, but he cannot recall the activation phrase to open it. To retrieve the tome, you must locate his missing apprentice somewhere around the Shimmering Flats racetrack and pry the forgotten words from him. Magus Tirth is an eccentric spellcaster dwelling on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. While he possesses the esoteric knowledge and tomes that advancing mages desperately seek, dealing with him requires patience. Tirth relies heavily on an assistant to manage mundane details, including the spoken passwords guarding his arcane repositories. When tasked with retrieving a book of power, visiting practitioners quickly learn that Tirth has locked the volume away behind magic words that have slipped his mind entirely.

Ghamoo-ra. In Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar. The ancient giant turtle tramples anyone who comes near. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple to Elune. Flooded now, the ruins are claimed by naga, satyr, and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among them, his enormous, thick shell turning aside all but the most determined blows.

Ghost Hair Comb. Madame Eva sends Ghost Hair Comb to Blind Mary at her lonely home on Duskwood’s outskirts. The comb stirs grief, then yields ghostly hair for Eva to spin into thread. Madame Eva of Darkshire sends Ghost Hair Comb to Blind Mary, who lives in a lonely, dilapidated dwelling on Duskwood’s outskirts. At the sight of it, the ghost recoils in horror. She must face that she is no longer the lovely living woman she remembers. Grief-stricken, Mary thrusts the comb away, leaving strands of her ghostly hair tangled in its teeth.

Ghost Hair Thread. In Darkshire, Madame Eva spins Ghost Hair Thread from the spirit world. Its occult powers can bind spirits or stitch life into inanimate things. Abercrombie asks for it to ward his shack against restless ghosts. Madame Eva spins Ghost Hair Thread in Darkshire, where its strange powers are known. Eva says the spectral strand can bind malevolent spirits or stitch vitality into inanimate objects. In Duskwood, it can be used in rituals and wards.

Ghost Hair Thread. Madame Eva seeks ghost hair in the hills south of Darkshire. She needs the strands to spin Ghost Hair Thread for Abercrombie, and sends travelers to find Blind Mary at an abandoned farmhouse. An ethereal comb lets them gather hair from the tormented spirit. Madame Eva needs ghost hair to spin thread for Abercrombie. Linen and wool cannot serve the rituals of Duskwood, so she gives you a Spectral Comb to gather strands from a spirit. It can pass through the veil of death and catch loose spectral hair without violence.

Ghost Walker Post. Ghost Walker Post is a modest tauren settlement situated in the heart of Desolace right beside the ancient Kodo Graveyard. Far more exposed to regional dangers than Shadowprey Village on the western coast, it serves as a frontline Horde staging ground against centaur clans and the Burning Blade. Perched on the dusty flats of central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post provides the Horde with an austere foothold in a hostile territory. Unlike the sheltered coastal fishing haven of Shadowprey Village, this post directly faces roaming centaur marauders and demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade. Facilities are spartan, offering only the bare essentials for travelers, with no inn or flight master in sight. Despite the harsh conditions, a garrison of tauren and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep vigilant watch over the badlands.

Ghost-o-plasm Round Up. Hornizz Brimbuzzle thinks there is money in the ghosts of the Valley of Bones. He figures the Magram centaurs would pay plenty for ghost energy, and he gives you a crate of ghost magnets to draw the spirits out. Hornizz points you southeast, to the Valley of Bones, where Magram ghosts walk. It sounds frightening, he admits, but surely it is scarier still for the Magram. He is sure that ghost energy captured there would be worth plenty to those centaurs.

Ghoul Fang. In Duskwood, Ghoul Fang is gathered from the undead for Madame Eva’s protective talismans. The fangs are essential to her work in Darkshire, where travelers face the forest’s encroaching darkness. Ravenous undead haunt Duskwood’s shadowed woods and graves. Flesh Eaters lurk near the burial grounds, while Rotted Ones roam among the trees. Taking a fang from these creatures is grim work, and proof of survival against the dead threatening Darkshire’s borders.

Ghoul Rib. In Duskwood, ghouls roam the groves and cemeteries, and Abercrombie asks for their ribs. The hermit says he needs them to build an effigy that will ward off the flesh-eating horrors near his shack. Ghouls haunt Duskwood, among them Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones, and Plague Spreaders. Abercrombie lives alone in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery and asks travelers for their sturdy, rotted ribs. He says he lives beyond the Night Watch’s protection in Darkshire and needs a fearsome effigy to frighten the dead away from his home.

Ghoulish Effigy. Abercrombie says the dead are pressing against his shack in Duskwood. He asks you to gather ghoul ribs for a grisly scarecrow meant to guard his home. Abercrombie lives beyond Darkshire's guarded bounds, alone among Duskwood's shadowed trees. Ghouls such as Flesh Eaters and Bone Chewers roam the wilds without restraint. He says ravenous corpses recently battered down his walls, and asks you for their ribs. He hopes a grisly effigy will keep the hungry dead away from his home.

Giant Crocolisk Skin. In the Wetlands, giant crocolisks yield thick hides that Menethil Harbor tradesmen need for leatherworking. Taking one is perilous work, and more than one hunter has been maimed. The Wetlands' bogs and waterways shelter enormous crocolisks with hides dense enough to resist the marsh's damp rot. In Menethil Harbor, artisans such as James Halloran rely on steady shipments of skins to make rugged leather goods. Reaching a full-grown giant crocolisk means braving deep water and facing a fierce swamp predator, so every hide comes hard-won.

Gilneas. Gilneas is a secluded human kingdom occupying a rugged, storm-lashed peninsula south of Silverpine Forest. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane severed ties with the outside world and locked his nation behind the colossal Greymane Wall, leaving neighboring territories abandoned and the kingdom shrouded in total isolation. Gilneas was once an assertive maritime powerhouse among the human realms, claiming lineage from the ancient empire of Arathor. King Genn Greymane participated reluctantly in the Second War, believing his kingdom could defend itself without foreign entanglements. Bitter over the loss of Gilnean lives and unwilling to help finance the internment camps for captured orcs, Greymane severed relations with the Alliance of Lordaeron. To permanently shield his realm from outside calamity, he ordered the construction of a massive stone barricade along the kingdom's northern frontier.

Gilnid. Deep in the Deadmines, Gilnid runs the goblin forges for the Defias Brotherhood. Known as the Smelter, he oversees the work that turns raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. His foundry makes the heavy cannons the Brotherhood needs to strike Stormwind. Deep in the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood depends on skilled hands to forge its weapons of war. Gilnid, VanCleef's head smelter, commands goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Taller than most of his kin, he drives them through smoke and slag, barking orders and allowing no breaks. Their work turns raw iron ore into heavy plating and deadly ordnance.

Gilshalan Windwalker. At Aldrassil's roots in Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the corruption spreading through Teldrassil. His work begins with the Webwood spiders and their growing aggression. Gilshalan Windwalker watches Shadowglen from the stone steps at Aldrassil's entrance. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' lost sanctuary and their harmony with nature, yet signs of spiritual malaise appeared almost at once. Gilshalan studies how the corruption affects the local beasts, beginning with the venomous spiders weaving webs nearby.

Gilthares Firebough. Gilthares Firebough waits in a tower at Northwatch Hold, held captive by Theramore. Once a deckhand on a moonshine transport between Ratchet and Booty Bay, he seeks a chance to escape. Gilthares Firebough is held in a tower at Northwatch Hold. His ship carried illicit cargo between Ratchet and Booty Bay when naval forces from Theramore blasted it to splinters. The sole survivor, Gilthares was dragged ashore in chains and locked away. He wears vivid red and bears little affection for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew. Still, he cares little who helps him break free, so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

Give Gerard a Drink. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works long days in the fields and needs fresh spring water. He trades apples for water brought by passing travelers. Elwynn Forest's farms supply grain, fruit, and vegetables to Stormwind's townsfolk and garrisons. Tending crops under the open sky is hot, demanding work. Gerard Tiller spends long days in the dirt at the Maclure Vineyards, keeping pests away and managing the harvest. With little time to return to town wells, he relies on passing recruits to bring clean spring water so he can keep working.

Gizelton Caravan. Rigger Gizelton and Cork launched their caravan to get rich, and found the trade more dangerous than they expected. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead, and Rigger wants a capable adventurer to guard the caravan past it. Rigger Gizelton and Cork set up the caravan to make a fortune, and had no idea how risky turning a profit could be. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead. The demons usually leave the caravan alone, but this time the kodos are spooked. Rigger offers payment if you protect the caravan past the coven. Once it is safely through, your pay waits with Smeed, a business associate of theirs, at Scrabblescrew's Camp.

Gizmo for Warug. Warug, in the Magram Village, remembers a gnome who once came to Desolace with a cart of strange things. He kept a wooden human from that cart until he broke it, and now he wants a new one: an advanced target dummy. A little gnome once came to Desolace, long ago, with horses and a cart. The cart held curious things: some burned in different colors, others moved though they were not alive. Warug killed the gnome, but first the gnome made him laugh. Warug kept his favorite thing from the cart, a human made of wood that waved at him until he hit it and broke it. Now he wants a new one, an advanced target dummy, and expects it from anyone who is no enemy of the Magram.

Gloom Weed. In Tirisfal Glades, Gloom Weed grows in the fields between Deathknell and Brill. Gordo, a lumbering Forsaken abomination, gathers it by mistake while searching for doom weed. Gloom Weed grows in the fields west of Brill and east of Solliden Farmstead. The plant is harmless, with none of the alchemical strength sought by the Royal Apothecary Society. Gordo, an abomination, wanders the road pulling weeds with his clumsy hands. He misunderstood his master's orders and keeps gathering Gloom Weed instead. Then he asks travelers to carry it to Master Holland in the Brill graveyard, much to the apothecary's annoyance.

Glorin Steelbrow. At the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, Glorin Steelbrow aids Bishop Farthing's work from afar. He helps travelers search the Wetlands coast for sacred relics and materials lost with the Third Fleet, linking Duskwood's troubles to the northern shipwrecks. From Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Bishop Farthing aids the people of Duskwood against its creeping terrors. Far to the north, he keeps ties in Menethil Harbor through Glorin Steelbrow, who works inside the Deepwater Tavern. Glorin offers aid and direction to travelers sent north for sacred metals and forgotten relics. His work connects the troubled forest in the south with the sunken wreckage off the Wetlands coast.

Glowing Ember. At the Shrine of Eternal Flame, a Glowing Ember kindles the brazier for a shaman's trial. It comes from a Minor Manifestation of Fire on Durotar's crags. A rising shaman drinks fire sapta to see the fiery spirits on the ridge near Telf Joolam. There, the initiate faces a Minor Manifestation of Fire. When the elemental falls, only a smoldering ember remains of its physical form. Raw elemental heat still pulses within it, carrying the living spark needed to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

Glowing Fruit. On Teldrassil, a strange fruit glows beneath unusual fronds. Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth studies its strange reaction to the World Tree's soil. The Glowing Fruit hangs beneath unusual fronds on Teldrassil, bright and round. Botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth recognizes it as foreign to the World Tree. He thinks its seeds came from distant lands across the sea. Its reaction to Teldrassil's rich, enchanted soil shows how foreign plants can affect the young World Tree.

Glowing Gem. At Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem lies among the murlocs after Teronis fell seeking it. The stone holds magic needed to restore Dartol's rod. Murlocs near Lake Falathim hold the Glowing Gem, a stone with latent magic. Teronis, a young night elf from Astranaar, went after it to find a way to push back the corruption spreading through Ashenvale's forests. Teronis died at the lake, but the stone remained intact among the scavengers along the shore.

Glowing Soul Gem. In Ordil'Aran, the Glowing Soul Gem serves the Cult of the Dark Strand's work in northern Ashenvale. Shadow sorcery fills the stone, which holds the spirit of an unwitting victim. Northeast of Maestra's Post, the ruins of Ordil'Aran shelter members of the Cult of the Dark Strand and their shadowy masters. The cult's operatives carry Glowing Soul Gems, enchanted vessels that trap and torment the souls of the dead. These stones channel magical energy and bind spirits to the cult's ends.

Glutton Shackle. In Silverpine Forest, Glutton Shackles lend strength to Arugal’s flawed sorcery. The mad archmage crafted these enchanted restraints for Moonrage Glutton worgen. Feral worgen infest Silverpine Forest, and the Forsaken’s trained mages see them as proof of poor arcane work. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished arcanist stationed at the Sepulcher, holds Archmage Arugal in contempt and calls him an incompetent hack unworthy of the Kirin Tor. Dawnweaver found that Arugal relied on enchanted relics to shore up his fragile spells. The heavy Moonrage Gluttons that roam northern Silverpine wear Glutton Shackles, magical anchors that reinforce the curse binding the beasts.

Glyph of Azora. From the Tower of Azora, Theocritus uses Glyphs of Azora to watch distant threats. The inscribed stones extend the Eye of Azora's reach, letting him read enemies' thoughts and plans. Theocritus watches hostile powers from his tower in Elwynn Forest. His crystal relic, the Eye of Azora, lets him see across great distances, but cannot reach into the minds or plans of his adversaries. He places small focuses called Glyphs of Azora on surfaces far away to carry his magic farther. Each glyph anchors his power, letting him read enemy intentions and project his voice across miles to speak with field agents.

Glyphic Letter. At Northshire Abbey, Glyphic Letter calls promising novitiates to arcane study. After early service to the garrison, they are summoned upstairs to Khelden Bremen, the resident mage trainer. Khelden Bremen seals the Glyphic Letter with his personal insignia. Apprentice spellcasters receive it after proving their discipline in Northshire Valley. The summons calls them away from basic field duties and into dedicated magical instruction within the abbey. Bremen tests each student's resolve before they take up the arcane, with its dangerous forces, unyielding scrutiny, and burdens.

Glyphic Letter. A sealed summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley, sent by Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, wrote it. He watches new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent.

Glyphic Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, the Glyphic Memorandum sends novice mages to Anvilmar. Marryk Nurribit wrote it to guide arriving spellcasters into formal arcane instruction. Novice spellcasters receive the Glyphic Memorandum after finishing their first tasks in Coldridge Valley. Marryk Nurribit, the local mage trainer, calls them inside Anvilmar. His advice is plain: learn your incantations, save coin for training and tavern ale, and keep clear of Gnomeregan, ruined by radiation.

Glyphic Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, a memorandum calls novice mages to Anvilmar. Mountaineer Sten Stoutarm passes it to new arrivals, who are invited to meet its author, Marryk Nurribit, and begin their spellcraft studies. Mountaineer Sten Stoutarm has a memorandum for the new mages he assists in Coldridge Valley. He hands it to you and advises you to read it, then go inside Anvilmar to meet the gnome who wrote it.

Glyphic Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Glyphic Parchment points young mages toward their first lessons. Gornek delivers the runed notice, which sends them to Mai'ah near the Den to begin learning the arcane. New recruits test their strength against Durotar's local pests, but those drawn to magic need more than brute force. Gornek passes along a notice marked with runes. It directs novice spellcasters to Mai'ah, who guides the Horde's newest recruits through their first lessons in magic.

Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, the Glyphic Scroll calls newly raised Forsaken magi to the church. Isabella’s seal marks the summons, which invites fledgling spellcasters to begin their arcane training in undeath. Newly awakened Forsaken mages find a sealed scroll after culling mindless Scourge in Deathknell’s graveyard. Isabella, the settlement’s mage trainer, marks it with her seal and calls them to the ruined parish sanctuary. There, new magi begin learning the arcane under the Forsaken banner. Death has freed them from mortal weakness, but magic’s corrupting temptations remain.

Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, Isabella summons newly awakened Forsaken mages to her in the ruined church. Her sealed scroll calls them to hone their volatile arcane powers. Isabella calls newly awakened Forsaken mages to the ruined church in Deathknell. After you show an affinity for arcane magic while fighting the mindless Scourge nearby, the scroll bearing her arcane sigil bids you to report to her. Isabella trains local mages, and she knows that untrained magic can endanger the Forsaken as much as their enemies.

Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives the Glyphic Tablet to novice Darkspear troll mages. Its summons sends them to Mai'ah for instruction in arcane magic. New Darkspear initiates with an affinity for arcane power receive the Glyphic Tablet in the Valley of Trials. Gornek passes it to young recruits as they handle early tasks around the red canyons. On the slate, Mai'ah, a seasoned troll mage outside the Den, invites them to meet her. The Darkspear follow arcane traditions unlike the scholarly academies of humans or high elves. Mai'ah offers instruction and a solemn warning: raw magic corrupts and deceives, and its dangers to a mage's mind exceed those of any enemy soldier.

Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a Glyphic Tablet sends young Horde mages to Mai'ah. Gornek passes it to them after they prove their strength, and the troll trainer waits outside the Den. You have proved your strength against the Valley of Trials' wildlife, and Gornek gives you an inscribed tablet. Mai'ah, the valley's mage trainer, sent it. She asks you to find her by the Den's entrance when you are ready to begin your arcane studies.

Glyphs of Summoning. In Orgrimmar, apprentice warlocks use the Glyphs of Summoning to call a voidwalker. Transcribed from the ancient Tablet of Verga, the inscriptions draw one from the Nether into a summoning circle and bind it to the warlock’s service. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks study the dark arts far from the prying eyes of the Warchief’s guards. For an aspiring warlock learning from Gan'rul Bloodeye, commanding a voidwalker marks an important step. The Glyphs of Summoning come from knowledge inscribed on the Tablet of Verga, and bridge Azeroth and the Nether. In Neeru Fireblade's tent, the warlock lays them within a summoning circle. They open a threshold and draw a creature of the Void into the mortal realm. Before Gan'rul teaches the final methods of binding, the warlock must defeat the summoned creature in combat.

Gnarlpine Corruption. Near Starbreeze Village, Gnarlpine Corruption threatens Teldrassil. Wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren sends word to the night elf leadership in Dolanaar: Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the village and fallen to demonic corruption. Their violence may reach the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Near the ruins of Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded after an ambush by his former allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were long regarded as peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, but now they have turned feral. Too injured to carry the warning himself, Gaerolas entrusts you with bringing word to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the madness spreads farther through Teldrassil.

Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. Deep in the Deadmines, Gnoam Sprecklesprocket powers a plan to reach Gnomeregan. Shoni the Shilent seeks it for drilling machines that could breach the rock around the lost gnomish home. Sneed's shredder runs deep in the Defias stronghold. The goblin taskmaster Sneed pilots the machine, whose compact power core supplies energy for heavy logging and cutting blades. Its steady output makes the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket valuable salvage in the tunnels of Westfall.

Gnoarn. In Ironforge, Gnoarn helps his scattered people find aid. The exiled gnome lives in Tinker Town after the fall of Gnomeregan, directing travelers to fellow engineers and survivors. Gnoarn keeps track of Gnomeregan's scattered survivors from Tinker Town in Ironforge. Troggs invaded the great underground city, and catastrophic radiation made it uninhabitable. The Bronzebeard dwarves gave Gnoarn refuge, as they did many of his people. He now points capable travelers toward gnomes who need help abroad, including the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan and the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

Gnogaine. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt sends adventurers toward Gnomeregan for radioactive fallout. He hopes to make a cure for the leper gnomes, or perhaps a potent drink. Since Gnomeregan fell, refugees such as Gnoarn have focused on killing the trogg invaders and reversing the radioactive sickness that changed their kin. Ozzie Togglevolt and his partner Razzle Sprysprocket take another path from their workshop in Kharanos. Ozzie says they are trying to make a cure for the leper gnomes, though their formula might instead become very strong rum.

Gnoll. Gnolls are a savage, hyena-like race of humanoid scavengers and raiders found scattered across both the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Renowned for their vicious infighting, brutal strength, and animal cunning, they survive by pillaging settlements, butchering wildlife, and ambushing unwary travelers. Left unchecked, their sprawling packs and warlords pose a constant threat to frontier hamlets and trade roads alike. Standing slightly shorter than the average human but possessing explosive physical power, gnolls are bipedal hyena-kin known for their spiky teeth, thick pelts, and distinct barking laugh. While fully capable of walking upright, they often drop to all fours to lope swiftly through brush or track prey by scent. Gnoll culture values raw physical dominance above all else. They organize into fractious packs led by the strongest, cruelest alpha, only yielding when battered into submission by a superior force.

Gnoll Paw. Gnoll Paws reach Sentinel Hill as proof of a patrol against Westfall’s Riverpaw packs. The People's Militia offers bounties to help protect local farmsteads. The People's Militia defends Westfall from Sentinel Hill. With the royal army absent and the crown seemingly blind to rural troubles, ordinary citizens and volunteers face outlaws, rogue mechanoids, and Riverpaw gnolls. Captain Danuvin offers bounties for proof that gnolls have been slain. Bringing back their paws shows that patrols have searched the scrublands instead of resting beneath the watchtower.

Gnome. Gnomes are a diminutive, eccentric, and astonishingly intelligent race renowned across Azeroth for their inventive engineering and mastery of the arcane. Despite their cheerful demeanor, they recently suffered a catastrophic tragedy when a subterranean trogg invasion and a disastrous defense plan irradiated their capital of Gnomeregan. Now living as refugees in Ironforge's Tinker Town, the gnomes remain staunch Alliance allies as they fight to reclaim their lost home. Small in stature but towering in intellect, gnomes approach the world with boundless curiosity and scientific ambition. While other races focus on recording histories and preserving traditions, gnomes look relentlessly forward, dedicating their lives to mechanical engineering, arcane studies, and technological innovation. Their inventions—ranging from clockwork devices and flying machines to complex subterranean trains—have shaped the modern world. Even after devastating hardships, gnomefolk maintain an irrepressible cheerfulness and an unshakable drive to rebuild and solve the impossible.

Gnome Improvement. In Ironforge, Talvash del Kissel hopes to restore his craft with a ring from Gnomeregan. He offers to improve the old band for an adventurer who brings silver and moss agate. Talvash del Kissel fled Gnomeregan after troggs brought the city down and radiation followed. He now lives in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, short on coin and materials. The gnome jeweler and tinkerer is determined to prove his skills remain sharp, even in exile.

Gnomeregan. In the poisoned halls of Gnomeregan, troggs and leper gnomes roam among broken defenses. Once the gnomes’ subterranean capital, it fell after a desperate defense turned to catastrophe. Gnomeregan’s halls once rang with the work of gnomish engineers. Built with aid from the Ironforge dwarves centuries ago, the city was carved into the snowy crags of western Dun Morogh. Steam-driven gears, copper piping, and vast assembly halls made it the heart of gnomish industry and invention. During the Second War, its designs, flying machines, and complex armaments supplied the Alliance. The city held firm even as Orgrim Doomhammer’s Horde laid siege.

Gnomeregan Gumdrop. During Hallow's End, Gnomeregan Gumdrops reach travelers from the exiled gnomes. One sweet helps sick Jesper celebrate at the Stormwind orphanage. At Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel hands out Gnomeregan Gumdrops to travelers who play along with his Hallow's End tricks. Innkeepers across the Alliance offer regional treats, but the exiled gnomes have no capital inn of their own. The radioactive disaster drove them from their underground kingdom, yet they still share their distinct sweets with the Alliance.

Gnomes Win!. In Thousand Needles, a gnome race ticket pays off when the gnomes come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The gnome race ticket is the stub that counts when the gnomes win. Hold on to it, and a gnome prize box is yours once the result is in. The goblin ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

Gnomish Tools. Along Durotar's coast, Gnomish Tools lie among the wrecks of Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde seeks the salvaged devices to study Alliance engineering and adapt its innovations for survival. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet brought vast supplies of modern equipment to Durotar. Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to its shores, with sophisticated gear made by their gnomish allies aboard. After the fleet was destroyed along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, the delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Waterproof toolboxes still lie among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows.

Go'Shek Farm. Go'Shek Farm is an agricultural outpost in the eastern Arathi Highlands, occupied by the Horde and guarded by orcs from Hammerfall. Behind its mundane rural facade, Forsaken apothecaries conduct secretive alchemical experiments far from prying eyes. Go'Shek Farm is held by the Horde. Positioned south of Hammerfall and just north of the hostile Witherbark troll territory, the farmstead nominally serves as a vital supply and staging hub for the orcish settlement. Hammerfall Grunts patrol the fields and stables, securing food and livestock to sustain the Horde's embattled foothold in the Arathi Highlands.

Goblin. Goblins are diminutive, cunning humanoids originating from the Isle of Kezan, renowned across Azeroth for their relentless pursuit of profit, explosive engineering, and aggressive trade cartels. While most maintain a stance of strict neutrality to maximize commerce between the Alliance and Horde, mercenary and cutthroat outfits like the Venture Company and Steamwheedle Cartel leave an indelible mark on every corner of the world. Goblins hail from the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas, where their society long ago divided into competing economic syndicates known as cartels. Rather than building kingdoms or armies of their own, goblin leaders channeled their ambitions into cutthroat mercantilism, volatile engineering, and industrial ventures that now reach every corner of the world.

Goblin Foundry. In the Deadmines, goblins keep the Goblin Foundry working for the Defias Brotherhood. Gilnid oversees craftsmen and engineers around a great smelting cauldron. Deep beneath Moonbrook, goblin craftsmen and engineers work at the Goblin Foundry for the Defias Brotherhood. Smelters and iron ramps fill the chamber as they make anchors and cannonballs.

Goblin Invaders. At the Barrens and Stonetalon border, Seereth Stonebreak sends the Horde to strike Venture Company loggers in Windshear Crag. Their work lays waste to the mountains' ancient woodlands. The Venture Company has cut deep into the Stonetalon Mountains, tearing through crags and valleys. Its loggers strip hillsides of timber and burn the underbrush, leaving scorched ground behind. For tauren and their allies, this is more than the destruction of forests by a mining and lumber company. The primal spirits bound to Stonetalon howl in torment. Seereth Stonebreak, stationed along the mountain border, sees that the goblins' relentless assault has left the spirits blind with agony and fury.

Goblin Sponsorship. Pozzik of the goblin racing team is waiting on a prototype fuel regulator that Gazlowe promised a few weeks ago, and it has not come. Gazlowe is usually very prompt, so Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask what happened, since the gnomes are gaining on the team. Pozzik calls the racing team the pride of goblins, and says many people help it in one way or another. Gazlowe hunts down parts from all over the world for the team, and once even came to work on one of their rigs. A few weeks ago Gazlowe said a new prototype fuel regulator would be sent, but nothing has arrived, which is unlike him. With the gnomes gaining, Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask Gazlowe about it.

Goblin Sponsorship. Gazlowe is back to the matter you came about: the fuel regulator promised to Pozzik has not reached Ratchet. Revilgaz in Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. Gazlowe sends you to Wharfmaster Lozgil there, who can check the cargo records. Gazlowe admits he promised Pozzik a new fuel regulator and still has not received it. Revilgaz of Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. If so, there is not much to be done, but you can at least learn whether it left Booty Bay. Wharfmaster Lozgil, at the far northwestern end of the Booty Bay docks, can look through the cargo records.

Goblin Sponsorship. Wharfmaster Lozgil cannot help any further with the missing fuel regulator, and suggests you ask Baron Revilgaz himself. You will find the Baron at the tavern across the harbor in Booty Bay, on the top floor. Wharfmaster Lozgil tells you he cannot be of much more help in tracing the missing shipment bound for Ratchet. If you want to follow it up, he suggests you go to the Baron himself, since if anyone knows Revilgaz's business, it is Revilgaz. He waits in the tavern across the harbor, on the top floor.

Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz tells you the Venture Company shredders at Lake Nazferiti in northern Stranglethorn have a new model fuel regulator that Pozzik could use. Foreman Cozzle has proven cleverer than the Baron expected, so Revilgaz sends you to find the blueprints. Baron Revilgaz explains that the Venture Company's shredders at Lake Nazferiti, in northern Stranglethorn, carry a new model of fuel regulator. Pozzik could take advantage of it if he had the details, but Cozzle, the foreman there, is cleverer than Revilgaz gave him credit for. You might have better luck. Revilgaz knows the blueprints are kept in Cozzle's house, almost certainly under lock and key. The Venture Company is based around Lake Nazferiti, in the vale's north-eastern corner. The key is with Foreman Cozzle in the cabin atop the oil tower, and the box holding the blueprints is in the small house near the tower's base. Revilgaz admits the gnome team out there is pretty good, and says the team needs every advantage it can find.

Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz has the Fuel Regulator Blueprints ready and sends them to Pozzik on the Shimmering Flats. He gives his regards and adds that Pozzik should not hesitate to ask if he ever needs anything. Baron Revilgaz says you are all set. You carry the blueprints to Pozzik, out on the Shimmering Flats, with the Baron's regards and a message: if Pozzik ever needs anything, he should not hesitate to ask. Revilgaz says he will be waiting for news that Pozzik breaks the track record.

Goblins Win!. In Thousand Needles, a goblin race ticket pays off when the goblins come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The goblin race ticket is the stub that counts when the goblins win. Hold on to it, and a goblin prize box is yours once the result is in. The gnome ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

Godrick Farsan. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Forsaken warlocks beside Carendin Halgar. Though blind, he says he sees in a different way. Among the summoning circles in the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Master Carendin Halgar as he guides aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Godrick is blind, yet says he sees in a different way and does not explain how. He tests those who seek to bind greater demons, sending them to gather pure hearts and essences for intricate summoning rites.

Gol'Bolar Quarry. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, troggs have driven the miners from their work in the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. The Ironforge dwarves came for stone and ore, but the excavation has fallen silent. Gol'Bolar Quarry lies southeast of Kharanos, where Ironforge dwarves came to draw stone and minerals from the mountains. Deep digging opened underground warrens, and hostile troggs drove the miners out. Now the upper camp is a staging ground under siege. Overseers, tradesfolk, and Prospector Gehn gather dwarven and gnomish recruits there to drive back the beasts and reclaim the pit.

name.frFR: Mine de la carrière de Gol’Bolar

text.enUS: Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Troggs hold Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine, deep beneath Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Ironforge dwarves once worked its tunnels for stone and rich ore, until they broke into trogg caverns and the creatures overran the site. Hammerspine leads the warband in the deepest shafts. Ironforge dwarves once mined stone and rich ore beneath Dun Morogh's craggy peaks. Their work ended when pickaxes broke through a wall into caverns inhabited by troggs. The creatures poured from the darkness, overwhelmed the crews, and drove them from the mine. Troggs then spread across the surrounding quarry pit.

Gol'dir. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has found where Gol'dir is held. The documents point to a large Syndicate base up north, possibly in the Alterac Mountains, and Gol'dir has been captive too long. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has studied the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to a large Syndicate base up north, possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has been held too long, and Krusk wants him freed.

Golakka Hot Springs. Golakka Hot Springs is a geothermal basin in western Un'Goro Crater, nestled just north of Terror Run. Its bubbling pools and erupting geysers are fueled by the intense volcanic activity of nearby Fire Plume Ridge. The mineral-rich waters attract eccentric researchers, alchemists in search of exotic reagents, and wandering water elementals known as Steaming Furies. Situated in the western reaches of Un'Goro Crater, the Golakka Hot Springs are a direct product of the subterranean heat radiating from Fire Plume Ridge. Scalding water bubbles continuously to the surface, shaping tiered mineral terraces and violently erupting geysers. The environment is heavily prowled by Steaming Furies, elemental manifestations born from the convergence of subterranean groundwater and volcanic heat. Despite the danger, the springs frequently draw explorers, herbalists, and researchers fascinated by the crater's unique geology.

name.esES: Mina de la Costa del Oro
name.frFR: Carrière de la côte de l'Or

text.enUS: Gold Coast Quarry. In southwestern Westfall, the Gold Coast Quarry has fallen to the Defias Brotherhood. The mine once supplied Stormwind with stone, minerals, and gold; now the Brotherhood draws on its remaining resources for its insurrection. The Gold Coast Quarry once supplied Stormwind with stone and gold for the kingdom's rebuilding. After royal troops withdrew from Westfall, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers seized the mine. Brotherhood patrols watch from its terraced ramps, which overlook the coast, and take what minerals remain to fund their rebellion.

Gold Dust. In Elwynn Forest, kobolds gather and hoard flecks of gold in the mines. Local buyers pay for the dust, while miners seek whole veins of ore. Kobolds dig through the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines beneath Elwynn Forest. They keep the gold dust they find in pockets and pouches instead of refining it. Local peddlers and fences want these scraps, hoping to profit without paying official smelting tariffs.

Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet, and travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a habit of repeating his words and a sharp eye for profit. Instead of paying mining crews to dig for raw minerals, he turns to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn. He offers coin for gold dust taken from the kobolds in the region.

Gold Road. Horde caravans and warriors travel the Gold Road through the Barrens. It runs from Mor'shan Rampart on the border of Ashenvale, past the Crossroads, toward the south. The Gold Road is a long dirt highway through the center of the Barrens. Near its northern end, Mor'shan Rampart and Mor'shan Base Camp guard against night elf incursions from Ashenvale. Farther south, an eastern roadway connects directly to Durotar before the Gold Road reaches the Crossroads. Beyond the settlement, it passes the waters of local oases and the foothills near the Wailing Caverns. The northern span ends at a dried-up riverbed, where travelers enter the more dangerous southern Barrens.

Golden Plains. The Golden Plains form a vast, sun-drenched basin stretching southeast of Thunder Bluff in central Mulgore. Cherished by the tauren, these sweeping grasslands serve as prime hunting territory and a vital grazing habitat for wandering herds of kodo. Spreading out beneath the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, the Golden Plains represent the untamed heart of Mulgore. The shifting sea of golden and green grass offers an abundant sanctuary for local wildlife, making it one of the most treasured traditional hunting grounds of the nomadic tauren. Broad kodo herds roam across the rolling basin, while hunters share stories of legendary quarry, most notably the great kodo Arra'chea, who wanders quietly through the tall stalks.

Goldshire. Goldshire sits where Elwynn’s roads meet, linking Stormwind City with Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after the First War, the town now offers travelers the Lion’s Pride Inn, while a hard-pressed Stormwind Guard defends it. Goldshire stands where the king’s highways meet, the civic and commercial heart of rural Elwynn. Threats press closer as Stormwind’s forces stretch thin and King Varian Wrynn remains mysteriously absent. Marshal Dughan relies on passing adventurers instead of regular troops to hold the surrounding borders. Riverpaw gnolls push in from the west, while hostile murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Their attacks have killed royal guards and brought danger close to the town center.

Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace is missing, and the Stonefield and Maclure families blame each other. Billy Maclure admits he lost it while playing nearby, and you follow the trail to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred up trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt, saying he only found the necklace before a creature snatched it away.

Goldwell the Elder. At Kharanos during the Lunar Festival, Elder Goldwell welcomes travelers and offers a chance to honor the ancestors. He keeps this old tradition alive across the snowy dwarven lands. Beside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches the busy trade path leading to Ironforge's gates. During the Lunar Festival, he welcomes weary travelers, adventurers, and locals. His presence carries the long memory of ancient days, when early mortals walked beneath Azeroth's stars.

Golm Fragment. The Golm Fragment is one of four missing pieces chipped from the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic uncovered at the Wetlands excavation site. Recovered by adventurers dodging ferocious raptors, it helps dwarven archaeologists piece together mysterious Titan inscriptions. Discovered at the excavation site in the southern Wetlands, the Golm Fragment is part of a monumental slab known as the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar discovered the stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back, but found its inscription severed in four critical places. The Golm Fragment was abandoned amid the dirt and overturned crates when the dig was overrun, hidden away inside an ancient relic box until brave explorers could retrieve it.

Golnir Bouldertoe. Beside Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe supplies miners and prospectors and receives dispatches for couriers and travelers. At Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen with the necessities of their trade. He sells sturdy mining picks, flux, and coal, supplies that fuel the smelting fires and smithies that define the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a reliable contact for workers arriving in the city. He directs fresh hands and receives supply messages carried from nearby outposts.

Good Steel. Good Steel is an Alliance quest originating at Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. In the wake of recent conflicts, high-quality metal has become scarce, leaving the camp's woodcutting equipment worn and difficult to replace. Craftsman Hagar Lowe tasks adventurers with delving into Jasperlode Mine to salvage well-crafted pickaxes so their steel can be repurposed. Following the devastating conflicts that have battered the human kingdoms, high-grade steel has become an increasingly scarce luxury in Elwynn Forest. At Eastvale Logging Camp, daily timber harvesting relies heavily on durable axes, saws, and hardware, but the tools currently available have suffered badly from substandard metal and constant wear. Without reliable shipments coming from Stormwind's foundries, camp craftsmen like Hagar Lowe are forced to find inventive solutions to keep the forestry camp functioning.

Gorbold Steelhand. In Auberdine, Gorbold Steelhand keeps trade moving along Darkshore’s coast. The dwarven merchant brings goods from far across the Great Sea for travelers, crafters, and night elves. Gorbold Steelhand brings Ironforge trade to Auberdine. Night elves populate much of northern Kalimdor, so Alliance outposts depend on merchants who cross the Great Sea. Gorbold works alongside the kaldorei, selling trade goods, reagents, crafting supplies, and tools. Travelers come to him as they prepare to explore Darkshore’s dangerous shores and forests.

Gordo's Task. Along the road to Brill, Gordo gathers plants for the Royal Apothecary Society. The wandering abomination cannot manage delicate work, so he asks travelers to pick Gloom Weed and bring it to Junior Apothecary Holland. Between Deathknell and Brill, Gordo trudges through the countryside on the Royal Apothecary Society's behalf. Abominations can fight with brute strength and haul heavy loads, but their huge, stitched hands make delicate work difficult. Sent into the meadows to gather ingredients, Gordo finds that his blunt fingers crush more stems than they pluck. He turns to passersby, bullying or bribing them to do the careful work for him.

Gordok Commons. The Gordok Commons comprise the fortified northern quarter of the ancient Highborne ruins of Dire Maul. Under the rule of King Gordok, this sprawling stone complex serves as the seat of power for the elite warrior caste of the Gordunni ogres. Occupying what was once an aristocratic wing of Eldre'Thalas, the Gordok Commons have been thoroughly desecrated and refitted for ogre tastes. Grand night elven pillars and arched passageways now house armories, crude barricades, and training grounds for the Gordok—the fiercest, most disciplined fighters among the Gordunni clan. At the deepest end of the wing lies Gordok's Seat, where King Gordok presides over his brutes through sheer force and intimidation.

Gordon Wendham. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham sells weapons and helps couriers from the surface find their way. Gordon Wendham sells weapons to those who take up arms for the Forsaken. His stock ranges from daggers and hand axes to broadswords and maces. Fledgling fighters can find dependable iron here before they venture into the contested reaches of Lordaeron.

Gordon's Crate. Weapons are bound for the Forsaken forces in Silverpine Forest, packed in Gordon's Crate in the Undercity. The shipment is meant for the remote garrison at the Sepulcher. The Forsaken keep a steady flow of supplies from the Undercity to hold Silverpine Forest. Gordon's Crate carries weapons for Deathguard Podrig's defenders at the Sepulcher. The outpost sentries face worgen, wild beasts, and human remnants in the woods.

Gordunni Cobalt. Orwin Gizzmick has just arrived in Feralas and heard that the Gordunni ogres keep interesting minerals buried. Orwin offers a shovel and asks you to head for the Gordunni Outpost, north of Camp Mojache, and dig up twelve samples of Gordunni cobalt, following the blue glow. Orwin Gizzmick has only just reached Feralas and has heard the Gordunni ogres possess some interesting minerals. Orwin does not know what the ogres are up to, but they guard it fiercely and do not leave it lying about. They bury it, to keep folks like Orwin from getting hold of it. Orwin gives you a shovel. The Gordunni Outpost lies north of the camp; a blue glow shows where to dig. Twelve samples of Gordunni cobalt are wanted.

Gordunni Outpost. Tucked into the rugged cliffs north of Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost serves as a fortified camp for the brutish Gordunni ogres of Feralas. The clan's corrupting influence has choked the once-vibrant wilderness here, leaving the surrounding earth dry, withered, and brown. Carved into the northern mountains above the Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost stands out as a stark scar against the lush canopy of Feralas. Wherever the Gordunni ogres settle, their reckless magical channeling and destructive habits sap the vitality of the wild, leaving the local flora dead and the hillsides barren. The outpost consists of dirt trails, a shallow entrance cave, and a larger ogre mound burrowed deep into the rear cliffs. Patrolled by heavily armed hillguards, cunning channelers, and ogre tamers, the camp also holds dangerous trophies—including a captured sasquatch named Bigfist kept in crude confinement near the deeper den.
