text.enUS: Incendosaurs? Whateverosaur is More Like It. Hansel Heavyhands says his bunions have bunions, and he cannot do any killing with his feet in such disarray. Scrange and Burninate told him to clear out the incendosaurs of the Slag Pit, so he sends you instead to slay twenty. Hansel Heavyhands is in no state to fight. Scrange and Burninate told him to kill the incendosaurs so that expeditionary teams can go down into the lava pools of the Slag Pit and explore. Hansel passes the work on to you.

name.ptBR: Café com pão, café com pão

text.enUS: Incoming Gumdrop. In Ironforge, Talvash del Kissel has a Gnomeregan Gumdrop for a sick child in Stormwind. He asks for a train impression before handing it over. At Hallow’s End, trick-or-treaters seek treats from the Alliance strongholds. In Ironforge’s Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel keeps the Gnomeregan Gumdrop. He feels for the young orphan who wants it, but asks anyone seeking the sweet to bring some mischief to the holiday with a convincing train impression.

Indurium. Martek the Exiled says the Badlands hold a wealth of metal for anyone with the nerve to get it. Indurium is said to stand up to heat and stress, and Martek wants samples to test whether it could serve Fizzle's racecar. Stonevault troggs out in the Badlands are the ones carrying flakes of it. Martek the Exiled tells you he is not out in the Badlands just to avoid company. The region holds indurium, a metal said to stand up to heat and stress, and it might do for Fizzle's car. Martek wants samples to test, and has the forge hot and waiting.

Indurium Ore. Pozzik plans to work indurium into several parts of the racers, which calls for a great deal of raw ore. The ore is to be had at the Uldaman dig in the Badlands, across the sea in Khaz Modan. The gnomes are already getting hold of their own, and Pozzik wants to keep up with them. Pozzik asks for four pieces of raw indurium ore. It can be had at the Uldaman dig in the Badlands, across the sea in Khaz Modan. The gnomes are already getting hold of their own, so Pozzik wants a supply too. This follows Rizzle's Schematics.

Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. Across the sea, Alliance adventurers reach Ironforge seeking an explosive answer to the Venture Company in Stonetalon. Lomac Gearstrip agrees to brew Nitromirglyceronium if you bring him the needed alchemical reagents. Gaxim Rustfizzle needs powerful explosives for his most advanced device against the Venture Company. He is stationed high in the craggy passes of the Stonetalon Mountains, far from his eccentric former colleague Lomac Gearstrip in Ironforge. Lomac created Nitromirglyceronium, a compound so unstable and destructive that he finds the thought of anyone using it hilarious, no matter who gets blown apart.

Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. Lomac Gearstrip sends volatile NG-5 to Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gaxim needs the chemical to ignite several wagons packed with dynamite, creating a distraction for Alliance operations in the disputed crags. Lomac Gearstrip hands over Nitromirglyceronium, or NG-5, an unstable compound born of gnomish engineering. He warns you to handle it with extreme care. Mishandled, the chemical could blow you to pieces on the road back to Gaxim Rustfizzle.

Infectis Scar. The Infectis Scar is a deep, unnatural chasm carved into the blighted terrain of the Eastern Plaguelands near Corin's Crossing. Unlike natural ravines, this wound in the earth was ripped open by necromantic power when a cursed runeblade shattered against a dwarven shield. The blight festering at the bottom of the fissure remains an enduring testament to the Scourge's dark sorcery. While neighboring gorges like the Pestilent Scar originated as natural terrain features poisoned by the plague, the Infectis Scar is entirely artificial. It was created during the third war's violent clashes near Corin's Crossing. When the notorious death knight Marduk Blackpool clashed with a stalwart dwarf captain, Marduk's cursed runesword shattered against the captain's shield. Discarding the broken weapon, Marduk kept the hilt, but the severed runeblade sank deep into the soil. Its foul enchantment violently tore open the crust of the earth, creating the jagged chasm that sits festering in the Plaguelands today.

Infestation Investigation. Infestation Investigation is an early task given to young adventurers stepping out into Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight orders a cull of pesky cirrusflies that have begun swarming the eastern groves. Left unchecked, the fast-breeding insects threaten to destabilize the peaceful grove and endanger local settlements. Thendal Grove has long maintained a delicate balance, but recent reports by local rangers indicate a sudden population surge of pesky cirrusflies on the eastern edge of the woods. While individual cirrusflies are minor pests, their swarms quickly turn aggressive and destructive when numbers balloon. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight wastes no time dispatching capable youth to cull the flying insects before their presence completely overwhelms the grove.

Infiltrating the Castle. Master cheese monger and intelligence broker Elling Trias directs you into the royal seat of Stormwind Keep. Your objective is to rendezvous with his fellow operative Tyrion, who has spent weeks watching the corrupt nobleman Lord Gregor Lescovar from the keep's gardens. When you bring your findings to Elling Trias in his Trade District cheese shop, he quickly grasps the gravity of the Defias threat nestled deep inside the kingdom's governance. Legal channels will not suffice to expose or punish someone as deeply entrenched and protected as Lord Gregor Lescovar. Trias offers a dangerous route forward: delivering extrajudicial justice within the very walls of Stormwind Keep to permanently sever the conspiracy.

Infiltrating the Cult. Infiltrating the Cult is a quest in Shen'dar Village where an unfamiliar adventurer is tasked with approaching a local missionary named Sania Silverstream. Beneath her benign religious exterior, Sania recruits followers for the Al'Aketh, a cult dedicated to the Windlord Al'Akir. The mission seeks to uncover the cult's true designs for the settlement before an uneasy peace shatters. In Shen'dar Village, an uneasy truce is beginning to unravel. For some time, local authorities have tolerated the presence of Sania Silverstream, a self-proclaimed missionary living among them. She represents the Order of the Al'Aketh, an organization that dresses itself in the vestments of a benign religious movement while deploying gentle recruiters to attract unsuspecting followers. Village leaders permitted her recruitment efforts solely to avoid provoking the cult into outright conflict, but the pretense of mutual coexistence is wearing thin.

Infiltration. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has at last heard word and rumor of Gol'dir. The Syndicate keeps moving the orc prisoner, and Krusk sends you to its large camp just north of town to bring back whatever information you can find. Krusk has at last heard word and rumor of Gol'dir, an orc prisoner held by the Syndicate. Its humans keep moving him, but the search has narrowed to their large camp just north of Tarren Mill. Krusk sends you there to find whatever information you can and carry it back. With each day, he fears Gol'dir's prospects grow darker.

Ink Supplies. In Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton needs fresh ink for his work as a monastic scribe. He sends you east to Lakeshire for Rethban ore, the mineral his fast-drying ink requires. Brother Paxton takes pride in his craft and uses a special ink for important writings such as The Stresses of Iron. His recipe dries quickly and resists smearing, but the ink can dry in its pot if left too long. To make more, he needs raw Rethban iron ore, mined in the rocky Redridge Mountains.

Innkeeper Allison. In Stormwind's Trade District, Innkeeper Allison keeps the Gilded Rose ready for travelers and merchants. The busy inn stands between the bank and auction house, where she offers hearthstone bindings, drinks, and shelter. Innkeeper Allison welcomes travelers at the Gilded Rose in Stormwind. The inn stands between the Trade District auction house and the city's main vaults, and its ground floor sees a steady flow of peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. She keeps order behind the main counter and offers lodging and hearthstone services. Allison also joins local holiday festivities and coordinates small errands for traveling heroes seeking rest in the capital.

Innkeeper Farley. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Innkeeper Farley welcomes travelers with food, beds, and hearthstones. Well-liked and observant, he keeps misplaced mail and hears the troubles of those on the road. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall, and Duskwood find Innkeeper Farley behind the Lion's Pride Inn counter in Goldshire. He offers meals, ale, cheese, and a bed, and sets hearthstones for those who need one. With a welcoming hand and a sharp eye, Farley serves all who pass through this busy waystation and keeps order at the inn.

Innkeeper Firebrew. At Ironforge’s Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew keeps travelers fed and rested at the Stonefire Tavern. His hearty dwarven fare welcomes mountaineers and visiting dignitaries beneath the mountain. Innkeeper Firebrew welcomes travelers at the Stonefire Tavern in the Commons. The tavern sits in the Commons’ central ring, and many travelers entering Ironforge through the Great Gates find it first. Behind a counter laden with ale, stout, and roasted meat, Firebrew offers hospitality to those bound for Dun Morogh’s snowy passes or deeper into the mountain kingdom. Miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather there to escape the drafty tunnels and trade tales around the hearth. The Stonefire remains a lively crossroads in the heart of Ironforge.

Innkeeper Grosk. At Razor Hill, Innkeeper Grosk welcomes travelers on the road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar. His inn offers food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Razor Hill links Durotar’s southern training grounds with Orgrimmar’s high walls. Innkeeper Grosk shelters warriors, scouts, and peons at his inn. Travelers find basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water beneath its sturdy timbers.

Innkeeper Gryshka. At the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers with food, drink, and a hearthstone binding. She keeps the inn supplied with meat from hunters across Durotar and the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers at the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The inn stands just beyond the city's main gates, where warriors, messengers, and newcomers to Thrall's Horde can find shelter.

Innkeeper Keldamyr. In Dolanaar, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers food, drink, and a place to rest. Young night elves leaving Shadowglen can find shelter at his inn beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Dolanaar is the first village many newcomers reach after leaving the sheltered glade of Aldrassil. At the village's central inn, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath Teldrassil's canopy. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus pause at his counter to rest, bind their Hearthstones, and gather rations for the journey through the boughs.

Innkeeper Norman. Innkeeper Norman keeps the Trade Quarter tavern ready for travelers in the Undercity. The quiet, diligent Forsaken offers Horde travelers rest, hearthstone bindings, and food for the living and the dead. Beneath Lordaeron's ruined capital, Innkeeper Norman tends the main tavern in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold find lodging there. Travelers come to bind their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for journeys into the Plaguelands.

Innkeeper Pala. On Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, travelers find Innkeeper Pala tending the Cat and the Shaman. She offers a place to rest, cold drinks, and a hearthstone binding for journeys across Mulgore and beyond. Innkeeper Pala tends the hearth at the Cat and the Shaman on Thunder Bluff’s lower rise. Travelers arrive from the central lifts or the plains of Mulgore. In the common room, weary warriors, wandering druids, and the Horde’s visiting allies can find shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar place to rest.

Innkeeper Renee. Travelers find food, drink, and shelter with Innkeeper Renee at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Innkeeper Renee welcomes weary newcomers to the Gallows' End Tavern, Brill's central inn. She sells food, drink, and general goods from behind her counter, and remarks that the Forsaken have huge appetites. Her tavern offers the undead of Tirisfal a cozy place to rest as plague victims make their way in the world.

Inquire at the Inn. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry sends you to the Scarlet Raven Tavern with a journal from Sven Yorgen's ruined farm. He hopes someone there can tell you who owned it. Clerk Daltry has finished examining the tattered book from Sven Yorgen's farm. He believes any stranger who visited Darkshire would have passed through its tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern is across town, the only gathering hall and lodging house in Darkshire. There, you may learn who came through and where they went.

Insane Druids. A massacre in Dor'Danil Barrow Den leaves its druids' spirits in torment. Kayneth Stillwind, a night elf sentinel in eastern Ashenvale, learns of the slaughter through a vision while battling Forsaken toxins. Kayneth Stillwind sees a massacre in a waking vision. The night elf sentinel is battling the effects of Forsaken toxins found in eastern Ashenvale when he witnesses what happened beneath the mounds of Dor'Danil Barrow Den. Undead infiltrators poisoned the druids in their sleep and slaughtered them. Their souls were torn from their bodies by the venom, leaving them as wild, shrieking spirits.

Insane Scribbles. In Darkshore, cultists carry Insane Scribbles torn from the Twilight Tome, a fragment of dark literature. The dancing text and distorted scrollwork cause dizziness and mental strain. Ancient forest protectors study the fragments to learn the Twilight's Hammer's motives. Reading the Twilight Tome can endanger a mortal's sanity. Its script writhes across the parchment, and graceful scrollwork warps into grotesque images before the reader's eyes. Tearing out even one sheet, called Insane Scribbles, leaves the bearer lightheaded and disoriented. Though the writing makes little sense, the parchment hums with primal, deeply ancient magic tied to dark powers long buried beneath Azeroth.

Inscribed Bark. In Teldrassil, Inscribed Bark carries word of the World Tree's state to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. The Oracle Tree entrusts it with news of the boughs and the threats troubling the woods. The Oracle Tree sends Inscribed Bark to the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus. After you drive the harpies from their nests, the ancient tree gives you its message, wary of sending ordinary couriers along Teldrassil's tainted paths. The report tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm of recent victories and the deeper blight still gripping the woods.

Insect Part Analysis. With Scrimshank lost, Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser sets about going over the surveying gear and putting Scrimshank's personal effects in order, and asks you to call on Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan about the insect parts. Fizzledowser means to spend some time with Scrimshank's surveying gear and personal effects, and has a sneaking feeling that these bugs will claim more losses. You are asked to call on Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan and learn whether the insect parts the surveyors sent have been processed yet. If they are ready, Fizzledowser wants them brought back.

Insect Part Analysis. Alchemist Pestlezugg has finished the report on the insect parts and says Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser must see it at once. The threat faces Tanaris and Gadgetzan and, if left unchecked, all of southern Kalimdor. Pestlezugg insists that Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser must see the report right away, and that everyone who can read must see it too. The threat is grave and serious, for Tanaris and Gadgetzan and, if left unchecked, for all of southern Kalimdor. It may even reach the whole of Azeroth, for it has given no sign that it will subside. You are asked to carry the report to Fizzledowser in Gadgetzan and have a duplicate made, to share freely with your allegiance. Everyone must know of this threat.

Intact Raptor Horn. Across the Barrens savannas, raptors are hunted for their intact horns. Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet wants them for a scheme built on rumors of raptor intelligence. Hunters prize raptor hides, talons, and trophies, but whole horns are harder to take in the field. Mebok Mizzyrix, an eccentric goblin alchemist in Ratchet, believes the Barrens raptors are more cunning than their kin elsewhere. He suspects their intellect lies in their horns. By grinding whole horns and brewing them into tonics, Mebok hopes to bottle that supposed genius in commercial drinks.

Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury. He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

Into the Field. Apothecary Zinge sends you into the Tanaris desert with a field testing kit to test the tissue of basilisks, scorpids and hyenas. The modified kit also needs a power source that the goblins of Gadgetzan have, so Zinge points you to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle there. Apothecary Zinge wants the consistency of the tissue of the desert's basilisks, scorpids and hyenas tested. You gather samples and run them through the testing kit you carry, though a good chunk of the samples will fail. Eight acceptable samples of each kind of creature are needed, and Zinge asks you to return only once you have succeeded.

Intrepid Strongbox Key. On the wreck of the Intrepid, Captain Halyndor still guards the key to his strongbox. The rusted iron key once kept a mysterious item locked away aboard the doomed Alliance vessel off the Wetlands. The Intrepid was wrecked with the Third Fleet off the Wetlands, and its crew became restless, cursed spirits. Captain Halyndor watched over a mysterious item inside the ship’s heavy strongbox. Now his ghost prowls the waterlogged deck, still clutching the rusted key that opens it.

name.frFR: Enquête sur la crête aux échos

text.enUS: Investigate Echo Ridge. Marshal McBride sends recruits north as kobolds gather at Echo Ridge Mine. The mine supplies ore and raw materials to Northshire Abbey and the Stormwind guard, and the growing threat puts both at risk. After early skirmishes with scattered vermin around Northshire's forested edge, scouts report a more organized threat. Kobolds have gathered in force at Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride sends you north to face the workers at the entrance and learn how deeply they have settled in.

name.frFR: Enquêter dans le magasin de l'Alchimiste

text.enUS: Investigate the Alchemist Shop. An arcane disturbance has brought invisible creatures into Algernon's shop in the Undercity. Anastasia Hartwell sends Horde mages to reveal and contain them before they can cause harm. Anastasia Hartwell sends arcane initiates to investigate a disturbance in the Apothecarium. Invisible magical creatures have been wandering through Algernon's alchemy shop, among its cauldrons and reagents. The Undercity's mage instructor suspects a breach in the flow of magic. The creatures must be contained before they cause serious damage.

Investigate the Camp. Investigate the Camp is an expedition task originating in Booty Bay to scout a newly established hunters' campsite in Stranglethorn Vale. Commissioned by Krazek, it tasks travelers with confirming rumors that the legendary dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary has arrived near Lake Nazferiti. Reports circulating through the docks of Booty Bay speak of an expedition of big-game hunters encamped in the northern jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Word has reached Krazek that the camp lies along the river just past the Venture Company's busy mining claim near Lake Nazferiti. In a lawless jungle teeming with dangers and competing interests, unexplained armed encampments always demand a watchful eye.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Darnassus
name.zhCN: 调查达纳苏斯的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. Lieutenant Beitha calls for help as the Scourge encampments press close to Darnassus. The Argent Dawn needs defenders to strike the undead and learn what the runes outside the gates are for. The Scourge has reached Teldrassil, and floating necropolises loom above the invasion camps near Darnassus. Ghouls, skeletons, and other undead horrors spill from them. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn coordinates the city's defense, calling on volunteers to slow the attack and gather information before the undead overwhelm the night elven homeland.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Forgefer
name.zhCN: 调查铁炉堡的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Ironforge. The Scourge has reached the gates of Ironforge, and Lieutenant Nevell calls for defenders. Undead troops and glowing runic circles threaten Dun Morogh beneath a hovering necropolis. The Scourge has brought its invasion to the mountain entrance of Ironforge. Floating necropolises cast their shadows over Dun Morogh’s frigid heights, far from Lordaeron and the plagued lands of the north. The Argent Dawn has placed observers there, including Lieutenant Nevell, to watch the undead and counter their spread before they breach the Bronzebeard fortress.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Orgrimmar
name.zhCN: 调查奥格瑞玛的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. Outside Orgrimmar, the Scourge has raised a camp beneath a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel calls on defenders to repel the undead, recover necrotic stones, and examine runic circles charged with necromantic energy. The attack brings the Lich King's reach to Durotar. The Scourge now threatens lands far from Lordaeron and the northern ice. Floating necropolises cast their shadows across Azeroth, even over Durotar. Undead forces have gathered at Orgrimmar's threshold, raising camps that threaten the Horde capital. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn coordinate the defense, calling on local champions to drive the invaders back before they can secure a siege.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Hurlevent
name.zhCN: 调查暴风城的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Scourge forces press against Stormwind, with necropolises looming beyond its walls. Lieutenant Orrin calls defenders to strike their camps, gather Necrotic Stones, and study the runes there. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital.

Invisibility Liquor. Invisibility Liquor gives Maybell Maclure a way to slip from her family's sight and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. Their households are locked in a feud. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks a quiet meeting with Maybell Maclure, though their families' feud keeps the households apart. Their kin watch closely, and ordinary secrecy is not enough. Invisibility Liquor lets the drinker pass unseen across the disputed farmland.

Iris Lake. In north-central Ashenvale, Iris Lake lies east of Astranaar, its waters turned yellow-green by corruption from Felwood. Bog beasts prowl its shores. Iris Lake lies between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, its waters fouled since the Third War. Fel energies drift south from the tainted heights of Felwood and poison the basin, turning clear water into a yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plants and water spirits, and aggressive bog beasts lash out at travelers who come near.

Iron Coral. In Ironforge, Klockmort Spannerspan seeks coral for a new suit of armor. The gnome blacksmith works in Tinker Town and sends you to the Wetlands coast for searing coral, hoping to test new smithing methods in a custom design. Klockmort Spannerspan has fresh ideas after exchanging insights with master dwarven smith Furen Longbeard. The gnome wants to bring Furen's metallurgy together with his own tinkering to make exceptionally resilient armor. Mountain ore alone will not suit the experiment. Klockmort needs searing coral, a naturally hardened material from the sea.

Iron Pike. In Lakeshire, Iron Pike supplies are needed to repair the Everstill Bridge. The shipment from Stormwind was seized by Redridge gnolls, leaving the town short of iron. Lakeshire spent its metal reserves forging armor, blades, and ammunition after recent attacks by the Blackrock orcs. Builders requested more iron from Stormwind City, but Redridge gnolls hijacked the caravan on the road. They carried crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, stopping repairs on the Everstill Bridge.

Iron Pommel. In Ashenvale, the Iron Pommel is the last missing piece of Dartol's Rod. The long-dead wizard Dartol made the rod, and the night elves of Astranaar seek it to slow the furbolg attacks on their people. Druids at Dor'Danil Barrow Den kept the pommel safe until their sanctuary was overrun and they were slaughtered. Dartol's Rod was split apart and scattered across Ashenvale to guard its mystic power. Night elf druids near the road south toward the Barrens took charge of the Iron Pommel. Their circle was massacred at Dor'Danil Barrow Den, and their shelter fell silent in ruins. The pommel vanished amid the destruction, swallowed by the bubbling oozes now moving through the defiled glade.

Iron Rivet. Iron Rivet shipments from Stormwind now lie in gnoll camps north of Lake Everstill. Foreman Oslow needs them to mend Lakeshire's damaged bridge. Lakeshire's iron stores went into weapons and armor when Blackrock orcs attacked. After the assaults eased, Foreman Oslow asked Stormwind for supplies to mend the damaged Everstill Bridge. Redridge gnolls ambushed the caravan before it reached town. They dragged its wagons and pack beasts into the hills north of Lake Everstill, scattering iron rivets and pikes among their camps.

Iron Shaft. Near Felwood, the Iron Shaft waits in a locked chest. It is one piece of Dartol's Rod, sought by Teronis to slow the furbolg assaults on Ashenvale. Dartol made the rod, then its pieces were scattered across Ashenvale. One was placed in the care of the druids of Dor'Danil. The Iron Shaft is the rod's sturdy metal core, kept in a locked chest in a glade near Ashenvale's northern border, close to Felwood.

Ironband's Compound. At Ironband's Compound, Tormus Deepforge seeks vengeance for his slain mentor. Sturgy Ironband's teaching outpost in eastern Dun Morogh fell after a shipment of rare umbral ore drew the Dark Iron dwarves. Sturgy Ironband taught smithing at a secluded compound south of Helm's Bed Lake. Across Ironforge, he was revered as an unmatched instructor. He trained promising pupils far from the crowded anvils of the Great Forge. That peaceful work ended when one student acquired an unfamiliar mineral called umbral ore. Intrigued by its properties, Ironband chose to experiment with the sample. He did not know that possessing the ore had marked his school for ruin.

Ironband's Compound. Dark Iron dwarves hold Ironband's Compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Once Sturgy Ironband's camp, it now threatens travelers and nearby settlements. Dark Iron dwarves hold the compound south of Helm's Bed Lake. Sturgy Ironband first established the camp as a staging post in Dun Morogh's snowy wilderness. Dark Iron infiltrators pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized it. Now their forces threaten travelers and nearby settlements, close to Ironforge.

Ironband's Excavation. In Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm worries over the slow work at Ironband's Excavation. Supplies still reach Prospector Ironband's team, but reports show little progress. Jern trusts Ironband's diligence and sends you to learn what has disrupted the dig. Jern Hornhelm watches shipments from Thelsamar cross Loch Modan to the Explorers' League. Provisions and tools arrive steadily, yet Prospector Ironband's dig makes little progress. Jern knows Ironband as an upright, diligent dwarf, so he suspects something has disrupted the work. He sends you to find out what is holding the team back.

Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband’s dig lies south of the Loch, where troggs have driven the miners from their trenches. The excavation in southeastern Loch Modan, southwest of Farstrider Lodge, has been halted. Prospector Ironband’s dig in southeastern Loch Modan began with a search into the dwarves’ ancient Titan origins. The work ended in disaster when the miners disturbed an unusually fierce, large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, drove the miners back, and made camp among scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics.

name.zhCN: 铁环挖掘场的进度报告

text.enUS: Ironband's Progress Report. In eastern Loch Modan, troggs keep Prospector Ironband's excavation from advancing. His report asks for more blastpowder after earlier supplies were sent weeks ago. Prospector Ironband's digging in Loch Modan is repeatedly disrupted by nearby troggs. His progress report, carried to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar and then sent on to the Explorers' League in Ironforge, describes the stalled work and asks for heavy munitions. League leaders already sent Ironband plenty of blastpowder weeks ago, and now wonder where those shipments went.

Ironbeard's Tomb. West of the road to Dun Modr, Ironbeard's Tomb lies defiled and overrun by acidic oozes. A stone statue watches over the outdoor graveyard, where travelers search the slime for lost possessions. Ironbeard's Tomb overlooks the marshes beside the road north to Dun Modr. A great stone statue, believed to show Ironbeard, watches over the burial plot. Black and crimson oozes have overrun the crypt below, tainting the resting place. Dwarves no longer bring their dead here. Those who enter the vaults search among the remains swallowed by the slimes.

Ironclad Cove. Deep beneath Westfall, Ironclad Cove holds a hidden shipyard and dock. The Defias Brotherhood builds its war juggernaught here, with a passage to the sea. Ironclad Cove lies at the deepest point of the Deadmines, where a vast sea cavern has become a fortified dockyard. Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood have built an enormous warship here, the juggernaught. Wooden scaffolding, islets, and loading catwalks fill the cavern, watched by Defias pirates, deckhands, and overseers. VanCleef aims to do more than raid Westfall's farmsteads: he plans to assemble a private naval force capable of bombarding Stormwind's shores.

Ironforge. Ironforge's Great Forge burns beneath the mountain, at the heart of dwarven rule and Alliance trade. Deep inside Ironforge Mountain in Dun Morogh, the city is the political and mercantile anchor of Khaz Modan and a bulwark of the Alliance. Ironforge fills the deep halls of Ironforge Mountain, its stone rings circling the Great Forge. The dwarves founded the city millennia ago, after awakening and migrating from Uldaman. It has weathered ages of history, including the ancient War of the Three Hammers, which left the Bronzebeard clan in sole control. Natural magma pours through the mountain to power the city, while massive stone gates guard its halls. Dwarven craftsmen and warriors share them with many exiled gnomes, who came after the recent fall of Gnomeregan.

Ironforge Airfield. High above Dun Morogh, gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers hold a remote airfield northeast of Ironforge. Its plateau overlooks jagged crags and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. High above Dun Morogh's trails, gnome flying machines line open landing strips among the mountain peaks. Dwarven masonry anchors the ridgelines, and mountaineers watch the perimeter. Nearby, engineers tend the machines and inspect their engines in the cold.

Ironstone Camp. Ironstone Camp is an outpost established by the Horde along the western border of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Originally deployed to expel Alliance dwarven excavators from the nearby digsite, the encampment's forces now face a deadly threat after subterranean silithid overran the excavation. Ironstone Camp sits directly on the threshold between the high pillars of Thousand Needles and the blazing salt expanse of the Shimmering Flats. The Horde detachment stationed here was initially dispatched with a clear and singular objective: dislodge the dwarven excavators digging at the Rustmaul Digsite. However, their military confrontation was cut short when a swarm of voracious silithid burst forth from a nearby cavern, violently engulfing the dig and attacking both sides. Led by Moktar Krin, the surviving camp defenders have diverted their efforts to combating the insectoid infestation before the swarm spreads unchecked across the region.

Irontree Woods. Irontree Woods is a blighted grove situated in northern Felwood, once cherished by the night elves as a peaceful forest sanctuary. Ravaged by the demonic corruption of the Third War, its ancient protectors have been petrified into stone while twisted treants and elementals prowl among the ruins. Irontree Woods was once a tranquil woodland glade tended by the kaldorei, but the demonic taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War choked the life from its soil. The grove's guardian Ancients—Hastat, Stoma, and Vartrus—succumbed to the dark magic, petrifying into lifeless stone monuments that still stand entombed amid the corrupted brush. Now, maddened treants, vile bog beasts, and tainted water elementals wander the twisted forest floor, striking violently at any travelers who dare approach.

Isha Awak. Along the Merchant Coast, Mahren Skyseer calls you to a hunt in the Great Sea. You are to slay Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, and bring back its heart for a rite of spirit and respect. South of Ratchet, Isha Awak prowls beneath the waves. Known as the Deep Doom, this immense sea creature commands the coastal waters with great strength. Human forces camped along the shore fear those waters after losing many scouts and soldiers to the predator's hunger.

Ishamuhale. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sends you to face Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. The hunt tests your skill and respect for nature's deadliest predators. Sunscale raptors hunt the Barrens in cunning, vicious packs, but none inspires more dread than Speartooth. Jorn Skyseer says Ishamuhale kills by instinct and passion, not for food or territory. He hunts because killing is his nature. To face him is to test whether you can withstand a predator's unbridled ferocity.

Ishamuhale's Fang. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer awaits Ishamuhale's Fang from the feared sunscale raptor Speartooth of the Barrens. The tooth proves the hunter bested one of Kalimdor's deadliest natural predators. Across the central savanna, hunters fear Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor alive. Some say the apex hunter kills from predatory passion, not hunger. Fresh zhevra meat draws the beast into the open beside a withered tree northwest of Ratchet, where it gives no quarter. Taking its massive fang proves to the Horde's hunting instructors that a traveler has overcome the savagery of the plains.

Isle of Dread. The Isle of Dread is a desolate, cliff-bound island situated in the Great Sea off the southwestern coast of Feralas, south of Sardor Isle. It is notorious for sheltering monstrous two-headed chimaeroks and an entrenched coven of hostile naga hidden within its subterranean sea caves. Rising out of the crashing surf of the South Seas, the Isle of Dread lives up to its ominous name. Ringed by sheer cliffs, the island's interior valley is only accessible through a narrow pathway on its southeastern coast. Within this enclosed highland roams a lethal population of chimaeroks—ravenous, two-headed beasts empowered by ambient arcane energies. These beasts are led by the monstrous Lord Lakmaeran, making the island a deadly deathtrap for unwary explorers who cross the channel from Sardor Isle.

Islen Waterseer. Beside the Tidus Stair, respected tauren shaman Islen Waterseer guides Horde initiates through the trials of water. She lives by a quiet fishing hut and teaches shamans to attune to water spirits as they seek their Water Totem. On the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer keeps to the craggy Tidus Stair, where arid plains meet the Great Sea. Water spirits are raw and near along this shore. Islen chooses this quiet outpost over thunderous halls and busy cities, spending her days listening to the tides. Shamans seeking communion with water come to her for guidance.

Items of Some Consequence. Tyrion gathers silk and apples for a spy inside Stormwind Keep. The covert operative needs the materials to disguise Spybot and send it past the royal guards to listen in on Lord Lescovar. Elling Trias has moved the operation against Lord Gregor Lescovar forward. The cheese merchant suspects Lescovar's schemes inside Stormwind Keep threaten the realm. In the keep's gardens, Tyrion agrees to the tighter schedule, but says the disguise needs careful preparation.

Itharius's Cave. Itharius's Cave is a secluded hollow tucked into the far southwestern cliffs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as the refuge of the enigmatic Itharius, who appears to be a high elf and tends to the brood of green dragonkin inhabiting the surrounding marsh. Tucked away in the treacherous, moss-draped crags of the southwestern Swamp of Sorrows, this damp cavern shelters the recluse Itharius. Outside its mouth, unruly green whelps wander the mire. Though he appears to be a high elf, a folk who rarely wander so far south into wild swamps alone, Itharius keeps a watchful eye on these young dragonkin as they grow, living alongside them in quiet isolation.

Ivar Patch. At Ivar Patch in northern Silverpine Forest, a ruined harvest hides the fate of its farmhands. Before the Third War, Ivar's pumpkin farm was a prosperous homestead in Lordaeron. Ivar employed lively farmhands and servants, but the Scourge spread the Plague of Undeath across the countryside and consumed the farm. Ivar, his family, and his laborers rose again as rotting, feral ghouls, bound to prowl the ruined soil without their minds. Unlike the Forsaken, they have no free will.

Ivar the Foul. At the Ivar Patch in northern Silverpine, Ivar the Foul has trapped two Deathstalkers. Rane asks Horde travelers to kill the savage ghoul so Quinn can recover and they can finish their report to High Executor Hadrec. Rane and Quinn Yorick, siblings and Deathstalkers, were sent to survey Silverpine Forest for High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their work ended in violence at a farmstead in the northern forest, where Ivar the Foul ambushed them.

Ivar's Head. In northern Silverpine, Ivar's Head proves Ivar the Foul is dead. Rane Yorick seeks it so her wounded brother Quinn can recover safely. Rane and Quinn Yorick were scouting northern Silverpine Forest on High Executor Hadrec's orders when Ivar the Foul ambushed them at an abandoned farmstead. The Forsaken Deathstalkers drove the feral ghoul off, but Quinn was badly mauled. Rane stayed at the ruined farm to watch over him and could not safely leave to finish their mission. Ivar's severed head proves the ghoul will no longer threaten the estate, giving Quinn time to recover under Rane's care.

Iverron. In Shadowglen, Iverron lies stricken by spider venom. His plight warns of growing corruption within Teldrassil. Iverron wandered beneath Shadowglen’s quiet canopies when webwood spiders bit him. Their venom left the young night elf unable to return to safety on his own. The spiders once shared the glade in peace, but now they grow increasingly aggressive.

Iverron's Antidote. Iverron's Antidote is an urgent task in Shadowglen to save a poisoned night elf scout. By gathering wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor, adventurers help Dirania Silvershine brew a remedy before the venom takes full hold. While scouting the boughs of Shadowglen, young Iverron fell victim to the poisonous fangs of the local Webwood spiders. Collapsed and dying, his survival depends entirely on the herbal knowledge of Dirania Silvershine at Aldrassil. With the youth fading fast, she must quickly prepare a specialized concoction to neutralize the aggressive venom coursing through his blood.

Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron waits for medicine before its strength fades. Poisoned by Webwood spiders, the night elf scout depends on Dirania Silvershine's brew, which must reach him within five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the cure from fresh venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi. The unstable mixture keeps its strength for only five minutes after it is distilled. Whoever carries the vial must sprint straight from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation.

Iverron's Antidote (item). In Shadowglen, Iverron's Antidote must reach a young night elf before it spoils. Dirania Silvershine brews it to counter the lethal venom of local Webwood spiders, but it lasts only five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the antidote in Aldrassil for Iverron, a young night elf bitten by Webwood spiders. Its volatile ingredients and herbal catalysts give the draught a shelf life of only five minutes. Couriers must hurry north to the Webwood cave and deliver it before it spoils.

text.enUS: JOB OPPORTUNITY: Culling the Competition. A notice announces that Taskmaster Scrange wants some capable hands to cull the competition in the Searing Gorge. The work is slaying Dark Iron Taskmasters and Dark Iron Slavers until your clothes are bloody enough, then returning to Scrange. Scrange wants applicants to head out through the gorge and slaughter the Dark Iron Taskmasters and Dark Iron Slavers they meet: fifteen of each. Come back when your clothes are bloody enough. You will know when that is, and you are not to ask.

Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Jade Phial to young initiates. It carries sacred water from Teldrassil’s moonwells to replenish the druids’ central well in Darnassus. The Jade Phial gathers water from a moonwell near Starbreeze Village. Teldrassil’s many moonwells channel lunar and natural energies that matter to night elf society and druidic worship. From time to time, the druids replenish their central moonwell in Darnassus with water from wells across the great bough. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the phial to young initiates, who use it to collect pure water without disturbing the moonwell’s spiritual potency.

Jadefire Run. Jadefire Run is a heavily fortified satyr encampment nestled in northern Felwood. It houses some of the most powerful and cunning satyrs in the region, serving as a bastion of demonic corruption deep within the tainted forest. Situated amid the blighted woods of northern Felwood, Jadefire Run functions as a stronghold for the Jadefire satyrs. Unlike lesser outposts scattered throughout the valley, this camp features substantial demonic construction and shelters formidable spellcasters and tricksters. The satyrs here actively conspire to spread corruption further across Kalimdor, employing dark sorcery and foul trickery against anyone who dares intrude on their territory.

Jaedenar. Jaedenar is a blighted hollow in central Felwood built over ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens. Named in foul homage to the demon lord Kil'jaeden, it serves as the primary base of operations for the Shadow Council in northern Kalimdor. Cultists, warlocks, and summoned demons scour the corrupt hollow, guarding the subterranean descent into the Shadow Hold. Long ago, these hollows sheltered night elf sacred grounds and slumbering druids connected to the Emerald Dream. After the devastation of the Third War, the vile remnant of the Shadow Council laid claim to the valley, christening it Jaedenar to honor the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Warlocks—predominantly renegade orcs and Forsaken—have gathered here alongside satyrs, succubi, and felguards. They occupy both the surface ruins and the deeper barrow dens, twisting what was once holy woodland into a grim center of demonic invocation.

Jagged Reef. The Jagged Reef forms the rugged northern coast of Azshara, where sandy beaches meet jagged stone spurs and churning surf. Treacherous rocks lurk beneath the shallow water, making maritime travel impossible. The desolate shore is primarily populated by prowling hydras, scavenging makrura, and territorial murloc tribes. Stretching across Azshara's northern edge, the Jagged Reef is a harsh littoral expanse where broken cliffs and jutting stone outcroppings divide the sandy shores into secluded inlets. Beneath the breaking waves lie submerged crags and shifting shallows, turning the waters into a graveyard for any vessel foolish enough to venture near. On land, the wild coastline offers little comfort; salt-crusted beasts, predatory hydras, and aggressive makrura wander the surf line alongside entrenched murlocs scouring the tides for scraps and unwary prey.

Jaggedswine Farm. South of Orgrimmar's main gate, Jaggedswine Farm raises swine for the capital. Its shed, pen, and watering hole serve the Horde's nearby stronghold. Jaggedswine Farm shows the harsh work of feeding an urban stronghold like Orgrimmar. Durotar's red soil supports little farming, so hardy livestock helps feed the city's warriors and laborers. A timber storehouse, a broad wooden pen, and a natural watering hole anchor the farm. Swine are herded, bred, and butchered here to keep the Horde's granaries supplied.

Jaguero Isle. Jaguero Isle is an isolated, jungle-covered island resting off the eastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale's Wild Shore. Dominated by fierce wild panthers and gorillas, it is infamous as the domain of the colossal silverback gorilla known as King Mukla. Situated off the southeastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, Jaguero Isle stands well apart from the mainland pirate camps and troll ruins. The island is entirely overrun by untamed fauna, mainly panthers and aggressive gorillas. Looming over them all is the gargantuan ape King Mukla, whose rule over the rocky interior is absolute and territorial. Few sailors willingly approach its reefs, though occasionally washed-up bottles along the mainland beaches carry desperate pleas for rescue from those unfortunate enough to be stranded ashore.

Jahan Hawkwing. At the Crossroads, Jahan Hawkwing keeps Horde travelers supplied with armor. The tauren armorer works from this outpost in the Barrens, where predators roam the plains. Jahan Hawkwing tends to the armor needs of Horde travelers and defenders at the Crossroads. In the Barrens, durable gear can mean survival against centaur, quilboar, and wild beasts. Jahan works with local leatherworkers, sending cured hides for delivery so his shop stays stocked with dependable tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion.

James Halloran. In Menethil Harbor, James Halloran makes a living tanning crocolisk hides. Passing travelers and nearby trade channels help him gather raw skins and carry finished leather to buyers across the eastern continents. James Halloran lives and works in Menethil Harbor, earning his living from the marsh just outside town. The dangerous bogs provide crocolisk skins, which he turns into fine leather through rare craftsmanship. Nearby trade channels carry his finished goods to buyers across Azeroth.

James Hyal. "James Hyal" is an Alliance quest concerning a human settler who sailed to Kalimdor with Lady Jaina Proudmoore's expedition. After setting out to open an inn on the frontier, his family in the Eastern Kingdoms lost touch with him and seeks news of his fate through Theramore's administrative records. During the Third War, countless souls left their ancestral homes in the Eastern Kingdoms to follow Lady Jaina Proudmoore across the Great Sea. Among them was James Hyal, remembered fondly by his kin as a gifted cook. After the fighting subsided and Theramore Isle was founded, James chose to carve out a living on the rugged continent of Kalimdor by opening an inn of his own to serve travellers and fellow settlers.

Janeiro's Point. Janeiro's Point is a small, rocky island situated just outside the harbor of Booty Bay in southern Stranglethorn Vale. It is crowned by a colossal stone statue of an unknown goblin welcoming incoming maritime traffic with outstretched arms. The island's waters and shores are dominated by the menacing sea giant known as Mok'rash the Cleaver. Standing as the monumental gateway to Booty Bay, Janeiro's Point greets every vessel charting a course into the southern seas of Stranglethorn Vale. Atop the crag looms an immense stone effigy of a goblin, arms spread wide in a grand gesture of welcome and unbridled mercantile ambition. Though visible to sailors and corsairs for miles around, landing on the island's shores is a perilous prospect due to Mok'rash the Cleaver, a terrifying sea giant who has claimed the outcrop as his territory.

Jangolode Mine. In Westfall’s rolling hills, the Defias Brotherhood works Jangolode Mine for itself. The mine once supplied Stormwind City with ore and raw materials. Before Westfall declined, Jangolode Mine sent metals to Stormwind City for its reconstruction and supply. As civil order weakened and the kingdom withdrew its garrisons, the Defias Brotherhood seized the mine to support its own operations. The bandits now work its rich veins and defend the shafts fiercely.

Jannok Breezesong. In Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong trains young night elf rogues. He teaches stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to kaldorei setting out beneath the World Tree's boughs. Beneath Dolanaar's boughs, Jannok Breezesong teaches novice night elf rogues. He trains those who work quietly beyond the ranks of Teldrassil's sentinels and druids. His lessons teach them to stalk through shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen among the boughs. When rogues finish their first lessons in Dolanaar, Jannok sends them to more experienced trainers in Darnassus.

Jansen Stead. Jansen Stead lies just west of the Elwynn border, where Defias bandits and mechanical Harvest Watchers now roam its fields. Jansen Stead lies beside the road from Elwynn into Westfall. The farm once fed the kingdom, but unrest has driven its family from the land. Now Harvest Watchers, mechanical constructs associated with the Defias Brotherhood, patrol the fields alongside brigands. Couriers and travelers between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill pass close by.

Jarl Needs Eyes. "Swamp Eye" Jarl at Swamplight Manor wants 40 unpopped Darkmist eyes, because Darkmist eye juice is smooth and salty. The spiders live in Darkmist Cavern, west of the manor. Following Soothing Spices, Jarl turns to eye juice, which is good for drinking. Most critters carry a mere pair of eyes, whereas spiders carry a great many, and Jarl finds Darkmist eye juice tasty. The Darkmist spiders live in Darkmist Cavern, west of the manor, and Jarl muses over whether the cave gave the spiders their name or the reverse.

Jarl Needs a Blade. "Swamp Eye" Jarl, in Dustwallow Marsh, has cutting to do and will not say what. Jarl wants a certain blade, a moonsteel broadsword, and does not want you to dawdle. "Swamp Eye" Jarl has cutting to do, and cannot say what is to be cut. Jarl needs a particular blade, which some call a moonsteel broadsword and Jarl calls a swing blade. You might find one in town, or a blacksmith might make one special. Jarl warns you not to sleep on it, since what is to be cut will not keep forever.

Jasper Fel. In Stormwind's Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies daggers and vials from SI:7 headquarters. He keeps watch on visitors and warns them to mind their speech. Inside SI:7 headquarters in Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies the agents who work there. He offers simple daggers and empty vials for brewing and applying poisons. Jasper works under Mathias Shaw's intelligence division and warns visitors to mind their speech. In a place built for espionage, careless words can put people in danger.

Jasperlode Mine. In north-central Elwynn, Jasperlode Mine lies lost to kobolds and giant spiders. Its shafts once supplied Stormwind City with vital iron and minerals, but the resource-strapped kingdom cannot reclaim them. Jasperlode Mine once supplied Stormwind with a steady wealth of minerals, alongside nearby Fargodeep. With the kingdom's forces stretched thin by outside threats and unrest, local garrisons cannot protect the shafts. Kobolds seized their chance, drove out the human miners, and hoarded stolen gold and tallow candles.

Je'neu Sancrea. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu Sancrea watches the Ashenvale coast for dark disturbances. The Darkspear troll and Earthen Ring shaman sends Horde adventurers to investigate corruption in the submerged temple of Blackfathom Deeps. Je'neu Sancrea watches the dangerous Zoram Strand from Zoram'gar Outpost. While most of the Earthen Ring works to keep the elements in harmony across Kalimdor, he keeps watch over the coast. Dark tremors and unnatural tides stir near the ruined temple of Blackfathom Deeps. His shamanic duties bind him to the Earthen Ring, but his loyalties to the Darkspear tribe and Thrall's Horde lead him to work only with Horde champions.

text.enUS: Je'neu of the Earthen Ring. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu of the Earthen Ring studies a spreading corruption. Horde travelers bring him a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals. As a shaman devoted to elemental harmony, he seeks to understand the blight along the Zoram Strand and within Blackfathom Deeps, in hope of halting the poison in the region's waters. Mastok Wrilehiss sends you to Je'neu Sancrea with a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals. Strange elementals have surfaced across the region, animated by unnatural power that scouts cannot explain. Among their remains, the intact globe pulses with corrupted magic. Mastok knows soldiers and scouts lack the spiritual insight to understand it, so he directs Horde travelers to someone versed in ancient legends and elemental lore.

Jen'shan. In the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan teaches young hunters the ways of the wild. The Darkspear jungle troll trains orc and troll marksmen in tracking, ranged combat, and survival. Jen'shan trains new hunters in the Valley of Trials. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls come to her with inscribed tablets and parchments that direct them to her. She teaches them archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, preparing them for the scorpids and boars on the canyon floor.

Jennea Cannon. In Stormwind, Jennea Cannon guides new mages through their first studies. From the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter, she teaches caution and self-control, and investigates disturbances in local arcane energies. At the top of the Wizard's Sanctum's spiral walkway, Jennea Cannon guides those who come to Stormwind to study the arcane. She teaches more than spells, insisting that students learn caution and self-control. Even those who do not study magic hear her warning: without training, magic can burn its wielder.

Jennea's Flask. At the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind, Jennea Cannon sends apprentices to Mirror Lake for water. They bring the sample back for arcane analysis. After magical struggles across Azeroth, arcane currents have torn loose from their ancient channels. Jennea Cannon seeks to learn how these shifts have affected Elwynn Forest. She gives promising apprentices a glass flask and sends them southwest of Stormwind's gates to the base of Mirror Lake's waterfall. The flask protects the water sample on the journey back to the Wizard's Sanctum, where it can be examined for arcane disturbances.

Jergosh the Invoker. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Jergosh the Invoker plots against the Horde. He leads Searing Blade cultists in Ragefire Chasm and practices demonic arts while Thrall guides the orcs toward honor and shamanism. Jergosh gathers the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. While Thrall leads the orcs toward honor and shamanism, Jergosh turns to demonic power. He hides in Ragefire Chasm, where he draws followers into a sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. From below the Horde capital, the cult works against the path the new Horde has chosen.

Jern Hornhelm. In Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm keeps the Explorers' League's work moving. The dwarven miner coordinates supplies and messages between the town, Ironforge, and the dig site deeper in Loch Modan. Travelers carry mining supplies and progress reports across the region for him. Jern Hornhelm works from Thelsamar to keep supplies moving to Loch Modan's dig sites. Dwarven scholars and field teams search the wilderness for their ancestral past, and they need steady deliveries of resources and tools. Jern also makes sure communications reach the active digs.

Jerod's Landing. Defias smugglers hold Jerod's Landing on the Elwynn Forest bank of the Nazferiti River. The dock gives them a hidden route for illicit shipments across the kingdom's waterways. Defias outlaws now control the river dock at Jerod's Landing, where Elwynn Forest meets the waters of the Nazferiti River. Once an ordinary boat dock, it now receives goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains under a Defias dockmaster's watch. The outlaws move the cargo discreetly downstream toward holdings such as Klaven's Tower in Westfall.

text.enUS: Jin'Zil's Forest Magic. At small Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil holds three night elven scouts in crude iron cages. He sends Horde adventurers to Stonetalon Peak for wilderness reagents to brew a grim forest magic. Under the Horde's watch, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil practices his craft in Malaka'jin's red-rock defile. When three night elf captives fall into his hands, he chooses a mocking ritual made for his woodland foes instead of ordinary butchery. He sends travelers north into the peaks for thick tree sap, feline whiskers from predatory twilight runners, a shimmering fey dragon scale, and scores of eyes from the local forest coursers.

Jitters. Among Raven Hill's ruins, Jitters lives alone and fears the dangers around him. He survives on help from travelers in western Duskwood, always watching the shadows. Jitters shivers among Raven Hill's ruined houses, afraid of the predators along Duskwood's western trails. He depends on travelers for food and keeps watch for danger. His habit of flinching and leaping clear of sudden threats earned him his name long ago. The fear comes from horrors he has faced himself.

Jitters' Completed Journal. Jitters gives up his completed journal, hoping to clear his name and expose the sinister forces haunting Duskwood. The reclusive man fears Sven Yorgen's vengeance after fleeing the massacre at Sven's farm.

Jitters' Growling Gut. In Raven Hill, Jitters is starving and afraid, with only weeds and insects to eat. He asks you to go east to Darkshire and seek a hot batch of Chef Grual’s famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill’s ruined streets shelter ravenous undead and lurking beasts. Jitters has hidden there for weeks, moving through its crumbling shanties under a sky that never seems to brighten. Grubs from the dirt and wild weeds are all he has found to eat. Hunger and fear wear him down, far from the comforts of ordinary life.
