text.enUS: Job Opening: Guard Captain of Revantusk Village. Guard Captain Malkhor has been lost, and Revantusk's guard needs a new captain. Anyone who wants the post must wipe out Vilebranch Berserkers, Shadow Hunters, Blood Drinkers and Soul Eaters, then bring an application to Primal Torntusk in the Hinterlands. A call to arms announces that Guard Captain Malkhor has been lost, so Revantusk's guard has no captain once more. Whoever wants to lead it is invited to do the work set out in the notice and then send an application to Primal Torntusk.

Jocaste. In Darnassus, Jocaste trains night elf hunters arriving from the wilds of Teldrassil. Jocaste trains night elf hunters in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Young trackers come to her after their first training in Shadowglen, ready to take up the hunt in the capital. She teaches marksmanship and survival in the wild, along with the bond between a hunter and the beasts of Kalimdor.

Johaan's Findings. Apothecary Johaan sends his findings south from Brill to the Sepulcher. His research carries recent alchemical work from Tirisfal Glades to Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine Forest. Apothecary Johaan sends his research from Brill to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society works under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's demand for a New Plague that can destroy both the living and the Scourge. Its researchers are scattered across Lordaeron's contested ruins, so they must share their findings between outposts. Renferrel directs the Society's efforts from Silverpine Forest, while Johaan records his local tests in Brill. His documents join the Society's wider work to refine its deadly brews.

Johaan's Special Drink. At Brill, Apothecary Johaan offers a drink with a deadly purpose. Disguised as a common refreshment, it tests the Royal Apothecary Society’s developing plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan prepares a brew from venomous components and local reagents. Though it looks like a tavern drink, the mixture is made to test how virulent the plague is against living beings. Johaan hands it over as if to quench a captive’s thirst. The work serves the Forsaken apothecaries’ effort to create a weapon potent enough to fulfill Sylvanas Windrunner’s designs for Azeroth.

John J. Keeshan. Corporal John J. Keeshan is a human soldier of Stormwind's army who fought the Blackrock orcs in the Redridge Mountains. After being captured during the fighting around Stonewatch, he was dragged deep into Render's Rock as a prisoner of war. John J. Keeshan is a corporal in the service of Stormwind, posted to the Redridge Mountains as the Blackrock orcs pressed against Lakeshire and its defenders. When the fighting flared up around Stonewatch Keep, Keeshan was in the thick of it alongside the other soldiers holding the line for the kingdom.

Jonathan Carevin. In Darkshire, Jonathan Carevin hunts the dangers gathering in Duskwood. He and his family take the fight beyond the Night Watch's patrols, pursuing undead, worgen, demons, and heretics beneath the forest canopy. The Night Watch guards Darkshire and patrols its roads, but Jonathan Carevin believes defense alone cannot protect the township. He hunts the unholy creatures roaming Duskwood with his family and allies such as Calor. His crusade, fought in the name of the Light, targets demons, undead, and heretics across the region.

Jorah Annison. In the Magic Quarter, Jorah Annison helps spellcasters find knowledge scattered across Azeroth. The Forsaken cartographer knows both the land and the ancient texts warlocks seek. Jorah Annison makes maps in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, but the work does not hold his interest. He would trade every map in the shop for one good book. Jorah knows more about ancient texts than almost anyone, and warlocks share his taste for a scholar's work.

Jordan Stilwell. Outside Ironforge’s gates in Dun Morogh, Jordan Stilwell works at his forge. He was meant for the Church of the Holy Light, but followed his father into smithing and learned from Bailor Stonehand. His craft serves paladins across the Alliance, and he forged Verigan’s Fist in honor of his old friend, Bosch Verigan. Jordan Stilwell was expected to take holy vows and become a paladin in the Church of the Holy Light. Instead, he followed his father’s path as a smith and took up his father’s enchanted hammer. The dwarven blacksmith Bailor Stonehand helped him refine his craft. Jordan remains deeply faithful to the Light, and puts his skill to work outfitting champions who fight in its name.

Jordan's Ore Shipment. Mo'grosh ogres hold Jordan's Ore Shipment in the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. The ore came by caravan from the Wetlands for Bailor Stonehand to refine into an alloy for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell's ore shipment was bound for Bailor Stonehand, a dwarf who would refine it into his special alloy. The caravan carried the ore south through the mountains from the Wetlands into Loch Modan when Mo'grosh ogres ambushed it. The ogres dragged the shipment to their stronghold in the wilderness. The surviving guards perished from their wounds, and Jordan's smithing project waits until the ore is recovered.

name.esES: Envío de mena refinada de Jordan
name.frFR: Cargaison de minerai raffiné de Jordan
name.ptBR: Carregamento de Minério Refinado do Jardel

text.enUS: Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment. Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment reaches Ironforge for a paladin's sacred trials. The high-grade metal is prepared for blacksmith Jordan Stilwell to forge a holy weapon of virtue. Jordan Stilwell needs rare, exacting materials to forge a weapon worthy of a dedicated paladin. The set includes a Purified Kor Gem, sturdy Whitestone Oak lumber, his lost smithing hammer, and a shipment of refined ore. This consignment supplies the metal for the sacred labor, brought to Ironforge for the Test of Righteousness.

Jordan's Smithing Hammer. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge, Jordan's Smithing Hammer carries a family legacy into his work. His father passed it down to him, and its recovery from Shadowfang Keep is needed for a weapon consecrated to the Light. Jordan Stilwell keeps his father’s hammer close, for it carries his family’s craft and his hopes for a masterwork. The human blacksmith works outside Ironforge, but the heirloom has somehow ended up in Shadowfang Keep, within the stone walls of Silverpine Forest. Jordan needs it back before he can forge a sacred weapon fit for a holy champion.

Jorgen. Jorgen keeps watch beside the water at Stormwind's Valley of Heroes entrance. His quiet perch draws people with matters they cannot discuss openly. Jorgen keeps to the water just right of Stormwind's great entrance. Above him, statues of heroes look over the bridge, while he watches those who come and go below. People seeking information they want kept off the record can find a quiet contact there.

Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons. You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south.

Josef Gregorian. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian trains tailors of the Horde. His skill guides them toward enchanted fabrics and specialized garments. Josef Gregorian teaches tailoring in the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, where Forsaken and their Horde allies practice the craft. Tailoring remains vital to warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian teaches foundational patterns and stitches the first robes for young mages who bring him the right materials.

name.ptBR: Siga para o Penhasco do Trovão

text.enUS: Journey into Thunder Bluff. Journey into Thunder Bluff is the culminating pilgrimage marking the end of a young hero's trials across Mulgore. Having completed the sacred Rites of the Earthmother under the guidance of the spirits, the adventurer is granted an audience with the High Chieftain of the tauren, Cairne Bloodhoof. Before any traveler or fledgling warrior can truly claim to have proven themselves in Mulgore, they must undergo the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. These trials test strength, vision, and wisdom across the rolling plains and ancestral sites of the land. Once the Ancestral Spirit acknowledges the final rite, the initiate is deemed worthy of entering the city of Thunder Bluff not as a mere visitor, but as an honored defender of the tauren people.

name.zhCN: 通往阿斯特兰纳的旅途

text.enUS: Journey to Astranaar. Fiora Longears sends Alliance travelers from Theramore north to Astranaar. There, they report to Shindrell Swiftfire in Ashenvale, where the night elves face war and unrest. Alliance travelers arrive in Dustwallow Marsh aboard the ferry from Menethil Harbor, often seeking purpose in northern Kalimdor. At Theramore, Fiora Longears directs capable hands inland toward Astranaar, Ashenvale's main night elven settlement. The route winds beneath ancient, shadowed canopies and leads into a forest strained by war and unrest.

name.deDE: Reise in das Vorgebirge des Hügellands
name.ptBR: Jornada ao Contraforte de Eira dos Montes
name.zhCN: 前往希尔斯布莱德丘陵

text.enUS: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Renferrel sends his research south to Tarren Mill, where the Forsaken press on with their plague studies. You carry his notes from Silverpine Forest to Apothecary Lydon in Hillsbrad Foothills. Since escaping the Lich King's control, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has pursued a New Plague that could destroy both the living and the Scourge. The Royal Apothecary Society works under the Banshee Queen's relentless pressure to create it. Its researchers are scattered across Lordaeron, so they share chemical data and test findings to hasten their work.

Journey to Tarren Mill. Apothecary Zamah seeks a way to drive the Venture Company from Stonetalon Mountains without open war. She sends you across the sea to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, where the Royal Apothecary Society works in Lordaeron. In Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah is a link between the Forsaken and the Earth Mother's children. The Venture Company is logging and mining the sacred lands of Stonetalon Mountains, and the tauren have found that ordinary methods will not stop them. Zamah turns to her peers in the Royal Apothecary Society for a chemical deterrent. She hopes their alchemy can drive the company out without a drawn-out war.

Journey to the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Kirge Sternhorn sends travelers north to aid Thork at the Crossroads. The journey carries them from Mulgore into the Barrens and the wider struggles of the Horde. Camp Taurajo is where many tauren first face the Barrens beyond Mulgore. Just past the mountain pass, mystic Kirge Sternhorn watches travelers descend into the dry grasslands. When Sternhorn sees that a traveler is ready to go farther, Kirge points north along the dusty trade route toward the Crossroads.

Joys of Omosh. After an adventurer's great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith brushes off his tears as soot, then performs the Omosh dance of joy to pass down an unusual piece of family heritage. Near Orgrimmar's scorching forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. The burly blacksmith has received great help from you, and the kindness overwhelms him. He stubbornly blames a stray bit of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping.

Juggernaught. A Juggernaught is an enormous, heavily armored battleship bristling with heavy naval cannons. Built with ogre help to serve as the iron core of the Old Horde's fleet during the Second War, these floating fortresses were built to pulverize coastal strongholds and trade routes. Reports of a great vessel beneath Westfall draw attention to the hidden workings of the Defias Brotherhood. Orcs were not traditionally a seafaring culture, so when the Horde required a fleet capable of crossing the Great Sea and contesting the Alliance's naval superiority during the Second War, they relied heavily on ogre ingenuity. The resulting craft—the ogre juggernaught—became the backbone of the Horde armada. Though vastly slower and less nimble than swift troll destroyers, these behemoths carried immense plating and devastating broadside batteries that could shatter Alliance hulls and smash shore fortifications to rubble.

Juice Delivery. In Darkshire, a potent brew draws raised eyebrows as you carry it west. Tavernkeep Smitts entrusts you with Zombie Juice for Abercrombie, a reclusive hermit on Duskwood’s western edge. The drink is meant to warm the shivering old man, but its uncanny potency raises questions. Tavernkeep Smitts of Darkshire brews a legendary draught called Zombie Juice. When it is ready, he hands you the bottle and warns you to handle it gently, saying the concoction is stout enough to raise the dead. You carry the potent drink across a haunted forest to an eccentric loner, on what seems like a simple act of charity.

Jungle Secrets. After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions. Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

Junkboxes Needed. Fahrad keeps Ravenholdt supplied with locked boxes for rogue training. His demand never ends, and he trades specialized throwing knives to anyone who brings authentic heavy junkboxes. Ravenholdt Manor is a hidden redoubt in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills. Training never ceases there. Master thief Fahrad oversees the guild's operatives and prizes practical skill at picking locks. Zan supplies practice contraptions for new recruits, but Fahrad finds them too crude for experienced thieves who must open stubborn mechanisms in the field.

Kaal Soulreaper. In the Undercity, orc warlock Kaal Soulreaper trains apprentices and keeps close ties with practitioners of the dark arts across the Horde. Among the Forsaken, he guides students toward mentors in distant lands. Kaal Soulreaper works in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where Horde warlocks come to learn from his mastery of demonic entities and curses. Thrall's Horde strictly regulates and monitors fel magic within Orgrimmar, while the subterranean sanctums of Lordaeron offer practitioners like Kaal ample harbor. Beyond teaching, Kaal connects those seeking greater power with mentors across the sea, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

Kadrak. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the northern frontier between the Barrens and Ashenvale. He directs dispatches and reinforcements into the contested forest, where the Horde fights the night elves. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the main route between the Barrens and Ashenvale. The barricade marks a hard border: Horde-held plains lie to the south, and night elf-guarded woods stretch north. Kadrak keeps watch against Sentinels and hostile woodland creatures, holding the perimeter against incursions.

Kadrak's Flag. At the edge of the Barrens and Ashenvale, Kadrak gives the Horde a mark to carry into enemy ground. The flag is planted in the Talon Den after Keymaster Rynthariel is killed. Kadrak sends the Horde flag into the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak. The dryad Rynthariel, Keymaster of the Den, has sent communications across the border, and Kadrak decides her death alone will not answer them. He gives you the crimson banner to plant deep inside the Den. The Horde colors there carry a warning to the night elves and dryads: incursions across the Barrens will meet retaliation on Alliance soil.

Kaela Shadowspear. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Kaela Shadowspear watches the wilderness southwest of Windshear Crag. She coordinates with fellow sentinels as tensions rise and the land suffers new disruptions. Travelers help scout dangerous ground and learn what has corrupted the ancient defenders. Kaela Shadowspear watches the passes southwest of Windshear Crag. The Horde presses into the Stonetalon Mountains, while goblin operations exploit the land's natural bounty. Working beside the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle, Kaela tracks threats pushing deeper into night elf ancestral territory.

name.ptBR: Deixando Kaela a par de tudo

text.enUS: Kaela's Update. Gaxim Rustfizzle sends you back to Kaela Shadowspear with letters taken from the Venture Company. Their contents help the Sentinels follow the goblin cartel's work in Stonetalon. Gaxim Rustfizzle sends you back to Kaela Shadowspear with captured letters. After you helped the gnome mage uncover Venture Company movements, he gathered correspondence detailing the cartel's operations. Kaela, a night elf Sentinel coordinator near Windshear Crag, is waiting for the letters. Gaxim also wants you to mention how his magic helped the investigation.

Kali Remik. In Sen'jin Village, Kali Remik guides young hunters toward their next training. She is a Darkspear troll hunter who knows the tracking and survival ways of Durotar. Kali Remik guides young scouts in Sen'jin Village, where they begin their lives beyond the Valley of Trials. A Darkspear troll tracker, she knows Durotar's dry lands and the Horde's settlements. When a novice is ready to leave the local training grounds, Kali sends promising hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill. There they begin learning to tame beasts, strengthening the Horde's frontier ranks.

Kaltunk. At the heart of the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Kaltunk welcomes young orcs and points them toward their first duties for the Horde. Kaltunk watches over new arrivals in the Valley of Trials and directs them toward Gornek and the path of discipline. While trainers and elders set trials and hunting rites, the orc overseer gives recruits clear orders so they know where to go.

Kam Deepfury. In Stormwind's Stockade, Kam Deepfury waits apart from the Defias rebels. The Dark Iron dwarf was captured after arranging the blast that shattered the Thandol Span, far to the north. Kam Deepfury is a Dark Iron dwarf held deep in the Stormwind Stockade. Most prisoners there are disgruntled Stonemasons or Defias rebels, but he belongs to neither. Captured and brought to Stormwind after an operation crippled vital northern infrastructure, he remains cut off from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain. Like the rebels who share the corridors, he is hostile to the Alliance.

Kanati Greycloud. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter stationed at Whitereach Post within Thousand Needles. Alongside his hunting companions, he musters what defense he can while enduring constant hostility from the local Galak centaur. Kanati Greycloud makes his camp at Whitereach Post, high atop the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. While the canyon offers abundant game and open vistas, it is hemmed in by the Galak centaur, whose warbands contest every inch of the arid flats below. Together with other tauren hunters, Kanati keeps watch over the canyon floor, striving to preserve the post against the brutal depredations of the surrounding marauders.

Kaplak. In Razor Hill, Kaplak trains young orc and troll rogues for the Horde. He teaches stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft before sending them to Orgrimmar. Kaplak trains new Horde rogues in Razor Hill. Orcish custom favors open combat and roaring charges, but he teaches the quieter skills needed to survive: stalking unseen, picking locks, and striking from behind. When his students outgrow his training in Durotar's dusty red ravines, he sends them north to Orgrimmar, where senior guild operatives can deepen their craft.

Karang Amakkar. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Karang Amakkar watches Ashenvale's rocky coast and the threats closing in around the Horde. At Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar guards one of the Horde's most exposed borders. The camp faces pressure from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Karang watches the hostile peoples along the road east, guarding Horde couriers and scouts from ambush by tribes defending their territory.

Karazhan. Karazhan is the ominous, secluded tower standing at the southern end of Deadwind Pass. Once the sanctum of Medivh, the Last Guardian of Tirisfal, the citadel sits atop a potent convergence of ley lines that warps time, space, and reality around it. Though Medivh was slain during the First War, the abandoned fortress still hums with volatile arcane energy, restless spirits, and hidden dangers. Long before the First War, the tower of Karazhan was raised upon ground shaped like a human skull, situated at a massive nexus of mystical ley lines. It served as a secluded refuge and repository of untold magical secrets for the Guardian Medivh. Within its curving halls, Medivh lived alongside his loyal castellan Moroes, entertaining noble guests and housing an immense archive of arcane texts and relics that eclipsed even the libraries of the Kirin Tor. Yet the tower was also the stage for Azeroth's greatest betrayal, as Medivh fell under the demonic possession of Sargeras and secretly orchestrated the opening of the Dark Portal.

Kargal Battlescar. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar guards the eastern edge of the Barrens. He watches the crossing from Durotar, judges incoming recruits, and sends capable fighters west to strengthen Horde defenses. Kargal Battlescar watches the road into the Barrens from the Far Watch Post. Travelers and new adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, leaving the Valley of Trials behind. The Barrens is a dangerous, contested land, where aggressive wildlife, centaur raiders, and quilboar tribes threaten the frontier. Kargal inspects those who pass and gathers willing recruits for the Horde. He sends them onward to the Crossroads, where they can aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

Kargath. Kargath is a fortified Horde outpost perched in the western Badlands, serving as their sole foothold in Khaz Modan. Established by the Kargath Expeditionary Force under Warchief Thrall's orders, the settlement anchors crucial transit lines across the Eastern Kingdoms while staging operations toward Blackrock Mountain and the excavation at Uldaman. Named in honor of the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist, the outpost of Kargath stands as the Horde's solitary settlement throughout the mountain realms of Khaz Modan. Surrounded by arid wastes, aggressive wildlife, and hostile dwarven factions, the garrison provides a vital midway sanctuary for travelers crossing the continent. Its flight master bridges the long divide between northern holdings like the Undercity and Hammerfall and southern redoubts like Stonard and Grom'gol Base Camp.

Kargathia Keep. Warsong overseers hold the eastern edge of their lumber camp at Kargathia Keep. The fortified stronghold guards the Southfury River border in Ashenvale and links the outpost to Orgrimmar. Kargathia Keep anchors the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp, just west of the Southfury River. Spiked barricades fortify the outpost, where Overseer Gorthak and his officers direct the Horde’s logging operations. From the river border, the Warsong clan watches for incursions. When night elf skirmishers strike, reinforcements can come swiftly from Durotar and Orgrimmar.

Karos Razok. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Karos Razok keeps the Forsaken bat roost ready. Karos Razok tends the skeletal bats from the wooden platform above the Sepulcher's crypts. Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill make the northern road through Silverpine Forest treacherous. Razok keeps messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies moving above the haunted canopy, linking the frontier outpost to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

Katie Hunter. At the Eastvale Logging Camp stables, Katie Hunter tends horses for Stormwind and trusted Alliance champions. She works with Randal Hunter to keep travelers and soldiers mounted for the kingdom’s roads. Katie Hunter tends the horses at the Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. While lumberjacks cut timber for Stormwind’s reconstruction, she raises dependable pintos, mares, and swift steeds for riders. Her horses carry people along the kingdom’s roads and the dangerous routes of southern Azeroth.

Kaya's Alive. In Stonetalon, Kaya Flathoof has survived the Grimtotem attack and reached safety. Makaba Flathoof sends you to Sun Rock Retreat with the news for her worried aunt, Tammra Windfield. The Grimtotem strike along Stonetalon's contested trails. After their village fell under attack, young Kaya Flathoof was feared dead or captured by the renegades. Her rescue brings relief amid the fighting between tribes in the crags.

Kaymard Copperpinch. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch sells Smokywood Pastures goods for Winter Veil. He trades in the Valley of Strength, where travelers can find festive wares and help with holiday troubles. Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures to the Valley of Strength each Feast of Winter Veil. Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby as Kaymard sells fine treats, festive wrapping paper, and other holiday goods. To a goblin, no grand festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin.

Kayneth Stillwind. Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire sends a courier east from Astranaar with a scouting missive for Forest Song. Druid Kayneth Stillwind needs help watching corruption spread through Ashenvale's ancient woods. In Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire watches over western Ashenvale. Druid Kayneth Stillwind, stationed at Forest Song in the forest's eastern reaches, has asked her to assess the region's security. Shifting wildlife and dark omens along the coasts and through the woods trouble him. Swiftfire puts her observations in a sealed note, trusting a traveler to carry it safely across the dangerous central forest.

Keep An Eye Out. In Booty Bay, the old sea dog Dizzy One-Eye lost his sight in battle and sees only through a special enchanted glass eye. Bloodsail Buccaneers ambushed him last night and took it, and Dizzy asks for help getting the eye back. Dizzy One-Eye lost both eyes in battle. By good fortune, Dizzy's ship docked at Menethil, where a traveling wizard made a special enchanted glass eye that gave Dizzy sight again. Without it, Dizzy feels useless, and recalls that the crow's nest was once home.

Keeper Albagorm. At Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm watches the Charred Vale burn and seeks help healing the wilds. Keeper Albagorm guards the night elven refuge at Stonetalon Peak. Like other sons of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world. South of the peak, the Charred Vale lies scorched by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists. Bloodfury harpies now hold the ruins and prevent new growth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works to halt the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

Keeper Bel'dugur. In the Undercity, Keeper Bel'dugur commissions expeditions to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts for his people. The scholarly Forsaken works deep within the Apothecarium. Among the Apothecarium's vats and researchers, Keeper Bel'dugur sends adventurers to recover dangerous arcane and occult relics from across Azeroth. The Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on extra-dimensional beings, is locked away inside Shadowfang Keep and draws his keen interest. While many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure or weaponize undeath, Bel'dugur's curated acquisitions seem chosen to uncover ancient, forbidden powers.

Keeper Bel'varil. At Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil studies magic and alchemy for the Forsaken. His work with Wordeen Voidglare draws Horde adventurers into the search for relics and binding materials across Hillsbrad Foothills. Keeper Bel'varil supports Forsaken magic and alchemy in besieged Tarren Mill. The royal apothecaries and soldiers focus on the Alliance garrison down the road at Southshore. Bel'varil turns to practical sorcery, sending travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

Keeper of the Flame. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the coast. The spectral sailor seeks oil to keep the beacon burning after murlocs killed the living keepers, so ships can pass the reefs safely. Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet off the zone’s southwest shore, where its light once guided sailors through the Great Sea’s shallow waters. That duty ended when Old Murk-Eye led a murloc attack and killed the keeper and his family. Captain Grayson, a sailor who died in the waters by these rocks, now watches over the tower as a ghost. Death left him unable to stop the slaughter, but he will not let the lighthouse go dark.

Keeping Pace. Pozzik is sure the Brassbolts brothers have found a new building material. Their cars run faster than before, yet their designs and the rest of the data from their runs are unchanged. Rizzle Brassbolts has stayed fixed on the plans for this discovery almost constantly, and Zamek can create a diversion so you can steal them. This follows News for Fizzle. Pozzik can find only one explanation for how fast the Brassbolts brothers' cars have become: a new building material. Their designs and everything gathered from their runs look the same as before. What is known is that Rizzle Brassbolts has stayed fixed on the plans for this discovery almost constantly.

Keg of Shindigger Stout. In Dun Garok, Shindigger Stout fills the dwarves’ kegs and draws interest from Tarren Mill. The Royal Apothecary Society wants the ale for a purpose far darker than drink. Dwarves of Ironforge hold Dun Garok in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills. Within its barracks and mess halls, defenders share Shindigger Stout through the cold and the siege against their regional enemies. The brew is a staple of the garrison’s daily life.

Keldran. North of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar, Keldran works to clear a path toward peace with the Alliance. He directs covert strikes against demonic remnants, hoping to show that the modern Horde has forsaken the Burning Legion. Keldran works from Orgrimmar’s red rock terraces while Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom. The Alliance still sees all orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation forged during the first wars. Keldran believes Thrall is weary of endless conflict, but peace talks cannot begin while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without the Warchief’s formal sanction, he takes the initiative himself. He directs trusted agents toward distant threats, hoping to erase the demonic stain and clear the way for diplomacy.

Kelm Hargunth. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth keeps the Warsong Outriders supplied. He equips Horde champions fighting night elves in Warsong Gulch with care packages and provisions. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth manages supplies for the Warsong Outriders. The camp stands on the northern edge of the Barrens, beside the border with Ashenvale. Scouts and raiders skirmish beyond its stockade while Kelm sees that weapons, armor, and rations reach the fighters. The Warsong Outriders face the Silverwing Sentinels, and a steady flow of provisions matters as much as fury in battle.

Ken'zigla's Draught. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Ken'zigla prepares a bitter draught for the gravely wounded. A careful half dose restores enough strength to move, while more can make a patient bleed out. Ken'zigla prepares the draught in the Stonetalon Mountains for those near death. Its strength must be measured with care: more than half a dose at once can make the patient bleed out as their circulation surges. Half a dose gives a wounded person enough vigor to move and flee danger. The rest must wait until the body steadies after a full night's rest.

Ken'zigla's Draught. In the Horde warlock chain to summon a succubus, Ken'zigla's Draught is bound for Camp Taurajo. The troll apothecary prepared it in the Stonetalon Mountains to save Dogran, a missing operative. Ken'zigla prepared a second dose after trouble with the first courier. The troll apothecary in the Stonetalon Mountains feared the emissary sent to find medicine for the missing scout Dogran had never returned. His draught is volatile and powerful. Half a dose gives a mortally wounded soldier strength to move without making the wounds bleed anew. The rest must wait until the next day, when it completes the recovery.

Kerlonian Evershade. At the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade wakes from a long sleep in the Emerald Dream. The night elf Druid of the Claw needs help crossing the troubled wilds to reach Maestra's Post. Kerlonian Evershade follows the bear totem as one of the Druids of the Claw. For centuries, these druids slept in barrows and communed with the Emerald Dream. They were called from their slumber during the Third War. Now Kerlonian rests beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his long sleep. He must travel through Darkshore's troubled forests to reach Maestra's Post on the Ashenvale border.

Kernobee. Deep within Gnomeregan, Kernobee is trapped among the ruins. The goblin engineer uncovered Dark Iron involvement in the super rig, then was captured, beaten unconscious, and left in the dormitory quarters among the troggs. While doing business or scavenging in Gnomeregan, Kernobee discovered the Dark Iron dwarves had helped build and operate the great super rig burrowing beneath the city. Knowing how dangerous this knowledge was, he tried to flee to Ratchet and warn his associate, Tinkerwiz. The Dark Irons caught him before he could escape.

Keryn Sylvius. On the second floor of Goldshire’s Lion’s Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius trains young rogues. In the reading room, she teaches stealth and bladecraft and quietly guides promising operatives toward Stormwind’s intelligence service. Keryn Sylvius keeps to the reading room above the Lion’s Pride Inn. Downstairs, travelers crowd the floor with town guards, while upstairs she watches the steady flow of road gossip. She mentors rogues learning their trade in Elwynn Forest. When promising operatives outgrow petty theft and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius discreetly sends them to Stormwind City to contact SI:7.

Key to the City. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill wants to know more about the Kirin Tor, whose city Archimonde destroyed and who have now rebuilt Dalaran on the Dark Lady's very doorstep. You are to search the Kirin Tor camps for something that can get the Horde into the city unnoticed. The Alliance once had an army of mages, the Kirin Tor, but the demonic Burning Legion proved the stronger. In a single stroke the arch demon Archimonde levelled their city, and the survivors were left as dispossessed vagabonds. Now they have rebuilt Dalaran, on the Dark Lady's very doorstep. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill wants to know more, and sends you to search their camps for something, such as an ancient tome or a secret relic, that can get the Horde into the city unnoticed. What you bring back is a grimy Dalaran sewer key.

Khan Dez'hepah. After The Kolkar of Desolace, Felgur Twocuts sets you against the Kolkar's leader, Khan Dez'hepah. Many centaur clans fight one another across Desolace, and Felgur wants the Kolkar disrupted before the clans unite. The Kolkar are only one of the centaur clans of Desolace. Many roam the dry plains, fighting and dying at one another's hands. Felgur Twocuts does not mind, because the centaur are strong and brutal, and a united centaur people would be a fierce foe for the Horde. They must be dealt with before that happens.

Khan Hratha. Uthek the Wise recalls how you helped the Gelkis against the Magram, and now asks you to strike at the Maraudine by slaying their clan's leader, Khan Hratha. Hratha holds a piece of a key, and Uthek wants it brought to him. Uthek the Wise says the Gelkis now need help against the Maraudine. The Maraudine War Horn stands on a tall bluff in the Valley of Spears, and sounding it is how Khan Hratha is called out. Yet the horn is useless without a warhorn mouthpiece, which is rare and carried only by trusted Maraudine centaur. When the horn sounds, more centaur arrive, and Hratha comes last.

Khan Hratha. Warug announces the death of the Gelkis Khan and says the Maraudine are next. Warug sends you after their Khan, Hratha, and wants the piece of a key that Hratha carries. Warug wants the Maraudine Khan, Hratha, dead. A horn on a bluff in the Valley of Spears calls him out, but it will not sound without a mouthpiece, and a mouthpiece is found by killing Maraudine centaur. After the blast, Maraudine centaur gather at the tower, and Hratha shows himself in the end.

Khan Jehn. Following Ongeku, Uthek the Wise tells you the earth says the Magram are growing weak, and that the hour has come to slay their Khan. Uthek wants the head of Khan Jehn brought to Gelkis Village. Uthek the Wise at Gelkis Village says the earth speaks to Uthek, and it tells of the Magram growing weak. Uthek names their Khan, Jehn, as the one to strike down and asks for the head of the Magram Khan. Uthek expects you to still count as a friend of the Gelkis when you come back.

Khan Shaka. Warug of the Magram, pleased with your help after Gizmo for Warug, now wants the head of Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis. He means to stare at it and laugh at his enemy. In Magram Village, Warug tells you that you have helped the Magram and he likes you. Now he wants you to kill Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis, and bring him the head. He says he wants to stare at it and laugh at him. He expects you to stay on good terms with the Magram.

Kharanos. Kharanos is a bustling mountain settlement nestled in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh, just down the road from Ironforge. Serving as the primary hub for travelers leaving Coldridge Valley, the town hosts a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Situated along the central road of Dun Morogh, Kharanos is the first true town welcoming recruits arriving from Anvilmar. Despite the biting cold and biting winds, the settlement thrives thanks to local dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity. It centers around a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, renowned across the eastern mountains for producing some of the finest ale in Khaz Modan. Between bustling crafters and weary travelers seeking warmth, the town stands as the essential staging ground for business in the lower peaks.

Khazgorm's Journal. At Bael Modan, Prospector Khazgorm leads the Ironforge dwarven excavation in the southern Barrens. His field ledger records the Explorers' League's work on lands claimed by the Stonespire tauren. Prospector Khazgorm directs the heavy machinery and blasting that cut into the southern Barrens hillsides. His notes show an excavation far from the Explorers' League's promised search for knowledge: its work has displaced the Stonespire tribe. The tauren tried to settle matters peacefully, but the dwarves refused. Gann Stonespire wants the journal to understand the Ironforge presence in his homeland and find a way to break it.

Khelden Bremen. On the upper floor of Northshire Abbey, Khelden Bremen teaches human mages their first spells. He prepares novices to serve Stormwind through the arcane arts. Khelden Bremen teaches new human mages in a study on the upper floor of Northshire Abbey. While clergy and defenders pursue their work below, he shows novices how to focus and shape magical energy safely. His lessons prepare them for the road through Elwynn Forest and for further study in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

Kidnapped Elder Torntusk!. Primal Torntusk of Revantusk Village says Vilebranch savages carried off her mate, Elder Torntusk, in a bold midnight raid. Spies say he is alive and held prisoner atop Jintha'alor, and she asks you to save him. Vilebranch savages struck Revantusk Village at midnight and took Elder Torntusk, mate of Primal Torntusk. Her spies say he is still alive, a prisoner atop Jintha'alor, capital of the Vilebranch in the southern Hinterlands. Primal Torntusk fears the village could not bear losing him.

Kil'hala. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala teaches Horde tailors to work cloth. He also weaves nether-lace robes for young Horde mages who bring him locks of hair from Ashenvale's laughing sisters. Kil'hala trains tailors at the Crossroads, where Horde recruits and travelers can learn his craft. He teaches work with common spun bolts and garments suited to life on the dry plains. At Deino's request, he also makes nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair from the laughing sisters, the dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

Kill Grundig Darkcloud. At Grimtotem Post, Grundig Darkcloud leads the Grimtotem force that sacked Makaba Flathoof's home. After you strike down the ruffians and mercenaries, Makaba sends you after Grundig and his brutes. Makaba Flathoof survived the assault on his settlement along the Stonetalon trail, but his grief is still raw. After you prove yourself against Grimtotem foot soldiers, he points you toward Grundig Darkcloud, the one behind the bloodshed. Grundig commands a devoted band of brutes and led the slaughter that leveled the village.

Kin'weelay. Kin'weelay is a renowned Darkspear witch doctor stationed at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Dispatched directly from Orgrimmar, he offers mystical aid and counsel to the Horde vanguard in the jungle. His spiritual expertise is vital in unravelling dark mojo and aiding the rescue of young Yenniku. Recognized among the Darkspear as one of their most powerful practitioners of traditional witchcraft, Kin'weelay commands deep knowledge of spirits, hexes, and soul magic. When matters involving ancestral spirits or hostile troll enchantments arise, Horde scouts in Stranglethorn Vale look to him to pierce the magical veil.

Kindal Moonweaver. Kindal Moonweaver is a night elf secluded within a concealed nook in the craggy mountains of Feralas, just north of the Grimtotem Compound. Deeply troubled by the mistreatment of wildlife in the wilderness, she watches the aggressive tauren tribe below while seeking help to free captured beasts. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, sharing a mission to defend the forest's innocent creatures. Perched upon a narrow, winding mountain path partially hidden behind timber east of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver maintains a secret vigil over the valley below. While much of Feralas is contested between the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas, Kindal focuses on a more localized and immediate cruelty. Down in the hollow, the Grimtotem tribe operates a fortified compound, capturing and penning up local fauna for reasons far from benign. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and undo the suffering inside.

King of the Foulweald. Karang Amakkar orders a Horde strike against the Foulweald furbolgs southeast of Astranaar. Horde champions plant a war banner on the tribe’s sacred totem mound, drawing out Chief Murgut and killing him. Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost sees the corrupted Foulweald as a danger to the Horde. The tribe is smaller than the northern Thistlefur, but its members are fierce. Rather than wait for them to ambush Horde patrols, Karang orders a show of force meant to break their will.

Kirge Sternhorn. In the Barrens, Kirge Sternhorn guides travelers crossing central Kalimdor. The tauren keeps watch over the southern trails and sends new Horde adventurers north to the Crossroads. New wanderers often find the sun-baked Barrens daunting. Kirge Sternhorn watches over travelers south of the central trails, between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Marauding quilboar and fierce predators roam the savanna, and Kirge helps young adventurers find their footing. He ensures they seek out the greater Horde presence gathering to the north.

Klannoc Macleod. On Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod puts warriors to the test. The human warrior welcomes fighters from both the Alliance and the Horde who seek mastery of combat stances. Those who earn his respect are sent inland to face greater trials of strength. Klannoc Macleod puts seasoned fighters through their paces on Fray Island, off the Merchant Coast in the Barrens. Though human, he leaves Alliance and Horde quarrels aside. He judges each contender by grit, blade work, and resolve under fire.
