text.enUS: Klaven Mortwake's Journal. Inside a chest from Duskwood, Klaven Mortwake's Journal records the Defias Brotherhood's search for a way to raise the dead. SI:7 operatives recovered it from the Defias tower in northeastern Westfall. Master Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's intelligence service, SI:7, and sought Mortwake's journal to trace the Brotherhood's wider alliances. The notes confirm experiments in reanimation and illicit support linking Duskwood, the Venture Company, and the Defias. For rogues serving the crown, recovering the research marks a step toward mastering poisons.

Klaven's Tower. Agent Kearnen watches Klaven's Tower from a camp in Westfall. Strange shipments and altered guards point to a threat inside the Defias Brotherhood. Near the river at Westfall's southeastern edge, Klaven's Tower rises north of the Dagger Hills. The Defias Brotherhood claims the stone spire, though its human thieves and brigands are common across the plains. Agent Kearnen has watched it alone for weeks and noticed strange developments. A bizarre shipment recently came straight from Duskwood's shadowed woods. Monstrous, deformed sentries escorted it, unlike any ordinary highwaymen.

Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower, also called the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

Klockmort Spannerspan. Furen Longbeard sends fire-hardened mail findings from Stormwind to Klockmort Spannerspan in Ironforge. The dwarf smith shares his discoveries with his gnomish colleague in Tinkertown. Furen Longbeard has forged fire-hardened mail and gathered his findings for a fellow craftsman. He trusts you to carry his notes from Stormwind to Ironforge, then into Tinkertown, where Klockmort Spannerspan works as a gnomish blacksmith.

Klockmort's Creation. In Tinker Town, Klockmort's Creation takes shape through a new forging method. Gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan uses the rigorous technique devised by master armorsmith Furen Longbeard to make armor from raw materials. Klockmort Spannerspan works in Tinker Town, where dwarven armor is usually forged at the Great Forge. With Furen Longbeard's rigorous methods, the gnome blacksmith finishes a pair of armored gauntlets. Dwarven metalworking and gnomish mechanical skill meet in gauntlets made to endure punishment that would crush ordinary steel.

Klockmort's Essentials. In Darnassus, Mathiel carries Klockmort Spannerspan's urgent plea across the sea. Bound to his post, Mathiel asks Alliance travelers to go to Ironforge and find his gnome friend in Tinkertown. Mathiel carries Klockmort Spannerspan's plea from Darnassus to Dun Morogh. Klockmort needs bold allies for a venture into Gnomeregan, but Mathiel cannot leave his post to travel to the mountain kingdom. From the Warrior's Terrace, he asks capable Alliance travelers passing through Darnassus to make the journey in his place.

Knights of the Silver Hand. The Knights of the Silver Hand are the legendary order of holy paladins founded after the First War to combine martial combat with the healing and smiting power of the Holy Light. Though their original northern chapter was broken during the fall of Lordaeron, surviving knights carry on their sacred vows in Stormwind and Ironforge, while scattered remnants battle the undead in the northern Plaguelands. Following the destruction of Stormwind during the First War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol recognized a dire flaw in the Alliance's defenses: the clerics of Northshire were devoted and skilled healers, but they lacked martial training and fell easily on the front lines. To ensure holy warriors could endure the brutal combat of the Second War, Faol and his premier student, Uther the Lightbringer, founded the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Faol recruited both battle-hardened knights willing to learn devotion to the Light and devout clerics willing to bear plate armor and warhammers.

Knowledge in the Deeps. Knowledge in the Deeps is an Alliance quest offered by Gerrig Bonegrip in Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. He tasks adventurers with trekking across the sea to the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale to recover the ancient Lorgalis Manuscript. Beneath Bonegrip's scholar veneer lies an ominous agenda tied to dark entities and apocalyptic prophecy. Hidden away in the damp reaches of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip presents himself as a devoted collector of ancient texts. Yet his scholarly pursuits carry a distinctly sinister undertone. Bonegrip is not interested in mundane history or civic chronicles; he explicitly hunts for forgotten lore capable of opening doorways and awakening 'Those Who Sleep.' His talk of surviving beyond 'the end days' marks him as an eccentric—or a dangerous devotee of shadowy, slumbering powers.

Kobold. Kobolds are diminutive, rat-like subterranean humanoids found scuttling through mines and caverns across Azeroth. Notorious for their obsessive devotion to the tallow candles strapped to their heads, they are individually cowardly but dangerous in swarms, fiercely defending their dig sites against any who threaten their light. Standing barely four feet tall, kobolds are filthy, subterranean scavengers who spend their lives delving into the earth. Though they possess low-light vision, the deepest shafts are pitch-black, compelling every kobold to affix a crude candle to their head. While cowardly when cornered alone, kobolds breed in massive numbers and work with relentless energy. When agitated, their rat-like tails whip violently, and they overwhelm intruders in frantic mobs, beating foes to death with heavy iron mining picks.

name.frFR: Le nettoyage du camp des kobolds

text.enUS: Kobold Camp Cleanup. At Northshire, Kobold Camp Cleanup puts new recruits to their first test defending Stormwind's borders. Marshal McBride sends volunteers after kobolds in the northern woods, where their growing numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and novice training. In recent years, Stormwind's forces have grown thin. With the King missing and royal garrisons scattered, wild creatures and opportunists press at civilization's edge. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey. He depends on fresh volunteers to keep threats from disrupting the abbey or endangering the surrounding vineyards.

Kobold Candles. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle seeks candles from kobolds that have overstocked Elwynn Forest's mines. Visiting from his shop in Stormwind, the alchemist needs their thick wax, and the errand introduces adventurers to the subterranean pests encroaching on the kingdom's valuable gold veins. William Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary with his brother in Stormwind City's Trade District. Wax is always in short supply as he brews remedies, ointments, and concoctions. Instead of buying polished candles from city merchants, Pestle turns to the vermin in Elwynn. The kobolds carry hefty lumps of tallow and wax on their brows, ready for an adventurer willing to pry them loose.

Kodo Graveyard. The Kodo Graveyard is a sprawling expanse in central Desolace littered with the massive, bleached remains of ancient beasts. By instinct or tradition, aging and dying kodos make a final pilgrimage to this desolate hollow to collapse among the ribs of their ancestors. Sprawling across the grey earth of Desolace, the Kodo Graveyard holds the colossal skeletons of ancient beasts, some far larger than any living kodo seen today. Dying kodos wander here to spend their final breaths among centuries of accumulated remains. This sacred peace is fragile: scavengers prowl the perimeter, and those who disturb the calcified ribs and skulls risk stirring furious kodo spirits from the dust.

name.itIT: La Sacca di Pelle di Kodo

text.enUS: Kodo Hide Bag. Kodo Hide Bag is a trade quest offered by Veren Tallstrider, a skilled tauren leatherworker atop the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. In exchange for fundamental crafting supplies, he passes on the traditional plains technique for stitching durable travel packs from sturdy beast hide. It serves as an early rite of passage for apprentice leathercrafters in Mulgore. Perched on Thunder Bluff's crafting rises, Veren Tallstrider upholds the long-standing nomadic tradition of wasting nothing from the hunt. To earn his tutelage, an aspiring leatherworker must present him with cured light leather and sturdy thread. By demonstrating their competence with foundational materials, apprentices prove they are ready to craft goods worthy of carrying survival gear across Kalimdor's rugged expanses.

Kodo Horn. In the Barrens, Kodo Horns are gathered from the roaming kodos. Tonga Runetotem uses them in herbal remedies for poisoned wildlife. Across the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem uses intact kodo horns in his herbal remedies. He works from the Crossroads, where the horns help strengthen his salves. Chips and fragments lack the strength he needs, so he gathers whole horns from mature kodos wandering the plains.

Kodo Liver. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn needs Kodo Liver for a strange ale. He learned to brew trogg ale from the wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout. Kodos roam the Barrens, where tauren and predators hunt them for their hides and meat. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn uses a fresh Kodo Liver with thunderhawk saliva glands and lightning glands to make trogg ale. Chen Stormstout taught Drohn the recipe, and Drohn says the blend packs a potent kick for adventurous travelers. The ingredients come from the wilds of central Kalimdor.

Kodo Rock. Young tauren shamans are directed to Kodo Rock on Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. The stone rises among Mulgore’s grasses, easy to miss against the rolling land. Kodo Rock marks the straight path between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine, where hostile quilboar hold territory. Worn earth circles its base. Its profile recalls the kodo beasts that wander the grasslands, though it is smaller than the bluffs around Red Cloud Mesa. For tribesfolk crossing Mulgore’s windswept plains, the stone offers a quiet landmark.

Kodo Roundup. At Scrabblescrew's Camp in Desolace, Smeed Scrabblescrew is expecting a caravan and wants five tamed kodos ready for it. You carry Smeed's kodo kombobulator out among the ancient, aged and dying kodos, and lead the ones it tames back to the camp. Bibbly believes no other goblin in Desolace knows how to turn a profit. Smeed Scrabblescrew disagrees: the one caravan willing to brave this land depends on Smeed, and Smeed has formed a partnership with Cork and Rigger. The caravan is due at the camp shortly.

Kodobane's Head. Near the Forgotten Pools, Barak Kodobane's severed head proves the cunning chieftain's death. The orc warlord Regthar Deathgate receives it as proof that the centaur threat there has been broken. Kolkar bands in the Barrens have long been divided, but ambitious warlords now threaten to gather them into an army. Barak Kodobane made his camp by the lush waters of the Forgotten Pools, where the oasis offers vital resources and nearby paths lie open to raids. Regthar Deathgate, stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads, demands Kodobane's severed head as proof that this commander can no longer rally his kin against the Horde.

Kolkar Crag. Kolkar centaur watch the southern Durotar flats from Kolkar Crag, a gorge they have claimed for their raids. Warlord Kolkanis leads them against nearby Horde settlements. Kolkar centaur hold a fortified gorge in southern Durotar. They guard its natural choke points and watch the surrounding flats for openings in orc and Darkspear holdings. Scouts and marauders range from the crag, probing those defenses. For young warriors training in the Valley of Trials and patrols along the southern coast, this is the nearest organized centaur threat.

Kolkar Leaders. Kolkar Leaders begins a campaign led by the orc Regthar Deathgate to crush rising centaur warlords in the Barrens. The nomadic Kolkar have plagued the tauren for generations, but newly emerged chieftains are organizing their disorganized bands into a genuine military threat. Regthar tasks champions of the Horde with cutting down Barak Kodobane at the Forgotten Pools before his influence can spread. For countless years, the horse-bodied centaur have terrorized Kalimdor, driving the nomadic tauren nearly to extinction before Thrall's Horde arrived to turn the tide. In the Barrens, the dominant Kolkar tribe generally roams in scattered, fractured marauding parties. Recently, however, aggressive chieftains have begun uniting the disparate bands, turning simple raiding parties into a cohesive military threat capable of contesting the Horde's fortified outposts.

Kolkar clan. The Kolkar are an aggressive clan of centaur native to central Kalimdor, claiming descent from the legendary first Khan, Kolk. They maintain strongholds in Desolace and across the Barrens, frequently raiding Horde settlements and fighting anyone who crosses their path. The Kolkar take their name from Khan Kolk, the legendary first centaur khan born from the union of Zaetar and Theradras. Driven by a deep hatred for other races and their fellow centaur clans alike, the Kolkar distinguish themselves by their red markings and an absolute refusal to form alliances. Historically based out of their ancient village in eastern Desolace, the restless spirit of Khan Kolk still wanders the subterranean depths of their ancestral lands.

Kor'ghan. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan watches over remedies and toxins. The Darkspear troll stands outside Rekkul's Poisons and seeks help preparing antidotes for Durotar’s venomous predators. Kor'ghan keeps watch over remedies and toxins outside Rekkul's Poisons in Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow. From the capital, he sends travelers into Durotar’s red canyons to gather venomous components from scorpids. He needs them to prepare antidotes for the dangers of the wilderness.

Kormek's Hut. Kormek's Hut is a remote, ramshackle dwelling sitting amid the barren flats of north-central Desolace. Despite its desolate surroundings and mysterious namesake, it currently shelters an eccentric pair: an oddly peaceful cultist and a goblin obsessed with harvesting kodo bones. Perched out in the arid wastes of north-central Desolace, this small hovel is named after a figure whose whereabouts and identity remain completely unknown. Instead of Kormek, travelers stumbling upon the hut encounter an unusual pairing living out in the middle of nowhere: Willow and Bibbly F'utzbuckle. Inside the hut sits Willow, a member of the otherwise hostile and nihilistic Twilight's Hammer who curiously treats outsiders with calm hospitality. Outside, a pen littered with sun-bleached kodo bones serves as the personal dance floor and staging ground for Bibbly, an excitable goblin captivated by the commercial potential of bone scavenging.

Korran. At the Crossroads, Korran watches the Barrens for threats to the Horde. The Darkspear troll serves Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar and studies the silithid emerging across the scrublands. At the Crossroads, Korran watches for threats beyond the quilboar and centaur clans. Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar stationed the troll scout there to observe changes in the land. Korran coordinates the gathering of intelligence for the Horde's leadership.

Kravel Koalbeard. Kravel Koalbeard is a scheming dwarven entrepreneur and con artist stationed out at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Rather than cheering purely for the love of the sport, he views the fierce gnome and goblin racing rivalry as a golden opportunity to fill his pockets. From scavenging stray machine parts to fixing race results through blackmail and booze, Kravel is always hunting for his next profitable scheme. While most spectators and crew members at the Mirage Raceway are consumed by mechanical rivalries and the roar of rocket engines, Kravel Koalbeard has his eyes squarely on everyone's coin purses. He is an opportunist who operates in the dusty cracks of the raceway encampment, quick to offer contracts and favors that rarely have clean motives. Kravel sees the high-stakes friction between gnome and goblin engineers not as an inspiring competition, but as a fertile ground for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

Kravel's Crate. Kravel's Crate is a heavy package dispatched by Kravel Koalbeard from the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Destined for the Nesingwary expedition in Stranglethorn Vale, it contains specialized hunting ammunition designed to bring down the jungle's deadliest game. Handed out by the shrewd entrepreneur Kravel Koalbeard at the Mirage Raceway, Kravel's Crate represents an unfinished business transaction across continents. Ordered weeks prior by a wealthy dwarven patron, the shipment was delayed long enough for its buyer to depart Kalimdor entirely. Rather than lose out on the favor of a wealthy customer who already paid for forwarding, Kravel entrusts passing adventurers to haul the crate all the way to northern Stranglethorn Vale.

Krazek's Cookery. Corporal Kaleb's mechanical cooking pot, bought off a goblin trader in Booty Bay, was a marvel until it broke. Kaleb asks you to take it back to the goblin Krazek for mending. Corporal Kaleb does most of the cooking for the camp. It used to be heavy work until Kaleb bought a mechanical pot off a goblin trader in Booty Bay, and the pot spared Kaleb hour after hour. Then it broke. Krazek's Crock Pot must go back to the goblin Krazek to be fixed, and Kaleb hopes you will carry it there.

Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk. At the Crossroads, Thork seeks proof that Kreenig Snarlsnout has fallen. His tusk marks the end of the Razormane leader's attacks on Horde caravans in the northern Barrens. Horde caravans traveling west from Durotar face constant attacks in the Barrens. Those raids grew bolder under Kreenig Snarlsnout, a fierce Razormane leader. Thork, commander of the Crossroads watch, ordered Kreenig killed to disrupt the quilboars' coordination. His tusk offers proof that the leader is dead and insults the Razormane, weakening their resolve and leaving their fighters without central direction.

Kreldig Ungor. Kreldig Ungor is an enterprising dwarven operative representing Reclaimers Inc., stationed high among the crags of Nijel's Point in Desolace. Tasked with managing field operations in the barren wasteland, he hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and secure valuable local reagents. His salvage and recovery contracts make him a central contact for travelers navigating the hostile region. Nijel's Point offers the Alliance a rare sanctuary amid the blighted canyons of Desolace, making it an ideal staging ground for commercial opportunists like Kreldig Ungor. Representing Reclaimers Inc., Kreldig has ventured far from the safety of Khaz Modan into a desolate wilderness contested by centaur clans, demons, and the Horde. Where others see ruin and ash, Kreldig sees untapped profit and lost assets ripe for recovery.

Krolg. South of Mystral Lake, Krolg lives uncorrupted in an isolated hut in Ashenvale. Cast out from the Foulweald tribe, he kept his sanity when his kin fell to demonic madness. He speaks only with those who appear to be furbolgs. South of Mystral Lake, Krolg remains lucid and untouched by madness. Most Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale have succumbed to the demonic taint left by the Burning Legion. In his secluded shelter, Krolg keeps a cautious vigil over the forest. He witnessed his brethren descend into senseless violence, and now speaks only with beings who appear to be kin.

Krom Stoutarm. In Ironforge, Krom Stoutarm studies the darker arts in the Hall of Explorers. A dwarven scholar and warlock, he reads arcane texts and demonic rites in the library, and guides Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Krom Stoutarm pursues occult lore in the Hall of Explorers. While dwarven archaeologists there focus on picks, shovels, and titan artifacts, Krom studies massive tomes and the rites used to bind demons. His work gives a warlock’s craft a place within Ironforge’s mountain halls, though many distrust those arts.

Krusk. At Tarren Mill, Krusk coordinates the search for his captured scouts and the Syndicate's relics. Sent by Warchief Thrall to investigate Durnholde Keep, he survived an ambush that scattered his team. Krusk leads the effort from Tarren Mill after a failed strike at Durnholde Keep. Warchief Thrall sent him and a small team to scout Syndicate activity and recover relics tied to the fortress's grim past. The human outlaws were more entrenched and coordinated than expected, and an ambush inside the crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scouts. Krusk fought his way out. Drull and Tog'thar were taken captive and locked within the ruins, while Gol'dir, the expedition's leader, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Krusk now directs Horde forces to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and free his trapped comrades.

Kul Tiras. Kul Tiras is an insular maritime human kingdom situated on an island archipelago in the Great Sea, west of Dun Morogh and Baradin Bay. Renowned for possessing the mightiest navy in Azeroth, it served as a cornerstone of the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. Following the fracturing of the old Alliance and tragic losses in Kalimdor, the island realm has largely receded into isolated waters. Kul Tiras blossomed into an unmatched seafaring power, sustained by an industrious merchant marine, rich fishing grounds, and a naval armada without peer in human history.

Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin watches the forest trails outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. The Darkspear scout guards the Horde encampment from night elf scouts. Outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin watches the forest for Alliance scouts. Silverwing Sentinels patrol the canopy and send swift outrunners across the border. Their task is to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Kuray'bin sends Horde fighters to hunt the outrunners before they can report to Silverwing Outpost, since scouts left unchecked can become an ambushing force.

Kurzen's Compound. Kurzen's Compound is a heavily fortified human settlement tucked into the hills of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Established by an expedition dispatched from Stormwind under Colonel Kurzen, the outpost has devolved into a rogue camp of cutthroats and wild beasts following their commander's descent into madness. What began as an official expedition into the untamed jungles of Stranglethorn turned into a nightmare when Colonel Kurzen lost his mind. Rather than fulfilling Stormwind's mission, the garrison broke away from the kingdom's authority, cutting ties with the crown and descending into tyranny. Today, the compound operates like a mercenary stronghold, complete with a functional lumber mill, stables for training captured Stranglethorn panthers and tigers as weapons of war, and an extensive cave complex known as the Stockpile where the rogue soldiers stash their plundered supplies.

Kurzen's Mystery. Brother Nimetz at the Rebel Camp wants to know what turned Colonel Kurzen to depravity. Suspecting that troll magic holds him, Nimetz sends you to the troll ruins of Stranglethorn to copy the legends written on four tablets. Colonel Kurzen was once a great and noble man, and Brother Nimetz means to learn what caused his fall into depravity. Nimetz suspects troll magic has a hold on the colonel. To test that, the old troll legends must be read, and they are carved on four tablets hidden among the troll ruins of Stranglethorn. You are asked to copy the markings from each tablet and carry the copies back.

Kuz's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Kuz's Skull marks the end of a feared Razormane raider. Kuz came from Razorfen Kraul and helped lead attacks on Horde outposts before a captive former kin sought vengeance. Kuz, Nak, and their chieftain Lok Orcbane led Razormane attacks across the southern Barrens. Sent from Razorfen Kraul, the three raiders struck travelers and settlements such as the Crossroads. Their betrayal of Mangletooth, a fellow quilboar, turned one of their own against them. They left Mangletooth to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo. From that cage, he revealed Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to kill the raider and take her head.

Kyle's Gone Missing!. Kyle's Gone Missing! is a local quest in Bloodhoof Village where Ahab Wheathoof asks passing adventurers to find his wayward dog, Kyle the Frenzied. Feeding the hungry pup a cut of tender strider meat soothes his temper and ensures his safe return home. In Bloodhoof Village, elder Ahab Wheathoof worries over his wayward pet, Kyle the Frenzied. While the title might sound alarming to outsiders, Kyle is Ahab's prized puppy who has slipped away onto the grassy plains of Mulgore. Ahab asks travelers passing through the settlement to track down his unruly companion and offer him a hearty meal to calm his wild spirits.

Kzan Thornslash. In the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to new Horde recruits. He is an orc merchant in Durotar. Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to young orcs and Darkspear trolls in the Valley of Trials. They are taking their first steps as Horde warriors. He offers basic hand axes, shortswords, clubs, and staves for recruits facing local wildlife and hazards.

Laced Pumpkin. At Apothecary Johaan's hand, Laced Pumpkin turns an ordinary gourd into a deadly test of Forsaken alchemy. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society seeks weapons against the Scourge and living human forces. In Tirisfal Glades, the pumpkin looks like ordinary produce salvaged from blighted soil. Apothecary Johaan in Brill treats it with experimental toxins meant to realize the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks weapons against the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south. Even a simple harvest can carry infection and chemical death.

Lack of Surplus. Dar is gathering supplies for the outpost by the beach in the east, where Tok'Kar has little time to spare between guard shifts and cooking for the soldiers. Dar asks you to bring Tok'Kar a shipment of sawtooth meat. Dar is collecting supplies for the outpost by the beach in the east. Tok'Kar does what is possible there, but guard shifts and cooking for the soldiers leave little time in the day. The soldiers enjoy cooking sawtooth meat when they can get it, and Dar has had no time to send them another shipment.

Lack of Surplus. Tok'Kar and the soldiers on the coast are stationed to guard Stonard against murlocs, or to send warning when the force is too large. Tok'Kar wants six sawtooth snapper claws and offers one of the outpost's weapons in thanks. With murlocs a threat along the coast, Tok'Kar and the soldiers are posted here to protect Stonard, or to warn it if the force is too large. That leaves little time for rest, and Tok'Kar could use more help. The claws of sawtooth snappers make fine weapons when properly prepared. Tok'Kar asks for six, and offers one of the outpost's weapons in return, grateful for the meat and the company.

Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once one of the night elf druids who followed Naralex in his ambitious effort to heal the Barrens, she was lost when her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare. Her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a drive to remake the land to match that twisted dream. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was one of Naralex's druids. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she followed him into the caverns. Her loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering her sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession.

Lady Sarevess. Within Blackfathom Deeps, Lady Sarevess works dark sorceries in the flooded ruins. Lady Sarevess performs rituals in a flooded grotto within the Pool of Ask'ar. The Twilight's Hammer cultists haunt the sunken temple too, pursuing their own worship deeper in the cavern.

Laird. At Auberdine's inn, Laird sells fish and cooking supplies to travelers along Darkshore's coast. Laird sells fish and supplies inside Auberdine's inn. Sailors, locals, and travelers come to him while Darkshore's waters churn with dangers greater than those along Teldrassil's sheltered shores. For anglers willing to cast from the misty beaches, the local catch can bring a handsome profit.

Laird's Response. Along Teldrassil's shores, Laird's Response carries a puzzle for Nessa Shadowsong. The fish there are larger and more plentiful than those along mainland Darkshore. Laird compares catches from across the Veiled Sea. Fish from Teldrassil's coast are larger and more plentiful than those from Darkshore's mainland beaches. In his reply to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird of Auberdine offers a theory: the newly planted World Tree's unusual presence and vitality may be changing the surrounding sea life. Travelers carry his letter across the water to Rut'theran Village, where the fisherfolk greet the news with wonder and quiet curiosity.

Lake Al'Ameth. South of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth's shores have turned perilous as the local plant life grows violent. Once a quiet haven with little more than a wooden jetty, the lake is one of Teldrassil's largest freshwater bodies. At Lake Al'Ameth, swarms of timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge. The lake lies just south of Dolanaar, where its calm waters and sparse settlement offer little sign of the danger ashore. An unnatural sickness spreading through Teldrassil has driven the plant life into a frenzy. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar send travelers to gather seeds and kill the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the forest.

Lake Creeper Moss. Around Lake Lordamere’s southern Dawning Isles, Lake Creeper Moss grows on aquatic beasts. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks the organic compound as a vital reagent for engineering a lethal new plague. Lake Creeper Moss grows on the hides of freshwater beasts in the waters by the southern Dawning Isles. Lordaeron’s blighted waters shape its unusual properties. Before Arugal’s curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard recorded the moss in his journal. He noted its resemblance to traces found on fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. Forsaken agents send recovered samples to the Apothecarium in the Undercity, where Master Apothecary Faranell uses them in his research.

Lake Elune'ara. Lake Elune'ara is the shimmering, sacred body of water that occupies the heart of Moonglade. Revering the Moon Goddess Elune, the lake serves as a place of spiritual reflection for the Cenarion Circle, though deep within its murky floor lies the dormant, corrupted demigod Omen. Framed by the moonlit groves of Moonglade, Lake Elune'ara provides serene waters said to be blessed by the White Lady herself. The lake lies at the spiritual center of the druidic haven, bordered by Nighthaven to the north and the shrine grounds of the Cenarion Circle. Initiates have long plumbed its tranquil depths to retrieve long-lost relics, attuning themselves to the currents of nature as they seek harmony with the land.

Lake Everstill. Murlocs and lake beasts now make Lake Everstill dangerous beside Lakeshire. Once known for calm fishing and clear mountain runoff, its waters and shores have grown perilous. Lake Everstill fills Redridge's central basin beside Lakeshire. Its clear waters run east toward Stonewatch, and a bridge crosses the lake at the heart of town. The lake has long supported local trade and drawn anglers seeking quiet. Now, wilderness threats have broken that calm along the shore.

Lake Falathim. At Lake Falathim, murlocs now overrun the western Ashenvale shore southwest of Maestra's Post. Night elves once came here to swim and fish, drawn by Elune's moonlight said to touch the water day and night. Lake Falathim lies southeast of the Zoram Strand, where the Kaldorei once swam and fished in peace. Local lore says Elune's gentle light rests on the water at every hour, by day and by night. Now ferocious murlocs have surged inland and seized the shores. Their numbers drive away travelers and scholars.

Lake Kel'Theril. Lake Kel'Theril is a vast, frozen lake nestled in the heart of Winterspring. Along its ice-locked shores stand ancient kaldorei ruins haunted by restless spirits who have lingered since the Great Sundering. Lake Kel'Theril is shrouded in eternal cold, its waters sealed under thick sheets of ice. Scattered across its surface and snowy banks are the shattered pillars and arches of ancient elven architecture. These are the remnants of Kel'Theril, once an outpost of the ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor. Rather than finding rest in death, the spirits of the fallen aristocracy wander the ice as tormented ghosts and specters, forever tethered to the tragic remnants of their former glory.

Lake Mennar. Lake Mennar is a tranquil body of freshwater nestled amidst the shattered ruins of Azshara. It is remarkably renowned as one of the exceedingly rare havens outside of Northrend where members of the blue dragonflight reside. While the perimeter teems with protective blue dragonspawn, the shores of the lake itself remain strangely serene. Situated in the ancient, broken landscape of Azshara, Lake Mennar serves as a secluded gathering ground for the blue dragonflight. Aside from Mazthoril to the north in Winterspring, it is virtually unheard of to encounter blue dragons in such numbers across Kalimdor. Blue dragonspawn tirelessly patrol the ridges and approaches circling the basin, fiercely guarding the waters. Yet for any wanderer daring enough to slip through this vigilant ring of sentries, the calm waters of the lake offer unexpected quietude, shielded from the arcane turmoil and roaming beast packs common to the rest of the peninsula.

Lake Mereldar. Lake Mereldar is a sprawling, contaminated body of water resting south of Corin's Crossing in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once part of the idyllic rural heartland of Lordaeron, its corrupted waters now spawn twisted elementals and rot beneath the lingering taint of the Scourge. Situated just south of the crossroads town of Corin's Crossing, Lake Mereldar was once a peaceful fixture of northern Lordaeron's countryside. Dotting its shores are the decaying ruins of an old homestead, an abandoned shack, and a dilapidated ferry that once carried local farmers and travelers across the gentle waters. With the coming of the Scourge and the plague of undeath, the lake fell into complete ruin. The surrounding soil withered, and the waters turned foul and poisonous.

Lake Nazferiti. Lake Nazferiti is a sprawling freshwater lake nestled in the dense jungle of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Fed by a vast river system stretching far north into the mountains, its waters are infested with ferocious crocolisks and snapping frenzies, while its shores host an industrial encampment operated by the goblin Venture Company. Lake Nazferiti sits along the Nazferiti River, one of the longest continuous waterways across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. The river traces its origins deep into the northern heights, tumbling down waterfalls from the Redridge Mountains and possibly originating as far inland as Deadwind Pass. Within Stranglethorn, the water widens into this murky lake, teeming with vicious predators like snapping river frenzies and ambush-hunting crocolisks that make casual swimming deadly.

Lake Skulker Moss. In northern Lake Lordamere, Lake Skulker Moss draws the Royal Apothecary Society's attention. Apothecary Berard identified it as an organic part of research into brewing a New Plague before Arugal's curse claimed his mind. Lake Skulker Moss is gathered from Lake Skulkers and Elder Lake Skulkers on the Dawning Isles. Before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard cataloged the plants and creatures of eastern Silverpine Forest. In his journal, he wrote that Lake Skulker and Lake Creeper mosses could stabilize or react with other ingredients. After Berard became Arugal's mindless servant, his journal was recovered from Pyrewood Village for Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel sent Forsaken champions to gather moss and a rare tumor from local Vile Fin murlocs, then deliver both to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

name.frFR: Grand-route de la Crête du lac

text.enUS: Lakeridge Highway. Travelers on Lakeridge Highway face ruin and danger along Lake Everstill's southern shore. Before the First War, this vital, heavily traveled road carried trade through Redridge; now gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage perilous. Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway carried goods and travelers through Redridge as a busy trade route along Lake Everstill's southern shore. In those peaceful days, travelers crossed between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under Stormwind's protection. The Horde's march shattered that safety, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate.

Lakeshire. Lakeshire's defenders face attacks from orcs, gnolls, and murlocs along Lake Everstill. Magistrate Solomon leads the town, while Marshal Marris commands its guard. Lakeshire once offered peace in the foothills east of Stormwind. Now it is the kingdom's hardest-pressed frontier. Blackrock clan orcs swept down from the north and overran the garrison at Stonewatch Keep. Dark wizardry stirred Shadowhide gnolls into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs also broke parts of the Everstill Bridge. Foreman Oslow and his crew struggle to mend the span under threat of attack. Murlocs crowd the lake's shores, while gnolls stalk the high passes. Lakeshire's defenders are close to breaking.

Lakeshire Inn. At Lakeshire Inn, travelers and townsfolk seek shelter as danger closes around Lakeshire. On Lake Everstill, the inn offers food, drink, and a place to hear news amid the town’s troubles. On the shore of Lake Everstill, Lakeshire Inn offers a short rest from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing against the town. Though Lakeshire’s military position grows more desperate, the tavern remains warm and welcoming. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna serve ale, wine, and hot meals to locals and travelers. Townspeople gather to trade news, ease their sorrows, and seek hired blades to defend the kingdom’s eastern border.

Lakeshire Town Hall. At Lakeshire Town Hall, Magistrate Solomon directs Redridge's affairs from the heart of Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls bring relentless threats to the lakeside settlement. Lakeshire Town Hall, an aging stone building, has been refurbished many times over the years. It stands prominently in Lakeshire and houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader who maintains order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Stormwind's military is stretched thin, and royal aid is scarce. The hall has changed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center, where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily.

Lakkari Tar Pits. The Lakkari Tar Pits are a series of foul-smelling, bubbling pools of thick black sludge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Situated just below the cliffs of Marshal's Refuge, they act as a natural death trap for unwary beasts and an incubator for hostile tar elementals. The Lakkari Tar Pits dominate the low ground of northern Un'Goro Crater, directly south of Marshal's Refuge. Thick, reeking pools of pitch entrap anything careless enough to step into them, quickly bogging down beasts and adventurers alike. The protruding bones of hundreds of prehistoric creatures break the black surface, bearing witness to generations of animals sucked into the mire. Opportunistic scavengers circle the margins waiting for trapped prey to exhaust itself, while living tar beasts, lurkers, and creepers rise directly from the muck to batter interlopers.

Lakota Windsong. Lakota Windsong is a young tauren held captive atop the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. After rejecting an unwanted proposal from Arnak Grimtotem, she was abducted by force and awaits rescue from the Grimtotem tribe's clutches. Not long after the Third War, Lakota Windsong was pursued by Arnak Grimtotem. Unwilling to join his clan or accept his courtship, she turned down his proposal. Arnak refused to take no for an answer; he returned under cover of night, slaughtered Lakota's brother when he tried to intervene, and carried her off into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Confined high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, she remains trapped under heavy guard while Arnak still insists on making her his bride.

Lakota'mani. At Camp Taurajo, hunters bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer after the hunt. The offering honors the mighty kodo's spirit and marks the hunter as an equal to its strength. Among the Barrens herds, Lakota'mani is a kodo of great size and endurance. In Taur-ahe, the tauren tongue, his name means “Earthshaker,” and his steps rumble across the plains. Tauren hunters track and defeat such a beast not for slaughter, but to meet the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife in a sacred hunt.

Land Ho!. At Faldir's Cove, the lookout Lolo greets you with news that Captain O'Breen's stop here will last far longer than planned. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, are lost, and Lolo suggests you speak with the captain. Lolo, ever on the lookout, spots you arriving at Faldir's Cove. Captain O'Breen had promised the crew only a few hours here, time enough to collect the treasure and head back to Booty Bay. Lolo doubts it will be so quick. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, now rest on the bottom of the sea. Anyone who means to stay is told to talk to the captain.

Land's End Beach. Land's End Beach is a desolate stretch of coastline at the far southern tip of Tanaris, effectively marking the southern edge of Kalimdor. Shielded by towering mountain ridges and vast ocean waters, it remains one of the most secluded and inaccessible shores on the continent. Tucked away behind the southern mountain ranges of Tanaris and the sealed titan gateway to Uldum, Land's End Beach represents the absolute southern edge of Kalimdor's mainland. Cut off from overland routes across the desert dunes, reaching this windswept coast requires swimming along the dangerous, fatigue-inducing open waters of the South Seas. The beach is a barren frontier of crashing surf, shifting sand, and quiet isolation, largely untamed by the cartels or desert explorers who dwell farther north around Gadgetzan.

Lanka Farshot. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot guides young tauren onto the hunter's path. He is stationed within the Red Cloud Mesa and teaches tracking, marksmanship, and survival on Mulgore's plains. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot welcomes new tauren called to the hunter's path. Fresh recruits arrive with an etched note that sends them to seek his counsel. Under his guidance, they learn ranged combat, how to track prey, and respect for the wild beasts roaming Mulgore's grassy plains. He prepares each young hunter to scout and provide for the tribe.

Lar Prowltusk. Southwest of Sen'jin Village, Lar Prowltusk watches the Durotar frontier. He guards the young troll settlement and sends travelers against nearby threats. Lar Prowltusk watches the coast southwest of Sen'jin Village. As a Darkspear sentinel, he helps guard the tribe's new home after its people fled their sunken island chain. Hostile neighbors keep harassing Sen'jin Village as the trolls work to secure a permanent home. Lar directs scouts and warriors to watch the coast and curb these attacks, especially those by the Kolkar centaur, giving the settlement room to breathe.

Lard Lost His Lunch. Lard, of the village of Revantusk in the Hinterlands, is hungry and frightened. A Vilebranch struck Lard during a private picnic, and Lard fled without lunch. You are asked to fetch it from an island to the north. Lard was picnicking at a secret spot when a Vilebranch, ugly and mean in Lard's telling, hit Lard with a big stick. Lard bolted for Revantusk and left the lunch behind. Now Lard is hungry, and afraid to go back.

Large Candle. In Elwynn's mines, kobolds carry Large Candles on their heads for light and wax. Their flames guide them through dark tunnels, and apothecaries value the wax. Kobolds use candle flame to find their way through the dark shafts beneath Elwynn Forest. They fasten the tapers to their heads, and Kobold Miners, Tunnelers, and Geomancers defend them fiercely from intruders. Though crudely made, the Large Candles carried in Fargodeep Mine and Jasperlode Mine hold valuable wax. Surface tradesmen cannot easily produce it in bulk, so the candles are both tools for the kobolds and a commodity for alchemists.

name.zhCN: 索兰鲁克宝珠的大碎片

text.enUS: Large Soran'ruk Fragment. The Large Soran'ruk Fragment rests in Shadowfang Keep, far from the other shards. Its broken orb once held a disgraced demon of the Burning Legion. Disgraced demons of the Burning Legion may be condemned to imprisonment in enchanted orbs. Mages and warlocks aligned with the Legion receive these vessels and draw on the fel forces trapped within. Even when an orb is shattered, its bound fiend's lingering essence still radiates power. Each fragment draws ambitious practitioners of shadow magic.

Laris Geardawdle. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle studies oozes across Azeroth. The gnome researcher gives his academic life to their strange nature and origins, and welcomes adventurers who bring him noxious slime samples. In the Library of the Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle studies how oozes begin. His dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings, but Laris searches the vile, gelatinous horrors of Azeroth for alchemical and biological secrets. He asks roving explorers to gather caustic samples from remote corners of the world. With them, he tests his unusual ideas about how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

Lariss Pavilion. Lariss Pavilion is an ancient elven structure tucked into the wilderness of Feralas just north of Camp Mojache. While once a peaceful retreat of classical night elf architecture, the surrounding forest has grown dangerous due to corrupted dryads, and an exiled Highborne mage now bides his time within its shade. Standing quietly on the bluffs north of Camp Mojache, Lariss Pavilion showcases the graceful stonework and towering archways of the ancient kaldorei empire. In its prime, it served the great city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Today, it offers a sheltered overlook above the dense canopy of Feralas, but the peace here is frail: the once-gentle dryads wandering the surrounding glades have fallen to madness and corruption, turning fiercely hostile to anyone who draws near.

Lars. At a camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars struggles to survive Duskwood with Sven Yorgen. The woods around them hold beasts, undead, and worgen. Lars keeps to a small camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, away from the uncertain safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is dangerous, and the surrounding woods hold ferocious beasts, undead, and worgen. He stays close to Sven Yorgen, trying to survive in the hostile forest.

Laughing Sister's Hair. In Ashenvale, laughing sisters' hair draws weavers seeking its natural magic. Kil'hala at the Crossroads uses the gathered locks to make enchanted robes. Near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale, laughing sisters are dryads whose hair holds natural magic. Dryads protect the woods and are linked to Cenarius and the night elves. Horde craftsmen prize their hair as a potent crafting material. Kil'hala, a troll tailor at the Crossroads, spins the locks into enchanted robes for Deino's promising pupils of the arcane.

Laughing Sisters. In Ashenvale, dryad hair is sought for an empowered robe. The experienced troll tailor Kil'hala at the Crossroads needs the enchanted locks to weave a mage robe, as Horde mages press against the woodland's native defenders. After securing water from Xavian, rising mages are sent by Deino in Orgrimmar to help craft their own enchanted vestments. These arcane garments need materials touched by raw magic. Dryad locks carry the forest's ancient vitality, giving them what is needed to weave intricate robes that shield and strengthen a caster.

Launch Bay. Hostile leper gnomes and corrupted machines hold Launch Bay, deep in Gnomeregan beyond the Hall of Gears. The underground airfield once served gnomish flying machines and bombers; now the city’s former hangar is under enemy control. Launch Bay’s two tiers once housed Gnomeregan’s aerial fleet. Ramps from the upper walkway lead to a central platform where flying machines and heavy bombers remain parked, left behind before the city was evacuated. Crazed leper gnomes now roam the flight decks, maintaining and guarding the idle war machines in place of skilled pilots.

Laurna Morninglight. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight teaches young night elf priests the rites of Elune. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides acolytes from Shadowglen in healing and spiritual practice as threats gather in Teldrassil. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight guides young priests from Shadowglen. As new initiates travel farther into Teldrassil, she teaches them to deepen their bond with Elune. Her lessons join healing with defensive rites, skills needed in an increasingly hostile wild.

Lazy Peons. Foreman Thazz'ril sends new Horde recruits across the Valley of Trials to wake sleeping peons. Their work keeps lumber moving to Durotar's settlements. Durotar's new homes need timber, stone, and hard labor. Peons, orcs with little skill in battle, carry much of that burden and keep the Horde supplied with workers. In the Valley of Trials, the heat and grueling work leave Foreman Thazz'ril's crews seeking shade beneath trees for unauthorized naps.

Leaders of the Fang. Leaders of the Fang is a pivotal Horde quest tasked by Nara Wildmane from the heights of Thunder Bluff. It directs adventurers into the Wailing Caverns to strike down the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang and retrieve their twisted dream gems. Halting these rogue druids is essential to preventing their serpentine nightmare from permanently overtaking the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex ventured into the subterranean springs of the Wailing Caverns with a selfless ambition: to use the Emerald Dream to restore lush vitality to the arid Barrens. Tragically, when his slumber took root, his dream turned into a waking nightmare. The acolytes who accompanied him lost their devotion to nature's harmony, succumbing to the nightmare's corruption and adopting the mantle of the Druids of the Fang.

name.esES: El libro de contabilidad de Tanaris

text.enUS: Ledger from Tanaris. After Caught!, the occupant of the wooden outhouse in Searing Gorge offers you a small job taken on in Tanaris. Krinkle Goodsteel in Gadgetzan wants certain things found in the gorge and a few other places, and you are to collect them and bring them to him. Having been helped, the occupant recalls a little job taken on while in Tanaris. Krinkle Goodsteel of Gadgetzan wants a list of things gathered, some from this gorge and some from elsewhere. Goodsteel's ledger will be slid under the door for you, and you are to carry it, along with everything on it, to Goodsteel in Tanaris.
