text.enUS: Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle. Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle marks the collection of a mysterious package held on your behalf. Left behind by an unidentified messenger, the parcel was narrowly saved from being dumped into the sea before reaching your hands. A mysterious parcel addressed specifically to you was dropped off with an unwilling caretaker. The unknown courier insisted you would arrive to collect it, leaving so swiftly that the receiver could not even refuse delivery. Fortunately, you arrived just before the unclaimed box was tossed into the ocean alongside the evening's refuse.

Legacy of the Aspects. Legacy of the Aspects is an ancient tome hidden deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in southern Ashenvale. Retrieved during a Horde trial of the intellect, the volume contains essential lore concerning the Great Aspects that shaped ancient Azeroth. While earlier trials set forth by tauren elders test physical endurance and resolve, the pursuit of Legacy of the Aspects is designed to challenge the mind. Tasked by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to the Talondeep Path in the Stonetalon Mountains, an aspirant must delve into the haunted barrow dens of Dor'Danil. Guarded by the restless spirits of fallen druids and the vicious creatures that slew them, the ancient text rests upon a stone pedestal. Claiming the volume is only the first step; the seeker must commit its contents to memory before relinquishing the book, as they are tested on its historical lessons.

Legging It. Legging It is a quest focused on clearing a dangerous southern path to protect working peons. Threats along the roadway had frightened the labor force into halting their travels, stalling essential duties. By driving back the dangers, adventurers restore safe passage and enable the workforce to return to their assignments. Legging It addresses a disruption in local labor operations where peons became too frightened to journey southward. Rather than performing their assigned tasks, the workers refused to risk travel along the road due to looming perils. By intervening to push back threats along the path, travelers restore enough security for overseers to send their crews back to work.

Lelanai. In Darnassus, Lelanai cares for the night elves’ saber mounts in the Cenarion Enclave. She offers nightsabers and swift war beasts to her kin and trusted allies of the city. Lelanai tends the great cats of Kalimdor in the Cenarion Enclave, beside riding instructor Jartsam. Night elves have long bonded with the fierce predators of northern forests. They train nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged ground with a predator’s grace. In the capital, Lelanai provides these mounts to riders.

Leonid's Letter. Leonid's Letter is a delivery quest directing travelers into the depths of Undercity. Wary of entering the Forsaken capital himself due to a strained past with Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Leonid hires an impartial courier to deliver a message to Glix Xizzix, an old goblin acquaintance stationed in the Trade Quarter. Leonid needs a courier to transport a sealed letter to an acquaintance in Undercity. Because of past friction and a fraught relationship with Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Leonid chooses not to walk the halls of the Forsaken capital himself, entrusting a traveling neutral party to pass past the city's guards without raising alarm.

Leper gnome. Leper gnomes are the tragic, mutated survivors of Gnomeregan's catastrophic irradiation during the Third War. Maddened by toxic fallout and lingering fumes, most have sworn fealty to the usurper Mekgineer Thermaplugg, fiercely defending their ruined city against all outsiders. When trogg invaders breached Gnomeregan during the Third War, Mekgineer Thermaplugg advised High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to flood the city with radioactive toxins. Thermaplugg claimed the poison would exterminate the troggs while sparing the gnomish population. Instead, the catastrophe wiped out eighty percent of the city's inhabitants. Those who survived within the sealed lower levels were warped in mind and flesh by toxic fallout, mutating into pale, pustulant wretches dubbed leper gnomes.

Lessons Anew. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends Alliance druids from Darnassus to Moonglade for training. There, Dendrite Starblaze begins their instruction in cleansing venom and toxins. Druids learn from Cenarius, the demigod whose teachings and blessings bind them to the living world. His gifts include the power to cleanse venom with a simple incantation. Such power is not given lightly. Before young druids can wield it, they must learn the hard, ordinary work of fighting toxins without nature's magic.

Lessons Anew. At Thunder Bluff, Turak Runetotem sends young tauren druids to Moonglade to learn how to cleanse natural and unnatural poisons. The sacred haven is where apprentices begin mastering that art under Dendrite Starblaze, a night elf druid, as real poisonings demand more than practice. Cenarius gave druids the power to purge virulent toxins with an incantation, and their charge is to protect the wilds. Turak Runetotem teaches that such magic needs a firm grounding. Before a druid uses it to clear a blight, they must understand venom’s physical toll and learn to treat it by ordinary means.

Lethlor Ravine. Lethlor Ravine is a jagged, rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Badlands. It serves as a perilous roost and breeding ground for the black dragonflight, swarming with aggressive whelps and mature drakes. Carved deep into the scorched plateaus of the eastern Badlands, Lethlor Ravine is one of the most hazardous stretches of the desert. The craggy canyon walls provide a natural aerie for the black dragonflight, housing nests of fierce dragon whelps guarded by larger, fire-breathing drakes. Few travelers dare approach the valley floor, as the shadows overhead constantly betray the flight of winged predators circling among the rocky spires.

Letter to Delgren. Balthule Shadowstrike sends a warning from the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. His letter to Delgren the Purifier describes the Dark Strand cult's demonic work and must reach Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the Dark Strand cult gather around the Tower of Althalaxx ruins. He cannot destroy the cult alone, so he writes to Delgren the Purifier, his tutor in the Holy Light, asking for aid. The cult's foul rites threaten more than Darkshore's coast. The letter must travel south through the region into western Ashenvale, where Delgren works with night elf Sentinels against demonic and undead threats.

Letter to Jin'Zil. At the Crossroads, Letter to Jin'Zil carries word of Serena Bloodfeather's defeat. Darsok Swiftdagger sends it to the Darkspear witch doctor in the Stonetalon Mountains, telling him the northern Barrens are free of the Bloodfeather threat. After the harpies at the Dry Hills are wiped out and Serena Bloodfeather is slain, Darsok Swiftdagger writes to an old comrade. The harpies of the Barrens first roosted in the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. Darsok sends news of the fallen matron to Jin'Zil, a witch doctor, and introduces a promising warrior to the wider frontier.

Letter to Jin'Zil. Darsok Swiftdagger sends you from the northern Barrens into Stonetalon Mountains with news for his old friend, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. Serena Bloodfeather has fallen, and Darsok wants Jin'Zil to know. Darsok Swiftdagger sends you into Stonetalon Mountains after Serena Bloodfeather falls. The Witchwing and Bloodfeather broods came from the rugged ridges northwest of the northern Barrens, not the scrublands. Now that you have defeated Serena, Darsok asks you to carry the news of her death to his old acquaintance, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. Jin'Zil lives at the troll settlement of Malaka'jin, in the dangerous mountain peaks.

Letter to Jorgen. A sealed letter calls on Jorgen in Stormwind City to help with a missing diplomat. A diplomat bound for Theramore failed to arrive for talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore, and royal investigators moved quickly to keep the matter quiet. While official agents searched the capital, other channels stirred. The letter bypasses military bureaucracy and seeks out Jorgen, a gruff veteran who fishes beneath the great statues in the Valley of Heroes. It invokes old obligations and draws him into a covert inquiry amid rumors of a Defias conspiracy.

Letter to Stormpike. Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore holds a cleverly encrypted letter, and he knows someone in Ironforge who might decrypt it. He sends you with the letter to Prospector Stormpike, in the Library of the Hall of Explorers. Prospector Stormpike is to be found in the Library, in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Dibbs wants you to tell Stormpike that he sent you, and to show the letter. Dibbs reckons that if anyone north of Blackrock Spire can read it, Stormpike is the one.

Lewis' Note. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis sends an urgent supply requisition to a private armorer in Stormwind. A courier carries it by gryphon, asking for protective gear for the Westfall garrison. The People's Militia at Sentinel Hill gets little support from Stormwind's House of Nobles. Skirmishes with the Defias Brotherhood keep draining its meager stocks of gear. To keep the defenders outfitted, Quartermaster Lewis turns to private business instead of crown supplies. His requisition bypasses official military channels entirely. An Alliance courier must fly by gryphon to Old Town and present the order to Osric Strang, proprietor of Limited Immunity.

Library (Ironforge). In Ironforge's Library, the Explorers' League keeps its histories and recovered relics. The eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers holds books and artifacts gathered from across Azeroth. Dwarven scholars study relics and field reports from across the world in a great chamber of the Hall of Explorers. The Explorers' League keeps the Library, where shelves hold chronicles of the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Librarian Mae Paledust helps visitors find rare books and records.

Library Wing (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing gathers scholars and new priests and mages. Its quiet southern rooms offer instruction for those joining Stormwind’s defense. The Library Wing branches south from Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall. Dusty shelves, study lecterns, and quiet alcoves fill its rooms, where aspiring mages and priests learn the Arcane and the Holy Light. Across the abbey, martial recruits drill in the Hall of Arms. Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in faith and healing, while Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages to shape primal elemental energy.

Library Wing (Tyr's Hand). The Library Wing is a secluded hall inside Tyr's Hand Abbey, nestled within the Scarlet Crusade's heavily fortified redoubt in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once dedicated to holy study and contemplation, its shelves are now consumed by the zealous order's rigid dogma and propaganda. Members of the Crusade congregate here to study scripture and guard the sanctum's religious relics. Situated off the central nave of Tyr's Hand Abbey opposite the martial quarters, the Library Wing reflects the ideological core of the Scarlet Crusade. Within these quiet stone alcoves, priests and crusaders immerse themselves in theological tracts, militant doctrines, and writings twisted by years of relentless warfare against the Scourge. Rather than preserving open scholarship, the texts sheltered here fuel the Crusade's paranoia, reinforcing their conviction that all outsiders carry the taint of corruption.

Lich King. The Lich King is the lord and psychic master of the undead Scourge, ruling from the Frozen Throne far to the north in Icecrown. Originally forged by the demon Kil'jaeden from the spirit of the orc shaman Ner'zhul, the entity eventually lured Prince Arthas Menethil into corruption, culminating in their fateful union atop Northrend's icy peaks. When the orc shaman Ner'zhul attempted to flee the dying world of Draenor, he fell directly into the clutches of Kil'jaeden the Deceiver. The demon lord tore Ner'zhul's body to shreds but bound his tormented soul into a block of diamond-hard ice cast out of the Twisting Nether. Flung into Azeroth, the glacial monolith struck the northern wastes of Northrend, forming the Frozen Throne. Kil'jaeden intended the Lich King to forge an unstoppable undead vanguard that would dismantle the mortal kingdoms without succumbing to the infighting that ruined the Orcish Horde. Instead, armed with immense telepathic power, Ner'zhul immediately began plotting his own bid for freedom.

Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. At Southshore's inn, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle drinks and leaves his duties to others. He resents his posting in the Hillsbrad Foothills and hopes for a transfer south. Marshal Redpath has assigned him to deal with the murlocs along the coast. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle spends his days at Southshore's inn, far from the Stormwind he prefers. Sent north from Stormwind City, he finds the contested shores of Hillsbrad a poor fit. Rather than patrol the fields or coordinate defenses with Marshal Redpath, he drinks, grumbles, and waits for an order transferring him south.

Lieutenant Haggerdin. Lieutenant Haggerdin is a dwarven officer stationed upon the Headland in the Alterac Mountains. Standing watch outside the fortified gate to Alterac Valley, he acts as the primary recruitment and liaison officer for the Stormpike Guard. He evaluates aspiring Alliance champions and rewards those who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. Perched in the snowy heights of the Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the muster point for the Alliance's ongoing campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners flutter beside the massive wooden gate as recruits and veterans assemble under his watchful eye, preparing to plunge into the frigid warzone.

Lieutenant Lisande. On Thunder Bluff’s high mesas, Lieutenant Lisande watches for signs of the Scourge. Lieutenant Lisande serves the Argent Dawn from Thunder Bluff, where human faces are rare. The holy order watches for signs of the Lich King's taint, even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, Lisande calls on Horde champions to ride out and investigate before the Scourge can defile the sacred earth.

Lieutenant Nevell. Outside Ironforge in Dun Morogh, Lieutenant Nevell watches for the Scourge. The Argent Dawn officer coordinates local defenders and warns arriving adventurers of undead threats near the dwarven kingdom. Lieutenant Nevell watches Ironforge's snowy approaches for the Scourge. Though the Argent Dawn is best known for holding the line in Lordaeron's shattered Plaguelands, its watch reaches farther south. From outside Ironforge, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front when Scourge activity stirs in Dun Morogh's mountain passes. The dwarven city's borders remain under watch.

Lieutenant Orrin. At Stormwind's gates, Lieutenant Orrin watches for Scourge incursions and calls for scouts. The Argent Dawn officer stands in the Valley of Heroes, where he directs recruits to investigate undead threats beyond the capital. Lieutenant Orrin watches the road from the Valley of Heroes. The Argent Dawn is known for holding the front lines in the ruined north, but it also guards strongholds farther south, including Stormwind City. When necromantic magic stirs beyond the capital, Orrin sounds the alarm and rallies adventurers before the undead can threaten the people within.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Something gleams beneath the rubble: a badge bearing Theramore's sign, a golden anchor over white enamel, with the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe embossed under the anchor. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is the one to bring it to. Something gleams beneath the rubble. Brushing off the ash and debris reveals a badge showing the sign of Theramore, with Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name embossed below it. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore should see it, and will ask what turned up in the ruins of the Shady Rest Inn.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Captain Garran Vimes does not recognize the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe, and sends you to Adjutant Tesoran in Theramore, who looks after the records of the Theramore guard. Captain Garran Vimes cannot place the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Adjutant Tesoran keeps the records of the Theramore guard, covering its people as well as its equipment, and Vimes expects a look through those books to show who Reethe is.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Beneath the rubble lies a badge bearing Theramore's sign, a golden anchor over white enamel, with the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe embossed under the anchor. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to bring it to. Something gleams beneath the rubble. Brushing off the ash and debris reveals a badge showing the sign of Theramore, with Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name embossed below it. Krog at Brackenwall Village awaits it, and will ask if you have a lead on what befell the Shady Rest Inn.

Lifting the Curse. First Mate Fitzsimmons seeks to free his fallen crewmates from a restless curse. He believes a dark artifact aboard the wrecked Intrepid binds them, and Captain Halyndor's ghost guards the key to its strongbox. First Mate Fitzsimmons survived the Third Fleet's fate, but memories of his comrades haunt him by day and by night. He believes an evil object locked in the Intrepid's strongbox is tied to the undeath gripping his shipmates. The wreck is watched by Captain Halyndor, whose ghost guards the key to the strongbox.

Light. The Light is a boundless primal cosmic force whose energy connects and suffuses all living things across creation. Manifested in the mortal realm as Holy magic, it responds to willpower, meditation, and unyielding faith to mend flesh, shield allies, and purge darkness. The Light is an omnipresent force of living energy. When brought into Azeroth, it manifests as Holy magic. Its power flows through living souls as a connective tissue, binding mortal hearts together. While mortals often personify it as a conscious protector, the Light fundamentally answers the absolute conviction of the soul calling upon it.

name.esES: Capilla de la Esperanza de la Luz

text.enUS: Light's Hope Chapel. Light's Hope Chapel is a sacred sanctuary situated in the eastern reaches of the Plaguelands, serving as the primary redoubt and headquarters for the Argent Dawn. Once a secluded shrine of the Church of the Holy Light in the Eastweald, it now stands as an enduring bulwark against the Scourge. Originally a chapel of the Church of the Holy Light within the verdant Eastweald, Light's Hope Chapel endured the fall of Lordaeron to become a vital shelter in a blighted realm. When the zealous extremists among the survivors splintered to form the Scarlet Crusade, more temperate knights and priests banded together to establish the Argent Dawn. Choosing this secluded, hallowed site as their forward base of operations, the Dawn opened its doors to all races and factions—Alliance and Horde alike—united in the common crusade to purge the Scourge and reclaim the northern lands.

Lightforge Iron. In Menethil Harbor, Glorin Steelbrow seeks the lost cargo of an elven destroyer. The Flying Osprey carried rare Lightforge iron when it sank with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras during the Second War. The Flying Osprey sailed from Lordaeron with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras. The elven destroyer carried a precious cargo of Lightforge iron and traveled beside the fleet for safety. But the Dragonmaw clan's enslaved red dragons swept down from the sky. They set the fleet ablaze, sending sailors and sanctified metal beneath the waves.

Lightning Gland. In the Barrens, Lightning Glands are taken from stormhides roaming the plains. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet needs them for trogg ale, a fiery brew Chen Stormstout taught him to make. Stormhides roam the Barrens savannas among other predators touched by the elements. Their flesh holds lightning glands, organs charged with latent electricity. These glands are poor fare on their own, but brewers prize them for the sting they bring to a brew.

name.frFR: Auberge de la Fierté du Lion

text.enUS: Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers gather at the Lion's Pride Inn, Goldshire's tavern and community center in Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps the inn, a place to rest, meet others, and find work just south of Stormwind City. The Lion's Pride Inn anchors Goldshire at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps it by the old motto, “Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold.” Inside, warm hearths, strong drinks, and rooms welcome weary travelers from Northshire. Goldshire sits on trade routes between Stormwind, Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, making the inn an indispensable gathering place. Town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers meet there to share news and hire passing mercenaries.

Llane Wrynn I. King Llane Wrynn I was the ruler of Stormwind during the catastrophic First War, whose reign ended with the fall of the kingdom and his own tragic murder. A beloved and proud monarch, his steadfast refusal to believe his friend Medivh had betrayed humanity ultimately doomed his defense of the capital. Born to King Barathen Wrynn, young Prince Llane grew up alongside Anduin Lothar and Medivh. In their youth, the three companions ventured into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale and clashed with the Gurubashi trolls there. In time, Llane ascended to the throne as Stormwind's king.

Load Lightening. Pozzik, the head goblin engineer out at the Mirage Raceway, needs materials to shave critical ounces off his rocket-car chassis. Rather than relying purely on heavy metal plating, the goblins salvage hollow bones from local desert vultures to build sturdy, ultralight steering and structural rigs. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers is decided by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust is useless if a racer is weighed down by excessive bulk. While gnome teams obsess over intricate gears and brass fittings, the goblin crew led by Pozzik seeks ruthless pragmatic efficiency: stripping out dense iron framing and replacing it with lighter, hollow structural components wherever the frame permits.

Loading Room. In Gnomeregan's depths, the Loading Room is a dangerous place to pass through. The ruined chamber once staged cargo for the city's transit networks, but radioactive fallout and rogue machinery now threaten anyone who enters. The Loading Room once handled cargo for Gnomeregan's underground transit network. Before the city fell, goods passed through its staging bay on their way across the tinker capital. Now the room is caught in the ruin that has overtaken Gnomeregan. Radioactive fallout, invading troggs, and failing machinery make the area perilous. Techbot, a rogue mechanized construct, guards the vicinity. Gnome survivors and Alliance reclaimers who try to secure the perimeter must face that danger.

Loganaar. Loganaar is a night elf druidic instructor residing in the haven of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Dedicated to guiding initiates from both the Alliance and the Horde, he instructs young druids as they attune to the wild and prepare for the call of the Emerald Dream. Situated amidst the serene boughs of Nighthaven, Loganaar serves as a primary mentor to newly initiated druids traveling to Moonglade. Regardless of whether an initiate hails from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, Loganaar provides guidance in balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. He reminds his students that even within cold stone and unfamiliar lands, true tranquility must be found within oneself. He also acts as a welcoming guide for those journeying deeper into the Cenarion Circle's affairs, sending promising students to wanderers like Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater or deeper into ancient woodland rites.

Logging Rope. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, Logging Rope keeps the mills and machinery supplied. Furbolg tribes have stolen shipments across Ashenvale, leaving the Warsong to recover the line they need. Logging Rope shipments meant for the Warsong Lumber Camp have been stolen. The Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolgs intercepted the line before it reached the loggers. The tribes keep the ropes in their encampments across northern and central Ashenvale. Corruption has driven the furbolgs mad, and they fiercely defend their ancestral woods.

Lok's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Lok's Skull marks the fall of a feared Razormane leader. Lok Orcbane led fierce quilboar raids against Horde supply routes, and the skull is his severed head. Lok Orcbane led aggressive Razormane assaults on Horde supply lines in the southern Barrens. He emerged from Razorfen Kraul with his lieutenants Nak and Kuz. After betraying Mangletooth and leaving him captive at Camp Taurajo, Lok became known to orcish defenders for ruthless raids they struggled to contain. Mangletooth directs Horde champions to Lok's camp, where claiming Lok's skull avenges the captive and strikes at the leadership driving the Razormane offensive.

Lomac Gearstrip. In Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues gnomish inventions. He formulated the NG-5 explosive and keeps in contact with fellow researchers in Kalimdor. Lomac Gearstrip works on gnomish ordnance in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Like many gnomes who fled Gnomeregan's tragedy, he has brought his tinkering operations to the dwarven capital. His workshop focuses on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions meant to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds.

Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is a weathered diary found clutched in the skeletal remains of the dwarven explorer Henrig Lonebrow at the base of the Great Lift. Its pages detail the final grim journey of Lonebrow through the Barrens and point toward dangers lurking within Razorfen Kraul. Henrig Lonebrow met an unfortunate end near the base of the Great Lift connecting the Barrens to Thousand Needles. Lying abandoned on a rocky ledge, his skeletal remains still grip this weathered journal. The diary serves as a testament to his final travels and directs whoever discovers it to bring word to the night elf druid Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, the border outpost leading into Feralas. Lonebrow's notes shed critical light on the quilboar menace brewing in the southern barrens.

Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is an Alliance quest initiated by finding a weathered book held in the hand of a dead dwarf at the base of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. The notes detail his final journey and prompt the finder to deliver the volume west to a night elf druid stationed on the Feralas border. Near the base of the Great Lift, the massive mechanical elevator connecting the Barrens to the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, lies the body of Henrig Lonebrow. Clutched in his hand is a personal journal detailing his travels through this rugged territory. Left behind in a hostile desert dominated by centaur and tauren, his corpse serves as a grim warning of how unforgiving the canyon can be to isolated travelers.

Long Wash. Along Darkshore, Long Wash runs south from Auberdine toward Ameth'Aran beneath a gray sky. Murlocs now make its shore dangerous. Long Wash is Darkshore's shortest distinct stretch of coast, despite its name. Beneath the region's perpetual overcast skies, damp sand lies strewn with flotsam, driftwood, and sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. Crabs comb the surf, but travelers heading south from Auberdine must watch for murloc tribes camped along the water's edge. The murlocs attack anyone who enters the territory where they scavenge.

Longbraid the Grim. Outside fallen Dun Modr, Longbraid the Grim keeps watch over the northern Wetlands. He mourns his brother and the loss of the Thandol Span, while leading the surviving dwarves against the Dark Iron clan. Longbraid the Grim rallies the dwarven garrison near the bridge to the Arathi Highlands. The Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr in a sudden assault that devastated the defenders. Longbraid's brother died during the siege of the Thandol Span. Grief and hatred keep Longbraid at the northern boundary, where he directs travelers and surviving mountaineers in strikes against the Dark Iron advance.

Longshore. Along Westfall’s western edge, Longshore’s broad sands are claimed by hostile murlocs and broken ships. Longshore runs along Westfall’s western coast, a wide stretch of unbroken sand. Travelers find little peace there. Murlocs dominate the surf, with Old Murk-Eye among the feared leaders, and sunken ships, including ruined elven destroyers, lie in the shallows. Near the south, Daphne Stilwell’s isolated farm faces Defias bandits. Across the water, the Westfall Lighthouse stands within sight.

Longwalker Malah. Longwalker Malah is a missing tauren scout dispatched to survey the eastern borderlands of Mulgore on behalf of Bloodhoof Village. As an elite Longwalker answering directly to the High Chieftain, her sudden failure to return after three days prompts an urgent search to ensure both her survival and the safety of the valley. The Longwalkers serve as the eyes and ears of the shu'halo, renowned across the plains for their tireless stride and survival prowess. Pledged directly to High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, these elite scouts are tasked with traversing vast territories to gather intelligence and deliver vital messages. Though their ultimate loyalty lies with the High Chieftain alone, young Baine Bloodhoof occasionally calls upon their aid to safeguard the settlement of Bloodhoof Village and its surrounding pastures.

Look To The Stars. In Duskwood, Viktori Prism'Antras looks beyond the canopy for answers to the forest's curse. He trusts observation over arcane superstition and asks you to gather parts for a telescope drawn up by his gnomish associate. Viktori Prism'Antras sees Duskwood's troubles differently from many in fearful Darkshire. He doubts that black magic, curses, and restless dead alone explain the land's corruption. He believes answers may lie above the canopy. With blueprints from his gnomish partner, Cog, he plans to build an instrument for looking into the heavens.

Look To The Stars. In Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras seeks a mirror for the telescope he is building from Cog's blueprints. He sends you into southern Duskwood to find Mary, remembered for carrying a looking glass. Viktori Prism'Antras has the bronze tube for his telescope. Now he needs a mirror to guide and reflect light through it, as Cog's blueprints require. Fine silvered glass is hard to make while Darkshire faces shortages, so Viktori recalls Mary, a local woman known across the region for carrying a looking glass.

Look To The Stars. Viktori Prism'Antras needs Blind Mary's looking glass for his telescope in Darkshire. An Insane Ghoul took it to Tranquil Gardens Cemetery in southern Duskwood. Blind Mary once treasured an ornate looking glass. After an incident took her sight and sanity and left her a weeping spirit, she threw it into the dirt behind her family barn. Now the astronomer Viktori Prism'Antras needs the mirror for his telescope in Darkshire. The looking glass was taken long before he began studying the heavens.

Look To The Stars. Viktori Prism'Antras needs one final piece for his telescope in Darkshire. Its frame is built, but no local glass is large enough for the lens his plans require. Viktori Prism'Antras is building a telescope in Darkshire from plans by the gnome engineer Cog Glitzspinner. He has gathered brass tubes and sturdy mountings from local supplies, but the design calls for an unusually large focusing lens. Magnifying glasses and optical parts from Stormwind traders are too small, so Viktori looks beyond ordinary materials for the piece he needs.

text.enUS: Look at the Size of It!. You have come into a gigantic, ornate pillow that once belonged to Chambermaid Pillaclencher. Evonice Sootsmoker, in the Searing Gorge, is bound to want it. The pillow Chambermaid Pillaclencher kept is now yours. Evonice Sootsmoker will surely be eager to get hold of it. Bring it to her in the Searing Gorge and see what she offers you for the trouble.

name.frFR: Le point de vue d'un vieil ami

text.enUS: Look to an Old Friend. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to seek an unusual contact in Stormwind's Trade District. Noble corruption shields traitors from ordinary justice, so Shaw turns to the city's finest cheesemonger and his intelligence network.

Looking Further. Looking Further is an Alliance espionage mission directed by the wizard Theocritus via an enchanted conduit. To investigate tensions between the rogue mage Morganth and the Blackrock orcs, you must infiltrate the watch tower beside Stonewatch Keep and plant an enchanted glyph inside an unnoticed container. From his sanctum in Elwynn Forest, the wizard Theocritus maintains a vigilant watch over eastern Redridge through scrying magic. While monitoring the Tower of Ilgalar, he detects sudden contention between the renegade human warlock Morganth and the Blackrock orcs entrenched in Stonewatch Keep. Rather than working together against the Kingdom of Stormwind, these hostile factions are locked in conflict over an unknown prize, prompting Theocritus to intervene before the balance shifts.

Loramus Thalipedes. Loramus Thalipedes is a reclusive night elf demon hunter secluded on a remote isle off the coast of Azshara. Flanked by loyal felhounds, he dedicates his existence to destroying Razelikh the Defiler, directing seasoned champions through rituals to strike down the dreadlord. Perched on a solitary, storm-tossed island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes stands apart from the rest of his kin. He is a demon hunter—an exile who underwent the agonizing ritual of blinding himself to gain spectral sight. Surrounded by three towering felhounds named Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, Loramus watches the unseen currents of demonic corruption across Azeroth while keeping a watchful vigil over the shattered ruins of Azshara.

Lord Aliden Perenolde. Krusk wants Lord Aliden Perenolde dead, and the Warchief's pendant recovered. Perenolde's manor lies north, on Lordamere Lake; his mistress Elysa knows about the pendant. After Blackmoore's Legacy, Krusk says Perenolde must die and his foulness be ended. His manor lies north, on the shores of Lordamere Lake at Dandred's Fold. Once the deed is done, ask his mistress Elysa about Taretha's pendant, which the Warchief desires.

Lord Arkkoroc. Lord Arkkoroc is an ancient, towering sea giant who dwells within the ruined Temple of Arkkoran along the ragged coast of Azshara. Described by the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes as a lesser deity, he holds sway over the surrounding waters and commands lesser sea giants who serve as his sons. Reclining amidst the brine-crusted ruins of the Temple of Arkkoran, Lord Arkkoroc is far more than a typical sea giant. To hermits like Loramus Thalipedes, this colossal being is considered a lesser deity whose divine will shapes the surrounding waters. His sons patrol the crags and shallows around the sanctuary, enforcing his quiet dominion over Azshara's tempestuous shores.

Lord Baurles K. Wishock. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock lives among the petitioners and dignitaries. Barkeeps know him for unpaid tabs and a taste for strong drink, but his nights in the city’s underbelly brought him near darker dealings. Lord Baurles K. Wishock moves among petitioners and dignitaries in Stormwind Keep, where he belongs to the influential House of Nobles. Though his station is high, he often drinks in the Mage Quarter’s dive bars, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, and leaves large bills unpaid. There, he hears of a warlock coven practicing dark arts in cellars beneath the floorboards. Wishock sets out to have the tavern closed and asks fellow nobles for a formal investigation. Uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn is one of the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf druid of Naralex's noble order, which hoped to heal the Barrens, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Taking a lethal serpent guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before his fall, Cobrahn was one of the noble druids who followed Naralex. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Cobrahn accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Cobrahn's mind shattered alongside his brothers.

Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Darkshire's mayor, Lord Ello Ebonlocke, works from the Town Hall to keep order amid the growing danger. Stormwind gives little aid, and the town faces horrors from the surrounding woods. Lord Ello Ebonlocke governs Darkshire from the town hall as danger closes around the settlement. Darkshire was once part of the prosperous rural haven called Grand Hamlet. Now perpetual shadow hangs over it, while ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts press against its borders. Ello leads the Council of Darkshire and struggles to keep the remnants of civic life working. Stormwind offers little help as the town fights to endure.

name.zhCN: 格雷森·沙东布瑞克公爵

text.enUS: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker trains champions of the Light. A veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he guides promising knights and oversees the sacred trials senior paladins must complete to claim their holy chargers. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker leads the Silver Hand's work in Stormwind City and ranks among the Alliance's foremost defenders. A veteran of the order, he trains recruits in arms and tests their faith in the Light. When promising knights are ready, he sends them north to the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands. There, they aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is the master of Ravenholdt, an elite guild of rogues and assassins operating out of a secluded estate in the Alterac Mountains. He directs the league's clandestine operations, training promising operatives while waging a bitter war against the regional bandits of the Syndicate. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over the Assassin's League from his hidden manor nestled in the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he opens his halls to outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins regardless of allegiance, provided they exhibit exceptional skill and respect his authority. Under his command, the league acts as both a fraternity for master thieves and an independent syndicate for wetwork and espionage. Ravenholdt harbors a fierce hatred for the Syndicate—the band of disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws—and routinely directs his subordinates and visiting freelancers to sabotage their camps and plunder their assets.

name.zhCN: 玛克斯韦尔·泰罗索斯男爵

text.enUS: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus is the supreme commander of the Argent Dawn, stationed at their forward redoubt of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand from the Third War, he guides the coalition's crusade against the Scourge and orchestrates strikes into blighted strongholds like Stratholme. Maxwell Tyrosus rode alongside Uther the Lightbringer during the catastrophic Third War, guarding the exits of Andorhal when the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After the fall of Lordaeron, he cast his lot with the Argent Dawn, an order that welcomes anyone willing to stand against the Scourge, in stark contrast to the human-only zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade.

Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally one of the personal guards of the druid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before his corruption, Pythas was a seasoned night elf warrior who served among the druid Naralex's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Alongside his martial training, he took up the druidic arts in service of Naralex's dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures.

Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as one of the four leaders of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a druid of great power and prestige in the order of Naralex, he was twisted into madness when Naralex's dream became a nightmare within the subterranean springs. Now, he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect deep in the caverns where the corrupted Naralex lies slumbering. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was a druid of great power and prestige, one of the noble order led by Naralex that hoped to use the caverns' springs and the Emerald Dream to heal the Barrens. However, when Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis was among the druids whose minds fell to the emerging madness.

Lord Shalzaru. Lord Shalzaru is the tyrannical leader of the Hatecrest naga operating out of the Isle of Dread off the coast of Feralas. Ruling his serpentine followers with absolute cruelty, he oversees extensive excavations among the submerged and ruined elven settlements. His recent discovery of a strange, ancient relic has drawn the attention of outside investigators eager to wrest it from his grasp. Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga, directing their presence along the southern coast of Feralas. From his subterranean lair within a cavern on the Isle of Dread, he enforces his rule through cruelty and ruthless authority. Under his command, the Hatecrest scour the ancient ruins of ancient Kalimdor, searching for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left behind from the Sundering.

Lordaeron. Lordaeron is the great northern subcontinent of the Eastern Kingdoms, once the glorious heart of human civilization and the Alliance. Following the devastation of the Third War, its former kingdoms lie in ruins, contested by the undead Scourge, Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, and desperate remnants of the living. Lordaeron shares its name with the human city-state of Lordaeron, which rose in the north after the ancient Empire of Arathor and grew into the most powerful of the human kingdoms. Stretching from the rugged Arathi Highlands in the south across scenic forests and waterways up toward Quel'Thalas, the region nurtured thriving kingdoms like Lordaeron, Dalaran, Gilneas, and Alterac. It was historically celebrated for fertile farmlands in Tirisfal and Hillsbrad, mountain strongholds, and the sacred cradle of the Holy Light.

Lordamere Internment Camp. Lordamere Internment Camp is a former Second War detention facility perched on the heights overlooking Dalaran. Once built to confine lethargic orcs, the camp is now occupied by surviving Dalaran magi and guards alongside a treacherous band of Forsaken defectors. Following the Second War, the Alliance constructed internment camps across the northern kingdoms to contain the defeated orcish Horde. Lordamere was unique as the sole camp established within the Alterac Mountains, placed under Dalaran's jurisdiction. With the orcs long since liberated or fled, the camp today functions under Warden Belamoore as an outpost for Dalaran remnants studying dangerous magical relics.

Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake lies between Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains, its waters now shadowed by the undead. Once the northern heart of human life, its cold waters and islands are haunted by Scourge necromancers and feral murlocs. Lordamere Lake once joined the centers of human power in the north. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, Dalaran rose near the southern reach, and Alterac lined the eastern edge beneath its mountains. Merchant vessels and fishing boats crossed the broad lake without fear. After the devastation of the Third War, the lake became a natural barrier between the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine and the treacherous heights of Alterac.

Lorekeeper Raintotem. South of Red Rocks, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends Mulgore’s sacred burial grounds. He asks travelers to drive off Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Lorekeeper Raintotem tends his people’s sacred burial grounds near Red Rocks in Mulgore. Bristleback Interlopers disturb the resting place, and he asks travelers to drive them away so the ancestors may rest in peace.

Lorgalis Manuscript. The Lorgalis Manuscript lies hidden beneath Ashenvale in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. The ancient text concerns the Old Gods, and dark scholars covet its words about powers that sleep. The Lorgalis Manuscript lies at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, where long-dead elves once lived before their city fell. Lorgalis wrote of the Old Gods, who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained and sleeping. The text praises Aku'mai, a servant of the Old Gods who dwells in the Deeps. Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient beings sleeping deep beneath the world. The manuscript rests in a pitted iron chest among the flooded corridors, drawing the attention of cultists and shadow scholars alike.

Lorgus Jett. In Blackfathom Deeps, Lorgus Jett commands the Twilight's Hammer among flooded ruins. The Horde has marked him as a target. Lorgus Jett is a human among the Twilight's Hammer in Blackfathom Deeps. While many cultists there are orcs or tauren, Jett ranges from the upper Moonshrine Ruins to the tunnels beyond Gelihast, the murloc defiler. He coordinates the cult's rituals and violent ambitions in the ancient night elf ruins.

Loslor Rudge. At Steelgrill's Depot, Loslor Rudge keeps Dun Morogh's tinkerers supplied. His tools, parts, and munitions reach craftsmen across the snowy ridges, including gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot. Loslor Rudge supplies engineering goods from Steelgrill's Depot, just down the road from Kharanos. His stock includes copper modulators, bronze tubing, blasting powder, and spanners. Harsh weather and scattered tinker operations keep practical parts in demand, and Loslor works to keep local gearheads supplied. The wilderness between outposts makes deliveries perilous. A courier taking a shortcut near the Grizzled Den was driven off by wendigos, leaving behind an ammunition shipment meant for Loslor's valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot.

Lost But Not Forgotten. Misha Tor'kren waits at her homestead for news of her son, Kron. He went west to hunt crocolisks along the Southfury River, and she fears the worst. Misha Tor'kren lives at a farmstead northwest of Razor Hill in Durotar. Days ago, her son Kron set out west toward the Southfury River, along the Barrens border, to hunt its fierce crocolisks. Misha warned him how deadly the beasts were, but pride drove him to leave and prove his strength. No one has seen him since.

Lost Deathstalkers. In northern Silverpine, two Forsaken scouts have been missing for weeks. High Executor Hadrec sent Rane and Quinn Yorick to survey haunted farmsteads, and now you must learn what became of them. High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher has heard nothing from Rane and Quinn Yorick for weeks. He sent the two Deathstalkers into northern Silverpine Forest to watch the abandoned farms and track enemy movements. Deathstalkers are the Forsaken’s hidden scouts and killers, serving Lady Sylvanas. Hadrec fears the Scourge or another threat has cut the scouts down.

Lost Fleet. The Lost Fleet lies broken off the Wetlands’ northern coast, along Baradin Bay. The Kul Tiras Third Fleet was destroyed in the Second War by red dragons enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan, and its wrecks are haunted by cursed undead sailors. On its last voyage in the Second War, the Kul Tiras Third Fleet came under attack from red dragons enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan. Dragonflame engulfed its ships, and the Wave Mistress and the Intrepid crashed onto the shallows and reefs of northern Bluegill Marsh. Almost the entire contingent drowned or burned. First Mate Fitzsimmons was the lone living survivor.

Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield searches for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the neighboring family, and asks you to find him across the road. The Stonefield and Maclure families live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but they share little goodwill. When "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield discovers her cherished necklace is gone, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain that Billy Maclure slipped onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

Lost Point. Lost Point is a dilapidated wooden watchtower standing in western Dustwallow Marsh, originally constructed by Theramore's forces as an advance scout post. It has since fallen into disrepair and slipped from the control of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's guard, now serving as a hideout for rogue deserters. Erected by the expeditionary forces of Theramore to monitor traffic and threats emerging from the Barrens, Lost Point has long outlived its intended military function. The outpost has decayed under the relentless moisture of the marsh, its timber rotting and its defenses abandoned by regular troops. Instead of garrison sentries, the tower and its immediate surroundings are occupied by human deserters who broke away from Theramore's service, finding shelter in the isolated wilderness far from the discipline of the city's commanders.

Lost Relic Carry. Lost Relic Carry involves recovering a fractured piece of an ancient rock-mech automaton and delivering it to Prospector Whelgar in the Wetlands. The relic's unknown composite material hints at the sophisticated engineering of the Titans, earning serious reverence from dwarven researchers. Deep within ancient grounds, adventurers can uncover a fractured component of a rock-mech automaton. Far from being simple rubble, its unusual composite material reveals the craftsmanship of an advanced, ancient mechanism tied to the Titans.

Lost Rigger Cove. Tucked away along the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, Lost Rigger Cove serves as the primary base of operations for the Southsea Pirates in the region. Shielded by towering desert mountains on three sides, this hidden port boasts docks, fortified encampments, and an active shipyard constructing new pirate vessels. Naturally fortified by sheer rock walls on almost every side, Lost Rigger Cove provides the Southsea Freebooters an ideal maritime stronghold on Kalimdor's southeastern edge. Here, pirate cutthroats, dockworkers, and brigands haul salvage and assemble fresh hulls right under the noses of Gadgetzan's authorities. The cove allows the Southseas to project power across the Great Sea while raiding trade routes between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and coastal settlements.

Lost in the Shadows. 'Lost in the Shadows' is a quest involving the rescue of Pal'juh, an impetuous hunter who ventured into danger alone. Her rescue highlights the delicate balance between raw aggression and patient stalking required of wilderness trackers. 'Lost in the Shadows' involves locating and rescuing Pal'juh, a talented but hotheaded hunter who ventured out alone into hostile territory. Unwilling to wait for support, she found herself in over her head, requiring outside assistance to ensure her safe return.

Lost in the Thicket Things. A concerned alchemist asks travelers to track down her missing husband, Ardin Grassman, who vanished after pursuing rumors of towering, unknown grasses. Ardin's botanical curiosity led him straight toward a nearby excavation site, where dangerous wildlife and spider attacks have besieged the crew. In 'Lost in the Thicket Things', an alchemist seeks help tracking down her missing husband, Ardin Grassman. Ardin possesses an uncanny, instinctual affinity for nature, routinely braving steep cliffs and distant wilderness to gather rare herbs and botanical specimens to stock her alchemy supplies. When a passing excavation crew brought word of bizarre, towering grasses unlike anything seen before, Ardin's curiosity got the better of him, and he set out to inspect the flora for himself.

Lotwil Veriatus. Lotwil Veriatus is an eccentric gnomish scholar conducting dangerous elemental experiments in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. Stationed east of Kargath with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and a mechanical attendant named Servo, he is dedicated to blending arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering into a unified discipline. Originally from Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil envisions a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes these three disciplines should not be practiced in isolation, but harmonized. In pursuit of this dream, he chose the harsh Badlands as his laboratory to study native rock elementals and construct binding shackles capable of mastering elemental forces. While an accomplished researcher—having studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs in the past—his single-minded focus often blinds him to the explosive hazards of his fieldwork.

name.esES: Una canción de amor para Narain

text.enUS: Love Song for Narain. Meridith the Mermaiden has a message for Narain Soothfancy, the gnome she once rescued from the wreckage of a crashed flying machine. She asks you to carry her love letter to him in Tanaris. You can take this up while seeking Narain's book in Draconic for Dummies. Meridith the Mermaiden seldom has visitors. The last was the gnome she rescued from the wreckage of a crashed flying machine, and she gazes into nothing for a moment, lost in the memory. She asks whether you know Narain Soothfancy, because she has to tell him how she feels, and she is sure it is love. She begs you to carry a message to him, and promises to be forever in your debt.

Love's Gift. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye awaits a pendant for the succubus rite. Dogran gives up a treasured keepsake after being found and revived in the Barrens. A warlock needs a talisman charged with strong, unblemished emotion to summon and control a succubus. These demons feed on mortal desire and twist genuine affection into anguish. Dogran's pendant bears his devotion and their parting. Bring it to Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar's shadowy clefts, where it is cleaned and polished. Its bright emotional force can draw the soul-devourer across the Twisting Nether.

Lower Wilds. The Lower Wilds form the eastern threshold of Feralas, where the humid forests meet the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. The main road cutting through these woods connects Thalanaar at the border to the settlements further west, flanked by ancient greenery and unpredictable woodland creatures. Spanning the eastern reaches of Feralas, the Lower Wilds serve as the natural transition between the sun-baked ravines of Thousand Needles and the deep, primordial jungle to the west. Travelers entering the zone must traverse this stretch of forest along the main highway, past the elven outpost of Thalanaar guarding the mountain pass. The dense canopies here house ancient treants, alongside indigenous wildlife that makes straying from the beaten path perilous.

Lucius. At the Lakeshire docks, Lucius watches the Redridge waterfront. The dwarf works undercover for Stormwind’s SI:7, helping agents with reconnaissance and trade skills. Lucius watches the Lakeshire docks for SI:7, Stormwind’s intelligence service. He keeps an eye on trade, unusual traffic, and threats moving into the Redridge Mountains. Agents sent east from Stormwind come to him to coordinate covert work and practice field skills such as lockpicking. Through Lucius, Stormwind keeps a hidden reach beyond Elwynn Forest.

Lunar Fungus. Lunar Fungus grows in Darkshore's caves, where druids gather it for healing. Mixed with Earthroot and water, it helps make a salve for sick deer. Lunar Fungus grows from Lunar Fungal Blooms in Darkshore's underground caverns. The Cenarion Circle values its amplifying effects. Mixed with soothing water and common Earthroot, it lends potency to a salve that counters debilitating afflictions. Damp caves where it grows are also frequented by territorial moonkin, so gathering it means navigating carefully.

Lurker Venom. Around Loch Modan, dwarven defenders need Lurker Venom to counter Dark Iron sabotage. The toxin comes from predatory spiders in the rocky hills and woods. Lurker Venom helps dwarves disarm Dark Iron explosives. Ashlan Stonesmirk, an explosives expert, named the spiders’ poison as an ingredient for the mixture Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. The solvent combines the venom with rare minerals and tears from the loch’s crocolisks, forming a reactive compound that can disarm complex explosives. Lurker spiders range from common wood lurkers to the matriarch Shanda the Spinner, and their bites threaten travelers and mountaineers across the hills and crags.

Lushwater Oasis. South of the Crossroads, Lushwater Oasis is one of three life-giving watering holes in the Barrens. Kolkar centaur threaten travelers who come for its water, while the tainted pools draw anglers seeking Deviate Fish. Lushwater Oasis lies a short march south of the Crossroads, beneath the Barrens sun. Its palms and springs draw thirsty beasts, but Kolkar centaur hold the banks and ambush wildlife and travelers. The oasis also marks the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. Energies from its underground passages taint the pools, where unnatural creatures and strange mutations take hold.

Lydon's Toxin. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon has made a toxin to disrupt the Venture Company's logging in the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde adventurers carry it to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, who must devise a way to spread it. Apothecary Lydon made the toxin in the Hillsbrad Foothills to fight the Venture Company loggers despoiling the Stonetalon Mountains. He says the compound is lethal on contact and may spread from one target to another. Before it can be used against the goblins near Windshear Crag, the mixture must cross continents to Thunder Bluff. Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative there, needs the raw toxin to devise a wide-dispersal device called the Toxic Fogger.

Lyria Du Lac. In Goldshire, Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors behind the village smithy. She teaches them to master their stances and arms. Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors in the yard behind Goldshire's forge. She teaches those fresh from Northshire Abbey, judges their readiness, and introduces specialized combat techniques. Warriors take up shield and blade for Stormwind, facing the threats of Elwynn Forest.

Ma Stonefield. At Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn, Ma Stonefield tends to hardships close to home. Beside Auntie Bernice, she faces farm troubles, neighboring rivalries, and pests. Ma Stonefield watches over the farm beside her family cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest, with Auntie Bernice Stonefield at her side. The neighboring Maclure homestead and nearby pumpkin patches bring little peace. Wild boars threaten the Stonefield crops, and Princess causes the greatest trouble. The enormous prize sow tramples fields and devours the harvest the family worked hard to grow.

MacGrann's Dried Meats. Tundra MacGrann has a month's worth of salted meat set aside for winter in Dun Morogh. His provisions are locked in a thorium meat locker, but Old Icebeard has carried off the whole cache. Tundra MacGrann prepared for winter by hunting game and salting the meat. He stored weeks of provisions in a sturdy chest, then locked it in a thorium meat locker to keep scavenging bears and prowling predators away from his homestead. Even so, he never expected an intruder strong enough to carry off the whole chest instead of trying to pry it open.

MacKreel's Moonshine. On the broken Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel brews moonshine strong enough to fell a sentry. Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore takes a batch to settle Foggy's debt. Foggy MacKreel brews his moonshine while stationed as a guard on the Thandol Span. The liquor has a fierce reputation, and even hardened dwarven sentries can be laid low after a night of drinking it. They wake with headaches like siege engines rolling overhead. Travelers value its warmth against the damp chill of Lordaeron and Khaz Modan.

MacKreel's Moonshine. Foggy MacKreel sleeps through his watch on the broken Thandol Span after drinking too much of his own moonshine. Now he needs an Alliance traveler to hurry a fresh batch to Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore and settle his debt. Foggy MacKreel keeps watch on the shattered Thandol Span, where the hours are wet, cold, and dull. To bear the damp chill, he drinks his homemade moonshine, a brew so fierce he likens its aftereffects to siege engines pounding across his skull. One drink too many leaves him passed out through his shift. Longbraid the Grim commands the dwarves defending the Span, and Foggy cannot afford another lapse in discipline.

Maclure Vineyards. In southern Elwynn, Maclure Vineyards sends grapes and wine to Stormwind. The Maclure family's estate is known as much for its bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields as for its harvest. The Maclure Vineyards should be a peaceful haven of farming and winecraft in southern Elwynn Forest. Instead, the feud with the Stonefields down the road overshadows the family's daily labor. Accusations of theft and old resentment keep tempers high between the households. Hungry boars prowl the land, while kobolds press toward both homesteads.

Madame Eva. In Darkshire, Madame Eva’s readings mark her as a revered matriarch. She practices ancient divination and cartomancy, and is often the first in town to sense unnatural disturbances across Duskwood. Townspeople and travelers seek her help with grim mysteries and occult charms against the creeping dark. Madame Eva reads cards and practices ancient folk rituals in Darkshire. Many in Stormwind’s cathedral would view her ways with suspicion. In a region troubled by feral beasts, the undead, and darker horrors, desperate townspeople and visiting adventurers seek her eerie insights.

Maestra's Post. Along the road through western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post watches the way between Astranaar and the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Night elven Sentinels guard the settlement, where a few humans serve the Alliance. Maestra's Post keeps watch beneath the trees of western Ashenvale. A slender night elven tower and an open lodge mark the settlement along the road between the coast of Darkshore and Astranaar. Sentinels scan the surrounding wilds as corrupted furbolg stir nearby. Horde movements also threaten Alliance supply lines.

Magatha Grimtotem. On Elder Rise, Magatha Grimtotem challenges Cairne Bloodhoof's vision for the tauren. The Grimtotem matriarch and Thunder Bluff's Elder Crone is a formidable shaman and political schemer. Magatha Grimtotem leads the Grimtotem tribe from Elder Rise, with her own retinue and bodyguards. She gained authority through an arranged union, then her mate died suddenly in a climbing accident. Her reclusive tribe follows her as its political and spiritual leader. Magatha preaches tauren dominance, unlike Cairne Bloodhoof. She sees other mortal races as intruders on Kalimdor, to be eradicated or swept aside.

Mage. Mages are scholarly spellcasters who bend the fabric of reality through arcane study, hurling destructive fire, controlling frost, and raw arcane energy. While physically fragile and cloaked only in cloth, their mastery over teleportation, conjuration, and battlefield crowd control makes them formidable allies and terrifying foes. Their discipline requires immense mental dedication, balancing immense destructive potential against the perilous history of arcane misuse. The path of the mage demands intellect, focus, and years of rigorous study. Rather than communing with spirits or relying on divine faith, magi treat magic as a precise cosmic science. By drawing upon arcane energies, a practitioner can weave raw destructive power, summon searing bursts of flame, or chill the surrounding air into solid ice and howling blizzards. Because heavy armor disrupts the delicate somatic gestures and mental focus required for incantations, mages wear light cloth, relying instead on wards, mana barriers, and evasive spells to protect themselves.

Mage Quarter. The Mage Quarter forms the arcane heart of Stormwind City, resting across the canals in the capital's southwestern corner. Towering over its cobblestone streets and esoteric specialty shops stands the Wizard's Sanctum, where the kingdom's conjurers hone their craft. Beneath the district's scholarly surface also lie shadowy recesses, harboring practitioners of far darker arts. Reachable by bridges crossing the canals from Cathedral Square or the Trade District, the Mage Quarter caters entirely to the mystical needs of the Alliance. Centered around the spire of the Wizard's Sanctum, human and allied spellcasters gather to study the weave of arcane magic and train apprentices. The surrounding streets are crowded with purveyors of tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves, creating an insular district dedicated to research and the defense of the kingdom.

Mage Summoner. Sentinel Velene Starstrike sends a strike south from Silverwind Refuge. After investigating corrupted water elementals near Mystral Lake, the Sentinels send adventurers across the border into the Barrens to kill the undead mage Sarilus Foulborne atop Dreadmist Peak. Night elves rarely send scouts south into the Barrens without grave cause. After investigating unnatural disturbances among the water elementals around Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike traces the meddling to Sarilus Foulborne, a Forsaken conjurer practicing his arts just across the border. For the Sentinels at Silverwind Refuge, an enemy sorcerer defiling nature so close to their home cannot be tolerated.

Magga. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Magga welcomes new arrivals. The orc lives in Durotar and greets Horde travelers beginning their journey through the valley. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls first meet the wider world in the Valley of Trials. Near the Den, Magga greets those arriving in the valley. Trainers and recruits keep busy nearby, while Magga helps bring the small camp together.

Maggot Eye's Paw. At Garren's Haunt, Maggot Eye's Paw proves the gnoll chieftain is dead. The paw is carried to Brill as proof of his execution for stealing corpses for the Scourge. Maggot Eye raided graves and pillaged the countryside near Garren's Haunt, supplying corpses to the Lich King's armies. The Forsaken posted a death sentence and bounty in Brill. To collect the bounty and close it, hunters must bring the gnoll's severed paw back to town. Executor Zygand accepts that proof in place of rumors of Maggot Eye's death.

Maggran Earthbinder. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder guards a Horde camp in the Stonetalon Mountains. Cairne Bloodhoof sent the battle-worn tauren to lead its defense against beasts and harpies. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof sent Maggran Earthbinder to the Stonetalon Mountains to lead Sun Rock Retreat. Countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns have hardened his heart, stripping away the gentleness natural to his people. The outpost was also meant to offer him respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might ease his battle-worn spirit.

name.esES: Dorso de la carta de Maggran

text.enUS: Maggran's Reserve Letter. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder sends orders to relieve a guard at the Great Lift. The letter promises Grish Longrunner leave to visit his family. Maggran Earthbinder sends orders from Sun Rock Retreat to the Great Lift. Grish Longrunner, a Horde sentry at the post, is to be relieved by a replacement warrior. The Great Lift's wooden winches stand far to the south, where Grish has kept watch. With the new warrior taking his place, he can leave his post and return home to visit his family.

Magic Quarter. In the Undercity's northeast, Forsaken spellcasters study arcane and fel arts. The Temple of the Damned anchors their work. In the Undercity's northeastern quadrant, Forsaken mages preserve arcane learning and explore darker arts. The Temple of the Damned dominates the district, a Scourge-built structure now used by the free-willed undead. Beneath its vaulted ceilings, mages shape magical energies while warlocks commune with demons. Their work makes the quarter a center of study and occult research in Lordaeron.

Magical Analysis. Baron Revilgaz directs you northward from Booty Bay to consult the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Taking a bag of water elemental bracers, you seek out Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver to decipher the arcane curse tied to the Stone of the Tides. Following your hunt for the water elemental bracers, Baron Revilgaz hands over a bundle of their bracers. The goblin leader knows that unraveling the curse behind the Stone of the Tides requires deeper magical expertise than Booty Bay can provide. He directs you north toward the ruins of Dalaran, where the wizards remain deeply engaged in rebuilding their broken kingdom. Convinced that arcane scholars cannot ignore an intriguing puzzle, Revilgaz recommends seeking Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver directly, having had dealings with the knowledgeable wizard in the past.

Magis Sparkmantle. In Kharanos, Magis Sparkmantle trains gnome mages inside the Thunderbrew Distillery. He guides fledgling spellcasters who travel from Coldridge Valley into Dun Morogh. Dwarves gather at the Thunderbrew Distillery for ale, and Magis Sparkmantle teaches among its casks and kegs. Gnome mages work closely with their dwarven allies across Dun Morogh. Magis helps novice spellcasters deepen their knowledge of the arcane and put it into practice.

Magistrate Henry Maleb. In Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb keeps order in the Alliance's chief coastal stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills. The port town faces threats from the Forsaken and the Syndicate. Magistrate Henry Maleb governs from Southshore's town hall, one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. Forsaken forces threaten the town from the north and west, while highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb took office after the previous magistrate was mysteriously assassinated, an act he blames on the Syndicate. He means to avoid the same fate. His investigations seek hidden assassins, Syndicate supply networks, and the nobles directing them from the ruins of Alterac.

Magistrate Sevren. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren directs the settlement's defense and sends newcomers to steady the lands around the Undercity. From Brill's town hall, Magistrate Sevren directs civil and strategic affairs in the lands north of the Undercity. New Forsaken arriving in Tirisfal Glades find local crises waiting. Sevren sends adventurers to restore order, secure ruined places, and suppress threats in the surrounding hills.

Magistrate Solomon. Lakeshire looks to Magistrate Solomon as gnolls and orcs close in. From the town hall, he governs local affairs and pleads with Stormwind for military aid, but the capital is distracted and gives no help. Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire as danger closes around the town. Redridge and Shadowhide gnolls prowl the surrounding hills, while Blackrock orcs descend from the north in organized warbands. Solomon and Marshal Marris work to keep order and muster a defense, but Lakeshire's guards and militia are stretched to their limit.

Magni Bronzebeard. In Ironforge, Magni Bronzebeard leads his people through grief and political strain. Lord of Ironforge, Thane of the Bronzebeard clan, and ruler of Khaz Modan, he is a veteran of the Second War who champions dwarven archaeology across Azeroth. Magni Bronzebeard grew up as the eldest of three brothers, knowing the mountain's rule would one day fall to him. When the Horde invaded during the Second War, he held Ironforge behind its impenetrable gates. Once the siege broke, he pledged Khaz Modan to the Alliance of Lordaeron. In the peace that followed, Magni welcomed his gnomish allies after Gnomeregan fell, granting High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the refugees sanctuary beneath the mountain. Magni then sought to unite the fractured northern and southern kingdoms. He asked Mekkatorque to build the Deeprun Tram, an unprecedented route beneath the earth that connects Ironforge directly to Stormwind.

Magram Alliance. Gurda Wildmane proposes turning the centaur clans' hatred against them: befriend one clan and use it to learn how all of them can be beaten. Siding with the Magram means slaying their enemies the Gelkis, then speaking with the Magram spokesman Warug at the edge of Magram Village, in the southeast of Desolace. Gurda Wildmane's plan is to exploit the centaurs' hatred of each other. A single clan is chosen as ally, and what it teaches shows how to defeat every clan. Choose the Magram and you cut down the Gelkis, their foes, which wins you respect among the Magram.

Magram Village. Magram Village is the settlement of the Magram centaur clan, situated among foul yellow pools in southeastern Desolace. It serves as the primary base for the Magram as they wage relentless war against their hated rivals, the Gelkis. Sprawled across islands and shores around stagnant, sulfurous pools in southeast Desolace, Magram Village is a rugged settlement cobbled together with crude wooden bridges and hide tents. The Magram centaur dwell here in constant vigilance against neighboring clans. Known for their sheer brutality and deep-seated animosity toward the southern Gelkis clan, the Magram are willing to tolerate outsiders only if those travelers prove their worth by slaughtering their Gelkis enemies.

Magus Rimtori. Magus Rimtori is a rogue blood elf sorceress leading an expedition among the ancient ruins of Azshara. Known for her ruthless deception, she manipulated the Horde into securing her passage across Kalimdor before butchering her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori led an expedition of high-borne blood elves across the sea to the ancient shores of Azshara. To ensure her party survived the perils of Kalimdor, she manipulated the orc Belgrom, charming and playing him until he agreed to supply an armed escort. Once the soldiers had delivered her safely to her destination, Rimtori revealed her true colors, turning on her protectors and massacring the entire garrison. Establishing her forces at the Thalassian Base Camp, she ventured out into the coastal wilds accompanied by elite bodyguards to hunt for forgotten magical artifacts.

Magus Tirth. Magus Tirth is an eccentric human wizard dwelling out on the salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Known locally for breeding chickens and tormenting his polymorphed apprentice, he is also a scholar of formidable arcane lore who has squandered valuable tomes on racing bets. While most mages of his caliber study in the libraries of Dalaran or Stormwind, Magus Tirth has taken up residence amid the grease and roar of the Shimmering Flats. Surrounded by speeding rocket cars, Tirth peddles chickens to passersby, drinks, gambles, and has long since cursed his unfortunate apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, into poultry form. Despite this eccentric demeanor, Tirth possesses genuine arcane mastery, having authored esoteric texts on magical power before losing them to reckless wagers on the speedway.

Mahren Skyseer. At Camp Taurajo, hunters who have mastered the plains are sent east to Mahren Skyseer. Jorn Skyseer sends them to his sister to learn coastal tracking along the Barrens shore. Jorn Skyseer tests hunters at Camp Taurajo against the dangerous beasts of the southern Barrens. Once they have proved themselves on the red plains, he points them beyond dry earth and open savanna. A tracker must learn to follow prey through swamps, over sheer crags, and beside the crashing waves of the Great Sea.

Mai'Zoth. Brother Nimetz believes Colonel Kurzen was driven to evil by a hidden power that still lives. An ogre mage known as Mai'Zoth lurks within the eastern mountains, wielding an artifact reputed to twist and control minds. Destroying him and recovering this relic is meant to ensure no other commander suffers the same corruption. Though Kurzen has fallen, Brother Nimetz insists the primary catalyst behind the rebellion remains intact. His research points to Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage dwelling inside an ogre mound deep within the eastern heights of Stranglethorn Vale. Nimetz is certain that Mai'Zoth employed mind-altering sorcery to warp Kurzen's thoughts, warning that leaving the ogre alive invites another commander to succumb to the very same sinister influence.

Mai'ah. At the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Mai'ah trains young Darkspear trolls in magic. She guides new spellcasters as they begin their path among the Horde. Young Darkspear trolls come to Mai'ah in the Valley of Trials to learn magic. Orcs favor the elements or the warrior's path, but trolls have a rare gift for arcane study. Candidates bring glyphic inscriptions, and Mai'ah teaches them to shape raw power into controlled incantations. That control matters in Durotar, where danger waits beyond the den.

Main Hall (Northshire). Newcomers report in the Main Hall at Northshire Abbey in western Elwynn. From there, they reach the Hall of Arms, the Library Wing, and the abbey tower, then receive their first assignments defending Stormwind. Trainees and clerics pass through the Main Hall after entering Northshire Abbey. The chamber links the Hall of Arms, where recruits prepare for battle, with the Library Wing and the stairs to the abbey tower. Strife in the valley reaches even this quiet place, and officers rally able newcomers to defend the kingdom's borders.

Major Mattingly. At Stormwind’s main gates, Major Mattingly helps guard the capital and advises crafters on protection from dragons. Major Mattingly is a high-ranking officer responsible for Stormwind City's landward defense. He stands watch in the Valley of Heroes under General Marcus Jonathan, alongside the city's garrison. His duties include overseeing gate patrols and travelers entering the city. Mattingly also knows the lethal nature of dragons and guides skilled crafters who seek to make protective dragonscale gear for facing dangerous lairs.

Major Samuelson. In Stormwind Keep, Major Samuelson commands the city guard and its personnel. The high-ranking veteran officer serves in the throne room and once mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Before Stormwind's royal court, Major Samuelson leads the Stormwind City Guard. He oversees officer postings and military orders across the realm. He mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, who serves at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. When junior commanders struggle or seek transfer from distant frontier garrisons, their requests and official reports travel across the kingdom to Samuelson's desk in the capital.
