Makaba Flathoof. At Camp Aparaje, Makaba Flathoof has lost his home to the Grimtotem clan. He seeks Horde champions to strike back and keep his family safe. Makaba Flathoof grieves for Camp Aparaje, his home in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Grimtotem clan struck without warning and laid the settlement low. Many tauren seek peace and unity under Cairne Bloodhoof, but the Grimtotem keep spreading discord and violence. Makaba is among the survivors left displaced and grieving.

Make Yourself Useful. Make Yourself Useful is an assignment at Windfield Orchard where adventurers help secure the stormapple crop against undisciplined bandits. An extortionist named Ferauu is due to collect his regular share of the harvest, but hungry outlaws have broken ranks to pilfer the trees ahead of time. Dealing with these rogue thieves earns the respect of the watchful orchard keeper. At Windfield Orchard, farming is complicated by extortion. A bandit leader named Ferauu and his crew have established an arrangement to collect their regular cut of the fruit harvest. However, lack of discipline within the bandit ranks means that petty outlaws cannot always wait for their boss's scheduled visit, sneaking in early to pick over the trees.

Maker's Terrace. The Maker's Terrace is a sprawling outdoor excavation site situated in the northern Badlands, directly fronting the entrance to the ancient titan vault of Uldaman. Travelers venturing south from Loch Modan must navigate its rugged perimeter, which is aggressively occupied by Dark Iron dwarves. The dig represents a contested threshold between the surface wastes and the titan mysteries entombed below. Sprawling across the northern bluffs of the Badlands, the Maker's Terrace serves as the exterior staging ground for the subterranean halls of Uldaman. Long before travelers delve into the subterranean ruins, they must contend with the sun-scorched earthworks, scaffolding, and stone trenches of this grand excavation. It sits right along the pass coming down from Loch Modan, making it the first landmark greeting any traveler daring to venture into the arid wastes. The Terrace buzzes with violent industry as rival factions seek a way into the ancient secrets buried beneath the rock.

Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin shelters Horde hunters in the lower Stonetalon hills, south of Grimtotem Post. Darkspear trolls make the camp a waystation for travelers climbing from the Barrens into the mountains. Malaka'jin sits beside the main trail into the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde travelers find a small camp of troll hunters living off the crags and scrublands. The hunters trade supplies and fresh game with those passing through, while watching for mountain predators and Grimtotem tauren farther up the trails.

Malden's Orchard. Black worgs prowl Malden's Orchard in northern Silverpine Forest. The ruined farmstead takes its name from Malden, the human farmer who fled during the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron. Its dark evergreen trees grow wild, and a crumbling cottage once sheltered a Forsaken scout cut off from his unit. Malden's Orchard once sent fresh fruit to the towns of Lordaeron. Malden, a human farmer, tended the land before the Third War. When the Scourge swept through the kingdom, he abandoned the farm and fled the plague. Since then, Silverpine's dark mists have closed over the orchard. Its evergreen trees go unpruned, and fruit rots on blighted boughs. Wild predators have claimed the plot.

Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage lies in a coma within the Emerald Dream, beyond the reach of his people. The first mortal druid and revered leader of the night elves beside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, he helped defeat the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients and the Third War. The kaldorei honor him as Shan'do, or honored teacher, and await his waking guidance. Malfurion Stormrage turned from the arcane to nature ten thousand years ago. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor, he studied under the demigod Cenarius. As Queen Azshara and her Highborne delved into the Well of Eternity's arcane power, Malfurion became Azeroth's first mortal druid. His fears proved true when Azshara's sorcery tore open a way for Sargeras and the Burning Legion, beginning the War of the Ancients.

Malin's Request. In Stormwind, Malin asks for help recovering relics from fallen Stromgarde. Archmage Malin sends seasoned Alliance adventurers north to Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands, where an expedition seeks the magical relics left behind when Stromgarde fell. Archmage Malin serves in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum and acts for his former mentor, Archmage Trelane. When Stromgarde fell into chaos, Trelane made a desperate stand at the Tower of Arathor. As hostile forces took the city, he had to abandon his post and leave powerful enchanted possessions behind. Malin fears those relics may fall into hostile hands. He sends capable mercenaries north to strengthen his agents in the field and reclaim Trelane's lost belongings.

Malin's Request. Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin, who is found in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It tells Malin that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon, and Skuerto is certain Malin will repay you well for helping them in Arathi. After the work in Arathi, Skuerto hands you a letter to take back to Stormwind. Its message for Archmage Malin in the Mage Quarter is that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto has no doubt that Malin will repay you well for helping them, and sends you off with a wish for a safe journey.

Manaweave Robe. In Stormwind, Wynne Larson presents the Manaweave Robe as a proud showcase for her family’s shop. She has woven the enchanted garment from fine materials for a commission that is now complete. Larson Clothiers serves spellcasters in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter with garments made to channel volatile energies. Fine magical robes call for rare materials, careful needlework, and threadwork that holds through mystic resonance. Wynne Larson takes pride in each piece that leaves her shop, where every robe worn into the field carries the Larson name.

Mangletooth. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth faces execution in a Horde cage and bargains with those who visit him. He offers knowledge of his rivals and Agamaggan's ancient lore in return for their help. Tauren hunters and orc sentries keep Mangletooth in a cage at Camp Taurajo. The captured Razormane quilboar awaits execution, but he still tries to sway his captors and visiting Horde adventurers. He urges them to strike at the enemies of his tribe, hoping to prove his worth or win his freedom.

Mangy Claw. In Dun Morogh, Mangy Claw bears the mark of a deadly hunt. The great ice claw bear Mangeclaw killed a stranded dwarven pilot, and the severed claw proves the beast was slain. Pilot Hildelve’s steam tank broke down in Dun Morogh’s frozen hills, leaving him to search for ore on foot and face the mountain wilderness alone. His recovered journal tells how he fought off an ice claw bear named Mangeclaw, though the struggle left him savagely mauled. The bear returned later and killed the weakened pilot. In his final written entry, Hildelve pleaded for vengeance. Taking the Mangy Claw from the fallen bear fulfills that request.

Manhunt. Marshal Dughan sends you after a Defias bagman called the Collector in Elwynn Forest. The Collector works from the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and sends stolen gold from the forest's mines into the Brotherhood's coffers. Marshal Dughan sends you to Brackwell Pumpkin Patch after Elwynn's gnolls are found carrying a schedule for gold pickups. Defias bandits and gnolls have taken over the once quiet homestead. The Collector hides among its overgrown vines, skimming ore from the kingdom's mines and arranging shipments for the growing rebellion.

Mankrik. At the Crossroads, Mankrik carries grief and a thirst for vengeance. A quilboar ambush separated him from his wife, Olgra, and he now hunts the bristled beasts across the Barrens. Mankrik and his wife Olgra traveled through the Barrens when quilboar swarmed them during a skirmish at a small tauren settlement. The fighting tore them apart, and Mankrik saw Olgra vanish beneath tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Fury drove him to fight recklessly until a blow left him unconscious. Along the Gold Road, a passing tauren druid found Mankrik bleeding out and bound his injuries. He survived the ambush, but Olgra was gone.

Mannoroc Coven. Mannoroc Coven is a demon-infested ruin in southern Desolace, named after the pit lord Mannoroth. Settled among ancient night elf architecture, it stands as the largest stronghold of the Burning Legion in central Kalimdor. Cultists of the Burning Blade maintain active summoning portals here, filling the ash-choked land with felhounds, succubi, and infernals.

Manor Mistmantle. In Duskwood's shadowed northeastern hills, Manor Mistmantle lies north of Darkshire. Once a family homestead, the estate has fallen into ruin, where ghouls prowl under the command of its infamous master. West of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle's ruined grounds are choked with decay. Vicious ghouls prowl there, guarding the broken house. In the untended garden, a solitary, sorrowful blossom called the Tear of Tilloa is the only sign of living beauty on the entire property.

Maps and Runes. In Silverpine Forest, maps and runes point to Dalaran's interest in Ambermill. A hidden crate holds regional charts and a rune-inscribed pendant, which adventurers recover for Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher. Horde agents find a Dalaran crate hidden along the border routes near Ambermill. Inside are detailed regional charts and an enigmatic pendant inscribed with runes. With human sentries nearby, the scouts retrieve the artifact carefully, wary of Dalaran's arcane reach so close to their borders.

Marcus Redpath. In Southshore, Marshal Marcus Redpath holds Lordaeron's last southern bastion on the coast. He organizes patrols and bounty contracts against nearby ogres, murlocs, and naga. Marshal Marcus Redpath guards Southshore, the Alliance port on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. The town endured the fall of Lordaeron's capital and the devastating Scourge invasion. Redpath now leads its defense, protecting the survivors who remain there.

Mardant Strongoak. Mardant Strongoak is a night elf druid trainer residing in Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil. He guides fledgling druids in communing with the spirits of nature and introduces them to the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, young night elves who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. His primary task is teaching novitiates how to open their senses to nature spirits, interpret their murmurs, and channel rejuvenating magics. For those taking their initial steps as protectors of the wild, he is often the first master to unveil the vast complexities and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

Mardenholde Keep. Mardenholde Keep is the imposing stone citadel overlooking Hearthglen in the northern reaches of the Western Plaguelands. Once the ancestral seat of Lord Tirion Fordring, it now serves as the regional command center for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade under the rule of his son, Highlord Taelan Fordring. Built as the administrative heart of the Hearthglen principality, Mardenholde Keep was long celebrated by the people of Lordaeron for having never breached during the Second War. From its council chambers, Lord Tirion Fordring governed the surrounding vales alongside his trusted advisors, maintaining peace until his controversial trial and exile for defending the orc Eitrigg. Following Tirion's fall, governance fell to his ambitious apprentice Barthilas and eventually passed to Tirion's son, Taelan, who inherited his father's domain on the eve of Lordaeron's destruction.

Marek Ironheart. At the Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart tests those who seek the respect of its hunters. The veteran dwarven hunter is stationed in south-eastern Loch Modan and keeps to the traditions of the wild. At the Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart expects hunters to prove their skill. The lodge overlooks the lake from a ridge in south-eastern Loch Modan and gathers marksmen and trackers from across the dwarven lands. Marek pays little heed to titles or boasts. Anyone seeking the lodge’s respect must show practical skill against the beasts roaming Loch Modan, with the patience and nerve of a true hunter.

Marg Speaks. From beyond death, Marg tells of the muckshell that killed Marg and of a duty still undone. Marg asks you to find that muckshell, recover the jeweled pendant stolen from Alliance soldiers and carry it to Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village. Near Theramore, Marg spotted Alliance soldiers camped on the beach. One of them wore a pendant studded with more gems than a soldier could ever pay for. That night Marg snuck into the camp and stole it, but a muckshell crab-man killed Marg on the way back to base. Now Marg asks you to find that muckshell, recover the pendant and bring it to Nazeer in Brackenwall Village.

Margoz. In northern Durotar, Margoz watches for the Burning Blade's growing threat. After the clash with fel corruption at Thunder Ridge, Orgnil Soulscar sends champions to seek the isolated orc shaman before they strike a nearby cultist stronghold. Margoz's counsel reveals Skull Rock, the Burning Blade's concealed cavern base. After Thunder Ridge revealed the depth of fel taint, Orgnil Soulscar sees that strength alone cannot cleanse Durotar. He sends champions to Margoz, an experienced orc shaman keeping a lonely camp in the crags northeast of Razor Hill. Between Drygulch Ravine and the eastern sea, Margoz watches the northern reaches for dark omens that Orgrimmar's busy warriors often miss.

Marisa du'Paige. In the caves outside the Deadmines, Marisa du'Paige fights beside Moonbrook's outlaws. Rare among their laborers and highwaymen, she uses arcane magic in the tunnels of southwestern Westfall. Deep in the caves leading toward the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs guard the tunnels. Marisa du'Paige is a skilled human mage among them. Many spellcasters train in Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, but Marisa has joined the outlaws and brigands in Westfall's underground passages.

Marla's Last Wish. In Deathknell, Marla's Last Wish calls you to bring a husband and wife together in death. Novice Elreth asks you to find Samuel Fipps, still bound to the Scourge, so he can be buried beside his wife, Marla. The Forsaken seek to honor the ties they had in life and to set themselves apart from the Scourge. Marla and Samuel Fipps were husband and wife in Lordaeron before the Third War devastated their home. When the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed and rose as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath, but not her husband. In his frenzy, Samuel killed her. Even then, Marla bore him no hatred. Novice Elreth remembers her final wish: to rest beside Samuel in the Deathknell graveyard.

Marleth Barleybrew. At Brewnall Village, Marleth Barleybrew works to prove her family’s ale can rival Thunder Ale. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan’s hold on the local beer trade, she schemes to put Barleybrew brew before drinkers. In Dun Morogh, beer matters as much as steel, and the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families have long been rivals. Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin control nearly all the trade from their distillery in Kharanos, to Marleth Barleybrew’s frustration. She believes her family’s brew is just as strong. Rather than challenge the Thunderbrews openly, Marleth turns to quiet tricks. She recruits travelers to secretly replace Kharanos tavern casks with Barleybrew kegs.

Marris Stead. Perched on a ridge in the southwestern Eastern Plaguelands, the Marris Stead was once a peaceful Lordaeron homestead. Following the devastation of the Third War, it now serves as the lonely, heavily defended redoubt of Nathanos Blightcaller, Champion of the Forsaken.

Marryk Nurribit. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Marryk Nurribit teaches young gnomes the arcane arts. He favors local brews over strict lessons and often asks his pupils for spare coins to buy a drink. Marryk Nurribit teaches young gnomes magic inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He knows the arcane arts, though he takes a casual approach to teaching. A flagon of dwarven ale often holds more of his attention than a lesson, and he asks his new pupils for spare pocket change. He also warns aspiring spellcasters about the dangers beyond Coldridge Valley, where Gnomeregan's ruins remain radioactive and infested with troggs.

Marshal Dughan. Goldshire's marshal faces threats on every road and mine. Marshal Dughan commands the Stormwind Army detachment there, but kobolds, gnolls, and bandits stretch his small garrison. He depends on independent adventurers to help protect the town and nearby farms. Marshal Dughan directs Elwynn Forest's defense from Goldshire, outside the Lion's Pride Inn. Stormwind's soldiers are tied up elsewhere, while trouble grows in the woods. Kobolds crowd the mines, gnolls gather along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers on the King's Road. With too few footmen under his command, Dughan sends new recruits to reinforce outposts and scout dangerous ground.

Marshal Haggard. At Eastvale, Marshal Haggard keeps the arms he gathered over a lifetime of service. Harry Burlguard sends novice warriors from Stormwind City to meet the retired marshal and seek better weapons. Stormwind's novice warriors need more than skill to face danger beyond the city. Harry Burlguard sends promising fighters east through Elwynn Forest to find Marshal Haggard, a retired officer who served the realm for years. Haggard gathered a personal armory over a lifetime in the field, and his home near the Eastvale Logging Camp holds weapons for young warriors seeking better arms.

Marshal Haggard's Badge. At his farm in Elwynn, Marshal Haggard has lost the badge he carried in Stormwind's service. Dead-tooth Jack stole it by trickery, and the Defias may use it to impersonate city officials. Marshal Haggard retired to a small farmstead in the hills of Elwynn Forest, but his old Stormwind Marshal's badge still carries official weight. One night, Dead-tooth Jack, a Defias rogue, wore a Stormwind tabard and posed as Marshal Dughan, Goldshire's garrison commander. He tricked Haggard into believing his former peers needed the insignia for official business. The aging marshal handed it over without suspicion. Jack fled into the woods before Haggard saw through the ruse. In Defias hands, the emblem of Stormwind authority could let outlaws pass checkpoints or confuse local patrols.

Marshal Marris. At Lakeshire's bridge, Marshal Marris directs a thin guard against the Blackrock advance. With Stormwind's army absent, he turns to visiting fighters to slow the orcs in the Redridge Mountains. Lakeshire faces gnolls to the west and the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris commands the guard line at the town's main bridge, but his supplies are low and his soldiers are stretched thin. Stormwind has sent no royal reinforcements, leaving Marris to keep the town from being overrun.

Marshal Maxwell. Marshal Maxwell is a high-ranking officer of the Stormwind army stationed at Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Tasked with holding the Alliance's northernmost fortified ridge above the Redridge Mountains against the Blackrock clan and the Dark Iron dwarves, he directs scouting missions into the hostile crags below. He also plays a crucial role in coordinating efforts to discover the fate of his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Morgan's Vigil stands as a precarious outpost on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes, overlooking a wasteland choked with ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Marshal Maxwell commands the Stormwind military detachment stationed here, providing a rare friendly sight for travelers braving the fiery crags. From this rocky bastion, he oversees defensive maneuvers to keep the hostile forces of the mountain contained before they can sweep southward into Redridge and Elwynn.

Marshal McBride. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride commands Stormwind's garrison and defends the valley. Kobolds threaten its farms and mines, so he directs new recruits against them. Marshal McBride commands Stormwind's garrison outside Northshire Abbey. The abbey is a place of faith and learning, while unrest across the kingdom has left military garrisons short of soldiers. With only a handful of sworn guards, McBride must keep the valley peaceful and protect its food and resources. Green recruits arrive seeking training from the abbey's masters, and he must put them to work.

Marshal's Refuge. Marshal's Refuge is a precarious, neutral haven tucked into the northern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Established by Williden Marshal and his expedition party, it serves as an emergency redoubt after the basin's primeval beasts routed their lower camps. When Williden and Hol'anyee Marshal led their expedition into Un'Goro Crater, they drastically underestimated the ferocity of its prehistoric denizens. After their initial base camps were repeatedly overrun by rampaging beasts, the battered survivors scrambled up into the cavernous northern cliffside to escape slaughter. Re-established as Marshal's Refuge, the camp clings high above the jungle floor, offering the only stable resting ground, basic supplies, and flight masters for weary explorers in the northern crater.

Marshlands. The Marshlands is a sprawling, sodden marsh occupying the southeastern reach of Un'Goro Crater. Sitting directly at the base of the winding ramp down from Tanaris, it is often the first wilderness newcomers witness upon entering the primeval basin. Descending the steep trail from the arid expanse of Tanaris brings travelers directly into the humid mire of the Marshlands. Navigating anywhere else along the sheer crater rim invites a lethal fall, making this treacherous swath of wetlands the primary threshold into Un'Goro. Dense canopies, standing water, and mud conceal abundant packs of fierce raptors, including venomous varieties that stalk the reeds. Amid the damp clearings, explorers can find Blue Power Crystals scattered across the earth, unique to this quarter of the crater.

Martek the Exiled. Fizzle Brassbolts is building a new engine for his car, but he cannot make pistons hard enough to take the strain. He sends you with a letter to a great smith named Martek the Exiled, far off in a camp in the Badlands. After Salt Flat Venom, Fizzle at the Mirage Raceway explains that his new engine should make the car so fast it could fly. All his trials have failed because he cannot make pistons hard enough for the heavy stress. He knows one person who might know how: Martek the Exiled, a great smith who knows more about metal than anyone. Martek is a long way off in the Badlands, camped there with a goblin, and you carry Fizzle's letter to him.

Martie Jainrose. In Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose tends a garden beside Lake Everstill. She gathers herbs and flowers for the town while wild beasts threaten her plots, and she seems fond of Guard Parker. Martie Jainrose tends herbs and flowers for Lakeshire as its herbalist. Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the Redridge Mountains, but Martie keeps the town supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Wild animals disrupt her work, especially Bellygrub, a monstrous boar that often ravages her garden beds. Martie also seems fond of Guard Parker. Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

Marukai. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai holds a remote Horde beachhead against the Wrathtail naga. The Darkspear jungle troll coordinates efforts to drive the naga back along Ashenvale's foggy northwest coast. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai works to keep the encampment from being overwhelmed. The outpost sits on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory, and the restless sea. Wrathtail naga emerge in force from the waters and ancient elven ruins to claim the shoreline. Marukai directs Horde champions to push them back into the tide and collect their heads, keeping the outpost a viable coastal stronghold.

Mary's Looking Glass. In Duskwood, Mary’s discarded looking glass passes from a ghoul to a stargazer. Blind Mary once treasured the polished mirror. After her death and the loss of her eyes, her reflection became an agonizing reminder of what she had lost. She cast the looking glass away behind her barn, where Duskwood's gloom closed in. An Insane Ghoul found it among the ruined outskirts and carried it south to the crypts of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.
Mast Room. Timber from Westfall reaches the Mast Room, deep in the Deadmines, where goblin woodcarvers shape it for the Defias.

Master Apothecary Faranell. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell leads the Royal Apothecary Society from the depths of the Apothecarium. Once a respected Dalaran scholar, he now directs the Forsaken's search for a New Plague to destroy the Scourge and the living. Before the Third War, Faranell spent decades studying alchemy alongside Dalaran's learned mages. In life, he sought cures, remedies, and potions to improve mortal health. The Scourge plague killed him, but he rose again as a free-willed Forsaken. His scientific curiosity turned cruel, and he traded healing salves for catastrophic reagents. His encyclopedic knowledge made him one of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's most valued researchers in the depths of Lordaeron's fallen capital.

Master Gadrin. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin guides the Darkspear through exile and loss. The elder witch doctor once trained the tribe's priests and mages with Zalazane. Now he helps his people and seeks to break the dark curse over their home on the Echo Isles. Before the Darkspear reached Kalimdor, Master Gadrin guided generations of his people in the South Seas. He served as a witch doctor on the islands they called home, teaching the tribe's mystical ways.

Master Vornal. In Sen'jin Village, Master Vornal brews for the Darkspear trolls and keeps his craft to himself. The elderly jungle troll refuses to take on apprentices despite his deep knowledge of alchemy. Master Vornal brews draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls in Sen'jin Village. Age is catching up with him, but he remains fiercely independent and refuses to train an apprentice. He mixes his remedies and volatile brews by his own hand.

Master's Cellar. The Master's Cellar is a sprawling subterranean complex situated beneath the ruined settlement south of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Once serving Medivh's estate as wine cellars and storage vaults, it has descended into a haunted ruin teeming with the restless spectres of former servants and caretakers. Just south of the imposing tower of Karazhan lie the ruined remnants of a hamlet that once housed the servants, groundskeepers, and attendants who maintained Medivh's estate. Beneath these crumbled homes sits the Master's Cellar. Accessible through two separate entrances in the surface ruins, the complex expands far underground. One doorway opens into an extensive vaulted wine cellar, while the other descends through collapsed stonework into deep natural caverns. Whatever dark demise befell Karazhan and its master swallowed this basement as well, leaving the unliving remnants of caretakers, wailing spectres, and damned souls trapped in endless servitude.

Master's Glaive. In southwestern Darkshore, the Master's Glaive rises from an ancient, unsettling site. Night elves once revered it as a sacred mystery, but Twilight's Hammer cultists now swarm around the colossal weapon, drawn by the malevolence that lingers there. At the Master's Glaive, an adamantine blade pierces a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell here. Night elves long believed that only the titans could wield a weapon so vast. The blade and skull remain a monument to that forgotten clash.

Mastok Wrilehiss. At Splintertree Post in eastern Ashenvale, Mastok Wrilehiss helps hold the Horde’s ground. He directs scouts and warriors to watch nearby borders and confront corrupting elemental forces amid the night elves’ hostility. Deep beneath Ashenvale’s canopy, Splintertree Post is surrounded by hostile night elf territory. Mastok Wrilehiss helps defend the outpost and watches its supply routes and the forest around it. The Sentinels see the settlement as an intrusion that despoils their lands, and they strike quickly at any sign of weakness.

Mathias Shaw. In Old Town, Mathias Shaw directs SI:7, Stormwind's covert intelligence agency. From the shadows, he sends spies and scouts to guard the realm against conspiracies within and horrors beyond. Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's spies and assassins from SI:7's hidden headquarters behind the barracks in Old Town. His covert network reaches across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Loyal to the House of Wrynn, Shaw weighs every threat with care. He trusts unseen daggers and stolen messages to defend Stormwind as much as armor and palace guards.

Mathiel. Furen Longbeard sends his crafting notes across the sea to Mathiel in Darnassus. The night elf smith works on the Warrior's Terrace, where dwarven mail forging may reach a new pair of hands. Furen Longbeard has mastered the forging of fire-hardened armor and chooses to share what he has learned with other Alliance craftsmen. He copies his technical diagrams and sends you across the continents to Mathiel, a smith on Teldrassil.

Mathiel's Armor. At the forge in Darnassus, Mathiel's Armor brings night elf and dwarven craft together. Mathiel works in the Warrior's Terrace, using methods devised by Furen Longbeard to shape exotic materials into armor for Alliance warriors. Night elf armorers have favored methods honed over millennia, with work shaped by nature, supple leathers, and carefully worked metals. Trade with the Eastern Kingdoms has led smiths such as Mathiel to try new ways. He brings the dwarven techniques devised by Furen Longbeard together with elven craft.

Mathredis Firestar. Mathredis Firestar is an eccentric blood elf mage residing at Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He crafts powerful enchantments known as Lesser Arcanums, drawing upon the arcane research of his deceased master. In doing so, he feeds on the residual energies unleashed during the binding process to stave off his magic addiction. Mathredis Firestar learned the craft of making arcanums—concentrated gems of arcane empowerment—from his mentor, Telmius Dreamseeker. Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself.

Mathrengyl Bearwalker. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides Alliance druids from the Cenarion Enclave. Once Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he helps young druids face spiritual trials, learn shapeshifting, and serve across Kalimdor. In Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave, Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides Alliance druids through their first rites. A respected elder of the Cenarion Circle, he sends initiates to commune with Moonglade and judges whether they are ready to take animal forms. Mathrengyl remembers his own bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit. He asks each initiate to test their spirit against Lunaclaw, the sacred moonkin, before entering the path of the Druid of the Claw.

Mathystra Relic. Among Mathystra’s overgrown ruins in northern Darkshore, ancient night elven relics still hold traces of magic. The Twilight's Hammer cult has taken an interest in them. Mathystra once stood on the Kalimdor coast as a city and bastion of elven civilization. Before the Great Sundering, it was a proud place. Now toppled columns and cracked stones lie half-swallowed by brush and sea mist, with restless spirits and lurking beasts among them. Relics from that age are scattered through the ruins. Ten thousand years of neglect have worn them, but traces of elven arcane craft remain, and they are dangerous in careless hands.

Mathystra Relics. This quest sends Alliance adventurers north along the coast of Darkshore to sift through the overgrown Ruins of Mathystra. Onu, an Ancient of Lore rooted in the Grove of the Ancients, seeks these ancient kaldorei artifacts to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cult is manipulating night elven sorcery for their sinister rites. To counteract this dark endeavor, Onu directs heroes to the Ruins of Mathystra, located along the northeastern shores of Darkshore. Long ago, Mathystra was a shining bastion of highborne civilization before it shattered during the Sundering. Though the city has collapsed into rubble, weeds, and naga infestation, powerful remnants of its original arcane and spiritual enchantments linger in shattered urns and ancient relics scattered across the stone foundations.

Maul (subzone). The Maul is a sunken fighting arena situated in the Broken Commons outside the ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Formerly a grand venue of ancient elven Eldre'Thalas, the pit is now an uncontrolled bloodsport ring where wanderers fight for glory or survival against fierce beasts and rival champions. Carved deep into the stone of the Broken Commons, the Maul once served the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas as a theater or ceremonial arena. Following the Sundering and the subsequent occupation by the Gordok ogres, the pit devolved into a raw colosseum. Like the notorious Gurubashi Arena in distant Stranglethorn Vale, entering the sands of the Maul suspends all allegiances, casting combatants into a lawless free-for-all where faction lines dissolve and survival depends purely on martial strength.

Maur Grimtotem. Deep in Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Maur Grimtotem lies dead. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent him to seek peace with the troggs, and his remains and satchel are still in the caverns. Maur Grimtotem went into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar as an envoy to the troggs. Most of the Horde saw them as savage brutes beyond negotiation, but Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought peace might be possible, or at least said so. Maur carried her offer into the winding caverns. The troggs killed him, and his body remains under the watch of their chieftain, Oggleflint.

Maur Raincaller. In Bloodhoof Village, Maur Raincaller watches over Mulgore’s herds and wild beasts. He attends to concerns tied to the plains’ natural and spiritual life. Maur Raincaller lives near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, on the shore of Lake Stonebull. He watches over matters involving Mulgore’s wildlife and the balance of the elements. After the strider Mazzranache bites him and infects his wound, Maur asks young travelers to gather animal parts for a remedy.

Maurin Bonesplitter. Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings. While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it.

Maxan Anvol. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Maxan Anvol trains dwarven priests in the Holy Light. He tests young acolytes before they earn the Church’s vestments. Maxan Anvol tends to the hamlet’s spiritual welfare from the Thunderbrew Distillery, where travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes gather. Kharanos lies between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge, and its inn draws those who pass through. Maxan offers prayers and counsel to anyone who enters, with pints of stout close at hand.

Maybell Maclure. At the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest, Maybell Maclure loves a Stonefield in secret. Her family’s bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields keeps her apart from Tommy Joe Stonefield. Maybell Maclure works the family vineyards under the shadow of a long feud with the Stonefields next door. She has fallen in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield, heir to the rival farm. Their relatives keep them apart, and Maybell searches for a way to speak with him beyond her family’s watchful eyes.

Mazthoril. Mazthoril is a massive, frostbitten cavern in central Winterspring that serves as the primary redoubt for the blue dragonflight in northern Kalimdor. Heavily guarded by dragonkin, spell-wielding wyrms, and arcane sentries, its winding ice tunnels conceal powerful magic and lead to the aerie of the reclusive blue matriarch Haleh. Carved into the frozen mountains just south of Everlook, Mazthoril houses an extensive brood answering to the Spell-Weaver, Malygos. The cavern and its surrounding crags are patrolled by vigilant dragonkin including Spellmaw, Azurous, and General Colbatann, while elite guardians watch the inner caverns. Intruders who wander into Mazthoril face dragonspawn thoroughly attuned to raw arcane energy, making any venture inside perilous without serious preparation.

Mazzranache. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village has fallen victim to a venomous bite from Mazzranache, a legendary plainstrider that terrorized his grandfather a generation ago. Struck by fever and delirious nightmares, the tauren requires a potent remedy brewed from Mulgore's wildlife before the infection claims his life. For years, Maur Raincaller regarded Mazzranache as little more than a harrowing family tale passed down by his grandfather. The elder tauren spoke of an unusually savage plainstrider armed with glowing red eyes, razor-sharp talons, and a toxic bite that defied the peaceful nature of most Mulgore wildlife. When Maur crossed paths with the beast out on the open grass, the legend proved all too real, leaving him severely wounded and struggling to make it back to safety.

Me Brother, Nipsy. Me Brother, Nipsy is an Alliance delivery quest that takes travelers across the Deeprun Tram between Ironforge and Stormwind. A gnome named Monty tasks commuters with transporting a crate of live rats to his brother Nipsy, who runs a rat kabob stall at the opposite terminal. Beneath the quirky errand lies a touching look at Monty's fractured mind following the tragedy of Gnomeregan. Me Brother, Nipsy is a brief courier errand that introduces commuters to the wonders—and hazards—of the Deeprun Tram. Stationed on the Ironforge side of the tramway, an odd gnome named Monty tasks travelers with ferrying a carton of fresh critters through the subterranean transit corridor to his brother Nipsy at the Stormwind depot. The delivery highlights the bizarre everyday commerce taking place beneath the mountains connecting the dwarven and human capitals.

Meal Appeal. Meal Appeal is an Orgrimmar errand given by Thatog, an orc tied down by his daily duties who worries his young son Migi is skipping meals to play. Travelers are asked to pick up a prepared lunch from Borstan's Firepit and track down Migi playing behind Grommash Hold. It offers a grounded look at domestic family life within the Horde's capital. In the bustling red-rock avenues of Orgrimmar, everyday domestic life continues alongside the drills of grunt warriors and the machinations of the Horde. Thatog, bound to his daily post by duty, finds himself unable to keep a watchful eye over his energetic young son, Migi. Left to his own devices, Migi spends from morning till dusk racing through the city streets with his friends, consistently neglecting his stomach until returning home famished.

Meats to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sends a parcel of Barrens meat toward Orgrimmar. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to carry it to Devrak, the wind rider master, and learn the flight route to the Horde capital. Wildlife fills the Barrens, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has prepared choice cuts for a personal delivery to Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Rather than risk the long, dusty trek across the Southfury River into Durotar, he sends runners from the Crossroads to the wind rider perch.

Mebok Mizzyrix. Mebok Mizzyrix is an enterprising goblin entrepreneur residing in the port town of Ratchet. Ever eager to turn bizarre wilderness reagents into profit, he hires passing adventurers to gather unusual flora and fauna from across the Barrens and beyond. His most notorious project involves concocting a commercial intellect-enhancing beverage out of raptor horns. Operating out of the bustling, neutral port of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic Steamwheedle spirit of relentless opportunism. While Ratchet caters to sailors, pirates, and merchants of all stripes, Mebok focuses his keen eye on Kalimdor's wilderness. Rather than mining standard ore or trading mundane cloth, he seeks out rare biological curiosities that he believes can be refined into highly lucrative concoctions and commodities.

Meddlesome Mages. Meddlesome Mages centers on rising friction in the Shen'dar Highlands, where apprentices of the High Order trespass near sacred standing stones. Local guardians must drive them away to protect the delicate mystical forces that hold their island together from reckless arcane tampering. Tensions have flared north of the village in the Shen'dar Highlands, where apprentices of the High Order have gathered around ancient standing stones. Despite repeated warnings to leave these sacred sites undisturbed, the mages have pressed forward with their arcane interests. The local leadership, though hesitant to shed the blood of their shen'dorei kin, has called for outside intervention to disperse the encroaching apprentices before their interference causes permanent harm.

Medivh. Medivh was the last Guardian of Tirisfal, an ancient order tasked with defending Azeroth from demonic corruption. Bound from before his birth by the spirit of the Dark Titan Sargeras, he opened the Dark Portal and brought the orcish Horde into the world, setting off decades of catastrophic warfare. Medivh was born to the powerful Guardian Aegwynn and the court conjurer Nielas Aran. Centuries earlier, Aegwynn had fought the fallen Titan Sargeras in Northrend, unaware that his dark essence slipped into her body to await an heir. When Medivh reached his fourteenth birthday, the vast magical inheritance bestowed by his mother manifested in a terrifying explosion of power, plunging the boy into a decade-long coma under the watch of the clerics at Northshire Abbey.

Mekgineer Thermaplugg. In ruined Gnomeregan, Mekgineer Thermaplugg rules from a massive mechanical battle suit. Once High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque’s trusted advisor, he brought about the city’s irradiation in a bid for power. The fallout transformed him into a leper gnome and left him deranged, ruling the ruined halls. For many years, Mekgineer Thermaplugg served as chief advisor to High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, who trusted him completely. In secret, Thermaplugg coveted the High Tinker’s office. Even Mekkatorque cannot say what finally drove him to betray that trust. The High Tinker can only note that Thermaplugg would have had both power and wealth in time.

Melenas' Head. At Fel Rock, Melenas' Head marks the end of a lingering demonic threat on Teldrassil. Taken as a bounty from Lord Melenas, the satyr commander encamped there, it is proof of his death. Satyrs on Teldrassil’s new World Tree shame the night elves who guard Shadowglen and the surrounding reaches. Lord Melenas made his lair in Fel Rock’s twisted caverns, just north of the elven settlements, and rallied aggressive grell warriors to his banner. The kaldorei prize discretion when dealing with corruption so close to their heartlands. Melenas' Head is private proof that his schemes have ended before his influence could spread.

Melithar Staghelm. Outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm guides young night elves. He sends them to learn why the dryad Tarindrella has returned to the glade. His Staghelm name links him to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, though their connection is unknown. Melithar Staghelm waits outside Aldrassil, where night elves first step into the world. A druid who listens to the forest spirits, he has learned that Tarindrella, a woodland protector, has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing trouble, Melithar sends newcomers southwest of Aldrassil to find the dryad and learn why she has come back to the grove.

Melor Sends Word. Jorn Skyseer brings word from Melor Stonehoof to promising hunters in the Barrens. Those who have proved their grit across Kalimdor are called to Hunter's Rise in Thunder Bluff for a harder trial. Across the Barrens, Jorn Skyseer watches the crossings and encampments. He carries word from the elders of Hunter's Rise to hunters and warriors who have shown promise in the surrounding lands. Melor Stonehoof, a revered tauren mentor, has marked out a path for them.

Melor Stonehoof. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Melor Stonehoof sets hunters to difficult trials. He sends Horde hunters after dangerous beasts across the Barrens and Thousand Needles to test their tracking and mettle. Melor Stonehoof watches the plains from Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. For the tauren, hunting joins survival with spiritual balance and respect for nature's greatest predators. Melor teaches those who carry bow and blade for the Horde to honor that balance, sending promising stalkers to test their craft against legendary beasts.

Menara Voidrender. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender teaches warlocks from both factions the dark arts. The human warlock shares her knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft from a refuge in Kalimdor, far from orthodox authorities. Menara Voidrender works from Ratchet, the neutral goblin port in the Barrens. Many warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms study in cellars or hidden slaughterhouses beneath their cities, but Ratchet keeps Menara away from the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, and Orgrimmar's overseers. There, she can pursue occult studies in plain sight. She teaches any capable apprentice, whatever their faction, making her a rare meeting point for practitioners of the dark arts.

Menethil Bay. Menethil Bay carries Alliance traffic along the western coast of the Wetlands. The sheltered waters open into Baradin Bay, with Menethil Harbor to the north and Dun Morogh's steep cliffs to the south. Crocolisks prowl the shallows, and sunken vessels lie below. Menethil Bay opens from the Wetlands into the Great Sea as part of Baradin Bay. Menethil Harbor lies to the north, Black Channel Marsh to the east, and Dun Morogh's coastal bluffs to the south. Crocolisks of many sizes prowl the shallow margins and marshy shores, making the water dangerous for travelers without a guide. The bay carries Alliance sea traffic, and near its mouth rests the ruined Flying Osprey, a warning of the wreckage beneath the surface.

Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor links the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor from its island off the Wetlands' western shore. Stone battlements and Menethil Keep's towers guard the port, where merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers gather. Menethil Harbor honors King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron and offers the Alliance a haven on the Wetlands coast. Its remote marshland setting leaves it exposed, so massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and Menethil Keep's four stone watchtowers guard the town.

Menethil Keep. Menethil Keep commands the skyline above Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Four watchtowers guard the Alliance port, and Captain Stoutfist leads its militia from within the stone walls. Menethil Keep rises over Menethil Harbor’s wooden docks and the Wetlands marshes. Four stone watchtowers overlook the town and bay, watching for seaward raiders, renegades, and swamp beasts pushing into the area. Within the fortress, Captain Stoutfist directs the town militia and organizes patrols to defend the port and protect Alliance interests across the region.

Menethil Statuette. Off the Wetlands coast, the Menethil Statuette lies lost from a shipwreck. The rare silver likeness honors Lordaeron's fallen king. King Terenas Menethil II appears in his youth, a long-haired paladin lifting a hammer toward the heavens. He was humble and disliked personal monuments, so few statues or likenesses were made in his honor. The Scourge's fall of Lordaeron destroyed almost all of them. This surviving effigy is extraordinarily valuable to the Alliance.

Mennet Carkad. In the Undercity, Marion Call sends you to report to Mennet Carkad. He waits deep in the Rogues' Quarter, where promising operatives are tested for the Deathstalkers. Marion Call has a summons for you from Mennet Carkad. In the Undercity, covert operatives draw the notice of higher leadership, and Marion passes along word when a scout or assassin is invited to report. The Forsaken's intelligence apparatus has a lethal reputation, so ignoring its orders is no real choice.

Mercenaries. In Thelsamar, Magistrate Bluntnose hires passing fighters as Mo'grosh ogres press into northeastern Loch Modan. Ironforge's promised soldiers are months away, leaving the valley's settlements, excavations, and Stonewrought Dam exposed. Ironforge has taken months to send help to Loch Modan. Two months passed before it promised a handful of soldiers for the valley's defense, and another two months will pass before they arrive. With Thelsamar's guards stretched thin and hostile forces gathering beyond the valley, Magistrate Bluntnose cannot wait.

Merchant Coast. Trade and piracy shape the Merchant Coast along the Barrens' eastern shore. Ratchet handles sea trade, while pirates contest the coast. The Merchant Coast runs along the Barrens' eastern edge, where ships link central Kalimdor with the Eastern Kingdoms and Theramore. The Steamwheedle Cartel's neutral port of Ratchet takes cargo from anyone with coin. Southsea Freebooters also haunt the sands and nearby waters, preying on merchant ships and setting up illicit operations along the beaches.

Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears. Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears is a bounty offered by a grieving enclave seeking violent vengeance against the Al'Aketh cult. After suffering a terrible tragedy at the cultists' hands, the enclave promises coin and access to the Nightclaw's hidden lore in exchange for trophies harvested from their slain enemies. Taking up this task plunges travelers directly into the conflict spreading across Shadowgale Forest and surrounding territories. The feud between the Nightclaw enclave and the Al'Aketh cultists is bitter and merciless. Following an unspecified but devastating tragedy inflicted upon the enclave, the survivors have abandoned any hope of peaceful reconciliation. To avenge their fallen kin, they turn to wandering adventurers and mercenaries, demanding violent retribution. In exchange for cutting down the cultists and taking their ears as grim proof of the deed, the enclave offers cold coin and the prospect of deeper trust.

Merissa Stilwell. At Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell welcomes newcomers to Northshire Valley. The young human townsperson offers a cheerful greeting and a helping hand to those training nearby. Merissa Stilwell greets fresh recruits arriving in Northshire Valley from her place at Northshire Abbey. She offers newcomers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting and finding their way. Her surname is shared by craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom, including the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell. Merissa remains a peaceful local presence amid the kingdom's rising tensions.

Merrin Rockweaver. On a ridge above Whelgar's Excavation Site, Merrin Rockweaver waits with the survivors. A raptor infestation drove them from the dig, where she represented the Explorers' League. Merrin Rockweaver came to the Wetlands for the Ironforge Explorers' League, seeking ancient Titan secrets beneath the muck. The expedition fell apart when the large bones the crew unearthed drew raptors to the dig. The beasts swarmed the trenches, and Merrin and the surviving crew fled, leaving their equipment, notes, and progress behind. Now Merrin is trapped with a few survivors on a bluff overlooking the overrun ruins.

Merrin's Letter. At the Whelgar's Excavation site, Merrin Rockweaver sends an urgent message from the Wetlands. Raptors have overrun the dig, but Merrin assures her loved ones that she survived. Merrin Rockweaver writes from the ruined dig at Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands. The dwarven expedition had been uncovering enormous prehistoric fossils and relics when they disturbed a nest of Mottled Raptors. The beasts swarmed the trenches, killed several workers, and cut off the surviving researchers. Amid the chaos, Merrin sends word to her husband Tarrel at Menethil Harbor. She, Prospector Whelgar, and Ormer Ironbraid survived behind a barricaded shelter.

Message in a Bottle. A washed-up bottle found along the shores of Stranglethorn Vale holds an urgent plea for rescue. Its author claims to be held prisoner by a great beast on an isolated island in the South Seas. Inside a glass container half-buried in the sand lies a neatly penned note asking for immediate assistance. The captive reports being trapped on a foreign island beneath thick jungle canopies, held by a great Skymane. Glimpses through the trees offer only faint landmarks: the coast of Wild Shore lies visible to the northwest, while large sailing vessels drift to the southwest.

Message in a Bottle. Having answered an ocean-borne plea, you find Princess Poobah chained as a captive on an isolated island off the Stranglethorn coast. The monstrous ape King Mukla commands the local beasts and keeps her bound, requiring his defeat to secure the key to her shackle. Following the message in the bottle brings you directly to Princess Poobah, who is held against her will by a heavy chain. The great Skymane gorilla known as King Mukla commands the creatures roaming the island and oversees her imprisonment. Poobah places her faith in you to face this formidable ape and retrieve the key needed to sever her bonds.

name.esES: Mensaje para el Poblado Viento Libre
name.frFR: Un message pour le poste de Librevent
name.ptBR: Mensagem para a Aldeia Vento Livre

text.enUS: Message to Freewind Post. Message to Freewind Post is a Horde quest tasking travelers with carrying urgent dispatches from Brave Moonhorn near the border lifts down into Thousand Needles. The missive warns Cliffwatcher Longhorn of intensifying centaur raids against local caravans. It also raises early concerns regarding the suspicious, standoffish behavior of the neighboring Grimtotem clan. Standing watch near the canyon's western approaches, Brave Moonhorn keeps a vigil over the roads leading down into Thousand Needles. With centaur aggression abruptly spiking, communication between border sentries and the regional leadership is vital. Moonhorn entrusts passing Horde adventurers with carrying an urgent dispatch southeast to Cliffwatcher Longhorn, the commander stationed atop the mesa settlement of Freewind Post.

name.esES: Un mensaje para los Martillo Salvaje

text.enUS: Message to the Wildhammer. At Revantusk Village in the Hinterlands, Otho Moji'ko says the Wildhammer are striking deals with the trolls' enemies, and this time the high elves are their partners. Otho wants a message sent to the Wildhammer dwarves in the blood of the Highvale high elves at Quel'Danil Lodge. The Wildhammer are forging new alliances with the trolls' enemies, and this time the high elves are their partners. Otho Moji'ko spits at the thought. A message is owed to the dwarves, written in the blood of their new friends: slaughter every Highvale high elf you come across and leave the bodies as a warning. Highvale Outrunners, Scouts, Marksmen and Rangers gather at Quel'Danil Lodge, in the Hinterlands' northwest.

Messenger to Darkshire. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Darkshire for aid. Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten Redridge, and Solomon turns to his neighbor for military support. A courier must cross Duskwood's shadowed roads to deliver the letter to Lord Ello Ebonlocke, Darkshire's mayor. Redridge faces growing pressure from Blackrock orcs and gnoll packs, and Lakeshire's guards are stretched thin. Stormwind's royal court has ignored Magistrate Solomon's pleas, while Westfall is caught up in its own insurrection. With little help nearby, Solomon writes to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Duskwood, hoping Darkshire can lend or hire its Night Watch to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses.

Messenger to Darkshire. Messenger to Darkshire concludes the desperate diplomatic correspondence between Lakeshire and Darkshire. Magistrate Solomon's plea for military reinforcement is firmly rejected by Lord Ello Ebonlocke, exposing the bitter truth that both towns have been abandoned to their fates by Stormwind. Facing an onslaught of Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Magistrate Solomon of Redridge hoped his old peer in Duskwood could spare troops. But Lord Ello Ebonlocke's reaction is bordering on outrage. Darkshire is barely holding back the living dead, ravenous beasts, and cursed magic pressing in from every corner of the woods. Ebonlocke bluntly states that the Night Watch exists only because Stormwind abandoned Duskwood first. Stripping Darkshire of its defenders would ensure the settlement falls before the patrol even crosses the forest's edge.

Messenger to Stormwind. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea for help to Stormwind. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs press around the town, and he has no garrison troops to spare for the journey. He entrusts a traveler with The State of Lakeshire for General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind City. Gnolls contest every road from Lakeshire, while Blackrock orcs raid from the north. The town's guardsmen are stretched beyond their limits. Magistrate Solomon cannot spare fighting men for the days-long ride to the capital, so a traveler carries his official plea for regular troops to the city gates.

Messenger to Stormwind. You carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply from Stormwind to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital offers no troops, leaving the settlement to face danger while Stormwind's leaders delay. You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his preliminary reply back to Redridge while he waits for approval from the throne. Without royal authorization, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens remain without city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling under the Blackrock clan.

name.frFR: Un message pour la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Messenger to Westfall. Magistrate Solomon sends a plea from Lakeshire to Westfall for help against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls. With Stormwind's forces absent, he hopes Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia can lend aid. Blackrock orcs and gnolls besiege Lakeshire, and the Stormwind Army has not arrived in force. Magistrate Solomon knows the town guards and irregulars cannot hold the Redridge Mountains alone. With no royal reserves in sight, he writes a formal plea for help. Word has reached him of a citizen defense group forming west of Elwynn Forest, so he sends his appeal there.

name.frFR: Un message pour la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Messenger to Westfall. A letter from Westfall brings Magistrate Solomon a hard answer in Lakeshire. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall has been left to face its own troubles. Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. He looks to the southern frontier for help and writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are.

Michael Garrett. In the Undercity, Michael Garrett awaits a crate bound for the Sepulcher. Gordon Wendham packs field supplies in the Trade Quarter, and you bring them to Garrett for the Forsaken bat network to carry toward Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken send supplies from the Undercity to outposts such as the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Gordon Wendham packs field supplies in a crate in the Trade Quarter. Moving freight along the ground through blighted forests is slow and leaves it open to ambush by Scourge remnants or wild beasts.

name.esES: Mitad de la llave de Gelkak
name.ptBR: Parte do Meio da Chave de Gelkak

text.enUS: Middle of Gelkak's Key. Off Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast’s key lies in three pieces after threshadons sank his ship. Greymist murlocs took the middle fragment from the shore. Gelkak Gyromast’s winding key broke when threshadons dragged his ship beneath the waves. The gnome pirate came ashore with his belongings shattered on the rocky shoals. The specialized key was made for his mechanical first mate, but the wreck split it into three pieces scattered along the strand. Coastal beasts carried off the top and bottom. Greymist murlocs prowling the Darkshore surf took the middle piece and kept it in their camps and among the wreckage they hold.

Miles Welsh. In the Pools of Vision, Miles Welsh teaches priests beneath Thunder Bluff. The Forsaken trainer offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline in the tauren capital. Miles Welsh teaches priests in the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff. Far from Lordaeron's plague-scarred ruins, the Forsaken priest makes his home in the grotto beneath the city. He instructs travelers in divine and shadowy energies. His place in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous ties between the Forsaken and the Horde. There, he shares sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in shadow and faith.

Military Ward. Red banners mark the Military Ward, where Ironforge's defenders gather and train. Its command halls, weapons masters, barracks, siege engines, and flying machines serve the mountain city's military. The Military Ward gathers Ironforge's defenses in a busy staging ground along the northern edge of the mountain fortress. At its center, the Hall of Arms holds warrior and hunter trainers and battlemasters, with hangars for dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Around the drill squares and training dummies, supply shops include Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms. The ward is Ironforge's main staging point for mountaineers and city defenders.

Milli Featherwhistle. At Steelgrill's Depot, Milli Featherwhistle keeps Gnomeregan's mechanostriders in motion. She builds and maintains these clockwork mounts for her kin and trusted allies among the exiles. Outdoors in the biting chill at Steelgrill's Depot, just east of Kharanos, Milli keeps clockwork steeds ready for Gnomeregan's displaced people. Dwarves and night elves favor living mounts, but Milli builds each mechanostrider herself. She calibrates its gears, pistons, and balancing gyros so it can travel across Dun Morogh's snowy crags.

Milly Osworth. At Northshire Abbey, Deputy Willem sends you to help Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in jeopardy, and she needs help across the abbey grounds. The work takes you from defending the abbey to aiding Elwynn Forest's civilians. After you prove your mettle against the Defias thieves encroaching on Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem recognizes you as capable and willing to help. He sends you to assist his friend Milly Osworth. This favor is personal, outside the abbey's official guard duties, and Milly is a civilian caught in the valley's growing unrest.

Milly's Harvest. In the Northshire Vineyards, Milly's grapes lie abandoned after the Defias arrive. Crates and buckets of fruit remain at risk of theft or being crushed beneath the abbey guards' boots. Milly Osworth gathers grapes in the Northshire Vineyards, where the harvest matters to local vintners and the abbey community. When armed brigands in red masks push into the fields, Milly flees to the abbey grounds. Her fresh-picked grapes remain scattered between the rows.

Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her harvest lies scattered in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, where it may be stolen or crushed. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. She left her gathered grapes behind in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears that boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind.

Milton Sheaf. In Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf guards the kingdom's written history. He tends the Royal Library and calls on Alliance travelers to recover lost books and records. Milton Sheaf tends the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. While the court handles politics, noble disputes, and military concerns, he preserves the written record. He sees accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms as a duty, especially amid war, loss, and instability.

Miner Johnson. Deep in the Deadmines, Miner Johnson wanders among the Defias laborers. He is a seasoned miner who oversees excavation ahead of the heavy machinery, though he appears only now and then. Miner Johnson works among the laborers digging beneath the Deadmines for Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress. He waits in an alcove to the left, before the shredders in the Mast Room. Stronger and more aggressive than the other miners, he can be hard to find as he wanders the tunnels.

name.frFR: La bonne fortune d'un mineur pauvre

text.enUS: Miner's Fortune. Wharfmaster Dizzywig has heard of a fist-sized emerald at the Venture Company's Boulder Lode Mine. He hires you to take the Cats Eye Emerald from the mine's supervisors and share the profits. Wharfmaster Dizzywig hears the merchants who pass through Ratchet's harbor on the routes between Ratchet and Booty Bay. Word reaches him of a huge gem found deep in the Boulder Lode Mine. The Venture Company strips the northern Barrens for its own gain, so few are likely to ask questions if its finest recent find disappears.

Miners' Gear. Miners' Gear lies stored in the Silver Stream Mine after its ore ran out. Kobolds have overrun the tunnels, and the Miners' League wants the tools recovered before local guards attack. The Silver Stream Mine in northern Loch Modan holds the Miners' League's stored tools. After the mine ran out of ore, the league turned its quiet tunnels into a depot for mining equipment. Kobolds soon overran the mine, took the goods, and made their nests among the crates. The league fears the dwarven gear could be wrecked in an assault by the Mountaineers or ruined by the scavengers. Adventurers are sent inside to bring the crates back to safety.

Miners' Union Card. In Moonbrook, union cards mark the laborers lost beneath the earth. Workers once carried them through the mines, and now the cards remain with skeletal dead in the dark drifts. Before the Defias Brotherhood took control of Moonbrook, miners worked below ground for the guild, drawing valuable ore for the kingdom. A tunnel collapse crushed a major shaft and killed dozens beneath the rock. The dead rose as skeletal miners, excavators, and dynamiters. Union cards remain in their bony pockets, the last proof of who they were. In Stormwind, surviving colleagues seek the cards to learn the dead workers' identities and bring closure to their families.

Mining Consultant. Mining Consultant is a Northshire Valley quest that sends adventurers to confer with Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed outside Echo Ridge Mine. Her observations reveal an unusual development: the local kobolds have begun plundering books from Northshire Abbey's library. The kobold infestation at Echo Ridge Mine has taken an unexpected turn. Rather than merely defending subterranean claims and gathering candles, the creatures have caught the attention of local authorities due to strange, coordinated disturbances. Adventurers are directed to seek out Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed near the mine's entrance, to ascertain what she has witnessed from her vantage point outside the tunnels.

Minor Manifestation of Earth. At sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar, Minor Manifestation of Earth waits unseen. Fledgling shamans who drink Earth Sapta can meet the spirit and receive rough quartz for carving their first earth totem. Earth spirits dwell beneath dirt and stone, but reaching them takes a deliberate rite. At Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger beyond ordinary sight, surrounded by lesser elemental presences. Only initiates who drink Earth Sapta, a draught brewed by shamanic mentors, can cross the veil between the physical world and the elements. When an initiate makes contact, the spirit grants the earth's blessings and a piece of rough quartz. The novice can use it as the spiritual focus for making an Earth Totem.

Minor Manifestation of Water. Along North Tide's Run, the Minor Manifestation of Water awaits shamans on Silverpine Forest's coast. Its corrupted counterpart must be cleansed before the peaceful spirit can be consulted. The Minor Manifestation of Water waits west of the Sepulcher, along North Tide's Run. For developing shamans, meeting the spirit is an essential rite. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, yet malevolent blight can corrupt them. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation before the pure spirit reveals itself. Once cleansed, the Minor Manifestation of Water guides shamans on their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

Minshina's Skull. On the Echo Isles, Minshina's Skull holds the bound soul of Minshina, a Darkspear troll and brother of Master Gadrin. Zalazane trapped him there after driving the tribe from the isles, and uses the skull to fuel dark rituals. Minshina was captured and slain when Zalazane seized the Echo Isles and drove out the Darkspear. The traitorous witch doctor bound his victim's soul to Minshina's severed skull instead of letting him pass into death. The skull lies within a circle of power on the southernmost isle, tethering Minshina to Zalazane's magic. Tormented by dreams of his brother calling to him, Master Gadrin seeks brave travelers to enter the occupied islands, reclaim the skull, and break Zalazane's hold over Minshina's spirit.

Minshina's Skull. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin hears the desperate cries of his dead brother, Minshina. Zalazane slew Minshina on the Echo Isles and bound his soul with dark magic to his own severed skull. To free him from torment, you must reclaim the skull from Zalazane's ritual grounds. Master Gadrin is one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village, yet dark visions torment him. His brother Minshina fell when Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized control of the Echo Isles. Minshina died in the conflict, but death has brought him no peace. In troll tradition and voodoo mysticism, the body can die while the spirit remains bound. Now Minshina's tormented voice reaches Gadrin in his dreams, pleading to be saved from a fate worse than death.

Mirage Flats. Mirage Flats is a barren, sun-scorched expanse nestled in the central wastes of the Badlands. Lying east of Dustbelch Grotto, this dry plateau is notorious for shimmering heat hazes and hungry predators. Situated east of Dustbelch Grotto, the Mirage Flats present travelers with an unforgiving stretch of cracked red dirt and shimmering heat waves that give the plain its name. Few civilized souls linger here; instead, the open flats are dominated by opportunistic scavengers and lethal beasts. Flocks of giant buzzards circle lazily on hot thermals above, watching for the leavings of ferocious ridge stalkers and pack-hunting crag coyotes that scour the brush for easy prey.

Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage.

Mirages. Hurrying away from the Uldaman excavation site, Sigrun Ironhew's party left wagons and crates behind. Ogres from Camp Kosh took the cart holding all their weapons, and since then the party has had no food. In their rush to leave the Uldaman excavation site, Sigrun Ironhew and company left many wagons and supply crates behind. Ogres from Camp Kosh have been picking over the leftovers like vultures. They took the cart holding all the party's weapons, and since then the party has had no food. Sigrun admits it is embarrassing and asks you to retrieve the supply crate.

Mirkfallon Lake. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Mirkfallon Lake fills a basin beneath Windshear Crag. Native wildlife crowds its waters and banks, from aggressive slimes to thunder lizards and wyverns. Mirkfallon Lake lies at the center of the Stonetalon range, between the passes to Webwinder Path in the south and Stonetalon Peak in the north. Runoff from the highlands feeds its waters, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their high roosts. Strange slimes bubble in the lake, making the crossing hazardous for travelers.

Mirror Lake. Novice Alliance mages in Stormwind's Mage Quarter are sent to sample Mirror Lake's waters for magical contamination. Jennea Cannon sends them southwest of the city gates to test the waterfall spray. Azeroth's arcane currents were shaken by conflicts from the opening of the Dark Portal through the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. Those shocks tore ancient currents from their stable channels. In Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, magi like Jennea Cannon watch the changes closely. They fear that displaced arcane power could reach the wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems.

Mirror Lake. Water spills into Mirror Lake beneath Stormwind's cliffs in northwestern Elwynn Forest, near an orchard. Defias bandits prowl the surrounding orchards, while mages watch for trouble in the forest's arcane currents. Mirror Lake lies beneath Stormwind City's walls, where fishermen and weary travelers might seek a quiet rest. Defias Brotherhood brigands stalk the surrounding orchards, making a long stay perilous for locals. Mystical disturbances across Azeroth have also begun to warp the forest's natural channels of arcane energy. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum watch the lake closely. They send practitioners to sample its currents and guard against chaotic arcane runoff poisoning communities downstream.

Mirror Lake Orchard. Defias bandits now hold Mirror Lake Orchard, on Mirror Lake's southern shore in western Elwynn Forest. The quiet homestead near Thunder Falls has fallen to outlaws while Stormwind's guards are stretched thin. Mirror Lake Orchard once fed a peaceful farmstead with the clean waters of Mirror Lake. Now Defias Brotherhood bandits have seized the cottage and grounds near Thunder Falls. With Stormwind's military stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn missing, rural homes across Elwynn are easy targets for outlaws seeking shelter.

name.esES: Muestra de agua del Lago Espejo
name.ptBR: Amostra de Água do Lago Espelhado

text.enUS: Mirror Lake Water Sample. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, a flask of water is gathered for Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. The mages will test it for signs of altered arcane currents in local water. Jennea Cannon sends promising apprentices to collect water from Mirror Lake. The lake lies just southwest of the Stormwind Gate, and they fill a specially prepared flask at the base of its waterfall. The Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind is concerned that the world's mystic channels remain unsettled after catastrophic conflicts. Its mages will examine the sample for stray magical taint in the waterways used by people nearby.

Misha. Misha is the loyal bear companion of Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde. She wanders Kalimdor faithfully at the half-ogre beastmaster's side. Misha is a brown bear who walks at the side of the wandering Rexxar, a solitary spirit who trusts beasts more than people. Together they have forged a fierce, protective partnership that has weathered countless wildernesses and bloody battles.

Misha Tor'kren. At the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, Misha Tor'kren waits for word of her son. Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks, but has not returned. Misha Tor'kren tends her farm near Thunder Ridge, southeast of the ridge. Her son Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle, but he never came home. With Durotar's frontier dangers stretching the orcish watchtowers thin, Misha has no word of where he is. She needs travelers willing to search the riverbanks for signs of her son.

Missing In Action. In the Redridge Mountains, Corporal Keeshan is missing after his regiment was overrun. Blackrock orcs knocked him unconscious and dragged him into a cave fortress. Now he needs an escort back to Lakeshire, where the garrison can learn what became of the missing men. Blackrock orcs descend from the northern peaks, making the Redridge Mountains more perilous. Town guard patrols often meet ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's unit suffered the worst of them. The regiment was outnumbered and overwhelmed, and most of its soldiers fell in the attack. Keeshan survived when a crushing blow knocked him unconscious before the orcs could execute him. They dragged him to their cave as a prisoner.

name.deDE: Mission: möglich, aber nicht sehr wahrscheinlich

text.enUS: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. In the northern Barrens, Horde rogues face a Venture Company outpost that tests stealth, theft, and combat.
