They infiltrate an oil tower, kill Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, and take a potent chemical brew for the Shattered Hand. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company keeps an isolated drilling tower. Taskmaster Fizzule, a Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, orders rogues to rely on underworld craft instead of an open assault. He asks them to pick the key from Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him. Then they climb past workers and sentries changed by the tower’s experiments.

Mist. In Teldrassil's shaded boughs, Mist lies wounded and separated from her companion. She needs a safe path back to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at a nearby moon well. A gray sabercat named Mist lies wounded among Teldrassil's undergrowth. Deep slashes mark her back and belly. Her blue eyes are bright, and she stays calm rather than acting like a feral beast. She looks to friendly travelers for guidance and protection.

Mist Veil's Lockbox. Off Darkshore, Mist Veil's Lockbox lies in the sunken night elven vessel. It holds the captain's log and personal effects, lost when coastal murlocs ambushed and sank the ship. The night elven vessel Mist Veil sank while sailing toward Auberdine. Coastal murlocs ambushed it alongside its sister ship, the Silver Dawning, and overwhelmed both vessels. The captain perished in the attack. Their logbook and personal belongings remain sealed in the lockbox in the flooded hold, surrounded by murlocs.

Mist's Edge. North of Auberdine, Mist's Edge follows Darkshore's western shore beneath ocean fog. Gray beaches hold shipwrecks, great sea creature remains, crabs, and murlocs. Mist's Edge runs along Darkshore's western edge, where damp sand and rocky tidepools lie beneath coastal fog. Shattered vessels, drift timber, and the remains of huge sea creatures litter the beach. Crabs forage along the shore, while murloc tribes make their homes in the surf.

Misty Pine Refuge. At Misty Pine Refuge, the Argent Dawn keeps a small outpost in central Dun Morogh. Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming Argent Dawn outpost among Dun Morogh's windswept hills. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the surrounding crags, while Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, keeps a quiet hearth amid the bitter cold and dangers of the mountain roads.

Misty Reed Post. Misty Reed Post is a rugged Horde encampment situated between Stagalbog and the Misty Reed Strand in the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Established as a frontline watch under the authority of Stonard, it serves to monitor the dangerous wetlands and the treacherous coastline. Tucked away in the humid gloom between the Stagalbog and the eastern shore, Misty Reed Post is little more than a spartan camp under Stonard's banner. It is manned by a handful of Stonard hunters, a shaman, Katar, and Tok'Kar, who oversees the watch. Conditions are rough, offering no fortified shelter from the marsh's hostile wildlife and lingering damp. Tok'Kar harbors quiet ambitions that the Horde command in Stonard will one day reinforce the position with a sturdy orcish burrow or watchtower, though for now, the scouts must hold the marsh with tents, campfire smoke, and sharpened steel.

Misty Reed Strand. The Misty Reed Strand is the fog-shrouded, desolate eastern coastline of the Swamp of Sorrows. Lined with jagged rocks, washed-up wreckage, and creeping swamp mist, it is home to aggressive crabs, crocolisks, and coastal murloc tribes. Travelers venturing down to the surf often find themselves contending with the local wildlife for whatever resources wash ashore. Stretching along the entire eastern border of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Reed Strand forms a damp barrier between the deep mire and the Great Sea. Heavy mists constantly roll in off the water, obscuring vision and muffling the cries of native wildlife. The beaches are littered with sea debris, driftwood, and decaying vegetation washed out from the bog inland. Because of its remote position and harsh climate, no formal permanent settlements hold the shoreline, leaving the sands to aggressive crustaceans, stalking crocolisks, and territorial murlocs who violently defend their foraging grounds.

Misty Shore. Misty Shore is the quiet lakeshore of the Alterac Mountains, skirting the eastern shore of Lordamere Lake. Stretching between Dandred's Fold and the perimeter of Dalaran, it offers wide, foggy views of the Dawning Isles and the sinister silhouette of Fenris Keep. Running along Lordamere Lake, the Misty Shore stretches between Dandred's Fold and Dalaran. Thick, damp air regularly drifts off the lake, obscuring snapping turtles and the occasional zealous fanatic who wanders down from regional strongholds.

Misty Valley. Tucked away in the northwestern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Valley is a shadowed, fog-drenched hollow north of the pass into Deadwind. The secluded basin is overrun by primordial swamp beasts, wandering swampwalkers, and tangled horrors. Deep in its rearmost cave dwells the colossal and terrifying Mire Lord. Nestled beneath the high cliffs separating the Swamp of Sorrows from Deadwind Pass, the Misty Valley is perpetually choked with thick marsh vapor. Unlike the open wetlands to the east, this isolated pocket is dense with colossal marsh elementals, including looming swampwalkers, ancient swampwalker elders, and creeping tangled horrors. At the far end of the misty gorge lies a cavern that serves as the lair of the Mire Lord, one of the most formidable natural threats haunting the bog.

Mitsuwa. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa mourns the trolls slain on their journey through Ashenvale. He calls on Horde champions to recover their stolen charms. Mitsuwa serves the Horde at Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, alongside Marukai. Thistlefur furbolgs of northern Ashenvale ambushed and slaughtered a group of traveling trolls bound for the outpost. Mitsuwa sees their deaths as a grievous offense. He sends warriors to the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen troll charms and honor the spirits of his kin.

Mizjah Ruins. The Mizjah Ruins are ancient stone remains nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long abandoned by their original troll architects, the crumbling structures have been seized by the brute-strength Mosh'Ogg ogres. From this vantage, the ogres launch disruptive ambushes against passing supply caravans traveling toward the Swamp of Sorrows. Like many of the ancient stone ruins scattered throughout Stranglethorn Vale, the Mizjah Ruins were built by the Gurubashi Empire long before modern empires rose. Today, the moss-choked arches and cracked flagstones are occupied by the Mosh'Ogg clan, primarily brute warriors and crude witch doctors. Far from keeping to their stolen perimeter, these ogres routinely raid nearby supply convoys bound for the Horde settlement of Stonard, transforming ancient history into a persistent, bloody thorn in the side of Grom'gol's commanders.

Mo'grosh Crystal. In northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres mine and hoard rare crystals with unusual alchemical properties. The crystals help dwarven engineers neutralize Dark Iron explosives. The Mo'grosh ogres mine these crystals in their stronghold in northeastern Loch Modan. Though the ogres favor brute strength over delicate metallurgy, their clan prizes the stones. Common enforcers, mystic shamans, and towering leaders carry them. The crystals are uncommon, so the ogres guard them closely within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold looms over the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. The fortified ogre den is dug among ancient ruins, and its inhabitants threaten the dwarven settlements below. Mo'grosh ogres raid supply caravans in northeastern Loch Modan. From their caves and outer camps, they threaten travelers and the peace of Thelsamar. Rugged stonework scattered around the camp points to an older settlement. The ogres claimed the site and raised their distinctive mounds.

Modr Fragment. At Whelgar Excavation Site, Modr Fragment lies among the relics and loose earth of a raptor-overrun dig. The ancient Titan script on it is one of four missing pieces of the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone, a massive tablet marked with ancient Titan writing, at his Wetlands dig. Vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from the site before they could finish their work. The translated inscription broke off at four gaps, hiding warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. Modr Fragment is one of the missing pieces, left among the relics and overturned soil when the diggers fled for their lives.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin seeks to harness the natural magic of Stranglethorn Vale for the benefit of the Horde. Building upon his previous rituals at Grom'gol Base Camp, he asks for sharp claws and a pristine feline fang to weave a powerful enchantment. Within Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin works to understand and bend the feral power of the wild to strengthen the Horde. Having seen success in his initial rites, he promises to craft a specialized enchanted relic for those willing to brave the dense underbrush and stalk the deadly predators prowling the surrounding territory.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin in Grom'gol Base Camp needs a sturdy magical binding to hold together the Stranglethorn trophies collected so far. To bind the feathers, claws, and fang securely, he requires an aged sinew harvested from the elder primates roaming southern Stranglethorn Vale. Having gathered feathers, claws, and a pristine fang, Far Seer Mok'thardin reaches the next stage of his ritual. To fasten these potent relics together, he requires a magical tether of exceptional toughness. Only the aged sinew of an Elder Mistvale Gorilla will suffice to endure the magic he intends to weave.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin continues assembling the components for a potent shamanistic item to aid the Horde. After working with feline trophies, he turns his attention toward the feathers worn by the raptors of Stranglethorn Vale. Following the recovery of materials from the jungle's feline predators, Far Seer Mok'thardin reveals that more components are needed before his shamanistic ritual can begin. To forge a tool fit to assist the Warchief, he requires feathers worn by Jungle Stalkers. These raptors inhabit the dense jungle south of Grom'gol Base Camp, not far from the great arena.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin requires one final sacred component to complete the enchantment of a ceremonial choker at Grom'gol Base Camp. He directs you to an elevated Holy Spring along the southern bluffs near the western sea, which has drawn the attention of a hostile naga expedition. Following the earlier stages of Mok'thardin's enchantment, the far seer seeks water from a Holy Spring situated high above the bluffs in the southern reaches of Stranglethorn Vale, near the western coast. The site is a point of contention among scholars of the mystic and divine, with every race across Azeroth claiming the holy waters were sanctified specifically for their own people.

Moldy Tome. A half of the Tome of the Cabal lies ruined on the Hillsbrad coast. Salvaged from a shipwreck, the Moldy Tome holds dark rituals sought by warlocks who study demonic summoning. The Tome of the Cabal was a rare work of dark arts held in Lordaeron. At some point, it was vandalized and torn in two. One half, now called the Moldy Tome, traveled by ship south toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The vessel never arrived. It sank in the dangerous waters west of Southshore, and the surviving half washed ashore south of Azurelode Mine. Damp and surf ruined its pages, while murlocs scavenged along the Hillsbrad coast.

Molsen Farm. Molsen Farm is an abandoned homestead located in the breadbasket region of Westfall. Once a fertile piece of farmland feeding Stormwind, it has fallen into ruin following the rise of the Defias Brotherhood and the prowling mechanical harvest golems left in their wake. Like many homesteads across Westfall, Molsen Farm stands as a casualty of the kingdom's neglect and criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, the resident farmers were driven out or worse, abandoning their crops and buildings. Now, instead of laborers gathering grain, hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the untended fields, making the farm a hazard to anyone traveling through the province.

Monte Gazlowe. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe keeps a neutral port open to traders from every side. He founded the town with the fortune he earned as the Horde’s chief engineer during the building of Durotar and Orgrimmar. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe runs a port where rivals can trade under the Steamwheedle Cartel. He founded the town on the barren coast after earning a handsome payday for his engineering work with the new Horde. Horde, Alliance, and independent traders may barter there, so long as they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy.

name.esES: Cubil del Horror de la Luna

text.enUS: Moon Horror Den. Moon Horror Den is a secluded, frost-rimed cave located just northeast of the goblin trading post of Everlook in Winterspring. Tucked against the jagged mountainside, the cavern serves as a nesting hollow for ferocious raging owlbeasts. Travelers must take care when venturing near its icy mouth, as these territorial wildkin fiercely defend their shelter. Situated only a short trek northeast from Everlook's guarded gates, the Moon Horror Den cuts deep into the mountain rock. The cave is home to powerful raging owlbeasts—formidable wildkin known for their brute strength and feral disposition in the harsh snows of Winterspring. Although geographically close to the furbolg settlement of Winterfall Village to the south, the sheer mountain face creates an impassable natural barrier, ensuring the den remains an isolated refuge for the wildkin rather than a corridor of travel.

Moon Priestess Amara. West of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara watches Teldrassil’s road to Darnassus. Two huntresses guard her as she keeps watch over the woodland paths. Moon Priestess Amara watches the road west of Dolanaar with two huntress companions, Nhemai and Yaeliura. As a priestess of the Sisterhood of Elune, she brings spiritual guidance to her post, while her watch helps keep Teldrassil’s roads secure. Travelers heading west can seek her direction toward Darnassus. Those burdened in spirit can also seek a path of redemption from her.

Moonbrook. In southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook lies under Defias control, its streets emptied of peaceful residents. The Brotherhood uses the town as a guarded screen for its hidden headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook stood at the heart of Westfall’s breadbasket, supporting farming families and the gold shafts of the Deadmines. The Old Horde razed the town, but it was rebuilt after the Second War. Its peace did not last. The House of Nobles in Stormwind neglected the settlement, and its military protection was stripped away. Unable to resist the red-masked bandits, Moonbrook’s people were driven from their homes. Citizens and teachers fled toward Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest.

name.esES: Espionaje en Arroyo de la Luna

text.enUS: Moonbrook Espionage. Alba Fairmoon sends you to scout Moonbrook, where signs of industry trouble the Alliance. The poison found across Westfall does not seem to come from the lesser mines, so attention turns to the Deadmines beneath the town. The mines already examined across Westfall offer no answer to the poison spreading through the region. No known surface excavation appears to be its source. One major site remains unexplored: the vast shafts of the Deadmines, directly beneath Moonbrook’s ruined streets.

name.esES: Escuela de Arroyo de la Luna

text.enUS: Moonbrook Schoolhouse. In Moonbrook's northwestern corner, the schoolhouse stands abandoned under Defias occupation. A small graveyard lies behind the hall where Stalvan Mistmantle once taught local children. Moonbrook's schoolhouse once welcomed children before ruin and bandits overtook the town. After Stalvan Mistmantle began tutoring local children, the mayor commissioned him to run a school. Students filled the hall in Moonbrook's brighter days, when the town prospered. Now outlaws occupy the abandoned building, and weathered headstones in its rear cemetery look out over Westfall's decline.

Moonglade. In Darnassus, young night elf druids learn to reach Moonglade. Mathrengyl Bearwalker teaches novices a spell to carry themselves across the world into Moonglade, where they meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. There begins their path toward mastering bear form. Moonglade is an ancient sanctuary apart from the rest of Azeroth, devoted to the teachings of Cenarius. Keeper Remulos watches over its groves, where druids find peace and communion with nature. Young druids learn a spell that lets them carry themselves across the world into Moonglade, reaching a heart of druidic wisdom beyond mortal distances.

Moonglade. In Moonglade, a young tauren druid learns to reach nature’s ancient keepers. Guided by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, the initiate learns to cross the waking world and commune with them directly. Moonglade lies beyond Kalimdor’s faction struggles. Keeper Remulos, son of Cenarius, watches over the ancient valley, a neutral refuge for all who follow nature. Night elf and tauren druids enter Nighthaven as equals, beneath the Cenarion Circle’s timeless mantle.

Moonglow Vest. In Darnassus, Lotherias needs leather gear for young adventurers setting out across Kalimdor. She offers the pattern for a Moonglow Vest in return for shipments of embossed leather goods. In Darnassus, leatherworkers work to outfit sentinels and young scouts. Night elves and allied wanderers leave Teldrassil for the wilds of Kalimdor, where sturdy armor is in demand. Lotherias is among the master leatherworkers supplying them with gear.

Moonpetal Lily. Moonpetal Lilies are large, luminous flora native to Teldrassil that flourish around freshwater pools. Renowned for their potent restorative qualities, their petals are prized as key ingredients in natural remedies and healing draughts. Moonpetal Lilies grow exclusively along the moist banks of freshwater pools and ponds, particularly favored along the northwestern side of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Like much of the plant life flourishing atop the newly grown World Tree, they absorb the unique essence of Teldrassil's sheltered groves. Their broad petals are gentle and radiant, easily spotted hugging the tranquil water's edge where natural moisture allows them to thrive.

Moonshrine Ruins. Deep in Blackfathom Deeps, the Moonshrine Ruins lie flooded and seized by the Twilight's Hammer. Their halls once honored Elune, but the cult now carries out dark rituals among the ancient stones. Beyond the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar, the Moonshrine Ruins lie along the Ashenvale coast. These partly submerged halls once echoed with chants to Elune, the Moon Goddess. The Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in seawater. Now murky waters churn with aggressive crabs and serpentine threshadons. The Twilight's Hammer cult holds the stones and performs dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origins.

Moonshrine Sanctum. Within Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight's Hammer gathers beneath Queen Azshara's statue. Twilight Lord Kelris watches over the ancient shrine, which guards the sealed way to Aku'mai's lair. Past the flooded Moonshrine Ruins, cultists gather in the Moonshrine Sanctum, the heart of Twilight's Hammer activity inside Blackfathom Deeps. Night elves built the hall millennia ago to honor the moon and their rulers. Now the cult has defiled it, yet carefully maintains the towering statue of Queen Azshara. Beneath the cavernous stone ceiling, Twilight Lord Kelris watches as the cultists chant dark rituals day and night.

Moonspray. Moonspray carries travelers between Darkshore and Teldrassil. The Alliance transport sails across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree. Moonspray sails between Auberdine and Rut'theran Village. Across the Veiled Sea, the vessel carries adventurers, couriers, and provisions between Darkshore's coast and the night elf sanctuary at Teldrassil's crown.

Moonstalker Fang. Near Auberdine, travelers gather Moonstalker Fangs for Wizbang Cranktoggle's sampling devices. The teeth come from the moonstalkers of Darkshore. Moonstalker Fangs come from saber cats that hunt along Darkshore’s forest fringes. Their long teeth can shear flesh and bone. Wizbang Cranktoggle, an eccentric gnome tinkerer, uses them in a different way. North of Auberdine, near the bridge, Buzzbox 323 crushes the durable fangs to dust for his ecological surveys.

Moonwarden the Elder. At the Crossroads, Moonwarden the Elder receives travelers beneath a beam of light. During the Lunar Festival, people honor ancestral spirits and seek his wisdom and directions to elders across Kalimdor. At the Crossroads, a column of light falls around Elder Moonwarden. He is one of the ancient spirits honored during the Lunar Festival, when mortals set aside their conflicts to seek the wisdom of generations past.

Moonwell (Ashenvale). This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research often seek out Shael'dryn, who keeps watch beside its tranquil basin. Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

text.enUS: Moonwell Water Tube. At Auberdine, water from the moonwell carries purifying nature magic. The vial is used to test a mysterious red crystal set among Darkshore’s eastern ridges. Water from Auberdine’s moonwell fills the tube. The sacred pool is tied to Elune and holds restorative, purifying magic. Even a small amount can be used against corruption or to test strange mystical forces.

Mor'Ladim. Mor'Ladim stalks the grounds of Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood, a vengeful skeletal warrior. He was once Morgan Ladimore, a noble knight who lost his family and was overcome by grief and madness, rising in undeath to kill those who cross his path. Before Raven Hill feared his name, Morgan Ladimore defended the helpless from Grand Hamlet, now called Darkshire. He married Lys at eighteen, and they raised three children in peace until war called him north. During the Third War, Morgan marched with Uther the Lightbringer to Lordaeron. There he witnessed the fall of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the spread of Kel'Thuzad's plague, and Uther's death.

Mor'rogal. In Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal guides travelers toward the dangers and promise of the Stonetalon Mountains. Mor'rogal watches the deep crevices and caverns of the Stonetalon Mountains from Sun Rock Retreat. Their twisting passages offer riches, but can also bring deadly danger. He sends brave Horde wanderers to troubled places such as Boulderslide Ravine. To Mor'rogal, facing those depths tests the spirit of anyone who seeks glory by following heart and soul.

Mor'shan Rampart. At Mor'shan Rampart, the Horde guards the northern end of the Gold Road and the way into Ashenvale. The Warsong clan built the barricade to shield Horde territory from night elf counterattacks and stage raids into the forest. Mor'shan Rampart guards the northern end of the Gold Road, where the Barrens meet Ashenvale. Its timber walls and watchtowers were raised against night elf strikes over the Horde's logging. From here, raiding parties head north toward Astranaar.

Morbent Fel. Above Raven Hill Cemetery, Morbent Fel's wards keep him beyond ordinary steel. Sven Yorgen sends you with Morbent's Bane to break those wards and end the necromancer's terror in western Duskwood. Morbent Fel haunts an abandoned house atop a rocky ridge just east of Sven's camp. The house looks over the sprawl of Raven Hill Cemetery. From there, the necromancer sends waves of undead through the surrounding forest and defiles Duskwood's graves. Dark magic and loyal undead thralls have kept ordinary steel from reaching him.

More Sparklematic Action. Deep in Gnomeregan, the Sparklematic 5200 still cleans what can be saved. The machine remained behind when the city was evacuated, and for a small silver fee it scrubs curiosities coated in muck and radioactive sludge. Gnomeregan's engineers installed automated devices throughout the city before the trogg invasion and the fallout that followed. Toxic waste and hostile automatons now fill its corridors, yet the Sparklematic 5200 still follows its exact programming. It needs three silver coins and an artifact caked in grime to begin.

More Wastewander Justice. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan now turns to the tougher Wastewander nomads: their rogues, assassins and shadow mages, to be found east and southeast of town. The fewer nomads left, the easier it will be to take back the water wells. You have done a good job so far, in Bilgewhizzle's view, but taking back the wells is best done against as few nomads as possible. Now the targets are the nomads' rogues, assassins and shadow mages, east and southeast of Gadgetzan. Bilgewhizzle admits they are a nasty lot, but says the wells are rightfully the company's.

Morgan Pestle. In Stormwind, Morgan Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. He works with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire, handling supplies and alchemical research for the capital. Morgan Pestle sells alchemical goods, reagents, and practical remedies at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. His brother William keeps a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, while Morgan tends their family trade in the capital. He receives supplies from the rural heartlands, including candles sent by William.

Morgan Stern. Angus Stern of the Blue Recluse in Stormwind is putting together a new menu of rural dishes with a bayou theme. Angus has a nephew, Morgan, who was sent to Theramore to gather recipes from the locals, and wants word of what Morgan has found so far. Angus Stern believes the customers of the Blue Recluse will love a menu of rural dishes in the bayou style. To build it, Angus sent nephew Morgan off to Theramore, a city beside Dustwallow Marsh, to gather the locals' recipes. The trip is too long for Angus to make, so a young traveler like you is wanted to go and speak with Morgan.

Morgan the Collector. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Morgan the Collector directs Defias extortion and gathering across Elwynn Forest. A high-ranking operative, he coordinates local theft from the farmhouse while Goldshire's guard keeps watch nearby. Morgan the Collector skims gold from Elwynn Forest's mines for the Defias Brotherhood. While common bandits harass travelers on the roads, he directs organized shakedowns and gathers stolen coin and supplies for the Brotherhood's wider network. His headquarters is the farmhouse at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where loyal enforcers including Surena Caledon and Erlan Drudgemoor surround him.

Morgan's Plot. Morgan's Plot is a desolate burial ground and crumbling chapel tucked away just behind the tower of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Dominated by restless undead and brooding silence, it holds the forgotten crypts and final resting places of those once tied to Medivh's domain. Nestled against the sheer rocky slopes directly behind Karazhan, Morgan's Plot is a sorrowful, overgrown cemetery centered on a ruined chapel and underground crypts. Long before the land decayed into Deadwind Pass, the estate served the burial needs of the tower's inhabitants and nearby grounds. Following the downfall of the Last Guardian, Medivh, dark energies seeped into the earth, driving away all normalcy. Today, restless unliving wander the chapel grounds, haunting the headstones of servants and historic figures alike.

Morgan's Vigil. Morgan's Vigil is a ruined Alliance redoubt nestled in the southeastern heights of the Burning Steppes. Once a small village, its charred homes and shattered wizard's tower now serve as an austere forward camp for scouts watching the passes to Blackrock Mountain. It remains the sole Alliance foothold in an ash-choked land dominated by Dark Iron dwarves and Blackrock orcs. Perched upon high stone overlooking the fiery wastes, Morgan's Vigil was once a modest settlement before the horrors of the Burning Steppes overran it. Today, charred timbers and the cracked shell of a ruined mage tower stand as grim reminders of the onslaught. The remaining defenders make do beneath rough canvas tents pitched amid the soot. Despite the ruin, the camp retains a gryphon roost, offering an unbroken aerial link back across the mountains to Stormwind City. It serves as a desperately needed haven where scouts, marshals, and passing adventurers catch their breath away from the marauding warbands below.

Morganth. Across Redridge, Theocritus watches Morganth hunt an ancient relic. From the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches the crags of Redridge through his scrying spells. He sees Morganth, a warlock in the Tower of Ilgalar, searching for the Scythe of Elune. Fearing Morganth is close to claiming it, Theocritus asks Alliance champions to stop him before Stormwind is threatened.

Morin Cloudstalker. Along the eastern road from Bloodhoof Village, Morin Cloudstalker watches over Mulgore. The tauren scout keeps an eye on trade routes and investigates threats to travelers. Morin Cloudstalker watches the trail east toward the Barrens. He scouts the road and guards those traveling through Mulgore. The plains are usually peaceful, but trade routes and shifting territories have brought opportunists and bandits close to the tauren homeland.

Morlos'Aran. Morlos'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in the southern reaches of Felwood. Once a proud and thriving settlement before the Great Sundering, it now stands as a grim monument to a lost golden age, drowned under the demonic blight that plagues the surrounding forest. Ten thousand years ago, prior to the Sundering, Morlos'Aran was a grand urban center of the ancient kaldorei civilization. Much like sister settlements such as Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and Ordil'Aran across northern Kalimdor, its marble arches and moonlit plazas bustled with elven life and arcana. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the city broke, leaving only shattered colonnades behind as monuments to their civilization's zenith.

Morningdew the Elder. Morningdew the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. Illuminated by a radiant beam of starlight, she offers ancient wisdom and directs pilgrims toward other elders scattered across Kalimdor. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their blessings with travelers. Elder Morningdew appears bathed in a shaft of lunar light, standing out starkly against the dusty red stone and noisy industrial hubbub of Thousand Needles. She reminds mortal travelers to look beyond earthly concerns to the starry expanse above.

Mortality Wanes. Heralath Fallowbrook lies dying in Razorfen Kraul, with one last plea for the living. He asks that his wife's stolen pendant reach Darnassus, along with word of his death. In Razorfen Kraul, Heralath Fallowbrook lies mortally wounded among the brambles. The stronghold is overrun by savage quilboar and dark magic, far from Alliance territory. With his strength fading, Heralath manages only broken whispers. He says a brave dwarf named Lonebrow was sent ahead to warn Falfindel. Heralath knows he will not leave the Kraul alive.

Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. The Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound is a fortified cavern complex in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just south of the ruins of Zul'Gurub. It serves as the primary stronghold for the brute Mosh'Ogg tribe in the jungle, dominated by their ruthless ogre mage chieftain, Mai'Zoth. Carved into the rugged jungle ridges south of Zul'Gurub, the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound swarms with brutish Mosh'Ogg maulers, shamans, and warmongers. The ogres seized the cavernous network as an ideal redoubt against hostile jungle trolls and prowling beasts.

Mosshide Fen. In eastern Wetlands, Mosshide Fen is held by the Mosshide gnolls. Its primitive camps lie far from the main trade roads, where travelers face danger. Mosshide gnolls hold the tangled marsh of eastern Wetlands. Rough lean-tos and bone-strewn camps mark their territory. Gnawbone and other pack leaders command the tribe, which ambushes and devours travelers, scouts, and prospectors who enter its hunting grounds.

Mossy Tumor. Around Wellspring Lake, mossy tumors mark Teldrassil's spreading corruption. Carved from the bark and flesh of corrupted timberlings, these poisonous growths show the malevolence taking hold in the young World Tree. Teldrassil's timberlings were made to nurture and tend the great tree's boughs, but many have grown hostile and diseased. Mossy tumors are signs of that sickness made flesh. Thick with toxins, they spread across the Mire Beasts, Tramplers, and Elder Timberlings around Wellspring Lake. Rellian Greenspyre and the keepers in Darnassus send travelers to cut away the tumors and burn them thoroughly, so their poison cannot take deeper root in the island's soil.

Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

Mountain Giant Muisek. Witch Doctor Uzer'i calls this the last job and sends you northwest to find the final enemy: mountain giants, whose size and strength Uzer'i is eager to harness. In Uzer'i's telling, the mountain giants came down out of the mountains to help the night elves once the Burning Legion arrived in the world. They are easy to know by their sheer size and the tremors underfoot on their rocky ground. Uzer'i is eager to harness power on that scale. Uzer'i wants seven Land Walkers or Cliff Giants brought down, each one shrunk and captured with the Muisek Vessel.

Mountain Lion Blood. Across Hillsbrad and Alterac, Mountain Lion Blood draws Apothecary Lydon’s interest. In Tarren Mill, Lydon seeks fresh blood to make the Royal Apothecary Society’s dreaded Elixir of Pain. Mountain lions prowl the highlands and foothills of Hillsbrad and Alterac. Hunters prize their pelts and claws, while the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society seek the blood in their veins. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill believes fresh mountain lion blood can form the base of a potent brew meant to bring misery to the living.

Mountaineer Barleybrew. At South Gate Outpost, Mountaineer Barleybrew watches the pass from Dun Morogh toward Loch Modan. He relies on dwarven brews to help sentries endure the cold. Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew watches the snowy road to Loch Modan from South Gate Outpost. He is part of Ironforge's border watch. Like other mountaineers in Dun Morogh's bitter winds, he values the strength of fine dwarven drink. His name links him to the renowned Barleybrew clan. He also helps send potent Shimmer Stout to fellow watchmen who need warmth and stamina during long shifts in the mountain passes.

Mountaineer Kadrell. Across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps watch over Loch Modan. Mountaineer Kadrell keeps watch in Thelsamar and organizes the dwarven defenses of Loch Modan. Outposts along the valley’s fringes face pressure from troggs, gnolls, and native beasts. From the center of town, Kadrell organizes reinforcements, relays orders, and weighs reports from scouts in the field.

Mountaineer Stormpike. At Algaz Station in northern Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike watches the road into the Wetlands. A proud member of the Stormpike clan, he guards Ironforge’s supply routes from troggs and kobolds. At Algaz Station, Mountaineer Stormpike guards the northern road out of Loch Modan. The station stands before the descent through Dun Algaz into the Wetlands, where rocky crags and threats from the wilderness surround it. Stormpike keeps communication open and the road clear for travelers and supply convoys crossing the pass.

name.esES: La tarea del montaraz Pico Tormenta

text.enUS: Mountaineer Stormpike's Task. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike needs a runner for business beyond the valley. Mountaineer Kadrell sends travelers to the northern watchtower, where Stormpike waits with an assignment that leads into neighboring lands. Mountaineer Stormpike watches from the northern guard tower, but his post keeps him from leaving Loch Modan. Mountaineer Kadrell points capable travelers toward guards who cannot leave their duties. With troggs and roaming wildlife threatening the roads and outposts, the Mountaineers have little room to spare. Stormpike needs a messenger for urgent personal business far beyond the region's borders.

Mountaineer Thalos. At Coldridge Pass, Mountaineer Thalos warns travelers of troggs in the tunnel. He guards the route from Coldridge Valley toward Kharanos and guides couriers carrying urgent reports. At the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Mountaineer Thalos guards the route out of Coldridge Valley. Troggs have burrowed up from below and overrun the tunnel, making the crossing dangerous. Thalos warns travelers who are not ready to turn back and judges whether couriers can brave the passage toward the wider kingdom.

Mr. Smite. At Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite keeps watch over the Defias ship and its crew. The tauren serves Captain Greenskin as first mate, guarding the docks where Edwin VanCleef's dreadnaught is being fitted out. Any intruder who meets him faces a changing array of weapons and formidable strength. Mr. Smite keeps order on the docks of Ironclad Cove as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. The Defias Brotherhood is made up mostly of disaffected humans and goblin tinkerers, yet Smite is a battle-hardened tauren far from Kalimdor's plains. He has charge of a rowdy pirate crew while they fit out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught, and he allows no disruption to the work.

Mudrock Soup and Bugs. In Theramore, Morgan Stern is working on a dish called Mudrock Soup and Bugs, which could be the next big thing at the inns of Stormwind City. Morgan Stern doubts they would survive a long trek through Dustwallow Marsh, and so asks you to gather tongues from the Mudrock turtles. Morgan Stern is working on a dish called Mudrock Soup and Bugs, and still needs the major ingredients. A long trek through Dustwallow Marsh is more than Morgan Stern expects to survive, so you are asked to do some hunting. First come the tongues of Mudrock turtles.

Mudsnout Blossom. Mudsnout Blossoms grow in Nethander Stead, south of Tarren Mill. Mudsnout gnolls guard the foul, toxic mushrooms, and Apothecary Lydon seeks them for his elixir research. South of Tarren Mill, Mudsnout Blossoms grow in Nethander Stead. Despite their name, they are large, foul-smelling mushrooms that flourish in soiled dirt among the local Mudsnout gnolls' camps. The gnolls defend the territory fiercely. The mushrooms' spores and flesh poison living things, causing agony and rapid bodily decay.

Mudsnout Composite. At Tarren Mill, Mudsnout Composite is prepared for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a new plague. Apothecary Lydon makes it from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills and sends it to the Undercity. Apothecary Lydon makes Mudsnout Composite from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The paste is noxious on its own, but Master Apothecary Faranell must bind it with a colloid of decay to bring out its deadlier qualities. Together, the ingredients form a key chemical component in the Dark Lady's Elixir of Agony.

Mudsnout Mixture. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell prepares a base for a deadly Forsaken poison. Mudsnout Mixture begins with mushrooms sent north from Tarren Mill. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon. He sends a composite made from Mudsnout Blossoms north to the Undercity. The toxic mushrooms grow at Nethander Stead, held by gnolls. Master Apothecary Faranell sees promise in the composite and adds his own colloid of decay. The resulting Mudsnout Mixture is volatile. It steadies the mushroom compound and prepares its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement in the foothills.

Mull Thunderhorn. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn watches over Mulgore’s sacred wells. He serves the Earth Mother and guards the balance of the land. Outside exploitation threatens the waters, and he guides young tauren in cleansing the ancestral springs. Mull Thunderhorn watches over Mulgore’s spiritual well-being from Bloodhoof Village. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to make a permanent home, but greed and reckless expansion already threaten their lands. Mull guides young braves setting out from Camp Narache and calls on them to protect their ancestors’ vital resources.

Mupsi Shacklefridd. Outside Ratchet in the Barrens, Mupsi Shacklefridd helps travelers repair ties with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Mupsi Shacklefridd works along the coastal road just outside Ratchet. Steamwheedle guards patrol the port town's edge as merchants come and go. Travelers on poor terms with the goblins can seek a way back into the cartel's good graces through Mupsi, if they bring the supplies and labor it demands.

Mura Runetotem. You carry a snapjaw shell from the Barrens across the sea to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. Its strange vitality may help the tauren healer aid the Forsaken. Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about altered snapjaws while investigating the magically changed wildlife around the Barrens oases. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. He asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, who is stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Muradin Bronzebeard. Muradin Bronzebeard was the brother of King Magni Bronzebeard and Brann Bronzebeard, as well as a renowned warrior, diplomat, and co-founder of the Explorers' League. Revered across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron alike, he is believed to have died in the frozen wastes of Northrend when Prince Arthas Menethil claimed the cursed runeblade Frostmourne. Muradin fought with distinction during the Second War, acting as the vital liaison between the mountain halls of Khaz Modan and the Alliance of Lordaeron. He helped hold Ironforge during the Horde's siege and marched alongside Alliance forces all the way through Blackrock Spire to the Dark Portal. In the peaceful years that followed, Muradin settled into Capital City as Ironforge’s official ambassador. Jovial yet formidable, he became a fixture in the palace, growing close to King Terenas Menethil and taking it upon himself to tutor young Prince Arthas in the arts of swordplay and combat.

Murdaloc. Agmond's battered remains lie in the Badlands, and a name is scrawled in the sandstone beside the dead hand: Murdaloc. Agmond's killer is to be put down, with word carried back to Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan. Agmond's trail comes in from the west, and the blood smeared over stone and sand tells how far the dwarf crawled before dying here. Beside the lifeless hand, scratched into the Badlands sandstone, is a single word: Murdaloc. Agmond's killer is to be slain, along with a number of Stonevault Bonesnappers, and the news taken to Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan.

Muren Stormpike. In Ironforge, Muren Stormpike awaits warriors sent from Kharanos for formal training. Granis Swiftaxe sends recruits who have proved their mettle in Dun Morogh to the city's Military Ward. Granis Swiftaxe sends promising warriors from Kharanos to Ironforge after they face local threats in Dun Morogh. He knows rough skirmishes can teach only so much. In the Military Ward, senior fighters oversee formal training for those bound for battle.

Murloc. Murlocs are amphibious, bipedal humanoids famous for their gurgling battle cries, territorial coastal villages, and sudden swarming tactics. Though historically dwelling in the deep ocean, they have steadily migrated inland along the shores, lakes, and rivers of Azeroth, acting with far greater coordination and cunning than their primitive appearance suggests. Murlocs dwell in densely populated settlements along coastlines, riverbanks, and freshwater lakes. Averaging roughly four feet in height, they possess bulbous, slime-coated bodies, wide mouths filled with sharp fangs, and keen vision capable of piercing pitch-black water. While individuals are rarely seen wandering far from their kin, encountering one murloc invariably means a dozen more lurk just beneath the surface. They rely on overwhelming numbers and sharp crude weaponry.

Murloc Gills. Alba Fairmoon sends Alliance help to Westfall's Longshore to gather murloc gills. She fears the crop blight may reach the Great Sea, and the gills could reveal whether the coastal waters are tainted. Westfall is already near ruin, with crops failing, farmers displaced, and bandits roaming the roads. Alba Fairmoon fears the blight may be draining from inland fields into the Great Sea. If the coast is tainted, the fish that feed Westfall's poor and grace Stormwind City's tables could vanish. That loss could tip an already strained kingdom into outright famine.

Murloc Head. Along the Western Strand, Murloc Head is grim proof of a threat Southshore wants brought under control. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle collects the severed heads for Marshal Redpath, who requires evidence of the murlocs being culled. Southshore's fishermen and coastal travelers face an immediate threat from aggressive murlocs along the Western Strand. Alliance fighters often clear the beaches, but Marshal Marcus Redpath wants proof before he approves reports of the threat being reduced. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle hires fighters to bring him murloc heads. Farren finds the work repulsive, and the sight has spoiled his appetite for Southshore's seafood.

Murloc Poachers. Along Lake Everstill, Murloc Poachers are stripping Lakeshire's waters of fish. Dockmaster Baren needs you to thin their swelling ranks before the town loses its main food supply. Dockmaster Baren needs you to protect the fish that feed Lakeshire. Lake Everstill supplies the mountain town and its market with fresh catches. Large tribes of murlocs now crowd the shallows and scour the waters for food. Left unchecked, they could wipe out the local fish and leave Lakeshire without its main food supply.

Musquash Root. Beneath the Stonewrought Dam, Musquash Root grows in the Wetlands. The rare root is hard to gather, and a hidden coven beneath Stormwind needs it for a brew. Musquash Root grows in the damp ground beneath the Stonewrought Dam's falls. The mist and secluded setting make it hard to gather. Few herbalists seek it, but practitioners of the darker arts prize its chemical and alchemical properties.

Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption gave that nightmare the shape of an immense, albino murloc.

Mux Manascrambler. Mux Manascrambler is an eccentric goblin engineer dwelling in the desert outpost of Gadgetzan. Unlike many of his peers focused strictly on explosives or mining equipment, Mux harbors a peculiar fascination with the supernatural and occult energies. Tucked away inside a building in central Gadgetzan, behind Driz Plunkbow and his clanking Butcherbots, sits Mux Manascrambler. While the Steamwheedle Cartel trades heavily in oil, guns, and salvage, Mux focuses his ingenuity on more esoteric pursuits: the realm of spirits and supernatural anomalies. He uses his technical acumen to design bizarre devices capable of detecting, distilling, and interacting with spectral remnants, bridging crude goblin craftsmanship with the invisible worlds of the dead.

Mydrannul. At the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Mydrannul keeps basic supplies ready for sentinels, soldiers, and visitors. Mydrannul keeps a supply stall among the Warrior's Terrace military pavilions and training grounds. Darnassus's defenders and travelers can find everyday field gear there, including ammunition for archers and gunners, throwing blades, flint, pouches, and simple rations. His stall helps sentinels and trainees preparing for duty on Teldrassil find the basic sundries they need.

Mysterious Fossil. Along Darkshore's coast, Prospector Remtravel uncovers the Mysterious Fossil. The Explorers' League sends it across the sea for study. Prospector Remtravel uncovers an unusual fossil while working along Darkshore's wild coast. He arranges for dwarven scholars to receive it instead of leaving it in the wilderness. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sees an extraordinary find among the stones of Kalimdor.

Mystic Ward. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, faith and arcane study share the city's quieter quarter. Pale blue banners mark its halls, and the Hall of Mysteries gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath stone arches. The Mystic Ward carries Ironforge's quieter pursuits of faith and learning. Pale blue banners mark the quarter between the Commons, the Forlorn Cavern, and the Great Forge. Shops such as The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents. At the Hall of Mysteries, followers of the Holy Light and practitioners of arcane magic find guidance in wielding powers unseen in defense of the Alliance.

Mystral Lake. Travelers from both factions reach Mystral Lake in south-central Ashenvale. Its deep waters draw them beneath the watch of the night elves. Mystral Lake draws travelers to its shores in southern Ashenvale. The vast lake lies south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, the largest lake in the forest. Night elves keep watch from their outpost on its northern shore. Travelers from both the Horde and the Alliance often find their journeys bringing them to its banks.

Myzrael's Allies. Myzrael cries out that she is free, and that she will gather her strength in hiding from her captors. She calls you a noble ally and sends you to Gerrig Bonegrip in a shop of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, who knows how she can be summoned. Myzrael is free, and means to gather strength hidden from her captors, since if they met her now they would surely overpower her and lock her away again. In time she means to face the giants, and she swears they will rue having held her. She calls you a noble ally and says she will need your help again, to summon her to the surface when she is ready.

Myzrael's Allies. Myzrael speaks through the keystone, declaring herself free but in hiding from her captors, and tells you to speak with Zaruk in Hammerfall, who knows how she can be summoned. Myzrael cries out that she is free. For now she must gather her strength out of sight of her captors, because if they faced her today they would overpower and imprison her again. In time, she vows, she will confront the giants who held her, and they will regret keeping her.

NG-5. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Gaxim Rustfizzle needs NG-5 for his explosive plans. The volatile chemical is Nitromirglyceronium, the ignition compound he needs to set off wagons loaded with dynamite as a distraction. Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome operative in the Stonetalon Mountains, needs NG-5 for his engineering plans. The compound is formally known as Nitromirglyceronium, a hazardous chemical solution that demands care—or reckless gnomish enthusiasm. Gaxim says it provides the reaction needed to detonate entire wagons loaded with dynamite, creating a massive explosion to distract his adversaries in the region.

Naga. The naga are a monstrous, serpentine race dwelling beneath the ocean's depths, ruled by their ancient empress, Queen Azshara. Once the Highborne elite of the Kaldorei Empire, they were warped into amphibious horrors during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Recently emerging from the dark waters, they have seized shorelines across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to reclaim their forgotten surface empire. Ten millennia ago, the Highborne nobility of the Kaldorei Empire ruled supreme from their grand capital of Zin-Azshari. Consumed by an obsession with arcane power, Queen Azshara and her inner court tapped the Well of Eternity to draw the gaze of the Dark Titan Sargeras, inviting the catastrophic invasion known as the War of the Ancients. When the Well of Eternity collapsed into ruin, triggering the Great Sundering, the palace slipped into the crushing abyss. Facing utter annihilation, Azshara bargained with the malevolent Old Gods deep below. In exchange for survival, she and her followers were transformed into cold, scaly, serpentine beings bound to the deeps.

name.esES: Nagas en la Ensenada de Zoram
name.frFR: Des nagas sur la grève de Zoram

text.enUS: Naga at the Zoram Strand. At Zoram Strand, Naga threaten the Horde's hold on Ashenvale's coast. From Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai seeks to drive the Wrathtail away from the sunken ruins of ancient Zoram. The Horde's hold on Zoram Strand is fragile. Hostile night elf territory and bitter woodland fighting surround the outpost, whose coast links the Horde to the sea. Aggressive naga have now crawled ashore. They could cut off that link and overwhelm the small garrison before its defenses are ready.

Nak's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Nak leads Razormane warbands against the Horde. His skull proves his defeat and gives Mangletooth a means to avenge betrayal by his former kin. Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane lead raids from Razorfen Kraul across the Barrens. Their warbands strike Horde settlements and roads, while defenders at the Crossroads do not know the three commanders are planning attacks beyond ordinary tribal skirmishing. At Camp Taurajo, the captive Razormane Mangletooth has been left to die in a cage by his own people. He now seeks revenge against those former brethren. Mangletooth demands proof that Nak and his companions are dead: their severed skulls, delivered by Horde adventurers. He means to use that proof to break the southern raiding parties.

Nalpak. Nalpak is a tauren druid disciple who watches over the troubled Wailing Caverns in the Barrens. Stationed in the high cliff-cave overlooking the cavern entrance, he enlists passing adventurers to help contain the nightmare twisting the subterranean ecosystem. Perched inside a hidden cavern directly above the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak remains loyal to the vision of Naralex. While his master lies trapped in a corrupted slumber deep below, Nalpak works to keep the spreading corruption at bay. He asks adventurers to gather deviate hides for use as leather.

Nara Meideros. In Stormwind's Park, Nara Meideros guides young seekers in Elune's teachings. As a night elf priestess in the human capital, she offers a familiar spiritual presence to her kin. Nara Meideros serves Elune far from Kalimdor, across the Great Sea in Stormwind City. In the Park, night elf druids and priests have tended a green refuge. Nara guides young seekers in devotion to the Moon Goddess. Human priests serve the Holy Light in nearby Cathedral Square, while Nara gives night elves visiting or living in the Eastern Kingdoms a connection to their own faith.

Nara Wildmane. Nara Wildmane is a young tauren druid in Thunder Bluff seeking to unravel the tragedy unfolding deep within the Wailing Caverns. After Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem peered into the Emerald Dream and withdrew from the corruption festering there, he dispatched adventurers to confer with Nara, whose fierce spirit endured long enough to witness the nightmare taking hold of their kin. She serves as the pivotal Horde contact directing champions to put an end to the Druids of the Fang. When strange, unnatural phenomena began spreading across the Barrens, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem journeyed into the Emerald Dream to discern the cause. There he witnessed a cult of druids who had originally sought to restore life to the arid savannah, only to lose their minds to a vile taint. Being aged and unable to linger long against the nightmare's assault, Hamuul fled back to the waking world. However, his younger disciple, Nara Wildmane, refused to yield so easily. Her fiery resolve kept her anchored in the dreamscape far longer, allowing her to observe the transformed cult firsthand.

Narain Soothfancy. Narain Soothfancy is an eccentric gnome dwelling in a secluded beach hut just north of Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris. While he loudly advertises himself as a master soothsayer capable of divining the future, those who know him consider his psychic talents a complete farce compared to his genuine engineering genius. Perched on the eastern coast of Tanaris just north of the goblin docks, Narain Soothfancy lives as a retired engineer turned self-proclaimed master fortune teller. He routinely greets visitors by pressing unopened envelopes against his forehead or making wildly inaccurate guesses about their business, such as wondering if they have arrived seeking the legendary Ashbringer. Despite his theatrical charade, Narain possesses deep technical knowledge. Even ancient beings like the blue dragon Azuregos note that while Narain is a terrible psychic, his engineering aptitude is undeniably brilliant. A handbook titled 'Soothsaying for Dummies' rests nearby.

Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed to the Barrens with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom.

Nat Pagle. Nat Pagle is widely hailed as the most renowned angler in all of Azeroth, despite claiming he only fishes as an excuse to drink heavily. He makes his home on a secluded inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, where he trains elite anglers from both the Alliance and the Horde who manage to prove their patience. Though his name is synonymous with angling mastery across the known world, Nat Pagle is remarkably casual about his craft. Having cast lines for several decades, he often admits he has no great reverence for the sport itself, famously calling it little more than a convenient excuse to sit back and drink heavily. Despite this gruff nonchalance, Nat understands aquatic life and the art of angling better than anyone alive, even licensing fishing gear sought out by professionals.

Nat's Landing. Nat's Landing is a modest fishing outpost nestled along the shores of Dustwallow Bay in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the personal camp and retreat of Nat Pagle, widely regarded as the most famous angler on Azeroth. Adventurers from across the world seek out this humble dock to hone their mastery of the fishing craft. Tucked away southwest of Theramore Isle along the murky waters of Dustwallow Bay, Nat's Landing is little more than a weathered campsite. It consists of a simple canvas tent, drying racks heavy with the day's catch, extra tackle hung from trees, and a rickety wooden pier jutting into the bay. Despite the mists and hazards of the swamp, this quiet patch of shoreline provides the legendary angler Nat Pagle with a solitary place to cast his line and enjoy a quiet drink away from civilization's clamor.

Natalia Mar'alith. Mistress Natalia Mar'alith is a night elf priestess and Cenarion Circle researcher lost deep within the silithid nests of Hive'Regal. Once part of the expedition investigating Silithus alongside her husband, Commander Mar'alith, she has succumbed completely to the maddening influence of the Old Gods. When the Cenarion Circle established their outpost at Cenarion Hold to monitor the awakening sands, Natalia accompanied her husband, Commander Mar'alith, into the wastes. Eager to unravel the mystery behind the resurgence of the silithid and the ancient Qiraji ruins, she joined an exploratory party led by the famed explorer Brann Bronzebeard, accompanied by the dwarven researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge.

Nathanos Blightcaller. Nathanos Blightcaller, once Nathanos Marris, stands at his ruined homestead in the Eastern Plaguelands as the deadly champion of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. In life he was the first and only human Ranger Lord of Quel'Thalas, and in undeath he trains Forsaken hunters while guarding the eastern frontier with biting contempt for all who approach. Before the Third War, Nathanos Marris was an extraordinary marksman and tactical genius hailing from the rural outskirts of Lordaeron. Trained by the high elves of Quel'Thalas and close to Sylvanas Windrunner, he became the only human to ever attain the prestigious rank of Ranger Lord. His home remained the family estate in Lordaeron, the Marris Stead.

Natural Materials. Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Camp Mojache needs materials to complete an endeavor, to be gathered alongside the other trials: splintered logs, encrusted minerals, resilient sinew and metallic fragments, taken from treants, mountain giants, faerie dragons, owlbeasts and hippogryphs. After you return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i, a further list of materials awaits, to be collected alongside the other trials. Two splintered logs are needed from a Feralas treant. Six pieces of encrusted minerals are found on mountain giants and faerie dragons, westward. Twenty pieces of resilient sinew come from owlbeasts in the Hinterlands or hippogryphs in Feralas. A large amount of metallic fragments, forty in all, can come from any of these creatures.

Nature's Call. Nature's Call is a Shadowglen quest where the dryad Tarindrella seeks to uncover why the local Gnarlpine furbolgs suddenly turned against their long-standing night elf allies. By gathering carved totems from their abandoned camps, adventurers help reveal the distressing spiritual corruption spreading through Teldrassil. Nature's Call is an investigative mission in Shadowglen given by the dryad Tarindrella. Refusing to believe that the Gnarlpine furbolg would abandon centuries of friendship with the night elves without reason, she asks travelers to comb through the furbolgs' hastily abandoned camps along the western border of the glen to recover intact engraved totems.

Need for a Cure. Rhinag lies poisoned on Durotar’s northwestern cliffs, far from the cure he needs. The Darkspear troll has little time before the venom kills him, so he sends a passing courier to Orgrimmar for Kor'ghan’s remedy. Rhinag was fighting venomtail scorpids near Durotar’s border when one stung him. Their venom can kill in less than an hour. The poison keeps him from walking to Orgrimmar, so his survival depends on a traveler reaching his remote camp in time.

Neeka Bloodscar. Helgrum the Swift sends you from Stonard to the Badlands outpost of Kargath, to speak with its head scout, Neeka Bloodscar. Word between Stonard and Kargath is often cut. The Badlands are harsh country and lie close to Loch Modan, which the Alliance holds. Because of this, word between Stonard and Kargath is often cut. Helgrum asks you to prove yourself by travelling to the Badlands and speaking with Neeka Bloodscar, who is head scout there. Neeka's report is then to be sent back to Helgrum.

Neeru Fireblade. In Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade studies dark arts he says can protect the Horde. Margoz sends you from Durotar with a Searing Collar taken from the Burning Blade cult, hoping the warlock can explain its demonic power. Margoz has found the limit of shamanic arts. The collars taken from Burning Blade cultists at Skull Rock carry demonic sorcery, beyond what he can unravel. Shamans draw on the elements and ancestral spirits, so Margoz sends you to a warlock in the capital to learn what the collars do.

Nek'mani Wellspring. Perched high in the cliffs above the Southern Savage Coast, the Nek'mani Wellspring holds a fountain of remarkably pure holy water. It is renowned as the only pristine source of fresh water found south of Duskwood. However, this sacred site has recently been overrun by hostile naga explorers who jealously guard its flow. The Nek'mani Wellspring sits tucked away in the jagged coastal heights of western Stranglethorn Vale. Dispensing the only untainted freshwater south of Duskwood, the spring is hailed by various scholars and pilgrims as holy. Because differing cultures and traditions each claim its divine waters were blessed uniquely for their own kind, it remains a subject of intense theological fascination. Despite its spiritual renown, peaceful contemplation here is impossible: a vicious contingent of naga has recently seized the basin and guards the waters against all intruders.

Nek'rosh's Gambit. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist fears a Dragonmaw siege. Chieftain Nek'rosh has built engines to bombard the vulnerable port town, while fighting at Dun Algaz cuts off reinforcements. You are sent into the marshes to destroy the catapults before the attack begins. Dwarven scouts uncovered Nek'rosh's plan as Alliance fighters clashed with Dragonmaw raiders. The chieftain has overseen the building of full-scale siege catapults in the Wetlands encampments. He means to bring the engines to Menethil Harbor and batter its fortress walls, threatening the Alliance's main shipping hub on the western coast.

Nek'rosh's Head. In the Wetlands, Nek'rosh's Head proves the Dragonmaw chieftain has fallen. Captain Stoutfist receives it as proof that the threat to Menethil Harbor has been broken. The Dragonmaw clan gathers forces and siege weapons across the marshlands, threatening the Alliance port of Menethil Harbor. After the clan's catapults are burned, the port's defense depends on killing Chieftain Nek'rosh. His severed head gives Captain Stoutfist and the Ironforge authorities proof that the warlord's hold over the Wetlands is broken.

Neru Fragment. Unearthed from disturbed earth, the Neru Fragment carries part of the Goaz Stone's ancient Titan script. The relic was discovered at Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, and its words tell of Azeroth's primeval history. Prospector Whelgar led the dwarven expedition that discovered the Goaz Stone. The relic broke into four pieces: Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. Raptors overran the dig, halting the work, and the Neru Fragment remained beneath loose soil among the aggressive beasts. Once recovered, it can join the other pieces and restore the tablet. Its surviving words speak of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy, giving dwarven scholars a record to decipher.

Nesingwary's Expedition. Nesingwary's Expedition is a rustic hunting encampment situated in northern Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Lake Nazferiti. Established by the famed dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary, the outpost serves as a staging ground for hunters seeking to test their mettle against the jungle's fiercest predators. Tucked alongside the river north of Lake Nazferiti, this remote encampment is a bustling haven for big game hunters, trackers, and marksmen. Hemet Nesingwary established the camp to stalk the legendary beasts of Stranglethorn Vale, surrounded by seasoned peers like Sir S. J. Erlgadin, Ajeck Rouack, and Barnil Stonepot. Guarded by hired marksmen and supplied by neutral vendors, the camp welcomes anyone capable of handling a rifle or bow, regardless of their allegiances, uniting them under the singular pursuit of tracking down the deadliest predators the jungle has to offer.

Nessa Shadowsong. In Darnassus, Mydrannul sends a courier to meet Nessa Shadowsong below the World Tree. The delivery runs from Rut'theran Village to Darkshore, linking the canopy city with the shore. Mydrannul watches over travelers seeking work and purpose in Darnassus. Fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package carried across the sea to Darkshore, so Mydrannul directs able couriers toward the coast. Many young night elves begin their journeys among Teldrassil's boughs; this delivery takes them beyond the tree.

Nessa's Collection. At Rut'theran Village, fish bones and scales gathered from nearby waters are prepared for study by Laird in Auberdine. Nessa's Collection shows the great size of aquatic life around Teldrassil's roots. Nessa Shadowsong lives in Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base, where she gathered fish bones and scales to compare island sea life with that of mainland Kalimdor. Catches from the waters around the Great Tree grow to striking size. Nessa sent physical proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant along Auberdine's docks. The parcel travels through Vesprystus, Rut'theran's hippogryph master, and offers practical evidence of Teldrassil's growing vitality.

Nethander Stead. Nethander Stead lies abandoned along the road east of Southshore, overrun by Mudsnout gnolls. Once a human farm, its fields now hold giant white Mudsnout Blossoms that draw Forsaken alchemists. At Nethander Stead, ruined fences and outbuildings stand within sight of Southshore's eastern borders. The farm once formed part of Hillsbrad's working fields, but it was abandoned as security weakened and wild packs moved in. Now the Mudsnout gnolls make their only home in the foothills here. They drive off travelers who come too close to their territory.

Nether Gem. Across Tirisfal Glades, the Nether Gem carries Gunther Arcanus’s image to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Gunther entrusts it to an emissary after his lost spellbook is returned, opening a path to the Forsaken.

Nether-lace Garment. At the Crossroads, Kil'hala weaves dryad hair into enchanted cloth for spellcasters. The finished garment marks the end of his specialized work in the Barrens. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala weaves nether-lace from the locks of laughing sisters. The dryads live in Ashenvale, and their hair is harvested for this work. Kil'hala binds the woodland enchantment in those rare, magically resonant locks into cloth that is comfortable and durable.

Nethergarde Keep. Nethergarde Keep is a fortified Alliance stronghold perched high upon the bluffs along the road entering the Blasted Lands. Raised by the Alliance after the Second War, it stands as a vigilant sentinel over the dormant Dark Portal and the chaotic energies bleeding across the red wastes. Today, mages and garrisons supported by Stormwind continue their lonely vigil against demons and lingering corruption. Following the destruction of the Dark Portal at the end of the Second War, Archmage Khadgar and the leaders of the Alliance of Lordaeron recognized that Azeroth could never again leave the rift unguarded. Builders labored to raise towering bastions, barracks, and mage spires along the canyon pass into the Blasted Lands. Staffed by Kirin Tor sorcerers, its dual purpose was to keep constant watch on the shattered gateway and weave wards preventing the demonic blight of the scorched landscape from creeping northward into the human kingdoms.
