text.enUS: Plainstrider Menace. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends new Horde adventurers after plainstriders east of the outpost. The birds threaten its food supplies, and the hunt gives newcomers a first measure of the Barrens. The Crossroads coordinates supplies across Kalimdor, but plainstriders east of the outpost have begun picking at its food crates. Sergra Darkthorn, an orc shaman, sends newly arrived Horde adventurers to hunt the birds before they damage the stores. Their attacks threaten provisions the settlement depends on.

Plainstrider Scale. Across Mulgore, Plainstrider Scale is sought for a remedy Maur Raincaller prepares in Bloodhoof Village. The tough scale helps counter a spreading infection. Plainstriders roam Mulgore with tough scales covering their powerful legs. The scales protect them, though only some are firm enough to grind for folk remedies.

Plainstrider Talon. Across Mulgore, tauren shamans gather Plainstrider Talon for cleansing totems. The sharp claws come from large, flightless plainstriders native to the region, and help cleanse corrupted water. Large, flightless plainstriders roam Mulgore’s open grasses, using powerful legs and sharp claws to forage through tough prairie earth and defend against predators. To the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, every part of a hunted beast carries spiritual resonance. When goblin ventures tainted sacred sources such as the Winterhoof Water Well, shaman Mull Thunderhorn sought plainstrider talons alongside prairie wolf paws. In tauren ritual crafting, reagents from native predators and foragers channel the land’s spiritual essence into totems that can purge unnatural poisons.

Planting the Heart. At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan tend a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. After clearing away its moss, he asks you to place it in his planter and see whether it can be healed. Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. Trusting his years of botany and soil tending, the herbalist asks you to bury the heart directly in his personal planter. He hopes the rich nutrients he blended can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

Plea To The Alliance. At the shattered Thandol Span, Plea To The Alliance carries a desperate call for aid from Dun Modr's dwarven survivors. Dark Iron infiltrators slaughtered the garrison, and the dwarves appeal to the human forces at Refuge Pointe, though the Alliance is stretched thin. Dun Modr lies devastated, and Dark Iron dwarves have sabotaged the Thandol Span. The survivors hold a precarious foothold at the Wetlands' northern rim. Ironforge's main reserves have yet to arrive, so Rhag Garmason and Longbraid the Grim look north to the Arathi Highlands. They learn that Alliance forces have made camp at Refuge Pointe. Garmason sends an emissary across the shattered bridge to ask Captain Nials for urgent military aid.

Plundering the Plunderers. Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters near Ratchet. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin contact in Ratchet, tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor, crewed by Southsea Freebooters. They must board without being seen, enter the pirates’ den where cutpurses train, pick the strongboxes in the hold, and bring back the plunder.

Podrig's Order. At the Sepulcher, Podrig's Order calls for fresh weapons from the Undercity. Deathguard Podrig found the Sepulcher's stores mostly adequate after an inventory ordered by Executor Hadrec. Replacement weapons were running desperately low. His dispatch lists the blades and arms needed by the Deathguards holding the outpost in Silverpine Forest, a frontier threatened by the Scourge, feral beasts, and other dangers.

Poison Water. In Mulgore, tainted wells threaten the water that sustains the tauren and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village asks young Horde defenders to gather parts from the plains for a cleansing totem. Goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted Mulgore's wells, threatening the water that sustains the tauren tribes and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder in Bloodhoof Village, has discovered the pollution. For the tauren, who recently settled here, the wells are vital to life on these sacred plains.

Pool of Ask'ar. Naga invaders and aquatic beasts crowd the Pool of Ask'ar, deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Its submerged halls hold night elven stonework and passages into the corrupted sanctuary. Past the Drowned Sacellum, cold, murky water fills the Pool of Ask'ar beneath a vast cavern vault. Oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs nest among natural caverns and ancient stonework, watched over by Ghamoo-ra, an enormous ancient chelonian. Naga have seized the temple and use this flooded threshold to guard the approaches leading deeper into the complex, toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins.

Pool of Tears. In Stonard, Fel'zerul asks you to search around the Pool of Tears for Atal'ai artifacts. The Warchief sent Fel'zerul's people to look into strange events at the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, and they arrived to find it sunk. The Atal'ai trolls are dark casters, a tribe notorious for forbidden magic. When Fel'zerul's party reached the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, they were astonished to find it sunk. Green dragons now watch over the place and call themselves protectors of Azeroth.

Pool of Tears. The Pool of Tears is a large, murky lake dominating the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Deep beneath its surface lies the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar, brought low by the Green Dragonflight to contain the horrors within. Today, vicious frenzies patrol the turbid waters, and ancient troll ruins litter its drowned banks. Long ago, fanatical Atal'ai trolls raised a monumental ziggurat to their bloodthirsty god, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Horrified by the blasphemies taking place within, the Dragon Aspect Ysera shattered the ground beneath the structure, submerging the massive temple into the depths of the marsh. The existing lake flooded over the temple ruins. While the dragons sought to bury the evil forever, the ziggurat still stands beneath the silt and waves, and green drakes remain vigilant in the area to keep its corruption sealed.

Pools of Arlithrien. South of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien have grown dangerous and neglected. Their moonwell once drew night elves to a quiet sanctuary, but beasts and nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs now threaten the springs. The Pools of Arlithrien lie beneath Teldrassil’s shaded boughs, south of Darnassus. A stone moonwell rests at their heart, holding waters touched by Elune’s grace. Though the sanctuary lies near the night elven capital, danger has driven the night elves to leave it untended. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the Gnarlpine furbolgs nearby remain hostile. What was meant to be a peaceful retreat now reflects the growing troubles across the island.

Pools of Vision. Forsaken gather in the Pools of Vision, beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. Still waters and dim caverns shelter their enclave within the tauren capital. The Pools of Vision lie beneath Spirit Rise, below Thunder Bluff's sunlit peaks. A cave path beside the bridge to the rise leads down into the grotto. Misty waters fill its shadowed chambers, where Horde spellcasters gather apart from the open-air lodges above.

Poor Old Blanchy. Verna Furlbrow waits beside the road in Westfall with her stranded family and starving mare. Their wagon broke during an attempt to escape, leaving Old Blanchy exhausted. Verna asks you to gather oats from nearby abandoned farmsteads and feed the old horse. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow are stranded beside Westfall's main road. Bandits and rogue mechanical harvest golems have driven families like theirs from their homes. As the Furlbrows tried to haul their belongings to safety, their wagon broke down, leaving them marooned in open country.

Pork Belly Pie. In Elwynn Forest, Billy Maclure wants a pie from the Stonefield farm before he speaks about a missing necklace. Auntie Bernice Stonefield bakes it despite the feud between their families. The Stonefield and Maclure families have quarreled over land and pride for years in Elwynn Forest. Young Billy Maclure has a weakness for Auntie Bernice's pork belly pie. When a valuable Stonefield family necklace goes missing, Billy refuses to share what he knows until an adventurer brings him a warm slice. Bernice bakes the pie reluctantly, wishing the greedy boy would choke on it.

Portals of the Legion. After Hand of Iruxos, Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village shows you the Hand and asks you to banish six demon portals at Mannoroc Coven, warning you to be wary of the portal guardians. Taiga Wisemane holds up the Hand of Iruxos, a grisly thing to look at, and says you must carry it if the demon portals around Mannoroc Coven are ever to be closed. The demon threat is increasing, and shutting the portals will check the number of demons crossing into this world. She wants all six portals banished, and she warns you to be wary of their guardians.

Powder to Ironband. A shipment of blasting powder is bound for Prospector Ironband's dig in southern Loch Modan. After Prospector Stormpike approves the request in Ironforge, the powder is sent to Thelsamar for the journey to Ironband's Excavation. The Explorer's League sends blasting powder from Ironforge to Prospector Ironband's expedition in southern Loch Modan. When the dig runs short, word reaches the League's leadership. Prospector Stormpike approves the request and directs the runner to coordinate with Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar, the valley's main supply hub.

Powdered Azurite. In Hillsbrad Foothills, Powdered Azurite is taken from the Azurelode Mine. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors. Powdered Azurite comes from the mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. Human workers dig the blue stone from Azurelode Mine, then grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals to make armor more durable and resilient.

Power Overwhelming. Power Overwhelming is a quest issued by High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind City to assist the secluded Kirin Tor. Players are dispatched to the ruined city of Dalaran to quell a dangerous outbreak of wayward arcane energy manifested as a Mana Elemental. Following the devastating destruction of Dalaran at the hands of the arch-demon Archimonde during the Third War, the Kirin Tor retreated inward. Once welcoming scholars and sorcerers from across the world, the surviving magi have grown secretive, reclusive, and deeply distrustful of outsiders as they work tirelessly behind closed borders to rebuild their ruined city.

Power over Poison. In Darnassus, a young druid returns to complete Power over Poison. The Cenarion Circle's trial began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong asks young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They brew a salve to heal stricken wildlife. Before granting the magic to purge toxins, the Cenarion Circle wants initiates to know the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. The work teaches them what common folk face when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care.

Power over Poison. At Thunder Bluff, a young Horde druid returns to claim the gift of Cure Poison. After healing poisoned gazelles near the Crossroads with herbal mixtures, the initiate faces Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise. Before granting a druid the power to cleanse venom, the Cenarion Circle asks them to learn what affliction feels like. Dendrite Starblaze sends the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem has them gather ingredients for a salve. The druid treats poisoned gazelles of the Barrens by hand, without spiritual aid, and sees the struggle ordinary creatures face against natural and unnatural toxins.

Powers of the Void. A stolen tome draws Drusilla La Salle's attention in Northshire. Powers of the Void was kept in a restricted wing of Northshire Abbey's library until a novice took it while defecting to the Defias Brotherhood. Drusilla seeks its recovery for her own study of dark magic. Powers of the Void was kept behind guarded shelves in Northshire Abbey's library. The abbey archives hold holy scripture and clerical records, along with scholarly works on shadow and nether energies. The tome was presumably penned by the archmage Khadgar. Because its subject was dangerous, abbey authorities kept the book under guard and away from casual visitors. That barred Northshire's warlock mentor, Drusilla La Salle, from browsing it without drawing the priesthood's suspicion.

Pozzik. Pozzik is an esteemed goblin tinkerer and racer stationed at the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Once one of the most respected engineers in Undermine, he now dedicates his technical genius to constructing experimental rocket cars and settling the ultimate debate of engineering supremacy against his gnome counterpart. Before retiring to the harsh salt flats of Thousand Needles, Pozzik built a legendary reputation among the goblins. As one of the most respected tinkerers out of Undermine, his technical expertise spans complex internal combustion, propulsion, and hazardous chassis construction. Rather than settling into comfortable obscurity, however, Pozzik took his mechanical mastery into the desert to push high-speed machinery far past its breaking point.

Practical Prey. Vel'rin Fang needs hunters to bring tiger hides from the Echo Isles to Sen'jin Village. The Darkspear need the supplies as their numbers grow and their stores run low. The Darkspear in Sen'jin Village have to make every resource last along Durotar's harsh coast. Tiger pelts can be made into tents, blankets and armor. As refugees arrive and scouts return, the village's stores have thinned, and leatherworker Vel'rin Fang has sent hunters out for more hides.

Prairie Alpha Tooth. Around Thunder Bluff, prairie wolf alphas roam Mulgore’s open plains. Mull Thunderhorn needs their teeth to cleanse the Wildmane Well. Mulgore’s wells sustain the tauren, and keeping them pure calls for rites of respect and sacrifice. Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village needs teeth from the prairie wolf alphas that prowl beneath Thunder Bluff to cleanse the Wildmane Well. These fierce pack leaders embody the strength of the wild. Their teeth honor the balance between hunter, prey, and the spirits of the earth.

Prairie Wolf Heart. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village needs a Prairie Wolf Heart for a remedy against venom. Maur Raincaller lives in Bloodhoof Village and is suffering from the venom of Mazzranache, the legendary plainstrider. The bite brings fever and threatens to spread poison through him. Maur seeks the heart of a prairie wolf, along with cougar bone and bird gizzard, for a traditional plains remedy meant to stop the infection before delirium proves fatal.

Prairie Wolf Paw. Across Mulgore, Prairie Wolf Paws are gathered from the wolves that hunt the plains. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village uses them with plainstrider talons to make a cleansing totem. Prairie wolves hunt in packs across Mulgore’s rolling grasses, alongside prairie stalkers and their pack alphas. They threaten young hunters and local livestock, and their place in the spiritual balance of the plains matters to tauren shamans. The shamans see the paws as more than trophies: they carry the land’s innate vitality.

Prayer to Elune. A spirit held in a cage in Searing Gorge, Zamael Lunthistle, asks if you will help him. He has not had visitors in many years, and first wants you to hear his tale. Zamael Lunthistle greets you with a praise to Elune and says that many years have passed since anyone visited him. He asks if you will help, and begins with a request that you hear his tale.

Prayer to Elune. Zamael Lunthistle asks you to find his prayer to Elune, set down on a tablet of gold. One of the idol-worshipping scoundrels must carry it, and Zamael wants it taken to Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus. Zamael's faith has been rekindled, but he says that matters little after the countless malevolent actions he has taken against the world and its inhabitants. He does not expect absolution. All he asks is that the prayer be heard, so he sends you to recover the golden tablet from the idol worshippers and carry it to Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus.

Prehistoric Prism. In the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar finds a relic marked by the keepers. He sends you with it to Ironforge, where the Explorers' League can study the titans' legacy. Prospector Whelgar finds a remarkable artifact while surveying the Wetlands. Intricate keeper inscriptions cover its many facets, and Whelgar authenticates the titan-like markings. He urges you to carry the relic to Ironforge, where scholars can study it. Whelgar hopes the discovery will enter the official catalogue, with both your recovery and his authentication properly credited.

Preserving Knowledge. In Southshore, Loremaster Dibbs sends you to recover books from the Ruins of Alterac. Ogres have settled among the precious volumes left there, and one worn leather book matters most: it holds The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Loremaster Dibbs fears for the books in the Ruins of Alterac, where ogres have made their home. You are to search for the tomes they have looted and recover what you can. Dibbs would climb into the mountains to search as well, but fears old bones would not survive the journey.

Pridewing Venom Sac. Around Mirkfallon Lake, Pridewing Venom Sacs are sought by the night elves of Astranaar. Reports suggest Horde agents harvest the poison for covert attacks, and the Sentinels mean to deny them that supply. Pridewings hunt from the crags south of Ashenvale, especially around Mirkfallon Lake. These airborne predators are native to the Stonetalon Mountains, and their venom can be gathered from the glands in their bodies. Reports from Theramore suggest Horde assassins are taking that poison to coat blades for covert attacks on night elf settlements. In Astranaar, Sentinels send scouts to hunt the wyverns and collect their venom glands before Horde agents can claim them.

Pridewings of Stonetalon. In the Stonetalon Mountains, pridewing venom has become a threat to the uneasy peace. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from Theramore that orc assassins gather the poison for covert raids. Astranaar's Sentinels send scouts south to claim the venom sacs first. The Alliance and Horde have not declared open war across northern Kalimdor, but their peace is fragile. Skirmishes break out beneath the forest canopy, and quiet attacks take the place of full armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar watch for enemy movements, knowing a careless moment could put their sanctuary at risk.

Priest. Priests are spiritual guides and conduits of immense unseen power who shape belief, mend flesh, and guard souls. Channeling the radiant energies of faith or plumbing the terrifying depths of the Void, they serve as the vital heart of any war party. Across Azeroth, their traditions range from the Church of the Holy Light to the Moon Goddess's Sisterhood and shadowy Forsaken cults. Priests guide the spiritual destiny of their communities. While physical combatants test their mettle with steel, priests draw power directly from conviction. Through divine connection, they soothe grievous wounds, raise fallen companions from death's threshold, and weave mystic barriers to repel incoming harm. Their presence on the field often marks the difference between survival and annihilation.

Priestess A'moora. Priestess A'moora is a devout night elf servant of the Moon Goddess residing within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Working closely under the guidance of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind's priesthood, she attends to rituals of spiritual purification and communion with Elune. Travelers exploring Teldrassil are often directed to her when matters involve sacred offerings and the mystical wildlife of the boughs. Within the serene marble halls of the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora spends her days in contemplation and service. As an ordained priestess of Elune, she assists in tending the spiritual needs of Darnassus and preserving the delicate rituals passed down through millennia. While much of the Sisterhood oversees military defenses or diplomacy, A'moora focuses on traditional devotions and sacred matters concerning the natural spirits of Teldrassil.

Priestess Alathea. Within Darnassus, Priestess Alathea guides night elf priests in the Temple of the Moon. Devoted to Elune, she teaches sacred rites and helps acolytes prepare for healing, protection, and celestial magic. Priestess Alathea teaches and guides the Sisterhood of Elune within Darnassus's Temple of the Moon. After leaving Shadowglen, night elf initiates come to the temple to deepen their bond with the Goddess. Alathea shares sacred knowledge with those who devote themselves to healing, protection, and divine light.

Priestess Anetta. Inside Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta teaches new priests their first rites of the Holy Light. She is a human cleric and a member of the Brotherhood of Northshire. On the ground floor of Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta keeps to the quiet library wing. Defias bandits and kobolds trouble the valley, and she reminds those who pass that the Light may be the one thing that saves them someday.

Priestess Josetta. In Goldshire, Priestess Josetta guides young priests beyond their first trials in Northshire. She teaches faith, devotion, and the work of serving others. Priestess Josetta tends to the people of Elwynn Forest from an upstairs room in the Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers, guards, and local workers come within her reach there. She offers spiritual care among ordinary folk, showing that service to the Holy Light can be given wherever people need comfort.

Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield wants Princess Must Die! before Princess ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning sow from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, and Ma wants the family to gather their crops in peace. Princess has put the Stonefield harvest at risk. The prize-winning sow belongs to the Brackwells, but she has grown enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots and devouring their vegetables. Ma Stonefield has had enough of the sow eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants Princess put down before the pig ruins the season’s yield.

Prismatic Punch Card. In Gnomeregan, the Prismatic Punch Card carries the highest security clearance. Gnome refugees in Ironforge seek the records it unlocks. When the gnomes fled Gnomeregan, troggs and toxic irradiation drove them from their city. Vast stores of research and civic records remained in its depths. The gnomes guarded high-level systems with rising levels of clearance. To reach the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D in the lower Engineering Labs, a card must pass through a series of terminals. It starts white, then advances through yellow, blue, and red before the final terminal stamps it Prismatic. The card's encoded clearance is listed as awaiting the invention of an entirely new number.

Prison Break In. In Tarren Mill, Magus Wordeen Voidglare faces a crisis during his research. Months ago, four Forsaken fled the Undercity with artifacts stolen from a secure vault, and Sylvanas wants them back. Magus Wordeen Voidglare came to Tarren Mill to research, but now a crisis demands his attention. Four Forsaken turned from their brethren and stole from the Dark Lady. They broke into a secure vault and took four artifacts the apothecaries need for certain studies. Sylvanas wants them returned.

Pristine Pesterhide Pelts. Pristine Pesterhide Pelts is a task undertaken on behalf of Kristy Grant, a traveler seeking the radiant coats of the Pesterhide hyenas in Thousand Needles. Lacking combat training herself, Kristy relies on capable adventurers to hunt the beasts and harvest their pelts. Her goal is to send these unique hides back across the sea to her sisters in Stormwind, where they can be fashioned into fine garments and goods. Far from the bustling cobblestone avenues of Stormwind, Kristy Grant finds herself traveling through the arid, sun-baked canyon floor of Thousand Needles. While observing the local wildlife, she is struck by the striking hue and quality of the coats worn by the native Pesterhide hyenas. Recognizing that such distinct pelts are virtually unknown in the Eastern Kingdoms, Kristy envisions sending a shipment of hides back home to her sisters. In her eyes, the pelts represent not only a piece of the Kalimdor frontier, but raw material that skilled family hands in the kingdom can transform into something truly extraordinary.

Pristine Spider Silk. Stormwind mages seek Pristine Spider Silk for robes woven to endure enchantments. The fine thread comes from venomous spiders in Duskwood. Stormwind mages need silk strong enough to bear enchantments and the wear of an adept. Tailors use common spider silk, but the strands gathered from carrion recluses and black widow hatchlings in Duskwood are more resilient. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum send rising adepts into those woods to collect the silk. Master tailor Wynne Larson then weaves it into a robe for an adept.

Pristine Spider Silk. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath sends rising Alliance mages to Duskwood for pristine spider silk. They bring eight samples to Wynne Larson in the Mage Quarter, where she makes a robe for an adept. High Sorcerer Andromath marks a mage’s passage beyond apprenticeship with vestments fit for an adept. In the Wizard’s Sanctum, arcane mastery is matched by the robes its practitioners wear. Rather than buy finished garments, the mage must show field skill and discernment by taking pristine, unblemished silk from dangerous spiders.

name.frFR: Une peau de yéti en parfait état

text.enUS: Pristine Yeti Hide. You have come into a yeti hide that is unusually thick and tough, tougher even than any you have seen from the yetis of Rage Scar. Pratt McGrubben at Feathermoon Stronghold is looking for yeti hides, and this one may interest him. This hide is pristine, and clearly thicker and sturdier than the hides taken from the yetis of Rage Scar. Pratt McGrubben, at Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas, wants to buy yeti hides, so this one is worth carrying to him.

Prompt Potion Runner. Prompt Potion Runner is an urgent Undercity delivery quest where players must race an unstable concoction across the slime canal to the Apothecarium. The quest highlights the physical infirmities of undeath and the volatile nature of Forsaken alchemical research. In the subterranean corridors of the Undercity, the Forsaken alchemist Alessandro urgently needs a swift courier. Having prepared a highly volatile concoction with an extremely short shelf life, he cannot risk transporting it himself across the city's toxic slime canal due to the fragile state of his undead joints. An adventurer must sprint against the clock to ensure the brew arrives intact before it degrades into useless sludge.

Proof of Demise. Proof of Demise is a military directive issued by Deathguard Burgess in Brill to thin the ranks of the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Initiated on the orders of Varimathras, Sylvanas Windrunner's dreadlord lieutenant, it tests a soldier's loyalty to the Forsaken cause. Recruits are ordered to strip signet rings from fallen crusaders as tangible evidence of their slaughter. The campaign across northern Tirisfal Glades is not merely defensive; it is a coordinated war of eradication. Varimathras, the dreadlord who surrendered and pledged his blade to Sylvanas Windrunner, oversees many of the Forsaken's aggressive military maneuvers against the living. His directives trickle down to commanders like Executor Zygand and frontline officers such as Deathguard Burgess. Burgess makes the directive clear: the human race is viewed as vermin to be purged from Lordaeron, and the zealous crusaders nearby are the immediate target.

Prospect of Faith. Hammertoe Grez, nursing wounds, sends you with the amulet to Prospector Ryedol in the Badlands. Ryedol knows what Hammertoe was seeking, and what the Shadowforge clan must not be allowed to find. Hammertoe Grez, clutching at wounds, pauses to steady himself, then asks you to find Ryedol and hand over the amulet. Hammertoe is sure Ryedol will figure out what to do. Ryedol knows Hammertoe was seeking the origins of their people, and that Hammertoe also meant to thwart the Shadowforge clan, who cannot be permitted to get hold of the scrolls.

Prospect of Faith. Prospector Ryedol sends you to Ironforge with Hammertoe's Amulet. Historian Karnik and Hammertoe were working together to find the lost artifacts of Uldaman, and Ryedol guesses the Shadowforge found out the pair knew more than they let on. Ryedol sorts through who might know what to do next and settles on Historian Karnik, who is in Ironforge. You are to tell Karnik what has happened to Hammertoe and place the amulet in the historian's hands. Karnik will say what needs doing from there.

Prospector Ironband. At Ironband's Excavation Site, Prospector Ironband directs a dig into Khaz Modan's buried past. He leads the Dwarven Explorers' Guild's work in southeastern Loch Modan, seeking the heritage of the dwarven people and sending reports and relics to Ironforge despite setbacks and hostile creatures. Prospector Ironband leads the dig at Ironband's Excavation Site in the hills of southeastern Loch Modan. Like other field researchers in the Explorers' Guild, he believes Khaz Modan's soil holds truths about the origins of the dwarven race. His camp digs trenches and sifts rubble for ancient relics, stone tablets, and earthen artifacts. The work moves slowly, but Ironband remains resolute and welcomes capable travelers who can safeguard the operation.

Prospector Remtravel. In southern Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel leads an Explorers' League dig among ancient relics. The dwarf's scattered focus and the dangers around camp make his work perilous. The Explorers' League sent Prospector Remtravel across the sea to establish a dig in southern Darkshore. Night elves guard their ancestral lands, yet the League's drive to uncover Azeroth's origins carries its prospectors into forgotten places. Remtravel unearths fossilized history and ancient stones, while aggressive wildlife and hostile local threats make the camp difficult for one scatterbrained dwarf to manage.

Prospector Ryedol. Prospector Ryedol is an Explorers' League surveyor stationed on a dusty rise overlooking the eastern Badlands. Watching over the perilous excavations below, he strives to recover lost dwarven relics and maintain hope in a barren wasteland overrun by troggs and beasts. Perched upon a rugged hill just south of Hammertoe's Digsite, Prospector Ryedol represents the ongoing efforts of Ironforge's Explorers' League in the Badlands. The arid valley is rich in ancient titan secrets and earthen heritage, but field expeditions here are constantly beleaguered by savage troggs, ravenous coyotes, and territorial drakes. Ryedol coordinates retrieval efforts for dwarven gear stolen by the Dark Iron dwarves and seeks signs of hope amid the ruined outposts, determined not to let the League's sacrifices in the wastes be in vain.

Prospector Stormpike. In Ironforge, Prospector Stormpike oversees support for distant archaeological digs. A blunt, short-tempered dwarf of the renowned Stormpike clan, he also uses his sharp mind to decipher coded messages. Prospector Stormpike coordinates excavations from the Library of the Hall of Explorers. His work sends supplies, including blasting powder, to distant sites across Khaz Modan and beyond. He is impatient with idle chatter, but his dedication to uncovering dwarven history runs deep. His keen mind can break intricate ciphers, making him a useful ally to scouts facing secret threats.

Prospector Whelgar. At Whelgar's Excavation Site, Prospector Whelgar's search for titan relics has stalled. Vicious raptors overran the dig, and he seeks hardy adventurers to recover ancient artifacts. Prospector Whelgar leads a dwarven dig in the Wetlands. His camp, Whelgar's Excavation Site, lies east of Menethil Harbor, where he searches for the history of the dwarven race. Ancient stone relics once filled the valley, but territorial raptors drove his team into hiding. Whelgar refuses to leave his duty unfinished. He still hopes to recover valuable relics, including the Goaz Stone, before predators or rival scoundrels ruin the site.

Protect Kanati Greycloud. Protect Kanati Greycloud is a Horde quest at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Warned that centaur assassins have targeted the tauren Kanati Greycloud, adventurers must make a stand beside him and repel a squad of Galak assassins. While stationed among the towering sandstone spires of Whitereach Post, the tauren Kanati Greycloud learns from intercepted centaur orders of an assassination plot directed squarely at his life. The Galak tribe of centaur, relentless in their hostility toward the nomadic tauren and their Horde allies, are not content merely raiding supply paths; they seek to eliminate those who settle in their canyons.

Protect Kaya. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Kaya Flathoof is found captive among hostile Grimtotem tauren. Horde adventurers guide her along dangerous mountain trails to Camp Aparaje, then bring word of her survival to her anxious father, Makaba Flathoof. Kaya Flathoof was captured and held prisoner deep in Grimtotem territory in the Stonetalon Mountains. The tauren clans are divided by bitter rivalries, and few are sharper than the hostility surrounding the Grimtotem. Kaya has escaped captivity, but reaching friendly ground on foot means winding through trails watched by enemies and predators. An armed escort is her best hope of getting through.

Protect the Frontier. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern bridge as predators threaten the frontier. Stormwind's forces are thin here, and wolves and bears have grown bold near the Eastvale Logging Camp. He asks capable adventurers to cull the beasts threatening travelers and workers. Guard Thomas watches the bridge over the river at Elwynn Forest's eastern edge. Goldshire and the Northshire Valley have a visible Stormwind garrison, but this frontier receives far less protection. With Stormwind's forces stretched across the realm, Thomas is one of few sentries between the settled heartlands and the wilderness. Travelers help keep vital supply roads open.

text.enUS: Protecting the Herd. At Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh, Rudra Amberstill faces the loss of mountain rams to Vagash. With Ironforge's forces spread thin, the breeders need passing fighters to defend their herd. Vagash has taken two mountain rams from Amberstill Ranch. The ranch supplies the Bronzebeard dwarves with riding and working beasts, and the herd matters to Dun Morogh's rustic economy. The savage predator prowls the crags above the ranch, hunting local livestock.

Protecting the Shipment. In southern Loch Modan, Miran carries blasting powder toward Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband needs it to keep his dig moving, but the road is dangerous. Prospector Ironband's dig in the hills of southern Loch Modan needs blasting powder to cut through stone. Supply lines have failed, and threats to the courier wagons leave Miran stranded on the road with a heavy load. You guide him along the uneven roads to the excavation site, where the powder can keep Ironband's work from stalling.

Proudhorn the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder receives visitors atop Thunder Bluff. Tauren honor him as an ancestral spirit and pay respect to the wisdom of those who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. During the Lunar Festival, Proudhorn the Elder appears high on Thunder Bluff's windblown mesas. Tauren hold their ancestors' voices in the highest regard. They believe ancient leaders and sages remain as spirits, offering guidance and strength to the living.

Prove Your Worth. At the Sepulcher, Prove Your Worth begins Dalar Dawnweaver's campaign against the worgen of Silverpine. The Forsaken seek a path south through human and dwarven lands, but feral worgen threaten the road. Their presence leads back to Archmage Arugal. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, seek to secure the lands south of Tirisfal Glades, including human and dwarven enclaves. Silverpine Forest lies in their path, but the route is dangerous. Feral Moonrage worgen prowl the pine-covered hills, threatening Forsaken supply lines and forward bases.

Proving Allegiance. Gunther Arcanus tests whether you serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. To earn his trust, you are sent to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a Scourge operative near his island. Gunther Arcanus has kept to an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath. He fiercely guards his freedom. Bethor Iceshard's enchantments on Gunther's spellbook showed that the emissary carries no Scourge taint. Still, words and charms cannot quiet the hermit's suspicions. An outsider must prove hostility toward the Lich King's minions through decisive violence before Gunther will trust them.

Proving Grounds. In Alterac, recruits face a trial before joining the Stormpike Guard. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends them into Icewing Caverns to recover a planted battle standard. Success earns an official Stormpike Insignia and begins their rise through the expedition’s ranks. The Stormpike Guard fights the Frostwolf Clan in Alterac Valley. Lieutenant Haggerdin directs Alliance forces from their encampment in the Alterac Mountains. He tests new recruits before sending them to the battlefield, demanding proof of skill and nerve in Icewing Caverns, southwest of Dun Baldar.

Proving Your Worth. In Duskwood, Sven Yorgen tests your strength before he lets you face Morbent Fel. The hermit seeks revenge for his family and needs proof you can overcome the undead at Raven Hill Cemetery. At a secluded camp north of the howling woods, Sven Yorgen grieves for his family and burns with fury over their slaughter. He has learned that the Dark Riders who destroyed his homestead were allied with the necromancer Morbent Fel. Sven wants revenge, but he will not send an untried ally straight into Fel's grasp. First, he asks you to prove your combat skill against the skeletal forces at Raven Hill Cemetery.

Prowler Claws. Across the Barrens, Prowler Claws are carried back to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. They show that a hunter can track and defeat the prowlers stalking the plains. Savannah Prowlers hide in the Barrens’ tall grass, waiting to strike with patience and cunning. These large cats ambush creatures that enter their hunting grounds, unlike grazing plainstriders and zhevra. Taking their curved claws means facing predators that rely on stealth and defend their territory. For Horde warriors and scouts, the hunt tests whether they can track a stalker through its own ground and make it the prey.

Prowlers of the Barrens. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after the savannah prowlers. Their claws will show whether you can face the Barrens' greatest beasts. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters who have already faced the plainstriders and zhevras. Southwest of the Crossroads, savannah prowlers vanish into the central Barrens' gold and ochre scrub. These great cats hunt instead of grazing with the herds. They wait in tall grass, then ambush their prey, and unwary travelers can fall to them.

Psychometric Reading. Quintis Jonespyre, still wobbly after reading the knife, passes on visions of Raschal and the Woodpaw gnolls and asks you to take them to Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold. Quintis Jonespyre is still unsteady but has seen something useful. In the vision Raschal pulls two big leather backpacks off the boat, heads inland, and then goes back to the boat. Gnoll scalps appear, and Quintis thinks Raschal met Woodpaw gnolls. Raschal is very worried, almost terrified, and does not notice water elementals forming behind. There the images stop. Quintis must rest and asks you to tell Ginro, who needs to know.

Pure Hearts. In the Undercity, Pure Hearts draw a succubus from the Twisting Nether. Carendin Halgar gives these ritual reagents to Forsaken warlocks, who use them to manifest the demon and attempt to defeat and bind her. Carendin Halgar gives Pure Hearts to warlocks who summon a succubus in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. Set on the summoning circle, these untainted spiritual essences lure the demon across the Twisting Nether and into the mortal realm. Once she appears, the warlock must resist her enthralling mind-charms and strike her down. Defeating the succubus asserts mystical dominance and sends her back to the Twisting Nether. Carendin then teaches the warlock the spell to summon her at will.

Purgation Isle. Purgation Isle is a spiraling, rocky island lying off the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Crowned with a cemetery and a ruined scout tower, the desolate rock is cursed and swarming with the restless, condemned spirits of fallen humans and dwarves. Rising abruptly from the sea south of Hillsbrad, Purgation Isle is a grim sight marked by winding paths that lead past tombstones to an abandoned watchtower. No living nation claims it today. Instead, the isle is plagued by condemned souls—former paladins, priests, mages, and judges who wander among the graves, unable to find peace in death.

Purified Kor Gem. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, a Purified Kor Gem is needed for a weapon of the Light. First, the corrupted stone must be cleansed by elven magic. A Corrupted Kor Gem is held by naga in Blackfathom Deeps beneath the coast of Ashenvale. A paladin takes it to Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine. Thundris draws on arcane and natural arts to purge the stone’s aquatic and shadowy taint. The cleanse leaves a Purified Kor Gem, fit to channel holy power.

Putrid Claw. Putrid Claws reach Deathguard Dillinger as proof that the Scourge near Brill is being held back. Mindless undead roam the woods west of town, especially by the old bridge. The mindless Scourge keeps crossing into Tirisfal Glades. Rotting dead and ravaged corpses wander the eastern borders, gathering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. Deathguards place bounties on these horrors to protect travelers and garrison supply lines. A severed putrid claw proves that one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

Pyrewood Ambush. Deathstalker Faerleia waits in Pyrewood Village, where Arugal's council keeps the afflicted in line. The Forsaken aim to break his hold on the town and weaken his position in Shadowfang Keep. Deathstalker Faerleia waits inside Pyrewood Village's town hall for the local leaders. Archmage Arugal keeps to Shadowfang Keep, tending his dark sorceries, and leaves the Pyrewood Council to maintain order among the afflicted villagers. Faerleia plans to strike the council in an ambush. Without its mediation, the Forsaken hope the worgen in the surrounding woods and village streets will break free of Arugal's control.

Pyrewood Shackle. At Pyrewood Village, enchanted shackles bind its beleaguered inhabitants to Archmage Arugal's strange magic. The bands are tied to the dark fate that grips the townsfolk when night falls.

Pyrewood Village. Isolated Pyrewood Village lies beneath Shadowfang Keep in southern Silverpine Forest. Once part of Gilneas, the settlement was stranded outside the Greymane Wall, and Arugal's curse now haunts its living residents. Pyrewood was once a prosperous Gilnean settlement. After the Second War, King Genn Greymane sealed Gilneas behind the massive Greymane Wall, leaving Pyrewood on the wrong side. Cut off from their homeland, the townsfolk were entirely defenseless as the Scourge crossed Lordaeron during the Third War. They survived the first wave of undead, but their nightmare began when the mage Arugal took refuge in the fortress above.

Quagmire. The Quagmire comprises the sprawling, treacherous heart of central Dustwallow Marsh. Bound by Brackenwall Village to the north and the Dragonmurk to the south, its waterlogged flats are notoriously difficult to navigate. Hostile beasts and ravenous oozes make any journey through this central fen perilous. Occupying the wide expanse between Lost Point in the west and Dustwallow Bay in the east, the Quagmire represents the wild core of the marsh. Footing is unreliable at best, with solid earth constantly giving way to murky water and clinging mud. Travelers must contend with predatory crocolisks lurking beneath the scum, aggressive spiders nesting in the dead brush, and strange oozes that seep through the muck.

Quartermaster Lewis. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Quartermaster Lewis keeps supplies moving to the People's Militia. He serves local defenders and travelers holding the frontier against the Defias Brotherhood. Quartermaster Lewis keeps the militia's supplies in Sentinel Tower. Stormwind's royal leaders offer little aid to impoverished Westfall, so Sentinel Hill depends on local volunteers and whatever provisions they can gather. Lewis hands out field necessities, including dry rations, fresh water, arrows, shot, and throwing blades. The fighters standing watch need these basics to endure Defias raids.

Quel'Lithien Lodge. Quel'Lithien Lodge is an isolated high elven hunting lodge nestled in the forested northern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands near the entrance to Quel'Thalas. Its Farstrider rangers hold out among the blighted woods, surrounded by the Scourge and hunted by Forsaken agents, while guarding old elven archives. Before the Third War, Quel'Lithien was a Farstrider camp on the road toward Quel'Thalas, and it housed elven records of the ranger order. The lodge fell on hard times after the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and into the elven kingdom. Today its rangers keep their vigil in the corrupted forest, one of only two major concentrations of high elves left in Lordaeron.

Quell The Uprising. Warden Thelwater calls for help as the Stockade erupts in riot beneath Stormwind. Defias prisoners have seized the cell blocks, and he wants the uprising crushed before the city's leaders learn how badly the prison has failed. The Stockade holds criminals, conspirators, and outlaws who threaten the Kingdom of Stormwind. Imprisoned Defias operatives have launched a sudden, violent uprising and taken the cell blocks from the guards. Armed felons crowd the corridors, and the usual order has broken down. The guards now depend on visiting champions to fight through the riot and retake the prison.

Questioning Reethe. Ogron, whom Krog sent to track the human Reethe, has found him at last after a long search and says he hid well for a human. Ogron worries that so much time in the swamp may have driven Reethe mad, and asks you to come along to get answers from him. Afterward the way leads back to Krog at Brackenwall Village. After a long search, Ogron found Reethe, who by Ogron's reckoning hid well for a human. Ogron fears that so many days in the swamp may have left Reethe crazy, and wants you alongside to get answers from him. Afterward, Krog at Brackenwall Village awaits your return.

Quilboar. Quilboar are aggressive, boar-like humanoids native to central Kalimdor, renowned for their sharp spinal quills and relentless territorial savagery. Claiming descent from the fallen demigod Agamaggan, they dwell within dense mazes of razor-sharp brambles across Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens. Their fierce struggle over water, soil, and sacred ground makes them a constant threat to travelers and Horde settlements. Quilboar revere Agamaggan, the colossal boar Ancient who perished battling the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. According to their sacred traditions, the quilboar are his mortal offspring. Where Agamaggan bled and died across central Kalimdor, enormous thorny vines erupted from the scorched earth, forming sprawling root-mazes that the quilboar treat as holy ground. His crystallized blood endures across the Barrens as crimson Blood Shards, which their geomancers dig up and revere as powerful talismans.

Quinn Yorick. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick hides from the ghoul that wounded him. The Forsaken scout waits in a ruined farmhouse, unable to finish his mission or retreat alone. Quinn Yorick lies gravely injured upstairs in a ruined farmhouse at the Ivar Patch. Ivar the Foul, a ghoul lurking in the farm’s barn in northern Silverpine Forest, wounded him in a vicious clash. Quinn and his sister Rane were sent to scout Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. Too hurt to finish the mission or make a safe retreat alone, he remains in hiding. Passing travelers working for the Forsaken bring him healing and deal with the creature that nearly tore him apart.

Quinn's Potion. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel brews Quinn's Potion to help an injured scout recover. Quinn Yorick needs it after a disastrous patrol in Silverpine Forest. Apothecary Renferrel brews a remedy for Deathstalker Quinn Yorick. Word reached the Royal Apothecary Society at the Sepulcher after Quinn was badly hurt and left unable to move near the Ivar Patch. Renferrel made the draught to help him recover. Though minor field casualties rarely draw Renferrel from his darker research for Lady Sylvanas, he supplied the remedy so the scout could regain enough strength to travel.

Raene Wolfrunner. In Astranaar, Raene Wolfrunner directs the Sentinels’ defense of Ashenvale. Her wolf and saber cat companions stay close as she faces Horde forces and corrupted furbolg tribes. Raene Wolfrunner keeps watch in Astranaar with Korra, her saber cat, and Dagri, her wolf. A Sentinel officer, she oversees patrols across Ashenvale and coordinates intelligence from beyond the forest. She sends scouts such as Kaela Shadowspear into neighboring regions, including the Stonetalon Mountains.

Raene's Cleansing. At Lake Falathim, Raene's Cleansing turns from a search for Teronis into a grim recovery. Raene Wolfrunner sent the night elf sentinel there, and now you must bring back his journal and a glowing gem held by the murlocs before reporting to her in Astranaar. Raene Wolfrunner sent you to Lake Falathim to find Teronis, a night elf sentinel. You find him dead beside the water. His belongings include an intact journal, with an account of his assignment and what he found about Ashenvale's strange disturbances.

Raene's Cleansing. A Glowing Gem brings Raene's Cleansing to a turning point in Ashenvale. Raene Wolfrunner sends you east of Iris Lake to ask the dryad Shael'dryn how Dartol's ancient rod can be restored. Raene Wolfrunner studies the field notes left by the sentinel Teronis, who died while investigating Ashenvale's troubled furbolgs. His research points to an ancient rod crafted by a night elf named Dartol. Raene has recovered a Glowing Gem, but her skill as a huntress cannot unravel the arcane and natural mysteries surrounding the relic.

Raene's Cleansing. In Ashenvale, Raene's Cleansing brings Dartol's Rod closer to being whole. Shael'dryn knows where its iron shaft lies, in a chest near the Felwood border. The search leads toward treants changed by corruption. Raene Wolfrunner sends you to Shael'dryn, a keeper who watches over a moonwell deep in Ashenvale. Shael'dryn knows where Dartol's Rod's iron shaft lies, but reaching it means facing the taint spreading through the northern woods. The shaft is locked in an old chest in a quiet glade near the Felwood border.

Raene's Cleansing. In Ashenvale, Raene Wolfrunner and Shael'dryn seek Dartol's Rod's final piece. They hope the relic can help cleanse the forest and slow the furbolg attacks on its night elves. The iron pommel of Dartol's Rod was entrusted to the night elf druids at Dor'Danil barrow den. Disaster struck the sanctuary, and its caretakers were slain. With their refuge overrun, the pommel's hiding place was lost. Scavengers and wandering oozes now consume what remains in the ruins east of the southern road.

Raene's Cleansing. At Shael'dryn's direction, Raene's Cleansing now leads you to a mountain shrine with the rebuilt Rod of Dartol. The basin there holds the magic needed to restore its enchantment. Shael'dryn sends you from her moonwell into Ashenvale's wild southeastern slopes. The ancient shrines of Ashenvale often stood high among mountain crags, far from roads and hidden beneath dense forest canopies. You must cross unmarked ground along the rock faces and climb winding trails known mostly to Sentinels and woodland hermits.

Raene's Cleansing. At Iris Lake, Shael'dryn entrusts you with Dartol's Rod of Transformation, restored for Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar. You carry it back to report success and honor Teronis, the fallen scout. Dartol's Rod of Transformation has been reforged with components and ancient gem fragments gathered from corrupted reaches of Ashenvale. Near Iris Lake, the dryad Shael'dryn cleanses and renews its magic, then sends you across the forest roads to Astranaar. Raene Wolfrunner awaits the restored artifact.

Raene's Cleansing. In Ashenvale, Raene Wolfrunner seeks a way to speak with an uncorrupted furbolg. Southeast of Mystral Lake, Krolg offers a rare glimpse of the surviving furbolgs’ resentment toward the night elves. Raene Wolfrunner believes the late night elf meant to use Dartol’s restored Rod of Transformation to approach the furbolgs in disguise. Ashenvale’s woods have grown perilous, and madness spreads through the tribes, leaving no path to direct diplomacy. The rod gives you the shape of a furbolg, so you can try to pass their territorial rage and find someone willing to speak.

Raene's Cleansing. Disguised by Dartol's Rod of Transformation, adventurers gain the trust of Krolg, an uncorrupted furbolg near Lake Mystral. Disillusioned with both the arrogant night elves and the corruption rotting his own kin, Krolg asks for the death of the depraved chieftain Ran Bloodtooth so that the furbolgs can police their own. Near the waters of Lake Mystral, Krolg keeps a secluded vigil. Displaced and weary, he carries deep resentment toward the night elves, whose ancient hubris he blames for bringing ruin upon Kalimdor and stirring the dark rot festering in Ashenvale. To reach him, seekers use Dartol's Rod of Transformation to walk among furbolgs undetected. Yet despite his bitter hatred of the kaldorei, Krolg does not seek senseless butchery or innocent deaths.

Raene's Cleansing. In Astranaar, Raene's Cleansing reaches its end as you return with Ran Bloodtooth's skull. The search began with Teronis and now leaves Ashenvale's furbolg threat diminished. After Ran Bloodtooth falls, Krolg sends you back to Astranaar. You carry the chieftain's severed skull to Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner, proof that the threat prowling the forest depths has been struck down.

Raene's Cleansing. At the hidden shrine in Ashenvale, Raene's Cleansing reaches a turning point. The Rod of Transformation is assembled and its magic restored, and you must return it to Shael'dryn at her moonwell sanctuary. At the hidden shrine in Ashenvale, you have restored the Rod of Transformation. Its shaft, pommel, and glowing gem are joined, and the rod has been re-enchanted. Shael'dryn needs it for Raene's investigation of the furbolg attacks.

Raene's Cleansing. Raene's Cleansing begins when Raene Wolfrunner asks an adventurer to track down her missing friend, Teronis. Seeking a way to halt the rampant furbolg aggression across Ashenvale, Teronis set off toward Lake Falathim to recover a magic gemstone. Raene Wolfrunner serves alongside the Sentinels in Astranaar, defending Ashenvale against mounting threats. Among her closest companions was Teronis, who took it upon himself to find a potent defense against the increasingly violent furbolg tribes. When days passed without his return, Raene grew deeply worried, unable to abandon her post while fearing the worst.

text.enUS: Rage Scar Hold. Rage Scar Hold is a cavern carved into the wilderness of Feralas, situated on the mainland not far from Feathermoon Stronghold. It is notorious for housing some of the most vicious yetis in the region. Strangely, scattered books, symbols, and traces of night elven architecture deeper within suggest the den once served a far more civil purpose before the beasts claimed it. Carved into the rugged wilds of Feralas, Rage Scar Hold is dominated by savage yetis that attack anyone venturing near their lair. The creatures make the surrounding forest trails hazardous for both Alliance sentinels and passing travelers. While yetis are common to the untamed reaches of Kalimdor, the denizens of Rage Scar Hold stand out for their raw aggression and territorial ferocity.

Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm threatens the Horde from below. Its magma-lit tunnels hold savage troggs, and the Cleft of Shadow gives access to the caverns. Beneath Orgrimmar, dangers threaten the capital from below. While Thrall works to secure Durotar above, Ragefire troggs infest the chasm’s unstable vents and magma rivers. They rose from unknown depths and violently rejected Magatha Grimtotem’s attempts at diplomacy. Left unchecked, their numbers could undermine the city and overrun it.

Ragefire Chasm (Classic). Ragefire Chasm threatens Orgrimmar from beneath its streets, where troggs have broken into the tunnels. The fiery caverns also shelter a cult whose plans reach beyond Durotar. Ragefire troggs have surged into the volcanic tunnels beneath Orgrimmar. They pushed up from deep fissures and now threaten the city's foundations. Magatha Grimtotem, a tauren, tried to make peace with them, but the troggs answered with violence. Their tunnels run below the stone streets and fortified towers, leaving Orgrimmar at risk if the creatures keep digging upward.

Ragnar Thunderbrew. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Ragnar Thunderbrew keeps the family tavern supplied and its patrons fed. The dwarven brewer is known across Dun Morogh for the family's Beer Basted Boar Ribs. Ragnar Thunderbrew tends the kitchen and brewing work at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Mountaineers, travelers, and gnome refugees fleeing Gnomeregan gather there. His Beer Basted Boar Ribs, made with dwarven ale, are a Dun Morogh specialty. Supplies have grown hard to find since his usual meat provider enlisted in the King's Army. Ragnar now relies on wandering mountaineers and hunters to bring fresh crag boar flanks to the kitchen.

Rahauro. On Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, Rahauro sends Horde fighters against threats beneath Orgrimmar. He serves Magatha Grimtotem, coordinating the response to troggs in Ragefire Chasm and the search for a fallen agent’s possessions. Rahauro attends Magatha Grimtotem on the high terrace of Elder Rise. He speaks and acts for the elder crone, who relies on trusted servants to recruit others. When wild creatures swarm beneath the orcish capital, Rahauro handles the arrangements and sends Horde mercenaries to face them.
