text.enUS: Raid on the Kolkar. After Strange Alliance, Uthek the Wise sends you against the Kolkar centaurs to the northeast. Kill them, take their charms, and bring ten of those charms back to Uthek. Uthek scoffs at the Kolkar centaurs for thinking their magic strong; in Uthek's view they know nothing of magic. You go northeast to the Kolkar, kill them, and take their charms. Uthek wants ten Crude Charms to throw in the fire, laughing as they burn.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands where Tor'gan seeks to lift the spirits of a despondent orc named Gor'mul. When tales of Orgrimmar and Warchief Thrall fail, Tor'gan turns to newly rediscovered shamanic traditions to craft a revitalizing amulet from highland raptor eyes. At the remote outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, the orcs face enemies from without and quiet battles within. One of their own, Gor'mul, has fallen into a deep, unshakable melancholy. His companions attempted to rally him with proud tales of Kalimdor, the mighty fortress city of Orgrimmar, and the visionary leadership of young Warchief Thrall. Yet none of these grand victories or distant wonders could pierce Gor'mul's gloom or give him reason to hope.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest aimed at rekindling the fighting will of Gor'mul, a broken warrior consumed by despair. An emissary delivers a Raptor Talon Amulet in hopes of awakening the fierce spirit he once possessed. However, Gor'mul remains bitter, questioning whether any simple trinket could ever mend his sorrow or restore glory to the Horde. Raising Spirits involves delivering a Raptor Talon Amulet to an orc named Gor'mul. His allies hope that the wild strength and ferocity of raptors, channeled through the talisman, will reawaken the warrior's flame that once burned fiercely within his veins.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live. In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.

Raleigh Andrean. In the Undercity, Raleigh Andrean lives among the Forsaken. His requests show how little regard he has for his human life and those he once knew. Before the Third War, Raleigh Andrean lived in Lordaeron as a human. He was married to Deliah and counted Valdred Moray as a friend. The Scourge swept through the kingdom, killing Raleigh and raising him as a mindless thrall in service to the Lich King. After the Lich King's grip shattered and Sylvanas Windrunner led her uprising, Raleigh regained his free will and joined the Forsaken in the Undercity.

Raleigh and the Undercity. This quest bridges an investigation from Brill to the Undercity, tasking an adventurer with delivering a recovered heirloom ring to a widower named Raleigh. Found on a woman's stolen corpse bound for Fenris Isle, the jewelry points to a tragedy among Lordaeron's former inhabitants. Delivering it sets into motion a dark pursuit of vengeance. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren pieced together clues surrounding a stolen corpse and an engraved ring that once belonged to a woman named Deliah. Hoping to confirm its origin and see it returned to her family, Sevren directed the finder deep into the subterranean halls of the Undercity to seek Deliah's surviving husband, Raleigh.

Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. In Ashenvale, Ran Bloodtooth's Skull bears proof that a corrupted furbolg chieftain has fallen. The night elves of Astranaar receive it as a sign that a fierce threat to their woodland realm has ended. The furbolgs of Ashenvale have fallen into murderous madness under demonic taint and wilderness corruption. Ran Bloodtooth led one of the fiercest tribes. His skull gives the night elf Sentinels proof that he has fallen and his hold over the local furbolgs is broken, bringing some respite to Astranaar.

Randis. In Cathedral Square, Randis waits for a chance to see the world beyond Stormwind. During Children's Week, he eagerly joins willing adventurers across Alliance lands. Randis lives in the orphanage near Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, one of many children left without family by the realm's conflicts. When Children's Week comes each year, Orphan Matron Nightingale gives sympathetic heroes a whistle and entrusts them with his care. Curious and full of questions, Randis dreams of adventure, asks riddles, and declares that he wants to be king of Stormwind when he grows up.

Rane Yorick. At a farmhouse in Silverpine, Deathstalker Rane Yorick and her brother Quinn are cut off from the Sepulcher. Sent to scout the northern farms, they must get word to High Executor Hadrec. Across Lordaeron, the Deathstalkers are Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades. Agents like Rane Yorick watch the wilds from hidden posts for threats to Forsaken rule. Rane and her brother Quinn were sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest. Feral dangers closed around them, turning their covert work into a fight to survive.

Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea. Near Auberdine's watch, Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea directs the defense of Darkshore. The seasoned night elf sentry sends travelers to meet threats and investigate strange signs along the coast. From Auberdine, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea coordinates scouts as corruption grows and hostile forces press into Darkshore. She watches the wilderness around town and relies on capable travelers to guard the perimeter and protect night elf holdings along the coast.

Raptor Grounds. In the southern Barrens, Sunscale raptors claim a secluded valley in the rocky hills west of Northwatch Hold. Their eerie, tool-using cunning and obsessive theft of bright trinkets set them apart from ordinary beasts. West of Northwatch Hold, Sunscale raptors make their home in the Raptor Grounds. Eerie and far from ordinary beasts, they fashion crude shelters, make primitive tools, and coordinate their hunts. Their obsessive fascination with shiny or unusual things drives them to raid passing caravans and Horde encampments. Coins, trinkets, and supplies disappear into their canyon dens.

Raptor Head. Across the Barrens, Raptor Head trophies answer a bounty from Gazrog at the Crossroads. The guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft. A stolen chest of guard payroll has left the Crossroads watchtower without its silver. The defenders caught a wild raptor red-handed, to their disbelief. Gazrog has put a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators will be culled before they can pilfer more Horde supplies.

Raptor Horns. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix wants intact raptor horns for a scheme of his own. The goblin believes the cunning of Barrens raptors lies in their horns and hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws. Mebok Mizzyrix looks for fortune in Ratchet, where goblins chase one scheme after another. He has watched the Barrens raptors act with unusual craft and coordination compared with beasts elsewhere. Mebok decided their intelligence must be held in their horns. He has no formal inquiry in mind; he wants to put this idea to profit.

Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

Raptor Mastery. Hemet Nesingwary raises the stakes of his hunting expedition by sending you after a elusive breed known as Jungle Stalkers. Tracking down ten of these cunning raptors will prove your mettle as a true stalker of wild beasts in Stranglethorn Vale. Having tested your aim against lesser raptors, Hemet Nesingwary presents a more demanding quarry. Jungle Stalkers are notably cagey and far more difficult to track and slay than the breeds hunted previously. Hemet expects you to venture out into the jungle, fell ten of these wary predators, and return to camp to earn a lead on his finest hunt yet.

name.itIT: La maestria nella caccia al raptor

text.enUS: Raptor Mastery. Deep in Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges seasoned trackers to bring down an elusive predator that has escaped even him. Having proven your mettle against lesser beasts, you are tasked with tracking the cunning raptor known as Tethis and securing its talon. Following your earlier trials in the jungle, Hemet Nesingwary reveals the existence of a particularly vicious raptor named Tethis. While lesser hunters have chased prey across the foliage, Tethis has evaded capture entirely, defying even the expedition leader himself. Ajeck Rouack bestowed the beast with its moniker, marking it as the ultimate prize among Stranglethorn's scaled horrors.

Raptor Ridge. Raptor Ridge rises above the eastern Wetlands, northwest of the Dragonmaw Gates. Razormaw raptors hunt and nest among its crags, with a vicious matriarch deep in the caverns. Razormaw raptors hunt in packs across Raptor Ridge, where rocky trails climb above the eastern Wetlands. Travelers near the foothills of Khaz Modan risk meeting these predators. In a cavern at the ridge's heart, the Razormaw Matriarch guards her brood and nests from intruders. The Dragonmaw Gates lie close by.

Raptor Thieves. A raptor has stolen the guards' payroll from the Crossroads tower, leaving the defenders baffled. Gazrog calls for a cull to keep the beasts from striking again. The Crossroads depends on mercenary and grunt guards to keep trade routes open across the Barrens. Their pay matters to morale and discipline. When silver vanished from the guard tower, leaders expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, a raptor was caught stealing in the dead of night, leaving the settlement stunned and short of coin.

Rare Books. Rare Books is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley focused on recovering two stolen magical primers for Brother Paxton. Kobolds have hauled the missing texts into the Jasperlode Mine, where they appear to be studying elementary magic and summoning rituals. Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey faces a crisis in his library: several volumes have been carried off by vermin infesting the valley. Only two books remain missing from his catalog: 'Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards' and 'Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words'. These educational primers were carted away into the depths of the Jasperlode Mine by the occupying kobolds.

Rare Earth. At Dolanaar, Rare Earth waits for delivery to Denalan's camp near Lake Al'Ameth. The mineral-rich soil came from Darnassus for his botanical experiments on Teldrassil. Rare Earth is late reaching Dolanaar from Darnassus. Denalan, an eccentric botanist on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, requested the parcel to study plants in Teldrassil's young ecosystem. Herbalist Syral Bladeleaf now entrusts the soil to travelers heading south, hoping it reaches Denalan before its potency fades.

Rascally Rodents. Rascally Rodents is a quest in Northshire Valley where Brother Paxton tasks adventurers with recovering stolen books from the local kobolds. Though Paxton initially fears the vermin are devouring his library, retrieving the texts reveals an unsettling mystery behind the creatures' motives. Brother Paxton in Northshire Valley is in distress over the local kobold infestation, which has spilled over from the surrounding hills and mines into the sacred grounds. Convinced that the ravenous creatures have begun devouring the texts from his collection, he enlists the aid of young adventurers to hunt down the vermin and salvage whatever volumes remain before the entire library is lost.

Ratchet. Ships crowd Ratchet's docks on the eastern coast of the Barrens. The Steamwheedle Cartel runs this neutral port, linking central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms by sea. Ratchet gives shelter to anyone who can pay, on the dry coast between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh. After the Third War, chief engineer Gazlowe founded the port, drawing smugglers, exiles, and daring traders to Kalimdor's frontier. The Steamwheedle Cartel runs the town, which keeps strict neutrality between the Horde and the Alliance. Ships such as The Maiden's Fancy cross the Great Sea to Booty Bay with goods, mercenaries, and raw materials. Ratchet Bruisers watch the docks and beat anyone who starts a fight and disrupts trade.

Rattlecage Skull. In Deathknell, novice Forsaken warlocks gather skulls from mindless undead. Venya Marthand asks for them as a test of their will before teaching them the dark arts of summoning. In Deathknell, Venya Marthand guides newly raised Forsaken who have a gift for dark magic. She sends them to subdue Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy and bring back their severed skulls. The trial tests whether a fledgling warlock can bend creatures from beyond this world to their command. It also lays the groundwork for breaching the void and binding a first demonic servant.

Rattling the Rattlecages. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken face a test against the Rattlecage Skeletons. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them to destroy twelve skeletons and prove they can defend their hard-won freedom. Newly risen Forsaken face a harder trial after culling the mindless zombies in Deathknell. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends recruits against the Rattlecage Skeletons roaming the settlement’s outskirts. The animated bones have no sapience or self-control, yet strike harder and fight more fiercely than the nearby decaying corpses. Surviving their clattering ambushes shows Sarvis that a recruit can withstand immediate pressure.

Rau Cliffrunner. Rau Cliffrunner is a tauren scout and scholar stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to protecting his people from regional threats, he studies the history and origins of the hostile Galak centaur through their ancient relics. Working closely with allies in Thunder Bluff, Rau coordinates ventures into dangerous enemy strongholds across the canyon. Perched on the perilous bluffs of Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner maintains a watchful eye over the sweeping, sun-scorched expanse of Thousand Needles. The tauren outpost serves as a crucial Horde sanctuary in an otherwise hostile territory teeming with ferocious predators, quilboar, and aggressive centaur clans. Rau acts as both an outpost organizer and a dedicated investigator, keen on neutralizing emerging threats before they can overwhelm the vulnerable mesa settlements.

Ravaged Caravan. Smoke still rises from the Ravaged Caravan on Stonebull Lake's northeastern shore in Mulgore. The Venture Company convoy was bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operation before tauren defenders destroyed it. The ruined wagons sit on a rise above Stonebull Lake, where tauren from Bloodhoof Village stopped the Venture Company. The convoy carried mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site, but tauren defenders wrecked it before it could arrive. Venture Co. survivors still cling to the wagons and smoldering crates, guarding what cargo remains.

Ravaged Twilight Camp. Tucked away in the secluded Crystal Vale of northwestern Silithus, the Ravaged Twilight Camp sits ruined among towering mineral formations. It serves as an isolated redoubt for the eccentric hermit Highlord Demitrian, a devotee of the Windseeker. While the Twilight's Hammer maintains numerous active outposts across the sands of Silithus, this broken encampment in the Crystal Vale tells a different story. Nestled far from the primary cult fortresses, the camp lies largely ruined and deserted, save for Highlord Demitrian. A servant of Thunderaan, Demitrian lingers amidst the stones, seemingly abandoned by or detached from the wider Twilight hierarchy while brooding over elemental bindings and the lost power of the Windseeker.

name.frFR: Talisman de la griffe du corbeau

text.enUS: Raven Claw Talisman. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Raven Claw Talisman is kept among relics needed to awaken sleeping druids. The sacred night elf relic is one of four Relics of Wakening used to guide the Druids of the Talon safely back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman rests in a designated chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered deep meditative sleep. Their hibernation is a delicate spiritual threshold. Without the proper ceremonial focus, a druid whose link to the waking world is broken may remain stranded in the Emerald Dream. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs this talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting to perform the awakening ritual and bring the sleepers back safely.

Raven Hill. In western Duskwood, shadows move through Raven Hill, and a light flickers in a ruined window. Elaine Carevin sends travelers from Darkshire to learn what has taken shelter there. The Night Watch has long left Duskwood’s far west to the dead and wilderness. Yet signs of life there demand attention. Calor, a watcher on the gloomy roads, saw movement among Raven Hill’s silent houses two nights in a row. A lantern flickered in a window. With ghouls, skeletons, and beasts across the land, the Night Watch cannot ignore what stirs among the ruins.

Raven Hill. In western Duskwood, Raven Hill lies in ruins beneath the shadow of its vast cemetery. Frightened squatters and invisible spirits are all that remain of the once lively human settlement. Raven Hill stands along Duskwood’s western road, just north of Addle’s Stead, a shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living fled east toward Darkshire or left the territory. Now ruined timber homes decay beneath the gloom. Travelers avoid them, fearing restless dead from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen among the crumbling walls.

Raven Hill Cemetery. At Raven Hill Cemetery, the dead rise from their graves in western Duskwood. The burial ground once served nearby hamlets, but now undead, spiders, and grave robbers roam among the tombs. Raven Hill Cemetery was once the burial ground for the settlements around the Dawning Wood. When dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead began clawing out of their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors now crowd the graveyard. Rotting abominations and giant spiders prowl among the tombs, while desperate grave robbers plunder ancestral crypts beyond the reach of local authorities. Raven Hill remains one of Duskwood's most dangerous places.

Ravencrest Monument. Perched upon the windswept cliffs of southern Azshara, the Ravencrest Monument marks the shattered remnant of an ancient night elven colossus. Once a towering tribute overlooking the Great Sea, the statue has long since broken apart, leaving only towering legs and scattered stone ruins now stalked by hostile Spitelash naga. Standing high above the ocean southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, the Ravencrest Monument was once an awe-inspiring marvel of Kaldorei stonework. Today, little remains of the majestic colossus beyond its pair of gigantic broken legs rooted to the stone plinth, with the shattered fragments of its torso and head either buried in the cliffside dirt or lost beneath the waves below. Reaching this remote coastal promontory requires trekking across the mainland bridges of Azshara, as sheer, rocky drops prevent any approach from the sea.

Ravenholdt. Ravenholdt, also known as the Assassin's League, is an elite guild of rogues, thieves, and killers based out of a secluded mountain manor above the Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the league maintains strict neutrality from faction politics while waging an unending shadow war against their bitter rivals, the Syndicate. They test and recruit only the most cunning operatives across Azeroth, valuing peerless discipline, stealth, and lethal efficiency above all else. Tucked away in the craggy mountains connecting Hillsbrad to Alterac, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the nerve center for Azeroth's premier brotherhood of assassins. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the organization operates far beyond the jurisdiction of kings and warchiefs. Within its walls, master specialists hone every lethal art: Master Kang instructs disciples in close combat and assassination, the Thunderwood brothers brew rare and deadly poisons, and gnome craftsmen engineer intricate locks to test fledglings. To non-rogues, entering the estate is an overt flirtation with death, where an unwary step easily ends with a poisoned dagger in the ribs.

Ravenholdt Manor. Ravenholdt Manor watches over Hillsbrad from high in the mountains. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt leads its guild of thieves and assassins, where practitioners of stealth hone their craft beyond the authorities’ reach. Northwest of Durnholde Keep, a narrow pass and winding cave lead to Ravenholdt Manor. The estate stands isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains, and belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. He keeps a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. A tranquil garden and outdoor training arena give them space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat under martial experts like Master Kang. Those with a talent for skullduggery are welcome, but watchful sentries greet clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors with cold suspicion.

Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat watches the northern approaches to Felwood from a great tree in Ashenvale. Dryads and Cenarion protectors guard the outpost, where Keeper Ordanus makes his home. At Raynewood Retreat, the great tree rises between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run. Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters guard the outpost. Their watch turns north, toward the taint spreading from Felwood.

Razor Hill. Razor Hill links the Valley of Trials, the Barrens, and Orgrimmar at a crossroads in central Durotar. Its fortified barracks train young orc and troll warriors for life in the wilderness. Razor Hill joins northern Durotar to the southern coast and the Barrens across the Southfury River. Stone-and-timber barracks and orcish burrows fill the settlement, founded early in Durotar's settlement. After the Third War, human forces from Kul Tiras lured the Horde here with a false offer of an emissary summit. Rexxar went in Thrall's stead and stopped their ambush. Razor Hill now stands fortified against further attacks from the coast.

name.ptBR: Torre de Vigia do Monte Navalha

text.enUS: Razor Hill Watchtower. Furl Scornbrow watches Durotar from the Razor Hill Watchtower. From its red stone bluffs, he keeps an eye on the plains and coast, guarding the settlement below. The Razor Hill Watchtower rises above Razor Hill and the canyons around it. Thick timber and iron framing hold the outpost together. Durotar faces threats from Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders across the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists in nearby crags. From the ridgeline, a lookout can spot warbands, smoke signals, and incursions before they reach the settlement gates.

Razorfen. Razorfen is the collective name associated with the predominant quilboar tribe of southern Kalimdor and their sprawling thorn-choked settlements. Carved into massive briars along the southern border of the Barrens and the edge of Thousand Needles, Razorfen encompasses the strongholds of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs. It serves as both the spiritual heart and the central bastion of quilboar power. According to legend, the colossal thorned brambles that make up the Razorfen sprouted ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. When the giant boar Ancient, Agamaggan, fell in battle against the Burning Legion, his blood seeped into the earth wherever he bled and died. From that divine sacrifice grew massive vines of petrified bramble and iron-hard thorns, creating a natural fortress where his descendants, the quilboar, have dwelled ever since.

Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

Razorfen Downs (Classic). Deep in the southern Barrens, the Scourge now holds Razorfen Downs, the quilboar's ancestral burial ground and capital. Led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer, its agents have raised the quilboar dead and threaten to spread their power across central Kalimdor. Razorfen Downs shares the towering, petrified vines of nearby Razorfen Kraul. It lies where the boar demigod Agamaggan fell in the War of the Ancients. For generations, this thorn labyrinth was the quilboar's sacred burial ground and seat of power, guarded by mystics of the Death's Head tribe. The quilboar hold its dense briars holy, for they were soaked in their divine progenitor's blood.

Razorfen Kraul (Classic). Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal thorns that sprang from the blood of the fallen boar demigod Agamaggan. Ruled by the ruthless crone Charlga Razorflank, this fortified labyrinth serves as a staging ground for bloody raids across the southern Barrens. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the colossal boar demigod Agamaggan perished battling the Burning Legion to save Azeroth. Wherever his sacred blood seeped into the soil of southern Kalimdor, massive, impenetrable thorn vines erupted from the earth. The quilboar, believing themselves the mortal progeny of the Great Boar, gathered within these dense briars to dwell and venerate his sacrifice. The dense mass known as Razorfen Kraul stands as their most revered redoubt, thick with quilboar warriors, beast trainers, and earth-shaping shamans.

Razorflank's Medallion. Charlga Razorflank's medallion lies deep within Razorfen Kraul, carried by the crone who rules the stronghold. Its return gives the night elf sentinels proof that she has fallen. Charlga Razorflank carries the medallion as the leader of the Razorfen quilboar. At Thalanaar, Falfindel Waywarder learns of fallen explorers such as Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow, then sends Alliance adventurers against the quilboar leader. The medallion confirms Charlga's death to the night elf sentinels guarding Feralas's borders. They can know that the gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

Razorhide. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Razorhide to those who bring him blood shards. The captive quilboar trades Agamaggan’s life essence for a blessing that hardens the skin before battle. The quilboar trace their power to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who died fighting the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood sank into the Barrens and hardened into crystalline shards, still alive with ancient power. The Horde and quilboar remain sworn enemies, yet Mangletooth, held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, will share sacred knowledge for these fragments.

Razormane Grounds. Razormane quilboar push east from the Barrens into central Durotar. Their thorn-choked camp marks the front of their unending clash with Orgrimmar's orcs. At the Southfury River, the Razormane Grounds threaten travelers beneath central Durotar's red cliffs. The camp marks the furthest east the quilboar have spread from the Barrens. Captain Flat Tusk of the Battleguard and Geolord Mottle lead raids on nearby orc settlements and passing supply lines. Patrols set out from Razor Hill and nearby outposts, but the Razormane keep replenishing their ranks among the briars faster than the Horde can clear them.

Razorwind Canyon. Dustwind harpies threaten travelers on Razorwind Canyon’s road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. The rocky gulch cuts through Durotar, and the harpies make the route north toward the Horde capital dangerous. Razorwind Canyon runs beside the main road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Its gullies reach into the eastern bluffs and west toward Tor'kren Farm. Dustwind harpies nest among the rocks and attack travelers who stray too close to their roosts. With the canyon so near the capital’s trade route, Durotar’s defenders must keep watch over its gullies.

Razzeric's Tweaking. On the Shimmering Flats, Razzeric adds personal modifications to racers once Pozzik has finished with them. A seaforium booster ordered from Shreev in Gadgetzan was on a zeppelin that Razzeric hears crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, and Razzeric wants it brought back. Razzeric grants that Pozzik is a great mechanic, but thinks Pozzik too wary of loading on firepower and hanging on for the ride. Once Pozzik is done with a racer, Razzeric spends time making personal changes: loosening the controls, removing frame sections and piling on power. A seaforium booster was ordered from Shreev at the Gizmorium in Gadgetzan, but the zeppelin carrying it crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, by Razzeric's account. The booster is needed back on the Shimmering Flats, since showing up at the track without that extra kick would be a travesty.

Razzle Sprysprocket. In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket works to recover gnomish machinery. He tinkers with Ozzie Togglevolt and seeks lost parts scattered through the snowy hills. After Gnomeregan's fall, Razzle found refuge in Dun Morogh and set up his workshop in Kharanos. He has a gift for delicate mechanical parts and works beside fellow engineer Ozzie Togglevolt. Together, they recover gyro-mechanisms and cog assemblies lost or scavenged during the flight from their irradiated homeland.

Reading the Ley Lines. Reading the Ley Lines is a rite of passage for young Skyborne discovering their Highborne magical heritage. Entrusted by Falorne Fallwind on Zephras Isle, novitiates travel to the standing stones in Thendal Grove to sense and draw upon the raw arcane currents surging through the elemental terrain. Even within the windswept confines of the elemental plane, latent arcane conduits run beneath the earth. While strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh drift across Zephras Isle, subterranean ley lines have begun pushing toward the surface. To practitioners of magic, these ruptures provide direct access to untamed arcane reservoirs, offering strength to any who possess the bloodline and knowledge necessary to channel them.

Reagent Pouch (shaman). Burning Blade cultists in Durotar carry reagents for a shaman's first fire sapta. Telf Joolam uses them with fire tar from Razormane quilboar to make the draught that lets a young shaman see the realm of fire. Burning Blade cultists carry reagents for a young shaman's first fire sapta. The hermit Telf Joolam uses the powders and oils in their pouches with fire tar from Razormane quilboar. Together, these components make a draught that grants sight into the realm of fire and attunes the shaman to the spirits of flame.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor is gathering reagents for the gnome mage Leftwitch, who lives in Kharanos, and the Reclaimers are short-handed. He wants claws and horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east before the rest of the list can begin. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor has another job on his hands: fetching reagents for Leftwitch, the gnome mage who lives in Kharanos. Roetten reckons it is easy coin, since the Reclaimers are already out in Desolace, and Kreldig says he does not care that the crew is short-handed.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Next on Leftwitch's list for Kreldig Ungor is venom from the scorpashi and hides from aged kodo. Kreldig cannot say where to find either, since he does not know Desolace well. Following the first part of Leftwitch's list, Kreldig Ungor turns to the next items. They look simple enough, but the instructions are exact. The mage wants venom from the scorpashi, any of them will do, and hides from kodo, but only aged kodo. Dying and ancient kodo are no use. Kreldig wants seven vials of venom and three hides. Mages, Kreldig muses, ask for some odd things.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor has the last of the items Leftwitch wants, and he admits it is not pretty and will take longer than the others. All of it comes from demons: brains, wings and vials of blood. Kreldig warns that the final set is a grim business, slower to gather than any before it. Leftwitch wants three kinds of parts, ten of each. The brains come from felhounds: mana eaters, mage hunters or ley hunters. The wings come from the nether maidens, sisters or sorceresses. The blood comes from doomwarder captains or lords. Kreldig says he would understand if you passed on this one.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor gives you Leftwitch's package and sends you back to Ironforge. Roetten Stonehammer is the one to see about your pay, and Kreldig promises a kind word about you once back home. Kreldig says your pay waits in Ironforge with Roetten Stonehammer himself. Roetten will be glad to be rid of Leftwitch's package, and handing it over should be enough to get what you are owed. Kreldig expects to be in Desolace only a little longer, and still means to speak well of you once home.

Rear Guard Patrol. At the Bulwark, Deathguard Linnea sends you to guard Tirisfal's eastern flank. Scourge horrors and lingering spirits haunt Balnir Farmstead, where they threaten the road and the supply lines that keep the front supplied. The Bulwark holds back the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands from Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Linnea oversees security behind the frontier. The defenders cannot spare troops to guard against attacks from the rear. Any undead that slip past the choke point must be destroyed before they can cut the supply lines feeding the front.

Rear Guard Patrol. Deathguard Linnea calls patrollers to defend Tirisfal Glades. She sends them after Riptear, an abomination roaming near Venomweb Vale that should never have passed the Bulwark. The Bulwark is the sole fortified barrier between Tirisfal Glades and the horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Forsaken military strategy depends on fighting on one front. If mindless undead slip behind the lines, they can choke the supply routes feeding the front. Stray spirits or ghouls sometimes bypass the barricades, but an abomination roaming the glades signals a grave failure of containment.

Reassignment. In Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle seeks a way back to Stormwind. He has compiled an exaggerated report of his deeds against the coastal naga and sends an adventurer to Stormwind Keep to deliver it to his former mentor, Major Samuelson. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle resents his posting in the Hillsbrad Foothills. In Southshore, far from the capital and under Marshal Redpath's stern watch, he spends his days plotting a transfer south. He takes credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga to make himself look like an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ready for promotion.

Rebel Camp. Tucked just off the road in northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Rebel Camp serves as a fortified refuge for Alliance soldiers who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. Led by Lieutenant Doren, these troops refused to surrender to the madness gripping their commander's expedition and now fight to survive and undo his descent into tyranny. When Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale on behalf of Stormwind, things rapidly fell apart. Afflicted by the dark jungle magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, the Colonel and his core loyalists succumbed to madness, turning rogue and terrorizing the wilds. A handful of sound-minded soldiers led by Lieutenant Doren refused to participate in the atrocities. Breaking away from Kurzen's Compound, they established this hidden camp in the north to stage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades.

Reception from Tyrande. Sentinel Thenysil sends you from Astranaar to Darnassus for an audience with Tyrande Whisperwind. After you help the Sentinels hold their ground against the Venture Company in Stonetalon, Tyrande receives you at the Temple of the Moon. The Venture Company puts pressure on night elf outposts across the Stonetalon Mountains. Sentinel Thenysil coordinates the defense from Astranaar, but the remote bases are hard to sustain. Supply lines and intelligence help the Sentinels keep an Alliance presence in Kalimdor's interior, and your aid strengthens their position.

Recipe of the Kaldorei. Zarrin teaches a lesson in balance through the Recipe of the Kaldorei. In Dolanaar, young cooks learn to gather only what they need from Teldrassil's woods. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and teaches young adventurers the traditions of his people. The night elves once called themselves the kaldorei, or children of the stars. Zarrin begins their understanding of that heritage with the bond between a hunter, their food, and Teldrassil's boughs, rather than the battlefield.

text.enUS: Reclaimers' Business in Desolace. In Ironforge, Roetten Stonehammer sends recruits across the sea to meet the Reclaimers in Desolace. At Nijel's Point, Kreldig Ungor offers paid work recovering lost treasures and relics. Roetten Stonehammer recruits travelers in Ironforge for the Reclaimers. The group seeks profit in forgotten ruins and barren lands across Kalimdor. Desolace is a harsh stretch ruled by warring centaur clans, but the journey may pay well for those willing to make it.

text.enUS: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. At Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm sends Alliance fighters to clear the Bloodfury harpies from the ruined Charred Vale. Their removal will open a path for druids and caretakers to begin healing the scorched land. South of Stonetalon Peak, the Charred Vale lies in ash and smoldering ruins where a lush alpine haven once stood. A mechanized logging and mining army swept through the sacred crags, stripping trees and setting uncontrolled fires. For the guardians around Stonetalon, ancient woodland lost to industrial greed is a wound they cannot ignore.

name.esES: La reconquista de La Vega Carbonizada
name.frFR: À la reconquête du Val calciné

text.enUS: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Keeper Albagorm seeks help for the Charred Vale from far to the south. The Bloodfury harpies have been driven back for now, but the wounded land needs more than force to heal. The Charred Vale lies beneath ash in southern Stonetalon Mountains, scarred by terrible destruction. Alliance forces under Keeper Albagorm have driven the Bloodfury harpies from their nests in the ruins, but their retreat may not last. Albagorm knows that force can only hold the harpies back. The ravaged earth must be healed before they return and take the Vale again.

Reconstructed Tome. In warlocks’ hands, the Reconstructed Tome gathers the scattered teachings of the cabal. Its pages hold the rites for summoning and binding a felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Warlocks of the Alliance and Horde search for the torn leaves of the Tome of the Cabal. They piece the grimoire back together and consult occult scholars, who are eager to glimpse its rare teachings before the finished book is surrendered.

Recover the Key!. Elder Torntusk is held at Jintha'alor in shackles. He says Hitah'ya the Keeper has the key to his bindings and is in the nearby cave, well guarded, and he asks you to kill her and bring it back. After Kidnapped Elder Torntusk!, you find Elder Torntusk bound in shackles at Jintha'alor. Hitah'ya the Keeper holds the key to his bindings and is in the nearby cave, well guarded. Elder Torntusk asks you to kill her and fetch the key so his shackles come loose, for only then can he go home.

Recruitment Letter. Takrin Pathseeker sends promising adventurers from Durotar west to serve in the Barrens. His letter directs able-bodied volunteers to the border outpost run by Kargal Battlescar. Takrin Pathseeker watches young warriors and scouts prove themselves around Razor Hill. He chooses those who seem strong enough for frontline service and gives them a letter for duty in the Barrens. Across the Southfury River bridge, recruits leave Durotar’s sheltered red dirt and join the Horde’s guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts.

Red Burlap Bandana. In Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves near the abbey vineyards. The cloth marks low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses of the Brotherhood. Red burlap masks mark the Defias Brotherhood's rank-and-file. Cheap, rough cloth dyed red hides a thief's features and signals allegiance to the growing rebellion. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs carry these scarves into the eastern orchards. The local guards recognize the striking red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

Red Jack Flint. In Menethil Keep, Red Jack Flint connects sailors with travelers bound across the sea. He is a seasoned human mariner and crew member of the Maiden's Virtue, helping travelers find passage and contacts toward Kalimdor. Red Jack Flint is a seasoned sailor in Menethil Keep. A crewman of the Maiden's Virtue, he knows the sea routes from Khaz Modan to distant shores. He also directs capable travelers to allies across the Great Sea, including Fiora Longears in Kalimdor.
Red Leather Bandana. In Westfall, Red Leather Bandanas mark those who defy Stormwind’s Crown. The Defias Brotherhood wears them as face coverings and a sign of their cause.

Red Leather Bandanas. At Sentinel Hill, Red Leather Bandanas mark the fight against the Defias Brotherhood. Scout Galiaan offers a reward for the red cloth masks worn by the outlaws, as the People's Militia struggles to track them across Westfall. Across Westfall, the red bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. The gang draws cutpurses, looters, and traitors from many walks of life, but its members rally beneath the same crimson sign. Scout Galiaan and the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill collect the bandanas as proof that bandits have fallen. The cloth also helps them follow the Defias as their fronts shift across the countryside.

Red Linen Bandana. Across Elwynn Forest, Red Linen Bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. Its cloth hides a wearer’s face and can be put to use by local settlers. Across Elwynn Forest, full Defias operatives wear woven red linen bandanas. In Northshire Valley, lower-ranking initiates and common thugs use coarse burlap masks instead. The crimson cloth hides a face and marks allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals their rebellion against Stormwind's crown.

Red Linen Goods. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs cloth for her tailoring. She asks passing adventurers to hunt Defias bandits and take their linen bandanas, then uses the cloth to make goods for travelers. Defias bandits across Elwynn wear red linen bandanas. Their less organized kin in Northshire Valley make do with cheap burlap masks. For local craftsmen short on materials, the bandanas offer cloth they can use.

Red Rocks. Red Rocks is a towering sandstone bluff in northeastern Mulgore that serves as a sacred ancestral burial ground for the tauren. Here, the most valiant fallen champions are laid to rest, and young braves travel to its quiet heights to seek the wisdom of their forebears. Rising high above the plains of northeastern Mulgore, the crimson formations of Red Rocks mark a sacred threshold between the living world and the next. Tauren tradition reserves this solemn ground for their most valiant heroes—chieftains, defenders, and champions who gave their lives founding and protecting Thunder Bluff. They are laid to rest here in honor, among the graves of their forebears. It is equally a place of spiritual beginning, where young tauren complete their rites of passage by honoring the ancestral graves and communing with the wind.

Red Silk Bandanas. Scout Riell sends the People's Militia after Red Silk Bandanas in the Deadmines. Their fine weave marks the Defias leaders who direct the uprising in Westfall. Scout Riell and the People's Militia have learned that cloth marks rank in the Defias Brotherhood. Common cutpurses and highwaymen across Westfall tie coarse red cloth over their faces. Senior conspirators and inner-circle operatives wear fine red silk. Bringing back their bandanas strikes at the experienced officers coordinating Edwin VanCleef's uprising.

Red Wool Bandana. Inside the Stormwind Stockade, Red Wool Bandana scraps mark Defias brotherhood. Imprisoned cutthroats tear them from jailhouse wool blankets and wear them as emblems of defiance behind bars. In the Stormwind Stockade, Defias Brotherhood inmates hold fast to their identity. They secretly tear scraps from prison wool blankets and stitch them into red bandanas to wear as their colors. Guards treat the scarves as contraband, and their discovery can spark fatal mutinies. For the prisoners, each bandana declares that their brotherhood and rebellion endure, even in chains.

Rediscovering the Light. In Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken paladins face the pain of calling on the Holy Light. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them to heal wounded Deathguards through the burning agony. Newly risen Forsaken paladins must face a hard truth: the Holy Light still answers them, but burns their withered bodies. Many were champions of the Silver Hand or knights of Lordaeron before they fell. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them that powers once used without thought now bring fierce pain. The Light clashes with the foul magic that sustains undeath, so calling on it takes resolve and endurance.

Redridge Goulash. In Lakeshire, Redridge Goulash helps feed a town under strain. Chef Breanna fed the active Stormwind garrison during the recent Blackrock orc uprising, emptying her pantry and leaving her to seek hearty ingredients from the mountains. Lakeshire remains under siege from Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and ferocious wild beasts. When the recent orc uprising began along the ridges, Chef Breanna took on feeding the entire brigade of Stormwind troops stationed in town. Keeping the active garrison fed quickly emptied her cupboards, though the town still had plenty of hungry mouths.

Redridge Rendezvous. Promising Alliance rogues are sent east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to train in Lakeshire. SI:7 wants them ready for dangerous field work under seasoned operatives. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, warns that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains, where they train under Lucius, stationed among Lakeshire’s docks.

name.frFR: Encore du carburant pour la zappette

text.enUS: Refuel for the Zapping. Zorbin Fandazzle needs more water elemental cores. Setting up shop on the Forgotten Coast is a struggle, so the pay will be smaller, but Zorbin promises to tell everyone in earshot of your help and says there are friends in the Cartel. Zorbin Fandazzle jokes about the heroic deed of collecting goo from inside elemental beings, wondering whether you will want more of the same. Melodrama aside, Zorbin does need more water elemental cores. Establishing the shop here is a desperate business, so there is little to give in return, but Zorbin promises to tell everyone in earshot how you helped, and says to trust this because Zorbin knows people in the Cartel. Six cores are wanted, taken from Sea Elementals and Sea Sprays on the Forgotten Coast, and brought to Zorbin near the dock.

Refuge Pointe. Refuge Pointe is the primary redoubt for the Alliance and the surviving remnants of Stromgarde within the Arathi Highlands. Perched centrally along the highlands' trade road, it serves as a staging ground to reclaim the shattered capital of Stromgarde Keep and hold back rival forces across the region. Following the devastation of the Third War and the catastrophic fall of Stromgarde Keep, the bulk of Stromgarde's surviving populace fled south toward friendlier lands. Those who remained formed a resolute vanguard, digging in at Refuge Pointe under Captain Nials. Composed of battle-hardened Stromgarde soldiers, League of Arathor forces, and supporting Alliance specialists, the encampment represents the kingdom's last organized stand in its ancestral homeland.

Refugee. Throughout the violent history of Azeroth, constant warfare has repeatedly driven civilian populations from their homes. From the exodus of Stormwind during the First War to the tragic flight from Lordaeron in the Third War, refugees remain living testaments to the devastating costs of invasion, plague, and betrayal. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War, settlements like Goldshire, Moonbrook, and Grand Hamlet burned. Following the assassination of King Llane Wrynn, Sir Anduin Lothar took command of the kingdom's remnants. He gathered surviving soldiers and desperate civilians, escorting them to the harbor as the city burned. Lothar led a massive fleet across the Great Sea to the northern shores of Lordaeron. Arriving near Southshore, the exiled survivors—including the young Prince Varian Wrynn—were granted sanctuary by King Terenas Menethil II.

Regthar Deathgate. In the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate calls seasoned Horde fighters west. The veteran warrior is gathering volunteers for a campaign across the mountains into Desolace, where centaur clans terrorize the frontier. Horde leaders watch the borders for threats. In the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate has set up a defensive post guarding the western passes. Horde officers send proven adventurers west of the Crossroads to answer his call for hardened fighters.

Rejold Barleybrew. At Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew works to perfect his mountain spirits. He gathers ingredients from across western Dun Morogh and tests his brewing recipes. In Dun Morogh, brewing is a craft dwarves take seriously. Rejold works from Brewnall Village, near the frozen lake of the Iceflow River. He keeps refining his blends, seeking rare hops, mountain minerals, and pristine ice water. He wants to brew stouts hearty enough to warm even the stoutest dwarven warriors.

Rejold's New Brew. In Dun Morogh, Rejold's New Brew brings you back to Brewnall Village. After you gathered Shimmerweed, Rejold Barleybrew has perfected a new recipe and wants you, a trusted friend, to sample it. Tharek Blackstone and Pilot Bellowfiz, your contacts in Dun Morogh, send you back to Brewnall Village. Rejold Barleybrew has finished fermenting his experimental batches and wants to share them with the traveler who made them possible: you, after securing Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes.

Release Them. A dying archaeologist in Searing Gorge urges you to release those whom the power of the Suntara still drives to keep at their labor, though their bodies have given out. Everything hinges on the altar of Suntara, and a relic guarded by Twilight's Hammer must be placed upon it. Before collapsing, the archaeologist begs you to release them. Their bodies have given out, yet the Suntara's power drives them on to keep at their labor. The key, says the archaeologist, is the altar of Suntara.

Rellian Greenspyre. At Denalan's lakeside retreat in Teldrassil, you carry a timberling seed to Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus. The handoff brings news of trouble spreading through the World Tree's boughs. Denalan has studied the plants and elemental life around Lake Al'Ameth. After gathering seeds from the local timberlings, he sends you to Darnassus with a sample for his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian is a druid who walks the Cenarion Enclave's terraces. He had shown interest in Denalan's research and hopes to grow a timberling of his own.

Rema Schneider. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider works from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is a human citizen who often helps local shopkeepers and artisans with trade deliveries. Rema Schneider manages daily trade from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. The shop stands just west of the stone bridge into Cathedral Square, along Stormwind's canals. Cloth and finished garments move between local craftsmen, and Rema relies on helpful couriers to carry supplies between workshops.

name.esES: Gotas que quedan del agua más pura
name.ptBR: Gotas Restantes da Mais Pura Água

text.enUS: Remaining Drops of Purest Water. Across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, shaman gather what Brine needs for a draught. Its last drops wait for a perilous journey. Brine prepares a water draught in the Barrens from water gathered across Kalimdor and Lordaeron. Part of it gives shaman vision of distant elements. The remaining drops are kept for a harder purpose. Shaman carry them to the coast of Silverpine Forest, near the Sepulcher, where the Brazier of Everfount stands. There, the drops are burned with the bracers of a fallen, tainted elemental. The pure water cuts through the undead plague’s corruption, calling an untainted water spirit to commune with the shaman and complete their communion with the element.

Remedy of Arugal. In Silverpine Forest, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks Arugal's spell to learn how his worgen magic works. Before taking Shadowfang Keep, Archmage Arugal sheltered at an abandoned wheat farm north of the river bridge in Silverpine Forest. He recorded his strange arts in spellbooks left among the farm tools and rotting floorboards. One scroll, the Remedy of Arugal, describes early methods and magical formulas from his experiments with the transmutations that cursed the local people.

name.ptBR: Lembre-se de que eu te amo

text.enUS: Remember That I Love You. "Remember That I Love You" begins with a torn, stained parchment discovered among the undead-stalked graves in the Ruins of Lordaeron. The letter tells the tragic tale of a lost child belonging to the Heartweaver family. Seeking answers requires carrying this fragile relic south to the orphanage in Stormwind City. Amid the blighted earth and shambling undead haunting the ruins of Capital City, survivors and scavengers occasionally stumble across reminders of the Third War's devastation. This torn, blood-stained bundle of parchment has barely survived the undead-trodden grounds of the graveyard. Mentioning a missing child of the Heartweaver lineage, it is a testament to lives shattered when Prince Arthas and the Scourge tore through the kingdom.

name.ptBR: Lembre-se de que eu te amo

text.enUS: Remember That I Love You. In Stormwind, a blood-stained letter is bound for Jeremy Heartweaver. He has left the orphanage for a new home with Avette Fellwood in Duskwood. Children at the Stormwind Orphanage have lost their families to war, hardship, and the chaos gripping the kingdom. Jeremy Heartweaver was one of them until Avette Fellwood adopted him. She took him to live in Duskwood, where the woods are gloomy and life brings peril and hard labor. The orphanage caretakers believed a home with a family offered him more than remaining in the city.

Remnants of War. Remnants of War tasks adventurers with recovering shattered shards of the necrotic focusing crystal blown off Naxxramas during its assault on the Undercity. Both the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn suffered heavy losses repelling the citadel, and gathering these dangerous fragments prevents Scourge cultists from reclaiming their dark magic. Not long ago, the dread citadel Naxxramas loomed directly over Tirisfal Glades, seeking to wipe out the Undercity and erase the Forsaken entirely. In a desperate defense, the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn fought back the floating fortress at great cost. During the clash, the immense necrotic focusing crystal mounted atop Naxxramas was destroyed, blasting fragments across the glades below.

Remtravel's Excavation. At Remtravel's Excavation, Prospector Remtravel's dig has broken into ancient ruins. Prospector Remtravel came to southern Darkshore seeking relics from the distant past. He established a large dig far from Auberdine's safety. As his team cut through ancient layers of earth, they uncovered Gravelflint troggs and hulking stone golems buried below. The creatures overran the quarry, scattering the miners. Remtravel now scrambles to recover his most promising finds.

Remulos. Keeper Remulos is a demigod son of Cenarius and the venerable protector of Moonglade. Alongside Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and Hamuul Runetotem, he helps guide the Cenarion Circle in the absence of his fallen father and the sleeping Malfurion Stormrage. Unlike Staghelm, Remulos prioritizes the broader balance of nature over night elven isolationism. Keeper Remulos is an immortal keeper of the grove, bearing the lower body of a great stag and the antlered torso of an ancient dryad-father. He watches over Moonglade, the sacred sanctuary of Azeroth's druids nestled north of Mount Hyjal. While Malfurion Stormrage remains trapped in the Emerald Dream, Remulos provides divine authority and counsel to the mortals of the Cenarion Circle. He remains deeply invested in healing Azeroth's scars, offering aid to druids pursuing their sacred rites around Lake Elune'ara.

Remy "Two Times". In Goldshire, Remy "Two Times" trades goods and pays for raw materials. He came from the Redridge Mountains and repeats the ends of his sentences. Remy "Two Times" trades from Goldshire, where he deals with travelers. He came west from the Redridge Mountains. When he speaks, he usually repeats the last words of each sentence twice. The odd habit gives him his nickname, but it does not keep him from seeking a profit in troubled Elwynn Forest.

Renato Gallina. In Stormwind's Trade District, Renato Gallina calls travelers toward his family's winery. Renato Gallina calls to passers-by among the Trade District stalls, proclaiming his family's vintages the finest in Stormwind. The Gallina family runs a winery along the Canals, and Renato promotes it with pamphlets. Travelers can bring one to his sister Suzetta at the shop for a free bottle of wine.

Render's Rock. Blackrock orcs hold Render's Rock above Redridge, near the pass to the Burning Steppes. From this cave, they prepare attacks on the valleys below. North of Lakeshire, Blackrock orcs guard a cave cut into the Redridge heights. The stronghold lies near the mountain pass leading to the Burning Steppes, where veteran orcs direct attacks against Redridge's defenders. Their guards make any attempt to enter perilous, whether to disrupt the orcs' supply lines or recover captives lost in the fighting.

Render's Valley. Blackrock orcs hold a small camp in the southeastern Redridge Mountains at Render's Valley. It threatens nearby travelers and keeps captives taken from surrounding lands. Render's Valley lies among rocky ridges southeast of Lake Everstill, where Blackrock orcs keep an auxiliary camp for their operations in Redridge. Unlike the fortified keeps and stone towers on the northern cliffs, this camp gathers around war tents, banners, and sentry posts. Its warriors are smaller in number and less armed than the clan's core forces, but they still raid local roads and harass travelers. Captured prisoners remain in crude cages under guard.

Rendered Spores. Across the Barrens, Rendered Spores are being rushed from Apothecary Helbrim to Thunder Bluff before they decay. Apothecary Zamah must stabilize the emulsion beneath the city. Apothecary Helbrim makes Rendered Spores from fungal spores gathered near the Barrens’ damp oases. He processes the strange spores into an active chemical emulsion, but it is unstable. After forty-five minutes, it breaks down and becomes useless for scientific study.

Renferrel's Findings. In Silverpine Forest, Renferrel's Findings carry research south to Tarren Mill. Apothecary Renferrel gathered the notes at the Sepulcher for Apothecary Lydon, who is helping brew the Forsaken's New Plague. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel records his work on the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society labours under direct orders from Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Dark Lady. Researchers scattered across Lordaeron must work together to achieve a breakthrough. Renferrel sends his findings south to Tarren Mill, where fellow researchers can build on his results.

Renzik "The Shiv". In Stormwind's Old Town, Renzik "The Shiv" directs SI:7's new rogue recruits. The goblin is Spymaster Mathias Shaw's trusted second-in-command, receiving promising agents sent from across the Alliance. Renzik keeps his past to himself. In Stormwind, he is known as a goblin who rose to become Spymaster Mathias Shaw's second-in-command in SI:7. He has little patience for pleasantries. When new recruits arrive, he asks whether they are ready to work or need a nap first.

Report Back to Fizzlebub. Kravel Koalbeard says the Fool's Stout worked great. He has put money on the next race, hoping the crew you made drunk wrecked their own car. You carry a note about the successful test to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay. This follows the pit crew you chose to make drunk. Kravel Koalbeard says the Fool's Stout worked great. He has put money on the next race, hoping the pit crew you made drunk wrecked their own car. One more job remains: take a note about the successful test to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay, who will want to hear of it. Kravel also hopes more of the stout can be had for future races.

name.deDE: Bericht über die Bruderschaft der Defias

text.enUS: Report on the Defias Brotherhood. At Stormwind Keep, a report on the Defias Brotherhood carries the findings of a long investigation to the royal court. City Architect Baros Alexston entrusts it to the adventurer who uncovered the conspiracy. City Architect Baros Alexston prepared a report for Stormwind's leaders after a long investigation into unrest in Westfall and nearby lands. He entrusted the document to the adventurer who unraveled the conspiracy. The report is carried to Stormwind Keep, where it is meant to accompany a personal audience about the conspirators' schemes and the danger they pose to the kingdom.

Report to Anastasia. Horde mages from across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms are called to the Undercity. Anastasia Hartwell has sensed an unknown magical disturbance there and needs capable spellcasters to investigate. Horde mages hear of trouble in the Undercity. Those studying atop the bluffs of Thunder Bluff, in the dusty heat of Durotar, or among the ruins of Lordaeron receive the same call if they have enough skill. The Undercity's mages have sensed an unexplained disturbance within their domain and need help investigating it.

Report to Captain Stoutfist. After the fighting at Dun Algaz, Report to Captain Stoutfist sends proven fighters into Menethil Harbor's keep. The harbor is an Alliance military post, where Valstag Ironjaw directs you to Captain Stoutfist as the Dragonmaw threat spreads across the Wetlands. Dwarven mountaineers have watched the narrow passes of Dun Algaz for years. The Dragonmaw clan's return reaches beyond Loch Modan, though, as the orcs push outward, raise encampments, and threaten the marshlands. Valstag Ironjaw knows that holding the pass is only the first step in protecting the road to Ironforge.

Report to Doren. After obtaining the patrol information, Corporal Sethman directs you back to Lieutenant Doren. Delivering these findings brings crucial military intelligence directly to the rebels' commander in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Corporal Sethman reminds you that Lieutenant Doren wants a direct report on the patrol information. You must bring what you learned back to Doren.

Report to Goldshire. Report to Goldshire marks an adventurer's formal transition from the sheltered grounds of Northshire Valley into the broader jurisdiction of Elwynn Forest. Bearing dispatches from Marshal McBride to Marshal Dughan, recruits are granted Acting Deputy Status amid growing regional neglect from Stormwind's nobility. Having proven their mettle against local troubles within Northshire Valley, recruits are officially released from Northshire's local guard by Marshal McBride. In recognition of their service, McBride prepares transfer papers directing them south past the border gates along the road into Goldshire, transferring their responsibilities to the wider expanse of Elwynn Forest.

Report to Gryan Stoutmantle. Westfall needs fighters, and Report to Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to answer the call. The crown leaves the outer farmlands to fend for themselves, so local defenders gather under Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Westfall calls for skilled fighters from across the river. Brigands, gnolls, and hostile harvest golems are driving the farmlands into chaos. With no royal battalions answering, local volunteers must defend the realm.

Report to Hadrec. Apothecary Renferrel sends you to Hadrec as the Scourge threat grows. After Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard investigate the Scourge presence in Lake Lordamere, High Executor Hadrec directs Silverpine's military preparations against Fenris Isle. Apothecary Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard have studied the danger posed by the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. But study alone cannot break the Scourge stronghold rising on Fenris Isle. Ravenclaw is binding the restless dead there, and Renferrel sees that alchemy and magic will not be enough. The Forsaken military must bring its steel and discipline to bear, so Renferrel sends you to the commander.

Report to Helgrum. Neeka Bloodscar has written a fresh report for Helgrum the Swift in Stonard, and asks you to carry it there. This follows your visit to Neeka at Kargath. Neeka Bloodscar has written a new report for Helgrum in Stonard and hands it to you. Neeka adds that anyone who calls themselves an outrunner must not lose the way, or fall to an enemy.

Report to Ironforge. Ironband’s report is bound for Ironforge from Thelsamar in Loch Modan. It carries news from the excavation site to Prospector Stormpike in the Assembly of Explorers, where the stalled dig and missing blastpowder need attention. The Explorers' League funds, supplies, and oversees archaeological expeditions across Khaz Modan. Prospector Ironband's dig in southern Loch Modan has run short of blasting supplies, and its overseers cannot simply requisition more nearby. At the Thelsamar inn, Jern Hornhelm entrusts you with Ironband's written report. You carry it over the mountain passes to Prospector Stormpike at the League's headquarters in Ironforge.

Report to Kadrak. At the Crossroads, Thork sends proven Horde fighters north to report to Kadrak. The orc holds a watch tower near the Ashenvale border and prepares recruits for the fighting ahead. The Crossroads faces quilboar, centaur, and local brigands, while the Horde looks north to Ashenvale's thick forests. Thork directs fighters who have proved themselves in the central Barrens to the northern border tower, where Kadrak is stationed.

Report to Kadrak. At Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip sends Horde warriors north to Kadrak's watch post. The dispatch carries them from defending Stonetalon's crags to the campaign in Ashenvale, where the Horde holds outposts at Splintertree Post and the Zoram Strand. Darn Talongrip watches the Horde's southern and mountain frontiers from Malaka'jin. The orc sees capable fighters passing through Stonetalon and directs them toward the northern Barrens watch tower. Ashenvale is the greater pressure point, where night elf sentinels clash with Warsong lumber gatherers. The Horde needs fighters there as the struggle over the forest continues.

name.frFR: Un rapport pour le Montagnard Rochegar

text.enUS: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Mountaineer Kadrell sends you north from Loch Modan to join Rockgar at Dun Algaz. Rockgar is organizing an expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands, along the pass between the dwarven homeland and the northern territories. Dun Algaz cuts through the northern ridge, linking Loch Modan with the marshy Wetlands. The fortified pass carries trade, messengers, and military detachments between Ironforge and Alliance settlements farther north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell watches travelers on the road and recruits hardy volunteers for the northern outposts.

Report to Orgnil. Master Gadrin sends word from Sen'jin Village to Razor Hill about the Burning Blade. This early Horde dispatch carries a warning of demonic corruption spreading through Durotar. Sen'jin Village faces its own troubles, especially Zalazane's treachery on the Echo Isles. Yet reports of the Burning Blade point to a danger far wider than the village's local woes. Demonic corruption was uncovered in the Valley of Trials, and Master Gadrin knows the threat cannot be met in isolation. He sends you north along the road to Razor Hill, where orc authorities watch over Durotar.

name.frFR: Faire un rapport au Village de Sen'jin

text.enUS: Report to Sen'jin Village. Zureetha Fargaze sends word from the Valley of Trials to Sen'jin Village. Burning Blade cultists have been active in the valley, and she asks young initiates to warn the Darkspear trolls. Master Gadrin tells them dark magic threatens the nearby Echo Isles. Young initiates leave the Valley of Trials after proving their combat mettle and recovering dark medallions from the Burning Blade Coven. Zureetha Fargaze sees that the demons in the sacred proving grounds are no isolated nuisance; they point to a blight spreading across Durotar. She sends the proven fighters east past the ravine's mouth, then south toward the coast, to warn the Darkspear tribe.

Report to Zor. Nazeer Bloodpike finds it strange that common soldiers were carrying the jeweled pendant Marg stole. Calling it a noble's piece, Nazeer sends you to Orgrimmar with it, to Zor Lonetree, who is well schooled in Alliance politics. Nazeer Bloodpike finds it strange that common soldiers held a pendant like this. Its owner may have been in disguise, or the soldiers may have stolen it themselves. Either way, Nazeer judges it a noble's pendant, and its true owner must be found if the mystery is to unravel. Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar knows a great deal about Alliance politics, and can say whether the pendant belongs to Stormwind's nobility.

Rescue OOX-09/HL!. After the beacon has stirred the fallen homing robot, Oglethorpe Obnoticus speaks from the robot itself. OOX-09/HL needs an open, safe place to begin its take-off, so it is to be escorted to the shoreline beyond Overlook Cliff, and then Oglethorpe waits in Booty Bay. Oglethorpe's voice crackles from the robot again. The machine needs an open, safe place to begin a lengthy take-off procedure, and the shoreline beyond Overlook Cliff will do nicely. Its built-in cloaking cannot be used yet, and Oglethorpe needs time to make it operational again.

Rescue OOX-17/TN!. The damaged homing robot OOX-17/TN speaks with Oglethorpe's voice. It needs an open, safe place for a lengthy take-off, and you are asked to see it safely to Steamwheedle Port, and then to find Oglethorpe Obnoticus in Booty Bay. Oglethorpe's voice crackles from the robot once more. The robot has built-in cloaking, but Oglethorpe needs time to make it operational again, so it must reach an open, safe place where its lengthy take-off procedure can begin. Steamwheedle Port is the spot Oglethorpe has in mind, and the trip gives the time needed to get things working. Your part is to escort the robot there safely.

Rescue OOX-22/FE!. After finding the homing robot OOX-22/FE in Feral Scar Vale, you hear the gnome's voice crackle from it once more. The robot is to be escorted to the Forgotten Coast dock, and afterwards Oglethorpe Obnoticus wants a word with you in Booty Bay. The gnome's voice says OOX-22/FE needs somewhere open and safe where a lengthy take-off can begin. The robot has built-in cloaking, but Oglethorpe Obnoticus needs time to make it work again. Oglethorpe suggests the Forgotten Coast dock, long enough for getting everything running, so the robot is to be walked there from where it stands.

Researching the Corruption. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper seeks corrupted brain stems from Blackfathom Deeps. Reports say blood elves across the sea are turning to demonic magic, and he hopes to learn from the naga and satyr before history repeats itself. The ruin of their ancient kin remains a living memory to night elves across Kalimdor. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne gave in to demonic energies and became horned satyrs or serpentine naga. Now the high elves call themselves blood elves and embrace dark magic. Gershala Nightwhisper sees the old disaster taking shape again.
Resonite Crystal. In Boulderslide Cavern, kobolds are digging frantically for Resonite Crystal. Their work has drawn Mor'rogal's concern at Sun Rock Retreat.

Rest and Relaxation. Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road. After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey.

Restabilization Cog. Outside Gnomeregan's irradiated ruins, leper gnomes still carry Restabilization Cogs. In Kharanos, tinkerers need the intact parts to build the Recombobulator, a machine meant to reverse leper mutation. Radiation flooded Gnomeregan in a failed attempt to wipe out the invading troggs. Countless gnomes became sick, hostile leper gnomes, driven from their home as exiles. Even in madness, they carry intricate gnomish machinery and fittings that can be salvaged. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket believe the terrible change can be undone. They need adventurers to recover parts from the afflicted outside Gnomeregan's gates and finish their prototype Recombobulation Device. Intact Restabilization Cogs will balance its inner combustion systems.

Resting in Pieces. On Fenris Isle, Resting in Pieces begins with Alaric's animated, severed head. He asks to be carried across Fenris Keep to an unmarked grave near the stables, where the rest of his remains lie. Alaric once served as Thule Ravenclaw's chief servant and personal bodyguard at Fenris Keep in Silverpine Forest. Thule was a powerful mage aligned with the Scourge. When the Plague of Undeath swept through the region, he promised his sorcery would shield Alaric from it. Instead, the ward trapped Alaric in endless agony and undeath, with his awareness intact in his severed parts.

Restocking the Larders. Restocking the Larders is a provisioning quest in the Shen'dar Highlands of Zephras. With escalating wilderness threats keeping villagers from foraging, an adventurer is enlisted to gather eggs and strider meat to sustain the settlement. As unrest and rising dangers spread across the Shen'dar Highlands, normal daily life on Zephras has grown increasingly fraught. Everyday villagers can no longer safely venture into the wilderness to forage or hunt, leaving communal food stores severely diminished. To keep the settlement fed, local cooks must turn to traveling adventurers with the strength and skill to brave the wild trails.

text.enUS: Restoring Fiery Flux Supplies via Heavy Leather. After What the Flux?, Master Smith Burninate turns to replenishing the dwindling supply of fiery flux in the Searing Gorge. Burninate wants incendosaur scales, heavy leather, and coal, and will take all you can offer. Master Smith Burninate has no time for idle talk. Fiery flux is running low, and Burninate asks for incendosaur scales, heavy leather, and coal: two scales, ten pieces of heavy leather, and coal. Burninate will take all that you can offer.

Burninate wants incendosaur scales, iron bars, and coal, and will take all you can offer. Master Smith Burninate has no time for idle talk. Fiery flux is running low, and Burninate asks for incendosaur scales, iron bars, and coal: two scales, four iron bars, and coal. Burninate will take all that you can offer.
