text.enUS: Restoring Fiery Flux Supplies via Kingsblood. After What the Flux?, Master Smith Burninate turns to replenishing the dwindling supply of fiery flux in the Searing Gorge. Burninate wants incendosaur scales, Kingsblood, and coal, and will take all you can offer. Master Smith Burninate has no time for idle talk. Fiery flux is running low, and Burninate asks for incendosaur scales, Kingsblood, and coal: two scales, four Kingsblood, and coal. Burninate will take all that you can offer.

Resupplying the Excavation. In Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm sends you after the slow powder wagon bound for Ironband's Excavation Site. The dwarves haul blastpowder south along the Loch's shore. Ironband's Excavation Site in southern Loch Modan needs blastpowder to break through hard rock. After the powder reaches Thelsamar, quartermaster Jern Hornhelm sends Huldar, Miran, and Saean south with heavy barrels. The cargo slows their pack team along the lakeside road, giving travelers in Thelsamar time to catch up and help along the way.

Rethban Caverns. Rethban Caverns wind through the northwestern cliffs of the Redridge Mountains. Aggressive Redridge gnolls infest this extensive cave system, the only source of uncommon Rethban ore. Deep in the northwestern mountains above Lake Everstill, Rethban Caverns shelter the local gnolls as a fortified redoubt. Their cunning leader, Ardo Dirtpaw, commands a pack that fiercely guards the twisting passages and chambers below. Wanderers who stray too close to the hillside entrance face attack.

Rethban Ore. Foreman Oslow sends you into Rethban Caverns in Redridge for a dark mineral the scribes of Northshire Abbey need for ink. It is too soft for strong weapons or armor, but its color makes it useful for their work. Scribes at Northshire Abbey prize Rethban Ore for its dark, flat color. Bart Rethban discovered the mineral, but it has little use at an armorer’s anvil. Smelted metal from the ore lacks the strength needed for sturdy weapons or plate. Its raw color instead makes a valued base for manuscript dyes.

Rethiel the Greenwarden. In the Wetlands, Rethiel the Greenwarden calls travelers to the Green Belt. He seeks help against threats that disturb the marsh's uneasy balance. Rethiel asks sympathetic travelers to ease the Wetlands' suffering. He urges them to hunt the destructive Mosshide gnolls that ravage wildlife and take the crude flints they use to burn the marsh's living trees. He also calls for the diseased fen creepers festering in the marsh waters to be thinned. Rethiel hopes these efforts will bring peace back to the wounded soil.

Retrieval for Mauren. In Stormwind, Collin Mauren asks travelers bound for Kalimdor to bring him rare basilisk scales. He wants scales from the Charred Vale in Stonetalon to grind into dust for his spellcraft. Collin Mauren, a wizard in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, listens to tales from wandering adventurers. He has heard that travelers are venturing deep into Kalimdor, where Stonetalon draws those seeking wild wyverns, unruly elementals, or deals and clashes with the Venture Company. Mauren is not after riches or glory. He wants to learn what rare natural wonders survive in the region's harshest corners.

Return of the Ring. You bring a golden ring from Gnomeregan's depths to its maker in Ironforge. You feed a grime-caked bauble into Gnomeregan's Sparklematic 5200, and the machine strips away years of irradiated grime. Beneath it lies a polished Brilliant Gold Ring, still humming with arcane power. Three initials, 'TdK', are neatly engraved inside the band beside Ironforge's hallmark seal.

name.ptBR: Ficar ou não ficar... eis a questão!

text.enUS: Return of the Ring. A ring from Gnomeregan bears Orgrimmar's seal and the letters NOG. Its trail leads to Nogg, a goblin engineer with a theory about the ruins. You clean a ring from Gnomeregan in the Sparklematic 5200. The machine strips away the filth and reveals Orgrimmar's official seal, a surge of magical power, and the partly legible letters NOG. Gnomeregan lies deep in Khaz Modan, an Alliance city far from the Horde capital. The ring may have been made in Kalimdor or carried there on a doomed expedition, but its seal points back to Orgrimmar.

Return the Book. Bethor Iceshard sends his enchanted message back to Gunther Arcanus on Brightwater Lake. The stolen spellbook may bring his old Kirin Tor companion into the Forsaken fold. Bethor Iceshard sends an arcane message to Gunther Arcanus through a stolen spellbook. Once Bethor learns the necromancer on Brightwater Lake is his old companion, he enchants the tome's pages. The spell leaves Bethor's own magical mark, showing he is active in Lordaeron and free of the Lich King's control.

Return the Comb. Madame Eva waits in Darkshire for the comb Blind Mary has returned. Its ghostly strands can be spun into Ghost Hair Thread. Blind Mary waits in a shack south of Darkshire, mourning her death and the change it brought. Madame Eva’s comb reminds her of mortal grooming, and deepens her sorrow. She sees only an apparition, a monster stripped of mortal grace, certain no one can love her again. In horror, she thrusts the comb and the ghostly hair tangled in its teeth back into your hands.

Return to Bellowfiz. Return to Bellowfiz is a short delivery quest in Dun Morogh where an adventurer brings a cask of local Evershine to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It concludes a local favor, rewarding the thirsty driver with a welcome drink. Return to Bellowfiz is an errand in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. After aiding with local hunting, an adventurer receives a freshly brewed cask of Evershine with instructions to carry it straight to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It is a straightforward favor that highlights the informal camaraderie and mutual support that keep the cold frontier running.

Return to Brock. You carry Brock Stoneseeker's missive to Ironforge and receive Honorary Picks for the return to Thelsamar. Gryth Thurden can take you across the mountains by gryphon. Gryth Thurden oversees Ironforge's gryphon flights from the city's central platform. The roosts link the mountain stronghold with settlements such as Loch Modan, carrying messages and trade between them. Before you can fly to Thelsamar, you need to have met its handler, Thorgrum Borrelson. Once that is done, Gryth can send you back with the picks.

Return to Corporal Kaleb. Krazek has mended the pot and added a second steam whistle, plus a new chopper in the base made to cut through leg bones. The pot now has to go back to Corporal Kaleb at the Rebel Camp. Krazek has finished with the pot you brought in. It now has one more steam whistle and a new chopper set into the bottom, able to cut through leg bones. Krazek calls it a guaranteed cook-pleaser and expects the owner to be happy with it. It must go back to Corporal Kaleb at the Rebel Camp.

Return to Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Return to Denalan carries Rellian's alarming news to the botanist studying corruption in Teldrassil. After examining the mossy tumors on timberlings, you head south to help Denalan with his discovery. Rellian Greenspyre studies the mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings when urgent word arrives from his colleague Denalan. At his camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan has finally isolated the cause of these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Rellian recognizes the gravity of this discovery and sends you south at once to lend a hand.

Return to Feathermoon Stronghold. Your search turned up a strange gazebo at the center of the Ruins of Solarsal. Now it is time to head back to Feathermoon Stronghold and tell General Shandris Feathermoon about it. General Shandris Feathermoon waits at Feathermoon Stronghold to hear about the strange gazebo you discovered in the heart of the ruins. Make your way back to the stronghold with your findings.

Return to Fel'Zerul. An exiled Atal'ai in the Hinterlands has looked over the artifacts brought to them and calls them harmless. They have darker worries about Jammal'an the Prophet, and Fel'zerul in Stonard is to hear them. The Atal'ai Exile once held Jammal'an the Prophet to be a worthy high priest. But the prophet's unyielding faith in the prophecy may doom the Atal'ai, if it has not done so already. Speaking up got the exile branded an infidel and driven out of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The artifacts you brought pose no harm. What frightens the exile is the chance that Jammal'an has found the right fetish enchantment for the summoning ritual, which would put the world in great peril. Fel'zerul in Stonard waits to hear what was learned.

Return to Jahan. You carry finished leather goods from Thunder Bluff back to Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads. The trip introduces travelers to the Horde’s wind rider routes between Mulgore and the Barrens, after they bring hides to Ahanu, the skinner in Thunder Bluff. Tal, the wind rider master on Thunder Bluff’s central mesa, arranges flights across central Kalimdor. For many travelers, this is their first ride on a trained wind rider. A rider can take you to another settlement once you have met its wind rider master, such as Devrak at the Crossroads. The beasts cross leagues that would otherwise mean a dangerous journey overland through the Red Rocks and northern Barrens.

Return to Jitters. At Raven Hill, you bring Jitters a meal from Chef Grual. The cakes finally satisfy the hermit's desperate hunger. Chef Grual cooks at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, where Duskwood's lack of livestock and sea life leaves him to use what the blighted forest provides. His specialty, Dusky Crab Cakes, contain no crab meat. Instead, Grual uses gooey legs from venom web spiders that creep through the wood. He calls it resourceful cooking; delicate stomachs may disagree.

Return to Kristoff. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Stormwind for a borrowed book to return. After a long search and a delay in Northshire, you bring The Stresses of Iron back to the Cathedral of Light. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Cathedral Square for The Stresses of Iron, a book on metallurgy. Its trail led from Stormwind Keep's Royal Library to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton was copying the text by hand. Paxton ran short of Rethban ore for the scribe's ink, so the work stalled. With the ore retrieved and the copy complete, you bring the original book back to Stormwind.

Return to Lewis. Dungar Longdrink sends armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Osric's Crate crosses Elwynn and Westfall by gryphon, carrying supplies to defenders under pressure. Westfall is slipping from the kingdom's grasp. Defias bandits, ravenous gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten the land. Overland supply routes face harassment, and roads are dangerous for solitary wagons. The flight master network offers a crucial lifeline. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, prepared a heavy crate of armor for the battered volunteers of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill.

Return to MacKinley. After the scare of the giblets, "Shaky" Phillipe hands you a pouch to carry to "Sea Wolf" MacKinley. Phillipe swears the debt was always meant to be paid and adds that there is no need to get rough. Phillipe presses a pouch of payment on you for Sea Wolf. Phillipe wants MacKinley told that the debt was always meant to be repaid, and swears to it. Phillipe puts it down to getting a little drunk and losing the way, and says MacKinley will understand and that there is no need to get rough.

Return to Marleth. Marleth waits in Brewnall Village for the Thunder Ale brought from Kharanos. You return with proof that her Scalder reached the Thunderbrew cellar. Marleth Barleybrew of Brewnall Village wants proof that her Scalder was slipped into the Kharanos cellar, where the distillers make Thunder Ale. You bring back a barrel of their brew, taken from beneath their noses. The prize proves the switch succeeded and gives Marleth a trophy from her rival.

Return to Narain. Dirge Quikcleave keeps his word and hands over the five-hundred-pound chicken. You carry it to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris. This comes after Dirge's Kickin' Chimaerok Chops. Dirge Quikcleave gives you the chicken he promised, saying he is a goblin of his word. He cannot imagine what a gnome would want with a bird that large, and grumbles that it must be to sleep in. From here you take it to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris.

Return to Nessa. You carry Laird's findings from Auberdine back to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. The journey is an introductory errand that teaches young travelers how to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. He has found stark differences between the fish caught off Darkshore and those near Teldrassil, and suspects the great World Tree changes the local marine life. You can return to Rut'theran Village by hiring a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or by boarding the regular ferry at Auberdine's pier.

Return to Onu. You carry a page from the Twilight Tome back to Onu in Darkshore. The scribbles are all you could bear to take from the cultists’ book. The Twilight Tome overwhelms anyone who tries to read it. Its words swim across the page, and its ornate scrollwork twists into grotesque figures. You tear out a single page of scribbles before the strain brings on vertigo.

Return to Podrig. At the Undercity, you receive a crate of weapons for the Sepulcher after delivering a dispatch to the capital. Forsaken bats carry you across Lordaeron to Deathguard Podrig. Deathguard Podrig's garrison at the Sepulcher needs a steady supply of weapons from the Undercity. In Silverpine Forest, its sentries face worgen, Dalaran remnants, and Scourge stragglers. Fresh armaments help the Forsaken hold the region and keep the outpost ready.

Return to Primal Torntusk. Elder Torntusk asks you to return to his mate, Primal Torntusk, at Revantusk Village and tell her that he is coming home. Elder Torntusk is free of his bindings, and he asks you to return to Revantusk Village. There you are to tell his mate, Primal Torntusk, that he is coming home.

Return to Quinn. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick waits for a draught that may let him travel again. Apothecary Renferrel sends you from the Sepulcher with the mixture, while Quinn remains wounded in dangerous country. After you gather wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel brews a restorative draught for Quinn Yorick at the Sepulcher. He hands it over without ceremony and returns to his secret alchemical research. You carry the mixture back into the wilderness.

Return to Rorian. Return to Rorian is a mission carrying urgent reports from the field back to Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After aiding Yala Windwatcher against encroaching forces, an adventurer is dispatched to inform Rorian the Dayseeker that the Al'Aketh cult has actively escalated their presence by disturbing the local wind spirits. Following the disruption dealt to the agitators harassing Zephras Isle, Yala Windwatcher stays behind to mop up remaining hostiles while tasking you with an essential duty: delivering intelligence. Thendal Grove needs to know that the mysterious Al'Aketh are no longer operating purely in the shadows.

Return to Sven. You carry Jitters' finished journal back to Sven Yorgen's camp near Westfall. Its pages may answer the questions that have haunted him since his family's murder. When Sven Yorgen's farm was attacked, Jitters fled into the woods, leaving an incomplete diary behind. Afraid of Sven's anger and haunted by what he had seen, Jitters hid deep in Duskwood. When you find him, he willingly gives you his completed journal. He hopes its full account of the attack will spare him from facing Sven in person.

Return to Thunder Bluff. Apothecary Lydon’s toxin is bound for Thunder Bluff, where Zamah awaits it. She needs the formula to make a device that can spread it against the Venture Company. Apothecary Lydon has made the toxin from the ingredients gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He wants to see it tested on living subjects, but the liquid needs a way to spread it. You carry the vial across the Great Sea to Mulgore, where Apothecary Zamah waits for it.

Return to Troyas. Daryn Lightwind hands over her book, Feralas: A History, and asks you to take care of it. It goes to Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold, who is surely eager for your return. With the Super Snapper FX behind you, Daryn Lightwind gives you her book and asks that you look after it. She urges you to hurry along, sure that Troyas is eager for your return. The book is bound for Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold.

Return to Vahlarriel. Dalinda Malem is ready to leave Thunder Axe Fortress. She thanks you for what you have done for her and her family, and says the time is yours to choose. You escort her out, then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer. Dalinda asks whether the time has come, and offers thanks for all you have done for her and her family, in case things do not go as hoped. If you are ready, nothing else keeps her here, and she will go when you judge the moment right. You escort her out of Thunder Axe Fortress and then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer in Desolace.

Return to Verner. You carry fifty freshly forged horseshoes from Goldshire back to Lakeshire. Smith Argus has finished the order, and Verner Osgood is waiting across the border in Redridge. Smith Argus has forged fifty horseshoes for Lakeshire, and you carry them east from Goldshire. Redridge faces supply shortages and gnoll attacks. The iron shoes help keep horses and draft animals working on its rugged mountain roads.

name.esES: Vuelve con el médico brujo Uzer'i

text.enUS: Return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i. With the shrunken head delivered in A Strange Request, Neeru Fireblade hands you the herbs and asks you to carry them to Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Feralas, along with word that Neeru is satisfied with the head. After A Strange Request, Neeru Fireblade gives you a pouch of herbs for Witch Doctor Uzer'i. You are also asked to tell Uzer'i that Neeru is satisfied with the shrunken head. The pouch is bound for Uzer'i in Feralas.

name.esES: El regreso a Las Tierras Devastadas

text.enUS: Return to the Blasted Lands. With newly forged weapons in hand, you are directed back from Stranglethorn Vale to the Blasted Lands. The spirit of the Fallen Hero of the Horde awaits your return to set you against the demon Razelikh. Following the completion of your enchanted armaments, Galvan the Ancient proclaims that the hour of redemption is at hand. You carry the newly crafted weapons back to the Blasted Lands, seeking out the Fallen Hero of the Horde. The ghostly warrior asks whether you are prepared to face Razelikh and his minions.

Return to the Crossroads.. Gryshka's reply is on its way from Orgrimmar to Zargh at the Crossroads. A wind rider carries it across the distance between Durotar and the Barrens. You carry Gryshka's written reply to Zargh after bringing her a parcel of prime meat in Orgrimmar. Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides a mount for the return to the Barrens. You have already met Devrak at the Crossroads, so the wyverns know the flight path. The ride crosses the desert sky and saves you the long march overland across the Southfury River.

name.esES: Vuelve a las Tierras del Interior

text.enUS: Return to the Hinterlands. Thadius Grimshade tells you where Sharpbeak is kept: in a cage on a high cliff, atop Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. Vile Priestess Hexx, high priestess of the Vilebranch trolls, has the key. You are to carry the news to Gryphon Master Talonaxe. Having done his part, Thadius wishes you fortune and tells you what he learned. Sharpbeak sits caged on a high cliff, atop Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. Vile Priestess Hexx, high priestess of the Vilebranch trolls, possesses the key to that cage. Take word of this to Gryphon Master Talonaxe.

Return to the Magistrate. At Brill, Magistrate Sevren receives a warning from the eastern frontier. Deathguard Linnea sends word that the Lich King's mindless servants still test the Forsaken borders. East of Tirisfal Glades, the road reaches the blighted ruins of the Western Plaguelands, where the Scourge holds sway. The Forsaken built the Bulwark to keep the undead from entering their homeland. Deathguard Linnea watches from a waystation behind the line, gathering reports from the eastern gate. She sends messengers west along the King's Road to Brill before enemy infiltrators can exploit gaps in the defenses.

Returning Home. In Goldshire, a novice night elf priest receives a call to return home. The novice has wandered as far as Elwynn Forest, where Priestess Josetta relays an urgent message from Darnassus: return to the Temple of the Moon and continue spiritual training under Priestess Alathea. Night elves are an unusual sight in Elwynn Forest, and a young acolyte among its human settlements draws attention. When you arrive in Goldshire, Priestess Josetta greets you warmly with news. A Sister of Elune has traveled across continents seeking you, bearing an urgent command from the Temple of the Moon. It is time to return to Kalimdor and advance your calling.

Returning Home. In Darnassus, Returning Home brings young night elf priests before the leaders of their faith. After proving themselves in Teldrassil’s wilds, they are summoned to the Temple of the Moon to meet Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Priests tending the wounded and cleansing corruption around Dolanaar draw the Sisterhood of Elune’s notice. Trainer Laurna Morninglight intercepts promising initiates with word that Priestess Alathea has asked to meet them. Aid to local settlements matters, but each devotee must also deepen their communion with the Moon Mother and answer the faith’s higher calling.

Returning Home. A summons reaches wandering night elf priests in Dun Morogh, calling them back to Darnassus. Maxan Anvol, the dwarven priest trainer, directs them to report to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon. In Kharanos, Maxan Anvol takes note of the night elf's fortitude amid Dun Morogh's bitter cold, far from Teldrassil's serene forests. The dwarven priest trainer brings urgent word: a priestess of Elune passed through looking for the elf, carrying orders from Darnassus that demand an immediate return.

Returning Home. In human lands, a night elf priest receives a summons to return to Teldrassil. Brother Joshua delivers the message from Priestess Alathea, who calls the young priest to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for advanced guidance in Elune’s mysteries. Night elf priests sometimes travel to human lands such as Stormwind to share spiritual fellowship with the Church of the Holy Light. Their deepest ties remain with the Sisterhood of Elune. Brother Joshua tells an acolyte that a night elf emissary has come searching for them. Their early travels are over, and their home temple calls them back for deeper training with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind’s inner circle.

Returning Home. Priestess Alathea calls promising night elf priests back to Darnassus. The summons brings them to the Temple of the Moon to be recognized by the Sisterhood of Elune and receive advanced guidance. A messenger from the Sisterhood reaches you while you visit Nara Meideros in Stormwind's Park. You have served your people abroad, and the order's leaders now require you in Darnassus. They have watched your spiritual growth and call you back for an evaluation and a rite of recognition. The journey marks your passage from a new initiate to an active servant of the Mother Moon.

Returning Home. Night elf priests in Ironforge are called back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. A Sisterhood emissary seeks out acolytes abroad and sends them to Priestess Alathea for urgent training and sacred duties. In Ironforge, night elf priests remain tied to the Sisterhood of Elune, though they are far from Teldrassil. Braenna Flintcrag, a dwarven priest trainer in the Mystic Ward, carries a message from a visiting night elf priestess. The messenger sought young disciples traveling abroad and said their mentors needed them back in the capital at once.

name.esES: La vuelta de la cartera perdida

text.enUS: Returning the Lost Satchel. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, the search for Maur Grimtotem ends with his satchel. You must carry it back to Rahauro on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Maur Grimtotem was slain by troggs in the fiery depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Even in death, his arms clung to his personal satchel. Freeing it from his grip is the only clue to why a member of the Grimtotem clan entered the volcanic caverns beneath Thrall's capital.

Revenge of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire prepares to strike back at the Bael Modan dwarves. After Prospector Khazgorm's death, he sends Horde allies into the fortress for volatile munitions to fuel his attack. Gann Stonespire knows Prospector Khazgorm's death only slowed the Bael Modan dig site. Dwarven work will resume, and another foreman will soon oversee the machines tearing through Gann's ancestral land. He refuses to watch the earth suffer more excavation. Instead, Gann plans to turn the invaders' demolitions gear against them and rupture their stronghold from within.

Revenge of Gann. At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ own plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for the fallen Stonespire tribe. At Bael Modan, the dwarven excavation sits atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors rely on a gyrocopter for their reach and military strength. It is stationed on a watchtower above the dig, where it surveys the surrounding Barrens and protects the dwarves’ supply lines. For Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

Rezlak. Along Durotar's roads south of Orgrimmar, Rezlak waits for help with his supply lines. The goblin entrepreneur belongs to the Tinkers' Union and hires travelers to recover missing supplies and drive off harpies. Rezlak waits beside the canyon road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. He represents the Tinkers' Union, a goblin syndicate focused on engineering, supply lines, and practical business. The factional tensions of Kalimdor matter little to him while trade runs smoothly. Dustwind harpies have raided his cargo caravans and made the routes unsafe. Rezlak remains at his post and hires passersby willing to earn a profit by recovering supplies and dealing with the harpies.

Rhahk'Zor. Deep in the Deadmines, Rhahk'Zor drives the work forward by force. As head foreman, he keeps Defias laborers and miners in line while they build Edwin VanCleef's underground fortress. The Defias Brotherhood has turned Moonbrook's abandoned gold mines into an underground fortress. Rhahk'Zor was appointed head foreman to coordinate the work. He oversees the excavation crews and laborers as they carve tunnels and build VanCleef's secret projects.

Rhapsody Shindigger. Gryphon Master Talonaxe tells of Rhapsody Shindigger, once the finest flyer at the aviary, who took so keenly to liquor that Rhapsody had to be let go. Talonaxe has heard that Rhapsody now keeps a brewing camp east of the aviary, in the Hinterlands. Talonaxe stresses that the dwarves of the aviary all love a good ale, but Rhapsody took to liquor the way a gryphon takes to the skies. No one could fly like Rhapsody, a damned shame as Talonaxe sees it. The first sign of trouble came when Rhapsody stumbled back from the trip with Brohann, and things went downhill fast. In the end Rhapsody had to be let go. The last word is that a brew camp now stands to the east of Aerie Peak.

name.esES: El cubata de Kalimdor de Rapsodio
name.zhCN: 拉普索迪的卡利姆多鸡尾酒

text.enUS: Rhapsody's Kalimdor Kocktail. Rhapsody Shindigger, found in the Hinterlands, will talk about what happened down in the swamp only if given something stiff to drink. A Kalimdor Kocktail needs Roc gizzards from Tanaris and Groddoc and Ironfur livers from Feralas. Rhapsody greets Brohann's messenger with a hiccup. The two of them had quite an adventure, and the tale of what happened down in the swamp, which was not a pretty scene, will only come out with something stiff to drink. Rhapsody has a recipe in mind, the Kalimdor Kocktail, and promises to tell everything once it is brewed.

Rhapsody's Tale. After Rhapsody Shindigger gets his Kalimdor Kocktail, he finally tells his tale of the flight with Brohann Caskbelly. He hands over an Atal'ai Tablet Fragment and asks that it be taken to Brohann in Stormwind. With the kocktail in him, Rhapsody Shindigger finally talks. Before the flight he drank a whole keg of stout, and Brohann followed him through the sky. What he kept from it is a troll souvenir, an Atal'ai Tablet Fragment, and he wants it taken to Brohann Caskbelly in Stormwind.

Rhinag. Among the rocks near Durotar's northwestern border, Rhinag waits, weakened by scorpids' venom. The Darkspear troll depends on passing travelers to find him a remedy in time. Rhinag shelters among the rocks near Durotar's northwestern border after a Venomtail Scorpid stung him. The poison has left the Darkspear troll weak and isolated. He needs a venomtail antidote, and his survival depends on whether a passing traveler can find one before the toxins take their toll.

Ride to Ironforge. You carry Brock Stoneseeker's list from Thelsamar to Golnir Bouldertoe at Ironforge's Great Forge. The names belong to Brock's top mining students. Young mountaineers and travelers often make their first gryphon flight between Thelsamar and Ironforge. Gryphon Master Thorgrum Borrelson handles the trip, carrying travelers over Dun Morogh's snowy ridges and into the mountain fortress.

Ride to Orgrimmar. A wind rider carries Horde travelers from the Crossroads to Orgrimmar. With Zargh’s fresh cuts of meat in hand, you fly to the capital’s Skytower and deliver them to Innkeeper Gryshka. Devrak sends trained wind riders between the Crossroads and Orgrimmar. The flight crosses the dry Barrens and reaches Durotar’s red cliffs, sparing travelers the hard journey on foot. From high above the dusty canyon trails, the wyverns carry messengers and travelers, along with dispatches and trade goods, straight to the capital.

name.esES: Un viaje a Cima del Trueno
name.ptBR: Voo para o Penhasco do Trovão

text.enUS: Ride to Thunder Bluff. You carry cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff by wind rider. The flight links the Barrens to the Horde capital above the plains. Devrak carries travelers over the Barrens on the back of a wind rider. For many, this is their first flight across Kalimdor. The wyverns link the young Horde's scattered settlements and spare travelers the ground roads, where quilboar and centaur packs roam.

Ride to the Undercity. A courier carries Podrig's weapons request from the Sepulcher to the Undercity. A dread bat bears the message over Silverpine Forest to the Forsaken capital. Karos Razok handles the dread bats at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. They carry messengers and supplies between the Forsaken capital and its frontline outposts. The roads below are dangerous, with hostile beasts, Moonrage worgen, and Scourge remnants. The bats give urgent military requests a swift route to the capital.

Ridgepoint Tower. Stormwind guards watch the eastern frontier from Ridgepoint Tower. They keep vigil over the perilous corridors, valleys, and roads leading into neighboring wilderness. At Ridgepoint Tower, the garrison watches the valleys and roads of eastern Elwynn. The tower stands on high ground, where Stormwind's authority reaches its eastern border and the wilds begin. Its guards keep watch over the routes before threats can reach the farms and settlements nearer Northshire and Goldshire.

Rilli Greasygob. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob is the specialist Wenikee Boltbucket seeks. She sends you there with a damaged samophlange, hoping his knowledge of its Venture Company origins can explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed the apparatus nearing collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone with knowledge of its design.

Rime's Wrath. Rime's Wrath is a quest focused on quelling a hazardous outbreak of minor ice elementals. Because methods to peacefully soothe the aggressive frost spirits were unknown, eliminating them became necessary to keep the area safe. Rime's Wrath involves dealing with a localized surge of minor ice elementals. These spirits of biting frost and cold have become an active danger in the area, necessitating swift intervention before their chill spreads further or harms passersby. Rather than a coordinated assault, the response is a containment measure against wild, hostile elemental manifestations.

Rime's Wrath. Following a rockslide, an unusually large elemental named Avala emerged and began triggering erratic weather swings and secondary landslides. An observer tasks adventurers with hunting down the elemental and claiming its core to secure the area. Defeating the creature restores stability to the mountain slopes and safeguards travelers from deadly winter perils. The disturbances began when a sudden rockslide destabilized the mountain pass, opening the way for elemental activity. Among the creatures that surfaced, one particular elemental stood out, towering over its kin in sheer size and raw power. Given the informal moniker "Avala" by the watchful questgiver, this potent entity is not merely an imposing presence—it directly fuels localized atmospheric turmoil and destabilizes the surrounding cliffs. Its presence poses an immediate peril to anyone attempting to navigate the area, as unstable earth and sudden winter chills make ordinary travel lethal.

Rin'ji is Trapped!. Rin'ji, a troll, has lost an axe and been captured in Quel'Danil Lodge, and begs for help to escape. Rin'ji knows that others may not like Rin'ji's kind, but promises something in return and mentions a secret hidden at the Overlook Cliffs. Rin'ji is a captive at Quel'Danil Lodge and badly frightened. The axe is gone, and Rin'ji begs any passer-by to help get away. Rin'ji knows many dislike Rin'ji's kind, but offers something for a kind soul who helps, and says a secret lies hidden at the Overlook Cliffs.

Rin'ji's Secret. After helping Rin'ji, you carry a tablet etched with Witherbark troll markings that nobody has yet read. Oran Snakewrithe, who studies the Witherbark, might decipher it, and lives in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Witherbark troll markings cover the tablet, and what Rin'ji's secret really is remains a mystery. It might be worth a great deal, or it might be worth nothing, because a Witherbark troll in trouble would probably do anything to get out of it.

Ring of Zoram. At Zoram, the ring of the city's rulers has surfaced again after millennia beneath the sea. The naga now hold it, and Talen seeks the key to an ancient statuette. Before the Well of Eternity collapsed, Zoram stood on Kalimdor's western coast as a jewel of the night elven empire. Its rulers wore the Ring of Zoram, whose inner band bears a strange code in the night elven language. The Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago, and the ring sank with the city beneath the tides. It lies beneath the waters of what is now the Zoram Strand.

Ringo. Ringo is an unfortunate goblin explorer who ventured up the blistering heights of Fire Plume Ridge in Un'Goro Crater. Overwhelmed by the volcano's stifling heat and noxious vapors, he collapsed inside a cave, desperate for someone to help him back down. His close friend Spraggle Frock remains worried sick back at Marshal's Refuge. While goblins are known for braving hazardous environments in search of wealth or oddities, Fire Plume Ridge proves harsh even by their standards. Towering in the center of Un'Goro Crater, the active volcano spews ash, magma, and boiling steam. Ringo climbed about halfway up the southern face before the suffocating heat finally proved too much for him. Leaving his belongings scattered just outside, he crawled into a cave to shelter from the sweltering atmosphere, completely incapacitated by heat exhaustion.

Ripped Missive. The Ripped Missive is a blood-spattered letter recovered from Haalien that sheds light on a brutal cultist assault against a druid den in Shadowgale Forest. Its contents expose the callous motives behind the slaughter and hint at dangerous subversion originating from within Valanaar. Tucked behind the bracer of Haalien, this torn and bloodstained document holds grim intelligence concerning the recent violence in Shadowgale Forest. Recovered after a fierce skirmish, the scrap of writing sheds light on the dark intentions of the cultists who fell upon the local druid den, offering vital clues for those seeking justice for the fallen.

Rise of the Silithid. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser urges you to carry the report on the insect threat to Gracina Spiritmight, a night elf scholar and historian in Darnassus. Fizzledowser wants the report to reach someone with working knowledge of such matters. Gracina Spiritmight is a night elf scholar who has spent a lot of time studying the life forms unique to Azeroth's ecology, and she is a historian too. Fizzledowser hopes she can help work out what the danger really is and, above all, how it might be halted. By Fizzledowser's last word, she was living in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.

Rise of the Silithid. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser hands you the report on the insect threat and urges you to take it to Orgrimmar, to a troll scholar named Zilzibin Drumlore. Fizzledowser wants the report in the hands of someone who has working knowledge of such matters. Zilzibin Drumlore is a troll scholar who has spent a lot of time studying the life forms unique to Azeroth's ecology, and is a historian besides. Fizzledowser hopes Zilzibin can work out what the danger really is and how it might be halted, and says all the help available will be needed. Zilzibin lives in a house on the Drag's second tier, in Orgrimmar.

Rise of the Silithid. General Shandris Feathermoon hands you a copy of Raschal's account of the infestation in southeastern Feralas. Darnassus is where the main report is filed, and she wants this copy to reach Gracina Spiritmight, a priestess of the Temple of the Moon who knows a great deal about such creatures. While the main report is filed in Darnassus, Shandris Feathermoon entrusts this copy to you. It is meant for Gracina Spiritmight, an associate of the Protectorate. She is a priestess, and her home is the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, and the General says her broad knowledge of such creatures, and her receiving the report, would benefit everyone. She dismisses you with good wishes and a prayer that Elune watch over all.

Rise, Obsidion!. After Release Them, a dying archaeologist gasps that it was all a trap, and begs you to kill the traitor for them and for Thorius. Both Lathoric the Black and Obsidion must die, and Curator Thorius in Ironforge wants proof of it. The archaeologist is barely able to speak. They say it was all a trap, ask for forgiveness, and plead for the traitor to be killed for them and for Thorius. Lathoric the Black and Obsidion must both fall, and Curator Thorius in Ironforge wants the head of one and the heart of the other.

Rising Spirit. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a ritual blessing drawn from Agamaggan's ancient power. Bring blood shards taken from his Bristleback rivals, and he strengthens your will and spirit. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth knows the geomancy and ancestral magic of the quilboar. He takes pride in his people's devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. To Mangletooth, an unbroken spirit carries a warrior onward when strength fails and defeat seems near.

Rite of Strength. At Camp Narache, young tauren face the Rite of Strength against Bristleback quilboar. They bring their belts to Chief Hawkwind to prove their courage and defend the tribe. Seer Graytongue calls young tauren to begin the Rites of the Earthmother with the Rite of Strength. Those who seek recognition from the tribal elders and acceptance in Thunder Bluff must face this duty. The trial tests whether an initiate can meet the tribe's mortal foes with courage and act to defend Red Cloud Mesa.

Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a pivotal coming-of-age trial within the Rites of the Earthmother, testing a young adventurer's spiritual maturity. Initiated by Baine Bloodhoof, the quest directs aspirants to seek counsel from the village seer, Zarlman Two-Moons. Undertaking this journey is essential for anyone seeking the blessings and respect of the elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff. For generations, the nomadic tauren have turned to the Earthmother to guide their people across the plains of Kalimdor. Now gathered within the safe borders of Mulgore, their spiritual traditions remain the cornerstone of their society. The Rite of Vision is one of the ancient trials known as the Rites of the Earthmother. While earlier trials test an initiate's physical strength and connection to the hunt, the Rite of Vision demands an inward journey, directing young tauren and honored allies to commune directly with the spirits.

Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a foundational spiritual trial undergone by young tauren stepping beyond the Red Cloud Mesa into greater Mulgore. To pierce the veil and receive guidance from ancestral spirits, initiates must gather natural reagents to brew the Water of the Seers under the watchful eye of Zarlman Two-Moons in Bloodhoof Village. Before any vision can be granted, the initiate must demonstrate an intimate understanding of the natural gifts found across Mulgore. Zarlman Two-Moons instructs the seeker to collect well stones found near the sacred communal water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath the roots of Mulgore's ancient trees. These natural elements are not merely physical objects; to the tauren, they hold the latent magic and lifeblood of the Earth Mother, ready to be channeled into ritual use.

Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is the spiritual climax of an ancient trial undertaken by young tauren in Bloodhoof Village. By drinking the sacred Water of the Seers beside the tribal bonfire, initiates summon a spectral guide to lead them toward their destiny. After gathering the necessary ritual herbs and passing the initial trials of faith, an initiate is granted the Water of the Seers by the village shaman, Zarlman Two-Moons. This potent draught must be ingested before the roaring tribal fire at the heart of Bloodhoof Village. When consumed with a focused and respectful mind, the sacred waters expand the drinker's perception beyond physical sight, bridging the veil between the material plane and the spiritual realm.

Rite of Wisdom. The Rite of Wisdom is the concluding trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young adventurers in Mulgore. After purifying their sight through the Rite of Vision, petitioners travel to the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks to commune with an Ancestral Spirit and receive the blessing of the dead. Having cleared their perception through the Rite of Vision, young protectors are directed east of Thunder Bluff toward Red Rocks. This ancient burial ground holds the physical remains and lingering spirits of those who fought and died to carve out a peaceful existence in Mulgore. Passing the trial requires approaching the resting grounds with proper reverence and communion, facing whatever territorial threats roam the hills to seek the counsel of the honored dead.

Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the beginning of an initiate's spiritual journey on Red Cloud Mesa. Directed by Chief Hawkwind, travelers seek out Seer Graytongue in the southern hills of Camp Narache. Undertaking these venerable ceremonies is considered a vital trial of passage for tauren coming of age. Upon the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind directs young tauren seeking to prove themselves to Seer Graytongue. Residing in the quiet hills directly south of Camp Narache, Graytongue oversees the spiritual beginnings of the youth. This simple journey marks the formal threshold between everyday camp life and the serious commitments demanded by tribal custom.

name.esES: Los ritos de la Madre Tierra

text.enUS: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the transition of a young tauren out of the secluded Red Cloud Mesa and into the wider plains of Mulgore. Having proven your mettle in Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you north to Bloodhoof Village with a carved totem to continue the ancient trials under Baine Bloodhoof. For generations, young tauren have tested their strength within the safe cradle of Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Completing the initial trials proves one has the discipline and resolve to survive, but the sacred Rites of the Earthmother require far more than surviving local wildlife. Chief Hawkwind recognizes when an initiate has outgrown the mesa's sheltered hunting grounds and must step into the broader community.

name.esES: Los ritos de la Madre Tierra

text.enUS: Rites of the Earthmother. This trial, set directly by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, tasks rising heroes with hunting down the great kodo beast Arra'chea across the plains of Mulgore. Though an initiate may have completed the traditional rites of passage, Cairne expects his people to continually reaffirm their strength, tracking, and devotion to the tribe. Returning with Arra'chea's horn proves an adventurer is ready to serve the wider Horde beyond the mesas. Reaching Thunder Bluff marks the end of simple youth for a tauren, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof does not let young hunters rest on their laurels. To Cairne, earning a place among the high bluffs is merely the beginning of one's responsibility to the United Tauren Tribes. Rather than sending initiates against petty pests, he demands proof of real fieldcraft: the tracking and clean harvest of one of Mulgore's most renowned wandering beasts.

Rivern Frostwind. Rivern Frostwind is a night elf riding instructor stationed high atop Frostsaber Rock in northern Winterspring. Accompanied by his frost tiger companion Glacier, he watches over the native wintersabers and trains riders deemed worthy by his order. Only the most dedicated champions of the Alliance are granted the honor of riding one of his prized mounts. Perched on the icy promontory of Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind oversees the breeding and stewardship of the legendary Winterspring frostsaber. While nightsabers roam the lush forests of Teldrassil and Ashenvale, their sub-arctic cousins are bred to endure the bitter cold of northern Kalimdor. Rivern acts as a gatekeeper for these majestic predators. He demands that outsiders prove their commitment to preserving the beasts—gathering fresh meat from the tundra, clearing out Winterfall furbolgs, and driving back rampaging frost giants—before he will even consider entrusting one of the sabers to them.
