text.enUS: Sarilus Foulborne's Head. Across the border from the Barrens, Sarilus Foulborne's Head reaches Ashenvale as proof of the sorcerer's death. The undead mage defiled Ashenvale's waters, and the Sentinels demanded his head.

Sarkoth. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua waits for help after Sarkoth's venom leaves him stranded. You have slain the scorpid that wounded him; now Gornek needs word at the Den so aid can reach the scout. Hana'zua, a Darkspear scout, lies stranded on the high bluffs of the Valley of Trials. Sarkoth's venom has left him too weak to descend the treacherous paths alone. You have avenged him by slaying the scorpid, but he still cannot cross the arid stones without help. A passing initiate must carry word down to the training encampment.

Sarkoth. On a southern plateau in the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth has left a young Darkspear hunter near death. Wounded beneath a tree, Hana'zua asks a passing warrior to kill the scorpid and bring back its mangled claw, so his last strike will count for something. In the Valley of Trials, the Horde tests aspiring warriors against Durotar's harsh desert. While hunting the valley's venomous creatures, young troll scout Hana'zua met a scorpid far larger and deadlier than the rest. He struck hard enough to mangle one pincer, but Sarkoth drove its tail into his chest. Now Hana'zua bleeds in the red dirt, fearing his life is near its end. He wants the beast dead before it can outlive him.

Sarkoth's Mangled Claw. Across the southern bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth's Mangled Claw bears the mark of a wounded hunter. Hana'zua's crushing blow scarred the scorpid's pincer before its venomous sting struck him down. Hana'zua, a young Darkspear troll, met Sarkoth while hunting in the Valley of Trials. The massive scorpid's venomous stinger pierced his chest, leaving him bleeding beneath a nearby tree. Before the blow landed, Hana'zua crushed the beast's pincer. Its severed, battered claw proves Sarkoth has been slain. For the wounded hunter, that scar on the beast is proof his desperate strike left its mark, and a last hold on his warrior's honor as venom courses through his veins.

Sarltooth's Talon. Above Whelgar's Excavation Site, Sarltooth's Talon marks the end of the raptor's attack. Ormer Ironbraid wants the claw as proof that the beast has been slain. Ormer Ironbraid watched from the ridge as raptors overran Whelgar's Excavation Site and butchered the dwarven expedition. He could not stop the slaughter. One massive raptor, Sarltooth, seemed to Ormer the likely pack leader. Seeking vengeance for his fallen kin, Ormer demanded the beast's death and one of its talons as proof. The claw marks the end of Sarltooth's reign over the ancient dwarven ruins.

Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah's spirit a chance at peace. Her silvery spinnerets come from the mighty spider who dwells in Teldrassil. Lady Sathrah was a venerable creature of Teldrassil, until creeping madness and corruption spread through the great tree's boughs and took hold of her. The Sisterhood of Elune asks you to bring back her silvery spinnerets as a consecrated offering, not a trophy. At the fountain in the Temple of the Moon, the remains are bathed in holy water. The rite washes away the taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind and frees her troubled soul. Her spirit then appears peacefully within the sanctuary, with the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice gives a fallen creature's spirit a final rite. You carry Lady Sathrah's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters, where the Priesthood seeks to cleanse her soul of corruption. Priestess A'moora asks you to perform a final rite after Lady Sathrah is slain. The great spider fell to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, which twisted her peaceful nature into mindless aggression. The Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence, not treat her death as a simple culling. You place her silvery spinnerets in the fountain at the heart of the Temple of the Moon. Its consecrated waters wash away the corruption and grant her release.

Satyr. Satyrs are twisted, caprine demons born from the curse of the Highborne sorcerer Xavius during the ancient War of the Ancients. Once night elves, they were warped by Sargeras into horned, hooved beasts dedicated to spreading fel corruption, tormenting their former kin, and furthering the Burning Legion's will. Across the wilds of Kalimdor, scattered satyr sects corrupt pristine woodlands, desecrate moonwells, and subvert vulnerable mortal cults. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the Highborne councilor Xavius failed to keep the Burning Legion's initial gateway stable against Malfurion Stormrage. Enraged by this blunder, Sargeras dismantled Xavius's spirit and rebuilt him as a punishment and tool: his torso retained elven features, but he gained wicked horns, taloned claws, a leonine tail, and the cloven lower body of a goat. Sent back into Zin-Azshari, Xavius gleefully passed his fel affliction to other power-hungry Highborne. Though Xavius was struck down, his demonic progeny survived, continually seeking to reproduce their kind by corrupting others.

Satyr Hooves. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek sends warriors north for Satyr Hooves. He needs their strange power to forge brutal gauntlets. Ula'elek sends you into Ashenvale's ancient woods to gather what his craft requires. Demonic corruption still clings to the satyr covens there, and he seeks more than iron and leather for armor meant to rival Kalimdor's fiercest forces.

Satyr Horns. In Ashenvale, Satyr Horns draw dryads seeking vengeance and traders bound for Ratchet. The horns come from satyrs whose corruption has taken root in the ancient forest. Ashenvale’s satyrs bear horns that mark their demonic corruption. At the Shrine of Aessina, the dryad Illiyana gathers them in grief and vengeance for her lost sister Anilia. Pixel, a traveling goblin resting at Splintertree Post, seeks them for trade. Demand for satyr horns has risen in Ratchet, where hunters can sell these remnants of slain demons.

Satyr Horns. At Splintertree Post, Pixel hires Horde adventurers to gather satyr horns for Ratchet. The traveling goblin sees a chance to trade them in the port town. Pixel, a traveling goblin, sees a chance to profit while resting at Splintertree Post. Satyr horns are in high demand in Ratchet, and Pixel wants them for the journey back south to the port town. Rather than risk facing the corrupted creatures, Pixel hires passing adventurers to bring back sixteen intact horns.

Satyr Slaying!. At the Shrine of Aessina, Illiyana asks Alliance champions to strike at the satyrs of Ashenvale. Grieving her sister Anilia, she seeks vengeance and asks you to bring back satyr horns as proof. Anilia's death has left Illiyana in grief at the Shrine of Aessina. Dryads are forest spirits bonded to nature, often playful and serene, and elusive to mortals. Anilia's brutal slaying shattered that calm for her sister. Illiyana now turns to Alliance travelers to strike down the demonic beasts responsible.

Satyrnaar. Satyrnaar lies in ruin under the Bleakheart satyrs in northeastern Ashenvale. The ancient night elf settlement sits beside the road from Splintertree Post toward Azshara, intact enough to be one of the forest’s easiest satyr strongholds to reach. You find Satyrnaar northeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of Forest Song, among Ashenvale’s three chief satyr settlements with Xavian and Night Run. Its elven buildings remain more intact than those deep in the wilderness, though tents now stand among the broken stone. The Bleakheart satyrs occupy the camp, making the trade road east toward Azshara dangerous for travelers. They have also allied with the Cult of the Dark Strand, whose soulgem lies among the corrupted stones.

Savage Coast. The Savage Coast is the rugged western shoreline of northern Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the southern border of Westfall down toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Prowled by river crocolisks, shore basilisks, and hostile troll tribes, the strand earns its brutal name with every tide. Running from the cliffs bordering Westfall south toward Grom'gol Base Camp, the Savage Coast marks the perilous western edge of northern Stranglethorn Vale. The sandy banks offer little hospitality: snapjaws, crocolisks, and stonestalkers roam freely among the tide pools and drift logs. Just inland lie territorial jungle troll encampments, making any casual walk along the beach a fight for survival. Offshore, the waters dip toward the submerged dangers of the Vile Reef, ensuring that danger lurks both on the sand and under the waves.

Savannah Lion Tusk. In the Barrens, Savannah Lion Tusks go from hunting trophies to ingredients in Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. The great cats roaming the Barrens carry sharp, heavy tusks. Prowlers, huntresses, prides ruled by patriarchs, and beasts like Humar the Pridelord all bear them. Travelers often take the teeth as proof of a successful hunt. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet uses the tusks with plainstrider kidneys and thunder lizard horns to recreate Chen Stormstout's famous namesake brew, a potent ale with a legendary kick few mortal gullets can withstand.

Save Techbot's Brain!. Tinkmaster Overspark sends Alliance adventurers into Gnomeregan for Techbot's memory core. The machine once aided researchers, but radiation and an electrical surge during the city's fall left its brain polarized and its behavior violent. Overspark hopes the core will help him reverse the damage and restore his creation. Before Gnomeregan fell, Techbot aided researchers with its many devices and vast technical knowledge. Tinkmaster Overspark designed the mechanical assistant, whose integrated gizmos made it a marvel of gnomish ingenuity. The trogg invasion brought chaos, and toxic radiation filled the city. A stray electrical surge jolted Techbot's delicate inner workings, polarizing its positronic brain into a volatile negatronic state.

Saving Sharpbeak. Gryphon Master Talonaxe sends you to the summit of Jintha'Alor, which stands in the heart of Vilebranch territory. Vile Priestess Hexx has the key to Sharpbeak's cage, and you are to take it from her and free the gryphon. Following Thadius Grimshade's divination and your report to Talonaxe, the way to rescue Sharpbeak is clear. Jintha'Alor stands in the heart of Vilebranch territory, and you are to fight your way to its summit. Vile Priestess Hexx holds the key to Sharpbeak's cage. Take it from her, then find the cage and save the gryphon.

Saving Yenniku. After obtaining the Mind's Eye, Kin'weelay crafts it into a specialized soul gem to rescue the young troll Yenniku from Zanzil the Outcast. The enchanted vessel is designed to stun Yenniku and capture his spirit, allowing him to be freed and carried back to Nimboya. Following the recovery of the Mind's Eye, Kin'weelay reshapes the potent relic into a magical soul gem. Its dual enchantment allows an adventurer to first stun Yenniku and then place the stone upon his head to capture his wayward spirit within. Once the boy's essence is contained inside the gem, it can safely be returned to his kin at Grom'gol Base Camp.

Scaber Stalk. In Darkshore, Barithras Moonshade seeks Scaber Stalks from a hidden cavern behind Cliffspring Falls. Scaber Stalks grow in a subterranean cave behind Cliffspring Falls, among the northeastern mountains of Darkshore. The pale mushrooms thrive in the damp, secluded cave network, far from ordinary forest growth. Their remote, hazardous home makes them rare to gather, and Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine commissions scouts to brave its darkness.

text.enUS: Scalding Mornbrew Delivery. Nori Pridedrift sends you across Coldridge Valley with hot mornbrew for Durnan Furcutter. The drink must reach Anvilmar before the mountain cold takes its heat. Nori Pridedrift has just sent a delivery to Grelin Whitebeard. Now he has no time to carry another fresh cup to Anvilmar before it freezes into slush. Rather than leave his customer waiting, Nori asks a swift traveler to brave the snow with the mornbrew.

Scale of Old Murk-Eye. On Westfall's coast, Old Murk-Eye terrorizes the shore. Captain Grayson, the ghost at Westfall Lighthouse, needs a scale from the murloc as proof of his death. Old Murk-Eye turned Westfall's coast into a killing ground. Captain Grayson, the ghost bound to Westfall Lighthouse, says the cunning murloc rallied weaker-minded murlocs to raid the shore. Murk-Eye drove away the keeper's family, leaving the beacon dark when Grayson's ship struck the rocks. When the family returned to relight the flame, Murk-Eye attacked again and slaughtered them. Grayson seeks a scale from the creature as proof that the shore is clear of its fiercest predator.

Scarab Dais. The Scarab Dais is an ancient raised platform situated northwest of the Scarab Wall in southern Silithus. It holds the legendary Scarab Gong, the ritual instrument tied directly to the magical wards sealing the qiraji empire within Ahn'Qiraj. Overlooking the shifting sands before the colossal barrier of the Scarab Wall, the Scarab Dais serves as the focal point for the seal placed upon Ahn'Qiraj a millennium ago. Upon this stone dais rests the Scarab Gong, a relic forged during the War of the Shifting Sands. According to ancient night elven history and the bronze dragonflight, striking this gong with the reconstructed Scepter of the Shifting Sands is the only means to shatter the magical barrier and breach the gates. Until that fateful moment arrives, the platform remains an ominous vigil over the sealed insectoid horrors slumbering beyond the wall.

Scarab Wall. The Scarab Wall is a colossal barricade at the southern border of Silithus, before the insectoid empire of Ahn'Qiraj. Conjured at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands, the barrier combined stone and bronze dragonflight sorcery to contain the ancient swarms. It stands as an imposing reminder of the terrible cost of that war. Spanning the desert from east to west, the Scarab Wall was raised a thousand years ago at the conclusion of the catastrophic War of the Shifting Sands. Pushed to the brink of annihilation by the qiraji, the night elf armies and their dragon allies forced the swarms back into their ancient kingdom. To contain them permanently, an immense rampart of desert stone was raised, crowned by a colossal magical barrier woven by the bronze dragonflight. The wall successfully severed the insectoid armies from Kalimdor, though the dread presence locked behind its stone remains palpable.

Scaring Shaky. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley can't stand unpaid gambling debts, and plenty of people owe him. First is "Shaky" Phillipe by the docks in Booty Bay, who still owes a good deal from last week's game. MacKinley's plan is a scare, using giblets from Elder Mistvale Gorillas. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley cannot abide gambling debts left unpaid, and many people owe. First among them is "Shaky" Phillipe, who is by the docks and whose debt from last week's game is large. The way to collect is to frighten Phillipe. You are sent out of town to hunt Elder Mistvale Gorillas and bring back a good haul of giblets for Phillipe. MacKinley wants it kept quiet that they came from an animal, so that Phillipe imagines the worst.

Scarlet Armband. In Deathknell, Scarlet Armbands mark the zealots pressing into Forsaken territory. Executor Arren demands them as proof that the newly risen have struck back. Scarlet Armbands mark the Scarlet Crusade's followers, from Initiates to fresh converts. The Crusade's red insignia warns newly risen Forsaken in Deathknell that danger waits close by. Crusaders make no distinction between the Scourge's mindless servants and the free-willed subjects of the Dark Lady. To them, every walking corpse must burn. Executor Arren gathers the armbands to confirm that enemy scouts southeast of Deathknell have died and that new Forsaken can defend their fledgling nation.

Scarlet Base Camp. Scarlet Base Camp is a fortified outpost on the eastern shore of Lake Mereldar in the Eastern Plaguelands, just west of Tyr's Hand. Its barricades mark an outer defensive position of the Scarlet Crusade. Perched on the eastern bank of Lake Mereldar, Scarlet Base Camp is a barricaded fortification just west of Tyr's Hand. It marks an outer position of the Scarlet Crusade in the blighted countryside.

Scarlet Basilica. The Scarlet Basilica is a grand cathedral standing at the heart of Tyr's Hand in the Eastern Plaguelands. It serves as the high seat of spiritual and military authority for the Scarlet Crusade in the east. Overseen by Crusader Lord Valdelmar, its halls represent the zealots' unyielding bastion against the Scourge. Rising prominently over the fortified enclave of Tyr's Hand, the Scarlet Basilica acts as the central cathedral and command hub for the Scarlet Crusade's operations in the Eastern Plaguelands. While the Scarlet Monastery far to the west in Tirisfal Glades serves as the order's spiritual heart, this basilica anchors their surviving territorial stronghold against the blighted horrors of Lordaeron. Guarded fiercely by elite crusaders, the cathedral houses Crusader Lord Valdelmar, who directs the local defense and zealously purges any outsiders who dare approach.

name.zhCN: 血色十字军指挥官莫格莱尼

text.enUS: Scarlet Commander Mograine. Scarlet Commander Mograine serves as the military leader garrisoned inside the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A zealous paladin of the Scarlet Crusade, he defends the chapel alongside High Inquisitor Whitemane. Both the Horde and Alliance target him to disrupt the zealots threatening Tirisfal Glades and the surrounding lands. Stationed within the grand Crusader's Chapel at the heart of the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine commands the standing garrison of the Scarlet Crusade. He wields the holy power of a paladin with ferocious dedication, relying on retribution, divine shields, and stunning blows to shatter any whom the Crusade deems corrupted or unclean.

Scarlet Crusade. Born from the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the Scarlet Crusade is a fanatical holy order obsessed with purging the undead from Lordaeron. Blighted by paranoia and radical zealotry, they view anyone outside their ranks as carriers of the plague and shoot outsiders on sight. From strongholds across Tirisfal Glades and the Plaguelands, their crimson banners wage a ruthless war against Scourge and living alike. When Prince Arthas betrayed Lordaeron and murdered King Terenas Menethil II, the Order of the Silver Hand was broken. Surviving paladins and priests rallied under leaders like Alexandros Mograine, Saidan Dathrohan, and General Abbendis to reclaim their ruined homeland. Reorganizing their forces at Hearthglen and Tyr's Hand, they swore to cleanse the undead scourge with holy fire. Yet as the war dragged on, tragedy and suspicion festered within their ranks. What began as a desperate resistance soon devolved into an unyielding, xenophobic crusade.

Scarlet Crusade Documents. At the Crusade's camp near Deathknell, a messenger carries Scarlet Crusade Documents through Tirisfal. The intercepted orders name field commanders and direct their forces, giving the Forsaken military leadership intelligence on Scarlet positions across the Glades. Meven Korgal carried the documents from the Crusade's encampment southeast of Deathknell. By order of the Highlord, they direct the captains of the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command. Captain Perrine must further fortify the southwest tower and gather information on the undead in Brill. Captain Vachon must crush undead movement near the northern tower, while Captain Melrose watches the borders of the Plaguelands. The orders name Scarlet field officers, their posts, and their duties across Tirisfal Glades.

Scarlet Insignia Ring. In Tirisfal Glades, Scarlet Insignia Rings mark the Crusade's members. In Brill, the Forsaken collect them as proof that another zealot has fallen. Every Scarlet Crusade fighter in Tirisfal Glades carries an insignia ring, from new neophytes and zealous friars to captains Melrache and Perrine. The Crusade's fiery sigil marks each ring, identifying members within an order consumed by paranoia. To outsiders, the rings identify Lordaeron's most fanatical human remnant.

Scarlet Monastery. Scarlet Monastery now shelters the fanatical Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Once a peaceful center of scholarship and worship for the Church of the Holy Light, it has become a fortified redoubt. Anyone approaching without red colors is treated as a carrier of the plague and executed on sight. Before the Third War, the Scarlet Monastery was a proud center of Lordaeron's priesthood. Its halls held theological studies and sacred archives, and paladins trained there. When the Scourge brought down the kingdom, surviving defenders held the site against the undead. Those survivors became the zealous Scarlet Crusade and fortified the cloister. Libraries, gardens, and the cathedral became parts of an armed stronghold.

Scarlet Monastery Armory. The Armory is the fortified martial wing of the Scarlet Monastery, dedicated to manufacturing weapons and training recruits for the Scarlet Crusade. Behind locked iron gates, ranks of zealous footmen and crusaders drill under the fierce command of Herod, the Scarlet Champion. Once part of a peaceful retreat for Lordaeron's priesthood, the monastery was completely overhauled following the Third War. The Armory now serves as the Crusade's primary forge, weapons depot, and combat proving ground. From the open training grounds to the deep weapon halls, ranks of Scarlet footmen, conjurers, and crusaders prepare relentlessly to purge the Scourge and anyone else they deem tainted. The wing remains locked away from the Grand Vestibule, accessible only to those carrying the Scarlet Key found in the neighboring Library.

Scarlet Monastery Cathedral. The Cathedral is the spiritual and military heart of the Scarlet Monastery, housing the Crusade's inner sanctum. Once a serene hall of worship for Lordaeron's priesthood, it now serves as the command seat for High Inquisitor Whitemane and Scarlet Commander Mograine, guarded by the Crusade's most devoted zealots. Once a peaceful center of enlightenment and prayer for the priesthood of Lordaeron, the Cathedral fell into madness in the wake of the Third War. Following the fall of the kingdom to the Scourge, surviving zealots transformed the complex into a fortress of unyielding hatred. Beyond the manicured cloister of the Chapel Gardens lies the grand Crusader's Chapel, where priests and warriors gather in devotion to their crusade. They view all outsiders—regardless of race or faction—as carriers of the undead plague who must be cleansed by blade and holy fire.

Scarlet Monastery Graveyard. The Scarlet Monastery Graveyard is the burial wing of the grand religious complex in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Once a serene resting place for Lordaeron's clergy and nobility, it has fallen into chilling neglect, overrun by lingering undead and the corrupted magic of the skeletal Bloodmage Thalnos. Before the Third War, this cloistered cemetery served as the peaceful burial ground for the priesthood of Lordaeron. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the undead, their fanatical vigilance failed to cleanse their own crypts. Today, the Graveyard is neglected and deeply haunted. Lingering spirits, restless corpses, and shambling horrors wander the Chamber of Atonement and the mist-covered Forlorn Cloister. Rather than hallowed rest, the dead have found endless torment beneath the crusade's uncaring gaze.

Scarlet Monastery Library. The Library is the eastern wing of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades, once dedicated to holy scholarship and Lordaeron's priesthood. Now guarded by battle hounds and zealots, it houses ancient archives and rare tomes fiercely coveted by scholars and mages from both factions. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a center for learning and enlightenment for Lordaeron's priesthood. The eastern cloisters housed vast archives of religious thought, historical records, and arcane treatises. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the Scourge, they retained these repositories, turning the quiet halls into an armed redoubt. Today, beastmasters run tracking hounds through the courtyards while battle-mages patrol the shelves, guarding historic volumes like the Compendium of the Fallen and ancient research on the Titans against outsiders.

Scarlet Raven Tavern. In Darkshire, the Scarlet Raven Tavern is the town’s primary inn and social center. Tavernkeep Smitts welcomes beleaguered locals, passing adventurers, and frightened travelers seeking shelter from the horrors beyond town. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, the hearth burns in the heart of Darkshire as eternal dusk hangs over the forest. Years ago, it was a busy stop where Marshal Haggard and the Stormwind Guard shared pints after patrols. Since then, business has withered alongside the town’s security. Tavernkeep Smitts tends the bar for a somber, anxious crowd huddled against cold and fear. The inn remains a crossroads for rumors and a starting point for travelers seeking answers to the dark phenomena consuming the region.

name.frFR: Poste de garde de la Croisade

text.enUS: Scarlet Watch Post. In northeastern Tirisfal Glades, Scarlet Watch Post guards the rocky hills just north of the Scarlet Monastery. Its garrison watches the monastery’s northern flank for attacks. Scarlet Watch Post watches the northern cliffs behind the Scarlet Monastery. The southern road to the monastery gate is busy and fortified, but the rugged cliffs along Tirisfal’s northern coast offer infiltrators a back route. The Scarlet Crusade built this stone tower to guard that blind spot. It is one of several Crusader outposts scattered across Tirisfal Glades. Captain Melrache commands a mixed, devout force of Neophytes, Vanguards, and Friars. They keep watch over the cliffs so neither the Scourge nor the Forsaken can surprise the order from behind.

Scavenged Goods. Around Deathknell, Forsaken gather Scavenged Goods from equipment boxes. Newly risen undead rely on these discarded supplies to arm and clothe the recruits who follow. New Forsaken rise in Deathknell's graveyard with little more than rotting burial shrouds. Nearby settlements and kingdoms offer the undead no aid, so they must salvage what they need. Deathguard Saltain gathers discarded weapons, tools, and garments from supply crates across the village, then gives them to the next recruits to rise.

Scavenger Paw. In Deathknell, Scavenger Paw comes from the young, ragged wolves roaming the hills. Newly awakened Forsaken gather the severed paws for local caretakers to stitch into crude protective gear. Deathknell's newly returned Forsaken have little to spare. The Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade press against Tirisfal, so every scrap of hide and bone goes to practical use. Novice Elreth assists Shadow Priest Sarvis and gathers paws from scavenger wolves, along with bat wings. She uses them to make serviceable garments and armor for Forsaken who have just risen from their graves, still disoriented by their return.

Scavenging Deathknell. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken gather supplies for the recruits rising from nearby graves. Deathguard Saltain sends them to search the blighted settlement for abandoned boxes and crates, where the Forsaken must find what they need to survive. Newly raised Forsaken wake in Deathknell with little to call their own. Deathguard Saltain sends them to gather what the recruits still climbing from their graves need: clothing and arms. The Forsaken must salvage supplies to outfit those newly risen, with every usable piece put to work.

Sceptre of Light. Azore Aldamort has heard that the Burning Blade of Thunder Axe Fortress, to the east, now hold the Sceptre of Light, which word says they obtained from the naga. Legend says it could sink whole cities beneath the great seas, and Azore will not let the Burning Blade keep such power. You are asked to bring it back to Ethel Rethor. Word has it that the naga's Sceptre of Light has come into the hands of the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress. Legend says it can sink whole cities beneath the great seas. Azore Aldamort holds that the Burning Blade cannot be allowed such power.

Scholomance. Hidden deep within the crypts beneath Caer Darrow, Scholomance is the Scourge's premier academy of dark arts and necromancy. Here, mortals and undead alike study the Plague of Undeath and fleshcrafting under the sadistic guidance of Darkmaster Gandling and the watchful gaze of the lich Ras Frostwhisper. Before the Third War, Caer Darrow was the proud seat of House Barov, a wealthy aristocratic dynasty holding vast lands across Lordaeron, including Brill, Tarren Mill, and Southshore. Fearing the loss of their wealth and mortality, the Barovs succumbed to Kel'Thuzad's seductive promises of eternal life. They deeded their fortress and ancestral catacombs to the Cult of the Damned, who promptly repaid the nobles by butchering them and turning the sprawling crypts into a hidden necromantic training ground.

Scholomance (Classic). Scholomance is a subterranean academy of necromancy hidden in the crypts beneath Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands. Founded by Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned, it serves as the Scourge's premier training ground for mortal spellcasters seeking to master death. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, the rogue archmage Kel'Thuzad sought recruits for his Cult of the Damned. He found willing benefactors in the wealthy Barov family, lords of Caer Darrow, who traded their lands and crypts in exchange for promised immortality. Instead, the cult slaughtered them and raised them as monstrous undead. Beneath the ruined fortress, the Cult renovated the ancient Arathorian catacombs into an academy for the dark arts. Here, mortal acolytes study plaguecraft, soul binding, and flesh shaping away from watchful eyes, honing the foul magics that shattered Lordaeron.

Scooty. In Booty Bay, Scooty runs a teleport link to Gnomeregan from the busy pirate port. The goblin engineer calls himself a master of his craft and keeps transponders tied to an experimental pad in the fallen gnome city. His device gives Horde forces a perilous route into Dun Morogh. Scooty holds court among Booty Bay’s wharves and workshops as one of the Steamwheedle Cartel’s most ambitious tinkerers. While many goblins favor gunpowder and explosives, he has turned to moving matter across great distances. He calibrates transponders to keep a working link with a teleportation pad inside Gnomeregan. Horde forces rely heavily on his craft to reach the subterranean gnome stronghold without crossing dangerous Alliance territory.

Scorched Spider Fang. Across the Wetlands, Scorched Spider Fangs are taken from Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind needs fifty to strengthen mail for Alliance warriors. In Stormwind, blacksmith Furen Longbeard uses unusual methods to strengthen mail. He calls for fifty scorched fangs from the giant spiders of the Wetlands. Their dense, venomous, toughened substance reinforces the mail links as he tempers them.

Scourge. The Scourge is an apocalyptic army of undead monsters, necromancers, and enslaved spirits bound to the will of the Lich King. Originally created by the Burning Legion to destabilize Azeroth ahead of the Third War, the legion of walking corpses broke free from demonic control and shattered the kingdoms of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas. Today, they wage unending war from their arctic stronghold in Northrend and their corrupt dominion over the Plaguelands. The Scourge was born as an instrument of destruction forged by the Burning Legion. The demon lords bound the spirit of the fallen orc shaman Ner'zhul to the Frozen Throne in distant Northrend, fashioning him into the Lich King. With terrifying telepathic power, he was commanded to prepare Azeroth for conquest. The Lich King unleashed the Plague of Undeath southward into the unsuspecting human realm of Lordaeron, relying on the mortal traitors of the Cult of the Damned to poison grain supplies. Those who perished arose not as restful dead, but as twisted thralls entirely subservient to the Lich King's iron mind.

Scout Riell. At Sentinel Hill, Scout Riell watches Westfall from the watchtower roof. She serves the People's Militia, tracking the Defias Brotherhood and calling on travelers to bring back the outlaws' red silk bandanas. Scout Riell watches the plains from the stone tower at Sentinel Hill, where banditry and harvest golems threaten Westfall. Stormwind's royal army is absent, and the crown refuses aid, leaving the People's Militia to defend the region. From the tower roof, Riell tracks the Defias Brotherhood's movements and gathers proof of their crimes. She calls on passing travelers to take red silk bandanas from the bandits.

Screaming Gully. Screaming Gully is the first sprawling subterranean cavern encountered just beyond the entrance of the Wailing Caverns. Bathed in unnatural fungal glow and shallow waters, it serves as the outer redoubt for the corrupted Druids of the Fang and their mutated beasts. Stepping through the threshold of the Wailing Caverns leads directly into Screaming Gully, an echoing chasm where the wind groans through subterranean fissures. Far from the arid Barrens above, the gully is choked with damp overgrowth, humid mist, and aggressive wildlife twisted by the Emerald Nightmare. The Fanglord Lady Anacondra oversees the chamber, surrounded by acolytes of the Druids of the Fang and vicious deviate raptors, while ancient snapping turtles like Kresh patrol the shallow waterways below.

Screecher Spirits. Yeh'kinya in Steamwheedle Port wants the spirits of the vale screechers found in Feralas, kin to an ancient god. You are sent to southern and central Feralas with a bramble wand, and Yeh'kinya promises to say more of that god on your return. Yeh'kinya says the vale screechers of Feralas are kin to an ancient god, and that their spirits are linked to him. You are given a bramble wand and sent to southern and central Feralas. Waving the bramble over a fallen vale screecher coaxes its spirit out, and touching the spirit gathers its essence. Three spirits are wanted, and Yeh'kinya expects the bramble and the essence back.

Scroll of Messaging. In Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle has a plan for the Scroll of Messaging. The gnome engineer means to use its sending spell to trigger remote explosives. Gaxim Rustfizzle plans to turn a message into a blast at the Venture Company's logging operation. He will combine the scroll's transmission incantation with volatile NG-5 charges. The explosion is meant to distract the guards, giving operatives time to slip past and steal engineering schematics and confidential correspondence.

Scrounging. Sigrun Ironhew needs materials to build defenses and other necessities for the camp, and has noticed the ogres nearby carry plenty of scrap metal. Sigrun wants seven pieces of it. Sigrun finds it hard going without materials for defenses and other necessities, and the Prospector has been worrying about the state of the little camp. Sigrun wants to get to work soon, and needs scrap metal to do it.

Scuttle Coast. Between Razor Hill and Tiragarde Keep, wreckage from Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet litters Durotar’s eastern shore. The sunken ships make the Scuttle Coast a place where the Horde scavenges and remembers the recent naval war. Sunken warships line Durotar’s eastern edge, where the shore meets the Great Sea. During Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s invasion, the Kul Tiras fleet attacked the young nation of Durotar. Fierce battles with the Horde drove many human warships onto jagged shoals, where they broke apart. Barnacled timber, broken rigging, cargo barrels, and sunken ships still mark the coast. For the nearby encampments at Razor Hill, the wreckage recalls how close the Kul Tiran threat remains.

Sea Creature Bones. On Darkshore, Sea Creature Bones come from massive marine carcasses washed ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers skeletal samples for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where the cause of the strandings is under investigation. Massive sea creatures have begun flinging themselves onto Darkshore’s shallows, where they perish. Among them are giant threshers far larger than those native to the local waters. Night elves see the sudden increase as an ominous portent. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, sent by the Temple of the Moon to Auberdine, gathers bones from the beached creatures. Hippogryphs carry the specimens to Darnassus for close examination.

Sea Turtle Remains. Along Darkshore, giant sea turtles lie dead on the coast and beneath the waves. Their remains go to researchers in Auberdine, who study the growing number of strandings. Giant sea creatures are washing ashore along Darkshore, while others lie beneath the water near sunken wrecks. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde oversees the collection of bone fragments and tissue from the bodies. The Temple of the Moon in Darnassus urgently requests these samples. Its scholars and priestesses fear the creatures may be fleeing an unnatural disturbance in the waters around Teldrassil.

Sea of Cinders. The Sea of Cinders is an expanse of scorched, windblown terrain lying across the southern stretch of the Searing Gorge, directly north of Blackrock Mountain. Ravaged by elemental heat and relentless gusts, the flat ground constantly vents ash and embers, creating a choking wasteland where very little can endure. Stretching between the rocky cliffs of the Searing Gorge and the imposing bulk of Blackrock Mountain, the Sea of Cinders earns its name from the suffocating haze of particulate and burning grit that constantly sweeps its plains. When the Firelord Ragnaros was summoned into the mortal world centuries ago, the violent upheaval fractured the Redridge Mountains and transformed the surrounding landscape into an arid slag heap. The Sea of Cinders is among the most barren remnants of that cataclysm, an uninhabitable plain where the earth itself refuses to cool.

text.enUS: Sealed Description of Thredd's Visitor. Warden Thelwater seals a report about a visitor to Bazil Thredd in the Stormwind Stockade. The confidential account helps track a covert operative moving through Stormwind's political and criminal spheres. Prisoner Bazil Thredd spent years in the Stockade without a visitor. Then a quiet man began coming once or twice each week, carrying valid identification papers under the name Maelik. Warden Thelwater took note of the unusual visits and wrote down the man's appearance. He sealed the description so no meddling eyes could read it before proper investigators acted.

Sealed Envelope. Fizziks has sealed Venture Company secrets inside the Sealed Envelope for delivery to Sputtervalve in Ratchet. After the Venture Company cast goblin engineer Fizziks out of its logging operations in the Stonetalon Mountains, he smuggled out company secrets. The envelope holds internal manuals, operating procedures, and technical specifications. Among them are schematics for the Super Reaper 6000, a machine built for industrial clear-cutting.

Sealed Note to Elling. Jorgen sends a sealed dispatch through Stormwind to Elling Trias, the proprietor of Trias' Cheese. The fisherman’s message draws Trias into a quiet inquiry about a vanished diplomat. Jorgen gives a strict charge for the sealed note in Stormwind: place it in Elling Trias's hands and keep silent. The stakes leave no room for careless talk. Trias runs a cheese shop in the Trade District, where Jorgen's message brings the inquiry into the diplomat's disappearance to his counter.

text.enUS: Sealed Note to Watcher Backus. In Stormwind, Elling Trias sends a sealed note to Watcher Backus in Duskwood. He asks the Night Watch guard to report Defias activity near Darkshire. Elling Trias agrees to use his contacts to help search for the missing diplomat. He seals a note for Watcher Backus, a Night Watch guard stationed in Duskwood. Trias sends a traveler south through the forest to deliver it by hand. He hopes Backus will report any Defias seen near Darkshire.

Search for Incendicite. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear seeks samples of volatile incendicite ore from the Wetlands. He believes its explosive force could change dwarven artillery, and needs miners to reach a secluded cave and bring back the dangerous mineral. Incendicite, a rare and unstable mineral, has drawn the attention of siege engine pilots and mechanics at Steelgrill's Depot. Rich veins are rumored to lie in a cavern northwest of Algaz Gate, in the Wetlands. The ore is highly reactive and dangerous to handle. Careless miners have found it detonating in their faces.

Search for Tyranis. Dalinda Malem tells you the orcs slaughtered all their guards and servants before bringing her and Tyranis here. Tyranis tried to speak to them, and she cannot leave until she knows what has become of her brother. She asks you to find him and come back when his fate is known. Dalinda tells you that orcs killed every guard and servant of theirs before dragging her and Tyranis to this place. She expected to die at once, yet the orcs clearly had other designs. Tyranis tried talking to them, perhaps hoping his arcane learning would impress them, though she cannot say why. She will not escape until she knows his fate, so she asks you to find him and return when you do. He is in a building left of the fortress entrance.

name.deDE: Die Suche nach dem verloren gegangenen Ranzen
name.frFR: À la recherche de la sacoche perdue

text.enUS: Searching for the Lost Satchel. Rahauro sends you from Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise into Ragefire Chasm. Magatha Grimtotem seeks her lost emissary Maur and the unusual discovery he made among the troggs. Magatha Grimtotem hears on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise that her emissary, Maur Grimtotem, entered the cavern beneath Orgrimmar to study the troggs and try to parley with them. He never returned, and rumors say he found something unusual shortly before his death. While Warchief Thrall and his advisers focus on the Shadow Council presence in Ragefire Chasm, the Grimtotem clan follows its own interests.

Searing Collar. At Skull Rock in Durotar, Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars in their rites. The heated torcs burn their flesh as the cultists attune themselves to demonic power. The Burning Blade gathers for dark rites in Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs wear Searing Collars around their necks, enduring heat that brands and sears their skin. Margoz, a hermit, studies the cruel devices. He suspects the burning and the enchantments bound to the metal attune the wearers to demonic energies. What part do these collars play in the corruption spreading through orc society under the Horde’s nose?

Searing Coral. Along the Wetlands coast, Searing Coral is gathered from living iron coral beneath the sea. Tinkerers and smiths value the mineral-rich material for its unusual ability to endure heat and strengthen armor. Searing Coral grows in the cold sea south of Menethil Harbor. The living iron coral thrives in saltwater, yet yields mineral-rich material that withstands extreme heat. Harvesters pry the hardened growths loose through dangerous surf, with coastal predators nearby.

Searn Firewarder. In Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder guides Horde shamans toward the elements. Inside Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder guides shamans seeking the elements. Many Darkspear trolls commune with spirits through witch doctors and voodoo rituals. Searn guides initiates toward distant mentors and rites for the Call of Fire, Call of Water, and Call of Air, which teach them to commune with the elemental spirits of fire, water, and air. He stands among the Horde's high command in Orgrimmar.

Seasoned Wolf Kabobs. In Darkshire, Chef Grual prepares his signature dish at the Scarlet Raven Tavern. He asks you to hunt Duskwood wolves for meat while his herbs arrive from Stormwind City. Darkshire sits isolated among Duskwood's creeping horrors. Trade caravans rarely come, farming has collapsed, and undead lurk nearby, yet the town still needs food. Chef Grual cooks at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, turning dangerous forest wolves into hearty skewers. Local timber and soil cannot support delicate crops, so he depends on spices brought from the capital to make the gamey meat palatable.

Second War. The Second War was the continent-spanning clash across the Eastern Kingdoms between the Orcish Horde and the newly forged Alliance of Lordaeron. Sparked after the sack of Stormwind, the war devastated Khaz Modan and northern human realms before turning at the gates of Capital City. It ended in the destruction of the Dark Portal and the dispersal of the old Horde. Following the fall of Stormwind during the First War, Regent Anduin Lothar led human refugees north across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. King Terenas Menethil II convened the Council of Seven Nations, forging the Alliance of Lordaeron alongside the high elves of Quel'Thalas, the Bronzebeard dwarves of Ironforge, and the gnomes of Gnomeregan. Meanwhile, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer consolidated the Horde, forging alliances with forest troll tribes and the Steamwheedle Cartel while subjugating red dragons through the Dragonmaw clan to invade the northern continents.

Secure Crate. In the Barrens, a Secure Crate waits for a traveler to carry it to Ratchet. Potions and alchemical goods inside are bound for the Eastern Kingdoms. Couriers, caravans, and goblin ships carry trade between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. When a Barrens caravan misses its departure, travelers take fragile cargo like this Secure Crate down to the coast. It holds potions, alchemical goods, and reagents for associates across the Great Sea. The crate is sealed against the Barrens trails and the sea spray on its voyage.

Secure the Mountain. Secure the Mountain is an Alliance quest addressing the sudden surge of wendigos overrunning the Grizzled Den in Dun Morogh. Adventurers are sent into the infested cavern to locate an overeager dwarven scout named Cornelius and recover a critical report for Whitebeard. Dwarven scouts monitoring the frigid mountain slopes face trouble on two fronts. Aside from the ever-present Frostmane troll threat, the local wendigos have begun multiplying aggressively, abandoning their usual solitary hollows to pack into the Grizzled Den to the north. These savage beasts make traveling the crags perilous for patrols and couriers alike.

Secure the Mountain. Secure the Mountain is an Alliance quest originating in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. A local official compiling intelligence for Ironforge sends adventurers west of town to check on Mountaineer Gretchen after scouts investigating aggressive wendigos fail to report back. Tasked with compiling local military intelligence for the high seat of Ironforge, an official in Kharanos finds his routine correspondence interrupted. A mountaineer team sent to assess nearby wendigo activity has failed to return with updates. Rather than spelunking through icy caverns himself, the bureaucrat enlists capable travelers to venture just west of town and determine the scouts' status.

Secure the Mountain. Secure the Mountain is a scouting report delivered on behalf of Mountaineer Gretchen to Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. After an expedition into a nearby cave proves catastrophic, Gretchen determines the cavern is a lost cause and refuses to send any more scouts into the overrun death trap. The mission highlights the ongoing struggle of Ironforge's mountaineers to keep Dun Morogh safe amidst rising threats. Stationed out in the freezing peaks of Dun Morogh, Mountaineer Gretchen stands watch with orders to ensure the high passes remain safe. However, a recent foray into a nearby cavern reveals that the wilderness is far from pacified. Having assessed the situation, Gretchen concludes that the cave has become a complete death trap, overrun by hostile mongrels. Rather than risk further lives, she remains at her post on the slopes, determined to hold the line while dispatching an emissary to deliver her written assessment.

Securing the Lines. Near Razorwind Canyon, Rezlak needs the goblin supply routes through Durotar protected. Harpies in Drygulch Ravine keep intercepting and plundering caravans, so he hires help to drive them out. Dustwind harpies make travel through Durotar’s dry valleys dangerous. Rezlak watches over regional supply operations for his boss, Gazlowe. The harpies roosting in Drygulch Ravine raid caravans in Razorwind Canyon and seize shipments before they reach their destinations.

Seek Redemption!. In Dolanaar, you face the Council of the Forest's demand for atonement. Adventurers were duped into doing Zenn Foulhoof's dirty work, and now the council sends you to trick the satyr into eating corrupted fel cones. Just outside Dolanaar, solitary satyr Zenn Foulhoof uses deceit to make passersby do his bidding. Adventurers who unwittingly slaughtered nightsabers, strigid owls, and webwood spiders to satisfy his twisted appetites draw the Council of the Forest's sharp disapproval. The council will not accept harm to nature, especially from its own allies.

Seek out SI: 7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends new rogues toward SI: 7. A sealed package carried to Stormwind City brings them before Master Mathias Shaw, who leads the crown's covert intelligence network. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, rogue trainer Keryn Sylvius wastes no time praising newcomers. She thinks fresh initiates look more like cheese delivery hands than covert agents, yet gives them a sealed delivery for the capital. The trip tests their reliability as couriers and quietly vets scouts for wider service to the realm.

Seeking Refuge. Seeking Refuge is a Tirisfal Glades quest involving the rescue of Bareth Dawnstone, an emissary from Bandarion Keep held captive at Crusader's Outpost. His struggle highlights the emergence of an unconventional order devoted to the Holy Light despite severe prejudice from local zealots. Safely returning news of his escape to Brill secures vital ties for this fledgling sanctuary. Seeking Refuge recounts the perilous journey of Bareth Dawnstone, a messenger dispatched from the secluded monastery of Bandarion Keep. While en route to confer with Shari Stilwell in Brill, Bareth was intercepted and captured by zealous warriors at Crusader's Outpost. Despite the hatred directed at his undead state, Bareth remains steadfast in his devotion to the Light, yearning only to escape his tormentors and ensure his message reaches its destination.

Seeking Strahad. Warlocks leave Stormwind City for Ratchet, where Strahad Farsan can teach them to summon felhunters. Beneath the goblin port, his knowledge offers a path into more dangerous demon summoning. Gakin the Darkbinder sends you from Stormwind to seek help with summoning a felhunter. He guides warlocks in the Slaughtered Lamb, below the Mage Quarter, but the rites call for knowledge beyond what he can offer there. Your journey carries you across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where another warlock may know the way.

Seeking Strahad. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye sends warlocks south to Ratchet for deeper training. There, a human summoner teaches arts beyond the reach of basic summoning. Gan'rul Bloodeye trains young warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow, where they learn to command the Nether. When an apprentice outgrows that teaching, Gan'rul points them beyond the city walls. More volatile beings call for instruction from someone with deeper mastery of dark arcana.

Seeking Strahad. Carendin Halgar sends Horde warlocks across the Great Sea to seek Strahad Farsan. Above Ratchet, a human sorcerer offers a path beyond basic shadowcraft toward the difficult art of summoning a felhunter. Carendin Halgar, a Forsaken warlock trainer in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, knows when an initiate has outgrown basic instruction. He sends his pupils beyond Lordaeron's ruins to find Strahad Farsan. Halgar warns that Strahad is a living human, but no weakling, and says not to treat him as an enemy. For warlocks, the pursuit of demonic mastery often crosses racial and factional lines.

text.enUS: Seeking Wisdom. In Stormwind, Sven Yorgen seeks holy counsel for Duskwood. He sends Jitters' Completed Journal to Bishop Farthing at the Cathedral of Light, hoping the bishop can reveal how to destroy Morbent Fel's shield. Duskwood suffers beneath lingering curses and ravenous undead, while Stormwind's royal court grows indifferent. Sven Yorgen, a broken-hearted survivor at a camp near the borders, knows ordinary strength cannot pierce Morbent Fel's dark wards. With Jitters' assembled journal, Sven asks you to seek the church's counsel. The road north leads to the Cathedral of Light.

name.frFR: À la recherche de la gemme de Kor

text.enUS: Seeking the Kor Gem. You cross the sea to Darkshore in search of a Kor gem for Jordan Stilwell. Thundris Windweaver sends an Alliance paladin initiate into Blackfathom Deeps, where naga corrupt the potent stone. Jordan needs it for his craft. Paladins in training cross continental borders to Darkshore for materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell. In Auberdine, the night elf Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Night elves keep their distance, and some fallen humans have betrayed their trust, yet Thundris still believes paladins can follow a righteous path. He tells them where ancient gems can be found.

Seer Graytongue. On Red Cloud Mesa, Seer Graytongue guides young tauren through their first tribal trials. Near Camp Narache in Mulgore, he teaches them to honor the Earthmother before they enter the wider world. Young tauren braves and spellweavers find Seer Graytongue atop Red Cloud Mesa. From there, he guides those setting out from Camp Narache through sacred steps, including the Rites of the Earthmother. Their trials test resolve against Mulgore’s harsh plains and dangerous beasts. Through them, Graytongue teaches honor, patience, and reverence, virtues every tauren carries into adulthood.

Seer Ravenfeather. At Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa, Seer Ravenfeather guides young tauren in the ways of the spirits and Mulgore's land. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather teaches young tauren who have chosen the shamanic path. Red Cloud Mesa is a sacred proving ground, and she prepares new practitioners for their duties before they venture farther into Mulgore. She teaches the rites that let them commune with elemental forces and honor the Earth Mother.

Seer Wiserunner. At his cave northwest of Bloodhoof Village, Seer Wiserunner guides young tauren through sacred rites. The respected elder helps them seek spiritual wisdom in Mulgore. Seer Wiserunner guides young tauren through their ancestral rites. After their first trials of strength and vision, they seek his counsel. He interprets visions of the Earth Mother and teaches them how to honor their forebears. His wisdom helps bind Mulgore’s scattered nomadic tribes into one community.

Seereth Stonebreak. Near Greatwood Vale, Seereth Stonebreak watches the land's disturbances. The orc shaman camps on the border of the Stonetalon Mountains and the Barrens, guiding travelers against environmental ruin, rogue machines, and rising tensions in Kalimdor. Seereth Stonebreak watches over Horde lands from her camp near Greatwood Vale. An orc shaman, she follows the harmony of the elements and protects the territories of the Horde. The land's spirits cried out against goblin plunder, and the Horde sent her to Stonetalon. There, she watches the landscape and guides travelers against dangers threatening the wild frontier.

Selling Fish. Dockmaster Baren pays travelers to bring in spotted sunfish from Lake Everstill. The fish are a Lakeshire staple, but murlocs along the shore make them dangerous to gather. Spotted sunfish are a delicate catch prized across the lands around Lake Everstill. Townspeople and passing merchants keep demand high, yet Lakeshire's supplies often run thin despite the fish below the surface. Local threats stretch the town's strength, so even trade in basic goods depends on travelers.

Senani Thunderheart. At Splintertree Post in Ashenvale, Senani Thunderheart puts hunters to the test. She serves the Horde by sending travelers after the forest’s fiercest predators, a trial of skill that also thins the beasts near Horde territory. At Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart carries on the tauren hunting traditions in Ashenvale. Far from Mulgore’s open plains, she sends Horde hunters against the forest’s great beasts to test their tracking and fighting skill. For Senani, the hunt is an honorable challenge and a way to survive in a wild, contested land.

Senator Mehr Stonehallow. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Senator Mehr Stonehallow faces a trogg infestation. The Ironforge politician and Explorers' League member has come to the front lines to oversee its containment, enlisting eager adventurers to cull the beasts before they overrun the quarry. Senator Mehr Stonehallow has left Ironforge's Senate halls for Gol'Bolar Quarry. A dwarf devoted to governance and the Explorers' League's historical pursuits, he knows the dangers facing the realm. When Rockjaw troggs clawed their way from the deep rock, Stonehallow traveled to the mining pit himself. He believes debate alone will not protect the workers, so he offers bounties to capable travelers who can drive back the aggressive troggs and reclaim the quarry.

Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser is a goblin researcher working from Gadgetzan in Tanaris. He investigates disruptions around the local water supply and sends adventurers to look into the disappearance of Scrimshank.

Senir Whitebeard. Outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard watches Dun Morogh's growing threats. The Senate of Ironforge sent him to assess the Frostmane troll offensive and report their movements to the dwarven leadership. Senir Whitebeard carries the Senate of Ironforge's authority into Kharanos. The city's halls are watching the growing unrest in Dun Morogh, and Senir links the scouts on its snowy frontier with the lawmakers behind Ironforge's stone gates.

Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard sends you east from Coldridge Valley with his report for Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. The tunnel out is overrun by troggs, and Mountaineer Thalos guards the way. Grelin Whitebeard has documented troll activity around Coldridge Valley. After Frostmane trolls stole his journal and it was recovered, he decided the report was too important for an inexperienced apprentice to carry. He sends you directly to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, who works outside the valley in Kharanos.

Senir's Observations. Grelin Whitebeard's report now travels from Coldridge Valley to Senir in Kharanos. Its findings carry news of the valley's threats beyond the sheltered training grounds of Anvilmar. Grelin Whitebeard has recovered his stolen journal from the Frostmane trolls and prepared a report on the valley's threats for his brother Senir. Mountaineer Thalos guards the gate out of Coldridge Valley and gives the dispatch to travelers passing through. The route leads through a mountain tunnel recently overrun by violent troggs that ambush anyone crossing. Beyond it, the main road runs through central Dun Morogh to Kharanos.

Senir's Report. In the cold foothills of Dun Morogh, Senir Whitebeard sends word of the Frostmane trolls to Ironforge. His report carries findings gathered under King Magni Bronzebeard’s directive for Senator Barin Redstone. Senir Whitebeard’s report gathers mountaineer observations from scouting against Frostmane trolls in Dun Morogh’s crags. Stationed in the cold foothills, Senir includes his brother Grelin’s account of Coldridge Valley, where Grelin acted under King Magni Bronzebeard’s sanction. Senir sends the findings to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge’s High Seat and advises couriers to leave out how much outside help he needed to compile them.

Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak. At Oracle Glade on Teldrassil, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak watches over the northern groves. She guards the enchanted waters and woodland wildlife. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak keeps watch in Oracle Glade, one of Teldrassil's most secluded reaches. Far from Darnassus, she serves the Sentinel army among ancient trees and ethereal springs, guarding the wilderness from disturbance.

Sentinel Aynasha. Along Darkshore’s wild borders, Sentinel Aynasha scouts the dangers threatening night elven lands. She watches enemy movements and carries urgent intelligence across the frontier. Sentinel Aynasha scouts and fights with the Sentinels where night elven lands meet hostile incursions. She carries urgent messages across rough country and watches for enemy patrols. Her skill with a bow and her knowledge of survival help her cross contested ground.

Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze. In Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze watches over the misty coast of Darkshore. From the upper floor of a lodge across the bridge, she tracks growing threats and directs travelers toward dangers in the wilderness. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze coordinates Auberdine's defenses from across the bridge. While other Sentinels patrol Darkshore's coast and woodlands, she watches from the upper floor of a building northeast of the town inn. She keeps alert for unusual disturbances across the region. Her directions send travelers to distant places, including the Tower of Althalaxx far to the north, so threats in the shadows do not catch Auberdine unaware.

Sentinel Farsong. At Silverwing Grove, Sentinel Farsong helps defend Ashenvale’s southern border. She rallies champions against the Warsong Outriders in Warsong Gulch. Sentinel Farsong keeps watch at Silverwing Grove as the Warsong clan cuts lumber and advances into night elf lands. She calls Alliance champions to strike at Warsong Outriders and sends field reports to Silverwing command. Her work helps check the Horde’s expansion and protect the woods.

Sentinel Hill. In Westfall, Sentinel Hill remains the Alliance's main stronghold and the People's Militia's command post. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and hostile outlaws surround the rise, the only secure foothold for lawful citizens in the region. Sentinel Hill rises above central Westfall, with a barracks-style inn, a gryphon roost linking travelers to Stormwind and beyond, a forge, and a lumber mill around Sentinel Tower. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and outlaws crowd the surrounding land. The encampment keeps a fragile perimeter where travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the watchful eyes of veteran defenders.

Sentinel Onaeya. At Maestra's Post, Sentinel Onaeya guards the northern edge of Ashenvale. The night elf guardian rallies Alliance adventurers to protect the forest and aid fellow sentinels. Maestra's Post is a wayside outpost on the road from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Sentinel Onaeya guards the lodge outside the settlement and coordinates its defense. Hostile wildlife, corrupting forces, and border tensions threaten night elf settlements in the region.

Sentinel Selarin. In Auberdine, Sentinel Selarin seeks help for Ashenvale's defenders. She carries Raene Wolfrunner's appeal to the coastal settlement as dangers threaten the forest. Sentinel Selarin carries Raene Wolfrunner's appeal from Ashenvale to Auberdine. With threats mounting across Ashenvale, the garrison is stretched thin. Selarin travels north along the forest road into Darkshore to find Terenthis and ask for help from the sentinels and scouts stationed on the coast.

Sentinel Thenysil. In Astranaar, Sentinel Tara Thenysil watches Ashenvale and the southern road into Stonetalon. She tracks military movements and keeps scouts watching neighboring lands, with special attention on allied forces moving south. At her post in Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil helps guard Ashenvale as hostility grows. Night elf lands across the region face steady encroachment, so outposts must stay in contact. While much of the garrison defends the forest road, Thenysil sends Alliance volunteers beyond Ashenvale to support distant allies.

Sentinel Tower. Defenders watch Westfall from Sentinel Tower atop Sentinel Hill. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia organize resistance against bandits, gnolls, and the Defias Brotherhood. Sentinel Tower rises above the unsettled plains of Westfall. With Stormwind's official army largely absent and aid withheld, local volunteers and veterans joined together around this central stronghold. From its stone heights, lookouts can see across the dusty plains, from abandoned pumpkin patches to the misty shores. They watch for highwaymen and gnoll raiding parties moving through the region.

Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Along Darkshore’s road, Sentinel Tysha Moonblade watches a troubled coast. The night elf scout stands west of Ameth'Aran, guiding travelers and seeking help with the restless spirits haunting the nearby ruins. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade watches the road through Darkshore. East of her lie the ruins of Ameth'Aran, where cursed Highborne ghosts and malevolent banshees linger among ancient stone pillars. Auberdine's defenses are stretched thin by dangers along the coast, so Tysha asks capable travelers to uncover the history of Ameth'Aran's fall and put down its restless dead.

Sentinel Velene Starstrike. At Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike guards central Ashenvale. She protects the sanctuary and nearby waters from rogue elementals and foul sorcerers, keeping their magic from corrupting the ancient woodland. At Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike keeps watch from Silverwind Refuge. Night elf sentinels across Ashenvale work to preserve the forest's balance and defend elven sanctuaries. Silverwind Refuge offers travelers a place to rest in the central woods, and Velene helps keep the area safe.

Sentinels. The Sentinels are the elite, predominantly female military force of the night elves, formed ten thousand years ago after the War of the Ancients. Guided by the Sisterhood of Elune and commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, they guard kaldorei settlements and defend sacred lands from Ashenvale to Feralas. Today, they wage a bitter war against Horde deforestation while watching over their new home on Teldrassil. Before the Great Sundering, the military of the ancient Kaldorei Empire had devolved into a decadent hierarchy where rank was decided by noble lineage rather than martial skill. The devastation of the War of the Ancients proved that this aristocratic structure was utterly unfit to defend Azeroth. In the aftermath, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind spearheaded radical reforms across night elf society. She turned to the Sisterhood of Elune, an order that had survived intact and possessed extensive experience in tactics, combat, and healing. From its devout ranks, Tyrande forged the Sentinels: a standing martial army dedicated to selflessly protecting their emerging society without regard to noble heritage.

Sentry Point. Sentry Point is a human watchtower stationed on the mainland edge of Dustwallow Marsh, guarding the causeway bridge that leads directly to Theramore Isle. Maintained by Theramore's forces, it monitors traffic entering and exiting Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island citadel. Positioned at the western end of the long bridge linking Theramore Isle to the treacherous wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Sentry Point serves as the stronghold's first line of defense on the mainland. The stone scout tower keeps watch over the swamp road, ensuring that hostile marsh beasts or Horde raiders cannot approach the island city unnoticed.

Separation Anxiety. Huntsman Markhor in Revantusk Village has lost his twin brother Malkhor, taken by the Vilebranch in the same raid that took Torntusk's mate. Malkhor met a swift, brutal end, and his remains were fed to the Vilebranch's oozes and wolves. Markhor says his brother's life is beyond saving, yet his soul can still be rescued, and he asks you to recover the remains. Markhor says that many in the village have lost loved ones to the wilds, and his own loss is Malkhor, his twin. The Vilebranch took Malkhor during the raid that took Torntusk's mate. Malkhor was not fated to live, and his captors put him to a swift, brutal death.

Sepulcher. The Forsaken hold the Sepulcher above Silverpine Forest’s western coast. Once a Lordaeron graveyard and burial crypt, it is now a fortified Horde refuge amid threats from across the region. The Sepulcher crowns the hills above Lordaeron’s western coast. You find an old cemetery and stone crypt beside the western road, now held by the Forsaken. Since the Third War, they have made its grounds and ancient vault a vital outpost. Danger presses from every side: feral worgen stalk the south, Scourge remnants wander east, and Kirin Tor wizards watch from Ambermill. For travelers crossing Silverpine, the Sepulcher offers shelter, supplies, and a place of command.

Serena Bloodfeather. Across the northern Barrens, harpy raids threaten the Crossroads supply lines. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing flock, driven by a blood feud with the Horde after Rexxar slew her sister. Ending her campaign could break the harpies’ coordination. Witchwing harpies strike the trails northwest of the Crossroads under Serena Bloodfeather’s command. Their attacks are driven by more than hunger: Serena seeks vengeance against the Horde. During Durotar’s founding, the beastmaster Rexxar slew her sister, the notorious matriarch Bloodfeather. Serena has rallied her flock to attack supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

Serena's Head. At the Dry Hills in the northern Barrens, Serena Bloodfeather's head is sought as proof of her death. Darsok Swiftdagger plans to display it on a Horde supply wagon as a warning against further harpy raids.

Serge Hinott. In Tarren Mill, Serge Hinott brews mixtures for the Forsaken war effort. The Forsaken alchemist works alongside Apothecary Lydon, preparing concoctions, antidotes, and reagents for the Royal Apothecary Society. Serge Hinott brews remedies and other mixtures for the Forsaken in Tarren Mill. He works beside Apothecary Lydon, whose work includes chemical development and plague research against nearby human settlements such as Southshore. Hinott handles specialized brewing, including restorative salves and antidotes for field agents and scouts who face poisons or other toxic mishaps.

Sergra Darkthorn. Having proven their basic tracking and stalking skills in the rolling hills of Mulgore, young tauren are directed outward into the arid wilderness of the Barrens. Melor Stonehoof sends aspiring hunters north of the border to report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. This journey marks the hunter's formal transition from local trials to the demanding predatory hierarchy of Kalimdor's broader plains. For a novice tauren hunter, completing initial rites in Mulgore is only the beginning. The lush valleys of their ancestral homeland are protected and familiar, nurturing beasts that test patience rather than sheer survival. Melor Stonehoof recognizes when a hunter's spirit has grown enough to require harsher trials. He instructs his pupils to pack their gear, leave the safety of Bloodhoof Village, and venture east across the mountain pass into the baked scrublands of the Barrens.

Serpent Wild. Serpent Wild is a Horde quest in Thousand Needles that connects the discovery of strange alien eggs to ancient tauren legends. Following an unsettling revelation at Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof dispatches adventurers northwest to Motega Firemane at Whitereach Post to confront the awakening of Arikara. When strange, unnatural eggs began appearing in Thousand Needles, local tauren feared an ecological disaster. However, inspecting the artifacts reveals something far older and more ominous than ordinary predators: signs pointing to the vengeance spirit Arikara. Stunned by the horrifying confirmation, Hagar Lightninghoof realizes the canyon faces a mythical threat long thought relegated to fireside lore.

Serpent's Coil. Serpent's Coil is a winding network of caves and burnt-out encampments nestled in the eastern ridges of the Blasted Lands. Littered with scorched orcish architecture left behind from the older wars, it serves as a secluded redoubt for dark cultists. Carved into the jagged eastern cliffs of the Blasted Lands, the winding path and caverns of Serpent's Coil wind past ruined orcish huts that date back to the First and Second Wars. Rather than simple beasts, the tunnels harbor cabals of Shadowsworn cultists and practitioners of dark arts drawn to the residual demonic energies permeating the red wastes. Deep within its twisting hollows, they work far from the watchful eyes of Nethergarde Keep.

Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a rare, subterranean herb found growing only in the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Its potent natural properties have drawn the keen interest of the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society. Serpentbloom grows exclusively within the damp, shadowy tunnels of the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens. Rooted in an ecosystem warped by unrestrained Emerald Dream energies, the plant thrives far from sunlight and often harbors venomous serpents nesting among its stems. Because the cave system is overrun with hostile beasts and corrupted druids, few who venture inside ever return with viable specimens.

Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a gathering task issued by Apothecary Zamah, an envoy of the Royal Apothecary Society residing in Thunder Bluff. Zamah seeks specimens of a rare herb native to the subterranean depths of the Wailing Caverns to aid the research of the Forsaken. Stationed in the Pools of Vision beneath the Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah serves as an envoy of the Royal Apothecary Society from the Undercity. While the tauren hosts focus on spiritual balance and healing the wounded land, Zamah's attention is fixed on rare and virulent materials. Having isolated a sample of an unusual plant known as Serpentbloom, she seeks bulk quantities to advance the research directives of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken.

Service to the Horde. The jeweled pendant now sits with Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar, delivered after Report to Zor, and Zor has one more word for you. You carried the jeweled pendant to Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar, and the pendant now sits with Zor. Return to Zor Lonetree and there is more to hear about what you have done for the Horde.

Set Them Ablaze!. Squire Maltrake tells you the four towers of Searing Gorge can never be destroyed, but the Torch of Retribution can set them burning for a very long time. While they burn, no guard or sentry can hold the watch posts, and the Dark Irons lose their first line of defense. The flames the torch lights cannot be put out by any element or force. Maltrake sends you inside each of the four sentry towers, North, South, East and West, to use the torch within their walls. The Dark Irons have posted lookouts at the towers, and Maltrake warns you to beware of them.
Sethir's Journal. On Teldrassil, Sethir's Journal was recovered through stealth. Its pages confirm that corruption from mainland Kalimdor has reached the World Tree.

Sevren's Orders. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends a proven Forsaken agent to the Undercity. The orders direct the agent to Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter. Skilled Forsaken agents who prove themselves against the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades are summoned south as their people strengthen their hold on Lordaeron. Magistrate Sevren writes the orders as an introduction and credentials for Bethor Iceshard, one of the Dark Lady's foremost arcane practitioners in the Magic Quarter. Sevren knows only that the assignment concerns reaching out to an errant lich. The Undercity's high mages give the summons their full authority.

Sewers. Beneath the hills west of Lordaeron's ruined palace, the Sewers offer a second way into the Undercity. Their stone passage carries bat handlers and travelers past the elevators descending from the throne room. The Sewers once drained Lordaeron's royal capital. Now Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken fold those old stone channels into the Undercity's defenses. The passage opens west of the surface ruins, near a Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, then slopes directly inside. Forsaken bat handlers fly riders through the cavernous conduit into the Undercity's subterranean rings, avoiding the slow cage lifts. The route also skirts the fortified courtyards, leaving a dangerous weakness that hostile infiltrators seek to exploit.

Shadow Council. The Shadow Council was the secret cabal of warlocks and necrolytes that orchestrated the corruption of the Old Horde on Draenor and guided its invasion of Azeroth. Founded by Gul'dan under the direction of the Burning Legion, the cult manipulated clan chieftains from behind the scenes until Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer purged their stronghold in Blackrock Mountain. Before the crossing into Azeroth, Gul'dan brought together a clandestine assembly of warlocks, necrolytes, and opportunistic chieftains to manipulate the orcish clans. By elevating Blackhand the Destroyer as a malleable figurehead, the Shadow Council ruled the Old Horde from the dark. They disseminated fel magic across Draenor and fed the blood of the demon Mannoroth to the clans, binding the orcs to the will of the Burning Legion.

Shadow Grave. Newly freed Forsaken awaken in Shadow Grave, above Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Shadow Grave sits on the rocky slope above Deathknell, a stone mausoleum where the newly freed Forsaken awaken. Once raised into the Scourge’s mindless service, the dead recover their free will in its vaults. Undertaker Mordo watches over them as they rise from stone slabs and take their first steps into a world that despises them. They follow the footpath down to Deathknell and pledge themselves to the Banshee Queen.

Shadow Hold. Shadow Hold is a sprawling subterranean complex hidden within the blighted canyon of Jaedenar in western Felwood. Once a sacred night elf barrow den, it has been seized and desecrated by the Shadow Council to serve as their primary bastion on Kalimdor. Beneath the corrupted red earth of Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, a vast underground labyrinth carved out of what was once an ancient night elf barrow den. Where sleeping druids once rested to tend the Emerald Dream, dark warlocks and demonic servitors now stalk twisted corridors illuminated by fel fire. At its deepest tiers, the cult commands a formidable force under the dreadlord Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan, making it the supreme seat of demonic influence in the region.

Shadow Magic. Marshal Marris calls for action against Shadow Magic in Redridge. Blackrock shadowcasters carry demon-tainted midnight orbs that turn dark energies against Lakeshire's defenders. The orbs must be taken from them and destroyed to protect the town's line. Blackrock strength has always rested on brute force, but the clan's raids in the Redridge Mountains now bring a darker threat. Shadowcasters wield dark powers and channel fel and shadow energies through demon-tainted midnight orbs.
