These artifacts have dealt terrible losses to the local militia, worsening a war already turning against the defenders.

Shadow Priest Allister. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister directs Forsaken efforts across Silverpine Forest. He watches nearby threats and helps secure Lordaeron's borders for the Dark Lady. Shadow Priest Allister directs Forsaken scouts from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. From this settlement, he keeps watch for renegade humans, beasts, and the arcane activity around Dalaran.

Shadow Priest Sarvis. In Deathknell's ruined chapel, Shadow Priest Sarvis guides the newly awakened Forsaken. He gives them purpose and directs them against mindless undead and local threats. Shadow Priest Sarvis guides Forsaken who have just risen from their graves in Deathknell. Their awakening can be jarring and horrific, and some lose their minds to frenzy or despair. Sarvis gives the newly risen a purpose. He sends them to put down the mindless corpses roaming the cemetery and secure Deathknell's borders against the Scourge.

Shadow of the Past. In Stormwind, the trail from a Stockade prisoner leads into the city’s hidden dealings. Baros Alexston sends you to Mathias Shaw after a mysterious visitor spoke with Bazil Thredd. Baros Alexston cannot identify the visitor who spoke with Bazil Thredd, the Stockade’s chief prisoner. Warden Thelwater’s account has brought investigators to the city architect, but he has no name to offer. Instead, Baros points you toward Master Mathias Shaw, who leads SI:7 and makes it his business to know Stormwind’s secrets.

Shadowbreak Ravine. Shadowbreak Ravine is a secluded mountain hollow tucked away in southeastern Desolace. Cloaked among jagged crags near Magram Village, this eerie ravine serves as a hidden redoubt for the demonic forces and mortal zealots of the Burning Blade. Tucked deep into the barren mountain ridges southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine provides the Burning Blade with a secluded staging ground away from the eyes of wandering centaur tribes. Amid strange, oversized mushrooms and grim ritual encampments, cultists labor alongside summoned demons. Here, dark practitioners invoke fel energies and tend heavy ritual chains, using the natural isolation of the ravine to marshal reinforcements and maintain a firm demonic foothold within the badlands of Desolace.

Shadowfang Keep. On a rugged bluff above Pyrewood Village, Shadowfang Keep broods over southern Silverpine Forest. Once Silverlaine Keep, it fell to worgen summoned during the Third War and became the lair of the mad Archmage Arugal, haunted by slain nobles and overrun by wolf-beasts. Before the Third War, Baron Silverlaine ruled nearby Pyrewood Village from his ancestral seat, Silverlaine Keep. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, desperate wizards sought forbidden means to stem the undead tide. Drawing on Dalaran mage Ur's dimensional research, Archmage Arugal summoned worgen from beyond this world. The savage beasts tore through the Scourge, then escaped control. They rampaged across southern Silverpine and besieged the keep, killing Baron Silverlaine, his family, and the defenders under Commander Springvale. Guilt and grief broke Arugal's sanity. He claimed the fortress, renamed it Shadowfang Keep, and called the monstrous predators his children.

Shadowguard. In the Undercity, Aelthalyste sends a Darkspear priest back to Orgrimmar. She sees that the young troll is ready for the tribe’s sacred rites, and Ur'kyo awaits in the Valley of Spirits. Aelthalyste watches visiting troll priests in the Undercity. When an initiate has grown strong enough to face the tribe’s trials, she sends them across the Great Sea to learn from their own elders. She does not impose Forsaken teachings on them; their faith follows the traditions of their people.

Shadowhide Pendant. In Redridge, Shadowhide Pendant charms pass among gnolls working with Morganth. Lakeshire accepts ten as proof that its law has been enforced. Shadowhide Pendant charms pass among the Shadowhide warriors, brutes, and spellcasters. Deep in Redridge's hills, the clan has gathered under Lieutenant Fangore and fallen under the sway of Morganth, a rogue wielder of the Arcane. To Lakeshire's townspeople, the crude charms mark an organized threat harassing settlements for an enemy of the Crown.

Shadowprey Village. Shadowprey Village is a remote Horde fishing settlement built along the rocky southern coast of Sar'theris Strand in Desolace. Populated largely by Darkspear troll fishermen and supported by tauren service keepers, it acts as a critical coastal outpost and trade lifeline amidst a barren wasteland. Tucked against the cliffs of southern Desolace, Shadowprey Village offers safe harbor in a region notorious for centaur clans and desolate wastes. The settlement is primarily an encampment of troll fishermen whose hauls sustain not only their own village but also inland outposts like Ghost Walker Post. Despite the rough shoreline, towering wooden piers reach out into the ocean, allowing local anglers to brave deep waters and dive for shellfish among the submerged wreckage dotting Sar'theris Strand.

Shadowsong Shrine. Shadowsong Shrine is a ruined hillside sanctuary situated in western Azshara, not far from the Ashenvale border. Haunted by the restless spirits of ancient Highborne, the site bears the illustrious name of the Shadowsong bloodline, though its true historical connection to them remains shrouded in mystery. Perched upon a high hill overlooking the shattered lands of Azshara, the Shadowsong Shrine lies in ancient, overgrown ruin. Like much of the surrounding coast, it is plagued by the lingering apparitions of Highborne ghosts who wander among the fallen stonework, seeking to extinguish any mortal life that trespasses upon their domain. The shrine shares its name with Maiev Shadowsong, the unrelenting warden of Illidan Stormrage. Whether this sanctuary honors her family or dates back to before the Sundering is a secret lost to the ages.

Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave lies beneath the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen, where its spiders have grown dangerous. Their brood now threatens young kaldorei near Aldrassil. Shadowthread Cave opens in Shadowglen’s shaded northwest, a lair for Teldrassil’s giant spiders. In earlier years, the spiders lived quietly alongside the World Tree’s young boughs. Now they guard their territory fiercely. Webwood silk chokes the stone corridors, and the brood threatens young kaldorei venturing beyond Aldrassil.

Shadumbra's Head. At Splintertree Post, Shadumbra's Head is proof that a feared predator has fallen. Bringing it to Senani Thunderheart completes a trial of the Ashenvale Hunt and helps secure the western roads toward the Zoram Strand. Shadumbra hunted the woods west of Splintertree Post, where Horde scouts and couriers traveled toward the Zoram Strand. Her speed and stealth made those paths perilous, and each westward patrol kept the post's defenders wary.

Shady Rest Inn. The Shady Rest Inn was once a welcoming human-built waystation sitting just off the road between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. Today, only charred timbers and smoldering ashes remain following a sudden and violent arson attack. The tragedy left the innkeeper shattered and sparked tension across the marsh as investigators sift through the wreckage for clues. Built to serve travelers navigating the treacherous crossing between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens, the Shady Rest Inn stood as an outpost of civilized comfort in a harsh wilderness. That ended when the inn was abruptly razed to the ground in a devastating fire. Innkeeper James Hyal managed to survive the inferno, but the blaze claimed the lives of his wife and child. Traumatized and grief-stricken, Hyal was left with nothing as the ruins became an active crime scene, drawing scrutiny from Theramore authorities desperate to identify who ignited the flames.

Shael'dryn. Beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn watches corruption spread through Ashenvale. East of Iris Lake, she aids night elf scouts and Astranaar's sentinels with relics tainted by demonic and foul influences. Beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn watches the forest's eastern approaches with the night elf sentinels. When corruption touches local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, she draws on her deep understanding of nature to guide adventurers in restoring spiritual balance.

Shalzaru's Lair. Shalzaru's Lair is a sprawling, submerged cavern located at the northern tip of the Isle of Dread in Feralas. It serves as a major stronghold for the Hatecrest naga and shelters their formidable master, Shalzaru. From within these damp tunnels, the serpentine invaders coordinate their aggressive presence just south of Feathermoon Stronghold. Carved into the rugged bluffs at the northern end of the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru's Lair is divided into a massive main cavern and a smaller auxiliary chamber, linked together by submerged subterranean waterways. The interior teems with Hatecrest serpent guards and spell-weaving sorceresses on high alert. Deep within the recesses dwells Lord Shalzaru, the serpentine overlord directing the Hatecrest brood across the island. Its proximity to Sardor Isle poses a direct, constant threat to the night elf Sentinels garrisoned at Feathermoon Stronghold just across the channel.

Shaman. Shaman are spiritual mediators who commune with the primordial forces of earth, air, fire and water. Balancing raw nature through totems, lightning and ancestral healing, they are the spiritual core of orc, tauren and troll culture under Warchief Thrall. Dwarves walk the path too, as the Wildhammer long have, and the Skyborne Windshapers seek to restore their people's bond with the winds. Unlike priests who revere the divine or mages who bend the arcane, shaman interact directly with the primal forces of nature. The elements of earth, air, fire, and water are inherently chaotic and locked in perpetual conflict. A shaman does not enslave these forces, but petitions and negotiates with them, serving as a balance keeper between primal fury and the mortal world. Through wooden and stone totems planted into the soil, shaman channel these elemental bargains to protect allies, hinder foes, or mend the wounded with cleansing water.

Shaman Voodoo Charm. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans wield the Shaman Voodoo Charm. Its vile magic can sever a sleeping druid's spirit from the body. The Gnarlpine tribe has fallen into madness and corruption on Teldrassil. Within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, its shamans wield magic beyond ordinary wilderness sorcery. Their voodoo charms let them tear a sleeping druid's consciousness from the mortal realm and trap it in the Emerald Dream. The furbolgs then animate the empty body. Night elf protectors become mindless guardians, killing anyone who enters the barrows.

Shan'do. Shan'do is a revered Darnassian honorific meaning "honored teacher" or "honored instructor." Traditionally used within night elven society and druidic circles, it denotes deep reverence toward a mentor who guides another along the path of wisdom and natural magic. Its direct counterpart is thero'shan, meaning "honored student." In the Darnassian language, shan'do translates directly to "honored teacher" or "honored instructor." It is far more than an occupational label: addressing an elder or mentor as shan'do expresses solemn humility, filial devotion, and enduring respect for their guidance.

Shanda. In Aldrassil, Shanda guides young night elf priests in the ways of Elune. She serves the Sisterhood of Elune in Shadowglen, teaching prayers, wards, and rites as her students prepare to defend Teldrassil. Shanda guides young night elves devoted to Elune from within Aldrassil. While druids tend Teldrassil's roots and boughs, priestesses keep the Kaldorei close to the White Lady. Shanda teaches new initiates to call on lunar grace for healing and protective wards, preparing them to face the corruption creeping into the World Tree's boughs.

Shandris Feathermoon. Shandris Feathermoon is the General of the Sentinel Army and, for ten thousand years, Tyrande Whisperwind's right hand. She now commands night elf military forces throughout Kalimdor from Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle off the coast of Feralas. Shandris Feathermoon is one of the oldest defenders of the night elves. For ten thousand years she has served at Tyrande Whisperwind's side as the high priestess's right hand among the Sentinels, through the long vigil that followed the Sundering.

Shaper's Terrace. Perched high on the northern bluffs above Marshal's Refuge, the Shaper's Terrace is a mysterious overlook marked by ancient titan architecture. It is named in honor of Khaz'goroth the Shaper and bears quiet witness to the primordial experiments that shaped Un'Goro Crater. Overlooking the lush, prehistoric basin of Un'Goro Crater, the Shaper's Terrace holds monumental stone edifices left behind by the titans. Believed to be dedicated to Khaz'goroth the Shaper, this high plateau stands as a testament to the celestial architects who cultivated the crater as a living laboratory for early life on Azeroth. From these elevated stones, ancient entities once observed and directed the flora and fauna below. Its cold stone arches and massive metallic plinths stand in stark, enigmatic contrast to the untamed wilderness thriving directly beneath them.

Shard of Water. Along the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer receives the Shard of Water from a shaman who has faced corruption. Shamans must understand balance, life, and preservation to master water. In the Call of Water, they travel to corrupted springs, even crossing the sea to blighted Silverpine Forest. After purifying the tainted waters, a shaman receives the Shard of Water. Returning the crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky Barrens shore proves the initiate's worth and provides the final key to forge a Water Totem.

Shari Stilwell. In Brill, Shari Stilwell trains Forsaken in the paladin's path. She is stationed in Tirisfal Glades, where the undead who endure the Light's pain learn holy and martial discipline. In Brill, Shari Stilwell guides Forsaken who seek the path of holy warriors. The Light brings the undead excruciating pain, yet she trains those willing to endure it. She helps newcomers find their footing in Tirisfal Glades, through early training and the adjustments of Forsaken life. Those she guides seek a place within the Forsaken kingdom.

Sharing the Land. In Mulgore, Baine Bloodhoof calls you to stop Palemane gnolls from killing the plains' wildlife. By striking their hunters, you help protect the herds and the tauren way of living with the Earth Mother. The tauren take from the land only what they need and honor the Earth Mother in all things. Palemane gnolls have settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, where they slaughter wildlife across the plains. Their hunting leaves carcasses behind and harms the balance of the grasslands. The tauren are building a peaceful home in Mulgore, but the gnolls' wasteful killing threatens it.

Sharptalon's Claw. Ashenvale's trails grow safer when Sharptalon's Claw is taken from the forest. Bring the trophy to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to prove Sharptalon has fallen and protect Horde supply lines. Sharptalon hunts the paths to Splintertree Post as the Horde seeks resources in Ashenvale. The aggressive hippogryph strikes peons and couriers traveling between forward logging camps and the outpost. Its attacks hinder Horde work in the region, where night elven sentinels and dangerous wildlife both threaten the newcomers.

Shatter Scar Vale. Shatter Scar Vale is a scorched basin in central Felwood, located just north of Bloodvenom Falls. It marks the ground zero where demonic infernals crashed into northern Kalimdor during the Third War. Today, the craters still burn with fel fire and host lingering remnants of the Burning Legion. During the Third War, the Burning Legion rained living siege engines down upon northern Kalimdor. Shatter Scar Vale bore the brunt of this celestial assault. Demonic infernals plummeted from the skies, tearing through the ancient canopy and smashing deep craters into the earth. The violent impact shattered the terrain, leaving blackened hollows that smolder with unholy fire to this day. Though the Legion was shattered at Mount Hyjal, the infernals and lingering lesser demons never truly dispersed, maintaining an entrenched foothold in the scarred earth.

Shattered Strand. The Shattered Strand is a wild, rugged coastline flanking the northern rim of the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Dominated by crashing surf and crumbling ancient ruins, the beach crawls with hazardous marine beasts and tribal aquatic creatures. Stretching along the northern edge of the Bay of Storms, the Shattered Strand is far from a peaceful shoreline. The rocky beaches and tidal shallows are heavily inhabited by aggressive wildlife, including towering sea giants, multi-headed hydras, and snapping makrura, alongside encampments of coastal murlocs. Crumbling elven architecture overlooks the waves, anchored by landmarks such as the ancient Temple of Arkkoran and the solitary Tower of Eldara. For travelers navigating Azshara's treacherous cliffs, descending to this isolated strip of coast means confronting some of the region's deadliest amphibious threats.

Shaw's Report. In Westfall, Shaw's Report carries confidential intelligence from SI:7 to Gryan Stoutmantle. Written by Master Mathias Shaw, it describes the Stonemasons Guild, Edwin VanCleef, and their grievance with the crown after Stormwind was rebuilt.

Shelene Rhobart. Along Tirisfal's road, Shelene Rhobart trains leatherworkers at a Deathguard waystation. She supplies cured hides and leathercraft training for the Forsaken's military and logistical efforts across the blighted lands. At a Deathguard waystation southeast of Brill, Shelene Rhobart works along the main road toward the ruins of Lordaeron. Practical crafts still matter in undeath, for survival and war. She turns pelts from Tirisfal's prowling beasts into tough hides, armor, straps, and field gear for Forsaken patrols facing the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders.

Shenthul. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul trains rogues and serves the Shattered Hand. He directs covert work across Kalimdor and brings promising rogues into its ranks. Shenthul trains rogues in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. While warriors and shamans march openly across Durotar, he teaches stealth, ambush, and subterfuge. His students learn fieldcraft and lethal arts for work in Kalimdor's harsh wilderness and unforgiving politics.

Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds. 'Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds' is a quest that leads adventurers out of Northshire Valley to track wandering kobolds into Elwynn Forest. Using a tracking kit, players discover the trail leads toward the infested Fargodeep Mine and report the findings to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire. As the kobold infestation in Northshire Valley escalates, signs indicate that the vermin are organizing beyond the isolated abbey grounds. Equipped with a tracking kit, scouts are dispatched to follow the trail of the creatures to determine where they are concentrating their efforts. This reconnaissance serves as a crucial bridge between Northshire's local troubles and the broader defense of Elwynn Forest.

Shifting Mire. The Shifting Mire forms the vast, muddy heart of the Swamp of Sorrows, lying just west of the Pool of Tears. Its name comes from the strange, restless silt beneath the murky water, which seems to drift and gather under the influence of an unseen force. Spanning the central reaches of the marshland, the Shifting Mire is an unsettling expanse where solid footing is hard to come by. The silt along the swamp floor shifts and collects as though moved by a living will, driven by a strange, ambient energy permeating the peat. Amidst the drifting mud prowl predatory swamp jaguars, massive sorrow spinners, and hungry sawtooth crocolisks, while bands of broken draenei known as the Lost Ones stalk the sunken paths.

Shimmer Ridge. Frostmane trolls hold Shimmer Ridge in northern Dun Morogh, west of the Gates of Ironforge. Its two camps span a chasm, and the ridge is the only place shimmerweed grows. Frostmane trolls hold the high ground west of Ironforge's gates. Two camps sit on opposite sides of a chasm, joined by a wooden bridge. Troll scavengers and their tamed mountain boars guard the camps. The ridge lies near the main road and the dwarven capital, so travelers and mountain patrols face raids from above.

Shimmer Stout. At Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew sends a fresh barrel of Shimmer Stout to his brother Wellart. Wellart guards the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink welcome. Rejold Barleybrew has perfected Shimmer Stout with shimmering fronds gathered from Dun Morogh’s icy crags. His family tends the vats and kegs of Brewnall Village, but his brother Wellart chose life as a Mountaineer. Rejold knows how lonely frontier guard duty can be, so he sends a fresh barrel with passing travelers. It is a favor between brothers and a chance to test the brew.

Shimmering Flats. The Shimmering Flats is an expansive salt flat lying at the southeastern tip of Thousand Needles, bordering the desert of Tanaris. Once the bed of an ancient lake, this sun-baked expanse is now famous for the high-speed mechanical rivalries of the Mirage Raceway and a harsh population of desert beasts. Stretching out under the blinding southern sun, the Shimmering Flats is a vast dried lakebed devoid of vegetation, dotted with the sun-bleached bones of turtles and even the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Its sheer, unbroken level surface makes it the premier testing ground on Kalimdor for experimental vehicles. At the center of the flats lies the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers constantly clash to see whose rocket cars, gyrocopters, and engines can achieve the highest speeds—often resulting in fiery crashes and smoking craters across the white crust.

Shimmering Frond. In the Oracle Glade, a strange plant casts a twisting, shimmering aura. Its fronds come from a species native to the Swamp of Sorrows, far across the Great Sea. A radiant plant grows among the trees near the Oracle Glade. Its aura pulses, and its fronds shimmer in the woodland light. Denalan, who tends planters beside Lake Al'Ameth, recognizes the leaves as belonging to a species from the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How seeds from that distant marsh crossed the Great Sea and took root on Teldrassil remains a mystery. Denalan is growing specimens in his own soil to study them.

Shimmerweed. On Shimmer Ridge, Frostmane trolls gather shimmerweed for their rituals. Dwarven brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew wants to test its sharp flavor in his stout. The Frostmane trolls tend shimmerweed on the icy crags of Shimmer Ridge, high above Dun Morogh's lowlands. They harvest the plant and store it in woven baskets throughout their camps, where it fuels their sacred rituals. Few mountaineers beyond troll society pay the herb much mind, though inventive outsiders have taken an interest.

Shindrell Swiftfire. Astranaar’s defense reaches beyond Ashenvale’s forest. Shindrell Swiftfire, a night elf sentinel and scout, watches from the town at the heart of night elf operations in Ashenvale. Alert to changing dangers along Kalimdor’s western reaches, she directs capable Alliance adventurers toward threats on the coast and nearby mountain passes, helping coordinate local defense against dangers from sea and wilds. From Astranaar’s winding walkways, Shindrell Swiftfire watches the frontiers beyond Ashenvale. Sentinels face Horde logging incursions from the east and south, while Shindrell keeps watch beyond the woodland itself. Travelers arrive from Darkshore or set out toward Stonetalon’s jagged ridges, and she helps ensure Astranaar is not left undefended against danger from the flank.

Shindrell's Note. In Astranaar, Shindrell Swiftfire writes a missive about corruption near the town and along Ashenvale's coast. She sends the intelligence report east through the forest to Kayneth Stillwind. Sentinels and druids coordinate to watch Ashenvale's borders as unrest spreads through the forest. In Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire writes of troubling disturbances along the western coast and among the central canopies. She addresses her report to Kayneth Stillwind, a druid at the shrine of Forest Song in the Nightsong Woods to the east. Couriers carry Shindrell's firsthand observations to aid Kayneth's investigation of corruption creeping through the sacred groves.

Shining Strand. Along eastern Silverpine, Shining Strand follows Lordamere Lake south from the Ruins of Lordaeron toward Alterac's rugged foothills. Vile Fin murlocs hold settlements in its shallows, making the shore dangerous for unseasoned travelers. Shining Strand follows Silverpine Forest's eastern edge beside the misty waters of Lordamere Lake. Several aggressive Vile Fin murloc settlements line the shallows, threatening anyone who travels the lake road. Feral worgen roam the deep woods behind the shore.

Ship Schedules. A scroll records ships sailing between Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, with marks beside some voyages. It belongs in the hands of an authority at Steamwheedle Port. The scroll lists the shipments that sail between Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, those already made and those to come, along with the ships' names. Some journeys are marked with a large X, and others carry notes about plunder to be had or a hard fight. It is meant for someone in authority at Steamwheedle Port.

Shipment of Boots. Off the Barrens coast, Shipment of Boots lies in a Southsea encampment south of Ratchet. Drizzlik sent the crate from Booty Bay for Gazlowe's trade network, but the pirates seized it before it reached port. Gazlowe arranged for Drizzlik, a clothing merchant in Booty Bay, to send boots to Ratchet. Southsea Freebooters patrolling the Merchant Coast ambushed the ship and carried the crates to their beach encampments south of the harbor. They scattered the stolen goods among their tents and shanties, and the shipment remains there, far from Ratchet's docks.

Shipment of Iron. In Hillsbrad Fields, a crate of raw iron waits at the human smithy. The metal feeds local arms production, making the shipment a target for Forsaken forces seeking to cut the supply lines that arm the townsfolk. Across the Hillsbrad Foothills, human peasants have mounted stiff resistance against Tarren Mill. Much of their strength comes from the smithy at the southwestern edge of Hillsbrad Fields, where Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices work round the clock, making weapons and armor from heavy shipments of iron. Forsaken commanders ordered the forge put out, its smiths killed, and its stored metal seized for the Horde war effort, hoping to break the farmers’ resolve.

Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother Morgan in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax supplies from Elwynn Forest to Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. William gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave his post at the Lion's Pride Inn, so he depends on travelers heading into the city to carry goods for him.

Shipping Label. A damaged Shipping Label points toward the Azeroth Commerce Authority's trade hub at Three Corners in the Redridge Mountains. It marks a supply crate as the authority's property and shows travelers where to report it. A damaged label marks a stocked supply crate as freight belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. The destination and recipient have been torn away, but the label tells anyone who finds the cargo to return it or report to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rough map sketches the roads toward the Three Corners intersection.

Shipping Schedule. At Jerod's Landing, the Defias Brotherhood moves contraband along Elwynn's waterways. Its dockmaster guards a schedule that maps shipments between Redridge and Westfall, and SI:7 wants it. South of Goldshire, Jerod's Landing sits on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River. The Defias Brotherhood seized the landing as a hub for river traffic. From there, they move contraband between Redridge and Westfall along waterways beyond the Stormwind Guard's notice. Their dockmaster keeps the Shipping Schedule close, recording these shipments.

Shoni the Shilent. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent sends a crew beneath Westfall. She leads the gnomish effort to reclaim Gnomeregan and seeks power for the machines meant to break a path back into the city. Shoni the Shilent directs a gnomish assault crew from Stormwind’s Dwarven District. With Gnomeregan held by troggs, she plans to retake the city and sends operatives into the tunnels beneath Westfall for the parts her crew needs.

Show of Force. Deputy Feldon sends you to drive gnoll packs back from Lakeshire. The Redridge guards need proof that the thrashers have been beaten. Gnoll packs have grown bolder in the Redridge Mountains. Their camps now lie close to Lakeshire and the human homesteads beyond it. Stormwind has too few soldiers to spare for the borderlands, so local authorities depend on travelers to hold the perimeter. The gnolls have not yet struck the town, but their camps bring them within reach of its homes.

Shredding Machines. In Windshear Crag, the Venture Company’s shredders wound Stonetalon’s spirits. Seereth Stonebreak hears their cries as XT:4 and XT:9 tear through the forest. Orc shaman Seereth Stonebreak is stationed along the dusty border between the Barrens and the Stonetalon Mountains. She listens to the unseen realm, though chaos drowns out much of Stonetalon’s spiritual voice. One vision came through with harrowing clarity: man-shaped contraptions tearing through ancient woods with unnatural haste. Marked XT:4 and XT:9, the goblin-engineered shredders butcher Windshear Crag’s timberlands and send waves of distress through the surrounding nature spirits.

Shrewd Negotiations. Magus Wordeen Voidglare praises your infiltration of the mages' city, and says the time has come to be more negotiatory. You are to carry the arcane mote you acquired to Archmage Celindra in Dalaran. Magus Wordeen Voidglare admits that no place on Azeroth rivals the Kirin Tor for knowledge of the arcane, and that even Wordeen's own brilliant work pales beside their ancient wisdom. He thinks it high time the Horde was granted access to their exclusive order. You are to carry the mote you acquired to Archmage Celindra in Dalaran, for Wordeen is sure the Kirin Tor will give anything to get it back.

Shrine of Aessina. At the Shrine of Aessina, night elves honor an ancient spirit of nature and wild creatures. The sacred place lies in southwestern Ashenvale, between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, amid growing border friction. West of Astranaar, the Shrine of Aessina honors a Wild God who embodies the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, night elves and their woodland kin have revered this quiet place and communed with nature away from the main roads. The Horde is pushing into Ashenvale to gather timber and establish footholds, and sacred grounds across the territory face an uncertain peace.

Shrine of the Dormant Flame. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, Horde shaman seek communion with fire atop Durotar’s highest peak northwest of the Valley of Trials. Telf Joolam keeps the secluded sanctuary, where initiates climb to prove their spiritual mastery. A narrow trail winds up from the Southfury River, at the southwestern edge of the Southfury Watershed. The summit rises above Durotar’s red cliffs, with a commanding view and a precipice where one misstep means certain death. Telf Joolam, a solitary hermit, oversees the sacred rites here. Aspiring orc and troll shaman come for the ritual Call of Fire. At the shrine’s brazier, they use the ember of a defeated elemental to kindle the sleeping coals and prove they can commune with fire and respect its destructive spirits.

Shrine of the Fallen Warrior. Perched upon a secluded ridge west of the Crossroads lies the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior, a quiet memorial overlooking the sweeping red savannahs of the Barrens. Marked by a stone plinth bearing the initials 'MK' and the body of a fallen orc warrior, it is watched over by the gentle presence of a Spirit Healer named Koiter. Tucked away high upon the hills northwest of the Crossroads, the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior stands as an unusually solemn haven amidst the dust and peril of the Barrens. To find it, travelers must scale a winding ridge pathway southwest of the summit until they reach a gentle mound. Upon the summit rests a carved stone monument, its plinth carved with the initials 'MK'. Before it lies the armored form of an orc warrior at rest, watched over day and night by a named Spirit Healer known as Koiter. There are no battle horns here, only quiet contemplation honoring a champion who walked Kalimdor's lands.

Sida. In Menethil Harbor, Sida lives apart from her estranged husband, Einar Stonegrip. She spends her days in the Wetlands port and sometimes ventures into the marshes, where she recently lost her bag near Ironbeard's Tomb. Sida lives in Menethil Harbor, the Alliance port in the Wetlands, apart from Einar Stonegrip. Their marriage is strained, and Einar refuses to travel to Menethil while Sida remains there. She still sometimes ventures beyond the coastal settlement into the Wetlands. On a recent trip toward Ironbeard's Tomb, she lost her personal bag.

Sida's Bag. In the Wetlands, Sida's Bag lies swallowed in an ooze near Ironbeard's Tomb. Sida, a resident of Menethil Harbor, fled after throwing her satchel at one of the slimes during her weekly visit; the bag and its contents must be recovered from the acidic creatures. Sida visits Ironbeard's Tomb near Dun Modr each week. Dreadful, dripping oozes ambushed her there, and panic drove her to fling her satchel at one of them. The ooze absorbed the bag into its body. The distraction gave Sida time to escape alive and return to Menethil Harbor, while her possessions remained trapped inside an unknown slime.

Sigil of Arathor. Following the Sigil of Thoradin, Zengu tells you the human prince entrusted another sigil to Lieutenant Valorcall, who commands the cavalry. Find him, and bring the sigil back to Zengu in Hammerfall. Zengu scoffs that the humans can scarcely call Stromgarde their own, never mind the whole of the Arathi Highlands, yet their prince keeps the last of his horsemen riding about the countryside. Zengu cannot understand why. More important is that one of the sigils rests with Lieutenant Valorcall, who leads those riders. Zengu wants him found and the sigil brought back to Hammerfall.

Sigil of Strom. Zengu in Hammerfall wants the sigils that guard Trol'kalar, the sword of Lord Ignaeus Trollbane. The first, the Sigil of Strom, was taken by the Syndicate, and a Syndicate agent in Stromgarde is likely to hold it. In ancient times the trolls fought the Arathorian Empire, and their ablest foe was Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane. He went into battle wielding Trol'kalar, a name that means troll slayer in the trolls' old tongue. Now Trollbane's sons are weakened and their stronghold lies in ruins.

Sigil of Thoradin. Tor'gan's reconstruction of the broken sigil worked flawlessly. The restored Sigil of Thoradin can now open the seal on Trollbane's tomb, and he tells you to return it to Zengu in Hammerfall. Tor'gan says the reconstruction worked flawlessly, and the Sigil of Thoradin is now able to open the seal on Trollbane's tomb. Take it back to Zengu in Hammerfall, who no doubt has more for you to do.

Sigil of Trollbane. Following the Sigil of Arathor, Zengu sends you to slay Prince Galen Trollbane and take the last sigil, the one that unlocks his father Thoras Trollbane's tomb. The prince keeps it on his own person, far inside Stromgarde. The last sigil that can open the tomb of Thoras Trollbane is kept by Thoras's son, Prince Galen, in person. He is to be found far inside Stromgarde, in a chapel within the districts the militia holds. Zengu warns that Galen is well guarded and a fine fighter, so this could prove very hard. You are to kill him and carry the sigil to Zengu in Hammerfall.

Signed Recruitment Letter. Kargal Battlescar sends the Signed Recruitment Letter west from the Far Watch Post. His mark directs new recruits to report for duty at the Crossroads. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar prepares recruits for service in the Barrens. The post stands east of the Southfury River, where newcomers cross from Durotar. When a conscript proves ready to Kargal, he stamps and signs a letter of introduction. The orders send recruits west along the road to the Crossroads. There, Sergra Darkthorn coordinates supplies and the defense of the dry plains.

Silithid Egg (The Barrens). Across the Field of Giants, silithid eggs lie buried beneath the soil. Horde researchers gather them to learn about the swarm spreading through the southern Barrens. Silithid mounds rise from the Field of Giants as strange insect-like creatures churn the earth. Their eggs lie beneath the hardened soil, guarded by territorial silithid. The Horde knows little about these creatures, but scouts at the Crossroads have seen signs of coordination and intelligence beyond that of ordinary wild beasts. Unhatched eggs may help scholars in Orgrimmar learn about the silithid’s life cycle and nature.

name.esES: Llave de la torre de Silixiz
name.frFR: Clé de la tour de Silixiz

text.enUS: Silixiz's Tower Key. Foreman Silixiz carries the key to the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Shattered Hand operatives must take it from his pocket as part of an undercover sabotage assignment. North of the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company keeps its tower under tight security. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix oversees the isolated lookout, while goblin mercenaries patrol the compound. Outside, Foreman Silixiz carries the tower key. A Shattered Hand operative from Orgrimmar must steal it and keep it. Force will not do: the operative must enter unseen and pick Silixiz's pocket, proving their stealth before climbing into the tower's toxic upper levels.

Silky Sutures. Silky Sutures is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands offered by Doctor Gregory Victor in the outpost of Hammerfall. Frustrated by unrepaired siege damage and dwindling medical supplies, the camp's resident physician recruits adventurers to gather venomous highland spider silk for use as emergency field sutures. The task highlights the desperate, resource-starved conditions facing the defenders of Hammerfall as they struggle to keep their guards and laborers on their feet. Hammerfall endures in the rugged Arathi Highlands, but the encampment shows visible signs of prolonged strain. Unrepaired siege damage marks the perimeter, leading the local physician, Doctor Gregory Victor, to bitterly observe that neglect seems to be official policy. Despite the crumbling fortifications and lack of broader support, Victor refuses to let the decay claim his infirmary. Maintaining a working clinic is essential for keeping the laborers and sentinel guards upright and ready for conflict.

Silver Dawning's Lockbox. Off the Darkshore coast, Silver Dawning's Lockbox lies in the wreck of a ship lost to coastal murlocs. Inside are the fallen captain's personal effects and ship log. The Silver Dawning sailed across the sea toward Auberdine when coastal murlocs attacked. They drove the ship beneath the waves north of the harbor, and the captain died in the assault. The flooded hull still holds the captain's personal lockbox, with the ship's log and private belongings inside. Recovering them could bring a final measure of peace to the surviving crew ashore.

Silver Stream Mine. In northern Loch Modan, Silver Stream Mine lies between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam, its silver veins exhausted. The Miners' League made the hollow a supply depot, but Tunnel Rat kobolds now occupy its tunnels and hoard stolen equipment and rare minerals. Silver Stream Mine once yielded rich silver for Ironforge. Dwarf miners dug until the main veins ran dry, leaving broad underground chambers. The Miners' League kept the hard-won shafts in use as a guarded storehouse for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. The mine is also the only known source of Charged Rift Gems, which draw arcanists seeking delicate tailoring reagents.

Silvervein the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Silvervein the Elder appears on the hills above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Travelers honor him and the ancient ties among Azeroth’s elder peoples, and he grants an ancestral blessing in return. Above Thelsamar, Silvervein watches the ridges in silence. During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor him as a keeper of memories from ages past. Below, Loch Modan faces trogg invasions and local disputes, while the elder spirit remains peaceful on his overlook.

Silverwind Refuge. Silverwind Refuge shelters travelers in south-central Ashenvale, just north of Mystral Lake. Sentinels guard this night elven settlement along the forest trails. Silverwind Refuge rests between Mystral Lake and Iris Lake, to the north. Alongside Astranaar, it is one of central Ashenvale’s major night elven waystations. Craftsmen and wilderness trainers teach herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Sentinels guard the refuge, where allies traveling through the ancient woods can rest.

Silverwing Grove. Silverwing Sentinels gather at Silverwing Grove in south-central Ashenvale, near Fallen Sky Lake. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors muster Alliance forces against the Warsong Clan loggers cutting through the forest. At Silverwing Grove, Silverwing Sentinels gather beneath the canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost. The night elves use the post to oppose the Horde's lumbering in Warsong Gulch. Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts assemble here to organize skirmishes and muster champions. They defend Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

Silverwing Outpost. Silverwing Outpost guards the eastern bank of the Falfarren River in south-central Ashenvale. Duriel Moonfire commands the garrison, the Alliance's easternmost hold against the Horde in the contested woodland. Silverwing Outpost lies southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the Barrens border. Its place on the eastern bank of the Falfarren River puts it in territory the Horde contests and patrols. From here, the garrison shields night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels face constant attacks from nearby orcs seeking to drive night elf forces from the area.

Silvery Spinnerets. Near Wellspring Lake, Silvery Spinnerets are harvested from Lady Sathrah in northern Teldrassil. Her silver webs once gathered healing evening dew for the Temple of the Moon. The Sisterhood of Elune seeks the spinnerets for a sacred rite honoring her soul. Lady Sathrah once spun shimmering webs by moonlight near Wellspring Lake. Her silver silk gathered evening mist into healing dew prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. But corruption reached her in Teldrassil, driving her into violent madness. Sathrah threatened her brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end her suffering and recover her spinnerets, bringing mercy to a once-revered creature of the great boughs.

Simple Letter. The Simple Letter is an introductory directive that guides novice warriors to trainer Llane Beshere at Northshire Abbey. It marks the beginning of their formal martial instruction and urges them to assist the troubled citizens of the valley. The Simple Letter serves as an initial introduction for aspiring warriors arriving in Northshire Valley. Directed to Llane Beshere, the resident warrior trainer at Northshire Abbey, the letter prompts newly arrived fighters to make contact with their instructor, familiarize themselves with their surroundings, and prepare for the demands of martial life.

Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, the Simple Memorandum sends novice gnome warriors to Anvilmar. It directs them to train with Thran Khorman for the war to take back Gnomeregan. The Simple Memorandum sends young gnome fighters to train in Anvilmar. As they face local wildlife and troggs in Coldridge Valley, they receive letters of introduction. This one directs its bearer to Thran Khorman, the warrior trainer there. Gnomes bring intellect and contraptions to battle, but taking back Gnomeregan calls for strength and martial discipline. The memorandum tells its bearer to leave early training behind and learn the art of war from Thran.

Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, a message calls new gnome warriors to Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm passes along Thran Khorman’s summons, inviting trained fighters to learn the arts of war and prepare to reclaim Gnomeregan. As you help Sten Stoutarm drive off troggs and boars in Coldridge Valley, he receives a short message for a young gnome warrior. Thran Khorman, a veteran trainer in Anvilmar, sees promise in the refugee fighter. He calls the newcomer to the central hall to begin martial instruction.

Simple Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Thran Khorman calls young dwarven warriors to Anvilmar. The Simple Rune is an inscribed stone token that directs recruits to seek instruction from their warrior trainer. The Simple Rune marks the start of a recruit’s training. Thran Khorman gives the inscribed stone to promising young fighters who have begun clearing threats from Coldridge Valley. Its marks are a formal summons, not a magical charm. A recruit who reads it is expected to report to Thran inside Anvilmar, where the warrior trainer teaches basic combat and offers practical advice for surviving Dun Morogh’s hostile wilds.

Simple Rune. At Anvilmar, new dwarven warriors receive a call to begin their training. Sten Stoutarm carries it from Thran Khorman, the trainer inside the hall. Young recruits prove their grit around Coldridge Valley as they clear pests, while veteran scouts watch for promising fighters. Sten Stoutarm brings them an inscribed stone from Thran Khorman. The simple rune summons them from the snowy valley paths into Anvilmar's warm forge-hall, where they can pledge themselves to the warrior's trade.

Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, a Simple Sigil calls novice night elf warriors to training with Alyissia. It marks their first step into Teldrassil’s defense. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine guides young night elves as they seek their calling. A runner brings a Simple Sigil from the warrior trainer Alyissia, and Ilthalaine gives it to fledgling warriors. Its inscription tells each recruit to report for instruction. The token marks the start of their martial training as troubling times come to the World Tree.

Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, Alyissia calls young night elf warriors to defend their people. Conservator Ilthalaine carries her summons as the Kaldorei face changes across Teldrassil and beyond. After you prove your basic survival skills against Shadowglen's restless wildlife, Conservator Ilthalaine gives you an inscribed sigil. The token formally marks your move into combat training. It carries a request from Alyissia, the warrior trainer at Aldrassil, asking you to dedicate your strength to defending your people.

Simple Tablet. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives new troll warriors a message to take to Frang. Gornek gives new troll warriors a message from Tar'sere, addressed to Frang, the warrior trainer near the Den. It introduces the recruit to combat training in Durotar and asks them to present themselves to Frang. The message calls on them to take up weapons for the Horde.

Simple Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a marked parchment sends you to Frang after you prove yourself against local beasts. The warrior trainer waits outside the Den. After you prove you can face the Mottled Boars, Gornek hands you a parchment marked specifically for you. Durotar is harsh, and the Horde quickly gives its fighters guidance. The parchment directs you to Frang, the veteran warrior trainer outside the Den.

Singed Scale. In Durotar, Singed Scale comes from the charred plates of electrified thunder lizards. Horde warriors bring the scales to prove their endurance and learn defensive combat. Horde veterans judge a warrior by the blows they can bear while shielding allies. In Thunder Ridge, a canyon in western Durotar, lightning hides and thunder lizards crackle with storm energy. Hunting these beasts means enduring relentless electrical shocks and crushing blows. Their blackened scales show that a fighter can withstand punishing assaults and hold firm under pressure.

Singing Blue Shards. Crank Fizzlebub seeks an enterprising adventurer to gather Singing Crystal Shards from the basilisks of Stranglethorn Vale. Competition with the Venture Company prevents him from harvesting the mineral deposits directly, leaving basilisk hides as the next best option. He promises a cut of the profits to anyone willing to bring him ten decent specimens. Crank Fizzlebub has identified an eager market for the Singing Crystals unique to Stranglethorn Vale. Unfortunately for his business ambitions, the aggressive presence of the Venture Company makes it hard for him to gather raw crystal in the field. To circumvent his rivals, Fizzlebub turns to an alternative method: basilisks consume the crystals, incorporating the mineral into their hardened hides, which allows usable shards to be retrieved from them instead.

Sirra Von'Indi. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi studies the records that hold Duskwood's history. The town's historian knows ancient languages and helps decipher mysterious documents and the region's past. In Darkshire Town Hall, Sirra Von'Indi keeps the settlement's archives. While the town guard faces threats in the woods, he studies old texts and preserves the history of Grand Hamlet from before shadow fell across the region.

Sishir Canyon. Sishir Canyon runs east through the Stonetalon Mountains, crowded with Deepmoss spiders. Webs choke the gorge on the dangerous approach to the Ruins of Eldre'thar, where travelers face venomous spiders and their matriarch. Sishir Canyon cuts through the Stonetalon Mountains toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Deepmoss spiders have overrun the gorge, covering its stone floor and walls with sheets of web and clusters of egg sacs. Travelers and sentinels heading for the night elven ruins must fight their way through swarms of aggressive webspinners.

Sister Aquinne. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne studies beneath the Priesthood of Elune at the Temple of the Moon. The novice acolyte serves in the Temple Gardens. Sister Aquinne studies with the Priesthood of Elune in the night elf capital. She is stationed in the Temple Gardens, beneath the Temple of the Moon, learning from the High Priestess and elder sisters. When a once-great creature of the forest needed help, Aquinne sent willing travelers to Priestess A'moora inside the temple to learn what had to be done.

Skeleton Finger. In Duskwood, Skeleton Finger is gathered from the restless dead. Madame Eva of Darkshire collects these remains with ghoul fangs and spider venom to make protective talismans. The dead rise throughout Duskwood, from skeletal raiders and warriors to necrotic mages and fiends. Most travelers leave their foul remains untouched, but fortune tellers and mystics prize their cold essence. Madame Eva, the seer of Darkshire, gathers the bony fingers to bind their lingering necrotic energies into the Totem of Infliction, a ward that strikes back at attackers.

Skin of Sweet Rum. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Skin of Sweet Rum is bound for Lakeshire, where war has thinned the tavern's stores. Lakeshire's tavern supplies are running low as the Blackrock orc invasion cuts off the roads into the Redridge Mountains. Barkeep Daniels needs drink for the town guards and refugees, so he sends travelers to gather regional specialties. Among them is a waterskin of sweet rum from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire.

name.esES: Escaramuza en la Mina del Eco

text.enUS: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. In Northshire Valley, recruits strike at kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride ordered the attack after scouts found the mine overrun. Marshal McBride sends recruits against the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Scouts found the mine overrun, and the garrison fears the creatures will strengthen their hold if left alone. The kobolds dig through the tunnels, gather stolen resources, and multiply. Recruits must thin their numbers to protect Northshire Valley, with its farms and spiritual retreat.

Skittering Blood. Skittering Blood feeds the Royal Apothecary Society's work on a New Plague. The reagent comes from arachnids in the Skittering Dark of Silverpine Forest, where Forsaken alchemists seek a weapon against the Scourge and humanity. Skitterweb lurkers, strikers, and their broodmother Krethis the Shadowspinner yield a venomous blood. Apothecary Renferrel found that, refined with toxins from grizzled bear hearts, it forms the base of an exceptionally lethal elixir. Its contaminating agents make it useful in the Apothecarium's chemical experiments.

Skittering Dark. In western Silverpine, Skittering Dark lies abandoned beneath a web of danger. Giant spiders fill the mine and nearby woods, hunting unwary beasts and travelers. The Skittering Dark lies east of North Tide's Run, where the western coast meets the hills. Once a working mine, its shafts now lie choked with cobwebs and serve as a sprawling nest for giant spiders. Krethis haunts the shadowed woods outside, while the spiders hunt anything that strays too close.

Skorn Whitecloud. At Bloodhoof Village, aging tauren hunter Skorn Whitecloud guides young hunters and aids travelers facing Mulgore’s dangers. Skorn Whitecloud lives at Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, where he guides young hunters in the ways of the hunt. He teaches respect for the plains’ wild creatures. Aspiring hunters prove themselves against cunning flatland prowlers, then take the claws to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff. Skorn wants those who take up bow or spear to understand the balance between predator and prey.

Skuerto. Skuerto is a dwarven scout stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Sent there by Archmage Malin alongside Apprentice Kryten, he aids the Alliance in the field, helping secure magical relics on Malin's behalf. Skuerto, a dwarf of Ironforge, works as a scout in the dangerous Arathi Highlands. Stationed alongside Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, he works under the direction of Archmage Malin to recover arcane reagents and potent magical artifacts that once belonged to Malin's old master, Archmage Trelane.

Skulk Rock Clean-up. Fraggar Thundermantle of Aerie Peak wants a clean-up crew for the area around Skulk Rock, which the Horde abandoned and which is now overrun with sludges and oozes. The Wildhammers have plans for the area once it is clear. The Wildhammers remember the past, more than their brothers in Ironforge do, and Fraggar Thundermantle says friends are made here by getting your hands dirty. The Horde abandoned their positions around Skulk Rock in the Hinterlands, and nasty sludges and oozes have since overrun them. The Wildhammers have plans for that ground, but first it needs a hole made in the infestation.

Skull Rock. Margoz sends you into Skull Rock, east of Orgrimmar. Burning Blade cultists have overrun the cave and use painful demonic devices to bind themselves to dark magic. Margoz needs the cursed artifacts to study the cult's presence near the capital. In northeastern Durotar, cultists gather close to Orgrimmar's gates. The cave lies among the hills, far from the open roads, yet near the Warchief's seat. The Burning Blade, a demonic cult that has long plagued orcish society, has made its home in the tunnels. Its followers perform rituals there while the Warchief's scouts watch nearby.

Skull Rock. Burning Blade cultists gather at Skull Rock, hidden in Durotar's eastern coastal cliffs. Their cavern lies east of Orgrimmar, where they plot against Thrall's Horde. Burning Blade cultists gather in Skull Rock, a perilous stronghold beneath northeastern Durotar's crags. Dark cultists, fel-worshipping orcs, and summoners meet in its winding tunnels to practice demonic arts and plot against the young Horde. The warlock Gazz'uz leads the cell. Its work threatens Orgrimmar's nearby gates and travelers along the eastern shore.

Skullsplitter Tusks. Kebok in Booty Bay needs materials to meet export demands for tiger fangs destined for the South Seas. Because hunting genuine jungle predators proves too costly, he has devised an undetectable forging process using tusks harvested from the Skullsplitter trolls. Supplying tiger fangs to distant island buyers across the South Seas has grown too expensive and difficult through ordinary hunting. Rather than abandon the trade, Kebok devised an undetectable forging method that turns mundane horn-like objects into convincing replicas. The closest physical match for these fangs comes directly from the jaws of the local Skullsplitter trolls, leading Kebok to hire adventurers willing to strip eighteen tusks from the jungle tribe to fill his upcoming export shipment.

Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder appears atop Sentinel Tower in Westfall. Travelers climb to honor her and receive her blessing in return. Sentinel Hill holds against Defias raiders and roving scavengers in Westfall's troubled scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, an ancestral spirit named Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower. From above the dust and wind, she watches over the weary soldiers and beleaguered settlers below. Anyone may climb the tower and pay her respect.

Skyseer the Elder. Skyseer the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit residing atop Freewind Post during the Lunar Festival. Travelers seek out his presence high above Thousand Needles to pay their respects to the ancestors and receive his ancient blessing. Perched upon the lofty wooden bluffs of Freewind Post, Elder Skyseer appears bathed in a radiant pillar of celestial light. Positioned near the bridges leading toward the massive mechanical lifts, his ghostly presence offers a quiet sanctuary amid the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles.

Skywall. Skywall is the vast, storm-swept domain of the air elementals within the Elemental Plane. Banished here by the titans in ancient days, the creatures of wind, cloud, and lightning dwell under the reign of Al'Akir the Windlord. When the titans overthrew the Old Gods eons ago, they crafted the Elemental Plane as a secure dimensional prison to contain Azeroth's unruly elemental spirits. The lords of the elements fought fiercely amongst themselves, ultimately carving out distinct dominions. The realm of wind and storm became known as Skywall, ruled by Al'Akir the Windlord. While sealed away from the surface world, its tempests continue to swirl in eternal isolation.

Slag Pit. The Slag Pit is an extensive subterranean mining excavation nestled inside the Cauldron of Searing Gorge. Overseen by ruthless Dark Iron taskmasters and slavers, these fiery tunnels are driven by forced labor under the shadow of Blackrock Mountain. Trespassers must contend not only with hostile dwarf overseers, but also ravenous incendosaurs prowling the lower levels. Carved into the depths of the Cauldron, the Slag Pit represents the grinding industrial engine of the Dark Iron dwarves in Searing Gorge. Day and night, enslaved workers are driven to extract rich ores and minerals under the lash of brutal overseers and taskmasters. The environment is harsh and suffocating, dominated by scorching heat, choking dust, and the clatter of iron picks. The Dark Irons maintain ruthless discipline over their excavation, violently repelling any outside interference with their supply lines to Blackrock Depths.

Slake That Thirst. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan can supply the 4711-FTZ power source for your kit, but first wants something to drink: five Wastewander Water Pouches, to be had from the Wastewander nomads east of town. After Into the Field, you know the kit needs a power source, and Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan can help. The price is a drink: five Wastewander Water Pouches. Bilgewhizzle points you to the Wastewander nomads east of Gadgetzan, suggests you simply walk up to one and ask, and wants to hear how that works out.

Slaughter Hollow. In the snowy heights of the Alterac Mountains, Crushridge ogres hold Slaughter Hollow as a secluded camp. Travelers rarely come here except to hunt ogres or cross the frozen passes. Slaughter Hollow shelters the Crushridge ogres high in the peaks between Hillsbrad and Alterac. Makeshift fires, scattered bones, and crude shelters mark the mound. Other ogre dens in the highlands often see fights over territory or stolen supplies, but Slaughter Hollow stays quiet and beyond the reach of major military campaigns.

Slaughtered Lamb. Tucked away in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb appears to be nothing more than a quiet, seedy tavern. Beneath its floorboards, however, sprawling catacombs hide the sanctum and training grounds of the Alliance's illicit warlocks. On the surface, the Slaughtered Lamb offers little more than dark corners and sparse patronage, attended by barkeep Jarel Moor, who warns casual visitors to stay away from the shadows. That warning is literal. Descending through the back passages reveals a subterranean complex of crypts and summoning circles, where human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan openly study fel arcana sheltered from the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

Slaying the Beast. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Neeru Fireblade sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm to hunt Taragaman the Hungerer. He claims Warchief Thrall ordered the hunt and demands the towering felguard’s heart as proof the demonic cult has fallen. Ragefire Chasm lies beneath Orgrimmar’s red earthen streets, a fiery fissure filled with troggs, beasts, and covert Searing Blade agents. In the Cleft of Shadow above, Neeru Fireblade presents himself as a loyal servant carrying out Thrall’s order to cleanse this demonic rot. He points to Taragaman the Hungerer, a massive felguard in the cavern’s heart, and names him as the mastermind behind the cult below the city.

Sleepers' Key. At Stonetalon Peak, Sleepers' Key helps guard a sacred druidic vault. Night elf druids made it one of three enchanted keys for the Talon Den Hoard. The Talon Den rises on Stonetalon Peak as a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor. To guard sacred relics and potent treasures from unwanted attention, night elf keepers built a system of locks and hidden caches. Sleepers' Key is one of three keys that together form a protective ward. The key lies in a secluded cache deep in the den, opened with the Gatekeeper's Key hidden near the threshold. The Claw Key and the Barrow Key complete the set. Set all three into the Talon Den Hoard's stone locks, and the ward fades, revealing the ancient items within.

Slimy Menace. Slimy Menace addresses a growing murloc infestation along the shores of Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. These aggressive creatures threaten to deplete the lake's fish supply and endanger nearby locals, requiring swift action to keep their numbers in check. Along the eastern shore of Crystal Lake, an aggressive enclave of murlocs has established a foothold. These savage, semi-aquatic creatures possess sharp teeth and fierce tempers, turning a once-peaceful body of water into a dangerous feeding ground. Local residents rely heavily on the lake for their daily livelihoods, but the murloc presence now threatens anyone daring to fish or approach the water's edge.

Slither Rock. Slither Rock is a secluded cave tucked into the far northeastern cliffs of the Burning Steppes, past the perilous Terror Wing Path. It serves as the solitary refuge of Cyrus Therepentous, a sharp-tongued black dragonspawn with his own hidden agenda. Tucked away in the scorched crags beyond the Terror Wing Path, Slither Rock is easy to overlook amid the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. Far from the roaring forges and marching orc warbands of Blackrock Spire, this remote hollow houses the solitary black dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous. While dragonspawn are typically fiercely loyal soldiers of the Black Dragonflight, Cyrus maintains a strange, cantankerous independence here, willing to converse with mortal travelers rather than slaughtering them on sight—though never without a steady stream of insults.

Slithering Scar. The Slithering Scar is a sprawling silithid hive dominating the southern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Home to the aggressive Gorishi swarm, its excavated tunnels and organic spires represent a dangerous insectoid encroachment into the primeval basin. Gouged into the red earth and rock of southern Un'Goro, the Slithering Scar stands as an alien intrusion against the lush prehistoric landscape. The hive is controlled by the Gorishi silithid, an organized strain of insectoids that have honeycombed the cliffs with damp burrows and egg chambers. Within these subterranean warrens, workers and tunnelers nurture vast clutches of eggs and grubs alongside towering wasp broods. More alarmingly, the colony cultivates fledgling silithid colossi, monstrous behemoths intended to carve an uncontested path through the crater's ecology. Strange crystalline formations nestled within the hive pulse with unnatural resonance, acting as focal points for the colony's dark, coordinated will.

Sludge Fen. In northeastern the Barrens, Sludge Fen's clear pool has become an oily industrial field run by the Venture Company. Supervisor Lugwizzle oversees the drilling, while rivals in Ratchet seek to sabotage the operation. Sludge Fen once held a clear pool fed by natural springs in the arid Barrens. The Venture Company built oil-drilling platforms and machinery over the basin, turning the wetland into a reservoir of sludge and industrial waste. Supervisor Lugwizzle oversees goblin drillers, engineers, and overseers as they pump crude oil around the clock. Runoff and toxic byproducts coat the water, choking the native aquatic life beneath the grease.

Smart Drinks. Smart Drinks is an entrepreneurial scheme cooked up by the goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Having failed to brew an intellect-enhancing tonic out of Sunscale raptor horns, Mebok now tasks adventurers with delving into the Wailing Caverns to harvest ectoplasmic residue for his latest beverage formula. Operating out of the bustling port town of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic goblin philosophy of turning any bizarre regional phenomenon into cold, hard coin. Convinced that an intellect-boosting draught will make him an overnight tycoon, he originally believed powdered raptor horns held the secret. When that batch proved thoroughly underwhelming, he simply set his sights on an even more dubious ingredient: the corrupting essence seeping out of the nearby Wailing Caverns.

Smith Argus. At Goldshire's forge, Smith Argus keeps travelers and local smiths supplied. He repairs gear, teaches new smiths, and sends horseshoes to Redridge while coordinating with Stormwind craftsmen. Smith Argus works the forge near the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Gnolls, kobolds, and Defias bandits threaten the area, but Argus keeps the local militia and passing adventurers equipped. He mends armor and makes sturdy tools. As a blacksmithing trainer, he teaches new smiths to work copper and bronze.

Smith Mathiel. In Darnassus, sacred ore is on its way to the forge. After you recover elunite from the shipwreck off Auberdine, Elanaria sends you to Mathiel to have it shaped into a weapon for the Kaldorei. Elanaria sends you across Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace with the elunite ore you recovered from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine. The warrior trainer packs it in a sturdy case and directs you to Mathiel, one of the capital's finest smiths. He can shape the metal into a weapon worthy of your calling.

Smoky Iron Ingot. At the Windshear dig sites, kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots from ore they pull from the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcish armorers prize the bars as raw material for sturdy mail gear for Horde warriors. Kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots in the Windshear Crag tunnels of the Stonetalon Mountains. They dig ore from the rocky slopes and heat it over crude, smoking fires. Residue and charcoal cling to the bars, but the metal remains dense and strong.

Smoldering Embers. In the Charred Vale, Smoldering Embers remain after fire elementals are extinguished. Night elf Sentinels gather them as proof that the fires are being subdued. Venture Company logging and industry set the Charred Vale ablaze and stirred destructive forces from deep within the earth. Burning Ravagers, Burning Destroyers, and Rogue Flame Spirits then swept across the scorched basin. When an elemental is extinguished, its ash-covered core remains as a Smoldering Ember. These cinders show that the fires overrunning the vale are being brought under control.

Snapjaws, Mon!. In the Hinterlands, Katoom the Angler of Revantusk Village can barely keep a line in the water because saltwater snapjaws keep wrecking it and stealing his bait. He wants fifteen of the turtles dead. Katoom urges you not to be taken in by the snapjaws' large eyes and calls the turtles a menace. By his account, he cannot fish for even five minutes before one of them tears his line and makes off with his bait. He asks you, as a favor to himself and to his neighbours in the village, to wipe out the whole lot; the count is fifteen.

Snatch and Grab. Master Mathias Shaw sends agents to Jerod's Landing for shipping intelligence. The Defias Brotherhood uses the river dock to move supplies in secret. Master Mathias Shaw tests aspiring operatives who seek a place in Stormwind's covert intelligence wing. He asks for finesse and stealth, not brute force. SI:7 agents take down key figures quietly and recover important papers without drawing the realm into open scandal. Each new operative must prove they can work unseen.

Sneed. Deep in the Deadmines, Sneed directs the Defias Brotherhood’s timber work. From the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design to cut lumber for Edwin VanCleef’s secret juggernaut. The Defias Brotherhood draws most of its members from human stonemasons and laborers, but an ironclad warship needs skilled trades. Edwin VanCleef brought Sneed in for his engineering knowledge and ruthless efficiency. Sneed works in the Mast Room, beside the underground rail network. There he directs the felling, cutting, and shaping of timber for VanCleef’s colossal dreadnaught.

Sneed's Shredder. Deep in the Deadmines, Sneed's Shredder cuts timber and guards the works. Goblin taskmaster Sneed pilots the machine for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights, turning its blades against intruders. In the Deadmines foundry, goblin shredders cut timber for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut. They also meet intruders with armored force. Sneed oversees the lumber works and pilots this modified machine himself, wielding its oversized buzzsaw as a weapon of defense.

Snellig's Snuffbox. At the Lost Fleet, Snellig's Snuffbox remains with its undead owner among the wrecks. First Mate Fitzsimmons in Menethil Harbor wants it as proof his cursed crewmate has been put to rest. First Mate Snellig still clutches his snuffbox in a wreck off the northern Wetlands. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras ran aground there, its sailors and officers drowned beneath a mysterious power tied to a hidden treasure aboard the ships. Bound by that power, the drowned crew rose again as tortured spirits and skeletal undead. Snellig haunts the rotting hold of the wreck closest to the coastline. His snuffbox is a small, ordinary reminder of his mortal life at sea. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the disaster's sole living survivor, wants this possession returned as proof that at least one lost shipmate has found release from torment.

Snufflenose Command Stick. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix sends trained gophers after blueleaf tubers in Razorfen Kraul. Mebok Mizzyrix has trained snufflenose gophers to find blueleaf tubers deep in Razorfen Kraul. The roots lie hidden beneath the thorny tunnels, where finding them is nearly impossible without help. Mebok, a merchant in Ratchet, avoids entering the quilboar dens himself. He gives adventurers the Snufflenose Command Stick to direct the gophers. From up to fifty paces away, the stick guides them to sniff out and uncover the roots.

Snufflenose Owner's Manual. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix keeps Snufflenose Owner's Manual beside him. Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc. wrote the booklet to explain how to send a trained Snufflenose Gopher after Blueleaf Tubers in Razorfen Kraul. Marwig Rustbolt, owner of Snuff Inc., wrote a guide to handling the company's trained snufflenose gophers. Their keen noses can detect Blueleaf Tubers buried underground from fifty paces away. The manual explains how to release a gopher from a ventilated crate and guide its rooting with a command stick. Prospectors direct it through Razorfen Kraul's thorns and quilboar tunnels to find the tubers.

Sodium Nitrate. At Bael Modan, Sodium Nitrate helps the dwarves blast through the southern Barrens’ stone. Gann Stonespire seeks the chemical for charges against the fortress. Dwarven excavators at Bael Modan use Sodium Nitrate to break through the southern Barrens’ rock. The Bael'dun expedition entered the Stonespire tribe’s ancestral lands with earthmovers and blasting reagents. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry the chemical inside the excavation works and nearby fortress.

Soft Saber Pelts. Soft Saber Pelts represents a trade agreement aimed at keeping wilderness roads secure from predatory cats. Hunters bring in the thick furs of local sabers so they can be crafted into warm, protective blankets and shawls. Traversing the untamed paths of Azeroth requires constant vigilance against prowling predators. Large sabers frequently roam near well-traveled thoroughfares, presenting a persistent hazard to couriers, merchants, and lone adventurers. While local inhabitants admire the grace and majesty of these great cats, allowing their numbers to swell unchecked along trade routes invites deadly ambushes. Gathering hunters to keep the local roads safe serves as a necessary measure for communal survival.

Solliden Farmstead. At Solliden Farmstead, human farmers still tend pumpkins in western Tirisfal Glades, just north of Deathknell. These native Lordaeronians survived the Plague of Undeath, a rare sight in northern Lordaeron, and hold fiercely to their soil beneath the Scarlet Crusade’s shadow. Solliden Farmstead’s fields still yield healthy crops while much of Lordaeron lies in ruin and rot. The surviving human farmers are traumatized and insular, living beneath the watch of Scarlet Crusade patrols from a nearby tower. They defend their home with fierce hostility, striking at outsiders who come near, whether Horde or Alliance.

Solm Hargrin. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Solm Hargrin teaches rogues the quiet arts. The dwarf trains young dwarves and gnomes, and holds that honor among thieves matters as tensions rise across Azeroth. Solm Hargrin trains rogues at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He welcomes young dwarves and gnomes, deciphers coded messages for them, and teaches techniques such as Eviscerate. Ironforge relies on mountaineers and warriors, but Solm knows some threats call for quieter methods. He teaches loyalty and honor among thieves as the world grows more unsettled.

Solomon's Law. In Lakeshire, Solomon's Law puts the Shadowhide gnolls under sentence of death for aiding Morganth, an enemy of Stormwind. Bailiff Conacher issues the decree from the town hall and seeks proof that the sentence has been carried out. Lakeshire governs Redridge with little military help from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon and the town officials rely on strict frontier authority to keep order. Bailiff Conacher works from the town hall as the magistrate court's arm. When threats reach the township, the court places bounties on offenders and depends on hired mercenaries and traveling defenders to uphold the kingdom's laws.
