text.enUS: Solomon's Plea to Darkshire. Magistrate Solomon asks Darkshire for aid as Lakeshire faces mounting threats. His urgent letter to Lord Ello Ebonlocke requests the Night Watch to help defend Redridge. Lakeshire faces attacks from Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, with few reinforcements arriving from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon sends a formal plea to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire, asking him to send Night Watch militia north into Redridge. With central military support failing across southern Azeroth, human settlements must seek help from one another to survive.

name.frFR: Demande d'aide de Salomon à la marche de l'Ouest
name.ptBR: Apelo de Salomão a Cerro Oeste
name.zhCN: 所罗门写给西部荒野的求救信

text.enUS: Solomon's Plea to Westfall. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent appeal to Westfall for help against Blackrock orcs and gnolls. He asks Gryan Stoutmantle to send the People's Militia while Stormwind's royal army fails to answer. Blackrock orcs and hostile gnolls threaten Redridge, and Magistrate Solomon is isolated in Lakeshire. Stormwind's royal army has not arrived in force to defend the region's borders. With no time to wait for support from the capital, Solomon writes to seek help beyond the regular army. Word has reached him of a volunteer defense force forming in Elwynn to the west, so he appeals to the People's Militia.

Some Assembly Required. In Booty Bay, Drizzlik reports that the boots are taking shape, but the skins you supplied will not cover the inner layers. Drizzlik proposes filling them out with cheaper, thicker hides from crocolisks near Lake Nazferiti. Drizzlik has settled the rough form of the boots and says they are coming along nicely, yet the skins from Supply and Demand do not go far enough for the insides. Nobody will ever see those layers, so Drizzlik will make do with thicker, cheaper hides from the crocolisks near Lake Nazferiti.

Songblade Search. Songblade Search is a dwarven errand in which Dorin Songblade asks travelers to check on his brother Daewyn in the Wetlands. Daewyn set off with an archaeological crew from Loch Modan to dig in unexplored hills, but his uncharacteristic silence left his brother fearing the worst. Dorin Songblade remained behind at his workshop, inundated with orders to refit girdles, while his brother Daewyn joined a dwarven excavation crew setting out from Loch Modan. Daewyn ventured north into the rugged hills of the Wetlands, eager to explore virgin ground untouched by dwarven pickaxes. However, Daewyn customarily sends letters immediately after arriving, and his silence left Dorin deeply unsettled.

Soothing Spices. "Swamp Eye" Jarl loves cooking, swamp style, and needs soothing spice for a stew. Jarl in Dustwallow Marsh asks you to bring three Soothing Spices. "Swamp Eye" Jarl is fond of cooking in the swamp manner, with fried green frog legs among the dishes. A stew is planned, and for it Jarl needs soothing spice. Whoever brings it will be given a share. Jarl wants three Soothing Spices, and wonders whether you like stew.

Soothing Turtle Bisque. Southshore's Chef Jessen wants Soothing Turtle Bisque back on his tavern menu. Unrest has cut off his supply of snapjaw turtle meat, so he asks cooks to brave the northern waters near Dalaran and Lake Lordamere. Southshore is one of the Alliance's last intact coastal towns in Lordaeron, holding to civilian life amid growing strife. Chef Jessen says his cooking rivals any tavern north of Stormwind. Patrons supposedly travel from Darkshire in Duskwood to taste his Soothing Turtle Bisque. The rich soup depends on fresh meat from snapjaw turtles native to the rivers and lakes of the northern mountains.

Soothing Turtle Bisque. In Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat is trying to prove the Forsaken can cook with care. He needs snapjaw meat from Hillsbrad's waterways and the shores of Lordamere Lake for his turtle bisque. Many believe the Forsaken have left the comforts of life behind, including fine cooking. Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill rejects that belief. He boasts that his rich turtle bisque could tempt souls back from beyond the grave. Through careful cooking, he means to show that undead hands can still make a warming dish in a land marked by plague and war.

Soran'ruk Fragment. In Blackfathom Deeps, cultists hold shards of Soran'ruk, a shattered prison orb. The pieces still carry fel energy from the demon once bound inside. Soran'ruk's prison orb was broken apart after the demon fell from favor with the Burning Legion. Demons who displease their masters may have their spirits sealed in orbs, then given to fel spellcasters as sources of power. The Twilight's Hammer cultists in the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps possess smaller shards from one half of the orb. They draw on the lingering demonic essence for their own workings.

Sorrow Hill. Sorrow Hill is an expansive graveyard resting south of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once the final resting place for commoners, soldiers, and nobility alike, it has been corrupted by nearby plague cauldrons into a sprawling haven of restless undead. Before the Third War, Sorrow Hill served as the primary burial ground for the city of Andorhal and its surrounding townships. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath, the gravediggers could not keep pace with the dead. Neatly kept crypts were soon surrounded by shallow, poorly marked earthen pits. Eventually, terrified survivors ceased traditional burials entirely, instead resorting to burning the corpses of their loved ones in a mass pyre to the south out of fear they would rise. Before the town fell completely, the remnants of the populace entombed Lord Uther the Lightbringer atop the cemetery's high ground, bestowing upon the hill its tragic name.

Sorrowmurk. The Sorrowmurk is the treacherous wetland expanse lying directly east of the Pool of Tears in the Swamp of Sorrows. Long dominated by patrolling green dragonkin guarding the approach to the Sunken Temple, it remains one of the most perilous regions in the eastern marshes. Stretching out along the eastern edge of the Pool of Tears, the Sorrowmurk is a dense and murky mire that borders the Forbidding Sea. For years, the waters and tangled boughs have crawled with ferocious green dragonspawn and towering drakes, remnants of the brood sent to watch over the submerged temple of Atal'Hakkar. Their presence ensures that only seasoned travelers dare wander through its sodden reaches.

name.ptBR: Posto de Guarda do Portão Sul

text.enUS: South Gate Outpost. Travelers stream through South Gate Outpost, a fortified post on the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Its mountaineers guard the southern road between Ironforge's frigid heights and the Loch's temperate valley. South Gate Outpost marks the frontier between Dun Morogh's snowy slopes and Loch Modan's basin. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the rocky switchbacks and keep dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Unlike their hard-pressed kin at North Gate Outpost, these defenders have largely secured their stretch of road. Travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons can journey toward Thelsamar in relative safety.

South Gate Pass. South Gate Pass carries travelers between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Its guarded road links Ironforge with Thelsamar. South Gate Pass cuts through the Khaz Modan range, joining the high mountains of Dun Morogh to Loch Modan's valley in the east. Stone archways mark the way from the cold slopes into the warmer dwarven heartlands. The road leads toward Thelsamar, carrying mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital.

South Seas. The South Seas encompass the vast, sun-drenched waters separating the southern regions of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Lapping at the shores of Tanaris and Stranglethorn Vale, these tropical expanses are famed for lucrative trade routes, perilous reefs, and brazen pirate crews. Spanning southward beneath the Great Sea and the Maelstrom, the South Seas wash against the deserts of Tanaris and the lush jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Since the Great Sundering shattered the primeval continent ten thousand years ago, this ocean has nurtured remote tropical islands, unique oceanic beasts, and independent merchant networks. Goblin shipping cartels, operating out of havens like Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, maintain tenuous shipping lanes across the waves. However, the waters remain notoriously lawless, crawling with corsairs, Bloodsail buccaneers, and predatory sea life that prey on any vessel daring to venture far from shore.

South Tide's Run. South Tide's Run follows Silverpine Forest's southwestern edge beside the cold Great Sea. These damp shores border the forested interior and form the southern counterpart to North Tide's Run. Along Silverpine Forest's southwestern edge, the Great Sea meets a desolate shore. The eastern roads lead toward the Greymane Wall under the forest's protection, but this open coastline takes the western tides. The bleak stretch remains largely untouched by the settlements inland.

Southern Gold Road. Caravans and travelers crowd the Southern Gold Road as it runs through the Barrens toward the Great Lift. Trade links the central plains with distant reaches of Kalimdor. At the stone bridge between the northern and southern Barrens, the Southern Gold Road turns south toward the Great Lift and Thousand Needles. Like the northern stretch, simply called the Gold Road, it takes its name from the lucrative merchant caravans that travel its length. Quilboar tribes and prowling predators harass those who use it, yet the road remains one of the continent’s busiest long-distance routes. Goods pass along it between remote outposts and ports.

Southern Savage Coast. The Southern Savage Coast encompasses the long strand of beaches and tidal waters hugging southwestern Stranglethorn Vale. Flanked by the treacherous depths of the South Seas, these shores are home to prowling wildlife, hostile naga, and the ever-present threat of coastal raiders. Stretching down the western edge of the southern jungle, the Southern Savage Coast marks where the mainland gives way to the warm currents of the South Seas. Divided from the northern Savage Coast by the submerged ruins and perils of the Vile Reef, this coastline skirts inlets near the Gurubashi Arena and Nek'mani Wellspring before tapering off past Booty Bay and Janeiro's Point. While the beaches offer open ground compared to the suffocating interior jungle, travelers must contend with aggressive reptilian predators, predatory naga hunting the shallows, and passing corsairs scanning the strand for easy prey.

Southfury River. The Southfury River is one of the most prominent waterways on central Kalimdor, carving a swift and wide path southward from the heights of Mount Hyjal. It forms the natural border separating Azshara from Ashenvale, as well as Durotar from the Barrens, before plunging into the Great Sea near Ratchet. Beginning high in Mount Hyjal, the Southfury drops over dramatic cascades before coursing through central Kalimdor. Its roaring waters serve as a clear geographic divide, separating the sacred forests of Ashenvale from ancient Azshara, and dividing the arid hills of Durotar from the savanna of the Barrens. Only a few strategic bridges dare cross its swift currents—most notably the heavy span guarding the rear gates of Orgrimmar and the crossing connecting Durotar to the Barrens. The river eventually empties into the Great Sea via a cascading waterfall just northeast of the neutral port of Ratchet.

Southmoon Ruins. The Southmoon Ruins are ancient stone remains situated in southern Tanaris, just north of the Valley of the Watchers. Long claimed by the brutish Dunemaul ogres, the crumbling stonework preserves remnants of the ancient troll civilization that dominated the desert before the sands swallowed it. Rising out of the blistering wastes of southern Tanaris, the Southmoon Ruins stand as a weathered testament to the ancient troll empires that once ruled Kalimdor's southern reaches. Like nearby Eastmoon and Noonshade, its stone pillars and altars have weathered thousands of years of wind and abrasive grit. The site has often served as a squalid camp for the Dunemaul ogres, who show little reverence for the craftsmanship of the past, using the ancient structures purely for shelter and territory.

name.frFR: Tour de la Pointe du Midi

text.enUS: Southpoint Tower. Forsaken scouts watch Alliance movements from Southpoint Tower, near Hillsbrad's western edge. The ruined Lordaeron post overlooks the road into Silverpine Forest. Southpoint Tower overlooks the highway between Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills. The Kingdom of Lordaeron built it to guard traffic between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. After the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Now the tower stands roofless and crumbling, a remnant of human rule in fractured lands.

Southridge Beach. Southridge Beach stretches along the southern shores of the Bay of Storms in central Azshara. Once a grand district of the ancient kaldorei city of Eldarath, its shattered ruins are now overrun by hostile naga, murlocs, and towering sea giants. Southridge Beach forms the southern boundary of the turbulent Bay of Storms. Thousands of years ago, this coast was part of the magnificent Highborne city of Eldarath, but the Great Sundering broke the land and plunged most of its palaces beneath the tides. Today, crumbling marble pillars and weathered stone pavilions dot the sand. Rather than scholars and noble courtiers, the strand is contested by aggressive Spitelash naga, prowling makrura, vicious hydras, and scavenging murloc tribes. Even massive sea giants occasionally wander ashore from the deeps.

name.esES: Los filibusteros de los Mares del Sur
name.frFR: Les flibustiers des mers du Sud
name.ptBR: Os Flibusteiros dos Mares do Sul

text.enUS: Southsea Freebooters. Along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Southsea Freebooters strike goblin trading vessels. Gazlowe hires adventurers to attack their camp and curb the raids. Ratchet's trade suffers from pirates on the Merchant Coast. The port sits in central Kalimdor, where merchant vessels travel between Kalimdor and the eastern continents. South of town, Southsea Freebooters hold a fortified beach camp. From there, they attack goblin cargo ships arriving and departing, cutting into profits and disrupting local shipping lanes.

name.esES: Tesoro de los Mares del Sur

text.enUS: Southsea Treasure. The Southsea Treasure is a valuable hoard kept deep within the hold of the Southsea Freebooter vessel, the Tide Razor. Sought by Wrenix the Wretched in Ratchet, retrieving it tests the lockpicking and infiltration skills of fledgling thieves. Anchored along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, the pirate vessel Tide Razor serves as a forward base and training ground for the Southsea Freebooters. Stashed deep in its lowest hold lies a coveted stash of plunder known as the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin scoundrel operating out of Ratchet, considers it the ultimate test for aspiring pickpockets. According to Wrenix, the last five operatives sent to filch the chest returned in pieces, owing to the alert pirates aboard and a surprisingly ferocious guardian guarding the hold.

Southshore. Southshore is a coastal human port in the Hillsbrad Foothills and one of the Alliance's few surviving strongholds in fallen Lordaeron. Once a sleepy fishing village, it now stands as an embattled bastion facing constant hostility from the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, rogue Syndicate bandits, and shoreline monsters. Southshore first rose to prominence during the First War when refugee boats carrying survivors from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind landed upon its beaches. Though contested and overrun during the Second War, it was rebuilt and later endured the horrors of the Third War. Today, while the rest of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under the rule of the Forsaken, Southshore remains fiercely loyal to the Grand Alliance. It offers shelter to displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor.

Southshore Town Hall. At Southshore Town Hall, Magistrate Henry Maleb directs the town’s affairs and defenses. It remains one of Lordaeron’s last centers of civil authority, while the Alliance struggles to hold ground in the plagued north. Southshore Town Hall keeps human rule alive amid Lordaeron’s ruin. Magistrate Henry Maleb governs from his office, working with officials such as Kundric Zanden to secure supplies and preserve order. Undead press from nearby lands, Syndicate rogues threaten the region, and Hillsbrad’s border sees fierce skirmishes. From the hall, town leaders direct Southshore’s survival against these threats.

Southwind Village. Southwind Village is the haunted ruin of a night elf outpost located in the sands of Silithus. Wiped out by the qiraji during the War of the Shifting Sands, its streets are now bound by the restless spirits of fallen defenders and prowling silithid. Southwind Village once served as a primary night elf stronghold during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands a thousand years ago. When the qiraji legions breached the defensive perimeter, Valstann Staghelm—son of Archdruid Fandral Staghelm—led a detachment to hold the village. The defense ended in utter disaster: the night elven defenders were overwhelmed and slaughtered, and Valstann himself was dragged away into captivity by General Rajaxx. The village was completely ruined, leaving its former buildings fractured under the sun.

Souvenirs of Death. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa envies those sent against the human settlements of the Hillsbrad Foothills. He asks for thirty human skulls taken in battle for his collection. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign against Hillsbrad's human settlements. Deathguard Samsa remains on sentry duty in Tarren Mill, while others are sent to raid, burn, and pillage. He envies their chance to slaughter the living, a privilege denied to a guard fixed in place.

Sparring Match. Sparring Match is an introductory trial overseen by the martial instructor Tang Stonehoof. Designed to test newcomers regardless of their class or background, the trial challenges adventurers to defeat three arena novices or fellow duelists to prove their mettle in direct combat. Overseen by the veteran instructor Tang Stonehoof, the sparring match invites adventurers of all backgrounds into the ring to test their mettle. Though Tang specifically acknowledges those who walk paths outside the warrior tradition, he maintains that martial discipline and direct battle offer universal wisdom to any traveler in a dangerous world.

Speak with Anastasia. In the Undercity, Cain Firesong sends a promising Forsaken mage to Anastasia Hartwell. Her summons calls you to the Magic Quarter for work among the Forsaken magi, with investigations in Tirisfal Glades ahead. Cain Firesong trains young Forsaken mages in Brill, then sends those with promise to the Undercity. In its Magic Quarter, the Forsaken magi pursue arcane study and plan defenses across Lordaeron. Cain judges which students are ready to serve more experienced practitioners. Those who show real talent are sent to Anastasia Hartwell, who needs capable hands in the field.

Speak with Bink. In Dun Morogh, Magis Sparkmantle sends novice mages to Ironforge at Bink's request. Bink needs an arcane specialist for her studies in the Hall of Mysteries. Magis Sparkmantle sends word from his colleague Bink to mages training near Kharanos. She asks for an arcane specialist and will trust the matter only to someone who can wield magic. When an apprentice has outgrown the early exercises, Sparkmantle directs them to answer her call.

Speak with Coleman. In Brill, Deathguard Dillinger sends proven fighters to Coleman Farthing for help. The tavern meeting opens the way to a private matter tied to the old Agamand lands. After you help contain grave threats near Brill, including Ulag the Cleaver, Deathguard Dillinger trusts your strength. He watches the roads into town and decides which fighters can take on work beyond the usual patrols. When he sees you are ready, he points you toward people who need specialized help.

Speak with Deino. In Orgrimmar, Deino calls promising Horde mages to aid their craft. The troll mage works from the Valley of Spirits and seeks an adept for important work. Her summons opens a path to deeper study and duties across Kalimdor. Horde mages hone their arcane abilities under the guidance of instructors. When a student is ready for harder work, mentors such as Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity point the way to Orgrimmar. In its troll quarter, specialized knowledge and dangerous work await.

Speak with Dillinger. In Brill, Austil de Mon sends fighters to Deathguard Dillinger for a hazardous mission in service of Lady Sylvanas. The order begins at the Gallows' End Tavern, where the warrior trainer directs able-bodied recruits to the west end of the village. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, warrior trainer Austil de Mon seeks fighters willing to serve the Dark Lady. When the Deathguards need capable hands, he sends untested recruits into the field. Deathguard Dillinger oversees security on Brill's western edge and has requested someone with martial skill for an urgent task.

Speak with Gramma. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks Gramma Stonefield's help to meet Maybell Maclure. Their families' bitter feud keeps the young lovers apart, and Tommy Joe hopes his grandmother can find a way for them to see each other. Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure keep their romance secret from their feuding families. The Stonefields and Maclures have fought over their farms for years, making their neighboring homesteads hostile ground. Tommy Joe wants to meet Maybell without provoking violence between their kin, so he turns to his grandmother for help.

Speak with Jennea. In Goldshire, Zaldimar Wefhellt sends novice mages to Stormwind for further instruction. He directs apprentices who have advanced beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest to Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum. Zaldimar Wefhellt sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind City as your training advances. Your time learning elementary spells from local tutors in Elwynn's hamlets has run its course. In the Mage Quarter, the Wizard's Sanctum is where the kingdom's senior mages pursue arcane study and instruction. They coordinate magical matters across the realm.

Speak with Renferrel. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel needs to discuss the tainted wolf hearts. High Executor Hadrec sends you back to the Royal Apothecary Society researcher with your findings. After you help the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec gives you an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has studied the discolored wolf hearts gathered from local wildlife and needs you at once.

Speak with Sevren. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren calls you north after Coleman Farthing's reckoning at Agamand Mills. The undead there threaten the settlement's northern border. Coleman Farthing wanted revenge on his former neighbors, the Agamands, and sent travelers north to kill the undead around their flour mills. After you delivered the remains, Coleman saw that his private grudge touched a wider danger. The Agamand estate still crawls with aggressive Scourge minions, close to Brill.

Speak with Shoni. Alliance travelers in Ironforge are sent south to find Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind. She leads an underground assault unit preparing to support the effort to reclaim Gnomeregan. After Gnomeregan fell to radiation, surviving gnomes made an exile quarter in Ironforge. Engineers, tinkers, and strategists there keep planning how to breach their lost home. Central planning remains in Tinkertown, but preparations reach far beyond Khaz Modan. Adventurers in the mountain city are directed south to Stormwind, where specialized military hardware is being prepared for fighting underground.

Speak with Thun'grim. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze, an acclaimed orc blacksmith camping in the Barrens. Having proved themselves through demanding physical trials, warriors are invited to have custom armor forged in recognition of their valor. The quest serves as the crucial bridge connecting general warrior testing with the crafting of Brutal Armor. After proving their mettle against the silithid hives during the Trial at the Field of Giants, Horde warriors earn more than simple praise from Ruga Ragetotem. Word of their endurance and martial prowess quickly reaches Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc smith who maintains a camp perched on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Recognizing a warrior worthy of his craft, Thun'grim sends word that he wishes to fashion them an exceptional suit of battle mail.

Speaking of Fortitude. Brother Kristoff prepares a sermon in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light. For his message on the Fortitude of the Spirit, he seeks a book in Stormwind Keep's Royal Library. Brother Kristoff, a priest in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, is preparing a sermon on the Fortitude of the Spirit. He wants to draw on the craft of metalworking alongside scripture. To make his point, he needs a treatise called "The Stresses of Iron." Its lessons on bearing pressure may help his congregation understand the strength of faith.

Speaking with Gan'zulah. Even after losing his head to the boiling brew at Grom'gol Base Camp, the Bloodscalp chieftain Gan'zulah seethes with fury. To appease his lingering rage, the severed spirit demands the death of his bitter Skullsplitter rivals and the ruin of their ruler, Ana'thek the Cruel. Following the collection of the Bloodscalp Clan Heads, Gan'zulah's severed head continues to curse anyone standing over the bubbling pot. Consumed by hatred for both his captors and his ancestral enemies, the dead chieftain offers an avenue to quiet his boiling temper: an assault into the eastern stronghold of the Skullsplitter tribe. He demands a slaughter of their hunters, headhunters, and berserkers, daring travelers to perish against their ferocious warband.

Speaking with Nezzliok. After defeating the Bloodscalp witch doctor, his severed head speaks from the bubbling cauldron at Grom'gol Base Camp. He claims to know where the lost Darkspear child was taken, but he refuses to give up the secret without a grim tribute. Though bound within the bubbling cauldron following the hunt for Bloodscalp Clan Heads, Nezzliok is far from cooperative. He admits knowing where Yenniku was taken, yet he demands appeasement before parting with the information. He commands that three trophy skulls be taken from the rival Skullsplitter tribe and brought to his resting place, ensuring his departed spirit will command thralls in the Nether.

text.enUS: Special Delivery for Gaxim. In Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle awaits a scroll from Stormwind. Collin Mauren provides the Scroll of Messaging, whose arcane power is needed to build a remote explosive against the Venture Company's deforestation. Gaxim Rustfizzle seeks to hinder the Venture Company's destructive work in the Stonetalon Mountains. He has made an explosive compound called NG-5, but lacks a reliable way to set it off from afar. Rather than use crude fuses, Gaxim enlisted help across the Great Sea. He contacted Collin Mauren in Stormwind's Mage Quarter to obtain an enchanted Scroll of Messaging.

Special Forces. Following the reduction of the rogue colonel's rank-and-file soldiers, Sergeant Yohwa asks you to target the elite core of the compound. You are sent into the Stockpile cave to eliminate the commandos and headshrinkers before reporting to Lieutenant Doren. With the regular soldiers of the Kurzen Compound diminished through the work of the Second Rebellion, Sergeant Yohwa sets her sights on the colonel's elite specialists. She knows many of Kurzen's troops personally and calls them skilled, loyal and cruel. When they are not out in the wilderness slaughtering rebel soldiers, they are found in a cave at the back of the compound called the Stockpile. To break their strength, you are sent into the cavern to dispatch ten Kurzen Commandos and six Kurzen Headshrinkers.

Spectral Comb. At a ruined farmstead south of Darkshire, the Spectral Comb gathers ghost hair from Blind Mary. Ghostly hair lies beyond the reach of ordinary combs, leaving mortal craftsmen few ways to gather such fibers. The Spectral Comb can pass through a spirit’s intangible tresses. Carried south of Darkshire to a ruined farmstead, it is offered to Blind Mary, a weeping ghost who wails alone. Grooming brings her solace, and she willingly uses the comb. The spectral fibers she leaves behind can be woven into Ghost Hair Thread.

Spellfire Robes. In the Undercity, Spellfire Robes mark a young Horde mage's rite of passage. Josef Gregorian, a tailor, completes the robes after the apprentice gathers rare components from across the realm. In Lordaeron, you seek more than ordinary cloth to channel and shield your growing magic. Josef Gregorian works as a tailor in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where he weaves magical garments from specialized materials gathered by promising Horde spellcasters. The final stitching marks your passage beyond basic incantations toward mastery of arcane and fire magic.

Spells of Shadow. Beneath Orgrimmar, Spells of Shadow rests in the hands of Searing Blade cultists. The Forsaken leadership in the Undercity wants the grimoire recovered. Searing Blade cultists keep Spells of Shadow among their guarded treasures in Ragefire Chasm. The splinter cult is tied to the Shadow Council, and its members wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. The book holds shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks keep it close as they plot beneath the Horde in Durotar.

Spirit Rise. Spirit Rise gathers Thunder Bluff’s spiritual and shamanic study on its northwest mesa. The Skychaser tribe guides seekers above the Pools of Vision, where seers look into spirit-touched waters. Spirit Rise crowns Thunder Bluff above the plains of Mulgore, devoted to communion with the elements and ancestor spirits. Rope bridges link it to the central mesa. The Hall of Spirits and the Spiritual Healing pavilion draw young and veteran shaman seeking a deeper bond with earth, air, fire, and water. The Skychaser tribe keeps a strong presence across the rise and guides seekers in ancient traditions.

Spirit Rock. Above the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Spirit Rock draws Horde initiates to commune with the elements. A winding trail called the Hidden Path leads to this sacred crag. Spirit Rock overlooks the red canyon where young Horde warriors and scouts train. The Hidden Path winds up the rocky ridgeline to this quiet altar. Aspiring shaman climb to the outcrop and drink sapta, a traditional brew that opens their senses beyond the physical world. They listen for the earth's rumblings and whispers.

Spirit of the Wind. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a burst of speed drawn from Agamaggan's blood shards. The captive quilboar's ritual helps them cross the Barrens swiftly. Crossing the Barrens quickly can help you avoid its beasts and centaur warbands. At Camp Taurajo, the captive quilboar Mangletooth draws on red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. Give him ten, and he channels their lingering power into a burst of swiftness called the Spirit of the Wind.

Splinterspear Junction. Splinterspear Junction is a strategic fork in the main road winding through the heart of the Swamp of Sorrows. Dominated by a rugged orc watchtower and regularly patrolled by Horde sentries, it divides the path between northern retreats and southern outposts. Standing near the center of the Swamp of Sorrows, Splinterspear Junction divides travelers between two paths: the northern trail leading toward the Lost One refuge of the Harborage and the Fallow Sanctuary, and the southern road running directly past the fortress of Stonard toward the Blasted Lands. An ancient orcish watchtower oversees the split, garrisoned and patrolled by active Horde troops. For members of the Horde, it serves as a secure landmark in a treacherous marsh; for Alliance travelers, it represents a deadly ambush point along an already unforgiving trail.

Splintertree Post. Splintertree Post holds the Horde’s eastern Ashenvale frontier, northwest of Felfire Hill. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan established it during the Third War as a fortified base against the night elves and a staging ground for expansion. Splintertree Post anchors the Horde’s military and supply lines across eastern Ashenvale. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan founded it when the orcs first entered the forest during the Third War. Orcish and tauren scouts and warriors still defend the armed outpost. An inn, a flight master, and steady supplies from Orgrimmar support the Horde’s contested hold beneath the trees.

Split Bone Necklace. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp calls upon Horde allies to hunt the Skullsplitter tribe living to the southeast. Although the Darkspears left Stranglethorn Vale behind, their ancient conflict with these jungle rivals remains unresolved. Returning with twenty-five split bone trophies aids the Darkspears in their war and earns their friendship. Following the collection of Bloodscalp trophies, Kin'weelay turns his attention toward another longstanding enemy. The Skullsplitter tribe dwells to the southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp, where they have clashed with the Darkspears across many years. Even though the Darkspears no longer reside within the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale, they remain bound to this enduring war.

Splithoof Crag. Splithoof Crag is a fortified settlement of the Galak centaur, tucked along the northern cliffs of Thousand Needles. It serves as one of the tribe's major enclaves alongside the high mesas, guarding the entrance to Splithoof Hold. Travelers traversing the canyon floor must contend with aggressive Galak patrols roaming near the bluffs. Nestled against the sheer northern rock face of Thousand Needles, Splithoof Crag sits just east of the towering Darkcloud Pinnacle. It is an established enclave of the Galak centaur, complete with crude tent encampments and dirt pathways cutting through the crags. At the heart of the village against the cliffside lies Splithoof Hold, a subterranean cavern holding the Cloven Hoof, an ancient relic of the centaur safeguarded by a sacred brazier.

Splithoof Hold. Splithoof Hold is a deep cavern stronghold carved into the stone of Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles. Held by the Galak centaur tribe, the cavern serves as a fortified den and houses the Ancient Brazier, a site holding an eternally burning sacred flame. Tucked away inside Splithoof Crag, Splithoof Hold serves as a fortified redoubt for the Galak centaur. Unlike the windswept canyon floor, this enclosed cave offers them shelter, defensible chokepoints, and a secure sanctuary from rival tribes and travelers passing through the Needles.

Spotted Sunfish. At Lake Everstill, Spotted Sunfish draw fishers and hungry murlocs alike. The fish bring trade to Lakeshire, though murlocs make the shallows dangerous. Spotted Sunfish bring trade to the Lakeshire piers. Dockmaster Baren buys them from the lake's steady catch, supplying food and commerce to a town under strain. Aggressive murloc tribes prowl the shallows and disrupt fishing. They gather sunfish at their camps, where travelers can take the fish by force.

Sprinkle's Secret Ingredient. After Marin Noggenfogger's brew turns out foul, Sprinkle in Gadgetzan offers to make it edible with her secret ingredient, a mushroom called the Violet Tragan. It grows underwater in a small lake in the Hinterlands. Sprinkle tells of her childhood, when her sister did all the cooking and the results were hard to stomach. Then she found a mushroom, the Violet Tragan, her "secret" ingredient, and it made every dish taste wonderful. She will use it to help turn Marin's horrid brew into something drinkable.

Sprite Darter. Sprite Darters are small, iridescent faerie dragons native to the lush canopy of Feralas. Revered for their innate spiritual and magical qualities, they flit gracefully among the ancient trees. Recently, these rare creatures have become targets for local Grimtotem tauren who seek to capture and exploit them. Sprite Darters are elusive, winged woodland beasts native to the ancient forests of Feralas. Characterized by their gleaming, iridescent wings and mysterious spiritual essence, they embody the whimsical yet fierce magical ecology of Kalimdor's deep forests. Though generally peaceful and shy, their innate resistance to magical forces and natural power make them significant to those attuned to the wilderness.

Sprite Jumpsprocket. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Sprite Jumpsprocket works among gnomish and dwarven artisans. Like many gnomes who sought refuge after Gnomeregan fell, she pursues engineering alongside fellow tinkers. Sprite Jumpsprocket works as an apprentice engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District, where gnomes and dwarves forge metal and design intricate devices side by side. She has made her place in the kingdom's capital, where apprentice tinkers hone their craft under experienced masters. Their inventive minds help maintain the Alliance's everyday mechanisms and marvels.

Sputtervalve. Under pressure in Ratchet, Sputtervalve races to finish shredder research for the Tinkers' Union. Director Riddlevox holds him to crushing deadlines, and he hires adventurers to steal designs from the rival Venture Company. In Ratchet, Sputtervalve answers to Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union. The goblin engineer oversees shredder development and has found the work brutal. Modern mechanization moves fast, the Venture Company presses hard, and his own prototypes are few. With the deadline closing in, Sputtervalve fears admitting failure to the Union. He turns to a familiar goblin practice: stealing better designs from those who built them first.

Squire Maltrake. After The Torch of Retribution, Kalaran Windblade sends you on to Squire Maltrake, an envoy of theirs. Maltrake will tell you how the torch is to be used. Kalaran Windblade points you toward Squire Maltrake, an envoy. Maltrake is the one who will explain how the Torch of Retribution is to be used.

Stagalbog. The Stagalbog is a dense, waterlogged marsh stretch across the southern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bordering the southern mountain range just below the Pool of Tears, it remains an untamed wilderness. Stretching beneath the shadow of the southern crags, the Stagalbog is typical of the Swamp of Sorrows: stagnant water, drooping reeds, and tangled vegetation. It sits immediately south of the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, caught between the tainted lake and the rocky boundary of the region. Apart from rough wildlife, civilization has established no foothold here.

Stagalbog Cave. Stagalbog Cave is a damp subterranean cavern situated in the Stagalbog within the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as a fortified den for the Marsh murlocs and their sinister spiritual leader, the Swamp Talker. Tucked away in the murky eastern wetlands of the Swamp of Sorrows, Stagalbog Cave provides shelter from the relentless swamp rains for the local murlocs. Known as the Marsh tribe, these amphibious creatures aggressively guard the winding cavern chambers alongside their chief mystic, the Swamp Talker. Travelers venturing near the sunken mire of the Stagalbog often hear their gurgling calls echoing out across the mossy banks, warning trespassers away from their nesting grounds.

Staghelm Point. Staghelm Point is an ancient night elven watchtower perched atop a craggy peak in northeastern Silithus. Overlooking the encroaching dunes and the nearby caverns of Twilight's Run, the tower stands as a vigil against the ancient threats haunting the desert. Rising high above the arid flats of northeastern Silithus, Staghelm Point is crowned by a solitary night elf tower. The outpost serves as a lonely sentinel, keeping watch over the wasteland and the shadowed cultists lurking in nearby caves like Twilight's Run. Watched over by Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher and accompanied by a bronze drake circling overhead, the tower bears the proud and tragic name of the Staghelm lineage—a reminder of the immense sacrifices made by the Kaldorei during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands.

Stagnant Oasis. Kolkar centaur guard the Stagnant Oasis in the dry heart of the Barrens. Its waters lie between the Gold Road and Merchant Coast, drawing wildlife to its banks. East of the Gold Road, inland from the Merchant Coast, the Stagnant Oasis breaks up the dusty scrub of the Barrens. Dense foliage grows around the pool, where aggressive snapjaw turtles prowl. Weakened kodos often stray here from the great herds of the Field of Giants. Kolkar centaur keep camps along the banks and fiercely guard the water from anyone entering their territory.

Stalker Claws. Across Mulgore, Stalker Claws are taken from prairie stalkers for a cleansing rite. Tauren shamans bind them into totems used to purify tainted wells. Prairie stalkers hunt across Mulgore’s grassy steppes. Their stealth and lethal precision make them deadly predators, yet they keep an essential balance within the Earth Mother's design. Mull Thunderhorn needs their claws to help heal the blighted land. He seeks no harm to the beasts; the natural force of their hunt holds the spiritual strength needed to counter artificial corruption.

Stalking the Stalkers. Huntsman Markhor, of the village of Revantusk in the Hinterlands, names the Silvermane wolves as one of the worst dangers to the village's hunters. You are asked to turn the tables and hunt the hunters. Markhor points to the many trolls the Hinterlands wilds have already claimed, and ranks the Silvermane wolves among the greatest dangers to Revantusk's hunters. The wolves wait hidden among the bushes and the lay of the land, then pounce when the moment is right. Markhor will not let that go unanswered, and urges you to think as a Silvermane does and turn the hunt on the hunters, putting every one of them down.

Standing Our Ground. Standing Our Ground is a decisive quest where an adventurer stands alongside Aamelia Windfield in a desperate confrontation against a menacing bandit leader. Having prepared the defenders for battle, you face what seemed like a lost cause to secure safety from the brigands. Standing Our Ground marks the climax of a desperate struggle against a gang of bandits. Having helped prepare the local defenders for an inevitable clash, you are given one final opportunity to walk away and return safely to Valanaar rather than throw yourself into what appears to be a doomed last stand.

Starbreeze Village. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Starbreeze Village, east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a quiet night elf hamlet, it now lies in ruins beneath the spreading corruption of the World Tree. Starbreeze Village lies southeast of Shadowglen, just down the road from Dolanaar. Peaceful night elf families once lived beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, but the village now lies in shambles. Aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun its wooden homes. Driven wild by corruption afflicting the World Tree’s boughs, they drove out the elven residents and fiercely defend the ruined grounds.

Starfall Village. Starfall Village is a tranquil night elven sanctuary nestled along the snowy road of Winterspring. As the sole Alliance outpost in the frozen valley, it offers shelter and supplies to travelers braving the bitter northern chill. It also stands watch over the nearby barrow den. Situated northwest of the goblin trading post of Everlook and south of Frostsaber Rock, Starfall Village represents the lone bastion of Alliance civilization in Winterspring. Composed of traditional night elven timber lodges, the settlement serves as a haven for wayfarers, providing critical supplies and a warm hearth amid the harsh mountain elements. Despite its peaceful appearance, the village remains ever vigilant, positioned adjacent to a quiet, unoccupied barrow den.

Stars of Elune. In Darnassus, night elf acolytes are called to the Temple of the Moon after proving their devotion to their people. There, the Sisterhood of Elune teaches them sacred arts of their faith. Night elf priests draw their holy power from Elune, their goddess, while humans and dwarves turn to the Light. When an acolyte serves the realm with steadfast devotion, the Sisterhood in Darnassus takes notice. The acolyte is summoned to the Temple of the Moon and judged ready for deeper communion. There, the priest learns sacred spells passed down through thousands of years of worship.

Starweave the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave receives visitors in Auberdine. Travelers come to honor Kalimdor's ancestral spirits and seek her wisdom and blessing. During the Lunar Festival, ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth beneath pillars of celestial light. Elder Starweave joins the night elves in Auberdine, a harbor on Darkshore's coast. Travelers come to honor her and seek guidance from ages past.

Stealing Supplies. Uthek the Wise says meat gives the Gelkis their strength, and that the Magram keep extra stores so they can fight longer between hunts. You are sent to raid the Magram village to the east and bring back six bags of dried meat. Between wars the Gelkis hunt, because meat means strength and a full belly fights harder than an empty one. Uthek the Wise says the Magram keep spare stock to last them between hunts. Raid their village to the east, take those stores, and their strength will fail. Six bags of crudely dried meat are wanted, to be brought to Uthek at the Gelkis Village.

Steamwheedle Cartel. The Steamwheedle Cartel is the largest and most influential goblin enterprise operating across modern Azeroth. Fiercely neutral, the cartel governs bustling commercial hubs like Booty Bay, Ratchet, and Gadgetzan, serving Alliance and Horde patrons alike so long as their coin is genuine. Their sprawling operations encompass cross-continental shipping, alchemy, salvaging, and cutthroat mercenary contracting. Originating from the subterranean goblin capital of Undermine, the Steamwheedle Cartel initially allied with the Old Horde during the Second War, supplying war machines, sappers, and naval engineering. After the dust settled, the cartel's leaders realized that picking sides cost more than it earned. Embracing absolute neutrality, they expanded across both continents, opening trade networks that welcome Alliance and Horde alike. Today, as open tensions simmer, Steamwheedle ports provide vital common ground where anyone with gold can purchase passage, bank resources, and hire local specialists.

Steamwheedle Port. Steamwheedle Port is a bustling coastal outpost on the eastern shore of Tanaris, directly connected to Gadgetzan. Operated by the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel, it serves as an essential sea link across the South Seas while constantly warding off encroaching Southsea Pirates. Tucked against the dunes along the South Seas, Steamwheedle Port offers the inland desert city of Gadgetzan a direct lifeline to maritime trade. Run by the Steamwheedle Cartel, the settlement bustles with dockhands, traders, and sea captains braving the treacherous waters. Supply vessels regularly ply the routes between here and distant goblin trading posts, bringing valuable mechanical components, luxuries, and raw materials into southern Kalimdor.

Steelgrill's Depot. East of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot keeps Alliance vehicles and machinery in working order. Beldin Steelgrill and his crew handle repairs, tinker supplies, and salvage efforts. Steelgrill's Depot rings with clanking metal, hissing steam vents, and the hum of experimental engines. Just off the snowy road east of Kharanos, dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather among heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and stockpiles of raw ores hauled from nearby quarries. Trogg disruptions and shortages of mechanical supplies trouble Dun Morogh. Beldin Steelgrill and his crew keep Alliance machinery in working order, making the depot an indispensable stop for travelers seeking spare parts or technical guidance in the bitter cold.

Steelgrill's Tools. At Steelgrill's Depot, Beldin Steelgrill needs fresh tools to keep his workshop running. The master technician pushes siege engines and his own equipment hard, so shipments from nearby Kharanos keep arriving. Beldin Steelgrill is among Dun Morogh's finest siege engine technicians, but merchants know his rough touch. He works without pause on armored tanks and mechanical contraptions, and delicate tools break quickly in his hands. Arclight spanners snap and fang-ratchets wear out, so Beldin keeps ordering replacements from Kharanos to stock his repair benches.

Steelsnap. In Thousand Needles, Melor Stonehoof sends you after a hyena whose pack terrorizes the wildlife. Steelsnap's hunt breaks with the usual reasons tauren take a life. Tauren hunters take life for sustenance, honor, or wisdom from the Earthmother. Melor Stonehoof asks you to hunt Steelsnap for another reason. The hyena is seen as a threat to nature's balance, bringing senseless violence and fear instead of keeping the cycle of life.

Steelsnap's Rib. In Thousand Needles, Steelsnap's Rib marks the end of a feared hyena's reign. Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff wants the bone brought to Hunter Rise as proof that Steelsnap has been slain. Tauren hunts often seek food, honor, or harmony with nature. Steelsnap is different. The alpha hyena roams the canyon floor south of Camp E'thok in Thousand Needles, terrorizing peaceful wildlife and rallying lesser predators to bloodshed. Hunt master Melor Stonehoof, on Hunter Rise, marks Steelsnap for death. He asks for the hyena's rib as proof the tyrant is slain and the canyon cleansed of its blight.

Sten Stoutarm. Outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm keeps recruits equipped and local messages moving through Coldridge Valley. He helps young mountaineers stay warm, fed, and informed in the harsh mountain conditions. Outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm meets new dwarven and gnomish recruits near the tavern. Coldridge Valley is cut off by winter blizzards and faces dangers nearby. Sten provides green apprentices with sturdy gear so they can face the snow prepared.

Stendel's Pond. Gnolls prowl Stendel's Pond southwest of Sentinel Hill, where anglers still seek fresh fish. Southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond draws anglers despite the danger along its muddy banks. Gnolls roam nearby, and scattered skeletons with two lone graves show that the shore is perilous. The water may be foul, or the beasts may be to blame, but the cause is unknown. Schools of sagefish still bring anglers to the pond.

Stepping Stones. A weathered note in the Barrens points travelers toward Stepping Stones, a mountain refuge near Desolace. It says two couriers made deliveries for the New Plague, and calls what happened to them simple apothecary accidents. A torn message hangs from a wooden plank at a backcountry camp in the Barrens. Mercenaries, cutthroats, and drifters pass through such camps for brief shelter, far from the eyes of the Crossroads or Ratchet. Among the wilds' ordinary signs, the note offers a reason to look beyond the camp and toward the mountains.

Stewvul, Ex-B.F.F.. After Translating the Ledger, Narain Soothfancy says nothing can be translated without the scrying goggles. Narain's ex-best friend forever, Stewvul, stole them, and you are to find Stewvul and take them back. Narain Soothfancy needs the scrying goggles before translating anything. They were stolen a while back by Stewvul, Narain's ex-best friend forever, who broke Narain's heart in five places and then abandoned Narain in this place.

Sticks and Bones. Deathguard Bartholomew asks travelers in Tirisfal Glades to gather dry branches for Eleanor Shackleton. The experienced survivalist camps in the western hills, far from the settlements. Deathguard Bartholomew pauses between patrols to help an acquaintance in Tirisfal Glades. Deathguards guard against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, but Bartholomew also looks out for Eleanor Shackleton. She spends her unlife in the harsh elements, so he asks you to gather dry branches for her campfire.

Stillwater Pond. At Stillwater Pond, gray water and skeletal fish mark the loss of a place where Lordaeron's children once swam. Dangerous scavengers prowl its western shore, just west of Brill. Stillwater Pond once drew families from nearby hamlets for picnics on its grassy banks. Before the Third War and the Plague of Undeath, its shallows gave children too young to brave Brightwater Lake a place to learn to swim. The water is now lifeless and gray. The living have vanished, leaving skeletal fish beneath the surface and wandering undead in the surrounding woods.

Sting of the Scorpid. Sting of the Scorpid is an early trial assigned by Gornek to Horde recruits at the Den in the Valley of Trials. Novices are challenged to hunt venomous scorpid workers northwest of camp and return ten tails to prove their combat readiness. The task serves as a vital lesson in surviving battlefield hazards and respecting even the smallest adversaries. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Gornek tests novice Horde recruits by sending them against the local wildlife. The venomous scorpids roaming the arid dirt northwest of the Den have humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. To prove their battlefield competence, young champions must venture into the rocks, slay scorpid workers, and return with ten of their severed tails as proof of prowess.

Stinglasher. While surveying the Writhing Deep, one of Hadoken Swiftstrider's scouts spotted a giant insect, far larger than the others, wandering the twisted terrain. It has been named Stinglasher, and Hadoken wants it brought down and its secretion glands brought back to Camp Mojache. One scout in the Writhing Deep saw an insect much bigger than the others, wandering about the twisted terrain. It also seems to give off an aura that sets it apart from the rest. It has been given the name Stinglasher. Its innards would be invaluable to study while Hadoken works out how to deal with this new threat, so Hadoken wants its secretion glands cut out and brought straight to Camp Mojache.

Stinky's Escape. "Stinky" Ignatz is out in the swamp, where Morgan Stern, a cook in Theramore, sent him to gather bogbean leaves. Critters have surrounded him, and he asks you to help him out and watch his back while he looks for a bogbean plant. Afterward, Morgan Stern in Theramore is the one to see. Ignatz is relieved to meet someone who does not see him as a meal. He says Morgan Stern, a cook, is working on a new recipe and sent him out to collect bogbean leaves, which Ignatz guesses Stern finds tasty. While looking for a plant, Ignatz was surrounded, and he asks you to help him out and guard his back as he searches.

Stinky's Escape. "Stinky" Ignatz is hemmed in by swamp critters and has not found the bogbean he came for. Mebok Mizzyrix, a goblin of Ratchet, wants bogbean leaves to brew a potion, and Ignatz asks you to get him out of this and watch over him while he searches. Afterward, Mebok Mizzyrix is to be found in Ratchet. Ignatz is relieved to meet someone who is not out to eat him. He says Mebok Mizzyrix, a goblin from Ratchet, needs bogbean leaves to brew some potion or other. Ignatz claims not to care why, since the money was good and he knows this swamp. He got surrounded before finding the plant, and asks you to help him out of the spot and guard him while he looks for it.

Stitches. Along Duskwood's western road, Stitches marches toward Darkshire, crushing the Night Watch and unwary travelers in his path. Near Abercrombie's shack, northeast of Raven Hill Cemetery, Stitches sets out east along the road toward Darkshire. Unholy sorcery and harvested corpses made the undead abomination, whose immense strength and malice overwhelm the Night Watch checkpoints. He tears through the defense camp across from Vul'Gol Ogre Mound and the outpost outside the Rotting Orchard, slaughtering travelers and town defenders along the way.

name.esES: Los suministros del reactor a vapor

text.enUS: Stocking Jetsteam. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam for a long deployment with the Ironforge Siege Brigade. The crew needs boar meat and bear pelts for the journey. Pilot Bellowfiz prepares Jetsteam at Steelgrill's Depot, just outside Kharanos. The siege tank is bound for a long operation with the Siege Brigade. Master engineer Beldin Steelgrill is tuning its mechanisms, while the crew needs a month's provisions for Dun Morogh's sub-zero cold.

Stolen Booty. Pirate cargo off Ratchet’s coast has left Gazlowe choosing what matters most. Stolen Booty brings him two vital goods: boots for local laborers and a delicate telescopic lens needed to complete his observatory. The Southsea Freebooters have troubled merchant lanes across the Great Sea for years. Their fortified camp just south of Ratchet brought them into direct conflict with Gazlowe. Pirates intercepted merchant vessels bound for the port and took valuable supplies from the Steamwheedle Cartel. Some goods could be written off as a cost of shipping. Specialized cargo mattered enough for Gazlowe to hire mercenaries to break into the pirate stronghold.

Stolen Enchanting Supplies. Stolen Enchanting Supplies is an errand undertaken near the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. An apprentice named Blixie Fitzwink lost a shipment of magical reagents during a gnoll ambush, and adventurers must retrieve the stolen goods from camps around Stone Cairn Lake. Recovering the materials spares the apprentice severe chore duty and keeps Master Theocritus's arcane studies supplied. A routine supply run turns perilous when Blixie Fitzwink, an apprentice assisting Master Theocritus, is ambushed by hostile gnolls between the trading post and the Tower of Azora. Fleeing for her life, she drops her cargo, leaving valuable enchanting reagents scattered among the gnoll camps dotting the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. Desperate to avoid weeks of disciplinary cleanup duty following arcane polymorph experiments, she appeals to passing adventurers to recover the missing goods.

Stolen Silver. At the Crossroads, a strongbox of Horde silver has gone missing from the guard tower. Sunscale raptors carried the coins to their nests at the Raptor Grounds south of Ratchet. Sunscale raptors carried a strongbox of silver from the Crossroads guard tower. The coins were meant as pay for the garrison guards. The raptors dragged the lockbox to their communal nests at the Raptor Grounds, south of Ratchet. Gazrog and the other overseers cannot explain why the predators took it. The theft leaves them wondering whether the raptors prize shiny things or possess a cunning beyond that of ordinary wild beasts.

Stolen Silver. Gazrog at the Crossroads sends you after payroll silver stolen by raptors. Rumors of their cunning lead you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and the raptors have taken their wages. You are sent to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog first sought vengeance. But killing the pack would not restore the missing money. The Horde must learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin, and where they took them.

Stolen Supplies. Stolen Supplies tasks adventurers with recovering plundered highland goods from the Al'Aketh in Falaath Village. Caravan ambushes have cut off vital shipments of food and windstones between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands, leaving local skyborne communities on the brink of starvation. For months, caravans traveling between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands have faced persistent attacks along their trade routes. These shipments transport vital necessities, including food and windstones, to sustain the highland settlements. Without steady deliveries, local townsfolk have been pushed to the brink of starvation, struggling to squeak by as supplies dwindle across the region.

Stoley's Debt. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley has a bet with his old friend Stoley, who tends the bar at Steamwheedle Port, over whose rum is stronger. Stoley seems to be dodging it, so MacKinley asks you to go and talk to him. Stoley owes "Sea Wolf" MacKinley a very special bottle of rum. Stoley boasted that the rum at Steamwheedle Port is stronger than anything in Booty Bay, and said the money owed would be doubled if MacKinley tried it and disagreed. Now MacKinley thinks Stoley has lost his nerve about handing it over, but MacKinley never backs away from a wager. You are asked to go and speak to Stoley at the Steamwheedle Port bar.

Stoley's Shipment. Stoley is out of rum and in debt to a friend over a wager. Captain Cuergo stole the last shipment and keeps it in the walled pirate town to the south, so Stoley asks you to bring it back. Stoley has none left of the rum promised to "Sea Wolf" MacKinley of Booty Bay to settle their wager. Captain Cuergo stole the last shipment, and has it stowed in the walled pirate town to the south, which is Lost Rigger Cove. Stoley asks you to find the rum and return it, so that he can show Kalimdor's drink is far better than anything Booty Bay pours.

Stonard. Stonard is a fortified Horde outpost situated in the southern marshes of the Swamp of Sorrows. Originally built during the First War, it serves the modern Horde as an essential foothold in the southern Eastern Kingdoms and an observation post watching the Blasted Lands. Stonard stands as one of the oldest orcish settlements on Azeroth. First established when the Old Horde spilled through the Dark Portal into what was once the Black Morass, Stonard and its sister post, Rockard, anchored the invaders' lines. Though abandoned and damaged during the fallout of the Second War, Thrall's New Horde moved to reconstruct and garrison Stonard. Anchored by a traditional orcish Great Hall and fortified burrows, the outpost is now a vital island of Horde authority in an untamed, perilous mire.

Stone Cairn Lake. At Stone Cairn Lake in northeastern Elwynn, hostile murlocs hold the southern shore and renegade wizards camp on the island. Heroes' Vigil honors those lost in the First War. Families and pilgrims once crossed the calm waters to honor the dead at Heroes' Vigil. The stone memorial was raised on the lake's central island to mark the heavy loss of human life in the First War against the Orcish Horde. Now renegade wizards have made camp beside the monument, and the island has become a hostile place.
