text.enUS: Stone Is Better than Cloth. Lucien Tosselwrench knows how cheap Lotwil can be, and offers to make something for your trouble: enchanted bracers built from the extra stones you collected. What Lucien lacks is a blacksmith's patterned bronze bracers. After the Study of the Elements: Rock trials, Lucien Tosselwrench admits how cheap Lotwil can be and wants to make it up to you. Lucien has been busy with the extra stones you gathered and can make fine enchanted bracers. They may even help guard you against what Lucien calls the coming atrocity of Lotwil's newest invention.

Stone Tokens. Stone Tokens is a Horde assignment issued by Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill to retrieve magical binding artifacts from Dalaran agents in the Alterac region. The Forsaken seek to study the arcane methods Dalaran's mages use to enslave and command powerful elementals. Gathering these inert tokens serves as the foundation for the Magus's research into elemental subjugation. The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized conduits and enchanted foci to bind creatures from other dimensions into servitude. While the city itself is still rebuilding, its agents and remnant forces patrol the surrounding territory, relying on elementals as laborers and defensive shock troops. Magus Voidglare, an arcane researcher working on behalf of the Forsaken in Tarren Mill, seeks to dissect the precise sorcery Dalaran uses to compel these entities into obedience.

Stone of Relu. In the Wetlands, the Stone of Relu is lost to a raptor after an ambush. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it can unlock secrets within ancient fossils. Explorers' League work uncovered the Stone of Relu. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it can decipher prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. He means to use it on his Wetlands specimens and on the fossil Prospector Remtravel unearthed in Darkshore.

Stonebull Lake. Stonebull Lake curves around Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore, giving the tauren fresh water and fish. Stonebull Lake curves around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, shaping the heart of central Mulgore. A wooden bridge crosses its narrowest stretch, carrying the main dirt road between the village and Thunder Bluff on the great mesa to the north. Native fish fill the calm water. Hunters rest on the banks, travelers pause there, and apprentice fishers learn their trade beneath the open sky.

Stonefield Farm. The Stonefield family works the fields in southern Elwynn Forest. Their long feud with the neighboring Maclures keeps the two households at odds. Stonefield Farm lies south of Goldshire, where the family grows crops for the realm. For decades, the Stonefields have quarreled with the nearby Maclure Vineyards. The households trade accusations of theft and trespassing, and even small disputes keep tensions high. Gramma Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield make their home here.

Stonefield family. The Stonefield family is a lineage of human farmers residing at the Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn Forest. Known for their long-standing rural roots, they tend their homestead while caught up in an ongoing rivalry with their neighboring peers, the Maclures. Despite the hostility between the two households, younger generations find themselves entangled across the family divide. The Stonefields are quintessential Elwynn agrarian stock, working the soil south of the road leading to Westfall. The homestead revolves around Gramma Mildred Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield. Daily life on the farm involves tending crops and managing livestock while fending off local pests and dealing with nearby kobold incursions that plague the region's mines and borders.

Stonefire Tavern. Travelers gather at Stonefire Tavern in Ironforge’s Commons, just north of the city gates. The inn offers a hearth, dwarven ale, and a place to rest for those arriving from across Khaz Modan. Stonefire Tavern welcomes travelers in Ironforge’s Commons, just north of the fortress gates. Innkeeper Firebrew runs the inn with his daughter Gwenna. Weary wayfarers can find meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain. Travelers come in from across the Alliance to rest from Dun Morogh’s mountain snows, trade tales, or gather supplies before exploring the city. Its hearth draws them together at the heart of the Commons.

Stonegear's Search. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear seeks a rare ore for his tank. He asks a daring traveler to find fresh fuel for its weapons. Pilot Stonegear, stationed just outside Ironforge, wants to make his siege engine more powerful. Word of his plans spreads through Ironforge and Loch Modan. Pilot Longbeard or Mountaineer Kadrell may send you to meet the ambitious pilot and hear his proposal.

Stonemasons Guild. The Stonemasons Guild was the collective of master builders and artisans responsible for reconstructing Stormwind City after the Second War. Following a bitter dispute over payment with the House of Nobles that ended in deadly riots, the guild was forcibly dissolved, driving its disenfranchised members into exile while leaving the true fate of its scattered artisans an enduring mystery. Led by elected Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef, the artisans of the Stonemasons Guild demonstrated a mastery of masonry that rivaled the Royal Stonecutters Union of the dwarves. Following the devastation of the First and Second Wars, the House of Nobles hired the guild to embark upon the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City from ruins, trusting them to restore the capital to its ancient grandeur.

Stonemaul Ruins. The Stonemaul Ruins are the shattered remnants of Stonemaul Village, once the proud Kalimdor settlement of the Stonemaul ogres. After being driven out by the black dragonflight, the clan fled north, leaving their former home overrun by Firemane dragonspawn. Following their migration to Kalimdor, the Stonemaul ogres founded their settlement amid the murky swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. The village became famous when the beastmaster Rexxar braved the clan's lethal trials, slew their brutal chieftain Kor'gall, and rallied the ogres to defend the nascent Horde against Admiral Proudmoore's forces. After the war, Rexxar left the ogre Mok'Morokk in command. Under Mok'Morokk's selfish rule, the village fell into decline and was ultimately ambushed and shattered by the black dragonflight. The surviving ogres fled north to establish Brackenwall Village, while Onyxia's brood took complete possession of the ruins.

Stones of Binding. After The Princess Trapped, a voice from the iridescent shards tells of four Stones of Binding spread across Arathi that hold it down under the ground. The strongest, the Stone of Inner Binding, can be unlocked only with keys taken from the other three. The voice tells of four Stones of Binding spread across Arathi, holding it down under the ground. To loosen them, the strongest must be unlocked first: the Stone of Inner Binding, which needs keys gathered from the other three, the Stones of West, East and Outer Binding. The keys are the Burning Key, the Cresting Key and the Thundering Key. Guardians watch over the stones, but someone clever or lucky may find a way to banish them. Once gathered, the keys are carried to the Stone of Inner Binding.

Stonesplinter Valley. Stonesplinter troggs have fortified a mountain vale in southwestern Loch Modan. Their chieftain, Grawmug, leads the tribe from the valley. Stonesplinter Valley lies among the crags of southwestern Loch Modan. Troggs clawed up from underground across Khaz Modan, ending the quiet that once filled the hollow. The Stonesplinter tribe claimed the valley and carved crude defenses into its rocky passes, digging dens and raising barricades. They hunt anything that comes too close. Their numbers threaten the roads through southern Loch Modan, and Mountaineers from Thelsamar hire mercenaries to thin their ranks and bring down Grawmug, the towering warlord who leads them.

Stonetalon Peak. At Stonetalon Peak, kaldorei Sentinels and druids keep watch over an ancient sanctuary. The sheltered valley is sacred to the night elves and remains the Alliance’s main foothold in the high mountains. Stonetalon Peak opens into a green valley high above the dry lower ranges. Its ruins reach back millennia, to temples that honored Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. Night elven Sentinels and druids now care for the sanctuary. They keep a barrow den and an Alliance flight roost here.
Stonetalon Sap. Near Mirkfallon Lake and Stonetalon Peak, sap beasts carry the sap Jin'Zil seeks. The Darkspear witch doctor uses it in a brew for his caged night elf prisoners.

name.frFR: Y a du gaz dans l’eau

text.enUS: Stonetalon Standstill. At Mystral Lake, befouled water spirits have halted Horde supply transports on the way to Stonetalon. Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post sends you to clear the hostile elementals and scout a night elf gazebo overlooking Silverwind Refuge. The Horde needs lumber, supplies, and messengers to travel between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The Talondeep Path carries them past Mystral Lake’s western shore. Hostile water elementals have stopped travel and battered the supply caravans. Mastok Wrilehiss calls for action to reopen the route before the Horde’s supply lines collapse.

Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch above the approaches from the Burning Steppes, threatening Lakeshire. The fortress once guarded Redridge against northern invasions. Stonewatch overlooks the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, where its tower and keep guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Lakeshire's defenders first held the fortress. Then Morganth, a rogue warlock, allied with the Blackrock clan. Dark magic helped the orcs overwhelm the 12th Sabre Regiment and seize the keep. Morganth later turned against his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls. The Blackrock orcs kept their hold under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun.

Stonewatch Falls. At Stonewatch Falls, water pours from Lake Everstill into a pool claimed by murlocs. The falls lie beneath Stonewatch in the eastern Redridge Mountains. Stonewatch Falls rushes down the slope beneath Stonewatch, the Blackrock orc stronghold. Its water flows from Lake Everstill’s eastern river and gathers in a deep pool against the mountainside. Murlocs have claimed the shore, raising crude reed hovels and preying on travelers who come too close to the water.

Stonewatch Keep. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch Keep in eastern Redridge Mountains, turning it against Lakeshire. The Kingdom of Stormwind built and manned the fortress before the invaders seized it as a base for their warlords. Stonewatch Keep once guarded the eastern ridges and the settlers of Lakeshire from hostile incursions. That changed when the renegade warlock Morganth allied with the Blackrock clan. Strengthened by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress and overcame its human defenders. After their victory, Morganth abandoned the Blackrock clan to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls. The invaders kept Stonewatch, turning a former Alliance bastion into a staging ground for assaults on the valley.

Stonewatch Tower. Blackrock sentinels hold Stonewatch Tower in northeastern Redridge. Once Lakeshire's outpost, it now helps the clan watch the ridges and guard its mountain stronghold. Stonewatch Tower rises above Lake Everstill, guarding the high mountain passes. The Kingdom of Stormwind built it as a forward scout for Stonewatch Keep. From its heights, sentries watched the eastern ridges and warned Lakeshire of threats coming from the Burning Steppes. Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights, overcame the human defenders, and seized the stronghold for their war effort. Blackrock sentinels now watch the tower, keeping Alliance scouts from reaching the fortress unnoticed.

Stonewrought Dam. Waters gather behind Stonewrought Dam along Loch Modan’s northern rim. The dwarven barrier holds back the Loch and drains the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. Stonewrought Dam stretches across the canyon east of Dun Algaz, one of the great works of dwarven craft. Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright designed it and pioneered the stonewrought technique used to build it. By trapping water in the mountain basin, the dam doubled the Loch’s surface area and steadily lowered the waters to the north. The Wetlands emerged from a valley once completely flooded.

Stonewrought Pass. Stonewrought Pass is an underground tunnel cut directly through the southern mountains of Loch Modan into the blighted expanse of the Searing Gorge. Masterfully engineered by the famed architect Franclorn Forgewright, this passage connects the Valley of Kings directly to Dustfire Valley. Heavy iron gates secure both ends to protect peaceful dwarven lands from the volcanic terrors to the south. Carved out of the bedrock by the legendary master architect Franclorn Forgewright—famed also for the massive Stonewrought Dam—the Stonewrought Pass serves as a direct corridor between the pastoral beauty of Loch Modan and the scorched wastes of Searing Gorge. Emerging in Loch Modan near the colossal Valley of Kings, it cuts straight through the mountain ridge down into Dustfire Valley. Because Searing Gorge is infested with Dark Iron dwarves and fiery beasts, the Ironforge mountaineers keep the passage locked tight behind heavy gates to prevent danger from spilling into the north.

Stop the Spread. Stop the Spread is a Silverpine Forest quest concerning the containment of the worgen curse linked to Archmage Arugal. While researchers seek a way to halt the affliction, preemptive measures are ordered against living human refugees at the Greymane Wall to prevent them from turning into Arugal's servants. In Silverpine Forest, the scourge of the worgen spreads at the hands of the renegade Archmage Arugal. While the exact methods and mechanics behind the spread of this feral condition remain largely unknown, the danger it presents to the territory is undeniable. Researchers are actively working to understand the nature of the magic, but their immediate focus is preventing Arugal from amassing an unstoppable host of savage followers.

Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder waits beside the water during the Lunar Festival. Travelers honor ancient traditions and the olden races of Azeroth, and receive a token of remembrance in return. A quiet pond lies just behind the smithy in Goldshire, where Stormbrow the Elder appears. Guards, tradesfolk, and weary travelers pass through town on their way into the forest. Beneath Elwynn Forest's canopy, the honored spirit welcomes anyone who comes to honor the realm's long history.

Stormpike Banner. Alliance recruits enter Icewing Cavern to earn the Stormpike Banner. The trial lies southwest of Dun Baldar in Alterac Valley, where harpies guard the standard. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends new Alliance soldiers into Icewing Cavern southwest of Dun Baldar. Before they face the Frostwolf orcs, recruits must brave the harpies, seize the Stormpike Banner, and bring it back alive. Those who return earn the rank and insignia of an initiate in the Stormpike Guard.

Stormpike's Deciphering. Loremaster Dibbs sends you to Ironforge with the ensorcelled parchment, hoping Prospector Stormpike, a master of decryption and deciphering, can make sense of it. After The Ensorcelled Parchment, Dibbs tells you to take it to Prospector Stormpike, who is at his studies in Ironforge's Prospector headquarters. Dibbs says to mention that he sent you, since he has been sending Stormpike quite a lot of business lately.

Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The road leads from Stormwind's Dwarven District to an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make a weapon for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The Stormpike clan is respected in Ironforge for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore turns to trustworthy travelers to carry the axe north, across the distance between Stormwind and the dwarven borderlands.

Stormpike's Order. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike is arranging a shield from Furen Longbeard. The armorsmith works far south in Stormwind City, so Stormpike asks a traveler to carry his order there. Mountaineer Stormpike wants a new shield, and he trusts only Furen Longbeard to forge it. The mountaineer is willing to pay well to place the commission in the smith’s hands, though Loch Modan and Stormwind City lie far apart.

Stormpike's Request. Mountaineer Stormpike sends a written commission from Loch Modan to Stormwind City. He asks Furen Longbeard to craft him a shield of exceptional dwarven quality. Mountaineer Stormpike needs a sturdy shield while stationed in Loch Modan. He trusts no ordinary smith with the work and asks Furen Longbeard, whose craft he greatly admires. Furen now lives among the humans in Stormwind's Dwarven District, having left Ironforge. Stormpike assumes a king's ransom drew him south, so traveling adventurers carry the commission across the kingdoms.

Stormrage Barrow Dens. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are an ancient subterranean sanctuary carved beneath the sacred valley of Moonglade. Named for Malfurion Stormrage, these quiet earth-hewn chambers serve as a dedicated resting place where druids enter long, restorative slumbers to wander the Emerald Dream. Barrow dens serve as sacred havens throughout night elven lands, providing druids a safe subterranean refuge where their physical bodies can lie undisturbed during lengthy immersions in the Emerald Dream. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are particularly esteemed within the sacred realm of Moonglade. Named in honor of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, these winding earthen halls hold both ancient reverence and quiet vigil. While some druids like Clintar Dreamwalker still slumber safely within its alcoves, the absence of the great Archdruid himself casts a somber shadow over the hollowed roots and peaceful glowing lanterns.

Stormwind (kingdom). The Kingdom of Stormwind is the southernmost and currently foremost human realm on Azeroth, holding dominion over Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains. Sacked and shattered during the First War, it was rebuilt through blood and labor after the Second, rising to become the military and cultural center of the Alliance following the tragic collapse of Lordaeron in the north. Today, the kingdom stands beset from within and without, ruled by the ten-year-old King Anduin Wrynn under the watchful guidance of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon while its crowned monarch remains missing. Stormwind was established over a thousand years ago by descendants of the ancient Arathi empire who ventured south beyond the crags of Khaz Modan into fertile, forested valleys. Far from the northern kingdoms, the realm grew into a culture fiercely proud of its self-reliance and the Light.

name.frFR: Bon pour une pièce d'armure de Hurlevent

text.enUS: Stormwind Armor Marker. Stormwind Armor Marker lets those who aid the realm claim crafted gear from sanctioned artisans. Sara Timberlain accepts one at the Eastvale Logging Camp. Stormwind's commanders issue armor markers to those who serve the realm. Keeping law and order across Elwynn Forest stretches Stormwind's resources thin, so commanders sometimes use these official requisition slips instead of handing out standard gear at military outposts. A marker confirms the bearer's service and authorizes local craftsmen under contract to provide tailored armor.

Stormwind Army. The Stormwind Army is the standing military force charged with defending the Kingdom of Stormwind and preserving the security of the Grand Alliance in the south. Though legendary for its resilient knights and marshals, the army is currently crippled by royal absence, political infighting, and crippling troop shortages across the provinces. The army traces its martial lineage through centuries of brutal conflict, from early frontier clashes against gnolls to the desperate defense against the Gurubashi trolls. In the First War, under King Llane Wrynn I and Sir Anduin Lothar, the Knights of Stormwind mounted legendary ambushes against the Orcish Horde, yet fell when the capital burned. Surviving remnants evacuated to Lordaeron, spearheading the formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron and fighting through the Second War. After the Dark Portal's fall, Stormwind's military was rebuilt alongside the restored kingdom.

Stormwind City. Stormwind City leads the Kingdom of Stormwind and the Alliance as their capital and seat of power. Rebuilt after the First War, it is the greatest remaining human stronghold in Azeroth since the northern kingdoms fell. Stormwind City rose over a thousand years ago, founded by Arathi descendants who migrated south. The coastal capital flourished behind stone ramparts, with swift rivermills powering the city. In the First War, the Orcish Horde laid siege, broke through its defenses, and burned Stormwind to the ground. Sir Anduin Lothar led the surviving refugees across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. After the Alliance won the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild rebuilt the capital with white stone, canals, and towering spires. The fortress now stands north of Elwynn Forest.

Stormwind Gate. At Stormwind Gate, sentries watch the road between Elwynn Forest and Stormwind City. The passage opens onto the Valley of Heroes, where the city’s stone monuments rise beyond the arch. Stormwind Gate guards the southern road from Elwynn Forest into the capital. The Stormwind City Guard watches from the stone portal, while patrols move between the outer arch and the Valley of Heroes. Unrest lingers in Elwynn, yet the massive iron and stone gates stay open. Travelers, merchants, and returning defenders pass through into the heart of the Alliance.

Stormwind Guard. The Stormwind Guard comprises the regional garrisons and sentries tasked with enforcing the kingdom's laws and defending its surrounding territories. Stretched perilously thin by political gridlock and distant military campaigns, its scattered marshals struggle to hold back gnolls, orcs, and bandits across Elwynn and Redridge. Operating as a vital branch of the Stormwind Army, the Stormwind Guard patrols the highways, crossroads, and stone watchtowers that bind the kingdom together. In outlying settlements, governance and defense fall to appointed marshals—such as Marshal McBride in Northshire Valley, Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, and Marshal Marris in Lakeshire. These officers muster recruits and maintain order, relying on trusty brown horses known for stamina to cover ground between fortified outposts like Westbrook Garrison.

Stormwind Ho!. Alliance High Command fears the naga threat, and Stormwind Ho! gives Farren Orinelle a chance to leave Southshore. He hopes to take credit for their defeat and win a reassignment to Stormwind City. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle finds his Southshore posting miserable. The town sits on Lordaeron’s edge, hemmed in by Forsaken forces, syndicate brigands, and sea fiends. A city guardsman used to drunks and petty brawls in Stormwind, Farren longs to return south. His former mentor tells him Alliance High Command is increasingly anxious about naga encroaching on the coasts. Farren sees a chance to leave the north behind.

Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep stands high above the capital as the stone fortress and seat of power for the Kingdom of Stormwind. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it currently houses the royal court of the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Perched upon a plateau overlooking the entire city, Stormwind Keep serves as both a palace and a military bastion. The original stronghold was burned to the ground by the Old Horde when King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. Raised anew upon the old foundations after the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, the reconstructed keep houses not only the grand throne room and the War Room, but peaceful garden courtyards and the expansive Royal Library.

Stormwind Library. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those with library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn has set aside royal funds for the work, opening these accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars. While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor guide Stormwind’s defenses and court in King Varian’s absence, young King Anduin turns royal support toward learning. He funds copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals, so the kingdom’s past can be preserved and studied. Within Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library keeps these written accounts and copies them for those in royal service.

Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind Stockade holds the city’s most dangerous prisoners beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, leaving the prison in chaos. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind keeps cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. Now a violent uprising led by the Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has forced the guards from the lower cells. The prisoners roam freely through the corridors. Thelwater has managed to secure the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to reach the canals. He depends on adventurers to enter the prison and put down the uprising.

Stormwind Stockade (Classic). Prisoners now control the Stormwind Stockade beneath Stormwind City's canal district. A revolt has driven the guards from its halls. The Stockade lies off the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter, holding Stormwind's most dangerous prisoners. Warden Thelwater oversees the underground prison. Its inmates include Defias Brotherhood cutthroats, a Blackrock orc, an ogre, and a Dark Iron dwarf. Bazil Thredd recently led a coordinated riot that overwhelmed the garrison. The surviving guards fled, leaving the prisoners in control of the halls.

Stormy Potential. Stormy Potential is a quest in Durotar given by the goblin Rezlak near Drygulch Ravine. Hoping to protect his trade caravan against marauding harpies, Rezlak seeks to supercharge a depleted orb using the potent electrical organs of native thunder lizards. Near the shadow of Drygulch Ravine in Durotar, the goblin Rezlak found himself facing two problems: a caravan under constant threat from local harpies, and an intact magical orb completely depleted of power. Remembering the pragmatic advice of Ratchet's chief engineer Gazlowe—to seize opportunity whenever it knocks—Rezlak hatched an ambitious plan to solve both problems at once by supercharging the dormant device.

Stout to Kadrell. A cask of Rejold Barleybrew’s new Shimmer Stout is bound for Mountaineer Kadrell in Loch Modan. You carry the brew from Dun Morogh’s frozen heights to the warmer valley. Mountaineer Barleybrew thinks Rejold’s new Shimmer Stout is too good to keep in Dun Morogh. From the eastern border post, he watches over the mountain passes and the kin guarding neighboring lands. The Mountaineers’ patrols can be cold and grueling, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Barleybrew wants an honest opinion from a fellow patrolman, so he sends a cask east with travelers bound for Loch Modan.

Stoutlager Inn. In Thelsamar, Stoutlager Inn gives travelers a warm hearth and a place to gather in western Loch Modan. Stoutlager Inn anchors community life in western Loch Modan, within Thelsamar. Miners, mountaineers, and travelers between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands stop to trade rumors, find lodging, and share dwarven ale. Troggs and kobolds make the wilderness beyond Thelsamar more dangerous, while the inn’s stone walls and fires offer shelter.

Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon. Gryan Stoutmantle sends a hard answer from Sentinel Hill to Lakeshire. His dispatch tells Magistrate Solomon that the People's Militia cannot spare a single soldier for Redridge Mountains. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks Sentinel Hill for reinforcements as Blackrock orcs and gnolls press his town. Gryan Stoutmantle replies in writing with sorrow for Lakeshire's losses, but Westfall faces a war of its own. The People's Militia formed from desperation after the Crown withdrew its garrison. Farmers and volunteers now fight the Defias Brotherhood alone. Stoutmantle's forces are already bleeding and stretched thin, with no men to spare for another abandoned frontier.

Strahad Farsan. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan teaches warlocks to bind demons. The human warlock lives in a stone tower in the Barrens, beyond the reach of ordinary Alliance and Horde politics. Students of fel magic come from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity to learn from him. Strahad Farsan keeps to a stone tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. The goblin port's neutral ground lets him practice dangerous summonings away from Alliance magistrates and Horde shamans. His acolytes gather around him as he studies the Twisting Nether, apart from the struggles over territory below.

Strahnbrad. Strahnbrad is a ruined human settlement nestled in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains, near the border of the Western Plaguelands. Once famous as the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's early defense against Blackrock orc raiders, the town has since fallen into decay and serves as a fortified stronghold for the criminal Syndicate. Originally a holding of the Kingdom of Alterac before being absorbed into Lordaeron following the Second War, Strahnbrad's misfortune began on the eve of the Third War. Blackrock clan orcs raided the settlement to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion, leading Prince Arthas Menethil and the Knights of the Silver Hand to ride to its defense. Though Arthas drove the raiders away and slew their slave master, the town was heavily bloodied. When Lordaeron crumbled beneath the Scourge shortly thereafter, Strahnbrad was abandoned to the elements.

Strange Alliance. Captain Pentigast sees luck in the way the centaur clans of Desolace fight each other, since as one force they could not be stopped. The Gelkis are locked in brutal war with the Magram, so Pentigast sends you to Uthek the Wise in southwestern Desolace to seek an alliance. Captain Pentigast counts it good fortune that the centaur clans war on one another, for joined together they could not be stopped. Pentigast wants to push that edge. The Gelkis and Magram are locked in brutal war, so striking at the Magram might win the Gelkis over.

Strange Smelling Powder. In Loch Modan, Strange Smelling Powder has raised alarm during an inquiry into sabotage. Chief Engineer Hinderweir suspects an explosive and seeks an expert's judgment. Strange Smelling Powder was found amid signs of sabotage against Loch Modan's infrastructure. Chief Engineer Hinderweir fears it may be an engineered explosive, unlike the usual powder used in mining. He cannot identify its mixture or origin, and will not tamper with it himself. Even a small spark could bring disaster.

Strangely Marked Box. Along Darkshore, a Strangely Marked Box is found among cargo on dead sea turtles. Its runes point to the naga and show that the turtles did not come ashore by chance. Dead sea turtles and other sea creatures wash up on Darkshore's beaches. Some carry broken harnesses and carriages strapped to their shells. Sealed boxes marked with foreign, winding runes lie among the wreckage. Greymist murlocs often shelter in the hollow ribs and broken wagons, feeding on the carcasses and guarding what remains.

Stranglethorn Fever. In Booty Bay, Fin Fizracket lies sick with Stranglethorn Fever, a deadly virus. He says the only cure is the heart of Mokk the Savage, an elusive white beast, and that he is dying. Fin Fizracket is stammering and fading, sure that he has caught Stranglethorn Fever. He says the only cure is to eat the heart of Mokk the Savage, an elusive white beast. Witch Doctor Unbagwa is the only one who can summon the creature, and Fin sends you to find Unbagwa in a hidden cave on the southern cape, the Spirit Den.

Stranglethorn Fever. Deep within Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa claims to know how to draw out the beast known as Mokk the Savage. Before communion with the spirits can begin, the witch doctor requires ten Gorilla Fangs as an offering. Once the ritual commences, defending the troll from agitated jungle beasts is necessary to lure the creature forth. Witch Doctor Unbagwa possesses the ritual knowledge needed to summon Mokk the Savage out of the surrounding jungle. To begin the incantation, the witch doctor demands ten Gorilla Fangs. Communing with the spirits carries a heavy risk, as the ritual chant draws the attention of other gorilla beasts in the vicinity, demanding protection while the magic does its work.

Stratholme. Stratholme was once the jewel of the Eastweald and the second greatest city in the Kingdom of Lordaeron. During the Third War, it became the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's infamous culling after its citizens consumed grain tainted by the Plague of Undeath. Today, the ruined metropolis still burns, serving as the Scourge's primary stronghold in northern Lordaeron. Long before its downfall, Stratholme stood as a cornerstone of northern civilization. Emerging centuries ago from the Arathi expansion into the Eastweald, it flourished into Lordaeron's second-largest settlement, renowned for holy shrines and sacred water capable of resisting dark sorcery. Prior to the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol gathered at the city's chapel to establish the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand, ordaining legends like Uther the Lightbringer. Throughout that war, Stratholme served as a vital port, supply hub, and northern oil refinery for the Alliance of Lordaeron, enduring an assault by the Old Horde before rebuilding in victory.

Stratholme (Classic). Stratholme, once northern Lordaeron's proudest jewel and the birthplace of the Silver Hand, is now a burning ruin serving as the Scourge's regional capital. Divided between the fanatical Scarlet Crusade and Baron Rivendare's undead legions, the cursed city remains locked in endless, violent war. Before the Third War, Stratholme was the northern powerhouse of Lordaeron and the sacred birthplace of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Its fate was sealed when Prince Arthas purged the city, slaughtering his own subjects after infected grain brought the plague within its walls. Left smoldering and ruined, Stratholme was claimed by the Scourge. Today, under the overarching authority of the lich Kel'Thuzad and the field command of Baron Rivendare, the city serves as the primary base for undead power in the Plaguelands.

Stratholme Main Gate. The Stratholme Main Gate stands as the grand, burning entrance to Lordaeron's northern metropolis in the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct access through the city's ruined avenues toward King's Square and the crusader fortifications within. Stratholme was once the pride of northern Lordaeron, famed as the birthplace of the Order of the Silver Hand. Today, its colossal arched main gates mark the threshold of an ongoing nightmare. It was here during the Third War that Prince Arthas turned on his mentor, Uther the Lightbringer, and purged his own citizens before the Plague of Undeath could claim them. The city has burned relentlessly ever since, transformed into the primary Scourge stronghold in the region.

Stratholme Service Entrance. The Stratholme Service Entrance is a fortified rear gateway located at Eastwall Gate in the northern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct, covert access into the Scourge-controlled eastern quarter of the burning city, bypassing the grand front gates. While the monumental Main Gate of Stratholme opens into King's Square and provides a route toward the Scarlet Bastion, the Service Entrance breaches the city's eastern fortification at Eastwall Gate. Today, it leads directly into the corrupted heart of the metropolis: Elders' Square and the blighted pathways leading toward Baron Rivendare's slaughterhouses.
Strigid Owl Feather. Strigid Owl Feathers are gathered from the owls in Teldrassil's boughs. Zenn Foulhoof seeks them for his covert dealings.

Stromgarde Badges. In Stromgarde, the Syndicate is fighting a contingent of militia, and its leaders pay gold for every badge taken from a fallen militiaman. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials wants those badges recovered. In Stromgarde the Syndicate is at war with a contingent of militia. To push their followers into fighting the better-trained soldiers, Syndicate leaders pay gold for each badge taken from a slain militiaman. Captain Nials calls them cutthroats and will not let them keep trophies of the brave fallen, so you are sent into the Syndicate-held part of Stromgarde to hunt for the badges and bring them back to Refuge Pointe. Nials wants the Syndicate to learn it cannot profit from the dead.

Stromgarde Keep. Stromgarde Keep is the battered, divided capital of the fallen human kingdom of Stromgarde in the Arathi Highlands. Once the proud cradle of human civilization known as Strom, the fortress is now partitioned between hostile Syndicate rogues, invading Boulderfist ogres, and a desperate remnant of royal defenders under Prince Galen Trollbane. Long before it bore its current name, this fortress was founded nearly three millennia ago as Strom, the first capital of the unified human empire of Arathor under King Thoradin. It served as the staging ground for humanity's victory against the forest trolls and was the birthplace of human wizardry, where high elven magi tutored the first hundred human spellcasters. Over centuries, as younger sister kingdoms like Dalaran, Lordaeron, and Stormwind rose and prospered, Strom's influence waned. Renamed Stromgarde by the stubborn Trollbane dynasty who stayed behind, it remained a proud warrior bastion throughout the Second War, anchoring the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde.

Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus has stopped in the Badlands to work on shackles of elemental binding. To test some offensive spells and a few pieced-together gizmos, Lotwil needs small stone shards from the lesser rock elementals nearby. Here in the Badlands, Lotwil Veriatus is working on a project: shackles of elemental binding. Once finished, they would let mages summon still stronger elementals for even greater uses. To get started, Lotwil wants ten small stone shards, easily taken from the lesser rock elementals in the hills immediately west.

Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus praises you as abler than all of Lotwil's apprentices combined, and wants the next step of the tests. This time the need is three large stone slabs, pieces best found on rock elementals. The next parts of Lotwil Veriatus's work need more strength. Rock elementals have larger, sturdier bodies, so they are likelier to carry pieces big enough for the tests. Lotwil points you further west, or southeast along the edges of the mountains, and has you gather three large stone slabs. Lotwil needs a while to test the smaller pieces you brought before.

Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus needs one more part from the elementals of the Badlands: bracers of rock binding, taken from greater rock elementals. By Lotwil's reckoning they are enough to gauge the strength of Lotwil's own shackles. After the stone slabs, Lotwil Veriatus asks for one last part from the Badlands' elementals. Bracers of rock binding, taken from greater rock elementals, should let Lotwil judge the strength of the shackles under construction. Lotwil's scrying showed a group of the elementals southwest, near some ogres, if memory serves. Five bracers are wanted, so there are spares, since Servo is notorious for misplacing reagents and research.

text.enUS: Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbone. At the Angerfang Encampment, renegade Dragonmaw orcs provide sturdy shinbones for armor. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely needs them to frame leg guards for warriors. Velora Nitely needs bones that can bear the strain of brutal leg guards. The renegade Dragonmaw orcs at the Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands have thick, sturdy frames, and their shinbones can brace the armor. Each bone must be tested by hand. Warriors discard any that snap under pressure.

Sully Balloo's Letter. Sully Balloo's Letter carries a soldier's farewell from the waters beneath the Thandol Span. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it bears the love that endured through his final days. Beneath the Thandol Span, where the Wetlands road crosses toward the Arathi Highlands, a dwarf's skeletal remains lie pinned under rushing water. In his grasp rests a fragile, waterlogged envelope. The letter inside begins, “My dear Sara...” Its parchment has suffered beneath the water, but the ink still holds the care with which the dwarven defender wrote in his final days or hours. He never returned to Ironforge.

Sully Balloo's Letter. At the Thandol Span, Sully Balloo's Letter carries a dwarf's final words from the icy waters below. Recovered from a drowned skeleton, it was written by a soldier lost in the battles for the bridge and addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge. Beneath the stone pilings of the Thandol Span, the land bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands, a drowned dwarf's skeleton rests in the riverbed. An envelope remains clutched in his bones, its paper damaged by water. Amid the fires of battle, the soldier wrote with painstaking care. His words begin, “My dear Sara,” and carry his voice beyond the river that claimed him.

Summoning Shadra. Master Gadrin gives you a parchment to read at the altar of Shadra'Alor, deep in the Witherbark realm of the Hinterlands, to summon Shadra the spider god. Her venom is then to be carried to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Gadrin's parchment is meant to be read at Shadra'Alor's altar, deep within the Witherbark realm of the Hinterlands. Doing so calls up Shadra the spider god. She must be defeated there, and her venom taken to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill.

Summoning the Princess. Theldurin the Lost says Myzrael must be beaten while she is still growing, before her strength is enough to challenge those who hold her captive. At the Shards of Myzrael you call her forth, defeat her, and bind her Eldritch Shackles to the Shards. Theldurin wants Myzrael stopped before her power swells enough to set her against her captors. Some claim she can be controlled; Theldurin asks why, then, the giants bothered to chain her at all.

Sun Rock Retreat. Atop the central Stonetalon peaks, Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde south of Mirkfallon Lake. Tauren hold the mountain sacred, while orcs and tauren use the settlement as a base and supply post. Sun Rock Retreat lies in a mountain basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, on ground the tauren have long held sacred. Ancient tradition says An'she, the Sun, kissed the peak above the village. For generations before the Horde came, tauren shamans and pilgrims traveled here for rites that crossed the mortal veil. They drew strength from the land's close bond with the spirit world.

Sundown Marsh. In the Wetlands' far west, Sundown Marsh holds deep water, stagnant pools, and dangerous wildlife. An eccentric pair keeps a solitary home along its muddy borders. Sundown Marsh fills the Wetlands' deepest, westernmost reaches, where deep water and thick mud hide a dense population of predators. Giant crocolisks, shifting oozes, roaming raptors, and territorial Mosshide gnolls move through the mist. Most travelers keep to the main cobblestone road between Menethil Harbor and Ironforge, leaving this corner largely untamed.

Sunken Treasure. Now that they are full-fledged Blackwater Raiders, Professor Phizzlethorpe and Doctor Draxlegauge are to help Mr. O'Breen find the lost elven treasure. To search the dark sea for the gems, the professor needs your protection while he charges a pair of goggles at an enchanted stone in a cave. The gems are next to impossible to find in the dark sea without help, so Doctor Draxlegauge has built goggles for the search. They need charging with power from the enchanted stone, in a cave a short way uphill. The cave is cursed, though: those who draw near are ambushed. Professor Phizzlethorpe asks you to defend him while he draws the stone's energy into the goggles.

Sunken Treasure. After the first part of Sunken Treasure, Doctor Draxlegauge lends you his Goggles of Gem Hunting and asks you to collect ten elven gems from the sea floor for Captain O'Breen, then bring the goggles back. Down on the sea floor, the gems have lain so many years that they have hardened into thick stone. The power built into the goggles lets you find them regardless, and Doctor Draxlegauge is proud of the gnomish ingenuity behind them. He lends you the goggles so you can gather the lost gems for Captain O'Breen.

Sunken Treasure. Doctor Draxlegauge hands you the elven gems and sends you to carry them to Captain O'Breen. After a few weeks among pirates, he and the professor know that holding on to their treasure is unhealthy. Doctor Draxlegauge does not want Captain O'Breen kept waiting, since the captain will want to see the elven gems for himself. After weeks among these pirates, the doctor and the professor have learned that being caught holding on to pirate treasure is bad for their health. He hands you the gems to carry to O'Breen, who waits at the bridge.

Sunken Treasure. After the previous step in the Sunken Treasure chain, Shakes O'Breen is stuck where he is and needs word taken to Fleet Master Seahorn at Booty Bay. He asks you to carry a sample gem as proof of the find. Shakes O'Breen wants Fleet Master Seahorn to hear of the find right away, yet he cannot easily get away. The tide is too low, and the creatures they disturbed are watching every move. He asks you to help the Blackwater Raiders by telling Seahorn in Booty Bay that the treasure is found and more is being brought up. A sample elven gem goes with you as proof.

Sunken Treasure. Fleet Master Seahorn, whose ships cannot sail from Booty Bay until they restock, asks you to carry a secret letter to Shakes O'Breen, busy off the Arathi coast. Fleet Master Seahorn sizes you up as the adventurous sort. His ships cannot leave Booty Bay until they have restocked, and he says heavy things are brewing both here and abroad. He needs top secret correspondence carried to Shakes O'Breen off the Arathi coast, and he asks whether he can trust you to deliver the message safely and in confidence.

Sunnyglade. Sunnyglade was once a wealthy, prosperous human settlement belonging to the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War. Devastated and eventually abandoned as the front lines collapsed, the ruined settlement now languishes under the dark influence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the First War tore southern Azeroth apart, Sunnyglade was celebrated for its wealth and comfortable prosperity. That peace was violently shattered when the Old Horde invaded. Orc raiding parties attacked the town and enslaved its surviving residents, leaving only a lone wizard's tower intact to study the arcane arts of human conjurers. Though Stormwind forces mounted an effort to rescue the captive peasants and rebuild the settlement, the surrounding Riverglades were steadily swallowed by the advancing Horde. Deeming the outer province lost, Stormwind's commanders eventually withdrew their resources to defend the homeland, leaving Sunnyglade to ruin.

Sunscorched Shell. Beneath Highperch, wyvern eggs leave shells hardened by Thousand Needles' desert heat. Armorer Mathiel in Darnassus uses them to make lacquer for mail links. Highperch wyverns lay eggs on the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor. Beneath their roosts, discarded shell fragments bake in the desert sun and searing winds. Their brittle remains hold a natural resilience that draws the attention of skilled artisans.

Sunscorched Shells. In Darnassus, Mathiel seeks wyvern eggshells to strengthen a new mailcrafting technique. The armorer works with the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard and sends warriors to gather shells from Highperch in Thousand Needles. Mathiel works from the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus and looks beyond night elven methods. He corresponds with Furen Longbeard, a skilled dwarven armorer in Stormwind, and draws on Furen's discoveries in metalwork and armor-smithing. Mathiel hopes to make mail reinforced with natural materials that can withstand great strain. To test the idea, he needs materials found nowhere near Teldrassil.

Suntara Stones. Dorius Stonetender is badly hurt in Searing Gorge, light-headed, with the world spinning and bleeding inside. He says he must get back to Ironforge and begs for your help to get him there. Dorius groans that he is badly injured. He feels light-headed, the world is spinning, and he is bleeding internally. His one wish is to get back to Ironforge, and he asks you to help him make the journey.

Suntara Stones. A singed letter that Dorius let fall is written to his brother. It tells of the Suntara stones, which are real and in the hands of the Dark Irons, whose leader Lathoric the Black uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. It is meant for Thorius at the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, and you are the one to carry it there. In the letter, Dorius writes to his brother that if it is being read, he is gone. The stones exist, and the Dark Irons hold them. Their leader, Lathoric the Black, uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. The team was taken to the cauldron, and their minds are twisted as they toil by day and by night to finish something called Obsidion. Dorius begs his brother to help them, his final wish, and asks that those who bring the letter be thanked.

Super Reaper 6000. At Windshear Crag, Ziz Fizziks seeks favor with his new boss, Sputtervalve. He wants the Venture Company’s plans for a great woodcutting machine designed by his rival, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. At Windshear Crag, the Venture Trading Company cuts deep into the Stonetalon Mountains to feed its logging operation. Ziz Fizziks, a goblin engineer recently cast out of the company, now works for Sputtervalve. He hopes to prove his worth to his new boss by taking the plans for the company’s massive automated woodcutting machine, the Super Reaper 6000.
