text.enUS: Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. In Windshear Crag, the Venture Company’s Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints are coveted by goblin rivals. They hold the technical schematics for an enormous mechanized woodcutter deployed in Stonetalon Mountains, designed under gnome engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle’s supervision. Venture Company operators carry the Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints through Windshear Crag. The plans show how to build the massive mechanized lumber harvesters driving the company’s relentless clear-cutting. To the dismay of traditional goblin engineers, the Venture Company put Gerenzo, a gnome, in charge of designing the model. When goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks was ousted from the operation, Sputtervalve quickly hired him to steal the designs. Yet Gerenzo’s dense, eccentric gnomish notations are almost as hard to decipher as the plans are to take by force.

Super Sticky. Tran'rek in Gadgetzan wants a fast profit and has a new idea: a super sticky glue. The tar for it must come from beasts in northern Un'Goro Crater, near the tar pits, and Tran'rek will share a little of the profit. Tran'rek hopes this newest idea will bring quick gold, and offers you a little of the profit. Ordinary tar is not sticky enough. Twelve samples are wanted, taken from creatures dwelling near the tar pits of northern Un'Goro Crater.

Supervisor Fizsprocket. Supervisor Fizsprocket is a high-ranking Venture Company overseer stationed within the mining tunnels of Mulgore. Charged by Morin Cloudstalker with putting an end to the goblin enterprise's calculated pillaging, Horde adventurers enter the mine to eliminate him and recover his detailed clipboard. Documents recovered from a destroyed Venture Company caravan revealed that the Venture Company was not merely digging for ore—they were deliberately formulating schemes to drive the tauren from Mulgore entirely. By uprooting the locals, the rapacious corporation sought unchecked freedom to strip the rolling hills and deep subterranean veins of every natural resource.

Supervisor Raelen. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Supervisor Raelen keeps timber moving toward Stormwind. She manages the laborers, tracks daily quotas, and oversees the lumber supply. Supervisor Raelen directs the woodcutters at Eastvale Logging Camp, near Marshal Patterson and the camp’s wagons. The camp stands on the edge of eastern Elwynn, near the Redridge Mountains, where the work brings its share of trouble. Raelen coordinates the crews and keeps them focused on their quotas despite hazards in the surrounding woods. She sees that gathered timber is processed, bundled, and sent on toward Stormwind.

Supplies for Sven. Darkshire sends provisions to Sven Yorgen's camp in northwestern Duskwood. The Carevin family keeps his small band supplied as they hold their watch against the shadows. Sven Yorgen and his few followers camp in the northwestern wilderness, far from Darkshire. Their numbers are too low, and their watch too demanding, to spare anyone for the journey into town. The Carevin family sends food, bandages, and other necessities to the isolated camp, helping the band hold its ground.

Supplies for the Crossroads. Thork needs supplies back at the Crossroads after Razormane quilboar raids. The stolen crates hold provisions the outpost needs amid conflict across the Barrens. Thork needs provisions restored to the Crossroads after a supply caravan is ambushed. The outpost links Horde travel, trade, and defense across the Barrens, and cargo arrives from Durotar and Mulgore. Without it, shortages of provisions, tools, and arms threaten daily life in the harsh wilderness.

Supplies from Darkshire. Abercrombie in western Duskwood asks travelers to fetch a rare thread from Darkshire. The hermit claims he is too frail to cross the haunted woods and asks for Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva. North of Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie lives alone in a shack in western Duskwood. He tells travelers that age and frailty keep him from making the dangerous journey through the woods to buy goods in Darkshire. His request seems simple: go to the township's town square and speak with Madame Eva for a spool of Ghost Hair Thread.

Supplies to Auberdine. Feero Ironhand carries provisions and messages north from Maestra's Post toward Auberdine, with Alliance adventurers guarding the way. Trouble around the Tower of Althalaxx and hostile infiltrators make the road unsafe. Maestra's Post lies on Ashenvale's western frontier, between the forest and Darkshore. After investigations into sinister activity around the Tower of Althalaxx, Delgren the Purifier sends supplies and intelligence to Sentinel Starbreeze in Auberdine. The outpost relies on armed escorts instead of solitary couriers, so Feero Ironhand travels with guards along the forest road.

name.zhCN: 列兵索尔森的补给物资

text.enUS: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek in Booty Bay hires a courier to haul miscellaneous goblin supplies north to Lieutenant Doren's camp. Local troll aggression has halted routine shipments, requiring an outside hand to ensure the goods reach Private Thorsen near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren and his outfit stationed near the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood rely on regular shipments arranged through Krazek. Persistent attacks from local trolls have made standard delivery hazardous, prompting the goblin merchant to contract an independent courier. The package must travel all the way up the jungle road, with Private Thorsen designated to receive it either in their camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

Supplies to Tannok. A crate bound for Tannok Frosthammer waits at the mouth of Coldridge Pass. Hands Springsprocket asks travelers to carry the inn supplies from Coldridge Valley to the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, since troggs have cut off the usual trade routes. Troggs have overrun Coldridge Pass, straining Coldridge Valley’s ties to the rest of Dun Morogh. The valley has long sheltered young Ironforge dwarves and Gnomeregan survivors in exile. Now the mountain pass is perilous to cross. Mountaineers are spread thin guarding settlements and defensive perimeters, so scheduled supply escorts can be delayed for days.

Supply and Demand. Drizzlik, a leathercrafter in Booty Bay, claims to be the finest in the South Seas. Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union has placed an order for twelve Excelsior-line boots, and Drizzlik needs skins from crocolisks by the northern Stranglethorn river to start shaping them. Drizzlik brags that this leatherwork is famed everywhere as exquisite, a connoisseur's choice. The latest order comes from Director Riddlevox, the Tinkers' Union's chief inventor, who wants a dozen of the Excelsior-line boots he favors, among Drizzlik's best sellers. To begin shaping them, Drizzlik needs skins from the crocolisks by the northern Stranglethorn river. The equipment stands ready, and leaving so important a customer unsatisfied would be a poor idea.

Supplying the Front. Ironforge sends smiths to help supply the Mountaineers in Loch Modan. Tormus Deepforge asks apprentices to forge weapons and armor for the defenders facing trogg attacks. Tormus Deepforge watches Khaz Modan’s borders from the forges of Ironforge. The Mountaineers in Loch Modan face sudden trogg attacks from ruins and caverns opened by excavation. Their defensive lines need fresh blades, belts, and fittings, so local smiths help keep them supplied.

Supplying the Sepulcher. At the Sepulcher, Deathguard Podrig seeks weapons for the hard-pressed garrison. He sends an order toward the Undercity as beasts, Scourge and other threats wear down its supplies. Deathguard Podrig says the Sepulcher is fairly well stocked, yet fighting in Silverpine Forest steadily drains its gear. Feral beasts, Scourge remnants and other local threats wear down weapons and armor or leave them behind after skirmishes. Acting under Executor Hadrec's orders, Podrig writes a requisition for Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer in the Undercity. Replacement arms and armor help the Forsaken hold their fragile footholds beyond Tirisfal Glades.

Surena Caledon. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin seeks his former pupil and a bloodstone choker. He sends an aspiring warlock after Surena Caledon, who betrayed him to join the Defias Brotherhood. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novices the forbidden arts of fel summoning. He once took a young woman named Surena Caledon as his pupil. He admired her natural magical talent and her beauty. Surena left her studies and Gakin's favor, then fled Stormwind with her lover, Erlan Drudgemoor, to join the Defias Brotherhood.

Surena's Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder seeks the choker he gave his former apprentice, Surena Caledon. After Surena fled to join the Defias Brotherhood, Gakin sent aspiring acolytes to take it back by force. Gakin the Darkbinder works quietly beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, where he took Surena Caledon on as a promising student of the dark arts. Drawn to her youthful charm and magical aptitude, he gave her a valuable bloodstone choker to aid her studies. Surena abandoned her training and fled with Erlan Drudgemoor, a rogue aligned with the Defias Brotherhood. Gakin will not leave a potent artifact in a traitor’s hands. He sends initiates seeking mastery over the void to find Surena at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and reclaim the necklace by force. Their deed will show where true loyalty lies.

Suspicious Hoofprints. Tracks of hooves stretch off from the Shady Rest Inn, whose bare frame still smokes. A few can be seen clearly, while more rows are nearly lost in the marsh's soft ground. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to report them to. The Shady Rest Inn is a bare frame now, still smoking, and trails of hoofprints stretch off from it. Some impressions are easy to see; others can hardly be made out in the soft ground. Krog at Brackenwall Village should hear about them.

Suspicious Hoofprints. Hoofprints trail away from the smoking remains of the Shady Rest Inn. A few are easy to see, while others are nearly lost in the soft marsh mud. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is the one to report them to. Rows of prints run off from the Shady Rest Inn, whose ruin is still smoking. A handful of the impressions are plain to see, while further rows are all but invisible in the marsh's soft mud. Captain Garran Vimes, in Theramore, should hear of them.

Suzetta Gallina. At the Gallina Winery in Stormwind City, Suzetta Gallina tends the family wine business. Suzetta Gallina helps run the Gallina Winery along Stormwind's Canals. The shop offers wines imported from across the kingdom or crafted there. Her family supplies taverns, nobles, and common folk. Suzetta is no figure in high politics, but her work keeps the capital's trade moving through troubled times.

Sven Yorgen. At the Hushed Bank, Sven Yorgen grieves his murdered family and seeks vengeance. He camps on the northern edge of the bank in western Duskwood with his companion Lars, determined to learn who ruined his home. Sven Yorgen remembers Duskwood before Medivh's fall brought gloom to the region. Born before the First War, he spent years working the soil at the Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood with his wife and children. Their quiet life ended when mysterious Dark Riders raided the homestead while Sven was away. They butchered his family and left the farm a graveyard.

Sven's Camp. In Duskwood, Sven Yorgen's grief still drives him to seek answers about his family's slaughter. A buried journal at the ruined farm may reveal who witnessed it. Sven Yorgen returned to find his family dead and his farm in ruins after dark riders struck while he was away. Grief and vengeance drove him to send allies to search the wreckage of the homestead. Beneath a mound of freshly turned earth lay a small, dirt-stained book, hastily hidden by a shadowy figure.

Sven's Revenge. In southern Duskwood, grief sends Sven Yorgen from his ruined farm in pursuit of its killers. Now camped in the western hills, he asks travelers to return to the farmstead where a stranger buried something near the barn. Hooded Dark Riders came down from Deadwind Pass and attacked Sven Yorgen's farm in southeastern Duskwood. While Sven was away, they killed his family. Returning to the slaughter, Sven saw an unknown figure skulking near the barn, hurriedly burying something. He left the hidden object behind and set out to hunt the killers.

Swamplight Manor. Swamplight Manor is an ironically named, ramshackle wooden shack nestled deep within Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the eccentric home and kitchen of 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, an isolated recluse known across the mire for his strange culinary appetites. Despite its humble, eerie isolation, the surrounding garden conceals intrigue that catches the attention of both Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Despite what its grandiose title suggests, Swamplight Manor is far from a lordly estate. It is merely a crooked, weather-beaten shack tucked into the haunted wetlands of Witch Hill. Its lone resident, the odd recluse known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, lives a solitary existence surrounded by fog, muck, and restless marsh ghosts. Jarl spends his days concocting unusual regional delicacies out of local wildlife, frequently recruiting wandering adventurers to hunt down bizarre ingredients like marsh frog legs and creature eyes to satisfy his strange craft.

Swarming Pillar. The Swarming Pillar is a towering rock formation in the heart of Silithus, thoroughly infested and reshaped by the silithid. Situated just south of Cenarion Hold, the spire takes its name from the relentless clouds of winged insectoids buzzing around its peaks and subterranean entrances. Rising abruptly from the shifting dunes of central Silithus, the Swarming Pillar serves as a grim monument to the unchecked expansion of the silithid. What began as a natural rock formation has been carved and encrusted with the resinous secretions and burrows of the insectoid swarm. Just south of Cenarion Hold, it constantly churns out broods of winged workers and soldiers, whose dark clouds fill the dry desert air and warn travelers to keep their distance.

Swoop Gizzard. Across Mulgore, swoops soar as predatory birds, and their gizzards go into traditional remedies for deadly toxins. Swoops hunt across Mulgore’s plains and mesas, with keen eyes and a taste for scavenging. Tauren use their feathers and meat in daily life, while herbalists and healers prize their internal organs, especially the gizzard. Dense and muscular, it helps counter venomous bites and festering infections when combined with cougar bones and wolf hearts.

Swoop Hunting. Swoop Hunting is a rite of tracking and marksmanship offered by Harken Windtotem in Bloodhoof Village. To prove their cleverness and patience, hunters and travelers are challenged to stalk the elusive birds across the rolling plains of Mulgore. Returning with their pristine trophy quills demonstrates both dedication to the hunt and respect for the natural trials of the Earth Mother. The grassy steppes of Mulgore are teeming with beasts, but few test a pursuer's instincts like the native swoop. These large predatory birds blend seamlessly into the skyline and plains, wheeling overhead or skimming low across the tall grass. Unlike lumbering plainstriders or grazing kodo, swoops demand acute focus and swift feet to run down, making their pursuit a traditional proving exercise for younger hunters seeking to earn their standing among the tribes.

Sylvanas Windrunner. In the Undercity, Sylvanas Windrunner rules the Forsaken from beneath Lordaeron's ruins. Once Silvermoon's Ranger-General, she was slain and raised by Arthas Menethil, then broke free of the Lich King's control. She joined Thrall's Horde to help secure her people's future and seeks vengeance on the Scourge. Sylvanas Windrunner once commanded Quel'Thalas's defense as Silvermoon's Ranger-General. When Prince Arthas Menethil led the Scourge into the high elven kingdom to reach the Sunwell, she fought to hold him back. Angered by her resistance, Arthas murdered her and denied her a clean death. He tore her soul from her body and made her a vengeful banshee, forcing her to serve the Scourge and help slaughter her own people.

Syndicate. The Syndicate is a widespread human criminal organization founded and led by dispossessed nobles of the fallen kingdom of Alterac. Operating out of fortified strongholds across the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the ruins of Stromgarde Keep, they wage an uncompromising war against both the Alliance and the Horde to restore their lost aristocracy. When the kingdom of Alterac collapsed in dishonor following King Aiden Perenolde's treachery during the Second War, its aristocracy was stripped of land and title. Refusing to accept their exile, the remaining Alteraci nobility banded together under the late king's son, Prince Aliden Perenolde. Adopting distinctive orange bandanas and standardizing their ranks with hired thugs, highwaymen, and hedge wizards, they forged the Syndicate. To the outside world, they behave like common brigands, raiding caravans, ambushing travelers, and running extortion rings. In truth, their criminal enterprises exist solely to fund an organized effort to reconquer their ancestral domains and subjugate surrounding lands.

Syndicate Assassins. Magistrate Henry Maleb, newly assigned to Southshore after the previous magistrate was assassinated, believes the Syndicate hired the killers. The trail led to a Syndicate camp north of Tarren Mill, and Maleb wants the members there slain. Magistrate Henry Maleb is the new magistrate of Southshore, assigned after the previous magistrate was assassinated. The assassins were never found, yet Maleb is almost certain the Syndicate hired them. The Syndicate is a gang of thieves, run by villainous nobles from Alterac, a kingdom that has since fallen. Maleb's last clues pointed to a Syndicate camp north of Tarren Mill, which the Horde occupies, and Maleb asks you to slay the Syndicate members found there.

Syral Bladeleaf. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf guides night elves arriving from Shadowglen. As a resident of Teldrassil, she speaks for the Council of the Forest and directs them to local caretakers, herbalists, and elders who watch over the crown's boughs. Syral Bladeleaf helps direct new arrivals through Dolanaar beneath Teldrassil's canopy. She speaks for the Council of the Forest, sending night elves to community leaders and herbalists in the village and nearby wilderness. Her guidance leads travelers to Denalan, a botanist at Lake Al'Ameth, and helps them replenish supplies for the village elders.

Syurna. In Darnassus, Syurna trains night elf rogues in the Cenarion Enclave. She guides aspiring scouts, spies, and covert operatives, then sends new rogues on trials of stealth and cunning. Syurna trains those who move unseen through Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, she teaches rogues evasion, lockpicking, and lethal strikes. The Sentinels display the Kaldorei’s martial strength, while the Sisterhood of Elune holds its spiritual wisdom. The Kaldorei also depend on shadows and stealth, and Syurna sharpens the eyes and blades that guard Teldrassil.

Tabetha. Tabetha is a reclusive, powerful human mage dwelling deep within Dustwallow Marsh at an isolated farmstead in the Quagmire. Far from the politics of Dalaran or Theramore, she instructs aspiring spellcasters and aids those seeking mastery over potent arcane and occult relics. Hidden away in the sodden expanse of Dustwallow Marsh north of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a secluded shack alongside her apprentices. Surrounding herself with alchemical vials and ancient tomes, she has deliberately chosen solitude over the academic hierarchies of the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite her remote location, her mastery of the arcane is renowned enough that spellcasters across Kalimdor brave beasts and mire alike to seek her guidance.

Tabetha's Farm. Deep in the murkiest reaches of the Quagmire lies Tabetha's Farm, an isolated homestead centered around a small wooden hut, a modest garden, and a private dock. Despite the treacherous marsh surroundings, this sanctuary serves as a hidden redoubt for the hermit mage Tabetha. Tucked away in the western wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Tabetha's Farm defies its unforgiving environment. Consisting of a weather-worn hut, small vegetable plots, and a dock for navigating the swamp's murky waterways, the homestead offers a quiet refuge far from the political rivalries of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Here, the reclusive human sorceress Tabetha lives in near-total seclusion, pursuing esoteric studies of arcane and fel power without interference from Dalaran or local authorities.

Tablet of Verga. In Skull Rock, the Tablet of Verga lies in Burning Blade hands, its demonic runes sought by warlocks in Orgrimmar. The Tablet of Verga bears ritual runes for summoning creatures of the Nether and bending them to a master's will. The Burning Blade cult stole the stone and hid it in a chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow seek it to study the markings and learn to summon a voidwalker. Recovering it also keeps the cult from gaining that same advantage.

Tahonda Ruins. The Tahonda Ruins are the sun-bleached remnants of an ancient tauren settlement swallowed by the salt and sand of the Shimmering Flats. Little is remembered of the villagers who once lived here, and dangerous Saltstone basilisks now stalk among the decaying tent poles and shredded leather. Situated in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats near the pass into Tanaris, the Tahonda Ruins stand as a somber monument to an abandoned tauren past. The village fell long ago, its weathered structures gradually engulfed by shifting white salt crusts. While some suspect the local Saltstone basilisks drove the inhabitants away, odd clues linger on the surviving structures. Two distinct sets of three parallel tears cut through the leather of a ruined lodge, suggesting the village met a violent end at the claws of powerful predators or hostile invaders before the desert claimed what remained.

Tai'jin. At the Razor Hill barracks, Tai'jin guides young Darkspear priests in their spiritual traditions. She teaches the balance of light and shadow and rites such as the Hex of Weakness. Tai'jin guides young priests from the Razor Hill barracks as they set out into Durotar. Orcs here turn chiefly to shamanism or warlock arts, while Darkspear trolls bring their communion with spirits and loas to the Horde. Tai'jin teaches the first principles of priesthood, the balance of light and shadow, and the spiritual heritage of troll culture.

Taiga Wisemane. Taiga Wisemane is a tauren elder residing in Shadowprey Village along the rugged western coast of Desolace. Watchful of demonic meddling across the barren wastes, he works to thwart the Burning Blade cult entrenched in the region. He directs Horde champions to disrupt demonic rituals and seal open gateways before the Burning Legion gains ground. Though Shadowprey Village is predominantly a Darkspear troll fishing settlement tucked away against the ocean, Taiga Wisemane has taken up station there to monitor the dark sorceries stirring across Desolace. He remains acutely aware of the spiritual corruption bleeding into the soil, keeping his focus fixed eastward where shadow cults and demonic remnants fester among ancient ruins.

Tainted Heart. In Teldrassil, Denalan gives adventurers a heart still troubled by corruption. Though its outer foul moss is gone, lingering energies remain, and he seeks to cleanse them with rich soil. Teldrassil's natural balance is troubled by a malady that warps its plants and beasts. After foul moss is stripped from a blighted growth, Denalan gives adventurers the Tainted Heart within. Darkness still clings to its tissue. Denalan hopes specially prepared, nutrient-rich earth can counter the taint and restore what was corrupted.

Tainted Keg. At Tarren Mill, Tainted Keg carries stolen dwarven stout laced with a lethal Forsaken brew made by Apothecary Lydon. Sent to imprisoned human farmers as refreshments, it tests poisons being developed by the Royal Apothecary Society. Dun Garok's dwarven riflemen lost a barrel of Shindigger Stout to thieves. Apothecary Lydon mixed the stout with his newly refined Elixir of Agony. The Forsaken chose an ordinary drink to carry the poison, hoping it would escape suspicion. A familiar ale became a swift death sentence.

Tainted Letter. Drusilla La Salle sends the Tainted Letter to human warlock initiates near Northshire Abbey. It bears her seal and directs them to seek her tutelage discreetly. The Tainted Letter bears Drusilla La Salle’s insignia and reaches initiates returning from nearby kobold camps. While priests, paladins, and soldiers train openly across Northshire Abbey’s lawns, fel practitioners must keep their path quiet. The letter directs novice warlocks to find their mentor near the abbey grounds without drawing the notice of town guards or clerics.

Tainted Letter. At Northshire, Tainted Letter calls novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards for instruction in the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle entrusts it to Marshal McBride, who delivers it to her recruits. Novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride after proving themselves against the kobold menace. While priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, warlocks must tread carefully. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter, which directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties.

Tainted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Alamar Grimm gives the Tainted Memorandum to novice gnome warlocks. His note urges them to leave old paths behind and seek power through the dark arts. At Anvilmar, fel practitioners are neither celebrated nor widely trusted. Alamar Grimm gives the Tainted Memorandum to young gnomes who study forbidden arts. He rejects the Holy Light and ordinary weapons, pointing to Gnomeregan’s fall as proof that old ways and tinkering failed their people. Grimm sees reliance on dwarven charity as a dead end. He urges gnomes to claim undeniable power and summon minions who will obey without question, if they are to secure their own future.

Tainted Memorandum. A quiet message draws a young gnome warlock toward the shadows of Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm passes it along, and Alamar Grimm calls the neophyte to learn dark power and rely on it rather than their dwarven hosts. In Coldridge Valley, the dark arts meet deep suspicion. While you help Sten Stoutarm deal with local threats, he slips you a note. His reluctance shows the uneasy truce that lets warlocks practice in Alliance lands. He warns you to watch yourself because your kind is not trusted around these parts.

Tainted Scar. The Tainted Scar is a demon-infested canyon carved into the southwestern Blasted Lands, saturated with foul fel magic from the nearby Dark Portal. It currently serves as the primary redoubt for the remnants of the Burning Legion on Azeroth, commanded by the doomguard Lord Kazzak. Once lush wetlands belonging to the ancient Black Morass, this desolate trench was utterly drained of life and turned the color of dried blood by chaotic fel energies leaking from the Dark Portal. Following Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal during the Third War, surviving forces of the Burning Legion rallied in the south. The colossal ered'ruin Lord Kazzak claimed the Tainted Scar as his stronghold, stationing elite demons across its blackened rises and dispatching dreadful lieutenants like Razelikh the Defiler to hold dominion over the wasted red soils.

Tainted Scroll. The Tainted Scroll is an early quest in Deathknell that directs newly awakened Forsaken warlocks to their trainer, Maximillion. Through this missive, Maximillion invites the initiate to embrace power and dark servitude as a means of securing genuine freedom. Shortly after newly risen Forsaken begin clearing out mindless Scourge remnants around Deathknell, an ominous missive arrives bearing the seal of Maximillion, the local warlock trainer. The scroll beckons the recipient to contemplate the nature of servitude and autonomy before returning to the ruined settlement to speak with him directly.

Takar the Seer. East of Camp Taurajo, Takar the Seer keeps a lone camp in the Barrens. Though surrounded by Horde lands, he remains loyal to the Alliance and shares occult knowledge with certain travelers. Takar the Seer lives alone beneath a simple tent east of Camp Taurajo. Tauren braves and orc patrols watch the surrounding Barrens, yet leave his remote clearing undisturbed. He distrusts curious Horde visitors but rarely starts a fight, keeping watch on the horizon and to himself. His camp lies far from Stormwind's politics.

Takata Steelblade. Takata Steelblade is an orc warrior stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Dispatched from Orgrimmar by Keldran alongside Maurin Bonesplitter, he spearheads the Horde's local campaign against demonic corruption. His primary focus is eradicating the regional satyr population affiliated with the sinister Burning Blade. Takata Steelblade was sent from the capital to Desolace under direct orders from Keldran, an influential figure in Orgrimmar committed to uncovering and purging demonic subversion. Operating out of the isolated Tauren encampment of Ghost Walker Post, Takata coordinates military efforts against the Legion-aligned forces plaguing the barren wastes.

Tal. At Thunder Bluff, Tal tends the Horde's chief wind rider roost above the plains of Mulgore. He sends seasoned wyverns carrying travelers across Kalimdor. Tal tends the wind rider roost on Thunder Bluff's central mesa, linking the tauren capital with the rest of the Horde. He cares for the loyal wind riders, or wyverns, keeping them healthy and well-fed for long journeys across Kalimdor. From the roost, he sends messengers to Camp Taurajo and scouts across the Barrens to Orgrimmar. The flights keep the towering mesa city in touch with its allies.

name.esES: Tal, maestro de jinetes del viento
name.frFR: Tal, le maître des coursiers du vent

text.enUS: Tal the Wind Rider Master. In Thunder Bluff, Tal the Wind Rider Master awaits a parcel from Ahanu. It is bound for Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads, linking Mulgore’s leatherworkers with Barrens merchants. Ahanu, a leatherworker on Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, sends finished hides to Jahan Hawkwing’s trade stall at the Crossroads. Trade between Mulgore and the Barrens matters to the young Horde, but the journey down the bluffs and across the plains takes hours on foot. Winged couriers carry parcels over the divide.

Talen. At his camp by the Zoram Strand, Talen searches for kaldorei relics along the coast. Nearby naga and Horde outposts make the work dangerous. At a camp beside the Zoram Strand, Talen studies the past instead of taking up arms. Naga and Horde outposts make the coast dangerous, but he keeps searching the ruins beneath the waves and sands for lost kaldorei relics. He depends on travelers to face the Wrathtail naga and recover artifacts, including pristine statuettes and the Ring of Zoram, held by their leader Ruuzel.

Talisman of Corruption. In Darkshore, Xabraxxis uses the Talisman of Corruption to turn the Blackwood furbolgs against their former allies. The satyr keeps it in his personal pouch, where its magic binds the tribe to fel madness. Auberdine's night elves have long sought the cause of the Blackwood furbolgs' turn against their former allies. Thundris Windweaver found that satyrs had brought about the tribe's fall. With talismans like this, demonic agents spread corrupting sorcery through the wilderness, tainting food and twisting peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. The devices channel fel magic that grips the minds and wills of local tribes.

Talk of the Town. A friendly barkeep points travelers eager for a livelier gathering toward the port of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Those looking for wilder company are directed to seek out Nixxrax Fillamug at the Salty Sailor Tavern. Word passes quickly between drink-servers and their patrons, and news travels far beyond the local counter. A friendly bartender passes along a tip about where the genuine commotion is brewing, pointing anyone searching for wilder spectacles toward the port of Booty Bay.

Tallonkai Swiftroot. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot watches the woods as corruption spreads beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. He sends young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and check the foul forces troubling the forest. Tallonkai Swiftroot watches the woods from Dolanaar, the settlement in Teldrassil’s canopy. Like many night elves beneath the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by wildlife acting in unnatural ways and shadows gathering at the edges of their homes.

Tallonkai's Jewel. On Teldrassil, Tallonkai's Jewel is lost from its druidic talisman. Ferocitas the Dream Eater prizes the emerald, which is needed to mend the Emerald Dreamcatcher. Tallonkai Swiftroot received the Emerald Dreamcatcher from Gaerolas Talvethen, warden of the druids in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The talisman is a powerful focus that draws energy from the Emerald Dream. When it was damaged, someone pried its radiant central emerald free and carried it into eastern Teldrassil. Ferocitas the Dream Eater, a corrupted Gnarlpine leader, took the jewel and made it into a necklace. Its green light glimmered in the forest gloom, but its harmony with the Emerald Dream meant nothing to the furbolg. To Ferocitas, it was only a trophy until it could be recovered.

Tallow. At Tarren Mill, Tallow watches the contested front lines for the Dark Lady and the Horde. The Forsaken warrior helps organize strikes against Alliance threats in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tallow stands with the Forsaken and Horde forces holding Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Conflict stirs across the region, with Southshore humans nearby, Syndicate outlaws on the roads, and hostile wildlife beyond the town. Tallow sends capable adventurers against the Boulderfist ogres of the Arathi Highlands to test their strength. Then he directs them to aid the besieged outpost of Hammerfall.

Talonbranch Glade. Talonbranch Glade is a quiet night elf redoubt nestled in the blighted hills of northern Felwood. Located just south of Timbermaw Hold, it provides a rare haven of pristine moonlight, sanctuary, and hippogryph transit in an otherwise corrupted wilderness. Perched on high ground near the tunnel to Timbermaw Hold, Talonbranch Glade serves as the northernmost bastion of the Alliance in Felwood. Centered around a sheltered night elf lodge and a functioning moonwell, the outpost offers a crucial refuge from the demonic corruption that has swallowed the surrounding forest. Alliance scouts, Sentinels, and passing adventurers use the glade to rest, recover, and plan their excursions deeper into the tainted woods or onward toward Winterspring and Moonglade.

Talondeep Path. Talondeep Path cuts beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The quiet tunnel links the woods west of Mystral Lake to Windshear Crag. Talondeep Path runs beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The tunnel links the woods west of Mystral Lake to the northwestern reaches of Windshear Crag. Surface trails cross dangerous country, with predators and warring factions, but the passage is calm and has no hostile beasts or encampments. Twisting side pockets, crevices, and natural alcoves break up the rock. Above ground, faint traces of an old road remain along the peaks, where travelers once crossed before the sheltered route through the stone.

Talondeep Vale. In south-central Ashenvale, Talondeep Vale lies between familiar landmarks and the road to the mountains. Talondeep Vale lies beneath the trees of south-central Ashenvale. Silverwind Refuge stands to the east, and the Ruins of Stardust lie nearby. To the south, the land rises toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers cross this wooded valley between the heart of Ashenvale and the high crags beyond.

Talvash del Kissel. Talvash del Kissel is a down-on-his-luck gnome jeweler who fled the fall of Gnomeregan and now resides in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Plagued by debt and persistent rumors following the loss of his home, he seeks capable adventurers to help recover lost treasures and restore shattered relics. His keen eye for precious gems and ancient baubles makes him a valuable contact for those plumbing the depths of Uldaman. Once a respected jeweler in the technological heart of Gnomeregan, Talvash saw his livelihood obliterated alongside his home when the troggs overran the underground city. Escaping with the surviving refugees to the dwarven capital of Ironforge, he set up camp in the Mystic Ward. Unfortunately, relocation did not treat him kindly. Rumors of questionable dealings and unpaid obligations quickly piled up, sinking the craftsman into deep financial distress. Unable to rebuild his trade through conventional means, Talvash relies on freelance adventurers to retrieve lost assets and salvage his ruined reputation.

Taming Rod. In Durotar, Taming Rods help novice hunters learn to command beasts. Trainers give them to students so they can practice before forming lasting bonds with animal companions. In Razor Hill, trainers such as Thotar give Taming Rods to aspiring orc and troll hunters. These enchanted tools help novices who cannot yet bind a wild creature permanently. A rod pacifies a regional predator, such as a dire mottled boar or an armored scorpid, so the hunter can practice giving commands and fighting beside an animal companion. The bond lasts only briefly, leaving the student free to learn without forming a lasting tie to the beast.

Taming the Beast. At Bloodhoof Village, Taming the Beast begins a young tauren hunter’s training with Yaw Sharpmane. The first trial takes the hunter into Mulgore to tame an adult plainstrider and begin a bond with the creatures of the Earthmother. Tauren hunters seek more than meat and hides when they hunt. Their ancestral traditions teach that meeting Mulgore’s wild creatures can bring a hunter closer to the Earthmother. Taming a companion turns a beast that might have been an adversary into a partner, joined with the hunter in the natural balance of the plains.

Taming the Beast. In Razor Hill, Taming the Beast begins a young Horde hunter’s training with a taming rod. Thotar guides aspiring hunters as they face a vicious dire mottled boar. Orc and Darkspear troll hunters in Durotar must learn to command the wild as well as survive it. Thotar, the veteran hunter trainer, gives young hunters an enchanted taming rod and sends them to face a fierce wild boar. They must subdue the beast without killing it, then make it a loyal ally.

Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast begins a night elf hunter’s trials with a wild Webwood Lurker. Dazalar lends an enchanted taming rod, and the hunter must win the spider’s trust through a bond with nature. For the kaldorei, hunting means more than tracking prey or surviving in the wild. It binds a hunter to nature, which is greater than any mortal. Animals are independent creatures, not tools to bend to a hunter’s will. Dazalar teaches novice hunters to meet them with respect. Before gaining a lifelong beast companion, a hunter must master local wildlife through ancient techniques, never brute force.

Taming the Beast. Taming the Beast is the first trial in a dwarven hunter's journey to mastering companion beasts in Dun Morogh. Guided by Grif Wildheart in Kharanos, young trackers learn to quell and bond with a ferocious Large Crag Boar using an enchanted taming rod. Up to this point, dwarven mountaineers and trackers rely solely on their gunplay, traps, and wilderness instincts. Yet the true soul of a hunter lies in forging a lifelong partnership with a wild beast. Grif Wildheart, stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, oversees this rite of passage. Rather than expecting a novice to permanently bind the first beast they come across, Grif instructs them to test their patience and resolve against several native species of Dun Morogh.

Taming the Beast. In Durotar, Taming the Beast tests a young Horde hunter's skill with wild creatures. Thotar in Razor Hill guides the hunter through one last trial: taming a dangerous armored scorpid. Success brings the ability to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting companion. Before a hunter can travel Kalimdor with an animal companion, they must prove they can command Durotar's harsh wildlife. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, sends trainees to subdue three kinds of creature with an enchanted taming rod. After facing dire boars and swift surf crawlers, they must now tame an armored scorpid, a venomous predator protected by heavy plates and known for resilience and speed.

Taming the Beast. In Durotar, Taming the Beast sends young hunters to the coast for their second trial. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, directs aspiring orc and troll hunters to pacify a surf crawler near the Echo Isles and extend their bond to coastal wildlife. After mastering a dire mottled boar, you turn your attention to the sea at Thotar's direction. Durotar's harsh shores are jagged, and shallow reefs teem with armored crustaceans. A surf crawler resists intrusion into its coastal domain, so taming one calls for patience and fortitude.

Taming the Beast. In Kharanos, Grif Wildheart sends a young dwarf hunter to face a snow leopard. This second trial follows the crag boar and tests a different kind of skill. Grif Wildheart points his students southeast of Kharanos, where snow leopards prowl Dun Morogh. The crag boar teaches a hunter to endure hard blows and raw force. The leopard demands another skill: meeting a swift, graceful predator on its own terms. Beneath its white coat lies dangerous strength, and Grif expects his students to learn how that strength strikes.

Taming the Beast. Grif Wildheart’s final trial in Kharanos tests a dwarf hunter’s control over a wild bear. You use an enchanted rod to subdue an aggressive Ice Claw Bear and learn to understand it. Passing unlocks the abilities to tame, call, and dismiss a permanent wild companion. Mountaineers and scouts across Dun Morogh rely on hardy beasts in its freezing crags. After students practice on swift, cunning predators, master huntsman Grif Wildheart sends you to capture an Ice Claw Bear. The bears prowl the snowdrifts east of Kharanos. Their raw strength and endurance test the control every dwarven huntsman must learn.

Taming the Beast. In Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane sets a young tauren hunter a new trial. The hunter must master the swift prairie stalker. After mastering the adult plainstrider’s endurance, you face a different kind of hunter. Prairie stalkers rely on speed, move in packs, and attack without fear. To tame one, you must approach this cunning predator without breaking stride, matching the wolf’s decisive nature.

Taming the Beast. In Mulgore, Taming the Beast brings a young tauren hunter to the last lesson under Yaw Sharpmane in Bloodhoof Village. A taming rod lets the hunter bond with a wild swoop and prove mastery of the air. Completing the trial grants lasting knowledge to tame, call, and dismiss a companion, with the Earthmother's trust. After you subdue predators on Mulgore's plains, Yaw Sharpmane turns your attention to the open sky. A swoop is a fierce bird of prey with a sharp beak, sweeping dives, and an intimidating air. Its talons test your reflexes and calm as you use the enchanted rod to bring its instincts into accord with your own.

Taming the Beast. Dazalar guides a night elf hunter through a second trial in Dolanaar. With an enchanted taming rod, you subdue a nightsaber stalker and learn how wild beasts differ. Dazalar teaches you that the forest's creatures do not all behave alike. Each species has its own temperament, and a hunter must learn to meet it on its own terms. Beneath Teldrassil's canopy, the next test brings you against beasts more cunning and predatory than webspinners.

Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast brings a young night elf hunter to the final trial of basic training. Under Dazalar’s direction, hunters tame a predatory owl of the skies before gaining the power to choose a lifelong companion. Night elf hunters must make peace with creatures across Teldrassil before their basic beastcraft is complete. After proving their will against beasts of the underbrush, they face the spirit of the skies, the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high in the boughs west of Dolanaar. Patience and a steady nerve are needed to pacify one with the enchanted Taming Rod.

Taming the Beast. Taming the Beast is an introductory trial where aspiring adventurers learn the art of pacifying and bonding with wild animal companions. Guided by Josephine Carson, initiates take a Taming Rod into the forest to tame a Rockhide Boar and practice essential survival skills. The task demonstrates that surviving harsh frontiers is far easier alongside a loyal beast, provided one honors and preserves the delicate balance of nature. For many wanderers of the wilds, venturing alone through untamed territories is an invitation to danger. An animal companion provides not only fierce protection in battle, but steadfast companionship through grueling journeys. Learning how to form such a bond is a vital milestone for any aspiring hunter or tracker. Through the guidance of Josephine Carson, novices are entrusted with a specialized Taming Rod and instructed to seek out a Rockhide Boar within the forest. Calming and directing such a creature serves as a foundational trial, proving whether a traveler possesses the focus and composure required to guide a beast without succumbing to fear or provoking needless bloodshed.

Taming the Beast. Taming the Beast is a hunter training lesson overseen by Josephine Carson. After learning the fundamentals of beast handling with a boar, the aspiring hunter must use a Taming Rod to earn the trust of a fiercer Gray Forest Wolf. A hunter's connection with the wild requires more than mere tracking and marksmanship; it demands the respect and patience needed to earn a wild creature's trust. After proving their foundational skills on simple boars, aspiring hunters are presented with a far fiercer challenge: venturing into the forest to tame a Gray Forest Wolf. Under the watchful eye of trainer Josephine Carson, the hunter is entrusted with an enchanted rod to calm the predator and learn the delicate balance between hunter and beast.

Taming the Beast. Taming the Beast is the culmination of a hunter's early training in Elwynn Forest, overseen by Josephine Carson. After demonstrating mastery over boars and wolves, hunters are tasked with using a Taming Rod to pacify and gain the trust of a Young Forest Bear. This final trial deepens a hunter's attunement to beasts and maintains the woodland's natural balance through respect and skill. Aspiring hunters in Elwynn Forest undergo rigorous training to understand the wild creatures sharing their lands. Having already demonstrated command over the cunning wolf and the hardy boar, hunters face a final test of courage and patience. Josephine Carson directs them to confront the Young Forest Bear, the burliest and mightiest of the forest's common predators. This rite tests whether a hunter can withstand the bear's raw strength and earn its trust rather than simply subjugating it.

Tammra Windfield. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield guides Horde travelers in honoring the land's renewal. The tauren watches over the wilderness and the safety of her kin in the Stonetalon Mountains. Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde among the crags of Stonetalon. Harpies, Venture Company loggers, and predators threaten the settlement. Tammra Windfield watches over the mountain wilderness and the travelers who enter. Her gentle manner carries the resolve needed to keep a home safe in such rugged country.

name.frFR: Les échantillons du désert de Tanaris

text.enUS: Tanaris Field Sampling. Switching on the power source sets the field testing kit glowing and vibrating. You now have two hours to gather what the Tanaris desert can give, or the data is lost. With the power source running, the kit glows and vibrates, so it seems to be working as planned. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle has said you have two hours to gather your data in the Tanaris desert: acceptable samples from eight basilisks, eight hyenas and eight scorpions. If time runs out, all of it is lost and another power source must be bought from Bilgewhizzle. The kit is meant to go back to Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan before the power runs out.

Tannok Frosthammer. At Thunderbrew Distillery outside Kharanos, Tannok Frosthammer waits anxiously for supplies from Coldridge Valley. Trogg attacks have cut off the roads to Anvilmar. Tannok Frosthammer watches deliveries and listens for news at Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Troggs have surged through Coldridge Pass, cutting off the usual route from Coldridge Valley and regular word from Anvilmar. Hands Springsprocket, a gnome tinkerer, carries supplies and news through the dangerous, snowy pass. Tannok shares the quiet worry of many Bronzebeards as subterranean troggs creep closer to their doorsteps.

Taragaman the Hungerer. Beneath Orgrimmar, Taragaman the Hungerer prowls the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm. The Horde seeks to destroy the hulking felguard, feared as the demonic master behind the Searing Blade cult, and end the demonic taint beneath the city. Taragaman the Hungerer prowls among Ragefire Chasm's magma pools, threatening Orgrimmar below. Scouts and young warriors sent into the dark caverns see the demonic felguard as the Searing Blade cult's leader. With infernal strength, he bends the weak-willed and corrupts the passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

Taretha's Gift. After the step with Lord Aliden Perenolde, Elysa gives up Taretha's pendant and asks only to be left in peace. You carry it back to Krusk in Tarren Mill. Elysa has no wish to hold on to any memory of Lord Aliden Perenolde. You may take the pendant, Elysa says, and begs only that you then go in peace. It once belonged to Taretha Foxton, a childhood friend of Thrall's. You are to bring it to Krusk in Tarren Mill, so that it returns to the orcs.

Targorr the Dread. Deep in the Stormwind Stockade, Targorr the Dread waits among the rioting convicts. His execution was delayed by corruption and neglect, and the Defias uprising gave him a chance to escape. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served Warlord Gath'Ilzogg as the Blackrock clan's supreme executioner. He worked from the occupied ruins in Redridge, where his cruelty surpassed even the Dark Horde's violent ways. Stormwind guards and militiamen who defended the borderlands suffered torment and slow deaths at his hands. Across the kingdom, few names were more reviled.

Tarindrella. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella watches over Teldrassil's sheltered woods. The dryad works with night elf protectors to investigate corruption among the World Tree's wildlife. Tarindrella dwells in Shadowglen, a protected glade atop Teldrassil. Dryads are fierce caretakers of nature, born of the demigod Cenarius. Many live deep in ancient Kalimdor forests such as Ashenvale, but Tarindrella watches over this young grove. She bridges the wild spirits and young night elf defenders taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil. Her chief concern is a taint creeping through the forest. She sends reliable adventurers to drive back local pests and gather clues to its source.

Tarrel Rockweaver. At Menethil Harbor’s bridge, Tarrel Rockweaver anxiously waits for news of his wife, Merrin. The dwarf fears for her safety after she joined an inland archaeological expedition. Tarrel Rockweaver watches the bridge at Menethil Harbor, where trade and military shipments pass. His wife, Merrin Rockweaver, joined Prospector Whelgar’s prestigious archaeological expedition deeper in the Wetlands. Violent raptors overran the excavation site and cut off regular communication. Stranded in town, Tarrel begs travelers to scout east toward Whelgar’s Excavation Site and learn whether Merrin survived.

Tarren Mill. Tarren Mill holds the Horde's line in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, beneath the Alterac Mountains. Once a peaceful human farming village, it is now a Forsaken outpost locked in conflict with Southshore to the south. Tarren Mill's fields and mill have fallen silent since the Third War. Before then, it was a thriving farming town loyal to Lordaeron. During the Second War, Alliance forces near the town freed captured high elven archers from orc encampments, securing Quel'Thalas's full commitment to the Alliance of Lordaeron. The town's living inhabitants are gone, replaced by the Forsaken. Its buildings are weathered, its fields barren, and its mill quiet. The Forsaken fortify Tarren Mill against mountain beasts, Syndicate outlaws, and Alliance skirmishers.

Tattered Manuscript. In Thousand Needles, the Tattered Manuscript lies hidden in Splithoof Hold. Its torn pages came from the Tome of the Cabal, and warlocks seek them to learn how to summon a felhunter. The Tome of the Cabal was once a unique, intact volume kept in the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. An unknown defiler tore almost half its pages from the binding. The remaining spine and pages became known as the Moldy Tome. They were sent south toward Khaz Modan, then lost at sea. The torn leaves crossed the Great Sea to Kalimdor and came into the hands of the Galak centaur inside Splithoof Hold.

Tatternack Steelforge. On the Barrens frontier, Tatternack Steelforge offers work to travelers who can handle raw metal and dangerous wildlife. The orc smith studies local ores and seeks to arm Horde forces against threats across the plains. Across the Barrens, Horde outposts need weapons to face wild beasts, centaur raiders, and hostile quilboar. Tatternack Steelforge brings his people's metalworking knowledge to the frontier. He seeks practical weapons and unusual geological specimens to strengthen the Horde's foothold against those threats.

Tauren. The tauren, or shu'halo in their native tongue, are a noble race of nomadic bovine humanoids native to central Kalimdor. Deeply devoted to the Earth Mother, shamanism, and the natural world, they were driven near extinction by ruthless centaur clans before forging a bond with Thrall's New Horde. Today, united under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, they have established a permanent home across the verdant plains of Mulgore and the high rises of Thunder Bluff. For countless generations, the tauren lived as seasonal nomads wandering the arid plains of the Barrens, hunting the great kodo and listening for the voice of the Earth Mother. However, their peaceful wanderings were plagued by centuries of brutal bloodshed. The ferocious centaur tribes, born from the tragic union of Zaetar and Princess Theradras, waged an unrelenting war of extermination against them. Lacking a fortified homeland and reluctant to wage endless war, the tauren tribes were pushed to the brink of annihilation, their very survival hanging by a thread.

Tavernkeep Smitts. At the Scarlet Raven in Darkshire, Tavernkeep Smitts hears the town’s gossip and its unsolved tragedies. His long memory and keen eye make him a valuable contact for anyone seeking the region’s dark history. Tavernkeep Smitts keeps the Scarlet Raven’s hearth fires warm and serves drink to weary travelers, townspeople, and nervous Night Watch guards facing Duskwood’s perils. He has been one of Darkshire’s familiar public faces for years, and rumors pass through his tavern every day. While other townsfolk hide behind locked shutters, Smitts watches those who enter and leave. He notices strange patrons, hurried departures, and behavior that does not fit the town.

Tazan's Satchel. Near Ratchet, Tazan carries a locked satchel as he deals with pirates along the coast. The Shattered Hand wants the secret information inside. Tazan deals with pirates camped along the Barrens coast near Ratchet. Therzok, a guild master of the Shattered Hand beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, takes notice. The guild seeks covert power beyond Warchief Thrall's cautious diplomacy, and marks Tazan for elimination to seize the intelligence in his satchel.

Tear of Tilloa. In Duskwood, the Tear of Tilloa grows on the Mistmantle estate near Darkshire. Its alchemical use draws interest from those seeking rare reagents. The Tear of Tilloa grows on the grounds of Stalvan Mistmantle’s estate outside Darkshire. Duskwood’s soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, yet the small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. It grows rarely and in a secluded place, drawing those who seek uncommon reagents beyond lawful markets.

Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan in the southern Barrens, dwarven excavators have unearthed the Tear of the Moons. Its strange power draws Feegly into obsession, while General Twinbraid fears what the crystal can do. Dwarven excavators unearthed the Tear of the Moons during the first digging at Bael Modan. The crystal's strange radiance captivated the miners, especially Feegly. He claimed it gave him great strength, then grew unstable and turned against his comrades. General Twinbraid, commander of the expedition, feared the relic's influence and declared it cursed. He took the crystal and locked it in his personal strongbox at Bael'dun Keep. Then he cast Feegly out into the Barrens.

Tears of the Lady. Tears of the Lady is an urgent mercy task undertaken for Elegael in the forest of Shadowgale. To treat wounded comrades left stranded in the Nightclaw Den, travelers must scour local tree trunks for Lady's Tear, an antiseptic moss vital for binding severe wounds. In the shadowed depths of Shadowgale, Elegael urgently seeks aid to treat companions trapped within the Nightclaw Den. With critically injured allies awaiting rescue, conventional supplies are lacking, requiring field medicine scavenged directly from the surrounding wilderness. The effort hinges on securing natural remedies before time runs out for those left behind.

Tears of the Moon. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora mourns Lady Sathrah's madness. Once cherished by Elune, the great spider has become dangerous, and the Sisterhood seeks to end her suffering and recover her sacred spinnerets. In Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Sathrah was once blessed by Elune. Beneath the night sky, she wove delicate silver webs that caught the evening mist on Teldrassil's boughs. The Sisterhood of Elune gathered and kept the shimmering dew from those webs, which held healing powers for their sacred ministrations.

name.zhCN: 尖端机器人的存储器核心

text.enUS: Techbot's Memory Core. In Gnomeregan, Techbot's Memory Core holds the data Tinkmaster Overspark needs to study its corrupted behavior. Before Gnomeregan fell, Techbot aided Tinkmaster Overspark and his fellow inventors with a wealth of devices and knowledge. During the city's fall, an errant electrical discharge jolted the automaton and inverted its positronic brain into a hostile negatronic state. Now Techbot wanders Gnomeregan's tainted halls, attacking anyone in sight. Overspark hopes the memory core will help him understand the malfunction and restore his creation to its senses.

Teldrassil. After the harpies are driven back, Arynia Cloudsbreak sends you with a report to Darnassus. The inscribed bark tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm about the boughs and the corruption still troubling the World Tree. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak entrusts you with a piece of inscribed bark after you clear the harpies from their nests in the Oracle Glade. The Oracle Tree watches over the forest, and with the harpies gone, Arynia can send word to the kaldorei leadership. You carry her report through the wilderness to Darnassus, the great forest of stone, and deliver it to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm.

Telescopic Lens. Gazlowe needs the Telescopic Lens to finish the observatory telescope above Ratchet’s harbor. Southsea pirates took it from a ship, and the lens remains in their camp south of town. Ratchet is known chiefly for ruthless commerce, but its overseer and chief engineer, Gazlowe, has greater mechanical ambitions. His observatory rises above the harbor to house a telescope for watching maritime traffic and the stars. The larger lens came safely overland from Durotar. The smaller, vital lens traveled by sea, where Southsea Freebooters prey on merchant lanes off the Barrens coast.

Telf Joolam. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, Telf Joolam guides Horde initiates through the trials of fire. The Darkspear shaman teaches them to commune with and command the volatile element. Telf Joolam tends the Shrine of the Dormant Flame among the crags overlooking the borderlands. Fire spirits demand sharp discipline and unwavering focus, unlike the calm certainty of earth or the patient depth of water. Telf prepares young shamans for trials that test their worth before the wild embers consume them.

Temple Gardens. Temple Gardens gather the waters and bridges at Darnassus's heart, with the city bank on their main island. The Temple of the Moon borders them to the south, and a glowing tree portal carries travelers to Teldrassil's base. Water and wooden bridges cross the center of Darnassus, linking the Temple Gardens' islets to the Cenarion Enclave in the north, the terraces to the east, and the Temple of the Moon to the south. Night elves tend the flowing waters and foliage, making a quiet place of rest for travelers and priestesses.

Temple of Arkkoran. The Temple of Arkkoran is an ancient night elven ruin resting on the northeastern cliffs of Azshara above the Shattered Strand. Originally built in honor of Elune, the crumbling structure has since been claimed by the towering sea giant Arkkoroc and his aquatic thralls. Like many of the grand ruins dotting Azshara's coast, the Temple of Arkkoran was once a sanctum dedicated to the moon goddess Elune before the Sundering shattered the ancient night elf empire. Today, its weathered marble steps and broken colonnades are overrun by tidal monstrosities. The sea giant Arkkoroc presides over the temple's highest level, surrounded by loyal makrura and vicious murlocs who violently defend the surrounding coastline from any land-dwelling intruders.

Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The Temple of Atal'Hakkar, widely known as the Sunken Temple, is a submerged fortress built by exiled troll priests dedicated to the blood god Hakkar. Sunk beneath the marshes by the green dragonflight centuries ago, its drowned halls remain a staging ground for forbidden rituals and dark corruption. Over a millennium ago, a catastrophic civil war shattered the Gurubashi Empire when the Atal'ai priesthood attempted to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer. Exiled to the north, the surviving zealots raised a massive stone temple in the Swamp of Sorrows to finish their dark work. Learning of their scheme, the Dragon Aspect Ysera smashed the ziggurat deep into the mire, inundating its chambers beneath the Pool of Tears. Green dragon wardens were left behind to guard the drowned ruins and ensure Hakkar's return was thwarted forever.

Temple of Zin-Malor. The Temple of Zin-Malor is an ancient night elven sanctuary located within the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Originally dedicated to the moon goddess Elune, the crumbling structure is now held by the Spitelash naga under the direct command of Warlord Krellian. Before the Great Sundering, the Temple of Zin-Malor stood as a grand house of worship dedicated to Elune. Its architecture closely mirrors both the nearby Temple of Arkkoran and the modern Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, bearing the graceful, sweeping stonework characteristic of pre-Sundering night elven civilization. Today, however, its moonlit marble is weathered and broken, overtaken by the serpent-bodied Spitelash naga. These invaders have claimed the holy grounds for themselves, turning a place of quiet reflection into a militarized redoubt.

Temple of the Moon. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people from the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The sanctuary is the seat of government on Teldrassil and home to the Sisterhood of Elune, whose priestesses tend a sacred moonwell. Built soon after the Third War, the Temple of the Moon rose as the night elves settled Teldrassil. It is among the largest stone structures made by modern kaldorei hands. Its marble came from quarries on the Kalimdor mainland and crossed the sea by magical means. At the heart of the temple, a broad moonwell rests beneath the statue of Haidene. Pilgrims come to worship and reflect beside its consecrated waters. The temple also holds Darnassus's highest seat of government, where High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people through a new age.
