text.enUS: Ten Signets for War Supplies. Warlord Gorchuk trades Horde Commendation Signets for war supplies in Orgrimmar. Champions give up formal recognition for equipment that can help keep soldiers supplied at the front. Warlord Gorchuk oversees the Horde's supplies in the Valley of Spirits. As the Horde gathers its legions, weapons, rations, and armor must reach the front. Champions who have proved their dedication can trade commendation signets for useful equipment drawn from the army's reserves.

Tenaron Stormgrip. High in Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves through their people's recent history. He also asks them to gather water from a moonwell. Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves on Aldrassil's winding wooden platforms. From high in Shadowglen's central tree, he watches the local woods and their moonwells. He teaches novices about their spiritual bond with the World Tree.

Tenaron's Summons. In Shadowglen, Tenaron's Summons calls you to Aldrassil. After helping Gilshalan Windwalker with woodland dangers, you are asked to meet Tenaron Stormgrip high in the great tree. The call draws you from local troubles toward the spiritual afflictions touching Teldrassil. Your work against the venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife in the glen has reached Tenaron Stormgrip. Gilshalan Windwalker tells you the elder has asked for your presence. Even night elves, with their long lives, know better than to keep an elder waiting atop Aldrassil.

name.zhCN: 泰瑞纳斯·米奈希尔二世

text.enUS: Terenas Menethil II. Across Lordaeron, Terenas Menethil II carries the weight of a kingdom through war and its aftermath. For more than five decades, he ruled as a wise and diplomatic king, forged the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War, and gave shelter to the young Prince Varian Wrynn. His murder by his corrupted son, Prince Arthas, began Lordaeron’s collapse to the Scourge. When refugees from Stormwind reached the north with Sir Anduin Lothar, King Terenas Menethil II answered their call. He gathered the monarchs of the divided human kingdoms, along with envoys from Ironforge and Quel'Thalas, and brought them together in the Alliance of Lordaeron. Terenas did not claim command of its armies. He chose Lothar as supreme commander, uniting humanity’s kingdoms for the first time in millennia. Together, they defeated the Old Horde.

Terenthis. Terenthis watches the corruption spreading through Darkshore from Auberdine. The Cenarion Circle sent the night elf druid to investigate its reach from Teldrassil and seek help from travelers and local allies. Terenthis investigates Fel Moss and other corruption in Darkshore. The Cenarion Circle sent him to Auberdine to track the blight spreading from Teldrassil. Night elves fear it may shatter the balance of northern Kalimdor. Terenthis seeks the cause of the rot and ways to stop it before it consumes the forests.

Teronis' Corpse. On an island in western Ashenvale, Teronis' Corpse lies in Lake Falathim. The night elf scout left Astranaar to find Dartol's Rod and help cleanse the forest. Teronis was sent from Astranaar to recover Dartol's Rod. Raene Wolfrunner gave the night elf scout this charge, seeking an ancient relic that could cleanse corrupted woodland magic. Teronis searched the waters of Lake Falathim, but hostile murlocs swarmed the island and killed him. His journal remains there, while the murlocs took the rod's radiant gemstone.

Teronis' Journal. Teronis' Journal follows a scout's search through Ashenvale for a gem tied to a rod he hoped could slow furbolg attacks. Teronis, a longtime friend of Raene Wolfrunner, aided the Sentinels and searched Ashenvale for a gem. He believed it belonged to a rod that could slow the furbolg attacks on his people. Near the shore, aggressive creatures brought his journey to an end. The journal was recovered from his personal effects in remarkably good condition. Its findings about a radiant gem that once formed part of the rod give Astranaar's defenders a trail to follow in his unfinished search.

Terrace of Repose. The Terrace of Repose is a pristine courtyard garden located just outside the entrance to the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Maintained by the Scarlet Crusade, it stands as one of the few places in northern Lordaeron completely untouched by the Plague of Undeath, complete with green hedges and clean water. Situated just north of the grand entrance into the Scarlet Monastery, the Terrace of Repose offers a surreal contrast to the rotting forests of Tirisfal Glades. While the rest of Lordaeron chokes under grey mist, corrupt soil, and stagnant bogs, this terrace boasts verdant, neatly pruned hedges and a functioning fountain fed by fresh, uncontaminated water. For the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, the garden serves as physical proof of their divine righteousness and purity, a sacred bastion demonstrating that holy devotion can ward off the Scourge's corruption.

Terror Run. Terror Run is a perilous swath of land situated in the southwestern reaches of Un'Goro Crater, directly west of the insectoid hives of the Slithering Scar. True to its fearsome name, the territory is stalked by predatory beasts, ranging from massive devilsaurs to ravenous diemetradons and swooping pterrordax. Stretching across the southwestern shelf of Un'Goro Crater, Terror Run lives up to its ominous reputation. Fierce pterrordax wheel through the humid air above while massive diemetradons, stegodons, and apex devilsaurs roam the low brush below. The territory sits directly in the shadow of the mountainous rim, wedged uncomfortably close to the chittering alien mounds of the Slithering Scar. Along the eastern edge of the flats lie the ruined remnants of a camp left behind by Williden Marshal's expedition, a sobering reminder of researchers who were caught unprepared when the crater's primeval predators closed in.

name.frFR: Chemin de l'Aile de la terreur

text.enUS: Terror Wing Path. Terror Wing Path is a rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Burning Steppes. Infested by whelps and dragonkin of the black dragonflight, it serves as a perilous approach into the remote northeastern corner of the Steppes. Carved into the craggy, ash-covered foothills of the eastern Burning Steppes, Terror Wing Path earns its name from the aerial predators and wyrmkin that claim it. Broods of the black dragonflight prowl these defiles, fiercely guarding clutches and hunting anything foolish enough to wander into their shadow. Ash and soot blanket the stone trails, making any trek beneath the canyon walls a treacherous venture.

Terrordale. Terrordale is a ruined, ghost-haunted settlement nestled in the northwestern edge of the Eastern Plaguelands. Bordered by the blighted Plaguewood and the arachnid-infested Terrorweb Tunnel, the ruined town swarms with the Scourge and the restless dead. Once a quiet settlement in northern Lordaeron, Terrordale fell along with the rest of the kingdom to the Scourge. Today, the village stands in grim ruin near the mouth of the Terrorweb Tunnel. Its streets are choked with restless shades and wandering undead, while the surrounding trees of the Plaguewood encroach on its rotten timber. Amidst the desolation, only a handful of eccentric residents dare remain—such as the peculiar merchant Augustus the Touched and the ghost hunter Egan, who attempts to free the tortured spirits caught between worlds.

Terrorweb Tunnel. Terrorweb Tunnel is a subterranean passage carving through the mountains between Terrordale and the Thondroril River. Infested with the Scourge's undead nerubian crypt fiends, it forms a hazardous subterranean shortcut across the western border of the Eastern Plaguelands. Bored straight through the mountains flanking the Thondroril River, the Terrorweb Tunnel links the contaminated village of Terrordale with the riverbanks to the south. Rather than typical ghouls or skeletal sentries, this dark subterranean bypass is claimed entirely by crypt fiends—mummified nerubian arachnids raised into servitude by the Lich King. Traveling the length of the passage cuts out long circuits around the mountain slopes, but requires navigating thick webs and avoiding towering nerubian overseers that patrol the dark.

Test of Endurance. The Test of Endurance is the second rite in a series of spiritual trials overseen by Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles. Having already proven their courage of spirit, Horde adventurers are tasked with pushing their physical endurance to the limit by infiltrating Roguefeather Den and drawing out the fierce harpy leader, Grenka Bloodscreech. Dorn Plainstalker, dwelling at the Weathered Nook, takes it upon himself to temper young warriors before they venture into the wider, harsher world. Where the initial rite proved that a traveler possessed unshakable faith and steady nerve, this trial tests physical fortitude. In Dorn's philosophy, true readiness requires harmony between spiritual devotion, mental discipline, and the sheer stamina to survive sustained brutality.

Test of Faith. The Test of Faith is a spiritual rite administered by the hermit Dorn Plainstalker high above the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. It challenges Horde adventurers to prove their resolve by stepping off a precarious wooden plank into the open chasm below. Dorn Plainstalker dwells in a secluded vantage overlooking the wind-carved spires of Thousand Needles, pondering the facets that make up a living being: the mind, the body, and the spirit. Rather than relying on simple tribal traditions, Dorn administers his own trials to measure what truly lies within an adventurer. He posits that while conviction can take many forms, the essential quality is simply having the fortitude to believe in something strongly enough to risk one's life on it.

Test of Lore. Following trials of faith, endurance, and strength in Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker directs Horde champions northward to Stonetalon Mountains. There, a wise shaman named Braug Dimspirit waits to administer the Test of Lore. This trial shifts the focus from physical resolve to an understanding of the world's deep history and widespread suffering. In the sheltered refuge of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker pushes initiates through demanding trials meant to test their spiritual conviction, physical endurance, and martial prowess. Yet brute strength and blind faith alone do not make a true champion of the Horde. Dorn recognizes his own boundaries as a teacher and sends those who have proven themselves to Stonetalon Mountains, where an elder shaman can test their intellect and worldliness.

Test of Lore. The Test of Lore is a trial set by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to Talondeep Path, testing a Horde adventurer's mind rather than their physical endurance. To pass, the seeker must venture deep into the haunted barrow dens of Ashenvale, recover an ancient tome of dragon history, and study its contents before being quizzed. After proving their physical endurance and unwavering faith across the salt flats and plateaus of Thousand Needles, candidates under Dorn Plainstalker's series of trials are sent north to Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. Stationed near the mouth of Talondeep Path, Braug dismisses the earlier challenges as simple physical exercises. To truly serve the Horde with distinction, an adventurer requires a sharp and disciplined intellect, prepared to understand ancient histories rather than merely striking down beasts.

Test of Lore. This leg of the Test of Lore sends Horde adventurers across the Great Sea to the ruins of Lordaeron. Having answered Braug Dimspirit's initial riddle in the Stonetalon Mountains, you are directed to seek a former human scholar among the Forsaken in the Undercity. After proving your mettle and unraveling the history of the Dragon Aspects recorded in the Legacy of the Aspects, Braug Dimspirit admits his own knowledge has limits. Rather than keeping the trial confined to Kalimdor, Braug demonstrates the broad, surprising reach of the Horde's ties by pointing you toward the undead capital beneath the ruins of Lordaeron.

Test of Lore. The Test of Lore is a trial of intellect and historical memory set by the hermit Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. After retrieving the ancient tome Legacy of the Aspects, travelers must demonstrate their understanding of ancient history by answering Braug's inquiry. Those who fail to heed the text find themselves abruptly banished across Kalimdor. Part of a broader series of trials originating with Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, the Test of Lore shifts focus away from martial survival or blind trust toward understanding the world's ancient past. Braug Dimspirit, residing in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, requires seekers to recover ancient texts and genuinely absorb the knowledge held within their pages.

Test of Lore. This trial marks the intellectual examination in a broader series of spiritual tests originating in Thousand Needles. After scouring the world for historical texts, initiates present themselves to Parqual Fintallas in the Undercity to prove they understand the darker histories that shape Azeroth. While many trials among the Horde test martial strength or raw endurance, the Test of Lore demands scholarly dedication. Originating from Dorn Plainstalker's spiritual regimen at the Weathered Nook, the journey carries candidates far from the wind-carved canyons of Thousand Needles into the shadowed halls of the Undercity. Parqual Fintallas serves as the examiner, holding seekers to an exacting standard of historical literacy.

Test of Strength. The Test of Strength is the third trial overseen by the tauren mystic Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles. To prove their physical prowess, Horde champions are tasked with hunting down Rok'Alim the Pounder, an ancient, free-roaming rock elemental, and returning with remnants of his shattered form. Long ago, during the reign of the Old Gods, primordial elementals blanketed the surface of the world, serving their dark masters. When those ancient entities were overthrown and sealed beneath the earth, the elemental spirits lost their tether to this realm, largely fading from physical existence unless bound and summoned by modern spellcraft. A few entities, however, were stubborn and potent enough to linger on Azeroth indefinitely without magical anchors. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such relic, wandering the arid canyons of Thousand Needles as a living echo of that primordial age.

text.enUS: Testing an Enemy's Strength. Magatha Grimtotem seeks retribution after troggs slaughter her emissaries beneath Orgrimmar. Rahauro on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to cull the troggs infesting it. Magatha Grimtotem sent tauren emissaries into the fiery depths beneath Orgrimmar to make peace with the troggs. The creatures slaughtered the delegates as soon as they arrived. Magatha saw the massacre as an insult to the tauren and a growing danger to the Horde. She resolved to answer it with force.

Testing the Vessel. Witch Doctor Uzer'i, after Return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i, calls this a test of the ritual Uzer'i performed and of your own abilities. You are given a vessel that can shrink and capture a creature, and sent to the Hinterlands to take ten wildkin with it, then bring them back to Uzer'i in Feralas. Witch Doctor Uzer'i calls this a trial, both of the ritual just performed and of your own skills. The vessel you receive can reduce a creature in size and trap it within. You make for the Hinterlands and seek out wildkin, whose kind once belonged to Elune, the night elf goddess, as pets. Uzer'i names the vicious, primitive and savage owlbeasts as your quarry. Ten must fall, each shrunk into the vessel before its spirit slips away. Ten, and the vessel, go back to Uzer'i in Feralas.

Testing the Wells. Alba Fairmoon sends you across Westfall to test the farm wells. The samples may reveal what is poisoning the soil and groundwater. Alba Fairmoon asks you to test Westfall's groundwater. Neglect and banditry have already hurt the open plains, and poison beneath the earth threatens the farmland that remains. You collect samples from farm wells so Alba can learn what is tainting the soil and water.

Thadius Grimshade. Thadius Grimshade is a Wildhammer dwarf diviner dwelling within the mage tower of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Though he parted ways with Aerie Peak long ago to study esoteric and darker magical arts, he remains loyal to his kin at heart. Unlike most Wildhammer dwarves who prefer the open skies and roaring winds of the Hinterlands, Thadius Grimshade makes his home inside Nethergarde Keep. Driven by a thirst for arcane divination and darker mystic lore, he relocated to the edge of the tainted Blasted Lands to pursue his esoteric studies. Despite his brooding discipline and separation from his clan, he retains a deep fondness for his homeland and gryphonkind, offering his rare scrying talents to those who come seeking aid on behalf of Aerie Peak.

Thadius Grimshade. Gryphon Master Talonaxe hands you a feather taken from the gryphon child Sharpbeak's nest. You are to carry it to the diviner Thadius Grimshade, who dwells in Nethergarde Keep's mage tower in the Blasted Lands. Years ago Thadius Grimshade quit Aerie Peak to chase darker knowledge, yet Talonaxe says he remains a Wildhammer at heart. With luck, divining magic and the feather from Sharpbeak's nest will let Thadius find the gryphon child. Talonaxe says Thadius is to be found in the mage tower at Nethergarde Keep, in the Blasted Lands.

Thalanaar. Thalanaar is a secluded night elf outpost nestled directly on the border between the verdant wilds of Feralas and the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. Serving as the primary eastern gateway into Feralas for the Alliance, it offers tired travelers a vital hippogryph roost and shelter beneath the canopy. Though modest in size, it acts as a critical link between mainland Kalimdor and the remote stronghold of Feathermoon. Perched at the natural choke point where the baked sandstone of Thousand Needles gives way to the dense, misty canopy of Feralas, Thalanaar is the first sign of night elven presence awaiting travelers from the east. It is little more than a fortified grove with a few sturdy pavilions and sentinels on watch, yet its position is vital. The outpost shelters Alliance scouts, couriers, and craftsmen venturing into the untamed forest, providing a secure staging ground against the beasts, ogres, and Horde forces roaming Southern Kalimdor.

Thalanaar Delivery. You picked up a parcel of goods in the Woodpaw gnoll camps, though it was meant for Thalanaar, a small way-station in the southeast of Feralas. Whatever became of the courier, the delivery remains unfinished, and a hand-written name on the packaging, Falfindel Waywarder, may point to the one it was meant for. The goods were supposed to reach Thalanaar, a small way-station in southeastern Feralas, but you found them in the Woodpaw gnoll camps instead. Closer inspection shows a name written by hand on the outside: Falfindel Waywarder. It is a fair guess that this is who the parcel was meant for, and Thalanaar is where to look.

Thalassian Base Camp. Tucked onto a high ridge in northern Azshara, the Thalassian Base Camp serves as the staging ground for an expedition of blood elves unearthing ancient arcane relics. Though initially funded under an agreement with the Horde, the camp's leadership quickly broke faith once digging commenced. Now, amidst their red pavilions and pulverized magical artifacts, darker summoning practices hint at their true objectives. The blood elf expedition nestled east of Ursolan was not supposed to be hostile to travelers from Orgrimmar. Their leader, Magus Rimtori, negotiated a formal pact with the Horde: in exchange for supply lines, funding, and armed escort through Azshara's treacherous wildlands, her researchers would share whatever magical riches they uncovered. Instead, as soon as the base camp was fortified and the first relics were pried from the elven ruins, Rimtori reneged entirely, driving away Horde emissaries. While Rimtori searches deeper reaches with an armed retinue, Magister Hawkhelm keeps watch over the ridge, guarding the encampment against retribution.

Thalia Amberhide. Thalia Amberhide is a tauren residing at Freewind Post in the jagged canyon of Thousand Needles. A loyal friend to her kin, she waits with mounting concern for the safe return of Lakota Windsong from the clutches of the Grimtotem clan. Perched atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Thalia Amberhide is a quiet presence among the bustling tauren settlement. Her heart is heavy with worry for her close companion, Lakota Windsong, who was taken captive by Arnak Grimtotem and his treacherous kin. Thalia relies on passing Horde adventurers who brave the canyon depths to find Lakota, break her bonds, and guide her safely back up the lifts to the haven of the mesa.

Thandol Span. The Thandol Span is a pair of colossal dwarven stone bridges connecting the Wetlands of Khaz Modan with the Arathi Highlands of southern Lordaeron. Long celebrated as a marvel of engineering and the vital artery between the northern and southern kingdoms, it is currently in a state of disaster following a sabotage attack by Dark Iron infiltrators. The surviving bridge remains contested and heavily guarded. Mountaineers from Ironforge fight desperately to preserve the remaining roadway and repel Dark Iron sappers, suffering painful losses in the process. The loss of the bridge would leave northern trade and military movements almost entirely reliant on maritime routes, cutting off Alliance forces stationed across the Arathi Highlands from immediate reinforcement.

Tharek Blackstone. In Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone keeps dwarven tools flowing to local craftsmen. Beldin Steelgrill at Steelgrill's Depot is his main customer, and Tharek also helps travelers find work around town. Tharek Blackstone keeps his forge busy in Kharanos, repairing gear and making tools for local workers. His main customer is Beldin Steelgrill, whose mechanostrider depot just outside town needs a steady supply of heavy wrenches, gears, and replacement tools. Tharek hires passing travelers to carry finished crates to the depot, so he can keep up with the work at his forge.

Tharil'zun. Near Stonewatch Keep, Marshal Marris puts a bounty on Tharil'zun, whose outrunners harass the roads. His death is a critical step in breaking the Blackrock clan's hold over northern Redridge, and his severed head brought to Lakeshire marks a hard-fought victory for its watch. The pass between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep has become a gauntlet of sudden ambushes. Blackrock outrunners and renegades prowl the rocky ridges, cutting off scouts and threatening reinforcements trying to reach the fortress. Marshal Marris names Tharil'zun as the commander behind these coordinated strikes. He says Tharil'zun must be eliminated, or Lakeshire may be hemmed in entirely.

Tharil'zun's Head. Tharil'zun's Head reaches Lakeshire as proof that the commander terrorizing the Redridge approaches is dead. He led the Blackrock Outrunners occupying Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep have pressed Lakeshire hard, raiding farms and ambushing travelers on the roads. Tharil'zun directed the Blackrock Outrunners at the head of these attacks. Lakeshire's garrison cannot risk acting on rumors or partial victories, so Marshal Marris demands proof that Tharil'zun is dead. His severed head shows that the Outrunners' coordinated ambushes from the keep have suffered a major blow.

Tharnariun Treetender. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches Darkshore’s wilds for signs of sickness. The night elf naturalist studies the corruption spreading through local plants and animals, seeking ways to protect them. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches the woods beyond the port. Hostile satyrs and foul shoreline washaways threaten the village, but his work centers on the natural world around it. He believes neglecting nature invites ruin, so he studies the decline of the local woods and searches for ways to fight the sickness spreading across the forest floor.

Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender seeks a way to study the sick thistle bears and find a cure. His trap calms them long enough to bring them to his camp. Tharnariun Treetender made a calming trap to study the sick thistle bears. Across Darkshore, a mysterious affliction has left the animals increasingly frenzied and violent. Tharnariun hopes to cure them rather than see them killed. Set on the ground, Tharnariun's Hope casts a soothing light. A rabid thistle bear that crosses it grows calm for a time and can follow a traveler back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turning point. After travelers put down infected beasts across the woodlands, he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of Auberdine. After the Third War, an unnatural rabid sickness began afflicting Darkshore's wild creatures. Tharnariun Treetender, stationed in Auberdine, spent days asking travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. But killing rabid thistle bears treated only a symptom. Tharnariun decided the source among the local bears had to be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother.

text.enUS: That Shadowvale Green Elixir. In Brill, Carolai Anise seeks bottles of Shadowvale's green elixir. The secluded village once distilled Whispering Elixir from local herbs, and buyers still prize the banned brew. Before the Scourge came, Shadowvale's secluded villagers brewed Whispering Elixir from rare herbs found only in Tirisfal Glades. The draught became known across northern Lordaeron. Though the Capital City outlawed it, mystics, poisoners, and apothecaries still sought its unusual properties, even at the risk of defying royal decrees.

Thazz'ril's Pick. Foreman Thazz'ril accidentally left his favorite enchanted mining pick deep inside the northern cavern during a mineral survey. Now overrun by dangerous beasts, the cave known as the Burning Blade Coven holds the glowing tool awaiting recovery. Foreman Thazz'ril, the supervisor overseeing work details in the Valley of Trials, previously ventured into the northern cavern to prospect for mineral veins. While surveying the rocky interior, he accidentally left behind his prized mining pick. By the time he realized his mistake and returned to fetch it, vicious beasts and hostile inhabitants had overtaken the cavern, forcing the foreman to seek assistance from capable recruits to recover his lost tool.

The Absent Minded Prospector. In southern Darkshore, hostile stone golems overrun a dig site, and Archaeologist Hollee seeks help in Auberdine. She fears for Prospector Remtravel, her senior colleague, whose research often blinds him to mortal danger. Archaeologist Hollee crossed the sea with the Explorers' League, sent by Master Greywhisker to apprentice under Prospector Remtravel. His discoveries had made him renowned in Ironforge's academic circles. The League sent him to study ancient ruins along Darkshore's untamed coast. As the pair excavated what seemed to be the remains of a great civilization, violent stone golems burst from the earth and overran the site.

The Absent Minded Prospector. At the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel presses on with his dig, hoping to find a prize for the Explorers' League. Hostile troggs and his forgetfulness make the search perilous, and word of his safety must reach his assistant in Auberdine. Far south in Darkshore, Remtravel's Dig lies among ancient ruins. Dwarven excavators searching there uncovered troggs, who drove out the workers and besieged the camp. Remtravel will not leave for Auberdine empty-handed. He wanders into danger to recover a fossil, hoping to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

The Absent Minded Prospector. Hollee sends Remtravel's fossil from Darkshore to Darnassus. She stays behind to watch the wandering prospector, and Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker takes a keen interest in the find. Prospector Remtravel has unearthed a curious fossil along Darkshore's coast. He cares more about digging deeper than following protocol. Archaeologist Hollee stays behind to watch over him among the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists. She asks you, an Alliance traveler, to carry the specimen to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild keeps a scholarly delegation.

The Absent Minded Prospector. A strange fossil carries a Darkshore mystery across the Great Sea to the Wetlands. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sends you to Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor, hoping he can unlock its secrets. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sees a likeness between the strange fossil from Darkshore and a relic shown at an Explorers' League conference in Ironforge. Archaeologist Flagongut presented that relic and believed such fossils held powers waiting to be unlocked. Greywhisker believes Flagongut is the only dwarf who can discern what makes this Kalimdor find so extraordinary.

The Absent Minded Prospector. In Darkshore, Remtravel's excavations set a search in motion. In Menethil Harbor, Archaeologist Flagongut hopes to join Remtravel's finds with his own fossil and the lost Stone of Relu to reveal the relics' hidden powers. You once helped the distracted Prospector Remtravel during an escort through northern Darkshore. His search now reaches across the Great Sea to the Wetlands marshes, where Prospector Whelgar keeps Flagongut's original fossil at his excavation site. After reviewing the collected finds, Archaeologist Flagongut believes a key artifact, the Stone of Relu, can unlock the mysterious powers within the fossils.

The Admiral's Orders. Recovered from a locked strongbox atop Tiragarde Keep, these weathered papers bear the personal seal of the late Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. The recovered orders reveal that the Kul Tiran human garrison along Durotar's coast is far more entrenched and organized than simple shipwreck survivors. Delivering them to Gar'Thok in Razor Hill exposes lingering military plans threatening the fledgling Orc nation. Hidden inside a heavy chest on the upper floors of Tiragarde Keep, an aged envelope survives under the watch of Lieutenant Benedict. Sealed with the crest of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, the parchment outlines direct naval commands issued during Kul Tiras's bloody invasion of Durotar. Even after the Grand Admiral fell at Theramore, his officers maintained their fortifications, clinging tightly to their mission to eradicate the Horde settlement.

The Adventurer. In Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends The Adventurer toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have shown your skill defending the abbey, and McBride wants you to look into the newcomer. As threats from the local Defias and vermin ease, Marshal McBride turns his attention to the road beyond Northshire Valley. Stormwind's regular forces are stretched thin across the kingdom, so the local garrison relies on promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods.

The Adventurer. At Dun Morogh's southern gate, The Adventurer carries supplies toward Kharanos. Mountaineer Thalos asks travelers to bring a bundle to Eric Brighthammer, a newcomer camped just outside the village. Ironforge Mountaineer Thalos watches the southern gate, where the trail leaves Coldridge Valley for the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. Guarding the high passes and tunnels keeps the Mountaineers busy, and Thalos watches for dangers as well as travelers on the road. When he hears that a lone adventurer has arrived near Kharanos, he asks trusted passersby to carry supplies onward. The bundle is meant to support newcomers venturing into the frozen crags.

The Adventurer. In Teldrassil, a lost journal waits to be carried to Lyreena Duskblade near Dolanaar. Its pages record an unknown traveler's simple journeys and camping outings. You find a journal among Teldrassil's boughs and roots. Its nameless writer records modest wanderings and the simple pleasure of making camp beneath the twilight canopy.

The Adventurer. "The Adventurer" is an introductory journey quest on Zephras Isle. Given by Aetheen of the Gales in Thendal Grove, it directs newly seasoned wanderers southwest toward Shen'dar Village to meet Raan Wildwind, a veteran camper who knows the wilds. While Thendal Grove provides shelter and quiet refuge, the wider expanses of Zephras Isle remain wild and perilous. Aetheen of the Gales watches over the initiates and sees when an aspiring traveler is ready to step beyond familiar borders. For those seeking fame, fortune, or purpose, remaining behind the grove's sheltered perimeter is no longer enough.

The Adventurer. In Durotar, The Adventurer finds a lost journal among the red wastes. Its pages tell of quiet travels and nights beneath the stars, and it is meant for Brakk near Razor Hill. A lost journal lies in Durotar's red dirt, far from the bloody battles and grand campaigns that mark the land. Its unknown writer fills the pages with day-to-day travels and the simple pleasure of making camp beneath the open sky. The book offers a quiet glimpse of life on the road through a harsh country.

The Adventurer. Near Deathknell, The Adventurer is sent to investigate a stranger by the road to Brill. Scarlet Crusaders threaten the region, but the stranger is Eleanor Shackleton, a Forsaken traveler with wilderness skills to share. Executor Arren watches Deathknell and the roads around it. Scarlet Crusaders spy on the region and infiltrate northern Lordaeron, so an unfamiliar figure near Brill draws suspicion. You have proved your dedication by striking at Crusader threats along the border. Now Arren asks you to investigate the stranger quietly and learn whether she threatens the Forsaken.

The Adventurer. Chief Hawkwind sends young travelers from Red Cloud Mesa with supplies for Kaga Wildhoof near Bloodhoof Village. She once aided him, and he means to repay that favor. Chief Hawkwind asks you to carry provisions to Kaga Wildhoof near Bloodhoof Village. Long ago, Wildhoof aided him when he needed help, and he remembers that kindness. Now she has made camp outside the village. As young travelers leave the mesa, Hawkwind entrusts them with supplies for his old benefactor.

The Affray. On Fray Island, warriors face a trial before Klannoc Macleod will train them. The Affray pits them against island challengers and their champion. Fray Island lies apart from the mainland, drawing brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not teach every wanderer who arrives by boat. Aspiring warriors must first enter the Affray, where stamina and awareness in battle prove who can fight beyond mere boasting.

The Algaz Gauntlet. Orcs have seized Dun Algaz, the pass between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. The Dragonmaw threaten Ironforge's route to Menethil Harbor, and Mountaineer Rockgar sends Alliance travelers to strike them and carry word to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz cuts through the crags between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. It is the only overland mountain pass between them. Ironforge depends on it for trade, troop movements, and supplies bound for Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's main coastal port in the region. If the pass falls, Ironforge's route to the western seas is cut, and isolated outposts lose access to dwarven reinforcements.

The Altar of Zul. The Witherbark trolls do not have Sharpbeak, so Gryphon Master Talonaxe wonders whether the Vilebranch trolls took the young gryphon instead. You are sent to the Altar of Zul, at the western edge of Vilebranch lands, to search for him. The cages of the Witherbark trolls held no sign of Sharpbeak. Talonaxe now suspects the Vilebranch trolls and sends you up to the Altar of Zul, at the western edge of their lands, to look on its top for the gryphon child. Talonaxe fears to think what the Vilebranch may be doing to the captive, if they hold him.

The Anchors of Zephras. The Anchors of Zephras is an introductory quest offered by Halaan Hawk-Eye on Zephras Isle. Halaan invites travelers to borrow his far-reaching vision to observe the ancient anchor pylons that tether and preserve the floating island. Though the soaring monoliths appear untouched from a distance, Halaan warns that the wind spirits' stabilizing magic has begun to waver. The anchor pylons of Zephras are ancient, towering monoliths gifted by the spirits of the winds. Deeply woven into the isle's mystical foundation, they serve to bind, steady, and sustain the landmass amidst the churning skies. To look upon one is to witness the fragile balance keeping Zephras aloft, relying continuously on the benevolence of the wind spirits.

The Ancient Egg. Yeh'kinya in Tanaris tells of an ancient egg named in the Prophecy of Mosh'aru, left from the age when trolls held vast empires. It can contain Hakkar's essence, and Yeh'kinya wants it fetched from Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. An ancient egg is spoken of in the Prophecy of Mosh'aru, a relic of the age when trolls held vast empires. Its power can contain Hakkar's essence, and Yeh'kinya believes it could be the sole means of guarding the world from his evil.

The Ancient Statuette. Near Zoram Strand, The Ancient Statuette lies lost after a naga attack. Talen, an elf camped on the northwestern coast of Ashenvale, needs you to recover the relic he dropped in the surf. Naga attacked Talen as he steered a small vessel through the shallows by Zoram's sunken ruins on Ashenvale's northwestern shore. He scrambled ashore with only bare provisions and made a hasty camp. In his desperate flight, he dropped the ancient statuette he had found among the ruins into the sands.

The Angry Scytheclaws. South of the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends hunters to face the savage scytheclaws stalking the Barrens. Bring sunscale raptor feathers to their breeding nests, and prove your courage in a land that gives little quarter. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters against the beasts of the Barrens. After lesser trials, she sends you south of the Crossroads to hunt vicious sunscale raptors and take their feathers. Then you carry those feathers southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, into the heart of raptor territory. Placing them in the nests is the true test: it shows you can face the scytheclaws without fear.

The Argent Emissary. The Argent Emissary marks the arrival of two Forsaken representatives of the Argent Dawn tracking Scourge cultists near the Undercity. Their presence underscores both the shared fight against the Scourge and the simmering tension between the neutral order and the Forsaken authorities. Two Forsaken emissaries from the Argent Dawn have recently arrived in Tirisfal Glades, setting local authorities on edge. Although the Argent Dawn opposes the Scourge, the local Forsaken remain suspicious of any armed, neutral order operating unmonitored within their sovereign territory. Even the shared heritage of the emissaries does little to soothe their vigilance.

The Ashenvale Hunt. Warcaller Gorlach sends the Horde north into Ashenvale to join the hunt. Report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post, where the Horde is pushing its frontier into the ancient forest. Orgrimmar needs timber, meat, and safe trade routes to keep growing. Warcaller Gorlach carries orders from the Horde's high command, sending seasoned wanderers and new adventurers toward active campaigns. For those coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, Ashenvale is the next test of skill and survival.

The Ashenvale Hunt. In Ashenvale, Horde hunters face a new test beneath the ancient trees. Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo sends proven hunters north to Splintertree Post, where Senani Thunderheart awaits. Horde hunters who have proven themselves in the Barrens are sent toward Ashenvale. Jorn Skyseer sees when a traveler has outgrown the local game and points the way north. For the young Horde, these old forests offer resources and mark a political and spiritual frontier they must learn to understand and claim.

The Ashenvale Hunt. In Ashenvale, Horde hunters face the ancient forest's three great predators. Senani Thunderheart oversees the trial at Splintertree Post, where hunters track Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon to prove their skill. Senani Thunderheart gives the Horde's presence in Ashenvale a different kind of test. While Orcs gather lumber, she sends hunters into the shadowed forest to face its strongest predators. The hunt calls for more than strength: hunters must meet the wilderness with cunning and respect, and learn what they can endure.

The Ashenvale Hunt. In Thunder Bluff, the Ashenvale Hunt calls young Horde champions north to serve at the forest outposts. Heralds direct them to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post for a proving hunt. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation through Thunder Bluff for proven adventurers. The Horde has established footholds in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, and its outposts need young warriors. Those who answer will face a harsher land and test their survival skills beyond Mulgore.

The Atal'ai Exile. While you were at the Pool of Tears, one of Fel'zerul's scouts brought back a scroll inked in blood on dried flesh. Fel'zerul now bundles the artifacts you gathered and sends you far north to the Hinterlands, to find an exiled Atal'ai priest. The scroll reads as a judicial ruling against a priest of the Atal'ai, a fate worse than death among his own people. He was exiled to live among the Witherbark trolls, far to the north in the Hinterlands. Fel'zerul will bundle the artifacts and sends you to find the exile, discover their true use, and return.

The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine calls newly awakened night elves to tend Shadowglen’s wildlife. Young nightsabers and thistle boars have grown too numerous, and keeping Teldrassil’s natural harmony calls for stewardship and difficult choices. In Shadowglen, beneath the Great Tree’s sprawling boughs, heavy spring rains have disrupted Teldrassil’s young, fragile forest cycle. Some wildlife populations have grown beyond what the land can sustain. They threaten to strip the glen of resources and bring famine to the ecosystem. Preserving the forest calls for active care.

The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine sends defenders into Shadowglen to thin its growing wildlife. Mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers threaten the glade's balance. Shadowglen's adult animals now threaten the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine sends young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers. Their appetites can exhaust the land's limited plants and game.

The Balnir Farmstead. In eastern Tirisfal, snapdragons at the Balnir Farmstead may show how far the Scourge's corruption has spread. Anastasia Hartwell sends young Forsaken mages to gather them for study in the Undercity. Forsaken mages watch the borderlands for signs of magical corruption. Anastasia Hartwell sends novice spellcasters to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons from its gardens. The flowers absorb magical energies from the soil and air. By examining them, arcane scholars in the Undercity can judge whether corruption from the Lich King's domain has reached Tirisfal.

The Barrens Oases. High on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem senses an unsettling surge of power flowing into the arid soils of the Barrens. To uncover the truth, he dispatches promising travelers eastward past Mulgore's gates to rendezvous with his kinsman, Tonga Runetotem, at the Crossroads. This mission marks the beginning of an investigation into the unnatural waters springing up across the sun-baked plains. While the plains of Mulgore flourish under the watchful gaze of the Earth Mother, the vast savannas of the Barrens to the east have remained harsh, scorched, and dry for generations. Recently, however, the tauren druids meditating atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise have detected strange currents of energy waking deep beneath the parched plains. Life is stirring where it ought not to be, and the Cenarion Circle fears that whatever force is causing this surge may harbor hidden peril for the land and its creatures.

The Barrens Port. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver sends you from Darnassus to Ratchet to search for Velinde Starsong. The Sentinels believe she took a ship across the Great Sea to the Eastern Kingdoms, and her trail leads through dangerous Horde lands. Clues among Velinde Starsong's personal effects suggest she sought passage across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms. Ratchet is the Barrens' only working harbor, where travelers from northern Kalimdor can arrange passage south or east without sailing from night elf lands. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver sends you south to search the harbor master's ledgers for Velinde's name.

name.esES: Los planes de batalla de los Zarpaleña

text.enUS: The Battle Plans. You have the gnolls' battle plans. What is left is to carry them back to Hadoken Swiftstrider at Camp Mojache, where he or someone there may puzzle out what the gnolls are after. After Woodpaw Investigation, you hold the Woodpaw battle plans, and the only step left is returning them to Hadoken Swiftstrider at the camp. Hadoken is looking for solid evidence of the gnolls' intentions.

The Battleboars. The Battleboars is a rite-of-passage hunting quest given by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. Young tauren are tasked with culling the vicious war-trained boars of Brambleblade Ravine to defend tribal lands and feed the settlement's youth. To the east of Red Cloud Mesa lies Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked scar held by the Bristleback quilboar. As tensions between the Shu'halo and the quilboar escalate into open war, the Bristlebacks have trained vicious battleboars to probe tauren boundaries and terrorize their traditional hunting grounds. Left unchecked, these aggressive beasts threaten not only game trails but the safety of Camp Narache itself.

The Befouled Element. Around Mystral Lake, you find glowing globes of tainted water among the slain elementals. You carry a specimen to Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post to learn what has poisoned the lake and its spirits. Mystral Lake lies in south-central Ashenvale, and its water elementals have grown violently aggressive and visibly corrupted. When slain, they leave strange, intensely glowing spheres of putrid fluid instead of pure elemental essence. The globes hold the corruption that has settled over the lake, showing that something more than natural territorial aggression is at work.

The Big Picture. The Big Picture is a Northshire Valley task concerning a thieving kobold named Shinyfinder Narf, who has been hoarding stolen books deep within the local mine. Adventurers are dispatched by local authorities to recover the illustrated volumes and return them to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey. A peculiar incident has disrupted the peace of Northshire Valley: kobolds lurking around the region have been seen scurrying away with books, crying out 'Picture for Narf!' While kobolds are typically infamous for scavenging candles and shiny trinkets, one particular cave-dweller known as Shinyfinder Narf has developed an appetite for illustrated tomes, accumulating a whole sack of them in his subterranean hideout.

The Binding. In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Forsaken warlocks seek to summon, conquer, and permanently command a voidwalker. Carendin Halgar oversees the rite that grants them this power. Forsaken warlocks must prove they can master a voidwalker before they may summon one. Unlike minor imps, which dark magic easily draws into pacts, creatures of the Void despise reality and possess formidable physical might. In the Magic Quarter, mentor Carendin Halgar provides the mystic runes required to tear a voidwalker from the Nether into the physical realm.

The Binding. In the Undercity, an initiate faces the rite that grants command of a succubus. Carendin Halgar directs the warlock to use Pure Hearts to draw a demon from the Twisting Nether into a ritual circle, then master it through combat. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks hone their command of demons. Summoning a succubus marks a critical passage in their training. A voidwalker relies on brute force, and an imp on lesser malice, but a succubus can ensnare its summoner with seductive and mental enchantments. Carendin Halgar demands that each initiate prove mind and magic unshakable before he entrusts them with lasting dominion over such a demon.

The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation ritual in Orgrimmar for young Horde warlocks seeking command over a voidwalker. Under the direction of Gan'rul Bloodeye, the petitioner inscribes glyphs from the Tablet of Verga within Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle to call forth, subdue, and perpetually enslave a creature of the Void. For an initiate warlock lurking in the dark tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow, summoning an imp is merely child's play. Subduing a voidwalker is the first true test of willpower and arcane dominance. Warlocks do not form polite pacts or commune with these otherworldly horrors; they wrest them across dimensions through raw force and bind them in eternal servitude. Gan'rul Bloodeye demands that the initiate draw upon the glyphs transcribed from the Tablet of Verga, calling the monstrosity directly into Neeru Fireblade's ritual circle to break it in single combat.

The Binding. At Neeru Fireblade's circle in Orgrimmar, a warlock faces the trial of binding a succubus. Dogran's Pendant draws the demon from the Twisting Nether, where spellcraft and force of arms must break its will. Beneath the clefts of Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade keeps a tent with a circle prepared for dangerous rites. Under Gan'rul Bloodeye's guidance, you activate its runes and face the summoned succubus in battle. Calling a demon is only the beginning; you must overpower it alone and bend its spirit to your will.

The Binding. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder puts a novice warlock through a final trial. With his recovered Bloodstone Choker, you draw a voidwalker into a hidden circle and force it to submit. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, forgotten catacombs run beyond the watchful gaze of the Silver Hand and Kirin Tor magistrates. Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novice warlocks that dark magic demands more than channeling power; they must also dominate otherworldly beings. You have recovered Gakin's stolen Bloodstone Choker from Surena Caledon. Now he asks you to call a voidwalker into the summoning circle beneath the tavern.

The Binding. Stormwind warlocks seek to bind a succubus to their will. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb, an initiate uses the enchanted core from the Heartswood to summon the demon and defeat it in combat. A crypt beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter shelters the city's warlocks. There, away from the city watch and the Cathedral of Light, they practice forbidden arts. Stone summoning circles channel the Nether's power and let initiates reach across the veil between worlds.

The Binding. Above Ratchet, warlocks face the rite that binds a felhunter to their will. Strahad Farsan oversees the summoning with the restored Tome of the Cabal, drawing an aggressive demon from the Nether to be subdued in combat. On Kalimdor's bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port, Strahad Farsan conducts dangerous trials in demon summoning. After a warlock gathers the fragments and reagents needed to restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal, Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays an inner glyph of containment while his acolytes channel power through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle. The circles keep whatever emerges isolated from the settlement below.

The Black Box. A metallic black box has turned up in a giant condor's stomach in the Badlands, its surface heavily pitted as if left in acid. Stamped on its underside, beneath a symbol, is a mark reading Engine #19 - Ironforge Siege Brigade. The pitting suggests the box sat inside the condor for ages while acid ate at the metal. Turn it over and a symbol is stamped on the bottom, with Engine #19 - Ironforge Siege Brigade written below. You are to carry it to the Hall of Arms in Ironforge, to Pilot Longbeard.

The Black Shield. The Shady Rest Inn lies burned out, and one of the few parts still standing is a crumbling chimney. A shield blackened by the flames is fixed to its brick. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to show it to. Fire tore through the Shady Rest Inn, and little of it remains. Fixed to the crumbling chimney is an iron shield charred black, and it can be worked free of the brick. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to bring it to, and will ask whether it counts as evidence from the inn's remains.

The Black Shield. An iron shield, blackened by fire, is fixed to the crumbling chimney of the burned Shady Rest Inn. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is waiting on evidence from the inn's site. The Shady Rest Inn burned, and one of the few parts left standing is a crumbling chimney. A fire-blackened iron shield is fixed to its brick, and it can be removed. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore wants evidence from the inn's site.

The Black Shield. Krog now recalls where the name Mosarn comes from: a highly regarded blacksmith in Thunder Bluff, whose armor set was once given to Krog by the Earthen Ring. Krog hopes Mosarn can say more about the blackened iron shield, since nothing useful came from Reethe. Mosarn is to be found in Thunder Bluff. Krog remembers where the name Mosarn was heard before: a blacksmith in Thunder Bluff, highly regarded. The Earthen Ring once thanked Krog with armor that Mosarn crafted, and Krog speaks well of the work. Krog says Mosarn made the shield too and may be able to tell more about it. It is a slim lead, Krog admits, but Reethe yielded nothing useful, so it is all there is. The blackened iron shield goes to Mosarn, who is in Thunder Bluff.

The Black Shield. Captain Garran Vimes is sorry to be of little help with the Blackened Iron Shield, but knows who can do better: Caz Twosprocket, one of the best blacksmiths around, who tends the forge in Theramore's smithy. Vimes apologizes for being unable to help much with the shield, but names someone who can. You are sent with it to Caz Twosprocket, one of the best blacksmiths, who tends the forge in Theramore's smithy. Perhaps Caz can tell you something about it.

The Black Shield. Caz Twosprocket looks over the black shield for the Shady Rest Inn mystery and almost misses one last detail. Caz sends you to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore with what was found. Looking over the black shield, Caz Twosprocket almost misses one last detail: the leather strap on its back has burned away, but the strap seems to have been made to fit a large person. Caz guesses a tauren. That is all Caz can tell, and you are sent to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore with the word, and with Caz's apology for not being more help.

The Black Shield. Krog looks over the Blackened Iron Shield and sees nothing unusual about it. Krog suggests that the blacksmith Do'gol inspect it, though without much hope, and sends you to Brackenwall Village. Krog sees nothing unusual about the shield. Do'gol, the blacksmith, might be able to tell more about it, Krog says, but warns against expecting much. Do'gol is in Brackenwall Village.

The Black Shield. At Brackenwall Village, Do'gol has noticed lettering along the shield's edge, but burned residue hides it. Clearing it needs acid, and Do'gol asks you for six venom sacs from the Darkfang spiders of the marsh. Do'gol can see lettering around the shield's rim, though the burnt-on grime makes it hard to read. Acid would clear it, and the marsh's Darkfang spiders carry venom that works well. Do'gol wants six of their acidic venom sacs to clean the shield up.

The Black Shield. Do'gol has rubbed the shield clear enough to see what appears to spell Mosarn, a name that means nothing to Do'gol. Krog in Brackenwall Village knows many people, so Do'gol sends you to ask there. Do'gol poured on a bit too much acid, but a little rubbing brings out writing that is still hard to read and seems to say Mosarn. The name means nothing to Do'gol. Krog in Brackenwall Village knows many people, so Do'gol sends you to talk with Krog.

text.enUS: The Blackwood Corrupted. Following evidence found in the tainted waters of Cliffspring River, Thundris Windweaver sends adventurers to sever the dark influence strangling the Blackwood tribe. By purifying their food supply with moonwell water, you provoke their demonic handler into the open to shatter his hold on the northern camp. The night elves of Auberdine have long struggled to understand why the once-peaceful Blackwood furbolgs turned so viciously against their neighbors. Investigations along the Cliffspring River traced the rot to satyr meddling. These ancient servants of the Burning Legion have been actively manipulating the tribe, channeling fel magic through insidious talismans to twist the minds of the furbolgs and drive them into feral aggression.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. First Mate Crazz of the Blackwater Raiders needs an adventurer to investigate rumors of rival pirates. With his crew busy drinking and chasing company in Booty Bay, he asks you to scout a nearby cove along the Savage Coast for signs of the Bloodsail Buccaneers. The Blackwater Raiders have newly docked in Booty Bay, only to hear word that their rivals, the Bloodsail Buccaneers, have been sighted across southern Stranglethorn Vale. With the rest of the crew distracted by grog and shoreline pursuits, First Mate Crazz turns to an outsider for help. He asks you to head north along the Savage Coast and scout a cove to see what the Bloodsail Buccaneers are up to.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. Recovered correspondence from the Bloodsail Buccaneers carries a map of Booty Bay and written orders to secure a quiet camp at the marked spot and wait for a signal from their southern command post before attacking. Following your earlier investigation into the Bloodsail Buccaneers, an intercepted map and written orders uncover the pirates' immediate plans. A red X on a map of Booty Bay marks the exact spot where the pirates are to make camp. The orders command the crew to hold their ground quietly, eliminate anyone who approaches, and await an attack signal sent from the southern command post.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. First Mate Crazz has learned that the Bloodsail Buccaneers intend to launch an assault against Booty Bay. The scale of the threat demands the attention of the Blackwater Raiders' commander, Fleet Master Seahorn, who needs to hear the warning immediately. Upon discovering that the Bloodsail Buccaneers scheme to strike Booty Bay directly, First Mate Crazz decides it is bigger than he thought. He directs you to seek out Fleet Master Seahorn, who is somewhere in the port town, and inform him of the brewing assault before the rival pirates can make their move.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. Fleet Master Seahorn trusts a loyal ally of the Blackwater Raiders with striking the Bloodsail Buccaneers' so-called southern command post on the Wild Shore. Recovering their charts and written orders will show exactly what those pirates are up to. Following earlier efforts for Crazz, Fleet Master Seahorn takes notice of your loyalty to the Blackwater Raiders. The Bloodsail Buccaneers have set up what they call a southern command post on the Wild Shore. Seahorn directs you to raid this encampment, cut down their swashbucklers, and seize their naval charts and written orders so the fleet can learn their intentions.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. With the Bloodsail Buccaneers preparing an attack, Fleet Master Seahorn decides against deploying his entire fleet for a counterstrike. Instead, he directs an adventuring crew to slip into the landing site and eliminate the buccaneers' top leadership before their attack can begin. Having learned the buccaneers' invasion plans, Fleet Master Seahorn refuses to wait for the enemy to muster an assault. Mocking Fleet Master Firallon's nautical skill, Seahorn aims to neutralize the threat swiftly by taking out its commanders. Rather than risking a full naval engagement, he sends a strike party directly to Firallon's landing camp to cut down Firallon alongside Captain Stillwater and Captain Keelhaul, ensuring the buccaneer force crumbles without leadership.

The Boar Hunter. Talin Keeneye asks for help in Coldridge Valley, where crag boars threaten the trails. The dwarf hunter wants young recruits to thin their numbers so seasoned hunters can track in peace. Coldridge Valley gives young mountaineers and scholars of Ironforge a quiet, protected place to train. In the harsh winter, its wildlife can grow restless and numerous. Talin Keeneye, a veteran hunter stationed outside Anvilmar, has seen small crag boars multiply across the valley. Their attacks threaten anyone walking the snowy trails.

The Book of Ur. Ur's book now lies in Shadowfang Keep, where Archmage Arugal found it before Forsaken scholars in the Undercity took interest. The Dalaran mage wrote of strange beings from other planes. Ur was a Dalaran mage known for studying other planes and their creatures. Before the Scourge came, the Kirin Tor knew his work well. Ur was fascinated by magic beyond this world, yet he chose to write down his findings instead of breaking through the veil recklessly. Caution and restraint shaped his research. When the Scourge attacked Dalaran, neither his magic nor his care could save him.

The Book of Ur. Keeper Bel'dugur sends Horde champions into Shadowfang Keep for The Book of Ur. In the Undercity's Apothecarium, he seeks the treatise of Ur, a dead mage of Dalaran, for the Forsaken's use of its research into other planes. Before the Third War destroyed Dalaran, the brilliant human wizard Ur devoted his scholarship to realms beyond Azeroth. The Kirin Tor strictly governed conjuration and contact with outer planes, but Ur studied beings from other dimensions, including the savage worgen. He hesitated to wield their alien powers, judging them dangerously uncontrollable. That restraint made his written legacy a coveted prize for those with fewer scruples.

The Borrower. Daryn Lightwind is fascinated by the snapjaws on the beach in the Hinterlands, and above all by a giant one named Gammerita. Her research keeps her where she is, so she gives you a letter to carry to Curgle Cranklehop in Tanaris. Daryn Lightwind says she has studied many subjects, and her latest fascination is the snapjaws that live along the beach in the Hinterlands. One she especially wants to see is a giant snapjaw called Gammerita. She would go herself, but her research keeps her here, so a picture of Gammerita would be the next best thing.

The Bounty of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong is sending fish samples from Rut'theran Village to Auberdine for comparison. She wants to learn whether Teldrassil's fish are larger and more plentiful than those along the mainland coast. Nessa Shadowsong asks you to carry fish bones and scales to Laird in Auberdine. Fishers in Rut'theran Village bring in large, plentiful catches, and she wants to know whether the mainland waters yield the same kind of fish. The samples will let Laird compare the island catch with fish from the coast of Darkshore.

The Branch of Cenarius. In eastern Ashenvale, Anilia's final plea sends you after the Branch of Cenarius. Geltharis has taken the sacred relic, and Illiyana waits for its return. You find Anilia near death while searching eastern Ashenvale for missing dryads. The wounded daughter of Cenarius points north, toward the satyr ruins. With her last breaths, she names Geltharis as the one who took the Branch of Cenarius and begs you to recover it.

The Brassbolts Brothers. Pilot Longbeard in Ironforge needs a courier to deliver a crate of reinforced siege engine helmets across the sea to Kalimdor. His friends, the Brassbolts brothers, are testing high-speed rocket cars in the Shimmering Flats and urgently need head protection for their accident-prone test drivers. While stationed among his aerial machinery in Ironforge, the dwarven aviator Pilot Longbeard received an urgent request from the Shimmering Flats in southern Kalimdor. His friends, a pair of inventive gnomes known as the Brassbolts brothers, had taken up residence on the vast salt pans to race experimental machinery. Longbeard is tied down by military and piloting duties, leaving him unable to deliver the supplies himself.

The Broken Construct. The Broken Construct involves aiding an artisan in Valanaar who is struggling to repair a rare, damaged automaton. These machines were originally gifted by the departed spirits of the wind and preserved by the Windshapers, making every remaining functional construct an invaluable relic of the island's past. Long ago, the spirits of the wind bestowed magical instruments, devices, and animated constructs upon the people of the island. The Windshapers were tasked with their upkeep, preserving these elemental gifts across generations. However, after the spirits left, the flow of their ancient patronage ceased, causing most of the wondrous creations to fall into disrepair until only a handful remained operational.

The Broken Construct. The Broken Construct involves lending aid to Riaani Nightwind, who is shoulder-deep inside the innards of an inoperable machine. Sent as an assistant by Ayessa, travelers must listen to Riaani's plans to discover how they can help restore the device. The Broken Construct begins when an adventurer is dispatched by Ayessa to aid Riaani Nightwind. Riaani is hard at work attempting to diagnose a damaged construct, his attention completely absorbed by the device's inner components. Though he is surprised to receive outside help and doubts whether an untrained traveler can handle delicate mechanical work, he agrees to outline a few necessary tasks once he pulls himself out of the machinery.

The Broken Sigil. After you took the first sigil from the Syndicate, Zengu sends you after the remaining two, which the dug-in Stromgarde militia guards. Galen, son of Thoras Trollbane, broke the Sigil of Thoradin into pieces, and you are to carry them to the troll shaman Tor'gan in Hammerfall. Three sigils guard the tomb of Thoras Trollbane, and you have already recovered the first from the Syndicate. The other two are harder to get, since the firmly entrenched Stromgarde militia holds them. Thoras' son, Galen, divided the Sigil of Thoradin into eleven pieces and dispersed them among the Stromgarde defenders.

The Brood of Onyxia. Draz'Zilb tells of the brood of Onyxia invading Stonemaul Village, and wonders why Deathwing's daughter would come to these lands. You are sent to bring word to Overlord Mok'Morokk in Brackenwall Village. Stonemaul Village was invaded by Onyxia's brood, and Draz'Zilb finds it troubling that the daughter of Deathwing would descend upon these lands. Draz'Zilb feels certain Onyxia came for more than a siege on a few ogres, and wants Overlord Mok'Morokk told at once in Brackenwall Village so action can be taken.

The Brood of Onyxia. Overlord Mok'Morokk has no wish to hear about dragons. He says there are no black dragons here and sends you back to Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village with the news that the ogres are staying. After Draz'Zilb sent word of the brood of Onyxia, Overlord Mok'Morokk wants only to be left alone. Mok'Morokk says the ogres stay where they are, that there is no black dragon here, and tells you to go and say so to Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village.

The Brood of Onyxia. Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village does not want a single more whelp of Onyxia to hatch. You are sent to find and destroy the black dragon's eggs near the Wyrmbog, down in the marsh's south. Onyxia's brood has been scattered through the Dragonmurk. Draz'Zilb urges haste: the Wyrmbog lies in the south of the marsh, and Draz'Zilb is sure the dragon has made her lair there, with her eggs riddled around it. As long as the land around Stonemaul Village is a nesting place for dragons, the ogres will never take it back, so you are sent to track the eggs down and destroy them.

The Captain's Chest. Captain Hecklebury Smotts used to sail between Booty Bay and Ratchet in Kalimdor, until sea giants wrecked the ship, killed the crew and sent Smotts off in a lifeboat toward Booty Bay. The giant Gorlash took Smotts' Captain's Chest, and Smotts wants it back. Smotts says the voyages to Ratchet in Kalimdor built a successful career and a fine reputation. The sea giants ended all that: they smashed the ship, killed the crew and sent Smotts off in a lifeboat toward Booty Bay.

The Captain's Cutlass. Captain Hecklebury Smotts bought a second vessel named Smotts' Revenge to hunt down the sea giants who took his first ship, only to suffer another defeat. The giants smashed the vessel and killed the crew, and one of them, Negolash, stole the captain's cutlass. Smotts directs you to consult his former ship cook, Sprogger, to track down the behemoth. Following the loss of his initial ship, Captain Hecklebury Smotts procured a second craft called Smotts' Revenge, gathering a fresh crew and provisions to take vengeance on the sea giants. The venture ended in disaster when the giants shattered the ship and slew the crew, leaving Smotts adrift once more in a lifeboat. During the onslaught, the giant Negolash took the captain's cutlass.

The Caravan Road. In Booty Bay, the search for Velinde Starsong turns north toward Darkshire. Caravaneer Ruzzgot remembers the missing night elf priestess traveling with his caravan through Stranglethorn Vale. Caravaneer Ruzzgot remembers Velinde Starsong as a passenger on his caravan. The search for the missing night elf priestess has brought you from Ashenvale to Booty Bay, at the southern edge of Stranglethorn Vale. She traveled with his caravan through the jungle, an unusual journey for a night elf priestess.

The Carevin Family. In Darkshire, the search for Velinde Starsong brings strangers to the Carevin family. Clerk Daltry points them to the hunters after hearing of wolf-men in Ashenvale. The search for Velinde Starsong leads from Kalimdor’s ancient forests to Duskwood. In Darkshire, clerk Daltry finds no town record of an elven priestess staying there. But mention the savage wolf-men seen in Ashenvale, and he listens closely. Beasts like those have begun terrorizing the woods around town.

The Charge of the Dragonflights. Anachronos, of the bronze dragonflight, meets you in Tanaris to wrap up the first part of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands. That chain is the road toward opening the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj. This meeting wraps up the opening stretch of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, the chain that leads toward opening the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj. Anachronos is the one who closes this first part with you.

The Chill of Death. In the town of Brill, a Forsaken tailor named Gretchen Dedmar struggles against the creeping cold of mortality and decay. Fearing that the encroaching mindless state will rob her of the ability to serve Lady Sylvanas, she asks for simple materials to sew herself a warm blanket. For the Forsaken, undeath is not a static condition of eternal preservation. As Gretchen Dedmar describes, the lingering Plague of Undeath runs through her body like an icy serpent, draining the warmth from her limbs and threatening to pull her into the mindless state that afflicts so many wandering corpses in Tirisfal Glades. Her shivering hands make ordinary work nearly impossible.

The Cirrusfly Queen. The Cirrusfly Queen is a hunt targeting the matriarch of the aggressive insect hive dwelling in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Following early reconnaissance of the infestation, Elatrell Featherlight directs recruits into the heart of the grove to eliminate the queen and cull the swarm at its source. Ending her reign provides immediate relief to the local rangers working to keep the wilderness manageable. Initial efforts against the cirrusflies revealed that simply swatting away stray worker drones would never curb the infestation spreading across Thendal Grove. Elatrell Featherlight tasks capable wanderers with penetrating deeper into the southeastern reaches of the grove where the main hive lies. There, the queen directs the colony under the vigilant protection of heavier soldier drones.

The Cliffspring River. In Darkshore, foul water now runs down the Cliffspring River toward Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver asks Alliance investigators to take a sample from the pool beneath a road bridge waterfall. He suspects the corruption began beyond the riverbanks. The Cliffspring River runs from the eastern highlands to the coastal shoals of Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Its waters have begun to carry an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Thundris Windweaver fears the foul water will poison the shores and the town's supplies, so he sends scouts upriver to take samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

The Coast Isn't Clear. Along Westfall's western shore, shipwrecked sailors face murloc tribes on the beaches. Captain Grayson at the Westfall Lighthouse calls for help clearing the coast so survivors can reach land safely. Westfall's western coast has claimed countless ships. Reefs, sudden squalls, and jagged rocks break vessels against the shoals. Survivors may cling to wreckage and crawl ashore, hoping for rescue. But murloc tribes control the beaches and show no mercy to castaways.
