text.enUS: The Coastal Menace. Captain Grayson's ghost watches Westfall's rocky coast, where his ship broke on the rocks. He blames Old Murk-Eye for driving the lighthouse keeper's family from their post, then killing them in a later attack. Now he calls on travelers to hunt the murloc chieftain and bring justice to the shore. The Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships through the southern coast's jagged shallows. Captain Grayson's vessel struck the rocks in the dark after murlocs frightened the lighthouse keeper's family into leaving their post. The family returned and lit the flame again, but safety did not last. A cunning, ruthless predator still stalked the shore.

The Collector. An intercepted dispatch from gnoll raiders in Elwynn Forest lays out when gold shipments leave the abandoned mines. It is addressed to a figure called 'The Collector' and points to an organized operation near Stormwind's garrison. Riverpaw gnoll packs in western Elwynn Forest carry more than furs and crude weapons. Among them, a parchment called the Gold Pickup Schedule lays out dates and times for gold taken from local mines. The intercepted note directs each shipment to an overseer identified only as 'The Collector.'

The Collector's Schedule. Near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, The Collector's Schedule marks when illicit gold shipments move through Elwynn Forest. Gnolls carry the handwritten itinerary, and Marshal Dughan recognizes the name it records. The Collector's Schedule marks dates and times for gold shipments from Elwynn's mines. Stormwind has not officially worked the mines for months, driven off by banditry and creature incursions, yet ore still leaves in an orderly flow. The itinerary names the days and hours when a figure called The Collector receives each shipment. The trail points to a camp near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn Forest. When Marshal Dughan sees the schedule, he recognizes the Collector's name. Who pays for the stolen gold remains unknown.

The Color of Blood. Nikova Raskol grieves for Mac, her young grandson, killed inside Stormwind City's prison. Anger consumes her, and she sends adventurers into The Stockade to take the Defias gang's red bandanas in retribution. Mac Raskol was fourteen when he took up arms as a guard in The Stockade. Stormwind's regular soldiers had been sent to distant fronts, leaving local defense to volunteers and the city's youth. Mac watched hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood in a place far more dangerous than his experience could prepare him for.

The Corrupter. A piece of flayed demon skin, taken from the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress, smells rotten yet is surprisingly pliable. Red markings of some language cover one side, and at the bottom is a clear symbol that looks like a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may be able to tell you more. The torn skin stinks of rot, yet it bends easily, though it seems dry and fragile. Unrolled, it carries red markings on one side, a written language of some sort. At the bottom is a plain symbol, which you take to be a signature.

The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, but first any wards the creature holds against scrying must be broken. For that, Maurin wants the scalp of a Hatefury shadowstalker, hunted in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, given the proper reagents. If the lord is as powerful as Maurin suspects, those must come from deadly creatures, and Maurin is sure you, acting in the Warchief's name, will take up the challenge. The first need is to break any wards the demon has against scrying. For that Maurin wants a scalp from a satyr, though only a Hatefury shadowstalker's will serve. They are to be sought in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast, near Sargeron.

The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter wants an oracle crystal, which the naga craft for their oracles, in order to find the demon lord Azrethoc. A vast coral reef lies northwest along the coast, home to the Slitherblade naga, and they will not welcome you. Maurin Bonesplitter says an oracle crystal will do the job of finding the demon lord Azrethoc, whose signature was on the skin you brought. Naga craft such crystals, and their oracles use them. Up the coast to the northwest lies a vast coral reef which the naga have made their home while near the shore, and the oracles can be found in that place. The Slitherblade there are deadly and will take your intrusion badly, so Maurin urges you to go carefully and quickly.

The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter has found the demon lord far more dangerous than expected. He is certain Takata Steelblade doubts his abilities, and leaving the swordsman uninformed of what happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin sends you to speak with Takata, who is nearby. Maurin Bonesplitter finds the creature much more dangerous than he had anticipated. No doubt Takata Steelblade questions whether Maurin can handle it, and not being told of what just happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin asks you to speak to the swordsman and offer to slay the demon, should Takata allow it. Maurin cautions you not to press Takata too hard, since it is better if Takata believes the idea is his own.

The Corrupter. Takata Steelblade knows nothing of Lord Azrethoc, yet sides with Maurin that the demon lord must be stopped, all the more if Azrethoc is trying to win influence over the Burning Blade. Takata trusts you to gather a party against Azrethoc and his warlock servant, Jugkar Grim'rod. Takata has never heard of Lord Azrethoc, yet agrees with Maurin that the demon lord must be stopped, above all if Azrethoc is reaching out to sway the Burning Blade. You have already shown you want to aid the Warchief, so Takata trusts you to gather a party and slay Azrethoc and his warlock servant, Jugkar Grim'rod. Takata tells you to head directly south, to Mannoroc Coven, where both are found.

The Corruption Abroad. Argos Nightwhisper, a night elf envoy visiting Stormwind, seeks capable adventurers to cross the Great Sea and aid his brother in northern Kalimdor. His brother Gershala studies spreading ecological decay in Darkshore, where fresh hands are desperately needed. While Stormwind contends with internal turmoil and regional unrest, representatives from the distant kaldorei lands can be found wandering its stone streets. Argos Nightwhisper came seeking seasoned champions willing to look beyond human borders. The kaldorei are relatively new allies to the Eastern Kingdoms, and formal military aid is scarce, leaving family members and researchers to recruit whatever independent champions answer the call.

The Criminal Element. The Criminal Element involves striking against the Highlands Bandits and their leader, "Badwind" Bennic, who operate out of a concealed cave behind a waterfall in the Shen'dar Highlands. With local forces overwhelmed by the recent arrival of a menacing cult, outside help is required to eliminate Bennic and disrupt the outlaw gang. In the Shen'dar Highlands, a den of outlaws known as the Highlands Bandits has entrenched itself inside a hidden cave concealed behind a northern waterfall. Led by the notorious "Badwind" Bennic, the cutthroats were already a persistent nuisance to locals before an enigmatic cult arrived in the highlands, after which their lawlessness escalated into an outright terror. With local defenders stretched thin and unable to spare forces, adventurers are tasked with infiltrating the waterfall redoubt, breaking the gang's ranks, and eliminating Bennic.

The Crone of the Kraul. At Thalanaar, on the border of Feralas and the Thousand Needles, Falfindel Waywarder sends adventurers after Charlga Razorflank. Henrig Lonebrow's recovered journal reveals the growing danger inside Razorfen Kraul. At secluded Thalanaar, the night elf outpost, Falfindel Waywarder grieves for the druid Heralath and the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow. Lonebrow traveled with the Explorers' League before the quilboar captured him. He escaped Razorfen Kraul, but died on the road, leaving a tattered journal that describes the growing menace inside. There is no time to send a runner to Darnassus for military reinforcements. Falfindel sends passing adventurers into the thorned dens to face the danger at its heart.

The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara prepares to weaken Mug'Thol's ogres before striking at their hold in the Ruins of Alterac. She sends you after the Crushridge maulers. Mug'Thol and the Crushridge ogres hold the Ruins of Alterac. Melisara sees little chance of punishing Mug'Thol while so many ogres remain around him. First, their numbers must fall; only then can the next move begin. You are sent to hunt the Crushridge maulers.

The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara seeks the heads of three ogres before Mug'Thol. Melisara names Targ, Muckrake and Glommus as Mug'Thol's loyal lieutenants, though she wonders what could make an ogre loyal. You are to kill all three and bring their heads to Tarren Mill. Then only Mug'Thol's head, crown and all, remains to be taken.

The Crown of Will. With Mug'Thol's lieutenants dead, Melisara in Tarren Mill sends you after him. Bring back his head and the Crown of Will, and the Crushridge resistance will be over. Only Mug'Thol remains. Melisara expects him to resist giving up the Crown of Will. After his lieutenants fell, he likely expects you. Find him, kill him, and bring his head and the Crown back to Tarren Mill.

The Crown of Will. Only one step remains: the Crown is bound for Sharlindra in the Undercity, who will see that it reaches Lady Sylvanas. Melisara sends you to take the Crown to Sharlindra in the Undercity, where she will pass it on to Lady Sylvanas. She warns you not to use it for your own purposes. Mug'Thol's fate is warning enough.

The Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a task confronting mortal servants of the Scourge active within Tirisfal Glades. By culling Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers, defenders prevent the Lich King's insidious living agents from repeating the betrayals that originally shattered Lordaeron. The Cult of the Damned represents the mortal face of the Scourge. Composed of living men and women who swore fealty to the Lich King, these cultists act where mindless dead cannot. In Tirisfal Glades, where inhabitants already contend with roaming undead and relentless zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, newly discovered cells of Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers signal an insidious attempt by the Scourge to re-establish a foothold.

The Curious Visitor. After the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater has a troubling discovery about Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, a man named Maelik visited Thredd with legitimate papers. Warden Thelwater learned that Bazil Thredd had not been abandoned by his former comrades, as the guards believed. Months before the riot, a quiet visitor began meeting with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized paperwork, and gave his name as Maelik. Thelwater suspects the visits helped coordinate the bloody uprising. He gathers a physical description and sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston to learn who the visitor was.

The Curse of the Tides. With her knife recovered from Pretty Boy Duncan, Catelyn the Blade loans the troll artifact so it can be used against a sunken altar off the coast. Baron Revilgaz in Booty Bay wants the Stone of the Tides for his collection of ancient troll artifacts. Catelyn the Blade lends her recovered troll dagger to break an altar submerged deep beneath the waves. Though no expert on troll ruins like her father, she has heard of a sunken troll city, and she points toward it, out near the reef northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp. Within the underwater ruins of the Vile Reef, the Altar of the Tides rests, surrounded by a distinct blue glow amid sea life and murlocs.

The Cursed Crew. Off the Wetlands coast, The Cursed Crew still haunts its sunken ships. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras's sole living survivor, asks for mercy for his lost brethren. A dark relic aboard one of the wrecks binds the drowned sailors and marines to the ships as restless undead. The Third Fleet of Kul Tiras wrecked along the jagged shores north of Menethil Harbor. First Mate Fitzsimmons alone made it ashore alive. His fellow sailors did not find peace beneath the waves. A mysterious treasure hidden deep in one of the hulls unleashed sorcery as they died. It bound their souls to the battered timbers and denied them the grave's rest.

The Damned. New Forsaken in Deathknell turn to Novice Elreth for clothing and battlefield wraps. She trades salvaged armor for the materials needed to make them. Novice Elreth tends the newly risen Forsaken in Deathknell. She assists Shadow Priest Sarvis, cares for battered soldiers, and mends their garments. Supplies run short, so she sends you into the surrounding glades to hunt duskbats and scavenger wolves. Their pelts, wings, and sinew help keep the camp supplied, and Elreth offers salvaged armor in return.

text.enUS: The Dark Iron War. At Dun Modr, on the Wetlands' northern edge, Motley Garmason leads a desperate defense. The Dark Iron clan holds the town after saboteurs shattered the Thandol Span, leaving the Ironforge Mountaineers with a tenuous line as they wait for reinforcements that may never come. Dun Modr guarded the southern end of the colossal Thandol Span, the bridge linking Khaz Modan to Lordaeron. Dark Iron saboteurs and demolitionists shattered its archway, severing Alliance travel before they overran the stronghold. Motley Garmason and a handful of surviving defenders withdrew to an observation camp just outside town. Without a counterattack, the northern gateway risks permanent Dark Iron dominion.

The Day After. In Ironforge and Kharanos, Gnomeregan's survivors seek a way to answer the city's ruin. Gnoarn sends travelers to Ozzie Togglevolt, who studies the contamination and hopes to find a solution. Gnoarn, a refugee in Ironforge's Tinker Town, mourns Gnomeregan and the loss of his gnomefro. Trogg invaders took the mechanical city, and toxic fallout blasted away his prized mane. Fury toward the troggs and hope of recovering the city drive him to send sympathetic travelers to colleagues with the skill to salvage what remains.

The Dead Fields. At the Dead Fields, Forsaken forces face a Scourge threat in northern Silverpine. High Executor Hadrec sends champions from the Sepulcher against the Rot Hide gnolls and the banshee who shields them. North of the Sepulcher, an abandoned farmstead lies overrun by Rot Hide gnolls. The fields once held ordinary farms, but now these plague ridden scavengers infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec sent small raiding parties to drive them out. Each attack stalled under a strange magical resistance.

The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, Mennet Carkad tests hopeful Deathstalkers with a demand for ruthless initiative: intercept a traveling messenger. The trial opens the way into the covert order serving Lord Varimathras. The Deathstalkers serve Varimathras as the Forsaken's secret police and elite assassination corps. In the Rogues' Quarter, handler Mennet Carkad sets a trial for anyone seeking a place among them. A hopeful agent must show cunning, discretion, and the will to eliminate a target. Carkad's test is meant to turn away the weak and those troubled by too many scruples.

The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, the Deathstalkers move against suspected treason in the Forsaken's own ranks. Under Lord Varimathras's orders, you pose as an expected messenger and question a merchant who may be aiding an outside faction. Deathstalker Mennet Carkad sets an infiltration in motion at Lord Varimathras's urging. The Deathstalkers watch the Forsaken's own citizens as closely as they guard against outside threats. With Astor Hadren's letter of introduction, forged or acquired, you approach the local merchant Andron Gant and try to pass as the courier he expects.

The Deathstalkers. In the Undercity, the Deathstalkers turn Andron Gant's trust against him. Still believing you are the messenger he expected, Gant gives you a ledger for his secret contacts. You carry it to Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter, opening the way to deeper covert work for the Forsaken state. Andron Gant works from the Undercity, keeping names and information in a personal ledger. Believing you are the courier he expected, he hands it over for delivery to the secret contacts he serves. Gant asks that the same courier carry future messages, unaware that the ledger is bound for the Deathstalkers.

The Deathstalkers. In Undercity, the Deathstalkers bring a new operative into their ranks. You carry Andron's Ledger to Varimathras, proof of the Syndicate's covert activities. Mennet Carkad welcomes you into the Deathstalkers after you uncover records from Andron Gant. The order serves Lady Sylvanas as eyes, ears, and daggers throughout Lordaeron. Its agents use intelligence networks, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to remove threats before they surface. Recognition by the order marks a step into service for the Forsaken.

The Deathstalkers' Report. The Deathstalkers' Report is a crucial military courier assignment delivered to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. After securing injured Deathstalkers in the northern wilds, you carry their gathered intelligence concerning unexpected Scourge activity back to Forsaken high command. This dispatch alters the Forsaken's assessment of their hold on Silverpine Forest. The Deathstalkers act as the eyes, ears, and daggers of the Dark Lady, pushing into the untamed wilderness ahead of standard military units. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, an advance patrol ran into catastrophic resistance while charting enemy movements. Though Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his injuries and Erland fought his way to safety, their scouting mission yielded intelligence essential to the Forsaken occupation of Silverpine Forest.

The Decrepit Ferry. At the Decrepit Ferry, rot hides swarm the dock east of The Sepulcher. High Executor Hadrec sends Forsaken champions to learn why the Scourge has gathered along Lordamere Lake's shore. High Executor Hadrec turns east after the Scourge presence in the Dead Fields is suppressed. The Decrepit Ferry lies among Silverpine Forest's eastern waterways, where mainland Lordaeron once connected to the island estates of Lordamere Lake. Now undead gather around its rotted piers. Hadrec sends scouts to find out what draws the Lich King's servants there.

The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard the Horde's foothold in Stranglethorn Vale and protect their supply chain to Stonard. To keep that supply chain safe, he directs Horde champions to thin out the Lashtail Raptors outside Grom'gol Base Camp. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Commander Aggro'gosh carries the duty of protecting every member of the Horde within the jungle. The camp exists to keep supplies flowing safely to Stonard, but some of the local inhabitants are standing in the way.

The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard Grom'gol's supply lines through Stranglethorn Vale. After the earlier hunt thinning the raptors outside the camp, a band of ogres encamped at the nearby Mizjah Ruins continues to harass supply caravans heading toward Stonard. The Horde's presence in northern Stranglethorn Vale is centered on supplying Stonard, an outpost of vital strategic interest. While Commander Aggro'gosh did not arrive with the intention of fighting every native group, a band of local Mosh'Ogg ogres has claimed the Mizjah Ruins southeast of the camp. Warnings have failed to stop their continuous raids against Horde supply shipments, prompting the commander to order a strike against the ogre brutes and witch doctors holding the ruins.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood is building a network beyond banditry. Wiley the Black sends word of its ties to gnolls, kobolds, and goblins. Gryan Stoutmantle needs this intelligence to measure the full reach of the conspiracy choking Westfall. Wiley the Black says telling what he knows about the Defias could cost him his life. Along the edges of Redridge and Westfall, he has caught wind of an operation far greater than highway robbery. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups that are usually hostile to one another across the countryside.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's troubles reach Stormwind. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to deliver Wiley's Note to Master Mathias Shaw, suspecting a link between the Defias and the old Stonemasons Guild. A mention of the Stonemasons in Wiley's communications catches Gryan Stoutmantle's attention. The builders rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, but the guild has long been thought scattered or dissolved. If the Defias Brotherhood shares ties with them, Westfall's rural insurgency is more than a disorganized band of outlaws.

The Defias Brotherhood. Mathias Shaw sends a confidential report from Stormwind to Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Shaw has investigated the former Stonemasons Guild to help Stoutmantle uncover the origins of the Defias Brotherhood.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the People's Militia seeks the Defias Brotherhood's hidden base. A turncoat agrees to guide Alliance champions there in exchange for protection. The road passes through Moonbrook, where Edwin VanCleef's inner sanctum lies hidden. Gryan Stoutmantle's fight against the Defias Brotherhood reaches a turning point when a captured brigand agrees to talk. His former brothers may execute or assassinate him, so the Defias Traitor bargains with the People's Militia. Escort him safely through hostile territory, and he will reveal where Edwin VanCleef and his ringleaders hide. The thieves' network silences those who speak out, and the turncoat needs armed protection along the road.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood still holds the farmlands in fear. Gryan Stoutmantle has found their stronghold beneath Moonbrook and calls for a final blow against their leader. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia have fought the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall for months. Now the thieves' stronghold lies exposed beneath Moonbrook. Stoutmantle orders Edwin VanCleef assassinated, believing his death will break the rebellion once and for all.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's thieves threaten the farms and roads. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you from Sentinel Hill east into Redridge to seek a contact who may know where they hide. Westfall's harvests are gone, and bandits in red bandanas roam the land. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold Sentinel Hill under near-constant attack, but they do not know who directs their enemies. Stoutmantle knows that fighting stray looters will not save the region. He needs to find the cartel's inner circle and learn who commands it.

The Defias Traitor. At Sentinel Hill, The Defias Traitor has given up the Brotherhood's hidden base to save his life. The captured outlaw is held beneath the watchtower after the People's Militia caught him stealing Farmer Saldean's wagon.

The Demon Scarred Cloak. The Demon Scarred Cloak is a ragged pelt recovered from the legendary white wolf Ghost Howl, who roams the grassy plains of Mulgore. Marked by an enduring wound inflicted during past clashes with the Burning Legion, the pelt serves as proof of the beast's release from torment. Bringing it to the elders of Bloodhoof Village brings closure to the story of a tragic local legend. Ghost Howl is an elusive white wolf known across Mulgore for both his ferocity and his sorrowful howl. When slain, the beast leaves behind a pelt that is visibly scarred by foul demonic corruption. These lingering marks date back to the wolf's desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion, a confrontation that left Ghost Howl wounded in both flesh and spirit long after the Third War came to a close.

The Demon Seed. Neeru Fireblade's orders reach Ak'Zeloth, who sends Horde travelers to destroy the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. An unstable Flawed Power Stone can break the Burning Legion's conduit before its influence spreads farther through the Barrens. High in a cave on Dreadmist Peak, the Demon Seed hangs above an altar of fire. The artifact anchors demonic power in the heart of the Barrens for the Burning Legion. The orc Ak'Zeloth prepares specialized power stones to break its link to the Nether. One must reach the peak before the stone's unstable energy runs out.

The Den. Braelyn Firehand sends Horde champions into the Talon Den's hidden barrow chambers to seize the druids' relics. This infiltration campaign reaches its climax as they face layered defenses beneath Stonetalon Peak. High on the Stonetalon Mountains, the Talon Den shelters night elf druids in halls carved deep into living stone. The barrow chambers protect meditating guardians and keep sacred treasures from prying eyes. Knowing the value of what lies within, Braelyn Firehand questions a captured druid to learn how the defenses work.

The Den. The Den is the sheltered cave at the heart of the Valley of Trials in southwestern Durotar. Serving as the primary base of operations for young orc and troll adventurers, it provides martial and magical training before they set out into the wider world. Tucked into the red canyon walls of the Valley of Trials, the Den serves as an austere proving ground. Within its carved, shadowy interior, novice fighters, spellcasters, and hunters report to veterans like Gornek and Zureetha Fargaze. It is here that fledglings receive their foundational combat instruction, supplies, and initial rites of passage, hardening them for the harsh realities of Durotar and the greater struggles facing the new Horde.

The Deserters. Captain Garran Vimes says deserters have settled into a tower that Theramore had abandoned. The tower stands at Lost Point, which lies southeast of the inn. A man called Jacken leads the deserters, and Vimes wants information about Reethe from him. Vimes admits that holding on in the marsh has been a struggle, though the resolve of Vimes's people has kept several defensive watchtowers standing. Scouting reports say deserters have moved into an abandoned one at Lost Point, which lies southeast of the inn. A man named Jacken leads them. Vimes asks you to see what information Jacken will give up about Reethe, and warns that Jacken may not part with it easily.

The Deserters. Asked about Reethe, Balos Jacken, leader of the Lost Point deserters, calls him a coward and says the deserters drove him from their camp. Jacken then asks you to forget you ever ran into them. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is the one to tell about Reethe. Jacken says the deserters drove Reethe out for repeatedly plundering the ogres' stores at Brackenwall Village. By Jacken's account the deserters are too few to stand against those ogres, and Reethe crossed the line once too often, so the band left him to manage alone. In return for the answer, Jacken asks that you forget the meeting.

The Disruption Ends. Thork orders a strike against the Razormane raids on the Horde road. Kreenig Snarlsnout leads the attacks from the northern Barrens, and his death is meant to break the warband's hold on the route between Durotar and the Crossroads. The road between Durotar and the Crossroads carries provisions and reinforcements through the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar ambushes have kept it under threat. Scout reports name their leader as Kreenig Snarlsnout, whose raiding party organizes the attacks. Thork orders a strike against Kreenig, hoping to break the warband's unity and secure the road.

The Divination. Thadius Grimshade asks you to give him room while he performs a ritual of divination. He means to follow the link between the feather you brought and its owner until it leads him to Sharpbeak. Thadius follows the link between Sharpbeak's feather and the gryphon who owns it, hoping to reach Sharpbeak himself. He asks for silence and room to work. He admits it may not go to plan, and warns that in that case you had better close your eyes.

The Doomed Fleet. Bishop Farthing sends you north from Stormwind to seek a way past Morbent Fel's wards. The trail leads across Khaz Modan to the wreckage of Kul Tiras's Third Fleet off the Wetlands. Morbent Fel's wards turn aside ordinary steel at his retreat on the Forlorn Rowe. Bishop Farthing sends you to seek a weapon bound to the Holy Light. Its key is Lightforge Iron, a rare consecrated metal whose strikes carry holy truth and pierce sorcerous protections.

The Dormant Shade. A dark rite waits at Gunther's Retreat on Brightwater Lake in Tirisfal Glades. Set a mystic candle on an old, blood-soaked table to summon Lillith Nefara, a Scourge agent, and prove to Gunther Arcanus that you oppose the Lich King. On Gunther's Retreat, an island in Brightwater Lake, a battered dinner table lies stained with blood. The table is no ordinary abandoned piece of furniture. It is the focus of a dark conjuration, a rough slab where dried gore marks the place death and dark magic gather.

The Dunemaul Compound. Andi Lynn in Gadgetzan warns of a large band of nomadic ogres that has lately arrived in Tanaris. South of town they have formed a compound, and Andi Lynn wants it destroyed before they can build up a force. A large band of nomadic ogres has arrived in Tanaris of late. South of Gadgetzan they have seized a broad stretch of desert and formed the Dunemaul Compound. Several smaller bands wander the desert as well, and some have invaded the old troll ruins. Andi Lynn says the ogres cannot be allowed to build up a force.

The Ectoplasmic Distiller. Mux Manascrambler in Gadgetzan is working on his extra-dimensional ghost revealer but has run out of funds and manpower. The first piece he needs is an ectoplasmic distiller, and he asks you for a list of costly materials and forty gold to build it. After A Supernatural Device, Mux Manascrambler welcomes your help with his ghost revealer, a machine meant to reach across dimensions. The first piece is a distiller, meant to gather the fabric of death itself, and he warns that building it will not be easy. He wants a delicate arcanite converter, four greater eternal essences, ten stonescale oil and twenty-five volcanic ash, plus forty gold. The ash is for a filter, and it must come from the lava pools of the Burning Steppes. Mux admits the materials are pricey, but swears every one will be needed.

The Eighteenth Pilot. Pozzik will be busy fitting the new fuel regulator into the racer designs, but suggests that you help the team further by speaking with Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth, and likes to add modifications to the racers. Pozzik says the fuel regulator is keeping him busy, but you can help the team some more by talking to Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth in fact, and likes to add little modifications of his own to the racers. Pozzik adds that Razzeric is a little off his rocker, so you should try not to seem too surprised.

The Elder Crone. Seereth Stonebreak sends word from Stonetalon to Thunder Bluff. Enraged by goblin deforestation and mining, the mountain's elements need spiritual guidance, so Seereth sends emissaries to seek counsel from Magatha Grimtotem on Elder Rise. Goblin deforestation and mining have enraged the elemental spirits of Stonetalon Mountains. Seereth Stonebreak sees that force alone cannot ease the land's spiritual anguish and turns to elder shamans for wisdom. Seereth knows few tribal leaders by name, but knows of Magatha Grimtotem, an elder famed for her knowledge and commanding presence.

The Embalmer's Heart. In Duskwood, Eliza's buried corpse holds a heart that still beats. The Embalmer placed his own heart in his dead wife through dark magic, and it became the anchor of his power. Darkshire's tales remember the Embalmer as a gentle alchemist. When his wife Eliza died, grief shattered his mind. He turned to foul sorcery, cut out his own heart, and placed it in her lifeless chest. The magic stirred her corpse to unlife, but the return twisted Eliza into a ravenous creature with an insatiable hunger for living human flesh. Horrified by what he had done, the alchemist buried her again.

name.ptBR: O apanhador de sonhos de esmeralda

text.enUS: The Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot asks you to recover a cherished heirloom from his abandoned home in Starbreeze Village. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druid warden, gave him the Emerald Dreamcatcher, which he left behind when corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the settlement. Recovering it keeps its gentle nature magic from falling into foul hands. Gaerolas Talvethren gave Tallonkai a rare druidic talisman. The warden watches over the sleeping druids within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Crafted to channel the serene currents of the Emerald Dream, the amulet draws on that pure spiritual energy to bring peace and fortune to its bearer. Such gifts go only to a trusted few whose lives are bound to the forest's care.

The Enchanted Glade. Bloodfeather harpies threaten the Oracle Glade on northwestern Teldrassil, where Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak guards the ancient Oracle Tree. After harpies kill a runner bound for Darnassus, Arynia calls for their nests to be thinned and their belts brought back as proof. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak watches over the Oracle Glade with an escort of warriors. The sacred retreat centers on the colossal Oracle Tree, an ancient rooted among Teldrassil's boughs. Bloodfeather harpies have spread through the surrounding canopy, nesting in the hollows and threatening anyone who comes near.

The Ensorcelled Parchment. A spell on a parchment makes its writing unreadable, apart from one word at the top: Nagaz. You are to take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore. A spell lies on the parchment and keeps its writing from being deciphered. Only a single word at the top can be made out, the name Nagaz. You are to take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore.

The Escape. Maybell Maclure waits for a way to slip away from her family and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. You bring her William Pestle's Invisibility Liquor, brewed from crystal kelp gathered across the region. The Maclures and Stonefields have feuded for generations, leaving no room for courtship. Gramma Stonefield turns to William Pestle, an alchemist in the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. With crystal kelp from nearby lakes, Pestle brews Invisibility Liquor strong enough to hide Maybell's escape from the Maclure homestead.

The Escape. You help Wizzlecrank flee the Venture Company drill site at the Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Trapped in a stolen prototype shredder, the goblin pilot needs protection from company mercenaries as he climbs from the industrial pit. Afterward, you report to his contact, Sputtervalve, in Ratchet. Wizzlecrank struggles to control the stolen shredder at the Sludge Fen. He has lit the prototype deep inside the Venture Company drill site, but knows little of its levers and switches. The heavy machine lurches across the muddy quarry floor, and its erratic driving and roaring joints alert nearby laborers and armed guards. A stealthy escape becomes a running battle up the excavation pit’s western ramp.

The Essence of Aku'Mai. Je'neu Sancrea has found the naga harvesting sapphires in Blackfathom Deeps. At Zoram'gar Outpost, the shaman asks Horde adventurers to recover them before their power is misused. Je'neu Sancrea watches over the Kaldorei ruins from the Zoram Strand. Naga now mine sapphire clusters in the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, where the gems grow along damp cavern walls. Sancrea senses the serpentine invaders mean to harness their power and seeks to stop the harvest before they can use it.

The Essence of Eranikus. You engage the Oathstone of Ysera's Dragonflight, and Itharius speaks straight into your mind. Taking up the charge means helping Ysera's Dragonflight redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus, and the first sacrifice is to give Itharius the gem that chains the part of Eranikus' mind that is still free. Itharius waits in the Swamp of Sorrows. Through the Oathstone, Itharius tells you that accepting this charge means aiding Ysera's Dragonflight to redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus. Itharius expects many sacrifices from the two of you, and the first is to hand over the gem that has bound whatever free-willed part of Eranikus' mind remains. The Oathstone and the Chained Essence of Eranikus must go to Itharius in the Swamp of Sorrows, and there you choose whether to aid the dragonflight.

The Everstill Bridge. In Lakeshire, The Everstill Bridge still waits for repairs. Iron meant for the work went into weapons during the last orc invasion, and Redridge gnolls ambushed the replacement caravan from Stormwind. You find Lakeshire's stone bridge across Lake Everstill unfinished. It links the western roads toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. Recent orc incursions brought the town close to ruin. To survive, Lakeshire melted its structural iron into munitions, blades, and plate armor to repel the Blackrock invaders. The bridge was left incomplete and vulnerable.

The Eye of Paleth. Fitzsimmons asks you to recover The Eye of Paleth from the sunken Intrepid. Bring the cursed gem to Glorin Steelbrow in Menethil Harbor, where the dwarven priest can seek a way to purge its blight. The locked strongbox aboard the Intrepid holds a blackened orb that pulses beneath the waters of Baradin Bay. It is The Eye of Paleth, warped from sacred light into a source of suffering. Its corruption is bound to the restless spirits and doom that claimed the sailors of the Third Fleet.

The Fall of Ameth'Aran. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade sends you to explore Ameth'Aran's ruins in Darkshore and read its ancient stone tablets. Their inscriptions tell of the Highborne city's ruin during the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine. Ameth'Aran was a flourishing settlement of Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who practiced powerful arcane magic. After the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city lay in broken marble and cracked pillars. Restless, anguished spirits of the Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins.

The Family Crypt. Scourge forces at the Agamand Mills threaten the Forsaken's hold on Tirisfal. From Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends agents against the undead in the family crypt. The Forsaken hold Tirisfal Glades, but the Scourge still grips much of its countryside. The Agamand Mills once produced flour for Lordaeron; now they are a Scourge stronghold. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren watches the enemy gather with grave concern. Every stretch of land lost to the undead weakens the Forsaken's independence.

name.enUS: The Family and the Fishing Pole

name.frFR: La famille à la canne à pêche
name.svSE: The Family and the Fishing Pole

text.enUS: The Family and the Fishing Pole. Gubber Blump and his heirloom Fishing Pole await a catch on Auberdine's docks. Hostile murlocs keep the town's small fishing boats ashore, so Gubber seeks help catching native Darkshore grouper from the coast. Gubber Blump takes pride in a family known for its skill with a fishing line. Night elves make up most of Auberdine, though dwarves and gnomes have settled around its docks and port. Gubber spends his days gazing over the Veiled Sea instead of digging into stone, hoping to bring in the local catch.

The Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds have overrun The Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure farms. The mine's fall points to a growing pest problem across Elwynn Forest. While Northshire Valley faces its own vermin, reports reach Goldshire that kobolds have claimed another vital site. Between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads south of town, the Fargodeep Mine once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering and tallow candles fill its damp tunnels. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is.

The Fate of Yenniku. At Grom'gol Base Camp, the head of Nezzliok speaks from the bubbling cauldron, ready to tell what became of the young Darkspear troll Yenniku. Kin'weelay stands beside the pot, waiting to hear the spirit's words. Having placated the spirits of Gan'zulah and Nezzliok, you listen as the head within the bubbling cauldron finally imparts its secret. Kin'weelay stands right beside the cauldron, waiting to hear it.

text.enUS: The Fate of a Loved One. The Fate of a Loved One is a quest concerning Resaan, who ventured into the dangerous Ruins of Ban'aethal to scavenge supplies and never returned. Over a week later, his grieving partner asks travelers bound for the ruins to discover his fate and bring him home or recover his cherished heirloom. The Fate of a Loved One centers on a desperate plea from someone whose partner, Resaan, ventured back into the Ruins of Ban'aethal. Despite earnest pleas for him to stay, Resaan felt compelled to brave the ruins in search of supplies, leaving behind someone who now waits in agonizing uncertainty.

The Fate of the Den. The Fate of the Den recounts the grim aftermath of a cultist assault upon a secluded druid den. An adventurer is dispatched to carry a recovered missive to Lotheluum in Valanaar, delivering news of severe casualties. The dispatch uncovers a deeply troubling reality: someone within Valanaar has been feeding vital information to the enemy. Following a violent incursion by cultists at the druid den, the surviving defenders find themselves battered and mourning the loss of their comrades. While the immediate crisis was stabilized with outside aid, the physical and emotional devastation is immense. Those who fell cannot be restored, and the wounded survivors remain in no condition to undertake a long trek while lingering cultists still roam nearby.
