text.enUS: The Final Message to the Wildhammer. Otho Moji'ko gives you a spear soaked in blood and bound with gryphon feathers. You are to take it to Aerie Peak, in the west of the Hinterlands, and drive it into the earth beside the well at the heart of the town. Following Another Message to the Wildhammer, Otho Moji'ko gives you the final message: a spear soaked in blood and bound with gryphon feathers. Carry it to Aerie Peak and plant it, dead center of town beside the well, to show the dwarves that trolls mean business. Otho hopes you come back alive, and warns of furious Wildhammer dwarves and rowdy Alliance folk.

The Flame's Casing. After Forging the Shaft, Kalaran Windblade says one final piece is needed for the torch. A large Twilight's Hammer encampment lies to the northwest, rumored to hold symbols and idols honoring its god, and Kalaran wants a single Symbol of Ragnaros. Kalaran calls this the last piece the torch needs. Northwest, among the mountains, a large Twilight's Hammer encampment is rumored to hold symbols and idols honoring their god, and these could carry enough enchantment for a magical casing. Kalaran asks for one Symbol of Ragnaros and will try to draw the magic out of it. The torch of retribution lacks one thing, a suitable source of arcane energy.

The Flawless Flame. Kalaran Windblade says you made the right choice, and that the blow must fall where it does most harm: the four sentry towers. With all four aflame, an offensive can begin before anyone has time to react. To set them alight, Kalaran needs to craft the torch of flawless flame. After Divine Retribution, Kalaran tells you the plan: burn the four sentry towers, so that an offensive can begin before anyone has time to react. Setting them ablaze takes the proper tool, and the tool takes materials. Kalaran will craft the torch of flawless flame if you bring four hearts of flame and four globes of golem oil, and points you first to the golems and elementals of these lands.

The Flying Machine Airport. Apothecary Zamah sends you to silence The Flying Machine Airport above Stonetalon. Carry her Toxic Fogger into the Venture Company’s logging grounds and strike at the cartel’s link to the outside world. Apothecary Zamah prepares Apothecary Lydon’s toxin for the Venture Company. The tauren seek to protect Stonetalon from deforestation and ravaging machinery, while the Forsaken answer with a different approach. Zamah targets the cartel’s connection beyond the mountains instead of its foot soldiers or loggers. A rumored copter pad carries light cargo and messages between Stonetalon and distant corporate offices.

The Forest's Bounty. The Forest's Bounty is a local quest in Shadowgale Forest where a timid forager asks for help collecting fallen acorns. Fierce predatory raptor-birds prowl the deeper woods, making harvesting too perilous without an adventurer's protection. The gathered acorns are then roasted into a tasty forest meal. A cautious forager seeking food in Shadowgale Forest finds themselves in a bind. While acorns lie scattered across the woodland floor, the surrounding trees are prowled by fierce, raptor-like creatures. Having gathered whatever fell near safety, the forager depends on passing travelers to venture into the wilder groves so that neither goes hungry.

The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, the Furlbrows have fled their farm, leaving a cherished heirloom behind. Recovering the pocket watch offers them a chance to salvage something personal from the chaos spreading through the region. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts rose from the pumpkin patches in the night, waking them with little time to gather what they could carry. In the rush to flee, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse.

The Forgotten Pools. At the Forgotten Pools, life surges through the dry Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids sense unseen forces beneath the earth. The Barrens once flourished as fertile land before ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent. The region became sun-baked scrubland, but lush oases have recently begun taking root in its dry basin. Druids of the Cenarion Circle find this sudden growth unnatural. They sense powers beneath the earth pressing upward, stirring vegetation and wildlife into life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

name.esES: La furia mora en las profundidades

text.enUS: The Fury Runs Deep. Motley Garmason seeks vengeance against Kam Deepfury, now held in Stormwind's Stockade. Deepfury planned the assault on the Thandol Span, where Bronzebeard defenders died, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Stormwind keeps Deepfury as a political prisoner, so Motley turns to an adventurer to carry out dwarven justice. Clashes between Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and Dark Iron insurgents keep the northern Wetlands in turmoil. When the Thandol Span came under attack, sabotage took the lives of several dwarves, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Roggo gathered intelligence showing that Kam Deepfury planned the strike. Rather than face execution on the front lines, Deepfury was taken to the Stormwind Stockade as a political prisoner, not executed for murder.

The General's Response. General Marcus Jonathan sends word to Lakeshire while Redridge waits for aid. His dispatch acknowledges Magistrate Solomon's plea against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, but offers no immediate reinforcements from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Stormwind City for troops to defend Redridge from the gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands. General Marcus Jonathan replies that the plea has been forwarded to the throne, but no soldiers are being sent now. He orders the letter returned to Lakeshire. Solomon is left troubled by Stormwind's delay and suspicious that something is wrong with its leaders.

The Giant Guardian. Rockbiter, a giant, was supposed to be watching over his little friend Shay, a night elf girl, but somehow she got away. Worried and unsure what to do, he asks you to go and look for her. Rockbiter was supposed to look after Shay. The last time he saw her, the two of them were walking through the ruins just north of where he stands. All was well until he turned around and found her gone. He cannot work out what to do, but he knows your legs travel much faster than his, so he asks you to search for her.

name.esES: El don de la Visión cielonata
name.ptBR: O dom da visão do céu

text.enUS: The Gift of Skysight. The Gift of Skysight is an early rite of passage for young Windshapers learning to harness their innate connection to the spiritual realm. Under the direction of Ventaari Brightwish, initiates travel to an Elemental Convergence to awaken their perception and listen directly to the whispers of the spirits. Windshapers possess an inherent bond with the elemental forces that shape their world, embodied by the sacred faculty known as Skysight. This gift allows mortal senses to attune to spiritual wavelengths, bridging the physical gap between the living and the unseen. While a Windshaper can invoke this inner vision across the wilds, doing so near points of concentrated power deepens the connection, unlocking resonant boons and hidden wisdom whispered on the wind.

The Glowing Fruit. The Glowing Fruit is a quest in Teldrassil initiated by discovering a strange fruited plant growing wild in the forest. Suspecting something unnatural, young adventurers deliver the luminescent specimen to the herbalist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth for study. While traversing the misty boughs of Teldrassil, explorers occasionally stumble across curious, luminous flora bearing large, round fruit. Given the delicate balance of the World Tree and the recent strange behaviors among the island's wildlife, unusual botanical specimens demand careful investigation. Convinced that the strange growth should not be ignored, adventurers pluck the radiant harvest to bring to someone versed in the flora of the wild.

The Glowing Shard. The Glowing Shard is a mysterious emerald-hued gem plucked from the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Swirling with smoky essence beneath its polished surface, this disturbing relic drives adventurers to seek answers in Ratchet and beyond. Drawn from deep within the Wailing Caverns, the glowing shard immediately unnerves those who hold it. Brilliant green and seemingly solid, it holds churning, mist-like shadows beneath its crystalline face. The crystal exerts a subtle pull, demanding attention while exuding a deeply unsettling aura that hints at the corrupted nature of the slumbering druids and their nightmare-infested sanctuary.

The Goddess Provides. The Goddess Provides is an introductory kaldorei quest centered on recognizing Elune's divine gifts. Set in the boughs of Teldrassil following the end of the Long Vigil, it teaches young night elves to embrace the lunar guidance and cloaking shadows bestowed by Mother Moon. For millennia following the Sundering, the kaldorei maintained their solitary Long Vigil, watching over Kalimdor and guarding the sacred peaks of Mount Hyjal. The devastation of the Third War and the climactic defense of the World Tree forced an end to that ancient seclusion. Now relocated to the sheltering boughs of Teldrassil, the night elves face an unfamiliar world, stepping onto the broader stage of Azeroth by aligning themselves with distant allies across the ocean.

name.enUS: The Good News and The Bad News
name.deDE: Die gute und die schlechte Nachricht
name.frFR: La bonne nouvelle et la mauvaise nouvelle
name.itIT: The Good News and The Bad News
name.ptBR: The Good News and The Bad News
name.roRO: The Good News and The Bad News
name.svSE: The Good News and The Bad News

text.enUS: The Good News and The Bad News. Narain Soothfancy has read through the ledger and has both good news and bad. He is nearly certain he can build an arcanite buoy to your specifications, but he needs a great deal of arcanite, elementium ore and fine gems. This comes once the chicken, the goggles and the second Draconic For Dummies book are all done. Narain Soothfancy reads the ledger in silence, mumbling under his breath. He is ninety-nine percent sure he can make an arcanite buoy that will work as you specified, but says all of that depends on the bad news. For the buoy he wants twenty arcanite bars, ten elementium ore, ten Azerothian diamonds and ten blue sapphires. Bring them, and he will craft it.

The Gordunni Orb. Rok Orhan knows the enemy well, but is a warrior and cannot say what the Gordunni orb is capable of. Rok knows of a mage in Orgrimmar who can tell more. The orb is yours to carry to Uthel'nay, at Orgrimmar's Darkbriar Lodge. This follows Dark Ceremony. After Dark Ceremony, Rok Orhan holds the orb, but admits to being a warrior who cannot begin to say what it can do. Rok knows a mage in Orgrimmar who will be able to say more, and sends you off with the orb to find Uthel'nay at the Darkbriar Lodge.

The Gordunni Scroll. A soiled scroll lies in the Gordunni Outpost, and picking it up shows what seems to be a meeting or ceremony. Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache would be interested in it, and in what it might mean for the Gordunni. Taking up the soiled scroll, you see that it appears to depict a gathering or ceremony of some kind. Rok Orhan in Camp Mojache, you judge, would want to see it, and to learn what it might mean for the Gordunni.

The Grand Skyseer. The Grand Skyseer is an introductory journey into the heart of Valanaar, directing travelers to seek an audience with Ayessa Dawnsinger at the Windshaper lodge. As tensions simmer between local factions and a shadowy cult threatens the region, the Windshapers urgently seek individuals gifted with spiritual sight. Upon arriving in the town of Valanaar, travelers are directed toward the central lodge where the Windshapers convene under the leadership of Grand Skyseer Ayessa Dawnsinger. Having caught the attention of Elder Amberwind through notable deeds in Shen'dar Village, new arrivals are welcomed into the fold of those attuned to the spirits. Yet Valanaar remains fraught with external and internal dangers, requiring newcomers to navigate fragile local politics carefully.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest where the traveler Sam teaches fledgling adventurers the art of roughing it in the wild. By pausing to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers learn how to sustain themselves on the road before pursuing specialized tradeskills. The wide lands of Azeroth call to countless restless souls seeking fortune, danger, and renown. Yet raw ambition alone cannot shield a fledgling adventurer from the biting cold or exhaustion of the open road. Mastering basic wilderness craft—knowing when to stop, build a fire, and gather one's strength—is the quiet foundation upon which every legendary journey is built. Sam's invitation offers newcomers a chance to pause and learn these essential outdoor survival habits.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory quest offered by the outdoorsman Raan, who teaches novice adventurers the fundamentals of wilderness survival. By resting beside a basic campfire to gain Boosted Rest, wanderers learn essential campcraft before venturing toward nearby trade trainers to learn practical professions. The Great Outdoors serves as an introductory lesson in surviving beyond the safety of settlement walls. Offered by an experienced wilderness traveler named Raan, the task reminds wandering adventurers that raw ambition and steel are useless without the practical campcraft needed to endure harsh elements. Raan welcomes aspiring wanderers into the ranks of restless souls seeking fortune and glory, offering practical guidance to those willing to learn.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest offered by Brakk to aspiring adventurers. By learning to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers discover the fundamentals of sustaining themselves in the wild before pursuing practical tradeskills. Venturing into the untamed reaches of Azeroth requires more than martial grit; it demands the basic knowledge to endure the elements. Brakk greets aspiring adventurers with a hearty 'Lok-tar', recognizing the restless spirit of those seeking fortune and glory. To survive the long road ahead, every traveler must first master the art of making camp and recovering their strength amidst the wilderness.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory quest that instructs aspiring adventurers in the fundamental arts of wilderness survival. Guided by the traveler Kaga, newcomers learn how to recuperate beside a basic campfire before advancing to learn tradeskills and craft specialized camp fixtures. Every adventurer setting foot beyond the safety of civilization quickly discovers that raw courage is not enough to survive the frontier. The Great Outdoors introduces newcomers to the vital necessity of wilderness acclimation. Taught by the experienced traveler Kaga, this brief lesson reminds fledgling heroes that thriving in unexplored territories begins with knowing how to establish a camp and endure the open elements.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival lesson offered to hunters by an experienced scout named Lyreena. It emphasizes the importance of resting beside a campfire to recover and gain the Boosted Rest buff while journeying through the untamed wilds. Venturing beyond civilization's borders demands more than sharp aim and keen senses; it requires respect for the raw untamed elements. An experienced scout named Lyreena offers guidance to wandering hunters, welcoming them to pause their trek and take comfort by her campfire. In the perilous wilds of Azeroth, knowing how to establish a hearth and replenish one's strength between hunts is just as critical as knowing how to track quarry.

The Great Outdoors. You learn how rest and preparation help you survive beyond city walls. Travelers across Azeroth teach new wanderers to rest by a campfire and prepare for the wilds. Even a sharp blade or potent magic cannot protect you from the wilds if you neglect the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers near roadside clearings share this lesson with travelers leaving their home valleys. Resting by a campfire eases sore boots, settles the mind, and readies you for the road ahead. Regular rest and preparation give you a better chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors introduces wandering adventurers to the essentials of wilderness survival and campcraft. By taking a seat at Eric's campfire, travelers learn how to recuperate properly in the wild before taking up tradeskills to support their journeys. Stepping out into the wider world requires more than ambition and a weapon or holy symbol. For fledgling travelers, survival depends on knowing how to rest properly amidst the elements. At his basic campfire, the seasoned traveler Eric welcomes wandering adventurers to take a seat, warm themselves by the embers, and discover how vital proper rest is before tackling the untamed wilderness.

The Green Hills of Stranglethorn. Barnil Stonepot was trusted to proofread the manuscript for Hemet Nesingwary's novel, but a fierce gust of wind scattered the loose pages across the jungle. To spare him his master's anger, you are asked to scour the wilds, assemble the missing pages into four complete chapters, and return the finished work. Following your arrival in the expedition camp after Welcome to the Jungle, Barnil Stonepot finds himself facing a disaster. While reviewing the draft of Hemet Nesingwary's novel, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, a sudden gale caught the loose leaves and flung them into the wild. Though he managed to recover a fair portion of the work, many sheets remain lost in the brush. To keep his master from discovering the mishap, he needs every misplaced page tracked down and compiled into Chapter I, Chapter II, Chapter III, and Chapter IV.

The Greenwarden. First Mate Fitzsimmons sends Alliance travelers from Menethil Harbor northeast into the Wetlands marshes. They seek a mysterious being rumored to dwell among the beasts. Sailors and wanderers at Menethil Harbor trade stories of a beast lurking in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons describes the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs and calls those who seek it gullible. Leave the dry road, he warns, and “ol’ Greenie” will bite you in two. To the folk on the docks, anything huge in the murky waters is another man-eating danger in the marsh.

The Grizzled Den. In Dun Morogh, Pilot Stonegear tests a recruit's grit in the Grizzled Den. From Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, he sends them west to hunt wendigos for thick pelts to warm his siege engine, Trollplow. Pilot Stonegear, stationed at Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, claims to have the nerves and constitution needed to operate a massive dwarven siege tank in freezing mountain air. He makes newcomers prove they share his grit. The test sends them into the frozen hills to face the native beasts.

name.esES: Las armas del Fuerte del Norte

text.enUS: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet wants the guns at Northwatch Hold silenced. Alliance gunners there have been blasting merchant vessels, so he sends you down the Merchant Coast to strike the artillery officers and bring back badges from fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold guards the southern Barrens coast for the humans of Theramore. Its soldiers watch Horde activity in Kalimdor, but fear has made them see every unfamiliar sail as a threat. The guns on the ramparts fire without warning at passing ships, endangering Ratchet's merchant traffic and its privateering vessels.

The Hammer May Fall. Tallow sends fighters from Tarren Mill across the mountains to relieve Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Before reporting to Drum Fel, you prove your battle readiness against Boulderfist ogres near the ruins of Stromgarde. In Tarren Mill, Tallow has little patience for untested fighters wandering the Foothills. While recruits stand idle, allies are under attack far away. He sends capable fighters east through Thoradin's Wall into the Arathi Highlands, where Hammerfall is besieged from several sides. Tallow wants them to prove their worth against a strong foe before he sends them to the outpost.

The Harvester. A severed head found in the southern Barrens brings The Harvester’s strange presence to Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer examines the remains, and the creature’s intrusion raises concerns for the land’s spiritual and ecological balance. In the southern Barrens, you find the severed head of a silithid called the Harvester. Lions, raptors, and kodos roam these grasslands, but this chitinous insectoid is unlike the native wildlife. Its presence suggests an alien ecology has reached the open plains of Kalimdor.

The Haunted Isle. Krazek keeps his ears open for unusual rumors throughout Booty Bay on behalf of Baron Revilgaz. A tale shared by tavern sailors speaks of a haunted island off the coast, inhabited by water elementals and the ghost of a raving goblin. Delivering this rumor to Revilgaz piques the baron's interest in an ancient troll legend. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Krazek gathers word of anything unusual happening throughout Stranglethorn Vale at the request of Baron Revilgaz. While Krazek normally pays little heed to spectral gossip, stories told by sailors drinking in the local tavern caught his attention. They speak of an offshore isle occupied by water elementals and haunted by a raving goblin ghost, so he asks you to relay the story to the baron.

The Haunted Mills. Coleman Farthing of Brill seeks vengeance on the Agamands, his former landowners. He sends you north to Agamand Mills to destroy their restless remains, beginning with Devlin, the family’s sharp-tongued younger son. Farthing’s hatred reaches back to the family’s failure to protect Tirisfal’s common folk from the Plague. Before the Third War, Agamand Mills fed northern Tirisfal under the rule of a wealthy landed family. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, common folk turned to the nobles for safety and found no shelter. Coleman Farthing survived as undead, but hatred for the family he served still consumes him. He wants their bones gathered, not to end their torment, but to desecrate them beneath his heel.

The Head of the Beast. In Stormwind, The Head of the Beast carries you from Elling Trias to Master Mathias Shaw in Old Town. Reporting Lord Gregor Lescovar’s death confirms your place in Stormwind’s covert intelligence network. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind’s covert apparatus through SI:7 from hidden chambers in Old Town. When you report Lescovar’s death, Shaw recognizes your skill and ruthlessness, praises your efficiency, and thanks you for serving the people of Stormwind.

The Hermit. Elaine Carevin in Darkshire sends you to check on Abercrombie, an elderly recluse who has not come to town for provisions. He lives in a rickety shack at the edge of Raven Hill Cemetery. Elaine Carevin remembers an old man who came to Darkshire for provisions, then stopped appearing. With danger on Duskwood’s roads, she asks you to visit his shack by Raven Hill Cemetery and see whether he is safe.

The Hidden Key. Tucked away in the binding of Bookie Herod's ledgers is a small brass key alongside notes referencing a secure strongbox. Locating this container deep within the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound may reveal how Private Thorsen was betrayed. Searching through Bookie Herod's ledgers yields no direct mention of Private Thorsen, but it reveals something else: a small brass key concealed inside a book's binding. Scraps among the paperwork make passing mention of a secure strongbox tucked away inside the Stockpile, the cavern complex at the rear of Kurzen's Compound. Opening that container might reveal how Thorsen's cover was blown.

The Hidden Niche. Alaric's memories lead you back into Fenris Keep. His remains point toward a forgotten alcove where he seeks rest and an old relic waits. Alaric remembers Fenris Keep in its better days. Horde scouts have lifted his bones from a shallow grave outside the stronghold, but he will not go quietly to the Sepulcher. He offers vital knowledge instead: a hidden niche in the keep's southwestern tower holds an item treasured by Thule Ravenclaw and his fellow mages.

The High Wilderness. Angelas Moonbreeze and Troyas look into old ruins in the forests of Feralas, yet lately Troyas goes alone to the High Wilderness, which worries Angelas. Gordunni ogres hold that ground. Angelas hopes you will make the ruins to the southeast a little safer by culling the ogres. Angelas Moonbreeze admits the work is dangerous, but Angelas and Troyas keep exploring the ruins scattered through the forests of Feralas. Lately Troyas goes to the High Wilderness alone, and Angelas worries. The Gordunni ogres have taken over there and do not take kindly to anyone who enters their territory. Angelas hopes you will go to the ruins southeast of here and cull some of them, to make it safer for Troyas: eight Gordunni Warlocks, eight Gordunni Shamans and eight Gordunni Brutes.

The Hills Have Eyes. "The Hills Have Eyes" is a quest in the Gustberry Lowlands where the beleaguered farmer Aamelia takes a stand against highwayman bandits. Adventurers launch a preemptive strike on an encampment in the northern hills to diminish the bandit forces before their leader, Ferauu, launches a raid. In the Gustberry Lowlands, a farmer named Aamelia faces an impending assault from a ring of outlaws led by Ferauu. Rather than waiting passively for doom to arrive at her doorstep, she urges travelers to launch a preemptive strike against a bandit encampment in the hills to the north. By taking out the highwaymen before they muster their attack, she aims to thin their ranks and buy precious time.

The Horn of the Beast. A gigantic horn that came from Margol the Rager in Searing Gorge is scratched and cracked, with a broken axe head lodged in its rough surface. The axe head is etched as the property of Mountaineer Pebblebitty, and it shatters into a million pieces when you try to dislodge it. The horn is to be taken to Pebblebitty. The horn from Margol the Rager is covered in scratches and cracks. Lodged in it is an unusual metal object, a broken axe head etched to show that it belonged to Mountaineer Pebblebitty. When you try to work it free, it shatters into a million pieces.

The Howling Vale. At the Howling Vale, worgen have overrun a ruined shrine near Felwood. Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow seeks the cause of their arrival in Ashenvale. Worgen cries echo from a ruined shrine in northern Ashenvale. The shrine of Mel'Thandris lies beyond a cavern path near the Felwood border. Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow fears the worgen may bring another disaster to the woodland realm. Night elf sentinels are already spending great effort holding back demonic corruption from Felwood.

The Hunt Begins. Young hunters at Camp Narache gather food and feathers for their people. Grull Hawkwind asks you to hunt plainstriders on Red Cloud Mesa, where the village depends on what the young can provide. On Red Cloud Mesa, the tauren hunt to feed and clothe their people. They also value the stalk and chase as a test of discipline and a sport. When Camp Narache's stores run low, the young hunters gather plainstrider meat for cooking and feathers for tribal garments.

The Hunt Completed. In Ashenvale, the hunt tests a Horde champion against three legendary predators. Felling Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon proves strength, tenacity, and primal prowess in a contested forest. Senani Thunderheart tests travelers among the Horde forces in Ashenvale. Her hunt tests more than loyalty to the warchief; it asks whether a hunter understands survival in the wild. Three legendary predators are its quarry: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the fierce hippogryph Sharptalon. Felling all three and securing their trophies proves a hunter's blood runs true.

The Hunt Continues. The Hunt Continues is an early rite of passage assigned by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. It tasks aspiring hunters with gathering mountain cougar pelts from the southern hills to clothe the tribe's children and mend their tents. In Camp Narache, young hunters are taught that taking a beast is never an idle pursuit or a search for trophies. Grull Hawkwind charges fledgling adventurers with venturing into the southern hills of Red Cloud Mesa to track down mountain cougars. Rather than proving martial prowess alone, the task emphasizes responsibility to the community, showing that true hunters must provide essential provisions for their people.

The Hunter's Path. In Mulgore, young tauren hunters are sent to Bloodhoof Village for advanced training. There, they seek Yaw Sharpmane and begin the trials of taming and bonding with wild beasts. Among the Shu'halo, hunting is sacred. A hunter learns the balance of nature, honors the spirits of the plains, and respects the animals that sustain the tribes. When young hunters prove they can survive in the wild and use a bow or gun, their elders send them to seasoned mentors. That journey marks their step beyond solitary tracking and toward adulthood in tauren culture.

The Hunter's Path. In Durotar, The Hunter's Path sends young orc and troll hunters to Razor Hill. There, Thotar teaches them to bind wild predators. In Durotar, young hunters learn to track prey with bow and cunning. Following trails through red clay canyons and harsh scrubland teaches patience. To master the hunter's way in the Horde, they must also learn to bond with the land's wild beasts. When class trainers judge a student ready, they direct them to Razor Hill.

The Hunter's Path. In Dun Morogh, novice hunters are sent to Kharanos to learn to tame wild beasts. The Hunter's Path begins when local trainers judge them ready to face that trial. Novice hunters travel Dun Morogh's snowy crags alone until they master bonding with beasts. Olmin Burningbeard and Tristane Shadowstone watch their pupils closely. They wait until a hunter can face a savage creature with the poise to spare its life. Once a novice shows enough discipline, the trainers send them down the mountain roads toward Kharanos.

The Hunter's Way. In Mulgore, Skorn Whitecloud guides aspiring trackers through the Hunter's Way. To prove their skill and respect for the wild, you hunt flatland prowlers and bring their claws to Melor Stonehoof on Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. For the tauren, hunting is among the highest honors. It calls for patience, attention to the Earth Mother's balance, and respect for the beasts across the plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud has spent decades tracking across Kalimdor and now rests in Mulgore. He sees young adventurers eager to roam and gives them a traditional trial to shape their ambition into discipline.

The Islander. Warrior trainers across Azeroth send proven fighters to Fray Island for a test among their peers. The island lies off the Merchant Coast, where chief warrior Klannoc Macleod awaits those who seek the next step in their training. Warrior trainers in Alliance and Horde capitals send students who have outgrown basic drills to test themselves against their peers. A fighter's progress comes through combat, not rank or loyalty. The journey leads away from civilized sparring yards to a rugged isle in the Great Sea.

The Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have overrun the Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn. Marshal Dughan sends scouts to learn how far the infestation has spread. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora and supplies raw stone and metal to the kingdom. Dughan cannot spare Stormwind guards from their town patrols, so he sends independent adventurers east to see whether kobolds have taken this mine too.

The Journey Has Just Begun. After Onyxia's fall, skilled leatherworkers in Orgrimmar learn how her scales can guard against the black dragonflight. Overlord Runthak recognizes their craft and teaches a rare technique for making protective cloaks, needed against the flames of Blackrock Spire. Onyxia's fall is a triumph for the Horde, yet the black dragonflight remains a threat. The broodmother's scaled hide resists draconic flame. Horde leaders seek craftsmen who can turn the dragon's remains into defensive armor rather than let them go to waste.

The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly recognizes the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft needed to make a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can also work her hide. When an artisan with master leatherworking reports to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer recognizes how much those skills matter in the battles ahead.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor tells you of Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck his ship in the northwest waters of Desolace, and he left a valuable chest behind and teleported away. The chest and what is inside are to be found. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor tells you of a first order of business. It concerns Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck Karnitol's ship in the northwest waters of Desolace. Karnitol and his servants tried to carry one of his costlier chests to shore, but the giants swarmed in, and he gave up the chest and teleported himself and his servants out. The chest and its contents are to be found, then returned to Karnitol in Stormwind. It lies along the northern coastline, in the Ethel Rethor stretch.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. The chest of the mage Karnitol has been pried open, and it is completely empty. Long, deep scratches on its sides and top suggest neither man nor giant was responsible, and you return to Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point. You study what forced the chest open. Long, deep scratches run along its sides and top. They point to something that was neither man nor giant, and they do not look like the work of a dagger or sword. The chest is completely empty. With nothing else to be done, you close it and prepare to leave, knowing Kreldig Ungor will be disappointed.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor still thinks Karnitol's belongings can be found. Up the same coast, by Ranazjar Isle, the Slitherblade naga hold a place among night elf ruins that lie at the bottom of the sea, and Kreldig reckons the satchel is most likely there. Following the second part of the Karnitol shipwreck search, Kreldig Ungor tells you hope is not lost. Along the same coast but farther north, close to Ranazjar Isle, sunken night elf ruins lie on the ocean floor, and the Slitherblade naga call them home. Kreldig judges it the likeliest place for Karnitol's satchel. A Recovery Diver's Potion is provided.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor sends you to Ironforge with Karnitol's satchel, to put it in the hands of Roetten Stonehammer, who will pay you for the work. Kreldig Ungor tells you to carry Karnitol's things back to Roetten Stonehammer in Ironforge, who will pay you for the work. With a laugh, Kreldig adds that Roetten may be so pleased that you get asked to join the Reclaimers full time. The way back should be made carefully and without dawdling, since Karnitol has little patience, though he is a generous man.

The Key to Freedom. A small brass key has found its way to you in Searing Gorge. A few words are scratched into its head, marking it as a Dark Iron outhouse key that is not to be copied. Where it leads, you cannot yet say. The brass key looks simple, but for the words scratched into its head, which read Dark Iron Outhouse and warn against duplicating it. Where it leads is unknown, and the way to learn is to search Searing Gorge for a use for it.

The Killing Fields. The Killing Fields is an Alliance quest offered by Farmer Saldean in Westfall. Saldean tasks adventurers with destroying the rogue Harvest Watchers that overrun his crops and the neighboring farmlands. It illustrates the collapse of local agriculture in the wake of the Defias Brotherhood's disruption. While many farmers across Westfall abandoned their acreage when bandits and outlaws swept through the region, Farmer Saldean and his family resolved to hold their ground. Unfortunately, squatting thieves are not the only threat choking the Saldean farm. The mechanical Harvest Watchers intended to tend and safeguard the grain have gone rampant, pacing the furrows and attacking anyone who approaches.

The Knife Revealed. Ginro Hearthkindle sends you with the knife to Quintis Jonespyre, the Stronghold's resident druid, who can learn an object's past by touching it. Ginro says Quintis owes a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt that this will clear. After Boat Wreckage, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you with the knife to Quintis Jonespyre, the resident druid of Feathermoon Stronghold, who has unusual skills. One is psychometry, learning an object's past just by touching it. Ginro will not say how it works, calling it magic Ginro does not and chooses not to understand, only that Ginro has seen it work. Quintis owes Ginro a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt, which will be paid if Quintis works some magic on the knife. Quintis lives in a little tree-house in the Stronghold.

text.enUS: The Kolkar of Desolace. The Kolkar threaten Horde lands from their stronghold in Desolace. Regthar Deathgate sends Horde champions west across the mountains to reinforce scout Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post. Centaur raiders keep pressing into the Barrens, and Regthar Deathgate knows that fighting them there will not end the threat. The Kolkar clan draws its strength from the rugged lands on Kalimdor's western coast. While their ancestral stronghold remains beyond Horde control, raiders will keep pouring through the mountain passes. To stop them, the Horde must strike at their home.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, The Legend of Stalvan begins with Madame Eva's vision of death for her granddaughter, Alyssa. Her cards and trance leave one name: Stalvan. She sends travelers to the Darkshire Town Hall to search the records. Madame Eva reads cards and portents for troubled locals in Darkshire. After a terrible disturbance jolts her awake, she draws the Death card for her young granddaughter, Alyssa. Eva enters a deep trance, seeking what the omen means, but finds only one clue: the name Stalvan. Fearing for her family and the town, she asks you to follow that name before tragedy strikes.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry searches the town records for Stalvan Mistmantle. The oldest entry points west to the abandoned schoolhouse in Moonbrook, Westfall, where the search for Stalvan’s past begins. After your inquiries in Darkshire, Clerk Daltry searches the town registry for Stalvan Mistmantle. The ledger has not been updated in years, and it gives Stalvan’s last known home as the schoolhouse in Moonbrook, far to the west. Daltry treats the old address as routine record keeping. He asks you to look into it and bring back any records that might bring Darkshire’s dusty archives up to date.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Moonbrook, The Legend of Stalvan leads back to Darkshire's records. A dusty, unsent letter from an old footlocker proves Stalvan Mistmantle stayed there before his trail went cold. You find a dusty, unsent letter in an old footlocker while tracing Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Moonbrook was once an agricultural settlement, but now lies in ruin, crowded with outlaws and restless specters. Few remember Stalvan's brief stay, yet the letter places him in the hamlet.

The Legend of Stalvan. A scratched entry in Darkshire points the search for Stalvan Mistmantle toward Goldshire. Clerk Daltry finds another destination beneath Stalvan Mistmantle's earlier entry in Darkshire's town registry. The hurried note is partly scratched out, as if someone meant to hide the route or changed their mind. It points northwest, toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Elwynn Forest.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Goldshire, the search for Stalvan Mistmantle turns to an old letter left at the inn. Its trail leads from Elwynn Forest to Stormwind's Canal District. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Innkeeper Farley remembers a stormy night from years ago. A traveling courier came in from the pouring rain to find shelter, then rushed downstairs around midnight in a panic. He wore only his sleepwear as he fled into the dark storm. No one saw him again.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Stormwind, you search the Flintridge belongings for clues to Stalvan Mistmantle. Sealed crates by the canals hold the household’s remaining possessions, while restless spirits tied to the massacre guard what remains. You trace Stalvan’s path from Duskwood to Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom watches over what remains of the Flintridge household. His father served the estate before him and had to mop up blood after a massacre that claimed the household. The name Stalvan is somehow tied to that slaughter.

The Legend of Stalvan. Beside Stormwind City's canals, the Flintridge crate yields a clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past. The torn journal page leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. A torn page from Stalvan Mistmantle's journal lies beneath a ceramic vase in a sealed crate. The crate holds musty Flintridge heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits. Stalvan's own hand offers a glimpse of the reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Elwynn, your search for Stalvan Mistmantle reaches Marshal Haggard's home. The aging veteran's eyesight has failed, and an upstairs chest holds papers left behind when he moved in. Marshal Haggard lives on Elwynn Forest's southeastern edge, near Duskwood and Redridge. An old chest upstairs holds parchments he found when he moved into his secluded home. His failing eyesight kept him from reading them, and they remain untouched until you ask about Stalvan.

The Legend of Stalvan. Marshal Haggard sends you back to Darkshire with a page he cannot read. Tavernkeep Smitts may know the hand that wrote it. Marshal Haggard cannot read the faded writing on the torn journal page you recovered from his chest in Elwynn Forest. His eyesight is failing. The retired commander remembers serving with the Stormwind Guard and spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. The trail leads back across the river, so he sends you to Tavernkeep Smitts. Years behind the bar have made Smitts a keeper of local history and rumors.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, The Legend of Stalvan now rests on proof in muddy journal pages. Tavernkeep Smitts gives them to you and sends you to Commander Althea Ebonlocke. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard once investigated the slaughter of a visiting noble family in Duskwood. Haggard was then a leader of the Stormwind Guard. They found torn, muddy journal pages at the scene, but had no handwriting samples or other papers to confirm who wrote them. The notes could not formally implicate the recluse rumored to live in the wilderness. Now, evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood links the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle. The rumors have become proof of murder.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, the search for Stalvan Mistmantle brings a bloodstained journal page before the Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends you to Clerk Daltry to compare its writing with the town records. The Night Watch has gathered journal pages from across Duskwood and the surrounding human territories. Together, they appear to condemn Stalvan Mistmantle, the elusive tutor. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has suspected him for some time, but she needs certainty before passing judgment. The bloodstained page alone cannot prove who wrote it. The writing must be matched to Stalvan’s own hand.

The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry matches the recovered handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle. His report to Commander Althea Ebonlocke turns the Night Watch's suspicion into fact. Back in Darkshire's town hall, Clerk Daltry compares the bloodstained journal page with signatures in the Town Registry. The handwriting is an exact match for Stalvan Mistmantle. After a trail through manors, inns, and civic records across the human kingdoms, the Night Watch now has the evidence to treat the danger as an urgent local threat.

The Lich's Identity. Bethor Iceshard seeks to learn who lives alone on Brightwater Lake. He sends an emissary to steal the recluse's spellbook and judge his power and allegiance. A lone lich lives in exile on a small island in Brightwater Lake, north of the Undercity. He has free will, unlike the Lich King's mindless pawns, but paranoia rules his life. He believes any undead who approach are Scourge thralls sent to drag him back into servitude. So he unleashes summoned minions on anyone who sets foot on his shore.

The Lich's Spellbook. On Brightwater Lake's island, a spellbook draws Bethor Iceshard's attention. He hopes its pages will reveal the lich's skill and who he was in life. A free-willed lich guards an island in Brightwater Lake with skeletal minions. He distrusts the outside world and mistakes other undead for Scourge thralls, ordering his guardians to kill anyone who approaches. Bethor Iceshard seeks skilled necromancers for the Forsaken beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. He sends an emissary into the island camp to take the lich's spellbook. Bethor hopes its pages will reveal the master's power and identity before death took Lordaeron.

The Loch. The Loch’s waters are held back by the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. The lake is the largest body of water on Khaz Modan and sustains the surrounding dwarven settlements. The Loch spans the center of Loch Modan, among the largest inland lakes in the known world. Only Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake in the north rival its size. Its waters support local fishermen and give Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges a peaceful setting. Aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts prowl beneath the calm surface, making a swim across perilous.

The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is bound for Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives the trophy, a sign that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory is among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history. Nefarian, brood-master of the Black Dragonflight and ruler of Upper Blackrock Spire, has long threatened the surrounding human kingdoms. His defeat ends his twisted experiments and schemes. Carrying his battle-scarred head back to Stormwind gives proof that the Lord of Blackrock has fallen to the Alliance's greatest heroes.

The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is carried from Blackrock Mountain to Orgrimmar as proof of victory. Presented to Warchief Thrall, it marks the fall of a great enemy of the Horde. Nefarian has fallen at last. He masterminded Blackwing Lair and led the black dragon brood in the Eastern Kingdoms. His colossal, battle-scarred head proves his death. For Horde warriors, carrying the prize from the burning heights of Blackrock Mountain across the Great Sea to Durotar brings great honor.

The Lord of Blackrock. In Orgrimmar, Nefarian's severed head is brought before the Horde. After Thrall confirms the black dragon's death, he sends the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength to show the trophy to all. Nefarian's head reaches Orgrimmar after the black dragon is slain atop Blackwing Lair. Warchief Thrall confirms that Deathwing's son has fallen, then sends the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength. There, the remains are prepared for public display, a warning to enemies and a rallying cry for the true Horde.

The Lost Caravan. After Encroaching Wildlife, Watcher Biggs has a further matter for you. Stunned in the Lost Ones' attack on the caravan, Biggs still saw a wagon hauled off to the Fallow Sanctuary, the Lost Ones' village in the north. A chest of valuable reagents rode in it, and Biggs wants those reagents brought back. Biggs was knocked senseless in the attack, yet glimpsed one of the caravan's wagons being dragged away to the Fallow Sanctuary, the Lost Ones' village to the north. In that wagon was a chest of reagents prized by the wizards of Nethergarde Keep for their studies. Biggs wants the chest found and its contents carried back.

The Lost Fragments. Theldurin the Lost is in a panic over the Scroll of Myzrael. Its magic could drag Myzrael up to the surface, yet if she is already free, the scroll may be the only way to bind her again. Elementals in a rage have shredded it and fight over the scraps, and you are sent to gather them. Theldurin the Lost is alarmed at the mention of the Scroll of Myzrael, fearing its magic could draw Myzrael to the surface. Then comes a change of heart: if she has already slipped free, or is gathering strength to strike, the scroll is just what you will need to trap her again.

The Lost Ingots. Glorin Steelbrow needs Lightforge iron from a shipwreck off the Wetlands. The chest holds only one ingot, and the Bluegill murlocs have taken the rest. The Flying Osprey lies broken off the Wetlands shore. Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven priest, sent you to recover its Lightforge iron. The waterlogged chest in the cargo hold holds only a single ingot. Bluegill murlocs near the wreck have scavenged the rest of the shipment.

The Lost Pages. A gust has scattered The Lost Pages across Ashenvale. Gurda Ragescar is stranded near Splintertree Post, unable to run the shredder she is taking from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp without its manual. The Warsong Clan uses steam-powered shredders bought from Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Their delicate workings are not easy for an orc warrior to master. As Gurda Ragescar carried a newly bought shredder north, a sudden gust tore the instruction booklet from her hands. Twelve parchment leaves scattered across the forest floor.

The Lost Pilot. Pilot Hammerfoot waits at the wrecked siege engine, fearing for Mori Hildelve in Dun Morogh's crags. Hildelve went on foot to find rare ore for potent blastpowder, but days have passed, and roars echo through the peaks. Pilot Mori Hildelve drove his siege engine up Dun Morogh's steep, jagged ridges while searching for rare ore needed to make high-grade blastpowder. The machine broke on the slope. Hildelve left Pilot Hammerfoot at the camp to guard the wreckage, then continued higher into the frozen wilderness on foot.

The Lost Report. Sifting through loose dirt in Dustwallow Marsh, you find an orc's severed hand clutching a tube carved from bone, with a dirt-stained parchment inside. It is a report written by an orc who watched Theramore as a spy for weeks, and it is meant for Nazeer Bloodpike, the orcs' spymaster at Brackenwall Village. In the loose dirt lies an orc's severed hand, gripping a tube carved from bone. The parchment inside is a report from an orc who watched Theramore as a spy for weeks. After scanning it, you see that it should go to Nazeer Bloodpike, the orcs' spymaster at Brackenwall Village.

The Lost Runner. The Lost Runner is a task to locate Sentinel Eralya Leafshadow, an initiate courier overdue from the Oracle Tree. It matters because communications between the sacred tree and the elders in Darnassus are vital to the night elf leadership. The Council of the Forest maintains a contingent of Sentinels stationed at the revered Oracle Tree within Teldrassil. The tree conveys sacred messages to the night elf elders, relying on dedicated runners to carry these dispatches back to Darnassus along the winding forest roads. Ensuring these missives arrive safely is essential for the guidance and governance of the kaldorei.

The Lost Supplies. A small, sturdy barrel has its seams sealed with pungent yellow wax. A stamp on its base names Quartermaster Lungertz and Nethergarde Keep, and that is where it belongs. Pungent yellow wax seals the seams of this compact, stout barrel. Underneath, a stamp reads Quartermaster Lungertz, Nethergarde Keep, so the barrel is meant for the quartermaster there.

The Lost Tools. Blackrock fire has sunk Foreman Oslow's tools in Lake Everstill. With Lakeshire under pressure, local hands must maintain its defenses, and the tools shipped from Goldshire are needed to rebuild the shattered bridge. The Great Bridge no longer connects Lakeshire to Elwynn Forest. A replacement shipment of stonemasonry and carpentry tools came overland from Goldshire, but the wagons could not reach town. The crew loaded the supplies into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill. A Blackrock orc catapult struck the boat, destroying it and sending Oslow's heavy ironbound toolbox to the lake floor.

The Mark of Quality. At Feathermoon Stronghold, the leatherworker Pratt McGrubben will not compromise on quality. Pratt has come across thick yeti hides and wants a stack of ten. Pratt McGrubben will not compromise on leatherwork: only the finest will do. While hunting for fine materials, Pratt came across thick yeti hides. The yetis are native to Feralas, with many around Feral Scar Vale, just inland of the Forgotten Coast.

The Mark of Quality. In Camp Mojache, the leatherworker Jangdor Swiftstrider holds that quality should never be compromised. Jangdor has found thick yeti hides and wants a stack of ten. Jangdor Swiftstrider takes pride in leatherwork and says quality should never be compromised. Lately Jangdor has discovered thick yeti hides. Feralas is home to the yetis, and they are often found west of Camp Mojache in Feral Scar Vale, just inland of the Forgotten Coast.

The Master's Glaive. In southern Darkshore, Onu sends Alliance scouts to investigate the Master's Glaive. He fears the Twilight's Hammer cult may have reached the fallen ancient horror. Along Darkshore, Onu sees corruption linger and wildlife driven from its homes. The naga on the coast trouble him, but signs of the Twilight's Hammer are worse. Its followers worship primal lords who ruled the world before they were overthrown in ages past.

The Might of Kalimdor. Anachronos greets you as the one fate has been waiting a thousand years to bring forward, a champion to lead their people into a new age. This opens the end of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, and comes only after the Blue, Green and Red Scepter Shard forks are done. Anachronos speaks of a fate a thousand years in the making. The Old God is shaken by your coming and fears your faith, and Anachronos urges you to break the prophecy of C'Thun. You bring Kalimdor's strength with you. Whenever you are prepared, you need only tell Anachronos, who will place the Scepter of the Shifting Sands in your hands.

The Mills Overrun. In Tirisfal, the Scourge gather at Agamand Mills, close to Forsaken settlements. Deathguard Dillinger sends soldiers from Brill to break their ranks before the ruined mills become a base for attacks deeper into the glades. The Agamand Mills once anchored Tirisfal Glades' agriculture. Since the Third War, their windmills overlook Scourge forces massing on the grounds under the Lich King's thrall. These mindless undead threaten the fledgling Forsaken holdings. If they secure the mills, they will have a base from which to push deeper into Tirisfal and strike at those settlements.

The Mind's Eye. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a powerful gem known as the Mind's Eye, an artifact essential for rescuing young Yenniku. The stone rests in the hands of the formidable ogre spellcaster Mai'Zoth, who dwells deep within the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. Following the recovery of the singing crystals, Kin'weelay turns his attention toward securing the Mind's Eye. This potent artifact is the solitary instrument capable of aiding the rescue of Yenniku, the son of the Darkspear chieftain. However, the stone is currently held by Mai'Zoth, a ruthless ogre mage whose presence Kin'weelay remembers from the tribe's earlier days in the jungle.

The Mindless Ones. Newly risen Forsaken face the Mindless Ones on Deathknell's northern edge. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them to cull Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies, Scourge thralls bound to the Lich King's command. Many who rise from Lordaeron's dirt never recover their minds. The Forsaken broke free of Ner'zhul's domination as his power waned, but countless corpses remain chained to his will. In northern Deathknell, Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies wander, driven to violence. For you, newly risen among the undead, putting them down is the first hard trial. You prove your freedom by ending the thrall of those who never escaped.

The Missing Courier. Latronicus Moonspear in Feathermoon Stronghold says a courier and the parcels he carried went missing about a week ago. The stronghold's own searches found nothing, so the courier is declared missing in action, and you are sent to Ginro Hearthkindle, who is seeking help. Latronicus Moonspear has reached an impasse. A courier has been missing for about a week along with the parcels he was carrying, and the stronghold's own searches have been fruitless, so Latronicus has declared him missing in action. An associate, Ginro Hearthkindle, is looking for help with the matter and should be in Feathermoon Stronghold, perhaps in his quarters. Latronicus asks that you speak with Ginro, if you have time and means to spare.

The Missing Courier. Ginro Hearthkindle tells you the courier, Raschal, set out for Thalanaar about a week ago, planning to row down the coast. Ginro could not find the boat and asks you to look for it along the coast of Feralas, in case it holds a clue to where Raschal is. About a week ago Raschal set out for Thalanaar. Raschal knows Feralas well and has been with the expeditionary forces since General Feathermoon led them here. Ginro's understanding is that Raschal meant to go by row boat down the coast and cross southern Feralas, avoiding the Horde camp. Ginro could not find the boat, which may be hidden or sunk, and asks you to look for it along the coast of Feralas, since it might hold a clue to where Raschal is. On the mainland, the Forgotten Coast stretches south from the jetty.

The Missing Diplomat. In Stormwind, an urgent inquiry begins after a diplomat fails to reach Theramore Isle. Bishop DeLavey suspects Defias foul play and sends trusted operatives to Jorgen, a discreet contact in the Valley of Heroes. A high-ranking diplomat sailed from the Eastern Kingdoms to meet Lady Jaina Proudmoore in Theramore Isle for sensitive talks, but never arrived. Royal investigators search Stormwind for clues. The disappearance remains secret to prevent panic and keep conspirators from learning that the crown is watching.

The Missing Diplomat. Jorgen sends trusted operatives across Stormwind with a sealed note for Elling Trias. The delivery carries the search for the missing diplomat from the Valley of Heroes to Trias' Cheese in the Trade District. After the first inquiries into the diplomat's disappearance, Jorgen asks trusted operatives to keep silent and carry a sealed note across the city. It is meant for Trias' Cheese in Stormwind's Trade District, not a barracks or magistrate's office. The handoff avoids ordinary guard channels as concern over the missing diplomat reaches beyond the palace.

The Missing Diplomat. Elling Trias sends you south to seek news of the missing diplomat. Leads in Stormwind point toward Duskwood and Watcher Backus, a contact near Darkshire who may know of Defias activity. After a frustrating exchange with Jorgen, cheesemonger Elling Trias turns to his wider circle of informants. To save his own coin, he sends you to do the fieldwork instead of hiring agents. You carry a sealed missive across the border into Duskwood, where beasts and the undead make travel dangerous.

The Missing Diplomat. In Duskwood, the search for Stormwind's missing diplomat follows a lead from Watcher Backus to Defias papers at Addle's Stead. Watcher Backus of the Night Watch brings the search to Duskwood. He says an unusually large gathering of Defias bandits came to Addle's Stead several weeks ago. The bandits usually keep to themselves across the border in Westfall, so their gathering in the dark woods marks an unusual move. Now you search the abandoned farmstead for the papers they left behind.

The Missing Diplomat. You carry the recovered Defias Docket back to Stormwind as the search for a missing diplomat grows more dangerous. In Duskwood, Watcher Backus wants no part of the Defias Docket you recovered. Its papers describe plans too intricate to be simple banditry or a diversion. Afraid of royal punishment and wary of his Night Watch superiors, Backus asks you to keep his involvement quiet. The papers point to schemes dangerous enough to end careers or cost lives, so you carry them to Stormwind.

The Missing Diplomat. In Old Town, a lead in the missing diplomat's case points to a street fighter. Elling Trias sends you to find Dashel Stonefist and get answers about the suspicious papers. The investigation reaches Stormwind's rough streets. Elling Trias recalls a name tied to the coded notes and leads: Dashel Stonefist, known as Fist. He is a rough street fighter, far from the nobility around Cathedral Square. Stonefist keeps to Old Town's cramped alleys. Finding him draws the search out of Stormwind Keep's grand halls and into the city's criminal circles.

The Missing Diplomat. Dashel Stonefist has confessed in Old Town, and you carry his warning to Elling Trias. The thug names a backup abduction plot and a contact in Menethil Harbor. Dashel Stonefist gives up when he fears for his health. In an Old Town alley, he admits the conspirators' first kidnapping plan fell apart, leaving his part in the plot in ruins. To shift blame, he tells you of a secret meeting weeks ago at Addle's Stead in Duskwood. He also names one lead in their backup plan: an insider in Menethil Harbor known only as Slim.

The Missing Diplomat. A quiet request in Stormwind draws you to Bishop DeLavey in Stormwind Keep. The Church and crown need help with a matter too perilous for public channels. As you travel through Stormwind, Thomas, an altar boy, approaches with a quiet request. Bishop DeLavey, a respected cleric of the Church of the Holy Light, needs an outsider's help at Stormwind Keep. He calls the matter delicate and urgent. You must keep it discreet, lest the people panic.

The Missing Orders. Dispatch Commander Ruag bristles when asked about the missing orders, insisting they were relayed. Ruag says the soldiers carrying them were ambushed by murlocs and only one lived, and sends you to speak with Bengor. Ruag takes offence at the question and insists the orders were relayed. The soldiers sent with them were, Ruag says, ambushed and brutally beaten by murlocs, and only one lived, if that can be called living. The survivor can barely speak, cannot walk and is fed through a tube. To learn what became of the orders, Ruag says, speak with Bengor, who is around here somewhere, and adds a warning to mind what you poke your nose into, lest it get bitten off.

The Missing Shipment. In Ratchet, Gazlowe waits for goods sent from Booty Bay across the Great Sea. He sends couriers to Wharfmaster Dizzywig to check the dock records, while the Southsea Freebooters remain a possible cause of the delay. Ratchet is the Steamwheedle Cartel's trading port on Kalimdor. Ships cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay with manufactured goods, exotic supplies, and heavy freight for the town's building and trade. When cargo goes missing, business suffers. Chief Engineer Gazlowe keeps close track of every crate brought into port.

The Missing Shipment. At Ratchet’s docks, Dizzywig’s ledger points away from harbor graft and toward the Southsea Freebooters. Gazlowe receives the records and prepares to reclaim his lost cargo. Ratchet’s trade and its port bring constant logistical headaches. When a shipment fails to arrive, Gazlowe suspects bad harbor accounts or foul play on the piers. Wharfmaster Dizzywig examines the manifest and insists his books are clean. The intake records account for everything, so the missing merchandise never made it onto the dock.

The Monogrammed Sash. A fine sash bearing embroidered initials hints at a rightful owner somewhere in Stranglethorn Vale. Finding the seafarer who lost it leads on to The Captain's Cutlass. This fine sash bears the letters 'HS' embroidered along its hem. Whoever lost it can only be traced by those two letters.

The Morrow Stone. The moment you take the artifact from the Equinex Monolith, the power in the Stave of Equinex starts to fade. You are to bring the Sparkling Stone and the stave back to Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold. As the artifact leaves the monolith, the stave's energy starts to fade. Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold is eager to hear what you found, so bring both the Sparkling Stone and the stave to him.

The Moss-twined Heart. Near Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies a strange heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid. Dark, oily moss covers the core, yet it keeps beating after being cut from the timberling. Blackmoss the Fetid's heart still pulses after being cut from the timberling. Dark, oily moss hides nearly all of the timberling's core, but a slow rhythm continues within it. That pulse points to a corruption reaching beyond ordinary rot in Teldrassil's wild plants.

The New Horde. In the Valley of Trials, veteran warrior Eitrigg calls new recruits to the Den. He sends you to Gornek to begin training and shares why he returned to the Horde and what Thrall hopes it can become. Eitrigg stands in the Valley of Trials under Warchief Thrall's orders, ready to evaluate and mentor the Horde's newest hopefuls. After the Second War, he abandoned the Old Horde, disillusioned by its corruption by the Burning Legion. He lived in quiet exile until humans captured him. Thrall rescued Eitrigg, and the veteran chose to return after learning of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism and entirely free of demonic masters.
