text.enUS: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. The Star, the Hand and the Heart is an Undercity quest wherein Keeper Bel'dugur tests an aspiring leader seeking to establish a new chapter of their order. To earn the essential Yagyin's Digest, the petitioner must track down three items of power whose names Bel'dugur dares not speak aloud. Within the shadowed corridors of the Undercity, ambitious practitioners seeking to lead their own circle turn to Keeper Bel'dugur. To establish a new flock and open a chapter of their order, an aspiring leader requires Yagyin's Digest, an authoritative text of ritual lore guarded by the keeper. Bel'dugur stands ready to support his fellow brother, but demands proof of worthiness before yielding such authority.

name.esES: El estado de Villa del Lago

text.enUS: The State of Lakeshire. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon's report calls for help before the town falls. It urges General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind to send royal army reinforcements against the crisis in Redridge. Magistrate Solomon writes of the attacks threatening Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls press the town, whose defenders cannot hold the borders indefinitely. Couriers carry his dispatch west along the road to Elwynn Forest. Solomon asks the Stormwind Army to intervene and protect the kingdom's eastern reach.

The State of the Mines. Alba Fairmoon finds toxic metals in Westfall's wells and fears for its farmland. She suspects the mines seized by the Defias and warns the soil could fail for decades. You head to Jangolode Mine and Gold Coast Quarry to disrupt the mining. Alba Fairmoon finds dangerous levels of toxic metals in Westfall's wells. Once Stormwind's main breadbasket, the region now faces a threat to its crops. Alba suspects the mines seized by the Defias Brotherhood are poisoning the water. If the contamination continues, the surrounding earth could lie barren for decades.

The Stave of Equinex. Troyas Moonbreeze thinks his stave may be the Stave of Equinex, a key to a monument in the Ruins of Ravenwind. To find out, you are to gather the essence of four flames that still burn among those ruins. After your return to Troyas Moonbreeze, he says his stave could be the Stave of Equinex, which is in fact a key to the Equinex Monolith. The monolith stands in the Ruins of Ravenwind. Among those ruins, four flames are still alight, named Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa. Each yields an essence, and standing by the monolith you are to use all four to energize the stave. If it truly is the Stave of Equinex, the monolith will open and give up a sacred artifact.

The Stockade Riots. At Stormwind's prison gates, Warden Thelwater sends you into the Stockade Riots to prove your loyalty to the city guards. The uprising has seized the prison, and he orders you to find and execute its ringleader, Bazil Thredd. Deep beneath the Mage Quarter's cobblestones, the Stockade has fallen into lawlessness. Criminals, Defias insurgents, and violent cutthroats have broken containment and seized the cell blocks, making the prison an impenetrable war zone. Warden Thelwater and his guards cling desperately to the entrance, unable to push inside and restore order by ordinary means.

The Stolen Journal. In Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard needs his stolen journal back. The Frostmane troll leader Grik'nir the Cold took it into the troll cave, and Grelin cannot finish his appraisal of the troll threat without his notes. Grelin Whitebeard has watched the Frostmane trolls press into Coldridge Valley and recorded their habits and sudden aggression. In the unrest, an imposing troll stole his personal journal and fled into the depths of the trolls' den. The loss matters beyond sentiment: the notebook holds most of Grelin's reconnaissance. Until it is recovered from the cavern, his assessment of the threat remains unfinished.

The Stolen Tome. In Northshire Valley, a novice human warlock is sent to recover a forbidden tome and prove their skill. Drusilla La Salle hopes to claim Powers of the Void from the Defias, whose camp lies in the vineyards. Warlocks in Stormwind's lands hide their craft and keep prying eyes from their research. Northshire Abbey guards forbidden grimoires in its archives. Drusilla La Salle, the warlock mentor on the abbey grounds, covets Powers of the Void but cannot risk suspicion from the clerics and paladins by entering the library's protected wing herself.

The Stone Circle. Marvon Rivetseeker once went into the Sunken Temple and only just got out. A round stone with a serpent symbol, now sitting in Marvon's workshop in Ratchet, might let Marvon tell you more, and you are asked to fetch it. Marvon Rivetseeker speaks of the evil in the Sunken Temple that seeps into everyone who walks its chambers. Escape was a struggle through the ooze now spread across the floors, and what remains is a memory of a big round room crowded with statues of serpents.

The Stone Watcher. You carried the platinum discs out to the Tanaris desert, and the Stone Watcher of Norgannon has appeared at the Uldum Pedestal. It guards entry to the Uldum compound and admits only those whose disc set includes the Plates of Uldum. You are to learn its story before going on. The Watcher's arrival is just the reaction that was hoped for when you were sent out to the desert of Tanaris carrying the platinum discs. It names itself a guardian of entry, and it will not let you into the Uldum compound unless the Plates of Uldum are already integrated with your disc set. Before going further you are to find out the story behind the Stone Watcher, and then use the Uldum Pedestal.

The Stone of the Tides. Following rumours of a haunted isle off the jungle coast, Baron Revilgaz suspects an ancient troll relic has resurfaced. He directs explorers to scout the mysterious landmass and delivers a pass to research the artifact within the archives of Stormwind. Having learned of strange apparitions and water elementals haunting an offshore island in Stranglethorn Vale, Baron Revilgaz sees an opportunity. Suspecting that the goblin mage Gazban may have uncovered the fabled Stone of the Tides, the ruler of Booty Bay sends you to locate the island and confirm whether the rumors are true. To satisfy any curiosity about the relic, he provides a library scrip redeemable among the scholars in Stormwind.

The Strange Hermit. The Strange Hermit is an introductory quest in Shadowgale Forest focusing on a shy, hooded recluse living away from civilization. Seeking conversation after long isolation, the hermit shares glimpses of his simple handcrafted life and his bond with the local singing forest spirits. Deep within the secluded canopy of Shadowgale Forest lives an enigmatic, hooded recluse known simply as the Strange Hermit. Far removed from settled towns and standard trade routes, he spends his days in quiet isolation among the trees. When approached, his awkward speech and nervous demeanor show how long he has lived without ordinary companionship, making even a basic greeting an unfamiliar challenge.

The Strength of Corruption. Talo Thornhoof, a hunter at Camp Mojache in Feralas, believes knowing an enemy well can turn a battle. Talo sends you to Felwood, north of Ashenvale, to face the fel-tainted bears and wolves and learn whether they have truly grown stronger. Talo Thornhoof is a hunter who strives to copy the strengths seen in opponents, and believes simply knowing an enemy well can turn a battle your way. Felwood lies north of Ashenvale, where a substance called fel has tainted the creatures. Talo thinks the bears and wolves there, driven mad by it, have also grown even stronger. Angerclaw grizzlies and Felpaw ravagers are the ones to face, twelve of each. Fel-touched things give off a strange green glow, which Talo senses is evil yet very powerful.

The Sunken Temple. Angelas Moonbreeze tells of the Sunken Temple, a place buried far underground, put there by powers greater than any Angelas has seen. To learn more, you are pointed to a goblin named Marvon Rivetseeker, last known to be in Tanaris. Angelas Moonbreeze speaks of a place sunk deep below the earth's surface, put there by forces mightier than any Angelas has seen: the Sunken Temple. For more, look for the goblin Marvon Rivetseeker, who, like Angelas and Troyas, has made a study of ancient sites across the world. Marvon left home in Ratchet to look into the troll ruins of Tanaris, and word of him has been missing for some time.

The Super Egg-O-Matic. Curgle Cranklehop's newest invention is an impressive piece of machinery, and it sputters wildly when you reach its control panel. Hippogryph eggs go into it. Curgle Cranklehop's newest invention makes an impressive sight. When you walk up to its control panel it sputters wildly. It is built to take a hippogryph egg, and the eggs are to be found in the mountains of southern Feralas, around the Ruins of Isildien.

The Super Snapper FX. Curgle Cranklehop has a new picture-taking device ready, the Super Snapper FX, and hands it to you to try out. The subject is Gammerita, a creature from the Hinterlands. With her snapshot in hand, you bring it and the device to Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village. This follows The Borrower. After The Borrower, Curgle Cranklehop presents you with the Super Snapper FX, a new invention of theirs. Using it is simple: aim at whatever you want pictured and press the button. Curgle gives it to you to try out.

The Swamp Talker. Bengor can barely speak, but he manages to tell what became of the orders. The dispatch commander gave them, and on the way to the Blasted Lands the group was ambushed by many murlocs. One of them, named Swamp Talker, took the orders from his hands. They must be recovered and brought to the Fallen Hero of the Horde. Bengor says the dispatch commander gave out the orders and that his group was on its way to the Blasted Lands when many murlocs ambushed them. One of the murlocs, named Swamp Talker, took the orders from his hands as a spear was thrust into his skull. Bengor manages a word about a cave to the east before passing out. The orders must be recovered and brought to the Fallen Hero of the Horde.

The Swarm Grows. Moktar Krin at Ironstone Camp says Belgrom wants the silithid pushed back into the depths they crawled out of. Moktar's own half-dead war party cannot do it, so Moktar asks you to take on the silithid at the dig site to the south. After The Swarm Grows (2), Moktar Krin says Belgrom considers the silithid a threat and wants them driven back into whatever depths they came from. Having already killed the dwarves the Explorers' League sent, Moktar now has a war party in no state to fight again, and cannot do it without help. The dig site lies to the south, and Moktar expects no more dwarves there. Searchers, hive drones and invaders are the silithid to be killed, and Moktar's party cannot leave until it is done.

The Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan, a relic called the Tear of the Moons has left Feegly the Exiled mad and obsessed. General Twinbraid has locked it away as a curse, but Feegly still demands its return. The dwarves found the Tear of the Moons while cutting into the southern Kalimdor hills for Bael Modan. It was their first major discovery, and its strange influence fell at once on Feegly, one of the expedition's workers.

The Temple of the Moon. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne calls for aid to a suffering ancient creature in Teldrassil. The Sisterhood of Elune needs help, and this is the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy. Sister Aquinne asks for help in the Temple Gardens. As a devoted servant of Elune, she speaks for her order: a venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to it alone.

The Test of Righteousness. In Ironforge, glad tidings bring Jordan Stilwell news of his wife. Duthorian Rall sends you from Westfall to tell the devout smith that Daphne survived the Defias attack. Duthorian Rall sends you from Cathedral Square with news for Jordan Stilwell. You have guarded Daphne Stilwell through a Defias ambush at her Westfall homestead, and she survived. Her husband left for Ironforge believing his family was in danger. Rall asks you to carry the news in person, so Jordan can know his wife is safe.

The Test of Righteousness. Jordan Stilwell offers a paladin a chance to earn a weapon forged for the Light. The Ironforge smith needs rare materials from distant lands, including his lost family hammer. Outside Ironforge's gates, Jordan Stilwell seeks a paladin worthy of the Light. He offers to forge a sacred weapon if you gather the materials his craft demands.

The Test of Righteousness. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, a paladin awaits the making of a mighty warhammer. You have gathered perilous components across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor for the smith. The hammer marks an apprentice’s passage into a recognized champion of the Light. Outside Ironforge’s gates, master smith Jordan Stilwell works at his forge. He admits to envying paladins who wander the land, yet takes pride in serving their cause with hammer and anvil. You bring him rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines. With them, Stilwell keeps his promise and forges a weapon worthy of a true defender.

The Testament of Rexxar. Rexxar says that slipping past the Black Flight's defenses calls for an illusion. He knows a master illusionist, Myranda the Hag, who lives in the Western Plaguelands, and sends you to her with a message. Rexxar asks what you know of illusions, since an illusion is how you will get around the Black Flight's defenses. He names someone who may assist you in such deception: Myranda the Hag, a master illusionist driven out by the Lordaeron alliance, living in the Western Plaguelands. Rexxar says she has lent his kind a hand before, whenever she found a cause worthy. You carry his message to her.

The Thandol Span. After a blast shatters the northern crossing, Rhag Garmason asks travelers to search for a missing dwarf scout. The Dark Iron clan has attacked Dun Modr, cutting off communication and stranding its defenders without reinforcements. Ol' Rustlocke may hold a clue to the sabotage. A blast has torn through the bridge between Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. Bronzebeard soldiers at the border were caught in the devastation when Dark Iron dwarves attacked Dun Modr. Their ranks are thinned, and their strongholds are under siege. The survivors, led by Longbraid the Grim, hold their ground against the attackers.

The Thandol Span. On the Thandol Span, a murder exposes a threat to Ironforge's northern road. Ebenezer Rustlocke has been killed, and Rhag Garmason finds that Kam Deepfury has hidden explosives to cut that route. A recovered document reveals what happened beneath the Thandol Span. Ebenezer Rustlocke was murdered in its substructure, and the papers expose a further act of sabotage. Kam Deepfury, the Dark Iron agitator who first destroyed part of the bridge, has not stopped. His network planted a second cache of heavy munitions just across the northern border in the Arathi Highlands, ready to finish the destruction.

The Theramore Docks. Two spies were sent to steal papers from a ship at Theramore, but were found out and had to cast the papers into the sea. Now Nazeer Bloodpike charges you with finding them. After you dealt with the Theramore spies, Nazeer Bloodpike has another matter for you. Two spies were sent to take papers from a ship by the Theramore docks. They got them, were discovered, and had to throw their haul into the sea. One of them got away but could not retrieve it, and came back to report the failure.

The Third Fleet. Outside the Deepwater Tavern, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks to drown his memories. He alone survived Kul Tiras's Third Fleet, burned off the Wetlands by red dragons enslaved by orcs during the Second War. First Mate Fitzsimmons spends his days outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, nursing a hangover and memories he cannot shake. He once served as an officer aboard the Wave Mistress, a ship-of-the-line that sailed under Kul Tiras's maritime banner. Now he trades those grim memories for dwarven mead. Anyone who buys him another drink can hear his account of one of the Second War's worst naval slaughters.

The Thirsty Goblin. Marin Noggenfogger in Gadgetzan is tormented by thirst. Rumor says the dew collectors of the cactus garden to the southwest store water in special glands, and Marin hopes one of those glands can become a drink that finally quenches it. Marin has heard of strange creatures called dew collectors, living southwest of Gadgetzan, that keep water in special glands. A laden gland, Marin reckons, could be the start of a drink to end the thirst for good. You are asked to find the cactus garden where they live and bring one back.

The Ties That Bind. The Ties That Bind is a quest in the Shadowgale Forest centering on a bitter betrayal within the druidic circle. Elegael Thornpaw discovers that a missing circle druid, Haalien, has joined the attacking cultists as a commander and orders his execution. The task reveals the painful personal cost of duty when family turns against their own kind. In the depths of Shadowgale Forest, druids encounter a vicious cultist presence sowing terror and bloodshed. For Elegael Thornpaw, the attack is compounded by a bitter discovery: the scent of a former circle druid named Haalien hangs over the slaughter. Having vanished months earlier, Haalien did not perish in the wilds, but instead threw his lot in with the invading cultists, taking command of their violent campaign against his former kin.

The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides young paladins through a solemn rite. Under Duthorian Rall's care in the Cathedral of Light, you face teachings on virtue, devotion, and the duties that come with the Holy Light. Duthorian Rall guides those who answer the paladin's calling in the Cathedral of Light. Early training teaches martial discipline and the order's rites, but advancement asks for a deeper commitment to the spirit. The trials ask you to look beyond battle and weigh the moral duties of a paladin. Stormwind faces dangers within its borders and beyond, and its people need defenders who understand that duty.

The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge places the Tome of Divinity in a dwarven paladin's hands. Its teachings begin trials meant to test devotion to the Light and readiness to defend Azeroth from dark forces such as the Scourge. Promising paladin initiates from across the eastern kingdoms come to Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries after mastering the martial and spiritual basics. Tiza Battleforge guides young dwarven paladins in the principles that set a champion of the Holy Light apart from an ordinary warrior. Taking up this calling means pledging a life to duty, self-sacrifice, and spiritual discipline.

The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall awaits paladins seeking trials of faith and courage in Stormwind. The Tome of Valor guides their first steps toward proving their devotion to the Church. The Tome of Valor teaches that valor must be forged through hardship. Its sacred text compares virtues to precious ores, valuable when found but needing refinement to endure. Through hard trials and true commitment, a paladin binds faith, compassion, and courage into a strength that can resist the evils threatening Azeroth.

The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall sends a paladin to protect Daphne Stilwell on Westfall's distant shore. With her husband away, Defias bandits threaten her homestead. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall tests aspiring paladins by asking them to defend the realm's people. After accepting the mantle of valor, you put those ideals to work where law and authority have failed.

The Tome of Valor. At Daphne Stilwell's farm in Westfall, a paladin faces a trial of valor. The Defias Brotherhood is pressing the homestead, and Daphne needs a defender at her side. Daphne Stilwell's homestead in Westfall lies in land contested by the Defias Brotherhood. While seeking the virtues recorded in the Tome of Valor, you are sent to defend her farm. The Defias have tried repeatedly to overrun the property and kill Daphne. After earlier clashes, another attack is expected. You must stand beside her house instead of retreating to safer ground.

The Tome of Valor. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, word returns that Daphne Stilwell is safe. After defending her Westfall homestead from bandits, an aspiring paladin reports to Duthorian Rall, completing the Church of the Holy Light's trials of valor. The Church's charge is to shield the innocent without thought for oneself. Daphne Stilwell's homestead in Westfall is safe after an initiate of the Church of the Holy Light defended it from bandits. Back at the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, the aspiring paladin reports her safety to Duthorian Rall. The defense shows the courage and conviction expected of one who stands between danger and the defenseless.

The Tome of Valor. Alliance paladins face a trial of courage and duty in the Tome of Valor. Mentors in Stormwind and Ironforge ask them to prove they will protect the innocent as well as fight with skill. Young paladins in Stormwind and Ironforge must prove their resolve. In the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries, instructors test whether each initiate can face terrible danger without faltering. The trial measures more than armor or skill with a weapon. Paladins must also show they will stay beside those who cannot defend themselves, whether the threat comes from dragons or demons.

The Torch of Retribution. After The Flame's Casing, Kalaran Windblade asks you to wait while the pieces are joined and the torch is enchanted. The work is a channeling that must not be disturbed. With the pieces gathered, Kalaran needs a moment to join them and lay the needed enchantments on the torch. The work is a channeling that must not be interrupted, so you wait while Kalaran casts.

The Torch of Retribution. With the torch made, Kalaran Windblade says it now needs an owner to be bound to, and tells you to pick it up. Kalaran says the torch needs to be bound to its owner. To do that, you are told to take it up yourself.

The Totem of Infliction. In Darkshire, Madame Eva offers travelers a ward against Duskwood's dangers. She needs ghoul fangs, skeleton fingers, and spider venom to enchant the Totem of Infliction, a charm that strikes back at attackers. Madame Eva reads the fortunes of those who enter her candle-lit home in Darkshire. She senses danger and violence ahead, then offers practical sorcery alongside her divinations. To make a ward against Duskwood's predators, she needs ten ghoul fangs, ten skeleton fingers, and five vials of spider venom gathered from the haunted woods.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Delgren's crusade against the Tower of Althalaxx cultists reaches its sixth chapter. From Maestra's Post, he deciphers orcish writings recovered from the cult's emissaries and learns that Athrikus Narassin hid two trapped Highborne soulgems in satyr strongholds deep in Ashenvale. Champions head to Night Run and Satyrnaar to shatter the vessels, free the tormented spirits, and weaken Athrikus's power. Delgren the Purifier puts his study of Orcish to use after Ilkrud Magthrull, an orcish courier, is cut down. His peers in the Holy Light often scoffed at learning an adversary's tongue, but Delgren's practical insight lets him decipher notes recovered from the cult's emissaries. They reveal that Athrikus Narassin hid two potent soulgems containing ancient Highborne essences far to the northeast, in the defiled groves of Night Run and Satyrnaar.

The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, demonic rites threaten northern Darkshore. Balthule Shadowstrike directs an Alliance assault on Athrikus Narassin, the ancient sorcerer who commands the cult from the tower’s peak. In northern Darkshore, the ruined Tower of Althalaxx shelters demonic summoning. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the tower from nearby and sees that the threat must be faced now. Athrikus Narassin dwells at the summit, an ancient night elf warlock who directs the dark rituals beneath the shattered roof.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Delgren sends you north to meet Balthule Shadowstrike before the assault on Athrikus Narassin. The scout has watched the Tower of Althalaxx and can report what has changed there. Delgren the Purifier sends you north to speak with Balthule Shadowstrike, his sentinel partner. You have purified corrupted relics and weakened the cult's hold along Darkshore's border. Before you confront the sorcerer Athrikus, Delgren wants fresh intelligence from Balthule, who has kept watch from the ruins overlooking the tower.

The Tower of Althalaxx. North of Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze fears trouble at an ancient ruin. She sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the Tower of Althalaxx, but he has missed his report. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze watches for danger around Auberdine. Suspicious activity near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore drew her notice, so she sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the ancient ruin. Days have passed without word from him. Elissa asks you to travel north, find Balthule, and make sure he has not met an untimely end.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Warlocks gather at the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, drawing the scout Balthule Shadowstrike’s attention. He asks travelers to recover parchment scraps from the fanatics camped outside the ruins, hoping to learn who they are and what they seek. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the misty shore of northern Darkshore, keeping sight of the ancient Tower of Althalaxx. Auberdine sent him to monitor the ruin and warn Delgren the Purifier if danger grew. But leaving his post to report might mean missing the dark spellcasters moving among the stones. So Balthule asks passing travelers to scout the camps around the tower.

The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Dark Strand cultists are gathering, and Balthule Shadowstrike needs help. He sends an Alliance courier to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale with a warning for his mentor, Delgren the Purifier. Balthule Shadowstrike sees that the Dark Strand threat is too great for one scout to face alone. After clashing with cultists near the Tower of Althalaxx, he writes a report and entrusts it to an Alliance messenger bound for his master, Delgren the Purifier. The cult's summoners are growing bolder, and Balthule needs seasoned leaders to direct a response.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Reports from the Tower of Althalaxx lead south into Ashenvale, where the Cult of the Dark Strand also threatens the woods. Delgren the Purifier at Maestra's Post sends you to the ruins of Ordil'Aran to recover a Glowing Soul Gem. After the trouble around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, reports lead south to Delgren the Purifier at Maestra's Post. The Cult of the Dark Strand is pressing into the ancient elven woods, and Delgren has fought them for a long time. Their reach crosses both territories, so he seeks to strike at the source of their sorcery.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Delgren the Purifier sends you south from Darkshore into Ashenvale to hunt Ilkrud Magthrull. The orc warlock resides at Fire Scar Shrine, where you are to slay him and recover his tome. Delgren the Purifier traces the dark cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx to Ilkrud Magthrull, an orc warlock. Ilkrud works from Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, and Delgren fears his magic could spread through the elven woodlands. He sends you to kill the warlock and take his tome, hoping its contents will reveal his master's designs.

The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, the Cult of the Dark Strand's hold has been broken. Word of the victory travels south to Delgren the Purifier in Ashenvale, closing the campaign against the cult in Darkshore. For weeks, the Tower of Althalaxx was a festering wound in northern Darkshore, held by the fanatical Cult of the Dark Strand and its shadowy masters. Tracking, gathered intelligence, and violent skirmishes dismantled the cult's operations. Its sorcerers are slain and its dark rituals broken, ending the immediate danger of demonic infiltration in Darkshore.

The Treaty of Understanding. The Treaty of Understanding is an ancient dwarven tablet detailing the historic peace agreement between the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans following the War of the Three Hammers. Recovered from subterranean depths and brought before King Magni Bronzebeard, the artifact preserves a pivotal moment in dwarven history while highlighting the bitter rift that left the Dark Iron clan excluded from the peace. Recovered from deep within an ancient vault, the Treaty of Understanding is a historic stone tablet documenting the formal cessation of hostilities between dwarven clans. Dating to the turbulent aftermath of the War of the Three Hammers, it represents the moment peace was forged between the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans after the Bronzebeards secured control of Ironforge mountain.

The Trogg Threat. At Loch Modan’s Southern Gate, Captain Rugelfuss faces a growing trogg threat with too few defenders. The Ironforge Reserve has been called away to support Alliance battlefronts, leaving the remaining garrison stretched thin. Rugelfuss asks travelers to thin the troggs in the hills and bring back their stone teeth. Captain Rugelfuss guards Loch Modan’s southern approach with only a small garrison. The dwarven mountaineers and Ironforge Reserve have been sent to reinforce Alliance battlefronts, leaving the Southern Gate guard tower short of troops. Rugelfuss is under strict orders to hold the gate, so he cannot lead an attack into the highlands. Nearby settlers and travelers remain exposed to ambushes.

The Troll Cave. In Coldridge Valley, young Frostmane trolls gather in caves along the southern ridge. Grelin Whitebeard sends willing recruits to thin their numbers while Ironforge faces a trogg invasion. Grelin Whitebeard watches the frozen valley from a bluff as Ironforge's soldiers fight troggs across the snowfields. The southern approaches still need watching. Grelin and his brother Senir came at the mountain authorities' command to learn whether the native ice trolls threatened the heartland. Grelin keeps watch alone and tracks their movements.

The Troll Witchdoctor. Nazeer Bloodpike means to learn what happened around Marg Nighteye's death, and says only the witch-magic of trolls can tell. You carry Marg's head to Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. After the severed head turned up, Nazeer Bloodpike insists the events around Marg's death must be known, and that only troll witch-magic can reveal them. Marg's head is to go to Kin'weelay in Stranglethorn Vale, at Grom'gol Base Camp. Among the Darkspear trolls no witchdoctor is mightier than Kin'weelay, and Nazeer reckons that Kin'weelay, if anyone, can reach Marg's spirit.

name.frFR: Le camp du Marteau du crépuscule

text.enUS: The Twilight Camp. Cultists gather around the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, and Alliance scouts seek to learn why. A scrying bowl has shown their ritual site; now you enter the excavation to discover what the Twilight's Hammer seeks beneath the earth. The Twilight's Hammer has made the Master's Glaive an active threat. After a scrying bowl reveals the cultists' fortifications, you enter their camp to learn their designs before the Alliance can prepare its defenses.

The Unsent Letter. In the Deadmines, The Unsent Letter waits to be carried to Stormwind. Its delivery reveals the grievances and shared history binding Edwin VanCleef to the city's master builders. Edwin VanCleef falls aboard his juggernaut beneath Moonbrook, leaving behind more than a broken rebellion. A newly penned, sealed letter is tucked into his clothing. He addressed it not to a criminal lieutenant or financier, but to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect.

The Venture Co.. Investigating a ravaged Venture Company caravan in Mulgore uncovers an aggressive buildup of Venture Company goblins digging into the eastern hills. Having had their formal requests for mining permits flatly rejected, the company chose to quarry the Earth Mother's soil anyway, prompting Morin Cloudstalker to commission a lethal response. The tauren of Mulgore revere the land as an extension of the Earth Mother, cherishing its pristine plains and balanced wildlife. When the Venture Company approached the tribes seeking rights to blast and excavate the rolling hills for raw ore, their petitions were categorically denied. Undeterred by tribal decrees or territorial sovereignty, the relentless cartel sneaked heavy machinery, laborers, and overseers directly into Mulgore's eastern ridges to mine illicitly.

The Videre Elixir. Gregan Brewspewer will make you a Videre Elixir, but only once an Evoroot is brought. Gregan also claims a great many things are known to him about herbs and alchemy. Gregan Brewspewer can make you a Videre Elixir as soon as an Evoroot is put in hand. Meanwhile Gregan boasts of knowing a great many things about herbs and alchemy, and begins a story about turning the cheese meant for lunch into gold, only to ask where you are going when you walk off. Gregan is the one to ask about where an Evoroot can be found.

The Vile Reef. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a piece of an ancient stone tablet resting deep beneath the Savage Coast. The sunken city, known as the Vile Reef, is infested with aggressive murlocs and holds the legendary history of Gri'lek, which the Darkspear tribe wishes to preserve in Orgrimmar. Northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp, an ancient troll city slipped beneath the waters along the Savage Coast when a violent earthquake shattered the land long ago. Now referred to as the Vile Reef, its flooded ruins crawl with hostile murlocs that assault anyone venturing near. Resting on the sea floor among the ruins is a massive stone tablet carved with the story of Gri'lek, a legendary troll hero whose memory remains sacred to the Darkspear.

The Warrior's Path. The Warrior's Path is an introductory martial quest offered to budding fighters on Zephras Isle. Following instructions delivered through Rorian the Dayseeker, young warriors are directed to Blademaster Ren in the Thendal Village watchtower. Ren stands ready to offer combat instruction and discipline to those prepared to shield their people. Upon returning to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Village after restoring balance nearby, aspiring fighters receive word that the settlement's blademaster has taken notice of them. Rorian delivers a crumpled note penned by Ren herself, asking the novice to seek her out directly. Elevated above the settlement within the village watchtower, Ren keeps an observant eye over both the island's borders and the recruits who may one day defend them.

The Warsong Reports. Kadrak sends couriers from the northern Barrens to gather reports across Ashenvale. The Warsong Reports carry orders and field observations from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs the pass because the Barrens cannot supply the timber Orgrimmar requires. The Warsong clan has pushed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help keep them in step, while night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails.

The Way of the Hunter. The Way of the Hunter is an introductory training quest for fledgling hunters in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After proving their mettle against the local vuldren threat, young trackers are directed by Rorian the Dayseeker to present themselves to Tai'ree Farsight to begin their formal tutelage. Upon returning from thinning the disruptive vuldren prowling the outskirts of Thendal Grove, young hunters find that their practical skills have caught local attention. Rorian the Dayseeker passes along a scribbled summons from Tai'ree Farsight, the grove's resident hunter trainer. For novice rangers setting out into the wider wilds of Zephras Isle, this marked the shift from simple island defense to true martial and survival instruction.

The Weaver. In Silverpine Forest, Ataeric works to awaken a dormant ley energy node for Dalaran. Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher sends you to stop the archmage and take his staff, keeping Dalaran’s magic from threatening Forsaken control of the southern reaches of Lordaeron. After earlier inquiries into Ambermill and Dalaran’s movements, the Forsaken learned that the wizards are trying to awaken a dormant ley energy node in Silverpine Forest. If Dalaran gains its concentrated arcane power, it could strengthen its position and threaten the Undercity’s hold over southern Lordaeron.

The Western Watch. The Western Watch is an urgent mission to recall Peacekeeper Vaaniel and the garrison from an isolated southwest outpost under siege by cultists. Recognizing that holding the fortification is not worth the lives it demands, local leadership seeks to pull defenders back to safeguard the main settlement. The western watchtower stands southwest of the settlement as an outpost guarding the frontier. Facing renewed pressure from hostile cultists, local leaders judged the isolated structure too costly to defend. Rather than sacrifice more lives trying to maintain an exposed position, orders were drafted to recall the peacekeepers and concentrate all available military forces on shielding the village and its citizens.

The Windshapers. "The Windshapers" is a quest in which Illaya Amberwind introduces the player to the Windshapers and their spiritual mission. Tasked with reconnecting with the wind spirits, the order strives to protect Zephras and ensure the survival of the Shen'dorei amidst threats within Skywall. The Windshapers are an order dedicated to communing with the wind spirits and protecting the Shen'dorei. Welcoming those with innate spiritual perception, they seek to bridge the growing rift between their people and the elemental forces that sustain their aerial realm. Illaya Amberwind guides new recruits into understanding the heavy burdens the order carries.

The Windwatcher. Warriors who have mastered the berserker stance are sent north to find The Windwatcher. After the Affray on Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod points them toward a weapon worthy of their fury. You have survived the Affray on Fray Island and learned the berserker stance from Klannoc Macleod. Now Klannoc sends you far from the Barrens coast, across continents, to find a solitary craftsman who can forge an exceptional weapon.

The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm hears troubling whispers from the forest spirits. He asks you to find Tarindrella, an elusive dryad whose unexpected return hints at trouble beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Melithar Staghelm receives troubling omens from the woodland spirits while training novices beneath Aldrassil’s boughs. Tarindrella, a dryad regarded as a protector of the wild, has returned to Shadowglen after many years away from Kalimdor’s woodlands. Dryads rarely appear without cause, and Melithar fears the natural order is out of balance.

The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella seeks the cause of the forest’s sudden unrest and the furbolgs’ disappearance. Grells have turned aggressive, and Fel Moss points to dark magic in Teldrassil’s boughs. Shadowglen’s quiet woods have grown hostile. The furbolgs have left their ancestral dens and gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Feral grells and grellkin now overrun the woodland paths, and Tarindrella has noticed the dark change spreading through Teldrassil.

The Woodpaw Gnolls. After Quintis's vision, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you to search the camps of the Woodpaw gnolls in southern Feralas for evidence of the courier or the courier's belongings. Ginro doubts the gnolls were Raschal's undoing, but they are the best place to start. Ginro Hearthkindle allows that the Woodpaw, whom Ginro puts in quotation marks as friends, may have done for Raschal in the end, though something tells Ginro otherwise. Still, they are the best place to start. Ginro has no clearer plan than searching their camps, and knows gnolls keep what they scavenge and fight over it, so they may have come across the backpacks Quintis mentioned. In past searches Ginro steered clear of open fighting, but with the vision to go on now says to rip into them. The camps lie in southern Feralas.

The Wounds of Betrayal. The Wounds of Betrayal is a quest in Shadowgale Forest centering on the aftermath of a tragic assault against the rare shen'dorei druids. Players are sent by Elegael to deliver urgent poultices to her wounded brethren in Nightfang Den and search for her missing mate, Jorel Windsinger. The mission quickly exposes the bitter costs of betrayal and fuels a vengeful conflict against the Al'Aketh. The Wounds of Betrayal begins with Elegael, a shen'dorei druid tending to the aftermath of a catastrophic assault in Shadowgale Forest. Having hastily prepared medicinal poultices, she urgently seeks an adventurer to deliver aid to her brethren taking shelter in the nearby Nightfang Den, just north across the clearing. The shen'dorei druids are exceedingly few in number, making the survival of every single member vital to their fragile enclave.

The Writhing Deep. Among the backpacks lies a hurried note signed by Raschal of Feathermoon. He writes of bug-like creatures he came across, and of his decision to look into them himself. Your search for him now leads there. The backpacks hold a parcel meant for Thalanaar, and a note scribbled in a hurry to no one in particular. Its author, Raschal of Feathermoon, describes insidious bug-like creatures he discovered in the Writhing Deep, south of the gnoll camps. He felt he had to see them with his own eyes, for they seemed a grave danger to all of Feralas. The note shows where he went.

The Zhevra. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde warriors after the zhevra. Their hunt tests the skills needed to face the Barrens' more dangerous beasts. After the plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after tougher prey. Zhevras run in herds across the northern and southern Barrens. They are not the savanna's fiercest beasts, but they are swift and stubborn, and their kicks can break bone.

The Zoram Strand. Naga now threaten Ashenvale from the Zoram Strand. Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar sends Alliance champions to scour the northwestern coast, where an ancient ruined city lies. Stopping the naga protects the forest from a haunting echo of the night elves’ distant past. At Ashenvale’s northwestern edge, the Zoram Strand meets the Veiled Sea. Its shore lies northwest of Astranaar, where the forest canopy gives way to the coast. The beach was quiet for ages, its stones left from a civilization shattered ten millennia ago. Now Wrathtail naga have come out of the dark tides in force. They have made a hostile beachhead on the borders of night elven territory, and threaten to press inland.

Theldurin the Lost. Theldurin the Lost is a reclusive, half-mad dwarf wandering the scorched expanses of the Badlands. Formerly aligned with the insidious Twilight's Hammer cult, he fled their ranks with stolen sacred relics after realizing the horror of their designs. Perched in the barren hills of the Badlands, clutching bags of explosives in wild paranoia, Theldurin is far more than a simple mad hermit. He was once an initiate of the Twilight's Hammer cult. When the sinister cabal sought to awaken a primordial elemental power trapped beneath the earth, Theldurin recoiled in terror, rejected their mad teachings, and fled into the desert. He carried with him the Scroll of Myzrael, desperate to prevent his former masters from unleashing an ancient horror upon the world. Though the escape cost him his sanity, his defiance dealt a serious blow to the cult's plans.

Theldurin the Lost. A member of the Twilight's Hammer asks you to find Theldurin the Lost, who was once of their order, lost his mind, and fled with the scroll of Myzrael. Rumor places him in the Badlands. Theldurin once belonged to the Twilight's Hammer, until his mind slipped and he turned his back on the order's teachings. As he fled, he took the scroll of Myzrael with him. Those he left behind could not catch him.

Thelgen Rock. In the southern mountain wall of the Wetlands, Thelgen Rock’s caverns hold volatile Incendicite Ore. Venomous spiders infest the passages. Thelgen Rock cuts deep into the mountains between the Wetlands and Loch Modan. Aggressive spiders fill its web-choked passages, and their venom makes every step dangerous. Miners and adventurers still brave the tunnels for the valuable Incendicite Ore embedded in the rock.

Thelsamar. Thelsamar keeps watch over the western bluffs above Loch Modan's great lake. The town lies on the road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands, offering shelter and trade while troggs and ogres press in nearby. Thelsamar gathers dwarven life in the valley beneath stout stone and timber roofs. Travelers find the Stoutlager Inn, a gryphon roost, crafting stations, and supply merchants. The town sits on the road from the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh to the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands, so travelers crossing the region pass through its doors.

Thelsamar Blood Sausages. In Thelsamar, Vidra Hearthstove keeps the town fed with blood sausages, a favorite across Loch Modan. She needs fresh ingredients from the valley to make them. Hungry children and miners returning from the Ironband Excavation fill Thelsamar's tavern. Vidra Hearthstove tends the stove and makes the blood sausages known across Loch Modan. The recipe draws on wildlife from the rugged mountain pass.

Theocritus. At the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn, Theocritus watches over the kingdom and opposes Morganth. The eccentric human archmage lives apart from others, surrounded by servants and magical scrying devices. Archmage Theocritus keeps his own stronghold in the kingdom of Stormwind. He lives in the Tower of Azora, near the eastern road to Redridge. Eccentric in his habits, he enjoys a comfortable life with a large household staff, including gnomish attendants and his clothier, Morley Eberlein. He keeps apart from the everyday concerns of local villagers, yet his magic guards eastern Elwynn.

Theocritus' Retrieval. In Redridge, an adventurer finds a gnoll pendant and hears a voice through it. The voice belongs to Theocritus, High Mage of Tower of Azora, who has intercepted the gnolls' mystical network and urgently asks for the pendant to study. Across the Redridge Mountains, travelers fighting the savage Shadowhide gnolls sometimes find a Shadowhide Pendant. Touching the enchanted trinket brings a calm, distant voice instead of barking or curses. The speaker is Theocritus, a human mage at Tower of Azora, across the border in Elwynn Forest. His message comes from long research into breaking the dark sorceries that direct the gnoll packs.

Theramore Isle. Theramore Isle is a heavily fortified human port citadel off the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Founded by Lady Jaina Proudmoore for refugees escaping the fall of Lordaeron, it stands as the Alliance's primary bastion in southern Kalimdor. Following the devastation of Dalaran and Lordaeron by the Scourge during the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore guided a fleet of survivors across the Great Sea to the shores of Kalimdor. After fighting alongside orcs and night elves to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal, her coalition of humans, dwarves, and high elves retreated to the misty fringes of Dustwallow Marsh. On a jagged island just off the coast, they built Theramore Isle—a thriving harbor city anchored by towering stone ramparts and Jaina's personal citadel, created to safeguard what remained of the northern kingdoms.

Theramore Medal. At Northwatch Hold, Theramore Medal marks service among the marines and officers defending the outpost along the Merchant Coast. The insignia bears Theramore’s mark and identifies the Alliance garrison. Marines, marksmen, commandos, and officers serving from Northwatch Hold carry stamped medals bearing Theramore’s mark. The soldiers are loyal to Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s realm. For the human troops on the cliffs above the Barrens, the medals show that their service is legitimate and their authority comes from Theramore. Others see the tokens as trophies from an overzealous foreign garrison, one that treats every vessel approaching the coast as a mortal threat.

Theramore Spies. The truce between Horde and Alliance is an uneasy one, with skirmishes and covert deeds on both sides. Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village wants the Alliance infiltrators east of the village hunted down and slain. Alliance infiltrators have settled in east of Brackenwall Village, watching it and sending word of Horde movements to Theramore. Nazeer Bloodpike, the local spymaster, will not stand for it. You are sent to find the infiltrators and kill them, so that their superiors know such spies are unwelcome.

Therylune. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Therylune waits for a chance to escape her captors. Twilight's Hammer cultists have trapped the dryad at the ancient site, and she needs a traveler's help to reach safety. Therylune is a dryad, a daughter of Cenarius who guards nature. She came from the tranquil woodlands of northern Kalimdor to the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. Twilight's Hammer cultists have gathered at the ancient excavation and ambushed her. Surrounded by their swarms, she cannot fight her way free alone. She needs an escort through the cultists and out to safety.

Therylune's Escape. Therylune is cornered by cultists at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. She wandered into its dig sites, and you are needed to guide her to safety and tell her worried sister, Therysil, at the Shrine of Aessina that she survived. At the Master's Glaive, Therylune is pinned down by Twilight's Hammer cultists. The ravine is dominated by the skull of an ancient monstrosity, pierced by a huge stone blade. Therylune wandered into the heart of the valley despite the dread surrounding it. She survives by reacting quickly and hiding among the rough terrain.

Therysil. At the Shrine of Aessina in central Ashenvale, Therysil waits for word of her sister. The dryad is devoted to protecting nature, but Therylune has been taken by the Twilight's Hammer cultists. Therysil keeps watch near the waters of the Shrine of Aessina in Ashenvale's ancient woods. As a dryad and daughter of Cenarius, she is bound to defend the wild and its spirits. Her thoughts now turn to Therylune, captured nearby by the deranged Twilight's Hammer cult. Therysil waits anxiously for a wandering ally who can help rescue her sister.

Therzok. In Orgrimmar, Therzok waits for a promising rogue from Durotar. Kaplak has seen your skill with violence and stealth and sends you to the Cleft of Shadow to meet a Shattered Hand operative. Kaplak draws promising young rogues aside when they begin making a name for themselves in Durotar. The new Horde honors Thrall, but not all its servants fight openly beneath his banner. Word of a fighter skilled in violence and stealth, willing to bend the rules of open warfare, reaches the underground guild in Orgrimmar.

name.deDE: Sie nennen ihn den lächelnden Jim

text.enUS: They Call Him Smiling Jim. Guard Byron feels sorry for a man called Smiling Jim and hints that he was not always the way he is now. Byron would rather not talk about it, and sends you to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore. Byron pities Jim and says it was not always like this for him: Jim once kept an inn in the marsh, and a wonderful one. Byron prefers not to go into it. Anyone who truly wants the story is told to take it up with Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore.

Thick Bear Fur. In Dun Morogh, Thick Bear Fur keeps travelers and soldiers warm against the mountain cold. The pelts come from bears roaming the snowfields and help make insulated clothing and bedding. Bears roam Dun Morogh's ridges through some of the harshest snowfields in the Eastern Kingdoms. Their thick coats protect them from blizzards, and locals and travelers put those pelts to use. Hunters gather them to line clothing, insulate drafty outposts, and pad cold sleeping rolls.

Third War. The Third War was the apocalyptic conflict that shattered the old world order just a few years ago. Orchestrated by the Burning Legion and unleashed through the Lich King's Plague of Undeath, the war saw the fall of the Kingdom of Lordaeron and the near-total destruction of Quel'Thalas before culminating in a desperate, unified stand at Mount Hyjal. The war began subtly in northern Lordaeron, disguised as a virulent sickness carried in infected grain distributed from Andorhal. The tainted harvest did not merely slaughter its victims; it raised them as ravenous ghouls bound to the Lich King's will. Prince Arthas Menethil raced to stem the contagion alongside the Kirin Tor sorceress Jaina Proudmoore. Blinded by grief, fury, and dreadlord manipulations, Arthas purged the infected population of Stratholme before pursuing his foe to the frozen waste of Northrend. There, he took up the cursed runeblade Frostmourne, casting aside his soul. He returned south only to murder his father, King Terenas, delivering Lordaeron into the hands of the Scourge.

This Fruit Could Bite Back. This Fruit Could Bite Back is a foraging quest focused on collecting wild prickly pears in the arid lands near Orgrimmar. The fruits are prepared into food while their seeds are saved for future planting, with the aim of cultivating a resilient desert crop to nourish the Horde capital. Durotar is a rugged, sun-baked landscape where traditional farming is nearly impossible. To support the burgeoning capital of Orgrimmar, resourceful inhabitants turn to native desert flora. The prickly pear, a hardy cactus fruit equipped with protective spines, thrives in the arid soil and provides much-needed nourishment when gathered with care.

text.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard. Lotwil Veriatus, busy with a set of shackles, sends you to speak with Lucien Tosselwrench in the Badlands. Lotwil needs a cog #5 and wants it brought back. Lotwil glances up at you briefly, then bends over the shackles again. You are to go and speak to Lucien Tosselwrench, because Lotwil needs a cog #5 and asks you to bring it.

text.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard. Lucien Tosselwrench hands you cog #5 for Lotwil Veriatus, and heads for cover, inviting you to come along. Lucien hands over the cog and says to take it to Lotwil Veriatus. Lucien will be waiting behind cover, and you are welcome to join. When you reach Lotwil, who is still bent over the shackles, a hand is held out and fingers waggle impatiently for the cog.
