text.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard. Lotwil Veriatus declares the shackles finished and calls on Lucien, Servo and you to bear witness as a powerful elemental is summoned. Lotwil cries out that the shackles are done and the time has come, calling Lucien and Servo to bear witness along with you. Lotwil presents the shackles as alchemy, engineering and the arcane in perfect combination, and means to summon a powerful elemental on what is declared a groundbreaking day for everyone there.

Thistlefur Hold. Corruption has turned the furbolgs of Thistlefur Hold against every outsider who draws near. Their cavern den lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. Thistlefur Hold lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village, at the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. Corruption has driven its furbolgs mad, and they attack travelers and neighbors who draw near. In the winding caverns, the tribe hoards scavenged relics, including troll charms sought by the Darkspear. Captives are kept in wooden cages deep within, among them Ruul Snowhoof, a tauren brave.

Thistlefur Village. Thistlefur furbolgs attack outsiders from their village north of Astranaar. The tribe has fallen to corruption and now threatens travelers who approach its dens. North of Astranaar, Thistlefur Village lies among Ashenvale’s woodland communities. Corruption has taken hold of the Thistlefur tribe, leaving its furbolgs maddened and hostile. They guard the paths through their settlement and attack travelers who draw near. Two fierce chieftains, Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl, lead the clan. Their aggression threatens those on the roads and in nearby settlements.

Thistlefuzz Arcanery. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery draws enchanters and scholars. Gnome practitioners run this prominent workshop and academy, a haven for those who weave magic into metal and parchment. Its chambers hum with arcane energy beside the fires of dwarven industry. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery contrasts with the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Across its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to study enchanting and the arcane arts. Dwarves reshape steel with muscle and fire; the gnomes here show how raw arcane energy can be bound into weapons, armor, and curious tools. For spellcasters making their way through the mountain stronghold, the Arcanery remains an essential sanctuary.

Thistlenettle's Badge. Foreman Thistlenettle's badge is all that remains after the collapse in the Deadmines. Before the Defias Brotherhood sealed Moonbrook and the tunnels beneath it, dwarven prospectors from Ironforge's Explorers' League worked the old gold mines of Westfall. Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew were deep underground when a tunnel collapsed and split them apart. His brother Wilder escaped to Stormwind City, but the foreman and several laborers were left trapped below.

Thistleshrub Valley. Tran'rek in Gadgetzan wants to get into Thistleshrub Valley, but the strange beasts there keep them away. Clear some of the thistleshrubs out, and Tran'rek might think about going back. Thistleshrub Valley lies south-west of Gadgetzan, and Tran'rek calls it a mighty dangerous place. They do not trust the strange beasts there, gnarled thistleshrubs and thistleshrub rootshapers, and with so many around they will not go back.

Thistleshrub Valley. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Tanaris, Thistleshrub Valley is a bizarre oasis of prickly plant life amidst endless dunes. The canyon is known for its strange grove of giant cacti and hostile animated thistleshrubs that attack anything stepping through their thorn-choked territory. While most of Tanaris is an arid wasteland stripped bare of vegetation, Thistleshrub Valley is curiously choked with life. Giant blooming cacti tower over the canyon floor, providing a sharp contrast to the surrounding sea of sand. However, this is no peaceful sanctuary. The valley takes its name from the hostile, living plant creatures that lurk among the brush. These thistleshrubs lash out with razor-sharp spines at any traveler who wanders near, making navigation hazardous for those trying to push past the cliffs toward the mysterious southern gates.

Thondroril River. The Thondroril River is a vital natural boundary separating the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. Originating in the mountains of Northern Lordaeron near the Terrorweb Tunnel, its blighted waters flow southward into Darrowmere Lake. Once a vibrant trade and travel waterway of the fallen kingdom, it is now flanked by monstrous Scourge beasts and the humble refuge of a legendary hermit. Before the fall of Lordaeron, the Thondroril served as an important waterway connecting northern holdings toward Stratholme and south to Darrowmere Lake. Today, the river marks the hazardous divide between the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. The waters carry the taint of the plague, and its banks are infested with giant maggots, plaguebats, diseased bears, and predatory snapjaws, turning what was once a scenic riverbed into a deadly crossing for travelers.

Thor. At Sentinel Hill, Thor keeps Westfall linked to Stormwind by gryphon flight. His trained mounts carry travelers and urgent messages above the dangerous roads. Thor tends the gryphon roost at Sentinel Hill, linking Westfall's defenders with the rest of the kingdom. The People's Militia faces bandits, gnolls, and malfunctioning harvest golems on the ground. Thor's gryphons carry travelers and military dispatches above the perilous roads. Reports from Gryan Stoutmantle and urgent requests for aid can reach the court in Stormwind far faster than a ground messenger.

Thoradin's Wall. Thoradin's Wall is a monumental, crumbling stone rampart dividing the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commissioned millennia ago by King Thoradin during the dawn of the Empire of Arathor, it was built to shield early humanity from the fierce incursions of the Amani trolls. Erected nearly three thousand years ago, Thoradin's Wall marks the western frontier of ancient Strom, the heart of the first unified human empire. King Thoradin recognized that humanity's fledgeling settlements were acutely vulnerable to the predatory raids of the Amani forest trolls. By raising this vast stone barrier across the valley corridor, Arathor secured its heartland and forged a defensible bastion from which humanity could survive and eventually contest troll supremacy in the north.

Thorgas Grimson. Inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Thorgas Grimson trains new hunters. A seasoned outdoorsman of Dun Morogh, he believes the frozen wilds teach survival best. Thorgas Grimson welcomes new mountaineers and scouts inside Anvilmar. He teaches young hunters to leave dry lectures behind and learn in the freezing winds. With bow or gun in hand, they track Dun Morogh's rugged beasts firsthand.

Thorgrum Borrelson. Above Thelsamar, Thorgrum Borrelson tends the gryphons that carry travelers across Loch Modan. His roost links the valley with Ironforge and the mountain passes nearby. Thorgrum Borrelson keeps the gryphon roost on the bluff above Thelsamar. His trained gryphons carry the Alliance across Loch Modan, where troggs and gnoll packs threaten the roads. They fly through South Gate Pass to the Great Forge in Dun Morogh, and onward toward the Wetlands and beyond.

Thorium Point. Perched upon the northern bluffs of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point serves as the primary staging camp for the Thorium Brotherhood. From this neutral outpost, these rogue Dark Iron dwarves recruit passing adventurers and strike back against their tyrannical kin deeper within the volcanic wastes. Overlooking the scorched slag heaps of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point is a modest mountain encampment built out of necessity. It is held by the Thorium Brotherhood, a renegade faction of Dark Iron dwarves who have severed ties with their enslaved brethren in Shadowforge City. Unwilling to bow to the Firelord or Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, these outcasts maintain an open-air forge, a busy flight master, and a well-guarded perimeter northeast of Firewatch Ridge. Because of their desperate struggle for survival and master-level smithing aspirations, the Brotherhood keeps the camp open to both the Alliance and the Horde, welcoming anyone willing to dig ores out of the ash or bash Dark Iron skulls.

Thork. At the Crossroads, Thork keeps watch over the settlement’s defenses. He sends Horde adventurers against raiders and works to keep supply routes open. Thork commands the defenses at the Crossroads, where roads link Durotar, Mulgore, and lands beyond. The town faces threats from every side. Quilboar raids, centaur attacks, and harpies on the prowl stretch his forces thin. Thork calls on capable travelers to meet dangers his guards cannot handle alone.

Thorn Hill. Razormane warbands strike Horde supply lines from Thorn Hill, east of the Crossroads. The fortified quilboar camp holds the high ridges between Durotar and the Barrens interior. Thorn Hill overlooks the roads between Durotar and the Crossroads. The Razormane gather here with hunters, trained wolves, and geomancers who shape the earth. Elder Mystic Razorsnout guides the quilboar as their attacks on Horde supply caravans grow bolder. The camp sits close to vital routes, making it one of the Crossroads guards' most immediate threats in the central savanna.

Thorvald Deepforge. At the Valley of Kings, Thorvald Deepforge arms travelers bound for Loch Modan. He helps defend the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Thorvald Deepforge supplies weapons at the Valley of Kings. Troggs and roaming wildlife threaten the mountain passes between Khaz Modan's interior and its outlying lands. Travelers from Dun Morogh and those heading deeper into Loch Modan can find blades and axes here to defend dwarven lands.

Those Blasted Troggs!. Foreman Stonebrow watches troggs wreck Gol'Bolar Quarry and calls for help. They have broken his equipment and powder barrels, and his fading aim keeps him from fighting them himself. He sends willing fighters into the pit to thin the Rockjaw Skullthumpers. Troggs have overrun the lower terraces of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. The dwarven excavation once produced well, until the creatures broke through the bedrock and flooded its tunnels. Now they smash the scaffolding and blast apart barrels of powder, leaving the quarry in ruin.

Thotar. In Razor Hill, Thotar teaches young Horde hunters the ways of tracking and taming beasts. He trains orcs and trolls who have left the Valley of Trials to face Durotar’s wildlife. In Razor Hill, Thotar trains Horde hunters for the wilderness of Durotar. New recruits learn the basics in the Valley of Trials, then come to him as they face more dangerous predators. He teaches marksmanship and the respect needed to live alongside and direct Kalimdor’s deadliest creatures, drawing on traditions passed down through generations of orcs.

Thrall. Thrall now rules from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar, Warchief of the Horde and ruler of Durotar. Once a human slave raised as an arena fighter, he freed his people, restored their shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to a new homeland. Thrall was born Go'el, son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka. Gul'dan's assassins murdered his parents when he was an infant, and human commander Aedelas Blackmoore found him and named him Thrall, meaning slave. At Durnholde Keep, Blackmoore raised him as an arena fighter and taught him human tactics. With help from his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped. The Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar guided him away from demonic corruption and taught him to master the elemental spirits. Thrall became the first orcish shaman of a new generation.

Thran Khorman. At Anvilmar, Thran Khorman trains new warriors for the dangers of Coldridge Valley. Thran Khorman drills dwarven recruits and visiting gnomes on the grounds of Anvilmar. Gruff and demanding, he has little patience for anyone who lacks the grit for front-line fighting. Though the Third War has ended, troggs press into Coldridge Pass, and danger still fills the mountains. Thran insists on relentless practice with axe, mace, and shield so Ironforge’s defenders stay ready.

Threat From the Sea. After Lack of Surplus, Tok'Kar begins work on your weapon and tells you to speak with Katar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Katar has said patrols along the beach could use some help. While working on your weapon, Tok'Kar suggests you talk to Katar, who has said patrols along the beach could use some help. Tok'Kar shares the camp with some louses who drink, and would rather see you keep your wits sharp and your weapons ready than join them.

Threat From the Sea. After Tok'Kar sends you to speak with Katar, Katar makes plain a hatred of the sea. Watching the fish men die at the hands of anyone who does the Horde's will gives Katar some pleasure, and Katar asks how many you can slay and whether you would test yourself against their strongest kind. Katar bears no affection for the sea or for any creature that comes out of it, and calls it a mistress strong but blind, callous and brutal. Killing the fish men by the hundreds would delight Katar, were it possible, and watching them fall to those who serve the Horde gives a little satisfaction. Katar, in the Swamp of Sorrows, asks you to slay marsh murlocs, marsh inkspewers and marsh flesheaters.

Threat From the Sea. After your work for Katar, you are told to see Tok'Kar once more before you rest. Katar believes Tok'Kar finished a few weapons while you were away, and that one will be offered to you for your help. Katar believes Tok'Kar finished a few weapons while you were away, and that Tok'Kar will offer you one for your help. Katar adds that you would do well to try its strength on the fish men when ready, though only to please Katar further.

Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a Horde quest centered on investigating a violent ambush along the eastern shores of Durotar. After scout Heglan Shadeeye is ambushed at her post in a fierce skirmish, adventurers must inspect the devastated area for clues regarding the attackers. Uncovering physical evidence reveals an encroaching threat that directly endangers Razor Hill's defensive lines. A violent skirmish along the Durotar coast leaves behind shattered earth and immediate cause for alarm among the Horde's defenders. Heglan Shadeeye, a Shattered Hand scout keeping watch from her post, was ambushed by an unseen adversary. The skirmish site clearly demonstrates that Heglan fought back fiercely and injured her attackers. With hostile forces moving unchecked along the eastern shoreline, Horde adventurers are called upon to survey the devastated campsite, comb the surrounding ground for clues, and determine what manner of enemy struck the scout.

Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a defensive mission to purge aggressive naga scouts who are setting up camp nearby. By striking the scout forces and taking their spinefins, adventurers aim to drive the serpentine invaders back north and safeguard the area. Threat from Below addresses a mounting border disturbance caused by encroaching naga scouts. The serpentine raiders have begun setting up advance camps nearby, prompting local defenders to strike before the intruders can secure a permanent foothold. Adventurers are dispatched to cull the scout forces and return with naga spinefins as proof that the encampment has been crushed.

Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a Horde bounty tasking adventurers with hunting down a dangerous sea giant prowling Durotar's north coast. Overcoming such an enormous coastal titan protects the nearby shores and earns the respect of the warriors of Durotar. Along the northern coastline of Durotar, the waters of the Great Sea wash against jagged sands and rocky shores. While typically frequented by simple scavengers and crabs, the northern coast harbors a far deadlier menace: a hulking sea giant roaming the shallows, threatening anyone attempting to travel or secure the waters bordering the Horde's arid new homeland.

Three Corners. At Three Corners, roads meet at the western edge of the Redridge Mountains. The routes link Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, while Stormwind guards watch for gnolls threatening travelers and supply wagons. At Three Corners, three roads link the southern settlements of Stormwind. Goldshire lies west in Elwynn Forest, Lakeshire northeast in Redridge, and Darkshire south in Duskwood. Stormwind built Tower Watch at the junction, where guards and scouts try to keep the roads clear. Gnolls from Redridge threaten travelers and supply wagons moving between the regions.

Thresher Eye. Along Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle wants Thresher Eyes for his Buzzboxes. He uses them to repair Buzzbox 411 on the beach north of Auberdine. Darkshore Threshers hunt the surf and outer shallows off Darkshore. They threaten local fishermen and travelers, and their large eyes have caught the interest of Wizbang Cranktoggle. The gnome engineer is stationed nearby and fond of crawler wine. He needs the eyes to repair Buzzbox 411, a far-speaking communication machine on the beach north of Auberdine.

Thule Ravenclaw. A courier brings strange Rot Hide ichor to Bethor Iceshard, who recognizes the work of his traitorous former colleague, Thule Ravenclaw. To help the Forsaken resist the gnolls, Bethor prepares a scroll of counter-incantations for Apothecary Renferrel. At the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Bethor Iceshard recognizes the arcane mark in a courier’s sample of Rot Hide ichor. Thule Ravenclaw made the distillation. Before the Third War, Thule was a bright young mage and Bethor’s colleague. When the Lich King rose to power, Thule betrayed his peers and swore himself to the Scourge. As Lordaeron fell, he abandoned his humanity.

Thule's Head. At the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec demands proof that Thule Ravenclaw is dead. His severed head confirms the commander of the Scourge forces on Fenris Isle has fallen and helps the Forsaken hold Silverpine Forest.

Thun'grim Firegaze. Atop Thorn Hill, Thun'grim Firegaze keeps to a reclusive life and a solitary forge. After their first lessons in defense, Horde warriors cross the Barrens to find him and seek steel fit for their growing skill. After you show skill in the defensive arts under veteran trainers like Uzzek, you are sent to sharpen your fighting with suitable steel. Ordinary armories can carry a frontline fighter only so far. True mastery calls for a personal weapon from a smith of renown. In the Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze is that smith, an aging orc who has left settlement life behind to keep an isolated forge high above the plains.

Thunder Axe Fortress. Thunder Axe Fortress is a fortified compound in northwestern Desolace serving as a stronghold for the demonic Burning Blade cult. Within its stone barracks, watchtowers, and darkened caves, cultists perform dark rituals to summon demonic entities and store stolen artifacts of power. The cult remains an active threat to anyone traversing the desolate wastes. Perched in northwestern Desolace, Thunder Axe Fortress serves as a heavily guarded redoubt for the Burning Blade. Composed of stone barracks, defensive watchtowers, and deep caverns, it allows the cult to maintain a fortified foothold far from the gaze of Kalimdor's major cities. Here, the cultists gather fel energies, summon lesser demons, and concoct schemes to bring far more dangerous entities into the world.

Thunder Bluff. On Mulgore’s high mesas, Thunder Bluff shelters the tauren as their capital. Cairne Bloodhoof founded the city after the Third War, bringing a people long scattered across Kalimdor together in a place of refuge and tradition. Thunder Bluff rises above Mulgore, where rope bridges link its stone mesas and wooden elevators carry travelers up from the plains. For generations, the tauren wandered across central Kalimdor, pursued by centaur raiding parties. During the Third War, Cairne Bloodhoof joined with Warchief Thrall and the New Horde. Together, they drove back the centaurs and claimed Mulgore’s fertile grasslands. Cairne gathered the scattered tribes and founded the city atop the mesas, where the heights offered shelter and a place for the tauren to trade and gather in worship.

Thunder Falls. Thunder Falls lies in Elwynn Forest’s northwestern heights, where bandits have taken a riverside cottage. Thunder Falls cuts through the ridges above Mirror Lake, where a mountain stream rushes between steep cliffs. It enters over an unreachable cascade in the north, then spills away in waterfalls on both sides. One fall empties into Mirror Lake; the stream’s downstream course runs west toward Westfall’s rugged border. A cottage, dock, and outdoor forge sit beside the water. Bandits now claim the clearing.

Thunder Lizard Blood. In the southern Barrens, hunters bring back Thunder Lizard Blood as proof of survival. The blood comes from the great beasts that roam the plains. Thunder lizards go by the names Stormsnouts, Stormhides, and Thunderheads across the plains. Their heavy steps shake the earth, and their crushing weight can flatten unwary hunters. Bringing back their blood shows the skill to hunt them and the endurance to survive beneath their thundering feet.

Thunder Lizard Horn. In the Barrens, Brewmaster Drohn seeks a Thunder Lizard Horn for Chen Stormstout's legendary brew. Thunder lizards roam the Barrens, their crested bodies crackling with lightning. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet values their horns as an ingredient for Stormstout ale. His mentor learned the recipe from the wandering pandaren Brewmaster Chen Stormstout and passed it down to Drohn. The horn gives the drink its potent kick.

Thunder Ridge. Thunder Ridge lies southwest of Orgrimmar, where thunder lizards roam a stripped canyon. Along the Southfury River in western Durotar, the former grove was ruined by human logging and dark sorcery. Agitated beasts and lingering cultists threaten nearby settlements. Thunder Ridge was once a green haven in arid Durotar, shaded by ancient trees. Shortly after the Third War, humans from Kul Tiras began felling its timber. The thunder lizards grew wild as their home was cut away. Then the Burning Blade used fel sorcery to destroy what remained of the canopy. Now the gorge lies barren and exposed, with angry, lightning-spewing beasts roaming through it.

Thunderaan. Prince Thunderaan is the ancient Prince of Air, a colossal elemental struck down and betrayed during the ancient wars between fire and wind. Consumed in part by Ragnaros the Firelord, his remnant essence was sealed into shattered bindings entrusted to the Firelord's lieutenants. Adventurers who recover these relics can seek out Highlord Demitrian in Silithus to unleash him once more. Long ago, during the Elemental Sundering—a five-thousand-year clash fought between the forces of fire and air deep within Azeroth—Ragnaros sought to destroy and consume Thunderaan. The Prince was ambushed and betrayed by Ragnaros's powerful lieutenants, Baron Geddon and Garr, before being struck down by the Firelord's hammer, Sulfuras. Although defeated, Thunderaan's essence proved too mighty for Ragnaros to fully absorb.

Thunderbrew. In Westfall, Grimbooze Thunderbrew is gathering what he needs for his next batch. Fresh hops keep his ale from turning thick as stew, and he shares kegs with those who help. Grimbooze Thunderbrew keeps his family's brewing tradition alive far from Dun Morogh. Even across Westfall's turbulent plains, he insists on the right ingredients: without proper hops, his current brew may turn into thick stew instead of refreshing ale.

Thunderbrew Distillery. Travelers find the Thunderbrew Distillery at the heart of Kharanos, where ale and shelter await. Its brewhouse and tavern draw mountain travelers, while mentors and tradesfolk offer their skills within. The Thunderbrew Distillery anchors Kharanos in southern Dun Morogh. Arkilus Thunderbrew founded the brewhouse, and his kin have kept it in the family. Across Khaz Modan, its strong ales are known for warming those who face the mountain cold. Innkeeper Belm manages the inn, where weary mountaineers find a fire, hearty food, and beds beyond the blizzards outside.

Thunderhawk Saliva Gland. Across the Barrens, greater thunderhawks yield a gland prized by Brewmaster Drohn. He needs it to recreate Chen Stormstout's fiery Trogg Ale. Greater thunderhawks hunt across the Barrens' arid savannas. These winged serpents are known for harnessing storms, and the older, more dangerous ones produce a saliva gland charged with natural potency. Travelers keep clear of the deadly beasts, but brewmasters value the gland as a rare base for exotic drinks.

Thunderhawk Wings. Across the central and southern Barrens, hunters claim Thunderhawk Wings from the wind serpents that soar overhead. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer receives them as proof of a hunter’s strength, cunning, and endurance. Hunters stationed at Camp Taurajo prize a pair of intact Thunderhawk Wings. Wind serpents, whom local hunters call thunderhawks, are fierce winged reptiles that strike swiftly from above. Tracking them across the open plains and claiming their wings in combat tests a hunter’s skill. For an initiate, bringing back the wings proves readiness to follow the lifelong path of an accomplished hunter.

Thunderhorn Cleansing. Thunderhorn Cleansing is an essential spiritual rite in Mulgore, charging travelers with purifying the corrupted Thunderhorn Water Well. Armed with a ritual totem prepared by Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers restore the contaminated spring vital to the local tribe. Successful purification earns the heartfelt approval of the Thunderhorn ancestors. Water wells across the sweeping plains of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren nomadic tribes who recently settled the grasslands. When foul poisons taint these underground springs, both wildlife and nearby settlements face devastating consequences. The Thunderhorn Water Well, situated north of Bloodhoof Village, fallen victim to contamination, requires deliberate spiritual intervention to heal the troubled land.

Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. Mull Thunderhorn prepares the Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem in Bloodhoof Village. Ancestral magic in the totem is meant to purify the Thunderhorn Water Well. Mull Thunderhorn entrusts a prepared totem to travelers in Bloodhoof Village. They carry it north to the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring, where foul agents have tainted the water. The ancestral wells dug by the tauren tribes nourish their herds and hunting grounds. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the water's disturbed spirits and cleanses the site.

Thunderhorn Totem. In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn asks young Horde champions to help make a sacred cleansing totem. Goblin pollution is spreading through Mulgore's water wells, and natural predator claws will bind the land's primal strength into ritual wood. Mull Thunderhorn needs natural claws to make a cleansing totem. The Venture Company is poisoning Mulgore's water sources through its industrial exploitation, and he works to craft a remedy. Prairie stalkers and flatland cougars roam east and west of Bloodhoof Village. Their claws carry the plains predators' natural essences, channeling their raw, uncorrupted predatory vigor directly into the totem.

Thunderhorn Water Well. At Thunderhorn Water Well, tauren and herds draw water in central Mulgore. The well lies along the path between Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff. The valley’s wells sustain life across the grasslands, and the tauren must keep them clean and defended. Thunderhorn Water Well draws from the aquifers beneath central Mulgore. Nomadic tauren and the valley’s settled villages depend on communal wells for water and sustenance. Water is precious across the plains, and control of the wells means control of the land. The Venture Company has repeatedly sought these sources for industrial use, threatening the balance the tribes work to preserve.

Thundris Windweaver. In Auberdine, reports of Blackwood aggression reach the village elder. Terenthis sends you to Thundris Windweaver with news of the furbolgs’ growing hostility. Thundris seeks the cause of the corruption spreading through Darkshore. After scouting corrupted furbolg camps in Darkshore, you carry Terenthis’s report to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Terenthis remains in the wilds to investigate the spreading corruption. As village elder, Thundris oversees the settlement’s daily welfare and considers the spiritual and environmental dangers facing the kaldorei. Your report gives Auberdine’s leadership evidence that the furbolgs are growing more than territorial: an unnatural malice is taking hold of them.

Thurman's Remains. At Agamand Mills, Thurman's remains bear witness to the family's failed stand against the Scourge. The once-wealthy mill owner fell to the Plague and now wanders his ruined estate as an undead thrall. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest landowners, with extensive mills and dozens of local workers. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, Thurman Agamand and his kin fortified their estate instead of fleeing. Certain their wealth and strong mills could withstand the attack, they persuaded their loyal workers to take up arms beside them. The defense failed. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered and made mindless servants of the Lich King. Coleman Farthing, a former worker who rose as Forsaken, now demands the destruction of his former masters. He seeks Thurman's remains as proof that the foolish patriarch paid for dooming his household.

Thurman's Sewing Kit. At Larson Clothiers, Thurman's Sewing Kit is needed for his tailoring work. The tools belong to young apprentice Thurman Schneider, who left them behind at his family's canal home to avoid a long day of stitching. Thurman's Sewing Kit holds the everyday tools of an apprentice tailor: needles, shears, and thread. Young Thurman Schneider studies tailoring at Larson Clothiers, deep in Stormwind's Mage Quarter near the Mage Tower. His mother, Rema Schneider, knows he cannot do his work without the kit, so she asks passersby along the Canals to carry it to the shop. When Thurman gets the tools, his reaction shows he left them behind on purpose, hoping to trade a day of stitching garments for leisure.

Thwarting Kolkar Aggression. Lar Prowltusk has found invasion plans in Kolkar Crag, west of Sen'jin Village. The Kolkar centaurs plan to strike Durotar's settlements and Orgrimmar. Lar Prowltusk, a troll tracker scouting western Durotar, slipped into Kolkar Crag under cover of night. There he found the Kolkar centaurs planning more than scattered coastal raids. Three centaur leaders had divided the invasion plans among them, with attacks aimed at the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the gates of Orgrimmar.

Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. At Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver searches for the vanished Priestess Velinde Starsong. She sends trusted Alliance adventurers after clues to Velinde's whereabouts and the mystery of the Scythe of Elune. On the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps watch as a night elf sentinel. Priestess Velinde Starsong vanished without a word, and Thyn'tel refuses to let her trail go cold. Believing grave forces may be involved, she sends trusted adventurers to search Velinde's belongings and learn where her journey led.

Tidefury Cove. Tidefury Cove is a treacherous stretch of water and rocky shallows along the southeastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. Renowned for its hazardous reefs and wrecked vessels, it serves as a secluded haven for roaming makrura and solitary anglers. Tucked away at the far end of Dustwallow Bay between Theramore Isle and the Wyrmbog, Tidefury Cove presents a notorious navigational hazard to passing sailors. Jagged reefs and shifting shoals have claimed multiple vessels over the years, leaving rotting wooden hulks half-submerged in the tideline. Today, the ruined ships are crawled over by opportunistic makrura, turning the cove into a dangerous, isolated stretch of coastline visited mostly by hardy scavengers or quiet hermits seeking distance from Theramore's busy docks.

Tidus Stair. At Tidus Stair, two tauren shamans seek insight from the coastal water spirits. Broad stone terraces rise above the Merchant Coast southeast of Ratchet, sheltered beside the Great Sea. Waves crash below the weathered stone terraces of Tidus Stair, cut into the coastal bluffs southeast of Ratchet. The Barrens around you are arid and dusty, and skirmishes trouble the region, but this stretch above the Merchant Coast is quiet. A modest hut stands on the terraces, home to the tauren Islen Waterseer and Mahren Skyseer. Far from the goblin trade docks, they spend their days fishing, watching the horizon, and seeking insight from the coastal water spirits.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. At the northern safari camp in Stranglethorn Vale, the hunter Ajeck Rouack offers to train adventurers in the discipline of big cat stalking. She starts newcomers against the younger tigers prowling near the camp to test basic hunting and tracking prowess. Having learned the art of hunting tigers from her father when she was a girl, Ajeck Rouack shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition following Welcome to the Jungle. She insists that tracking and slaying the youngest felines is the essential foundation before any hunter can advance to greater quarry.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack escalates his hunting trials. Having seen your early promise with young stalkers, he now sends you into the jungle to fell mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Following your initial success against younger predators, Ajeck Rouack seeks to test your growing skills against more seasoned beasts. She directs you back out into the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale to hunt down ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers before you can pursue even greater challenges.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. Deep in the jungle at Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack raises the stakes of his hunting trials. He demands the death of ten elder Stranglethorn tigers to prove your prowess before the final test. Following the earlier hunts, Ajeck Rouack asks you to pursue ten elder Stranglethorn tigers across the wilds. He considers these beasts both the most elusive to track and the fiercest to overcome. Felling ten of them serves as the prelude to a concluding trial, after which he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre
name.itIT: La maestria nella caccia alla tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. Ajeck Rouack offers the ultimate challenge in his series of hunts within northern Stranglethorn Vale. After weeks of tracking an elusive beast, he challenges you to seek out the tiger Sin'Dall and bring back her paw. Having completed the earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers, you are offered one last challenge by Ajeck Rouack at Nesingwary's Expedition. The hunting camp has tracked an extraordinarily elusive tiger known as Sin'Dall across the jungle for weeks. Ajeck challenges you to track her down, fell the beast, and claim her paw as indisputable proof.

Timberling Seed. Across Teldrassil, Timberling Seeds are gathered from plant spirits that have grown hostile. Naturalists and druids study them to learn why the forest's plant life has turned aggressive. Timberlings are nature elementals of Teldrassil, and their temper reflects the World Tree's balance. Lately they have grown hostile and angry, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists such as Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth suspect trouble in the soil. They gather seeds from wild timberlings, hoping that purified, carefully tended soil might let docile offspring sprout.

Timberling Seeds. At Lake Al'Ameth, botanist Denalan studies the growing hostility of Teldrassil's nature elementals. He seeks to harvest Timberling Seeds and test whether enriched soil can help them grow calmer. His work is one quiet effort by night elf herbalists to understand the subtle afflictions troubling the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to Teldrassil's boughs, closely bound to the health and vitality of the surrounding flora. They are usually peaceful reflections of the forest's balance, but their recent hostility has alarmed the local night elves, and no cause is known. Botanist Denalan hopes to learn what has stirred them rather than simply cull them.

Timberling Sprout. Along Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts take root already touched by corruption. Night elf wardens pull them before they grow into aggressive timberlings. Timberlings are plant spirits bound to Teldrassil's natural vitality. Along Lake Al'Ameth, the night elves find seedlings that sprout tainted and aggressive instead of healthy and in harmony with the wild. The young sprouts seem beyond cleansing or natural healing, so the caretakers gather and destroy them. They hope to stop hostile timberlings from spreading across the fragile boughs of the newly planted World Tree.

Timberling Sprouts. Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings. Corrupted sprouts are spreading along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly grow into aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting the sprouts helps protect the grove.

Timbermaw Hold. Timbermaw Hold is a fortified subterranean network of tunnels that links Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. It serves as the stronghold for the Timbermaw furbolgs, one of the last tribes to resist the demonic corruption plaguing northern Kalimdor. Carved deep into the mountain roots between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring, Timbermaw Hold stands as a desperately guarded bastion. While neighboring furbolg tribes fell to the foul taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War, the Timbermaw clan weathered the nightmare within these stone corridors. Though safe beneath the earth, they were forced to watch their beloved forests warp into corrupted mockeries. Extremely protective and deeply suspicious of outsiders, the furbolgs guard every tunnel entrance fiercely, expecting violence from anyone wandering in from the infected woods.

name.esES: Puesto de los Fauces de Madera

text.enUS: Timbermaw Post. Timbermaw Post is a small furbolg camp situated in the snowy expanse of Winterspring, nestled between Frostfire Hot Springs and Lake Kel'Theril. Despite bearing the name of the uncorrupted Timbermaw tribe, the encampment has fallen under the aggressive grip of the corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. Positioned just southeast across the road from Frostfire Hot Springs and west of the frozen Lake Kel'Theril, Timbermaw Post stands as a bitter reminder of the furbolgs' internal strife in Winterspring. Despite its Timbermaw name, travelers approaching the camp will find no friendly welcomes. The outpost is controlled by the hostile Winterfall tribe, driven mad and violent by demonic corruption. Now crowded with savage Winterfall furbolgs, the camp serves as an aggressive staging ground encroaching upon the central road.

Time to Strike. At the Hillsbrad border, Time to Strike carries Lesh's signal east to Tarren Mill. Her coded message moves word from a quiet watch to Forsaken plans against Hillsbrad's humans. Deathstalker Lesh watches the valley from high ground near the border of Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills. Below, human settlers and militia move through the valley. The Deathstalkers serve as the Undercity's eyes and ears, watching enemy settlements before troops deploy. Lesh stays at her post and asks passing Horde travelers to carry her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

Tinker Town. In Tinker Town, gnomes make a home in exile beneath Ironforge. After Gnomeregan fell, the district became the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque's government and the Ironforge terminus of the Deeprun Tram. Tinker Town shelters the gnomes who fled Gnomeregan. When troggs overran their high-tech city, Ironforge's dwarves opened their gates, setting aside a cavern that had housed dwarves and held the Deeprun Tram entrance. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council lead the refugees here. Around a massive spherical contraption, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization amid whirring gears, experimental alchemy, and gadgetry. Though cramped guests in a stone city, they remain determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland.

Tinkers' Court. In Gnomeregan's heart, Tinkers' Court once gathered the city's leaders. Now Mekgineer Thermaplugg holds it. Before disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan, its leaders met in Tinkers' Court. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque gathered there with advisors and master inventors, including Tinkmaster Overspark. They debated new technology, governed civic matters, and guided gnomish society. The chamber stood beyond the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay, at the center of gnomish government and invention.

Tinkmaster Overspark. In Stormwind, Brother Sarno hears that Tinkmaster Overspark is grieving in Ironforge over Techbot's malfunction. He sends Alliance adventurers to Tinker Town, where Overspark mourns the failure of his creation. His plea begins the effort to recover Techbot's memory core from Gnomeregan. Brother Sarno tends to travelers in Stormwind City and tells them of trouble among the gnomish refugees. Tinkmaster Overspark, one of the minds behind Gnomeregan's wonders, grieves over Techbot's corruption. The mechanical servant once helped the tinkerers faithfully, before the city fell into ruin.

Tiragarde Keep. Kul Tiran marines still hold Tiragarde Keep on Durotar's Scuttle Coast, south of Razor Hill. Built during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion, the ruined stronghold remains garrisoned under Lieutenant Benedict, a hostile thorn in the Horde's own territory. Tiragarde Keep gave Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet a beachhead on Durotar's red shores. He built it during his campaign to destroy Thrall's newly founded realm. The Horde eventually broke the siege and killed Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, but the keep was never fully abandoned. Resupply forces under Lieutenant Benedict reclaimed its shattered stone walls. They follow the late Admiral's standing orders to wage unyielding war against the orcs and reject the peace Lady Jaina Proudmoore forged.

Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the order Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded during the Second War, Tirion fought the Old Horde with plate, hammer, and holy devotion. He was revered as an unyielding paragon of the Holy Light.

Tirisfal Pumpkin. At Solliden Farmstead, living humans still tend pumpkins in blighted Tirisfal. The Forsaken take them for the Royal Apothecary Society’s mixtures. West of Brill, crops still grow despite the corruption spreading across Lordaeron. At Solliden Farmstead, living human farmers work the soil and grow large orange pumpkins under the watch of the nearby Scarlet Crusade. The harvest feeds these farmers. To the Forsaken of Brill, the pumpkins are targets for sabotage and raw materials for Apothecary Johaan.

Titan. The titans are a primordial race of colossal, godlike beings who wander the cosmos bringing order and shaping worlds. In ancient antiquity, they came to Azeroth to vanquish the chaotic Old Gods, establish massive terrestrial facilities, and foster life before departing into the Great Dark Beyond. The titans are cosmic giants forged from primordial matter and arcane magic, embodying the forces of order and creation. In their journeys across the Great Dark Beyond, they sought out slumbering worlds to cultivate, raising up continents, calming chaotic elemental forces, and designing life. To enforce balance, they established powerful constructs made of stone, iron, and sea to watch over their works.

Tiza Battleforge. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge guides young dwarven paladins in the Hall of Mysteries. She teaches that the Light calls for virtue, charity, and self-sacrifice, and tests initiates before they may wield its gift of resurrection. Tiza Battleforge guides paladins in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. Across the Alliance, tutors send initiates to her for deeper spiritual study. Brandur Ironhammer sends them from Ironforge, Azar Stronghammer from Dun Morogh, and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker from Stormwind. Tiza teaches that the Holy Light asks more than martial skill. Its servants must offer humble service, show compassion, and stand firm against the Scourge and other threats.

Tkashi Ruins. The Tkashi Ruins are ancient stone remnants situated southwest of Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Overrun by hostile Bloodscalp trolls, the site remains a stronghold of the tribe. Perched southwest of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting camp, the crumbling stone masonry of the Tkashi Ruins marks the ancient domain of Stranglethorn's jungle trolls. Today, the encampment is heavily occupied by the Bloodscalp tribe, who aggressively defend the territory and practice their shamanistic rituals among the vines and decayed stone. While Hemet Nesingwary noted passing through the ruins without trouble in his hunting memoirs, modern travelers find the trolls far less accommodating, guarding valuable tribal relics buried among the rubble.

To Darnassus. In Darnassus, your trial with the Great Cat Spirit brings you back to the Cenarion Enclave. After proving yourself to Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, you return to Mathrengyl Bearwalker to learn cat form. You return to Teldrassil after communing with the Great Cat Spirit under Dendrite Starblaze's guidance in Moonglade. Starblaze sees that you have proved yourself a worthy student and sends you to your primary instructor, Mathrengyl Bearwalker. He waits beneath the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus.

To Gadgetzan You Go!. In Orgrimmar, Zamja sends Horde cooks south to learn from an eccentric goblin butcher. Zamja trains cooks in the Drag, where she feeds warriors and travelers passing through Durotar. When a cook has learned every recipe and technique she can teach, Zamja admits she has imparted all her culinary mojo. She sends her seasoned pupil to Tanaris, saying only a master of strange and exotic meats can help a talented cook advance further.

name.esES: Ir a Forjaz a buscar el "Compendio" de Yagyin
name.frFR: Aller à Ironforge chercher le « Sommaire de Yagyin »

text.enUS: To Ironforge for Yagyin's Digest. Theldurin the Lost sends you to Ironforge with a sigil. In a shop in the Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip is to take you for one of the people Theldurin fled, and you are to ask Gerrig for Yagyin's Digest. The Tablet tells Theldurin much, but not nearly enough. Yagyin wrote a digest in ages past, and the people Theldurin fled keep copies in many places, with their most learned studying it. Theldurin believes it holds vast knowledge that can offer protection, and wants it brought back.

To Orgrimmar!. Kaplak sends a young rogue from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There, you are to find Shenthul in the Cleft of Shadow and enter the Shattered Hand's network. Kaplak sends you north from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Your budding skills have caught the notice of more prominent handlers, though they remain unpolished. The red crags of Durotar are behind you as you make for the capital.

To Thunder Bluff. After communion in Moonglade, a young tauren druid makes a triumphant return to Thunder Bluff. Having earned the Great Cat Spirit's favor, the initiate goes to Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise to master feline shapeshifting. You return to Mulgore after meeting Dendrite Starblaze and the Great Cat Spirit in Moonglade's sacred groves. The communion joins ancient night elven teachings with the tauren's earthen heritage, marking a pivotal milestone in a druid's training.

To Valanaar. "To Valanaar" is an island quest in which adventurers carry an urgent military report from Aonda in Shen'dar to Peacekeeper leader Valennia Stormfist. The message alerts the settlement at the southeastern edge of the island that an aggressive cult is expanding rapidly and that direct conflict can no longer be avoided. Following the defense of Shen'dar and its pylon, the highlander Aonda dispatches a trusted traveler to carry urgent word across the island to Valanaar. Situated at the southeastern edge of the land, Valanaar houses the headquarters of the island's peacekeepers under the command of Valennia Stormfist. The mission carries a vital warning: the peaceful days on the island are ending, and Valennia must prepare her people for an inevitable clash with an aggressive, expanding cult.

To the Top. Marli Wishrunner can send you up to see the sights from one of the twin colossals of Feralas, with a warning attached: the trip goes only one way. Marli Wishrunner asks whether you would like to see the view from the top of one of the twin colossals, and can send you there. Marli adds a word of caution: think about how you will get down, because this is a one-way trip.

text.enUS: To the Undercity for Yagyin's Digest. Theldurin the Lost sends you to the Undercity of Lordaeron with a sigil. Keeper Bel'dugur is to take you for one of the people Theldurin fled, and you are to ask the keeper for Yagyin's Digest. The tablet tells Theldurin much, but not nearly enough. Yagyin wrote a digest in ages past, and the people Theldurin fled keep copies in many places, with their most learned studying it. Theldurin believes it holds vast knowledge that can protect them, and wants it brought back.

Token of Thievery. In the Redridge Mountains, rogues face a test set by Lucius at Alther's Mill. A locked footlocker holds the Token of Thievery, proof of skill recovered during their training. In Lakeshire, Lucius tests promising rogues in the field. He hides the Token of Thievery in a locked footlocker among the ruins of Alther's Mill, where Blackrock orcs threaten the area. Recovering it tests whether an initiate can pick a lock under mortal danger. Success earns a Certificate of Thievery.

Tomb Weed. At Balnir Farmstead, Holland's altered doom weed now draws the Scourge. The crop has become a new specimen called tomb weed, and Holland wants it for his experiments. Junior Apothecary Holland wants more than a place among the Royal Apothecary Society. He gathers doom weed, makes small alchemical changes, and replants it in the soil of Balnir Farmstead. There, he has cultivated a new strain he calls tomb weed. Holland sees the hybrid as the heart of his work and a sign of the future he seeks for himself.

Tome of Divinity. In Dun Morogh, Azar Stronghammer calls young dwarven paladins away from their field duties and sends them to Ironforge. He directs each initiate to Tiza Battleforge in the Hall of Mysteries for guidance, beginning deeper trials in service to the Holy Light. Dwarven initiates begin by guarding Dun Morogh's snowbound villages and roads. When Azar Stronghammer sees that a defender is ready for deeper spiritual instruction, he sends the promising candidate from field duties to Ironforge. There, the initiate can seek guidance from the city's holy elders.

Tome of Divinity. A summons bearing the Tome of Divinity calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Answering Brother Wilhelm's call begins the sacred trials needed to master resurrection through the Holy Light. Novice paladins in Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows martial discipline and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. Leaders of the paladins take note of promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind and report straight to the kingdom's spiritual heart.

Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, young dwarven paladins begin a rite of passage beyond basic martial training. Brandur Ironhammer sends them upstairs in the Hall of Mysteries to seek Tiza Battleforge and take up the deeper duties and sacred vows of the Holy Light. Young paladins first defend Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls. When their martial discipline is proven, Brandur Ironhammer, their paladin trainer in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, sends them upstairs for guidance. Senior paladins there prepare initiates for the order's spiritual duties.

Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker sends dwarf paladins back to Ironforge. There, Tiza Battleforge guides them toward the sacred trials of the Tome of Divinity. Dwarf paladins often aid Stormwind and travel through human lands, but their spiritual and martial roots lie in Khaz Modan. When Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker judges that a dwarf has gained enough field training, he sends them to Ironforge. Their own people there guide the spiritual duties expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand.

Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Master Brandur Ironhammer sends human paladins south for deeper training. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Master Duthorian Rall oversees their study of the sacred Tomes of Divinity. Stormwind calls promising holy warriors south to the Cathedral of Light. Dwarven paladins train in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, while the Silver Hand's wider traditions remain tied to the Church of the Holy Light in human lands. The summons asks these initiates to stand before the Cathedral's senior priests and paladin mentors.

Tome of the Cabal. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan sends an aspiring Alliance warlock to the Library of Ironforge. A felhunter’s hunger can overwhelm an unprepared summoner, and the Tome of the Cabal holds the knowledge needed to summon and bind the demon. An imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus can be subdued through ritual, but a felhunter brings a different hazard. Felhunters serve the Burning Legion and hunt down arcane energy to devour it. A standard summoning circle will crumble before one, draining the summoner’s magic before a binding can take hold. From his redoubt in the Barrens, Strahad Farsan watches over Ratchet and knows an amateur must not attempt the binding unprepared.

Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan sends Horde warlocks east in search of a lost grimoire. The Tome of the Cabal holds rites for summoning and binding a felhunter, and the search begins with cartographer Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Strahad Farsan says a felhunter takes more than ordinary fel magic to summon. These predators feed on magical energies and resist standard summoning circles. An initiate needs specialized circles and an ancient grimoire called the Tome of the Cabal. The first order of warlocks to bind a felhunter without outside aid wrote the book. Its rites and seals show how to enslave such a dangerous demon.

Tome of the Cabal. Your search for the Tome of the Cabal leads from Ironforge to a lost manuscript and a sunken ship. Its scattered pages hold rites for binding a felhunter. Only one copy of the Tome of the Cabal was ever written, and violence left it in pieces. Its remnants were torn apart, defaced, and scattered to distant corners of the world. A tattered manuscript, ripped from the binding, crossed the sea to Kalimdor and fell into the hands of centaur clans. The other section was sent by sea from Lordaeron toward Khaz Modan, but its vessel sank before reaching port.

Tome of the Cabal. Horde warlocks seek the Tome of the Cabal's severed halves for Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Once kept in Lordaeron, the grimoire was torn apart and scattered across the world. Its damp, tattered remnants lie along hostile Eastern Kingdoms waters and deep in Kalimdor's centaur territory. The Tome of the Cabal once rested in the library of Lordaeron. Someone deliberately defaced the sinister grimoire, stripping away nearly half its pages and splitting it in two. The surviving formal text was bound for the dwarven halls of Ironforge, but the transport wrecked along the rocky coast west of Southshore. Its pages now rot in the shallows beneath the watch of scavenging murlocs.

Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan waits for a warlock to bring him the Tome of the Cabal and channeling rods. Together, they prepare the way to bind a felhunter. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Krom Stoutarm binds the Tome of the Cabal's tattered, mouldering remnants back together. The dwarf scholar reluctantly parts with this rare work of dark scholarship, but first secures a promise of a copy. He also passes along a fresh missive from Strahad Farsan. The tome holds the rites for breaching the Nether, though parchment alone cannot conduct the ritual.

Tome of the Cabal. A warlock's work with the Tome of the Cabal now leads into hostile territory. After helping Jorah Annison restore the tome, you must claim three Rods of Channeling and bring them to Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. In the Undercity, Jorah Annison studies the recovered fragments of the Tome of the Cabal. The Forsaken scholar pieces together its eldritch passages and welcomes the rare knowledge they offer. Then Jorah delivers an urgent directive from Strahad Farsan. Knowledge alone cannot bind a felhunter. A warlock needs precise instruments to focus demonic power into a binding circle.

Tome of the Cabal (quest item). Warlocks in Ratchet receive the Tome of the Cabal from Strahad Farsan after gathering dangerous components. Its pages hold the incantations for drawing a felhunter across the Twisting Nether and binding it. A felhunter is a vicious beast from the chaotic Twisting Nether, feared for devouring mana. Subduing one marks a passage for seasoned warlocks. The Tome of the Cabal holds the rites for opening a path to such a demon. Strahad Farsan, an experienced conjurer in Ratchet, gives the tome to an aspirant only after they gather the rare and dangerous components its magic requires.

Tommy Joe Stonefield. At the river west of Stonefield Farm, Tommy Joe Stonefield longs for Maybell Maclure. Their families have feuded for years, so he relies on secret notes and quiet banks to keep their love hidden. Tommy Joe Stonefield waits by the river west of Stonefield Farm, looking toward the Maclure homestead across the water. The Stonefields and Maclures have clashed for years over land, pride, and farmyard squabbles. Their elders keep the feud alive, but Tommy Joe has fallen in love with Maybell Maclure. The two cannot meet openly without angering both households. Gramma Stonefield, Tommy Joe’s sympathetic grandmother, helps them exchange secret notes and tokens of affection.

Tonga Runetotem. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem watches the Barrens' oases grow sick. Sent from Thunder Bluff, the tauren druid studies a corruption harming the region's wildlife and seeks its source before the fragile ecosystem fails. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies the Barrens' changing land. His elders in Thunder Bluff sent him from Mulgore, and he knows the dry savannah well. Where travelers see scrub and predators, Tonga watches for signs of the land's health. Lately, those signs have turned troubling. He seeks travelers who can help him investigate the scattered oases, the heart of life across the savannah.

Tooga's Quest. Tooga, a lost turtle, was sent out to fetch dinner by his wife Torta and took a wrong turn somewhere. Tooga asks you to lead him back to Torta, who waits just south of Steamwheedle Port. Tooga wanders near a crashed goblin zeppelin close to Thistleshrub Valley. Torta sent Tooga out to fetch dinner, and a wrong turn somewhere has left the turtle hopelessly lost. Tooga asks you to lead the way back.

Tools for Steelgrill. Tools for Steelgrill is an early Alliance delivery errand that introduces travelers leaving Kharanos to the nearby mechanic workshop at Steelgrill's Depot. Tharek Blackstone sends you up the road with a fresh crate of heavy equipment for Beldin Steelgrill, the master siege engine tech who works through spanners and ratchets faster than town suppliers can keep up. Beldin Steelgrill carries an undisputed reputation across Dun Morogh as the sharpest siege engine mechanic in the mountains, but his violent work ethic takes a heavy toll on his workshop. According to Tharek Blackstone in Kharanos, Steelgrill cracks arclight spanners and snaps tools almost as fast as local supply crates can arrive. When a fresh batch of durable gear is assembled in Kharanos, anyone heading northeast is quickly recruited to lug the heavy parcel out to the depot.

Tools of the Highborne. Thundris Windweaver sends help from Auberdine to the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Restless Highborne spirits still carry enchanted relics through the shattered settlement, and he wants them taken away. South of Auberdine and east of the coastal highway, Ameth'Aran's stone foundations lie overgrown. Ten thousand years ago, the settlement was a stronghold of the Highborne, the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire. Their unchecked use of arcane magic helped bring about the Sundering, which shattered Ameth'Aran. The inhabitants never truly left. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report that the Highborne ghosts still haunt the sunken plazas, clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they held in life.

Tools of the Trade. Horde rogues are sent from the Undercity to steal a report from Ambermill. Lord Varimathras orders them to obtain lockpicking tools and recover Kirin Tor intelligence on Dalaran’s condition. A prisoner’s interrogation points the Deathstalkers toward intelligence hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and human mages guard the village’s communications fiercely. Lord Varimathras orders Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad to direct promising operatives around the Kirin Tor sentries and recover the Dalaran Status Report.
