text.enUS: Top of Gelkak's Key. A giant foreststrider carries the Top of Gelkak's Key into the woods near Darkshore. It is one of three broken pieces of a mechanical key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome Gelkak Gyromast. Threshadons attacked Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore and sent it beneath the waves. The gnome washed ashore with the winding key for his mechanical first mate. The impact against the coastal rocks broke it into three pieces. Before the dizzy pirate could gather his wits, beasts scavenged the wreckage. A giant foreststrider carried the ornate upper piece into the woods.

Tor'kren Farm. At Tor'kren Farm in northwestern Durotar, Misha Tor'kren waits anxiously for news of her son Kron. He has not returned from a hunting trip. Tor'kren Farm struggles to raise pigs in Durotar's dry red dirt. The homestead lies southeast of Thunder Ridge, near the Southfury River. Feed and water are scarce, and the farm is isolated beneath nearby bluffs. Its yields are meager.

Torch of the Dormant Flame. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, a shaman prepares to kindle the Torch of the Dormant Flame. The unlit torch waits for a fire spirit's ember, earned on a mountaintop in Durotar. A shaman seeking fire's favor carries the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame up the peaks above Durotar. Fire sapta lets the shaman see a Minor Manifestation of Fire on the mountaintop and challenge it. When the spirit falls, its glowing ember goes into the weathered brazier at the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. The shaman touches the torch's head to the white-hot blaze, and the wood awakens as a burning emblem of elemental mastery.

Torek's Assault. From Ashenvale's wilds, Torek's Assault strikes Silverwing Outpost. Under orders from Splintertree Post, the orc raider Torek leads a brazen, bloody skirmish to crush Sentinel resistance and slay their commander, Duriel Moonfire, in the war for Ashenvale's borders. The Horde's lumber camps and the native night elves are locked in an escalating border war across Ashenvale. Torek gathers a pack of Splintertree raiders just outside Silverwing Outpost to break the Alliance's defensive perimeter. He leads a head-on charge before the night elves can counterattack or mount a reinforced campaign against Splintertree Post.

Tormus Deepforge. At Ironforge's Great Forge, Tormus Deepforge keeps weapons flowing to the Alliance. He coordinates iron deliveries and arms defenses across Khaz Modan and beyond. Tormus Deepforge oversees the Bronzebeard clan's metalwork beside the Great Forge fires. He still hammers steel himself, but he also mourns Sturgy Ironband, his mentor. Dark Iron dwarves overran Sturgy's smithing compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh after a load of strange umbral ore arrived there.

Torn Fin Eye. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Torn Fin Eyes draw the Royal Apothecary Society's attention. The Forsaken seek them for alchemical work on new plagues. The Royal Apothecary Society puts rare biological components to use in its work on the Forsaken's New Plague. Torn Fin Eyes come from murlocs along the Western Strand of Hillsbrad Foothills. Their organic properties help activate volatile alchemical compounds. Mixed with Daggerspine naga scales, restorative troll elixirs, and gnoll-derived sludge, the eyes help stabilize and trigger toxic mixtures meant to spread death through enemy lands.

Torn Murloc Fin. In eastern Elwynn, Torn Murloc Fins show the Stormwind Army's bounty is being answered. Taken from foragers and lurkers along the riverbanks, they show that local waterways are being systematically cleared. Murlocs have grown numerous along eastern Elwynn's streams and lakes, and the Stormwind Army offers a bounty to reduce their numbers. Guard Thomas, who watches the bridge over the eastern river, collects the severed fins as proof of kills. Stormwind's soldiers are stretched thin by unrest at home and threats nearby, so local authorities depend on travelers to bring proof that murloc camps have been cleared.

Torwa Pathfinder. Torwa Pathfinder is a lone tauren hunter and tracker camped at the entrance to Un'Goro Crater, just below the ramp descending from Tanaris. He observes the basin's primordial wildlife, studying the dangerous predators that rule the jungle floor. Adventurers seeking to test their mettle against the crater's legendary beasts often seek his guidance. Perched at the eastern base of the crater where the desert sands of Tanaris give way to humid jungle steam, Torwa Pathfinder serves as an informal warden for newcomers. He respects the wild forces of Un'Goro, understanding that careless wanderers quickly become fodder for the local fauna. His campsite provides a rare moment of respite before travelers dive into the sweltering depths.

Totem of Hawkwind. At Camp Narache, young tauren receive the Totem of Hawkwind before departing for Bloodhoof Village. They present it to Baine Bloodhoof as proof that they have completed their first trials and are ready to continue the Rites of the Earthmother. Chief Hawkwind carves the Totem of Hawkwind atop Red Cloud Mesa for youth coming of age. The token introduces its bearer and proves their passage. Tauren rarely use formal writ; meaningful symbols and familiar tribal craft carry a leader's intent. After a youth completes the first trials at Camp Narache, Hawkwind sends them onward with the totem, along the road into the wider lands of Mulgore. Its distinct carvings identify the bearer to Baine Bloodhoof and show they have the spirit and strength for the next trials, on the way to seeking the blessing of Thunder Bluff.

Tough Wolf Meat. Northshire and Coldridge wolves prowl their valleys, leaving raw Tough Wolf Meat for hungry locals. Coarse and stringy, it feeds people in Elwynn Forest and supplies dwarven outfitters in Dun Morogh. Wolves prowl near Northshire Valley and Dun Morogh, threatening nearby settlements and providing a hard-won source of food. Their meat is coarse, stringy, and chewy, but resource-strapped frontiersmen prize it. Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner hates the vicious beasts yet cooks their meat into steaks. He trades basic supplies and gear to those willing to cull the packs.

Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, the Tourmaline Phial gathers blessed moonwell water for Teldrassil's rituals. Corithras Moonrage gives the Tourmaline Phial to travelers for rituals that tend the World Tree. Druids in Dolanaar use gemstone vials to collect pure moonwell water across Teldrassil. This phial is meant for the moonwell beside the Pools of Arlithrien, southeast of the road to Darnassus, where hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs are growing more troublesome.

Tower of Althalaxx. Dark sorcery stirs within the Tower of Althalaxx on northern Darkshore's coast. Once Athrikus Narassin's retreat, the ancient Highborne spire now shelters demonic cultists and warlocks. Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne servants in Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran ten thousand years ago, placing the powerful sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in authority over them. As he grew distant from civic governance, Athrikus chose to isolate himself in the nearby Tower of Althalaxx. The Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, but the tower endured on Darkshore's desolate coastline, a quiet ruin of forgotten elven magic.

Tower of Arathor. The Tower of Arathor is a ruined wizard's tower situated in the former mage district in the southwestern reaches of Stromgarde Keep. Once the workshop of Archmage Trelane, it was overrun during the fall of the city and is currently occupied by Boulderfist ogres. Erected in the heart of Stromgarde Keep's mage district and named after the ancient Empire of Arathor, this spire long served the realm's sorcerers. Its most notable resident, Archmage Trelane, devised a magical defensive grid keyed to enchanted gemstones to protect the sanctum. However, when the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogre clan assaulted Stromgarde following the Third War, the kingdom fractured. Despite Trelane's desperate attempts to hold the tower using his arcane wards, the sheer brutish force of the ogres overwhelmed him. Forced to flee the city for his life, the archmage left behind his most prized arcane artifacts, leaving the spire in the hands of the Boulderfist brute Ruul Onestone and his followers.

Tower of Azora. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus leads a scholarly outpost in eastern Elwynn Forest. The slender spire stands north of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where its human master keeps watch over a silent magical feud with a hostile tower in the Redridge Mountains. The Tower of Azora stands beside the eastern road to the Redridge Mountains, staffed almost entirely by gnome spellcasters. Archmage Theocritus guides their studies of strange curiosities and teaches wandering spellweavers. A wild magical aura surrounds the spire and sometimes warps nearby wildlife. Within the tower, gnome servants contend with enchanted household items and mutated insects that creep past the doorway.

Tower of Eldara. The Tower of Eldara is an ancient, sealed night elven spire situated on the far northeastern promontory overlooking the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Though long abandoned, its sturdy stone architecture has survived the Sundering, standing silent above coasts roamed by aggressive coastal beasts. Perched on a remote cliff edge northeast of the Bay of Storms, the Tower of Eldara stands as a lonely testament to the vast kaldorei empire that once dominated this coastline. Like much of Azshara's ruined architecture, it fell into disuse following the Great Sundering thousands of years ago. Today, the entrance remains firmly closed and barred against the outside world, giving no hint of whatever relics or chambers lie sealed inside. The surrounding shores are fraught with danger, prowled constantly by wandering murlocs, clawing makrura, and predatory hydras that keep all but the most daring travelers away.

Tower of Ilgalar. In eastern Redridge, Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar and commands the Shadowhide gnolls. The banished sorcerer practices dark magic there, far from Stormwind. Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar above eastern Redridge. Cast out of Stormwind's Mage Quarter for forbidden magic, the sorcerer retreated to these rugged heights to pursue the dark arts beyond imperial interference. He rules the local Shadowhide gnoll clan, whose members guard the spire's base. Inside, conjured demonic hounds stalk the tower, and shadowy power threatens Lakeshire below.

Toxic Fogger. In Stonetalon, the Toxic Fogger is bound for the Venture Company's air routes. The Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society filled the device with lethal poison to contaminate the company's flights. Apothecary Zamah sends the Toxic Fogger against the Venture Company's mining work. Apothecary Lydon brewed its toxin in Tarren Mill, and Zamah dispatched it from Thunder Bluff. She suspects the goblins use courier flying machines to carry messages and light cargo between Stonetalon and their headquarters. Her plan is to release the poison where those machines land and refuel. The Forsaken aim to strike the company's supply route instead of fighting its mercenary crews in drawn-out skirmishes.

Trade District. Past the Valley of Heroes, Trade District draws Stormwind’s merchants and travelers. Its bank, Auction House, guild registry, and shops serve citizens and adventurers alike. You pass beneath the stone arches from the Valley of Heroes into Trade District. The open plaza is Stormwind’s main marketplace and a hub for goods and travel. The Auction House stands at its center, with the Stormwind Counting House, the city’s main bank, and The Gilded Rose nearby. From here, routes lead to Old Town, the Cathedral Square, and the Mage Quarter. Coin, raw goods, and supplies for adventurers pass through the district on their way across the realm.

Trade Quarter. The Trade Quarter forms the central core of the Undercity, resting directly beneath the lifts from the Ruins of Lordaeron. It functions as the beating economic heart of the Forsaken, housing their primary bank vaults, auction market, and essential civic services. From this concentric hub, vaulted corridors branch outward into the surrounding districts. Descending from the shattered surface of Lordaeron, travelers step off the lifts into the echoing stone expanse of the Trade Quarter. Designed around a tiered, circular layout, its central platform holds the city coffers and central bank, framed by bridges spanning noxious runoff canals. Surrounding terraces buzz with vendors, guild registries, and auctioneers bargaining amidst the eerie gloom. Even basic accommodations reflect Forsaken pragmatism: the local inn offers unlined wooden caskets rather than soft beds. From this central nexus, stone archways lead outward into the city's specialized quarters, making it the unavoidable crossroads for any business conducted within the capital.

Tradesmen's Terrace. Tradesmen's Terrace gathers Darnassus's merchants and craftspeople along the city's southern edge. Its auction house and shops connect travelers with goods from Teldrassil and beyond. Tradesmen's Terrace fills the southern stretch of Darnassus with shops and merchants. Here, kaldorei and travelers from the wider Alliance find provisions, crafting supplies, and the city's central auction house. Paths lead north to the Warrior's Terrace and west toward the Temple Gardens and the Temple of the Moon. For journeys into the wilds, this is where travelers gather what they need.

Train Depot. Beneath Gnomeregan's surface entrances in Dun Morogh, the Train Depot lies overrun by leper gnomes and troggs. Once a center of gnomish rail travel, it now stands in ruin. The Train Depot lies below the grand elevator from Dun Morogh, where rail lines once carried gnomes through Gnomeregan. Its platforms and tracks now lie in ruin. The radiation that swept through the city changed the workers who remained into crazed leper gnomes, and troggs from below have overrun the rails. You must cross the depot to reach deeper parts of the city, including Clockwerk Run, the Loading Room, and the inner engineering facilities.

Training the Beast. In Durotar, young orc and troll hunters are sent to learn from veteran master hunter Ormak Grimshot. After proving themselves with the plains beasts, they travel from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There they learn to care for, feed, and train a lifelong animal companion. In Durotar's arid canyon lands, skill with a bow and survival in the harsh wilds are only part of a hunter's duty. Young hunters first tame the plains beasts: fierce boars, crab scavengers, and armored scorpid stalkers. Once they prove their resilience, Thotar sends them from Razor Hill north through the red clay gulches to Orgrimmar's fortified gates, ready to take responsibility for a companion.

Training the Beast. In Dun Morogh, Training the Beast brings young dwarven hunters to the end of their first trials. After learning to soothe and tame wild predators in the snowy crags, they travel to Ironforge to learn how to care for, train, and sustain an animal companion. After taming large crag boars, snow leopards, and sturdy ice claw bears with a taming rod, young hunters finish their trial near Kharanos under Grif Wildheart’s watch. Taming a beast is only half the bond. Grif sends his pupils up the mountain pass to Ironforge, where they seek the Hall of Arms in the military district.

Training the Beast. In Mulgore, young tauren hunters learn to live and hunt beside a beast. After proving their patience and resolve by soothing the plains’ wild creatures, they travel to Thunder Bluff to learn the lasting bond of care and command. After facing plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops in Mulgore, tauren hunters are ready to take up the full mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, their mentor in Bloodhoof Village, sends each novice to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There, Holt Thunderhorn teaches them. The shu'halo honor him for communing with the wilds, and his reverence for the Earthmother is greater still.

Training the Beast. In Teldrassil, Training the Beast sends night elf hunters from the wilds to Darnassus. After taming beasts among the boughs, they learn pet care and discipline from Jocaste. Dazalar sends you from the wilds near Dolanaar to Darnassus once you prove you can tame a beast. Before you travel Kalimdor with a loyal companion, you need to learn more than how to use a taming rod. Subduing a wild creature tests your strength and will, but an untrained beast can still be unpredictable.

Training the Beast. Training the Beast is a foundational quest for young hunters, directing them to seek out the veteran woodsman Isaac Chan in Goldshire. By completing this step, hunters learn to properly train, nourish, and revive their animal companions, transforming a freshly tamed beast into a loyal combat partner. Learning to tame a wild creature is only the initial step for an aspiring hunter; maintaining a lasting partnership demands discipline and knowledge. The quest directs fledgling hunters to seek out Isaac Chan, an experienced woodsman stationed in Goldshire, to acquire the essential craft of beast training. Without proper guidance, a tamed beast remains an unruly wild animal rather than a steadfast ally in the wilderness.

Tramping Paws. At Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands, Rethiel watches the Mosshide numbers rise near the Gate of Algaz. Their fires and trampling threaten the bog, and Rethiel asks travelers to thin their ranks. Mosshide gnolls lived in the Wetlands for many years without overwhelming the natural order. Now their numbers have surged south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and paws crush rare fen plants, while their logging strips groves for campsite fires. If the packs keep growing, the fragile marsh will suffer.

Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh puts smiths through an advanced blacksmithing trial. Forging green iron armor tests their endurance and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, with the Omosh bloodline's secret techniques at stake. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar through hard physical trials. He sees metalworking as more than heating ore and shaping it; the work honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and repeated crafting of tempered green iron armor is meant to build muscle and discipline.

Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Southeast of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery is overrun by shambling skeletons and ghouls. The former burial site has become an immediate hazard for the nearby town. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery was once a quiet resting place for the departed of Grand Hamlet. Dark curses settled over Duskwood, and the dead buried here began clawing their way out of their plots. Skeletal warriors, skeletal mages, and wandering undead haunt the gravestones. Though relatively weak beside the horrors deeper in the woods, they pose a relentless threat to townsfolk so close to Darkshire.

name.frFR: La traduction de la lettre d'Abercrombie

text.enUS: Translate Abercrombie's Note. In Darkshire, Translate Abercrombie's Note brings a strange letter before the town's leaders. Mayor Ello Ebonlocke turns to Sirra Von'Indi, the scholar who knows obscure scripts. Abercrombie sends Mayor Ello Ebonlocke a sealed letter from his home. Ebonlocke expects an eccentric plea or bitter ramblings from the cemetery hermit, but the parchment bears strange writing that ordinary Common cannot explain. Without the learning to read ancient or obscure languages, the mayor will not dismiss it. Even a mad hermit may pose a danger in Duskwood.

name.esES: La traducción del libro de contabilidad

text.enUS: Translating the Ledger. You bring Azuregos's ledger to Narain Soothfancy, who must work out what is written in it. It is a step on the road toward opening the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj. You take Azuregos's ledger to Narain Soothfancy. Someone has to work out what Azuregos wrote in it, and that falls to Narain.

Treacherous Cold. Treacherous Cold is a recovery effort in the treacherous high peaks of Dun Morogh following devastating snow and ice slides. Adventurers are tasked with retrieving the inscribed rifles of fallen Ironforge mountaineers to ensure their identities are confirmed and their families receive closure. The rugged, snowy crags of Dun Morogh pose a constant danger to travelers and soldiers alike. Even the hardened mountaineers of Ironforge can find themselves overwhelmed by sudden avalanches and sheets of falling ice, with novice recruits paying with their lives when winter strikes without warning.

Treant Muisek. Witch Doctor Uzer'i's next target is the wandering forest walkers, treants that slowly roam the forest. After the faerie dragons, you are sent to find three of them. Uzer'i says the night elves have recruited treants as allies in their fight against the Horde. They move slowly, but Uzer'i calls their role as protectors undeniable, and plans to turn that power to the Horde's own benefit.

name.esES: Golosinas para el Gran Padre Invierno

text.enUS: Treats for Great-father Winter. At the Smokywood Pastures display in Orgrimmar, the Greatfather Winter performer is worn out from hearing holiday wishes. He asks you for gingerbread cookies and milk. The Greatfather Winter who greets visitors in the Valley of Strength works for Smokywood Pastures. Long hours listening to citizens speak of festive treats leave him hungry. He turns to passing travelers for warm baking and a cold drink.

name.esES: Golosinas para el Gran Padre Invierno
name.ptBR: Um agrado para o Papai Inverno

text.enUS: Treats for Greatfather Winter. During Winter Veil in Ironforge, the performer portraying Greatfather Winter asks passersby for a treat. Bring him freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk, and he offers a festive gift with warm thanks. In the Commons of Ironforge, a dwarf sits by the holiday tree dressed as Greatfather Winter. The figure’s roots lie in ancient titan lore and dwarven myths of an immortal being cloaked in winter’s chill, but modern festivities rely on Smokywood Pastures. For hours, the performer hears holiday wishes from citizens and eager children.

Trek to Ashenvale. Sentinel Selarin sends travelers south from Auberdine into Ashenvale. There, you report to Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar, where the Sentinels face spreading corruption. Sentinel Selarin's call for aid brings you from Auberdine, on Darkshore's somber gray coast, toward the night elf lands to the south. The Sentinel trusts capable fighters and scouts to make the journey into the heart of that territory. With local threats in Darkshore handled, the greater perils of Ashenvale now demand attention.

Trelane's Defenses. With the wand in hand, Skuerto turns to the ogres that surround the Tower of Arathor. To bring the tower's defenses to life, he needs an azure agate from the Boulderfist shaman, to be taken to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe. Ogres surround the Tower of Arathor in Stromgarde. Skuerto says the tower's defenses must be activated if you are to stand a chance against them and still reach the items alive.

Tremors of the Earth. Garek has concluded that Blacklash and Hematus cannot be trusted to stay in their prison at Lethlor. Black dragons have moved in there and ogres took the Sign of the Earth, so Garek sends you to free the drakes and kill them. Garek can no longer be sure Blacklash and Hematus will stay imprisoned. Black dragons now dwell at Lethlor, and ogres have made off with the Sign of the Earth. Garek judges that something harsher is needed, and the drakes must die.

Tremors of the Earth. Garek has heard from Sigrun how much you have helped, and asks for your help in turn. Garek's master, Krasus of the Kirin Tor, sent Garek to stop whatever is brewing in Lethlor Ravine, and first a stolen Sign of the Earth must be found. Garek was sent to the Badlands by Krasus of the Kirin Tor, Garek's master, to stop the trouble that is brewing in Lethlor Ravine. The exact assignment cannot be shared, only that it matters greatly. A band of roving ogres, now and then spotted around Camp Boff, took the Sign of the Earth, and Garek needs it. Bring it back and there will be more to learn.

Treshala Fallowbrook. In Darnassus, Treshala Fallowbrook waits at home for news of her husband. Heralath Fallowbrook has gone far away, into Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. On the second floor of a Tradesmen's Terrace workshop, Treshala Fallowbrook waits for word from her husband. Heralath journeyed to Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens, where thorny growth surrounds the quilboar's warrens. Their marriage is marked by a pendant of bonding, which Heralath carried with him.

Treshala's Pendant. In Razorfen Kraul, a pendant carries the bond between Treshala and Heralath Fallowbrook. Heralath brought it from their home in Darnassus into southern Kalimdor, where the quilboar tore it from him as he lay dying. Heralath Fallowbrook carried the pendant close when he left Teldrassil on perilous journeys. The necklace reminded him of home and of his beloved wife, Treshala, and the devotion they shared.

name.enUS: Trial at the Field of Giants
name.deDE: Prüfung auf dem Feld der Riesen
name.svSE: Trial at the Field of Giants

text.enUS: Trial at the Field of Giants. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem sends warrior aspirants south to face an unfamiliar foe. They must slay silithid in the Field of Giants and return with several twitching antennae within half an hour. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem challenges growing warriors to prove themselves against an unfamiliar adversary. The Horde's warrior trainers test more than combat skill: aspirants must slay the creatures and bring back fresh antennae within half an hour. The run across the southern Barrens tests their speed and resolve, while the antennae must still twitch when they reach Taurajo.

Tribes at War. Mangletooth bargains for help against the Bristleback from his cage in Camp Taurajo. The captive Razormane quilboar offers intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the deaths of rival spiritual leaders. Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar, is held in Camp Taurajo by the tauren. The Barrens has long been contested by two powerful quilboar tribes, the Razormane and the Bristleback. The Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes. Mangletooth offers insight into who is tormenting Thork's outpost, but he asks a Horde champion to kill the Bristleback's most revered casters.

Trinkets.... After Set Them Ablaze!, a chest called the Hoard of the Black Dragonflight waits for you in Searing Gorge. It looks locked. The Hoard of the Black Dragonflight looks to be locked, and it is yours to open. The chest comes into being once the towers of Searing Gorge are burning.

Trogg. Troggs are brutish, subterranean humanoids descended from the earliest, failed titan-forged experiments sealed deep within the earth. Having recently clawed their way to the surface after dwarven excavations disturbed their ancient vaults, these relentless diggers have overrun dwarven quarries and driven the gnomes out of their beloved capital of Gnomeregan. Long before mortal races recorded history, the titan-forged keepers sought to fashion servants from stone. Their initial design went awry, yielding stone-skinned brutes of low intelligence and unbridled savagery. Distressed by their botched creations, the keepers refined the matrix into the earthen race, who would eventually become the ancestors of the dwarves. Unwilling to annihilate the imperfect troggs, the giantess Ironaya sealed them deep underground within the vault of Uldaman, intending for them to remain trapped in eternal stasis.

Trogg Stone Tooth. In Loch Modan, Trogg Stone Tooth comes from the Stonesplinter troggs in the hills. Rugged and mineralized, each tooth gives dwarven defenders proof that the troggs are being hunted along the southern frontier. Captain Rugelfuss calls for volunteers to hunt the Stonesplinter troggs near Loch Modan's southern gate. With the Ironforge Reserve committed to the Alliance Front, local dwarven garrisons are stretched thin across Khaz Modan. Rugelfuss cannot spare the soldiers at the southern gate guard tower for patrols in the nearby hills. His standing call asks volunteers to hunt the lurking troggs and bring back Trogg Stone Teeth as crude, undeniable proof of each beast slain.

Trol'kalar. Following the Sigil of Trollbane, Zengu finds that the four sigils have formed a single one that can break the wardings on Trollbane's tomb. He sends you to Stromgarde to retrieve Trol'kalar from the tomb. Zengu finds that the four sigils have come together and formed one, the Sigil of Ignaeus. He has no doubt it can break the wardings placed on Trollbane's tomb. Trollbane lies entombed in Stromgarde, in the Sanctum that lies behind the chapel, and Zengu sends you there to retrieve Trol'kalar. A fenced path beside the chapel entrance, on its right, descends to the crypt.

Trol'kalar. The long Trol'kalar chain reaches its last step. The light slowly fades, and Trol'kalar, held in a stone sheath, is released. Carry it to Zengu in Hammerfall. At Trollbane's Tomb the light slowly fades, and Trol'kalar, kept in a stone sheath, is released. You take the sheathed sword to Zengu in Hammerfall, in the Arathi Highlands.

Troll. Trolls are among the oldest sentient races native to Azeroth, having arisen around the Well of Eternity long before the Sundering. Renowned for their incredible physical regeneration, worship of primal spirits known as loa, and mastery of voodoo, their fractured empires once ruled vast swaths of the ancient world. Today, while ancient kingdoms like the Gurubashi and Amani remain deeply hostile to outsiders, the Darkspear tribe has found a lasting haven within Thrall's Horde. Long before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, the primal energies of the Well of Eternity nurtured the rise of trollkind. Emerging as savage, highly agile hunter-gatherers, the early trolls possessed a unique physiology that granted them astonishing regenerative powers, allowing them to recover rapidly from grievous wounds and even regrow severed limbs over time. Settling around the sacred mountains of Zandalar, they directed their reverence toward primal spirits they called loa. Under the spiritual guidance of shadow hunters and witch doctors, these rituals coalesced into the practice of voodoo.

Troll Charm. In Ashenvale, Troll Charms have been taken from fallen Darkspear travelers. The Thistlefur furbolgs seized the sacred amulets after ambushing the party on its way to Zoram'gar Outpost. Darkspear trolls carry spiritual charms as marks of dignity. Scout Mitsuwa says a troll without one is as diminished as an orc without battle scars. A party of Darkspear kin traveled through Ashenvale's canopy toward Zoram'gar Outpost when corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed and slaughtered them. Their spirits were commended to the afterlife, while the furbolgs took the charms as trophies and stashed them in chests deep within Thistlefur Hold.

Troll Charm. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa seeks sacred charms stolen from his kin. A traveling party of Darkspear trolls was ambushed and slaughtered by the Thistlefur furbolgs, who took the talismans into their den. Zoram'gar Outpost is a remote Horde refuge on Ashenvale's western coast. Woodland paths make travel there dangerous. A party of Darkspear trolls never reached the post after the Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed them. Mitsuwa accepts that his kin have died and will one day meet him in the afterlife. Their sacred charms were stolen from the dead, however, and he cannot abide that insult.

Troll Necklace Bounty. Fraggar Thundermantle of Aerie Peak insists the Wildhammers answer to no Alliance and judge folk by what they do. Five tribal necklaces taken from Hinterlands trolls would be a good start for you. Fraggar Thundermantle has no use for talk and wants it clear that the Wildhammers are independent. Whoever hopes for friends among them must first prove their worth. Trolls that roam the hillsides of the Hinterlands sometimes wear tribal necklaces, and five of those brought to Fraggar in Aerie Peak would mark a good beginning.

Troll Necklace Bounty. Fraggar Thundermantle, a Wildhammer, has already taken troll tribal necklaces from you once under this bounty. The offer stands for more, as long as you bring them five at a time. Fraggar reminds you the first handing-over is behind you, yet more troll tribal necklaces are still welcome whenever you find them and choose to hand them over. Fraggar says those who fight for the Wildhammers will find the Wildhammers ready to fight for them in return. Fraggar counts a batch only when it holds five necklaces.

Troll Witchery. Brother Nimetz seeks insight into the corruption of Colonel Kurzen by examining dark troll enchantments. Following Kurzen's Mystery, he asks you to venture south into Skullsplitter territory and secure fetishes from their spellcasters. While reviewing the legends recovered from the jungle, Brother Nimetz turns his attention to the second troll tribe lingering further south. He suspects that dark troll sorcery may be responsible for Colonel Kurzen's descent into evil. To verify his theory, he asks you to venture into Skullsplitter lands and pry fetishes directly from their Witch Doctors and Mystics so he can study their magic at the Rebel Camp.

Trollbane. Vol'jin has ordered the Darkspear trolls to recover the ancient sword Trol'kalar from the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. With King Thoras Trollbane fallen, the blade is meant to serve the Horde in future conflicts against the trolls of Zul'Gurub. Following the death of King Thoras Trollbane and the collapse of Stromgarde into ruin, Chieftain Vol'jin has ordered that every effort be made to spirit Trol'kalar away. This storied blade has long rested in human hands, but the Darkspear tribe hopes to claim it for the battles looming against the jungle trolls dwelling within Zul'Gurub.

Trophy Swoop Quill. Across Mulgore, swoops circle above the plains, and their quills mark a hunter’s skill. Tauren bring these feathers to Harken Windtotem in Bloodhoof Village. Swoops ride high above Mulgore’s grasslands, where they are hard to track. Young tauren hunters and travelers in Bloodhoof Village seek a trophy quill to prove their cleverness and resolve. Bringing one to elders such as Harken Windtotem honors the hunter’s clan and shows the sharp senses needed to thrive on the plains.

Trouble at the Docks. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz caused a clumsy cargo accident on the Ratchet docks, allowing a petty troublemaker named Mad Magglish to snatch a priceless vintage bottle. The vintage—a 99-Year-Old Port sent directly from Baron Revilgaz to Gazlowe—must be recovered from the shadows of the Wailing Caverns before the dockmaster fires the negligent crane operator. Ratchet thrives on constant sea trade with Booty Bay across the Great Sea, but its goblin efficiency occasionally cracks under sheer volume. When an unusually massive morning shipment arrived at the port, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz tried to cut corners to speed up the unloading process. Lifting far more than his crane could manage, he dropped the entire haul across the docks. In the ensuing chaos, a local nuisance named Mad Magglish took advantage of the spilled crates, snatched a single valuable bottle of liquor, and fled inland.

Trouble in Darkshore?. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker seeks help for his missing crew. His introductory appeal sends travelers across the sea to Auberdine, where the dwarven expedition met Darkshore's wild, shadowy coast. Darnassus, the grand night elven capital, is home to dwarven researchers from Ironforge studying Kalimdor's ancient mysteries. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to unearth artifacts of antiquity. Weeks have passed without a message or progress report, and Greywhisker fears his field crew has met dangers they could not survive alone.

Trouble in the Deeps. Tsunaman sends Horde travelers from Stonetalon Mountains to aid Je'neu Sancrea on Ashenvale's remote coast. The troll scholar waits at Zoram'gar Outpost, where danger gathers along the shore. Tsunaman hears troubling reports from the north and calls on Horde travelers to reach Je'neu Sancrea. The troll scholar is at Zoram'gar Outpost, on Ashenvale's far western shore, the Zoram Strand. Je'neu faces mounting danger and needs help from beyond the outpost.

Tsunaman. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tsunaman watches the currents of Kalimdor for signs of unrest. He works with the Horde against forces that threaten the waters. Near the path from Sun Rock Retreat down to the Charred Vale, Tsunaman serves the Tribunal of the Tides, high-ranking servants aligned with the Tidehunter, Neptulon. He works with the Horde to watch for elemental unrest throughout Kalimdor, especially disturbances spreading from the submerged caverns of Blackfathom Deeps.

Tumors. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle seeks to contain the sickness spreading through Teldrassil. You are sent to Wellspring Lake to gather mossy tumors from afflicted timberlings, so druids can study the poison and burn the growths safely. Teldrassil’s native plants and animals are being twisted by a strange affliction. Its timberlings, usually placid nature spirits with bark for skin, have grown hostile and erratic. Grotesque mossy tumors spread across their living wood, pulsing with unnatural poison. Cenarion scholars Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the cause, while timberlings already lost to the sickness must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs.

name.esES: La reserva robada de Tundra MacGrann

text.enUS: Tundra MacGrann's Stolen Stash. In Dun Morogh, Tundra MacGrann needs his winter stores back from Old Icebeard. The injured hunter cannot reach the yeti's cave himself. Tundra MacGrann had salted away a month's worth of dried meat for the cold season. He lives beyond the warmth of Kharanos and Ironforge, where surviving winter takes careful preparation. To keep hungry bears from his provisions, he locked them in a thorium-reinforced meat chest. Old Icebeard carried the whole chest away rather than trying to open it.

Tundrid Hills. Snowbound ridges cut across the Tundrid Hills in south-central Dun Morogh, west of the Gol'Bolar Quarry. Dangerous wildlife keeps travelers to the rocky passes at their peril. The Tundrid Hills offer a rough route from Coldridge Valley to eastern Dun Morogh, away from the main roads through Kharanos. Jagged, snowy slopes make the crossing dangerous. Ferocious predators prowl the hills, so travelers who leave the beaten path face peril without a drawn weapon.

Turak Runetotem. Turak Runetotem is a revered tauren druid trainer residing in the Hall of Elders atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Serving as a trusted assistant to Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, he guides novice tauren along the sacred paths of nature and balance. Through Turak, young druids undertake foundational trials to commune with spirits and master animal aspects. Within the serene confines of the Hall of Elders, Turak Runetotem stands as one of the Horde's foremost druidic mentors. Renowned for his deep patience and balanced demeanor, he assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem in reviving the ancient druidic arts among the tauren people. Turak ensures that every aspiring druid honors the will of the Earthmother, teaching that physical power must always be grounded in spiritual respect and harmony with nature.

Twilight Base Camp. The Twilight Base Camp is a fortified outpost of the Twilight's Hammer cult situated in the arid wastes of Silithus. It serves as an active ritual site where cultists convene to commune with elemental powers and orchestrate their apocalyptic agenda. The camp is characterized by strange wind stones and heavily armed cult zealots. Perched among the desolate sands of Silithus, the Twilight Base Camp is one of several enclaves established by the Twilight's Hammer cult. The outpost brims with zealots, geomancers, and stonecallers dedicated to summoning devastating elemental forces. Surrounded by jagged ritual stones, the camp acts as a staging ground where leaders like Twilight Keeper Havunth and Twilight Lord Everun direct efforts to hasten Azeroth's end, standing in open defiance of the Cenarion Hold forces attempting to restore balance to the region.

Twilight Falls. At Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight's Hammer cultists join with naga beneath the Ashenvale coast. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus calls on Alliance champions to gather pendants from the fallen cultists and hinder their plans to awaken ancient evils. Beneath Ashenvale's Zoram Strand, Blackfathom Deeps lies in ruins. The night elf temple was once sacred to Elune and held a powerful moonwell, until the Sundering shattered it and plunged it beneath the sea. Now naga and cultists fill its halls. The waters have turned foul, and the cultists revere powers darker than the sea.

Twilight Grove. Tucked away in the center of Duskwood, the Twilight Grove is a stunning enclave of lush Kalimdor flora contrasting the grim, blighted forest around it. Beneath its towering great tree and ancient night elf architecture sits a moonwell and a massive emerald gateway connected directly to the Emerald Dream. Hidden behind steep crater ridges in the heart of Duskwood, the Twilight Grove looks utterly alien to the Eastern Kingdoms. Ancient night elf gazebos, vibrant green meadows, and a serene moonwell frame an unnamed great tree that towers over the gloomy canopy. The tree stands as a conduit of nature, filtering the raw vigor of the Emerald Dream into the waking world and allowing this crater to thrive even beneath the eternal gloom of Duskwood.

Twilight Lord Kelris. Twilight Lord Kelris is an orc warlock and high-ranking leader within the Twilight's Hammer cult operating deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. From his perch in the Moonshrine Sanctum, he leads dark rituals in worship of the primordial hydra Aku'mai, aiming to usher in a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, Kelris slipped through the grasp of watchful eyes in Darnassus, evading the Argent Dawn and earning a grim reputation: whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of orchestrating it. Rather than serving warlords or clans, this orc has pledged himself entirely to the Old Gods, seeking to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to a state of absolute, primordial chaos.

Twilight Outpost. The Twilight Outpost is a fortified encampment of the Twilight's Hammer cult nestled in the southwestern sands of Silithus. Located just northwest of the ancient Scarab Wall, it serves as a staging ground where cultists conduct dark rituals to commune with and summon elemental horrors. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Silithus, the Twilight Outpost serves as one of several major cultist strongholds dotting the desert wastes. Positioned in the shadow of the colossal Scarab Wall and west of the Bronzebeard Encampment, the outpost teems with fanatical Twilight Avengers, Geolords, and Stonecallers. Under the command of leaders like Twilight Keeper Exeter and the rare Twilight Lord Everun, these zealots toil tirelessly in service of their maddening apocalyptic masters.

Twilight Pendant. In Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight Pendants mark the cultists who serve the Twilight's Hammer. The Argent Dawn seeks them as proof of the cult's work along Ashenvale's coast. Beneath the drowned ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, the Twilight's Hammer gathers with the naga to honor the chaotic Old Gods. Shadowmages, aquamancers, reavers, and loreseekers all wear Twilight Pendants as signs of devotion to their shadowy patrons. The cult keeps to the ruins of the former night elf temple, so these pendants offer outsiders one of the few ways to learn how many cultists gather there and hinder their plans.

Twilight Post. Twilight Post is a fortified encampment established by the Twilight's Hammer cult in northwestern Silithus. Situated far west of Cenarion Hold and northwest of the Twilight Base Camp, it serves as a critical site for the cultists' elemental summoning rituals. Adventurers venturing here face zealous cultists and the wind stones they use to contact otherworldly forces. Tucked away in the desert sands of northwestern Silithus, Twilight Post serves as an outpost for the Twilight's Hammer cult. The camp is populated by heavily armed defenders and ritualists, including Twilight Avengers, Geolords, and Stonecallers under the leadership of Twilight Keeper Mayna and the rare fanatic Twilight Lord Everun. Like other encampments scattered across the wastes, the post revolves around ancient summoning conduits—Lesser, regular, and Greater Wind Stones. Through dark rites and elemental communion, the cultists utilize these stones to entreat and bind elemental horrors from the realms beyond, threatening the fragile peace maintained by the Cenarion Circle in the region.

Twilight Shore (Darkshore). Murloc tribes and hungry sea creatures crowd the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore. The rugged coast runs from the Long Wash to Ashenvale, where misty beaches meet cliffs, islets, and dangerous surf. The Twilight Shore runs south from the Long Wash, past Ameth'Aran's ruins, toward Ashenvale. Gray beaches give way to sharp cliffs and rocky islands. Threshadons and sea crawlers prowl the waters, while aggressive murloc camps line the shore.

Twilight Vale. In Twilight Vale, beasts and furbolgs prowl the dark woods between Darkshore and Ashenvale. The southern forest is a perilous threshold between Darkshore’s tainted coast and Ashenvale’s sacred canopies. Twilight Vale stretches from south of Ameth'Aran to the Ashenvale border, where dusk holds over Darkshore’s southern woods. Corruption has reached deep into the wildlife. Rabid bears roam beside feral nightsabers, while hostile furbolg tribes stalk the trees. Sentinels and travelers advise you to keep to the main road. Even a few paces into the woods can bring a swift, deadly ambush.

Twilight Whisker. In Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil gathers Twilight Whisker for his brew. Twilight runners carry the whiskers in the northern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Twilight runners prowl the high crags near Stonetalon Peak. Hunters prize their pelts, while Witch Doctor Jin'Zil of Malaka'jin wants their stiff whiskers for a darker purpose. He seeks vengeance on night elves captured after defending these woodlands. To mock and poison his captives, Jin'Zil gathers resinous sap, countless eyes, fey dragon scales, and Twilight Whisker for a lethal draught he calls forest magic.

Twilight's Hammer. The Twilight's Hammer is a nihilistic, apocalyptic cult dedicated to awakening the Old Gods and bringing about the end of Azeroth. Originally an orcish clan led by the ogre-mage Cho'gall, it has evolved into a secretive, multiracial order actively conducting dark rituals across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. The Twilight's Hammer began on Draenor as an orc clan of the Old Horde, led by the two-headed ogre-mage Cho'gall, one of Gul'dan's chief lieutenants in the Shadow Council. Under Cho'gall the clan embraced a grim, apocalyptic creed, coming to see the Horde as merely an engine of destruction meant to bring about the end of all things.

Twilight's Run. Twilight's Run is a secluded subterranean cavern carved into the northern mountains of Silithus beneath Staghelm Point. Occupied by the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cult, it serves as a secluded sanctuary and ritual redoubt away from the harsh desert winds. Tucked away in the northern cliffside below Staghelm Point, Twilight's Run provides the Twilight's Hammer cultists with a natural bastion amidst the windswept hazards of Silithus. Rather than weathering the dust storms or contending directly with roaming silithid hives across the surface dunes, cultists retreat into these shadowy tunnels to commune with dark forces, guard ritual materials, and marshal their forces. Under the direction of overseers such as Vyral the Vile, cult members within the cave maintain a vigilant, hostile presence, ready to strike down any curious travelers or scouts who draw too close to their subterranean encampment.

Twin Colossals. The Twin Colossals are a pair of towering, sheer-faced mesas that dominate the northwestern skyline of Feralas. Rising high above the canopy, the narrow passage between their sheer cliffs forms the primary overland route connecting Feralas with the arid wastes of Desolace to the north. Towering over the western reaches of Feralas, the Twin Colossals stand as the highest landforms in the region. Their vertical rock faces cut a striking silhouette against the sky, serving as unmistakable landmarks for travelers venturing south out of Desolace. While the lower slopes merge into the dense jungle and the lands stretching toward the Forgotten Coast, the summits are isolated plateaus far above the forest floor.

Twisted Hatred. Tallonkai Swiftroot sends trusted champions into Fel Rock to stop Lord Melenas. The satyr has rallied the cave’s grell into an organized force, threatening night elf settlements near Teldrassil. Satyrs recall an ancient betrayal that still stains kaldorei history. They were Highborne who gave themselves to the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Now one has made a foothold on Teldrassil, the young World Tree meant to be a sanctuary. For defenders like Tallonkai Swiftroot, that presence is a bitter disgrace.

Twisted Hatred. Twisted Hatred is a quest in Teldrassil uncovering the puppeteer behind Lord Melenas's actions. Adventurers journey into the Cleft northwest of Dolanaar to confront Xethorr the Wicked and eradicate his corrupted spiders before his vile schemes can spread across the boughs. The discovery that Lord Melenas did not operate in isolation reveals a darker undercurrent running through Teldrassil's wilderness. Behind Melenas stood Xethorr the Wicked, an entrenched satyr pulling strings from the shadows of the forest to undermine the tranquil boughs of the World Tree.

Twitching Antenna. In the southern Barrens, silithid antennae still twitch after they are cut free. Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo seeks them as proof of a young warrior’s speed and skill in combat before the nerves go still. Silithid Grubs, Swarmers, Harvesters, and Creepers carry antennae that twitch after they are cut from the head. The spasms fade soon after the insects are slain. A young warrior must hunt silithid in the southern wastes and hurry back across the scrublands while the antennae still twitch. Bringing them back in time tests both speed and skill, making the hunt a rite of passage for Horde warriors.

Tyr's Hand. Tyr's Hand is a heavily fortified human stronghold situated in the southeastern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands. Long revered as an ancient holy site for the Church of the Holy Light, the city now serves as the primary regional bastion and supply hub for the zealous Scarlet Crusade. Perched defensively in what was once Lordaeron's green Eastweald, Tyr's Hand is one of humanity's most ancient sacred sites. The settlement became known as a 'city of churches' as shrines and holy structures were raised across its grounds. Unlike the blight-rotted ruins that litter the rest of the Plaguelands, Tyr's Hand remains remarkably preserved behind formidable masonry, thick walls, and the towering silhouette of the Scarlet Basilica.

Tyr's Hand Abbey. Tyr's Hand Abbey is a well-maintained sanctuary nestled within the fortified bastion of Tyr's Hand in the southeastern Eastern Plaguelands. Controlled by the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, it serves as an auxiliary house of worship and study alongside the grand Scarlet Basilica. While the imposing Scarlet Basilica dominates the skyline of Tyr's Hand, the abbey provides a quieter, functional center of devotion and martial doctrine for the Scarlet Crusade. Its architecture closely mirrors traditional Holy Light foundations such as Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest, featuring a central Main Hall flanked by a Hall of Arms and a dedicated Library Wing. Despite the relentless horrors of the Plaguelands, the Crusade maintains the abbey with meticulous care, fiercely defending its cloisters from all outsiders.

Tyrande Whisperwind. Tyrande Whisperwind keeps watch over the night elves from Teldrassil. She is Elune’s High Priestess and the supreme leader of her people, who endured the War of the Ancients and the ten millennia of the Long Vigil under her guidance alongside Malfurion Stormrage. Now she commands the Sisterhood of Elune and directs the Sentinel army in Kalimdor’s defense. Born in the ancient kaldorei empire, Tyrande grew up with the twin brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage. The brothers turned to druidism and sorcery, while she became a priestess of Elune. When the Burning Legion first invaded Azeroth in the War of the Ancients, Tyrande stood against it beside Malfurion. The Moon Goddess granted her direct favor, and Tyrande shaped the Sisterhood into a fighting force. Her priestesses wielded divine healing and lunar wrath as the kaldorei faced annihilation.

Tyrion. Inside Stormwind Keep, Tyrion watches the court and aids covert work. The gnome works with Elling Trias to gather intelligence and counter plots against the kingdom. Tyrion keeps to the halls of Stormwind Keep, watching the palace and staying in touch with contacts beyond official oversight.

Ukor. Near the eastern path outside the Valley of Trials, Ukor rests after carrying supplies from Razor Hill. The training grounds already had plenty, and he hopes the provisions can still help his people. Ukor rests by the eastern road outside the Valley of Trials, tired from carrying food south from Razor Hill. Orc peons often spend their days cutting lumber or hauling rocks under harsh taskmasters. Ukor chose to bring provisions to the recruits on his own initiative. He crossed Durotar's red plains, where scorpids and boars prowl, only to find the training grounds already well-stocked. His bundle was not needed. Now he asks passing young adventurers to carry the provisions back north to Innkeeper Grosk.

Ukor's Burden. At the Valley of Trials, Ukor's food is turned away, and he needs help bringing it back to Razor Hill. Ukor, an orc peon, rarely acts on his own, but he carried provisions from the inn in Razor Hill to help young recruits in the Valley of Trials. The journey led him through Durotar's red dust and dangerous wildlife. The overseers and instructors refused the food, believing hardship and hunger make true warriors. Now Ukor waits outside the canyon's mouth, afraid of the beasts along the trail back. He has entrusted the sack to passing travelers, asking them to return it to Innkeeper Grosk.

Ula'elek. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek works armor for warriors across the Horde. The Darkspear smith joins forces with Thun'grim Firegaze, shaping specialized gear from traditional troll craft and trophies gathered across Kalimdor. Ula'elek is a skilled armorsmith serving the Darkspear in Sen'jin Village. Nearby quilboar and sea crawlers threaten the coastal settlement, so the tribe needs sturdy armor and working blades. Ula'elek's skill also draws seasoned warriors from across the Horde.

name.frFR: Ula'elek et les Gantelets de brutalité

text.enUS: Ula'elek and the Brutal Gauntlets. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you from the Barrens to Sen'jin Village for the Brutal Gauntlets. There, Darkspear craftsman Ula'elek will forge them. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east after you prove your valor in the Barrens and begin assembling the Brutal Armor set. The veteran orc smith relies on skilled artisans across Horde lands instead of forging every piece at his mountain perch. For the heavy mail gauntlets, he directs you to Durotar's rocky southern shores.

Ulag the Cleaver. In Tirisfal, a captive Scourge warrior tests the resolve of young Forsaken. Deathguard Dillinger sends you to release Ulag the Cleaver beneath a mausoleum north of Brill and face him in combat. After the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the Forsaken captured an unusual undead warrior who called himself Ulag the Cleaver. His mind remained clear, yet the Lich King still held his spirit in psychic thrall. The Forsaken bound him beneath a mausoleum north of Brill with a magical seal. They hoped to learn how the Scourge chained a mind and to break the hold over him.

Uldaman. Carved deep beneath the northern mountains of the Badlands, Uldaman is an ancient titan vault dating back to the ordering of the world. Recently unsealed by dwarven excavators, its halls contain the buried origins of the dwarven race alongside savage troggs and vigilant stone sentinels. Uldaman was constructed by titan watchers as a subterranean redoubt and research facility. When early experiments in shaping living stone produced the misshapen troggs, the titans sealed their failed creations within the vault's stasis chambers and began anew, culminating in the stone-skinned earthen. Its deepest chambers came to hold vital archives, including the fabled Discs of Norgannon, guarded by the stonekeeper Archaedas and the giantess Ironaya. Dwarven legend holds that in time the stone-skinned earthen gave rise to the dwarven race, and that their cradle lay buried and forgotten beneath the hills.

Uldum. Uldum is a massive, sealed Titan research installation tucked behind colossal stone gates in the southernmost cliffs of Tanaris. Long hidden away behind ancient wards and forgotten machinery, it remains inaccessible to modern explorers. Carved into the rugged southern mountain range bordering the Tanaris desert, the monumental gateway to Uldum stands silent and impassable. Built during the ordering of ancient Kalimdor, the compound served as an advanced Titan facility tied to their mysterious efforts to shape and oversee the planet's biosphere. Titanic wardens and defensive constructs once maintained the perimeter, leaving modern mortals only monumental stone carved arches and buried secrets that have defied all mundane attempts at entry.

Umpi. In Tarren Mill, Umpi endures Apothecary Lydon's experiments. The frog is kept in the Royal Apothecary Society's workshop as a test subject for toxins and plague brews. Umpi is a frog in Tarren Mill who bears the cost of Apothecary Lydon's experiments. For Lydon, testing his formulas requires living flesh, and he gives Umpi lethal brews such as the Elixir of Suffering and the Elixir of Agony. The poisons kill her, but Lydon re-animates her so she can face another dose for the Royal Apothecary Society.

Uncloven Satyr Hoof. In Ashenvale, satyrs gorge themselves on the ancient forest’s magic. Their swollen hooves hold the power they steal, and Ula'elek uses it to forge armor in Sen'jin Village. Satyrs haunt the corrupted groves of northeastern Ashenvale, feeding on the ancient forest’s magical purity. The more they consume, the more corruption distorts their demonic bodies. Their hooves swell and lose their natural cleft, becoming dense stores of absorbed energy. Skilled shamans and leatherworkers can harvest that volatile power.

Undamaged Venom Sac. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill wants a fresh sample of the venom already delivered, and sends you after the spiders that yield it in the Hinterlands. Time matters, since it must arrive fresh. After Venom Bottles, Apothecary Lydon asks for something fresher. The spiders that yielded the venom must live in the Hinterlands, and an undamaged venom sac is wanted from them. Many roam near the troll city of Shadra'Alor. There is no time to waste, because the sac has to be fresh on arrival. Lydon is eager to run experiments with it, and has ordered in several small, terribly cute animals to test it on.

Underbelly Scales. Verner Osgood needs black dragon whelp underbelly scales to settle his trade debt with Smith Argus of Goldshire. You gather them from young drakes wandering the crags south of Lakeshire. The scales settle Verner’s account and leave enough raw hide to craft a piece of gear. Verner Osgood runs a forge on the outskirts of Lakeshire and often trades with craftsmen beyond the Redridge Mountains. Smith Argus of Goldshire sent him a shipment of horseshoes, but Verner is short on coin. Argus demands valuable dragonhide in payment: the highly prized, softer underbelly scales of the black dragon whelps nesting in the region. Without them, collectors may come from Elwynn Forest to claim the debt.

Underbelly Whelp Scale. South of Lake Everstill, Underbelly Whelp Scale trades hands among Redridge craftsmen. Black dragon whelps provide the pliable scales, and local artisans value them when coin is scarce. Black dragons bear tough scales, but facing a full-grown one is deadly for ordinary folk. South of Lake Everstill, black dragon whelps nest among the crags. Their back plates can be brittle or coarse, while the softer scales beneath their bellies bend more readily and still offer protection. Those qualities make Underbelly Whelp Scale valuable in local trade. Craftsmen prize it, and creditors can accept it in place of coin.

Undercity. Carved beneath the shattered palace of Capital City, the Undercity serves as the sprawling subterranean stronghold of the Forsaken. Originally a tangle of royal crypts, dungeons, and sewers expanded by the Scourge, it was seized by Sylvanas Windrunner and forged into a heavily fortified capital for her free-willed undead. Before the Third War, the depths beneath Capital City held a vast network of sewers, royal catacombs, and dungeons. During the fall of Lordaeron, Prince Arthas Menethil ordered his Scourge to begin expanding these depths into a subterranean seat of power. When the Lich King summoned Arthas away to Northrend, the death knight left the construction unfinished.

Undercroft. The Undercroft is an ancient burial crypt nestled in the southwestern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a dignified tomb of Lordaeron, it has been desecrated by a band of undead trolls under the command of Zaeldarr the Outcast. Amid the defiled catacombs lies an ersatz grave dug long ago to feign the death of the exiled paladin Tirion Fordring. Carved into the rugged bluffs southwest of Corin's Crossing, the Undercroft was originally built as a final resting place for the honored dead of Lordaeron. The fall of the kingdom stripped away its sanctity, and the tomb is now infested by a band of savage undead trolls. Led by the hulking monstrosity Zaeldarr the Outcast, these ghoulish marauders use the underground halls as a redoubt from which to stalk the Plaguelands, even daring to raid the grave pits of Light's Hope Chapel to gather raw corpses for their sinister practices.

Underground Assault. Shoni the Shilent sends Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines for a power core. The displaced gnomes need it to power drills that can break through the rock around Gnomeregan and help reclaim their home. After Gnomeregan fell catastrophically to primitive troggs, surviving gnomish tinkerers fled across Khaz Modan and Stormwind. Shoni the Shilent is among the engineers already planning how to breach the rock around their lost home. Her gyrodrillmatic excavationators need great power to bore through the underground stone. Without local power grids in human lands, the gnomes have turned to goblin heavy machinery in the criminal underworld.

Underground Map. Recovered from infiltrating spies near Ironband's Compound, the Underground Map reveals clandestine tunnel networks burrowing toward the roots of Ironforge. Its jagged Dark Iron runes outline a stealthy subterranean route piercing straight toward ancient chambers beneath the mountain. Delivering it to Earthseer Farsen marks the first step in uncovering an impending invasion below. The parchment recovered from Dark Iron spies near Ironband's Compound displays an intricate maze of subterranean roads. Inscribed in harsh, jagged runes unique to the Dark Iron clan, the diagrams map deep underground passages that converge directly beneath Ironforge. The converging passages suggest a possible threat beneath the Bronzebeard capital, but the map's Dark Iron annotations remain uncertain.

Undertaker Mordo. At Deathknell's crypt, Undertaker Mordo greets newly awakened Forsaken. He tells them they are free of the Lich King's control and sends them toward Queen Sylvanas's cause. Bodies that never stir go to the fire. Undertaker Mordo tends the crypt in Tirisfal Glades as corpses break free of the Scourge. Newly awakened Forsaken find him in a world they no longer recognize. He tests their sanity, tells them what they have become, and directs them toward service under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner.

Unidentified Ore. At Windshear Crag, Unidentified Ore draws the Venture Company's attention. Piznik recovered a sample and passed it to Ziz Fizziks for study in Undermine. The Venture Company's clear-cutting and strip mining at Windshear Crag exposed unusual mineral strata in the Stonetalon Mountains. The site's new boss, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, ordered large amounts of strange gold-green ore mined. Demoted goblin worker Piznik remained loyal to his fired former boss, Ziz Fizziks, and secured a sample while plotting his exit from the outfit. He handed it to a traveler bound for the crag's western ridge. Ziz planned to send most of the ore to Undermine for study and keep a small cut for personal profit.

Unnerving Silence. Unnerving Silence concerns an abrupt loss of communication from a druid enclave nestled inside a cave in northeastern Shadowgale Forest. In the wake of Ban'aethall's ruin and growing regional unrest, an investigator is dispatched to locate Elegael Thornpaw and assess the conclave's fate. A quiet unease hangs over the wilderness following the fall of Ban'aethall. With that village reduced to ruins and mysterious unrest stirring through the territory, established lines of contact have begun to fray. In particular, regular dispatches from a secluded druid conclave dwelling deep inside a cave in northeastern Shadowgale Forest have abruptly ceased, leaving their allies on edge.

Unrefined Ore Sample. In Thousand Needles, an unusual ore draws the Horde's attention. Tatternack Steelforge seeks a sample to judge whether the raw mineral can strengthen the weapons of Warchief Thrall's armies. South of the Barrens, Gravelsnout kobolds dig through the stone beneath the canyon walls of Thousand Needles. Travelers returning north found a curious mineral among slain vermin, unlike the usual veins of Kalimdor. They refused to surrender their prize to the Horde. The kobolds who dig and survey the depths carry raw chunks of the ore from their excavations.

Unrequited Love. Unrequited Love is an Alliance delivery quest originating in Auberdine on the shores of Darkshore. Hollee asks travelers taking the vessel to Menethil Harbor to deliver a personal note to Tarrel Rockweaver, an excavation classmate for whom she still holds quiet affection. In the port town of Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore, Hollee watches travelers boarding ships for the Eastern Kingdoms. She seeks aid from passersby to reach an old classmate, Tarrel Rockweaver, with whom she shared years studying the craft of excavation before graduation separated them across continents.

name.esES: Hasta que la muerte nos separe
name.frFR: Jusqu'à ce que la mort nous sépare
name.ptBR: Até que a morte nos separe

text.enUS: Until Death Do Us Part. In Silverpine Forest, Until Death Do Us Part brings Clarice Foster’s old grief to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to leave her keepsake pendant on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children. Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage without fondness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead, declaring service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away.

Unwanted and Unworthy. Unwanted and Unworthy is a quest on Zephras where adventurers aid Elegael in retaliating against the Al'Aketh Cultists after a bloody ambush in Shadowgale Forest. By slaying the cultists and recovering stolen heirlooms, players avenge fallen druids and reclaim sacred ancestral relics for the High Elder. The peaceful balance of Zephras was abruptly shattered when the Al'Aketh Cultists launched a surprise ambush against the local druids in Shadowgale Forest. Elegael, once dismissive of these zealots as harmless dreamers with 'clouds between their ears,' was caught off guard by the sheer brutality of their assault. The attack left druid blood spilled across the forest floor, prompting a demand for swift retribution against the Footsoldiers and Stormchasers responsible.

Up to Snuff. In Booty Bay, the pirate Deeg likes a bottle of grog and fine snuff whenever in port, but the town's herbalist has sold out. The herbalist says Bloodsail Raiders hijacked the shipment, and Deeg wants fifteen shares of snuff brought to him. Deeg admits the sea life may not be the good life, yet it is the only one Deeg has. In port, Deeg looks for grog and good-quality snuff: bad habits, but a pirate needs his vices. Deeg was crushed to learn that the herbalist in Booty Bay has none left. The herbalist claims Bloodsail Raiders hijacked the shipment. Deeg figures a fearless adventurer could talk the raiders into sharing, and wants fifteen shares of snuff.

name.frFR: Une mise à jour pour la Sentinelle Thenysil
name.ptBR: Deixando a Sentinela Tenysil a par de tudo

text.enUS: Update for Sentinel Thenysil. Word of relief travels from Stonetalon to Astranaar. After helping Kaela Shadowspear and Gaxim Rustfizzle against the Venture Company, you are sent to reassure Sentinel Tara Thenysil that their outpost still holds. Stonetalon's jagged passes leave the night elf frontier isolated and exposed. The Venture Company cuts down the crags and pollutes the waterways, threatening the outpost where Kaela Shadowspear and the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle serve. With the immediate danger blunted, Kaela sends you northeast across the border into Ashenvale to report that they remain safe.

Uplands. The Uplands is a rolling, elevated territory in the northeastern Alterac Mountains that once served as the agricultural heartland of the fallen Kingdom of Alterac. Following the kingdom's collapse, the fertile hills fell entirely under the sway of the Syndicate. Today, the criminal organization maintains its strongest base of power here, fortifying multiple encampments across the slopes. Before the Second War broke Alterac apart, the hills of the Uplands were celebrated as the kingdom's breadbasket, providing grain and livestock to feed its mountain fortresses. When the core of the realm fell to ruin and infamy, the farming estates were abandoned by honest folk. In their place rose the Syndicate, led by dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats determined to reclaim their stolen inheritance through force. The Uplands now represents the Syndicate's most heavily concentrated territory in the region, dotted with camps, patrols, and outposts like Dandred's Fold along its western borders.

Ur'kyo. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo guides priests in the ways of shadow and light. The Darkspear regard him as their spiritual leader and greatest priest, and he teaches their traditions in the Horde capital. Ur'kyo guides Darkspear mystics and visiting practitioners from the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. After fleeing the Echo Isles, the Darkspear made a home in Durotar alongside Thrall's Horde. Their sacred traditions remain vital to the tribe, and Ur'kyo keeps those ancestral practices alive through his teaching.

text.enUS: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Stormwind's mages once guarded Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, but Morganth stole the perilous tome and hid it in the Tower of Ilgalar. Ur of Dalaran wrote a treatise on shadow magic and its subtle, corruptive nature. The mages of the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind feared that such arts could bring doom and ruin to the unwary, so they sealed the volume against readers. After Morganth surrendered to dark arts and Stormwind's magical circle exiled him, he took the tome east into the Redridge Mountains, to his stronghold at the Tower of Ilgalar.
