text.enUS: Wanted: Vile Priestess Hexx and Her Minions. Primal Torntusk has ordered Vile Priestess Hexx and her minions brought to justice, and a grand prize awaits anyone who slays the priestess and her elite Aman'zasi guard. You will find them atop Jintha'alor in the Hinterlands. Primal Torntusk has ordered that Vile Priestess Hexx and her minions be brought to justice. The targets are the priestess herself and the Aman'zasi guards, her elite. Atop Jintha'alor, in the Hinterlands, is where they are found. Once they are slain, you report back to Torntusk at Revantusk Village.

War Banners. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist sends Alliance champions against Dragonmaw orcs gathering strength in the Wetlands. He wants their war banners claimed from a camp northeast of town. The Dragonmaw clan once held the red dragonflight captive at Grim Batol during the Second War. When that control broke, the freed dragons hunted their captors nearly to extinction. The few orcs who survived fled Grim Batol into the high mountains east of Whelgar's Excavation, hiding from the red flight's wrath.

War Quarter. The War Quarter is the northwestern district of the Undercity, serving as the command post and martial training ground for the Forsaken. Within its echoing stone chambers, the soldiers, priests, and crafters of Lordaeron hone their weapons and shadow magic in defense of their fledgling kingdom. It houses training halls for warriors and priests alongside weapon masters and heavy industry. Occupying the northwest sector of the subterranean metropolis, the War Quarter stands as the bastion of martial strength for the Forsaken. Beneath its gloomy stone arches, rank-and-file guards and elite champions assemble to drill in armed combat. Unlike traditional barracks of living kingdoms, this military center combines ruthless iron warfare with the chilling rites of shadow, housing an ominous Altar of Darkness where spiritual discipline merges with military ambition.

War Room. Deep inside Stormwind Keep, the War Room gathers the arms, records, and charts used to plan the Alliance’s defense. Beyond Stormwind Keep’s grand chambers, commanders turn to military logistics and high-level campaign planning. Swords, blunderbusses, and heavy artillery cannons line the stone walls. Military treatises and chronicles of past wars fill nearby tables. At the center, a large map lets commanders assess Alliance deployments across Azeroth, while the royal court handles affairs of state just steps away.

War of the Ancients. Ten thousand years ago, the reckless sorcery of Queen Azshara and her Highborne tore a portal through the Well of Eternity, unleashing the demonic Burning Legion onto Azeroth. Led by the young druid Malfurion Stormrage, his brother Illidan, and Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, a desperate coalition of night elves, dragons, and ancient forest demigods repelled the invaders. The resulting destruction of the Well triggered the Great Sundering, violently shattering the ancient continent of Kalimdor and permanently altering the face of the world. At the height of the ancient Kaldorei Empire, Queen Azshara and her elite caste of sorcerers, the Highborne, relentlessly drew upon the vast arcane depths of the Well of Eternity. Their reckless manipulation sent massive ripples into the Great Dark Beyond, attracting Sargeras, the master of the Burning Legion. Entranced by promises of ultimate power and perfection, Azshara and her advisor Xavius opened a trans-dimensional rift within the Well. Legions of felhounds, felguard, doomguard, and monstrous commanders poured into the capital city of Zin-Azshari, slaughtering all non-Highborne and beginning their crusade to purge the world of life.

War on the Woodpaw. At Camp Mojache, Hadoken Swiftstrider calls the gnolls a lasting danger to the camp itself, with attacks growing more fevered of late. Hadoken asks you for ten Woodpaw Gnoll Manes to thin their numbers. To Hadoken, it makes no difference whether the gnolls belong in Feralas. If the camp does not harden its resolve, he warns, it will be pushed out of the whole region. With the attacks on the camp growing more fevered, he wants their numbers thinned and offers generous pay for ten Woodpaw gnoll manes.

Warcaller Gorlach. Warcaller Gorlach patrols Orgrimmar, calling Horde champions to distant battlefronts. He rallies travelers and seasoned warriors to answer commands at outposts across Kalimdor and beyond. Warcaller Gorlach walks Orgrimmar's thoroughfares, carrying the Horde's calls for expansion and defense. He gives orders among the city's people, seeking volunteers ready to test their mettle. Some he sends to the contested canopy of Ashenvale. Others he directs toward Camp Mojache in Feralas, where scouts face the wilderness. He also calls warriors to distant campaigns in the Plaguelands. As threats rise abroad, Gorlach calls on those in the capital to take up arms.

Ward Restocking. Ward Restocking is a task in the Arathi Highlands where travelers assist Doctor Gregory Victor in Hammerfall. With the outpost's infirmary running short on vital elixirs, couriers are dispatched to retrieve neglected supplies from Apothecary Jorell's lab at Go'Shek Farm. At the Horde settlement of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Doctor Gregory Victor tends to the wounded and ailing in the outpost's medical ward. Keeping the infirmary functional demands a regular supply of remedies, antidotes, and elixirs, which are usually provided by the Forsaken apothecary stationed nearby. When these deliveries stall, Victor must enlist capable travelers to step in and keep the clinic stocked.

Warden Thelwater. In Stormwind, a prison riot has left Warden Thelwater besieged at the Stockade entrance. He calls for capable adventurers to stop the Defias prisoners before the uprising reaches the city above. Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them locked away, but an organized revolt caught the guards off guard. The prisoners overwhelmed security and seized the cells, leaving Thelwater barricaded at the entrance as he struggles to contain an armed uprising beneath the capital's streets.

Warlord Goretooth. Warlord Goretooth is the commanding orc officer stationed at Kargath in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. From his watchtower, he coordinates the Horde's frontier campaigns against the neighboring Dark Iron dwarves and monitors the volcanic menace of Blackrock Mountain. Though strict in military matters, he can occasionally be found relaxing around the camp's bonfire. Perched atop the watchtower of Kargath, Warlord Lunk Goretooth directs Horde operations on the hostile eastern frontier. Kargath serves as Orgrimmar's primary staging ground against the threats lurking within Blackrock Mountain and the surrounding ravines. Goretooth oversees patrols, coordinates scout forces like the Kargath Expeditionary Force, and issues direct kill orders targeting the Dark Iron clan's ranks and leadership. When he descends from his lookout, the stern commander shows a lighter side, frequently warming himself by the camp bonfire and trading quips with the camp's Forsaken casters before returning to duty.

Warmaster Laggrond. Outside Alterac Valley, Warmaster Laggrond prepares Horde fighters for the Frostwolf clan. He commands from the valley’s entrance in the Alterac Mountains, where warriors answer the call to aid the Frostwolves. Warmaster Laggrond directs the Horde's fight against the Stormpike Expedition at Alterac Valley's entrance. In the bitter cold, he admits only capable fighters to represent the Frostwolf clan and the wider Horde.

Warpwood Quarter. The Warpwood Quarter encompasses the eastern district of the ruined Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Once a center of elven nature cultivation and lush gardens, it has devolved into a warped, demon-tainted ruin overrun by frenzied flora and corrupted satyrs. Formerly known for its grand botanical marvels, the Warpwood Quarter has become a choking forest of twisted ancients and lethal lashers. The district fell under the sway of Alzzin the Wildshaper, a satyr who bent his dark magic toward defiling the ancient Fruit of Fertility. Under his malign influence, the plant life grew grotesque and predatory, saturating the halls with vile Felvine shards and drawing demons, rebellious imps, and demonic thralls into the ruined halls.

Warrior. Warriors are the quintessential frontline combatants of Azeroth, mastering heavy plate armor, shields, and nearly every form of martial weaponry. Fueling their most devastating strikes with pure combat rage, they charge into the thick of battle to defend weaker allies or carve through enemy ranks. They are found across every race and civilization, serving as everything from stalwart city guards and royal champions to wandering mercenaries. Warriors rely neither on divine prayers nor arcane incantations. Their power stems entirely from physical endurance, battlefield discipline, and an exhaustive mastery of weaponry. Clad in the heaviest plate mail, they dictate the frontline. Some fight behind towering shields to withstand punishing assaults and draw peril away from spellcasters and archers. Others step forward with two-handed polearms, axes, and greatswords, or wade into melee wielding a blade in each hand to cleave through whole formations.

Warrior's Terrace. At Darnassus's eastern edge, Sentinels patrol the Warrior's Terrace and its fortified gate. The district houses battlemasters and warrior trainers, with open plazas for drills and duels overlooking the road into greater Teldrassil. Sentinels guard Darnassus at the Warrior's Terrace, also called the Hall of Justice. Mounted on nightsabers, they watch the high arched gates for travelers coming from the Teldrassil wilds. In the open-air plazas, aspiring combatants drill beside seasoned veterans on dueling grounds and target ranges. Weapon smiths and armorers meet practical military needs, while battlemasters coordinate night elf forces across the wider world.

text.enUS: Warsong Axe Shipment. At Booty Bay, the Warsong Axe Shipment waits for its voyage to Ashenvale. The newly forged axes are bound for the Warsong Outriders and the work at their lumber camp. Axes for the Warsong Lumber Camp wait in Booty Bay. The camp’s woodcutters need a steady supply of durable tools, and not every tool can be forged on the front lines. Orders cross the Great Sea to this neutral goblin port, where the crate is stored near Wharfmaster Lozgil. The sharpened axes are meant for Splintertree Post, where they can be sent onward to the camp. Keeping distant frontier camps supplied takes a long journey across the sea.

name.esES: Campo de trabajos forzados Grito de Guerra

text.enUS: Warsong Labor Camp. Warsong Labor Camp cuts Ashenvale timber for the growing Horde. Its Warsong loggers and orcish sentries work in southeastern Ashenvale, far from help and under threat from the forest's defenders. East of Fallen Sky Lake and southwest of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Warsong loggers cut Ashenvale's dense timber. Durotar's dry plains offer little wood for building cities such as Orgrimmar, so the Warsong clan has pushed into these contested woods. Loggers and orcish guards work far from other Horde settlements, felling ancient trees while night elf scouts and Alliance warbands threaten the camp.

Warsong Lumber Camp. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts timber from Ashenvale for the Horde, keeping its conflict with the night elves alive. Kargathia Keep anchors the fortified operation. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts into eastern Ashenvale's dense canopy for the Horde. Orc peons and hired goblin engineers use whirring shredders to turn towering trunks into lumber for nearby Splintertree Post and the fledgling nation of Durotar. Kargathia Keep's stockades anchor the defenses against night elf counterattacks, and the camp keeps war wolves in an active kennel. For the Warsong, each felled tree means survival and strength. For the native Sentinels, each saw blade is an act of sacrilege.

Warsong Oil. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, Warsong Oil keeps the logging machinery running. A satyr ambush has carried a shipment into corrupted forest enclaves. Warsong Oil keeps the Warsong Clan's logging machinery running in Ashenvale. Goblin-engineered shredders and massive sawmills need a steady supply of the lubricant. Without it, timber cutting could halt, slowing the lumber needed to build Orgrimmar and fortify Horde settlements across Durotar and the Barrens.

Warsong Outrider. On the road east from Ashenvale, the Warsong Outrider watches the Horde's frontier. She scouts for the Warsong clan, watches travelers, and sends intelligence to its forward encampments. She keeps watch unless someone provokes her. The Warsong Outrider watches the road between Ashenvale and Azshara's shattered ruins. Far from Splintertree Post and the lumber camps, she tracks troop movements along the route. Her bow and toxic stingers are ready, but she fires only at Alliance trespassers who attack her.

text.enUS: Warsong Outrider Update. Along Ashenvale’s eastern border, a Warsong Outrider prepares a dispatch for the Horde. Stationed there, the outrider records frontline intelligence for couriers serving the Horde to carry, helping secure the crossing toward Azshara and strengthen the orcish foothold against night elf resistance. Beyond Splintertree Post, the eastern road runs toward the ancient ruins of Azshara through Ashenvale’s volatile borderlands. Mounted orcish vanguards patrol this frontier and record tactical sightings, patrol movements, and resource evaluations. They send their field notes to Kadrak at the northern watchtower, which guards the Barrens border. The reports give Horde commanders a clear view of enemy troop concentrations and territorial threats beneath the forest canopy.

text.enUS: Warsong Outrider Update. A Warsong scout keeps watch along eastern Ashenvale’s perilous paths. Warsong Outrider Update carries intelligence about nearby Alliance forces, entrenched satyr, and naga moving through neighboring Azshara. A lone Warsong Outrider watches the contested eastern edge of Ashenvale. Horde supply lines face constant harassment here, so the outriders scout enemy movements before raiding parties can strike Mor'shan Rampart or Splintertree Post. Meeting one on patrol means the forest is under watch, and the report he carries may help decide whether a Horde fortification holds or falls to ambush.

text.enUS: Warsong Runner Update. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Warsong Runner Update carries reports from western Ashenvale to Kadrak. The Warsong runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches the coast and nearby threats in western Ashenvale. The dispatch records observations gathered by scouts at the outpost and reports on local activity. It travels to Kadrak's watchtower on the Barrens border, helping Horde leaders strengthen their position and plan their movements into the elves' ancestral woods.

text.enUS: Warsong Runner Update. Runners carry word through Ashenvale as the Warsong Clan faces growing pressure along the border. Their report warns commanders of increasingly bold naga attacks on Horde outposts. Warsong scouts and runners watch the fighting across Ashenvale and keep supply lines open. They face night elf sentinels and the dangers of the forest, so commanders need word from the frontier quickly. Couriers carry dispatches to remote garrisons and commanders such as Kadrak at the Mor'shan Rampart.

Warsong Saw Blades. Warsong Saw Blades keep the Horde's lumber machinery cutting in Ashenvale. The Warsong Clan relies on goblin-made machines for its logging, and these blades supply its clear-cutting work. In Ashenvale, the Warsong Clan's logging depends on heavy machinery supplied and maintained by goblin engineers. Axes alone cannot meet the Horde's demand for Kalimdor lumber, so steam engines and circular saws cut through raw timber. Ashenvale's ancient hardwood quickly dulls and breaks ordinary blades. Replacement saw blades must keep arriving for the mills at the Warsong Lumber Camp to keep running.

Warsong Saw Blades. At Splintertree Post, the Warsong loggers wait on blades from Ratchet. Pixel, their courier, will trade the shipment for a weapon to protect herself on Ashenvale's dangerous roads. The blades are needed to keep the Horde's lumber camps working. Pixel has brought heavy saw blades from Ratchet to Splintertree Post, but she will not hand them over for free. In Ashenvale's wilds, she values safety more than coin. She asks for a Deadly Blunderbuss in trade, so she can protect herself on her dangerous travels through hostile territory.

text.enUS: Warsong Scout Update. At Splintertree Post, a Warsong scout records what the Horde needs to know about Ashenvale. Warsong scouts watch the woods as the Horde seeks timber and supply routes through Ashenvale. From Splintertree Post, a fortified encampment, they track night elf sentinels and movements across the territory. Their observations reach Kadrak at the Barrens-Ashenvale border among routine orders. He uses them to judge troop readiness and coordinate supplies and travel through the contested woods.

text.enUS: Warsong Scout Update. Orders from Kadrak reach Warsong Scout Update as scouts watch the contested woods. The Horde depends on their reports to guard its positions in Ashenvale against night elf attacks. Kadrak depends on scattered Warsong scouts to watch the Ashenvale border. The forest gives night elf sentinels cover, and the scouts face the risk of being cut off. Couriers carry written updates between them so isolated outposts can report what they see and remain connected to Horde command.

Warsong Supplies. At Splintertree Post, Locke Okarr needs supplies to keep the Warsong Lumber Camp running. Some await in town, some in Booty Bay, and others lie in enemy hands across Ashenvale. Locke Okarr works to keep the Warsong Lumber Camp supplied from Splintertree Post. The Warsong Clan needs a steady flow of heavy tools to harvest Ashenvale's ancient timber. Raids by furbolgs and satyrs have scattered or seized local supplies, leaving the camp short of vital gear.

Warsong clan. The Warsong clan is one of the most ferocious and legendary fighting forces among the orcs, formerly led by the revered chieftain Grommash Hellscream. Having survived exile, the internment camps, and demonic corruption, the clan now operates primarily in Ashenvale as the Warsong Outriders, fiercely securing lumber for the fledgling Horde while clashing ceaselessly with the night elves. Long before crossing into Azeroth, the Warsong forged their reputation across the open plains of Draenor through mobile wolf-rider tactics. After the Horde's defeat, while other orcs languished in Alliance internment camps, the Warsong evaded capture, wandering the wilderness and clinging to their warlike spirit until Thrall united with Hellscream to forge the New Horde.

Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, Washed Ashore begins an inquiry into the many sea creatures dying on its shore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde starts it in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Darkshore has seen great sea creatures beach themselves from time to time, a tragic but occasional sight. Now the strandings come in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon see more than a natural oddity in these deaths. They fear the pattern may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor.

Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore's misty coast, dead sea creatures have drawn Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde into a troubling inquiry. She serves the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and seeks to learn why marine life is stranding or dying along the shore. Dead sea creatures line Darkshore's beaches and shallows, puzzling the night elves of Auberdine. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde has already examined one stranded creature along the beach. Now she asks you to dive west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, and inspect the bones of a massive sea turtle. The evidence will help her report to the Temple of the Moon.

Washte Pawne. Across the southern Barrens, Washte Pawne's quill leaves a sting that hunters carry to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. Its pain makes the hunt a trial of regret for the tauren. Thunderhawks are elusive creatures of the Barrens, and wandering nomadic tribes treat them with reverence. Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter” in Taurahe and holds a special place among them. Its death is no ordinary hunt: shamans whisper that striking down a thunderhawk can bring omens of triumph or misfortune.

Wastewander Justice. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle of the Gadgetzan Water Company says the Wastewander nomads now hold nearly every water well in the Tanaris desert. You are sent east of Gadgetzan to bring justice to the Wastewander Bandits and Thieves. Out in the Tanaris desert, the Wastewander nomads now hold nearly every water well, and Gadgetzan's supply will soon run dry without access to them. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle, who has a taste for goblin-style justice, wants ten Wastewander Bandits and Thieves brought down east of town, and then a report back at once.

Watch Captain Parker. At Three Corners, Watch Captain Parker guards the road and travelers bound for Lakeshire. He patrols the junction and watches the gnoll packs gathering nearby, an early line of defense for those heading into town. At Three Corners, Watch Captain Parker watches the roads between Elwynn Forest, Duskwood, and Redridge. Stormwind has few troops to spare, and little official help reaches the region. Parker and other lone watchmen must keep the crossroads clear of bandits, prowling predators, and raiding gnolls.

Watcher Backus. Along Duskwood's road, Watcher Backus keeps watch for danger and suspicious traffic tied to Stormwind's political intrigues. He patrols between Darkshire and Manor Mistmantle, watching for undead and strange travelers. Watcher Backus walks a solitary beat north of Darkshire, passing near Manor Mistmantle. Like the rest of the Night Watch, he struggles against Duskwood's curse. Stormwind's garrison gives the region little support, so local volunteers guard its misty paths on their own. Backus keeps beast and ghoul at bay along the road.

Watcher Dodds. At Duskwood's central crossroads, Watcher Dodds keeps watch for the Night Watch. From his roadside outpost, he watches for danger and asks travelers to thin the giant spider population. Watcher Dodds guards the crossroads for the Night Watch, under Commander Althea Ebonlocke. His post stands where the roads from Darkshire, Raven Hill, and Deadwind Pass meet. Darkshire's palisades shelter the town, but Dodds keeps watch beyond them, amid wolf packs, ravenous ghouls, and oversized spiders. From his roadside camp, he watches for threats and asks passing mercenaries to kill spiders emerging from the undergrowth before they overrun the roads.

Water Elementals. Following discoveries regarding the Stone of the Tides, Baron Revilgaz seeks a way to counteract the artifact's curse. He sends adventurers back to the island to harvest bracers from conjured water elementals so their magical residue can be inspected by experts. Believing the water elementals were summoned by the goblin wizard Gazban, Baron Revilgaz suspects their magical residue holds clues to dealing with the Stone of the Tides. The stone is said to curse anyone who wields it, causing the bearer to drift in and out of reality. To find a countermeasure, Revilgaz directs you back to the island off the coast to gather elemental bracers that might be scrutinized by the scholarly mages of Dalaran.

Water Pitcher. At Red Cloud Mesa, Water Pitcher carries fresh spring water from the local well to Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks young tauren to bring it back as a lesson in humility, service, and respect for tribal elders. Water Pitcher rests beside the well southeast of Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks a novice to fill it and carry it to Chief Hawkwind. The chore tests their character and teaches young braves that no duty is beneath a tribal protector. Caring for the everyday needs of their kin matters as much as wielding a weapon on the hunt.

name.frFR: Prime de la poche à eau

text.enUS: Water Pouch Bounty. Spigot Operator Luglunket in Gadgetzan wants the Wastewander water pouches the nomads stole, wherever you find them out in the desert. The Gadgetzan Water Company offers an official care package in return for each five. Luglunket, a seasoned spigot operator, would like nothing better than to receive the Wastewander water pouches you come across in the desert. It was Gadgetzan's water in the first place, and the nomads simply stole it. For every five pouches brought in, the Gadgetzan Water Company offers an official care package, and you are helping Gadgetzan help itself.

name.frFR: Prime de la poche à eau

text.enUS: Water Pouch Bounty. Spigot Operator Luglunket greets you again, hoping you carry five more Wastewander water pouches, and keeping a care package ready. After Water Pouch Bounty, Luglunket welcomes you back and asks whether five more Wastewander water pouches are in your pack. If so, a care package is already set aside with your name on it.

Water Sapta. The Water Sapta is a ceremonial draught used to attune one's spiritual sight to the hidden spirits and corruptions of water. Entrusted with this preparation, the bearer is sent to locate tainted pond water within the fields of Westfall to investigate an elemental imbalance. In the elemental traditions of shamans, a sapta is a ceremonial concoction prepared to pierce the veil between the physical realm and the spirits. The Water Sapta attunes the senses specifically to the element of water, granting the spiritual vision necessary to perceive elemental disturbances and hidden spirits. Without such an attunement, ordinary travelers could look directly upon an elemental manifestation and see nothing more than ordinary ripples.

Water Sapta. At Islen Waterseer's shore, a young Horde shaman receives Water Sapta for a journey across the Great Sea. The trial leads from the Barrens to Silverpine Forest, where a spring has been corrupted. Among Horde shaman, a sapta is a draught made to open the senses to the world's spirits. To ordinary eyes, a stream may look calm and a pond still. Drink a sapta, and the veil of the physical world parts, showing the elementals that dwell in the water.

Water of the Seers. In Bloodhoof Village, young tauren drink the sacred Water of the Seers before their tribal trials. The draught opens the mind to the spirit world and summons a Plains Vision to guide them. Young tauren drink the Water of the Seers before the tribal fire in Bloodhoof Village. Tribal mystics prepare the draught for the ancient Rite of Vision. It opens the drinker’s spiritual sight, and the Plains Vision appears from the embers to guide the way to Seer Wiserunner.

Waters of Xavian. Deino seeks a sample from the waters of Xavian, deep in Ashenvale. The troll mage hopes to study the ancient city's lingering arcane power, and sends her apprentice to draw water from its highest waterfall. Deino, a troll mage in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, searches Kalimdor for traces of primal arcane energy. Her attention turns to Xavian, an ancient night elf city hidden beneath Ashenvale's eastern canopy. Scholars say the city held great magical knowledge before the Sundering. Its waters are believed to retain arcane power that modern mages hope to understand.

Waterspring Field. Waterspring Field is a vital water-pumping operation in northern Tanaris, constructed by the goblins of Gadgetzan to tap underground aquifers. Instead of supplying the boomtown, the field has been overtaken by the ruthless Wastewander bandits, who now hoard the desert's most precious resource. In the searing wastes of Tanaris, nothing carries more value than fresh water. Seeking to support their expanding trade hub, the Steamwheedle Cartel goblins of Gadgetzan erected an array of industrial pumping towers across Waterspring Field to draw from underground reserves. Their plans collapsed when the Wastewanders—a sprawling band of human outlaws and desert marauders—seized the entire field. The bandits now guard the hijacked pumps with their lives, forcing Gadgetzan to look for hired blades willing to reclaim the moisture.

Wavestrider Beach. Wavestrider Beach is the sun-scorched coastal strip lining the eastern edge of Tanaris. Stretching between Steamwheedle Port and the pirate stronghold at Lost Rigger Cove, its sands are inhabited by aggressive crustacean wildlife and overlook distant naval skirmishes out at sea. Running along the ocean border of eastern Tanaris, Wavestrider Beach connects the goblin settlement of Steamwheedle Port in the north to the cliffs guarding Lost Rigger Cove to the south. Rather than a gentle resort, the shoreline is plagued by vicious Steeljaw Snappers and Desert Crawlers scuttling across the baking sand. Out in the deep water just offshore, burning vessels remain locked in a perpetual naval clash, serving as a grim warning of the piratical violence that dominates these coastal waters.

Wayward Weapons. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new recruits to recover weapons for the encampment. With young warriors arriving to serve the Horde, supplies run thin, and the weaponsmith needs old arms returned to use. New recruits face harsh trials in Durotar's red wastes. Many arrive ready to pledge their blades to the warchief, straining the encampment's weapon stocks. Weaponsmith Kzan Thornslash struggles to meet demand, especially when early lessons prove fatal or humiliating for the unready.

Weapons of Choice. At Camp Taurajo, Tatternack Steelforge investigates reports of sturdy Razormane weapons. He sends travelers past the Field of Giants to recover them, so the Horde can judge the threat. The Razormane are making unusually durable weapons in the southern Barrens. Most quilboar are dismissed as crude fighters with tools of wood, bone, and stone, so the reports have caught the Horde’s attention. Tatternack Steelforge, an orc smith at Camp Taurajo, is investigating under orders from Warchief Thrall. He doubts the quilboar know proper metalwork and wants proof of whether they have learned new techniques or found better supplies.

Weapons of Elunite. In Darnassus, Weapons of Elunite brings a young warrior's early rite of passage to its close. After recovering ore blessed by Elune, you bring it to Mathiel to forge arms for a defender of Kalimdor. Night elf warriors defend Teldrassil and the kaldorei people. Promising young warriors gather elunite, a mineral blessed by the Moon Goddess, rather than relying on mundane steel alone. Its ore calls for a smith skilled in metalcraft and mindful of Elune's gift.

Weapons of Spirit. Witch Doctor Uzer'i now has everything needed and the spirits you captured. Binding them into weapons is hard work, so Uzer'i asks you to wait a moment while the preparations are made. Uzer'i admits that imbuing weapons with muisek is hard going. Now holding all the materials needed, along with the spirits you captured, Uzer'i can begin, and asks you to wait while the weapons are prepared.

Weathered Nook. Tucked away along the northern cliffside of Thousand Needles, the Weathered Nook is a secluded cleft and shelter perched high above the canyon floor. Overlooking the vast sea of stone spires, it serves as a modest home and retreat for solitary tauren dwellers seeking quiet contemplation away from bustling settlements. Carved into the sheer sandstone wall north of Freewind Post, the Weathered Nook is easily missed by travelers passing along the canyon basin below. A natural ramp winds up the cliff face, leading to a sheltered ledge and cave out of the prevailing winds. Rather than housing a military outpost or large settlement, the nook serves as a humble homestead for solitary wanderers like Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer, offering safety, seclusion, and a sweeping view across the windswept needle plateaus.

Weazel's Crater. Weazel's Crater is a deep gouge carved into the hard salt of the northern Shimmering Flats. Its origins are mysterious, and Saltstone basilisks inhabit the hollow. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, experimental goblin and gnome rocket-cars constantly push the boundaries of mechanical sanity. Debris, scorched earth, and impact hollows litter the plains, but Weazel's Crater stands out for its sheer size and depth. The crater's origins are unknown. Today, the mechanical wreckage has largely settled, and the hollow has been claimed as a sunning pit by aggressive Saltstone basilisks.

Webwinder Path. Webwinder Path winds through the lower Stonetalon Mountains, linking Malaka'jin with Mirkfallon Lake. Spiders and native beasts roam its crags and woods. Webwinder Path runs from Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake through the lower Stonetalon Mountains. Thick webs hang among the trees and along the jagged cliffs. Mountain spiders prowl the road, while thunder lizards and territorial rams roam nearby. Travelers must watch their step along the winding route.

Webwood Egg. In Shadowthread Cave, Webwood Eggs lie in brooding nests in Shadowglen. Naturalists seek viable eggs to study the young spiders in secure laboratory conditions. Researchers cannot safely tame or subdue a fully grown, venomous Webwood spider alone. Scholars like Gilshalan Windwalker instead collect unhatched eggs from clutches hidden in Shadowthread Cave. An egg can be carried safely, and the spiderlings contained when they hatch, giving naturalists live subjects to study without facing adult spiders’ deadly fangs.

Webwood Egg. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks an unhatched Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. After gathering venom samples, he needs a living specimen to examine the unnatural aggression afflicting the forest’s creatures. An egg can be studied safely without subduing a full-grown spider. Gilshalan Windwalker needs live subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting the Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have secured raw venom from the aggressive spiders, but carrying a thrashing giant out of the depths would be deadly for a novice. Gilshalan asks you to bring back an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave.

Webwood Ichor. In Shadowglen, Webwood spiders carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine needs their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to brew an antidote. Webwood spiders in Shadowglen carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine asks for their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to prepare an antidote.

Webwood Spider Silk. Webwood Spider Silk is gathered from Webwood Lurkers in the woods of Teldrassil. Crafters use spider silk in many ways, but these swatches draw the interest of suspicious figures among the World Tree’s boughs. Webwood Lurkers around Dolanaar spin a fine, strong thread that is dangerous to gather. Zenn Foulhoof, a satyr along the forest road, asks young adventurers to collect the silk with nightsaber fangs and strigid owl feathers. He says these rare reagents are needed for his forest business, and newcomers gather them without asking about his corrupt nature or true motives.

Webwood Venom. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the giant webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He asks young night elves to gather venom sacs so he can learn how Teldrassil's growth has affected the forest's wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has come to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. They are far larger and more aggressive than their cousins elsewhere. He suspects Teldrassil's immense magical energies are changing the local wildlife. He asks for venom sacs to compare with those of ordinary spiders and learn what has changed.

Webwood Venom Sac. In Shadowglen, Webwood Venom Sacs draw the attention of naturalists studying Teldrassil's growth. The sacs come from overgrown spiders, and their venom may show how the new World Tree has changed local wildlife. Webwood spiders live around and within Shadowthread Cave, and they are cousins to a much smaller breed found elsewhere. Their sudden growth and predatory aggression worry night elf researchers. Naturalists such as Gilshalan Windwalker study the venom in their sacs, examining its strength and composition. They hope to learn how Teldrassil's rapid, unblessed growth is changing the creatures that live on its boughs.

Weeping Cave. The Weeping Cave is a foul, subterranean cavern tucked into the hills of the northeastern Western Plaguelands, just west of the Thondroril River. Once a natural cave system, it now seeps with toxic blight and festers with grotesque fungal beasts and oozes. Carved into the rugged bluffs above the Thondroril River, the Weeping Cave earned its name from the continual trickling of moisture through its rocky ceiling—water that has long since turned rank and corrupt. The Scourge's plague has thoroughly permeated the soil above, draining virulent filth down into the dark. Within, rotting horrors, decaying behemoths, and caustic oozes wander the damp tunnels, accompanied by an enigmatic corrupted elemental entity known simply as The Husk.

Welcome to Azeroth. 'Welcome to Azeroth' is an introductory quest that sends a traveler from Thunder Bluff to Orgrimmar on behalf of the Windshapers. Guided by the spiritual ties of the Earthen Ring, the emissary meets with Warchief Thrall to forge bonds of survival and alliance with the Horde. Venturing into the sprawling expanse of Kalimdor, newcomers quickly discover that survival hinges on brotherhood. The Windshapers look beyond their isolated origins to the peoples walking below, recognizing that isolation offers no defense against the threats of Azeroth. By extending a hand to the neighboring tauren city of Thunder Bluff and looking toward the orcish bastions to the east, they seek steadfast companions to brave the wilderness together.

Welcome to Shen'dar Village. Welcome to Shen'dar Village introduces travelers to the key figures and local dynamics of Shen'dar Village. Upon arrival, newcomers are directed to consult the local Windshaper elder and the village innkeeper before assisting with pressing threats like regional bandits. Arriving in Shen'dar Village, travelers are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the settlement's key residents before taking on local tasks. Newcomers exhibiting spirit-touched qualities are directed to meet with Elder Illaya Amberwind near the village square, as well as Coriella Calmbreeze at the village inn for lodging and supplies. This greeting ensures visitors understand the settlement's delicate social dynamics before taking up arms.

Welcome to Shen'dar Village. Welcome to Shen'dar Village introduces travelers to a remote haven shaped by ancient Highborne bloodlines and simmering factional rivalries. While the High Order and the Windshapers maintain an outward truce within the settlement, bitter tensions linger just beyond the village borders. Shen'dar Village serves as a delicate haven where differing elven factions coexist under a tense truce. Newcomers who show traces of Highborne blood are promptly sent to pay respects to the elder of the High Order, Rathiril Sunlance, inside the settlement's main lodge, and to secure lodging with the local innkeeper, Coriella Calmbreeze.

Welcome to the Jungle. Barnil Stonepot welcomes newcomers arriving at the hunting camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Recognizing a fellow battle-tested wanderer, he arranges an introduction to the expedition's leader, the renowned huntsman Hemet Nesingwary. Barnil Stonepot greets newcomers at the camp in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, and he can tell a seasoned combatant when he sees one. He points out Hemet Nesingwary, a famous Alliance war hero and peerless tracker. Nesingwary reserves his fellowship for proven veterans, and Barnil believes the old marksman might be convinced to share his hunting wisdom with someone who has endured the trials of battle.

Well Stone. Across Mulgore, Well Stones rest beside the water wells. Their earth and water magic helps prepare the Water of the Seers for tauren rites of passage. Well Stones rest in the soft earth beside Mulgore’s wells, where they absorb the spiritual resonance of the plains and the waters beneath them. Shaman and seers such as Zarlman Two-Moons know these stones as vessels of vital magic, not ordinary river pebbles. Combined with grounded Ambercorn beneath the plains’ mighty trees, their mineral properties temper the brew that awakens visionary trances in young tauren during the sacred Rite of Vision.

Wellspring Lake. At Wellspring Lake, springs feed the river while corruption stirs the wildlife. The lake lies northeast of Darnassus, where night elf fishermen once found a quiet retreat. Wellspring Lake lies between Darnassus and the Oracle Glade, beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Night elves once came to its clear waters to fish and sit in quiet thought. Springs deep within the World Tree feed the lake, and its waters flow north through the Wellspring River. Now a blight troubles the surrounding wilds. Aggressive spiders, prowling nightsabers, and agitated timberlings roam the banks, making the shore dangerous for travelers.

Wellspring River. In Teldrassil, Wellspring River carries fresh water north from Wellspring Lake before plunging to the ocean below. Its banks have grown dangerous as the timberlings turn hostile. Wellspring River runs north from Wellspring Lake through Teldrassil's forest before falling from the great tree into the sea below. Its banks are no longer safe. The timberlings living there have grown crazed and attack travelers and druids who come near the water.

Wendigo Mane. Across Dun Morogh, wendigo manes are gathered from the beasts roaming its frozen crags. Their thick coats offer warmth against the mountain cold, and Pilot Stonegear has a use for them. Dun Morogh’s wendigos roam the snowdrifts, and their coarse fur shields against bitter drafts. Pilot Stonegear, stationed outside Kharanos, sends adventurers to Grizzled Den for their heavy manes. He plans to weave them into an insulating floor rug for the interior deck of his prized dwarven siege engine, Trollplow.

Wenikee Boltbucket. Near the Mor'shan Rampart, Wenikee Boltbucket may be able to mend a broken samophlange. Sputtervalve tinkered with the device after it was retrieved from the Sludge Fen, and now needs an expert hand before his colleagues in Undermine demand results. Sputtervalve's claims to his fellow engineers in Undermine now hang on a broken machine. An adventurer retrieved the mysterious samophlange from the Venture Company's control console at the Sludge Fen, and Sputtervalve could not resist showing it off. His tinkering damaged the delicate contraption. He needs someone with sharper skill to diagnose the damage and repair it.

Westbrook Garrison. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer's few guards hold Elwynn's western road against gnolls and bandits. The outpost is short on soldiers and supplies, with danger rising near the Westfall border. Westbrook Garrison watches the road where Elwynn Forest thins toward Westfall. Deputy Rainer and a handful of guards patrol the western roads with too few soldiers to cover them. Much of the Stormwind Army serves abroad, while political indecision in the capital leaves the outpost without needed support. Thieves grow bolder, and Riverpaw gnolls have overrun the southern woods. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire has not sent formal reinforcements, so the guards depend on travelers to help secure the highway.

name.esES: El Cuartel de Arroyoeste necesita ayuda
name.frFR: Au secours de la garnison du ruisseau de l'Ouest !

text.enUS: Westbrook Garrison Needs Help!. Marshal Dughan sends available adventurers west to Westbrook Garrison, the outpost at Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Stormwind's army is stretched thin across the kingdom, while Deputy Rainer and his guards face growing pressure from Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves without regular reinforcements. Westbrook Garrison guards the western edge of Elwynn Forest, where settled woodland meets Westfall's troubled plains. Gnoll warbands and bandits grow bolder along the waterways and western roads, and the small garrison has asked for more men. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's administration have no Stormwind soldiers to spare. Local commanders must hire traveling mercenaries and wandering adventurers.

Westfall Lighthouse. Westfall Lighthouse watches over the rocky isle off Westfall's southwestern shore, its beacon dark and its keepers gone. Old Murk-Eye led the attack that killed them, and Captain Grayson's spirit remains by the tower. Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships along Westfall's dangerous southwestern bluffs and the coast near Stormwind. As law and order failed across the region, royal patrols dwindled and coastal dangers grew unchecked. Murloc tribes drove the lighthouse keepers inland. The family returned to relight the beacon, but Old Murk-Eye rallied his kin for another attack. The murlocs killed the keepers and put out the light.

name.esES: Estofado de los Páramos de Poniente
name.frFR: Le ragoût de la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Westfall Stew. In Westfall, another family is leaving its farm as banditry drives homesteaders from their land. Before departing, Verna Furlbrow entrusts her cherished local recipe to Salma Saldean. Defias thieves and wild mechanical harvest reapers have driven Verna and Farmer Furlbrow from their family acreage. They pack their wagon and prepare to seek refuge behind Stormwind's walls. Before leaving, Verna gives her neighbor Salma Saldean the recipe for Westfall Stew, hoping the farm's home-cooked tradition will live on.

name.esES: Estofado de los Páramos de Poniente
name.frFR: Le ragoût de la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Westfall Stew. Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew on her farm, making a meal from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how Westfall homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers contend with bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a sustaining meal for working farmhands.

Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Kravel Koalbeard, a dwarf at the Mirage Raceway, makes it his business to get people what they need. The gnomes there are waiting on parts that reached Ratchet a week ago, and Kravel cannot go himself. He sends you to Ratchet with his parts order for Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Kravel Koalbeard sees to it that people get the things they need. The gnomes of the Mirage Raceway are waiting on a batch of parts that reached Ratchet a week ago, and Kravel cannot make the journey himself. He asks you to do the legwork, and promises more jobs with serious profit potential if you do.

Wharfmaster Dizzywig. At Ratchet's pier, a crate of alchemy supplies waits for passage across the sea. Wharfmaster Dizzywig arranges its journey to the Old World aboard a ship bound for Blackwater Cove. A crate of potions and reagents waits at the Barrens port, bound for colleagues in the Old World. Caravans that might have carried it have already departed, so you are asked to take the secure shipment to Ratchet's water's edge. The port offers a route across the Great Sea between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms.

What Comes Around.... Guard Berton in Lakeshire is pressing for Targorr the Dread's execution. The Blackrock orc remains in Stormwind Stockade despite his sentence, while political delays keep justice out of reach. Targorr the Dread earned his name in the Redridge Mountains, where he served as supreme executioner under General Gath'Ilzogg, chieftain of the Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep. Even among the invaders, his cruelty was notorious. He oversaw the torture and execution of many Redridge defenders. After his capture, Stormwind sent him to its high-security prison, the Stormwind Stockade, and condemned him to die for his crimes against the realm.

What Is My Purpose?. "What Is My Purpose?" is a quest centered on a giant Malfunctioning Cyclone Construct wandering aimlessly through agricultural fields. Repeating broken fragments of speech beneath its armor plating, the ancient machine has forgotten its original duties after decades of neglect following the departure of the wind elementals. Investigating the construct leads adventurers to consult local orchardist Aamelia Windfield to learn about its mysterious past and former caretakers. Deep within the fields stands a towering Cyclone Construct, aimlessly pacing across the land while trapped in a broken operational loop. Those who approach the armored giant can hear muffled, fragmented speech vibrating from beneath its heavy plates, endlessly repeating errors and questioning its own fundamental function. Decades of isolation have left the machine hollow of purpose, its internal directives corrupted or forgotten. While towering and formidable in appearance, the automaton poses no active threat to passersby, existing instead as a melancholic relic of an older era whose voice has been reduced to static queries echoing over the soil.

What the Flux?. Master Smith Burninate says that when Maltorius left their clan, he took their recipe for fiery flux, worth more than a pristine arcane crystal. Burninate wants the secret plans back and is sure they are near Maltorius, deep in the Slag Pit. Master Smith Burninate calls Maltorius a traitor who left the clan with the recipe for fiery flux. Burninate would bet the recipe came with Maltorius's new promotion among the Dark Irons, and wants the secret plans returned.

Whelgar's Excavation Site. Dwarven prospectors are trapped above Whelgar's Excavation Site, cut off from their findings. The dig sought ancient Titan relics, prehistoric secrets, and fossils, but mottled raptors overran the quarry. Between Menethil Harbor and Dun Modr, dwarven prospectors dug for ancient fossils and earthen mysteries. Their search for prehistoric remnants stirred the native mottled raptors. Overwhelmed and under-equipped, the archaeologists fled to a ridge overlooking the site. Their tents, tools, and unearthed relics remain scattered among the prowling predators.

name.frFR: La bibine perdue de Whiskey Slim

text.enUS: Whiskey Slim's Lost Grog. In the pirate haven of Booty Bay, Whiskey Slim finds himself in dire trouble with his captain. During a violent storm off the coast of the Hinterlands, Slim tapped into a seized crate of Pupellyverbos Port, only to lose the bottles to the churning sea. To escape a brutal flogging, he needs an adventurer to retrieve his misplaced grog. Whiskey Slim's crew was battling severe weather off the Overlook Cliffs, with the shore of the Hinterlands looming nearby, when the sailor sought a dose of liquid courage. His ship had seized a crate of Pupellyverbos Port from a privateer vessel sailing toward Stormwind. Facing waves that threatened to swallow their ship whole, Slim broke into the captain's crate, but a sudden surge swept the bottles right over the side.

Whispering Forest. Behind Deathknell, the Whispering Forest lies quiet beneath western Tirisfal’s cliffs. Its lake, giant mushroom ring, and uncanny wildlife break the stillness, while corruption stirs beneath the soil. Beyond Northface Rock and Bandarion Keep, the Whispering Forest feels far removed from plague-touched Tirisfal. Afflicted deer and roaming predators share its woods with a tranquil lake. Nearby, giant mushrooms form a ring beneath a hovering cloud of mist, glowing with uncanny energy. The ghostly Knight of Mourning wanders among them, bound by oath. Natural magic lingers here in a land scarred by the Scourge.

Whispering Gardens. The Whispering Gardens occupy the terraced hillside just south of the Scarlet Monastery in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Once a place of quiet contemplation, it became the site of a savage clash between early crusade defenders and a massive host of the Scourge. Today, crusaders patrol its overgrown pathways while the faint voices of the fallen linger in the air. Before the Scarlet Crusade fully retreated behind the fortress walls of the Monastery, a fierce battle erupted across these terraced slopes against an encroaching army of undead. The clash claimed countless lives on both sides. In the twilight, travelers through the gardens report hearing strange, soft murmurings on the wind—believed to be the restless echoes of the soldiers and priests who perished defending the holy grounds.

Whispering Horror Residue. Whispering Horror Residue is the squirming remnant of a strange beast recovered from beneath the Whispering Forest. Gathered by intrepid adventurers, these void-touched remains are brought to Father Lankester in Undercity's War Quarter for shadow research. Whispering Horror Residue represents the bizarre, squirming remains scraped up from a defeated beast dwelling beneath the Whispering Forest. Rather than abandoning such an unnatural curiosity, resourceful adventurers gather the twitching material in hopes that researchers within the Undercity can turn it to good use.

Whispering Shore. Along Tirisfal Glades' western coast, the Whispering Shore lies north of Solliden Farmstead, its waters claimed by hostile murlocs. Before the Third War, Lordaeron's fishermen came to the Whispering Shore for calm waters and plentiful catches. Now the Great Sea breaks against an empty coast, and the water is cold and dark. Travelers coming down from the hills risk an ambush from the murlocs along the shore.

Whitereach Post. Whitereach Post is a small Horde encampment nestled along the dusty canyon path in Thousand Needles. Serving as a minor waystation near Camp E'thok, it offers respite and watchful eyes over the harsh desert highway. For travelers moving between Feralas and the salt flats, it stands as an outpost of Horde safety beneath the looming sandstone pillars. Perched along the beaten path winding through the depths of Thousand Needles, Whitereach Post is one of several modest Horde footholds carved out of the rugged landscape. Stationed in close proximity to Camp E'thok, the post helps maintain a reliable presence along the canyon floor, monitoring travel between the windswept mesas. While not as fortified as the great lift or major tribal settlements, it serves as an indispensable stop for couriers, scouts, and adventurers traversing the contested wastes.
Whitestone Oak Lumber. Beneath Moonbrook, Whitestone Oak Lumber is shaped for the Defias fleet. Its strength also draws the attention of Alliance smiths seeking a haft for a sacred weapon.

Wild Hearts. Rane Yorick seeks help in Silverpine Forest as her brother Quinn lies badly wounded. She needs discolored worg hearts for Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher, whose alchemy may help Quinn recover. Rane Yorick stays beside her severely wounded brother, Quinn, after the Deathstalkers' disastrous mission left them pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul mauled Quinn, and he is failing to recover. Ordinary rest cannot mend an undead body torn by such savagery. Rane turns to the Royal Apothecary Society and its grim arts for a way to put her brother back together.

Wild Shore. The Wild Shore is the southernmost coastline of Stranglethorn Vale, where the jungle meets the waves of the South Seas. It serves as a staging ground and anchorage for the Bloodsail Buccaneers, whose ships lie moored along the shallows. Stretching along the bottom tip of the continent, the Wild Shore marks the border where Stranglethorn Vale plunges into the South Seas. To the northwest lies the fortified inlet of Booty Bay, while a shallow ocean strait separates the mainland beach from Jaguero Isle to the east. The beach continues northeast toward the Crystal Shore. Because of its secluded position away from the Blackwater Raiders' direct cannons, the coast has become a hotbed of piratical activity and wild perils.

Wildbend River. Near the Grove of the Ancients, Wildbend River carries demonic poison toward the sea. Its tainted waters run through southern Darkshore from the corrupted heights of Felwood, endangering the wilderness. Wildbend River brings corruption, not clean nourishment, to southern Darkshore. It flows west past the Grove of the Ancients and empties into the sea. The river continues from Felwood's Bloodvenom River, tumbling through rocky ridges with foul runoff. Night elves watch its banks for twisted wildlife and the spread of demonic blight.

Wilder Thistlenettle. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Wilder Thistlenettle drinks alone with old grief. He once entered Moonbrook’s Deadmines with his brother and their mining crew, but a cave-in left him the sole survivor. Wilder Thistlenettle drinks away his sorrow in an alehouse near the Dwarven District’s southeastern gates. Years ago, he joined his brother and their companions in the deep lodes of Moonbrook’s Deadmines. A cave-in sealed the rest of the crew underground, and Wilder barely reached the surface alive.

Wildhammer clan. The Wildhammer clan is a rugged, nature-dwelling branch of the dwarven race famed for taming wild gryphons and wielding storm-charged hammers. Driven from their ancestral fortress of Grim Batol centuries ago, they carved a fiercely independent home across the wooded peaks of the Hinterlands. Though reclusive by nature, they remain stalwart friends of the Alliance, defending the skies whenever called upon. Before the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammers lived in the foothills around Ironforge. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, civil war fractured the dwarven kingdom, and the victorious Bronzebeards claimed Ironforge for themselves. Thane Khardros led his clan north to establish a magnificent hold inside the peak of Grim Batol. Yet peace was short-lived: the defeated Dark Irons soon laid siege to the fortress. While Khardros personally slew the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud, her dying curse blighted the mountain so deeply that the halls became uninhabitable. Refusing an invitation to move back under Bronzebeard rule, the Wildhammers chose self-reliance, marching north into the forests and rocky crags of the Hinterlands.

Wildmane Cleansing. Wildmane Cleansing marks the culmination of the tauren ritual efforts to purify the vital watering holes of Mulgore. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, heroes take the completed Wildmane Totem north to cleanse the final poisoned well. Driving back goblin pollutants restores balance to the plains and secures the pastoral livelihood of the tauren tribes. Water is sacred lifeblood across the sun-drenched plains of Mulgore, sustaining the herds, the soil, and the nomadic tribes who have recently gathered around Thunder Bluff. When the Venture Company and encroaching goblins began contaminating these aquifers with toxic industrial runoff, the tauren elders recognized an existential threat. Following the purification of the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, the Wildmane Water Well stands as the third and final corrupted site requiring spiritual intervention.

Wildmane Cleansing Totem. At Mulgore’s Wildmane Water Well, one last cleansing remains. Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem for the northern well after the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are cleansed. The Wildmane Water Well still needs cleansing. Goblin ventures have poisoned the land and fouled Mulgore’s scarce water, so the tauren turn to sacred ritual against the blight. After the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are cleansed, Mull Thunderhorn crafts a final totem for the well north of Thunder Bluff. Infused with natural spirits, it purifies the fetid water so life can nourish the plains again.

Wildmane Totem. Wildmane Totem represents the third and final stage in Mull Thunderhorn's efforts to craft cleansing totems for Mulgore's poisoned wells. To restore the Wildmane Well, the ritual demands offerings taken from the territory's fiercest natural predators: prairie wolf alphas. After securing the materials required to consecrate totems for the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, only one afflicted source remains in central Mulgore: the Wildmane Well. The poisoned water across the plains threatens both migrating wildlife and settlements, demanding powerful primal ingredients to restore the earth's natural balance.

Wildmane Water Well. At Wildmane Water Well, poisoned waters threaten Mulgore’s northern plains and the herds that depend on them. Across Mulgore, sacred wells sustain the nomadic tauren and their wandering kodo herds. Wildmane Water Well lies at the northern edge of the plains, just beyond Thunder Bluff’s shadow. The Venture Company’s goblins have poisoned its waters to control the regional supply. A tauren-crafted totem is needed for the cleansing ritual that can make the water pure again.

Wiley the Black. At the Lakeshire Inn, Wiley the Black keeps out of sight. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle and shares what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood. Wiley the Black keeps to the Lakeshire Inn, away from Westfall's turmoil and Redridge's gnoll-infested borders. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia, who once saved him. Stoutmantle grumbles that he should have let Wiley rot. When the militia needs insight into the Defias conspiracy, it turns to Wiley. He reluctantly shares covert intelligence to repay his debt.

Wiley's Note. Wiley's Note is a confidential missive penned by the Lakeshire rogue Wiley the Black, paid as a debt to Gryan Stoutmantle. Its contents reveal alarming alliances formed by the Defias Brotherhood and draw Stormwind's intelligence service into the investigation. Penned in Redridge by the shady rogue Wiley the Black, this scribbled dispatch is handed over to settle an old favor owed to Gryan Stoutmantle. Within, Wiley exposes what he knows about the Defias Brotherhood's clandestine ambitions. His intelligence reveals that the brotherhood is not operating alone: they have brokered alliances with regional gnolls, kobolds, and goblin operatives to further their operations across the kingdom.

Willem. Outside Northshire Abbey, Willem sends recruits to meet the valley's threats. He serves under Marshal McBride in the Stormwind Army, with the Defias Brotherhood pressing into Northshire. Deputy Willem watches the gates of Northshire Abbey, where the Stormwind Army keeps a foothold in the valley. The kingdom's soldiers are spread across many territories, leaving local defense to small groups like Marshal McBride's garrison. Willem meets incoming volunteers and sends them to aid residents and guard the valley's edges.

William Pestle. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle gathers supplies for Stormwind's apothecary. He and his brother Morgan run the shop in the Trade District, and William hires travelers to find candles, kelp, and herbs. William works from Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn while his brother Morgan Pestle tends the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind City's Trade District. From Elwynn Forest, William works with local gatherers to secure raw materials the city shops need. He sends regular shipments to the capital, where Stormwind's citizens rely on a steady supply of restorative salves, draughts, and powders.

William's Shipment. In Goldshire, William Pestle packs candles from Elwynn's kobolds for his brother Morgan in Stormwind. William Pestle keeps trade moving between Goldshire and the capital. He gathers materials in Elwynn Forest, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot leave his duties to travel north, so he depends on couriers to carry the parcel of wax and candles into the city.

Williden Marshal. Williden Marshal is the ambitious human leader of Marshal's Expedition, based out of Marshal's Refuge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Driven by the lure of rare flora, mysterious crystals, and profitable scientific research, he brought his team into the crater only to watch their lower camps overrun by the basin's colossal beasts. Williden Marshal brought an entire scientific expedition deep into Un'Goro Crater seeking fortune and discovery. Intrigued by accounts of alien crystals, uncataloged plants, and untapped resources, he established multiple forward camps across the valley floor. However, the primeval wilderness quickly turned against them. The savage beasts of the crater dismantled their research posts, forcing Williden and his survivors to retreat up into the northern cliffs to establish Marshal's Refuge.

Wind Rider. Wind Rider is a Horde quest offered by Elu atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Aspiring to become a wind rider himself, Elu tasks adventurers with climbing into the craggy heights of Highperch to gather wild wyvern eggs to bolster the Horde's aerial mount reserves. Across Kalimdor, the Horde relies heavily on wind riders to ferry couriers, scouts, and warriors across vast distances. At Freewind Post, a young tauren named Elu aspires to join their esteemed ranks. With the demands of the expanding Horde outpacing the availability of mounts, Elu has been charged with helping procure new wyverns to supply the master wind riders, offering eager travelers a chance to assist in this vital effort.

Windbreak Canyon. Windbreak Canyon is a winding gorge along the northern side of Thousand Needles, situated between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats. Famous for its harsh drafts and jagged stone, it is heavily infested with nesting wind serpents. Travelers passing along the main road must tread carefully near its mouth to avoid being hunted from above. Carved into the sheer northern walls of the canyon floor, Windbreak Canyon spans a large stretch of territory east of Freewind Post. Rather than offering shelter, the ravine channels whistling winds between the rock spires, creating ideal perches for feral wind serpents. The predators lay their clutches along the stone ledges and strike at unwary travelers drifting off the main road. Those braving the canyon interior will also find the winding trails that climb upward toward the Weathered Nook.

Windfury Ridge. Windfury Ridge looms over Mulgore’s pastures, where harpies nest among wolves and cougars. Its slopes threaten travelers, while tauren hunters prize the harpies’ feathers. Windfury Ridge rises above Mulgore’s plains, where Windfury harpies nest among the crags. They swoop on wanderers who pass too close to the hills. Prairie wolves and mountain cougars prowl the rocky slopes, making this border of the tauren heartland dangerous. Tauren warriors hunt the harpies, whose iridescent feathers are sought in Thunder Bluff for ceremonial garments worn at feasts and weddings.

Winds in the Desert. A stolen supply caravan leaves Rezlak waiting in Durotar. Dustwind harpies ambushed it in Razorwind Canyon, scattering the construction materials among the cliffs. Rezlak came directly from Ratchet, sent by Chief Engineer Gazlowe to help the Horde build across Durotar. The harsh, barren land already makes fortification work hard. Now shipments keep vanishing before they reach the building sites, and without the cargo, work stops. The irritable goblin supervisor has nothing to build with.

Windshear Crag. In central Stonetalon, Windshear Crag lies scarred by the Venture Company's logging. The old forest is gone, replaced by machinery, muddy runoff, and logging crews. Kobolds dig for ore nearby, while a mountain passage leads beneath the ridges to Ashenvale. Windshear Crag's old forest is gone, cut down by the Venture Company for profit. Stumps and machinery now fill the basin. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a leper gnome, oversees the logging from a platform above Cragpool Lake. His engineering gave the company the Super Reaper 6000, which fells great trees in moments. The operation strips the mountain bare, stirring anger among rival engineers and local inhabitants alike.

Windtotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder receives travelers on a bluff above Ratchet. She welcomes those who honor the wisdom of ages past and offers an ancestral blessing and guidance to other elders across Kalimdor. On a grassy hill just northwest of Ratchet’s flight master, Windtotem the Elder watches over the goblin docks and open sea. Iron, gunpowder, and coin pass through the harbor below, while quiet Barrens winds and a shaft of celestial light reach the elder.
